title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet peppers, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the boiled pepper mixture, add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt, and let fry for 15 minutes.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well to coat the grains with the sauce.
Pour in the chicken broth, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir the rice well and serve hot.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibe (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat and cook, stirring frequently, until they release their moisture and turn golden brown.
Add the niter kibe, minced garlic, and minced ginger to the onions and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken stock, stirring well to form a paste.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes, adding small amounts of stock as needed to prevent burning.
Add the chicken pieces and salt, turning them to coat well in the sauce.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs, make shallow slits in them, and submerge them into the stew for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot with injera.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half a cup of milk, then squeeze out the milk and mash the bread.
Heat oil in a large skillet and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add curry powder and turmeric, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the mashed bread, apricot jam, vinegar, sultanas, chutney, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish and press it down evenly.
Beat the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour over the meat mixture.
Top with bay leaves and bake in the oven for 35 minutes until the topping is set and golden.
Serve warm with yellow rice.

title: Ugali with Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens, washed and finely sliced
instructions: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Slowly pour in the cornmeal while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and let simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until thick and pulling away from the sides.
Transfer the ugali to a serving plate and shape it into a dome.
Heat vegetable oil in a separate pan and sauté the chopped onions until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a paste.
Add the sliced collard greens, salt, and black pepper, stirring well.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the greens are tender yet vibrant green.
Serve the sukuma wiki hot alongside the ugali.

title: Tagine Lamb with Prunes and Almonds
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1/2 cup whole almonds, blanched and toasted
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and brown the lamb chunks on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, and saffron, stirring to combine.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small pot, cover the prunes with water and simmer for 15 minutes until plump, then drain.
Add the honey and a pinch of cinnamon to the prunes and let them caramelize slightly.
Add the prunes to the lamb tagine and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes.
Garnish the tagine with toasted blanched almonds and sesame seeds before serving warm.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, red bell pepper, scotch bonnet pepper, and half of the chopped onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the boiled tomato mixture and fry until the oil floats to the top.
Add the curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, and salt.
Stir in the washed rice and chicken stock, then mix well.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 30 minutes until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed.

title: Moroccan Tagine
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or traditional tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb chunks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot, cooking until soft.
Stir in the ginger, cumin, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and black pepper, cooking for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot and pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the dates and honey to the pot, stirring gently.
Simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes until the sauce thickens into a glaze.
Garnish with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Ethiopian Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Clean the chicken pieces with lemon juice and water, then drain and set aside.
Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat and cook, stirring frequently, until they release their water and soften completely without oil.
Add the niter kibbeh to the softened onions and sauté for 10 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, fresh ginger, and berbere spice blend, cooking for about 5 minutes while stirring continuously.
Pour in the chicken stock, cover, and simmer the sauce for 30 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot, coating them well in the thick sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, prick them lightly with a fork, and add them to the stew for the last 10 minutes.
Serve hot with injera flatbread.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the white bread in half of the milk, then squeeze out the excess milk and mash the bread.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the chopped onions and garlic until soft.
Add the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, and cook until browned.
Stir in the mashed bread, apricot jam, fruit chutney, raisins, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the meat mixture into a greased baking dish, smoothing the top.
Push the bay leaves into the meat mixture.
Whisk together the remaining milk and the eggs, then pour the mixture evenly over the beef.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is set and golden brown.

title: Senegalese Thieboudienne
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish fillets or steaks
1 cassava root, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and a paste made from some of the garlic.
Heat the peanut oil in a large pot and fry the fish until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add the chopped onions and remaining garlic, cooking until translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring often to prevent burning.
Pour in the water or fish stock and bring to a boil.
Add the carrots, cabbage, sweet potato, cassava, eggplant, and whole habanero peppers to the pot.
Simmer the vegetables until tender, then remove them along with the peppers and set aside, keeping warm.
Wash the broken rice and steam it over the remaining broth in a steamer basket or add it directly to the pot depending on traditional preference.
Cook the rice until fluffy and infused with the rich fish and vegetable broth.
Serve the rice on a large platter, topped with the fried fish and cooked vegetables.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté half of the chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently to avoid burning.
Pour in the blended tomato, bell pepper, and habanero mixture, and cook until the liquid reduces significantly.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt to taste.
Add the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice, stir well, and reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid to trap the steam, and let the rice cook for 25 to 30 minutes until tender.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the onions and garlic until soft and golden.
Add the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and brown it thoroughly, breaking up any clumps.
Stir in the apricot jam, chutney, lemon juice, tomato paste, raisins, and drained bread mixture. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish, pressing it down evenly.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour the mixture over the beef.
Top with bay leaves and bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is set and golden brown.

title: Doro Wat
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium-low heat and cook, stirring frequently, until completely soft and caramelized without adding any oil.
Add the niter kibbeh and stir until melted and combined with the onions.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, garlic paste, and ginger paste, cooking for about 5 minutes while stirring constantly.
Add the chicken stock and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces and lemon juice, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 40 to 50 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Prick the hard-boiled eggs gently with a fork and add them into the stew during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot with injera flatbread.

title: Bunny Chow
ingredients: 1.5 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into bite-sized cubes
2 tablespoons Durban masala or curry powder
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, add cinnamon sticks and cardamom pods.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the minced garlic, ginger, Durban masala, and turmeric, cooking for 1 minute.
Add the cubed lamb and brown on all sides.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the cubed potatoes and beef stock, then cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until the lamb and potatoes are tender.
Cut the loaf of white bread in half crosswise to create two hollowable blocks, and scoop out the soft crumb from the inside.
Ladle the hot lamb curry into the hollowed-out bread loaves and garnish with fresh coriander.

title: Ndole
ingredients: 1 pound bitter leaves (ndole), cleaned and boiled
1 pound raw peanuts, shelled and blended into a smooth paste
1 pound cooked beef and smoked fish, shredded
1 small piece of fresh ginger, minced
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, combine the boiled bitter leaves, peanut paste, and 3 cups of water, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook the mixture on low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent the peanuts from sticking to the bottom.
In a separate pan, heat the vegetable oil and sauté half of the sliced onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the shredded beef and smoked fish to the pan, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Transfer the meat and fish mixture into the pot with the simmering bitter leaves and peanuts.
Add the stock cubes, salt, and white pepper, and stir well to combine.
Stir in the cooked prawns, simmer for another 5 minutes, and remove from heat to serve warm with plantains or bobolo.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, and scotch bonnet peppers until smooth.
Boil the blended mixture until the water reduces significantly.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry half of the chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in the reduced pepper mixture and cook until the oil floats to the top.
Add curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, and salt to taste.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well to coat with the sauce.
Pour in the chicken stock, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat until the rice is tender.
Stir the rice, let it steam for another 5 minutes, and serve.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until all their moisture evaporates.
Add the niter kibbeh to the onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken broth, stirring continuously to prevent burning.
Simmer the sauce on low heat for about 45 minutes, adding broth gradually as needed.
Add the chicken pieces and salt, coating them thoroughly in the sauce.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for an additional 10 minutes before serving hot with injera.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it dry, reserving the remaining milk.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the chopped onions until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any clumps.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, raisins, and salt.
Mix in the squeezed bread, transfer the meat mixture to a greased baking dish, and press down firmly.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour over the baked meat mixture.
Arrange the bay leaves on top and bake for another 15 minutes until the custard topping is set and golden.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, habanero peppers, tomatoes, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the reduced pepper mix and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the chicken stock, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.

title: Egyptian Koshari
instructions: Cook the brown lentils in boiling water until tender, then drain.
Boil the macaroni and spaghetti until al dente, drain, and mix together.
Sauté the rice in a pot with a little oil, add water and salt, and cook until fluffy.
Fry the sliced onions in hot oil until deeply golden and crispy, then set aside on paper towels.
In the same oil, sauté the garlic, add crushed tomatoes, cumin, and salt, and simmer for 15 minutes to make the tomato sauce.
Stir the vinegar into the tomato sauce.
Layer the rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas in a serving dish, top with crispy onions, and serve with the tomato sauce.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Add the chopped onions and garlic to the pot and sauté until soft.
Stir in the ginger, cumin, turmeric, and saffron.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the chicken broth.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the green olives and preserved lemon slices, and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then squeeze out the milk and mash the bread.
Sauté the onions and garlic in a pan until soft, then add the ground beef and cook until browned.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, raisins, salt, and pepper.
Add the mashed bread to the meat mixture and mix well.
Transfer the mixture into a greased baking dish and press down firmly.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, pour over the meat, and top with bay leaves.
Bake in the oven for 45 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

title: Ethiopian Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Cook the finely chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat, stirring constantly until all their water evaporates.
Add the niter kibbeh to the onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken stock, stirring well to form a thick paste.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them thoroughly with the sauce.
Pour in the remaining chicken stock, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for another 10 minutes before serving hot with injera.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, habanero peppers, tomatoes, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the boiled pepper mixture and fry for another 15 minutes.
Add curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, chicken stock, and salt.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat until the rice is tender and absorbs the liquid.

title: Moroccan Tagine with Chicken and Olives
ingredients: 1/3 cup preserved lemons, rinsed and sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and garlic, cooking until softened.
Season the chicken pieces with ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper, then add them to the pot.
Brown the chicken on all sides for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth, reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the green olives and preserved lemon slices to the chicken.
Cover and simmer for another 15 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Ethiopian Doro Wat
ingredients: 3 pounds chicken drumsticks and thighs, skinned
instructions: Place the chicken pieces in a bowl, rub with lemon juice, and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
In a dry heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, cook the diced onions without oil, stirring frequently until they soften and turn golden.
Add the niter kibbeh and stir until melted and combined with the onions.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, garlic, and ginger, cooking for about 5 minutes while stirring constantly.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make shallow slashes in them, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for another 10 minutes to let the eggs absorb the flavors before serving.

title: South African Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the white bread in half a cup of milk, then squeeze out the milk and mash the bread.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the chopped onions and minced garlic until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, raisins, lemon juice, mashed bread, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish and press down evenly.
Whisk the remaining half cup of milk and the two eggs together, then pour over the meat mixture.
Top with bay leaves and bake in the oven for 35 minutes until the egg topping is set and golden.

title: Senegalese Thieboudienne
ingredients: 1 small cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small sweet potato, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and garlic, then pan-fry in peanut oil until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the chopped onions and tomato paste until fragrant and darkened slightly.
Add the carrots, cassava, sweet potato, and water to the pot, bringing it to a boil.
Place the fried fish and the whole habanero pepper on top of the vegetables, cover, and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Remove the cooked vegetables, fish, and pepper, keeping them warm.
Add the broken jasmine rice to the remaining boiling fish broth in the pot, cover, and cook on low heat until the rice is fluffy.
Serve the rice on a large platter topped with the fish and vegetables.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, habanero peppers, tomatoes, and half of the onion until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the blended pepper mixture and cook until the liquid reduces by half.
Add curry powder, thyme, salt, and bay leaves, then stir well.
Add the washed rice and chicken stock, stirring to combine.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes until the rice is cooked.

title: Moroccan Tagine
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Brown the lamb chunks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Add ginger, cumin, cinnamon, saffron, and salt, stirring for one minute.
Return the lamb to the pot and add the beef broth.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Stir in the green olives and preserved lemon slices, simmering for 15 more minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan and sauté the onions until golden.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, raisins, and soaked bread.
Season with salt and pepper, then transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish.
In a bowl, whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour over the beef mixture.
Top with slivered almonds and push bay leaves into the top.
Bake for 45 minutes until the custard topping is set and golden brown.

title: Doro Wat
instructions: Dry-sauté the chopped onions in a large pot over medium heat without oil until they are soft and translucent.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, sautéing for 5 minutes.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken stock, cooking for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces and salt, cover, and simmer on low for 45 minutes.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the pot.
Simmer for another 10 minutes before serving hot with injera.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 lb assorted meat (beef, tripe, and cow skin), cooked
instructions: Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste and set aside.
Heat palm oil in a pot for 2 minutes, then add the chopped onions and scotch bonnet peppers.
Add the egusi paste in small lumps to the oil without stirring immediately, allowing it to fry for 5 minutes.
Gently stir the fried egusi, then add the cooked assorted meat and meat stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally so it does not burn.
Add the smoked fish, ground crayfish, and chopped spinach.
Simmer for another 5 minutes, season with salt to taste, and serve hot.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet peppers, and half of the onion until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in the blended pepper mixture and cook until the liquid reduces by half.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and chicken stock, then bring to a simmer.
Add the washed rice, stir well, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.

title: Egyptian Koshari
instructions: Cook the brown lentils in boiling water until tender, then drain.
Boil the macaroni and spaghetti until al dente, drain, and mix together.
Sauté the rice in a bit of oil, add water and salt, and cook until fluffy.
Fry the sliced onions in hot oil until crispy and golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
In a saucepan, sauté garlic in oil, add crushed tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, and salt, and simmer for 15 minutes to make the sauce.
Layer the rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas in a bowl, top with tomato sauce and crispy onions.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
ingredients: 1/2 cup preserved lemon, rinsed and sliced
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Add onions and garlic to the pot and sauté until soft.
Stir in ginger, cumin, turmeric, and saffron, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pot, pour in the chicken broth, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes.
Add green olives and preserved lemon slices, cover, and simmer for 15 more minutes until the chicken is tender and sauce is reduced, then garnish with cilantro.

title: Ethiopian Doro Wat
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken drumsticks and thighs, skinned
instructions: Dry-sauté the chopped onions in a heavy pot over medium-low heat without oil until they are soft and golden.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and cook for 10 minutes, adding small amounts of water to prevent burning.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Add the chicken pieces and salt, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs, make shallow slits in each, add them to the stew, and simmer for 10 more minutes before serving.

title: South African Bobotie
ingredients: 2 slices white bread, soaked in 1 cup milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat vegetable oil in a pan and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, draining excess fat.
Stir in curry powder, turmeric, salt, raisins, apricot jam, lemon juice, and chutney.
Squeeze milk from the bread, mash the bread, and mix it into the beef mixture.
Transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish.
Whisk the eggs and extra milk together, pour over the beef, and top with bay leaves.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is set and golden brown.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, and scotch bonnet peppers until smooth.
Boil the blended mixture until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry half of the chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the reduced pepper puree and cook for 15 minutes.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, chicken stock, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce the heat to low to steam the rice until tender.

title: Egyptian Koshari
instructions: Boil the brown lentils in water until tender, then drain and set aside.
Cook the macaroni pasta according to package instructions and drain.
Heat oil in a pot and brown the vermicelli noodles, then add the rice, water, and salt, cooking until done.
Fry the sliced onions in hot oil until deeply golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
In a saucepan, sauté minced garlic, add crushed tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, and salt, simmering for 15 minutes to make the tomato sauce.
Layer the rice and lentils, top with macaroni, pour over the tomato sauce, and garnish with crispy fried onions.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
instructions: In a bowl, mix the ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, black pepper, and garlic with a little olive oil.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly over the chicken pieces.
Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot and sauté the sliced onions until soft.
Place the spiced chicken pieces on top of the onions.
Pour water into the pot, cover, and simmer on medium-low heat for 45 minutes.
Add the green olives and preserved lemon quarters to the tagine.
Cover again and simmer for another 15 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the sauce thickens.

title: Ethiopian Doro Wat
ingredients: 3 pounds chicken drumsticks and thighs, skinned
instructions: Dry-cook the finely chopped red onions in a heavy pot over medium heat without oil until they release their moisture and soften.
Add the niter kibbeh to the onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, garlic, and ginger, cooking for 5 minutes while stirring constantly.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces and salt, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the stew for the last 10 minutes of cooking.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Sauté the chopped onions in a pan until translucent, then add the ground beef and brown it.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, raisins, salt, and pepper.
Mix in the mashed bread and transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour the mixture over the beef.
Push the bay leaves into the top and bake in the oven for 30 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, and scotch bonnet pepper until smooth.
Boil the blended mixture in a pot until the water evaporates to concentrate the flavor.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry half of the chopped onions until golden brown.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Pour in the reduced pepper-tomato puree and fry for another 15 minutes until the oil floats to the top.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce the heat to low and let it steam for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir the rice, remove from heat, and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibe (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter) or unsalted butter
instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice and salt, then set aside for 30 minutes.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, dry-cook the chopped onions over medium-low heat, stirring frequently until caramelized and dry.
Add the niter kibe and sauté the onions for another 10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and cook for 5 minutes, adding a little stock if it sticks.
Add the remaining chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, prick them lightly with a fork, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for an additional 10 minutes, then serve hot with injera.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread slices in the 1 cup of milk, then mash with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the chopped onions and garlic until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, salt, and black pepper, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, and sultanas. Mix well.
Remove from heat, squeeze excess milk from the soaked bread, and stir the bread into the meat mixture.
Transfer the meat mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top.
In a small bowl, whisk together the eggs and the extra 1/2 cup of milk, then pour over the meat.
Place bay leaves on top and bake in the oven for 30 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

title: Senegalese Thieboudienne
ingredients: 1 kg broken rice, washed and drained
1 kg white fish fillets or steaks
1 cup dried tamarind paste soaked in water
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Make a stuffing by pounding garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper, then make small incisions in the fish and stuff them.
Heat peanut oil in a large pot and brown the fish on both sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, fry the onions until golden, add tomato paste, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, carrots, cabbage, sweet potatoes, cassava, and the scotch bonnet pepper to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Return the fish to the pot, reduce heat, and simmer until the vegetables are tender. Remove fish and vegetables and set aside.
Add the washed broken rice to the remaining boiling broth, cover, and cook on low heat until the rice absorbs the liquid and steams.
Fluff the rice and serve on a large platter topped with the cooked fish and vegetables.

title: North African Tagine Lamb with Prunes
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a traditional tagine or heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium heat.
Brown the lamb chunks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Add the sliced onions and minced garlic to the pot, sautéing until soft and translucent.
Return the lamb to the pot and stir in the ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, saffron, salt, and black pepper.
Pour in the water or stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small saucepan, simmer the prunes with honey, a pinch of cinnamon, and a splash of water for 15 minutes until plump.
Add the prunes and orange blossom water to the lamb tagine and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and toasted sliced almonds before serving warm with couscous.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the boiled pepper mixture, add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt, and fry for another 15 minutes.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well to coat the grains with the sauce.
Pour in the chicken stock, cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir the rice, let it steam for 5 more minutes, and serve.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan and fry the onions until soft and golden.
Add the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the mashed bread, apricot jam, chutney, raisins, vinegar, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the beef mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top.
Press the bay leaf into the center of the meat mixture.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, pour over the baked beef, and bake for another 15 minutes until set and golden brown.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/4 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice and let them rest for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, cook the chopped onions over medium-low heat without oil, stirring frequently until completely soft and caramelized.
Add the niter kibbeh and stir until melted and integrated with the onions.
Add the garlic and ginger, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and cook for 10 minutes, adding small amounts of chicken stock if it starts to stick.
Add the remaining chicken stock and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the stew for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot with injera.

title: Tagine Lamb with Prunes and Almonds
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: In a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and brown the lamb chunks on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, saffron, and salt, stirring well to coat the meat.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small pot, cover the prunes with water, add honey and cinnamon, and simmer for 15 minutes until plump and syrupy.
Fry the blanched almonds in a little oil until golden brown.
Add the cooked prunes and their syrup to the lamb tagine and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Garnish the tagine with toasted almonds and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Egusi Soup
instructions: Season the beef with salt and half of the chopped onion, add water, and boil until tender.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot for 2 minutes, then add the remaining chopped onions.
Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the hot oil to form small clumps, frying gently for 5 minutes without stirring too much.
Pour in the meat stock, blended scotch bonnets, and ground crayfish, and bring to a boil.
Add the cooked beef and smoked fish to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or bitterleaf and salt to taste, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and serve hot with pounded yam or eba.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, and scotch bonnet peppers until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry half of the chopped onions until translucent.
Add tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in the blended pepper mixture and cook until the liquid reduces and oil floats to the top.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce heat to low and let steam for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir well and serve hot.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak white bread in half of the milk, then mash it.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook onions and garlic until soft.
Add ground beef and brown thoroughly.
Stir in curry powder, turmeric, apricot jam, chutney, lemon juice, raisins, and salt.
Mix in the mashed bread and transfer to a greased baking dish.
Press bay leaves into the top of the meat.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Whisk remaining milk and eggs, pour over the beef, and bake for 15 more minutes until the custard sets.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until they release their moisture and turn translucent.
Add the niter kibbeh and continue to sauté the onions until they are deeply browned and caramelized.
Stir in the garlic paste, ginger paste, and berbere spice blend. Cook for 5 minutes, adding small splashes of broth to prevent burning.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them thoroughly with the sauce.
Pour in the remaining chicken broth, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, prick them lightly with a fork, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for another 10 minutes so the eggs absorb the flavors.
Serve hot with injera.

title: Ndole
ingredients: 1 pound bitter leaves, washed and boiled
2 pounds raw peanuts, boiled and blended into a paste
instructions: Wash the bitter leaves thoroughly in multiple changes of water to reduce bitterness, then set aside.
Heat palm oil in a large pot until hot, then add half of the chopped onions and fry until golden.
Add the blended peanut paste and stir continuously for 10 minutes to cook the peanuts.
Add the cooked beef, ground crayfish, garlic, and bouillon cubes, stirring well.
Stir in the washed bitter leaves and a splash of water, letting the mixture simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cooked prawns and remaining onions, stirring gently.
Season with salt to taste and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Serve warm with plantains or boiled yams.

title: Tagine Lamb with Prunes and Almonds
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Brown the lamb chunks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onions and garlic until softened.
Add the ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, saffron, and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot, add water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small saucepan, combine the prunes, honey, and a cup of water, and simmer for 15 minutes until syrupy.
Add the cooked prunes and their syrup to the lamb tagine and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Garnish with toasted blanched almonds and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend tomatoes, red bell pepper, and habanero pepper until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté half of the chopped onions until translucent.
Add tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Pour in the blended pepper and tomato mixture, cooking until the liquid reduces and oil separates to the top.
Add curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, salt, and chicken stock, then bring to a boil.
Stir in the rinsed rice, ensuring the liquid level is just below the rice surface.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid to trap steam, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Bunny Chow
ingredients: 1 small loaf of white bread, hollowed out
500g mutton or lamb, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add curry powder, turmeric, and cinnamon sticks, stirring for one minute.
Add the mutton pieces and sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften into a paste.
Add potatoes and beef stock, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour until the meat is tender and potatoes are cooked.
Season with salt to taste.
Cut the loaf of white bread in half horizontally to create two hollow bowls, and remove the soft crumb inside.
Ladle the hot curry into the bread bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread in half a cup of milk, then squeeze out the excess milk and mash the bread.
Melt butter in a pan and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add curry powder and fry for 2 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the mashed bread, apricot jam, chutney, lemon juice, raisins, and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the meat mixture into a greased baking dish and press down evenly.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, then pour over the meat mixture.
Top with almond flakes and press bay leaves into the custard layer.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard topping is set and golden brown.

title: Ndole
ingredients: 500g bitter leaves (ndole), thoroughly washed and boiled
500g raw peanuts, blended into a smooth paste
300g cooked beef or smoked fish, shredded
instructions: Boil the washed bitter leaves in water for about 20 minutes to reduce bitterness, then drain.
In a large pot, combine the peanut paste with water and bring to a simmer, stirring frequently to prevent burning.
Add the boiled bitter leaves to the peanut sauce and stir well.
In a separate pan, heat palm oil and sauté half of the chopped onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add the shredded beef and prawns to the pan, cooking for 5 minutes.
Transfer the meat and prawn mixture into the pot with the ndole and peanut sauce.
Add bouillon and salt to taste, then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve hot with fried plantains, boiled yams, or bobolo.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into pieces and skin removed
1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice and let rest for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
In a dry, heavy pot, cook the chopped onions over medium-low heat without oil, stirring often, until completely soft and moisture has evaporated.
Add the niter kibbeh to the onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, garlic paste, and ginger paste, cooking for about 10 minutes while stirring constantly.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs should be gently pierced with a fork and added to the stew during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot, traditionally accompanied by injera.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the reduced pepper mixture, curry powder, thyme, and bay leaves, and fry for 15 minutes.
Add the chicken stock and washed rice, stirring well to combine.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce heat to low and let steam for 30 minutes until the rice is cooked.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add ground beef and brown it thoroughly, breaking up any clumps.
Stir in curry powder, turmeric, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, and raisins, then season with salt and pepper.
Mix in the soaked bread and transfer the beef mixture to a greased baking dish.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, pour over the beef, top with a bay leaf, and bake for 35 minutes until set and golden.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/4 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Cook the chopped onions in a dry heavy pot over medium heat, stirring frequently, until moisture evaporates and they turn deep golden brown.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken broth, stirring continuously for 10 minutes to cook the spices.
Add the remaining chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Prick the hard-boiled eggs with a fork and add them to the pot, simmering for another 10 minutes before serving.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 pound assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow foot), cooked
1 cup smoked fish, cleaned and flaked
instructions: Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste.
Heat palm oil in a pot, add half of the chopped onions, and fry for 2 minutes.
Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the oil to form small clumps, frying gently for 5 minutes without stirring too much.
Add the meat stock, blended scotch bonnets, crayfish, and remaining onions, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cooked assorted meat and smoked fish, stirring gently, and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or bitterleaf, season with salt to taste, and simmer for 5 more minutes before removing from heat.

title: Tagine Lamb with Prunes and Almonds
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and brown the lamb chunks on all sides.
Add the sliced onions, garlic, ginger, ground cinnamon, turmeric, and saffron, stirring to coat the meat.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small pot, combine the prunes, honey, and a pinch of cinnamon with a little water, simmering for 15 minutes until syrupy.
Add the prunes and their syrup to the lamb tagine and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Garnish with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and slice the remaining onion, frying until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the reduced pepper puree and cook for 15 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the chicken stock, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt.
Stir in the washed rice, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the rice is tender.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat and cook, stirring frequently, until they release their moisture and turn golden brown.
Add the niter kibbeh and continue to sauté the onions until completely soft and paste-like.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and Berbere spice blend, cooking for about 5 minutes while adding small splashes of stock to prevent burning.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them thoroughly with the spiced onion sauce.
Pour in the remaining chicken stock, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs should be gently pricked with a fork and added to the stew.
Simmer for another 10 minutes before serving hot with injera.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet and sauté the chopped onions and garlic until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any clumps.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, chutney, lemon juice, raisins, and salt.
Mix in the soaked bread, transfer the meat mixture to a greased baking dish, and press down evenly.
Whisk the eggs and remaining milk together, pour over the meat, and bake for 30 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

title: Ndole
ingredients: 1 lb bitter leaves, washed and boiled multiple times to remove bitterness
1 lb raw peanuts, boiled and blended into a smooth paste
instructions: Boil the cleaned bitter leaves in fresh water for 20 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat palm oil in a large pot until hot, then fry half of the chopped onions until golden.
Stir in the blended peanut paste and cook for 10 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent sticking.
Gradually add the water or stock, simmering until the peanut mixture thickens.
Add the boiled bitter leaves, diced beef, shrimp, crayfish powder, and salt.
Stir well, cover, and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until all flavors combine and the oil surfaces slightly.
Serve warm with boiled plantains, yams, or bobolo.

title: Tagine Lamb with Prunes
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and brown the lamb pieces on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, and saffron, sautéing until the onions are soft.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
In a separate small saucepan, simmer the prunes with a little water, honey, and a pinch of cinnamon for 15 minutes until plump and syrupy.
Add the cooked prunes and their syrup to the lamb tagine.
Simmer uncovered for another 10 minutes to let the sauce reduce and thicken.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and slivered almonds before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and half of the onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry the remaining chopped onions until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the boiled pepper mixture, add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt. Fry until the oil floats to the top.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well to coat the grains with the sauce.
Pour in the chicken stock, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Mix well, turn off the heat, and let it steam for another 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then squeeze out the excess milk and mash the bread.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and sauté the onions and garlic until soft and golden.
Add the curry powder and turmeric, stirring for one minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the mashed bread, apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, raisins, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the beef mixture into a baking dish and press down evenly.
Whisk the eggs and the remaining milk together, then pour over the meat mixture.
Top with the bay leaves and bake in the oven for 35 minutes until the topping is set and golden brown.

title: Doro Wat
instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with lemon juice and let rest for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, cook the chopped onions completely dry without any oil or water over medium-low heat until soft and caramelized.
Add the niter kibbeh and stir until melted and integrated with the onions.
Add the berbere spice blend, minced garlic, and ginger, stirring continuously for about 10 minutes.
Gradually pour in the chicken stock, cover, and simmer the sauce for 30 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot, spooning the sauce over them.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make shallow slashes in them, and add them to the pot for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot with injera.

title: Ndole
ingredients: 1 lb bitter leaves, washed and boiled multiple times to reduce bitterness
1 lb raw peanuts, boiled and blended into a paste
1 lb cooked beef and smoked fish, chopped
instructions: Heat the palm oil in a large pot until hot, then add the chopped onions and garlic, sautéing until fragrant.
Add the blended peanut paste to the pot and stir continuously to prevent burning, cooking for about 10 minutes.
Add the cooked beef, smoked fish, and ground crayfish, stirring well to combine.
Stir in the prepared bitter leaves and mix thoroughly with the peanut sauce.
Add the bouillon cubes and salt to taste, adding a small amount of water if the mixture is too thick.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and serve hot with fried plantains, cassava, or yams.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 lb assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow foot), cooked
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Mix the ground egusi with a little water and chopped onions to form a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot for a minute, then drop small spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the oil to form small lumps.
Fry the egusi lumps gently for about 5 minutes without stirring too much so they hold their shape.
Pour in the meat stock, blended scotch bonnet peppers, and crayfish, then bring to a boil.
Add the cooked assorted meat and smoked fish to the pot, letting it simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or bitterleaf and adjust seasoning with salt and cubes.
Simmer for an additional 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender, then remove from heat and serve.

title: Traditional Tunisian Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and chopped bell peppers, cooking until soft and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic, grated tomatoes, ground caraway, harissa, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer the sauce uncovered for 20 minutes until thickened.
Use a spoon to make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook for 5 minutes until the egg whites are set and yolks are still runny.

title: Tunisian Couscous with Fish
ingredients: 1 kg fine or medium semolina couscous
4 firm white fish fillets, such as grouper or sea bass
3 carrots, peeled and cut into long halves
3 zucchini, cut into thick lengthwise pieces
1 cup chickpeas, soaked overnight and cooked
instructions: Prepare the couscous by steaming it in the top pot of a couscoussier over simmering water, rubbing it between your hands with a little oil and water twice.
In the bottom pot, heat olive oil and sauté tomato paste, harissa, coriander, turmeric, and salt.
Add water to the pot along with carrots, potatoes, and chickpeas, and bring to a boil.
Place the fish fillets and zucchini into the broth during the last 15 minutes of cooking so they do not overcook.
Fluff the steamed couscous with a tablespoon of olive oil and spread it onto a large serving platter.
Arrange the fish, vegetables, and chickpeas gracefully over the couscous and ladle some of the rich broth on top.

title: Brik a l'Oeuf
ingredients: 4 sheets of malsouka or spring roll pastry
1/2 cup canned tuna, drained and flaked
Pinch of salt and black pepper
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the flaked tuna, chopped parsley, minced shallot, and capers.
Heat an inch of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Lay one sheet of malsouka flat on a clean surface.
Place a small ring of the tuna mixture in the center and crack an egg right into the middle of it.
Season the egg with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Quickly fold the pastry edges over to form a semicircle, enclosing the filling completely.
Slip the brik carefully into the hot oil and fry for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

title: Ojja Merguez
ingredients: 6 authentic merguez sausages, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy skillet over medium heat and brown the merguez pieces, then remove them.
In the same oil, sauté the sliced onion and bell peppers until tender.
Add the diced tomatoes, crushed garlic, harissa, cumin, and salt, simmering until a thick sauce forms.
Return the cooked merguez sausages to the tomato sauce.
Crack the eggs directly into the mixture, cover the pan, and cook for 5 minutes until the egg whites are just set.
Serve hot straight from the pan with crusty Tunisian bread.

title: Lablabi
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight with 1 teaspoon baking soda
4 stale or toasted Tunisian bread loaves, broken into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Drain the soaked chickpeas, rinse them well, and place them in a large pot covered with fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the chickpeas are very tender.
In a bowl, mix the minced garlic, cumin, harissa, olive oil, and lemon juice with a ladle of the hot chickpea cooking liquid to create a flavorful paste.
Place the broken pieces of bread at the bottom of deep serving bowls.
Ladle the hot chickpeas and their broth generously over the bread so it absorbs the liquid.
Stir in a spoonful of the garlic-cumin-harissa sauce into each bowl.
Top each serving with a peeled soft-boiled egg, a drizzle of olive oil, and a few olives.

title: Classic Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons and Olives
ingredients: A generous pinch of saffron threads, crumbled
1 preserved lemon, pulp discarded and peel cut into strips
1 cup red or green Moroccan olives
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro and parsley
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and garlic, sautéing until soft and translucent.
Add the chicken pieces, ginger, turmeric, paprika, black pepper, salt, and saffron.
Coat the chicken well with the spices and brown lightly on both sides.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Add the preserved lemon strips and olives to the sauce around the chicken.
Cover and simmer for another 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and parsley before serving warm with crusty bread.

title: Traditional Beef and Vegetable Couscous
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into large chunks
2 tablespoons butter or smen (aged fermented butter)
1 small kabocha squash or pumpkin, cut into wedges
1 bunch fresh cilantro and parsley, tied with kitchen twine
instructions: In the base of a couscoussier, heat the oil over medium heat and brown the beef chunks.
Add the onions, grated tomatoes, salt, pepper, ginger, turmeric, and cinnamon.
Pour in the water, add the herb bundle, and bring to a boil.
Place the dry couscous in a wide bowl, rub with a little oil and water, and break up any lumps.
Transfer the couscous to the top steamer pot, place it over the boiling broth, and steam for 30 minutes once steam escapes.
Dump the couscous back into the bowl, sprinkle with a cup of cold water, and separate the grains with a fork.
Add the carrots and turnips to the broth, and let them cook for 15 minutes.
Add the squash, zucchini, and chickpeas to the broth, then steam the couscous a second time for 20 minutes.
Transfer the fluffy couscous to a large platter, make a well in the center, arrange the meat and vegetables, and ladle the rich broth over top.

title: Moroccan Harira Soup
ingredients: 1/2 pound lamb shoulder, cut into very small cubes
3 large tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and pureed
1/2 cup all-purpose flour mixed with 1 cup water to form a smooth slurry
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large soup pot over medium heat and sauté the lamb cubes and chopped onions.
Add the cilantro, parsley, celery, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, salt, and cinnamon.
Stir in the tomato puree, tomato paste, lentils, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 45 minutes until lentils are tender.
Stir in the cooked chickpeas.
Slowly pour in the flour-water slurry while stirring constantly to thicken the soup without lumps.
Add the vermicelli pasta and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring frequently so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
If desired, drizzle in the beaten egg just before turning off the heat, stirring gently to create ribbons.
Serve hot with dates and traditional honey pastries.

title: Zaalouk (Smoked Eggplant and Tomato Salad)
ingredients: 1/3 cup chopped fresh cilantro and parsley
instructions: Prick the eggplants with a fork and roast them directly over a gas flame or in a 400°F (200°C) oven until the skin is charred and the flesh is completely soft.
Allow the eggplants to cool, peel away the charred skin, and finely chop the smoky flesh.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the minced garlic for one minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, paprika, cumin, salt, and cayenne pepper, cooking until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Add the chopped eggplant to the skillet and mix well with the tomato sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, mashing everything together with a wooden spoon until well combined and pasty.
Stir in the chopped cilantro, parsley, and lemon juice.
Remove from heat and serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.

title: Msemen (Layered Flaky Flatbread)
ingredients: 1 cup vegetable oil and melted butter mixture for folding
1/2 cup fine semolina flour for dusting
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the fine semolina, all-purpose flour, salt, and instant yeast.
Gradually add the warm water and knead vigorously for 10 to 15 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft, and elastic.
Divide the dough into equal golf-ball-sized portions, brush with oil, cover with plastic wrap, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Lightly oil a work surface and flatten one dough ball using your oiled palms into a very thin, translucent circle.
Drizzle with the oil-butter mixture and sprinkle lightly with fine semolina flour.
Fold the top edge down to the middle, then the bottom edge up to create a rectangle, dusting with semolina between folds.
Fold the left side to the right and the right side over to form a neat square, and set aside to rest while repeating with remaining dough.
Flatten each square gently into a slightly thinner square.
Heat a heavy skillet or griddle over medium-high heat, lightly oil it, and cook the flatbread until golden brown and flaky on both sides.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Dry-sauté the chopped onions in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat without oil until translucent.
Add the niter kibbeh, minced garlic, and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and a splash of chicken stock, simmering on low heat for about 45 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the chicken pieces and remaining stock, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Peel the hard-boiled eggs, make shallow slits in them, and add them to the stew.
Simmer for another 10 minutes and serve hot with injera.

title: Misir Wat
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until golden brown.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and berbere, stirring constantly for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed red lentils and stir to coat them well with the spice mixture.
Pour in the water or broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.
Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat and serve.

title: Atakilt Alicha
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions, garlic, and turmeric, cooking until the onions are soft.
Add the cubed potatoes and sliced carrots, cooking for about 10 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the shredded cabbage, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring gently until all vegetables are tender.
Serve warm as a side dish with injera.

title: Tibsi
ingredients: 1 lb beef sirloin, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Heat niter kibbeh in a hot skillet over high heat.
Add the cubed beef and sear quickly until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced onions, garlic, and green chili peppers, stirring continuously for 5 minutes.
Toss in the chopped tomatoes and fresh rosemary, cooking until the tomatoes break down into a light sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat and serve sizzling hot.

title: Shiro Wat
ingredients: 1/3 cup niter kibbeh or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a medium pot and sauté the chopped onions until soft and golden.
Add the minced garlic and berbere, cooking for a minute until fragrant.
Whisk the shiro powder and warm water together in a bowl until smooth to avoid lumps.
Pour the shiro mixture slowly into the pot, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring frequently so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Season with salt and serve hot with injera.

title: Classic Nigerian Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, red bell peppers, scotch bonnets, and one onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot and fry chopped onions and tomato paste for 10 minutes.
Add the boiled tomato-pepper mixture to the pot and fry until the oil floats to the top.
Stir in the curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt.
Add the rinsed rice and stock, stir well, then cover tightly with foil and a lid.
Cook on low heat for 30 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Mix well and serve hot with fried plantains.

title: Rich Egusi Soup
ingredients: 500g assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow foot), pre-cooked
2 large handfuls chopped spinach or bitterleaf
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Heat the palm oil in a pot for 2 minutes, then add half of the chopped onions.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste.
Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the heated oil without stirring.
Cover the pot and let the egusi cook and form solid lumps for about 10 minutes.
Gently stir the lumps, then add the meat stock, blended peppers, crayfish, and remaining onions.
Add the pre-cooked assorted meat and smoked fish, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach or bitterleaf and adjust salt and seasoning.
Simmer for another 5 minutes and remove from heat.

title: Puff Puff
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, yeast, nutmeg, and salt.
Gradually pour in the warm water while mixing with your hand until a smooth, stretchy batter is formed.
Cover the bowl with a clean towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 2 hours until doubled in size.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Scoop batter with your hand and squeeze out small balls directly into the hot oil.
Fry, turning frequently, until golden brown on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

title: Beans Porridge (Ewa Riro)
instructions: Rinse the beans and put them in a pot with water, then boil for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse again.
Return the beans to the pot, add fresh water, and cook until tender.
In a separate pot, heat the palm oil and bleach it slightly for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped onions and tomatoes, and fry until soft.
Stir in the chopped peppers, ground crayfish, seasoning cubes, and salt.
Pour the cooked beans into the fried sauce, along with a little water.
Stir thoroughly, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until well blended.
Mash slightly if desired and serve hot.

title: Ofada Rice and Ayamase Sauce
instructions: Rinse the Ofada rice multiple times in warm water, then cook with fresh water until tender and set aside.
Blend the green bell peppers, green scotch bonnets, and green onions coarsely, then boil to remove excess water.
Heat the palm oil in a pot until it turns clear and bleaches completely black.
Allow the oil to cool slightly, then add chopped onions and the blended green pepper mixture.
Add the bleached oil back to heat, then stir in the boiled assorted meat, ponmo, shaki, and smoked prawns.
Stir in the ground crayfish, seasoning cubes, and salt.
Simmer on medium heat for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil floats to the top.
Serve the sauce hot over the cooked Ofada rice.

title: Ghanaian Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long grain basmati rice, washed and drained
2 pounds chicken pieces, seasoned and fried
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add half of the sliced onions and fry until translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes until the color darkens and oil separates.
Add the blended tomato and onion mixture, garlic, ginger, curry powder, thyme, and bay leaves.
Let the stew simmer until reduced and well cooked, about 15 minutes.
Add the seasoned chicken pieces and chicken stock, bringing it to a boil.
Stir in the washed rice, making sure the liquid level is just slightly below the rice.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid, then reduce the heat to the lowest setting.
Let it steam for 30 minutes until the rice is tender and infused with the smoky flavor.

title: Light Soup with Goat Meat
ingredients: 2 pounds goat meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon ground egusi or kontomire for thickening (optional)
instructions: Season the goat meat with salt, chopped onions, minced garlic, and ginger, then steam in a pot with no added water for 10 minutes.
Add the whole tomatoes, onion, and habanero peppers to the pot along with the water.
Bring to a boil and cook until the vegetables are very soft.
Remove the boiled vegetables, blend them into a smooth paste, and strain them back into the boiling soup pot.
Add the tomato paste and stir well to combine.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 30 to 45 minutes until the goat meat is tender and the soup has a light, fragrant consistency.
Adjust salt to taste and serve hot with fufu or omotuo.

title: Red Red (Bean Stew) with Fried Plantains
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and boiled until tender
1 teaspoon smoked paprika or cayenne pepper
2 smoked fish or dried shrimp powder
3 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced diagonally
instructions: Heat the red palm oil in a pot over medium heat until hot but not smoking.
Add half of the chopped onions and fry until golden brown.
Stir in the tomato paste, garlic, ginger, and ground pepper, frying for 5 minutes.
Add the dried shrimp powder and cooked black-eyed peas along with a cup of water from the boiled beans.
Simmer the stew on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and flavorful.
In a separate pan, heat vegetable oil and fry the plantain slices until golden brown on both sides; drain on paper towels.
Serve the hot bean stew garnished with the remaining raw onions alongside the fried sweet plantains.

title: Banku and Tilapia
ingredients: 2 whole fresh tilapia fish, cleaned and scored
instructions: Marinate the scored tilapia with garlic, ginger, pepper powder, and salt, then grill or broil until well cooked and crispy.
Mix the fermented corn dough and cassava dough together in a pot with water until completely smooth.
Place the pot over medium heat and stir continuously with a wooden spatula to prevent lumps.
As the mixture thickens, cover and let it steam for a few minutes, then vigorously knead and fold it until smooth and elastic.
Shape the banku into smooth mounds using a wet bowl.
Prepare the pepper sauce (shito/raw pepper) by mixing the blended green chilies, chopped tomatoes, and chopped onions with a pinch of salt.
Serve the hot banku alongside the grilled tilapia and fresh pepper sauce.

title: Kontomire Stew (Palava Sauce)
ingredients: 1 pound fresh cocoyam leaves (kontomire), washed and shredded
1 cup egusi (ground melon seeds), mixed with a little water to form a paste
2 tablespoons ground crayfish or dried shrimp powder
instructions: Blanch the shredded cocoyam leaves in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat the red palm oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and fry until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Drop in the egusi paste in small spoonfuls without stirring immediately, allowing it to form soft curds.
Gently stir in the flaked smoked fish, crayfish powder, and habanero peppers.
Add the blanched cocoyam leaves and mix everything together thoroughly.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until well combined and oil starts to settle on top. Serve with boiled yam or plantains.

title: Ceebu Jën (Senegalese Red Rice and Fish)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs broken jasmine rice, washed and drained
1 small cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small sweet potato, cut into chunks
1 small head of cabbage, cut into wedges
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the fish with a paste of garlic, parsley, and salt, then fry in peanut oil until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the onions and tomato paste for 5 minutes until darkened.
Add the water, root vegetables, cabbage, and scotch bonnet pepper. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, then remove them.
Steam the broken rice over the simmering fish broth until tender and fluffy.
Serve the rice topped with the fried fish and cooked vegetables.

title: Yassa Ayam (Chicken Yassa)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the chicken in lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Remove chicken from marinade and sear in a large pot with peanut oil until browned. Remove chicken.
In the same pot, cook the sliced onions until translucent and caramelized.
Return chicken to the pot, add the remaining marinade, bay leaves, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened. Serve over rice.

title: Mafé (Senegalese Peanut Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and cayenne pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in peanut oil in a large pot, then remove and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onions and tomato paste until fragrant.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook down for 10 minutes.
Stir in the beef broth and peanut butter until smooth, then return the beef to the pot.
Add carrots and sweet potato, simmer on medium-low for 1 hour until the meat is tender and the sauce thickens. Serve hot over rice.

title: Soupou Kandia (Senegalese Okra Soup)
instructions: Boil the meat in salted water until tender.
Add the finely chopped okra and palm oil to the pot with the meat.
Add the whole scotch bonnet peppers and let everything simmer on low, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add the shrimp in the last 10 minutes of cooking until pink and cooked through.
Serve the thick, slimy okra stew over a bed of white rice.

title: Thiere (Senegalese Couscous with Peanut Sauce)
instructions: Steam the millet couscous in a steamer basket over boiling water until fluffy, fluffing with a fork and adding a little water twice during steaming.
In a separate pot, brown the lamb with onions and tomato paste in a bit of oil.
