Add water, carrots, and pumpkin, simmering until the vegetables are half cooked.
Stir in the peanut paste to create a rich sauce and cook until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Serve the steamed millet couscous generously topped with the lamb and peanut sauce.

title: Ugali na Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens (sukuma wiki), washed and finely shredded
instructions: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed sufuria (pot).
Gradually add the maize flour while stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon (mwiko) to prevent lumps.
Keep kneading and stirring until the ugali is firm and pulls away easily from the sides of the pot, then cover and let it cook on low heat for 5 minutes before molding.
In a separate pan, heat the vegetable oil and sauté the onions until golden brown.
Add the diced tomatoes and salt, cooking until they form a thick paste.
Add the shredded collard greens, stir well, cover, and let them steam in their own juices for 5 minutes until tender.

title: Kenyan Beef Pilau
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
500 grams beef, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the sliced onions until deeply browned, being careful not to burn them.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and pilau masala, stirring constantly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef pieces and salt, cooking until the meat is browned and its juices have evaporated.
Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil, letting the meat cook until tender.
Add the soaked and drained basmati rice to the pot, stirring gently to combine.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.

title: Maharagwe ya Nazi (Beans in Coconut Milk)
instructions: Heat oil in a sufuria and sauté the onions until translucent.
Add the garlic and cumin powder, cooking for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and tomato paste, cooking until the tomatoes soften completely.
Add the boiled red kidney beans and mix well with the tomato base.
Pour in the thick coconut milk and season with salt.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and flavors meld.

title: Chapati
ingredients: 3 tablespoons vegetable oil (plus extra for layering and cooking)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the flour, salt, and sugar.
Add the warm water and 3 tablespoons of oil, kneading for about 10 minutes until a soft and smooth dough forms.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into equal balls, roll each ball out flat, brush with oil, cut a slit from the center to the edge, and roll it into a cone to create flaky layers.
Roll out each layered cone into a flat circular disc.
Cook on a hot, dry pan (tawa) for a minute on each side, then brush with oil and fry until golden brown spots appear on both sides.

title: Kenyan Mandazi
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and ground cardamom.
Rub the melted butter into the dry flour mixture using your fingertips.
Gradually pour in the coconut milk, kneading continuously until you get a soft, non-sticky dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest in a warm place for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls, roll each ball flat to about 1/2-inch thickness, and cut into quarters (triangles).
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan and fry the triangles in batches over medium heat until they puff up and turn golden brown on both sides.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the onions and garlic until soft and translucent.
Add the curry powder and turmeric, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Add the minced beef and brown it well, breaking up any lumps with a wooden spoon.
Stir in the apricot jam, chutney, vinegar, sultanas, and soaked bread.
Season well with salt and pepper, then simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Transfer the meat mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top.
Press the bay leaves into the surface of the meat.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and pour the custard over the meat.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is set and golden brown.
Serve hot with yellow rice, chutney, and sliced banana.

title: Chakalaka
ingredients: 2 cans (400g each) baked beans in tomato sauce
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, and ginger, and fry until soft and golden.
Stir in the curry powder and smoked paprika, cooking for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the diced green and red bell peppers and the grated carrots to the pot.
Sauté the vegetables for about 5 to 7 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sliced green chillies, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the canned baked beans and season with salt to taste.
Simmer uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes until all the flavors are well combined.
Remove from heat and let it cool slightly before serving.
Serve cold or at room temperature as a side dish with bread, pap, or meat.

title: Bunny Chow
ingredients: 1 loaf white bread, uncut and halved crosswise
500g lamb shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 cups potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add the cinnamon sticks, cardamom pods, and star anise, letting them sizzle for a minute.
Add the chopped onions and fry until golden brown.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and Durban curry powder, cooking for 1 minute while stirring constantly.
Add the lamb pieces and brown them well on all sides.
Add the grated tomatoes, potatoes, stock, and salt, then stir well.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for about 1 hour until the lamb and potatoes are tender.
Scoop out the soft crumb from the center of each bread half to create a hollow bread bowl.
Ladle the hot, spicy lamb curry generously into the hollowed-out bread halves.
Place the soft bread crusts back on top or serve them on the side for dipping.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve immediately with sambals.

title: Malva Pudding
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a medium ovenproof baking dish.
Cream the apricot jam, butter, and white sugar together in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg until well combined.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl.
Mix the milk and vinegar together.
Alternately fold the dry ingredients and the milk mixture into the creamed butter mixture.
Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and bake for 30 to 45 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
While the pudding bakes, combine the cream, butter, sugar, water, and evaporated milk in a saucepan.
Heat the sauce ingredients together, stirring until the butter is melted and the sugar is dissolved.
As soon as the pudding comes out of the oven, poke holes in it with a skewer.
Pour the hot sauce evenly over the hot pudding, letting it soak in completely.
Serve warm with custard or vanilla ice cream.

title: Potjiekos
ingredients: 1 kg lamb chuck, cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat a traditional cast-iron potjiekos pot (or heavy-bottomed pot) over an open fire or stove.
Add the cooking oil and brown the lamb chunks in batches until golden, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, fry the sliced onions and garlic until soft and translucent.
Return the meat to the pot and pour in the red wine and half of the beef stock.
Put the lid on and let it simmer gently for about 1 hour without stirring.
Layer the harder vegetables on top of the meat, starting with potatoes and carrots.
Add the remaining beef stock, season with salt, pepper, and dried herbs, and cover with the lid.
Simmer gently for another 45 minutes, resisting the urge to stir the layers.
Add the butternut squash and button mushrooms, then cook for 20 more minutes.
Finally, scatter the frozen peas on top, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat, gently stir the layers together just before serving.
Serve hot directly from the pot.

title: Traditional Tunisian Shakshouka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell peppers, and sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, harissa, coriander, caraway, and salt, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the grated tomatoes and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Use a spoon to make small wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the skillet and cook on low heat until the egg whites are set and yolks are still runny.

title: Tunisian Brik à l'Œuf
ingredients: 4 sheets of malsouka or fillo pastry
1/2 cup canned tuna, drained and flaked
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the tuna, minced onion, parsley, and capers.
Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Place one sheet of malsouka on a clean surface and place a quarter of the tuna mixture in the center.
Make a small depression in the center of the mixture and carefully crack an egg into it.
Season the egg with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Quickly fold the pastry edges over to form a semicircle, enclosing the filling.
Carefully slide the brik into the hot oil and fry for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.

title: Kefteji (Tunisian Spiced Vegetables and Eggs)
ingredients: 3 green bell peppers, cored and halved
instructions: Fry the potato cubes in hot oil until golden and cooked through, then drain on paper towels.
Fry the bell peppers and hot peppers until blistered and tender, then let cool slightly.
Chop the fried peppers and potatoes coarsely together with a sharp knife or cleaver.
In a skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil, add the chopped tomatoes and harissa, and cook until reduced.
Add the chopped vegetables to the tomato mixture and stir well to combine.
Fry the eggs separately sunny-side up or scramble them directly into the vegetable mixture.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley and serve warm with crusty bread.

title: Tunisian Couscous with Fish
ingredients: 4 firm white fish fillets (like grouper or sea bass)
3 carrots, peeled and cut into lengths
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In the bottom pot of a couscoussier, heat olive oil and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Stir in tomato paste, harissa, caraway, coriander, salt, and enough water to create a broth.
Add the carrots and potatoes to the broth and bring to a boil.
Place the couscous in the top steamer basket and steam over the simmering broth for 20 minutes.
Empty the couscous into a large bowl, sprinkle with a cup of salted water, rub between your palms to separate the grains, and let rest.
Add the zucchini and the fish fillets to the broth, simmering gently until the fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Return the couscous to the steamer for a final 10 minutes of steaming.
Mound the couscous on a large serving platter, arrange the fish and vegetables on top, and ladle some of the rich broth over it.

title: Mloukhia (Tunisian Jew's Mallow Stew)
ingredients: 1kg beef chuck, cut into medium cubes
instructions: In a wide, heavy-bottomed pot, whisk the powdered mloukhia with the olive oil until completely smooth with no lumps.
Place the pot over medium-low heat and stir constantly for about 30 minutes until the mixture bubbles and the oil begins to separate.
Carefully pour in the boiling water, stirring continuously to prevent lumps from forming.
Add the beef cubes, smashed garlic, coriander, caraway, harissa, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 3 to 4 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the sauce has a rich, dark green-black oil sheen on top.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with crusty white bread.

title: Classic Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons and Olives
ingredients: A large pinch of saffron threads
1 preserved lemon, rind sliced into strips
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and garlic, and sauté until soft and translucent.
Add the chicken pieces, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, salt, and saffron, stirring to coat the chicken.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the olives and preserved lemon strips to the sauce around the chicken.
Cover and simmer for another 15 minutes to blend the flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Beef and Prune Tagine (L'ham L'massal)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into large chunks
1/4 cup raw almonds, blanched and fried
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the beef chunks on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Stir well, cook for 5 minutes until onions are soft, then add the water.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and let simmer for 1.5 hours until the beef is very tender.
In a separate small saucepan, combine the prunes, honey, orange blossom water, and 1/2 cup of water from the main pot.
Simmer the prunes gently for 15 minutes until they are plump and the syrup thickens.
Add the cooked prunes and their syrup to the beef tagine, warming through for 5 minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with fried almonds and toasted sesame seeds.

title: Traditional Vegetable Couscous
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
4 carrots, peeled and cut into halves lengthwise
1 small pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and chunked
instructions: Place couscous in a wide bowl, rub with vegetable oil and 1 teaspoon of salt, then sprinkle with 1 cup of water, separating the grains with your hands.
Set the couscous in the top tier of a couscoussier (steamer) over the simmering broth.
In the base of the couscoussier, combine lamb, onions, chickpeas, spices, olive oil, grated tomatoes, and 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil.
Once steam rises through the couscous grains for 20 minutes, dump the couscous back into the wide bowl.
Sprinkle the couscous with 2 cups of water, break up any lumps with a fork, and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Add the carrots, pumpkin, zucchini, and cabbage to the broth.
Return the couscous to the steamer for a second 20-minute steam.
Transfer the fluffy couscous to a large platter, make a well in the center, arrange the meat and vegetables, and ladle the rich broth over the top.

title: Moroccan Tomato and Pepper Salad (Taktouka)
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Roast the bell peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is charred all over.
Place the charred peppers in a bowl, cover with a plate for 10 minutes to steam, then peel off the skin, remove seeds, and chop finely.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the minced garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt, and cayenne pepper.
Cook the tomatoes, mashing them with a wooden spoon, until they break down into a thick sauce, about 15 minutes.
Add the chopped roasted bell peppers to the tomato sauce.
Simmer together uncovered for another 10 minutes until most of the liquid evaporates.
Stir in the fresh parsley and cilantro, remove from heat, and serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Moroccan Mint Tea (Atay)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon loose green tea leaves (Gunpowder tea)
1 large bunch of fresh spearmint, washed
instructions: Place the green tea leaves in a traditional Moroccan teapot.
Pour 1 cup of boiling water into the pot, swirl it around for 30 seconds to rinse the leaves, and discard the water.
Add the fresh spearmint leaves and the sugar into the pot with the rinsed tea.
Pour 4 cups of boiling water into the pot over the mint and sugar.
Place the teapot on the stovetop over medium heat for 1 minute until it just begins to bubble at the surface.
Remove from heat and stir or let steep for 3 to 4 minutes.
Hold the teapot high above traditional tea glasses and pour to aerate and create a light foam on top.
Serve hot.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/2 cup niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
instructions: Dry-cook the chopped onions in a heavy pot over medium heat without oil until they release their moisture and soften, about 20 minutes.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic paste, and ginger paste, and sauté until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice blend and a splash of water, reducing the heat to low, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the chicken pieces and broth, cover, and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Peeled hard-boiled eggs, make small slits in them, and add them to the pot.
Simmer for another 10 minutes to let the eggs absorb the flavors, then serve hot with injera.

title: Misir Wat
ingredients: 2 cups red lentils, rinsed and drained
3 tablespoons vegetable oil or niter kibbeh
instructions: Heat oil in a medium pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onions until translucent and soft.
Add the garlic paste, ginger paste, and berbere spice blend, stirring constantly for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed red lentils and 3 cups of water, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally until the lentils are tender and creamy.
Season with salt to taste and serve warm.

title: Shiro Wat
ingredients: 1 cup shiro powder (ground chickpeas or split peas)
1/2 cup niter kibbeh or vegetable oil
instructions: Sauté the chopped onions in a pot over medium heat until golden brown.
Add the niter kibbeh and minced garlic, cooking for another minute.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a paste.
Whisk the shiro powder slowly into the water to avoid lumps, then pour it into the pot.
Reduce heat to low, add the whole green chili pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring frequently so it does not stick.
Adjust salt and serve hot.

title: Tibs
ingredients: 1 lb beef tenderloin or lamb, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a skillet over high heat.
Add the beef cubes, salt, and black pepper, and sear until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced onions, garlic, and fresh rosemary, tossing well.
Add the jalapeño peppers and optional spice, cooking for another 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve immediately while sizzling hot.

title: Atakilt Wot
ingredients: 3 carrots, peeled and sliced into coins
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the sliced onions until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, and turmeric powder, stirring until aromatic.
Add the cubed potatoes and sliced carrots, cooking for about 10 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped cabbage and salt, mixing well to combine all the vegetables.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes until all the vegetables are tender, stirring gently to prevent sticking.
Remove from heat and serve warm.

title: Classic Nigerian Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the red bell peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnets, and one chopped onion until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into a pot and boil until the excess water evaporates.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot, add the remaining sliced onion, and fry until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder, thyme, and bay leaves.
Add the reduced tomato-pepper purée and chicken stock, then season with salt to taste.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the boiling stew, stirring to combine.
Cover the pot tightly with foil paper and a lid to trap the steam, then turn the heat to low.
Cook for 30 minutes until the rice is tender and has absorbed all the liquid.
Stir well before serving to mix the bottom crust with the rest of the rice.

title: Nigerian Egusi Soup
ingredients: 500g assorted meat (beef, tripe, cow foot), cooked
instructions: Mix the ground egusi with a little water and chopped onions to form a thick paste.
Heat palm oil in a pot on medium heat for two minutes, without bleaching it.
Add the remaining chopped onions and fry for a minute.
Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the oil to form small lumps without stirring immediately.
Cover the pot and let the egusi cook and fry in the oil for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the cooked assorted meat, smoked fish, meat stock, blended peppers, and crayfish.
Season with bouillon cubes and salt, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach or bitterleaf and stir well.
Simmer for another 5 minutes until the greens are tender and the soup is well combined.
Remove from heat and serve hot with pounded yam.

title: Efo Riro (Yoruba Spinach Stew)
ingredients: 4 bunches fresh spinach (efo shoko or tively), washed and sliced
4 large red bell peppers, coarsely blended
instructions: Heat the palm oil in a large pot on medium heat for a few minutes.
Add the chopped onions and fry until fragrant.
Add the coarsely blended red bell peppers and scotch bonnets, and fry until the liquid reduces.
Stir in the ground crayfish, cooked assorted meat, ponmo, and flaked smoked mackerel.
Season with bouillon cubes and salt, then cook for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Add the sliced spinach directly into the pot without adding extra water.
Stir thoroughly to combine the greens with the rich stew base.
Cook for 3 to 5 minutes until the spinach is wilted and tender, ensuring the bright green color remains.
Turn off the heat and serve warm.

title: Beans Porridge (Ewa Riro)
ingredients: 3 cups brown beans or honey beans, picked and washed
2 medium onions, one sliced and one chopped
2 smoked fish, cleaned and broken into chunks
instructions: Rinse the beans and place them in a pot with 4 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, then drain the water to remove gas-producing elements.
Add fresh water to the beans, add the sliced onion, and cook on medium heat until the beans are soft.
Once the beans are tender, add the palm oil, chopped onions, chopped scotch bonnets, ground crayfish, and smoked fish.
Season with bouillon cubes and salt to taste.
Stir well and mash some of the beans slightly with the back of your spoon to create a thick consistency.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, allowing the palm oil to integrate fully.
Stir occasionally to prevent burning at the bottom, then serve hot.

title: Nigerian Fried Plantains (Dodo)
ingredients: 3 ripe plantains with yellow and black-spotted skin
instructions: Peel the plantains by slicing off the ends and scoring the skin lengthwise with a knife.
Cut the plantains diagonally or into rounds about half an inch thick.
Sprinkle a tiny pinch of salt over the plantain slices and toss gently.
Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until hot.
Carefully place the plantain slices into the hot oil in a single layer without overcrowding.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside turns golden brown.
Flip the slices and fry the other side for another 2 minutes until evenly golden and caramelized.
Remove the fried plantains with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serve warm as a side dish or snack.

title: Ghanaian Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long grain parboiled rice, washed
500g chicken or beef, seasoned and pre-cooked
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add half of a sliced onion and fry until translucent.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 15 minutes, stirring frequently to avoid burning.
Pour in the blended tomato, onion, and pepper mixture and cook until the liquid reduces and oil floats to the top.
Add curry powder, dried thyme, salt, and bay leaves.
Add the pre-cooked meat and stir well.
Add the washed rice and water or stock, stirring to combine everything.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, then turn the heat down to low.
Let it steam for 35 to 45 minutes until the rice is tender and forms a slight crust at the bottom.
Fluff and serve warm.

title: Ghanaian Red Red (Bean Stew with Fried Plantains)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and boiled until tender
1 tsp cayenne pepper or ground chili
3 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced diagonally
instructions: Boil the soaked black-eyed peas in plenty of water until soft and set aside with their cooking liquid.
Heat palm oil in a pot over medium heat and warm gently without bleaching.
Add the chopped onions, minced garlic, and ginger, sautéing until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes, ground shrimp, and cayenne pepper, simmering until the sauce thickens and oil separates.
Add the boiled black-eyed peas along with a cup of their liquid into the stew.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, seasoning with salt to taste, until the stew is thick and rich.
In a separate pan, heat vegetable oil and fry the plantain slices until golden brown on both sides.
Drain the fried plantains on paper towels.
Serve the hot red red bean stew alongside the fried sweet plantains.

title: Fufu and Light Goat Soup
ingredients: 1 kg goat meat, cut into pieces
2 bulbs of fresh garden eggs (African eggplant)
2 cups cassava flour and 2 cups plantain flour (or fufu powder)
instructions: Season the goat meat with salt, blended onion, ginger-garlic paste, and steam in a pot for 10 minutes.
Add the whole tomatoes, remaining onion, scotch bonnet peppers, garden eggs, and 4 cups of water to the pot.
Boil until the meat is tender and the vegetables are soft.
Remove the boiled tomatoes, onions, peppers, and garden eggs, and blend them into a smooth paste.
Strain the paste back into the goat soup, add tomato paste, and simmer for another 15 minutes until the soup is flavorful.
To make the fufu, mix the cassava and plantain flour in a saucepan with a little water over medium-low heat.
Stir vigorously with a wooden paddle as it thickens and becomes stretchy.
Add small splashes of water and continue kneading until fully cooked and smooth.
Mould the fufu into smooth balls and place them in deep bowls.
Pour the hot light goat soup over the fufu and serve immediately.

title: Ga Kenkey with Shito and Fried Fish
ingredients: 3 rolls of cooked Ga Kenkey (fermented corn dough wrapped in corn husks)
2 medium red snapper or tilapia fish, cleaned and scored
1 cup ready-made Ghanaian black pepper sauce (Shito)
instructions: Season the cleaned fish with garlic powder, ginger powder, and salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet and fry the fish until crispy and golden brown on both sides.
Remove the fish and set aside to drain.
Unwrap the Ga Kenkey and slice it into bite-sized wedges.
Steam the kenkey wedges for 10 minutes to warm them through.
In a small bowl, mix the diced tomatoes and onions together.
Serve the warm Ga Kenkey with the fried fish, a generous dollop of shito, and the fresh tomato-onion mix on the side.

title: Kokonte and Groundnut Soup
ingredients: 1 cup smooth natural peanut butter (groundnut paste)
instructions: Boil the meat with chopped onion, salt, and water until tender.
Add the whole tomatoes, onions, and scotch bonnet peppers to the boiling meat pot and cook until soft.
Remove the boiled vegetables, blend them into a smooth puree, and pour back into the meat pot.
Whisk the peanut butter with a little warm water to form a smooth paste, then stir it into the soup.
Add the tomato paste and simmer the soup on medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally until the oil separates to the top.
To make the kokonte, bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a separate pot.
Gradually pour in the dried cassava flour while stirring vigorously with a wooden spatula to prevent lumps.
Cover and let it simmer on low heat for 5 minutes, then knead until smooth, dark brown, and thick.
Mould the kokonte into portions and serve alongside the hot groundnut soup.

title: Ceebu Jën (Senegalese Red Jollof Rice with Fish)
ingredients: 2 lbs broken jasmine rice, washed and drained
2 large white fish fillets (like grouper or snapper)
1 small cassava root, peeled and cut into chunks
1 sweet potato, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small head of cabbage, cut into wedges
1 cup dried tamarind soaked in warm water (optional)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the fish with a paste made of garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper, then fry in hot peanut oil until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the chopped onions and tomato paste until browned and caramelized.
Add the blended tomatoes, water, and all the tough vegetables (cassava, sweet potato, carrots) and simmer until tender.
Remove the cooked vegetables and fish, then add the washed broken rice to the remaining flavorful broth.
Cover tightly and steam the rice on low heat until tender and fluffy.
Serve the red rice on a large communal platter, topped with the fried fish and vegetables.

title: Yassa Ayam (Senegalese Lemon and Onion Chicken)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into serving pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces in lemon juice, Dijon mustard, sliced onions, minced garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and brown in a large pot with peanut oil over medium-high heat until golden on all sides. Remove chicken.
In the same pot, add the leftover onions and marinade liquid, cooking until the onions are soft and caramelized.
Return the chicken to the pot, add the chicken broth and whole scotch bonnet peppers.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot over white rice or couscous.

title: Soupou Kandia (Senegalese Okra and Palm Oil Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into cubes
1/2 lb dried fish or smoked fish, cleaned and flaked
instructions: Heat the palm oil in a large pot, then add the chopped beef and onions, cooking until browned.
Add the water, dried fish, and minced garlic, bringing to a boil until the meat is tender.
Stir in the finely chopped okra and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, until the okra releases its mucilage and blends smoothly with the oil and broth.
Add the shrimp in the last 10 minutes of cooking until pink and cooked through.
Serve hot poured generously over freshly steamed white rice.

title: Mafé (Senegalese Peanut Butter Stew)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs lamb or beef shoulder, cut into cubes
1 small sweet potato, peeled and cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat peanut oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the meat cubes on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, and tomato paste, stirring well for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water or stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the meat starts to become tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with a little warm broth to loosen it, then stir it into the pot along with the carrots and sweet potato.
Add the habanero pepper and simmer on low heat, stirring frequently so the peanut butter doesn't burn at the bottom, for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender and sauce is thick.
Serve warm over a bed of broken white rice.

title: Thakry (Senegalese Couscous and Sweet Yogurt Dessert)
ingredients: 2 cups plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
instructions: Steam the dry millet couscous in a steamer basket over boiling water for about 15 minutes until soft and fluffy.
Transfer the steamed couscous to a large bowl and fluff with a fork, letting it cool down completely.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla extract, and grated nutmeg until smooth.
Pour the creamy yogurt mixture over the cooled millet couscous and stir gently to combine.
Fold in the raisins and grated coconut.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least an hour before serving cold in bowls.

title: Ugali na Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens (sukuma wiki), finely chopped
instructions: Bring the 4 cups of water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed sufuria (pot).
Gradually add the maize flour while stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon (mwiko) to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat, cover, and let it simmer until the mixture firms up and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Turn out the cooked ugali onto a serving plate and shape it into a dome.
In a separate pan, heat the vegetable oil and fry the onions until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and salt, cooking until they form a thick paste.
Stir in the chopped collard greens and beef masala, cover, and let them wilt and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve the hot sukuma wiki alongside wedges of ugali.

title: Kenyan Beef Pilau
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a large pot and fry the sliced onions until deeply golden brown.
Add the garlic, ginger, and pilau masala, stirring constantly for one minute until fragrant.
Add the beef chunks and sear until browned on all sides.
Pour in the beef broth, cover, and simmer until the beef is tender and cooked through.
Add the rinsed basmati rice and salt, stirring gently to combine with the meat and spices.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot with kachumbari.

title: Ndengu (Green Grams Stew)
ingredients: 2 cups dry green grams (ndengu), soaked overnight
instructions: Boil the soaked green grams in fresh water until tender, then drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a pot and sauté the onions until golden brown.
Add the minced garlic and cumin powder, stirring until aromatic.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a rich paste.
Stir in the cooked green grams and season with salt.
Pour in the coconut milk, lower the heat, and let the stew simmer for 15 minutes to thicken.
Serve warm with chapati or rice.

title: Kenyan Chapati
ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (plus extra for layering and cooking)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the flour, salt, and sugar.
Gradually add warm water and a little oil, kneading for about 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into equal golf-ball-sized portions.
Roll out each ball into a flat circle, brush with oil, cut a slit from the center to the edge, and roll it up into a cone shape to create flaky layers.
Roll the cone flat again into a round disc.
Cook on a hot dry pan (tava) for a minute, then brush with oil and fry until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
Stack the cooked chapatis in a hot pot to keep them soft.

title: Maharagwe ya Nazi (Coconut Beans)
ingredients: 2 cups dry red kidney beans, soaked and boiled until tender
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a sufuria and fry the chopped onions until soft and golden.
Add the curry powder and turmeric, stirring for 30 seconds.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook until they form a thick, smooth sauce.
Stir in the boiled kidney beans and mix well to coat them in the spice paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Season with salt, reduce heat, and let it simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Serve hot with ugali, rice, or chapati.

title: Traditional Bobotie
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 180 degrees Celsius.
Soak the bread in half a cup of milk, then squeeze out the excess and mash well.
Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the onions and garlic until soft.
Add the curry powder, turmeric, salt, and pepper, and fry for another minute.
Add the beef mince and cook until well browned.
Stir in the apricot jam, vinegar, and mashed bread, mixing thoroughly.
Transfer the mince mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top.
Push the bay leaves into the mixture.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes.
Whisk the remaining milk and eggs together, pour over the baked mince, and return to the oven for 15 minutes until set.
Serve hot with yellow rice and chutney.

title: Chakalaka
ingredients: 1 can baked beans in tomato sauce
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger until translucent.
Add the curry powder and smoked paprika, stirring constantly for one minute.
Add the green and red bell peppers and grated carrots, cooking for about 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and reduce heat to simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the can of baked beans and mix well.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for another 5 minutes, then remove from heat.
Serve cold or warm as a side dish.

title: Durban Lamb Bunny Chow
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into bite-sized cubes
3 tbsp Durban masala or hot curry powder
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add onions, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves, and fry until golden brown.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, and Durban masala, stirring for one minute.
Add the lamb cubes and brown them on all sides.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and salt, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and a splash of water if needed, continuing to simmer until the meat and potatoes are tender.
Cut the loaf of white bread in half across the middle to make two bunny chow quarters.
Hollow out the inside of each bread half, leaving a thick crust.
Spoon the hot lamb curry into the hollowed-out bread.
Top with the bread lid and serve immediately with sambals.

title: Milktart
instructions: Preheat oven to 180 degrees Celsius and grease a 23cm pie dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Mix the egg yolk and ice water, then bind the pastry dough together.
Press the pastry evenly into the pie dish and bake blind for 15 minutes.
In a saucepan, heat 3.5 cups of milk with the cinnamon stick until just before boiling.
Whisk the remaining milk, sugar, cornflour, cake flour, and egg yolks together in a bowl.
Remove the cinnamon stick from the hot milk, then slowly whisk in the egg mixture.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the custard thickens significantly.
Remove from heat and stir in the butter and vanilla essence.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the hot custard.
Pour the custard into the baked pastry crust and dust generously with ground cinnamon.
Allow to cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before slicing.

title: Potjiekos
ingredients: 1.5 kg lamb neck or chuck, cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat a traditional cast-iron potjiekos pot over an open fire or gas stove.
Add oil and brown the lamb pieces in batches, then set aside.
In the same pot, fry the onions and garlic until soft and caramelized.
Return the meat to the pot on top of the onions.
Pour in the beef stock and white wine, cover with the lid, and let it simmer slowly without stirring for 1 hour.
Layer the carrots, potatoes, and sweet potatoes on top of the meat in distinct layers.
Season with salt, pepper, and dried thyme, cover, and simmer for another 45 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and frozen peas on top, cover, and cook for 15 more minutes.
Gently stir the pot just before serving to combine the layers and gravy.
Serve warm in deep bowls.

title: Traditional Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 120C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the prepared baking tray, shaping into a circle with a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside with the door closed.
Whip the thickened cream until soft peaks form.
To serve, top the cooled pavlova with whipped cream and arrange the strawberries, kiwifruit, and passionfruit pulp over the top.

title: Classic Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C and grease and line a 20x30 cm lamington tin.
Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cream butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then stir in vanilla extract.
Fold in the dry ingredients alternately with the milk until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Allow the cake to cool completely, preferably overnight, then cut into even squares.
To make the icing, whisk icing sugar, cocoa powder, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing to coat all sides, let excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Place on a wire rack to set.

title: New Zealand Cheese Scones
instructions: Preheat oven to 210C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt, mustard powder, and cayenne pepper into a large bowl.
Add the diced cold butter and rub it into the dry ingredients using your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in three-quarters of the grated cheese.
Make a well in the center and add the milk, mixing quickly with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it into a square about 3 cm thick.
Cut the dough into even squares with a sharp knife.
Place scones on the prepared tray, top with the remaining cheese, and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown and risen.

title: Aussie Meat Pies
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Heat a little oil in a pan and brown the minced beef and chopped onion over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and cook for another minute.
Pour in beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook until the gravy thickens richly, then season with salt and pepper and let cool.
Cut out four circles of shortcrust pastry to line the base and sides of the pie tins.
Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Cut out four circles of puff pastry to fit over the tops, placing them on and crimping the edges to seal.
Brush the tops with beaten egg wash and cut a small steam vent in the center of each pie.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden and puffed.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine oats, flour, coconut, and caster sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix the bicarb soda with boiling water, then add it to the melted butter and syrup mixture, stirring as it froths.
Pour the liquid mixture into the dry ingredients and stir well until thoroughly combined.
Roll tablespoonfuls of the mixture into balls and place them on the baking trays, leaving space for spreading.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.
Allow the biscuits to cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely and crisp up.

title: Traditional Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whip egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add granulated sugar, one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the white vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the parchment paper, shaping it into a circle and creating a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside with the door closed.
Whip the heavy cream until stiff peaks form and spread it over the cooled pavlova.
Top with fresh mixed berries and sliced kiwifruit before serving.

title: Classic Aussie Meat Pies
ingredients: 1/4 cup cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cornstarch mixture to thicken the gravy, stir well, and remove from heat to cool slightly.
Cut shortcrust pastry to line the base and sides of the pie tins, and cut puff pastry for the tops.
Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Place the puff pastry tops over the filling, trim the edges, press to seal, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden brown and puffed.

title: ANZAC Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Combine oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a saucepan over low heat.
Mix the boiling water and baking soda together, then add it to the melted butter mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir well to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the baking sheets, leaving space for spreading.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Allow biscuits to cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: New Zealand Cheese Scones
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt, and mustard powder into a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the dry ingredients using your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in three-quarters of the grated cheddar cheese.
Make a well in the center and add the milk, mixing gently with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and pat it gently into a square about 2 cm thick.
Cut the dough into squares and place them on the prepared baking tray.
Top each scone with the remaining grated cheese and brush the edges with extra milk.
Bake for 15 minutes until risen and golden brown.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and grease and line a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Beat softened butter and sugar in a separate bowl until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then stir in the vanilla extract.
Alternately fold the dry ingredients and milk into the butter mixture until smooth.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then cut it into even squares.
To make the chocolate glaze, whisk icing sugar, cocoa powder, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate glaze to coat all sides, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Place on a wire rack to set.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 120C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whip egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until thick and glossy.
Fold in vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Spoon the meringue onto the baking paper and shape into a circle with a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let it cool completely inside.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
Top with mixed fresh berries just before serving.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C and grease and line a 20x30 cm lamington pan.
Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cream butter, caster sugar, and vanilla until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Fold in the dry ingredients alternately with the milk until smooth.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely, then cut into square blocks.
To make the icing, combine icing sugar and cocoa powder in a bowl, stir in melted butter and boiling water until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing, let excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Place on a wire rack to set.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 160C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a large bowl.
Melt butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix bicarb soda with boiling water, add to the melted butter mixture, and stir.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix well.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place on trays, leaving space for spreading.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté onion until translucent.
Add minced beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Add beef stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Mix cornflour with water to form a slurry, stir into the beef mixture, and cook until thickened. Cool slightly.
Line the base and sides of the pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Spoon the meat filling into the pastry cases.
Top with puff pastry sheets, trim edges, and press to seal.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and bake for 25 minutes until golden and puffed.

title: Cheese Rolls
ingredients: 1 can condensed cream of onion soup
instructions: Combine cheddar cheese, tasty cheese, diced onion, cream of onion soup, and evaporated milk in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until the cheese melts and thickens into a paste. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Flatten the bread slices with a rolling pin and crusts removed if desired.
Spread a generous amount of the cheese mixture onto each slice of bread.
Roll up tightly into cylinders.
Brush the outside of each roll with melted butter.
Place on a baking tray and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

Pile meringue onto the baking paper, shaping into a circle with slightly higher edges.
Bake for 1.5 hours, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
Top with mixed berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.

Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Top with puff pastry sheets, trim edges, seal, and brush with beaten egg.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
Aluminium foil and wet hessian sacks for covering
instructions: Prepare a deep pit, build a hardwood fire over river stones, and let it burn down until stones are glowing hot.
Season the meats and vegetables generously with salt and pepper.
Wrap the meats and vegetables securely in parcels using aluminium foil to lock in juices.
Place the heavy meat parcels at the bottom of the hot stones in the pit.
Layer the vegetables and cabbage parcels on top of the meat.
Cover the food tightly with wet hessian sacks and a layer of clean earth to trap the steam.
Leave everything to cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 hours.
Carefully unearth and remove the parcels, then serve the food hot.

Wrap the seasoned meats individually in heavy-duty aluminium foil parcels.
Wrap the vegetables individually in foil parcels, keeping different types separate.
Line a large roasting pan or oven-safe container to simulate a hangi basket if cooking indoors.
Layer the wrapped meat parcels at the bottom, followed by denser vegetables like potatoes and kumara, and top with pumpkin and cabbage parcels.
Cover the entire top tightly with wet clean sacks and multiple layers of foil to trap steam.
Bake in a preheated oven at 150°C for 4 to 5 hours until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Unwrap carefully and serve hot.

title: Traditional Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
2 cups mixed fresh berries and sliced kiwifruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 120C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the baking paper, shaping it into a circle with a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside with the door closed.
Top the cooled meringue with whipped cream and fresh fruit before serving.

title: Classic Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 160C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix the boiling water and bicarbonate of soda together, then add it to the melted butter mixture.
Pour the liquid ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until well combined.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving space for spreading.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown, then cool on the trays.

title: Aussie Meat Pies
ingredients: 1/4 cup cornflour mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Cook the minced beef and onion in a large pan over medium heat until browned.
Add the beef stock, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook until the gravy thickens; remove from heat and cool.
Cut shortcrust pastry to line the base and sides of the pie tins.
Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined bases.
Top with puff pastry rounds, trim the edges, press to seal, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C and grease and line a 20x30cm baking pan.
Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat butter and caster sugar in a bowl until pale and creamy, then add eggs one at a time.
Fold in the dry ingredients alternately with the milk.
Pour batter into the pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, then cool completely and cut into squares.
To make the icing, whisk icing sugar, cocoa, melted butter, and boiling water together until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing, let excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.

title: New Zealand Cheese Scones
ingredients: 1 tablespoon grated cheese extra for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 210C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the dry ingredients using your fingertips until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the grated cheddar cheese.
Make a well in the center and pour in the milk, mixing gently with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface, pat into a thick rectangle, and cut into squares.
Place scones on the prepared tray, sprinkle the extra cheese on top, and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and risen.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 2 cups mixed fresh berries like strawberries, kiwifruit, and passionfruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 120C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whip egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Pile the meringue onto the baking paper into a circle, shaping the sides up and creating a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
Top with fresh mixed berries and serve immediately.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 160C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine rolled oats, flour, coconut, and caster sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix the boiling water and bicarb soda together, then add to the melted butter mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir well to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, allowing room for spreading.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C and grease and line a 20x30 cm lamington pan.
Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat softened butter, caster sugar, and vanilla in a bowl until pale and creamy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Fold in the flour mixture alternately with the milk until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30 minutes, then cool completely before cutting into squares.
To make the icing, whisk icing sugar, cocoa, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing, let excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut until fully coated.
Place on a wire rack to set.

title: Meat Pie
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornflour mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Cook the minced beef and onion in a large pan over medium heat until browned.
Stir in tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce, cooking for 1 minute.
Add beef stock and bring to a simmer, then stir in the cornflour mixture and cook until thickened.
Remove meat filling from heat and allow to cool slightly.
Line the base and sides of the pie tins with shortcrust pastry sheets.
Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Top with puff pastry sheets, trim edges, press to seal, and cut a small slit in the top of each.
Brush pastry tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden and puffed.

title: Cheese and Bacon Rolls
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Mix warm water and olive oil, then pour into the dry ingredients to form a dough.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 200C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Punch down the dough, divide into 8 equal portions, and shape into round rolls on the tray.
Press a deep indentation into the top of each roll using your thumb or a spoon.
Fill the indentations with diced bacon and top generously with grated cheese.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the rolls are golden and the cheese is melted and bubbling.

title: Traditional Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat your oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whip the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add the caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the baking paper, shaping it into a circle with a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside with the door closed.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
Top with fresh berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.

title: Classic Aussie Meat Pies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Cook the minced beef and onion in a large pan over medium heat until the meat is browned.
Add the beef stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce, then bring to a simmer.
Mix the cornflour and water together into a smooth paste, then stir it into the beef mixture to thicken.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Line the base and sides of the pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Spoon the meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Top with squares of puff pastry, trim the edges, press to seal, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the rolled oats, plain flour, desiccated coconut, and caster sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix the boiling water and bicarbonate of soda together, then stir it into the melted butter mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir well until combined.
Roll tablespoons of the mixture into balls and place them on the trays about 5cm apart.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown, then cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: New Zealand Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease and line a 20x30cm baking pan.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and caster sugar in a separate bowl until pale and creamy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each, then stir in the vanilla.
Alternately fold in the dry ingredients and the milk until smooth.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 35 minutes, then cool completely before cutting into squares.
Make the icing by whisking icing sugar, cocoa powder, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing, let excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.

title: NZ Green-Lipped Mussels in Garlic Butter
ingredients: 1 kg fresh New Zealand green-lipped mussels, cleaned and debearded
instructions: Rinse the mussels thoroughly in cold water and discard any that do not close when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and bring to a simmer.
Add the mussels to the pot and cover with a tight-fitting lid.
Steam for 5 to 7 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until all the mussels have opened.
Discard any mussels that remain closed.
Stir in the chopped parsley and serve immediately with lemon wedges and crusty baguette slices.

title: Traditional Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 120 degrees C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Spoon the meringue onto the lined tray and shape into a circle with slightly higher sides.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled meringue.
Top with mixed berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.

title: Classic Aussie Meat Pies
instructions: Preheat oven to 200 degrees C and grease a 4-hole pie tin.
Cook the minced beef and chopped onion in a large pan over medium heat until browned.
Add the beef stock, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce, then bring to a simmer.
Mix the cornflour with water to form a paste, then stir it into the beef mixture to thicken.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Cut shortcrust pastry to line the base and sides of the pie tins.
Spoon the cooled meat filling into the pastry-lined tins.
Top with puff pastry rounds, press edges to seal, and brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.

title: New Zealand Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
instructions: Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Combine caster sugar and golden syrup in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil and let it bubble without stirring until it turns an amber color.
Remove from heat immediately, whisk in the bicarb soda until it foams up vigorously, and pour onto the prepared tray to cool.
Once hardened, break the hokey pokey honeycomb into small pieces.
Whisk the thickened cream, milk, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl until well combined.
Churn the mixture in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer instructions.
Fold in the crushed honeycomb pieces and freeze for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 160 degrees C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the rolled oats, plain flour, desiccated coconut, and caster sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Mix the boiling water and bicarb soda together, then add it to the melted butter mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir well until combined.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving space for spreading.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Allow the biscuits to cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180 degrees C and grease and line a 20x30 cm lamington pan.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy, then add eggs one at a time.
Fold in the dry ingredients alternately with the milk and vanilla extract.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, preferably overnight, then cut it into even squares.
To make the chocolate icing, combine icing sugar, cocoa, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing to coat all sides, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Place on a wire rack to set.

title: Traditional Pavlova
instructions: Preheat your oven to 120°C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whip the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add the sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the parchment paper and shape into a circle with a slight depression in the center.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside with the door closed.
Whip the heavy cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
Top with fresh berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.

title: Classic Australian Meat Pies
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and grease a 4-hole muffin tin or pie tins.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, and beef broth, then bring to a simmer.
Mix the cornstarch and cold water together, then stir into the beef mixture to thicken.
Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Cut the shortcrust pastry to line the bases and sides of the pie tins.
Fill the pastry cases with the meat mixture.
Top with cut circles of puff pastry, press edges to seal, and brush tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.

title: Homestyle Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease and line an 8x12 inch baking pan.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cream the butter, sugar, and vanilla extract together until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Alternately fold in the dry ingredients and the milk until just combined.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Allow the cake to cool completely, then cut it into uniform squares.
To make the icing, whisk icing sugar, cocoa powder, melted butter, and boiling water in a bowl until smooth.
Dip each cake square into the chocolate icing to coat all sides, letting excess drip off.
Roll the coated cake squares immediately in the desiccated coconut and place on a wire rack to set.

title: New Zealand Cheese Rolls
instructions: Preheat your oven grill to high.
In a bowl, combine the grated cheddar cheese, grated onion, onion soup mix, and evaporated milk.
Trim the crusts off the slices of white bread.
Spread a thin layer of softened butter on one side of each bread slice.
Spoon a generous amount of the cheese mixture onto the unbuttered side of each slice.
Roll the bread up tightly around the filling to form cylinders.
Place the rolls seam-side down on a baking sheet lined with foil.
Grill for 3 to 5 minutes, turning once, until the outside is golden brown and the cheese filling is bubbly and melted.

title: ANZAC Biscuits
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, flour, coconut, and sugar.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter and golden syrup together over low heat.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water, then add it to the melted butter and syrup mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir well until fully combined.
Roll tablespoons of the mixture into balls and place them on the baking sheets, leaving space for spreading.
Flatten each ball slightly with the back of a fork.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown, then let cool on the trays for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

title: Crayfish Mornay
ingredients: 1 whole Western Rock Lobster, cooked, halved and meat removed from shells
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
2 tbsp finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
instructions: Preheat your oven grill to high.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time, until smooth and thickened.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the Dijon mustard, cheddar cheese, and half the parmesan until melted and smooth.
Season the cheese sauce with salt and pepper, then gently fold through the lobster meat.
Spoon the mixture back into the cleaned lobster half-shells.
Top with the remaining parmesan cheese and grill for 5 to 7 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Barbecued King George Whiting
ingredients: 4 whole King George Whiting, scaled, gutted and cleaned
instructions: Preheat a barbecue hotplate or outdoor grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, and chopped dill.
Score the thickest parts of the fish on both sides with a sharp knife to ensure even cooking.
Brush the whiting generously all over with the lemon and garlic oil mixture, making sure to get some inside the cavity.
Season the fish generously inside and out with flaky sea salt and black pepper.
Place the fish directly onto the hot barbecue plate.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side without moving them, then carefully flip.
Cook for another 2 to 3 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Transfer to a warm serving platter and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.

title: South-West Marron with Garlic Butter
ingredients: 4 live or freshly thawed South West freshwater marron, split in half lengthwise and cleaned
instructions: Preheat the oven grill to high.
In a small mixing bowl, combine the softened butter, crushed garlic, tarragon, lemon juice, sea salt flakes, and cayenne pepper until well blended.
Place the marron halves shell-side down on a baking tray lined with foil.
Generously dollop and spread the garlic herb butter mixture over the exposed marron flesh.
Place the tray under the preheated grill for 8 to 10 minutes until the marron meat turns bright red and opaque, and the butter is bubbling.
Remove from the oven and spoon any remaining melted butter from the tray back over the marron.
Serve hot with crusty bread to soak up the garlic butter.

title: Shark Bay Snapper and Chips
ingredients: 4 Shark Bay Snapper fillets, skinless and boneless
4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cut into thick chips
1 L vegetable oil for deep frying
Tartare sauce and lemon wedges, to serve
instructions: Soak the cut potato chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep fryer or heavy-bottomed pot to 160°C (320°F).
Cook the potato chips in batches for 5 minutes until soft but not browned, then remove and drain on wire racks.
Increase the oil temperature to 190°C (375°F).
In a large bowl, whisk together the plain flour, self-raising flour, and salt.
Gradually whisk in the chilled beer and sparkling water until a smooth batter forms.
Dust the snapper fillets lightly in a little extra plain flour, then dip them into the batter, letting any excess drip off.
Carefully lower the battered fish into the hot oil and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and crisp; remove and drain.
Flash-fry the potato chips for a second time in the hot oil for 3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve the snapper and chips hot with tartare sauce and lemon wedges.

title: Guilderton Lancelin Honey Cake
ingredients: 3/4 cup pure local Western Australian wildflower honey
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (320°F) fan-forced and grease and line a 22cm round cake tin with baking paper.
In a medium saucepan over low heat, combine the butter, honey, and brown sugar, stirring until the butter is fully melted and the sugar dissolves; remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Whisk the beaten eggs and milk into the cooled honey and butter mixture.
Sift the self-raising flour, ground cinnamon, and ground ginger into a large mixing bowl.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the wet mixture.
Gently fold everything together with a spatula until just combined and smooth, avoiding over-mixing.
Pour the batter evenly into the prepared cake tin.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow the cake to cool in the tin for 15 minutes before transferring it to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with icing sugar before slicing and serving.

title: Tasmanian Scallop Pie
ingredients: 1 kg fresh Tasmanian scallops, roe on
1 cup fish stock or vegetable stock
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 egg, lightly beaten for egg wash
instructions: Preheat oven to 200 degrees C.
Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat and sauté the onion and garlic until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour and curry powder, cooking for 1 minute while stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in the stock and cream, bringing the mixture to a gentle simmer until it thickens into a rich sauce.
Add the scallops and parsley, cook for just 2 minutes, then season with salt and pepper and remove from heat.
Line four individual pie tins with the shortcrust pastry.
Spoon the scallop mixture into the pastry-lined tins.
Top each pie with a sheet of puff pastry, trim the edges, seal, and brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.

title: Leatherwood Honey Damper
instructions: Preheat oven to 220 degrees C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Sift the flour and salt into a large mixing bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour using your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Make a well in the centre and pour in the milk and Leatherwood honey.
Using a butter knife, mix gently until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and place it on the prepared baking tray.
Score a deep cross on top of the loaf with a sharp knife and brush with a little extra milk.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until the damper sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.

title: Huon Salmon with Warrigal Greens
ingredients: 2 Tasmanian Huon salmon fillets, skin on
Sea salt flakes and cracked black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the salmon fillets completely dry with paper towel and season both sides with sea salt flakes.
Heat olive oil in a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat.
Place the salmon skin-side down in the pan and press gently for 10 seconds; cook for 4 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Flip the salmon, add the butter to the pan, and spoon the melted butter over the fish for 2 minutes until cooked to your liking.
Remove salmon from the pan and let it rest.
In the same pan, toss in the sliced garlic and blanched Warrigal greens, sautéing for 2 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest, then remove from heat.
Serve the salmon resting on a bed of the sautéed Warrigal greens with pan juices drizzled over top.

title: Tasmanian Raspberry and Apple Crumble
ingredients: 6 Tasmanian apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 180 degrees C.
Place sliced apples, water, and caster sugar in a saucepan over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes until apples start to soften.
Gently fold in the raspberries and cinnamon, then transfer the fruit mixture into a baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, rolled oats, brown sugar, and chopped hazelnuts.
Rub the cold butter into the dry mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the apple and raspberry mixture.
Bake in the oven for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is golden and crisp and the fruit is bubbling.

title: Tasmanian Potato and Cheddar Soup
ingredients: 1 kg Tasmanian chipping potatoes, peeled and diced
1 leek, white part only, washed and sliced
4 rashers bacon, diced and crispy fried
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large soup pot over medium heat and sauté the leek and garlic until soft and fragrant.
Add the diced potatoes and stock to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Use a hand blender to puree the soup until smooth and creamy.
Stir in the thickened cream and three-quarters of the grated Pyengana cheddar, stirring gently until the cheese melts completely.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish with the remaining grated cheddar, crispy bacon bits, and chopped chives.

title: Classic New Zealand Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 120C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whip egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating constantly until thick and glossy.
Fold in vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla extract gently.
Mound the meringue onto the baking paper, shaping into a circle with a slight depression on top.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let cool completely inside.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread over the cooled pavlova.
