Add the carrots and parsnips to the pot and simmer uncovered for another 30 to 45 minutes until the vegetables and meat are tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Full English Breakfast
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sausages and cook, turning frequently, for about 12 to 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the bacon to the skillet and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crispy.
In a separate small saucepan, warm the baked beans over medium-low heat.
Add the tomato halves and sliced mushrooms to the skillet, cooking until tender and slightly caramelized.
Remove the cooked meats and vegetables from the skillet and keep warm.
In the same skillet, fry the eggs to your desired doneness.
Toast the bread and butter generously.
Assemble the sausages, bacon, eggs, beans, tomato, mushrooms, and toast on warm plates to serve.

title: Classic Toad in the Hole
ingredients: 1 tbsp beef drippings or extra oil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, and salt until smooth to form the batter; let it rest for 30 minutes.
Place the vegetable oil and sausages in a heavy roasting pan or baking dish.
Bake the sausages in the oven for 10 minutes until they start to brown.
Add the sliced onions to the pan around the sausages and bake for another 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and immediately pour the rested batter all around the hot sausages.
Return to the oven quickly and bake undisturbed for 35 to 40 minutes until the batter has puffed up and is golden brown and crisp.
Serve immediately with gravy.

title: Traditional Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F and dust a baking sheet with flour.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk, mixing quickly with your hands to form a dough.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently shape it into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on the baking sheet, cut a deep cross into the top, and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden.

title: Irish Beef and Guinness Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs chuck steak, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Toss the beef cubes in the flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and sear the beef until browned on all sides.
Remove the beef and set aside, then add the onions and garlic to the pot and cook until soft.
Pour in the Guinness to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef to the pot, add the beef broth, tomato paste, and thyme, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the carrots and potatoes, and continue to simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.

title: Traditional Irish Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes, then drain well.
While potatoes cook, steam the shredded cabbage in a small pot with a splash of water until soft and wilted.
Heat the milk and butter together in a small saucepan until the butter is melted.
Mash the cooked potatoes thoroughly with the hot milk and butter mixture.
Fold the steamed cabbage and chopped green onions into the mashed potatoes.
Season with salt and white pepper, and serve hot with a well of melted butter in the center.

title: Full Irish Breakfast
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sausages and bacon, cooking for about 5 to 7 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the black and white pudding slices, tomato halves, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Warm the baked beans in a small saucepan over low heat.
Fry the eggs in the same skillet to your desired doneness.
Toast the bread and serve everything hot together on a large plate.

title: Traditional Irish Potato Boxty
ingredients: 1 cup grated raw potatoes, squeezed dry
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the grated raw potatoes and the cold mashed potatoes.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Stir the dry ingredients and the buttermilk into the potato mixture until a smooth batter forms.
Heat the butter in a large skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot skillet and flatten slightly to form pancakes.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.

title: Traditional Ulster Fry
instructions: Melt butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the sausages and bacon until browned and cooked through, then keep warm.
Fry the mushrooms and tomatoes until tender.
In the same pan, fry the soda bread and potato bread until golden and crisp on both sides.
Fry the egg to your liking.
Serve everything hot on a warmed plate.

title: Northern Irish Champ
ingredients: 2 lbs Russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, then drain well.
In a small saucepan, gently heat the milk and chopped scallions for about 5 minutes until the scallions soften.
Mash the cooked potatoes thoroughly with half of the butter.
Gradually pour the warm milk and scallion mixture into the mashed potatoes, beating until smooth and creamy.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve in bowls with a well in the center holding the remaining butter so it melts into the champ.

title: Belfast Chicken Soda Farls
ingredients: 4 leftover or freshly baked soda farls
instructions: In a bowl, mix together the shredded chicken, mayonnaise, mustard, celery, salt, and pepper.
Split the soda farls horizontally.
Butter the insides of the soda farls lightly.
Fill each soda farl generously with the chicken salad mixture.
Cut in half and serve immediately.

title: Traditional Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs neck of lamb or lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 325F (165C).
In a heavy-bottomed casserole dish, layer the potatoes, onions, and lamb, seasoning each layer with salt, pepper, and a little thyme.
Finish with a top layer of overlapping potato slices.
Pour in the stock, ensuring it comes up just below the top layer of potatoes.
Cover tightly with a lid and bake in the oven for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the lid for the last 15 minutes if you want the top potatoes to brown, garnish with parsley, and serve hot.

title: Fifteens (No-Bake Ulster Traybake)
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the crushed digestive biscuits, halved marshmallows, and glacé cherries.
Pour in the condensed milk and mix well until everything is coated and sticking together.
Turn the mixture out onto a sheet of cling film dusted with desiccated coconut.
Shape the mixture into a tight log shape, rolling it in the coconut to coat the outside completely.
Wrap tightly in the cling film and chill in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours.
Slice into 15 equal rounds to serve.

title: Traditional Yorkshire Pudding
ingredients: 2 tbsp beef dripping or vegetable oil
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F).
Whisk together the flour and salt in a bowl.
Gradually beat in the eggs and milk until smooth, then let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
Place a muffin tin or small roasting tin with the beef dripping into the hot oven for 10 minutes until smoking hot.
Carefully pour the batter evenly into the hot tins and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until risen and golden brown.

title: Yorkshire Curd Tart
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C (400F) and line a pie dish with the shortcrust pastry.
Drain any excess liquid from the curd cheese.
In a large bowl, mix the curd cheese, melted butter, sugar, and egg together.
Stir in the dried currants and grated nutmeg.
Pour the mixture into the pastry case and bake for 30 minutes until set and lightly browned on top.

title: Parkin
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160C (325F) and grease a 20cm square baking tin, lining it with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the oatmeal, flour, ginger, and mixed spice.
Gently melt the butter, brown sugar, golden syrup, and black treacle together in a pan over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk the egg and milk together, then stir them into the warm syrup mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and beat well until combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 to 55 minutes until firm, then let it mature in an airtight tin for at least a few days before eating.

title: Fat Rascals
ingredients: Blanched almonds and glacé cherries for decoration
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190C (375F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, mixed peel, currants, and mixed spice.
Mix in the egg and enough milk to bring everything together into a stiff dough.
Divide the dough into balls, flatten them slightly onto the baking sheet, and press two almonds and a piece of cherry on top of each to make a face.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden brown.

title: Pan Haggerty
ingredients: 4 large potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190C (375F).
Heat the butter and oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium heat.
Layer half of the sliced potatoes and onions in the pan, seasoning with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with a third of the cheese.
Add the remaining potatoes and onions in another layer, pouring the stock over them.
Cover the pan with foil and bake in the oven for 45 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the foil, sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top, and return to the oven for 15 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Classic Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 900g Maris Piper potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion and carrots until soft.
Add the minced lamb and brown well, draining off excess fat.
Stir in the flour and tomato purée, then gradually add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer the meat mixture for 20 minutes until rich and thick, then transfer to a baking dish.
Mash the cooked potatoes with butter and milk until smooth, season with salt and pepper.
Spread the mashed potato evenly over the lamb mixture and roughen the top with a fork.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling.

title: Traditional Toad in the Hole
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and salt together in a bowl to make a smooth batter, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Place the vegetable oil and sausages in a roasting tin and roast in the oven for 10 minutes until the sausages start to brown.
Carefully pour the rested batter around the sizzling sausages in the hot tin.
Return to the oven immediately and bake for 30 to 35 minutes without opening the door, until the batter is puffed and golden brown.
While the toad in the hole bakes, melt the butter in a pan and cook the sliced onions slowly until soft and caramelized.
Stir the flour into the onions, cook for 1 minute, then gradually stir in the beef stock and balsamic vinegar.
Simmer the gravy for 10 minutes until reduced and rich, then serve alongside the sliced toad in the hole.

title: Proper London Jellied Eels
ingredients: 1 kg fresh eels, cleaned, skinned, and cut into 2-inch chunks
instructions: Place the eel chunks into a wide, shallow saucepan.
Add the sliced onion, chopped celery, water, malt vinegar, salt, white peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring the liquid to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pan and simmer gently for about 20 to 25 minutes until the eel meat is tender and easily comes away from the bone.
Remove the eel pieces carefully with a slotted spoon and arrange them neatly in a shallow serving dish.
Strain the remaining cooking liquor through a fine sieve into a jug.
Pour the strained liquid over the eels, ensuring they are fully covered.
Allow the dish to cool to room temperature, then place it in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours until the stock sets into a clear jelly.
Serve cold with slices of fresh lemon and a dash of chilli vinegar.

title: Classic British Steak and Ale Pie
ingredients: 800g chuck steak, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Toss the steak cubes in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Heat half the oil in a large casserole dish and brown the beef in batches, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the dish and gently fry the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in the tomato purée and return the beef to the casserole.
Pour in the ale and beef stock, add the thyme sprigs, and bring to a simmer.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and bake in the oven for 2 hours until the beef is meltingly tender.
Remove the casserole from the oven, discard the thyme sprigs, and let the filling cool slightly, then increase the oven temperature to 200°C (180°C fan).
Transfer the beef filling to a pie dish, top with the puff pastry sheet, trim the edges, and crimp to seal.
Brush the pastry with the beaten egg and cut a small slit in the top for steam to escape.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and risen.

title: Traditional Spotted Dick
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the self-raising flour, suet, caster sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Stir in the sultanas, currants, and lemon zest.
Gradually pour in the milk, mixing with a wooden spoon until you have a soft, pliable dough.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and shape it into a sausage log.
Wrap the pudding loosely in a large sheet of buttered greaseproof paper, then wrap it again in a layer of foil to make it waterproof, leaving a little room for expansion.
Place a wire trivet inside a large saucepan and fill with boiling water to come halfway up the sides of the pudding.
Lower the wrapped pudding onto the trivet, cover the pan with a tight lid, and steam gently for 1.5 hours, topping up the boiling water as needed.
Remove from the steamer, unwrap carefully, slice into thick rounds, and serve hot with plenty of hot custard.

title: Traditional Cornish Pasty
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200C (180C fan).
Roll out the pastry and cut into four large circles using a large plate as a guide.
Layer the potato, swede, onion, and beef evenly across the pastry circles.
Dot the fillings with butter and season generously with salt and pepper.
Bring the edges of the pastry up and crimp them tightly to seal the pasties.
Place on a lined baking tray and brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Stargazy Pie
ingredients: 6 fresh pilchards or sardines, scaled and gutted
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Line a pie dish with the shortcrust pastry and blind bake for 10 minutes.
Sate the onion in butter until soft, then mix with cream, cheese, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Pour the cream mixture into the pastry base.
Arrange the fish in a circle with their tails pointing up through the center of the pie.
Cover with the puff pastry top, making small slits for the fish heads to poke through.
Brush with egg and bake for 35 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Cornish Saffron Cake
instructions: Infuse the saffron in the warm milk for 20 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, then rub in the butter and lard.
Stir in the sugar, yeast, and dried fruit.
Add the saffron milk and enough warm water to form a soft dough.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled in size.
Shape into a loaf, place in a greased tin, let rise for 30 minutes, then bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

title: Hevva Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190C (170C fan) and grease a baking tin.
Rub the butter and lard into the flour until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, dried fruit, mixed peel, and mixed spice.
Gradually add the milk to bring the mixture together into a stiff dough.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared baking tin.
Score a diamond pattern across the top with a knife to represent fishing nets.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden brown, then cool on a wire rack.

title: Authentic Cornish Cream Tea Scones
ingredients: Strawberry or raspberry jam to serve
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220C (200C fan) and line a baking sheet.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the sugar.
Combine the milk and vanilla extract, then pour into the dry ingredients.
Mix quickly to a soft dough, then gently roll out to 2cm thickness on a floured surface.
Cut out rounds with a floured cutter and place them on the baking sheet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden, then serve warm with jam first, followed by clotted cream.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160C / 140C fan / gas mark 3.
Layer the lamb and sliced onions in a large, deep casserole dish, seasoning each layer with salt and pepper.
Pour in the lamb stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Arrange the sliced potatoes neatly on top in overlapping rows to form a crust.
Brush the potatoes with melted butter and cover the dish tightly with a lid.
Bake in the oven for 2 hours, then remove the lid and bake for another 30 minutes until the potatoes are golden and crisp.

title: Lancashire Cheese and Onion Pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C / 180C fan / gas mark 6.
Melt the butter in a large pan and gently cook the onions over low heat for 20 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then remove from heat and let it cool slightly.
Stir the crumbled Lancashire cheese into the onions and season with salt and pepper.
Line a pie dish with the shortcrust pastry, add the onion and cheese filling.
Top with the puff pastry, crimp the edges to seal, brush with the beaten egg, and cut a small slit in the centre.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and risen.

title: Parkin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150C / 130C fan / gas mark 2 and grease a 20cm square cake tin, lining it with baking parchment.
In a large bowl, mix together the flour, oatmeal, ground ginger, and mixed spice.
In a saucepan, gently melt the butter, dark brown sugar, black treacle, and golden syrup together over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Remove the syrup mixture from the heat and allow to cool slightly, then whisk in the milk and beaten egg.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and beat well until smooth.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake for about 1 hour to 1 hour 10 minutes until set and firm to the touch.
Allow to cool in the tin completely before wrapping in parchment and foil to store for a few days before eating.

title: Black Pudding Hash
ingredients: 250g good quality Lancashire black pudding, sliced into rounds
4 large potatoes, boiled in their skins, cooled and diced
instructions: Heat the oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the diced onions and cook until soft and translucent, about 8 minutes.
Add the diced cooked potatoes to the pan, turning up the heat slightly to get them crispy and golden, about 10 minutes.
In a separate pan, fry the black pudding slices for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until heated through and slightly crisp.
Gently stir the black pudding into the potato and onion hash, breaking it up slightly.
In another pan, fry the eggs to your liking using the remaining butter.
Serve the hash topped with the fried egg and a scattering of chopped parsley.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220C / 200C fan / gas mark 7 and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, mix together the currants, mixed peel, melted butter, light brown sugar, and mixed spice.
Unroll the puff pastry and cut out rounds using a 10cm pastry cutter.
Place a spoonful of the currant filling into the centre of each pastry round.
Dampen the edges of the pastry with a little water, bring the edges up and over the filling, and pinch them together to seal.
Turn the cakes over gently so the seam is at the bottom, and flatten them slightly with the palm of your hand.
Brush the tops with milk, make three small slashes across the top of each cake with a sharp knife, and sprinkle with caster sugar.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden brown and puffed, then transfer to a wire rack to cool.

title: Traditional Scottish Porridge
ingredients: Cold milk or cream for serving
instructions: Pour the water into a heavy-bottomed saucepan and bring to a rapid boil.
Add the pinch of salt, then slowly pour in the oatmeal while stirring constantly with a wooden spurtle.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer gently for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and let it rest for 2 minutes.
Serve in warm bowls with a jug of cold milk and a spoonful of brown sugar.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 2 medium floury potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Place the smoked haddock in a wide pan, pour over the milk and water, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach the fish for 5 minutes until just cooked through, then lift out with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Once cool enough to handle, flake the fish into bite-sized pieces and discard any skin and bones, reserving the poaching liquid.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the diced potatoes and the reserved milk and water mixture to the pot.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the flaked smoked haddock and heat through for 3 minutes.
Season with black pepper and garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

title: Scotch Broth
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Place the lamb neck chops and stock in a large soup pot and bring to a boil.
Skim off any foam from the surface, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Drain the soaked pearl barley and add it to the pot along with the onion, carrots, and turnip.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the lamb chops from the pot, shred the meat off the bones, and return the meat to the soup.
Add the leek and shredded cabbage to the pot and cook for another 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Minced Tatties and Neeps
instructions: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and brown the minced beef and chopped onion together.
Add the diced carrots and stir in the flour, cooking for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, stirring continuously until the sauce thickens.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer the mince for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes and swede in separate salted pots until tender.
Drain both thoroughly, then mash the potatoes with butter and milk, and mash the swede with a little butter and white pepper.
Serve the mince hot alongside the creamy mashed potatoes and swede.

title: Traditional Scottish Cranachan
instructions: Spread the oatmeal evenly on a baking sheet and toast under a hot grill until lightly browned and nutty, stirring frequently. Set aside to cool.
Whip the double cream in a large bowl until soft peaks form.
Gently fold the Scottish honey and Scotch whisky into the whipped cream.
Crush half of the raspberries slightly with a fork to release their juices.
Layer the toasted oatmeal, whipped cream, crushed raspberries, and whole raspberries in four tall dessert glasses.
Chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Traditional Welsh Cawl
ingredients: 1.5 kg neck of lamb, cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the lamb pieces into a large heavy-bottomed pot and cover with the stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the meat starts to become tender.
Add the carrots, swede, and potatoes to the pot.
Simmer for another 30 minutes until the root vegetables are nearly cooked.
Add the sliced leeks and chopped parsley, then season well with salt and pepper.
Cook for a final 15 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Serve hot in deep bowls, traditionally accompanied by a chunk of crusty bread and a piece of Caerphilly cheese.

title: Welsh Rarebit
ingredients: 4 thick slices of crusty white bread
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and mustard powder to create a thick paste, cooking for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the dark ale and Worcestershire sauce until smooth and thickened.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the grated Cheddar until it melts completely into a thick, rich sauce.
Season with cayenne pepper and let the mixture cool slightly.
Toast the slices of bread lightly on both sides under a broiler.
Spread the cheese mixture thickly over the toast, covering right to the edges.
Broil for 3 to 4 minutes until the topping is bubbling, golden brown, and starting to blister.

title: Bara Brith
instructions: Place the mixed dried fruit in a large bowl, pour the hot black tea and brown sugar over it, and stir well.
Cover the bowl and leave it to soak overnight so the fruit plumps up.
Preheat your oven to 160C (325F) and grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Add the self-raising flour, mixed spice, beaten eggs, and marmalade to the soaked fruit mixture.
Stir thoroughly until everything is well combined and no dry flour remains.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf tin and level the top with a spatula.
Bake in the center of the oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow to cool in the tin for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice and butter generously to serve.

title: Welsh Cakes
ingredients: 75g caster sugar, plus extra for dusting
A splash of milk if needed to bind
instructions: Rub the chilled butter into the plain flour in a large bowl until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the caster sugar, currants, and mixed spice.
Add the beaten egg and mix to form a firm dough, adding a tiny splash of milk if it is too dry.
Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1 centimeter.
Cut out rounds using a 6cm fluted pastry cutter.
Heat a heavy cast-iron bakestone or griddle over medium heat and lightly grease it with a little butter.
Cook the Welsh cakes on the griddle for 3 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through.
Dust them immediately with caster sugar while still warm.

title: Glamorgan Sausages
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix the grated Caerphilly cheese, half of the breadcrumbs, chopped leek, herbs, and mustard powder in a large bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, then bind the mixture using the 2 egg yolks.
Divide the mixture into 6 equal portions and shape them into small, plump sausage shapes with your hands.
Lightly coat each sausage in plain flour, dip them in the lightly beaten egg whites, and then roll them in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Place the coated sausages in the refrigerator for 20 minutes to firm up.
Heat a shallow layer of sunflower oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the sausages for 8 to 10 minutes, turning frequently until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with homemade chutney.

title: Traditional Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and lightly flour a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Using your hand or a wooden spoon, quickly mix until the dough comes together; do not overmix.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface, gently shape it into a round loaf, and place it on the baking sheet.
Cut a deep cross into the top of the loaf.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until the loaf is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.

title: Classic Irish Beef and Guinness Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs stewing beef, cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Toss the beef chunks in the flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add the onions and garlic, cooking until soft and translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste, beef broth, and Guinness, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the beef to the pot along with the thyme, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1 hour.
Add the carrots and potatoes to the pot and continue to simmer for another 45 minutes until the vegetables and meat are tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving hot.

title: Traditional Irish Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 small head green cabbage, cored and finely shredded
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Place the potatoes in a large pot of salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender, about 20 minutes.
While the potatoes cook, melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a pan and sauté the shredded cabbage until wilted and soft.
In a small saucepan, warm the milk and the remaining butter together.
Drain the cooked potatoes and mash them thoroughly.
Stir the warm milk and butter mixture into the mashed potatoes until smooth and creamy.
Fold in the cooked cabbage and chopped green onions.
Season with salt and white pepper, and serve with a dollop of butter in the center.

title: Irish Potato Boxty
ingredients: 1 cup grated raw potatoes, squeezed dry
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the grated raw potatoes, mashed potatoes, flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually stir in the buttermilk to form a smooth, thick batter.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the skillet, flattening them slightly to form pancakes.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve warm with butter or alongside a cooked breakfast.

title: Irish Battered Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, cut into thick chips
2 fillets of fresh cod or haddock
1 cup ice-cold sparkling water or beer
Lemon wedges and malt vinegar for serving
instructions: Soak the potato chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or deep pan to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) and fry the chips for 5 minutes until soft; remove and drain.
Increase the oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a bowl, mix 1 cup of flour, baking powder, and salt, then whisk in the ice-cold sparkling water until just combined.
Dust the fish fillets in the remaining flour, dip them into the batter, and carefully lower them into the hot oil.
Fry the fish for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and crispy; remove and drain on paper towels.
Flash fry the chips for another 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp, then serve immediately with the fish, lemon, and malt vinegar.

title: Ulster Fry
instructions: Melt butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add sausages, bacon, and puddings, cooking until browned and cooked through.
Add tomato halves to the pan and fry until soft.
In the same pan, fry the soda bread and potato bread until golden and crisp on both sides.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve all components hot together on a plate.

title: Traditional Boxty
ingredients: 2 cups grated raw potatoes, squeezed dry
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the grated raw potatoes and the mashed potatoes.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Gradually add the buttermilk to form a soft dough.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and roll to about half-inch thickness.
Cut into wedges or rounds.
Melt butter in a griddle or frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the boxty for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lbs floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
1/2 head of green cabbage, finely shredded
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, steam or boil the shredded cabbage until tender, then drain well.
Drain the potatoes and mash them thoroughly with half of the butter and all of the milk.
Stir the cooked cabbage and chopped green onions into the mashed potatoes.
Season generously with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with a well in the center filled with the remaining melted butter.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb neck chops or shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat your oven to 325 degrees F (160 degrees C).
In a heavy-bottomed casserole dish, layer half of the potatoes, onions, and carrots.
Add the lamb pieces on top of the vegetables, and season with salt and pepper.
Add the remaining vegetables on top of the meat and tuck in the thyme sprigs.
Pour the stock over the contents of the dish.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and bake in the oven for 2 hours until the meat is tender.

title: Traditional Yorkshire Pudding
ingredients: 2 tbsp beef dripping or vegetable oil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220C (425F).
Whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, and salt until smooth, then let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
Put the beef dripping into a 12-hole muffin tin and place in the hot oven until smoking hot.
Pour the batter quickly into the hot oil, filling each hole about halfway.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes without opening the oven door until risen and golden brown.

title: Yorkshire Curd Tart
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C (400F).
Line a tart tin with the shortcrust pastry and chill in the fridge.
Beat the curd cheese, butter, and sugar together in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the beaten eggs, currants, and grated nutmeg.
Pour the mixture into the pastry case and bake for 30 minutes until set and lightly golden.

title: Parkin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150C (300F) and grease a 9-inch square baking tin.
Gently melt the butter, golden syrup, black treacle, and brown sugar together in a pan over low heat until dissolved.
Mix the oatmeal, flour, ginger, and mixed spice together in a large mixing bowl.
Pour the melted syrup mixture and the milk into the dry ingredients and stir well until combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes until firm, then let it mature for a few days before eating.

title: Fat Rascals
ingredients: Blanched almonds and glacé cherries for decoration
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C (400F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, dried fruit, mixed spice, and candied peel.
Add the egg and just enough milk to bring the mixture together into a stiff dough.
Divide into mounds on the baking sheet, press halved almonds and cherries on top to make a face, and bake for 15 minutes.

title: Panackelty
ingredients: 2 lbs boiling potatoes, peeled and sliced
1.5 lbs corned beef or leftover cooked beef, cubed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160C (325F).
Grease a large heavy casserole dish with butter.
Layer the sliced potatoes, onions, and cubed beef alternately in the dish, seasoning each layer with salt and pepper.
Pour the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce over the top layer.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and bake in the oven for 2 hours until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden and crisp.

title: Classic Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 1 kg russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash with butter and milk.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat, add the onion and carrots, and cook until softened.
Add the minced lamb and cook until browned, draining excess fat.
Stir in the flour and tomato purée, cooking for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, bring to a simmer, and cook for 15 minutes until thickened.
Transfer the lamb mixture to a baking dish and spread the mashed potato evenly on top, roughing the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.

title: Traditional Toad in the Hole
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220C (200C fan).
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, and salt until smooth to make the batter, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Place the sunflower oil and sausages in a roasting tin and roast for 15 minutes until the sausages start to brown.
Add the sliced onions to the tin around the sausages.
Carefully pour the rested batter directly into the hot tin over the sausages and onions.
Bake immediately for 30-35 minutes without opening the oven door, until the batter has puffed up and is crisp and golden.
Serve hot cut into portions with rich beef gravy.

title: Proper Steak and Ale Pie
ingredients: 750g chuck steak, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
1 large egg, beaten, for egg wash
instructions: Toss the beef cubes in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and sear the beef until well browned on all sides, then remove.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft, then stir in the tomato paste.
Pour in the dark ale to deglace the pot, scraping up any browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot along with the beef stock and thyme sprigs, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Allow the filling to cool slightly, then transfer to a pie dish.
Preheat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Cover the dish with the puff pastry sheet, trim the edges, cut a small vent in the top, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.

title: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
ingredients: 1 kg King Edward potatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190C (170C fan) and bake the sausages for 25 minutes until cooked through and browned.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, then drain well.
Mash the potatoes with butter and double cream until smooth and creamy, keeping them warm.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the sliced onions slowly for 15-20 minutes until caramelized and sweet.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the beef stock and balsamic vinegar, simmering until the gravy thickens nicely.
Serve the sausages resting on a generous mound of mash, generously drizzled with the onion gravy.

title: Classic Bread and Butter Pudding
ingredients: 8 slices stale white sandwich bread, crusts removed
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C (160C fan) and lightly butter a 1.5-litre ovenproof baking dish.
Butter each slice of bread, cut them diagonally into triangles, and arrange a layer of bread, buttered-side up, in the dish.
Scatter half of the sultanas and a pinch of cinnamon over the bread, then repeat with another layer of bread and sultanas.
In a bowl, whisk together the double cream, whole milk, eggs, granulated sugar, and vanilla extract.
Pour the custard mixture evenly over the bread and let it soak for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle the demerara sugar evenly over the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the pudding is set, puffed up, and golden brown on top.

title: Traditional Cornish Pastry
ingredients: 1 lb shortcrust or rough puff pastry, chilled
1 lb potatoes, peeled and diced small
8 oz swede (rutabaga), peeled and diced small
2 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix the diced skirt steak, potatoes, swede, and onion together.
Roll out the pastry on a floured surface and cut out four 8-inch circles using a plate as a guide.
Divide the vegetable and meat mixture evenly onto one half of each pastry circle.
Season each mound generously with salt and pepper, and top with a few small pieces of butter.
Brush the edges of the pastry with water, fold the pastry over the filling, and crimp the edges tightly to seal in a traditional Cornish crimp.
Transfer the pasties to the prepared baking sheet and brush the tops with the beaten egg.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until golden brown and bubbling inside, then let cool slightly before eating.

title: Stargazy Pie
ingredients: 1 lb fresh sardines, whole with heads on, scaled and cleaned
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Melt the butter in a pan, cook the onions until soft, stir in the flour, and gradually add the milk to make a thick white sauce. Stir in the parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Line a deep pie dish with one sheet of pastry.
Layer half of the sliced potatoes and onions on the bottom of the pastry.
Arrange the sardines radially in the dish with their heads poking up through the gaps near the rim so they look like they are gazing at the stars.
Layer the remaining potatoes and onions over the fish, then pour the white sauce evenly over everything.
Cover the pie with the second pastry sheet, carefully cutting small slits to let the fish heads poke through the top.
Crimp the edges to seal, brush with the beaten egg, and bake for 40 minutes until the pastry is golden and crisp.

title: Saffron Cake
ingredients: 1 cup mixed dried currants and sultanas
instructions: Steep the saffron threads in the boiling water for at least 30 minutes to release the color and flavor.
In a large bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar and let it sit until frothy.
Add the flour, softened butter, remaining sugar, salt, and the saffron liquid (including the threads) to the yeast mixture.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Work the currants, sultanas, and mixed peel evenly into the dough.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a towel, and let rise in a warm place for 2 hours or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough, shape it into a neat loaf or round cake, and place it into a greased loaf pan or cake tin.
Cover and let rise again for 45 minutes, then bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35 to 40 minutes until hollow when tapped on the bottom.

title: Cornish Hevva Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a shallow baking tin.
In a large bowl, rub the butter and lard into the flour until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, raisins, mixed peel, and mixed spice.
Gradually add the milk, mixing with a knife until the ingredients come together to form a stiff dough.
Turn the dough out into the prepared tin and press it down evenly to fill the corners.
Score a diamond pattern across the top of the cake with a knife, representing the fishing nets used to spot pilchards.
Bake in the oven for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool in the tin before cutting into squares to serve.

title: Authentic Cornish Cream Tea
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
1 jar traditional strawberry or raspberry jam
1 pot of freshly brewed English breakfast tea
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sift the flour and baking powder into a large bowl, add the sugar, and rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the raisins if using, then gently mix in the milk to form a soft dough.
Turn out onto a floured surface, gently pat down to about 1-inch thickness, and cut out rounds using a round pastry cutter.
Place the scones on the baking sheet and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden on top.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on a wire rack.
Split the warm scones in half.
Spread a generous layer of strawberry or raspberry jam on each half first, then top with a dollop of Cornish clotted cream, and serve with hot tea.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb neck chops and shoulder, trimmed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 large potatoes, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
instructions: Preheat your oven to 325F (160C).
Layer the sliced onions and lamb in a large, heavy-based casserole dish, seasoning each layer with salt, pepper, and a dusting of flour.
Dot the butter over the top and pour in the lamb stock.
Arrange the sliced potatoes in an overlapping layer on top to cover the meat completely.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and bake in the oven for 2 hours.
Remove the lid and bake for another 30 minutes until the potatoes are golden and crispy.

title: Black Pudding Hash
ingredients: 1 lb potatoes, boiled in their skins, cooled, and diced
8 oz good quality Lancashire black pudding, crumbled
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Add the diced potatoes and crumbled black pudding to the pan.
Fry everything together, pressing down with a spatula to get a nice crust, for about 10 to 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a separate pan, fry the eggs and serve them on top of the hash.

title: Parkin Cake
instructions: Preheat your oven to 300F (150C) and grease a deep 8-inch square baking tin.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the oatmeal, flour, ginger, mixed spice, and brown sugar.
In a saucepan, gently melt the butter, golden syrup, and black treacle together until combined.
Stir the milk and beaten egg into the melted syrup mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and beat well until smooth.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes until firm.
Allow to cool in the tin, then wrap in greaseproof paper and store for a few days before eating.

title: Lancashire Cheese and Onion Pie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375F (190C).
Melt the butter in a pan and gently cook the sliced onions until soft and sweet, but not browned.
Remove the onions from the heat and stir in the grated Lancashire cheese until it begins to melt slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Roll out half the shortcrust pastry and use it to line a pie dish.
Spoon the onion and cheese mixture into the pastry case.
Roll out the remaining pastry to form a lid, place it over the pie, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400F (200C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, mix together the currants, melted butter, dark brown sugar, mixed spice, and mixed peel.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to about 1/8-inch thickness.
Cut out circles from the pastry using a 4-inch saucer or pastry cutter.
Place a spoonful of the currant filling in the center of each pastry circle.
Bring the edges of the pastry up over the filling and pinch them together to seal.
Turn the cakes over, flatten them gently with a rolling pin, and make three small slashes on the top of each.
Brush with a little water and sprinkle generously with granulated sugar.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

title: Traditional Scottish Porridge
instructions: Combine the oatmeal, water, and salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, stirring frequently with a spurtle.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often until creamy.
Pour into warm bowls and serve with a splash of cold milk and a side of sugar for dipping.

title: Cullen Skink
instructions: Place the smoked haddock in a pan with the milk and water, and gently poach for 5 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Remove the fish, set aside to cool, and strain the cooking liquid, reserving the milk and water.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the diced potatoes and the reserved cooking liquid, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Flake the haddock into the pot, discarding any skin and bones, and heat through.
Season with black pepper, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Scottish Stovies
ingredients: 1 kg russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
300g leftover roast beef or lamb, chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Melt the lard in a large, heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook slowly until soft and golden brown.
Layer half of the sliced potatoes over the onions, then add the chopped leftover meat, and top with the remaining potatoes.
Pour in the beef stock, season well with salt and pepper, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover tightly with a lid, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 45 minutes without stirring until the potatoes are completely tender and have absorbed the liquid.
Mash slightly in the pot to combine and serve hot with oatcakes.

title: Scotch Broth
instructions: Place the lamb neck chops and water in a large soup pot, bring to a boil, and skim off any scum.
Drain the soaked pearl barley and yellow peas, and add them to the pot.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the sliced leek, diced carrots, and turnip to the pot.
Continue to simmer for another 45 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the meat falls off the bone.
Remove the meat, shred it, and return it to the soup, discarding the bones.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Traditional Cranachan
instructions: Toast the oatmeal in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring constantly until golden and nutty, then allow to cool.
Whip the double cream in a chilled bowl until soft peaks form.
Fold the heather honey and Scotch whisky gently into the whipped cream.
Layer the toasted oatmeal, fresh raspberries, and honey cream into serving glasses.
Repeat the layers and top with a few extra raspberries and a dusting of oatmeal before serving.

title: Traditional Welsh Cakes
ingredients: 1/2 cup caster sugar, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Rub the butter into the flour in a large bowl until it resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, mixed spice, and currants.
Add the beaten egg and enough milk to bring the mixture together into a soft dough.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 1/2-inch thickness.
Cut into rounds with a cutter and cook on a hot, greased bakestone or heavy frying pan for 3 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Dust with caster sugar while still warm.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in the ale, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard until smooth and thick.
Remove from heat and stir in the grated Cheddar until completely melted and combined.
Toast the bread slices lightly on both sides.
Spread the cheese mixture thickly over the toast, covering to the edges.
Place under a hot broiler until bubbly, golden brown, and bubbling.

title: Cawl
ingredients: 1.5 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot and brown the lamb chunks on all sides.
Add the stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the carrots, turnip, and potatoes to the pot.
Simmer for another 20 minutes until the root vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the sliced leeks and cook for an additional 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and garnish with chopped parsley before serving hot.

title: Glamorgan Sausages
instructions: Mix the grated cheese, breadcrumbs, chopped leek, thyme, and mustard powder in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper.
Separate the eggs, beating the yolks into the mixture and keeping the whites in a separate bowl.
Shape the mixture into sausage shapes with your hands.
Dip each sausage into the lightly beaten egg whites, then coat with extra breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the sausages for 8 to 10 minutes, turning frequently until golden brown and crispy on all sides.

title: Bara Brith
instructions: Place the dried fruit and brown sugar in a large bowl, pour over the cold black tea, and soak overnight.
Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease and line a 2 lb loaf tin.
Add the flour, mixed spice, and beaten egg to the soaked fruit mixture.
Stir thoroughly until everything is well combined and no dry flour remains.
Spoon the batter into the prepared loaf tin and smooth the top.
Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing and serving with butter.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick fries
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Add the potato fries and cook until golden brown and crispy, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove the fries and drain them on paper towels.
In a saucepan, heat the beef gravy until piping hot.
Place the hot fries in a serving bowl or dish.
Top the warm fries generously with fresh cheese curds.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds, and serve immediately.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pie crusts for a 9-inch double crust pie
instructions: Preheat your oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pie crust and cut out 4-inch circles, pressing them gently into the muffin cups.
In a bowl, cream together the softened butter and dark brown sugar until smooth.
Stir in the beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and white vinegar until well combined.
Scatter a few raisins into the bottom of each pastry crust.
Spoon the butter and sugar mixture evenly into the pastry shells, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the filling is set and bubbling.
Allow the tarts to cool completely in the pan before carefully removing them.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper.
In a metal bowl set over a pot of simmering water, melt the 1/2 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa powder.
Whisk in the beaten egg and stir constantly until the mixture thickens, then remove from heat.
Stir in the graham cracker crumbs, chopped almonds, and shredded coconut until thoroughly mixed.
Press the crumb mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of the prepared baking pan, then place in the refrigerator to chill.
For the filling, beat the 1/4 cup softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and powdered sugar together until light and smooth.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer and return to the refrigerator.
In a microwave-safe bowl, melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 1 tablespoon butter together, stirring until smooth.
Spread the melted chocolate evenly over the custard layer.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting into small squares.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 recipe pastry for a double-crust 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet over medium heat, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, and water.
Cook, stirring frequently to break up the meat, until the meat is thoroughly browned and the liquid is mostly evaporated.
Drain off any excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in the ground cinnamon, ground cloves, salt, and black pepper, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with half of the pastry dough.
Spoon the meat mixture into the pastry-lined dish.
Cover with the top crust, flute the edges to seal, and cut a few small slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.
Allow to cool for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Montreal Style Bagels
instructions: In a large bowl, dissolve yeast and 1/4 cup honey in warm water and let stand until frothy.
Whisk in vegetable oil, 1 egg, and salt.
Gradually stir in the flour until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 24 equal pieces, rolling each piece into a rope and sealing the ends to form a ring.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and stir in 1/4 cup of honey.
Preheat your oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Boil the bagels in batches for about 1 minute per side, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain briefly.
Mix the poppy seeds and sesame seeds in a shallow dish, then dip the boiled bagels into the seed mixture to coat both sides.
Place the bagels on the prepared baking sheets and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until deeply golden brown.

title: Classic Poutine
ingredients: 4 large Russet potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Fry potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes until soft but not browned, then remove and drain.
Increase oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Return fries to the hot oil and fry until golden brown and crispy, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove fries, drain excess oil, and place them in a serving dish while hot.
Scatter fresh cheese curds over the hot fries.
Pour hot beef gravy generously over the curds and fries, and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
ingredients: 0.33 cup unsalted butter, softened for filling
instructions: Melt 0.5 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa in the top of a double boiler.
Whisk in the egg and stir constantly until the mixture thickens, then remove from heat.
Stir in graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and chopped almonds until well combined.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan and chill in the fridge.
To make the filling, beat 0.33 cup butter, custard powder, milk, and powdered sugar together until light and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer and return to the fridge.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter together over low heat.
Spread the melted chocolate smoothly over the custard layer and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix flour and cold cubed butter in a bowl until crumbly, then add ice water to form a dough.
Roll out the pastry dough on a floured surface and cut into circles to fit a muffin tin.
Place pastry circles into the muffin cups and chill in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a bowl, whisk together brown sugar, melted butter, eggs, milk, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Distribute raisins evenly into the unbaked pastry shells.
Pour the brown sugar filling mixture over the raisins, filling each shell about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 minutes at 400 degrees F, then reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 minutes until the filling is bubbly and set.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: double pie crust for a 9-inch pie
1 large egg beaten with 1 tablespoon water for egg wash
instructions: Place ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, and water in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook until the meat is thoroughly browned and the liquid has reduced, breaking up any large clumps.
Drain excess fat, then stir in cinnamon, cloves, salt, and black pepper, and let cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pastry crust.
Transfer the seasoned meat mixture into the pastry-lined pie plate and spread evenly.
Cover with the second pastry crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top crust for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the egg wash.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the filling is hot.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
instructions: In a bowl, mix salt, brown sugar, black peppercorns, coriander seeds, mustard seeds, garlic, and paprika to make the curing rub.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly over all sides of the beef brisket.
Place the brisket in a large ziplock bag or non-reactive container and refrigerate for 5 to 7 days, turning daily.
Remove the brisket from the cure, rinse thoroughly under cold water, and pat dry.
Preheat a smoker to 225 degrees F (110 degrees C) using fruitwood or maple wood.
Smoke the brisket until the internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C), about 5 hours.
Transfer the smoked brisket to a roasting pan, add a little water, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 300 degrees F (150 degrees C) for 3 more hours until tender.
Slice the meat thinly against the grain, pile high on rye bread with yellow mustard, and serve warm.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 350 degrees F.
Fry potatoes in batches until soft and golden, about 5 to 6 minutes, and drain on paper towels.
Reheat oil to 400 degrees F and fry potatoes a second time until crispy and golden brown.
Transfer hot fries to a serving dish, top with fresh cheese curds, and pour hot beef gravy over the top to melt the cheese.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pie crusts for a 9-inch double crust pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F and lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pastry and cut out 12 circles, then press them gently into the muffin cups.
In a bowl, mix together the melted butter, brown sugar, beaten eggs, vinegar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Stir in the raisins if desired.
Divide the filling evenly among the pastry-lined muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 10 minutes at 450 degrees F, then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is set.
Cool completely in the pan before removing.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: Pastry for a 9-inch double crust pie
instructions: Combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, and water in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally until meat is cooked and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Stir in cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat and let cool.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pie crust, add the meat mixture, and top with the second crust.
Flute the edges to seal and cut a few slits in the top crust for steam to escape.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown and flaky.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Whisk butter, sugar, and cocoa in the top of a double boiler, then add egg and whisk until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan and chill in the fridge.
Beat softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and icing sugar together until smooth and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base and refrigerate again.
Melt chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter together over low heat, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill until firm before cutting into small squares.

title: PEI Potato Soup
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook chopped bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add onion and celery to the bacon drippings and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Whisk flour into heavy cream until smooth, then stir into the soup.
Simmer for another 5 minutes until the soup thickens slightly.
Stir in the shredded cheddar cheese until melted and smooth, season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with reserved crispy bacon and sliced green onions before serving.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick fries
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Add the cut potatoes and fry until golden brown and crispy, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove the fries and drain them on paper towels, then season lightly with salt.
Warm the beef gravy in a saucepan over medium heat until hot.
Place the hot fries in a serving dish or bowl.
Scatter the fresh cheese curds evenly over the hot fries.
Pour the hot gravy generously over the curds and fries, and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 1/2 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa powder in the top of a double boiler.
Whisk in the beaten egg and stir constantly until mixture thickens, then remove from heat.
Stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut until well combined.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an ungreased 8x8 inch baking pan and chill.
In a bowl, beat 1/4 cup softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer and return to the refrigerator.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 1 tablespoon of butter together until smooth.
Spread the chocolate glaze evenly over the custard layer and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pastry for double-crust 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pie crust and cut out circles large enough to fit into the muffin cups.
Place raisins evenly into the bottom of each unbaked pastry shell.
In a bowl, cream together the softened butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Beat in the eggs, vinegar, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Spoon the filling mixture into the pastry shells over the raisins, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the filling is bubbly and set.
Cool completely in the pan before removing.

title: Tourtiere
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, garlic, and water over medium heat.
Cook, stirring frequently to break up the meat, until the meat is no longer pink.
Drain excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, black pepper, and breadcrumbs, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with half of the pastry dough.
Spoon the meat mixture into the pastry-lined dish.
Cover with the top crust, trim and crimp edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick french fries
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Add the cut potatoes and fry until golden brown and crisp, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove the fries and drain on paper towels.
Warm the beef gravy in a saucepan over medium heat.
Place the hot fries on a serving platter or in bowls.
Scatter the fresh cheese curds over the hot fries.
Pour the hot gravy generously over the cheese curds and fries, and serve immediately.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pastry dough and cut out 12 circles to fit the muffin cups, pressing them gently into the cups.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the softened butter, brown sugar, beaten eggs, vinegar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Place a small handful of raisins into the bottom of each pastry crust.
Spoon the filling mixture into the pastry shells, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is set.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 1/2 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa powder in a top of a double boiler.
Whisk in the beaten egg and stir constantly until thickened, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an 8x8-inch baking pan and chill in the refrigerator.
For the filling, beat 1/4 cup softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and powdered sugar together until light and fluffy, then spread evenly over the chilled base and return to the fridge.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter together over low heat, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill the bars until set, about 1 hour, before cutting into squares.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, combine the ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, and water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring and breaking up the meat, until thoroughly cooked, about 15 minutes.
Drain excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with half of the pastry dough.
Transfer the meat mixture into the pastry-lined dish.
Cover with the top crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown. Let cool for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the kosher salt, cracked black peppercorns, ground coriander, brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika to create a dry rub.
Rub the spice mixture evenly over all sides of the beef brisket.
Place the seasoned brisket in a resealable plastic bag or non-reactive container, seal, and refrigerate for 5 to 7 days, turning daily.
Remove the brisket from the refrigerator and rinse thoroughly under cold water to remove excess surface salt, then pat dry.
Preheat a smoker or a charcoal grill for indirect cooking at 225 degrees F (110 degrees C) using fruitwood chips.
Place the brisket in the smoker and cook until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), about 4 to 5 hours.
Wrap the brisket tightly in butcher paper and return to the smoker or an oven heated to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C) until the internal temperature reaches 203 degrees F (95 degrees C).
Remove from heat, rest for 1 hour, slice thinly against the grain, and serve on rye bread with mustard.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 3/8-inch thick fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat oil to 325 degrees F and fry potatoes for 5 minutes until soft but not browned; remove and drain.
Increase oil temperature to 375 degrees F and fry potatoes a second time until golden and crisp.
Transfer fries to a serving dish, top with fresh cheese curds, and pour hot beef gravy over the top to melt the curds.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pie pastry for a 9-inch double crust
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F and grease a standard muffin tin.
Roll out pastry and cut into 12 circles, pressing them gently into the muffin cups.
In a bowl, whisk together melted butter, brown sugar, eggs, vanilla, and vinegar until smooth.
Place a few raisins in the bottom of each pastry shell and pour the sugar mixture over them.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for 10 more minutes until filling is set and bubbling.
Cool completely in the pan before removing.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 recipe pastry for a double-crust 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large skillet, combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.
Cook over medium heat, breaking up the meat, until thoroughly browned and liquid has reduced, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the grated potato and remove from heat to cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with half the pastry, fill with the meat mixture, and top with the second crust, crimping edges to seal.
Cut small slits in the top crust to vent steam.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Cut potatoes into fries and soak in cold water for 30 minutes.
