Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 375 degrees F.
Fry potatoes in batches until golden and crisp, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Drain fries on paper towels and season lightly with salt.
Place hot fries on a serving dish, top with cheese curds, and pour hot brown gravy over the top to melt the curds.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pie crust for a 9-inch double crust
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F and grease a standard muffin tin.
Roll out the pie dough and cut out circles to fit into the muffin cups.
In a bowl, mix melted butter, brown sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and white vinegar until smooth.
Place a few raisins at the bottom of each pastry-lined cup.
Pour the sugar mixture over the raisins, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425 degrees F, then reduce heat to 350 degrees F and bake for another 10 minutes until the filling is set.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 1/2 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa in the top of a double boiler, then stir in the beaten egg and cook until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan and chill.
Beat softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and powdered sugar together until light and fluffy, then spread over the base layer and chill again.
Melt chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter together, spread over the custard layer, and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: Double pie crust for a 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large skillet, combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat, drain excess fat, and stir in the mashed potatoes to bind the mixture.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with one pie crust, add the meat filling, and cover with the top crust, sealing the edges and cutting slits for steam.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
instructions: Crush coriander seeds, mustard seeds, and peppercorns coarsely with a mortar and pestle.
Mix the salt, crushed spices, brown sugar, garlic powder, and bay leaf to create a curing rub.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly all over the beef brisket.
Place the brisket in a zip-top bag or non-reactive container and refrigerate for 7 days, turning daily.
Rinse the brisket thoroughly under cold water to remove excess salt, then soak in cold water for 1 hour.
Smoke the brisket at 225 degrees F until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F, then steam until tender before slicing.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cut into french fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat canola oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes until soft but not browned, then remove and drain.
Increase oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and fry the potatoes a second time until golden and crispy.
Drain fries on paper towels and place them in a warm serving dish.
Scatter fresh cheese curds evenly over the hot fries.
Pour hot beef gravy generously over the cheese and fries, and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Whisk butter, sugar, and cocoa in the top of a double boiler over boiling water until melted and blended.
Add the beaten egg and stir constantly for about 3 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in graham crumbs, chopped almonds, and shredded coconut.
Press the crumb mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan, then chill in the fridge.
For the filling, beat butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and icing sugar together until smooth and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer, and return to the refrigerator to set.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter together over low heat, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill until firm, cut into small squares, and serve cold.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix flour with a pinch of salt, cut in cold butter until crumbly, and add ice water to form a pastry dough.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut into circles to fit a muffin tin, then chill.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
In a bowl, whisk together brown sugar, maple syrup, melted butter, beaten egg, vinegar, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Place a few raisins into the bottom of each prepared pastry shell.
Pour the syrup filling into the pastry shells, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425 degrees F, then lower the temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for 10 more minutes until bubbly and set.
Cool completely in the pan before removing.

title: Tourtiere
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, garlic, and water.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain excess fat from the meat mixture.
Stir in cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, pepper, and breadcrumbs, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Line a pie plate with one of the pie crusts.
Spread the seasoned meat mixture evenly into the crust.
Cover with the top pie crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Maritime Fish Chowder
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups fish stock or chicken broth
1.5 pounds fresh white fish fillets, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook diced bacon in a large soup pot over medium heat until crisp, then remove bacon and set aside, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add chopped onion and celery to the bacon drippings and cook until softened.
Add diced potatoes and fish stock, drop in the bay leaf, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
In a small bowl, mash butter and flour together into a paste.
Stir the milk, heavy cream, and butter-flour paste into the soup pot, stirring constantly until slightly thickened.
Add the chunks of white fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, remove bay leaf, and garnish with reserved bacon and fresh parsley before serving.

title: Classic Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick fries
instructions: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes until tender but not browned, then remove and drain.
Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C) and fry the potatoes a second time until golden and crisp.
Transfer the hot fries to a serving dish and toss lightly with salt.
Scatter the fresh cheese curds evenly over the hot fries.
Pour the hot beef gravy generously over the cheese curds and fries, then serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars

instructions: Melt the first 1/2 cup of butter, sugar, and cocoa powder in the top of a double boiler.
Whisk in the egg and stir constantly until the mixture thickens, then remove from heat.

Press the crumb mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan and chill.
For the filling, beat the second amount of butter, milk, custard powder, and icing sugar together until smooth and light.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer and return to the refrigerator.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter together over low heat, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill until set, then cut into small squares before serving.

title: Tourtiere

Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pastry crust, fill with the cooled meat mixture, and cover with the top crust.
Trim and crimp the edges to seal, cut a few vents in the top crust, and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.

In a medium bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, melted butter, beaten eggs, maple syrup, vinegar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Carefully spoon the filling into each pastry cup, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake at 450°F for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 350°F (175°C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the filling is set and bubbly.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before running a knife around the edges to remove them.

title: Montreal Style Bagels
instructions: In a large bowl, dissolve the yeast and 1 tablespoon of sugar in warm water, letting it sit for 10 minutes until frothy.
Whisk in the remaining sugar, oil, and eggs, then stir in the salt.
Gradually add the flour one cup at a time until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for about 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Punch down the dough, divide it into 24 equal pieces, and roll each piece into a rope, shaping them into rings with a large hole.
Bring the 10 cups of water and honey to a boil in a wide pot.
Boil the bagels in batches for about 1 minute per side, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Dip the boiled bagels immediately into a shallow bowl of sesame seeds to coat both sides.
Place on the prepared baking sheets and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until deeply golden brown.

instructions: Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper.

title: Maritime Fish Chowder
