Add the cubed potatoes and fish stock to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Gently stir in the cod chunks, whole milk, and heavy cream, and simmer for 5 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
In a small bowl, whisk together the flour and cold water until smooth, then stir it slowly into the chowder to thicken.
Season with salt and white pepper, simmer for another 2 minutes, and remove from heat.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with the reserved crispy bacon and chopped fresh parsley.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat canola oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Add the cut potatoes and fry until golden and crispy, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove the fries and drain them on paper towels.
Place the hot fries in a serving dish and top with fresh cheese curds.
Pour hot brown gravy generously over the fries and curds, and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Whisk butter, sugar, and cocoa in a bowl over simmering water until thick.
Whisk in the egg until thickened, then remove from heat.
Stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut; press firmly into an 8x8 inch pan.
Beat softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and icing sugar until smooth; spread over the base layer.
Melt chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter together, then spread evenly over the custard layer.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting into squares.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 pkg prepared pie crusts for a 9-inch double crust pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pie crust and cut out circles to fit into the muffin cups.
Place raisins evenly into the bottom of each pastry shell.
Cream together the butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Beat in the eggs, white vinegar, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Spoon the filling into the pastry shells over the raisins, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 10 minutes at 450 degrees F, then reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the filling is set.
Cool completely in the pan before removing.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 pkg pastry for a double-crust 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Combine ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally until liquid is absorbed.
Stir in mashed potatoes to bind the meat mixture, then let cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with half of the pastry.
Spoon the meat filling into the pastry-lined dish.
Cover with the top crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown. Let cool before slicing.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
instructions: Mix kosher salt, cracked black pepper, crushed coriander seeds, brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, and mustard seeds in a bowl.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly over all sides of the brisket.
Place the brisket in a resealable plastic bag or non-reactive container and refrigerate for 5 to 7 days, turning daily.
Rinse the brisket thoroughly under cold water to remove excess surface salt and pat dry.
Preheat a smoker to 225 degrees F (110 degrees C) using fruitwood or maple wood.
Smoke the brisket until the internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).
Wrap the brisket tightly in butcher paper and place it back in the smoker or oven at 225 degrees F until the internal temperature reaches 203 degrees F (95 degrees C).
Rest the meat for 1 hour, slice thinly across the grain, and serve on rye bread with mustard.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/4-inch thick french fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat oil in a deep fryer to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Fry potatoes in batches until golden and crisp, about 5 to 7 minutes; drain on paper towels.
Heat the beef gravy until hot.
Place hot fries in a serving dish, top with cheese curds, and pour hot gravy over the top to melt the curds slightly.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 pastry for a 9-inch double crust pie, chilled
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out pastry and cut into 12 circles, then press gently into the muffin cups.
In a bowl, cream together the butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Whisk in the eggs, vanilla extract, and flour until well combined.
Divide raisins evenly among the pastry cups.
Pour the filling mixture over the raisins, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbly and set.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 recipe pastry for a double-crust 9-inch pie
Salt and black pepper to taste
1 large egg beaten with 1 tablespoon water for egg wash
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid evaporates.
Line a 9-inch pie dish with half of the pastry.
Spoon the meat mixture into the pastry-lined dish.
Cover with the top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush top crust with the egg wash.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 1/2 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa in the top of a double boiler, then whisk in the egg and stir until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut; press firmly into an 8x8-inch baking pan and chill.
Beat 1/4 cup softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and icing sugar together until smooth; spread evenly over the base layer and refrigerate.
Melt chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter together, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill in the refrigerator until set before cutting into small squares.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
ingredients: 1 beef brisket, flat cut, about 4 pounds
instructions: Grind the peppercorns, coriander seeds, and mustard seeds coarsely.
Mix the ground spices with salt, brown sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika to create a rub.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly all over the beef brisket.
Place the brisket in a resealable plastic bag or container and refrigerate for 5 to 7 days, turning daily.
Rinse the brisket thoroughly under cold water to remove excess salt, then soak in cold water for 1 hour.
Smoke the brisket at 225 degrees F (110 degrees C) until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Transfer the brisket to a steam pan, cover tightly with foil, and steam or bake at 300 degrees F (150 degrees C) for 3 more hours until tender enough to shred with a fork.
Slice against the grain and serve hot on rye bread with yellow mustard.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Fry potatoes in batches for about 5 to 6 minutes until tender but not browned, then remove and drain.
Increase oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and fry potatoes a second time until golden and crisp, about 2 to 3 minutes.
In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Gradually whisk in beef broth and chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook until thickened into a gravy.
Place hot fries on a serving plate, top with fresh cheese curds, and pour hot gravy over the top to melt the curds slightly.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pie crusts for 9-inch double crust
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the pie dough and cut out circles large enough to fit into the muffin cups.
Place raisins evenly into the bottom of each pastry-lined cup.
In a bowl, cream together the softened butter and brown sugar until smooth.
Beat in the eggs, white vinegar, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Spoon the filling mixture into the pastry cups, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425 degrees F, then reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 minutes until the filling is set.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: In a metal bowl set over simmering water, whisk together melted butter, sugar, cocoa powder, and egg until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, chopped almonds, and shredded coconut.
Press the crumb mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of an 8x8-inch baking pan and chill in the fridge.
In a mixing bowl, beat softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer and return to the refrigerator.
Melt semi-sweet chocolate and 1 tablespoon of butter together until smooth, then spread over the custard layer.
Chill until firm before cutting into small squares with a warm knife.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 package pastry for a double-crust 9-inch pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove cover and simmer until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and breadcrumbs, then let the mixture cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with half of the pastry dough, add the meat filling, and cover with the top crust.
Crimp the edges to seal, cut a few slits in the top crust for steam, and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Montreal Bagels
instructions: In a large bowl, combine warm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar; let stand until frothy.
Whisk in remaining sugar, oil, eggs, and salt, then gradually mix in the flour to form a dough.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Divide dough into small pieces, roll into ropes, and shape into rings by pinching the ends together.
In a large pot, bring water and honey to a boil, then drop bagels in a few at a time and boil for 1 minute per side.
Remove bagels from water, dip both sides generously in sesame seeds, place on baking sheets, and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden.

title: Classic Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cut into french fries
instructions: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes until soft but not browned, then remove and drain.
Increase the oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Return the fries to the hot oil and fry until golden brown and crispy, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain the hot fries on paper towels and season lightly with salt.
Transfer the hot fries to a serving dish and scatter the cheese curds evenly over top.
Pour the hot beef gravy generously over the fries and cheese curds, and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.
Whisk together melted butter, sugar, cocoa, and egg in a metal bowl set over a pot of simmering water until thick.
Remove from heat and stir in graham cracker crumbs, almonds, and coconut.
Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan, then place in the fridge to chill.
In a bowl, beat softened butter, heavy cream, custard powder, and icing sugar until smooth and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base layer, and return to the fridge.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter together in a microwave-safe bowl until smooth.
Spread the melted chocolate mixture evenly over the custard layer and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: Tourtière (French-Canadian Pork Pie)
ingredients: 1 large egg, beaten for egg wash
instructions: Combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg in a large saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid and cook for another 15 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the mashed potatoes to bind the meat mixture, then let it cool completely.
Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pie crust, fill with the cooled meat mixture, and top with the second crust.
Crimp the edges to seal, cut a few slits in the top crust for steam to escape, and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown, then let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually stir in ice water just until the dough comes together, shape into a disk, and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut out circles to fit the muffin cups.
Place a few raisins in the bottom of each unbaked pastry shell.
Whisk together brown sugar, melted butter, eggs, maple syrup, vinegar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour the filling mixture into the pastry shells, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425 degrees F, then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 minutes until the filling is bubbly and set.

title: Maritime Fish Chowder
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
2 cups fish stock or chicken broth
1 lb firm white fish fillets, such as haddock or cod, cut into chunks
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the diced bacon in a large soup pot over medium heat until crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the chopped onion and celery to the bacon fat in the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the cubed potatoes and fish stock to the pot along with the bay leaf.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk together the heavy cream, whole milk, and flour in a small bowl until smooth.
Gently stir the cream mixture and the fish chunks into the pot.
Simmer gently over low heat for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, garnish with crispy bacon and fresh parsley, and serve hot.

title: Jiggs Dinner
instructions: Place the soaked salt beef in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
Add the filled pudding bag to the pot and simmer for about 1 hour.
Add the carrots and turnips, cooking for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage wedges, and cook for another 20 to 25 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Remove meat and vegetables, carve, and serve hot with the split pea pudding.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 1 lb hard tack salt fish (cod), soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked salt fish, place in a pot of fresh water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes until flaky.
Drain the soaked hard bread, place in a separate pot of boiling water, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
In a frying pan, fry the diced salt pork over medium heat until crisp, rendering the fat into scrunchions.
Add the chopped onion to the pork fat and sauté until translucent.
Flake the cooked fish and combine with the drained hard bread, then top with the hot scrunchions and onion mixture.

title: Cod Gratin
instructions: Poach the cod fillets in salted water for 10 minutes until flaky, then flake into a greased baking dish.
Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until the sauce thickens.
Stir in half of the cheddar cheese, salt, pepper, and savory until melted.
Pour the cheese sauce over the fish, top with breadcrumbs and remaining cheese, and bake at 375 degrees F for 25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Toutons with Molasses
ingredients: 1 loaf portion of fresh bread dough
instructions: Pinch off small balls of bread dough and flatten them into round, flat cakes about 1/2-inch thick.
Melt the butter or oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the dough pieces for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and puffed up.
Remove from skillet and drain briefly on paper towels.
Serve warm drizzled with molasses.

title: Flippers
instructions: Soak the flippers in salted water with vinegar overnight, then drain and rinse.
In a heavy pot, fry the salt pork until crisp, remove scrunchions, and reserve the fat.
Brown the flippers in the hot pork fat on all sides.
Add the onions, carrots, beef broth, salt, and pepper to the pot, cover, and simmer on low for 2 hours until tender.
Mix flour with a little cold water to form a slurry, stir into the pot to thicken the gravy, and serve.

title: Tourtiere
ingredients: 1 large russet potato, peeled and boiled
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Mash the boiled potato until smooth and set aside.
In a large skillet, cook the pork, beef, onion, and garlic over medium heat until the meat is fully browned.
Drain excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, sage, salt, pepper, beef broth, and mashed potato until well combined.
Line a pie plate with one pastry crust, then pour in the meat mixture.
Cover with the top crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top to vent steam.
Bake for 30 minutes, then reduce the heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 15 minutes until golden brown.

title: Pate Chinois
ingredients: 1.5 cups canned whole kernel corn, drained
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, add butter and milk, and mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
In a skillet, brown the ground beef and chopped onion together until the meat is cooked through. Drain any excess fat and season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a 9x13-inch baking dish, spread the cooked beef and onion mixture evenly on the bottom.
Layer the creamed corn and whole kernel corn evenly over the beef.
Spread the mashed potatoes carefully on top of the corn layer, making grooves with a fork.
Sprinkle paprika over the potatoes and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and slightly golden on top.

title: Grand-Peres dans le Sirop
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Stir in the melted butter and milk just until a soft, sticky dough forms.
In a wide, deep skillet or pot, combine the maple syrup and water and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough into the simmering syrup to form dumplings.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and let them simmer gently for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove the lid and spoon the warm maple syrup over the dumplings.
Serve warm in bowls with extra syrup from the pan drizzled on top.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch thick fries
2 cups fresh Quebec cheese curds, at room temperature
instructions: Soak the cut fries in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 to 6 minutes until tender but not browned. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Increase the oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Return the fries to the hot oil and fry for another 2 to 3 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Drain and salt lightly.
Heat the brown gravy until piping hot.
Place a generous portion of hot fries in serving bowls, scatter cheese curds over the top, and generously ladle the hot gravy over everything to melt the curds slightly.

title: Ontario Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package prepared pastry for 9-inch pie crusts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Roll out pastry and cut into 12 circles, then press into a muffin tin.
In a bowl, mix together the brown sugar, melted butter, egg, vinegar, and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in the currants or raisins.
Spoon the mixture evenly into the pastry-lined muffin cups.
Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until filling is set.
Cool completely before removing from the pan.

title: Tourtiere
instructions: Combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and allspice in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally until liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in the mashed potatoes to bind the meat.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pastry crust.
Spread the meat mixture evenly into the crust.
Top with the second pastry crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut slits in the top to vent steam.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Peameal Bacon on a Kaiser Roll
ingredients: 4 tbsp yellow mustard or grainy mustard
instructions: Slice the peameal bacon roast into 1/4-inch to 1/2-inch thick slices.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the bacon slices for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Slice the Kaiser rolls in half and lightly toast them.
Spread mustard on the bottom half of each roll.
Layer with lettuce, tomato, and the hot cooked peameal bacon slices.
Top with the other half of the roll and serve immediately.

title: Ontario Sweet Corn Soup
ingredients: 6 cobs of fresh Ontario sweet corn, kernels cut off
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and celery, and sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the corn kernels and broth, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup to your desired consistency, leaving some texture.
Stir in the milk, salt, and white pepper, and heat through without boiling.
Garnish with fresh chives before serving.

title: Apple Pandowdy
ingredients: 6 cups tart Ontario apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Toss apple slices with sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and 2 tbsp flour, then transfer to a greased 8x8-inch baking dish.
In a bowl, mix 1 cup flour and salt, then cut in the butter until crumbly.
Stir in ice water just until dough comes together.
Roll out dough on a floured surface and place it over the apples, tucking in the edges and cutting slits in the top.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven, cut the crust into squares with a knife, press the squares down into the juices, and return to the oven for another 15 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Nova Scotia Lobster Rolls
ingredients: 1 lb fresh lobster meat, cooked and chunked
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: In a medium bowl, gently mix the lobster meat, mayonnaise, melted butter, lemon juice, celery, and chives.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Lightly butter the outside of each hot dog bun.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and toast the buns on both sides until golden brown.
Divide the lobster salad evenly among the warm toasted buns and serve immediately.

title: Traditional Acadian Rappie Pie
instructions: Boil the chicken with half the onion, salt, and pepper until cooked through; remove meat, debone, chop, and reserve the broth.
Grate the raw potatoes finely using a cheesecloth or special rappie pie press to extract as much liquid as possible.
Measure the extracted potato liquid and replace it with an equal amount of boiling chicken stock.
Slowly pour the boiling stock into the grated potatoes while stirring constantly to thicken the mixture.
Preheat oven to 375F (190C).
Spread half of the potato mixture in a large greased roasting pan, layer the chopped chicken evenly over it, and cover with the remaining potato mixture.
Dot the top with butter and bake for 2.5 to 3 hours until the crust is golden and the center is set.

title: Digby Scallops in Garlic Butter
ingredients: 1 lb fresh sea scallops, preferably Digby scallops
instructions: Rinse the scallops and pat them completely dry with paper towels; season lightly with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over high heat until foaming.
Add the scallops in a single layer without overcrowding and sear for 2 minutes without moving them.
Flip the scallops, add the minced garlic, lemon juice, and white wine to the pan.
Cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until the scallops are opaque and tender.
Remove from heat, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve immediately with pan juices.

title: Nova Scotia Oatcakes
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 350F (175C) and lightly grease a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, whisk together the oats, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut the cold butter and shortening into the dry mixture using a pastry blender until it resembles fine crumbs.
Gradually add the cold water, stirring just until the dough comes together.
Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface to about 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into squares or rounds using a biscuit cutter and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the edges are lightly browned, then cool on a wire rack.

title: Solomon Gundy (Pickled Herring)
ingredients: 1 lb salt herring fillets, soaked overnight in water and drained
instructions: Cut the soaked and drained herring fillets into bite-sized pieces.
In a medium saucepan, combine the vinegar, water, sugar, allspice berries, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes to meld the flavors; let the brine cool completely.
In a clean glass jar, layer the herring pieces and sliced onions alternately.
Pour the cooled spiced brine over the herring and onions, ensuring they are completely submerged.
Cover the jar tightly and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving.

title: Acadian Fricot
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and cook the chopped onion until translucent.
Add chicken pieces and brown lightly on all sides.
Pour in chicken broth, add salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Add cubed potatoes and chopped savory, simmering for another 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Mix flour and cold water together in a small bowl until smooth to create the slurry.
Drizzle the slurry slowly into the simmering pot, stirring constantly to thicken the broth.
Cook for an additional 5 minutes before serving hot.

title: New Brunswick Dulse and Potato Chowder
ingredients: 3 cups fish stock or chicken broth
instructions: Cook diced bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat until crisp, then remove bacon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
Add onion and celery to the bacon fat and sauté until tender.
Add potatoes and fish stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are fork-tender.
Pour in the whole milk and heavy cream, heating through gently without letting it boil.
Stir in the chopped dulse, salt, and white pepper, simmering for 5 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with the reserved crispy bacon.

title: Poutine Rapée
instructions: Grate the raw russet potatoes using a fine cheesecloth or potato ricer to extract as much liquid as possible.
Combine the grated raw potato starch with the cooked riced potatoes, salt, and pepper, kneading gently to form a dough.
In a skillet, fry the diced salt pork and chopped onion until the pork is crisp and onions are browned.
Take a portion of the potato dough, flatten it in your hand, place a spoonful of the pork mixture in the center, and wrap the dough around it to form a smooth ball.
Repeat for all dumplings.
Drop the dumplings gently into a large pot of boiling salted water, cover, and simmer gently for at least 2.5 hours until cooked through and translucent.

title: Acadian Meat Pie (Pêté de Viande)
ingredients: Double pie crust for a 9-inch deep dish pie
instructions: Combine ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, water, salt, cloves, cinnamon, and pepper in a large saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat with a wooden spoon.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally until most liquid is absorbed.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch deep dish pie plate with one pastry crust.
Spoon the cooked meat mixture into the crust and level it out.
Cover with the top pie crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg.
Bake for 45 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.

title: Solomon Gundy (Pickled Herring)
ingredients: 2 fillets of salted herring, soaked in water overnight and drained
instructions: Cut the soaked and drained herring fillets into bite-sized pieces.
In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, pickling spices, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Bring the pickling liquid to a boil, stirring until the sugar completely dissolves, then remove from heat and let it cool to room temperature.
In a clean glass jar, layer the herring pieces and sliced red onion.
Pour the cooled pickling liquid and spices over the herring and onions until completely submerged.
Seal the jar tightly and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Winnipeg Goldeye with Lemon Butter
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place the smoked goldeye fillets on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together the melted butter, lemon juice, dill, and black pepper.
Brush half of the lemon butter mixture over the fillets.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until heated through.
Drizzle the remaining lemon butter over the fish before serving.

title: Classic Manitoba Perogies with Fried Onions and Bacon
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: In a large bowl, mix flour, salt, egg, and water to form a soft dough, then knead for 5 minutes and let rest.
Boil potatoes until tender, mash them, and mix with grated cheddar, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out dough, cut into circles, place filling in the center, fold, and pinch edges to seal.
Boil perogies in salted water until they float, then remove with a slotted spoon.
In a large skillet, fry the diced bacon until crisp, remove bacon, and cook sliced onions in the bacon fat until caramelized.
Toss the boiled perogies in the pan with onions and bacon, and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Bannock
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the shortening using your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the water or milk and stir gently just until a soft dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead gently a few times.
Pat the dough into a round 1-inch thick disc and place in a greased cast-iron skillet.
Bake at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: In a large pot, bring broth and water to a boil, then add potatoes and cabbage, simmering for 15 minutes.
In a separate skillet, sauté the onion, carrot, and grated beets in a little oil until softened.
Stir the tomato paste and minced garlic into the vegetable mixture and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add the sautéed vegetables to the pot with the potatoes and cabbage.
Stir in the white vinegar to preserve the bright red color and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Serve hot garnished with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
In a large bowl, toss the Saskatoon berries with sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and cinnamon.
Fit one pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Pour the berry mixture into the crust and dot with the small pieces of butter.
Cover with the top crust, flute the edges, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake for another 30 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Classic Alberta Steakhouse Ribeye
ingredients: 2 Alberta beef ribeye steaks, about 1 inch thick
Coarse sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Pat the ribeye steaks completely dry with paper towels.
Season both sides generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Add the steaks and sear for 3 minutes without moving them to develop a deep crust.
Flip the steaks, then add the butter, garlic, and rosemary to the pan.
Spoon the melted foaming butter continuously over the steaks for another 2 minutes for medium-rare.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Traditional Prairie Perogies and Farmer Sausage
ingredients: 1 ring fresh Mennonite farmer sausage, sliced
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the perogies according to the package instructions until they float, then drain.
In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat and brown the farmer sausage slices until crispy, then remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining butter and sliced onions, caramelizing them slowly until golden brown.
Add the boiled perogies to the onions and fry until lightly browned and crispy on the edges.
Serve the perogies and sausage hot, topped with caramelized onions and a large dollop of sour cream.

title: Bison Stew with Root Vegetables
ingredients: 2 lbs Alberta bison stew meat, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Toss the bison cubes in flour, salt, and pepper until well coated.
Heat canola oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the bison cubes on all sides, then remove.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until translucent.
Pour in the beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the bison to the pot, add the thyme, cover, and simmer on low for 1.5 hours.
Add the carrots, parsnips, and potatoes to the stew.
Simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the meat is melt-in-your-mouth soft.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 1 double pie crust, homemade or store-bought
4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with the bottom pie crust.
In a large bowl, gently toss the Saskatoon berries with sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and salt.
Pour the berry mixture into the prepared pie crust and dot the top with small pieces of butter.
Cover with the top crust, flute the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg.
Bake at 425 degrees F for 20 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for another 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbly.

title: Tourtiere (Alberta Prairie Style)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large skillet, cook the ground pork, ground beef, onion, and garlic over medium heat until the meat is fully browned.
Drain off any excess fat.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, sage, and beef broth, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in the mashed potatoes to bind the meat mixture together.
Line a pie plate with the bottom crust, add the meat filling, and cover with the top crust, sealing the edges and cutting vents.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the filling is hot.

title: West Coast Salmon Bake
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Place the salmon fillets on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Brush the melted butter over the top of each fillet.
Sprinkle the minced garlic, salt, pepper, and fresh dill evenly across the fish.
Arrange the lemon slices over the top of the salmon.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the salmon flakes easily with a fork.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt the first amount of butter, sugar, and cocoa powder in a double boiler.
Whisk in the egg and stir constantly until thickened, then remove from heat.
Stir in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and almonds.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking pan and chill.
Beat the second amount of butter, cream, custard powder, and icing sugar together until light and fluffy.
Spread the custard filling evenly over the chilled base and refrigerate again.
Melt the semi-sweet chocolate and remaining butter together, then spread smoothly over the custard layer.
Chill until set before cutting into small squares.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 2 tablespoons melted lard or vegetable oil
instructions: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Add the melted lard and warm water to the dry ingredients.
Stir gently until a soft dough forms, being careful not to overmix.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead gently for about one minute.
Pat the dough into a thick round disk about one inch thick.
Cook in a greased skillet over medium heat until golden brown on both sides, or bake in the oven at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 minutes.

title: Creamy Chanterelle Mushroom Toast
ingredients: 1 pound fresh wild chanterelle mushrooms, cleaned and sliced
4 thick slices of rustic sourdough bread
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced chanterelles and cook until their moisture releases and evaporates, about 5 minutes.
Add the shallots and garlic, sautéing until fragrant and the mushrooms are golden brown.
Reduce the heat to low, pour in the heavy cream, and simmer gently until thickened.
Stir in the fresh parsley, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Toast the sourdough slices until golden and crisp.
Spoon the creamy mushroom mixture generously over the warm toast and serve immediately.

title: Okanagan Fruit Cobbler
ingredients: 6 cups fresh peaches and cherries, pitted and sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit and grease an 8x8 inch baking dish.
Toss the sliced peaches and cherries with the granulated sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch, then transfer to the baking dish.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the cold butter using a pastry blender or your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk and vanilla extract just until a moist dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter over the top of the fruit filling.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until the fruit is bubbling and the topping is golden brown.

title: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 2 lbs salt beef, soaked overnight and drained
1 head green cabbage, cut into wedges
6 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
6 medium parsnips, peeled and cut into chunks
1 yellow turnip (rutabaga), peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Place the soaked salt beef in a large pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 1 hour.
Tie the yellow split peas in a clean cloth bag (a pudding cloth) and drop them into the pot with the beef.
Add the turnip and carrots to the pot, simmering for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes, parsnips, and cabbage wedges to the pot. Cook for another 20 to 25 minutes until all vegetables and the split peas are tender.
To make the doughboys, mix flour, baking powder, salt, melted butter, and water in a bowl to form a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough directly into the boiling broth, cover, and steam for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove the meat and vegetables to a warm platter, slice the beef, and serve immediately with the cooked split peas and doughboys.

title: Cod Gratin
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and grease a baking dish.
Poach the cod fillets in simmering water for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through. Drain well and flake into large pieces in the baking dish.
Melt 4 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour, salt, pepper, and dry mustard, cooking for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens and bubbles.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
Pour the cheese sauce evenly over the flaked cod.
Mix the breadcrumbs with 2 tbsp melted butter and Parmesan cheese, then sprinkle over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes until the top is golden brown and the sauce is bubbly.

title: Toutons with Molasses
ingredients: 1 loaf store-bought or homemade bread dough
1/4 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
1/2 cup dark molasses or corn syrup
instructions: Pinch off golf-ball sized pieces of bread dough.
Flatten each piece of dough with your hands into round patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat lard or oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the dough patties into the hot skillet and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.
Flip the toutons and fry the other side for another 3 minutes until cooked through and crispy.
Remove from the skillet and drain briefly on paper towels.
Serve hot, drizzled generously with dark molasses or butter and jam.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 1 lb salt cod, soaked in cold water overnight
1 lb hard tack salt beef biscuits (brewis)
1/4 lb salt pork, diced into small cubes
instructions: Drain the soaked salt cod, place in a pot of fresh water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes. Drain, flake, and keep warm.
In a separate pot, soak the hard tack biscuits in salted water for 1 hour, then boil for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain well and break into bite-sized pieces.
In a frying pan, fry the diced salt pork over medium heat until crispy, rendering the fat.
Add the chopped onions to the pork fat and cook until soft and golden.
Add the butter to the pan and let it melt into the pork and onion mixture to create scrunchions.
Combine the flaked cod and cooked brewis in a large serving bowl.
Pour the hot scrunchions and melted fat over the fish and brewis mixture, toss gently to combine, and serve hot.

title: Nose Bleed Soup
ingredients: 1 lb salt riblets or salt pork, cubed
instructions: Place the salt riblets and chopped onions in a large soup pot with 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes to the pot and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the flour and cold water until smooth to create a slurry.
Slowly pour the flour slurry into the boiling soup, stirring constantly to thicken the broth.
Season with salt and pepper, reduce heat, and simmer for another 5 minutes before serving hot in bowls.

title: Classic Quebec Tourtière
instructions: Combine pork, beef, onion, garlic, water, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, and pepper in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 1 hour, stirring occasionally until liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in the mashed potatoes to bind the meat mixture. Let cool completely.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pie crust, fill with the cooled meat mixture, and cover with the top crust.
Crimp the edges to seal and cut a few slits in the top crust for steam to escape.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown.

title: Traditional Poutine
ingredients: 4 large Russet potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Heat canola oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) and fry potatoes in batches for 5 minutes until soft but not browned. Remove and drain.
Raise oil temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and fry potatoes a second time until golden and crispy. Drain and season with salt.
To make the gravy, melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook for 2 minutes until golden.
Gradually whisk in beef broth and chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook until thickened.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture to thicken the gravy further, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Place hot fries in a bowl, top generously with fresh cheese curds, and ladle piping hot gravy over the top to melt the cheese.

title: Pouding Chômeur
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and grease an 8x8 inch baking dish.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl.
In a separate bowl, cream the butter and 3/4 cup sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Alternate adding the dry ingredients and the milk to the butter mixture, stirring just until combined.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared baking dish.
In a saucepan, heat the maple syrup and heavy cream until warm, then carefully pour the mixture over the top of the batter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the cake is golden and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

title: Grand-Pères dans le Sirop
instructions: Combine maple syrup, water, and 2 tablespoons of butter in a large wide saucepan or Dutch oven and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add the melted butter and milk to the dry ingredients, stirring gently with a fork just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough into the simmering maple syrup.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 to 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove the lid and serve the grand-pères warm in bowls, drizzled with the remaining maple syrup sauce.

title: Quebec Pea Soup (Soup aux Pois)
ingredients: 1 lb dry yellow whole field peas, rinsed and picked over
1 ham hock or 1 lb thick cut smoked salt pork
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the rinsed yellow peas in a large bowl, cover with cold water, and soak overnight. Drain.
In a large soup pot or Dutch oven, combine the soaked peas, 8 cups of fresh water, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until peas are tender and falling apart.
Remove the ham hock from the pot, pull the meat off the bone, chop it finely, and return the meat to the soup.
Discard the bone and bay leaves.
Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving hot with crusty bread.

title: Classic Ontario Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Whisk together the brown sugar, melted butter, eggs, vinegar, and vanilla until smooth.
Divide the raisins evenly among the thawed tart shells.
Pour the filling mixture into the tart shells, filling them about three-quarters full.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbly and set.
Cool completely in the pan before serving.

title: Traditional Peameal Bacon and Eggs
ingredients: 1 lb peameal bacon, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the peameal bacon slices and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and heated through.
Remove bacon from the skillet and keep warm.
Crack the eggs into the same skillet and fry to your desired doneness.
Serve the fried eggs alongside the peameal bacon and buttered white toast.

title: Ontario Apple Crisp
ingredients: 6 medium Honeycrisp apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and grease an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Toss the sliced apples with granulated sugar and cinnamon, then place them in the prepared baking dish.
In a medium bowl, combine the rolled oats, flour, brown sugar, melted butter, and chopped walnuts until crumbly.
Spread the oat topping evenly over the spiced apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the apples are tender and the topping is golden and crisp.
Serve warm, ideally with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

title: Ontario Corn Chowder
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the diced bacon in a large soup pot over medium heat until crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Sauté the diced onion and celery in the remaining bacon fat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, corn kernels, and chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the heavy cream and season with salt and pepper, heating through without boiling.
Garnish with the reserved crispy bacon before serving.

title: Perch Fry with Tartar Sauce
ingredients: 1 lb fresh Ontario yellow perch fillets
instructions: Pat the perch fillets completely dry with paper towels.
Set up a breading station with flour mixed with garlic powder and paprika in one bowl, the beaten egg in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each fillet in the flour, dip in the egg, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fillets for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.

title: Nova Scotia Lobster Rolls
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh lobster meat, cooked and roughly chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine mayonnaise, celery, lemon juice, dill, salt, and pepper.
Gently fold in the chopped lobster meat until well coated.
Brush the outside of each hot dog bun with melted butter.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and toast the buns on both sides until golden brown.
Stuff the toasted buns generously with the lobster mixture and serve immediately.

title: Acadian Rappie Pie
ingredients: 10 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and grated
1 whole chicken, about 4 lbs, boiled and meat removed
8 cups rich chicken broth, kept hot
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Place grated potatoes into a clean cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible, measuring the extracted liquid.
Replace the exact amount of extracted liquid with an equal amount of boiling hot chicken broth, pouring it over the dry potato pulp while stirring vigorously.
Sauté the chopped onion in butter until translucent.
Grease a large roasting pan and spread half of the potato mixture on the bottom.
Add a layer of shredded chicken and the cooked onions.
Cover with the remaining potato mixture and pour the remaining hot chicken broth over the top.
Bake uncovered for 2.5 to 3 hours until the top is golden brown and crisp.

title: Nova Scotia Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 russet potatoes, cut into thick fries
Tartar sauce and lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Soak cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Fry the potatoes in batches until cooked through but not browned, about 5 minutes; remove and drain.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and cold beer until a smooth batter forms.
Increase oil temperature to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Dip each haddock fillet into the batter, letting excess drip off, and carefully drop into the hot oil.
Fry fish for 4 to 6 minutes until golden brown and crispy; remove and drain on paper towels.
Flash fry the potatoes a second time until crispy and golden, then serve alongside the fish with tartar sauce and lemon.

title: Solomon Gundy
ingredients: 1 lb salted herring fillets, soaked overnight in cold water and drained
instructions: Cut the soaked and drained herring fillets into bite-sized pieces.
In a saucepan, combine vinegar, water, brown sugar, pickling spices, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool completely.
In a glass jar, layer the herring pieces and sliced onions.
Pour the cooled pickling liquid over the herring and onions, ensuring everything is submerged.
Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving with crackers and cream cheese.

title: Traditional Blueberry Grunt
instructions: In a deep skillet or Dutch oven, combine wild blueberries, sugar, water, and lemon juice.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until the berries release their juices.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt.
Stir in the melted butter and milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of the dumpling dough directly onto the simmering blueberries.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid and let it simmer without lifting the lid for 15 minutes, allowing the dumplings to steam.
Serve warm in bowls with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

title: Acadian Fricot
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the cubed pork and cook until browned on all sides.
Add potatoes, chicken broth, summer savory, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
In a small bowl, mix flour, baking powder, and cold water to form a soft dough for dumplings.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering stew.
Cover and cook without lifting the lid for 12 more minutes until dumplings are cooked through.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Acadian Plaies Râpées
ingredients: 5 large russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
instructions: Finely grate the raw potatoes using a potato grater or cheesecloth to extract as much liquid as possible, reserving the starch that settles.
Mash the boiled potatoes and mix them thoroughly with the grated raw potato and the saved starch.
Season the potato mixture with salt and pepper.
In a skillet, fry the salt pork and onion until the pork is crisp and onions are golden, reserving the rendered fat.
Flatten a handful of potato mixture in your hand, place a spoonful of salt pork and onions in the center, and wrap the potato around it to form a smooth ball.
Drop the balls carefully into a large pot of boiling salted water.
Simmer gently, covered, for 2.5 to 3 hours until the balls are firm and cooked through.
Serve hot with molasses or maple syrup.

title: Bay of Fundy Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb salted cod, soaked overnight and drained
4 medium russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork tender, then drain well.
In a separate pot, cover the soaked cod with fresh water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain and flake, removing any bones.
Mash the cooked potatoes with butter and heavy cream.
Combine the mashed potatoes, flaked cod, minced onion, parsley, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Stir in the beaten egg until the mixture holds together.
Form the mixture into small patties and dredge lightly in flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish cakes for 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with chow-chow or ketchup.

title: New Brunswick Dulse and Potato Chowder
ingredients: 3 cups fish stock or chicken broth
instructions: Rinse the dulse quickly in cold water to remove any grit, pat dry, and chop coarsely.
In a soup pot, cook the chopped bacon over medium heat until crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon leaving the fat in the pot.
Sauté the onion and celery in the bacon fat until soft.
Add the diced potatoes and fish stock, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Whisk the flour into the milk until smooth, then stir into the pot along with the heavy cream.
Add the chopped dulse and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the chowder thickens.
Season with black pepper and top with reserved crispy bacon before serving.

title: New Brunswick Sugar-Pie
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with the unbaked pie crust and set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the dark brown sugar and all-purpose flour.
Gradually pour in the heavy cream and whole milk, whisking constantly until smooth.
Stir in the vanilla extract.
Pour the liquid mixture into the prepared pie crust.
Dot the top of the filling with the small pieces of unsalted butter.
Bake at 425 degrees F for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for another 30 to 35 minutes until the filling is set and slightly jiggle in the center.
Cool completely before slicing to allow the filling to firm up.

title: Winnipeg Goldeye on Rye
ingredients: Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Flake the smoked goldeye fillets into bite-sized pieces, removing any small bones.
In a small bowl, mix the cream cheese, fresh dill, and lemon juice until smooth.
Spread the dill cream cheese evenly onto each slice of dark rye bread.
Layer the flaked goldeye and thinly sliced red onion over the cream cheese.
Top with freshly cracked black pepper and serve open-faced.

title: Traditional Manitoba Perogies
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then stir in the egg and lukewarm water to form a soft dough; knead until smooth and rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until tender, mash them, and mix with grated cheddar cheese, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or round cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Boil the perogies in salted water until they float, then pan-fry them in butter with diced onions until golden brown and serve with sour cream.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/4 cup lard or vegetable shortening, chilled
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F and grease a cast-iron skillet.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut the chilled lard into the dry mixture using your fingers or a pastry cutter until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the milk or water and stir gently just until a soft dough forms.
Pat the dough into the prepared skillet and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Pickerel Pan-Fry with Lemon Butter
instructions: Pat the pickerel fillets dry with paper towels.
In a shallow dish, combine the flour, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Dredge each fillet in the seasoned flour, shaking off any excess.
Heat the canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the fillets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then top with butter and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice before serving.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
1 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F.
In a bowl, gently toss the Saskatoon berries with sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with the bottom pastry crust and pour the berry mixture inside.
Dot the filling with small pieces of butter, then cover with the top crust, crimp the edges, and cut slits for venting.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg and bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 375 degrees F and bake for another 30 minutes until bubbling and golden.

title: Classic Alberta Steak with Garlic Butter
ingredients: 2 Alberta beef ribeye steaks, about 1 inch thick
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Pat the steaks dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Add the steaks to the skillet and sear for 4 minutes without moving them.
Flip the steaks and add the butter, minced garlic, and rosemary to the pan.
Baste the steaks continuously with the melted garlic butter for 2 to 3 minutes for medium-rare.
Remove the steaks from the skillet and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Perogies with Fried Onions and Bacon
ingredients: 1 package frozen potato and cheddar perogies
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the perogies according to the package directions until they float, then drain.
In a large skillet, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the butter and sliced onions to the bacon fat in the skillet and cook slowly over medium-low heat until caramelized and golden brown.
Add the boiled perogies to the onions and fry until golden and slightly crispy on both sides.
Toss the crispy bacon back into the skillet with the perogies.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream on the side.

title: Alberta Bison Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs stewing bison meat, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions: Toss the bison cubes in flour, salt, and pepper until well coated.
Heat the canola oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the bison cubes on all sides.
Remove the meat and set aside, then add the chopped onion and garlic to the pot, sautéing until translucent.
Pour in the beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot, and return the bison to the Dutch oven.
Add the thyme, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat begins to tenderize.
Add the carrots and potatoes, cover again, and cook for another 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
2 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large bowl, gently toss the Saskatoon berries with the granulated sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one of the pie crusts.
Pour the berry mixture into the crust and dot the top with the small pieces of butter.
Cover with the second pie crust, crimp the edges to seal, and cut a few slits in the top crust for steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes at 400 degrees F, then reduce the temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for another 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbly.

title: West Coast Salmon Bake
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Place salmon fillet on a parchment-lined baking sheet skin-side down.
Mix melted butter, minced garlic, salt, and pepper, then brush over the salmon.
Top the salmon with fresh dill and lemon slices.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 0.5 cup butter, sugar, and cocoa in a double boiler, then whisk in the egg until thick.
Stir in graham crumbs, coconut, and almonds, then press firmly into an 8x8 inch pan.
Beat heavy cream, custard powder, icing sugar, and remaining butter together until smooth, then spread over the base layer.
Chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter together, spread over the custard layer, and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: Bannock
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl.
Cut in the butter or lard until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add water or milk gradually and stir until a soft dough forms.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead gently for a minute.
Press into a round pan or skillet and bake at 400 degrees F for 25 minutes, or fry in hot oil until golden brown.

title: BC Spot Prawn Boil
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh BC spot prawns, whole
4 ears of corn, cut in half
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a large pot with Old Bay seasoning, garlic, and lemon quarters.
Add potatoes and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
Add corn and smoked sausage, and boil for another 5 minutes.
Drop in the fresh spot prawns and cook for just 2 to 3 minutes until they turn bright pink.
Drain excess liquid and dump everything onto a large table lined with parchment paper to serve family-style.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Mix Saskatoon berries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and almond extract together in a bowl.
Line a pie plate with one pie crust and pour the berry mixture inside.
Dot the filling with small cubes of butter and cover with the top crust, crimping the edges to seal and cutting vents.
Brush the top crust with beaten egg and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbly.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine all ingredients except the chicken in a food processor and blend until smooth.
Coat the chicken thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 40 minutes until fully cooked and slightly charred.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup pigeon peas, canned and drained
2 cups parboiled rice, washed and drained
instructions: Season chicken with green seasoning, salt, and pepper; marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and add brown sugar, stirring until it melts and turns dark brown.
Add the seasoned chicken immediately and stir well to coat with the caramelized sugar.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes until chicken releases its juices.
Add onion, garlic, sweet pepper, and carrots, cooking for another 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice, pigeon peas, coconut milk, water, and thyme sprig.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Place flank steak and water in a large pot, bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Remove steak from the pot and let cool slightly, then shred the meat using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic, sautéing until soft and translucent.
Add the shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, cumin, oregano, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the olives and serve hot over white rice.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
instructions: Marinate beef with lime juice, vinegar, garlic, green onions, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the squash cubes in a pot of water until very soft, then blend into a smooth purée and set aside.
Brown the marinated beef in a large pot with olive oil over medium heat.
Add water to the pot, bring to a boil, and add potatoes, carrots, celery, and thyme.
Cook for 20 minutes, then add the cabbage and rigatoni pasta.
Pour in the blended squash purée and stir well.
Add the whole scotch bonnet pepper on top for flavor without excess heat, and simmer for another 20 minutes before serving.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb fresh conch meat, cleaned and minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and finely minced
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, salt, and cajun seasoning.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk and beaten eggs, then stir into the dry ingredients until a thick batter forms.
Fold in the minced conch, bell pepper, onion, celery, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 365°F (185°C).
Drop rounded tablespoons of batter into the hot oil.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving with spicy mayo.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, soy sauce, vegetable oil, brown sugar, salt, and lime juice in a blender to form a smooth jerk paste.
Prick the chicken pieces with a fork and rub the jerk marinade thoroughly over all the chicken.
Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill for medium-high heat or oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Cook the chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 45 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F and the meat is charred and cooked through.
Remove from heat, let rest for 10 minutes, and serve warm.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces

Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and add the brown sugar.
Allow the sugar to melt and turn a dark, foamy amber color without burning.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the pot and stir well to coat the pieces in the caramelized sugar until browned.
Stir in the onions, sweet pepper, carrot, and thyme, cooking for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and pigeon peas, stirring to combine with the chicken and vegetables.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover the pot tightly and let simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters

Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per batch, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving with spicy dipping sauce.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja

Remove the beef from the pot and use two forks to shred the meat into thin strips.

Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30 minutes so the flavors meld.

Simmer uncovered on low heat for 20 minutes to let the flavors blend.
Stir in the sliced olives and serve hot with white rice and black beans.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Marinate the beef cubes in lime juice, garlic, shallots, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the calabaza squash in a pot of water until tender, about 20 minutes, then puree the squash in a blender with some of the cooking water and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Add water to cover the beef, bring to a boil, and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes, carrots, turnip, and cabbage to the pot and cook until slightly tender.
Stir in the pureed squash, butter, pasta, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Simmer for another 15 minutes until the pasta is cooked through, remove the scotch bonnet pepper before serving.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 cup conch meat, cleaned and finely minced
1 small scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, Creole seasoning, and salt.
Stir in the minced conch meat, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, onion, celery, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper.
In a separate small bowl, combine the beaten egg and milk, then pour into the dry mixture, stirring just until a thick batter forms.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Drop rounded tablespoons of the batter into the hot oil in batches.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve warm with a dipping sauce.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, vegetable oil, brown sugar, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper in a food processor and blend until smooth.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 40 minutes until cooked through and nicely charred.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup pigeon peas, canned and drained
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, garlic, and green seasoning, and let marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot, add brown sugar, and let it melt and froth until dark brown.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the caramelized sugar and stir well to coat.
Cover and let the chicken cook in its own juices for 10 minutes.
Add onion, sweet pepper, carrots, pigeon peas, and rice, stirring to combine.
Pour in coconut milk, water, and add the thyme sprig and whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove from heat, discard the pepper and thyme, and fluff before serving.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Place flank steak in a large pot with water, bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Remove steak from the pot and let cool slightly before shredding it using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, and sauté onions, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper until soft.
Add garlic, cumin, oregano, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, bay leaves, salt, and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Stir in sliced olives, remove bay leaves, and serve hot over white rice.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 cups calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Marinate beef in sour orange juice, garlic, and salt for at least 2 hours.
Boil the calabaza squash in salted water until very tender, then puree the squash with the cooking water and set aside.
In a large pot, brown the marinated beef in butter with the onion, celery, parsley, and thyme.
Add water to the pot and simmer the beef until partially tender.
Add the potatoes, carrots, cabbage, and the scotch bonnet pepper, cooking until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the squash puree and the rigatoni pasta, cooking for another 10 minutes until pasta is done.
Remove the scotch bonnet pepper and serve hot.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb fresh conch meat, cleaned and minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, black pepper, paprika, and thyme.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg and milk together, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined to form a batter.
Fold the minced conch, onion, green bell pepper, celery, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper into the batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 350 degrees F.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve warm with a spicy dipping sauce.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, vegetable oil, brown sugar, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a food processor and blend until smooth.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 40 minutes until cooked through and nicely charred.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 1 lb dasheen leaves, washed and chopped
2 tbsp salted pigtail, diced and boiled
instructions: Boil the salted pigtail pieces in water for 15 minutes to remove excess salt, then drain.
In a large pot, combine dasheen leaves, spinach, okra, onion, garlic, pigtail, and vegetable broth.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the greens are tender.
Add the whole hot pepper and pour in the coconut milk.
Simmer for another 15 minutes, remove the hot pepper, and blend or whisk the mixture until smooth before serving.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place flank steak in a large pot, cover with water, bring to a boil, and simmer until tender, about 2 hours. Remove and shred the meat.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic; sauté until soft.
Add the shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, cumin, oregano, and bay leaves to the skillet.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 30 minutes until the flavors are well blended and the sauce has thickened.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
instructions: In a medium pot, combine coconut milk, water, red kidney beans, garlic, green onion, ginger, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes to infuse the flavors.
Add the rinsed rice, butter, and salt to the pot, stirring gently.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove from heat, discard the ginger, green onion, and scotch bonnet pepper, and fluff with a fork.

title: Puerto Rican Mofongo
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium heat.
Fry the green plantains in batches until golden and tender inside, but not browned, about 10 minutes.
Remove plantains and drain on paper towels.
In a wooden mortar, mash the warm plantains with minced garlic, crumbled bacon, olive oil, and a splash of chicken broth until well combined and molded.
Shape into dome-shaped balls and serve warm with extra broth or meat.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, vegetable oil, brown sugar, and salt in a blender and blend until smooth.
Score the chicken pieces with a knife and place them in a large bowl.
Pour the jerk marinade over the chicken, ensuring it is well coated, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 40 minutes until fully cooked and slightly charred.

title: Trinidadian Roti with Curry Chicken
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the chicken with half of the curry powder, salt, black pepper, and garlic; let marinate for 30 minutes.
