Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and add the remaining curry powder, cumin, and turmeric until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add onion, tomatoes, potatoes, and water to the pot, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until potatoes are tender and sauce is thick.
Warm the paratha roti skins on a hot griddle according to package instructions.
Serve the curry chicken wrapped inside the warm roti.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place flank steak in a large pot with water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until tender, about 1.5 hours.
Remove steak, let cool slightly, and shred the meat using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onion, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper until soft.
Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cooking for 1 more minute.
Add shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, bay leaves, and beef broth to the skillet.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the sauce is reduced and flavors are blended.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot with white rice.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 1/2 cup pumpkin puree or fresh calabaza squash
instructions: Marinate beef cubes with lime juice, garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
In a large pot, heat vegetable oil and brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Add water to cover the beef and bring to a boil, then simmer until the meat is tender.
Add the pumpkin puree or squash, stirring well to thicken the broth.
Add carrots, potatoes, and cabbage, cooking for another 15 minutes.
Add the rigatoni pasta and the whole scotch bonnet pepper (do not burst it).
Simmer until pasta and vegetables are cooked through, remove the pepper, and serve hot.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cleaned and finely minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and finely minced
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and cayenne pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk the milk and egg, then stir into the dry ingredients until a thick batter forms.
Fold the minced conch, green bell pepper, onion, celery, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper into the batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 365 degrees F.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with hot sauce or remoulade.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, garlic, ginger, allspice, cinnamon, brown sugar, soy sauce, vegetable oil, and lime juice in a blender; blend until smooth.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill for medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 30 to 40 minutes until cooked through and nicely charred.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 cups parboiled rice, washed and drained
1 can pigeon peas, rinsed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken with salt, black pepper, and garlic; set aside.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat, add brown sugar, and let it melt and foam until it turns dark brown.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken and stir well to coat with the caramelized sugar.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes until chicken releases its juices.
Add onion, bell pepper, tomato paste, pigeon peas, and rice; stir continuously for 3 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth, add thyme and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is cooked.
Remove scotch bonnet pepper, fluff rice, and serve warm.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Place flank steak in a large pot, cover with water, and boil for about 1.5 hours until tender; drain and shred the meat using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and bell peppers, cooking until softened.
Stir in garlic, cumin, oregano, and cook for 1 minute.
Add shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, and bay leaves.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in sliced olives, season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaves, and serve.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into cubes
1 small calabaza squash or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Marinate beef cubes with lime juice, half of the epis, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the squash cubes in a pot of water until tender, then blend into a smooth puree and set aside.
In a large pot with olive oil, brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Add water, onions, garlic, remaining epis, carrots, potatoes, and celery; simmer until beef is tender.
Add the cabbage, rigatoni pasta, and the squash puree to the pot.
Drop in the whole scotch bonnet pepper and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Remove the scotch bonnet pepper carefully, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb fresh conch meat, cleaned and minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, cajun seasoning, egg, and milk to form a batter.
Fold in the minced conch, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, onion, celery, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil.
Fry for 3 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with a spicy dipping sauce.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 3 tablespoons scotch bonnet peppers, finely chopped
instructions: Combine all ingredients except the chicken in a food processor and blend into a smooth paste.
Make deep cuts in the chicken pieces to allow the marinade to penetrate.
Coat the chicken thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally and basting with remaining marinade, for 35 to 45 minutes until fully cooked and charred.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup pigeon peas, canned and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, salt, and pepper, and let marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add brown sugar and let it melt and caramelize until it turns dark brown and frothy.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken and stir well to coat in the caramel.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes until chicken releases its juices.
Add onion, garlic, bell pepper, celery, pigeon peas, and rice, stirring to combine.
Pour in coconut milk, water, add thyme, and place the whole scotch bonnet pepper on top.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
instructions: Place flank steak and water in a large pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Remove the beef and let it cool slightly, then shred it using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and bell peppers, cooking until soft and lightly browned.
Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in shredded beef, tomato sauce, and red wine.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes to let flavors meld.
Stir in capers and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into cubes
3 lbs calabaza squash or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
3 cups rigatoni or other short pasta
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the beef with lime juice, epis, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the squash cubes in a large pot of water until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Blend the cooked squash with some of its cooking water until smooth to create the soup base.
In a large soup pot, heat olive oil and brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Add water, potatoes, carrots, celery, and onions, bringing to a boil.
Pour in the blended squash soup base and stir well.
Add cabbage, pasta, and the whole scotch bonnet peppers.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 45 minutes until vegetables and beef are tender.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb fresh conch meat, cleaned and finely minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and finely minced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, black pepper, and creole seasoning.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg and milk together.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients just until a thick batter forms.
Fold in the minced conch, bell peppers, onion, celery, scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of the batter carefully into the hot oil.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine all ingredients except the chicken in a food processor and blend until smooth to make the jerk marinade.
Score the chicken pieces with a knife to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply.
Rub the marinade generously over the chicken, ensuring all parts are covered.
Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat a grill for medium-high indirect heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally and basting with leftover marinade, for 40 to 50 minutes until fully cooked and charred.

title: Trinidadian Roti and Curry Chicken
instructions: Season the chicken with half of the curry powder, half of the garlic, and salt, then set aside for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add the remaining curry powder and a splash of water, stirring until it turns dark brown and fragrant.
Add the seasoned chicken to the pot and stir well to coat with the curry paste, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add onions, tomatoes, and remaining garlic, stirring until softened.
Add potatoes and water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and sauce is thick.
Serve hot alongside warm dhalpuri roti.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the flank steak in a large pot with beef broth, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the beef from the broth and shred it using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onions and bell peppers until soft.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and oregano, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the shredded beef, tomato sauce, and white wine to the skillet, stirring well.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes to let the flavors meld, seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 3 lbs pumpkin or calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Marinate the beef with lime juice, garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the pumpkin cubes in water until tender, then blend the cooked pumpkin into a smooth puree and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown the marinated beef on all sides.
Add water to the pot along with celery, carrots, and potatoes, and simmer until the beef is tender.
Stir in the pumpkin puree, cabbage, and rigatoni pasta.
Drop in the whole scotch bonnet pepper for flavor without bursting it, and simmer for another 20 minutes before serving.

title: Bahamian Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cleaned and finely minced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and Creole seasoning.
Stir in the minced conch, green bell pepper, celery, onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk and eggs, then pour into the dry mixture, stirring just until a thick batter forms.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy skillet to 365 degrees Fahrenheit.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, working in batches.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden brown and crispy, then drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Place all ingredients except the chicken into a food processor and blend until smooth to make the jerk marinade.
Pierce the chicken pieces with a fork and rub the marinade thoroughly over and under the skin.
Cover the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat your grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 35 to 45 minutes until cooked through and slightly charred.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 scotch bonnet pepper, whole and unpierced
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the garlic and green onions for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, water, kidney beans, thyme, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice and place the whole scotch bonnet pepper gently on top.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid, discard the scotch bonnet and green onions, fluff the rice with a fork, and serve.

title: Jamaican Beef Patties
instructions: Mix flour, 1 tsp curry powder, and salt in a bowl, then cut in the cold butter until crumbly.
Gradually add ice water to form a dough, shape into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
In a skillet, cook ground beef, onion, garlic, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper until meat is browned.
Stir in 1 tbsp curry powder, beef broth, and breadcrumbs, simmering until the mixture thickens, then cool.
Roll out the dough, cut circles, spoon filling into the center, fold over, seal edges with a fork, brush with egg wash, and bake at 400F for 25 minutes.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Place flank steak in a pot with water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 hours until tender, and shred the meat.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sauté onions and bell peppers until soft.
Add garlic, cumin, oregano, and salt, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, and olives.
Simmer covered on low heat for 30 minutes to let the flavors meld together before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Season chicken with green seasoning and salt, and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy pot, add brown sugar, and let it melt and caramelize until it foams and turns dark brown.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the caramelized sugar and stir well to coat and brown the meat.
Add rice, pigeon peas, onion, bell pepper, carrots, coconut milk, water, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine green onions, scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, brown sugar, soy sauce, vegetable oil, and lime juice in a blender; blend until smooth.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for 30 to 40 minutes until cooked through and nicely charred.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup pigeon peas, canned and drained
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, garlic, and green seasoning if available; let marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and add brown sugar.
Stir constantly until the sugar melts and turns a frothy dark amber color.
Quickly add the marinated chicken to the caramelized sugar, stirring well to coat evenly.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes until chicken releases its juices.
Add onion, bell pepper, carrots, and garlic; sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas and washed rice, mixing well to absorb flavors.
Pour in coconut milk, chicken broth, and add the sprig of thyme; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place flank steak in a large pot, cover with water, and boil for about 1.5 to 2 hours until tender and easy to shred.
Remove steak from the pot and use two forks to shred the meat into thin strips; set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and oregano, cooking for another minute.
Stir in the shredded beef, tomato sauce, dry white wine, and bay leaf.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes so the flavors meld.
Stir in the olives, season with salt and pepper to taste, and cook uncovered for 5 more minutes before serving.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 1/2 calabaza squash or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the cubed beef with lime juice, epis, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Boil the squash cubes in a pot of water until tender, about 20 minutes; drain and mash into a smooth puree.
In a large pot, brown the marinated beef on all sides over medium-high heat.
Add the beef broth, onion, garlic, celery, carrots, potatoes, parsley, and thyme to the pot; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the beef and vegetables are tender, about 45 minutes.
Stir in the mashed squash puree and add the whole scotch bonnet pepper on top for flavor without excess heat.
Simmer for another 15 minutes, remove the scotch bonnet pepper, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Puerto Rican Mofongo
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into 1-inch rounds
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium heat.
Fry the plantain rounds until golden and tender inside, but not crispy like chips; remove and drain.
In a separate skillet, cook the diced bacon until crisp, then remove and reserve the bacon fat.
In a wooden mortar (pilón), mash the warm fried plantains with minced garlic, a splash of warm chicken broth, a drizzle of olive oil, a spoonful of bacon fat, and pieces of crispy bacon.
Continue mashing and mixing until the ingredients form a cohesive, thick dough ball.
Shape the mofongo into a dome or cylinder and serve warm with additional broth or meat sauce.

title: Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 1 packet sazón with culantro and achiote
instructions: Heat the achiote oil in a caldero over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and cook until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, water, sazón, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and let simmer until the water is absorbed.
Cover the pot tightly, reduce heat to low, and cook for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Mofongo
ingredients: 4 tablespoons pork lard or vegetable oil
instructions: Peel the green plantains and cut them into 1-inch thick rounds.
Fry the plantain rounds in hot oil until golden and cooked through, but not browned.
Transfer the fried plantains to a wooden mortar (pilón).
Add the minced garlic, pork lard, and chicharrón to the mortar.
Pound and mash the mixture together while slowly adding warm chicken broth until well combined and pliable.
Shape the mixture into a dome and serve hot with broth or meat.

title: Pastelón de Plátano Maduro
instructions: Slice the ripe plantains lengthwise and fry them in olive oil until golden brown; set aside.
In a skillet, cook the ground beef with sofrito, tomato sauce, and salt until browned and cooked through.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and grease a baking dish.
Layer half of the fried plantains on the bottom of the baking dish.
Spread the cooked ground beef evenly over the plantains, then sprinkle with half of the cheese.
Top with the remaining plantains, pour the beaten eggs over the top, and cover with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Carne Guisada
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck roast, cut into bite-sized cubes
1/2 cup Spanish olives stuffed with pimentos
instructions: Season the beef cubes with adobo seasoning.
In a large pot, brown the beef on all sides over medium-high heat.
Stir in the sofrito and tomato paste, cooking for 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and add the bay leaves, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and olives, then simmer uncovered for another 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens.

title: Tembleque
instructions: In a medium saucepan, whisk together the coconut milk, cornstarch, sugar, and salt until smooth.
Place the saucepan over medium heat and stir constantly with a wooden spoon.
Cook until the mixture thickens and begins to bubble, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
Pour the pudding into a rinsed mold or individual ramekins.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until fully set, then dust with ground cinnamon before serving.

title: Griyo ak Pikliz
ingredients: 3 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Marinate pork chunks in lemon juice, garlic, scallions, salt, pepper, and sour orange juice for at least 4 hours.
Transfer pork and marinade to a pot, add water to cover, and boil until tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove pork from pot and let drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy skillet and fry the pork pieces until deep golden brown and crispy.
Prepare pikliz by mixing shredded cabbage, carrots, sliced onion, scotch bonnet pepper, and vinegar in a bowl.
Serve the crispy fried pork hot with the spicy pikliz on top.

title: Diri ak Pwa Nwa
ingredients: 1 cup dried black beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Boil soaked black beans in 4 cups of water with garlic, thyme, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper until tender.
Strain the beans, reserving the cooking liquid. Discard garlic and thyme, and set the pepper aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until translucent.
Add the reserved bean liquid and enough extra water to equal 3 cups of liquid, bringing it to a boil.
Add salt, butter, rice, and the cooked black beans to the pot.
Stir, place the reserved scotch bonnet pepper on top, cover, and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.

title: Tassot Kabrit
ingredients: 3 lbs goat meat, cut into pieces
instructions: Wash goat meat thoroughly with lime halves and rinse with cold water.
Season goat meat with garlic, scotch bonnet pepper, cloves, salt, and sour orange juice. Marinate for 3 hours.
Place goat and marinade in a pot with 2 cups of water, cover, and simmer until the meat is very tender.
Remove meat from the pot and let cool slightly.
Heat oil in a skillet and fry the goat pieces until crispy and browned on the outside.
Serve hot with fried plantains and pikliz.

title: Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs pumpkin or calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the pumpkin cubes in salted water until very tender, then puree the pumpkin in a blender with its cooking water.
Marinate beef with lime juice, epis, salt, and pepper.
Brown the marinated beef in a large pot with butter, then add water and simmer until the meat starts to soften.
Add onions, celery, carrots, potatoes, and cabbage to the pot and cook until vegetables are tender.
Add the rigatoni pasta and cook until al dente.
Pour in the pumpkin puree, stir well, simmer for another 15 minutes, and serve hot.

title: Mayi Moulen ak Pwa
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for two minutes.
Add water, red kidney beans, thyme, and salt, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Slowly pour in the yellow cornmeal while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook while stirring frequently with a wooden spoon until the cornmeal thickens and pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the butter just before serving warm.

title: La Bandera Dominicana
ingredients: 1 lb red kidney beans, cooked with broth
instructions: Season the chicken with adobo, oregano, and garlic, then let it marinate for 30 minutes.
Brown the chicken in a large pot with a little oil, adding drops of water to create a rich brown sauce (caramelo), then simmer until tender.
In a separate pot, boil water with oil and salt, add the white rice, cover, and cook on low heat until fluffy.
For the beans, sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic, add the tomato paste, cooked beans with their broth, and cilantro, then simmer until thickened.
Serve the rice, beans, and chicken together on a plate, traditionally accompanied by fried green plantains and a simple green salad.

title: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
1/2 cup cold water or warm milk
instructions: Boil the green plantain chunks in salted water until fork-tender, about 20 minutes.
While plantains boil, marinate the sliced red onion in white vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Drain the plantains, reserving some of the hot cooking water, and mash them thoroughly with the butter and cold water or milk until smooth.
Fry the salami and frying cheese in a skillet with a little oil until golden brown on both sides, then remove.
Fry the eggs in the same skillet to your liking.
Serve the warm mangú topped with the pickled onions, alongside the fried salami, cheese, and eggs.

title: Sancocho de Siete Carnes
ingredients: 1 lb pork ribs, cut into pieces
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Marinate the fresh meats (beef, pork, chicken) with garlic, sour orange juice, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, brown the marinated meats in a little oil, starting with the beef and pork.
Add water, onions, bell pepper, and the pumpkin (auyama) which will melt into the broth and thicken it.
Bring to a boil, then add the root vegetables (yuca, yautía, sweet potatoes) and green plantains.
Add the smoked pork chops and longaniza sausage, then simmer on medium-low until all meats and root vegetables are tender.
Stir in fresh cilantro just before serving hot in large bowls with a side of white rice and avocado.

title: Pollo Guisado
instructions: Season the chicken with adobo, oregano, and minced garlic, allowing it to marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and add the sugar, stirring constantly until it turns a deep amber caramel color.
Quickly add the chicken pieces to the pot, browning them on all sides in the caramel.
Add onions, bell peppers, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, and chicken broth, stirring well.
Drop in the whole Scotch bonnet pepper for flavor without too much heat, cover, and simmer on low for 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is rich.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot over white rice or moro de habichuelas.

title: Locrio de Puerco
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into small bite-sized cubes
instructions: Season the pork cubes with adobo, oregano, and garlic.
Heat oil in a heavy pot, add sugar to caramelize, then add the seasoned pork and brown well on all sides.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and tomato paste, stirring for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, and let simmer for 15 minutes until the pork begins to soften.
Add the rinsed rice and chopped cilantro to the pot, stirring gently, and cook uncovered until the water is mostly absorbed.
Cover the pot with a tight lid, reduce heat to the lowest setting, and let the rice steam for 20 minutes until fluffy and cooked through.

title: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
ingredients: 4 fresh flying fish, filleted and cleaned
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season flying fish fillets with lime juice, Bajan seasoning, salt, and pepper; set aside.
In a saucepan, boil the sliced okra in water with a pinch of salt until tender.
Whisk the cornmeal with a little cold water to form a smooth paste.
Reduce heat under the okra water, pour in the cornmeal paste slowly while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook the cou-cou on medium-low heat, stirring frequently with a wooden spurtle until thick and smooth, then stir in butter.
In a separate skillet, sauté onion and sweet pepper, add tomato sauce, and simmer the seasoned flying fish gently until cooked through.
Serve the flying fish and its sauce hot over a mound of cou-cou.

title: Bajan Macaroni Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and grease a baking dish with butter.
Cook the macaroni in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain.
In a large bowl, mix together most of the grated cheddar cheese, grated onion, mustard, ketchup, hot pepper sauce, and evaporated milk.
Add the cooked macaroni to the cheese mixture and stir well to combine.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Top with the remaining cheese and a sprinkle of breadcrumbs.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and bubbling.

title: Bajan Salt Fish Bul Jol
ingredients: 1 small hot pepper, seeded and finely minced
3 tbsp vegetable oil or olive oil
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water overnight, changing the water once or twice to remove excess salt.
Drain the fish, place it in a pot of fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes to finish desalinating.
Drain again, let cool slightly, and flake the fish apart with a fork, checking carefully for any bones.
In a mixing bowl, combine the flaked fish with diced tomatoes, chopped onion, green onions, sweet pepper, and minced hot pepper.
Drizzle with vegetable oil and fresh lime juice.
Toss everything together gently and season with black pepper to taste.
Serve at room temperature with boiled ground provisions like yams or sweet potatoes.

title: Bajan Chicken Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, washed and cut
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and Bajan seasoning, then set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot and add the brown sugar, stirring until it melts and turns a dark froth (browning).
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the caramelized sugar and stir well to coat.
Cover and let the chicken brown in its own juices for about 10 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, sweet pepper, rice, and pigeon peas, stirring to combine all ingredients.
Pour in coconut milk, water, and add the fresh thyme and whole scotch bonnet pepper on top.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

title: Bahamian Crack Conch
instructions: Clean and tenderize the conch meat thoroughly, then cut into bite-sized strips.
In a bowl, whisk together the evaporated milk and egg.
In a separate dish, mix the flour, baking powder, seasoned salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip the conch pieces into the milk mixture, then dredge generously in the seasoned flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the conch pieces in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with lime wedges and Bahamian pigeon peas and rice.

title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients: 4 cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly grated
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cook the elbow macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
In a large bowl, combine the hot macaroni with the butter so it melts.
Stir in the diced onion, green bell pepper, and 3 cups of the grated cheddar cheese.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the evaporated milk, whole milk, beaten eggs, mustard, seasoned salt, and black pepper.
Pour the milk mixture into the macaroni and stir well to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish and top with the remaining 1 cup of cheddar cheese.
Sprinkle smoked paprika over the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and the top is golden brown and crusty.

title: Bahamian Boiled Fish
ingredients: 2 lbs grouper fillets, cut into large chunks
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, rendering the fat.
Add the sliced onion, celery, and green bell pepper to the pot and sauté until tender.
Pour in the water and add the quartered potatoes, lime juice, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook the potatoes until they start to soften.
Gently lay the grouper chunks and whole scotch bonnet peppers into the boiling broth.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for about 15 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in the butter right before removing from heat.
Serve hot in bowls, traditionally accompanied by homemade Johnny cake.

title: Bahamian Pigeon Peas and Rice
ingredients: 2 cups dried pigeon peas, soaked overnight and boiled until tender
1 small green bell pepper, finely diced
2 cups water or reserved pea liquid
instructions: Heat the cooking oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and fry the bacon until crisp.
Add the onion, celery, green bell pepper, and garlic to the pot, sautéing until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and fresh thyme, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Add the boiled pigeon peas and stir well to coat them in the aromatics.
Pour in the water or reserved pea liquid, then add the salt and black pepper, bringing the liquid to a boil.
Stir in the rinsed white rice and place the whole scotch bonnet pepper right on top without breaking it.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and let it simmer undisturbed for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat, discard the pepper, fluff the rice with a fork, and serve warm.

title: Bahamian Johnny Cake
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and grease an 8-inch round cake pan.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the melted butter and milk.
Using your hands or a wooden spoon, mix until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for about 2 to 3 minutes until smooth.
Shape the dough into a round loaf that fits your prepared baking pan.
Place the dough in the pan and prick the top multiple times with the tines of a fork.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Brush the top with melted butter immediately after removing from the oven, slice into wedges, and serve warm.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1/2 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and finely diced
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water overnight, or boil it in fresh water for 20 minutes to remove excess salt, then flake the fish and set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, scallion, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper, sautéing until fragrant and translucent.
Add the flaked saltfish, chopped tomato, and black pepper, stirring well to combine.
Gently fold in the drained ackee, taking care not to mash the lobes.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes until heated through, then serve hot.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 4 lbs chicken pieces, washed and patted dry
instructions: Place the scotch bonnet peppers, scallions, onion, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice berries, brown sugar, soy sauce, vegetable oil, and salt into a blender or food processor, and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Score the chicken pieces deeply with a knife to allow the marinade to penetrate.
Rub the jerk marinade all over the chicken, ensuring every piece is well coated.
Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and grill the chicken, turning occasionally and basting with remaining marinade, for 35 to 40 minutes until fully cooked and charred.

title: Trinidad Chicken Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, washed and cut
instructions: Season chicken with green seasoning, salt, onion, garlic, and pimento.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and add brown sugar, letting it melt and foam until it turns a dark amber color.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken and stir well to coat in the caramelized sugar, letting it brown for 5 minutes.
Add rice, pigeon peas, coconut milk, and water to the pot, stirring well.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

title: Trinidad Saltfish Bul Jol
instructions: Soak saltfish in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain and repeat to remove excess salt.
Flake the fish into small pieces, discarding any bones.
Heat coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, sweet peppers, tomatoes, and hot pepper until tender.
Add the flaked saltfish to the skillet and toss well to combine and heat through.
Garnish with chives and parsley before serving.

title: Geera Pork
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Season pork with half of the geera, garlic, onion, pimento, hot pepper, and salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the seasoned pork, searing until browned.
Add the remaining geera and curry powder, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to toast the spices.
Add water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 lb dasheen bush leaves (or spinach), washed and chopped
10 oz salted pigtail, boiled and chopped (optional)
instructions: Combine dasheen leaves, okra, onion, garlic, salted pigtail, and water in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the vegetables are very soft.
Add the coconut milk and whole hot pepper to the pot, stirring gently.
Use a wooden ladle or traditional swizzle stick to whisk the mixture until smooth and creamy.
Remove the hot pepper, season with salt to taste, and simmer for another 5 minutes before serving.

title: Doubles
ingredients: 2 cups yellow split peas, boiled until tender
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water to form a soft dough, then let rise for 2 hours.
Mash the boiled split peas and season with sauteed curry powder, garlic, and salt to make the channa filling.
Roll the dough into small balls, flatten into thin discs, and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden (these are the bara).
To serve, place two baras on paper, spoon warm channa in the middle, and top with chutney.

title: Ropa Vieja
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the flank steak in salted water until tender, about 1.5 hours, then let it cool and shred it.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté the onions and bell peppers until soft.
Add the minced garlic, cumin, and oregano, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the shredded beef, tomato sauce, and white wine.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Arroz Blanco y Frijoles Negros
ingredients: 1 lb dried black beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Cook the white rice with water, vegetable oil, and salt in a pot until fluffy and tender.
In a separate pot, cook the soaked black beans with fresh water, onion, green pepper, garlic, and bay leaf until tender.
Mash a small portion of the cooked beans and stir them back in to thicken the broth.
Add cumin, salt, and vinegar to the beans and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Serve the black beans hot over the white rice.

title: Tostones
ingredients: Mojo sauce for serving (garlic, lime juice, and olive oil)
instructions: Peel the green plantains and cut them into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the plantain pieces until golden on the outside but still firm inside, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove and flatten each piece using the bottom of a glass or a tostonera.
Dip the flattened plantains quickly in salted water, then fry again until crispy and golden. Serve with mojo sauce.

title: Yuca con Mojo
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh yuca (cassava), peeled and cut into chunks
1/4 cup sour orange juice (or fresh lime and orange juice mix)
instructions: Boil the yuca chunks in salted water until fork-tender and translucent, about 30 minutes, removing the fibrous core.
Drain the yuca well and place it on a serving platter.
In a small pan, warm the olive oil over low heat and gently sauté the minced garlic until fragrant but not browned.
Remove from heat and carefully whisk in the sour orange juice and a pinch of salt.
Pour the warm mojo sauce generously over the cooked yuca before serving.

title: Flan de Leche
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt the sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until golden brown, then pour it quickly into the bottom of a round baking mold, coating evenly.
In a large bowl, whisk together the sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, eggs, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour the custard mixture over the hardened caramel in the mold.
Place the mold inside a larger roasting pan filled with hot water to create a water bath, and bake for 50 minutes until set. Chill before serving.

title: Mofongo con Camarones
ingredients: 3 green plantains, peeled and cut into 1-inch rounds
4 tablespoons pork fat or canola oil
1 packet sazón with culantro and achiote
instructions: Fry plantain rounds in hot oil until golden and cooked through but not crisp.
Transfer plantains to a pilón, add half the minced garlic and a pinch of salt, and mash well. Form into balls or cylinders.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and sauté remaining garlic and shrimp until pink.
Add sazón and tomato sauce to the shrimp, simmering until sauce thickens.
Serve the shrimp over and alongside the mofongo.

title: Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) pigeon peas, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a caldero over medium heat and sauté sofrito and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Stir in sazón, water, and pigeon peas, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Add rinsed rice and stir gently. Cook until most of the water is absorbed.
Reduce heat to low, cover with a tight lid (or banana leaf and foil), and cook for 20 minutes without stirring.
Fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Carne Guisada
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season beef cubes with salt, pepper, and cumin.
Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat on all sides.
Add sofrito and tomato paste, stirring constantly for 3 minutes.
Pour in beef broth, add potatoes, carrots, and olives, and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and the sauce is rich.

title: Pastelón de Plátano Maduro
ingredients: 4 ripe yellow plantains, peeled and sliced lengthwise
Butter for greasing the baking dish
instructions: Fry plantain slices in oil until caramelized and soft, then drain on paper towels.
Cook ground beef in a skillet, adding sofrito, tomato sauce, sazón, and salt until cooked through.
Grease a baking dish and arrange a layer of fried plantains on the bottom.
Spread the cooked beef evenly over the plantains, then top with remaining plantains.
Pour beaten eggs over the top, cover with mozzarella cheese, and bake at 350°F for 25 minutes until golden and bubbly.

title: Asopao de Pollo
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in achiote oil in a large pot.
Add sofrito and cook for 3 minutes until aromatic.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then add the rice.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally so it stays soupy.
Stir in green peas, roasted pepper, and cilantro, simmering for 5 more minutes before serving.

title: Griyo ak Bannann Peze
ingredients: 3 lbs pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Wash the pork cubes thoroughly with lemon juice and water.
Season the pork with garlic, scallions, epis, salt, black pepper, and one habanero pepper.
Marinate the meat for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Place the marinated pork in a heavy pot with the sour orange juice and enough water to cover. Simmer on medium heat until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the pork from the liquid and set aside.
Peel and slice the green plantains into 1-inch rounds.
Fry the plantain rounds in hot oil until slightly golden, remove, flatten with a plantain press or bottom of a glass, dip briefly in salted water, and fry again until crispy.
In a separate pan or deep fryer, fry the boiled pork pieces until deeply browned and crispy on the outside.
Serve the griyo hot alongside the twice-fried plantains and pikliz.

title: Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs calabaza squash (joumou), peeled and cubed
1 cup rigatoni or other short pasta
instructions: Clean the beef with lime juice and water, then season with epis, salt, and pepper. Marinate for 1 hour.
In a large pot, boil the calabaza squash cubes in water until very tender. Remove the squash, blend it into a smooth puree, and set aside.
In the same pot or a Dutch oven, brown the seasoned beef and soup bones with a little oil.
Add water to the pot, bring to a boil, and add the onions, celery, carrots, and potatoes.
Simmer until the vegetables and meat are nearly tender.
Stir in the blended squash puree, cabbage, and pasta.
Simmer for another 15 minutes until the pasta is cooked and the soup thickens to a rich consistency.
Stir in the butter, adjust salt to taste, and serve hot.

title: Diri Pwa nwa (Haitian Black Beans and Rice)
ingredients: 1 cup dry black beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Boil the soaked black beans in fresh water until tender, about 45 minutes. Reserve the bean liquid.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Sauté half of the onions and garlic until fragrant.
Add the cooked black beans and their liquid to the pot, along with the cloves, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper (keep the pepper whole so it doesn't break open).
Bring to a boil, add salt, and let simmer for 10 minutes to build flavor.
Remove the scotch bonnet pepper and cloves.
Add the rinsed white rice to the bean mixture. The liquid should sit about an inch above the rice level; adjust with water if needed.
Cook uncovered over medium-high heat until the water evaporates.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and let steam for 20 minutes until the rice is fluffy.

title: Legim (Haitian Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1 small chayote squash, peeled and cubed
1 cup green beans, cut into pieces
instructions: Wash the beef with lime juice, season with epis, salt, and pepper, and cook with a little water until tender. Set aside.
In a large pot, boil the eggplant, chayote, carrots, and green beans in a small amount of water until soft enough to mash.
Mash the boiled vegetables together in the pot, leaving some texture.
In a separate pan, heat the vegetable oil and sauté the garlic and tomato paste for a minute.
Add the cooked beef, shredded cabbage, and chopped spinach to the pan, cooking until the greens are wilted.
Combine the meat and greens mixture with the mashed vegetables.
Simmer everything together on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally so the flavors meld.
Serve hot with white rice or cornmeal.

title: Pwason O Sòs (Haitian Fish in Creole Sauce)
ingredients: 2 whole red snapper, cleaned and scaled
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Clean the red snapper thoroughly with lime juice and water, then pat dry.
Make a few diagonal slashes on both sides of each fish. Season inside and out with epis, garlic, salt, and black pepper, and let marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the fish until golden brown and crispy on both sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, leave about 2 tablespoons of oil and sauté the onions, bell peppers, and tomatoes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and water to create a rich sauce.
Add the whole scotch bonnet pepper to the sauce and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently place the fried fish back into the sauce, spooning the sauce over the fish.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes so the fish absorbs the flavors. Serve hot with white rice or boiled plantains.

title: La Bandera Dominicana
ingredients: 2 cups dry red beans, soaked and boiled (or 2 cans red kidney beans)
instructions: Boil water with oil and salt, add rice, cover and cook on low until fluffy.
Sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic, add beans, water or broth, and simmer until thick.
Season meat with sofrito, oregano, and soy sauce, then brown in a pot.
Cover meat and simmer until tender, scraping the bottom for flavor.
Serve the rice, beans, and meat together on a plate, traditionally with a side of fried plantains.

title: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
ingredients: 1/2 cup warm milk or reserved boiling water
8 oz Dominican salami, sliced into rounds
8 oz white cheese for frying (queso de freír), sliced
instructions: Peel and cut green plantains into chunks, then boil in salted water until fork-tender.
Marinate sliced red onion with vinegar, a pinch of salt, and sugar.
Drain plantains, reserving some cooking water, and mash with butter, milk, and water until smooth.
Fry the salami and cheese in a skillet with a little oil until golden brown on both sides.
Fry or scramble the eggs.
Serve the warm mangú topped with the pickled onions, alongside the salami, cheese, and eggs.

title: Sancocho Dominicano
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into chunks
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Marinate all the meats with garlic, oregano, sour orange juice, and salt for at least one hour.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, brown the meats starting with pork and beef, then chicken.
Add water, onions, bell pepper, and bring to a boil.
Add the harder root vegetables first (yautía, yuca, auyama) and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the green and yellow plantains and cook until everything is tender and the broth is thickened.
Stir in cilantro and adjust salt, then serve hot with white rice and avocado.

title: Pollo Guisado
ingredients: 1 tbsp cane sugar or brown sugar
2 tbsp sour orange juice (or lime juice)
instructions: Clean chicken and season with garlic, oregano, soy sauce, sour orange juice, and salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and add sugar, stirring until it turns dark brown and caramelizes.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the caramel to brown it, stirring constantly.
Cover and let the chicken cook in its own juices for 10 minutes.
Add onion, bell pepper, tomato paste, chicken bouillon, water, and the whole Scotch bonnet pepper.
Cover and simmer on medium-low for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and a rich sauce forms.
Stir in cilantro and serve hot.

title: Locrio de Puerco
ingredients: 2 lbs pork chops or pork shoulder, cubed
instructions: Season pork with garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in a caldero (heavy pot) and add sugar to caramelize.
Brown the seasoned pork in the caramelized sugar until deep golden.
Add onion, bell pepper, Cubanan pepper, and tomato paste, stirring for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil, then add the washed rice and stir.
Cook uncovered over medium-high heat until the water evaporates.
Cover with a tight lid, reduce heat to low, and steam for 20 minutes until rice is cooked.

title: Bajan Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
ingredients: 4 salted flying fish or fresh flying fish fillets
instructions: Season fish with salt, lime juice, thyme, and pepper sauce, then steam or pan-fry until cooked.
Boil the sliced okra in water with a pinch of salt for about 10 minutes until tender.
Remove half the okra and set aside the okra water.
Whisk the cornmeal with a little cold water to form a smooth paste.
Lower the heat, pour the cornmeal paste into the boiling okra water, stirring constantly with a traditional cou-cou stick to prevent lumps.
Add the remaining okra and butter, stirring until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Serve the warm cou-cou alongside the steamed or fried flying fish.

title: Bajan Pudding and Souse
ingredients: 2 lbs pork trotters and head, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Mix grated sweet potatoes, breadcrumbs, onion, marjoram, salt, pepper, and blood if using.
Stuff the mixture into greased sausage casings or bake in a greased casserole dish until set and browned.
Boil the pork pieces in salted water until tender, then drain and let cool.
Prepare the souse liquor by combining water, lime juice, sliced cucumber, minced Scotch bonnet peppers, salt, and finely chopped onions.
Submerge the cooked pork pieces in the seasoned lime liquor and let pickle for at least an hour.
Serve slices of the sweet potato pudding alongside the cold pickled pork souse.

title: Bajan Macaroni Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and grease a baking dish.
Cook the elbow macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
In a large bowl, mix together the cooked macaroni, most of the grated cheese, grated onion, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, hot pepper sauce, and evaporated milk.
Season well with salt and black pepper and pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Top with the remaining grated cheese and a dusting of breadcrumbs.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and bubbly before slicing.

title: Bajan Salt Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 hot pepper (Scotch bonnet), seeded and finely minced
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water overnight, or boil it for 15 minutes to remove excess salt, then flake finely.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, diced onion, thyme, minced hot pepper, garlic, and flaked fish.
Gradually stir in the water to create a thick, drop-ready batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving hot with pepper sauce.

title: Authentic Bajan Chicken Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, seasoned with green seasoning and salt
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add the brown sugar and stir constantly until it melts and turns a dark, frothy brown.
Quickly add the seasoned chicken pieces and stir well to coat them evenly in the caramelized sugar.
Cover and let the chicken brown in its own juices for about 10 minutes.
Add the rice, pigeon peas, diced carrot, and sweet pepper, stirring to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

title: Bahamian Cracked Conch
ingredients: 4 large conch meat pieces, cleaned and tenderized
instructions: Pound the conch meat with a meat mallet until tender and about 1/4 inch thick.
Cut the conch into bite-sized strips.
Whisk together the beaten eggs and milk in a shallow bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour, seasoned salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Dip each piece of conch into the egg mixture, then dredge thoroughly in the seasoned flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 375 degrees F.
Fry the conch pieces in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve hot with lime wedges.

title: Bahamian Peas and Rice
ingredients: 2 cups pigeon peas, canned and rinsed (or fresh if in season)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, fry the diced bacon until crisp and render the fat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, and garlic to the bacon fat, sautéing until tender.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the pigeon peas, chicken broth, fresh thyme, and season with salt and pepper.
Bring the liquid to a boil, then stir in the rinsed rice.
Place the whole Scotch bonnet pepper on top of the rice without breaking it.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from heat, discard the Scotch bonnet pepper, fluff with a fork, stir in the butter, and serve.

title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients: 3 cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly grated
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cook the elbow macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth and thickened.
Stir in the sharp cheddar, processed cheese, yellow mustard, seasoned salt, black pepper, and nutmeg until melted and smooth.
Fold the cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce until well coated.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and sprinkle the top with paprika.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbly and golden brown on top.

title: Bahamian Boil Fish
ingredients: 2 lbs grouper fillets, cut into large chunks
4 large russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: In a large pot, bring 4 cups of water to a boil with the allspice berries and sliced onions.
Add the quartered potatoes and celery, cooking for about 10 minutes until they start to soften.
Gently add the grouper chunks, whole Scotch bonnet pepper, and salt to the pot.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish is flaky and cooked through.
Stir in the butter and fresh lime juice just before removing from heat.
Serve hot in bowls, traditionally accompanied by grits or Johnny cake.

title: Bahamian Johnny Cake
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F and grease an 8-inch round baking pan.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the melted butter and milk.
Stir gently with a wooden spoon or your hands until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for about 1 minute until smooth.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared baking pan.
Poke the top of the dough multiple times with the tines of a fork.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Slice into wedges and serve warm with butter.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water overnight, or boil it for 20 minutes to remove excess salt, then flake into small pieces.
Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, sweet pepper, scallions, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper until tender and fragrant.
Add the flaked saltfish and black pepper to the skillet, stirring well to combine.
Gently fold in the drained ackee and chopped tomatoes, being careful not to break up the ackee too much.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes until heated through, then remove the scotch bonnet pepper and serve hot.

title: Jamaican Brown Stew Chicken
ingredients: 3 lbs chicken pieces, washed and trimmed
instructions: Season chicken with browning sauce, soy sauce, salt, black pepper, and pimento. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed Dutch pot over medium-high heat.
Add brown sugar and let it melt and bubble until it turns dark brown and foams.
Add the seasoned chicken pieces to the pot, turning to brown on all sides.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, carrots, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Pour in the chicken broth, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.

title: Authentic Jamaican Oxtail
ingredients: 3 lbs oxtail, trimmed of excess fat
instructions: Season oxtail with browning sauce, Worcestershire sauce, salt, black pepper, and all-purpose seasoning. Marinate for at least 2 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pressure cooker or heavy Dutch pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the oxtail pieces on all sides, then remove excess oil if necessary.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, scallions, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper, sautéing until fragrant.
Add beef broth, cover, and cook on medium-low heat for 3 hours (or 45 minutes in a pressure cooker) until the meat is falling off the bone.
Add the butter beans and simmer uncovered for another 10 minutes until the gravy is rich and thick.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) gungo peas or red kidney beans, rinsed
instructions: In a medium pot, combine coconut milk, water, kidney beans, smashed garlic, scallion, thyme, and salt.
Bring the liquid to a rolling boil over medium-high heat and let it simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add the washed rice and butter to the pot, stirring gently.
Cook uncovered until the water level drops below the surface of the rice.
Cover the pot tightly with foil and a lid, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and steam for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve warm.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 3 lbs goat meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Season goat meat with 2 tablespoons of curry powder, salt, black pepper, and all-purpose seasoning. Marinate for at least 4 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch pot over medium heat.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of curry powder to the hot oil and let it 'burn' or toast for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the seasoned goat meat and sear until browned on all sides.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, thyme, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the cubed potatoes during the last 30 minutes of cooking until they are fork-tender and the sauce thickens.

title: Trinidad Chicken Pelau
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, washed and seasoned
instructions: Season chicken with green seasoning, salt, garlic, and onion, and let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and add brown sugar.
Allow the sugar to melt and bubble until it turns a deep amber foam (browning).
Quickly add the seasoned chicken to the pot and stir well to coat evenly, letting it brown for about 5 minutes.
Add the rice and pigeon peas, stirring to combine with the chicken.
Pour in the coconut milk, water, and drop in the pimento pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and let simmer for 25 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and rice is cooked.
Stir in the butter just before serving.

title: Saltfish Bul Jol
instructions: Rinse the saltfish thoroughly to remove excess surface salt.
Place saltfish in a pot of water, bring to a boil, and let boil for 10 minutes to remove salt.
Drain the water, repeat the boiling process once more if it is still very salty, then flake the fish and remove any bones.
In a mixing bowl, combine the flaked saltfish with chopped tomatoes, sliced onions, pimento peppers, and thyme.
Pour the extra virgin olive oil over the mixture and toss well.
Season with black pepper to taste.
Serve at room temperature with slices of cucumber, boiled green fig, or bake.

title: Trinidad Doubles
instructions: Mix yeast, sugar, and warm water, letting it sit until frothy.
Combine flour, baking powder, turmeric, and salt in a bowl, then add the yeast mixture to form a soft dough.
Knead lightly, coat with oil, cover, and let rise for 2 hours.
Pressure cook or boil the soaked channa with onion, garlic, and salt until very tender.
In a separate pan, heat oil, add curry powder and more garlic, and cook until fragrant.
Add the cooked channa and water, simmering until the sauce thickens and coats the chickpeas (curry channa).
Pinch off small pieces of dough, flatten into small rounds, and fry in hot oil for a few seconds on each side to make 'baras'.
To assemble, place two baras on paper, top with generous spoonfuls of curried channa, and add pepper sauce and cucumber chutney if desired.

title: Oildown (Breadfruit and Saltfish)
ingredients: 1 large ripe breadfruit, peeled and cut into chunks
1 bunch fresh spinach or dasheen leaves, washed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the prepared breadfruit and flaked saltfish at the bottom of a large, deep pot.
Add the onion, garlic, green seasoning, and butter or coconut oil.
Pour in the coconut milk and water.
Lay the spinach or dasheen leaves flat over the top of the ingredients to seal in the steam and flavor.
Cover the pot tightly and bring to a medium heat.
Let it cook for about 35 to 40 minutes, allowing the breadfruit to soften and the coconut milk to reduce into a rich, thick sauce.
Remove the lid, gently stir everything together so the sauce coats the breadfruit, and serve hot.

title: Bake and Saltfish
ingredients: 1/2 lb saltfish, boiled, cleaned, and flaked
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Gradually add lukewarm water and knead into a smooth, elastic dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Divide dough into balls, flatten them into discs, and fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides and puffed up (fried bake).
In a separate skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil and sauté the onion and sweet peppers until tender.
Add the flaked saltfish to the skillet and sauté for 5 minutes until heated through.
Cut the fried bakes in half and stuff them generously with the cooked saltfish.

title: Ropa Vieja
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the flank steak in salted water until tender, about 1.5 hours.
Let the meat cool, then shred it finely along the grain.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté the onions, bell peppers, and garlic until soft.
Add the shredded beef, tomato sauce, white wine, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 25 minutes until the flavors blend and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with white rice and fried sweet plantains.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 1 packet sazón with culantro and achiote
instructions: Season the chicken pieces generously with salt.
Heat olive oil in a large caldero or heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the onion, green bell pepper, and garlic until translucent.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cooking wine, sazón, and rice, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken broth and return the chicken pieces to the pot, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Gently fold in the green peas, cover for 5 more minutes, and fluff before serving.

title: Tostones
instructions: Peel the green plantains and slice them crosswise into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the plantain slices until golden on the outside but still firm inside, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Using a tostonera or the bottom of a glass, press each fried piece flat.
In a small bowl, mix the water, minced garlic, and salt.
Quickly dip the flattened plantains into the garlic water and return them to the hot oil.
Fry for another minute until crispy and golden, then drain and serve immediately.

title: Frijoles Negros
ingredients: 1 lb dry black beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked black beans and place them in a large pot with 6 cups of fresh water and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the beans are tender, about 1 hour.
In a separate small skillet, heat the olive oil and sauté the onion, green bell pepper, and garlic until soft (this is the sofrito).
Add a ladleful of the cooked beans to the sofrito, mash them slightly, and stir everything back into the main pot.
Add the cumin, oregano, salt, and vinegar to the beans.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 20 to 30 minutes until the broth thickens nicely.
Serve hot over white rice.

title: Flan de Leche
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt the 1 cup of sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly until it turns into a golden-brown caramel.
Carefully pour the hot caramel into a round baking mold, swirling to coat the bottom and sides evenly; let it set.
In a large bowl, whisk together the condensed milk, evaporated milk, eggs, vanilla extract, and pinch of salt until smooth.
Pour the custard mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into the caramel-lined mold.
Place the mold inside a larger roasting pan and fill the pan with hot water halfway up the sides of the mold (water bath).
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until the center is just set.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours before inverting onto a serving plate to serve.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes
3 green onions, white and green parts separated, chopped
instructions: Marinate the chicken cubes with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the Chinkiang vinegar, hoisin sauce, sugar, and water to create the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add the dried red chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry until the meat turns white and is nearly cooked through.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and white parts of the green onions, cooking for another minute.
Pour the sauce mixture into the wok and toss everything to coat the chicken evenly.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and green parts of the green onions.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp Sichuan doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
2 tbsp cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water)
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in a pot of boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the ground pork until cooked through.
Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans to the pork, stir-frying until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and half of the Sichuan peppercorn powder, cooking for 30 seconds.
Pour in the chicken stock, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Carefully slide the drained tofu cubes into the wok and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry gradually to thicken the sauce, stirring gently to avoid breaking the tofu.
Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with the remaining Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped green onions.

title: Classic Pork Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 1 package round gyoza or dumpling wrappers
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, minced napa cabbage, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper to the meat mixture, mixing vigorously in one direction until sticky.
Place a wrapper on your palm, add 1 tablespoon of filling to the center.
Dip your finger in water and moisten the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper in half and pleat the edges tightly to seal the dumpling securely.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, then drop the dumplings in batches.
Stir gently to prevent sticking and cook until they float to the top.
Add a cup of cold water to the pot, let it return to a boil, and cook for 2 more minutes.
Remove the dumplings with a slotted spoon and serve with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and vinegar.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, cooled and day-old
1/2 cup cooked char siu (Chinese BBQ pork), diced
1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and scramble the beaten eggs, breaking them into small pieces. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and turn the heat to high.
Add the diced carrots and green peas, stir-frying for 2 minutes until tender.
Add the diced char siu and chopped shrimp, tossing for 1 minute.
Add the cold day-old rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Stir-fry the rice mixture vigorously for 3 minutes until heated through.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and mix well.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Toss in the green onions, turn off the heat, and serve.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat them lightly with a fork.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently until they form large, soft curds. Remove the eggs from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the same wok over high heat.
Add the tomato wedges and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they begin to soften and release their juices.
Stir in the sugar, salt, and water, covering the wok for 1 minute to let the tomatoes break down into a rich sauce.
Return the cooked eggs to the wok, gently breaking them up to combine with the tomato sauce.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve warm over steamed white rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Marinate the chicken cubes with Shaoxing rice wine, light soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the black vinegar, hoisin sauce, sugar, and an extra teaspoon of soy sauce for the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add the dry red chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant and darkened.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and slightly browned.
Toss in the minced garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce mixture and toss everything to coat evenly.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and green parts of the scallions, then remove from heat and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang (broad bean chili paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil, add the tofu cubes, and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain carefully.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and brown the ground pork until crispy.
Add the doubanjiang and mashed fermented black beans, stir-frying until the oil turns a vibrant red.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, cooking until aromatic.
Pour in the chicken stock and light soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Gently slide in the blanched tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry gradually to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Garnish with Sichuan pepper powder and chopped scallions before serving hot.

title: Classic Pork Dumplings
ingredients: 2 cups napa cabbage, finely chopped and salted
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to form a dough, knead until smooth, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Squeeze excess moisture out of the salted napa cabbage using a clean towel.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and ginger.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt, mixing vigorously while slowly incorporating the chicken broth until paste-like.
Roll the dough into a long cylinder, cut into small equal pieces, and roll each piece into a thin circular wrapper.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper and pleat the edges to seal.
Cook dumplings in a large pot of boiling water, stirring gently, until they float and the skins are translucent.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce of black vinegar and soy sauce.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
ingredients: 3 ripe red tomatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly with chopsticks.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just soft and slightly runny. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the same wok and toss in the tomato wedges.
Stir-fry the tomatoes for 2 minutes until they begin to soften and release their juices.
Add sugar, salt, and water to the tomatoes, covering with a lid for 1 minute to create a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, gently breaking them up and mixing with the tomatoes.
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with chopped scallions before serving.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, day-old and chilled
1/2 cup cooked char siu (Chinese BBQ pork), diced
1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a hot wok, pour in the beaten eggs, scramble quickly, and break into small pieces. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the diced carrots and green peas for 2 minutes.
Add the diced char siu pork and chopped shrimp, tossing until heated through.
Add the chilled cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula over medium-high heat.
Drizzle light soy sauce and sprinkle salt over the rice, tossing continuously until grains are hot and well-coated.
Fold the cooked eggs and chopped scallions back into the fried rice.
Stir for another minute and serve immediately.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 4 dried red chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Marinate the diced chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and cornstarch in a small bowl to create the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add a little more oil and stir-fry the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the garlic, ginger, and white parts of the scallions, cooking for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok, pour in the sauce, and toss until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the peanuts and remaining green scallions, then serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into cubes
2 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat oil in a wok and brown the ground pork until cooked.
Add the doubanjiang, fermented black beans, garlic, and ginger, stir-frying until the oil turns bright red.
Pour in the chicken stock and soy sauce, bringing it to a gentle boil.
Add the tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce.
Garnish with chopped scallions and Sichuan peppercorn powder before serving.
