title: Classic Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt until well combined.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just soft and set. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the tomato wedges until they start to soften and release their juices.
Add the water, sugar, and salt, covering the wok for 2 minutes to let the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and gently toss everything together for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Sichuan Boiled Beef
instructions: Marinate the beef slices with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, egg white, and cornstarch for 20 minutes.
Boil the napa cabbage in water until tender, then place it at the bottom of a large serving bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok, fry the doubanjiang, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Slide the marinated beef slices into the simmering broth one by one, cooking for 2 minutes until just tender. Transfer beef and broth over the cabbage.
Top the beef with dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil until smoking hot, and pour it directly over the spices to sizzle. Garnish with cilantro.

title: Dim Sum Pork and Shrimp Shumai
ingredients: 1/4 lb shrimp, peeled and finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, minced shrimp, and shiitake mushrooms.
Add the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, and salt. Stir vigorously in one direction until the mixture becomes sticky.
Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of a wonton wrapper.
Gather the edges of the wrapper around the filling, pleating it gently to form an open-topped cylinder, and flatten the base.
Top each shumai with a small pinch of grated carrot for color.
Arrange the shumai in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment paper or cabbage leaves.
Steam over boiling water on high heat for 12 to 15 minutes until fully cooked, then serve with soy sauce or chili oil.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 4 dried red chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Marinate the diced chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water in a small bowl to create the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add a little more oil and flash-fry the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions, stirring for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok along with the peanuts and the sauce mixture.
Toss everything together until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients.
Garnish with the green parts of the scallions and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into bite-sized cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and cook the ground pork until browned.
Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans, stirring constantly until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic and ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Gently slide in the tofu cubes and let them simmer in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce, stirring very gently to avoid breaking the tofu.
Transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle generously with Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped scallions.

title: Classic Red Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse with warm water and drain.
Heat a dry wok over low heat, add the rock sugar, and stir until it melts and turns a golden caramel color.
Add the pork belly cubes to the wok and stir-fry until evenly coated with the caramel.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, ginger, scallions, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Remove the lid and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until thick and glossy.
Serve hot with steamed white rice.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just set (still slightly soft). Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until they begin to soften and release their juices.
Add sugar, salt, and water, cover the wok, and simmer for 2 minutes to create a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and toss gently with the tomatoes for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve warm over rice.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 1 cup diced cooked char siu (barbecue pork)
1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium heat, scramble the eggs until just cooked, and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok over high heat.
Add the diced char siu, shrimp, and peas and carrots, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Add the chilled cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Toss the rice continuously until heated through and grains are slightly toasted.
Stir in the scrambled eggs, light soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Mix in the chopped scallions, toss for another minute, and serve immediately.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, diced
4 dried red chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Marinate the chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix the vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and an extra teaspoon of soy sauce in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through, then remove from the wok.
In the same wok, add dried red chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the wok along with the roasted peanuts.
Pour the sauce into the wok and toss everything together until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients.
Stir in the green parts of the scallions and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into small cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and minced
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Gently blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok and cook the ground pork until browned.
Add the Doubanjiang, fermented black beans, garlic, and ginger, stir-frying until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Add the tofu cubes gently to the wok and simmer for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce.
Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped scallions.

title: Classic Pork Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 1 cup Napa cabbage, finely chopped and salted
instructions: Mix the flour and warm water to form a dough, knead until smooth, and rest for 30 minutes.
Squeeze excess moisture out of the salted Napa cabbage.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, cabbage, ginger, scallions, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt, mixing vigorously until sticky.
Roll the dough into a long cylinder, cut into small equal pieces, and roll each piece into a thin round wrapper.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper, fold in half, and pleat the edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the dumplings, and cook until they float and the wrappers are translucent, adding a cup of cold water once during boiling.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve with black vinegar.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until soft-set, then remove.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and stir-fry the tomatoes until they soften and release their juices.
Add sugar, salt, and water to the tomatoes, covering for 2 minutes to create a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and gently mix with the tomatoes.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve warm over steamed rice.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 2 tbsp chicken fat or vegetable oil
Chili dipping sauce and ginger-scallion sauce for serving
instructions: Stuff the chicken cavity with ginger, garlic, and scallions, then poach in a large pot of simmering water for 35 minutes until cooked.
Remove the chicken and immediately plunge it into an ice bath for 10 minutes, then drain and rub with sesame oil.
In a wok, heat chicken fat or oil, then sauté the minced garlic and ginger for the rice until fragrant.
Add the drained jasmine rice to the wok and toast for 2 minutes.
Transfer the rice to a rice cooker and use the warm chicken poaching liquid as the cooking liquid.
Slice the chicken and serve it alongside the cooked chicken rice and dipping sauces.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Marinate the chicken cubes with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the black vinegar, hoisin sauce, sugar, and an extra teaspoon of soy sauce to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Add dried red chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns, stirring until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and no longer pink.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, and white parts of the green onions, tossing for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Pour the prepared sauce into the wok and toss everything to coat evenly.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and remaining green onions, then remove from heat and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 tbsp Sichuan doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil, add the tofu cubes, and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain carefully.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the ground pork and stir-fry until browned and crispy.
Add the doubanjiang and mashed fermented black beans, stirring continuously until the oil turns a bright red color.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and soy sauce, then bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the blanched tofu cubes into the sauce and simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes so the flavors absorb.
Slowly pour in the cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce, stirring gently to avoid breaking the tofu.
Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with Sichuan pepper powder and sliced green onions.

title: Classic Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
ingredients: 1 tsp salt (for drawing out moisture from cabbage)
instructions: Place the chopped napa cabbage in a bowl, sprinkle with 1 tsp salt, and let sit for 15 minutes. Squeeze out as much excess water as possible using a clean towel.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, minced green onions, grated ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and Shaoxing wine. Stir vigorously in one direction until the mixture becomes sticky.
Add the squeezed cabbage to the pork mixture and mix well.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each dumpling wrapper. Wet the edges with water and fold to seal, pleating the edges tightly.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the dumplings in batches and stir gently so they don't stick to the bottom.
When the water returns to a boil and the dumplings float, add a cup of cold water. Repeat this boiling cycle one more time.
Remove the cooked dumplings with a slotted spoon and serve hot with a dipping sauce of black vinegar and soy sauce.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white rice, chilled and day-old
1/2 cup cooked char siu (Chinese BBQ pork), diced
1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium heat. Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble softly, breaking them into small pieces. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and turn the heat to high.
Add the diced char siu, shrimp, and peas and carrots, stir-frying for 2 minutes until hot.
Add the cold cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula, and toss continuously for 3 minutes until heated through.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and add the chopped green onions.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edge of the wok, and season with salt and white pepper.
Toss everything together for another minute until well combined and aromatic, then serve.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
ingredients: 3 medium ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
2 green onions, chopped (separated into white and green parts)
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat well until frothy.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and let them sit for a few seconds until the edges start to set. Gently push the eggs into soft curds, keeping them tender. Remove the eggs from the pan and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the same pan. Add the white parts of the green onions and sauté until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges to the pan and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they begin to soften and release their juices.
Stir in the ketchup, sugar, salt, and water, then cover the pan with a lid for 2 minutes to let the tomatoes break down into a rich sauce.
Return the cooked eggs to the wok along with their juices, gently breaking them up to mix with the tomato sauce.
Garnish with the remaining green onion greens and serve immediately over steamed white rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Marinate the diced chicken in soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix vinegar, hoisin sauce, and sugar in a small bowl to create the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add dried red chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger, and green onions, stirring until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the wok along with the peanuts and pour in the sauce.
Toss everything together until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients, then serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat oil in a wok and brown the ground pork until crispy.
Add doubanjiang, fermented black beans, garlic, and ginger, stir-frying until the oil turns bright red.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add the tofu cubes and simmer gently for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Mix cornstarch and water to create a slurry, then stir it into the wok to thicken the sauce.
Garnish with chopped green onions and Sichuan peppercorn powder before serving.

title: Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
instructions: Toss the minced napa cabbage with salt and let it sit for 10 minutes, then squeeze out all excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, drained cabbage, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil, mixing vigorously until sticky.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of a dumpling wrapper.
Wet the edges of the wrapper with water and fold it into half-moons, pleating the edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, drop the dumplings in, and cook until they float to the top and the wrappers are translucent.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and black vinegar.

title: Red Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 stalks green onion, cut into large pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Heat a dry wok over medium heat, add rock sugar, and stir until it melts and turns into a golden-brown caramel.
Carefully add the pork belly cubes to the caramel and stir until evenly coated.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, ginger, green onion, star anise, cinnamon stick, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Uncover and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick, then serve.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir Fry
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just soft; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and stir-fry the tomato wedges until they start to soften and release their juices.
Add sugar and water to the tomatoes, covering for 1 minute to create a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and gently mix with the tomatoes.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve warm over steamed rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken

title: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)

2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar for dipping
1 slice fresh ginger, julienned for dipping
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to form a dough, knead until smooth, and rest for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine ground pork, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and scallion.
Gently fold the chilled gelatin stock cubes into the pork filling.
Roll the dough into a long cylinder, cut into small pieces, and roll into thin wrappers.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper and pleat the edges to seal.
Steam the dumplings in a bamboo steamer over boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve hot with Chinese black vinegar and julienned ginger.

instructions: Blanch pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Heat a dry wok over medium heat and melt the rock sugar until it forms a amber caramel.

Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 60 minutes.
Uncover the wok and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice

Add the remaining oil to the wok and sauté the peas, carrots, diced char siu, and shrimp for 2 minutes.
Add the chilled cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Stir-fry the rice mixture vigorously until heated through.
Drizzle soy sauce and sprinkle salt evenly over the rice, tossing continuously.
Fold in the scrambled eggs and chopped green onions, then serve immediately.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Marinate the chicken cubes with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix the Chinkiang vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and an extra teaspoon of soy sauce in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add dried red chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns, stirring until fragrant and dark red.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry until completely cooked through.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions, tossing for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss everything until the liquid reduces and coats the chicken.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and remaining green scallion pieces, then remove from heat and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into small cubes
2 tbsp Sichuan doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil, add the tofu cubes and blanch for 2 minutes, then drain carefully.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the ground pork until crispy.
Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans, stirring constantly until the oil turns a bright red color.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, cooking until aromatic.
Pour in the chicken broth and soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Gently slide the blanched tofu cubes into the wok and let them simmer in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry gradually to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with Sichuan pepper powder and chopped green onions.

title: Classic Pork Dumplings
ingredients: 2 cups napa cabbage, finely chopped and salted
1/4 cup water for the filling mix
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to form a dough, knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Squeeze excess moisture completely out of the salted napa cabbage.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, squeezed cabbage, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt.
Gradually whip the 1/4 cup of water into the pork mixture in one direction until juicy and thick.
Roll the dough into a long cylinder, cut into equal pieces, and roll each piece into a thin circular wrapper.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper and pleat the edges to seal securely.
Boil the dumplings in a large pot of water for 6-8 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce of black vinegar and chili oil.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
ingredients: 3 ripe medium tomatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly until combined.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just soft and slightly runny, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and toss in the tomato wedges.
Stir-fry the tomatoes for 2 minutes until they start to soften and release their juices.
Add the sugar, salt, and water, covering the wok with a lid for 1 minute to break down the tomatoes into a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and gently fold them into the tomato sauce.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Hong Kong Style Soy Sauce Chow Mein
instructions: Boil the egg noodles for 2 minutes, drain thoroughly, and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
In a small bowl, whisk together light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large wok over high heat and stir-fry the bean sprouts and chives for 1 minute, then remove them.
Add the remaining oil to the hot wok and spread the drained noodles evenly.
Pan-fry the noodles undisturbed for 2 minutes to get slight charring, then flip and loosen them.
Pour the sauce mixture evenly over the noodles, tossing continuously until fully absorbed and heated through.
Toss the cooked bean sprouts and chives back into the noodles, mix well, and serve.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 4 dried red chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Marinate the diced chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, hoisin sauce, sugar, and a splash of water for the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry the chicken until cooked through, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add garlic, ginger, and white parts of the scallions, cooking for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok along with the roasted peanuts.
Pour the sauce mixture into the wok and toss everything until well coated and thickened.
Garnish with the remaining green scallions and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into cubes
2 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok and fry the ground pork until browned.
Add doubanjiang and fermented black beans, stir-frying until the oil turns red.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Add the drained tofu cubes and gently simmer for 5 minutes to absorb flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped scallions before serving.

title: Classic Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Pour in the eggs and gently scramble until just set and still soft, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the tomato wedges until they start to soften and release juices.
Add sugar, salt, and water, covering the wok for 2 minutes to let the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and mix gently with the tomatoes.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve warm over rice.

title: Beef Chow Mein
instructions: Boil the egg noodles according to package instructions, rinse with cold water, and drain well.
Marinate the sliced beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok and stir-fry the beef until browned, then remove.
In the same wok, stir-fry the garlic, cabbage, carrots, and bean sprouts until tender-crisp.
Add the cooked noodles and beef back into the wok.
Pour in oyster sauce and toss everything continuously over high heat until evenly combined and hot.
Serve immediately.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole fish (about 1.5 lbs, such as sea bass or flounder), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Pat the fish dry and place it on a heatproof ceramic plate.
Place ginger slices inside the cavity and on top of the fish.
Set the plate in a steamer basket over boiling water, cover, and steam on high heat for 10 minutes.
Remove the plate from the steamer and discard the old ginger and any accumulated liquid on the plate.
Arrange fresh scallion matchsticks and cilantro on top of the cooked fish.
Pour light soy sauce around the base of the fish.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan until smoking hot, then carefully pour it over the scallions and fish to sizzle, and serve.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Marinate the chicken cubes with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Mix Chinkiang vinegar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and an extra teaspoon of cornstarch in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add dried chili peppers and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry until the meat changes color and is almost cooked through.
Add garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions, stir-frying for another minute.
Pour in the prepared sauce and toss everything until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and green parts of the scallions, give it a final toss, and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully add the tofu cubes and blanch for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and cook the ground pork until browned and crispy.
Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans to the pork, stirring until the oil turns a vibrant red.
Add the minced garlic and ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Slide the blanched tofu gently into the wok and let it simmer for 3 to 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry gradually to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Garnish with Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped scallions before serving.

title: Classic Red Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in a pot of boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse with warm water and drain.
Heat a dry wok over low heat, add rock sugar and melt it until it turns a light amber caramel color.
Add the blanched pork belly cubes to the caramel and stir-fry until evenly coated.
Add ginger, garlic, scallions, star anise, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves, stirring for 1 minute.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce, stirring well.
Add hot water, bring to a boil, then cover, lower heat, and simmer for 60 minutes until the pork is tender.
Remove the lid and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
ingredients: 3 medium ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat until well combined.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and gently scramble until just soft and set, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the wok and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they start to soften and release their juices.
Add sugar, salt, and water, cover the wok, and simmer for 2 minutes until the tomatoes turn into a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, gently breaking them up and mixing them with the tomatoes.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Cantonese Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion
ingredients: 1 whole live whitefish (such as sea bass or flounder), about 1.5 lbs, cleaned and scaled
instructions: Pat the fish dry with paper towels and place it on a heatproof serving plate.
Scatter half of the julienned ginger and scallions inside the cavity and on top of the fish.
Set up a steamer with water and bring it to a rolling boil.
Place the plate with the fish into the steamer, cover tightly, and steam over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Remove the plate from the steamer and carefully drain any watery liquid accumulated on the plate.
Disgard the cooked ginger and scallions from the top, and replace them with fresh remaining julienned ginger and scallions.
Mix light soy sauce, sugar, and water, then pour the mixture around the base of the fish.
Heat the cooking oil in a small pan until smoking hot, then carefully drizzle the hot oil directly over the ginger and scallions to release their aroma, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Marinate the chicken with Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the Chinkiang vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, chicken broth, and cornstarch to create the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Toss in the garlic, ginger, and white parts of the green onions, stirring for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and cook until it thickens and coats the chicken.
Stir in the roasted peanuts and remaining green onions, then serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Gently blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the ground pork until cooked through.
Add the Doubanjiang, fermented black beans, garlic, and ginger, stir-frying until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Carefully slide the blanched tofu into the wok and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture gradually to thicken the sauce.
Garnish with Sichuan peppercorn powder and chopped green onions before serving.

title: Classic Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Whisk the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and a splash of water.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and pour in the eggs.
Stir gently to form soft curds, then remove the eggs from the wok while still slightly runny.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and stir-fry the tomato wedges until they soften and release their juices.
Sprinkle sugar and salt over the tomatoes to balance the acidity.
Return the cooked eggs to the wok and gently mix with the tomatoes.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Red Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
2 stalks green onion, cut into segments
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse with warm water and drain.
Heat a dry wok over low heat, add the rock sugar, and stir until it melts and turns a golden caramel color.
Add the pork belly cubes to the wok and stir to coat them evenly with the caramel.
Add the ginger, green onion, star anise, cinnamon stick, Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Remove the lid and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked char siu (barbecue pork), diced
1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and chopped
1/2 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium heat, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble quickly into small pieces, then remove.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and turn the heat to high.
Add the peas, carrots, diced char siu, and shrimp, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Add the chilled cooked rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Drizzle soy sauce over the rice and season with salt, tossing continuously for 3 minutes.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and mix well.
Stir in the green onions and serve immediately.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, cooled and day-old
1/2 cup Chinese BBQ pork (char siu), diced
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs until just set, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and stir-fry the shrimp and char siu for 1 minute.
Add the green peas and cooled rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula, and toss well for 3 minutes until heated through.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, breaking them into smaller pieces.
Season with salt and white pepper, garnish with chopped scallions, toss everything together, and serve hot.

title: Lion's Head Meatballs
ingredients: 4 cups napa cabbage, cut into large chunks
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the minced pork, water chestnut, scallions, ginger, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, salt, and cornstarch in one direction until sticky.
Form the meat mixture into four large, smooth meatballs.
Heat a little oil in a pot and lightly sear the meatballs on all sides until golden.
Add the chicken broth and bring to a simmer, then layer the napa cabbage around and under the meatballs.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour until the meatballs are tender and the broth is rich.

title: Crystal Sweet and Sour Spareribs
ingredients: 1 lb pork spareribs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork spareribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a pan, add ginger and scallions, then add the spareribs and sear until lightly browned.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, rock sugar, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 45 minutes until the ribs are tender.
Uncover and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until thick and glossy, then garnish with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Braised Duck with Salt and Soy
instructions: Blanch the duck pieces in boiling water for 5 minutes, then remove and drain.
Heat oil in a wok, add ginger, garlic, and star anise until fragrant.
Add the duck pieces and stir-fry for 3 minutes until the skin is lightly browned.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, and water, bringing it to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes, then turn up the heat to reduce the sauce before serving.

title: Jiangsu Stir-Fried Shredded Eel
ingredients: 1 lb eel fillets, cleaned and cut into thin strips
1/2 cup garlic chives, cut into sections
instructions: Marinate the eel strips with Shaoxing wine, salt, and cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Mix light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and 2 tablespoons of water in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok and quick-fry the eel strips until firm, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add remaining oil and stir-fry garlic, ginger, and bamboo shoots for 1 minute.
Return the eel to the wok, add garlic chives and the sauce mixture, toss quickly over high heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and serve immediately.

title: Dongpo Pork
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into large cubes
5 stalks scallions, cut into long sections
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then remove and rinse.
Line a heavy-bottomed clay pot or Dutch oven with the scallions and ginger slices.
Place the pork belly pieces skin-side down on top of the aromatics.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and add the rock sugar.
Bring to a boil, then cover with a tight lid, reduce heat to the lowest setting, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Flip the pork pieces skin-side up and simmer for another 30 minutes until tender.
Transfer to a steaming bowl, steam for an additional 30 minutes to achieve melt-in-your-mouth texture, and serve.

title: West Lake Water Shield Soup
instructions: Bring the chicken stock to a boil in a medium pot along with the ginger slices.
Add the shredded cooked ham to the boiling stock and let simmer for 2 minutes.
Gently stir in the rinsed water shield.
Season with salt and white pepper powder, being careful not to over-salt due to the ham.
Cook for another minute until the soup returns to a gentle boil.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot in individual bowls.

title: Longjing Shrimp
ingredients: 300g fresh river shrimp or medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Steep the Longjing tea leaves in 1/2 cup of hot water for 2 minutes, then strain and reserve both the tea liquid and 1 tsp of softened leaves.
Pat the peeled shrimp completely dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, gently mix the shrimp with egg white, cornstarch, and a pinch of salt until coated.
Heat cooking oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the shrimp, and stir-fry for just 30 seconds until they turn pink.
Splash in the Shaoxing wine and the reserved tea liquid along with the tea leaves.
Toss quickly for another 10 seconds and remove from heat immediately to serve.

title: Hangzhou Braised Duck with Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 1 small duck, about 2.5 lbs, chopped into bite-sized pieces
2 fresh winter bamboo shoots, peeled and sliced
instructions: Blanch the duck pieces in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a wok, add ginger, garlic, and duck pieces, stir-frying until the duck fat renders slightly.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce, stirring until the duck is evenly colored.
Add the sliced bamboo shoots, rock sugar, and water, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Cover the wok, reduce heat, and simmer for 45 minutes until the duck is tender.
Turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick, then serve.

title: Steamed Pork with Preserved Mustard Greens
ingredients: 500g pork belly, in a single piece
100g Meigan cai (Zhejiang preserved mustard greens), rinsed and soaked
instructions: Boil the pork belly piece in water for 15 minutes, remove, prick the skin with a fork, and brush with dark soy sauce.
Pan-fry the skin side in a little oil until blistered, then slice the pork thinly crosswise without cutting all the way through the bottom.
Squeeze excess water from the soaked preserved mustard greens and finely chop them.
Heat oil in a pan, sauté garlic, ginger, and the preserved greens, seasoning with light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Arrange the sliced pork belly in a deep bowl skin-side down, and top tightly with the cooked preserved greens.
Steam in a steamer over high heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the pork is extremely tender.
Invert the bowl onto a serving plate and serve hot.

title: Fujian Red Yeast Rice Wine Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, chopped into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Rinse the red yeast rice and soak it in the rice wine for 15 minutes.
Heat sesame oil in a wok and fry the ginger slices until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and stir-fry until the surface turns golden.
Pour in the red yeast rice, the soaking wine, and additional water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and the broth is deep red.
Season with salt before serving hot.

title: Fujian Oyster Omelet
ingredients: 300g fresh small oysters, rinsed and drained
Fujian sweet chili sauce for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix sweet potato starch, flour, water, and a pinch of salt to form a smooth batter.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat and scatter the oysters.
Pour the batter evenly over the oysters.
When the batter starts to turn translucent, pour the beaten eggs around and over the mixture.
Scatter chopped scallions on top, drizzle the remaining oil around the edges, and flip carefully once.
Cook for another minute, slide onto a plate, and serve with sweet chili sauce.

title: Lychee Pork
ingredients: 400g pork tenderloin, scored and cut into bite-sized pieces
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Marinate pork with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and egg white for 15 minutes.
Coat each piece of pork thoroughly in sweet potato starch.
Deep fry the pork pieces in hot oil until crispy and golden, then remove and drain.
In a separate pan, combine vinegar, sugar, ketchup, dark soy sauce, and water, bringing it to a simmer.
Add water chestnut pieces and thicken the sauce with the cornstarch mixture.
Toss the fried pork quickly into the hot sauce until well coated and serve immediately.

title: Fujian Taro Duck
instructions: Marinate the duck meat with soy sauce, oyster sauce, and five-spice powder.
Steam the taro slices until soft, then mash half and cut the rest into small cubes.
Layer the mashed and cubed taro over the duck pieces in a deep heatproof bowl.
Pour chicken broth over the taro and duck layer.
Steam the entire bowl over high heat for 45 minutes until flavors meld.
Invert onto a serving plate before serving warm.

title: Minnan Beef Soup
instructions: Blanch the beef brisket chunks in boiling water for 3 minutes, then remove and rinse.
Heat a clay pot with a little oil, and sauté ginger and shallots until aromatic.
Add the blanched beef, rice wine, and water to the pot.
Bring to a rolling boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the beef is tender.
Season with salt and light soy sauce to taste.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot in individual bowls.

title: Hunan Stir-Fried Pork with Chili Peppers
ingredients: 500g pork belly, boiled and sliced thin
10 large green finger chilies, sliced diagonally
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 10 minutes, then slice thinly once cooled.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and add the pork slices, stir-frying until the fat renders and edges are slightly browned.
Push pork to the side, and add garlic, ginger, and fermented black beans to the oil until fragrant.
Add the chili paste and toss everything together to coat the pork.
Add the sliced green chilies, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and rice wine.
Stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes until the chilies are tender-crisp and bright green, then serve.

title: Mao's Red Braised Pork
ingredients: 800g pork belly, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Blanch the pork cubes in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil and rock sugar in a wok over low heat until the sugar melts and turns a golden brown caramel.
Add the pork belly cubes and stir well to coat them in the caramel.
Add garlic, ginger, star anise, cinnamon stick, and dried red chilies, stirring for 1 minute.
Pour in light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water, bringing the liquid to a boil.
Cover with a lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and turn up the heat for 5 minutes to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick before serving.

title: Hunan Steamed Fish Head with Chopped Salted Chilies
ingredients: 1 bighead carp fish head, split in half
1 cup homemade pickled red chilies, chopped
instructions: Clean the fish head and rub it with salt and Shaoxing rice wine, letting it marinate for 15 minutes.
Place the fish head on a deep heat-proof plate with ginger slices underneath.
Mix the chopped pickled red chilies and minced garlic together, then spread them evenly over the fish head.
Place the plate in a steamer over boiling water and steam on high heat for 12 minutes.
Remove from steamer, scatter chopped scallions over the top.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan until smoking hot, then pour it directly over the scallions and chilies to sizzle before serving.

title: Hunan Sour and Spicy Shredded Potatoes
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, peeled and julienned
3 dried red chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Soak the julienned potatoes in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch, then drain well.
Blanch the potatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds, then immediately rinse in cold water and drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and add Sichuan peppercorns, dried red chilies, and minced garlic until fragrant.
Turn heat to high, add the drained potatoes, and toss quickly.
Drizzle in the white vinegar and add salt, stir-frying for another minute until potatoes are tender-crisp.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Sour Beans with Minced Pork
ingredients: 300g pickled long beans, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Chop the pickled long beans into small pieces and dry-fry them in a wok without oil for 3 minutes to remove excess moisture, then set aside.
Heat cooking oil in the wok and fry the ground pork until browned and cooked through.
Add minced garlic and chopped red chilies to the pork, stirring until aromatic.
Add the dry-fried pickled beans back into the wok.
Season with light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Stir-fry everything together on high heat for 2 minutes to let the flavors meld, then transfer to a plate.

title: Stuffed Fermented Tofu Puffs
instructions: Mix the minced pork with Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, cornstarch, scallion, and ginger.
Poke a small hole in each tofu puff and stuff them generously with the pork mixture.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and sear the stuffed sides of the tofu puffs until golden.
Pour in the chicken broth and mashed fermented bean curd, stirring gently to dissolve the curd.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the pork is cooked through and the tofu has absorbed the savory sauce.

title: Anhui Wild Rice Stem with Shredded Pork
ingredients: 300g wild rice stems (jiaobai), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Marinate the pork strips with light soy sauce and cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and quick-fry the pork until it changes color, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add a bit more oil and sauté the garlic and red bell pepper until fragrant.
Add the wild rice stems and stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Return the pork to the wok, add salt, sugar, and water, toss everything well, and serve hot.

title: Liuan Stuffed Tea Dried Tofu
ingredients: 1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), rinsed and chopped
instructions: Slice each piece of dried tofu halfway through to create a pocket.
Mix the minced pork with chopped black beans, garlic chives, light soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Stuff each tofu pocket firmly with the pork mixture.
Heat oil in a wide pan and pan-fry the stuffed tofu on both sides until golden brown.
Pour in the vegetable broth, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until the liquid is mostly reduced and absorbed.

title: Hefei Egg Dumplings
ingredients: 1 tbsp lard for greasing the ladle
instructions: Mix the minced pork with scallions, ginger, light soy sauce, and salt.
Heat a traditional round metal soup ladle over a very low flame and lightly grease it with lard.
Pour about 1 tablespoon of beaten egg into the hot ladle, swirling quickly to form a thin round egg skin.
Before the egg is fully set, place a small spoonful of the pork filling on one half of the egg skin.
Use chopsticks to gently fold the egg skin over the filling, press the edges to seal, and cook until the pork is cooked through.

title: Authentic Sichuan Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 tbsp Sichuan doubanjiang (broad bean paste), finely chopped
1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp Sichuan chili flakes or powder
3 stalks garlic sprouts (or scallions), cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp water mixed with 1 tbsp cornstarch (for slurry)
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a gentle boil, add a pinch of salt, and blanch the cubed tofu for 1 minute. Drain gently and set aside.
Heat wok over medium-high heat, add oil, and brown the ground meat until cooked through and slightly crispy.
Add the chopped doubanjiang and mashed fermented black beans, stir-frying until the oil turns a vibrant red.
Add the minced ginger, garlic, and Sichuan chili flakes, stir-frying for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock or water, bring to a simmer, and gently slide in the blanched tofu.
Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes so the tofu absorbs the flavors.
Add the garlic sprouts and pour in the cornstarch slurry in two batches, gently stirring until the sauce thickens and clings to the tofu.
Transfer to a serving bowl, sprinkle the ground Sichuan peppercorn evenly over the top, and serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork (Hui Guo Rou)
ingredients: 12 oz pork belly, block with skin on
2 leeks (traditional Sichuan style) or green bell peppers, sliced on the diagonal
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot with cold water, ginger slices, scallions, and Shaoxing wine. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer for 25 minutes until the pork is just cooked through.
Remove the pork, let it cool slightly, and slice it thinly into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil in a seasoned wok over medium heat, add the sliced pork belly, and stir-fry until the fat renders and the edges curl up slightly.
Push the pork to one side, add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans to the oil, and stir-fry until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the sweet bean paste and toss everything together to coat the pork.
Add the sliced leeks or peppers and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until tender-crisp.
Drizzle with light soy sauce, toss well, and transfer to a plate.

title: Sichuan Cold Noodles in Chili Oil (Liang Mian)
ingredients: 8 oz fresh alkaline wheat noodles (or thin Chinese egg noodles)
2 tbsp toasted sesame paste (or smooth peanut butter)
2 tbsp Sichuan chili oil with sediments
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, cook the noodles according to package instructions until just done, then rinse thoroughly under cold running water until completely cooled. Drain well.
Toss the cooled noodles with a teaspoon of sesame oil to prevent sticking, and divide them among serving bowls over a bed of blanched bean sprouts.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sesame paste, light soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, sugar, minced garlic, and 1 tablespoon of cold water until smooth.
Pour the sauce mixture over the chilled noodles.
Top generously with the Sichuan chili oil, crushed peanuts, and chopped scallions.
Toss thoroughly before eating.

title: Sichuan Dry-Fried Green Beans (Gan Bian Si Ji Dou)
ingredients: 12 oz fresh green beans, washed and ends trimmed
2 dried red chili peppers, cut into segments
1 tbsp yaacai (preserved Sichuan pickled mustard greens), rinsed
instructions: Pat the green beans completely dry with paper towels to prevent oil spitting.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the green beans and pan-fry, stirring frequently, until the skins become blistered, wrinkled, and slightly shriveled (about 5-7 minutes). Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and sauté the minced pork until it is browned and crispy.
Add the dried chili peppers, Sichuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger, and yaacai, stir-frying for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Return the green beans to the wok.
Splash the Shaoxing wine and light soy sauce around the edges of the wok, add salt, and toss everything together over high heat for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and serve hot.

title: Sichuan Tomato and Egg Drop Soup
ingredients: 1 tbsp scallions or cilantro, chopped for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a soup pot over medium heat, add the smashed garlic and ginger, and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges and cook, stirring occasionally, until they soften and release their juices, creating a rich red broth base.
Pour in the chicken broth or water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes so the flavors meld.
Season the soup with salt and white pepper powder.
Stir the simmering soup in a circular motion to create a gentle vortex, and slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream.
Let the eggs sit undisturbed for 5 seconds to form soft ribbons, then gently stir once.
Drizzle with sesame oil, garnish with chopped scallions or cilantro, and serve hot.

title: Steamed Pork Belly with Preserved Mustard Greens (Mui Choi Kow Yoke)
ingredients: 100g preserved mustard greens (mui choi), rinsed and soaked
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Pierce the pork skin with a fork and rub it with dark soy sauce.
Pan-fry the pork skin-side down until golden and blistered, then slice into thick pieces.
Sauté the minced garlic and chopped preserved mustard greens in a wok.
Arrange the pork pieces skin-side down in a deep bowl and top with the mustard greens.
Mix soy sauces, Shaoxing wine, fermented bean curd, sugar, and water, then pour over the pork.
Steam over high heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the pork is tender.
Invert the bowl onto a serving plate before serving.

title: Steamed Chicken with Dried Shiitake Mushrooms and Red Dates
ingredients: 1/2 free-range chicken, chopped into bite-sized pieces
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with ginger, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornstarch, sesame oil, sugar, and Shaoxing wine for 30 minutes.
Mix the sliced mushrooms and red dates into the marinated chicken.
Place the mixture evenly on a heatproof shallow dish.
Top with scallion pieces.
Place the dish in a steamer over boiling water and steam on high heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Serve hot with steamed white rice.

title: Cantonese Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt until well combined.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just soft and slightly runny. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges and tomato paste, stir-frying until the tomatoes begin to soften and release their juices.
Add the sugar, salt, and water, cover with a lid, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok and gently toss everything together.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Choy Sum with Garlic
instructions: Wash the choy sum thoroughly and cut into sections, separating the stems from the leafy parts.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking hot.
Add the smashed garlic and stir-fry for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the choy sum stems first and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the leafy parts of the choy sum, salt, and water.
Cover the wok for 1 minute to let the greens steam and soften.
Sprinkle in the chicken bouillon powder, toss well, and transfer to a serving plate.

title: Steamed Minced Pork with Salted Duck Egg
instructions: In a bowl, mix the minced pork with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sugar, water, and vegetable oil until sticky.
Spread the minced pork evenly onto a shallow heatproof plate, pressing it down slightly.
Separate the salted duck egg white and yolk. Mix the egg white into the minced pork or pour it over the top.
Place the whole salted egg yolk in the center of the meat patty.
Steam over high heat in a wok for 12 to 15 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve hot.

title: Lu Cuisine Braised Sea Cucumber with Scallions
ingredients: 4 dried sea cucumbers, soaked and cleaned
5 stalks scallions, cut into long sections
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Boil the soaked sea cucumbers in ginger water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the scallions until golden brown and aromatic, then remove scallions.
In the same wok, add ginger, garlic, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and chicken broth.
Add the sea cucumbers and fried scallions to the wok, cover, and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce, and serve hot.

title: Shandong Sweet and Sour Carp
ingredients: 1 whole carp (about 1.5 lbs), scaled and cleaned
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Score the fish body diagonally on both sides, then coat thoroughly with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a large wok and fry the fish until golden and crispy on both sides; remove and set on a plate.
In the remaining oil, sauté garlic, ginger, and scallions until fragrant.
Add vinegar, sugar, water, soy sauce, and salt to the wok and bring to a simmer.
Thicken the sauce with the cornstarch slurry and pour it over the crispy fish.

title: Shandong Stir-Fried Pork Loin Slices with Garlic Sprout
instructions: Marinate pork slices with Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok and quickly stir-fry the pork until it changes color; remove from wok.
Add the remaining oil to the wok, sauté garlic and fermented soybean paste until fragrant.
Add garlic sprouts and stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Return the cooked pork to the wok, add salt, toss well, and serve.

title: Shandong Scrambled Eggs with Shrimp and Chives
ingredients: 100g Chinese chives, cut into small pieces
instructions: Marinate the shrimp with Shaoxing wine and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add salt, and beat well.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok and quickly cook the shrimp until pink; remove and set aside.
Mix the cooked shrimp and chopped chives into the beaten eggs.
Heat the remaining oil in the wok, pour in the egg mixture, and gently scramble until just set; drizzle with sesame oil and serve.

title: Shandong Fried Pork Sauce for Noodles (Zha Jiang Mian)
instructions: Mix the sweet bean paste and yellow soybean paste together in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the diced pork belly until fat renders and pieces turn golden.
Add minced ginger and garlic, stir-frying until aromatic.
Add the mixed pastes and water, stirring well, then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until thick.
Cook the noodles, place in bowls, top with the rich pork sauce and julienned cucumber, and mix well before eating.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cooked day-old jasmine rice, chilled
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and scramble the eggs until just set, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and turn the heat to high. Add the diced char siu and shrimp, stir-frying for 1 minute.
Add the green peas and chilled rice, breaking up any clumps with a spatula and tossing continuously for 3 to 4 minutes until the rice is heated through.
Drizzle the Shaoxing wine and light soy sauce around the edges of the wok for aroma.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, add the scallions, salt, and white pepper, toss everything together well, and serve hot.

title: Lion's Head Meatballs
ingredients: 1/2 cup napa cabbage leaves, washed and separated
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the minced pork, ginger, scallions, egg, Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, salt, and cornstarch slurry.
Vigorously stir the meat mixture in one direction until it becomes sticky and cohesive.
Divide the meat into four equal portions and shape them into large smooth meatballs by tossing them back and forth between your hands.
Line the bottom of a heavy clay pot or dutch oven with the napa cabbage leaves, then place the meatballs gently on top.
Pour in the chicken stock, bring to a gentle simmer, cover with a lid, and braise on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and melt-in-your-mouth.

title: Squirrel-Shaped Mandarin Fish
ingredients: 1 whole mandarin fish (about 750g), scaled and cleaned
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Fillet the fish, remove the backbone, score the flesh in a crisscross diamond pattern without cutting through the skin, and coat thoroughly with cornstarch.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok to 190 degrees Celsius (375 degrees Fahrenheit) and fry the fish until golden and crispy, then transfer to a serving platter.
In a separate small pan, combine ketchup, sugar, rice vinegar, and chicken broth, bringing it to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sweet and sour sauce until glossy.
Stir in the pineapple and green peas, pour the hot sauce over the crispy fish, and garnish with pine nuts before serving.

title: Wuxi Braised Spare Ribs
ingredients: 500g pork spare ribs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork spare ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, then remove and drain.
Heat oil in a wok, add rock sugar, and melt over low heat until it turns a deep amber caramel color.
Add the blanched ribs to the wok and stir-fry until evenly coated with the caramel.
Add ginger, scallions, Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon stick, and hot water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes, then remove the lid and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until thick and glossy.

title: Crystal Shrimp
ingredients: 400g fresh river shrimp or large shrimp, shelled and deveined
2 tablespoons lard or neutral vegetable oil
instructions: Rinse the shelled shrimp thoroughly, pat them completely dry with paper towels, and place them in a bowl.
Add salt, egg white, and cornstarch to the shrimp, and mix vigorously in one direction until the shrimp turn slightly sticky.
Cover the shrimp and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Heat lard or oil in a wok over low heat, add the chilled shrimp, and gently stir until they just turn opaque and white, about 1 minute.
Splash in Shaoxing wine, chicken bouillon powder, and scallion oil, toss quickly for 10 seconds, and immediately remove from heat to serve.

title: Dongpo Pork
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
4 stalks scallions, cut into long sections
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then remove and rinse with warm water.
Place a bamboo mat or a layer of scallions and ginger at the bottom of a clay pot to prevent sticking.
Place the pork pieces skin-side down on top of the ginger and scallions.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and rock sugar.
Bring to a boil, then cover with a tight lid, turn heat to low, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Flip the pork pieces skin-side up and simmer for another 30 minutes until tender.
Steam the pork in individual bowls for 30 minutes before serving for an extra melt-in-the-mouth texture.

title: West Lake Vinegar Fish
ingredients: 1 whole grass carp, about 1.5 lbs, cleaned and scaled
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Cut the fish in half lengthwise along the backbone, keeping the tail intact, and rinse well.
Bring a pot of water to a boil with ginger slices, scallions, and Shaoxing rice wine.
Slip the fish into the boiling water, reduce heat to low, and poach for about 4 to 5 minutes until just cooked.
Carefully lift the fish out with a slotted spatula and place it on a serving plate.
In a separate pan, combine 1 cup of the fish poaching liquid, Chinkiang vinegar, light soy sauce, and rock sugar.
Bring the sauce to a simmer until the sugar dissolves completely.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sweet and sour sauce.
Pour the hot glossy sauce evenly over the poached fish and serve immediately.

title: Longjing Shrimp
ingredients: 12 oz fresh shrimp, shelled and deveined
2 tablespoons lard or neutral vegetable oil
instructions: Steep the Longjing tea leaves in 1/2 cup of hot water for 2 minutes, then strain and reserve both the tea leaves and 2 tablespoons of the tea liquid.
Rinse the shelled shrimp in cold water, drain thoroughly, and pat completely dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, mix the shrimp with egg white, cornstarch, and salt until well coated, then chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat lard or oil in a wok over medium-high heat until warm, not hot.
Add the shrimp and stir gently for about 30 seconds until they just turn pink and opaque.
Pour in the reserved tea liquid and add the steeped tea leaves.
Toss quickly for 10 seconds and remove from heat immediately.

title: Shepherd's Purse and Rice Cake Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 lb slice rice cakes, soaked in water if dry
5 oz fresh shepherd's purse greens, washed and chopped
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Drain the sliced rice cakes and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and stir-fry the pork slices until they change color.
Add the sliced shiitake mushrooms and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the rice cakes and chicken stock to the wok, cover with a lid, and simmer for 3 minutes until the rice cakes soften.
Add the chopped shepherd's purse greens, light soy sauce, and salt.
Stir-fry everything together vigorously for 2 minutes until the greens are tender and the sauce is absorbed.

title: Braised Bamboo Shoots with Pickled Mustard Greens
ingredients: 2 fresh spring bamboo shoots, peeled and sliced
3 oz preserved mustard greens, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Blanch the sliced bamboo shoots in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the chopped preserved mustard greens and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the blanched bamboo shoots, sugar, salt, and water to the wok.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the bamboo shoots absorb the savory flavors.
Uncover and toss on high heat for 1 minute to reduce any remaining liquid before serving.

title: Fujian Red Yeast Rice Wine Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, about 3 lbs, chopped into bite-sized pieces
4 tablespoons Fujian red yeast rice (angkak), soaked in warm water and mashed
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a wok or clay pot over medium heat.
Add the ginger slices and stir-fry until fragrant and slightly browned.
Add the chopped chicken pieces and sear until the skin is lightly golden.
Pour in the mashed red yeast rice and stir well to coat the chicken evenly.
Add the glutinous rice wine and water, bringing the mixture to a gentle boil.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot.

title: Fuzhou Fish Balls in Clear Broth
ingredients: 12 frozen authentic Fuzhou fish balls (with pork filling)
instructions: Bring the chicken bone broth to a boil in a medium pot along with the ginger slices.
Add the Fuzhou fish balls directly to the boiling broth.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for about 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish balls float and are heated through to the center.
Add the scallion pieces, salt, and white pepper.
Stir gently and cook for another minute.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with chopped cilantro, and serve hot.

title: Fujian Oyster Omelet
ingredients: 1 cup fresh small oysters, rinsed and drained
Fujian sweet chili sauce for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix the sweet potato starch and water together until smooth.
Beat the eggs in a separate bowl and season with salt and chopped scallions.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a non-stick skillet over high heat.
Quickly sauté the oysters for about 30 seconds until they just begin to plump.
Pour the sweet potato starch mixture evenly over the oysters.
Pour the beaten eggs all around and over the starch mixture.
Cook until the bottom is crispy and golden, then carefully flip and cook the other side.
Transfer to a plate and serve immediately with sweet chili sauce.

title: Lychee Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into bite-sized pieces and scored in a crosshatch pattern
1 fresh water chestnut, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
instructions: Marinate the pork pieces with salt for 15 minutes, then coat thoroughly with cornstarch.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok to 350 degrees F and deep-fry the pork until crispy and golden. Remove and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, mix the ketchup, rice vinegar, sugar, and water to create the sweet and sour sauce.
Leave about 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok, sauté the minced garlic until fragrant, then add the sliced water chestnuts.
Pour in the sauce mixture and bring to a simmer until it thickens and becomes glossy.
Toss the fried pork quickly into the sauce until every piece is evenly glazed.
Serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Rice Vermicelli with Dried Seafood
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried shrimp, soaked in warm water and drained
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked, stemmed, and thinly sliced
instructions: Soak the rice vermicelli in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain well.
Heat oil in a large wok over medium heat and sauté the soaked dried shrimp and sliced shiitake mushrooms until fragrant.
Add the shredded Napa cabbage and julienned carrots, stir-frying until slightly softened.
Pour in the chicken broth and light soy sauce, bringing the mixture to a simmer.
Add the drained rice vermicelli directly into the wok, spreading it out over the vegetables.
Cover the wok and let the noodles absorb the broth over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove the lid, toss everything vigorously with chopsticks until the liquid is fully absorbed and noodles are tender, then mix in the scallions and serve.

title: Hunan Stir-Fried Pork with Garlic Sprouts
ingredients: 200 g garlic sprouts, cut into 2-inch segments
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium heat and add the sliced pork belly.
Stir-fry until the pork fat renders and the edges turn slightly golden.
Push the pork to the side, then add garlic, fermented black beans, red chilies, and doubanjiang into the oil, frying until fragrant.
Toss the pork and aromatics together, then splash in the Shaoxing wine and light soy sauce.
Add the garlic sprouts and stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Serve hot.

title: Mao's Red Braised Pork
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil and rock sugar in a wok over low heat until the sugar melts and turns a light amber caramel color.
Add the pork belly cubes and stir quickly to coat them evenly with the caramel.
Add ginger, scallions, star anise, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves, tossing for 1 minute.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and hot water.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and turn up the heat to reduce the sauce until glossy and thick before serving.

title: Hunan Steamed Fish Head with Chopped Salted Chilies
ingredients: 1 bighead carp fish head, about 1 kg, split in half
1/2 cup pickled and salted red Hunan chilies, chopped
instructions: Rub the fish head with salt and Shaoxing wine, letting it marinate for 15 minutes.
Place the fish head cut-side up on a large heatproof serving plate.
In a bowl, mix the chopped salted chilies, minced garlic, and minced ginger together.
Spread the chili mixture evenly over the top of the fish head.
Bring a steamer to a rolling boil, place the plate inside, and steam over high heat for 12 minutes.
Remove from steamer, sprinkle chopped scallions over the top.
Heat the lard or oil in a small pan until smoking hot, then pour it directly over the scallions and chilies to sizzle. Serve immediately.

title: Hunan Sour and Spicy Shredded Potatoes
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, peeled and julienned
3 dried red chili peppers, cut into small pieces
instructions: Rinse the julienned potatoes in a bowl of cold water several times to remove excess starch, then drain well.
Heat cooking oil in a wok over high heat, add Sichuan peppercorns and dried red chilies, stirring until fragrant.
Add minced garlic and half of the scallions.
Toss in the drained potato shreds and stir-fry vigorously for 1 minute.
Drizzle in the Chinkiang vinegar and light soy sauce along the hot sides of the wok.
Add salt and the remaining scallions, toss quickly for another 30 seconds until potatoes are tender-crisp, then dish out.

title: Pan-Fried Tofu with Spicy Chili Sauce
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into bite-sized triangular slices
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Place the tofu slices in the pan and pan-fry until both sides are golden brown and crispy. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil and sauté the garlic, chopped red chilies, and fermented soybean paste until fragrant.
Return the fried tofu to the pan and gently toss to coat with the spicy paste.
Pour in the water, light soy sauce, and sugar. Simmer for 2 minutes until the tofu absorbs the flavors.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve hot.

title: Stuffed Fermented Tofu Puffs
instructions: Mix the minced pork with scallion, ginger, Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, mashed fermented bean curd, and cornstarch.
Poke a small hole in each tofu puff and stuff them generously with the pork mixture.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and place the tofu puffs stuffed-side down first to sear until golden.
Flip the puffs, pour in the chicken broth, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a plate and drizzle the remaining pan sauce over the top before serving.

title: Anhui Steamed Salty Mandarin Fish
ingredients: 1 fresh mandarin fish (about 600g), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Rub the fish thoroughly inside and out with coarse sea salt, place in a container, and let it cure in the refrigerator for 24 hours.
Rinse the cured fish gently under cold water to remove excess surface salt and pat dry.
Place ginger slices and scallion sections on a heatproof steaming plate, then lay the fish on top.
Drizzle Shaoxing wine and light soy sauce over the fish.
Steam over high heat for 12 minutes until the flesh flakes easily.
Remove scallions and ginger, garnish with fresh red chili, pour hot vegetable oil over the top to sizzle, and serve.

title: Liuan Red Braised Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 500g fresh winter bamboo shoots, peeled and sliced
instructions: Blanch the bamboo shoot slices in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the bamboo shoot slices and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, and water, bringing it to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce is reduced and glossy.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve warm.

title: She County Dried Bean Curd with Pork
ingredients: 300g dried pressed bean curd (qianzhang), sliced into strips
1 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang (fermented chili bean paste)
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and render the pork belly slices until slightly browned.
Add garlic and Pixian doubanjiang, stir-frying until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the dried bean curd strips and stir-fry for 2 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the water and light soy sauce, bring to a simmer, and cook for 5 minutes.
Toss in the green bell pepper strips and stir-fry for another 1 minute until tender-crisp, then serve.

title: Anhui Fried Crispy Wontons
ingredients: 100g minced shepherd's purse (or spinach if unavailable)
instructions: Mix the ground pork, minced greens, salt, sesame oil, and light soy sauce together in a bowl to form the filling.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper, seal the edges with water, and press into a traditional shape.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep wok to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Drop the wontons in batches into the hot oil and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve hot with chili vinegar.

title: Classic Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into bite-sized cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the tofu cubes in boiling salted water for 1 minute, then drain gently.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the minced meat until crispy and browned.
Add doubanjiang and fermented black beans, stir-frying until the oil turns a vibrant red.
Add garlic, ginger, and half of the scallions, cooking until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the drained tofu and let it gently simmer for 3 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture in stages to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with the remaining scallions and Sichuan peppercorn powder.

title: Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork (Hui Guo Rou)
instructions: Boil the pork belly in a pot of water with ginger slices and Shaoxing wine for 25 minutes until just cooked through.
Remove the pork, let it cool slightly, and slice it thinly into bite-sized pieces.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and pan-fry the pork slices until the fat renders and the edges curl.
Push the pork to the side, add doubanjiang and fermented black beans to the oil, and stir-fry until fragrant and red.
Add sweet bean paste and toss everything together.
Add the sliced leeks and stir-fry on high heat until they soften and absorb the savory sauce.
Serve hot with steamed white rice.

title: Sichuan Dan Dan Noodles
instructions: In a serving bowl, combine the sesame paste, soy sauce, black vinegar, garlic, and chili oil.
Heat a little oil in a pan and stir-fry the minced pork until dry, then add ya cai and cook for another minute.
Boil the noodles in a large pot of water until al dente, then drain.
