Pour the hot chicken broth into the seasoning bowl and stir well to create the soup base.
Add the cooked noodles into the bowl.
Top with the seasoned pork, crushed peanuts, and chopped scallions. Mix well before eating.

title: Dry-Fried Green Beans (Gan Bian Si Ji Dou)
ingredients: 400g fresh green beans, ends trimmed and strings removed
3 dried red chili peppers, cut into segments
instructions: Pat the green beans completely dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and shallow-fry the green beans until the skins are wrinkled and blistered, then remove and drain.
Leave about 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok, add Sichuan peppercorns and dried chili peppers, and stir-fry until aromatic.
Add garlic, ginger, and minced pork, cooking until the pork is browned.
Add the green beans back into the wok.
Season with Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and salt, tossing everything together on high heat for 1 minute.

title: Sichuan Cold Chicken in Chili Oil (Bang Bang Ji)
instructions: Place chicken thighs in a pot with cold water, ginger, scallions, and Shaoxing wine, bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the chicken and immediately submerge it in an ice bath to make the skin springy.
Shred the chicken meat into thin strips and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix together the chili oil, light soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, garlic, and half of the sesame seeds.
Place the julienned cucumber on a serving plate as a bed.
Arrange the shredded chicken over the cucumber, pour the spicy sauce evenly over the top, and garnish with remaining sesame seeds.

title: Steamed Pork Belly with Preserved Mustard Greens (Mui Choi Kow Yoke)
ingredients: 100g preserved mustard greens (mui choi), soaked and finely chopped
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Rub the pork skin with dark soy sauce and let it dry for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok and pan-fry the pork belly skin-side down until golden and blistered.
Slice the pork belly into half-inch thick pieces.
In a bowl, mix garlic, soy sauces, Shaoxing wine, and sugar, then coat the pork slices.
Layer the pork slices and preserved mustard greens in a deep steaming bowl.
Steam over high heat for 90 minutes until the pork is tender.
Invert the bowl onto a serving plate before serving.

title: Steamed Chicken with Dried Shiitake Mushrooms and Jujubes
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, about 1.2 kg, chopped into bite-sized pieces
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with ginger, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornstarch, sesame oil, and salt for 30 minutes.
Mix the sliced mushrooms and red dates into the marinated chicken.
Spread the mixture evenly on a shallow heatproof dish.
Place the dish in a steamer over boiling water.
Steam on high heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Garnish with scallions and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt until well combined.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat, pour in the eggs, and gently scramble until just set; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges and tomato paste, stir-frying for 2 minutes until the tomatoes start to soften.
Add water, sugar, and salt, cover with a lid, and simmer for 3 minutes to create a rich sauce.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, breaking them up slightly, and toss with the tomatoes.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve warm.

title: Pan-Fried Dace with Salted Black Beans and Choy Sum
ingredients: 1 can (184g) fried dace with salted black beans
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the choy sum and stir-fry for 1 minute until bright green.
Pour in the water and add salt, then cover the wok to steam the vegetables for 2 minutes.
Push the choy sum to the sides of the wok to create a space in the center.
Add the canned dace and its black beans into the center, breaking the fish slightly.
Let it simmer for another minute until the flavors meld together.
Transfer everything to a serving plate and serve immediately.

title: Cantonese Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole live sea bass or tilapia, about 600g, cleaned and scaled
2 inches fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
3 stalks scallions, cut into matchsticks and separated
instructions: Rub the fish inside and out with salt and Shaoxing wine.
Place half of the ginger matchsticks inside the fish cavity and scatter the rest on top.
Place the fish on a heat-proof plate and steam in a wok over boiling water for 10 minutes.
Remove the plate from the steamer and carefully discard the liquid that pooled during steaming.
Scatter the fresh scallion matchsticks over the top of the fish.
Heat the canola oil in a small pan until smoking hot, then pour it directly over the scallions and ginger to release their aroma.
Pour the light soy sauce around the base of the fish and serve hot.

title: Sweet and Sour Carp
ingredients: 1 whole Yellow River carp (about 1.5 lbs), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Rinse the fish and pat dry. Score the flesh diagonally on both sides at 1-inch intervals without cutting the bone.
Coat the fish thoroughly with cornstarch, shaking off the excess.

Heat oil in a wok or deep skillet to 375°F (190°C). Carefully hold the tail and slide the fish into the oil, frying until golden brown and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels, then place on a serving platter.
Pour out most of the oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the wok.
Sauté the garlic, ginger, and half of the green onions until fragrant.
Add the rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens slightly.
Drizzle the hot sweet and sour sauce over the crispy fish, garnish with the remaining green onions, and serve immediately.

title: Shandong Stir-Fried Pork Tenderloin with Scallions
ingredients: 300g pork tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
4 large Chinese scallions (white parts only), cut into 2-inch julienne strips
instructions: Marinate the pork strips with light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking hot.
Add the marinated pork and stir-fry quickly until the meat changes color and is just cooked through. Remove the pork and set aside.
In the remaining oil, add the minced garlic and sweet bean sauce, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the julienned scallions and stir-fry for 1 minute until they begin to soften.
Return the pork to the wok, toss everything together quickly, splash with dark vinegar and sesame oil, and serve hot.

title: Stir-Fried Eggs with Chinese Leeks
ingredients: 200g Chinese green leeks (jiucai), washed and cut into 1-inch segments
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and 1 tablespoon of water, and beat well.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble gently until large soft curds form. Remove the eggs from the wok and set aside.
In the same wok, turn the heat to high and add the Chinese leeks. Stir-fry rapidly for about 1 minute until they just start to wilt.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok, add the remaining salt and sesame oil, and toss everything together for 30 seconds before serving.

title: Braised Sea Cucumber with Scallions
ingredients: 4 soaked sea cucumbers, cleaned and sliced into bite-sized pieces
5 stalks green onions, cut into long segments
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Blanch the sea cucumber pieces in boiling water for 1 minute to remove any fishy odor, then drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the green onion segments and ginger, frying until the onions are golden brown and aromatic.
Add the Shaoxing wine, chicken broth, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar to the wok.
Add the sea cucumber to the sauce, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes so it absorbs the flavors.
Remove the lid, turn the heat to high, and pour in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce into a glossy glaze. Serve hot.

title: Shandong Cabbage and Pork Dumplings
ingredients: 2 cups Napa cabbage, finely minced and excess water squeezed out
instructions: Mix the flour and warm water to form a smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, minced ginger, green onions, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and salt. Stir vigorously in one direction until the mixture becomes sticky.
Fold the squeezed Napa cabbage and sesame oil into the pork mixture until well combined.
Divide the rested dough into small equal portions, roll each into a thin round wrapper, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and pleat the edges to seal.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil, drop the dumplings in, and stir gently. When the water returns to a boil, add a cup of cold water. Repeat this boiling cycle twice more until the dumplings float and are plump, then remove with a slotted spoon and serve with black vinegar.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess.
Dip the cutlets into the beaten eggs.
Coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat clarified butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Classic Bavarian Soft Pretzels
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix in flour and melted butter to form a dough, then knead until smooth.
Let the dough rise for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Divide dough into ropes and shape into pretzels.
Dissolve baking soda in boiling water and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds.
Place on baking sheet, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake for 12 minutes until dark brown.

title: Traditional Swiss Fondue
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard.
Pour in white wine and lemon juice, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese to the wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight pattern until melted and smooth.
Stir in Kirschwasser and nutmeg.
Serve immediately with cubed baguette for dipping.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk egg yolks, milk, flour, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt into a smooth batter.
Whip egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold them into the batter.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Scatter the rum-soaked raisins over the top.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces using two spatulas.
Continue cooking until all pieces are lightly browned.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: German Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins until tender, then peel while warm and slice thinly.
Fry the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, remove bacon, and leave the bacon fat in the pan.
Sauté the diced onion in the bacon fat until translucent.
Whisk beef broth, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and pepper into the onions to create the dressing.
Pour the warm dressing and crispy bacon over the sliced potatoes and toss gently.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Pound the veal cutlets until they are about 5mm thick.
Season the cutlets with salt.
Set up a breading station with flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the egg, and coat in breadcrumbs without pressing them down.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on both sides, swirling the pan continuously, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Bavarian Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced onions, carrots, bay leaves, cloves, and peppercorns in a pot and bring to a boil; let cool completely.
Place the beef roast in a large container, pour the marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning daily.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat dry, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and sear the beef on all sides until browned.
Add the reserved marinade and vegetables, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the beef and blend the sauce with the crumbled gingerbread cookies until smooth, cooking for another 5 minutes to thicken.
Slice the beef, pour the gravy over the top, and serve.

title: Authentic Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a caquelon (fondue pot) with the halved garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
In a bowl, toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch.
Pour the white wine and lemon juice into the pot and heat over medium heat until gently simmering.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until melted and smooth.
Stir in the pinch of nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a rechaud (burner) at the table.
Serve immediately with cubed bread for dipping.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with half of the granulated sugar until creamy.
Stir in the flour, milk, and salt until a smooth batter forms.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites with the remaining sugar until stiff peaks form, then gently fold into the batter along with the raisins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Using two forks, tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum compote.

title: Bavarian Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: 1 cup beef or vegetable broth, warm
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, let them cool slightly, then peel and slice them into thin rounds while still warm.
Place the sliced potatoes in a large bowl and add the diced onions.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the warm broth, vinegar, oil, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the potatoes and gently toss to combine without breaking them.
Let the salad rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Garnish with chopped chives before serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 150g each, pounded thin
1/2 cup clarified butter or lard for frying
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets with salt.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip into the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs without pressing them down too hard.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on one side, about 3 to 4 minutes, then flip and fry the other side until golden and crispy.
Remove, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Bavarian Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef roast, such as rump or chuck
1/2 cup crushed gingerbread cookies or Lebkuchen
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced onion, carrots, bay leaves, peppercorns, and cloves in a pot to make the marinade, then bring to a boil and let cool completely.
Place the beef roast in a large non-reactive container, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat dry with paper towels, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the beef on all sides until well browned.
Add the reserved vegetables from the marinade to the pot and sauté until soft, then stir in the tomato paste.
Pour in 2 cups of the strained marinade, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, whisk the crushed gingerbread into the sauce to thicken it, season with salt and pepper, slice the beef, and serve with the sauce.

title: Authentic Swiss Käsefondue
ingredients: 1.5 cups dry white wine, preferably Swiss Chasselas
1 loaf crusty artisan bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed fondue pot with the halved garlic clove and discard the garlic.
In a bowl, toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses together with the cornstarch.
Pour the white wine and lemon juice into the fondue pot and heat over medium heat until gently simmering.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until the cheese is completely melted and smooth.
Stir in the Kirschwasser and a pinch of nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a table burner to keep it warm and serve immediately with the bread cubes for dipping.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels (Brezeln)
ingredients: 50 g food-grade lye pellets or 50g baking soda for a safer alternative
1 liter water for the lye bath
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in a large bowl, then add the softened butter and lukewarm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces, roll each into a long strand tapering at the ends, and shape into traditional pretzels.
Let the shaped pretzels rest uncovered in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to dry the surface slightly.
Prepare the lye solution by dissolving the lye in cold water in a non-metal bowl, wearing gloves and safety goggles.
Dip each pretzel into the lye solution for 20 to 30 seconds, remove with a slotted spoon, and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Score the thick part of the pretzel with a sharp knife and sprinkle generously with coarse salt.
Bake in a preheated oven at 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes until deep brown.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
ingredients: Stewed plums or applesauce for serving
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, milk, flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl until a smooth batter forms.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the rum raisins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is lightly browned, then flip the large pancake in sections and cook the other side.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan, stirring for another minute until lightly caramelized.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve hot with stewed plums or applesauce.

title: Traditional Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
1/2 cup clarified butter or lard for frying
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets with salt.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip into the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs without pressing them down too hard.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and fry the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Authentic Bavarian Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced onion, carrots, celery, juniper berries, cloves, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot, bring to a boil, and let cool completely to create the marinade.
Place the beef roast in a deep glass container, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the meat from the marinade, pat dry with paper towels, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid.
Heat vegetable oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the beef on all sides until well browned.
Pour in 2 cups of the reserved strained marinade, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and slice it. Stir the crushed gingersnaps into the pan juices, simmering until thickened to create a smooth gravy, then season with salt and pepper before pouring over the beef.

title: Classic Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
1 loaf crusty French bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed fondue pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
Pour the white wine into the pot and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until the cheese is completely melted and smooth.
Stir in the kirschwasser, nutmeg, and black pepper.
Place the pot over a burner on the table and serve immediately with cubed bread for dipping.

title: Traditional Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until a smooth batter forms.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the raisins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip the large pancake in sections and cook the other side.
Using two forks, tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan and sauté for another 2 minutes until slightly crisp.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum compote.

title: Swabian Maultaschen
ingredients: 1 package large wonton wrappers or homemade pasta dough
2 cups spinach, blanched and finely chopped
1 stale bread roll, soaked in water and squeezed dry
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the ground beef, ground pork, chopped onion, blanched spinach, soaked bread roll, eggs, parsley, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Lay out the wonton wrappers on a clean surface.
Place a tablespoon of the meat filling in the center of each wrapper.
Brush the edges of the wrappers with water, fold them over to enclose the filling, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Bring the beef broth to a gentle simmer in a large pot.
Drop the Maultaschen into the simmering broth and cook for about 10 to 12 minutes until they float and are cooked through, then serve hot in the broth or pan-fried with onions.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Place the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs into three separate shallow bowls.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the eggs, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot garnished with lemon wedges.

title: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
ingredients: 2 cups fermented sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the sliced onions until soft.
Add the sauerkraut and caraway seeds to the skillet, stirring to combine.
Place the bratwurst sausages on top of the sauerkraut mixture.
Pour the beer into the skillet and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then uncover and cook until the liquid evaporates and sausages are browned.
Serve hot with Dijon mustard.

title: Traditional Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 French baguette, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard.
Pour the white wine and lemon juice into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight pattern until melted and smooth.
Stir in the kirsch and nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a fondue burner and serve immediately with cubed baguette for dipping.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 3 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the sliced apples, granulated sugar, cinnamon, and raisins together in a bowl.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface.
Sprinkle the breadcrumbs down the center of the pastry, then top with the apple mixture.
Fold the pastry over the filling and seal the edges tightly, placing it seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush the top with melted butter and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly, dust with confectioners' sugar, and slice to serve.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and granulated sugar in warm water in a large bowl, letting it sit for 5 minutes until frothy.
Add the salt, flour, and melted butter, mixing until a dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 5 minutes until smooth, then let rise for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces, roll each into a long rope, and twist into a pretzel shape.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water, and dip each pretzel into the solution for 20 seconds before placing on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle with coarse sea salt and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until dark golden brown.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess.
Dip the cutlet into the beaten eggs, letting excess drip off.
Coat the cutlet in breadcrumbs, gently pressing them down.
Heat clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzel until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Bratkartoffeln
ingredients: 2 lbs waxy potatoes, boiled in their skins and cooled
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Peel the cooled boiled potatoes and slice them evenly.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced bacon and fry until crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Add the sliced potatoes and onions to the skillet with the bacon fat.
Fry, tossing occasionally, until the potatoes are golden and crispy, about 20 minutes.
Stir the crispy bacon back in, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with parsley.

title: Kasespatzle
ingredients: 2 cups Gruyere and Emmental cheese, grated
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, sparkling water, and salt into a thick, smooth dough using a wooden spoon until bubbles form.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then drop the dough in batches using a spaetzle press or scraping board.
Cook until the spaetzle float to the top, then remove with a skimmer and drain.
Melt butter in a pan and caramelize the sliced onions until golden brown.
In a warm serving dish, layer the hot spaetzle and grated cheese, repeating until all is used, and cover to melt the cheese.
Top with caramelized onions and fresh chives before serving.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 1 sheet store-bought puff pastry or homemade strudel dough
4 tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix the sliced apples, sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and walnuts in a bowl.
Roll out the pastry dough on a floured surface.
Brush the dough with melted butter and sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over it.
Spread the apple mixture along one side of the dough.
Roll the dough tightly around the filling and place it seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown, slice, and serve warm.

title: Kartoffelknodel
ingredients: 2 lbs starchy potatoes, boiled in skins
Cubed white bread, toasted in butter for filling
instructions: Peel the hot boiled potatoes and pass them through a potato ricer.
Allow the riced potatoes to cool slightly, then add egg yolks, starch, semolina, salt, and nutmeg.
Knead the mixture gently until a smooth dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal portions, flatten each, place a few toasted bread cubes in the center, and shape into round dumplings.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer (do not boil).
Drop the dumplings into the water and cook for about 20 minutes until they float.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve warm.

title: Traditional Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
1/2 cup clarified butter or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets lightly with salt.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip into the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs without pressing them down.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzel until golden brown on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and fry for another 2 minutes, constantly spooning hot fat over the top.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Authentic Bavarian Sauerbraten
ingredients: 3 lbs beef bottom round or chuck roast
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced onion, carrots, celery, juniper berries, cloves, and bay leaves in a pot and bring to a boil; let cool completely.
Place the beef in a large container, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat dry, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a Dutch oven and sear the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of the strained marinade to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, whisk the crumbled ginger snaps into the remaining pan juices to thicken the gravy, and slice the beef to serve with the sauce.

title: Classic Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty French or artisanal bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed pot or fondue pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
Pour the white wine into the pot and heat over medium heat until gently simmering.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until melted and smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice and ground nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a tabletop burner and serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Traditional Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk together the egg yolks, milk, flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the raisins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip the large pancake and cook the other side.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan.
Sprinkle with a little extra sugar and toss for 1 minute until lightly caramelized, then dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: German Kartoffelsalat (Warm Potato Salad)
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the potatoes in a pot of salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender when pierced with a fork, about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, let them cool slightly, then peel and slice them into 1/4-inch thick rounds.
Cook the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, remove the bacon with a slotted spoon, and leave the bacon fat in the pan.
Sauté the chopped onion in the warm bacon fat until translucent.
Whisk the beef broth, vinegar, mustard, and oil into the skillet with the onions, and season with salt and pepper; bring to a gentle simmer.
Pour the warm dressing and crispy bacon over the sliced potatoes, gently toss to combine, garnish with parsley, and serve warm.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
1/4 cup clarified butter or vegetable oil for frying
1 lemon, cut into wedges for serving
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets lightly with salt.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off excess, dip into the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat the clarified butter or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzel until golden brown on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and fry the other side for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess fat and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Bavarian Sauerkraut and Bratwurst
ingredients: 3 cups fermented sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
1 tart cooking apple, peeled and shredded
1 cup chicken broth or dry white wine
instructions: Heat the lard in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the sliced onions until translucent.
Add the shredded apple, sauerkraut, bay leaf, juniper berries, caraway seeds, and salt, stirring well to combine.
Pour in the chicken broth or white wine, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a separate skillet, brown the bratwurst sausages over medium heat until cooked through and nicely charred.
Serve the warm sauerkraut topped with the grilled bratwurst and mustard.

title: Authentic Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 cup dry white wine, preferably Sauvignon Blanc
1 loaf crusty French or Swiss bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed fondue pot or Dutch oven with the cut garlic clove, then discard it.
Pour the white wine into the pot and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine gradually, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until melted and smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice, nutmeg, and black pepper.
Transfer the pot to a tabletop burner and serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Classic Apfelstrudel (Apple Strudel)
ingredients: 3 large tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Soak the raisins in rum or warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet and lightly toast the breadcrumbs until golden brown.
In a large bowl, toss the sliced apples, drained raisins, toasted breadcrumbs, sugar, and cinnamon together.
Roll out the puff pastry sheet on a floured surface, brush with a little melted butter, and spread the apple filling along one side.
Roll the pastry tightly around the filling, tucking in the ends, and place seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush the top with the remaining melted butter and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Let cool slightly, dust with powdered sugar, and slice to serve.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt together in a bowl until smooth.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the batter, scattering the raisins over the top.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then carefully flip the large pancake.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the skillet.
Stir and sauté the pieces for another 2 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Transfer to plates, dust generously with powdered sugar, and serve warm with plum compote.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
1 lemon, cut into wedges for serving
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets with salt on both sides.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in the beaten eggs, and finally coat evenly in breadcrumbs without pressing them down.
Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot and foaming.
Fry the schnitzels for about 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy, spooning the hot fat over the top while cooking.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Bavarian Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1/2 cup crushed gingerbread cookies (Lebkuchen) or gingersnaps
instructions: In a large bowl, combine vinegar, water, sliced onion, carrots, celery, cloves, peppercorns, and bay leaves to make the marinade.
Submerge the beef roast in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat once a day.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat dry with paper towels, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and discarding the vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the beef on all sides until well browned.
Pour in 2 cups of the reserved marinade, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the beef is tender.
Remove the beef and slice. Stir the crushed gingerbread cookies into the pan liquid to thicken the gravy, season with salt, and serve over the sliced beef.

title: Authentic Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty artisan bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed fondue pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
Pour the white wine into the pot and heat over medium-low heat until simmering.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with cornstarch in a bowl.
Add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine gradually, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until the cheese is completely melted and smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice, Kirschwasser, and nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a tabletop burner and serve immediately with cubes of crusty bread for dipping.

title: Classic Austrian Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 1 sheet store-bought puff pastry or strudel dough, thawed
4 large tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small skillet, cook the breadcrumbs in 2 tablespoons of melted butter until golden brown and toasted.
In a large bowl, toss the sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and slivered almonds.
Roll out the pastry dough on a floured surface into a large rectangle.
Sprinkle the toasted breadcrumbs evenly over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges, then top with the apple mixture.
Roll the pastry up tightly enclosing the filling, place seam-side down on the baking sheet, and brush with the remaining melted butter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown, let cool slightly, dust with powdered sugar, and slice to serve.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels (Laugengebäck)
ingredients: 1/4 cup food-grade lye or 1/2 cup baking soda (for boiling water bath)
instructions: In a bowl, combine warm water, yeast, and sugar, letting it sit for 5 minutes until frothy.
Add the flour, melted butter, and salt, mixing until a dough forms, then knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces, roll each into a long rope, and shape into traditional pretzel forms.
If using baking soda, dissolve it in 4 cups of boiling water, and dip each pretzel into the solution for 30 seconds before placing on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle the pretzels generously with coarse salt and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Pound the veal cutlets gently until they are about 1/4 inch thick.
Season the cutlets lightly with salt.
Set up a breading station with flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve hot garnished with lemon wedges.

title: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
ingredients: 2 cups fermented sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté the sliced onions until soft.
Add the sauerkraut and caraway seeds to the skillet, stirring to combine with the onions.
Pour in the beer, place the bratwurst sausages on top, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and let simmer for 15 minutes until the sausages are cooked through.
Remove the lid and let the remaining liquid evaporate, browning the sausages slightly.
Serve the bratwurst inside bread rolls alongside the warm sauerkraut.

title: Authentic Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty artisan bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard it.
Pour the white wine into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses together with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine a handful at a time, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until melted.
Stir in the lemon juice and ground nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a tabletop burner and serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels (Laugengebäck)
ingredients: 1/3 cup food-grade lye or baking soda
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let stand for 5 minutes until frothy.
Mix in flour, melted butter, and salt, then knead into a smooth, elastic dough.
Cover the dough and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, roll each into a long rope, and shape into traditional pretzels.
Dip each pretzel into a solution of water and baking soda for 30 seconds.
Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake at 425°F for 15 minutes until deep brown.

title: Traditional Austrian Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 4 large tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the sliced apples, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins together in a large bowl.
Roll out the puff pastry sheet on a floured surface.
Brush the pastry with melted butter and sprinkle the breadcrumbs evenly over it.
Mound the apple mixture along one side of the pastry, leaving a border.
Roll the pastry tightly around the filling, tucking in the ends, and place seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown, then dust with powdered sugar before slicing.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 150g each, pounded thin
1/2 cup clarified butter or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets with salt on both sides.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in the beaten eggs, and finally coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Fry the schnitzels for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy, swirling the pan occasionally.
Remove and drain on paper towels, then serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups dry white wine, preferably Swiss Chasselas
1 French baguette, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a caquelon (fondue pot) with the cut garlic clove, then discard the garlic.
In a bowl, toss the grated Gruyère and Vacherin cheeses with the cornstarch.
Pour the white wine and lemon juice into the pot and heat over medium heat until gently simmering.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until the cheese is completely melted and smooth.
Stir in the nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a table burner and serve immediately with cubed bread for dipping.

title: Bavarian Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced vegetables, and spices in a pot, bring to a boil, then let cool completely.
Place the beef roast in a large non-reactive container, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning daily.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat dry with paper towels, and strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the beef on all sides until well browned.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of the strained marinade to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and slice it.
Whisk crumbled ginger snaps and flour into the pan juices, simmer until thickened into a gravy, and pour over the beef.

title: Classic Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 4 tart cooking apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Soak the raisins in rum or warm water for 15 minutes, then drain.
In a bowl, toss the apple slices with sugar, cinnamon, and drained raisins.
Roll out the puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface.
Brush the pastry with melted butter and sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over it, leaving a small border.
Mound the apple mixture along one side of the pastry.
Roll the pastry tightly around the filling, seal the edges, and place seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown, then let cool and dust with powdered sugar before slicing.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 600g veal tenderloin or sirloin, cut into thin strips
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over high heat.
Quickly sear the veal strips in batches for about 1-2 minutes until just browned, then remove and set aside on a warm plate.
Add the remaining butter to the same pan and sauté the chopped onion and sliced mushrooms until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and onions, stirring well for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine, scraping up any browned bits, and let it reduce by half.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the veal and any accumulated juices to the pan just to heat through, season with salt and white pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt.
Place flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow bowls.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets until golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Swiss Fondue
instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard.
Pour the white wine and lemon juice into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight pattern until melted and smooth.
Stir in the Kirschwasser and nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a rechaud over a flame and serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Bavarian Sauerbraten

Heat oil in a large Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of the strained marinade, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until tender.
Remove the meat, whisk the crushed gingersnaps into the pan juices to thicken the gravy, season with salt and pepper, and serve sliced over the meat.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk egg yolks, milk, flour, sugar, and salt together in a bowl to form a smooth batter.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the raisins.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum compote.

title: Classic German Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain, peel while warm, and slice into thin rounds.
Fry the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, remove bacon, and leave the bacon fat in the pan.
Sauté the chopped onion in the bacon fat until translucent.
Whisk beef broth, vinegar, mustard, vegetable oil, salt, and pepper into the pan with the onions and bring to a warm simmer.
Pour the warm dressing over the sliced potatoes, add the bacon and parsley, and toss gently.
Let the salad rest for at least 30 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
instructions: Season the pounded veal cutlets with salt.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess.
Dip the cutlets into the beaten eggs, letting excess drip off.
Coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, gently pressing them on.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side, spooning hot butter over the top constantly.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onions, carrots, celery, cloves, peppercorns, and bay leaves in a pot to create the marinade.
Place the beef roast in a large bowl, pour the marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning daily.

Heat vegetable oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of the strained marinade to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, stir the crushed ginger snaps into the liquid to thicken the gravy, season with salt and pepper, and slice the beef to serve with the gravy.

title: Classic Swiss Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty French or artisan bread, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a caquelon or heavy-bottomed pot with the cut garlic clove, then discard.
Pour the white wine into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated Gruyère and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl.
Gradually add the cheese mixture to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until melted and smooth.
Stir in the Kirschwasser and a pinch of nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a table burner and serve immediately with cubed bread for dipping.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt together in a bowl until smooth.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the batter.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and add the raisins if using.
Pour the batter into the skillet and cook until the bottom is golden brown.
Quarter the pancake with a spatula, flip the pieces, and tear them into bite-sized chunks using two forks.
Sauté the pieces until cooked through and slightly caramelized, then dust generously with powdered sugar and serve.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels (Brezeln)
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in flour, salt, and melted butter, then knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, roll each into a long rope, and twist into pretzel shapes.
Dissolve the baking soda in hot water in a wide bowl, and dip each pretzel into the solution for 30 seconds.
Place on the baking sheet, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake for 12-15 minutes until deep golden brown.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt.
Place the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow bowls.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets until golden brown on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve hot garnished with lemon wedges.

instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté the onions until translucent.

Pour in the beer and bring to a simmer.
Prick the bratwurst sausages with a fork and nestle them into the sauerkraut mixture.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the sausages are cooked through.
Serve the bratwurst in bread rolls topped with sauerkraut and mustard.

title: Bavarian Soft Pretzels (Brezen)
instructions: Mix warm water, yeast, and sugar in a bowl and let sit until frothy.
Add flour, melted butter, and salt; knead into a smooth dough.
Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Dissolve baking soda in boiling water in a shallow bowl.
Divide dough into 6 pieces, roll into ropes, and shape into pretzels.
Dip each pretzel into the baking soda solution for 30 seconds, then place on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle with coarse sea salt and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until dark golden brown.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk together the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold into the batter along with the rum-soaked raisins.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan.

Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum compote.

instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy-bottomed pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard it.

Toss the grated Gruyere and Emmental cheeses with the cornstarch.

Stir in the kirschwasser and a pinch of nutmeg.
Transfer the pot to a tabletop burner and serve immediately with cubed baguette for dipping.

Slice beef and serve with the gravy.

title: Authentic Swiss Fondue

instructions: Rub the inside of a heavy pot with the halved garlic clove, then discard.
Pour wine and lemon juice into the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch.
Gradually add cheese to the simmering wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight pattern until melted and smooth.
Stir in kirsch and a pinch of nutmeg.
Place the pot over a portable burner and serve immediately with baguette cubes for dipping.

instructions: Whisk egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt together until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.

Cook bacon in a skillet until crisp, remove bacon, and leave the drippings in the pan.
Sauté the chopped onion in the bacon drippings until translucent.
Whisk beef broth, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and pepper into the onion mixture and bring to a warm simmer.
Pour the warm dressing over the sliced potatoes, toss gently, and let sit for 30 minutes to absorb.
Garnish with crispy bacon and fresh parsley before serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in beaten eggs, and finally coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on both sides, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Kasespatzle
ingredients: 2 cups grated Gruyere or Emmental cheese
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, sparkling water, and salt into a thick dough, beating until bubbles form.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then press or drop the dough into the water.
Remove the spatzle with a slotted spoon as soon as they float to the surface.
Sauté the sliced onions in butter until caramelized.
Layer the hot spatzle and grated cheese in a warm dish, topping with caramelized onions and parsley before serving.

title: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
ingredients: 2 cups fermented sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet and sauté the sliced onion until soft.
Add the sauerkraut and beer to the skillet, bringing it to a simmer.
Prick the bratwursts with a fork and nestle them into the sauerkraut.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, then uncover to let the liquid reduce.
Serve the bratwurst and sauerkraut hot with mustard and pretzels.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 1 sheet store-bought puff pastry or strudel dough
4 tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs over the dough, leaving a small border.
Toss the sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon, and raisins, then arrange them over the breadcrumbs.
Roll the dough tightly around the filling, seal the edges, and brush the top with melted butter.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown, then dust with powdered sugar before slicing.

title: Kartoffelpuffer
ingredients: 4 large starchy potatoes, peeled and grated
instructions: Place the grated potatoes and onion in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible.
In a bowl, combine the squeezed potato mixture with the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the potato mixture into the hot oil, flattening them into patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crispy and golden brown, then drain on paper towels.

title: Berner Platte
ingredients: 500 g dried green beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Cook the soaked beans in fresh water with the onion, bay leaves, and juniper berries until tender.
In a separate large pot, simmer the meats (except the sausage) in water for about 1.5 hours.
Add the fresh pork sausage during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Arrange the meats, beans, and potatoes on a large warmed platter and serve hot.

title: Zurcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 600 g veal tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and freshly ground white pepper
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet and brown the veal strips quickly over high heat, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the onion and mushrooms until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and stir well.
Deglaze the pan with white wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the veal and its juices to the sauce, season with salt and pepper, heat through without boiling, and garnish with parsley.

title: Traditional Berner Zopf
ingredients: 1 egg yolk mixed with 1 tbsp milk for brushing
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the center.
Dissolve yeast and sugar in lukewarm milk, then pour into the well.
Add softened butter and knead everything for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into two equal pieces and braid each into a loaf.
Place on a baking sheet, brush with the egg yolk mixture, and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Älplermagronen
instructions: Boil the potatoes and macaroni together in salted water until tender, then drain.
In a large pot, combine the cooked mixture with heavy cream, broth, and half of the grated cheese.
Stir gently over low heat until the cheese melts and creates a creamy sauce; season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Fry the onion slices in butter until golden and crispy.
Serve the macaroni topped with the remaining cheese and crispy fried onions, traditionally with applesauce on the side.

title: Basler Flour Soup
ingredients: 100 g Gruyere or Sbrinz cheese, grated
instructions: Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed pot and add the flour.
Sauté the flour and chopped onions over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until both are deeply browned and nutty in aroma.
Slowly whisk in the warm broth to prevent lumps.
Simmer the soup on low heat for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Ladle into bowls and serve generously topped with grated cheese.

title: Schweinsbraten mit Knödel
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Rub pork with salt, pepper, and caraway seeds.
Place pork in a roasting pan with onions, carrots, and celery.
Pour in 1 cup of beer and roast for 2 hours, basting occasionally and adding more beer as needed.
Increase oven temperature to 400 degrees F for the last 30 minutes to crisp the crackling.
For the dumplings, soak bread cubes in warm milk.
Mix soaked bread with eggs, parsley, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt, then shape into balls.
Simmer dumplings in salted water for 20 minutes until they float.
Slice the roast and serve with the pan gravy and dumplings.

title: Bayerischer Kartoffelsalat
instructions: Boil potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender.
Drain, let cool slightly, peel while still warm, and slice into thin rounds.
In a bowl, whisk warm beef broth, vinegar, oil, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the warm potato slices and gently mix.
Fold in the diced onions.
Let the salad rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Garnish with freshly chopped chives before serving.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Soak raisins in rum for 15 minutes.
Whisk egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, and salt together until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites and rum-soaked raisins into the batter.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces using two forks.
Cook for another 2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve hot with apple compote or plum roasted fruit.

title: Obatzda
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Mash the soft Camembert, cream cheese, and butter together in a bowl with a fork until well combined but still slightly chunky.
Mix in the minced onion, paprika, caraway seeds, and beer.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving dish and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Serve cold with freshly baked soft pretzels and sliced radishes.

title: Bayerische Leberkäsesemmel
ingredients: 1 lb Bavarian Leberkäse loaf, sliced thick
4 crusty bread rolls or Kaiser rolls
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the thick Leberkäse slices for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until a dark, crispy crust forms.
Slice the bread rolls in half.
Spread a generous amount of sweet mustard on the bottom half of each roll.
Place a hot slice of fried Leberkäse inside each roll.
Top with the upper half of the roll and serve immediately while hot.

title: Königsberger Klopse
ingredients: 1 stale bread roll, soaked in milk and squeezed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Mix the meat, soaked bread roll, onion, and egg in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Form small meatballs with wet hands.
Bring the beef broth to a simmer with the bay leaves and allspice berries.
Drop the meatballs into the simmering broth and poach for about 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Melt the butter in a separate saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for a minute to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in 500ml of the strained meat broth and the cream, simmering until thickened.
Stir in the capers and season the sauce with salt, pepper, and a splash of lemon juice.
Return the meatballs to the sauce to heat through before serving.

title: Berliner Kartoffelsuppe
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and diced
2 pairs of Frankfurter or Wiener sausages, sliced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and sauté the leek, carrots, and celery root for 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and pour in the broth.
Add the bay leaves, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes until all vegetables are soft.
Remove the bay leaves and mash some of the soup with a potato masher to achieve a thick, rustic consistency.
Add the sliced sausages and let them heat through in the soup for 5 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of freshly grated nutmeg.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

title: Eisbein mit Sauerkraut und Erbspüree
instructions: Place the pork knuckles in a large pot, cover with water, and add the studded onion, bay leaves, and juniper berries.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for about 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
In a separate pot, cook the soaked split yellow peas in salted water until soft, then mash them into a smooth purée with butter, salt, and pepper.
In another pot, heat the lard and gently warm the sauerkraut for about 30 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
Serve the tender pork knuckle alongside the warm sauerkraut and yellow pea purée with mustard.

title: Buletten mit Gurkensalat
ingredients: 1 stale bread roll, soaked in water and squeezed
2 tbsp butter or lard for frying
instructions: Mix the ground beef, squeezed bread roll, egg, minced onion, and mustard in a bowl. Season well with salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture into flattened round patties (Buletten).
Melt the butter or lard in a skillet over medium heat and fry the patties for about 5 to 7 minutes on each side until browned and cooked through.
For the salad, toss the sliced cucumbers with salt and let rest for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Whisk together vinegar, oil, sugar, salt, and pepper to make a dressing.
Toss the cucumbers with the dressing and chopped dill, and serve alongside the hot Buletten.

title: Berliner Pfannkuchen
ingredients: 42g fresh yeast (or 2 packets active dry yeast)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and a pinch of sugar in the lukewarm milk.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, remaining sugar, salt, lemon zest, butter, egg yolks, and the yeast milk.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough to about 1.5 cm thickness and cut out circles using a glass or round cutter.
Cover the circles and let them rise again for 30 minutes.
Heat the frying oil in a large pot to 175°C (350°F).
Fry the dough rounds in batches for about 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown with a distinct white ring in the middle.
Remove, drain on paper towels, and while still warm, fill a piping bag with jam and inject it into the side of each pastry.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the beef in a mixture of vinegar, broth, sliced vegetables, and spices for 4 to 5 days in the refrigerator.
Remove the meat from the marinade, pat dry, and season with salt and pepper.
Sear the meat in a Dutch oven with butter on all sides until browned.
Strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Add the vegetables and marinade to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, stir the crumbled gingerbread and raisins into the sauce to thicken, and season to taste.
Slice the beef and serve with the rich gravy, potato dumplings, and red cabbage.

title: Himmel un Äd (Heaven and Earth)
ingredients: 1 kg tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
Salt, pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
In a separate pot, cook the apple slices with a splash of water until soft, then mash them coarsely.
Drain the potatoes, mash them with butter and warm milk, and season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Gently fold the apple mash into the potato mash to create the 'Heaven and Earth' mixture.
Dust the onion slices with flour and fry them in vegetable oil until crispy and golden brown.
Fry the blood sausage slices in a pan over medium heat until warm and slightly crispy.
Serve the potato and apple mash topped with the warm blood sausage and crispy fried onions.

title: Rheinische Rinderrouladen
ingredients: 4 large beef cutlets, cut thin from the round
3 large dill pickles, cut lengthwise into strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Lay the beef cutlets flat on a board and pound them slightly to an even thickness.
Spread each cutlet generously with mustard, then layer with bacon slices, pickle strips, and some chopped onion.
Roll up the cutlets tightly, tucking in the sides, and secure them with kitchen twine or toothpicks.
Season the outside of the roulades with salt and pepper.
Brown the roulades on all sides in a Dutch oven with melted butter.
Add the remaining onions, pour in the beef stock and red wine, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours.
Remove the twine, thicken the pan juices with a little cornstarch if desired, and serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Rheinischer Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: 150 g good quality Bockwurst or Vienna sausages
3 tbsp gherkin liquid from the jar
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender, drain, and let them cool completely.
Peel the cooled potatoes and cut them into bite-sized cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, gherkin liquid, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
Add the diced gherkins and onions to the dressing.
Gently fold in the potato cubes until they are evenly coated.
Slice the sausages into rounds and gently mix them into the salad.
Let the salad rest in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before garnishing with chopped parsley and serving.

title: Möhrenuntereinander (Carrot and Potato Stew)
ingredients: Salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste
instructions: Place the carrots and potatoes in a large pot and pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes until tender.
Drain any excess liquid, reserving a little on the side just in case.
Add the butter and warm milk, then mash everything together coarsely with a potato masher.
Season generously with salt, pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg.
Prick the Mettwurst sausages with a fork, submerge them in the stew, and heat through for 10 minutes.
Serve the hearty carrot and potato mash in deep bowls with one warm sausage per portion and a sprinkle of parsley.

title: Swabian Maultaschen
ingredients: 1 stale bread roll, soaked in milk and squeezed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Mix the ground pork, chopped spinach, squeezed bread roll, diced onion, eggs, and parsley in a large bowl.
Season the filling generously with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Roll out the pasta dough into long rectangles on a floured surface.
Place spoonfuls of the filling along the lower half of the dough at intervals.
Fold the upper half of the dough over the filling and press down the edges.
Cut between the mounds to separate the individual Maultaschen and press the edges firmly sealed.
Simmer the Maultaschen in hot beef broth for about 10 to 15 minutes until they float.
Serve them hot either directly in the broth or browned in a pan with butter and caramelized onions.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, salt, and enough lukewarm water in a bowl to form a thick, bubbly dough that drops heavily from a wooden spoon without tearing.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Scrape portions of the dough off a wet board into the boiling water, or use a Spätzle press.
Remove the Spätzle with a slotted spoon as soon as they float to the surface and drain them.
Fry the sliced onions in butter in a large skillet over medium heat until golden brown and crispy, then set aside.
Layer the warm Spätzle and grated cheese in a preheated casserole dish, finishing with a layer of cheese.
Cover the dish briefly to let the cheese melt from the residual heat.
Top with the crispy fried onions and freshly ground black pepper before serving.

title: Flädlesuppe
instructions: Whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, and salt in a bowl to create a smooth, thin pancake batter.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Ladle in thin layers of the batter and cook until light golden on both sides to make thin crêpes.
Roll up the cooled crêpes tightly and slice them crosswise into thin strips (Flädle).
Bring the clear beef broth to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Distribute the sliced pancake strips evenly into warm soup bowls.
Ladle the hot beef broth over the Flädle.
Garnish with freshly chopped chives and serve immediately.

title: Linsen mit Spätzle
instructions: Rinse the lentils and set them aside.
Melt the butter in a pot and sauté the diced onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir well to create a light roux.
Deglaze with the broth and add the lentils to the pot.
Simmer on low heat for about 30 to 40 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the red wine vinegar and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat the Wiener sausages gently in hot water without boiling.
Serve the hot lentils alongside freshly prepared Spätzle and top with the sausages.

title: Swabian Potato Salad
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Boil the unpeeled potatoes in salted water until fork-tender.
Drain the hot potatoes, peel them while still warm, and slice them thinly into a large bowl.
Pour the warm beef broth over the sliced potatoes and let them absorb the liquid for 10 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, sunflower oil, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the potatoes and mix gently to avoid breaking them too much.
Fold in the chopped onion and fresh chives.
Let the potato salad rest at room temperature for at least an hour before serving so the flavors develop.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 150g each, pounded thin
Lard or clarified butter for frying
instructions: Season the veal cutlets lightly with salt.
Place the flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow bowls.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off the excess, dip into the egg, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs without pressing them down.
Heat a generous amount of lard or clarified butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown on one side, then flip and fry the other side, constantly spooning hot fat over the crust.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Tafelspitz
ingredients: 1 kg beef rump or top round (Tafelspitz cut)
3 leeks, washed and cut into large pieces
1 onion, cut in half with skin on
instructions: Place the beef in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Add the leeks, carrots, celery root, unpeeled onion halved, a few peppercorns, and salt.
Reduce heat and simmer gently for about 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
For the apple horseradish sauce, grate the apples and mix with freshly grated horseradish, a pinch of salt, and a splash of broth.
Slice the tender beef against the grain and serve in warm soup bowls with the strained broth, root vegetables, and the apple-horseradish sauce.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with milk, flour, vanilla sugar, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites with the sugar until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the yolk batter.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat, pour in the batter, and scatter the rum-soaked raisins over the top.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip the pancake and tear it into bite-sized pieces using two forks.
Stir until all pieces are golden and cooked through, dust with powdered sugar, and serve warm.

title: Erdäpfelgulasch
ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat lard in a pot and sauté the chopped onions slowly until they are deeply golden brown.
Remove the pot from heat, stir in the sweet paprika powder and caraway seeds, and immediately pour in the broth.
Add the diced potatoes and bring to a simmer.
Season with salt, pepper, and vinegar, then cover and cook for about 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a few potato pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.
Add the sliced sausages, heat through for 5 minutes, and serve hot.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 1 package store-bought strudel dough or filo pastry
1 kg tart apples (like Granny Smith), peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sauté the breadcrumbs in a tablespoon of melted butter until lightly golden.
In a large bowl, mix the sliced apples, sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and slivered almonds.
Roll out the strudel dough on a clean kitchen towel, brush with melted butter, and sprinkle with the toasted breadcrumbs.
Distribute the apple mixture evenly over the lower half of the dough.
Using the kitchen towel to help you, roll the strudel tightly, tucking in the ends.
Place seam-side down on the baking sheet, brush with remaining butter, and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Tyrolean Knödel (Tiroler Knödel)
ingredients: 250 g stale bread, cut into small cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a pan and gently sauté the diced bacon and chopped onion until translucent.
In a large bowl, combine the bread cubes with the warm milk, eggs, parsley, salt, and pepper. Let it soak for 10 minutes.
Add the sautéed bacon, onions, and flour to the bowl, then mix everything thoroughly with your hands.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into firm, round dumplings.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, add the dumplings, and cook for about 15 minutes until they float.
Remove the dumplings with a slotted spoon and serve hot in bowls with warm beef broth.

title: Tyrolean Gröstl (Tiroler Gröstl)
