ingredients: 500 g boiled potatoes from the previous day, peeled and sliced
200 g Tyrolean bacon (Speck) or leftover roast pork, diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the lard or butter in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the diced bacon and sliced onions, cooking until the onions are golden and the bacon renders its fat.
Add the sliced potatoes and crushed caraway seeds to the skillet, spreading them out evenly.
Fry the mixture, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes develop a nice, crispy golden crust.
Season with salt, pepper, and chopped marjoram.
Make four small wells in the hash and crack an egg into each one. Cover the skillet and cook until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Garnish with chopped chives and serve directly from the pan.

title: Schlipfkrapfen
ingredients: Warm water as needed for the dough
300 g starchy potatoes, boiled and riced
100 g grayish mountain cheese (Bergkäse) or curd cheese, grated
instructions: Mix flour, egg, oil, salt, and enough warm water to knead into a smooth, elastic pasta dough. Let it rest for 30 minutes.
Sauté the minced onion in butter until soft. Mix it with the warm riced potatoes, cheese, chives, salt, and pepper to create the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut out circles using a round cutter.
Place a small spoonful of filling onto each circle, fold over into a half-moon shape, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Cook the pockets in gently simmering salted water for about 5 minutes until they rise to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon, plate them up, and drizzle generously with hot brown butter.

title: Tyrolean Cheese Dumplings (Kaiserschmarren)
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, milk, flour, vanilla sugar, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl until smooth.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites with the granulated sugar until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the yolk batter, adding the rum-soaked raisins if desired.
Melt the butter in a large, heavy skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip the pancake in sections using two spatulas.
Tear the pancake apart into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan and sauté briefly until golden and cooked through.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve hot alongside warm stewed plums.

title: Tyrolean Speckknödel Soup
ingredients: 4 small cooked Tyrolean Speckknödel (bread and bacon dumplings)
instructions: Bring the rich beef bouillon to a gentle simmer in a large pot.
Add the julienned carrots, sliced leek, and diced celery to the broth.
Simmer the vegetables in the soup for about 10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Gently place the pre-cooked Speckknödel into the simmering broth to heat them through for 5 minutes.
Ladle the hot soup into deep bowls, ensuring each bowl gets one warm dumpling.
Generously sprinkle fresh chives over the top before serving.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500 g veal tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Pat the veal strips dry with paper towels and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a heavy skillet over high heat and quickly sear the veal in batches for about 1-2 minutes until just browned. Remove the meat and set aside.
In the same pan, melt the remaining butter and sauté the shallots and mushrooms until tender.
Sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms and stir well to combine.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in the heavy cream and lemon zest, letting the sauce simmer until it thickens slightly.
Return the veal and any accumulated juices to the sauce, warm through for 1 minute without boiling.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Zürcher Zopf
ingredients: 1 egg yolk mixed with 1 tbsp milk for brushing
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt together, making a well in the center.
Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm milk, pour into the well, and let rest for 10 minutes.
Add the soft butter and knead the mixture for about 10 minutes until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into two equal pieces, then roll each into long strands.
Braid the two strands together into a traditional loaf and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cover and let rise for another 30 minutes, then brush the top with the egg yolk and milk mixture.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200°C for about 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Traditional Bärli-Biber
instructions: In a small saucepan, gently heat the honey, sugar, and water until the sugar is fully dissolved, then let it cool until lukewarm.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves, ground almonds, and salt.
Pour the honey mixture into the dry ingredients and knead until a smooth dough forms.
Divide the dough in half. Roll out one half to fit a square baking pan lined with parchment paper.
Roll out the marzipan between two sheets of plastic wrap and place it on top of the first dough layer.
Roll out the second half of the dough and place it over the marzipan layer, pressing down gently.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Brush the warm cake with a little kirsch and let it cool completely before slicing into squares.

title: Basler Mehlsuppe
ingredients: 1 liter good beef or vegetable broth
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add the dark brown flour and stir constantly until the flour turns a deep brown color and smells nutty, about 10 minutes.
Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent.
Slowly pour in the warm broth while whisking vigorously to prevent any lumps from forming.
Reduce the heat and simmer the soup gently for about 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and serve generously topped with grated Gruyère cheese.

title: Chäschüchli
ingredients: 1 sheet of shortcrust pastry or puff pastry
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C and grease small tartlet molds.
Roll out the pastry and cut circles to fit the molds, pressing them gently into the bottom and sides.
Prick the bottoms of the pastry crusts lightly with a fork.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.
Mix the Gruyère and Emmental cheeses together and distribute evenly among the pastry-lined molds.
Pour the egg and cream mixture over the cheese in each mold.
Bake in the oven for 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is set and golden brown on top.
Let cool for a few minutes before removing from the molds and serving warm.

title: Berner Platte
instructions: Soak the dried white beans in cold water overnight, then drain.
Place the beans in a large pot with fresh water, the studded onions, leeks, and bouquet garni. Simmer until tender, about 1.5 hours.
In a separate large pot, gently simmer the smoked pork loin, bacon, and cured beef tongue for about 1.5 to 2 hours until tender.
Add the fresh pork sausage during the last 30 minutes of cooking the meats.
In another pot, prepare or reheat the sauerkraut, and boil the potatoes until tender.
Slice the meats and arrange them on a large warmed platter alongside the beans, potatoes, and sauerkraut, serving hot.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes with Rösti
ingredients: 600 g veal fillet, cut into thin strips
Salt and freshly ground white pepper
1 kg starchy potatoes, boiled in skins the day before
3 tbsp lard or clarified butter for the Rösti
instructions: Peel the cold boiled potatoes and coarse-grate them into a bowl.

Melt lard in a large non-stick skillet, add the grated potatoes, and press them into a flat cake. Fry over medium heat until golden brown on the bottom, about 15 minutes, then flip and fry the other side.
For the veal, heat butter in a pan and quickly sear the veal strips on high heat for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the shallot and sliced mushrooms until golden.
Dust the mushroom mixture with flour, stir well, and pour in the white wine and heavy cream. Simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the veal and its juices to the sauce, season with salt and white pepper, and heat through without boiling.
Serve the creamy veal immediately alongside slices of the hot crispy Rösti.

title: Älplermagronen
ingredients: 400 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cubed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for about 5 minutes, then add the macaroni pasta and cook together until both are tender. Drain well.
Return the pasta and potatoes to the warm pot, stir in the heavy cream and grated Gruyère cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
In a skillet, melt the butter and fry the sliced onions slowly until they are caramelized and crispy.
Transfer the cheesy macaroni and potatoes to a warm serving dish and top generously with the crispy caramelized onions.
Serve hot with a side of cold applesauce.

title: Bündner Röteli-marinated Pear Tart
ingredients: 4 firm pears, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) and grease a round tart pan with butter.
Roll out the puff pastry and fit it into the tart pan, poking the base lightly with a fork.
Toss the pear slices in the Bündner Röteli liqueur and let them marinate for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, sugar, ground almonds, lemon zest, and melted butter until smooth.
Spread the almond cream evenly over the puff pastry base.
Arrange the marinated pear slices in a neat circular pattern over the cream.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is set. Let cool before serving.

title: Berner Zibelechueche (Onion Tart)
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a round baking pan with the pie crust and prick the bottom with a fork.
Melt the butter in a large pan and sauté the sliced onions (and diced bacon, if using) on low heat until soft and translucent, but not browned, about 20 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk together the sour cream, eggs, flour, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Stir the soft onions into the sour cream mixture until well combined.
Pour the onion filling evenly into the prepared pastry crust.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the filling is set and the top is golden brown. Serve warm.

title: Bayerischer Schweinsbraten
instructions: Score the pork rind in a diamond pattern using a sharp knife.
Rub the meat generously with salt, pepper, crushed garlic, and caraway seeds.
Place the pork in a roasting pan, rind side down, and add the vegetables and 1 cup of beer around it.
Roast in a preheated oven at 350 degrees F for about 1.5 hours, basting occasionally.
Flip the roast so the rind is on top, pour the remaining beer and broth over the pan, and roast for another 1.5 hours until the rind is crispy.
Remove the meat, strain the pan juices to make a rich gravy, and serve sliced with dumplings.

title: Kartoffelknödel
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain, peel immediately, and press through a potato ricer while hot.
Let the riced potatoes cool slightly, then add the potato starch, egg yolks, salt, and nutmeg.
Knead the mixture gently until it forms a smooth dough.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the bread cubes until golden brown to make croutons.
Shape portions of the dough into balls, pressing a few croutons into the center of each.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, drop the dumplings in, and cook for 20 minutes without letting the water boil.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, and salt together in a bowl until smooth.
In a separate clean bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the soaked raisins.
Melt the butter in a large heavy skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip the large pancake in sections.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces right in the pan.
Sauté for another minute until caramelized, then dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Obatzda
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Mash the softened Camembert, cream cheese, and butter together in a bowl using a fork until well combined but still retaining some texture.
Stir in the minced white onion, paprika, caraway seeds, and wheat beer.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, mixing thoroughly.
Cover and let the spread rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Serve chilled with fresh radishes, chives, and warm soft pretzels.

title: Bayerischer Leberkäse
instructions: Place the ground pork and beef into a food processor along with the crushed ice and process until a very smooth, sticky paste is formed.
Transfer the meat paste to a bowl and fold in the curing salt, white pepper, mace, coriander, grated onion, and marjoram.
Grease a loaf pan thoroughly and pack the meat mixture firmly into the pan, smoothing the top.
Use a wet knife to score a diagonal diamond pattern across the top of the loaf.
Bake in a preheated oven at 325 degrees F for about 1 hour and 15 minutes until a dark golden crust forms.
Slice thick and serve warm with sweet Bavarian mustard and a crusty roll.

title: Königsberger Klopse
ingredients: 500 g ground pork and beef mix
1 stale bread roll, soaked in water and squeezed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Mix the ground meat, soaked bread roll, diced onion, egg, chopped capers, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Form small meatballs with wet hands.
Bring the beef broth to a simmer with the bay leaves and allspice berries.
Drop the meatballs into the simmering broth and poach for about 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Strain 500 ml of the cooking broth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for a minute to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in the strained broth and heavy cream, bringing it to a gentle boil while stirring.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes, then stir in the whole capers and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper, return the meatballs to the sauce to warm through, and serve with boiled potatoes.

title: Berliner Kartoffelsuppe
ingredients: 1 kg starchy potatoes, peeled and diced
2 pairs of traditional German Frankfurter sausages
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and sauté the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the diced potatoes, carrots, celery root, and leek to the pot, stirring for a few minutes.
Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Mash about half of the soup with a potato masher to achieve a thick, rustic consistency while leaving some chunks.
Slice the sausages and add them to the soup to heat through for 5 minutes.
Season generously with salt, pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with freshly chopped parsley.

title: Eisbein mit Sauerkraut und Erbspüree
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Soak the split peas in water overnight, then drain.
Place the pork knuckles in a large pot, cover with water, and add the halved onion, carrots, celery stalk, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
In a separate pot, cook the soaked split peas with fresh water and diced bacon until soft, then mash into a smooth puree and season with salt and pepper.
In another pot, heat the sauerkraut with a little of the pork broth for 30 minutes until tender.
Remove the pork knuckles from the broth and optionally crisp them up in the oven at 200 degrees Celsius for 15 minutes.
Serve the Eisbein hot alongside the sauerkraut, pea puree, and boiled potatoes.

title: Buletten mit Gurkensalat
ingredients: 500 g ground beef and pork mix
1 stale bread roll, soaked in milk and squeezed
2 tbsp lard or vegetable oil for frying
150 g sour cream or plain yogurt
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Combine the sliced cucumber with a pinch of salt in a bowl and let sit for 15 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture.
Whisk the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, dill, salt, and pepper together in a bowl, then toss with the cucumbers to make the gurkensalat.
In a large bowl, mix the ground meat, squeezed bread roll, minced onion, egg, mustard, salt, and pepper thoroughly.
Shape the meat mixture into thick, slightly flattened patties with your hands.
Heat the lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the buletten for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until nicely browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with the chilled cucumber salad and mustard.

title: Kartoffelpuffer mit Apfelmus
ingredients: A pinch of freshly ground black pepper
1 jar or homemade batch of sweet apple sauce (Apfelmus)
instructions: Grate the peeled raw potatoes and the onion using the fine side of a box grater.
Transfer the grated potato and onion mixture to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible into a bowl.
Let the liquid sit for a minute so the potato starch settles to the bottom, then pour off the water and add the recovered starch back to the potatoes.
Add the egg, flour, salt, and pepper to the potato mixture and stir well to combine.
Heat a generous amount of sunflower oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the potato mixture into the hot pan, flattening them slightly to form thin patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with sweet apple sauce.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
ingredients: 4 slices Aachener Printen (or dark gingerbread), crumbled
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, sliced vegetables, and spices in a pot, bring to a boil, and let cool completely.
Submerge the beef in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for 4 to 5 days, turning daily.
Remove the meat from the marinade, pat dry, and season with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven and sear the meat on all sides until browned.
Strain the marinade, reserving the liquid and vegetables.
Add the vegetables to the pot and sauté briefly, then pour in the reserved marinade.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, stir the crumbled Printen and raisins into the sauce, and simmer until thickened.
Slice the beef, return to the sauce to warm through, and serve hot.

title: Himmel un Äd (Heaven and Earth)
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
500 kg tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
200 g black pudding (Blutwurst), sliced into thick rounds
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes; drain well.
In a separate pot, cook the apple slices with a splash of water until soft, then mash coarsely.
Mash the potatoes with butter and warm milk until smooth, season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Gently fold the apple mash into the potato mash to create the classic 'Heaven and Earth' mixture.
Heat oil in a skillet and fry the onion slices until crispy and golden brown; set aside.
In the same skillet, fry the black pudding slices on medium heat until heated through and slightly crisp.
Serve the potato and apple mash topped with the fried black pudding and crispy onions.

title: Rheinische Rievkooche (Potato Fritters)
ingredients: A generous pinch of ground nutmeg
Applesauce or dark pumpernickel bread for serving
instructions: Finely grate the raw potatoes and the onion using a box grater or food processor.
Transfer the grated potato and onion mixture to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and add the eggs, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg; mix well.
Heat a generous amount of sunflower oil in a large heavy-bottomed frying pan over medium-high heat.
Drop large spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and flatten them slightly with a spatula.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess oil and serve hot with applesauce.

title: Rheinische Erbsensuppe (Split Pea Soup)
ingredients: 500 g dried green split peas, rinsed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley for garnish
instructions: Place the rinsed split peas in a large pot with the broth and bay leaves, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for about 45 minutes until the peas start to break down.
Add the diced carrots, leeks, celery root, and potatoes to the pot.
Add the diced Kassler into the soup and continue simmering for another 30 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Slice the Mettwurst sausages and add them to the soup for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Remove the bay leaves, season with salt and pepper to taste, and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten-Style Pot Roast with Makkaroni
instructions: Season the beef roast with salt and pepper on all sides.
Melt butter in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onions in the same pot until translucent.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, apple cider vinegar, and beef broth.
Return the beef to the pot, add the bay leaves and juniper berries, cover, and simmer on low for 2 hours.
Cook the macaroni pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; drain.
Remove the cooked beef from the pot and slice.
Whisk flour with a little cold water, stir into the pan juices, and simmer until thickened to make a rich gravy.
Serve the sliced beef and gravy over the cooked macaroni.

title: Swabian Maultaschen
ingredients: 2 stale breadrolls, soaked in milk and squeezed
Salt, pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg to taste
Butter and roasted onions for garnishing
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, salt, and water to form a smooth pasta dough. Knead well and let rest for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the ground meats, chopped onion, parsley, spinach, soaked bread, and the extra egg. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Roll out the pasta dough into long, thin rectangles.
Place spoonfuls of the meat filling at even intervals along the lower half of the dough.
Fold the upper half of the dough over the filling, press down around the filling to seal, and cut into individual rectangles.
Simmer the Maultaschen in hot beef broth for about 10 to 12 minutes until they float.
Serve hot in the broth or remove, slice, and pan-fry with butter and roasted onions.

title: Kässpätzle
instructions: In a large bowl, beat the flour, eggs, salt, and sparkling water vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough bubbles and drops heavily from the spoon.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Scrape portions of the dough into the boiling water using a Spätzle press or board. When they float to the top, remove them with a slotted spoon.
Preheat an oven to 100°C (210°F).
In a warm baking dish, layer the hot Spätzle and grated cheese, finishing with a final layer of cheese.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the onion rings until golden brown and crispy.
Top the layered Spätzle with the crispy onions and black pepper, cover briefly to melt the cheese, and serve immediately.

title: Linsen mit Spätzle und Saitenwürstle
ingredients: Freshly made Spätzle (prepared from 400g flour and 4 eggs)
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and sauté the diced bacon, onion, carrots, and root parsley until soft.
Add the flour to create a light roux, stirring constantly.
Add the rinsed lentils and pour in the stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 35 to 40 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Season the lentils with salt, pepper, and vinegar to taste for that traditional slight tang.
Prepare the fresh Spätzle according to standard method.
Warm the Saitenwürstle gently in hot water without boiling them.
Serve the lentils hot, accompanied by the fresh Spätzle and the sausages on the side.

title: Flädlesuppe
instructions: Whisk together flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt to form a smooth, thin pancake batter. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a little butter in a small frying pan and ladle in thin layers of batter, cooking thin pancakes (Flädle) on both sides until golden. Repeat for all batter.
Roll up the cooled pancakes tightly and slice them crosswise into thin strips (Flädlesstreifen).
Heat the clear beef broth in a pot until simmering.
Distribute the sliced pancake strips into serving bowls.
Ladle the hot beef broth over the pancake strips and garnish generously with chopped chives before serving.

title: Zwiebelrostbraten
ingredients: 4 thick beef ribeye or sirloin steaks (approx. 250g each)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 large onions, sliced into thin rings
instructions: Pat the steaks dry, season with salt and pepper, and lightly brush one side with mustard.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the steaks to your desired doneness. Remove and keep warm in a low oven.
In the same pan, reduce heat, add butter, and fry the onion rings until deeply caramelized and crispy. Remove half of the onions for garnish.
Dust the remaining onions in the pan with flour and paprika, then pour in the red wine and beef stock.
Simmer the sauce until thickened and rich, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the steaks and their resting juices to the sauce for a minute to warm through.
Serve the steaks smothered in the rich onion gravy, topped with the reserved crispy onions, alongside Spätzle or fried potatoes.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 veal cutlets, about 150g each, pounded thin
Lard or clarified butter for frying
instructions: Season the veal cutlets lightly with salt.
Place flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow bowls.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off excess, dip in the beaten egg, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs without pressing them down.
Heat a generous amount of lard or clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side, swirling the pan occasionally.
Remove, drain on paper towels, and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Tafelspitz
ingredients: 1 kg beef rump or tender brisket (Tafelspitz)
1 large onion, cut in half with skin on
Chive sauce and apple horseradish for serving
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot, then add the beef.
Skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Add the halved onion (cut side charred in a dry pan first for color), carrots, celery root, leek, parsley root, peppercorns, bay leaf, and salt.
Reduce heat and simmer gently for about 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Slice the beef against the grain and serve in warm bowls with the strained broth, boiled potatoes, chive sauce, and apple horseradish.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla sugar, and salt together into a smooth batter.
In a separate bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter along with the raisins.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Using two forks, tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces directly in the pan.
Sprinkle with a little extra sugar and let it caramelize briefly, then dust with powdered sugar and serve hot with stewed plums.

title: Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: 1 kg waxy potatoes, boiled in their skins
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Peel the boiled potatoes while still warm and slice them evenly into a bowl.
Pour the warm beef broth over the sliced potatoes and let them absorb it for 10 minutes.
Whisk together the vinegar, sunflower oil, mustard, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the potatoes, add the diced onion, and gently toss to combine without breaking the potato slices.
Let the salad rest for at least an hour at room temperature before serving.
Garnish with freshly chopped chives right before serving.

title: Grießnockerlsuppe
instructions: Cream the softened butter in a bowl until fluffy, then beat in the egg, salt, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Stir in the fine wheat semolina until well combined.
Let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for 20 minutes so the semolina can swell.
Bring the clear beef broth to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Dip two teaspoons in hot water, shape oval dumplings (nockerl) from the mixture, and slide them into the simmering broth.
Cover and simmer gently over low heat for about 15 minutes without boiling.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Tyrolean Knödel (Tiroler Knödel)
ingredients: 300 g stale white bread, cut into small cubes
instructions: Melt butter in a pan and gently fry the diced bacon and chopped onion until translucent.
Pour lukewarm milk over the bread cubes in a large bowl and let soak for 10 minutes.
Add the fried bacon and onions, eggs, parsley, flour, salt, and pepper to the bread.
Mix everything thoroughly with your hands and let rest for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and form firm, round dumplings from the mixture.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer and cook the dumplings for about 15 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls filled with clear beef broth.

title: Tyrolean Groestl (Tiroler Groestl)
ingredients: 500 g boiled potatoes from the previous day, peeled and sliced
250 g leftover roast beef or pork, diced
Fresh marjoram and salt to taste
instructions: Melt lard in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced onions and diced bacon, frying until the onions are golden brown.
Add the sliced potatoes and diced meat to the skillet.
Season with salt, crushed caraway seeds, and marjoram.
Fry everything together, stirring frequently, until a nice, crispy brown crust forms on the potatoes.
Make four small wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each one.
Cover the pan and cook until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Garnish with freshly chopped chives and serve directly from the pan.

title: Schlutzkrapfen (Tyrolean Ravioli)
ingredients: 150 g ricotta or dry curd cheese (Topfen)
Melted butter and grated Parmesan cheese for serving
instructions: Mix rye flour, wheat flour, egg, water, olive oil, and salt to form a smooth dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
For the filling, mix the warm riced potatoes, ricotta, sauteed onion, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Roll out the dough very thinly on a floured surface.
Cut out circles using a glass or pastry ring.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over to form a half-moon and press the edges firmly to seal.
Cook the Schlutzkrapfen in simmering salted water for 4 to 5 minutes until they float to the top.
Drain well and serve generously drizzled with melted butter and grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Tyrolean Cheese Dumplings (Kaspressknödel)
ingredients: Beef broth or green salad for serving
instructions: Saute the chopped onion in butter until soft.
In a large bowl, combine the bread cubes, cheeses, sauteed onion, and parsley.
Whisk the warm milk and eggs together, pour over the bread mixture, and season with salt and pepper.
Mix well and let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Form small balls with your hands and press them down firmly into flat patties.
Heat lard in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties until golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 4 minutes per side.
Serve hot either floating in a warm beef broth or alongside a crisp green salad.

title: Tyrolean Apple Kiachl (Apfelkiachl)
ingredients: 3 firm tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced into rings
Lard or vegetable oil for deep frying
instructions: Whisk together flour, milk, egg yolks, sugar, salt, and a splash of rum to create a smooth, thick batter.
Whip the egg whites until stiff and gently fold them into the batter.
Heat plenty of lard or oil in a deep frying pan or pot.
Dip the apple rings into the batter, ensuring they are fully coated.
Carefully drop the battered apple rings into the hot oil.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, flipping once.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Generously dust with cinnamon sugar while still warm and serve immediately.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500 g veal tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and freshly ground white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a skillet over high heat and quickly sear the veal strips until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the shallot and mushrooms until softened.
Dust the vegetables with flour and stir well.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the veal and its juices to the pan, season with salt and pepper, heat through without boiling, and garnish with parsley.

title: Zürcher Tirggel
instructions: Gently warm the honey until it is liquid, then stir in the rose water and spices.
Gradually add the flour and salt, kneading until a smooth, firm dough forms.
Roll out the dough to about 5mm thickness.
Press the dough firmly into traditional wooden Tirggel molds, then trim the edges.
Carefully transfer the shaped dough onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 200°C for about 8 to 10 minutes until lightly golden and completely crisp.

title: Zigerkrapfen
instructions: Mix the Schabziger, ricotta, egg yolk, chives, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Roll out the puff pastry and cut out circles using a round cutter.
Place a small spoonful of the cheese filling in the center of each circle.
Brush the edges with the beaten egg, fold the pastry over to form half-moons, and seal the edges tightly with a fork.
Place the pastries on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush the tops with the remaining egg wash.
Bake at 200°C for 15 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden brown.

title: Birchermuesli
ingredients: 2 tart apples, unpeeled and coarsely grated
instructions: In a bowl, soak the rolled oats in the milk overnight or for at least 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Stir in the condensed milk or yogurt and the lemon juice.
Fold in the freshly grated apples right before serving to prevent browning.
Top with the chopped hazelnuts or almonds and serve chilled.

title: Zürcher Hafechabis
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed pot and brown the pork cubes on all sides.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until translucent.
Layer the chopped cabbage and pork in the pot, sprinkling caraway seeds, salt, and pepper between the layers.
Pour the beef broth over the mixture.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer on low heat for about 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and the cabbage is soft.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and carrot until soft.
Add shredded beets and vinegar, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in beef broth, add potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Add cabbage and tomato paste, then simmer until all vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Traditional Pierogi
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
instructions: Mix flour, water, and egg to form a smooth dough, then let it rest for 20 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes with cheddar cheese, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out the dough and cut into circles using a glass or biscuit cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges to seal.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float to the top, then pan-fry in butter with diced onions until golden.

title: Golubtsi (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head until leaves soften and peel off easily.
In a bowl, mix ground beef, cooked rice, chopped onion, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, roll up tightly, and tuck in the sides.
Arrange the rolls in a large pot, pour tomato sauce and melted butter over them.
Cover and simmer on low heat for about 45 minutes until the meat is fully cooked.

title: Chicken Kiev
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, boneless and skinless
instructions: Mix softened butter, dill, garlic, and a pinch of salt, then shape into small logs and freeze until firm.
Flatten chicken breasts, place a frozen butter log in the center of each, and roll the chicken tightly around it, securing with toothpicks.
Dredge each stuffed chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet and fry the chicken rolls until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to an oven and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes to ensure the chicken is cooked through.

title: Syrniki (Farmer's Cheese Pancakes)
ingredients: 2 cups farmer's cheese or dry cottage cheese
3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: In a bowl, mash the farmer's cheese with a fork until smooth.
Add the egg, sugar, vanilla extract, and flour, mixing well to combine.
Shape the mixture into small patties and coat them lightly with flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties for about 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown, and serve dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and carrot until soft.
Add shredded beets and vinegar, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in beef broth, add potato and cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Stir in tomato paste, reduce heat, and simmer until all vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Traditional Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, water, and egg to form a smooth dough, then let it rest for 20 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes with butter, cheese, salt, and pepper to create the filling.
Roll out the dough and cut into circles using a glass or biscuit cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges to seal.
Boil the pierogi in salted water until they float to the surface, then drain and serve.

title: Golubtsi (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head until leaves soften and peel off easily.
Mix ground meat, cooked rice, half of the chopped onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Sauté the remaining onion and carrot in oil, then mix with tomato sauce.
Layer the cabbage rolls in a pot, pour the tomato sauce over them, cover, and simmer on low for 1 hour.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: Mix softened butter with dill, garlic, salt, and pepper, then shape into two logs and freeze until firm.
Pound chicken breasts thin, place a frozen butter log in the center of each, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, sealing the edges.
Coat each chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep skillet and fry the chicken rolls until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to an oven and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes until fully cooked.

title: Goulash
ingredients: Salt and caraway seeds to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and cook onions until translucent.
Remove pot from heat briefly, stir in paprika and garlic, then add beef cubes.
Return to heat and sear the beef until browned on all sides.
Pour in beef broth, add caraway seeds, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add potatoes and bell pepper, and continue simmering until the vegetables and meat are tender.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Sour cream and fresh dill for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion and carrots until soft.
Add the shredded beets and tomato paste, cooking for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the potatoes and cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Let the soup rest for 15 minutes before serving with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Classic Pierogi with Potato and Cheese
ingredients: 2 cups russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes with shredded cheese, salt, and pepper to create the filling.
Sauté the diced onion in 2 tablespoons of butter until golden brown and mix into the potatoes.
Mix flour and salt in a bowl, add the egg, melted butter, and warm water, then knead into a smooth dough.
Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut into circles using a glass or biscuit cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Drop pierogi into a pot of boiling salted water and cook for 3 minutes after they float to the surface, then remove with a slotted spoon.

title: Golubtsi (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head in salted water until the leaves soften, then peel them off carefully.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, cooked rice, chopped onion, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture into the center of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in a large Dutch oven or deep baking dish.
Mix the tomato sauce, chicken broth, and melted butter together, then pour the mixture evenly over the rolls.
Cover and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 1 hour and 30 minutes until tender.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: In a bowl, mix the softened butter, parsley, minced garlic, and salt, then shape into 4 logs and freeze for 15 minutes.
Pound each chicken breast thin between plastic wrap, place a frozen butter log in the center, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the ends.
Coat each rolled chicken breast in flour, dip in the beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs to coat completely.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken rolls until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) for 20 minutes until fully cooked.

title: Mushroom Goulash
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté the chopped onions until translucent.
Remove the pot from heat briefly and stir in the paprika, then add the sliced mushrooms and red bell pepper.
Return to heat, add the minced garlic, and cook until the mushrooms release their liquids.
Pour in the broth, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, then stir a spoonful of hot broth into the mixture to temper it.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the goulash, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for another 5 minutes until thickened.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a pot and sauté the onion and carrot until soft.
Add the shredded beets and tomato paste, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, add the cubed potatoes and shredded cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Pierogi
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix flour, warm water, egg, and melted butter to form a soft dough, then let it rest for 20 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with shredded cheddar cheese, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or biscuit cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges to seal.
Drop the pierogi into a pot of boiling salted water and cook until they float to the surface.
Drain and toss with butter before serving.

title: Chicken Kiev
ingredients: 2 chicken breast halves, boneless and skinless
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix softened butter, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper, then shape into small logs and freeze until firm.
Pound the chicken breasts flat, place a frozen butter log in the center of each, and roll up tightly, tucking in the edges.
Coat each rolled chicken breast in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken rolls for 5-7 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to an oven and bake at 375 degrees F for 15 minutes to finish cooking through.

title: Goulash
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and caraway seeds to taste
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté the chopped onions until translucent.
Remove the pot from heat temporarily and stir in the paprika and beef cubes.
Return to heat and sear the beef until browned on all sides.
Add minced garlic, caraway seeds, chopped bell pepper, and beef broth.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot.

title: Golubtsi
ingredients: 1 lb ground pork and beef mix
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage head and boil it in a large pot of water until the leaves soften and peel away easily.
In a bowl, combine the ground meat, cooked rice, half of the chopped onion, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides inward, and roll it up tightly.
In a skillet, sauté the remaining onion and grated carrot in vegetable oil until soft, then stir in the tomato sauce.
Arrange the cabbage rolls in a large pot or baking dish, pour the tomato sauce mixture over them, and add the water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the cabbage is tender.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onions and carrots until soft.
Add shredded beets and tomato paste, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Add shredded cabbage, reduce heat, and simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in minced garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Serve hot topped with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Traditional Pierogi
ingredients: 2 cups russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, make a well, and add water, egg, and melted butter.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and let rest for 30 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes with cheddar cheese and salt to create the filling.
Roll out the dough thin and cut into circles using a glass or biscuit cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch edges to seal tightly.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, then pan-fry in butter with diced onions until golden.

title: Chicken Kiev
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix softened butter, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, shape into a log, and freeze until firm.
Pound chicken breasts thin, place a piece of chilled butter mixture in the center of each, and roll tightly to enclose the butter.
Coat each chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Chill the breaded chicken rolls in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep skillet and fry chicken until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes until fully cooked.

title: Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and caraway seeds to taste
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy pot and sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat briefly, stir in paprika and minced garlic, then add beef cubes.
Return to heat and sear the beef until browned on all sides.
Add chopped bell pepper, tomatoes, and enough beef broth to cover the meat.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add cubed potatoes and caraway seeds, cooking for another 20 minutes until potatoes are soft.

title: Cabbage Rolls (Golubtsi)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage head and boil it in a large pot of water until leaves soften and peel off easily.
In a large bowl, mix ground pork, ground beef, cooked rice, chopped onion, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto the base of each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll up tightly.
Layer the cabbage rolls in a large baking dish or Dutch oven.
Whisk together crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, chicken broth, and melted butter, then pour over the rolls.
Cover the dish and bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 1.5 hours until meat is cooked and cabbage is tender.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the shredded beets, carrots, and tomato paste, stirring well, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, add the diced potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add the shredded cabbage, and simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Pierogi with Potato and Cheese
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then mash them thoroughly.
Sauté the diced onion in butter until golden brown, then mix half of it into the potatoes with the cheddar cheese, salt, and pepper.
In a bowl, mix flour and salt, then stir in the egg, warm water, and melted butter to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, roll it out thinly, and cut into circles using a glass or cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop pierogi into a pot of boiling salted water; when they float to the top, cook for 2 more minutes and remove with a slotted spoon.
Pan-fry the boiled pierogi in butter with the remaining onions until golden brown and serve with sour cream.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the softened butter, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper, then shape into a log and freeze for 15 minutes.
Flatten each chicken breast with a mallet, place a piece of chilled herb butter in the center, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the edges.
Coat each rolled chicken breast in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs to coat thoroughly.
Chill the wrapped chicken breasts in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350 degrees F and fry the chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 to 7 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Goulash
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides, then remove the meat.
In the same pot, add the chopped onions and sauté until soft and golden.
Remove the pot from heat temporarily, stir in the paprika and caraway seeds, then return to heat and add the beef back in.
Add garlic, bell pepper, tomatoes, and enough beef broth to cover the meat.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add the cubed potatoes and continue to simmer until the potatoes and beef are tender, about 25 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving hot.

title: Cabbage Rolls (Golubtsi)
instructions: Core the cabbage and submerge the head in a large pot of boiling water, peeling away softened leaves as they loosen.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, pork, cooked rice, onion, carrot, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides inward, and roll up tightly.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven and place the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot.
Whisk together the tomato paste, tomato sauce, and beef broth, then pour the mixture over the cabbage rolls.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for about 1 hour and 15 minutes until the cabbage is tender and meat is cooked through.
Serve warm with the cooking sauce poured over the top.

title: Traditional Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Sour cream and fresh dill for serving
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion and carrot until soft.
Add the shredded beets, tomato paste, and white vinegar to the pot, cooking for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, add the cubed potatoes and shredded cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Let the borscht rest for 15 minutes before serving with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Classic Pierogi with Potato and Cheese
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour and salt, then add warm water, egg, and melted butter to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes, cover, and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with the shredded cheese, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut circles using a glass or pastry cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges to seal.
Cook the pierogi in a large pot of boiling salted water until they float to the surface, about 3 minutes.
Sauté the chopped onion in butter until golden, then toss the boiled pierogi in the butter and onions before serving.

title: Golabki (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head in a large pot of water until leaves soften, then peel them off carefully.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, cooked rice, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto the center of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven and arrange the cabbage rolls snugly inside.
Mix the tomato sauce and beef broth together, then pour the mixture over the cabbage rolls.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is fully cooked and cabbage is tender.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: Mix the softened butter, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper, then shape into a log and freeze for 20 minutes.
Pound each chicken breast thin, place a piece of chilled herb butter in the center, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the ends.
Dredge each stuffed chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken rolls until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees F for 15 minutes until fully cooked through.

title: Honey Cake (Medovik)
instructions: In a saucepan, combine honey, sugar, and butter, heating over medium until melted and bubbly.
Remove from heat, let cool slightly, then whisk in the eggs one by one.
Stir in the baking soda and gradually add the flour to form a soft, sticky dough.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, roll each very thin, and bake individually at 350 degrees F for 5 minutes until golden.
Trim the edges of the warm layers while soft, and save the scraps to crush for the cake coating.
Whip the sour cream, heavy whipping cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract together to make the cream.
Layer the baked honey layers with the cream, frost the outside, and coat with the crushed pastry scraps before chilling overnight.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh dill and sour cream for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and carrots until softened.
Add shredded beets and tomato paste, cooking for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, bring to a boil, then add diced potatoes and cabbage.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in minced garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Classic Pierogi
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour, warm water, egg, and melted butter to form a smooth dough, then let rest for 20 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with shredded cheddar, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or cookie cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop pierogi into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook until they float to the top, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Melt additional butter in a skillet and pan-fry the boiled pierogi until golden brown.

title: Chicken Kiev

Pound each chicken breast thin, place a frozen butter log in the center, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the ends.
Coat each chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Chill the breaded chicken rolls in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet and fry the chicken rolls until golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes to ensure the chicken is fully cooked.

title: Golabki (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage head and boil it in a large pot of water until leaves loosen, then peel them carefully.
In a large bowl, mix ground pork, ground beef, cooked rice, chopped onion, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven and line the bottom with leftover cabbage leaves.
Arrange the stuffed cabbage rolls snugly in the pot.
Pour tomato sauce and beef broth over the rolls, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is cooked through.

title: Beef Stroganoff
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear beef strips until browned, then remove from the pan.
In the same skillet, melt butter and sauté onions and sliced mushrooms until tender.
Add minced garlic and sprinkle flour over the mushrooms, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef broth, scraping up browned bits from the bottom of the pan, and let simmer until thickened.
Return the beef to the skillet, stir in Dijon mustard and sour cream, and heat through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot over cooked egg noodles.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Fresh dill and sour cream for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onions and carrots until soft.
Add shredded beets, tomato paste, and vinegar, cooking for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add potatoes and cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Pierogi with Potato and Cheese

Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, then mash them.
Sauté diced onion in butter until golden brown, then mix half into the mashed potatoes with the shredded cheese, salt, and pepper.

Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or round cutter.
Place a spoonful of potato filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch edges tightly to seal.
Drop pierogi into boiling salted water and cook for 3 minutes after they float to the surface.
Pan-fry the boiled pierogi in butter with the remaining onions until golden brown.

title: Chicken Kiev
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix softened butter, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, then shape into a log and freeze for 15 minutes.
Pound chicken breasts gently until thin, place a piece of chilled butter in the center of each, and roll tightly to enclose the butter completely.
Coat each chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Chill the breaded chicken rolls in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet and fry the chicken rolls until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes until fully cooked.

title: Goulash

Salt and caraway seeds to taste

title: Traditional Ukrainian Borscht

Sour cream and fresh dill for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion and carrots until soft.

Pour in the broth, add potatoes and cabbage, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until all vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.

title: Classic Polish Pierogi with Potato and Cheese
instructions: Mix flour, egg, warm water, and salt to form a smooth dough, then rest for 20 minutes.
Sauté diced onion in butter until golden brown.

Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch edges to seal.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and caraway seeds to taste

Remove pot from heat momentarily and stir in the paprika and garlic.
Add beef cubes and cook until browned on all sides.
Add bell pepper, tomatoes, and a splash of beef broth, then simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add potatoes, caraway seeds, and remaining broth, cooking until potatoes and beef are tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot.

title: Lithuanian Cepelinai
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Sour cream and bacon bits for serving
instructions: Grate raw potatoes finely and squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a cheesecloth.
Mix the squeezed raw potato pulp with the riced cooked potatoes and a pinch of salt to form dough.

Take a portion of dough, flatten it, place a ball of meat in the center, and shape it into a zeppelin shape.
Drop dumplings carefully into a large pot of boiling salted water.
Simmer for 25 minutes until cooked through and serve with sour cream and crispy bacon bits.

title: Romanian Sarmale

1.5 lbs ground pork and beef mix

Pour tomato juice and water over the rolls until covered, and bake in the oven at 325F (160C) for 3 hours.

Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat lard or oil in a heavy pot and sauté the chopped onions until translucent.
Remove the pot from heat, stir in the paprika, and immediately add the cubed beef to coat.
Return to heat and cook until the beef releases its juices, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic, caraway seeds, chopped bell pepper, and tomatoes to the pot.
Pour in the beef broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2 hours until the beef is fork-tender and the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving warm.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and carrots until soft.
Add shredded beets, tomato paste, and a splash of broth, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in the remaining beef broth, add potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add shredded cabbage, and simmer until all vegetables are tender.
Stir in minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Serve hot topped with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Pierogi
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour and salt, then stir in egg, sour cream, and melted butter to form a dough.
Knead dough until smooth, cover, and let rest for 20 minutes.
Mix mashed potatoes and shredded cheese for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or round cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pierogi until they float to the top.
Sauté the chopped onion in butter, add boiled pierogi, and fry until lightly browned.

title: Golubtsi
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head in salted water until leaves soften and peel off easily.
In a large bowl, combine ground beef, ground pork, cooked rice, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll up tightly.
Place the rolls seam-side down in a large baking dish.
Mix tomato sauce and beef broth, then pour the mixture over the cabbage rolls.
Cover the dish with foil and bake at 350 degrees F for 1 hour and 30 minutes until tender.

title: Chicken Kiev
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix softened butter, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, then shape into a log and freeze until firm.
Pound each chicken breast until thin, season with salt and pepper.
Place a piece of the chilled herb butter in the center of each chicken breast.
Roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the edges to seal completely.
Coat each roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep skillet and fry chicken rolls until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Honey Cake (Medovik)
instructions: In a saucepan, melt honey, sugar, and butter together over medium heat until smooth.
Remove from heat, whisk in eggs one at a time, then stir in baking soda.
Gradually add flour to form a soft dough, divide into 8 equal pieces, and chill.
Roll each piece of dough thin and bake at 350 degrees F for 5 minutes until golden.
Trim the warm layers into neat circles and crush the leftover trimmings for crumbs.
Whip sour cream, heavy whipping cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla together for the frosting.
Layer the baked biscuit sheets with cream, frost the outside, and cover with the reserved crumbs before chilling overnight.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add shredded beets and carrots, cooking for about 5 minutes until they soften.
Stir in the tomato paste, vinegar, and a ladleful of broth, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining broth, cubed potatoes, and cabbage to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, and remove from heat.
Serve hot garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Pierogi
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt.
In a separate bowl, mix the egg, sour cream, and melted butter, then combine with the flour to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and let rest for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the mashed potatoes and cheddar cheese to make the filling.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut into circles using a glass or cookie cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pierogi in batches until they float to the top.
Melt butter in a skillet and fry the boiled pierogi until lightly browned and crispy.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: In a bowl, mix the softened butter, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, and salt, then shape into a log and chill in the freezer.
Pound each chicken breast thin, place a piece of chilled herb butter in the center, and roll the chicken tightly around the butter, tucking in the edges.
Dredge each rolled chicken breast in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken rolls for about 5 to 7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain before serving.

title: Goulash
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the onions until golden brown.
Remove the pot from heat temporarily and stir in the paprika and caraway seeds.
Add the beef cubes and garlic, returning to the heat to brown the meat on all sides.
Stir in the chopped bell pepper, tomatoes, and beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot.

title: Golumpki
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head in a large pot of water until the leaves soften and peel off easily.
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, cooked rice, onion, egg, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto the base of each cabbage leaf, roll up, and tuck in the sides.
Place the rolls seam-side down in a large baking dish.
In a bowl, mix the tomato soup, brown sugar, and lemon juice, then pour the sauce over the cabbage rolls.
Cover the dish with foil and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 1.5 hours until the meat is fully cooked.

title: Traditional Borscht
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion and carrot until soft.
Add the shredded beets and tomato paste, cooking for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, bring to a boil, then add the potatoes and cabbage.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the minced garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Let the soup rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm topped with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Classic Pierogi with Potato and Cheese
ingredients: 2 cups russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
instructions: In a large bowl, mix flour, salt, egg, warm water, and melted butter to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes, cover, and let rest for 20 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with grated cheese, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut circles using a glass or round cutter.
Place a spoonful of potato filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pierogi in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float.
Sauté the chopped onion in butter until golden brown, then toss the cooked pierogi in the butter and onions before serving.

title: Chicken Kiev
instructions: In a bowl, mix softened butter, garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, then shape into a log and freeze for 15 minutes.
Pound each chicken breast until thin, place a piece of frozen butter mixture in the center, and roll tightly tucking in the sides.
Coat each chicken roll in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Chill the wrapped chicken rolls in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken rolls for 5 to 7 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 375 degrees F for 15 minutes until fully cooked.

title: Golabki (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage head and boil it in a large pot of water until leaves soften and peel off easily.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, cooked rice, chopped onion, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a portion of the meat mixture onto the base of each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll up tightly.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven and line the bottom with leftover cabbage leaves.
Arrange the cabbage rolls snugly inside the pot.
Pour tomato sauce and beef broth over the rolls.
Cover and simmer on low heat for about 1.5 hours until the meat is cooked and tender.

title: Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until translucent.
Remove the pot from heat temporarily and stir in the paprika and minced garlic.
Add the beef cubes back to the pot and sear on all sides until browned.
Stir in the green bell pepper, diced tomatoes, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the beef broth, bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer gently for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is melt-in-your-mouth tender.
Serve hot with dumplings or crusty bread.

title: Bryndzové Halušky
ingredients: 2.2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Mix grated potatoes, flour, and salt into a semi-thick dough.
Press the dough through a spaetzle maker or off a cutting board directly into the boiling water.
Cook until the dumplings float to the top, then drain.
Fry the diced bacon in a pan until crispy.
Toss the warm dumplings with bryndza, sour cream, and top with the crispy bacon and its rendered fat.

title: Kapustnica
ingredients: 1 oz dried porcini mushrooms, soaked in warm water
instructions: In a large soup pot, cover the ribs with water, add caraway seeds, and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add the chopped sauerkraut and soaked mushrooms with their water to the pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion in lard until translucent, then add garlic, paprika, and sliced sausages.
Add the sausage mixture to the soup along with the bay leaf and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream and flour together, temper with a little hot soup, and stir into the pot to thicken slightly.
Remove the meat from the bones, chop, return to the soup, and serve hot.

title: Vyprážaný Sýr
ingredients: 14 oz Edam or Gouda cheese block
instructions: Cut the cheese block into slices about 1/2-inch thick.
Set up a breading station with flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in the second, and breadcrumbs in the third.
Coat each cheese slice thoroughly in flour, dip in beaten eggs, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating a second time to prevent the cheese from leaking out during frying.
Heat a generous amount of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the cheese slices until golden brown on both sides, about 2 minutes per side, and serve immediately with tartar sauce and boiled potatoes.

title: Sviečková na Smotane
ingredients: 2 large carrots, root vegetables peeled and diced
Whole black peppers, allspice berries, and bay leaf
Cranberry jam and lemon slice for serving
instructions: Lard the beef with bacon strips, season with salt, and sear in a pot with butter on all sides until browned; remove meat.
In the same pot, sauté the onions, carrots, parsley, and celeriac until golden.
Add the whole spices, return the meat to the pot, add a splash of water, cover, and roast in the oven at 350F (175C) until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and whole spices, then blend the vegetables and pan juices into a smooth sauce.
Stir in the heavy cream, bring to a simmer, and adjust flavor with sugar, vinegar, and salt.
Whisk flour with a little water, stir into the sauce to thicken, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Slice the beef, pour the sauce over it, and serve with bread dumplings and a dollop of cranberry jam topped with a lemon slice.

title: Povidlové Buchty
instructions: In a small bowl, combine warm milk, a teaspoon of sugar, and yeast; let it sit until frothy.
In a large bowl, mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, egg yolks, melted butter, and the yeast mixture into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 1/2-inch thickness and cut into equal squares.
Place a spoonful of thick plum jam in the center of each square, fold the corners over the filling, and pinch tightly to seal.
Place the buns seam-side down in a greased baking pan, brush them with melted butter, and let rise for another 20 minutes.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 25-30 minutes until golden brown, and dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Sarmale (Traditional Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head of fermented sour cabbage (murata)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Separate the sour cabbage leaves and cut away any thick veins.
In a pan, sauté the chopped onion in oil until translucent, then stir in the uncooked rice and sweet paprika for one minute before letting it cool.
Mix the ground pork, ground beef, cooked onion-rice mixture, salt, and pepper thoroughly in a large bowl.
Place a spoonful of meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Layer the bottom of a heavy-bottomed pot or clay pot with shredded sour cabbage and pieces of smoked bacon.
Arrange the cabbage rolls tightly in concentric circles inside the pot, interspersing with more bacon and bay leaves.
Pour the tomato juice and enough warm water over the rolls to cover them completely.
Cover with a lid and simmer on low heat on the stovetop or bake in the oven at 160°C for at least 3 hours.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Smântână (Polenta with Cheese and Sour Cream)
ingredients: 2 cups telemeaua cheese (or salty feta), grated
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a traditional heavy-bottomed pot (ceaun).
Gradually pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low and cook for about 20-25 minutes, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon until the polenta thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in the butter at the very end.
Turn the hot polenta out onto a wooden board.
Serve warm, topped generously with grated telemea cheese and a large dollop of sour cream.

title: Ciorbă de Perișoare (Meatball Sour Soup)
ingredients: 3 tomatoes, peeled and chopped, or 1 cup tomato puree
1.5 liters borscht (fermented wheat bran) or lemon juice to taste
instructions: In a bowl, mix the minced pork, rice, beaten egg, half of the chopped onion, salt, and pepper to form the meatball mixture.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into small, bite-sized meatballs.
In a large pot, sauté the remaining onion, carrots, parsnip, and bell pepper in a little oil until soft.
Add the 2 liters of water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Carefully drop the meatballs one by one into the simmering soup.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for about 25 minutes until the meat and rice are cooked.
In a separate pot, heat the borscht and add it to the soup (or use lemon juice for sourness).
