Season with salt, remove from heat, and stir in plenty of freshly chopped lovage and parsley.

title: Salată de Boeuf (Traditional Beef and Vegetable Salad)
ingredients: 500g beef round or brisket, boiled and diced
4 large potatoes, boiled in their skins, peeled and diced
1 cup frozen green peas, boiled until tender
Salt and white pepper to taste
Optional: extra pickles and hard-boiled eggs for decoration
instructions: Boil the beef, potatoes, carrots, and parsnips in salted water until tender, then let them cool completely.
Dice all the boiled vegetables, the cooked beef, pickled cucumbers, and pickled peppers into very small, uniform cubes.
Place the diced ingredients and boiled green peas into a large mixing bowl.
In a small bowl, mix most of the mayonnaise with the mustard, salt, and white pepper.
Pour the mayonnaise mixture over the vegetables and meat, stirring gently until evenly coated.
Transfer the salad to a serving platter and smooth the top to form a neat mound.
Spread a thin layer of remaining mayonnaise over the top and decorate with patterns made from boiled egg slices, pickles, and red peppers.

title: Papanași (Fried Cottage Cheese Doughnuts)
ingredients: 500g cow's milk cottage cheese (brânză de vaci), well-drained and mashed
1 cup fruit jam (blueberry or sour cherry)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mashed cottage cheese, eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and salt.
Mix in the baking soda and gradually add the flour, kneading gently until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal portions; reserve a small piece of dough from each portion to form a small ball.
Shape the large portions into flattened doughnut rings and the small portions into small balls.
Heat deep sunflower oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the rings and small balls in batches until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per batch.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot, topped with a generous spoonful of sour cream and fruit jam, placing the small fried ball on top of the ring.

title: Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 lb farmer's cheese or dry curd cottage cheese
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash them thoroughly.
Sauté one diced onion in butter until golden brown and caramelized.
Mix the mashed potatoes, caramelized onions, farmer's cheese, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Mix flour, warm water, egg, and salt to form a smooth, pliable dough. Let it rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or round cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Cook the pierogi in a large pot of boiling salted water for 3 to 4 minutes after they float to the top.
Sauté the remaining diced onion in butter and serve over the hot pierogi.

title: Tradycyjny Rosół
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Place chicken and beef in a large pot, cover with cold water, and bring slowly to a simmer.
Skim off the foam that rises to the surface during the initial heating.
Add the carrots, parsnips, celery root, leek, charred onion, bay leaves, and allspice berries.
Simmer on very low heat uncovered for at least 3 hours until the meat is tender and the broth is rich.
Add the bunch of parsley in the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Strain the clear golden broth into bowls.
Serve hot over freshly cooked egg noodles with sliced carrots from the broth.

title: Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
ingredients: 1 cup dried forest mushrooms, soaked and chopped
instructions: Cook the shredded fresh cabbage in a pot with a little water until soft.
In a separate pot, simmer the sauerkraut with the soaked mushrooms and their soaking liquid until tender.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, fry the diced bacon until crisp, then remove the bacon.
Brown the pork cubes and sliced sausage in the bacon fat.
Add the chopped onion to the pot and sauté until translucent.
Combine the cooked fresh cabbage, sauerkraut, mushrooms, meats, bacon, and onion in the large pot.
Add red wine, bay leaves, juniper berries, and caraway seeds.
Simmer on low heat for 2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. Best served after resting for a day or two.

title: Placki Ziemniaczane (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: Lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Grate the raw potatoes and the onion using the fine grating disc of a food processor or a manual box grater.
Transfer the grated potato and onion mixture to a clean cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Let the liquid settle for a few minutes, pour off the water, and scrape the recovered potato starch back into the mixture.
Add the egg, flour, salt, and black pepper to the grated potatoes and mix well.
Heat a generous amount of lard or oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop large spoonfuls of the batter into the hot pan and flatten them into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream or applesauce.

title: Kotlet Schabowy (Polish Pork Cutlet)
ingredients: 4 pork loin cutlets, about 6 oz each
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Lard or clarified butter for frying
instructions: Rinse the pork cutlets and pat them dry with paper towels.
Place each cutlet between plastic wrap and pound them out very thin using a meat mallet.
Season both sides of the pounded cutlets generously with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Melt lard or clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the crust is golden brown and crispy and the pork is cooked through.
Serve hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice alongside potatoes and mizeria.

title: Classic Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh dill and sour cream for serving
instructions: Place beef and water in a large pot, bring to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Remove the beef, shred the meat off the bone, and return it to the broth.
Add diced potatoes to the pot and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat sunflower oil in a skillet and sauté onions and carrots until soft.
Add grated beets and tomato paste to the skillet, cooking for another 5-7 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and the beet mixture into the pot with the broth and potatoes.
Simmer everything together for 15 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Stir in minced garlic, season with salt and pepper, turn off the heat, and let it rest for 20 minutes before serving with sour cream and dill.

title: Traditional Potato Vareniki
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, drain, and mash thoroughly.
Sauté diced onion in 2 tablespoons of butter until golden brown, then mix half of the onions into the mashed potatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, whisk water, egg, and salt, then gradually add flour to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes, cover, and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out the dough thin on a floured surface and cut out circles using a glass or pastry cutter.
Place a spoonful of potato filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop vareniki into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook for 3-4 minutes after they float to the top.
Remove with a slotted spoon, toss with the remaining butter and onions, and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Syrniki (Sweet Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
ingredients: 1 lb dry farmer's cheese or full-fat quark
4 tbsp all-purpose flour (plus extra for dredging)
Powdered sugar and jam for serving
instructions: Mash the farmer's cheese in a bowl with a fork until smooth.
Add the egg, sugar, vanilla extract, and 4 tablespoons of flour, mixing until well combined.
Shape the dough into small balls, flatten them slightly into thick patties, and dredge them lightly in flour.
Heat sunflower oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the syrniki for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve warm dusted with powdered sugar and your favorite fruit jam.

title: Holubtsi (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 lb ground pork and beef mix
1 cup medium-grain white rice, cooked halfway
instructions: Core the cabbage and boil the whole head in salted water, peeling off softened leaves one by one.
In a bowl, mix ground meat, half-cooked rice, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll tightly.
Sauté the chopped onion and grated carrot in sunflower oil until soft, then stir in the tomato paste.
In a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven, layer a few leftover cabbage leaves at the bottom.
Arrange the cabbage rolls snugly in the pot and top with the vegetable and tomato mixture.
Pour chicken broth over the rolls, add bay leaves, cover with a lid, and simmer on low heat for 1 hour.
Serve hot with the cooking broth poured on top.

title: Deruny (Crispy Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes and the onion using the fine side of a box grater into a bowl.
Transfer the grated mixture to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible.
Place the squeezed potato and onion mixture back into the bowl, add the egg, flour, salt, and pepper, and mix well.
Heat sunflower oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the potato mixture into the hot pan, flattening them into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess oil and serve immediately with a dollop of cold sour cream.

title: Classic Beef Borscht
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into bite-sized pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil beef in beef broth for 45 minutes until tender.
Sauté onion, carrot, and shredded beets in vegetable oil with tomato paste for 10 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and shredded cabbage to the broth and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in the sautéed beet mixture, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for another 10 minutes, remove from heat, and let rest.
Serve warm topped with sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Traditional Olivier Salad
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, boiled in their skins
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Peel and finely dice the boiled potatoes and carrots.
Finely dice the hard-boiled eggs, cooked chicken, and dill pickles.
Combine all diced ingredients and green peas in a large mixing bowl.
Add mayonnaise, salt, and black pepper, then mix gently until well combined.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Syrniki (Sweet Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
ingredients: 500g farmer's cheese or dry curd cottage cheese
3 tbsp all-purpose flour plus extra for coating
instructions: Mash the farmer's cheese in a bowl using a fork until smooth.
Mix in the egg, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt.
Stir in 3 tablespoons of flour until a soft dough forms.
Shape the dough into small balls, flatten them slightly, and dredge in flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the pancakes for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Beef Pelmeni
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Butter and sour cream for serving
instructions: Mix flour, egg, warm water, and salt to form a firm dough, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground beef, ground pork, minced onion, cold water, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut out small circles using a glass.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges together to form dumplings.
Drop the pelmeni into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until they float.
Serve hot tossed with butter and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Beef Stroganoff
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef tenderloin or sirloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season beef strips with salt and pepper.
Heat butter and vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat and quickly sear the beef until browned, then remove from the pan.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced onions and mushrooms until soft.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and onions, stirring for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef broth and bring to a simmer until thickened.
Stir in sour cream and Dijon mustard, return the beef to the pan, and warm through without boiling.
Serve hot over cooked egg noodles.

title: Classic Belarusian Draniki
ingredients: 0.5 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion on the fine side of a box grater.
Transfer the grated mixture to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible.
In a large bowl, combine the drained potato mixture, egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil or lard in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot pan, flattening them into thin patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Machanka with Pancakes
instructions: In a heavy skillet, render the diced pork belly over medium heat until crispy.
Add the sliced sausage and chopped onion to the skillet, cooking until the onions are soft and translucent.
Sprinkle the flour evenly over the meats and stir well to cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually pour in the beef broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Simmer the sauce on low heat for 15 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the sour cream, dill, salt, and pepper, and heat through without boiling.
Serve hot in bowls accompanied by folded thin pancakes for dipping.

title: Cold Beet Soup (Holodnik)
ingredients: 3 medium red beets, boiled and peeled
instructions: Grate the boiled beets coarsely using a box grater.
In a large pot or bowl, combine the grated beets, diced cucumbers, chopped eggs, green onions, and dill.
Whisk together the kefir, cold water, lemon juice, sugar, and salt in a separate pitcher.
Pour the liquid mixture over the vegetables and herbs, stirring well to combine.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon juice if needed.
Place the soup in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours to chill thoroughly before serving.

title: Kolduny with Meat
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt, then gradually stir in the boiling water and oil to form a dough.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and let rest for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the ground pork, ground beef, minced onion, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut out circles using a glass or pastry cutter.
Place a small spoonful of meat filling in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a crescent shape and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop the dumplings into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook for 6 to 8 minutes after they float to the surface.
Toss the cooked kolduny with melted butter before serving.

title: Babka in a Clay Pot
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit).
Dice the bacon and fry it in a skillet until crisp, then add the chopped onion and cook until soft.
Grate the raw potatoes finely.
Drain any excess liquid from the grated potatoes.
In a large bowl, mix the grated potatoes, fried bacon and onions with their rendered fat, egg, sour cream, salt, and pepper.
Grease a large clay baking pot or Dutch oven and pour the potato mixture into it.
Cover with a lid and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Remove the lid for the last 15 minutes of baking to form a golden brown crust.
Serve warm straight from the pot with a side of sour cream.

title: Traditional Hungarian Goulash Soup
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat lard in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until translucent and golden.
Remove the pot from heat, stir in the sweet Hungarian paprika, and immediately add the cubed beef.
Return to heat, add minced garlic and caraway seeds, and sear the beef until browned on all sides.
Add a little water, cover, and let the meat simmer in its own juices for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped bell pepper, tomatoes, and enough water or broth to cover everything, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour until the beef is tender.
Add the cubed potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and cook for another 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the soup is rich.
Serve hot with crusty white bread.

title: Chicken Paprikash with Egg Dumplings
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3-4 lbs, cut into pieces
For the dumplings: 2 large eggs, 1/2 cup water, 2 cups all-purpose flour, a pinch of salt
instructions: Melt lard in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté the onions until golden brown.
Remove from heat, stir in the paprika, then add the chicken pieces, turning them to coat well.
Add the chopped tomato, bell pepper, chicken broth, and salt, then cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
While the chicken cooks, make the dumplings: mix eggs, water, flour, and salt into a thick, slightly lumpy dough.
Drop small pieces of the dough into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook until they float to the top; drain.
Remove the cooked chicken from the pot and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk the sour cream and flour together until smooth, then whisk in a few spoonfuls of the hot pan juices to temper.
Pour the sour cream mixture into the pot, stirring constantly, and simmer gently until the sauce thickens.
Return the chicken to the sauce to warm through, and serve hot over the prepared egg dumplings.

title: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
ingredients: 1 large head of sour pickled cabbage (sauerkraut leaves)
1 smoked pork knuckle or thick-cut bacon, diced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Separate the sour cabbage leaves and trim away any thick center veins; set aside.
In a bowl, combine the ground pork, uncooked rice, half of the chopped onion, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper, mixing well.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides inward, and roll them up tightly.
In a large heavy pot, melt the lard and sauté the remaining onion and the diced smoked bacon.
Layer half of the rinsed sauerkraut at the bottom of the pot.
Arrange the stuffed cabbage rolls tightly on top of the sauerkraut, and cover with the remaining sauerkraut.
Add enough water to cover the rolls, place a small plate on top to keep them pressed down, cover the pot, and simmer on low for about 2 hours.
In a small pan, make a roux with a little lard, flour, and paprika, stir in some cooking liquid, and pour over the cabbage to thicken the sauce slightly.
Serve warm topped with a generous dollop of sour cream.

title: Hungarian Potato Casserole
ingredients: 3 lbs potatoes, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
1 lb Hungarian garlic sausage (kolbász), sliced into rounds
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a baking dish with lard.
Cook the potato slices in boiling salted water for about 5 minutes until partially softened; drain well.
In a bowl, mix the sour cream with a pinch of salt and paprika.
Layer half of the sliced potatoes evenly on the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Arrange the sliced sausage and hard-boiled eggs over the layer of potatoes.
Spread a portion of the seasoned sour cream over the sausage and eggs.
Add the remaining potatoes as the top layer, and spread the rest of the sour cream evenly over them.
Sprinkle the breadcrumbs over the top and dot with small pieces of lard or butter.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes until the top is golden brown and bubbly.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

title: Traditional Plum Jam Crepes
ingredients: For the crepes: 1.5 cups all-purpose flour, 2 large eggs, 1 cup milk, 1 cup sparkling water, 2 tbsp melted butter, 1 tbsp sugar, a pinch of salt, butter for frying
For the filling: 1.5 cups thick Hungarian plum jam (szilvalekvár)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, sparkling water, sugar, and a pinch of salt until smooth and thin.
Let the batter rest at room temperature for about 20 minutes.
Heat a crepe pan or small skillet over medium heat and lightly coat with butter.
Ladle a small amount of batter into the pan, swirling quickly to coat the bottom in a thin layer.
Cook until the edges start to lift and the bottom is golden, then flip and cook for another minute.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the finished crepes on a warm plate.
Spread a generous tablespoon of thick plum jam across each crepe.
Roll the crepes up tightly or fold them into quarters.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving warm.

title: Traditional Beef Sirloin in Cream Sauce (Síčková na smetaně)
ingredients: 2.5 lbs beef tenderloin or top round
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Lard the beef with strips of bacon, season with salt, and sear in a roasting pan with melted butter on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, grated carrots, parsley root, peppercorns, allspice, and bay leaves around the meat.
Pour in the beef broth, cover, and roast in the oven for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and slice it.
Blend the vegetables and pan juices until smooth, then transfer to a pot.
Stir in the heavy cream and a slurry of flour mixed with a little water, simmer for 10 minutes.
Add lemon juice to taste and serve the sauce over the sliced beef with bread dumplings and cranberries.

title: Czech Potato Soup (Bramboračka)
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or rehydrated dried forest mushrooms
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large soup pot and sauté the diced carrots, parsley roots, and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir well to create a light roux.
Gradually pour in the broth, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Add the diced potatoes, garlic, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the potatoes and vegetables are tender.
Rub the dried marjoram between your palms and stir it into the soup along with black pepper.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving hot.

title: Sweet Plum Dumplings with Poppy Seeds (Kynuté švestkové knedlíky)
instructions: Mix warm milk, sugar, and yeast in a small bowl and let it sit until frothy.
In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, egg, and the yeast mixture, then knead into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut into squares.
Wrap each square of dough around a pitted plum, sealing the edges tightly to form a round dumpling.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil and drop the dumplings in.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning gently halfway through.
Remove with a slotted spoon, pierce each dumpling to let steam out, and top with melted butter, ground poppy seeds, and powdered sugar.

title: Fried Breaded Pork Schnitzel (Vepřový řízek)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
1 cup lard or neutral oil for frying
instructions: Pound the pork cutlets between plastic wrap until they are about 1/4-inch thick.
Season both sides of the cutlets with salt and white pepper.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet first in flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in the beaten eggs, and finally coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges and potato salad.

title: Braised Red Cabbage (Dusené červené zelí)
ingredients: 1 medium head of red cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
2 tart apples, peeled, cored, and grated
instructions: Melt butter or lard in a large pot and sauté the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the caraway seeds and sliced red cabbage, cooking for a few minutes until it begins to soften.
Stir in the grated apples, vinegar, sugar, bay leaf, and water.
Cover the pot and simmer over low heat for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding more water if needed.
Season with additional salt, sugar, or vinegar to achieve a balanced sweet-and-sour flavor.
Serve warm as a side dish with roasted meats and dumplings.

title: Bryndzove Halusky (Potato Dumplings with Sheep Cheese)
ingredients: 2.2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Mix grated potatoes, flour, and salt into a semi-thick dough.
Press the dough through a spaetzle maker or off a cutting board directly into the boiling water.
Cook until the dumplings float to the top, then drain.
Fry the diced bacon in a pan until crispy.
Toss the warm dumplings with bryndza and sour cream.
Top with the crispy bacon and rendered bacon fat before serving.

title: Kapustnica (Traditional Christmas Cabbage Soup)
ingredients: 1 oz dried porcini mushrooms, soaked in warm water
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse sauerkraut lightly if it is too sour.
In a large pot, combine sauerkraut, smoked ribs, soaked mushrooms with their water, and cover with additional water.
Simmer on medium-low heat for about 1 hour until meats are tender.
Add the whole sausages and cook for another 20 minutes, then remove sausages and slice them.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion in lard until translucent, add garlic and paprika, then stir into the soup.
Whisk flour into sour cream, temper with a little hot soup, and stir into the pot to thicken.
Add sliced sausages back, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 15 more minutes.

title: Gulasova Polievka (Beef Goulash Soup)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef chuck, cut into bite-sized cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté onions until golden brown.
Remove pot from heat briefly, stir in the paprika and caraway seeds, then add the beef cubes.
Return to heat and sear the beef until it releases its juices.
Add enough water or broth to cover the meat, season with salt and pepper, and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add diced potatoes and cook until tender.
Stir in minced garlic and dried marjoram in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Stpany Kuraci Spon (Breaded Chicken Cutlets with Mashed Potatoes)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Vegetable oil or lard for frying
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, drain, and mash with butter and warm milk to make smooth mashed potatoes.
Season chicken cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil or lard in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve hot alongside the warm mashed potatoes and a wedge of lemon.

title: Buchty na Pare (Steamed Buns with Plum Jam Filling)
ingredients: Powdered sugar and cocoa powder for dusting
instructions: Mix warm milk, sugar, and yeast in a small bowl and let it activate for 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, egg, and the yeast mixture, then knead into a smooth dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 0.5-inch thickness and cut into squares.
Place a spoonful of plum jam in the center of each square, fold the edges over, and seal into round buns.
Let the buns rest for another 15 minutes.
Steam the buns in a steamer basket over boiling water for 12-15 minutes.
Brush the steamed buns generously with melted butter and dust with powdered sugar and cocoa powder before serving.

title: Ciorba de Burta (Tripe Soup)
ingredients: 1 kg beef tripe, pre-boiled and sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the beef bones, carrots, parsnip, and onion in a large pot of salted water for 2 hours to make a rich broth.
Strain the broth, discard the vegetables and bones, and return the clear broth to the pot.
Add the sliced pre-boiled tripe to the broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk together the sour cream, egg yolks, and minced garlic.
Temper the sour cream mixture by slowly adding a ladle of hot soup, then whisk it back into the pot.
Season with salt, pepper, and vinegar to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with melted butter and fresh parsley.

title: Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head of fermented sour cabbage (murata)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Separate the sour cabbage leaves and cut away any tough veins.
In a pan, sauté the chopped onions and half of the diced bacon until translucent, then let cool.
In a large bowl, mix the ground pork, ground beef, rinsed rice, sautéed onion and bacon, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the ends.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot with leftover shredded cabbage and the remaining diced bacon.
Layer the cabbage rolls snugly in the pot, adding bay leaves between the layers.
Pour tomato paste dissolved in water over the rolls until completely covered.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 3 to 4 hours, or bake in the oven at 160°C (320°F).

title: Mici (Grilled Minced Meat Rolls)
ingredients: 1 head of garlic, crushed and steeped in 200ml warm water (garlic juice)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, pork, and lamb.
Add the salt, baking soda, black pepper, thyme, and aniseed, mixing well with your hands.
Gradually knead in the garlic-infused water a little at a time until the meat mixture becomes very fluffy and sticky.
Cover the bowl tightly and refrigerate overnight to let the flavors develop and the baking soda tenderize the meat.
Shape the mixture into cylindrical rolls about the size of a small sausage, wetting your hands to prevent sticking.
Grill over hot coals or a hot indoor grill for about 8 to 10 minutes, turning frequently until browned on all sides but still juicy.
Serve hot with yellow mustard and crusty bread.

title: Mamaliga cu Branza si Smantana (Polenta with Cheese and Sour Cream)
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot or traditional cauldron (ceaun).
Reduce the heat to medium and slowly pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Cook on low heat, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon, for about 20 to 25 minutes until the polenta thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in the butter until melted.
To serve, layer hot polenta in bowls or on a wooden board, alternating with generous amounts of grated telemea cheese.
Top with a large dollop of sour cream and serve immediately.

title: Papanasi (Fried Cottage Cheese Doughnuts)
ingredients: 500g cow's milk cottage cheese (branza de vaci), well-drained
150g sour cherry jam or blueberry jam
instructions: In a large bowl, mash the cottage cheese until smooth.
Add the eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and baking soda, mixing well.
Gradually fold in the flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and divide it into portions.
For each portion, roll a large ball of dough and flatten it slightly, then poke a hole in the center to form a doughnut shape, and roll a separate small ball for the top.
Heat sunflower oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Fry the doughnuts and small balls until golden brown on both sides, about 4 to 5 minutes per batch.
Serve warm, topped with a generous dollop of sour cream and fruit jam.

title: Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 lb dry farmer's cheese or full-fat cottage cheese
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, then drain and mash thoroughly.
Sauté the diced onions in butter until golden brown and caramelized.
Mix the mashed potatoes, half of the caramelized onions, and the farmer's cheese together, then season well with salt and pepper.
Mix the flour, salt, water, and egg to form a smooth, elastic dough, then let it rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut circles with a glass, place a spoonful of filling in the center, fold, and pinch the edges to seal.
Cook the pierogi in boiling salted water for 3 to 4 minutes after they float to the top, then serve with the remaining onions.

title: Traditional Bigos
ingredients: 1 cup dried wild mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Cook the sauerkraut and fresh cabbage in separate pots with a little water until tender, then combine them.
Sauté the bacon and onions in a large heavy pot until the onions are translucent.
Add the pork cubes to the pot and brown on all sides.
Add the sliced kielbasa, mushrooms, bay leaves, allspice, and caraway seeds to the meat mixture.
Combine the cooked cabbage mixture, meat, red wine, and tomato paste into the large pot.
Simmer on low heat for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally, and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Kotlet Schabowy
ingredients: 4 pork loin cutlets, about 6 oz each
1/2 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Pound the pork cutlets thinly using a meat mallet until they are about a quarter-inch thick.
Season both sides of the pounded cutlets generously with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat the lard or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy, then serve with lemon wedges.

title: Rosól
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken parts, such as wings, backs, and drumsticks
instructions: Place the chicken and beef in a large stockpot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and skim off any foam.
Char the cut side of the onion in a dry skillet until blackened, then add it to the pot along with the garlic.
Add the carrots, parsnips, celeriac, leek, bay leaves, and peppercorns to the pot.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover partially, and simmer gently for at least 3 hours.
Add the parsley and dill bunches in the last 30 minutes of simmering.
Strain the broth, season with salt, and serve hot over cooked egg noodles with sliced carrots.

title: Placki Ziemniaczane
ingredients: Sour cream or applesauce for serving
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion using the fine grating disc of a food processor or a manual box grater.
Transfer the grated mixture to a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible.
In a bowl, combine the drained potato mixture, egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a generous amount of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the potato batter into the hot pan, flattening them slightly to form pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply golden and crispy, drain on paper towels, and serve with sour cream or applesauce.

title: Classic Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh dill and sour cream for serving
instructions: In a large pot, cover the beef with 8 cups of water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender, then remove, shred, and return to the broth.
Add the diced potatoes to the pot and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat sunflower oil in a skillet and sauté the onions and carrots until soft.
Add the grated beets and tomato paste to the skillet, splash with vinegar, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and the beet mixture to the pot, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, turn off the heat, and let it rest covered for 20 minutes before serving with sour cream and dill.

title: Potato and Cottage Cheese Varenyky
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
1 cup dry farmer's cheese or dry cottage cheese
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes and mix them with the farmer's cheese, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
Sauté the chopped onion in butter until golden brown and stir half into the potato mixture.
In a large bowl, mix flour, salt, and baking soda, then stir in warm kefir to form a soft dough.
Knead the dough on a floured surface until smooth, then let it rest for 15 minutes.
Roll out the dough to 1/8-inch thickness and cut out circles using a glass.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop varenyky into a large pot of boiling salted water, and cook for 3 minutes after they float to the top.
Remove with a slotted spoon, toss with the remaining fried onions, and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Crispy Pork Salo and Garlic Pampushky
ingredients: 1/4 lb cured pork fat (salo), thinly sliced
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let sit for 10 minutes until frothy.
Mix flour, salt, yeast mixture, and 2 tablespoons of oil into a smooth dough, then let rise for 1 hour.
Shape the dough into small round rolls, place them close together in a greased baking pan, and let rise for 20 minutes.
Bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Mix the crushed garlic, remaining oil, water, and chopped parsley to make the garlic glaze.
Brush the hot baked rolls generously with the garlic glaze.
Serve the warm pampushky alongside thinly sliced cured salo and dark rye bread.

title: Traditional Cabbage Holubtsi
ingredients: 1 lb ground pork and beef mix
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Core the cabbage head and boil it in a large pot of water, peeling off the softened leaves one by one.
Sauté the chopped onion in sunflower oil until translucent.
In a bowl, combine the ground meat, partially cooked rice, sautéed onion, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto the base of each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll tightly.
Layer the rolls snugly in a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven or pot.
Whisk together the tomato juice and chicken broth, pour it over the cabbage rolls, and add the bay leaves.
Cover tightly and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat and rice are fully cooked.

title: Sweet Cherry Vareniki Nalisnyky
ingredients: 2 cups pitted sour cherries, fresh or frozen
1/4 cup granulated sugar for the filling
instructions: Whisk together eggs, milk, flour, sugar, salt, and melted butter to make a smooth, thin crêpe batter.
Heat a lightly greased skillet and pour a thin layer of batter, cooking until edges turn golden, then flip for 30 seconds.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make a stack of thin crêpes (nalisnyky).
Toss the pitted cherries with sugar and cornstarch, and simmer in a small pan for 5 minutes until thickened.
Place a spoonful of the cherry filling onto each crêpe, fold the sides inward, and roll into neat cylinders.
Lightly fry the rolled crêpes in butter until warm and slightly crisp on the outside.
Serve warm, optionally dusted with powdered sugar or with a side of sour cream.

title: Classic Russian Borscht
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh dill and sour cream for serving
instructions: Boil the beef in water or broth for about 1 hour until tender, then remove and shred the meat before returning it to the pot.
Add the diced potatoes to the simmering broth and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a skillet, sauté the onions and carrots until soft, then stir in the tomato paste.
Add the julienned beets and a splash of broth to the skillet, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Add the shredded cabbage and the beet mixture into the soup pot, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, turn off the heat, and let the borscht rest for 20 minutes before serving.
Serve hot topped with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped dill.

title: Traditional Olivier Salad
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken breast or good quality bologna, diced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes and carrots in their skins until fork-tender, then let them cool completely, peel, and dice into small cubes.
Peel and dice the hard-boiled eggs to the same size as the vegetables.
Dice the cooked chicken and dill pickles into uniform small cubes.
Combine the potatoes, carrots, eggs, chicken, pickles, green peas, and onion in a large mixing bowl.
Add the mayonnaise, salt, and black pepper, then gently stir until everything is evenly coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving to let the flavors meld.

title: Syrniki (Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
ingredients: 16 oz farmer's cheese or dry curd cottage cheese
4 tbsp all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
Sour cream, jam, or fresh berries for serving
instructions: Press the farmer's cheese through a fine mesh sieve or mash it well with a fork to remove lumps.
Add the egg, sugar, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt to the cheese, mixing until combined.
Stir in the 4 tablespoons of flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Shape the dough into small balls, flatten them slightly into thick patties, and dredge each in flour.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the pancakes for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve warm with sour cream, jam, or fresh berries.

title: Pelmeni (Siberian Meat Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion, finely grated or minced
Salt and black pepper to taste
Butter and sour cream for serving
instructions: Mix the flour, egg, warm water, and salt to form a firm dough, knead for 10 minutes, and let it rest covered for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, grated onion, cold water, salt, and pepper, mixing well.
Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut out circles using a small glass or round cutter.
Place a small spoonful of meat filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges together, then connect the two ends to form a hat shape.
Drop the pelmeni into a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring gently so they do not stick.
Cook for about 5 to 7 minutes after they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon, toss with butter, and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Beef Stroganoff
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef tenderloin or sirloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef strips with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef quickly until browned, then remove the meat and set aside.
In the same skillet, melt the butter and sauté the sliced onions and mushrooms until tender and golden.
Sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms and onions, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef broth and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and sour cream, returning the beef and any accumulated juices to the sauce.
Simmer gently for 2 minutes until heated through without boiling, then serve immediately over cooked egg noodles.

title: Classic Belarusian Draniki
ingredients: 3 tablespoons lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and the onion using a traditional fine-mesh grater.
Transfer the grated mixture to a clean cheesecloth and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible.
In a large bowl, combine the squeezed potato-onion mixture, egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat lard or oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot pan, flattening them into thin patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot immediately with a dollop of cold sour cream.

title: Machanka with Pancakes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Blini or thick crepes for serving
instructions: In a deep heavy skillet, fry the chopped pork belly until it renders its fat and turns crispy.
Add the sausage links and sliced onions, cooking until the onions are soft and golden.
Sprinkle the flour evenly over the meats and stir well to cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the warm broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps from forming.
Simmer the mixture on low heat for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the sour cream, dill, salt, and pepper, heating through without boiling.
Serve hot in bowls accompanied by freshly made crepes for dipping.

title: Cold Sorrel Soup (Holodnik)
ingredients: 4 cups fresh sorrel leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a pot, add the chopped sorrel, and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until it wilts and changes color.
Remove from heat and let the sorrel broth cool completely.
In a large soup tureen, combine the diced cucumbers, chopped eggs, green onions, and dill.
Pour the cooled sorrel broth over the vegetables and herbs.
Whisk together the kefir and sour cream, then stir it into the soup.
Season with salt to taste and chill in the refrigerator for at least two hours before serving.

title: Babka (Potato and Bacon Casserole)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F) and grease a traditional clay baking dish or casserole dish with butter.
Fry the diced bacon and onion in a skillet until the bacon is crispy and the onions are caramelized.
Grate the potatoes finely, drain off any excess watery liquid, but keep the starchy sediment at the bottom of the bowl.
In a large bowl, mix the grated potatoes, the settled potato starch, egg, salt, pepper, and the fried bacon and onions along with their rendered fat.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake uncovered for 1 hour until the top forms a deep golden, crispy crust.
Slice and serve warm with cold sour cream.

title: Kalduny (Meat-Stuffed Dumplings)
ingredients: Salt and pepper for the filling
instructions: Mix flour, salt, egg, and warm water in a bowl to form a smooth, pliable dough, then let it rest for 20 minutes.
In a separate bowl, combine the ground meat, minced onion, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut out circles using a glass.
Place a small spoonful of meat filling in the center of each dough circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Drop the dumplings into a large pot of boiling salted water.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes after they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon, toss with melted butter, and serve hot.

title: Authentic Hungarian Goulash Soup
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt lard in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the onions until translucent and golden.
Remove the pot from heat briefly, stir in the Hungarian paprika and minced garlic, and stir well to combine.
Add the cubed beef and caraway seeds, return to heat, and sear the meat on all sides until it releases its juices.
Pour in enough beef broth to cover the meat, season with salt and pepper, cover, and simmer on low heat for about 1 hour.
Add the carrots, parsnips, potatoes, bell pepper, and tomato to the pot, adding more broth if needed.
Simmer gently for another 30 minutes until all vegetables and the beef are tender before serving hot.

title: Traditional Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 3 lbs chicken pieces (legs, thighs, and breasts)
instructions: Heat lard in a Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same fat, sauté the chopped onions until soft and golden brown.
Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the paprika, then add the diced tomato, bell pepper, and chicken broth.
Return the chicken to the pot, season with salt, cover, and simmer over low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sour cream and flour until smooth.
Temper the sour cream mixture with a few spoonfuls of the hot cooking liquid, then stir it into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.

title: Hungarian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
ingredients: 1 large head of sour pickled cabbage (sauerkraut leaves)
1 lb smoked pork ribs or bacon, chopped
instructions: Rinse the sour cabbage leaves in cold water if they are too salty, and cut away the thick hard veins.
In a bowl, mix the ground pork, uncooked rice, half of the chopped onion, garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, fold the sides in, and roll them up tightly.
In a large pot, melt the lard, layer the bottom with shredded sour cabbage and smoked ribs.
Arrange the stuffed cabbage rolls tightly on top, cover with water, and simmer on low heat for about 2 hours.
Make a roux with lard and flour, thicken the juices in the pot, and serve the rolls hot with a generous dollop of sour cream.

title: Hungarian Potato Paprikash
ingredients: 3 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
2 fresh Hungarian wax peppers or sausages, sliced (optional)
instructions: Melt the lard in a pot and sauté the chopped onions until golden and translucent.
Remove from heat, sprinkle in the paprika, and stir quickly to prevent burning.
Add the potato chunks, sliced bell pepper, and tomato to the pot.
Pour in enough water to just cover the potatoes, and season with salt and pepper.
Add the sliced sausages if using, cover the pot, and cook over medium heat for about 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and create a thick starchy sauce.
Serve warm, slightly mashed with a fork so the starch thickens the broth.

title: Sweet Cottage Cheese Palacsinta
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter plus extra for frying
instructions: Whisk together flour, eggs, milk, sparkling water, sugar, salt, and melted butter to create a smooth, thin crepe batter.
Heat a palacsinta pan or skillet with a little butter, pour in a thin layer of batter, and cook until golden on both sides, repeating for all batter.
In a bowl, mash the cottage cheese with powdered sugar, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and sour cream until creamy.
Spread a generous layer of the cottage cheese filling onto each crepe.
Roll the crepes up tightly or fold them into quarters.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm.

title: Svieckova na smetane
ingredients: Bread dumplings and lingonberry jam for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Season the beef with salt and sear it on all sides in a large Dutch oven with melted butter.
Remove the beef, add the onions, carrots, parsley root, and celeriac to the pot, and sauté until golden brown.
Add the peppercorns, allspice, bay leaves, thyme, and beef broth, then place the beef back into the pot.
Cover and bake in the oven for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Remove the beef and slice it. Strain the vegetables and sauce, reserving the liquid.
In a saucepan, mash the cooked vegetables with a little sauce, add the heavy cream mixed with flour, and simmer until thickened.
Season the sauce with lemon juice, sugar, and salt to taste.
Serve the sliced beef with the creamy vegetable sauce, bread dumplings, and a dollop of lingonberry jam.

title: Traditional Goulash (Hovezi Gulas)
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Bread dumplings or crusty bread for serving
instructions: Heat the lard in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the onions until deeply golden brown.
Add the minced garlic, caraway seeds, and sweet paprika, stirring constantly for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef cubes and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste and pour in the beef broth.
Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 2 hours, stirring occasionally until the beef is tender.
Rub the dried marjoram between your palms and stir it into the goulash during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with bread dumplings or fresh crusty bread.

title: Potato Soup (Bramboracka)
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or rehydrated dried forest mushrooms
instructions: Melt the butter in a soup pot, add the flour, and stir continuously to make a golden roux.
Gradually whisk in the broth to prevent lumps.
Add the diced potatoes, sliced carrots, parsley roots, and mushrooms to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the minced garlic, dried marjoram, salt, and pepper, and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving hot.

title: Plum Dumplings (Svestkove Knedliky)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose potatoes, boiled, peeled, and riced
12 to 15 fresh Italian prune plums, pitted
1/2 cup grated dry cottage cheese or hard curd cheese (tvaroh)
instructions: Mix the riced potatoes, egg, all-purpose flour, semolina, and salt to form a smooth dough.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1/4-inch thickness and cut into squares.
Place a pitted plum in the center of each square, wrap the dough around the plum, and seal the edges to form round dumplings.
Drop the dumplings gently into a large pot of lightly salted boiling water.
Cook for about 8 to 10 minutes until they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain well.
Serve warm drizzled with melted butter, sprinkled with grated tvaroh, and dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Fried Breaded Pork Schnitzel (Veprovy Rizek)
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Season both sides of the pounded pork cutlets with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the beaten eggs, and coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Heat about 1/2 inch of lard or vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzels for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and a side of potato salad.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread beef or lamb cubes onto skewers.
In a small bowl, mix together olive oil, garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Brush mixture onto skewers.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally.

title: Jollof Rice (West African One-Pot Dish)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, ginger, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, yeast, and salt.
Gradually add water, stirring with a wooden spoon until smooth.
Cover and let rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour in 1/4 cup of batter and tilt to evenly coat the pan.

title: Kenkey (Ghanaian Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine cornmeal and water. Mix until smooth.
Add salt and yeast. Mix until combined.
Transfer mixture to a ceramic or glass container.
Cover and let ferment in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Serve with a spicy sauce or pepper.

title: Matooke (East African Steamed Green Bananas)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Peel bananas and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add garlic and cumin. Cook for 1 minute.
Add bananas and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and steam for 15-20 minutes.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together oil, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Add the meat and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread the meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill the sosatie for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked to your liking.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley and cilantro.

title: Groundnut Stew (West African Peanut Stew)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef or lamb and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned.
Stir in groundnuts, broth, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until thickened.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and yeast.
Gradually add water, stirring to form a smooth batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 24-48 hours, or until doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of batter into the pan and tilt to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.

title: Fufu (Central African Starch)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
Gradually add water, stirring to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, or until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Cook the fufu in boiling water for 5-10 minutes, or until it rises to the surface.

title: Bobotie (South African Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 cup dried fruit, such as raisins or cranberries
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground meat, onion, garlic, dried fruit, milk, eggs, curry powder, salt, and pepper.
Mix well to combine.
Roll out the pie crust and place in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Pour the meat mixture into the pie crust.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is set.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add onion, garlic, tomato, and bell pepper, cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat the rice with the spice mixture.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes or until the rice is tender.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef or lamb, onion, garlic, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, brown sugar, soy sauce, olive oil, salt, and black pepper, mix well.
Thread the meat mixture onto the skewers.
Grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes or until the meat is cooked through.
Serve hot with a side of rice or bread.

title: Fufu with Peanut Stew
instructions: To make fufu, combine cassava flour and warm water in a large bowl, knead for 5 minutes until the dough comes together.
Divide the dough into 4-6 pieces, shape each piece into a ball, and flatten slightly.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, tomato, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper, cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add peanut butter and stir to combine.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the stew thickens.

title: Kenkey with Pepper Sauce
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic, onion, ginger, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
Serve the pepper sauce with kenkey.

title: Groundnut Stew (West African Peanut Stew)
instructions: Grind the groundnuts into a smooth paste using a blender or food processor.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and tomato, cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add groundnut paste and stir to combine.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the stew thickens.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add rice; cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add water and crushed tomatoes; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Sosatie (South African Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together lemon juice, oil, garlic, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add meat; marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, or until cooked through.

title: Kenkey (Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal and water.
Add yeast and salt; mix until smooth.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Punch down dough and shape into a round loaf.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour and water.
Add yeast and salt; mix until smooth.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 24-48 hours, or until doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour in 1/4 cup of batter; tilt pan to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.

title: Fufu (Boiled Cassava or Yams)
ingredients: 2 large cassava or yams, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Place cassava or yams in a large pot and add enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until tender.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
Serve with vegetable oil for dipping.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, beef broth, and tomato paste; stir to combine.
Add rice; stir to coat rice with spice mixture.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add water; mix until a smooth batter forms.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours or until the batter has risen and has a sour smell.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour about 1/4 cup of batter onto the skillet and tilt to evenly coat the surface.
Cook for 1-2 minutes or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip the injera and cook for another 30 seconds to 1 minute or until the other side is lightly browned.

title: Sosatie (South African Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef or lamb, brown sugar, soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper; mix well to coat.
Thread the marinated meat onto the bamboo skewers, leaving a little space between each piece.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Brush the skewers with oil to prevent sticking.
Grill the skewers for 8-10 minutes or until the meat is cooked through, turning occasionally.

title: Kenkey (Ghanaian Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: Combine corn flour and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add water; mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes or until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Shape the dough into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Place the kenkey in a warm, humid place for 24-48 hours or until it has fermented and has a sour smell.
Serve with a spicy sauce or pepper.

title: Maafe (West African Beef Stew)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add beef; stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add beef broth, water, tomato paste, and peanut butter; stir to combine.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 1-2 hours or until the beef is tender.

title: Jollof Rice (Ghana)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, broth, and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until rice is tender.

title: Sosatie (South Africa)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into bite-sized pieces
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine sugar, soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Add meat and mix well to coat.
Thread meat onto skewers.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally.

title: Groundnut Stew (West Africa)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add groundnuts and cook for 2 minutes.
Add broth and water; bring to a boil.
Add meat and cook until tender.

title: Injera (Ethiopia)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and yeast.
Gradually add water and mix until smooth.
Cover and let rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour in batter and cook for 1-2 minutes, until edges start to curl.

title: Fufu (Central Africa)
ingredients: 2 pounds cassava or yams, peeled and grated
instructions: In a large bowl, combine grated cassava or yams and water.
Knead until smooth and pliable.
Add salt and knead for 10 minutes.
Divide into small pieces and shape into balls.
Cook in boiling water for 10-15 minutes, until tender.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5 minutes.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add rice; cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes.
Add water, tomato puree, and beef broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender, 20-25 minutes.

title: Injera Bread
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and yeast; mix well.
Gradually add water, stirring until a smooth batter forms.
Cover bowl with a clean cloth; let batter rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter into the pan; tilt to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl; flip and cook for another minute.

title: Sosatie (South African Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine meat, oil, garlic, sugar, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; mix well.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 8-10 minutes.

title: Fufu with Light Soup
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and warm water; mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes, until pliable.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces; shape each into a ball.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Add water; bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer until heated through.

title: Kenkey (Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and yeast; mix well.
Gradually add water, stirring until a smooth dough forms.
Cover bowl with a clean cloth; let dough rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes, until smooth.
Shape dough into a ball; flatten slightly into a disk shape.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add rice, stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add tomato puree and beef broth, stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, serve hot.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: Combine teff and all-purpose flour in a large bowl.
Add water, yeast, and salt, mix until a smooth batter forms.
Cover and let rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter onto the skillet, tilt to evenly coat.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip and cook for another minute, repeat with remaining batter.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together oil, garlic, lemon juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add meat, mix to coat with marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through.
Serve hot with your choice of sides.

title: Fufu (West African Starch)
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine cassava flour and salt.
Gradually add boiling water, stirring to form a sticky dough.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on desired size.
Shape each piece into a ball, then flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Serve with your choice of soup or stew.

title: Mafe (Malian Peanut Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until onion is translucent.
Add meat, cook until browned on all sides.
Add peanut butter, stir to combine with meat and onion mixture.
Add beef broth, heavy cream, tomato paste, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 20-30 minutes.
Serve hot over rice or fufu.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or lamb, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, curry powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add the meat cubes to the bowl and toss to coat.
Thread the meat onto the skewers.
Grill the skewers for 8-10 minutes, or until the meat is cooked through.

title: Jollof Rice (West African One-Pot Dish)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the cumin, paprika, and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the water, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and the liquid has been absorbed.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and yeast.
Gradually add the water and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Add the salt and mix well.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the batter rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of the batter into the skillet and tilt to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip the injera and cook for another minute.

title: Fufu (Central African Starch Dish)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
Gradually add the water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, or until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Divide the dough into 4-6 pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Cook the fufu in boiling water for 10-15 minutes, or until it floats to the surface.

title: Kenkey (Ghanaian Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine cornmeal and salt.
Gradually add the water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, or until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Shape the dough into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Wrap the dough in a cloth and let it ferment in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Steam the kenkey for 10-15 minutes, or until it is cooked through.

title: Kenkey
ingredients: 2 cups fermented corn dough, broken into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the corn dough and water. Mix well until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes pliable.
Shape the dough into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the kenkey until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with a sprinkle of salt.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add the cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Add the rice and stir to coat the rice in the spice mixture.
Add the water and tomato puree. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the rice is cooked.

title: Sosatie
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the meat, sugar, oil, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Thread the meat onto the bamboo skewers.
Grill the sosatie over medium heat for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Fufu
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt.
Gradually add the water, mixing until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes pliable.
Divide the dough into small pieces and shape into small balls.
Boil the fufu in a large pot of water for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Groundnut Stew
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add the cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Add the groundnuts and stir to coat in the spice mixture.
Add the water and potatoes. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are cooked.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add rice and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add water, tomato puree, and beef broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together brown sugar, oil, garlic, rosemary, coriander, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add meat and mix until coated with marinade.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Kenkey (Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal and water until smooth.
Add yeast and salt; mix until combined.
Transfer mixture to a clean cloth, tie into a bundle, and let ferment in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Knead dough and shape into small balls.
Steam or boil balls for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Fufu (Boiled Cassava Starch)
instructions: In a large pot, combine cassava starch and water.
Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until starch has broken down.
Knead dough with your hands until smooth and pliable.
Serve with your favorite soup or stew.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together teff flour and water until smooth.
Add yeast and salt; mix until combined.
Let batter rest in a warm place for 24-48 hours, or until it has started to bubble.
Heat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour in 1/4 cup of batter and tilt pan to evenly coat the surface.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until rice is tender, 20-25 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 5 minutes.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10-12 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together brown sugar, oil, garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add meat to the bowl and toss to coat with the marinade.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
