Grill skewers over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 8-10 minutes.

title: Kenkey (Fermented Corn Dough)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together cornmeal and water until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth.
Place dough in a warm, draft-free place and let ferment for 24 hours.
Punch down dough and shape into small balls.
Steam balls over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Tagine (Moroccan Chicken Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large clay or ceramic pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, ginger, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth, diced tomatoes, carrots, and potatoes. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.

title: Fufu (Boiled Cassava and Plantain)
ingredients: 2 large cassava tubers, peeled and chopped
instructions: In a large pot, combine cassava and plantain.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until cassava and plantain are tender.
Use a fork to mash the mixture into a sticky dough.
Serve with your choice of soup or stew.

title: Jollof Rice (West African)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and continue to simmer for 5 minutes.

title: Sosatie (South African)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes
10-12 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together oil, garlic, curry powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add meat and mix to coat with spice mixture.
Thread meat onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill skewers over medium heat, turning occasionally, until meat is cooked through.

title: Kenkey with Pepper Sauce (Ghanaian)
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, salt, and pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Serve pepper sauce over kenkey.

title: Injera (Ethiopian)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together flour and yeast.
Gradually add water, stirring to form a smooth batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter into the skillet and tilt to form a circular shape.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip and cook for another minute.

title: Fufu with Light Soup (Central African)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together flour and water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4-6 pieces and shape each into a ball.
Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper; sauté until onion is translucent.
Serve fufu with light soup.

title: West African Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water, tomato puree, and beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cover.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked.

title: Ethiopian Injera Bread
instructions: In a large bowl, mix flour and water to form a smooth batter.
Add yeast and salt, and mix well.
Cover the bowl with a cloth and let it ferment for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of batter onto the pan and spread it evenly.
Cook for 1-2 minutes or until the edges start to curl.
Flip and cook for another minute.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and ginger, and cook until onions are translucent.
Add spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add broth, apricots, and parsley.
Cover the pot and simmer for 30-40 minutes or until chicken is cooked.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large skillet, cook beef over medium heat until browned.
Add onion, garlic, cilantro, parsley, and mint, and cook until onion is translucent.
In a large bowl, mix breadcrumbs, eggs, milk, cheese, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Add cooked beef mixture to the bowl and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and bake for 35-40 minutes or until set.

title: Senegalese Groundnut Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add ground beef and cook until browned.
Add cilantro, parsley, and mint, and cook for 1 minute.
Add groundnuts, broth, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until thickened.

title: Jollof Rice (Ghana)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; cook, stirring constantly, 1 minute.
Add rice; cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, and tomato paste; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in chopped tomatoes.

title: Sosatie (South Africa)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine sugar, coriander, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add beef or lamb; toss to coat.
Thread meat onto skewers.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent.
Add beef or lamb; cook, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Add beef broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, covered, until meat is cooked through.

title: Kenkey (Ghana)
instructions: Cut kenkey into 1-inch pieces.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant.
Add kenkey; cook, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Add water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, covered, until liquid is absorbed.
Stir in parsley and salt.

title: Fufu (Central Africa)
instructions: Gradually add boiling water to cassava flour; mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough until smooth.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add dough; cook, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Stir in parsley.

title: Injera (Ethiopia)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, water, yeast, and salt; mix until smooth.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap; let mixture ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium-high heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter into skillet; cook until edges start to curl.
Loosen injera with a spatula; flip and cook until other side is lightly browned.

title: Jollof Rice (Ghana)
ingredients: 2 cups uncooked long grain rice, rinsed
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add water, beef broth, diced tomatoes, and tomato paste; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked.

title: Sosatie (South African Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch pieces
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread beef or lamb onto skewers, leaving a little space between each piece.
In a small bowl, mix together oil, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, cumin, coriander powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Brush skewers with spice mixture and cook for 10-12 minutes or until meat is cooked to desired doneness.

title: Fufu with Light Soup (Cameroon)
instructions: In a large bowl, gradually add boiling water to cassava flour, stirring until smooth dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until pliable and smooth.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken broth and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until soup has thickened.

title: Kenkey with Pepper Sauce (Ghana)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add bell peppers and cook until tender.
Add tomatoes and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Serve pepper sauce over kenkey.

title: Injera (Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine teff flour, yeast, and salt.
Gradually add water, stirring until smooth batter forms.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let sit in a warm place for 24-48 hours or until batter has fermented and expanded.
Heat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter into the pan and tilt to evenly coat the surface.
Cook for 1-2 minutes or until edges start to curl and surface is dry.

title: Shakshuka
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and bell peppers, cook until softened.
Add garlic, smoked paprika, and cumin, cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, salt, and pepper, bring to a simmer.
Make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.

title: Msemen
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour and salt.
Gradually add water, knead until a smooth dough forms.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Brush with vegetable oil, cook in a dry skillet over medium heat until puffed and crispy.
Serve hot with butter, honey, or cheese.

title: Brik
ingredients: 1/2 cup of spiced tuna salad (see note)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F.
Cut puff pastry into 4 equal squares.
Place a tablespoon of spiced tuna salad in the center of each square.
Fold the pastry in half to form a triangle, press edges to seal.
Fry the brik until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes on each side.

title: Harissa Chicken Tagine
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large clay pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and garlic, cook until softened.
Add harissa paste, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, and cayenne pepper, cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken, cook until browned on all sides.
Add chicken broth and water, bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.

title: Ghoriba
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, confectioners' sugar, and salt.
Add butter, mix until a crumbly dough forms.
Add almonds, pistachios, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, rose water, and orange blossom water, mix until well combined.
Roll out the dough into a thin circle, place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large clay pot over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add preserved lemons, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.

title: B'stilla (Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook ground meat over medium heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces.
Add onion, garlic, cinnamon, ginger, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper. Cook until onion is softened.
Mix in parsley, cilantro, and almonds.
Roll out puff pastry and place on a baking sheet.
Spread meat mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2-inch border.
Fold the other half over the filling and press edges to seal.
Brush with beaten eggs and bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Harira (Moroccan Lentil Soup)
ingredients: 1 cup dried green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add lentils, tomatoes, parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, cayenne pepper, and salt. Stir to combine.
Add broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until lentils are tender.

title: Msemen (Moroccan Pancakes)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, pepper, cumin, and coriander.
Gradually add water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes or until smooth.
Divide dough into 4-6 pieces and roll out each into a thin circle.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook pancakes for 1-2 minutes or until bubbles appear.
Flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Zalabia (Moroccan Doughnuts)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt.
Gradually add milk and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Add cardamom and mix well.
Add beaten egg and mix until combined.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Drop batter by spoonfuls into oil.
Fry doughnuts for 2-3 minutes or until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.

title: Misir Wot (Red Lentil Stew)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add lentils, water, and berbere spice mix. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until lentils are tender.
Stir in niter kibbeh and serve over injera bread.

title: Doro Tibs (Chicken Stew with Hard-Boiled Eggs)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in niter kibbeh and serve over injera bread, topped with sliced hard-boiled eggs.

title: Siga Tibs (Beef Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add beef and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in niter kibbeh and serve over injera bread.

title: Tibs (Stir-Fried Meat)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef, lamb, or chicken, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add meat and cook until browned.
Stir in niter kibbeh and serve over injera bread.

title: Injera (Traditional Ethiopian Flatbread)
instructions: Combine teff flour, all-purpose flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add water and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Cover and let the batter rest in a warm place for 24 hours.
Heat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of the batter into the skillet and tilt to form a round, flat shape.
Cook for 1-2 minutes or until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add rice; stir to coat with spice mixture.
Add water, tomato puree, and beef broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked.

title: Suya Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast or thighs, cut into thin strips
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; blend until smooth.
Add chicken to the peanut butter mixture; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread chicken onto bamboo skewers.
Brush skewers with oil; grill for 5-7 minutes per side or until cooked through.

title: Egusi Soup
instructions: Grind egusi seeds into a fine paste using a blender or food processor.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; stir for 1 minute.
Add egusi paste; stir for 2-3 minutes.
Add water, beef broth, and diced meat; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer for 20-25 minutes or until meat is tender.
Stir in chopped spinach; cook until wilted.

title: Akara
ingredients: 1 cup dried split peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Grind soaked peas into a fine paste using a blender or food processor.
Add mashed plantains, onion, parsley, cheese, salt, and black pepper; mix well.
Add eggs; mix until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small amounts of batter into the oil; flatten slightly.
Fry until golden brown and crispy; flip and fry the other side.

title: Puff-Puff
instructions: Combine flour, salt, sugar, and yeast in a bowl; mix well.
Gradually add warm water; mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth; let rise for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small amounts of dough into the oil; fry until golden brown and puffed up.

title: Groundnut Stew
ingredients: 1 cup beef or goat meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until onions are translucent.
Add groundnuts and cook for 2 minutes.
Add meat and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes, beef broth, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for 30 minutes or until meat is tender.
Serve hot with fufu or rice.

title: Banku and Tilapia
ingredients: 4 tilapia fillets, deboned and cut into small pieces
instructions: Prepare banku according to traditional method.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until onions are translucent.
Add tilapia and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes or until tilapia is cooked through.
Serve with banku.

title: Kelewele Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into small pieces
instructions: Marinate chicken in ginger, garlic, Scotch bonnet pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add marinated chicken and cook until browned.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with fufu or rice.

title: Fufu with Light Soup
instructions: Prepare fufu according to traditional method.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until onions are translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add beef broth, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes or until soup thickens.
Serve with fufu.

title: Keja Keja
instructions: Heat palm oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until onions are translucent.
Add grated yam and cook for 5 minutes.
Add cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes or until yam is tender.
Serve hot with fufu or rice.

title: Thieboudienne (Senegalese Fish Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds fish (such as bream or tilapia), cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add fish and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add fish broth, water, cabbage, carrots, and parsley. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve hot over rice or with bread.

title: Mafe (Groundnut Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add peanut paste, beef broth, water, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Acarajé (Fried Dough Balls)
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Grind black-eyed peas in a food processor until coarsely ground.
In a large bowl, combine ground peas, flour, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Mix well.
Gradually add water to form a dough. Knead for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Fry dough balls until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Drain on paper towels.

title: Sosatie (Grilled Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine meat, onions, garlic, parsley, cilantro, oil, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Thread meat mixture onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium heat, turning occasionally, until meat is cooked through, about 10 minutes.

title: Yassa (Grilled Chicken with Onions and Peppers)
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken, onions, bell peppers, garlic, oil, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Grill mixture over medium heat, turning occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and onions are caramelized, about 20 minutes.

title: Nyama Choma (Grilled Meat)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef (or goat meat), cut into thin strips
instructions: Marinate the meat in lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, black pepper, cumin powder, and coriander powder for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the meat from the marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Grill the meat for 5-7 minutes per side, or until it reaches your desired level of doneness.
Transfer the grilled meat to a serving platter and garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Ugali (Cornmeal Porridge)
instructions: In a large pot, combine the cornmeal and water. Whisk until smooth.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the porridge thickens.
Add salt to taste and serve hot.

title: Matooke (Steamed Green Bananas)
instructions: Peel the green bananas and place them in a steamer basket.
Steam the bananas over boiling water for 15-20 minutes, or until they are tender.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, then add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the steamed bananas to the pan and stir in salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Kachumbari (Tomato and Onion Salad)
instructions: In a bowl, combine the diced tomatoes and onion.
Stir in chopped cilantro, lemon juice, vegetable oil, salt, and black pepper to taste.
Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature.

title: Sukuma Wiki (Stir-Fried Greens)
ingredients: 2 pounds collard greens or kale, chopped
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, then add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped greens to the pan and stir to combine with the onion and garlic.
Cook the greens for 5-7 minutes, or until they are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned.
Add the curry powder, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
In a separate bowl, mix the breadcrumbs, cheese, and milk.
Add the egg and stir to combine.
Add the meat mixture to the breadcrumb mixture and stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and dot the top with butter.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until set and golden brown.

title: Sosaties
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a bowl, mix the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the lamb or beef skewers to the marinade and mix to coat.
Thread the onions and bell peppers onto the skewers.
Grill the skewers for 8-10 minutes or until cooked through.

title: Malva Pudding
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a bowl, mix the flour, sugar, and baking powder.
Add the softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Add the milk and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Pour the batter into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.
While the pudding is baking, mix the apricot jam and brown sugar in a saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove the pudding from the oven and pour the jam mixture over the top.
Return the pudding to the oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Bunny Chow
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned.
Add the curry powder, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the diced tomatoes, tomato paste, and beef broth, and stir to combine.
Simmer the mixture for 10-15 minutes or until thickened.
Spoon the meat mixture into the hamburger buns.
Dot the top with butter and serve.

title: Melktert
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a bowl, mix the flour and confectioners' sugar.
Add the softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Add the milk and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Roll out the dough and place in a 9-inch tart pan.
In a bowl, mix the eggs, vanilla extract, and salt.
Pour the egg mixture into the tart shell.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until set and golden brown.

title: Harissa Chicken Tagine
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add harissa, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Add broth and bring to a boil.
Cover and transfer to oven; cook at 300°F for 30 minutes.
Stir in parsley and cilantro; serve over couscous.

title: Grilled Merguez Sausages with Couscous
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill sausages until browned, 5 minutes per side.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add couscous and cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook until couscous is tender, 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper; serve with sausages and parsley.

title: Brik with Tuna and Capers
ingredients: 1 can of tuna in oil, drained and flaked
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F.
Place a phyllo sheet on a flat surface.
Brush edges with egg and place a spoonful of tuna mixture in the center.
Fold phyllo into a triangle and press edges to seal.
Fry until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with parsley, cilantro, and capers.

title: Shakshuka with Eggs and Spices
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and bell peppers and cook until softened, 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Add tomatoes and bring to a simmer.
Create 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Transfer to oven and cook at 375°F for 15-20 minutes, or until eggs are set.

title: Zalabia (Tunisian Doughnuts)
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Add sugar, milk, and eggs; mix until a dough forms.
Knead for 5 minutes and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F.
Punch down dough and roll into balls.
Fry until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add spices, preserved lemons, and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Stir in parsley and serve.

title: B'stilla (Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a 1/4-inch thickness.
In a large skillet, cook beef over medium-high heat until browned, breaking up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in spices and cook for 1 minute.
Spread meat mixture over half of pastry, leaving a 1/2-inch border.
Fold other half of pastry over filling and press edges to seal.
Brush with oil and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Zaalouk (Eggplant Stew)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add eggplant and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, spices, and salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until eggplant is tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in parsley and serve.

title: Msemen (Savory Pancake)
ingredients: Filling ingredients (such as onions, garlic, and meat or vegetables)
instructions: Combine flour, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes, until elastic.
Divide dough into 4-6 pieces, depending on desired pancake size.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Brush with oil and cook in a large skillet over medium heat until browned and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Serve with filling ingredients.

title: Harira (Lentil Soup)
ingredients: 1 cup dried red lentils, rinsed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add lentils, water, diced tomatoes, spices, and salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until lentils are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in parsley and serve.

title: Misir Wot (Red Lentil Stew)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, cook for another minute.
Stir in cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes or until lentils are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Tibs (Stir-Fried Meat)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, sliced into thin strips
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for another minute.
Add meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve with niter kibbeh on top.

title: Injera (Sourdough Flatbread)
instructions: Mix teff flour, water, yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Cover and let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium heat.
Pour in a small amount of batter and tilt to evenly coat the pan.
Cook for 1-2 minutes or until the edges start to curl.
Flip and cook for another 30 seconds to 1 minute.

title: Sambusa (Fried or Baked Pastry)
instructions: Mix flour, oil, water, and salt in a large bowl.
Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth dough forms.
Divide into small balls and roll out into thin circles.
Place a tablespoon or two of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold in half and press edges to seal.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown, or bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15-20 minutes.

title: Doro Wot (Chicken Stew)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, cook for another minute.
Stir in cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until softened.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, stir to combine.
Add rice, water, and bay leaves, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove bay leaves, fluff with a fork.

title: Suya Beef
ingredients: 1 pound beef (preferably rump or rib), sliced into thin strips
instructions: In a bowl, combine peanut paste, oil, onion, garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add beef, mix well to coat.
Thread beef onto skewers.
Grill or broil until cooked through, serve hot.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 pound beef or goat meat, cut into small pieces
1 cup leafy greens (such as spinach or kale)
instructions: Grind egusi seeds into a fine paste.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until softened.
Add beef or goat meat, cook until browned.
Add egusi paste, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, stir to combine.
Add water, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, simmer for 10 minutes.
Add leafy greens, cook until wilted.

title: Puff-Puff (Deep-Fried Dough Balls)
instructions: In a bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast.
Gradually add warm water, mix to form a dough.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of dough into oil.
Fry until puffed and golden, drain on paper towels.

title: Akara (Fried Bean Cakes)
ingredients: 1 cup dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Grind beans into a coarse paste.
Add garlic and onion, mix well.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of bean paste into oil.
Fry until golden and crispy, drain on paper towels.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add rice; cook for 2 minutes.
Add water, crushed tomatoes, and tomato paste; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked.

title: Groundnut Stew
ingredients: 1 pound beef or goat meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add beef; cook until browned.
Add beef broth, groundnut paste, and tomato paste; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until meat is tender.

title: Banku and Light Soup
ingredients: 1 pound dried fish, cut into small pieces
instructions: Soak banku in water for 30 minutes.
Grate banku and squeeze out excess water.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add dried fish and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until fish is tender.

title: Fufu and Pepper Soup
ingredients: 1 pound beef or goat meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Knead cassava flour and water to form fufu dough.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add beef; cook until browned.
Add water and Scotch bonnet peppers; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until meat is tender.

title: Groundnut Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Mix groundnuts, sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla extract in a large bowl.
Add baking powder and salt; mix well.
Add flour; mix until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth top.
Bake for 30-40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

title: Thieboudienne
ingredients: 2 pounds fish (such as bream or tilapia), cut into large pieces
2 pounds mixed seafood (such as shrimp, mussels, and clams)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is softened.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add fish, seafood, and tomatoes; cook until seafood is pink.
Add rice; stir to combine.
Add 4 cups water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is tender.

title: Mafé (Groundnut Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or lamb, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; cook until onion is softened.
Add beef or lamb; cook until browned.
Add carrot and potato; cook for 5 minutes.
Add groundnuts, beef broth, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low; simmer for 20-25 minutes or until meat is tender.

title: Acarajé (Fried Bean Cakes)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Grind peas, onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, and coconut in a food processor until smooth.
Add salt and black pepper; mix well.
Shape mixture into small patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry patties until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.

title: Sosatie (Grilled Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Thread beef or lamb onto skewers.
In a large bowl, whisk together oil, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add onion and garlic; mix well.
Add skewers; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat until cooked through.

title: Yassa (Grilled Chicken with Onions and Peppers)
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together oil, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add onion and garlic; mix well.
Add chicken; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Grill chicken over medium-high heat until cooked through.
Grill onions and peppers until tender.
Serve chicken with onions and peppers.

title: Nyama Choma
ingredients: 2 pounds beef, cut into thin strips
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together lime juice, garlic, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, paprika powder, and salt.
Add the beef to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Remove the beef from the marinade and cook for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired doneness.
Serve with chopped cilantro and your favorite sides.

title: Matooke
ingredients: 1 pound green bananas, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add ginger and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped green bananas and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the bananas are tender.
Stir in coconut milk and season with salt to taste.
Serve hot with your favorite sides.

title: Ugali
instructions: In a large pot, bring the water to a boil.
Gradually add the cornmeal, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the ugali is smooth and creamy.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot with your favorite stews or sauces.
Drizzle with oil before serving.

title: Sukuma Wiki
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add ginger and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped collard greens and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the greens are tender.
Stir in tomato paste and season with salt to taste.
Serve hot with your favorite sides.

title: Kachumbari
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the diced tomatoes, onion, and bell pepper.
Stir in chopped cilantro and garlic.
Squeeze lime juice over the mixture and season with salt to taste.
Serve as a condiment or side dish.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds ground beef, lamb or a combination of the two
1 cup dried fruit, such as raisins or currants
2 cups white bread, torn into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned.
Mix in the dried fruit, spices, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish.
Mix the eggs, flour, and melted butter in a bowl.
Add the milk and mix until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture over the meat mixture.
Top with the torn bread pieces.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Malva Pudding
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the sugar, flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add the softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Add the milk, eggs, and vanilla extract and mix until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.
While the pudding is baking, mix the apricot jam and heavy cream in a saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a simmer over medium heat.
Pour the sauce over the pudding and return to the oven.
Bake for an additional 10-15 minutes or until the sauce is bubbly.

title: Sosaties (South African Lamb Skewers)
ingredients: 10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Thread the lamb, onion, and garlic onto the skewers.
Mix the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, curry powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Brush the mixture onto the skewers.
Grill the skewers for 8-10 minutes per side or until cooked through.

title: Melktert (South African Milk Tart)
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, chilled and cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the flour, confectioners' sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add the cold butter and mix until crumbly.
Add the ice-cold water and mix until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough and place in a tart pan.
Bake the crust for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.
Mix the eggs, milk, granulated sugar, salt, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Pour the mixture into the baked crust.
Bake for an additional 25-30 minutes or until set.

title: Bunny Chow
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned.
Mix in the curry powder, cumin, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Add the tomato paste and beef broth and bring to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let cook for 10-15 minutes.
Spoon the meat mixture into the hollowed-out buns.

title: Lamington
ingredients: 2 cups (250g) sponge cake, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) squares
instructions: Dip each cake square into the chocolate mixture, then coat in coconut.
Place on a wire rack to set.
Repeat the chocolate and coconut coating process for a second layer.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 1 whole lamb (2-3 kg), boned and cut into pieces
instructions: Prepare the hangi by digging a hole in the ground and heating stones.
Soak the lamb pieces in water for 30 minutes.
Drain the lamb and add to the hangi with the sliced onions and minced garlic.
Pour in the beef broth, water, tomato paste, brown sugar, thyme, and rosemary.
Cover with more hot stones and let cook for 2-3 hours.

title: Kakadu Plum Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease a 9x13-inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Beat in the eggs, kakadu plum jam, and vanilla extract.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish and bake for 35-40 minutes.

title: Fisherman's Basket
ingredients: 4 x 120g white fish fillets (such as snapper or tarakihi)
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Dip each fish fillet into the panko breadcrumbs to coat.
Place the coated fish in the hot oil and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side.
Remove the fish from the oil and top with grated cheese and chopped parsley.

title: Kumara and Pumpkin Gratin
ingredients: 2 large kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 9x13-inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
Layer the kumara and pumpkin slices in the prepared baking dish.
Dot the top of the kumara and pumpkin with the softened butter.
Sprinkle the grated cheese and chopped parsley over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Lamb Shanks with Rosemary and Garlic
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Season the lamb shanks with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb shanks, then set aside.
Add the garlic and rosemary to the pot and cook until fragrant.
Add the wine, broth, tomato paste, and thyme. Stir to combine.
Return the lamb shanks to the pot and cover with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and braise for 2 1/2 hours.
Remove the pot from the oven and let the lamb rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 kg lamb shoulder or beef brisket
1 kg sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Prepare a hangi by digging a hole and building a fire.
Once the fire has died down, add the oil, garlic, and stock to the hangi.
Add the lamb or beef, potatoes, carrots, and sweet potatoes to the hangi.
Cover the hangi with leaves and earth.
Cook for 3-4 hours or until the food is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.

title: Kumara (Sweet Potato) Gratin
ingredients: 2 kg kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Butter a 20x20cm baking dish.
Layer the kumara slices in the dish, overlapping them slightly.
Dot the top of the kumara with butter.
Sprinkle the cheddar and mozzarella cheese over the kumara.
Pour the heavy cream over the cheese.
Season with garlic, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 45-50 minutes or until the kumara is tender and the top is golden brown.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add the sugar, flour, and salt to the egg whites and beat until smooth.
Spread the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours or until the meringue is crisp and dry.
Remove from the oven and let cool completely.
Whip the butter until smooth, then whip in the heavy cream.
Spread the whipped cream over the cooled meringue.
Top with mixed berries and sliced kiwi fruit.

title: Aussie Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cook the beef in a large pan over medium-high heat until browned.
Add the onion, garlic, peas and carrots, broth, tomato paste, flour, salt, and pepper to the pan and stir to combine.
Simmer the mixture for 10-15 minutes or until the filling has thickened.
Roll out the puff pastry and use to line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Spoon the filling into the pastry-lined muffin tin.
Dot the top of the filling with butter.
Roll out the remaining pastry and use to cover the pies.
Crimp the edges of the pastry to seal the pies and cut a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Combine beef mince, onion, garlic, mixed vegetables, beef gravy, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Roll out puff pastry and place in a greased 24cm (9.5 inch) pie dish.
Fill pastry with meat mixture and brush edges with a little water.
Place second sheet of puff pastry on top and press edges to seal.
Cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 kg lamb or beef, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add lamb or beef and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots, parsnips, and onions to pot and cook until browned.
Add soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and water to pot, then stir to combine.
Return lamb or beef to pot and bring to the boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1-2 hours or until meat is tender.
Serve with vegetables and sauce.

title: Lamb Koftas
instructions: Preheat barbecue or grill to medium heat.
Combine lamb mince, onion, garlic, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and paprika in a large bowl.
Use your hands to mix ingredients until just combined.
Use your hands to shape mixture into 8-10 koftas.
Thread koftas onto skewers, if using.
Barbecue or grill koftas for 5-7 minutes per side or until cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Kumara and Pumpkin Fritters
instructions: Combine kumara, pumpkin, onion, garlic, flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Stir in eggs and milk until just combined.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Drop tablespoonfuls of mixture into pan and flatten slightly.
Cook for 4-5 minutes or until golden brown, then flip and cook for a further 4-5 minutes.
Serve hot with your choice of toppings.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Combine flour, coconut, sugar, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Add softened butter and mix until just combined.
Beat in egg and golden syrup until a dough forms.
Roll out dough on a floured surface to 5mm (1/4 inch) thickness.
Cut into shapes or use a glass to cut out circles.
Place on a baking tray lined with parchment paper and bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Lamb Shanks with Rosemary and Garlic (Australian)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Season the lamb shanks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb shanks until browned, then set aside.
Add garlic and rosemary to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef broth, wine, carrots, and celery to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the lamb shanks to the pot, cover, and transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 2 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender and falls off the bone.

title: Hangi (Traditional Maori Earth Oven)
ingredients: 1 whole lamb, boned and cut into pieces
instructions: Dig a hole in the ground and line it with large rocks.
Build a fire in the hole and let it burn until the ashes are cool.
Add oil to a large pot over medium heat. Sear the lamb pieces until browned, then set aside.
Add onions and garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Add cabbage, carrots, potatoes, and kumara to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the lamb pieces to the pot and cover with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the prepared hangi and cook for 2-3 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Pavlova (Australian Meringue Dessert)
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°F (90°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add sugar to the egg whites and continue beating until stiff and glossy.
Sift flour over the egg mixture and fold until combined.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet and shape into a round.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meringue is crisp and dry.
Remove from oven and let cool completely.

title: Kai Moana (Traditional Maori Fish Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound fish (such as snapper or tarakihi), cut into pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Add cabbage, carrots, and potatoes to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the fish pieces to the pot and cook until cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Anzac Biscuits (Traditional Australian Cookies)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine flour, coconut, and baking soda in a bowl.
Add butter, sugar, and golden syrup to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough to 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut into desired shapes and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the biscuits are golden brown.

title: Kangaroo Burgers with Barbecued Onions
ingredients: Lettuce, tomato, cheese, pickles, and any other desired burger toppings
instructions: Preheat a barbecue or grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine the chopped kangaroo, olive oil, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, Worcestershire sauce, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Use your hands to mix the ingredients until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 4 patties.
Grill the patties for 3-4 minutes per side, or until they are cooked to your desired level of doneness.
Serve the kangaroo burgers on toasted hamburger buns with barbecued onions, lettuce, tomato, cheese, pickles, and any other desired burger toppings.

title: Barbecued Onions
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the sliced onions and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Barbecue the onions over medium heat for 20-25 minutes, or until they are caramelised and golden brown.
Serve the barbecued onions hot.

title: Hangi
instructions: Preheat a hangi to medium heat.
In a large bowl, combine the lamb, potatoes, kumara, stock, olive oil, garlic, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the mixture to the hangi and cook for 2-3 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Serve the hangi hot.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 1 cup mixed berries, such as strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F).
In a large bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form.
Gradually add the sugar to the egg whites and continue beating until stiff peaks form.
Sift the flour over the egg mixture and gently fold until just combined.
Transfer the mixture to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and shape into a round, flat disc.
Bake the pavlova for 1 1/2 hours, or until it is crisp and golden brown.
Allow the pavlova to cool completely.
Split the pavlova in half horizontally using a serrated knife.
In a large bowl, whip the heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
Spread the whipped cream over the bottom half of the pavlova.
Top the whipped cream with the mixed berries.
Place the top half of the pavlova over the berries and serve.

title: Kumara and Pumpkin Fritters
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the kumara, pumpkin, onion, garlic, flour, cornmeal, cheese, parsley, chives, salt, and pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs and a pinch of salt.
Add the egg mixture to the kumara mixture and stir until just combined.
Heat a large frying pan with about 1-2cm of vegetable oil over medium heat.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the kumara mixture into the hot oil and flatten slightly with a spatula.
Fry the fritters for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until they are golden brown and crispy.
Drain the fritters on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large pan, cook the beef until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add onion, garlic, peas and carrots, beef broth, tomato paste, flour, salt, pepper, and thyme to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes.
Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of 1/8 inch (3 mm).
Transfer the beef mixture to one half of the pastry and brush the edges with butter.
Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling and press edges to seal.
Use a knife to create a decorative edge around the pie.
Place the pie on a baking sheet and brush with butter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: New Zealand Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (any white fish works well)
1 cup beer-battered tartar sauce (store-bought or homemade)
instructions: Cut the fish into desired shapes and season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
In a shallow dish, mix together flour, cornstarch, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dip the fish into the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Heat about 1/2 inch (1 cm) of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 3-4 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain the fish on paper towels.
Fry the French fries according to package instructions.
Serve the fish and chips hot with beer-battered tartar sauce.

title: Australian Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whip the egg whites and sugar until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cream of tartar, and salt.
Fold the flour mixture into the egg mixture until no streaks remain.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet and shape into a circle.
Bake for 1-2 hours or until the meringue is crisp and dry.
Allow the meringue to cool completely.
Top the meringue with whipped cream, mixed berries, and additional whipped cream if desired.

title: New Zealand Hangi
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into chunks
2 medium-sized kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and chopped
instructions: Prepare the hangi pit or a large cooking vessel with a steamer basket.
In a large bowl, combine the lamb or beef, potatoes, kumara, onion, garlic, chicken broth, tomato paste, brown sugar, soy sauce, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Mix well to combine.
Place the mixture in the steamer basket and cover with a lid.
Steam for 2-3 hours or until the meat is tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.

title: Australian Damper
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Add the melted butter and water to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-10 minutes.
Shape the dough into a round or oblong shape.
Place the damper on a baking sheet and bake for 30-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Lamington
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and baking powder.
In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the butter until creamy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, beating until just combined.
Pour in the milk and vanilla extract, beating until smooth.
Dip the squares of cake into the chocolate, coating completely.
Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 kg lamb or beef, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and garlic, cooking until softened.
Add the lamb or beef, cooking until browned.
Add the carrots, potatoes, water, stock, tomato paste, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the egg whites until frothy.
Gradually add the sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.
Add the cream of tartar and salt, beating until combined.
Spoon the mixture onto the prepared tray.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until crisp.
Allow to cool completely.
Top with whipped cream, berries, and additional whipped cream.

title: Kumara (Sweet Potato) Fritters
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and grated
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the sweet potato, flour, cornstarch, and cheese.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg and milk until combined.
Add the egg mixture to the sweet potato mixture, mixing until just combined.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop the mixture into the oil, flattening slightly.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and season with salt and pepper.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, coconut, sugar, and baking powder.
In a separate bowl, beat the butter until creamy.
Add the baking soda and salt, beating until combined.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, beating until just combined.
Stir in the oats and nuts (if using).
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto the prepared tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 kg pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
2 kg lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Preheat the hangi to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine the pork, lamb, onions, potatoes, carrots, and sweet potatoes.
In a small bowl, mix together the oil, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Add the spice mixture to the meat and vegetable mixture and stir to combine.
Add the tomato paste and water to the mixture and stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the preheated hangi and cook for 2-3 hours.
Serve hot.

title: Lamb Shanks with Kumara and Pumpkin
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb shanks on all sides, then remove them from the pot.
Add the garlic and onion to the pot and cook until the onion is softened.
Add the kumara and pumpkin to the pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Return the lamb shanks to the pot and bring the mixture to a boil.
Transfer the pot to the oven and cook for 2-3 hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 pieces of fish (such as snapper or tarakihi)
2 cups potato chips (or thinly sliced potatoes)
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together the flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Dip each piece of fish into the flour mixture, then into the milk, and finally into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Fry the potato chips in batches until golden brown.
Serve the fish and chips hot, topped with cheese if desired.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 1 cup mixed berries (such as strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C.
In a large bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar until stiff peaks form.
Gradually add the sugar to the egg mixture and continue beating until stiff peaks form.
Add the vanilla extract to the egg mixture and beat until combined.
Spoon the meringue mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake the meringue for 1-2 hours, or until crisp and dry.
Allow the meringue to cool, then top with whipped cream, berries, and meringue cookies.

title: Anzac Biscuits
ingredients: 1 cup chopped nuts (such as almonds or walnuts)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, coconut, sugar, and baking soda.
Add the butter to the bowl and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the oats and nuts to the bowl and mix until combined.
Drop the mixture by spoonfuls onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake the biscuits for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Allow the biscuits to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Grease a 20cm x 20cm (8 x 8 inch) baking pan and line with parchment paper.
Sift flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt into a bowl.
Add softened butter and mix until just combined.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Add vanilla extract and mix until combined.
Pour in milk and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture into prepared pan and smooth top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Allow to cool in pan for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and coat in desiccated coconut before serving.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 kg lamb shoulder or beef brisket
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb or beef until browned on all sides.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened.
Add garlic, thyme, and tomato paste, and cook for 1 minute.
Add water, soy sauce, carrots, potatoes, and sweet potatoes.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2-3 hours.
Serve lamb or beef with cooked vegetables and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 3 large egg whites, at room temperature
Fresh berries, such as strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Beat egg whites and sugar until stiff peaks form.
Sift flour over egg mixture and fold until combined.
Spread mixture onto prepared baking sheet and smooth top.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours or until crisp and golden.
Allow to cool completely.
Beat softened butter and egg yolks until smooth.
Add vanilla extract and mix until combined.
Spread butter mixture over pavlova base.
Top with whipped cream and fresh berries before serving.

title: Feijoa Crumble
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Combine sliced feijoas and granulated sugar in a bowl.
Transfer feijoa mixture to a 20cm x 20cm (8 x 8 inch) baking dish.
Mix flour, rolled oats, brown sugar, cold butter, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl until crumbly.
Spread crumble mixture over feijoa filling.
Bake for 30-40 minutes or until golden brown and topping is crispy.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

title: Kumara and Pumpkin Soup
ingredients: 2 large kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and chopped
Fresh herbs, such as parsley or cilantro, for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté chopped onion and garlic until softened.
Add chopped kumara and pumpkin, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Use an immersion blender to puree soup until smooth.
Stir in coconut milk and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs.

title: Lamington
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Line a 20x20cm baking tray with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add softened butter and mix until a crumbly mixture forms.
Beat in eggs and vanilla extract.
Spread mixture evenly onto prepared baking tray.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.
Allow to cool completely before cutting into squares.
Dip each square into a mixture of 1 cup (120g) desiccated coconut and 1/2 cup (120ml) boiling water, then coat in extra coconut.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 1 whole lamb or pork shoulder, boned and cut into 2.5cm pieces
2 cups (250g) kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and chopped
instructions: Prepare a traditional hangi by heating rocks in a pit or using a hangi pot.
In a large bowl, combine lamb or pork, oil, onions, garlic, kumara, pumpkin, potatoes, cabbage, carrots, and potatoes.
Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Place mixture into the prepared hangi or pot.
Add tomato paste, beef stock, and water.
Cover and cook for 2-3 hours or until meat is tender.
Garnish with parsley and thyme before serving.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar and continue beating until stiff peaks form.
Add cream of tartar and salt, and beat until combined.
Sift flour over egg mixture and gently fold until just combined.
Spread mixture onto prepared baking tray.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours or until crisp and dry.
Allow to cool completely before topping with coconut, berries, and whipped cream.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine oats, coconut, sugar, and butter.
Beat in eggs and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Roll into balls and place onto prepared baking tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Kumara and Bacon Fritters
ingredients: 2 cups (250g) kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and grated
instructions: In a large bowl, combine kumara, bacon, onion, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, and cheese.
Add dry ingredients to kumara mixture and mix until just combined.
Add parsley and egg, and mix until a dough forms.
Using a spoon, drop dough into hot oil and fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Lamington
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Line a 20x20cm (8x8 inch) baking pan with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour and sugar.
In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to cream butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to butter mixture, beating until combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Allow cake to cool in pan for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
Once cake is completely cool, cut into 2.5cm (1 inch) squares.
Dip each square into a shallow dish of chocolate and then roll in shredded coconut to coat.
Place coated squares on a plate or tray and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to set.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 1 large kumara (sweet potato), peeled and chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine pork, onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots, parsnip and kumara.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, soy sauce, honey, ginger, cumin, salt and pepper.
Pour sauce over meat and vegetables, tossing to coat.
Line a large steaming basket with large leaves (such as cabbage or spinach).
Place meat and vegetables in the steaming basket, leaving some space between each piece.
Cover the basket with a lid and place over boiling water.
Steam for 1-2 hours or until meat is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 500g (1.1lb) firm white fish (such as snapper or cod), cut into 2.5cm (1 inch) pieces
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
In a separate dish, beat eggs.
In a third dish, mix together panko breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt, pepper and paprika.
Dip each piece of fish into flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Dip floured fish into eggs, making sure they are fully coated.
Roll fish in breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat about 5cm (2 inches) of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
When oil is hot, add a few pieces of fish and fry for 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fish from oil with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with tartar sauce if desired.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 2 cups mixed berries (such as strawberries, blueberries and raspberries)
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
In a large bowl, beat egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar to egg mixture, beating until stiff peaks form.
Sift flour and salt over egg mixture and gently fold until combined.
Spread mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours or until meringue is crisp and dry.
Allow meringue to cool completely on baking sheet.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
Spread whipped cream over cooled meringue, leaving a 2.5cm (1 inch) border around edges.
Top whipped cream with mixed berries and sprinkle with shredded coconut.
Serve immediately.

title: Kumara and Kumaru Salad
ingredients: 2 large kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and diced
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss kumara and kumaru with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread kumara and kumaru on a baking sheet and roast for 20-25 minutes or until tender.
In a large bowl, combine roasted kumara and kumaru, red onion and apple.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over kumara mixture and toss to coat.
Sprinkle with parsley and mint and serve.

title: Lamington
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Line a 20x20cm lamington tin with parchment paper.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.
Add softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Add buttermilk and vanilla extract, and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture into prepared tin and bake for 25-30 minutes.
Remove from oven and let cool completely.
Dip cooled cake into a mixture of 1 cup (120g) shredded coconut and 1 cup (120g) powdered sugar.
Cut into squares and serve.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 2 pounds (1kg) lamb shoulder, cut into 4 pieces
instructions: Prepare a hangi by building a fire and heating rocks to high heat.
In a large bowl, combine lamb, potatoes, carrots, parsnips, oil, sugar, garlic, and ginger.
Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Place mixture in a large basket or bag, and add stock and cabbage.
Cover basket or bag with a lid or foil, and place over heated rocks.
Cook for 1-2 hours, or until meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs.

title: Kumara (Sweet Potato) Fritters
ingredients: 2 large kumara (sweet potatoes), cooked and mashed
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mashed kumara, onion, flour, cornstarch, cheese, parsley, egg, salt, and pepper.
Mix well until a thick batter forms.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan with 2-3cm of vegetable oil over medium heat.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop batter into the pan.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Feijoa Crumble
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine feijoas, sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
Mix well until feijoas are evenly coated.
Transfer mixture to a 20x20cm baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine oats, brown sugar, almonds, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add melted butter and mix until crumbly.
Spread crumb mixture evenly over the feijoa mixture.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until topping is golden brown.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine flour, oats, coconut, and baking soda.
Add butter, sugar, and golden syrup, and mix until a dough forms.
If using walnuts, fold them into the dough.
Roll dough into balls, about 1 tablespoon each.
Place balls onto prepared baking sheet, leaving 2cm space between each biscuit.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until lightly golden.

title: Lamington
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Sift flour and sugar into a large bowl.
Add baking powder and salt, mix well.
Add softened butter, mix until crumbly.
Add eggs and vanilla extract, mix until smooth.
Pour into a greased and floured 20cm (8 inch) square cake pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Allow to cool completely.
Cut into squares, dip into melted chocolate, then coat in desiccated coconut.

title: Hangi
ingredients: 1 whole lamb or goat, boned and cut into large pieces
2 cups kumara (sweet potatoes), peeled and halved
instructions: Prepare a hole in the ground, about 30cm (12 inches) deep.
Line the hole with rocks and kindle a fire.
Once the fire is burning well, add wood and allow to burn out.
Add potatoes, kumara, pumpkin, carrots, onions, and garlic to the hole.
Add lamb or goat pieces to the hole.
Cover the hole with a large piece of cloth or a tarpaulin.
Weight down the cloth with rocks and allow to cook for 2-3 hours.
Remove from the hole and garnish with parsley.

title: Kiwifruit Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Sift flour into a large bowl.
Add sugar, cream of tartar, and salt, mix well.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form, then fold into the flour mixture.
Spread onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until crisp and dry.
Allow to cool completely.
Top with whipped cream, kiwifruit, and granola.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Sift flour into a large bowl.
Add sugar, cream of tartar, and salt, mix well.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form, then fold into the flour mixture.
Spread onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until crisp and dry.
Allow to cool completely.
Top with whipped cream, strawberries, blueberries, and granola.

title: Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
instructions: Combine heavy cream and granulated sugar in a saucepan.
Heat over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Temper egg yolks with the hot cream mixture, then return to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in crushed Hokey Pokey.
Chill in the refrigerator before churning in an ice cream maker.

title: Lamb Koftas (Australian)
ingredients: 500g minced lamb, 1 onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
2 lemons, quartered, 1 cup mixed salad leaves, 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Mix lamb, onion, garlic, olive oil, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add breadcrumbs and mix well.
