Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the breakfast hot, topped with toasted bread and butter.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat a large stew pot over medium heat.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pot and cook until they're softened and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the carrots and potatoes to the pot and cook for 5 minutes, until they start to soften.
Add the lamb or beef broth, Guinness stout, flour, thyme, and rosemary to the pot.
Return the browned lamb or beef to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the ground lamb or beef and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, then add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the frozen peas and carrots and cook until they're tender.
Stir in the beef broth and flour, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, until the mixture has thickened.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the top of the mixture, then sprinkle with grated cheese.

title: Bangers and Mash
instructions: Heat a large pot of salted water over high heat.
Add the chopped potatoes and cook until they're tender, then drain and set aside.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sausages and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until softened, then add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the beef broth and flour, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, until the mixture has thickened.
Serve the sausages with the mashed potatoes and the onion gravy.

title: Guinness Beef Stew
instructions: Heat a large stew pot over medium heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pot and cook until they're softened and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the carrots and potatoes to the pot and cook for 5 minutes, until they start to soften.
Add the Guinness stout, beef broth, flour, thyme, and rosemary to the pot.
Return the browned beef to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Bangers and Mash
ingredients: 1 pound Irish sausages, such as bangers, sliced
2 pounds high-quality potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water until tender.
While the potatoes cook, melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced sausages and cook until browned on all sides.
Remove the sausages from the skillet and set aside.
Melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter in the skillet, then add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef broth and bring to a simmer.
Return the sausages to the skillet and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Serve the sausages and sautéed onions over the boiled potatoes.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 4 cups high-quality potatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Boil the chopped potatoes in a large pot of salted water until tender.
While the potatoes cook, melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add the chopped cabbage and cook until wilted.
Mash the cooked potatoes with a fork or potato masher.
Add the cooked cabbage mixture, garlic, butter, milk, salt, and pepper to the mashed potatoes.
Mix until smooth and creamy.

title: Boxty
ingredients: 2 cups high-quality potatoes, peeled and grated
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the grated potatoes, flour, beaten egg, milk, salt, and pepper.
Mix until just combined.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
Drop the potato mixture by 1/4 cupfuls onto the skillet or griddle.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip the boxty and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until golden brown.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 cup Guinness stout or other dark beer
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned on all sides.
Remove the browned meat from the pot and set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pot and cook until softened.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped carrots and potatoes to the pot and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the lamb or beef broth, Guinness stout, tomato paste, and flour to the pot.
Return the browned meat to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, salt, and sugar.
Add the softened butter to the bowl and mix until the dough comes together.
Add the buttermilk to the bowl and mix until a sticky dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Cut a deep cross in the top of the loaf.
Bake the bread for 35-40 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Ulster Fry
instructions: Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add sliced potato and cook until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add sausages and bacon, cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Make two wells in the potato mixture, crack an egg into each well.
Cook until eggs are set, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve with toasted bread and a sprinkle of salt and pepper.

title: Irish Soda Bread
ingredients: 1/4 cup butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Add butter and rub into flour mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Make a well in the center, pour in buttermilk, and mix until a dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Colcannon
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain and mash with butter and milk until smooth.
In a separate pan, sauté chopped onion and garlic until softened.
Add chopped cabbage and cook until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Combine cooked cabbage mixture with mashed potatoes and season with salt and pepper.

title: Guinness Beef Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, carrots, and potatoes, cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in Guinness and beef broth, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours.
Season with thyme and serve hot.

title: Barmbrack
ingredients: 1 cup dried fruit, such as raisins and currants
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Combine dried fruit, sugar, and softened butter in a large bowl.
Beat in eggs until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until golden brown.

title: Parkin
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 20cm (8in) square tin.
In a large bowl, whisk together oat flour, sugar, and baking soda.
In a separate bowl, whisk together treacle, tea, ginger, and cinnamon.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until combined.
Pour the mixture into the prepared tin and bake for 25-30 minutes.

title: Panackelty
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the meat and cook until browned.
Add the onions, garlic, carrots, and potatoes to the pan and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper to the pan and stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the pastry to a thickness of 3mm (1/8in).
In a small bowl, mix together currants, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Spread the currant mixture evenly over the pastry, leaving a 2.5cm (1in) border around the edges.
Brush the edges with the beaten egg and fold the pastry in half to form a triangle.
Press the edges to seal and use a knife to cut a decorative edge.
Place the cakes on the prepared baking sheet and brush with the beaten egg and milk mixture.

title: Toad in the Hole
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Heat oil in a large oven-proof pan over medium heat. Add the sausages and cook until browned.
Add the onion and garlic to the pan and cook until the onion is tender.
Pour the Yorkshire pudding batter over the sausages and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the pan to the oven and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until the pudding is golden brown.

title: Steamed Ginger Pudding
instructions: Preheat steamer and fill the bottom with water.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, ginger, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, and water.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until combined.
Pour the mixture into 4 individual pudding basins or ramekins.
Place the basins in the steamer and steam for 1-2 hours, or until the pudding is cooked through and a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 pounds cod fillets, cut into chunky pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F.
Dredge the fish pieces in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured fish in buttermilk, then coat in panko breadcrumbs.
Repeat the breading process with the remaining fish pieces.
Fry the fish in batches until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the fried fish on paper towels.
Heat the vegetable oil to 320°F.
Fry the chips in batches until golden brown, about 3-5 minutes.
Drain the fried chips on paper towels.
Serve the fish and chips hot with malt vinegar.

title: Full English Breakfast
ingredients: 2 slices of bangers and mash (or hash browns)
instructions: Cook the bacon in a pan over medium heat until crispy.
Remove the cooked bacon from the pan and set aside.
Add the sliced mushrooms to the pan and cook until they release their moisture.
Add the sliced tomatoes to the pan and cook until they start to soften.
In a separate pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat.
Add the sausages to the pan and cook until browned on all sides.
In the same pan, crack in the eggs and scramble them until cooked through.
Add the cooked bacon, mushrooms, and tomatoes to the pan with the scrambled eggs.
Serve the full English breakfast hot with black pudding and bangers and mash on the side.

title: Bangers and Mash
instructions: Boil the sausages in a large pot of water until browned on all sides.
Remove the cooked sausages from the pot and set aside.
Add the beef broth to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer and whisk in the flour and thyme.
Add the butter to the pot and stir until melted.
Mash the potatoes in a separate pot until smooth.
Serve the cooked sausages on top of the mashed potatoes with the gravy spooned over.

title: Cornish Pasties
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Make the pastry dough by combining flour and salt, then adding butter and water.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Place 1/2 cup of the filling ingredients in the center of the dough circle.
Fold the dough in half to form a half-circle and press the edges together to seal the pasty.
Brush the pasty with egg wash and bake for 45-50 minutes.

title: Stargazey Pie
ingredients: 2 pounds cod or haddock fillets, cut into large pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the fish pieces, flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Add the melted butter, chopped onions, and minced garlic to the bowl and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.

title: Cornish Cream Tea Scones
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add the diced butter and use a pastry blender to work it into the dry ingredients.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the heavy cream, beaten egg, and vanilla extract.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times until it comes together.

title: Cornish Yarg Cheese
instructions: Heat the milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add the cheese cultures and let sit for 45 minutes.
Add the rennet and let sit for 30 minutes or until the milk has fully coagulated.
Cut the curds and let sit for 10 minutes.
Drain the whey and transfer the curds to a cheesecloth.
Let the cheese age in a cool, dry place for at least 6 months.

title: Cornish Hogs Pudding
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the sausage, breadcrumbs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Add the milk and beaten eggs to the bowl and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Bake for 45-50 minutes or until the pudding is cooked through.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 1 lb lamb or beef, cut into small pieces
instructions: Brown the lamb or beef in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Remove the browned meat and set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pan and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, flour, and herbs to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the stock to the pan, stirring constantly.
Return the browned meat to the pan and bring to the boil.
Transfer the mixture to a large casserole dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Dot the top of the potatoes with butter and season with salt and pepper.
Bake in a preheated oven at 300°F for 25-30 minutes.

title: Panackelty
ingredients: 1 lb beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
instructions: Brown the beef or lamb in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Remove the browned meat and set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pan and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the flour to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the stock to the pan, stirring constantly.
Return the browned meat to the pan and bring to the boil.
Stir in the shredded suet and season with thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a large casserole dish and serve.

title: Lancashire Egg Curry
ingredients: 1 lb beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the beef or lamb and cook until browned.
Add the stock, curry powder, turmeric, cumin, salt, and pepper to the pan.
Bring the mixture to the boil and then reduce the heat to low.
Make 2 holes in the mixture and crack in the eggs.
Cover the pan and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the eggs are cooked through.

title: Chorley Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb beef or lamb, finely chopped
instructions: Combine the chopped beef or lamb, onion, garlic, flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper in a large bowl.
Mix well until just combined.
Add the melted butter and beaten eggs to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Divide the mixture into 4-6 portions, depending on desired size.
Shape each portion into a patty.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat and add a small amount of oil.
Cook the patties for 3-4 minutes on each side or until cooked through.

title: Bury Black Pudding Hotpot
instructions: Brown the sliced black pudding in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Remove the browned black pudding and set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the pan and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the flour to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the stock to the pan, stirring constantly.
Return the browned black pudding to the pan and bring to the boil.
Transfer the mixture to a large casserole dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Dot the top of the potatoes with butter and season with thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Bake in a preheated oven at 300°F for 25-30 minutes.

title: Cullen Skink
instructions: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add smoked haddock and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in milk and water, then add thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot garnished with parsley.

title: Scottish Shortbread
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Gradually add flour and salt, mixing until a dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead a few times.
Roll out to 1/4 inch thickness and cut into desired shapes.
Place on prepared baking sheet and bake for 18-20 minutes.

title: Neeps and Tatties
instructions: Place chopped turnips and potatoes in a large pot of salted water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Drain and mash with butter and milk.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Aberdeen Angus Beef Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds Aberdeen Angus beef, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, carrots, and potatoes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add beef broth, red wine, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cranachan
instructions: In a large bowl, whip heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, mix granulated sugar and toasted oats.
Fold whipped cream into oat mixture until well combined.
Fold in raspberries.
If using whisky, stir in at this point.
Serve chilled.

title: Cawl (Welsh Lamb Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb neck or shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the lamb and cook until browned.
Remove the lamb and set aside. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, carrots, potatoes, and turnip. Cook for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot, add the stock, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Bara Brith (Welsh Tea Bread)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed dried fruit (currants, raisins, and sultanas)
instructions: Soak the dried fruit in the tea for at least 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, combine the sugar, spice, and eggs.
Add the soaked fruit, milk, flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix well.
Pour in the melted butter and mix until combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

title: Laverbread (Welsh Seaweed Pâté)
instructions: Soak the laver seaweed in water for at least 2 hours.
Drain the seaweed and blend with the oatmeal, breadcrumbs, melted butter, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and stir in the lemon juice.
Serve the laverbread with bacon, eggs, and cockles.

title: Cockles (Welsh Mussels)
instructions: Heat the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until softened.
Add the cockles, white wine, water, salt, and pepper. Cover the pot.
Cook for 5-7 minutes or until the cockles open.
Serve the cockles hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Crempogs (Welsh Pancakes)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, and melted butter.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until smooth.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Drop the batter by 1/4 cupfuls onto the pan.
Cook for 2-3 minutes or until bubbles appear on the surface. Flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes.

title: Irish Beef Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds beef stew meat, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Remove beef from pot and set aside. Add onion and garlic to pot and cook until onion is translucent, 5 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes to pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, red wine, thyme, salt, and pepper to pot. Stir to combine.
Return beef to pot and bring to a boil. Cover pot and transfer to oven.
Bake at 300°F for 2 1/2 hours or until beef is tender.

title: Colcannon
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, 15-20 minutes. Drain and mash.
Sauté cabbage and onion in butter until softened, 5 minutes.
Add milk, salt, and pepper to mashed potatoes. Stir to combine.
Add sautéed cabbage and onion to potatoes and stir to combine.

title: Boxty
instructions: Sift flour into a bowl. Add egg, milk, salt, and grated potato. Mix until just combined.
Add grated onion and garlic to potato mixture. Mix until just combined.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop potato mixture into skillet.
Press potato mixture flat with spatula. Cook for 4-5 minutes or until golden brown.
Flip boxty and cook for an additional 4-5 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Irish Soda Bread
ingredients: 1/4 cup butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Add butter to flour mixture and mix until just combined.
Add buttermilk to flour mixture and mix until just combined.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 1 minute.
Shape dough into a round loaf and place on prepared baking sheet.
Cut a cross in top of loaf and bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Full Irish Breakfast
ingredients: 4 slices of toasted Irish soda bread
instructions: Cook Irish bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy, 5 minutes.
Add sausages to skillet and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms to skillet and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Fry eggs in a separate skillet until cooked to desired doneness.
Toast Irish soda bread and serve with full Irish breakfast.

title: Ulster Fry
ingredients: 2 cups new potatoes, peeled and sliced
2 cups black and white pudding, sliced
instructions: Cook the sliced bacon and sausage in a large pan over medium heat until browned.
Remove the cooked bacon and sausage from the pan and set aside.
Add the sliced potatoes to the pan and cook until they are golden brown.
Add the sliced black and white pudding to the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Push the cooked potatoes and puddings to one side of the pan.
Crack the eggs into the other side of the pan and scramble them until cooked through.
Serve the Ulster fry hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Belfast-Style Chicken and Dumplings
instructions: In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add the chicken to the pot and cook until browned.
Add the garlic, flour, chicken broth, thyme, and rosemary to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer.
Stir in the buttermilk to make the dumplings.
Cook for an additional 10 minutes, or until the dumplings are cooked through.

title: Grilled Irish Sausages with Colcannon
instructions: Preheat a grill to medium-high heat.
Grill the Irish sausages until browned and cooked through.
Boil the chopped potatoes until tender.
Drain the potatoes and mash with butter, milk, and flour.
Stir in the chopped kale into the mashed potatoes.
Serve the grilled Irish sausages with colcannon.

title: Northern Irish Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cook the ground beef in a large pan over medium heat until browned.
Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pan and cook until softened.
Add the frozen peas and carrots, beef broth, and tomato paste to the pan.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and dot with butter.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until the potatoes are golden brown.

title: Barmbrack
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Mix together the flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the brown sugar, softened butter, eggs, and mixed spice to the bowl.
Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough until smooth.
Roll out the dough to 1 inch thickness.
Cut out shapes with a biscuit cutter.
Place the shapes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Traditional Yorkshire Parkin
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Grease a 20cm square cake tin and line with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together treacle, sugar, eggs, and milk.
Sift in flour, ginger, cinnamon, and salt. Mix until smooth.
Pour in oil and mix until combined.
Pour into prepared tin and bake for 40-45 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a large pan, cook beef until browned, breaking up with spoon.
Add onion, garlic, peas, and carrots. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Stir in beef broth, tomato paste, and flour. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Transfer mixture to a 20cm square baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and dot with butter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until potatoes are golden brown.

title: Fat Rascals
ingredients: 1 teaspoon dried fruit (such as currants or raisins)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs until well combined.
Sift in flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix until smooth.
Stir in dried fruit and mixed spice.
Drop spoonfuls of mixture onto prepared baking sheet, leaving space between each.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Steamed Yorkshire Pudding
ingredients: 1/4 cup beef drippings or vegetable oil
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour and eggs until smooth.
Add milk and whisk until combined.
Pour into a greased 12-hole muffin tin or a 20cm round cake tin.
Place in oven and immediately reduce temperature to 180°C (350°F).
Steam for 20-25 minutes or until puffed and golden brown.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
On a lightly floured surface, roll out puff pastry to a thickness of 3mm.
Cut into 6-8 equal rectangles.
In a small bowl, mix together sugar, butter, eggs, vanilla, and salt.
Spread a tablespoon of mixture onto one half of each rectangle, leaving a 1cm border.
Sprinkle with currants and fold other half over to form a triangle.
Press edges to seal and use a knife to cut a small slit in the top.
Brush with egg and bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Brown ground beef in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, and peas to the pan and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in beef broth, tomato paste, flour, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Spread mashed potatoes over the top of the meat mixture.
Dot the top of the potatoes with butter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the potatoes are golden brown.

title: Bangers and Mash
instructions: Cook the sliced sausages in a large pan over medium-high heat until browned.
Remove the sausages from the pan and set aside.
Add olive oil to the pan and cook the sliced onions until tender.
Add garlic to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef broth, flour, butter, mustard, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pan and stir to combine.
Return the sausages to the pan and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve the sausages with mashed potatoes.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into chips (fries)
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each piece of fish into the buttermilk, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish in batches until golden brown.
Drain the fish on paper towels.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a separate large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden brown.
Drain the potatoes on paper towels.
Serve the fish with chips.

title: Full English Breakfast
instructions: Cook the sliced bacon in a large pan over medium heat until crispy.
Remove the bacon from the pan and set aside.
Add sausages to the pan and cook until browned.
Remove the sausages from the pan and set aside.
Add black puddings to the pan and cook until browned.
Remove the black puddings from the pan and set aside.
Add sliced kidneys to the pan and cook until browned.
Remove the kidneys from the pan and set aside.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan and cook until tender.
Add sliced tomatoes to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Make four wells in the pan and crack an egg into each well.
Cook the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to desired doneness.
Serve the eggs with bacon, sausages, black puddings, kidneys, mushrooms, and tomatoes.

title: Steak and Kidney Pie
ingredients: 2 pounds beef steak, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat butter in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the steak and kidney until browned.
Add flour to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add beef broth and brown gravy to the pan, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the filling to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cover the filling with the puff pastry, pressing the edges to seal.
Brush the top of the pastry with a little bit of water.
Cut a few slits in the top of the pastry to allow steam to escape.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25-30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Cornish Pasties
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1/2 cup leftover beef or lamb, diced
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Make the pastry by combining flour and salt, then adding butter and water.
Roll out the pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Place the filling ingredients in the center of the pastry.
Brush the edges of the pastry with the beaten egg and fold over the filling.
Bake the pasties for 45-50 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Stargazey Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season the salmon and set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add milk and fish stock, stirring constantly.
Add the butter and parsley, then place the salmon on top.

title: Cornish Splits
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Sift the flour, salt, and baking powder into a bowl.
Add sugar, softened butter, egg, milk, and vanilla extract.
Mix the batter until smooth and combined.
Spoon the batter into greased muffin tin cups.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Porthleven Pasty Crust
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Make the pastry by combining flour and salt, then adding butter and water.
Roll out the pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Use the pastry to line a greased pie dish or individual tart pans.

title: Cornish Cream Teacakes
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt into a bowl.
Add sugar, softened butter, eggs, heavy cream, and vanilla extract.
Mix the batter until smooth and combined.
Spoon the batter into greased muffin tin cups.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 1 pound lamb or beef, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat.
Add lamb or beef, cook until browned, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, and potatoes to the pan, cook until vegetables are tender.
Add beef broth, tomato paste, flour, salt, and pepper to the pan, stir to combine.
Return lamb or beef to the pan, bring to a boil, then cover and transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Panackelty
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat.
Add beef or lamb, cook until browned, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, and potatoes to the pan, cook until vegetables are tender.
Add beef broth and flour to the pan, stir to combine.
Return beef or lamb to the pan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour, or until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Scouse
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat.
Add beef or lamb, cook until browned, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, and potatoes to the pan, cook until vegetables are tender.
Add beef broth and flour to the pan, stir to combine.
Return beef or lamb to the pan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour, or until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine warm milk and yeast, let sit for 5 minutes.
Add sugar, flour, and salt to the bowl, mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of currants in the center of each circle, brush the edges with egg wash.
Fold the dough in half to form a triangle, press edges to seal.
Brush the tops of the cakes with melted butter and confectioners' sugar.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Braised Red Cabbage with Apples
instructions: In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat.
Add cabbage and apples to the pan, cook until the cabbage is tender.
Add brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, and cinnamon to the pan, stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 1 pound smoked haddock, cut into large chunks
instructions: Boil the diced potatoes until tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until softened.
Add the smoked haddock chunks to the saucepan and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the milk and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Stir in the dried parsley, salt, and pepper.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the haddock chunks from the saucepan, then flake the fish into small pieces.
Return the flaked fish to the saucepan and stir in the single cream.
Serve the Cullen Skink hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Neeps and Tatties
instructions: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced turnips and potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, until the turnips and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the heavy cream and chopped parsley.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the Neeps and Tatties hot.

title: Scottish Shortbread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Gradually add the flour to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Cut the shortbread into desired shapes using a cookie cutter.
Place the shortbread shapes on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes.
Transfer the shortbread to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Scotch Broth
ingredients: 2 pounds beef or lamb, cut into large chunks
instructions: In a large saucepan, brown the beef or lamb chunks over medium-high heat.
Remove the browned meat from the saucepan and set aside.
Add the chopped onions to the saucepan and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, carrots, and celery to the saucepan and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, water, and tomato paste. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return the browned meat to the saucepan and add the thyme and rosemary.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, until the meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the Scotch Broth hot.

title: Rumbledethumps
instructions: Boil the diced potatoes until tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until softened.
Add the cooked potatoes to the saucepan and stir to combine with the onion.
Transfer the potato mixture to a baking dish and top with the grated cheese and chopped parsley.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15-20 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve the Rumbledethumps hot.

title: Cawl (Welsh Lamb Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add lamb and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onions, garlic, carrots, potatoes, and turnip, and cook until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add pearl barley, broth, water, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Bara Brith (Welsh Tea Bread)
ingredients: 1 cup dried fruit (such as raisins and currants)
instructions: Soak dried fruit in brewed tea for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large bowl, cream together butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs, then stir in soaked fruit, spice, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add flour and milk, mixing until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes, then shape into a round loaf.
Place loaf on a baking sheet and bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

title: Laverbread (Welsh Seaweed Pâté)
instructions: Rehydrate laver seaweed in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Squeeze out excess water from seaweed and chop into small pieces.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add cream, whisking until smooth.
Beat in eggs, then stir in seaweed and season with salt and pepper.

title: Crempog (Welsh Pancake)
instructions: Whisk together flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, and salt in a large bowl.
Heat a non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat.
Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls onto the pan, cooking until bubbles appear on surface and edges are dry.
Flip pancakes and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Welsh Rarebit (Welsh Cheese Sauce)
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add milk, whisking until smooth.
Add cheddar and Parmesan cheese, stirring until melted and smooth.
Add beer, mustard, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1/2 pound ground beef, 1/4 cup finely chopped onion, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 2 eggs, beaten, 1/4 cup milk, 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
2 tablespoons lard or vegetable shortening, 2 cups all-purpose flour, for dusting
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
Add flour and mix until just combined.
Beat in eggs and milk.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Divide dough in half and shape each half into a ball.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of lard or shortening in the center of each circle.
Fold dough over filling to form a triangle and press edges together.
Dust tops with flour and brush with melted butter.
Place on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, 1/4 cup ice water, 1 egg, beaten, 1 tablespoon milk, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and cold butter. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ice water, stirring with a fork until dough comes together in a ball.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll out dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of melted butter in the center of each circle.
In a small bowl, whisk together egg, milk, sugar, and salt. Pour into each circle.
Top with a sprinkle of granulated sugar and a few chopped nuts, if using.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch fries, 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1 cup beef broth, 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup grated cheddar cheese, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1/4 cup chopped fresh chives, Salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (180°C).
Fry potatoes in batches until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
Drain fries on paper towels and season with salt and pepper.
In a small saucepan, whisk together beef broth and flour. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, or until thickened.
Stir in cheddar and Parmesan cheese until melted. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve fries hot, topped with cheese curds and a drizzle of beef gravy.

title: Tourtiere
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, garlic, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, cloves, and allspice.
Mix the ingredients well until just combined.
Add the flour and mix until just combined.
Turn the mixture onto a lightly floured surface and knead a few times until it comes together.
Form the mixture into a ball and flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Wrap the disk in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Place the tourtiere on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch (1 cm) thick fries
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (180°C).
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain the fries on paper towels and sprinkle with salt.
Heat the cheese curds in the microwave or in a saucepan over low heat until melted.
Place the fries in a bowl and top with the cheese curds and beef gravy.
Serve immediately and enjoy!

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch (3 mm).
Cut out circles of pastry using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of melted butter in the center of each pastry circle.
In a small bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, granulated sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Pour the sugar mixture over the butter in each pastry circle.
Fold the pastry over the filling to form a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Place the tarts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
If using pecans, sprinkle on top of the tarts before baking.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Grill or pan-fry the peameal bacon until crispy.
Toast the hamburger buns.
Spread a layer of mayonnaise and Dijon mustard on each bun.
Add a few slices of peameal bacon to each bun.
Top with lettuce, tomato, and pickles.
Serve immediately and enjoy!

title: Bannock
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the lard or shortening until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times until smooth.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the bannock for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.

title: Tourtiere (Traditional Quebecois Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper. Mix well.
Add eggs to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Roll out dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch. Place into a 9-inch pie dish.
Fill pie crust with the meat mixture and dot the top with lard or shortening.
Roll out remaining dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch. Use to cover the pie and crimp edges to seal.
Cut a few slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of pastry using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
In a small bowl, mix together sugar, flour, and salt.
Add melted butter, eggs, vanilla extract, heavy cream, and brown sugar to the bowl. Mix until well combined.
Place a spoonful of the filling onto one half of each pastry circle.
Fold the other half of the pastry circle over the filling and press edges to seal.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook peameal bacon slices for 3-4 minutes per side, or until crispy.
Toast hamburger buns by grilling or baking for a few minutes.
Spread mayonnaise and Dijon mustard onto the bottom bun.
Add shredded lettuce, sliced red onion, sliced cucumber, and diced tomato to the bottom bun.
Place a cooked peameal bacon slice on top of the vegetables.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

title: Blueberry Grunt
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, mix together blueberries, sugar, flour, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together milk, eggs, and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Pour the batter into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the fruit is bubbly.

title: Fish and Brewis (Salt Cod and Scrunchions)
ingredients: 1 pound salt cod, soaked and flaked
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together flaked salt cod, flour, salt, and black pepper.
Heat butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped scallions to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until crispy.
Add the cod mixture to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Serve with diced hard-boiled eggs and mayonnaise.

title: Tourtière (Traditional Québécois Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, 2 large eggs, 2 tablespoons milk, 2 tablespoons butter, melted, 2 cups pie crust dough, homemade or store-bought
1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley, 1/2 cup chopped fresh thyme
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook the chopped onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add the ground pork and ground beef to the skillet, cooking until browned.
Stir in the flour, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cloves.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs and mix in the milk.
Add the cooked meat mixture to the bowl and stir until well combined.
Roll out the pie crust dough and place in a 9-inch pie dish.
Fill the pie crust with the meat mixture and top with the melted butter.
Bake for 45-50 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Poutine (French Fries with Cheese Curds and Gravy)
ingredients: 2 pounds potatoes, peeled, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 1 cup cheese curds, 1 cup beef gravy
Salt, to taste, Optional: additional toppings such as bacon bits or chopped scallions
instructions: Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch thick fries and soak in cold water for 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (180°C).
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden brown.
Drain the fries on paper towels and season with salt.
Serve the fries hot with cheese curds and beef gravy on top.
Optional: add additional toppings such as bacon bits or chopped scallions.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 large onion, finely chopped, 3 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon ground allspice, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
instructions: In a large pan over medium heat, cook the ground pork and ground beef until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper, allspice, nutmeg, and cinnamon to the pan and cook until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the beef broth, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the butter until melted.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish and let cool to room temperature.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, 1/4 cup ice water, 1 egg, beaten, 1 tablespoon milk, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup chopped pecans (optional)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour and cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the ice water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of melted butter in the center of each dough circle, followed by a tablespoon of granulated sugar and a sprinkle of brown sugar and chopped pecans (if using).
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle, pressing the edges together to seal.
Brush the tops of the tarts with the beaten egg and sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Place the tarts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Pouding Chômeur
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted, 2 large eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, 1 cup milk
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, and brown sugar.
Add the melted butter, eggs, and vanilla extract to the bowl and whisk until smooth.
Pour the batter into 6 (6 oz) ramekins or small baking dishes.
Place the ramekins in a large baking dish and add enough hot water to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cakes are golden brown and set.
Remove the cakes from the water bath and let cool for 5 minutes.
In a small saucepan, combine the heavy cream and granulated sugar.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the cream mixture over the cakes and serve warm.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and cold butter. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour.
Gradually add ice water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of sugar in the center of each circle, followed by a few raisins and a sprinkle of pecans.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle, pressing the edges to seal.
Place the tarts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush with a little bit of milk.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground pork and ground beef.
Add chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and cinnamon to the bowl. Mix well.
Gradually add flour, mixing until just combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together milk and eggs.
Add the wet ingredients to the meat mixture and mix until just combined.
Turn the mixture out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Shape the mixture into a log and wrap in plastic wrap.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours, or until cooked through.

title: Pouding Chômeur
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add sugar, melted butter, milk, eggs, and vanilla extract to the bowl. Mix until just combined.
Pour the batter into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a pan or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the peameal bacon slices until crispy and golden brown.
Meanwhile, toast the hamburger buns on the griddle or in a toaster.
Spread a layer of mayonnaise on the bottom bun, followed by a slice of bacon, some shredded lettuce, and a few slices of red onion.
Top with the top bun and serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and softened butter. Mix until just combined.
Press the mixture into the bottom of a 9x9 inch baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Meanwhile, prepare the filling by whisking together sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Pour the filling over the baked crust and smooth the top.
Melt the chocolate in a double boiler or in the microwave in 30-second increments.
Pour the melted chocolate over the filling and smooth the top.
Refrigerate until set, then cut into bars and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large pan, cook the pork and beef over medium heat until browned.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until the onion is translucent.
Mix in the allspice, ginger, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the water and stir until the mixture thickens.
Beat in the eggs and stir until well combined.
Pour the mixture into a greased 9-inch pie dish and bake for 45 minutes.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the flour, cold butter, and confectioners' sugar.
Gradually add the ice water and stir until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times.
Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each into a ball.
Roll each ball into a thin circle and place a tablespoon of granulated sugar in the center.
Fold the dough over the sugar and press the edges together to seal.
Brush the tops with melted butter and bake for 20-25 minutes.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium heat.
Cook the peameal bacon slices for 3-4 minutes per side, or until crispy.
Split the hamburger buns in half and toast until lightly browned.
Spread mayonnaise and Dijon mustard on the bottom bun.
Add a lettuce leaf, tomato slice, and pickle slice.
Place a cooked peameal bacon slice on top and cover with the top bun.

title: Pouding Chômeur
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and sugar.
Add the melted butter, milk, eggs, and vanilla extract, and stir until well combined.
Pour the mixture into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the pudding is set.

title: BeaverTails
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, and salt.
Add the yeast and warm water, and stir until the yeast is dissolved.
Add the melted butter and stir until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Roll the dough out into a large rectangle, about 1/4-inch thick.
Cut the dough into long, thin triangles, about 1-inch wide at the base.
Deep-fry the dough triangles in hot oil until golden brown.
Roll in cinnamon sugar while still warm.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together 1 cup of flour and confectioners' sugar.
Add cold butter and use a pastry blender or fingers to work into flour mixture.
Press mixture into the bottom and up the sides of 12 tart shells.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, heavy cream, and vanilla extract.
Pour egg mixture into pastry-lined tart shells.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until filling is set.

title: Tourtière
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork and beef.
Add chopped onion, garlic, flour, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper.
Mix well with your hands until just combined.
Divide mixture into 6-8 portions, depending on desired size.
Shape each portion into a ball and then flatten slightly into a disk.
Dust with flour and set aside.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 lbs potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch fries
instructions: Heat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (180°C).
Fry potatoes in batches until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain fries on paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine hot fries and cheese curds.
Pour beef gravy over top and serve immediately.

title: Smoked Meat Sandwiches
ingredients: 1 cup rye bread, cut into 1-inch slices
instructions: Preheat a panini press or grill to medium-high heat.
Butter one side of each bread slice.
Assemble sandwiches by placing a few slices of smoked meat on one slice of bread.
Top with sliced onion, mustard, and pickle slices.
Top with another slice of bread, buttered side up.
Cook until bread is golden brown and cheese is melted.

title: BeaverTails
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and salt.
Add lard or shortening and use a pastry blender or fingers to work into flour mixture.
Gradually add warm water and mix until dough comes together.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Roll out dough to 1/4-inch thickness and cut into 4-6 triangles.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package of frozen puff pastry, thawed
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out puff pastry to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of pastry using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
In a small bowl, mix together sugar, flour, and salt.
Add melted butter, eggs, and vanilla extract to the sugar mixture and mix until well combined.
Place a spoonful of the sugar mixture onto one half of each pastry circle.
Fold the other half of the pastry circle over the filling to form a triangle or a square, and press the edges to seal.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Pouding Chômeur (Poor Man's Pudding)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium saucepan, combine milk, sugar, and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour and eggs.
Gradually add the hot milk mixture to the flour mixture, whisking constantly.
Add melted butter and vanilla extract, and mix until well combined.
Pour the mixture into 6-8 ramekins or small baking dishes.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pudding is set and golden brown.

title: Tourtière (Traditional Québécois Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook the ground pork and beef over medium-high heat, breaking up with a spoon as it cooks, until no longer pink.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
In a small bowl, mix together flour, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper.
Add the flour mixture to the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs and water.
Add the egg mixture to the skillet and cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.

title: Smoked Meat Sandwiches
instructions: Split the hoagie rolls in half and toast until lightly browned.
Spread a layer of mustard on the bottom half of each roll.
Add a layer of sliced smoked meat on top of the mustard.
Spread a layer of mayonnaise on top of the smoked meat.
Top with chopped dill, chives, and thinly sliced red onion.
Place the top half of the roll on each sandwich.

title: Bannock (Traditional Indigenous Flatbread)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add vegetable shortening to the flour mixture and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water to the mixture, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 2-3 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/2 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large skillet, cook the pork and beef over medium heat until browned.
Add the onion, garlic, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, salt, and pepper to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
In a large bowl, combine the flour and eggs.
Add the milk and lard or shortening to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of the meat mixture in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Place the tourtières on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 25-30 minutes.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the flour and cold butter and mix until the butter is fully incorporated into the flour.
Add the ice water to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch (3 mm).
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a spoonful of the sugar mixture into the center of each dough circle.
Top the sugar mixture with a spoonful of the melted butter and a sprinkle of chopped pecans (if using).
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Place the tarts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 20-25 minutes.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a pan or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the peameal bacon slices until crispy and golden brown.
Butter the hamburger buns on the inside.
Place a cooked egg on the bottom bun.
Add a slice of cheese (if using), a few slices of lettuce, a tomato slice, and a pickle slice.
Top with a slice of peameal bacon.
Place the top bun on the sandwich and serve.

title: Poutine
instructions: Cook the French fries according to your preference.
In a small saucepan, heat the beef gravy over low heat.
Add the cheese curds to the gravy and stir until melted and smooth.
Serve the French fries in a bowl and top with the cheese curd gravy.

title: Bannock
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add the lard or shortening to the bowl and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the warm water to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/2 inch (1 cm).
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the bannock for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/4 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup flour and cold butter until crumbly.
Gradually add ice-cold water, stirring with a fork until dough forms.
Roll out dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch and cut into circles.
Fill each circle with a spoonful of sugar and an egg yolk.
Fold dough in half and press edges to seal.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Tourtière (Traditional Quebecois Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook ground pork and beef over medium-high heat, breaking up with a spoon.
Add onion, garlic, flour, salt, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice. Cook until onion is translucent.
Gradually add beef broth, stirring to combine.
Roll out pie dough and place in a 9-inch pie dish.
Fill pie crust with meat mixture and dot top with butter.
Cover with another pie crust and crimp edges to seal.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Smoked Meat Poutine
ingredients: 2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
instructions: Heat beef broth in a large pot and bring to a simmer.
Add sliced smoked meat and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until heated through.
Fry potatoes in hot oil until golden brown.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
Add flour and whisk to combine, cooking for 1-2 minutes.
Gradually add beef broth, whisking to combine.
Add cheese curds and stir until melted and smooth.
Serve smoked meat with fries and cheese sauce.

title: Bannock (Traditional Indigenous Flatbread)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add lard or shortening and use a pastry blender or fingers to work into flour until crumbly.
Gradually add warm water, stirring with a fork until dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 2-3 minutes.
Divide dough into 4-6 pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Cook in a hot skillet or on a griddle until golden brown and puffed.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Cook peameal bacon slices until crispy and golden brown.
Butter hamburger buns and toast until lightly browned.
Assemble sandwiches by placing cooked bacon on buns, followed by shredded cheese.
Serve immediately and enjoy.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/4 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together 1 cup of flour and confectioners' sugar.
Add cold butter and use a pastry blender or fingers to work into flour mixture.
Gradually add ice-cold water, stirring with a fork until dough comes together.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead a few times.
Roll out dough to about 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Press each dough circle into a tart pan with a removable bottom.
In a small bowl, whisk together eggs, vanilla extract, granulated sugar, and brown sugar.
Pour egg mixture into each tart shell, leaving a 1/2 inch border around edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Let cool completely in pans before serving.

title: Tourtière
instructions: In a large skillet, cook ground pork and beef over medium-high heat, breaking up with a spoon, until browned.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper, cloves, and cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute.
Transfer meat mixture to a large bowl and stir in cognac (if using).
Let cool to room temperature.
In a small bowl, whisk together eggs and flour.
Add eggs to meat mixture and stir until well combined.
Transfer meat mixture to a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Pour in beef broth and cover with aluminum foil.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 1 1/2 hours or until hot and bubbly.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
ingredients: Lettuce, tomato, pickles, and any other desired toppings
instructions: Cook peameal bacon slices in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Butter hamburger buns and toast until lightly browned.
Fry eggs in a separate skillet until sunny-side up.
Assemble sandwiches by placing a slice of bacon on each bun, topping with a fried egg, cheese (if using), and desired toppings.

title: Montreal-Style Smoked Meat
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together brown sugar, coriander, black pepper, pickling spice, mustard seeds, coriander seeds, and kosher salt.
Rub spice mixture all over smoked meat, making sure to coat evenly.
Let sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Preheat a smoker to 225°F (110°C) or a charcoal grill to low heat.
Smoke meat for 2-3 hours or until tender and slightly charred.
Slice thinly against the grain and serve.

title: Butter Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, and 1 tsp of garam masala.
Add chicken to marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Heat ghee or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and cook until browned and cooked through.
Transfer chicken to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
In the same skillet, add remaining garam masala, cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper (if using).
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomato puree and chicken broth.
Bring to a simmer and cook until sauce has thickened slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken with sauce spooned over the top and garnished with cilantro.

title: Tourtiere
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook the ground pork and beef over medium-high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it's softened.
Stir in the garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the beaten eggs and cook until the mixture is thickened.
Transfer the mixture to a pie dish and pour in the pork broth.
Cover the pie with puff pastry and bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the ice water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and melted butter.
Spoon a small amount of the sugar mixture into the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges to seal.

title: Peameal Bacon Back Bacon
instructions: Trim any excess fat from the back bacon.
Dredge the bacon in the peameal, pressing the peameal onto the bacon to adhere.
Let the bacon sit for 30 minutes to allow the peameal to set.
Pan-fry the peameal bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy and golden brown.

title: Pouding Chômeur (Poor Man's Pudding)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, milk, granulated sugar, brown sugar, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Beat in the eggs until well combined.
Stir in the melted butter.
Pour the mixture into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the pudding is set and golden brown.

title: BeaverTails
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, and salt.
Add the yeast and whisk until well combined.
Gradually add the warm water, stirring with a wooden spoon until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Cut the dough into long, thin strips.
Fry the dough strips in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and serve.

title: Tourtière (Traditional Québécois Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice, 2 tablespoons lard or vegetable shortening, 1 egg, beaten, 2 tablespoons milk, 2 pie crusts
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, flour, salt, black pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice. Mix well.
Add lard or shortening and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Beat in the egg and milk until just combined.
Roll out one of the pie crusts to fit a 9-inch pie dish. Fill with the meat mixture and cover with the second pie crust.
Crimp the edges to seal the pie and cut a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 45-50 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts (Classic Canadian Dessert)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, 1/4 cup confectioners' sugar, 1/4 cup ice water, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 2 large eggs, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Make the pastry dough by combining flour, cold butter, confectioners' sugar, and ice water in a bowl. Mix until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough to fit a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cut out small squares of dough to fit into 12 muffin cups.
Fill each muffin cup with a spoonful of raisins and a sprinkle of granulated sugar.
Pour a small amount of melted butter over the raisins and top with a piece of dough.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Poutine (Classic Canadian Street Food)
ingredients: 2 pounds French fries, 1 cup cheese curds, 1 cup beef gravy
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (180°C).
Fry the French fries until golden brown.
Drain the fries on paper towels.
In a separate pan, warm the beef gravy over low heat.
Add the cheese curds to the gravy and stir until melted.
Place the fries in a bowl and top with the cheese curd gravy.

title: Montreal-Style Smoked Meat Sandwiches
ingredients: 1 pound smoked meat, sliced, 1 onion, thinly sliced, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 4 hoagie rolls, 1 cup mustard, 1 cup pickles, thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook until caramelized.
Add the sliced smoked meat and cook until heated through.
Warm the hoagie rolls by wrapping them in foil and heating in the oven.
Assemble the sandwiches by spreading mustard on the bottom bun, adding a few slices of smoked meat, some caramelized onion, a few slices of pickles, and a slice of Swiss cheese.
Top with the top bun.

title: Nanaimo Bars (Classic Canadian Dessert)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, 2 cups confectioners' sugar, 2 large eggs, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Make the crust by combining flour, granulated sugar, and cocoa powder in a bowl.
Add the softened butter and mix until a dough forms.
Press the dough into a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the crust is set.
Make the filling by beating the confectioners' sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Pour the filling over the crust and smooth the top.
Melt the chocolate chips in a double boiler and spread over the top of the filling.
Refrigerate until set before cutting into bars.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 package of frozen puff pastry, thawed
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry and cut into squares.
In a small bowl, whisk together sugar, eggs, heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt.
Place a tablespoon of melted butter in the center of each pastry square.
Brush edges with water and fold pastry in half to form a triangle.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook pork and beef over medium heat until browned.
Add onion and garlic and cook until onion is translucent.
In a small bowl, mix together flour, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and allspice.
Add flour mixture to meat mixture and cook for 1 minute.
Add cognac (if using), beaten eggs, and beef broth. Stir until combined.
Roll out pie crust dough and place in a 9-inch pie dish.
Pour meat mixture into pie crust and dot top with butter.
Roll out remaining pie crust and use to cover pie. Crimp edges to seal.

title: Pouding Chômeur
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together melted butter, milk, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Add raisins and stir until coated.
Pour into a 9x13 inch baking dish and dot top with butter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove from oven and pour heavy cream over top. Return to oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes or until cream is bubbly.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook peameal bacon slices until crispy and golden brown.
