Assemble sandwiches by spreading mayonnaise on the bottom bun, followed by a lettuce leaf, a tomato slice, a pickle slice, a red onion slice, a slice of peameal bacon, and finally the top bun.
Serve immediately and enjoy.

title: Québecois Sugar Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together sugar, flour, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together melted butter, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Pour into a 9-inch pie dish and dot top with butter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove from oven and pour heavy cream over top. Return to oven and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes or until cream is bubbly.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 2 pounds ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 medium onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, 2 large eggs, 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup lard or vegetable shortening, 1/2 cup cold water
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, garlic, salt, black pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves. Mix well.
Add the eggs and flour to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces and shape into disks.
Roll out each disk of dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch and use to line 2 9-inch pie dishes.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, lard or shortening, and cold water. Mix until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch and use to cover the pies.
Crimp the edges of the pies and cut a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces, 1/4 cup ice water, 1 egg, beaten, 1 tablespoon milk, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and cold butter. Mix until the dough resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water and mix until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and shape into balls.
Roll out each ball of dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch and use to line a 9-inch tart pan.
In a separate bowl, combine beaten egg, milk, vanilla extract, brown sugar, granulated sugar, and melted butter. Mix until smooth.
Pour the filling into the pastry-lined tart pans and bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the filling is set and the pastry is golden brown.

title: Jiggs Dinner
instructions: Place the corned beef brisket in a large pot and cover it with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 3 hours.
Add the sliced carrots, turnips, potatoes, onion, and garlic to the pot. Continue to simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the beef broth, brown sugar, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot. Simmer for an additional 15 minutes.
Serve the Jiggs Dinner hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 1 pound salt cod, soaked and drained
instructions: Boil the potatoes and onion in a large pot of salted water until tender. Drain and set aside.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the diced pork and cook until crispy.
Add the soaked and drained salt cod to the skillet and cook until flaked and tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together the flour and milk to make a slurry. Add the slurry to the skillet and stir to combine.
Serve the fish and brewis hot, topped with the boiled potatoes and onion.

title: Pea Soup
ingredients: 1 pound split peas, rinsed and drained
instructions: In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until tender.
Add the garlic, split peas, and smoked ham hock to the pot. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth. Alternatively, transfer the soup to a blender and blend until smooth.
Return the soup to the pot and add the milk. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Mum's Cod Cakes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flaked cod, flour, panko breadcrumbs, egg, milk, melted butter, onion, and garlic. Mix until just combined.
Using your hands, shape the mixture into small patties.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add a small amount of oil to the skillet and cook the cod cakes until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve the cod cakes hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.

title: Figgy Duff
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Add the cold butter to the bowl and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
In a small bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, and vanilla extract. Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times until it comes together.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1 inch. Cut into squares or use a biscuit cutter to cut out rounds.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, flour, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper. Mix well.
Add the beaten eggs and mix until just combined.
Turn the mixture onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 2-3 minutes.
Shape the mixture into a large rectangle, about 1 inch thick.
Brush the top with the melted butter and bake for 45-50 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Poutine Râpée
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt. Mix well.
Add the lard or shortening and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work it into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the warm water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Shape the dough into a ball and flatten it slightly into a disk.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Brush the dough with the melted butter and sprinkle with the cheddar and Gruyère cheese.
Fold the dough in half and press the edges to seal.
Cut into wedges and serve with your favorite toppings.

title: Sugar Pie (Tarte au Sucre)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the sugar, flour, and salt. Mix well.
Add the melted butter and mix until the mixture is smooth.
Beat in the eggs and vanilla extract until well combined.
Roll out the pie crust and place it in a 9-inch pie dish.
Pour the sugar mixture into the pie crust and smooth the top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the filling is set and the crust is golden brown.

title: Pea Soup (Potage Saint-Germain)
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the peas, chicken broth, and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the peas are tender.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth.
Stir in the heavy cream and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Québecois Meat Pie (Tourtière au Feu)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, ground beef, onion, garlic, flour, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper. Mix well.
Add the beaten eggs and mix until just combined.
Turn the mixture onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 2-3 minutes.
Shape the mixture into a large rectangle, about 1 inch thick.
Brush the top with the melted butter and bake for 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown.
Transfer the pie to a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot.
Add the beef broth and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for an additional 20-25 minutes, or until the filling is hot and the crust is golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough and place in tart pans.
Mix sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Add raisins if using and mix well.
Pour the filling into the dough-lined tart pans.
Dot the top with butter and bake for 25-30 minutes.

title: Peameal Bacon Back Bacon
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix peameal and black pepper in a shallow dish.
Coat the back bacon in the peameal mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Place the coated bacon on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until crispy.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches
instructions: Preheat slow cooker to low heat.
Season the pork shoulder with salt and pepper.
Place the pork in the slow cooker and cook for 8-10 hours.
Shred the pork with two forks and mix with BBQ sauce.
Split the hamburger buns in half and toast.
Assemble the sandwiches with the pulled pork, cheese, and coleslaw.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook the onion and garlic in a pan until softened.
Add the ground pork and beef to the pan and cook until browned.
Mix in the flour, salt, black pepper, allspice, and nutmeg.
Add the water and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a pie dish and bake for 45-50 minutes.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add the lard or shortening and mix until crumbly.
Add the milk and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5 minutes.
Shape the dough into a circle and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 2 cups salt cod, soaked overnight and drained
2 cups salted bread, toasted and cubed
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add soaked cod, cook until flaked and heated through.
Stir in scallions, parsley, dill, salt, and pepper.
Serve with hard-boiled eggs and toasted bread.

title: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 1 pound salt beef, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add soaked beef, cook until browned.
Add carrots, turnips, and cabbage, cook until tender.
Stir in brown sugar, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Serve with boiled potatoes and bread.

title: Blueberry Griddle Cakes
instructions: Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together sugar, milk, eggs, and melted butter.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, stir until combined.
Gently fold in blueberries.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat, cook until golden brown.

title: Fried Cod Tacos
ingredients: 4 cod fillets, cut into small pieces
Sliced lettuce, diced tomatoes, and tartar sauce for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix together flour, paprika, salt, and cayenne pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate bowl.
Dip cod pieces into buttermilk, then coat in flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep fryer to 350°F, fry cod until golden brown.
Serve in tacos shells with lettuce, tomatoes, and tartar sauce.

title: Pea Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add carrots and celery, cook until tender.
Add split peas, broth, thyme, and parsley.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until peas are tender.

title: New Brunswick Fiddleheads with Bacon and Garlic
instructions: Cook the diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Remove the cooked bacon from the skillet and set aside.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the fiddleheads to the skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes until tender.
Return the cooked bacon to the skillet and stir to combine with the fiddleheads.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve with butter.

title: Digby Scallops with Salt Pork and Potatoes
ingredients: 12 large scallops, rinsed and patted dry
instructions: Cook the diced salt pork in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Remove the cooked salt pork from the skillet and set aside.
Add the diced potatoes to the skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes until tender.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the scallops to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until cooked through.
Return the cooked salt pork to the skillet and stir to combine with the scallops and potatoes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve with chicken broth.

title: New Brunswick-Style Jiggs Dinner
instructions: Cook the diced salt beef in a large pot of boiling water for 2-3 hours until tender.
Add the sliced carrots and turnips to the pot and cook for an additional 30 minutes.
Remove the cooked salt beef from the pot and set aside.
Add the sliced cabbage leaves to the pot and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour to make a roux, then slowly add the beef broth, whisking continuously.
Return the cooked salt beef to the pot and stir to combine with the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve.

title: Moose Stew with Root Vegetables
instructions: Cook the diced moose meat in a large pot over medium heat until browned.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the sliced carrots, turnips, and potatoes to the pot and cook for 5-7 minutes until tender.
Add the beef broth to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1-2 hours until the meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve.

title: New Brunswick-Style Fish Cakes
instructions: Combine the flaked cod, flour, panko breadcrumbs, chopped onion, and minced garlic in a large bowl.
Add the beaten egg and mayonnaise to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Divide the mixture into 6-8 portions and shape into patties.
Pan-fry the patties in a large skillet over medium heat until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with your favorite tartar sauce.

title: Traditional Perogies
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine 1 cup of flour, eggs, warm water, shortening, salt, and pepper. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Roll out the dough to 1/4 inch thickness.
Use a cookie cutter or glass to cut out circles of dough.
Place a tablespoon of cottage cheese and farmer's cheese mixture in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough in half to form a half-circle and press edges together to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook perogies for 5-7 minutes.
Serve with melted butter, sour cream, or fried onions.

title: Bannock Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add lard or shortening and mix until a crumbly mixture forms.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Shape the dough into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Moose Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds moose meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add moose meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove meat from pot and set aside.
Add onion and garlic to pot and cook until softened.
Add carrots and potatoes to pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, thyme, and rosemary to pot.
Return meat to pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1-2 hours or until meat is tender.

title: Pickerel Fish Fry
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each fish fillet into buttermilk, then coat in flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add coated fish fillets to pan and fry for 3-4 minutes per side or until golden brown.

title: Kubasa Sausage and Sauerkraut Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic to pot and cook until softened.
Add kubasa sausage to pot and cook until browned.
Add sauerkraut, chicken broth, water, and caraway seeds to pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Alberta Beef Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove beef from pot and set aside. Add onions and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, red wine, tomato paste, flour, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Return beef to pot and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Bannock
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add lard or shortening and mix until crumbly.
Gradually add warm water and mix until dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 4-6 pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Cook bannock for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown.

title: Perogies with Fried Onions
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, eggs, warm water, and melted butter. Mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes and divide into 4 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece of dough into a thin sheet. Cut into circles using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a spoonful of sauerkraut and cheese in the center of each circle. Fold dough over filling and press edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook perogies for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Drain perogies and top with fried onions.

title: Alberta-Style Roast Beef with Gravy
ingredients: 2 lbs beef roast, tied with kitchen twine
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C). Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove beef from pot and set aside. Add flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef broth, red wine, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Return beef to pot and bring to a boil. Cover pot and transfer to preheated oven.
Roast beef for 2-3 hours, or until tender and falling apart. Strain gravy and serve over beef.

title: Tourtière
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork and beef. Mix until just combined.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic and mix until just combined.
Add flour, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg and mix until just combined.
Add lard or shortening and mix until dough forms.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll out each piece into a thin sheet.
Cut into desired shapes using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass. Brush with beaten eggs and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: B.C. Wild Salmon with Lemon Dill Sauce
ingredients: 4 wild salmon fillets (6 oz each), skin removed
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Season salmon with salt and pepper.
Bake salmon for 12-15 minutes or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix together lemon juice, dill, garlic, mayonnaise, and sour cream.
Serve salmon with lemon dill sauce.

title: Vancouver Island Crab Cakes
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, gently combine crab meat, panko breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, egg, mayonnaise, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce.
Divide mixture into 8 portions and shape into patties.
Pan-fry crab cakes until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer crab cakes to a baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes or until cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Prairie Farm-Style Meatloaf
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, cheese, onion, garlic, egg, ketchup, and Worcestershire sauce.
Shape mixture into a loaf.
Place meatloaf on a baking sheet and bake for 45-50 minutes or until cooked through.
Let meatloaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Kootenay River Smoked Salmon Dip
instructions: In a bowl, mix together cream cheese, sour cream, dill, garlic, smoked salmon, and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve with crackers or chips.

title: Fraser Valley Roast Chicken with Root Vegetables
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until browned on all sides.
Transfer skillet to the oven and roast chicken for 45-50 minutes or until cooked through.
Toss root vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Add vegetables to the skillet with the chicken and roast for an additional 20-25 minutes or until tender.

title: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 2 pounds salt beef, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place salt beef in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Add cabbage, carrots, turnips, onion, and garlic to the pot.
Return to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in molasses, brown sugar, mustard, and ginger.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 1 pound salt cod, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and cook until softened.
Add flour to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add eggs and milk to the skillet, whisking constantly.
Cook until the mixture thickens, stirring constantly.
Add salt and pepper to taste.

title: Mussels in White Wine and Garlic
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add mussels to the pot and cook until they start to open.
Add white wine, fish stock, and lemon juice to the pot.
Cover the pot and cook until the mussels are fully open.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cod Cheeks in Beer Batter
ingredients: 1 pound cod cheeks, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, and salt.
Gradually add beer to the bowl, whisking until smooth.
Add egg to the bowl and whisk until combined.
Add cod cheeks to the bowl and toss to coat.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry cod cheeks in batches until golden brown and crispy.

title: Pea Soup
instructions: In a large pot, combine peas, bones, carrots, celery, and onion.
Add chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour, or until peas are tender.
Stir in thyme and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 medium onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup lard or vegetable shortening, 1/2 cup milk, 2 large eggs
2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced, 1 cup chicken broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook the ground pork and beef over medium-high heat, breaking up with a spoon, until browned.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice to the skillet and cook until the onion is softened.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, lard or shortening, milk, and eggs to form a dough.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough in half and roll out each half to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Place one half of the dough in a 9-inch round cake pan and top with the meat mixture.
Top with the diced potatoes and cover with the remaining dough.
Bake for 45 minutes, then reduce heat to 350°F (175°C) and bake for an additional 15 minutes.

title: Tourtiere (Traditional Quebecois Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork, 1 pound ground beef, 1 large onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
2 cups pie crust dough, thawed (homemade or store-bought)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook the ground pork and ground beef over medium heat until browned, breaking up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and cloves to the skillet and cook until the onion is softened.
Stir in the flour to thicken the mixture.
Roll out the pie crust dough to fit a 9-inch pie dish.
Fill the pie crust with the meat mixture and cover with another pie crust or a pie crust top.
Bake the pie for 40-50 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Butter Tarts
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces, 1/4 cup ice water, 1 egg, beaten, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
1 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Make the pastry by combining the flour and cold butter in a bowl until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the ice water and mix until the dough comes together.
Roll out the dough to fit a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cut the dough into squares to fit individual tart pans.
In a bowl, whisk together the heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt.
Pour the cream mixture into the pastry-lined tart pans.
Bake the tarts for 20-25 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
ingredients: 4 slices peameal bacon, 4 hamburger buns, toasted, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 cups shredded lettuce, 2 cups thinly sliced red onion
instructions: Cook the peameal bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Assemble the sandwiches by spreading mayonnaise and Dijon mustard on toasted buns.
Add a slice of peameal bacon, shredded lettuce, and thinly sliced red onion to each bun.
Drizzle with maple syrup and serve.

title: Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 pound cod, flaked, 1 onion, finely chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 cup panko breadcrumbs
instructions: In a bowl, combine the cod, chopped onion, garlic, flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Mix in the panko breadcrumbs and beaten eggs.
Shape the mixture into patties.
Heat a skillet with a small amount of oil over medium heat.
Cook the fish cakes until golden brown and crispy.

title: Newfoundland Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 2 pounds salt beef, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the salt beef in a large pot and cover it with cold water. Bring to a boil and then reduce heat to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Add the chopped carrots, turnips, and potatoes to the pot. Cook for an additional 30-40 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pot and cook for 5-10 minutes, or until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the beef broth and butter until the butter is melted.
Serve the Jiggs Dinner hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Cape Breton Lobster Rolls
instructions: In a medium-sized bowl, combine the diced lobster meat, mayonnaise, chopped chives, lemon juice, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Split the hot dog buns in half and toast until lightly browned.
Brush the toasted buns with unsalted butter.
Spoon the lobster meat mixture onto the toasted buns.
Serve the lobster rolls hot, garnished with additional chopped chives if desired.

title: Nova Scotia Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 2 pounds salt cod, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the salt cod in a large pot and cover it with cold water. Bring to a boil and then reduce heat to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 hours, or until the fish is tender.
Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pot and cook for 5-10 minutes, or until the onion is translucent.
Add the chopped carrots and turnips to the pot. Cook for an additional 30-40 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the chicken broth and butter until the butter is melted.
Serve the fish and brewis hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Maritime Pea Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried split peas, rinsed and drained
2 pounds salt pork, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: In a large pot, combine the split peas, salt pork, chopped onions, and garlic. Add enough cold water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 1-2 hours, or until the peas are tender.
Stir in the chicken broth and butter until the butter is melted.
Serve the pea soup hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Prince Edward Island Blueberry Grump
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9-inch (23cm) round cake pan.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add the cold butter to the dry ingredients and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the beaten egg until the mixture forms a crumbly dough.
Gently fold in the blueberries.

title: New Brunswick Sugar Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out pie crust and place in a pie dish.
In a large bowl, combine brown sugar, granulated sugar, and melted butter.
Beat in eggs and vanilla extract.
Pour filling into pie crust and bake for 40-45 minutes.

title: Fried Bannock
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add lard or shortening and mix until crumbly.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes and divide into 4-6 pieces.
Roll out each piece into a circle and fry in hot oil until golden brown.

title: Jiggs Dinner
instructions: Place salt beef in a large pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 2-3 hours.
Add carrots, turnips, and potatoes to the pot.
Simmer for an additional 30-40 minutes.
Add cabbage to the pot and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve with butter and your choice of sides.

title: Cape Breton-Style Fish Cakes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine fish, panko breadcrumbs, onion, and scallions.
Beat in egg and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Shape mixture into patties.
Pan-fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.

title: New Brunswick Ployes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add milk and mix until a batter forms.
Beat in egg and melted butter.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls onto skillet or griddle.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/4 cup lard or vegetable shortening, melted
instructions: Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add melted lard and warm water to the dry ingredients.
Mix until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk.
Cook for 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown.

title: Pemmican
ingredients: 1 cup dried meat (beef or bison), finely chopped
1 cup dried fruit (cranberries or cherries), chopped
instructions: Combine fat, dried meat, and dried fruit in a bowl.
Mix until well combined.
Add honey and salt to the mixture.
Mix until smooth.
Pack into airtight containers or wrap in wax paper.

title: Klahowya Bannock Soup
instructions: Combine beef broth, beef, carrots, potatoes, onion, and garlic in a large pot.
Bring to a boil and then reduce heat to low.
Add flour and stir to thicken.
Add crumbled bannock and stir to combine.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the soup has thickened.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Combine saskatoon berries, sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Roll out the pie crust and place in a pie dish.
Fill the pie crust with the berry mixture.
Roll out the remaining pie crust and use to cover the pie.
Crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg for a glaze.
Bake for 40-50 minutes or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Perogies
instructions: Combine flour and warm water in a bowl.
Add shortening and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin sheet.
Combine cottage cheese, farmer's cheese, dill, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a tablespoon of the cheese mixture in the center of each dough sheet.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle or square shape.
Boil the perogies in salted water for 5-10 minutes or until they float to the surface.

title: Beef on a Bun
ingredients: 2 pounds beef, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Season the beef strips with paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Dredge the beef strips in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the beef strips until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve on hamburger buns with lettuce, tomato, and cheese, if desired.

title: Alberta-Style Bannock
instructions: Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add lard or shortening and mix until the dough resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a sticky dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4-6 pieces and shape into balls.
Flatten each ball into a disk and cook in a hot skillet or on a griddle until crispy and golden.

title: Roast Beef with Horseradish Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Season the roast with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sear the roast on all sides until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the roast to a roasting pan and roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes per pound, or until desired doneness.
While the roast is cooking, combine horseradish, mustard, and beef broth in a small bowl.
Serve the roast with horseradish sauce spooned over the top.

title: Wild Rice and Sausage Casserole
ingredients: 2 cups wild rice, rinsed and drained
1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Cook the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned, breaking up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
Stir in wild rice, chicken broth, and heavy cream.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish and top with grated cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Tourtière (Traditional Alberta Meat Pie)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Combine ground pork and beef in a large bowl.
Add onion, garlic, flour, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the dough to a 9x13 inch baking dish and fill with the meat mixture.
Dot the top of the filling with melted butter.
Roll out the remaining dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch and use to cover the pie.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Add cold butter and use a pastry blender or fingers to work it into the dry ingredients until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Make a well in the center and add warm water. Mix until dough comes together.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Shape dough into a circle and cut into 8 equal pieces. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Smoked Salmon Pâté
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine smoked salmon, cream cheese, lemon juice, and chopped dill.
Blend until smooth, stopping to scrape down sides as needed.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with additional dill if desired.

title: Tourtière
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, dried sage, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Add flour and mix until just combined.
Transfer mixture to a greased 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350°F (180°C) for 1-1 1/2 hours, or until cooked through.

title: B.C. Seafood Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound fish (such as cod or halibut), cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add fish, shrimp, and mussels. Cook until seafood is lightly browned.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add fish stock and heavy cream, whisking constantly.
Bring to a simmer and cook until chowder has thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Kootenay Apple Crumble
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine sliced apples, granulated sugar, flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Mix until apples are evenly coated.
Transfer apple mixture to a 9x9-inch baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine rolled oats, brown sugar, and cold butter. Mix until crumbly.
Spread oat mixture evenly over apple filling.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and apples are tender.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 cups mixed bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, and scotch bonnet peppers (if using).
Add the chicken to the marinade and mix until coated.
Let the chicken marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Grill the chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving with bell peppers and onions.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, cornmeal, cheese, cilantro, scallions, panko breadcrumbs, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined.
Do not overmix.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop the conch mixture into the oil and fry until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add the goat meat and cook until browned on all sides.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until goat is tender.
Stir in coconut milk and continue to simmer for 10-15 minutes.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in lard or shortening until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-10 minutes, until smooth.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry dumplings until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet peppers, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add beef broth, water, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots and continue to simmer for another 20-25 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in cilantro (if using) and serve hot.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and lime juice. Mix well to coat.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess liquid drip off.
Cook chicken until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Serve hot with your choice of sides.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Add conch meat and mix well to coat.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs and buttermilk.
Add panko breadcrumbs to the egg mixture and mix well.
Add the egg mixture to the conch mixture and mix until just combined.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the mixture into the oil and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add coconut milk and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook until meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add shortening and mix until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes.
Cover dough with plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of dough into the oil and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Coconut Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and cook until lightly toasted, about 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk, water, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until liquid is absorbed, about 18-20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in unsweetened shredded coconut.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and brown sugar.
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add chicken to the skillet and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a preheated grill and cook until cooked through.
Serve with scallions and Scotch bonnet peppers, if desired.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Add conch meat, parsley, scallions, garlic, and cheese to the bowl and stir to combine.
Gradually add buttermilk and stir until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop batter into hot oil and flatten slightly.
Fry fritters until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain fritters on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 cup ackee meat, drained and chopped
1 cup saltfish (dried cod), soaked and flaked
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and sauté until softened.
Add saltfish to the skillet and stir to combine.
Add ackee meat to the skillet and stir to combine.
Add Scotch bonnet pepper, if using, and stir to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until softened.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper to the pot and stir to combine.
Add goat meat to the pot and stir to combine.
Add Scotch bonnet pepper, if using, and stir to combine.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook, covered, until meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.

title: Jamaican Patties
ingredients: 1/2 cup beef or chicken filling (see below)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour and salt.
Add shortening to the bowl and use a pastry blender to work into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add cold water and stir until dough comes together.
Turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces and roll into balls.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Blend until smooth.
In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces and jerk marinade. Toss to coat and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade and cook for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, cornstarch, scallions, cheese, egg, hot sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop conch mixture into oil, making sure not to overcrowd the skillet.
Fry for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound boneless goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove goat meat from pot and set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger to pot and cook until onion is translucent.
Add curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Return goat meat to pot and cook until tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Flying Fish Cakes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flying fish, flour, panko breadcrumbs, cheese, egg, scallions, cilantro, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop fish mixture into oil, making sure not to overcrowd the skillet.
Fry for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
ingredients: 1 cup diced beef (such as chuck or round)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook until onion is translucent.
Add beef broth, beef, potatoes, carrots, cumin, and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes, or until beef is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine jerk seasoning, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Blend until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk together marinade ingredients. Add chicken and mix until coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Grill chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Goat Curry
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours or until goat is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper. Garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve over rice or with roti.

title: Fried Fish with Bammy
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (such as snapper or cod)
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each fish fillet into buttermilk, then coat in flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add 2-3 coated fish fillets to skillet and fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with bammy and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
ingredients: 1 pound beef or pork, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using); cook for 1 minute.
Add beef or pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, tomato paste, curry powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
Add potatoes, carrots, and celery. Simmer, covered, for an additional 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs, if desired.

title: Coconut Rice Pudding
ingredients: Raisins or chopped nuts, for garnish (optional)
instructions: Rinse rice in a fine-mesh sieve until water runs clear. Drain and set aside.
In a medium saucepan, combine coconut milk, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Add rice and stir to combine. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes or until rice is tender and creamy.
Stir in vanilla extract and cinnamon. Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in butter until melted. Serve warm or chilled, garnished with raisins or chopped nuts, if desired.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, brown sugar, soy sauce, olive oil, garlic, ginger, and scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Mix well to coat the chicken evenly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Grill the chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, cornstarch, cheese, scallions, cilantro, panko breadcrumbs, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Mix well to combine.
Add the beaten eggs and mix until just combined.
Gradually add the buttermilk and mix until the mixture is smooth.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Using a cookie scoop or spoon, drop the mixture into the hot oil, making sure not to overcrowd the pan.
Fry the fritters for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy.
Drain the fritters on paper towels and serve hot with your favorite dipping sauce.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the goat meat and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the beef broth, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and continue to simmer for 10 minutes.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Add the softened butter and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the buttermilk and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-7 minutes, or until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the dumplings for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and puffed up.
Drain the dumplings on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Coconut Rice
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine rice, coconut milk, water, salt, melted butter, grated ginger, and coconut oil.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve hot.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper.
Add the chicken to the bowl and toss to coat with the marinade.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers.
Brush the grill with oil to prevent sticking.
Grill the chicken for 8-10 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with thyme.

title: Coconut Shrimp
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together panko breadcrumbs, coconut, and Parmesan cheese.
Dip each shrimp into the beaten egg and then coat in the breadcrumb mixture.
Dip the coconut-crusted shrimp into the coconut milk, then coat in the breadcrumb mixture again.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the shrimp in batches until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain the shrimp on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add in the warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat about 2-3 inches of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the dumplings until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Conch Fritters
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together conch meat, flour, cornmeal, panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, egg, onion, bell pepper, jalapeño pepper, and cilantro.
Cover the mixture and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop the conch mixture into the oil, making sure not to overcrowd the skillet.
Fry the fritters until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain the fritters on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder, ginger, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, beef broth, brown sugar, and salt, and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces, or 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Grill chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add cilantro and garlic, and mix well.
Add panko breadcrumbs and mix until just combined.
Add eggs and mix until conch is evenly coated.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop conch mixture into the oil.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 pounds goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add beef broth and tomato paste, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until goat is tender.
Add potatoes and continue to simmer for 30 minutes, or until tender.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 cup dried saltfish, soaked overnight and drained
2 cups ackee fruit, removed from pods and chopped
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add saltfish and cook until broken up and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add ackee and cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Coconut Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and cook, stirring constantly, for 2-3 minutes.
Add coconut milk, water, and unsweetened shredded coconut.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and season with salt to taste.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Grill chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a bowl, combine conch, flour, cornstarch, panko, cilantro, scallions, jalapeño, and garlic. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk. Add to conch mixture and mix until just combined.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the conch mixture into the hot oil. Fry for 2-3 minutes or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add curry powder, cumin, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned on all sides.
Add coconut milk and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Add melted butter and buttermilk. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes until smooth.
Roll out dough to 1/4-inch thickness. Cut into 2-inch squares.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry dumplings until golden brown, flipping halfway through.

title: Callaloo
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using). Cook for 1 minute.
Add callaloo and cook until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in cilantro and scallions. Serve hot.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine flour, jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper.
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken to the skillet and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a preheated grill and cook until cooked through, about 10-12 minutes.
Brush with soy sauce and brown sugar during the last 2 minutes of cooking.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, cornmeal, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Add scallions, cheese, egg, and milk to the bowl and stir until just combined.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the mixture into balls and flatten slightly.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fritters until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound boneless goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic, ginger, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the skillet and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add goat meat to the skillet and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and coconut milk to the skillet and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until the sauce has thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Jamaican Patties
ingredients: 1/4 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
Add shortening and butter to the bowl and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work them into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water to the bowl and stir until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon or two of filling in the center of each circle and fold the dough over to form a half-moon shape.
Press the edges to seal and use a fork to crimp.

title: Flying Fish with Pepper Sauce
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper to the skillet and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add flying fish fillets to the skillet and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Transfer the fish to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
In the same skillet, add flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add water to the skillet, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in butter and parsley until melted and combined.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, soy sauce, pineapple juice, and Scotch bonnet peppers (if using).
Mix well to coat the chicken evenly.
Thread chicken onto skewers, if using.
Grill the chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch, flour, cornmeal, cheese, scallions, cilantro, and panko breadcrumbs.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and milk.
Add the egg mixture to the conch mixture and mix well.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop the conch mixture into the oil and fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lime wedges.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, nutmeg, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Cook until the onions are softened.
Add the beef broth and tomato paste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the meat is tender.

title: Jamaican Patties
ingredients: 1 lb beef, cut into small pieces
instructions: To make the dough, combine flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add the shortening and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work it into the flour.
Gradually add the water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
To make the filling, combine beef, scallions, cilantro, cheese, pimento peppers, curry powder, and cumin.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-circle and press the edges together to seal.

title: Coconut Rice and Peas
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the rice and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, water, and peas and carrots.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with grated coconut.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a blender, blend jerk seasoning, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, scotch bonnet pepper, soy sauce, lime juice, allspice, and thyme.
Rub the jerk seasoning mixture onto the chicken pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until browned on all sides.
Transfer the chicken to a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes or until cooked through.

title: Conch Fritters
instructions: In a bowl, mix conch meat, flour, cornstarch, onion, bell pepper, garlic, egg, panko breadcrumbs, parsley, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the conch mixture into a hot skillet with about 1 inch of vegetable oil.
Fry the conch fritters until golden brown and crispy.
Drain the fritters on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound goat meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add the goat meat and cook until browned on all sides.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper, and stir for 1 minute.
Add coconut milk, beef broth, and tomato paste, and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook, covered, for 1 1/2 hours or until the goat is tender.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 cup saltfish (dried cod), soaked and flaked
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add the ackee and saltfish and stir to combine.
Add the Scotch bonnet pepper, soy sauce, and lime juice, and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Jamaican Patties
ingredients: 1/2 cup beef or chicken, finely chopped
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour and salt.
Add the shortening and use a pastry blender or fingers to work it into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the water and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-7 minutes or until smooth.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of each circle and fold the dough over to form a triangle, pressing the edges to seal.
Brush the tops with the beaten egg for a glaze.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning, garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat with the jerk seasoning mixture.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a preheated grill and cook until cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 lb conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add onion, garlic, and cilantro to the bowl and stir to combine.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs and stir in panko breadcrumbs.
Add egg mixture to the conch mixture and stir until just combined.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop small amounts of the conch mixture into the oil and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using) to the pot and cook until onion is translucent.
Add goat meat to the pot and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper to the pot and stir to combine.
Add beef broth and tomato paste to the pot and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until goat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
If using potatoes, add them to the pot during the last 30 minutes of cooking.

title: Jamaican Patties
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, butter, confectioners' sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Using a pastry blender or your fingers, work the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add beaten egg and warm water to the bowl, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead a few times until smooth.
Divide the dough into 6-8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle and place a tablespoon or two of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-circle and press edges together to seal.

title: Flying Fish with Pepper Sauce
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.

Gradually add fish broth and water to the skillet, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Add butter to the skillet and stir until melted.
Add flying fish fillets to the skillet and cook until cooked through, about 3-5 minutes per side.
Serve fish with pepper sauce spooned over the top.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning, brown sugar, soy sauce, and olive oil.

Let marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Remove chicken from marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Coconut Rice and Peas

Add garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add rice and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly toasted.
Add coconut milk, water, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and stir in peas.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add onion and cook for 2-3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add goat meat and cook for 2-3 minutes, until browned.
Add curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and beef broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1-2 hours, or until meat is tender.

title: Fried Dumplings

Gradually add warm water, stirring with a fork until dough comes together.

Divide dough into 8-10 pieces. Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten slightly into a disk.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry dumplings for 2-3 minutes on each side, until golden brown.

title: Conch Fritters

Heat about 1/2-inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

title: Jerk Chicken

Let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Grill the chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Conch Fritters

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, cornmeal, cheese, scallions, cilantro, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.

Heat about 1-2 inches of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Fry fritters until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
ingredients: 2 lbs beef or pork, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add beef or pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet peppers and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add potatoes and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add ackee and saltfish and stir to combine.
Add ginger and stir to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro.

title: Curry Duck
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet peppers and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add duck and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add 1 cup of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the duck is cooked through.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped (optional)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, jerk seasoning, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).

Serve hot.

title: Conch Fritters
instructions: In a large bowl, combine conch meat, flour, cornstarch, panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, scallions, and cilantro.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk.
Add egg mixture to conch mixture and stir until just combined.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop mixture into balls.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add coconut milk and beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until goat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Flying Fish Cakes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flying fish, panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, scallions, and cilantro.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk.
Add egg mixture to flying fish mixture and stir until just combined.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop mixture into balls.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry cakes for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 cup saltfish (dried cod), soaked and flaked
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped (optional)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
