Add onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add ackee and saltfish and cook, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes.
Add Scotch bonnet pepper (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, and annatto seeds, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add rice, pigeon peas, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
Add chicken broth and sofrito, and stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

title: Mofongo
instructions: Boil plantains in water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain plantains and mash in a large mortar.
Add oil, garlic, and salt, and mash until combined.
Add pork cracklings and mash until combined.
Gradually add chicken broth, and mash until a dough forms.
Shape into small cylinders and serve.

title: Carne Guisada
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add beef broth and tomato paste, and stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours.
Serve hot with rice or yuca.

title: Alcapurrias
instructions: In a large bowl, combine pork, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper, and mix until combined.
Divide yuca dough into small balls.
Flatten each ball into a disk.
Place a tablespoon of pork mixture in the center of each disk.
Fold dough over filling and press edges to seal.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, and fry until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes on each side.

title: Empanadas
ingredients: Filling of your choice (e.g., ground beef, chicken, or cheese)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt, and mix until combined.
Add lard or shortening, and mix until a dough forms.
Gradually add egg and water, and mix until a ball forms.
Divide dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough over filling and press edges to seal.
Fry or bake until golden brown.

title: Grilled Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 4 lbs chicken legs, skin removed, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tablespoon scotch bonnet peppers, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a bowl, mix together allspice, thyme, scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, and black pepper.
Add chicken to the spice mixture and toss to coat.
Grill chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Brush with soy sauce, lime juice, and cilantro during the last minute of cooking.

title: Haitian Stew (Tassot)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot, sauté until softened.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add beef broth, water, potatoes, carrots, and green bananas to the pot.
Return the beef to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Riz Djon Djon (Black Rice)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, carrot, and celery and sauté until softened.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Add water to the saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the rice is tender.
Stir in black mushrooms and parsley.

title: Bouyon de Poisson (Fish Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs fish (such as tilapia or snapper), cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the fish in batches, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot, sauté until softened.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add fish broth, water, potatoes, carrots, and green bananas to the pot.
Return the fish to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through.

title: Poulet à la Creole
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken in batches, then set aside.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot, sauté until softened.
Add cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce, water, potatoes, carrots, and green bananas to the pot.
Return the chicken to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.

title: Sancocho
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
1 pound chicken, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the beef, pork, and chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, yuca, and potatoes to the pot. Stir to combine.
Pour in the beef broth and add the cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Chicharrón con Yuca Frita
ingredients: 2 pounds pork rinds, cut into large pieces
1 large yuca, peeled and cut into sticks
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the pork rinds until crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Fry the yuca sticks until crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the fried pork rinds and yuca sticks to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Season with salt, vinegar, and soy sauce. Stir to combine.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into large pieces
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the garlic, rice, chicken broth, tomato sauce, saffron, cumin, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice is tender.

title: Sopa de Mariscos
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, shrimp, mussels, and clams to the pot. Cook until the seafood is lightly browned.
Pour in the fish broth and add the coconut milk, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 10-15 minutes, or until the seafood is cooked through.

title: Chivo Guisado
ingredients: 2 pounds goat meat, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the goat meat to the pot and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the chopped cilantro, parsley, beef broth, coconut milk, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
ingredients: 2 cups cornmeal, 1 cup okra, 1/2 cup grated coconut, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
instructions: Grate the coconut and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the cornmeal, okra, salt, and pepper.
Gradually add 2 cups of water to the bowl and mix until the cou-cou is smooth.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the flying fish to the pan and fry until golden brown.
Serve the flying fish with the cou-cou and a side of grated coconut.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 onion, chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped
1 pound beef or goat meat, cut into small pieces, 2 cups water, 1 teaspoon thyme, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
2 potatoes, peeled and chopped, 2 carrots, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add the meat to the pot and cook until browned.
Add the water, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and carrots to the pot and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Serve the soup hot.

title: Fried Dumplings
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cold water, 1/4 teaspoon salt
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt.
Gradually add the water to the bowl and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and divide into 8 equal pieces.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Dip each piece of dough into the beaten egg and then fry in the oil until golden brown.
Serve the fried dumplings hot.

title: Braised Beef and Sweet Potatoes
ingredients: 1 pound beef, cut into small pieces, 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 onion, chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped, 1 teaspoon thyme, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add the beef to the pot and cook until browned.
Add the sweet potatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot and stir to combine.
Add the water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer the mixture until the sweet potatoes are tender.

title: Coconut Rice and Peas
ingredients: 2 cups uncooked white rice, 2 cups coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1/2 cup pigeon peas, 1/4 teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the Scotch bonnet pepper to the pot and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the rice to the pot and stir to combine with the oil and pepper.
Add the coconut milk and water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the pigeon peas to the pot and stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low and simmer until the rice is cooked.

title: Cracked Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a bowl, mix together flour, cornstarch, panko breadcrumbs, onion, bell pepper, garlic, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add conch meat to the bowl and mix well.
Add egg and milk to the bowl and mix until the conch meat is well coated.
Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the conch mixture into the hot oil.
Fry the fritters until they are golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the fritters on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Guava Duff
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
In another bowl, mix together guava jam, heavy cream, butter, granulated sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth.
Roll the dough out to about 1/4 inch thickness.
Transfer the dough to a 9x13 inch baking dish and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Peas and Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using) to the saucepan and sauté until softened.
Add garlic to the saucepan and sauté for 1 minute.
Add rice and peas to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Add water to the saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover the saucepan, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice and peas are tender.
Fluff the rice and peas with a fork and season with salt and black pepper.

title: Conch Stew
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using) to the saucepan and sauté until softened.
Add garlic to the saucepan and sauté for 1 minute.
Add conch meat to the saucepan and cook until browned.
Add diced tomatoes, fish broth, salt, and black pepper to the saucepan.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the conch is tender.
Stir in parsley and serve hot.

title: Flying Fish Cakes
instructions: In a bowl, mix together flour, panko breadcrumbs, onion, bell pepper, garlic, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add flying fish to the bowl and mix well.
Add egg and milk to the bowl and mix until the flying fish is well coated.
Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the flying fish mixture into the hot oil.
Fry the cakes until they are golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the cakes on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 2 cups saltfish (dried cod), soaked overnight and flaked
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until softened.
Add saltfish and stir well.
Add chopped ackee, salt, and black pepper; stir gently.
Cook for 5 minutes, then add butter and stir until melted.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a bowl, mix together jerk seasoning, garlic, Scotch bonnet peppers, soy sauce, brown sugar, and thyme.
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat with the jerk seasoning mixture.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken until browned.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1 pound goat meat, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and garlic; sauté until softened.
Add Scotch bonnet pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper; stir well.
Add beef broth and tomato paste; stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Fried Dumplings
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a bowl, combine flour, salt, black pepper, and baking powder.
Add cold butter and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for 5-7 minutes, or until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 6-8 pieces and shape each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle and fry in hot oil until golden brown and puffed.

title: Coconut Rice Pudding
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine coconut milk, water, rice, sugar, salt, and cinnamon.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 18-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in butter until melted.
Let the pudding cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until chilled.

title: Curry Duck
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the duck until browned on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté the onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper until the onions are translucent.
Add the curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the broth, tomato paste, and brown sugar. Stir to combine.
Return the duck to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the duck is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Callaloo
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper until the onion is translucent.
Add the callaloo and cook until wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve with additional garlic, cilantro, and lime wedges.

title: Fried Bake
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, sugar, and baking powder.
Add the shortening and mix until the dough comes together.
Gradually add the warm water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 2-3 equal pieces, depending on desired thickness.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the bakes until golden brown and puffed, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Channa (Chickpea Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper until the onions are translucent.
Add the curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, water, and tomato paste. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Aloo Pie
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Add the shortening and mix until the dough comes together.
Gradually add the warm water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 2-3 equal pieces, depending on desired thickness.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper until the onion is translucent.
Add the potatoes, curry powder, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes.
Place a spoonful of the potato mixture onto one half of each dough circle.
Fold the other half over to form a half-moon shape and press the edges to seal.
Fry the pies until golden brown and puffed, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Lechon Asado
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
In a large bowl, combine pork, sour orange juice, garlic, olive oil, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Mix well and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Place the pork on a rack in a roasting pan and roast for 2-3 hours, or until the meat is tender and caramelized.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add onion and garlic and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add rice, chicken broth, saffron, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.

title: Tamales de Carne
instructions: Soak corn husks in water for at least 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine masa harina and chicken broth.
Add lard or shortening and mix until the dough is smooth.
Add shredded meat, onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of dough on a corn husk, add a tablespoon of filling, and fold the husk to form a tamale.

title: Frijoles Negros
ingredients: 1 cup dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add soaked black beans, cilantro, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add 4 cups water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1-2 hours, or until the beans are tender.

title: Tostones con Mojo
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice plantains into 1-inch rounds and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and flatten with a fork.
In a small bowl, combine sour orange juice, garlic, and cilantro.
Serve tostones with mojo sauce.

title: Arroz con Gandules (Puerto Rican Rice with Pigeon Peas)
ingredients: 1 pound dried pigeon peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add pork sausage and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add smoked pork, pigeon peas, rice, sazón seasoning, annatto seeds, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add 4 cups water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

title: Alcapurrias (Meat-Filled Fritters)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine pork, onion, garlic, cilantro, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine flour and warm water. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Place 1-2 tablespoons of pork mixture in center of each disk.
Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon shape and press edges to seal.
Fry alcapurrias in hot oil until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Tostones (Fried Green Plantains)
instructions: Peel plantains and cut into 1-inch rounds.
Heat oil in large saucepan over medium heat.
Fry plantain rounds until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove from oil and place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Use a flat surface to flatten each plantain round slightly.
Serve tostones hot with salt to taste.

title: Pollo Al Ajillo (Garlic Chicken)
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
instructions: In a large bowl, combine garlic, cilantro, olive oil, salt, pepper, cumin, and smoked paprika.
Add chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and cook until cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Serve chicken hot, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.

title: Mofongo (Mashed Plantains with Garlic and Pork Cracklings)
instructions: Peel plantains and mash in a large bowl using a fork or masher.
Add pork cracklings, garlic, chicken broth, and oil to mashed plantains.
Mix until a dough forms.
Shape dough into 4-6 mofongo patties.
Serve mofongo hot with additional pork cracklings and garlic, if desired.

title: Grilled Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat
In a large bowl, mix together chicken, jerk seasoning, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and smoked paprika
Let marinate for 30 minutes
Grill chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through

title: Riz et Pois (Rice and Peas)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute
Add rice and stir to coat with oil
Add water and bring to a boil
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes
Add pigeon peas and salt, stir to combine

title: Fried Plantains
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
Dredge plantains in a mixture of salt and pepper
Fry plantains in batches until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side
Drain on paper towels

title: Fricassee de Poulet (Chicken Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes
Add water, thyme, and oregano, stir to combine
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes

title: Akara (Haitian Fried Bean Fritters)
instructions: In a large bowl, mash black beans with a fork until mostly smooth
Add onion, garlic, salt, and pepper, stir to combine
Add flour and stir until a thick batter forms
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat
Drop batter by tablespoonfuls into oil and fry until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side
Drain on paper towels

title: Sancocho
ingredients: 2 pounds beef, cut into large pieces
1 pound pork, cut into large pieces
1 pound chicken, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the beef, pork, and chicken; cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet; cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and celery; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Add the beef broth and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, covered, until the meat is tender, about 1 hour.

title: La Bandera
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the tomato; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, beans, and chicken; stir to combine.
Add the oregano, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture is heated through.

title: Chicharrón
ingredients: 2 pounds pork skin, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the pork skin; cook until crispy, about 10 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the salt, pepper, and cumin; stir to combine.
Continue cooking, stirring frequently, until the pork is golden brown and crispy.

title: Mangú
ingredients: Sour cream or cheese, for serving (optional)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the mashed plantains; stir to combine.
Add the cilantro; stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with sour cream or cheese, if desired.

title: Chivo Guisado
ingredients: 2 pounds goat meat, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the goat meat; cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the Scotch bonnet; cook for 1 minute.
Add the cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Add the beef broth and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, covered, until the meat is tender, about 1 hour.

title: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Combine cou-cou mix and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, season flying fish with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Add flying fish to the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side.
Serve flying fish on top of cou-cou.

title: Pepper Pot Soup
ingredients: 1 pound beef or pork, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Add beef or pork to the pot and cook until browned.
Add beef broth, coconut milk, and thyme to the pot.
Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: Combine flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Gradually add water to the bowl and mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 6-8 pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan and fry dumplings until golden brown.

title: Conch Fritters
instructions: Combine conch meat, onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using) in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix flour, cornstarch, coconut, and cilantro.
Add egg to the dry ingredients and mix until a batter forms.
Add conch mixture to the batter and mix well.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan and fry fritters until golden brown.

title: Barbadian Rice and Peas
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper (if using).
Add rice and pigeon peas to the pot and stir to combine.
Add water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until rice is cooked and liquid has been absorbed.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Guava Duff
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Press half of the mixture into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Spread guava jam over the mixture.
Top with remaining mixture.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Conch Fritters
instructions: In a bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add conch meat and mix well.
Add panko breadcrumbs and mix until just combined.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs and mix with buttermilk.
Add egg mixture to conch mixture and mix until just combined.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the mixture into the oil and fry until golden brown.

title: Peas and Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion and sauté until translucent.
Add garlic and sauté for another minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with oil.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes or until water is absorbed.
Add frozen peas and carrots and stir to combine.

title: Cracked Conch with Garlic Butter
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, sliced into thin strips
instructions: In a bowl, mix together softened butter, garlic, lemon zest, salt, and black pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add conch strips and cook for 2-3 minutes per side or until cooked through.
Serve with garlic butter spooned over the top.

title: Guava BBQ Pork
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F.
In a bowl, mix together guava BBQ sauce, brown sugar, garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Place pork shoulder in a large baking dish and brush with the BBQ sauce mixture.
Cover and bake for 2-3 hours or until pork is tender and falls apart easily.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 lb salted cod, soaked overnight and drained
2 cups ackee, removed from shells and chopped
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add garlic, onion, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until softened.
Add chopped ackee and cook until heated through.
Flake salted cod into the pan and stir to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Push ackee mixture to one side of the pan.
Pour beaten eggs into the other side of the pan and scramble until cooked.
Combine eggs with ackee mixture and serve garnished with cilantro, if desired.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine jerk seasoning, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper.
Blend until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk together jerk seasoning mixture, soy sauce, brown sugar, and olive oil.
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat with jerk seasoning mixture.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and grill for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Garnish with thyme and serve.

title: Fried Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Fry dumplings for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (use gloves when handling)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper; sauté until softened.
Add curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add goat meat and cook until browned on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk and beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until goat meat is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot over rice or with roti.

title: Coconut Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until softened.
Add rice and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until lightly toasted.
Pour in coconut milk and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid has been absorbed.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Chicken Roti
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into small pieces
instructions: Combine flour, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a bowl.
Gradually add warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the roti until golden brown and puffed.
In a separate pan, cook the chicken until browned and cooked through.
Add green chilies, garlic, curry powder, soy sauce, and cooked chicken to the pan.
Simmer for 5 minutes and garnish with cilantro (if using).

title: Pholourie
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, potatoes, peas, onions)
instructions: Combine gram flour, all-purpose flour, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a bowl.
Gradually add lukewarm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the pholourie until golden brown and puffed.
In a separate pan, cook the mixed vegetables until tender.
Add green chilies, garlic, and cooked vegetables to the pan.
Simmer for 5 minutes and garnish with cilantro (if using).

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 2 pounds amaranth leaves or callaloo, chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until softened.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped callaloo and salt to the pan.
Cook until the callaloo is tender and the liquid has evaporated.
Add black pepper and butter or margarine to the pan.
Simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with cilantro (if using).

title: Doubles
instructions: Combine soaked peas, water, onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet pepper in a pot.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 30-40 minutes or until the peas are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the bara or roti until golden brown and puffed.
Serve the doubles with the cooked peas and bara or roti.

title: Pelau
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrots, potatoes, peas, onions)
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add garlic and Scotch bonnet pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice, split peas, water, salt, and black pepper to the pot.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the rice and peas are tender.
Add mixed vegetables to the pot and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve the pelau hot.

title: Lechon Asado
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
In a blender, combine sour orange juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth.
Place pork shoulder in a large Dutch oven or a heavy roasting pan. Pour the marinade over the pork, turning to coat evenly.
Roast the pork for 2 1/2 hours, or until it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Let the pork rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the rice, chicken broth, saffron, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.

title: Tostones
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cut the plantains into 1-inch rounds.
Fry the plantains until they are golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the tostones on paper towels and sprinkle with salt.

title: Empanadas de Queso
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated queso fresco or feta cheese
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Add the lard or shortening and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes. Wrap in plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a ball and flatten into a disk.
Place a tablespoon of cheese in the center of each disk. Fold the dough in half and press the edges to seal.
Brush the tops with the beaten egg and water mixture. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Pollo Frito
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces (legs, thighs, wings, and breasts)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour the buttermilk into a separate large bowl.
Dredge the chicken pieces in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured chicken in the buttermilk, making sure it is fully coated.
Dredge the chicken in the flour mixture again, pressing the coating onto the chicken to adhere.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, and onion to the wok.
Cook until the onion is translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with green onions and crushed red pepper flakes.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3 minutes.
Remove the beef and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, and broccoli to the wok.
Cook until the broccoli is tender-crisp, about 2 minutes.
Return the beef to the wok and stir to combine.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch.
Cook for an additional 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Combine the pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic in a bowl.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface, about 5 minutes.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the scallions, cabbage, bean sprouts, and garlic to the skillet.
Cook until the vegetables are tender, about 2 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side of the skillet.
Add a small amount of oil to the other side of the skillet.
Pour in a small amount of the egg mixture.
Tilt the skillet to distribute the eggs evenly.
Cook until the eggs are set, about 1 minute.
Loosen the egg mixture with a spatula and fold it in half.
Repeat with the remaining egg mixture.
Serve hot with soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using).

title: Cantonese-Style Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pot and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the pork belly to the pot and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, cornstarch, sesame oil, and five-spice powder to the pot.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add enough water to the pot to cover the pork belly.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Braise the pork belly for 2 1/2 hours, or until it is tender and the fat is crispy.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 2 pounds beef (such as flank steak or sirloin), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic and broccoli, and cook until the broccoli is tender-crisp.
Return the beef to the wok and stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the ground pork, chopped cabbage, chopped scallions, and garlic.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture onto the center of a wonton wrapper.
Moisten the edges of the wrapper with water, then fold the wrapper into a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Heat the chicken broth in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface.
In a small bowl, mix together the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine.
Add the soy sauce mixture to the pot and stir to combine.
Serve immediately.

title: Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a small spoonful of the ground pork mixture onto the center of each circle.
Moisten the edges of the dough with water, then fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape.
Press the edges together to seal, then repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium heat, add a small amount of vegetable oil, and fry the dumplings until they are golden brown on the bottom.
Serve immediately with a dipping sauce of your choice.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a small bowl, beat the eggs and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped scallions, cabbage, and carrot, and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add the beaten eggs to the pan and cook until the eggs are set.
In a small bowl, mix together the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch.
Pour the soy sauce mixture over the eggs and vegetables in the pan.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional chopped scallions if desired.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, and onion to the wok.
Cook until the onion is translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes to the wok.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir to coat with the sauce.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3 minutes.
Remove the beef from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, and onion to the wok.
Cook until the onion is translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add the broccoli to the wok and cook until tender, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef to the wok and stir to combine with the broccoli.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil to the wok.
Cook for an additional 1 minute, until the sauce is bubbly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Mix well to combine.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface, about 2 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using) to the pot.
Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a small bowl, beat the eggs until well combined.
Add the scallions, cabbage, carrots, soy sauce, and a pinch of salt and pepper to the bowl.
Mix well to combine.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan and cook until the bottom is set, about 2 minutes.
Loosen the edges of the omelette with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes, until the other side is set.
Repeat with the remaining eggs and filling.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add the cornstarch and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the chicken broth to the saucepan, whisking constantly.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the oyster sauce (if using) to the sauce and stir to combine.
Serve the Egg Foo Young with the sauce spooned over the top.

title: Cantonese-Style Roast Pork
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, garlic, and five-spice powder.
Mix well to combine.
Rub the mixture all over the pork, making sure to coat it evenly.
Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and roast the pork for 20 minutes per pound, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 160°F (71°C).
Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before slicing it thinly.
Serve the pork with hoisin sauce (if using) spooned over the top.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining oil, garlic, and onion to the wok.
Cook until onion is translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, sugar, and red pepper flakes.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the wok and stir-fry until coated in the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with green onions and scallions.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining oil, garlic, and broccoli to the wok.
Cook until broccoli is tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return beef to the wok and stir-fry until coated in the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with green onions.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, breaking up with a spoon.
Add cabbage and scallions and cook until wilted.
Add wonton wrappers to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: Beat eggs in a bowl and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add scallions, cabbage, and chicken to the pan and cook until wilted.
Add beaten eggs to the pan and scramble until cooked through.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil to the pan.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Dumplings
ingredients: Filling ingredients (ground pork, chopped cabbage, chopped scallions, etc.)
instructions: Combine flour and oil in a bowl.
Gradually add warm water and mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes.
Divide dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough over filling and press edges together to seal.
Cook dumplings in boiling water for 5-7 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the garlic, onion, bell pepper, and chili pepper, and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return the chicken to the wok and add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch mixture.
Stir-fry until the sauce is bubbly and slightly thickened.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a serving platter and garnish with green onions and peanuts.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove the beef from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the broccoli and garlic, and cook until the broccoli is tender-crisp.
Return the beef to the wok and add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Stir-fry until the sauce is bubbly and slightly thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the beef and broccoli mixture to a serving platter and garnish with green onions.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the ground pork, garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture onto a wonton wrapper, and brush the edges with water.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, bring the chicken broth and water to a boil.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface.
Add the green onions and garlic to the pot, and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Serve the wontons in bowls and garnish with chopped scallions.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a small bowl, beat the eggs and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a small non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the scallions, cabbage, and bean sprouts to the skillet, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables and cook until the eggs are set.
Loosen the edges of the egg mixture with a spatula, and slide the omelette onto a plate.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Add the chicken broth to the bowl and stir until the mixture is smooth.
Pour the sauce over the egg mixture and serve hot.

title: Dumplings
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the flour and vegetable oil.
Gradually add the warm water to the bowl, and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture onto the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
In a large pot, bring 2 cups of water to a boil.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add garlic and onion and cook until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, wine, cornstarch, and spices. Stir until combined.
Return chicken and cook until coated.
Stir in peanuts and season with salt and pepper.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir Fry
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add garlic and broccoli and cook until tender.
Return beef and stir in soy sauce and oyster sauce.
Season with salt and pepper.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Heat oil in pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
In a separate bowl, mix cornstarch and broth until combined.
Add broth mixture to pot and bring to a boil.
Add wontons and cook until cooked through.
Stir in soy sauce and garnish with scallions and cilantro.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add Szechuan peppercorns and cook for 1 minute.
Add pork and cook until browned.
Add tofu and stir in soy sauce and cornstarch.
Return pork and stir in fermented bean paste.
Season with salt and pepper.

title: Dumplings
instructions: Mix flour and water in a bowl until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough in half and press edges together to seal.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and cook dumplings until golden brown.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add the ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch mixture. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry for another minute.
Add the peanuts and green onion and stir-fry for another minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 2 cups beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the broccoli and cook until tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes.
Return the beef to the wok and stir-fry for another minute.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), brown sugar, and sesame oil. Stir-fry for another minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a large pot, bring the chicken broth to a boil.
Reduce heat to a simmer.
In a small bowl, mix together the scallions, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Place a wonton wrapper in the center of a clean surface.
Place a tablespoon of the scallion mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Add the wontons to the simmering broth and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Add the cabbage and mushrooms to the pot and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Steamed Dumplings
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the pork, scallions, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and ginger.
Place a dumpling wrapper on a clean surface.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a half-circle and press the edges together to seal.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Place the dumplings in a steamer basket and steam over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
Serve with a dipping sauce made from equal parts soy sauce and vinegar.

title: Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, chicken broth, and brown sugar. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2-3 hours, or until the pork is tender.
Remove the pork from the pot and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing.
Strain the cooking liquid and discard the solids.
Return the liquid to the pot and bring to a boil.
Whisk in the cornstarch and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened.
Serve the pork with the sauce and garnished with scallions and cilantro.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 teaspoons Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch mixture to the wok, and stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir to combine with the sauce.
Season with sesame oil, salt, pepper, and Szechuan peppercorns.
Serve immediately.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove the beef from the wok and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil.
Add the garlic, onion, and broccoli, and cook until the vegetables are tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch mixture to the wok, and stir to combine.
Return the beef to the wok and stir to combine with the sauce.
Season with sesame oil, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Place a wonton wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, bring the chicken broth to a boil.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface, about 5-7 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch mixture.
Add the mixture to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a small bowl, beat the eggs and set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together the scallions, cabbage, and carrots.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 of the egg mixture into the pan and cook until the edges start to set, about 1-2 minutes.
Add 1/4 of the vegetable mixture to the center of the egg and fold the egg over to enclose the filling.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the egg is cooked through and the bottom is golden brown.
Repeat with the remaining egg and vegetable mixture.
Serve hot with soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using).

title: Dumplings in Hot Pot
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Place a dumpling wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a small spoonful of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a half-moon shape by bringing the two opposite edges together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, bring the water to a boil.
Add the dumplings to the pot and cook until they float to the surface, about 5-7 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch mixture.
Add the mixture to the pot and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp oil in wok over high heat. Add chicken and cook until browned.
Remove chicken and set aside. Add remaining 1/4 cup oil, garlic, onion, and red bell pepper.
Stir-fry until vegetables are tender. Add peanuts, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Return chicken to wok and stir-fry until combined. Mix in sesame oil and cornstarch.
Cook for 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with scallions, if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 lb beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in wok over high heat. Add beef and cook until browned.
Remove beef and set aside. Add remaining 1 tbsp oil, garlic, and broccoli.
Stir-fry until broccoli is tender. Return beef to wok and stir-fry until combined.
Mix in soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Cook for 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Combine pork, scallions, and garlic. Mix well.
Place a wonton wrapper on a flat surface. Place a small spoonful of pork mixture in center.
Dip fingers in water and run around edges of wrapper. Fold wrapper into a triangle and press edges together.
Heat broth and water in a large pot over medium heat. Add wontons and cook until they float.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Serve hot.

title: Dumplings
instructions: Combine flour and oil. Gradually add warm water and mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes. Divide into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle. Place a small spoonful of pork mixture in center.
Fold dough over filling and press edges together. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot. Add dumplings and cook until they float.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: Beat eggs in a bowl. Add scallions, mushrooms, and garlic. Mix well.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium heat. Add egg mixture and cook until edges are set.
Loosen egg with a spatula and fold in half. Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Mix in soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil. Cook for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the garlic, onion, red bell pepper, and Thai chili pepper, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch mixture to the wok, and stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir to coat with the sauce.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove the beef from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and onion, and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the broccoli and cook until tender.
Return the beef to the wok and stir to combine with the vegetables.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil, and stir to combine.

title: Steamed Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, chopped cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sesame oil to the bowl, and mix to combine.
Place a wonton wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the dumpling.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, scallions, and garlic.
Bring the broth to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Add the wonton wrappers to the pot, and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil to the pot, and stir to combine.
Mix the cornstarch with a little water until smooth, and add to the pot.
Stir to combine and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the soup has thickened.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a large bowl, beat the eggs and mix in the chopped scallions, cabbage, bean sprouts, and garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat.
Add the egg mixture to the skillet, and cook until the eggs are set.
Loosen the edges of the eggs with a spatula, and flip the egg foo young over.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the other side is golden brown.
Add the soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using) to the skillet, and stir to combine.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 dried red chili peppers, crushed or 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the wok.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the peanuts and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the cooked chicken back into the wok and stir to combine.
Add the crushed red pepper flakes and cook for an additional minute.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 2 cups sliced beef (such as sirloin or ribeye)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned and cooked through, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove the beef from the wok and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the wok.
Add the broccoli and cook until tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and green onions and cook for an additional minute.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), cornstarch, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the cooked beef back into the wok and stir to combine.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Combine the flour and vegetable oil in a bowl and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the dumplings for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the scallions, cabbage, and carrots and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), cornstarch, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour the beaten eggs over the vegetables and cook until the eggs are set.
Loosen the edges of the omelette with a spatula and slide it onto a plate.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Combine the ground pork, scallions, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), cornstarch, sugar, salt, and pepper in a bowl and mix until just combined.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a clean surface and place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pot and cook the wontons for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, onion, and bell pepper to the wok.
Cook until vegetables are tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Add peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes to the wok.
Stir to combine and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Return chicken to the wok and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, garlic, and broccoli to the wok.
Cook until broccoli is tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch to the wok.
Stir to combine and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Return beef to the wok and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Dumplings
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour and oil.
Gradually add warm water and mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes until smooth.
Divide dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon shape.
Seal edges with a fork or by pressing with fingers.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook dumplings for 5-7 minutes.
Serve with your favorite dipping sauce.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Mix well to combine.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper.
Brush edges with water and fold wrapper over filling to form a triangle.
Press edges to seal.
Bring a large pot of chicken broth to a boil.
Add wontons to the pot and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Heat oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Stir into soup and serve hot.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs and mix in scallions, cabbage, ginger, and garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add egg mixture to the skillet and cook until edges start to set.
Sprinkle soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using) over eggs.
Use a spatula to gently lift edges of omelette and tilt skillet to allow uncooked egg to flow to edges.
Cook until eggs are almost set, about 2-3 minutes.
Dust with cornstarch and serve hot.

title: Beef with Broccoli in Oyster Sauce
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or ribeye), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then add garlic and ginger and cook for 10 seconds.
Add broccoli and cook until tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Return beef to the wok and stir in oyster sauce, soy sauce, and cornstarch mixture.
Cook until sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 small Sichuan peppercorn, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then add garlic and onion and cook until onion is translucent.
Add bell pepper and cook until tender, about 2 minutes.
Add Sichuan peppercorn and cook for 10 seconds.
Return chicken to the wok and stir in soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch mixture.
Cook until sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Stir in sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions and toasted Sichuan peppercorns, if desired.

title: Steamed Dumplings
instructions: Combine flour and cornstarch in a large bowl.
Gradually add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until smooth.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press edges to seal.
Steam the dumplings for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve with soy sauce and sesame oil, if desired.

title: Egg Foo Young
instructions: Beat eggs in a large bowl and set aside.
Heat oil in a small non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add scallions, cabbage, and carrots and cook until tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Pour in eggs and cook until the edges start to set, about 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle soy sauce and oyster sauce over the eggs and stir to combine.
Use a spatula to gently lift and fold the edges of the omelette towards the center.
Cook until the eggs are almost set, about 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle cornstarch over the eggs and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 30 seconds to 1 minute, until the eggs are cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Combine broth, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to a simmer and add cornstarch mixture.
Cook until the soup thickens, about 2-3 minutes.
Add scallions, cabbage, and carrots and cook until tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Add wontons to the pot and cook until cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil, garlic, onion, and red bell pepper to the wok. Stir-fry until the vegetables are tender.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil, garlic, and broccoli to the wok. Stir-fry until the broccoli is tender.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok and stir-fry until the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the ground pork, scallions, garlic, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine. Mix well.
Place a wonton wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, water, and sesame oil. Bring to a boil.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the flour and vegetable oil. Gradually add the warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
In a small bowl, combine the ground pork, scallions, garlic, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine. Mix well.
