Place a dough ball on a flat surface and flatten it slightly.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the dough.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Fermented Bean Paste
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the fermented bean paste, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and five-spice powder to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Braise the pork belly for 2-3 hours, or until it is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Beef with Broccoli Stir Fry
ingredients: 2 pounds beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the broccoli and cook until tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok and stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the beef and broccoli over cooked rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup dried red chili peppers, chopped
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the peanuts, chili peppers, and scallions and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Dongpo Pork
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pork from the wok and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch to the wok.
Return the pork to the wok and stir to coat with the sauce.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the pork is coated and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Wonton Soup
ingredients: Filling ingredients: 1/2 pound ground pork, 1/4 cup chopped scallions, 1/4 cup chopped cabbage
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using) to the pot.
Bring the broth to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer.
Meanwhile, prepare the wonton filling by mixing together the ground pork, scallions, and cabbage.
Place a small spoonful of the filling in the center of a wonton wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Add the wontons to the simmering broth and cook for 2-3 minutes, until they float to the surface.

title: Steamed Dumplings
ingredients: Filling ingredients: 1/2 pound ground pork, 1/4 cup chopped scallions, 1/4 cup chopped cabbage
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and vegetable oil.
Gradually add the warm water to the flour mixture and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the filling by mixing together the ground pork, scallions, and cabbage.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a small spoonful of the filling in the center of the dough circle.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the dough.
Fold the dough into a half-moon shape by bringing the two opposite edges together to form a point.
Steam the dumplings over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, until they are cooked through.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 pound beef (sirloin or flank steak), sliced into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove the beef and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and broccoli and cook until the broccoli is tender-crisp.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and cornstarch.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the wok and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until the beef is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Wonton Soup
ingredients: Sliced scallions and wonton wrappers for garnish (optional)
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the ground pork, scallions, cabbage, and garlic.
Place a wonton wrapper in a small bowl or a cupped hand.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sesame oil.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Add the wontons to the pot and cook for 5-7 minutes, until they float to the surface.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with sliced scallions and wonton wrappers, if desired.

title: Kung Pao Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the tofu and cook until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Remove the tofu and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the wok.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Return the tofu to the wok and stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the tofu is coated in the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Dumplings with Soy Sauce Dipping Sauce
ingredients: Soy sauce dipping sauce ingredients (see below)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and oil.
Gradually add the warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of the dough.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce dipping sauce ingredients.
Serve the dumplings with the soy sauce dipping sauce.

title: Jiangnan-Style Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole fish (2 pounds), cleaned and scaled
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Rinse the fish under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Season the fish with salt and white pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the scallions and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and Shaoxing wine, and stir-fry for another minute.
Transfer the fish to a steamer basket and place it over the wok.
Steam the fish for 10-12 minutes, or until it's cooked through.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Mushrooms and Fermented Bean Paste
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cups mushrooms (such as shiitake or cremini), sliced
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the pork and cook until browned on all sides.
Remove the pork from the wok and set aside.
Add the garlic and ginger to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the fermented bean paste, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch to the wok.
Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the pork broth to the wok and bring to a boil.
Return the pork to the wok and simmer, covered, for 1-2 hours, or until the pork is tender.

title: Stir-Fried Noodles with Vegetables and Fermented Bean Paste
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as cabbage, carrots, and bean sprouts)
2 cups noodles (such as rice noodles or egg noodles)
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry until they're tender-crisp.
Add the fermented bean paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the noodles to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until they're well coated with the sauce.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and Shaoxing wine to the wok, and stir-fry for another minute.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.

title: Jiangnan-Style Braised Eggplant with Garlic and Ginger
ingredients: Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the eggplant and cook until browned on all sides.
Remove the eggplant from the wok and set aside.
Add the garlic and ginger to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch to the wok.
Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the pork broth to the wok and bring to a boil.
Return the eggplant to the wok and simmer, covered, for 10-15 minutes, or until the eggplant is tender.

title: Pan-Fried Wontons with Dipping Sauce
instructions: In a bowl, mix together the ground pork, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle and press the edges together to seal the wonton.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the wontons to the wok and pan-fry until they're golden brown and crispy.
Serve the wontons with dipping sauce.

title: Steamed Shrimp with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Prepare steamer basket with water
Combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, and salt in a small bowl
Add sliced ginger and chopped scallions to the bowl
Add shrimp to the bowl and mix well
Steam shrimp for 8-10 minutes or until pink and cooked through
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve

title: Braised Pork Belly with Mushrooms and Eggplant
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat
Brown pork belly until golden brown, then set aside
Add garlic and ginger to the pot and stir-fry until fragrant
Add mushrooms and eggplant to the pot and stir-fry until tender
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, five-spice powder, sesame oil, salt, and black pepper to the pot
Return pork belly to the pot and braise for 2 hours or until tender and caramelized

title: Stir-Fried Noodles with Vegetables
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
instructions: Cook rice noodles according to package instructions
Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat
Add onion and garlic to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant
Add mixed vegetables to the wok and stir-fry until tender
Add cooked noodles to the wok and stir-fry until combined with vegetables
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, salt, and white pepper to the wok and stir-fry until combined

title: Pan-Fried Dumplings with Soy Sauce and Ginger
instructions: Combine flour and water in a large bowl to form a dough
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic
Divide dough into small balls and roll out into thin circles
Combine chopped cabbage, scallions, and garlic in a small bowl
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each dough circle and fold into a dumpling shape
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry dumplings until golden brown
Serve with soy sauce and sesame oil

title: Wok-Fried Chicken with Sichuan Peppercorns
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 tablespoons Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat
Add garlic and ginger to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant
Add chicken to the wok and stir-fry until browned and cooked through
Add Sichuan peppercorns, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, five-spice powder, salt, and black pepper to the wok and stir-fry until combined
Serve hot and garnish with chopped scallions

title: Stir-Fried Wontons in Chili Oil
ingredients: 1 small red bell pepper, thinly sliced
1 small green chili, seeded and chopped
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 10 seconds.
Add onion and bell pepper and cook until they start to soften, about 2 minutes.
Add wontons and cook until they start to brown, about 2 minutes.
Add chili, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and chili oil. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Braised Pork Belly in Soy Sauce
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 10 seconds.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch mixture. Stir to combine.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and braise for 2 hours, or until the pork is tender.
Garnish with chopped scallions before serving.

title: Steamed Fish in Ginger Soy Sauce
ingredients: 2 whole fish (such as tilapia or catfish), scaled and gutted
instructions: Heat oil in a large steamer basket over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 10 seconds.
Add fish and steam for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, combine soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar in a small bowl.
Brush the sauce over the fish during the last 2 minutes of steaming.
Garnish with chopped scallions before serving.

title: Fujian-Style Braised Eggplant
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 10 seconds.
Add eggplant and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch mixture. Stir to combine.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and braise for 30 minutes, or until the eggplant is tender.
Garnish with chopped scallions before serving.

title: Stir-Fried Greens with Garlic and Ginger
ingredients: 2 cups mixed greens (such as bok choy and Chinese broccoli)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 10 seconds.
Add greens and cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Add soy sauce and oyster sauce. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

title: Hunan Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add garlic, onion, and bell pepper to wok and stir-fry until tender.
Return chicken to wok and stir in peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, Szechuan peppercorns, salt, and pepper.
Stir-fry until sauce is thickened and chicken is cooked through.

title: Hunan-Style Smoked Pork Belly
instructions: Preheat smoker to 225°F.
In a small bowl, mix together brown sugar, five-spice powder, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.
Rub mixture all over pork belly, making sure to coat evenly.
Place pork belly in smoker and smoke for 4-5 hours, or until tender.
Remove pork belly from smoker and brush with vegetable oil.
Return pork belly to smoker and continue to smoke for an additional 30 minutes.

title: Hunan-Style Stir-Fried Bok Choy
ingredients: 2 bunches bok choy, cleaned and drained
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Add garlic and ginger to wok and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add bok choy to wok and stir-fry until tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, sugar, and black pepper.
Continue to stir-fry for an additional 1-2 minutes, until sauce is thickened.

title: Hunan-Style Spicy Lamb Dumplings
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together lamb, scallions, cilantro, garlic, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, salt, and pepper.
Knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into small balls and flatten each ball into a disk.
Place a tablespoon of lamb mixture in center of each disk and fold dough over to form a dumpling.
Steam dumplings for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Hunan-Style Pickled Mustard Greens
ingredients: 2 pounds mustard greens, cleaned and drained
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mustard greens, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, and salt.
Mix well to combine.
Let pickles sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours, or until greens are tender.
Store pickles in refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Stir-Fried Eggplant with Garlic
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add eggplant and cook until it starts to soften, about 3-4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and white pepper, and stir-fry until eggplant is tender.

title: Anhui-Style Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Brown pork belly on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, star anise, cloves, and cinnamon stick, and cook for 1 minute.
Add water, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and white pepper, and bring to a boil.
Transfer to the oven and braise for 2-1/2 hours, or until pork is tender.

title: Steamed Bao with Fermented Bean Paste
instructions: Combine flour, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Add warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces, and shape into balls.
Flatten each ball into a disk, and place a tablespoon of fermented bean paste in the center.
Fold dough over filling to form a bun, and seal edges.
Steam buns for 10-12 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Anhui-Style Braised Greens
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add kale and cook until wilted, about 3-4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and white pepper, and stir to combine.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until greens are tender.

title: Fried Wontons with Scallions and Ginger
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry wontons until crispy and golden, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Drain fried wontons on paper towels.
Combine scallions, ginger, and garlic in a bowl.
Add soy sauce and Shaoxing wine, and stir to combine.
Serve fried wontons with scallion-ginger sauce.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the wok.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and stir-fry until the vegetables are tender.
Return the chicken to the wok and stir in the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, Sichuan peppercorns, and chili bean paste.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into small cubes
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and stir-fry until the vegetables are tender.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the tofu and stir-fry until it is coated with the pork mixture.
Stir in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, Sichuan peppercorns, and chili bean paste.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Boiled Fish with Preserved Mustard Greens
ingredients: 1 pound fish fillet (such as tilapia or catfish)
2 cups preserved mustard greens, rinsed and drained
instructions: Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
Add the fish and cook for 3-4 minutes, until it is cooked through.
Remove the fish from the pot and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in the pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the preserved mustard greens and stir-fry until they are tender.
Stir in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch.
Return the fish to the pot and cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
ingredients: 8 ounces noodles (such as lo mein or udon)
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package instructions.
Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and stir-fry until the vegetables are tender.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Stir in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, Sichuan peppercorns, and chili bean paste.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Add the cooked noodles to the wok and stir-fry until they are coated with the sauce.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pork from the wok and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the wok.
Add the garlic, onion, and red bell pepper, and stir-fry until the vegetables are tender.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, Sichuan peppercorns, and chili bean paste.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Return the pork to the wok and stir-fry until it is coated with the sauce.
Stir in the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Cantonese Roasted Goose
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a small bowl, mix together five-spice powder, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, honey, and rice vinegar.
Rub the mixture all over the goose, making sure to get some under the skin as well.
Stuff the goose cavity with garlic, ginger, and scallions.
Truss the goose and place it in a roasting pan.
Drizzle the goose with vegetable oil and roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce heat to 375°F (190°C) and continue roasting for another 45-50 minutes, or until the goose is golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).

title: Stir-Fried Noodles with Shrimp and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bell peppers, carrots, broccoli)
1 cup large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Add the cooked noodles, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Braised Abalone in Oyster Sauce
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the abalone and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the oyster sauce, chicken broth, sugar, and cornstarch. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the abalone is cooked through.
Garnish with chopped scallions.

title: Cantonese-Style Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the pork belly and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and five-spice powder. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until the pork is tender.
Stir in the cornstarch and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes.

title: Steamed Egg Tarts (Dan Ta)
instructions: Preheat the steamer.
In a bowl, combine flour and lard or shortening. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the fat into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the ice-cold water and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball of dough into a disk and place a small amount of egg mixture in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the egg mixture and press the edges together to seal the tart.

title: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Garlic and Ginger
ingredients: 2 bunches bok choy, cleaned and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add bok choy, stir-fry until wilted.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving platter, garnish with chopped green onions.

title: Shandong-Style Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add pork belly, brown on all sides.
Add soy sauce, rice wine, sugar, star anise, cinnamon stick, and Sichuan peppercorns.
Add pork broth, bring to a boil.
Transfer to the oven, braise at 300°F for 2 hours.
Remove from the oven, stir in cornstarch mixture.
Simmer until sauce thickens, serve with steamed rice.

title: Pan-Fried Dumplings with Scallion Oil
instructions: Combine pork, garlic, ginger, and chopped green onions in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling on a dumpling wrapper, seal the edges.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Pan-fry dumplings until golden brown, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels, serve with scallion oil.

title: Shandong-Style Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 2 pounds fish (such as cod or tilapia)
instructions: Prepare the fish by making diagonal cuts on both sides.
Combine ginger, green onions, and garlic in a bowl.
Place a few slices of ginger and some chopped green onions on a plate.
Place the fish on the plate, drizzle with soy sauce, rice wine, and sugar.
Steam the fish over high heat until cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve immediately, garnish with additional ginger and green onions.

title: Shandong-Style Braised Eggs with Mushrooms and Scallions
ingredients: 2 cups mixed mushrooms (such as shiitake and button)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add mushrooms, stir-fry until softened.
Crack in eggs, stir-fry until scrambled.
Add soy sauce, rice wine, and sugar, stir-fry for 1 minute.
Transfer to a serving platter, garnish with chopped green onions.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole fish (2 pounds), scaled and gutted
instructions: Rinse the fish under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ginger and garlic, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the fish, cook until it's half-cooked.
Transfer the fish to a steamer basket, steam for 5-7 minutes.
Serve with soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and scallions.

title: Jiangsu-Style Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add pork belly, cook until browned on all sides.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and water, stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2-3 hours.
Stir in cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened.

title: Cantonese-Style Egg Tarts
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a bowl, whisk together flour and confectioners' sugar.
Add softened butter, mix until a dough forms.
Roll out dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place dough circles in a tart pan with a removable bottom.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Garlic and Ginger
ingredients: 2 bunches bok choy, cleaned and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ginger and garlic, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add bok choy, stir-fry until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Jiangsu-Style Steamed Dumplings
instructions: In a bowl, combine flour and oil, mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough until smooth, then rest for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into small balls, roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each dough circle, fold in half to form a half-moon shape.
Steam dumplings over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Shaoxing Wine
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add pork belly and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger, and cook until onion is translucent.
Add Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, sugar, and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, until pork is tender, about 2 hours.
Mix cornstarch and water, and stir into braising liquid until thickened.

title: Steamed Eggplant with Garlic and Ginger
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger, and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add eggplant and cook until tender, about 3 minutes.
Steam eggplant until tender, about 5 minutes.
Mix soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using), and brush over eggplant.

title: Zhejiang-Style Wontons in Light Broth
instructions: Combine pork, scallions, and garlic in a bowl.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a flat surface, and place a tablespoon of pork mixture in the center.
Dip your finger in water, and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle, and press edges to seal.
Bring chicken broth to a boil, and add wontons.
Mix cornstarch and water, and stir into broth until thickened.

title: Pan-Fried Dumplings with Soy Sauce
instructions: Combine pork, cabbage, and garlic in a bowl.
Lay a dumpling wrapper on a flat surface, and place a tablespoon of pork mixture in the center.
Dip your finger in water, and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a half-moon shape, and press edges to seal.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add dumplings and cook until browned, about 3 minutes.

title: Stir-Fried Bok Choy with Garlic and Ginger
ingredients: 2 bunches bok choy, cleaned and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger, and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add bok choy and cook until tender, about 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Stir-Fried Egg Noodles
ingredients: 1 package egg noodles, cooked and drained
1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add mixed vegetables and cooked chicken, stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add cooked noodles, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve garnished with chopped scallions if desired.

title: Fujian-Style Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on all sides.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, five-spice powder, and star anise. Braise for 2 hours.
Add chicken broth and continue braising for another 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (such as tilapia or catfish)
instructions: Heat oil in a large steamer basket over high heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add fish fillets and steam for 8-10 minutes or until cooked through.
Mix soy sauce and oyster sauce in a small bowl.
Serve fish with steamed scallions and a drizzle of soy sauce mixture.

title: Fujian-Style Fried Rice
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, green onions)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and mixed vegetables, stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add cooked chicken and stir-fry for another minute.
Add cooked rice and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Mix soy sauce and oyster sauce in a small bowl. Pour over rice mixture and stir-fry for another minute.
Push rice mixture to one side of the pan. Add beaten eggs to the other side and scramble until cooked through.
Mix eggs with rice mixture and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Fujian-Style Oyster Omelette
instructions: Beat eggs in a large bowl and set aside.
Mix oyster sauce, water, flour, and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Add diced oysters and garlic to the bowl and mix well.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add egg mixture and cook until edges start to set.
Pour oyster mixture over eggs and cook until edges start to curl.
Loosen omelette with a spatula and fold in half. Serve hot.

title: Spicy Hunan Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 teaspoons Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat. Add chicken and cook until browned.
Remove chicken and set aside. Add garlic, onion, peanuts, and scallions to wok.
Cook until onion is translucent. Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch mixture, Szechuan peppercorns, and red pepper flakes.
Return chicken to wok and stir-fry until coated with sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Hunan-Style Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in Dutch oven over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on all sides.
Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, cornstarch mixture, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cinnamon, cumin, and cayenne pepper.
Cover and transfer to oven. Braise for 2 hours or until pork is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve.

title: Hunan-Style Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 2 pounds fish fillets (such as catfish or tilapia)
instructions: Rinse fish under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Place fish in steamer basket. Add ginger and scallions on top of fish.
In small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch mixture.
Pour sauce over fish. Steam for 8-10 minutes or until fish is cooked through.
Brush with sesame oil and season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve.

title: Hunan-Style Stir-Fried Eggplant
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Szechuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat. Add eggplant and cook until browned.
Remove eggplant and set aside. Add garlic, onion, and scallions to wok.
Cook until onion is translucent. Add soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch mixture, Szechuan peppercorns, and red pepper flakes.
Return eggplant to wok and stir-fry until coated with sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Hunan-Style Smoked Pork Ribs
instructions: Preheat smoker to 225°F. In small bowl, mix together five-spice powder, brown sugar, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, hoisin sauce, and rice vinegar.
Rub mixture all over pork ribs. Place ribs in smoker and cook for 4 hours or until tender.
Meanwhile, heat oil in wok over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add ribs to wok and cook until caramelized on all sides.
Serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Eggplant in Garlic Sauce
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry the eggplant until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the eggplant and set aside.
Add more oil to the wok if necessary, then stir-fry the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the doubanjiang, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Return the eggplant to the wok and stir to coat with the sauce.
Mix the cornstarch and water in a small bowl, then stir into the eggplant mixture.
Cook until the sauce thickens, about 2 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with chopped scallions, if desired.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Mushrooms
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cups mixed mushrooms (such as shiitake and button)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Stir-fry the pork until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pork and set aside.
Add more oil to the pot if necessary, then stir-fry the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Return the pork to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the pork is tender, about 2 hours.
Mix the cornstarch and water in a small bowl, then stir into the pot.
Cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Steamed Buns with Pork and Vegetables
instructions: Combine the flour, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl.
Gradually add the warm water and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Punch down the dough and divide into 8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of each circle.
Top with chopped cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a bun and press the edges to seal.
Steam the buns over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, until cooked through.
Brush with sesame oil and serve.

title: Anhui-Style Braised Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 cup mixed mushrooms (such as shiitake and button)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Stir-fry the tofu until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Remove the tofu and set aside.
Add more oil to the pot if necessary, then stir-fry the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Return the tofu to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the sauce thickens, about 20 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch and water in a small bowl, then stir into the pot.
Cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cantonese-Style Stir-Fried Noodles
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as bean sprouts and cabbage)
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry until they are tender-crisp.
Add the cooked chicken and stir-fry until combined with the vegetables.
Add the noodles and stir-fry until they are well coated with the sauce.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil.
Stir-fry until the noodles are well coated with the sauce.
Serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 dried red chilies, crushed or 1-2 teaspoon red pepper flakes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic, onion, and bell pepper, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the peanuts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, Sichuan peppercorns, salt, and black pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked chicken back into the wok and stir to combine.
Add the crushed red chilies and stir-fry for another minute.
Serve immediately.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into small cubes
1 teaspoon Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 dried red chilies, crushed or 1-2 teaspoon red pepper flakes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the tofu and cook until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the fermented bean paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, Sichuan peppercorns, salt, and black pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked tofu back into the wok and stir to combine.
Add the crushed red chilies and stir-fry for another minute.
Serve immediately.

title: Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pork belly and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic and ginger, and cook until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, rice vinegar, cornstarch, five-spice powder, salt, and black pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the pork belly back into the wok and braise until tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Serve immediately.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: In a bowl, mix together the ground pork, cabbage, scallions, and garlic.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sesame oil, salt, and black pepper.
Mix well to combine.
Place a wonton wrapper in a bowl and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in water and run it along the edges of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
In a large pot, bring the chicken broth to a boil.
Gently add the wontons to the pot and cook until they float to the surface.
Serve immediately.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pork and set aside.
In the same wok, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add the garlic and ginger, and cook until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, rice vinegar, cornstarch, five-spice powder, salt, and black pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the pork back into the wok and braise until tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove the pork from the wok and let cool.
Shred the pork with two forks and return it to the wok.
Stir-fry the pork with the sauce until the sauce has thickened.
Serve immediately.

title: Cantonese-Style Roasted Goose
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix five-spice powder, brown sugar, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine in a small bowl.
Rub the mixture all over the goose, then place it in a roasting pan.
Roast the goose in the preheated oven for 20 minutes.
Reduce oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue roasting for another 1-2 hours, or until the goose is golden brown and crispy.
Baste the goose with vegetable oil every 20 minutes during roasting.
Let the goose rest for 10-15 minutes before carving and serving.

title: Stir-Fried Noodles with Vegetable and Egg
ingredients: 8 oz rice noodles, cooked according to package instructions
2 cups mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, carrots, cabbage, scallions)
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and stir-fry until they start to soften.
Push the vegetables to one side of the wok.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble them until cooked through.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables.
Add cooked noodles to the wok and stir-fry until combined with the vegetables and eggs.
Season with soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using).
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Cantonese-Style Braised Abalone
ingredients: 2 cups dried scallops, soaked and drained
2 cups dried mushrooms, soaked and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add soaked scallops and mushrooms, and stir-fry until they start to soften.
Add fish stock, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and cornstarch mixture.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Add abalone to the saucepan and braise for 5-7 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
Season with Shaoxing wine and salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Crispy Fried Wontons
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Wrap a small amount of cabbage, scallions, garlic, and ginger in a wonton wrapper.
Fry the wonton in hot oil until crispy and golden brown.
Drain the fried wonton on paper towels.
Serve hot, sprinkled with soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sesame oil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cantonese-Style Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
instructions: Rinse the fish fillets under cold water, pat them dry with paper towels.
Place a slice of ginger and a few chopped scallions on a piece of parchment paper.
Place a fish fillet on top of the ginger and scallions.
Drizzle soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and Shaoxing wine over the fish.
Steam the fish over boiling water for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions and steamed ginger.

title: Shandong-Style Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole fish (2 lbs), scaled and cleaned
instructions: Prepare the fish by cleaning and scaling it.
Combine soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Place the fish in a steamer lined with parchment paper.
Add sliced ginger and scallions on top of the fish.
Steam the fish over high heat for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with the ginger and scallions on top.

title: Shandong-Style Pan-Fried Noodles
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g. cabbage, carrots, bean sprouts)
instructions: Cook the noodles according to package instructions.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mixed vegetables and bean sprouts, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the cooked noodles and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and pepper to taste.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Mushrooms and Scallions
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the mushrooms and scallions, and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Braise the pork belly for 10-15 minutes, or until tender.
Serve hot.

title: Shandong-Style Fried Dumplings
instructions: Combine the flour and warm water to make a dough.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until smooth.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll out into thin circles.
Place a tablespoon of ground pork in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the dumplings until golden brown on both sides.

title: Shandong-Style Braised Eggplant with Garlic and Ginger
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the eggplant and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the garlic and ginger, and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and sesame oil.
Braise the eggplant for 10-15 minutes, or until tender.
Serve hot.

title: Sauerbraten (Beef Pot Roast)
ingredients: 3 lbs beef pot roast, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef, onion, garlic, vinegar, beef broth, sugar, mustard, allspice, cloves, and bay leaves. Mix well and cover.
Refrigerate for at least 2 days, turning occasionally.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Remove beef from marinade, letting excess liquid drip off.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef on all sides.
Transfer pot to oven and cook for 2-3 hours, or until beef is tender.

title: Wiener Schnitzel (Breaded Veal Cutlet)
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip in beaten eggs, then coat in breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan, paprika, and garlic powder.
Heat a large skillet with about 1/2 inch oil over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Raclette (Melted Cheese Dish)
instructions: Preheat broiler.
Place raclette cheese under broiler and melt.
Serve with baguette slices, ham, pickles, and apples.
Sprinkle paprika over dish for garnish.

title: Apple Strudel (Flaky Pastry)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
On a lightly floured surface, roll out puff pastry to a 1/4-inch thickness.
In a bowl, mix together apples, sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Arrange apple mixture on one half of pastry, leaving a 1-inch border.
Fold other half of pastry over apples and press edges to seal.
Brush pastry with melted butter and cut slits in top.

title: Zürigeschnätzlets (Sautéed Veal with Mushrooms and Cream)
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet with about 1/2 inch oil over medium heat.
Fry cutlets until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Remove veal from skillet and set aside.
Add mushrooms and garlic to skillet and cook until tender.
Stir in cream, paprika, and thyme. Simmer until sauce thickens.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 3 lbs beef pot roast, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef, onion, garlic, vinegar, water, brown sugar, cinnamon, allspice, cloves, salt, and pepper.
Mix well and cover bowl with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate for at least 2 days, turning meat occasionally.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Remove meat from marinade, letting excess liquid drip off.
Place meat in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot.
Add bay leaves and cover pot with a lid.
Bake for 2-1/2 to 3 hours, or until meat is tender.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 veal cutlets, pounded to 1/4 inch thickness
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip floured cutlets in beaten eggs, making sure they're fully coated.
Roll cutlets in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add a few cutlets to skillet (do not overcrowd).
Cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat broiler or grill to medium-high heat.
Slice raclette cheese into 1/4-inch thick rounds.
Arrange potatoes, onion, and bell pepper on a large platter.
Place a raclette cheese round on a small baking sheet or heat-proof plate.
Place under broiler or grill until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Spoon melted cheese over potatoes and vegetables.
Repeat with remaining cheese and ingredients.
Serve immediately, garnished with parsley.

title: Austrian Apple Strudel
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour, melted butter, sugar, raisins, and walnuts.
Mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Roll out dough to a 1/4-inch thickness.
Spread apple filling over dough, leaving a 1-inch border around edges.
Roll strudel into a tight log, starting from one long side.
Place strudel on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Swiss Fondue
instructions: In a large bowl, combine Gruyère and Emmental cheese.
Add wine, sherry (if using), garlic, and lemon juice.
Mix until smooth and well combined.
Transfer mixture to a fondue pot or a small saucepan.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until cheese is melted and fondue is smooth.
Add Kirschwasser (if using) and stir to combine.
Serve immediately with assorted dipping breads.

title: Schnitzel
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the veal cutlets in the flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the veal cutlets in the beaten eggs, then coat in the breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan cheese.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the veal cutlets until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Wiener Würstel (Viennese Sausages)
instructions: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced sausages and cook until browned.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the beef broth, water, tomato paste, and paprika.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Zürigesfleisch (Zurich-style Meat)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef cubes, then remove from heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook until browned.
Add the garlic, beef broth, red wine, tomato paste, and paprika.
Return the beef cubes to the pot and stir to coat.
Cover and simmer for 2 hours or until the meat is tender.

title: Käsespätzle (Cheesy Spaetzle)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and eggs.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes, then let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Cut into long, thin strips and cook in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes.
Drain the spaetzle and top with melted butter, Emmental cheese, Gruyère cheese, and chopped parsley.
Serve hot and enjoy.

title: Apfelstrudel (Apple Strudel)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, mix together the sliced apples, granulated sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Spread the melted butter over the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Arrange the apple mixture in the center of the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the pastry over the apple mixture and press to seal.

title: Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 pork or veal cutlets, pounded thin
instructions: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured cutlets in eggs, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat a large skillet with about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets until golden brown and cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Zurich-Style Apple Strudel
ingredients: 2 cups mixed berries (such as blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, butter, confectioners' sugar, and granulated sugar. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a large rectangle.
In a separate bowl, mix the chopped almonds, eggs, vanilla extract, raisins, mixed berries, and sliced apples.
Spread the apple mixture over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Roll the strudel into a log shape and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until golden brown.
Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving, if desired.

title: Wiener Würstel (Austrian Sausages)
ingredients: Bun and toppings (such as mustard, sauerkraut, and pickles)
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the chopped beef, pork, onion, garlic, caraway seeds, paprika, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Mix well with your hands until just combined.
Add the egg and mix until the meat is just bound together.
Add the flour and mix until the meat is just combined.
Cover the mixture and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Divide the mixture into 4-6 portions, depending on desired sausage size.
Shape each portion into a log shape and wrap in plastic wrap.
Heat a large skillet with about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Fry the sausages until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Serve in a bun with desired toppings.

title: Basler Läckerli (Basle Delicacy)
ingredients: 1/4 cup candied orange peel, finely chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large saucepan, combine the honey, brown sugar, and 1/4 cup water.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped almonds, hazelnuts, citron, orange peel, rose water, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and salt.
Mix until well combined.
Stir in the melted butter.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to a large rectangle.
Spread the honey mixture over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Roll the Basle delicacy into a log shape and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Raclette (Swiss Cheese Fondue)
ingredients: 1/4 cup Kirsch or other fruit brandy
Assorted meats and bread for serving (such as cured meats, bread, and potatoes)
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine the sliced raclette cheese, white wine, Kirsch, lemon juice, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the cheese is melted and smooth.
Transfer the fondue to a fondue pot or a small saucepan with a candle warmer.
Serve with assorted meats and bread for dipping.
Serve hot, and enjoy!

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 3 pounds beef pot roast, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef, onion, garlic, vinegar, beef broth, brown sugar, salt, black pepper, allspice, and bay leaves. Mix well and refrigerate for at least 2 days.
Remove the meat from the marinade and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the meat on all sides, then transfer to a plate.
Add the marinade to the pot and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
Return the meat to the pot and cook until tender, about 1 hour.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 veal cutlets, pounded to 1/4 inch thickness
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the veal in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured veal in eggs and then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat melted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the veal until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve immediately.

title: Zurich-Style Fondue
instructions: In a large bowl, combine cheese, wine, Kirschwasser, garlic, lemon juice, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth.
Transfer the cheese mixture to a fondue pot or a small chafing dish.
Heat the fondue over low heat, stirring constantly, until melted and smooth.
Serve with bread and assorted dipping items.

title: Apple Strudel
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour, confectioners' sugar, and salt. Add softened butter and mix until crumbly.
In a separate bowl, whisk together sour cream, eggs, and vanilla extract. Add to the flour mixture and mix until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough to a large rectangle. Spread the berry mixture, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges to seal. Brush with egg wash and sprinkle with sugar.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat the raclette grill or a double boiler over low heat.
Place the raclette cheese on the grill or in the double boiler and melt.
Serve the melted cheese with bread and assorted dipping items.
Butter the bread slices before serving.

title: Sauerbraten (Pot Roast in Vinegar Sauce)
ingredients: 3 pounds beef pot roast, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef, onion, garlic, vinegar, beef broth, brown sugar, mustard, salt, black pepper, and bay leaves. Mix well and refrigerate for at least 2 days.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C). Remove beef from marinade and pat dry with paper towels.
In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium-high heat. Sear beef until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add flour to Dutch oven and cook for 1 minute. Add marinade and bring to a boil. Scrape up any browned bits.
Return beef to Dutch oven and cover. Transfer to preheated oven and braise for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender.

title: Wiener Schnitzel (Breaded and Fried Veal Cutlets)
instructions: In a shallow dish, combine flour, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Dip each veal cutlet in flour mixture, coating both sides.
Dip floured cutlet in beaten eggs, making sure to coat completely.
Dip egg-coated cutlet in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry cutlets until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Bircher Muesli (Swiss Oat Breakfast Bowl)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed fruit (such as apples, bananas, and berries)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine oats and mixed fruit.
In a small bowl, whisk together yogurt and honey until smooth.
Pour yogurt mixture over oat mixture and stir until combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Just before serving, sprinkle with chopped almonds and shredded coconut.

title: Apple Strudel (Austrian Pastry Filled with Apples and Nuts)
ingredients: 1/4 cup lard or butter, chilled and cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Add lard or butter and use a pastry blender or fingers to work into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add sugar and mix until dough comes together.
Roll out dough to a large rectangle. In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs and vanilla extract.
Brush edges of dough with egg mixture and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Arrange apples, walnuts, and raisins in the center of the dough rectangle. Fold in sides and roll up dough to form a log.

title: Raclette (Swiss Cheese Fondue)
ingredients: Assorted meats and bread for serving
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine wine, water, lemon juice, and garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add raclette cheese to saucepan and stir until melted and smooth.
Transfer cheese mixture to a fondue pot or a small ceramic bowl.
Serve with assorted meats and bread for dipping. Stir occasionally to keep cheese smooth and melted.

title: Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 pork or veal cutlets, pounded thin
instructions: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured cutlets in the beaten eggs, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded cutlets and fry until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Apple Strudel
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Combine the flour, butter, and confectioners' sugar in a bowl to form a dough.
Roll out the dough to a large rectangle.
Mix the granulated sugar, walnuts, eggs, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Arrange the sliced apple and mixed berries on the dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
Fold the dough over the filling, pressing the edges to seal.
Bake for 40-50 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured cutlets in the beaten eggs, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded cutlets and fry until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Arrange the sliced potatoes, onion, bell pepper, and tomato on a baking sheet.
Place the raclette cheese under the broiler until melted and bubbly.
Spoon the melted cheese over the vegetables and serve.

title: Bircher Muesli
ingredients: 1 cup chopped dried fruit (apricots, apples, raisins)
instructions: Combine the oats, dried fruit, and nuts in a bowl.
Mix the honey, yogurt, milk, vanilla extract, and cinnamon in a separate bowl.
Pour the wet ingredients over the dry ingredients and mix until combined.
Refrigerate overnight and serve chilled.

title: Sacher Torte
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Butter and flour two 9-inch (23cm) round cake pans.
Beat egg yolks and 1 cup (200g) sugar until pale and thick.
Melt chocolate and 1 cup (120g) sugar in a double boiler.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold egg whites into chocolate mixture.
Divide batter between prepared pans and smooth tops.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until edges are set.
Let cool in pans for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with confectioners' sugar before serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip cutlets in milk, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat about 1/2 inch (1cm) of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Raclette
ingredients: Pickled onions, chopped fresh chives, and cornichons, for serving
instructions: Preheat broiler.
Rub raclette cheese with butter.
Place cheese under broiler and melt, flipping halfway through.
Serve with baguette slices, pickled onions, chives, and cornichons.

title: Sachertorte Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Butter and flour two 9-inch (23cm) round cake pans.
Beat egg yolks and 1 cup (200g) sugar until pale and thick.
Melt chocolate and 1/2 cup (120g) sugar in a double boiler.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold egg whites into chocolate mixture.
Divide batter between prepared pans and smooth tops.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until edges are set.
Let cool in pans for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Zuger Kirschtorte
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Butter and flour a 9-inch (23cm) round cake pan.
Beat egg yolks and 1 cup (200g) sugar until pale and thick.
Melt chocolate and 1/2 cup (120g) sugar in a double boiler.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold egg whites into chocolate mixture.
Divide batter between prepared pans and smooth tops.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until edges are set.
Let cool in pans for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and serve with whipped cream.

title: Sauerbraten (Traditional German Pot Roast)
ingredients: 3 lbs beef pot roast, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine beef, onion, garlic, vinegar, water, brown sugar, mustard, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 days.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Remove the meat from the marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Transfer the meat to a Dutch oven or a large oven-safe pot with a lid.
Add the sliced carrots and cubed potatoes to the pot.
Cover the pot with a lid and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Braise the Sauerbraten for 3-4 hours, or until the meat is tender and falls apart easily.

title: Wiener Schnitzel (Traditional Austrian Breaded Veal Cutlets)
ingredients: 4 veal cutlets, pounded to 1/4 inch thickness
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the veal in flour, shaking off any excess.
Dip the floured veal in eggs, making sure they're fully coated.
Roll the egg-coated veal in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat the melted butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded veal to the skillet and fry until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the Wiener Schnitzel to a plate and garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.

title: Raclette (Traditional Swiss Melted Cheese Dish)
instructions: Preheat the broiler.
Slice the Raclette cheese into 1/4-inch thick pieces.
Arrange the sliced cheese on a baking sheet or a raclette grill.
Broil the cheese until melted and bubbly, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve the melted cheese with sliced baguette, onion, apple, cornichons, and gherkins.
Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.

title: Leberkäse (Traditional German Meatloaf)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, chopped onion, minced garlic, egg, milk, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Mix the ingredients until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
Transfer the mixture to a loaf pan or shape it into a loaf shape on a baking sheet.
Bake the Leberkäse for 45-50 minutes, or until cooked through and lightly browned on the outside.

title: Bircher Muesli (Traditional Swiss Breakfast Cereal)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, diced apple, and diced pear.
Mix in the honey, chopped almonds, and shredded coconut until well combined.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Just before serving, stir in the plain yogurt and vanilla extract.
Serve the Bircher Muesli chilled, topped with additional yogurt and fruit, if desired.

title: Sacher Torte (Austria)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Mix ground almonds and confectioners' sugar.
Add softened butter and mix until combined.
Beat in egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Beat in egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Pour into a greased and floured pan and bake for 25-30 minutes.
Let cool and glaze with chocolate

title: Zürigeschnätzlets (Switzerland)
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Sear in butter until browned, then set aside.
Sauté garlic, mushrooms, and onions until tender.
Add white wine and beef broth, simmer until reduced.
Return veal cutlets to the pan and simmer until cooked through.

title: Schnitzel Wiener Art (Austria)
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dip in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip in eggs, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Raclette (Switzerland)
ingredients: 1 pound (450g) cured meats (e.g. ham or prosciutto)
instructions: Preheat raclette grill or broiler.
Place raclette cheese on the grill and melt.
Serve with cured meats, pickled vegetables, and bread.

title: Spätzle (Germany/Austria)
instructions: Combine flour, eggs, and milk to form a smooth batter.
Season with salt.
Press through a spätzlepresse or a colander into boiling water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, then drain and serve.

title: Sacher Torte (Austria)
ingredients: 3 ounces high-quality dark chocolate, finely chopped
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Sift flour and sugar into a medium bowl.
Melt chocolate in a double boiler or in the microwave.
Beat egg yolks and vanilla extract in a separate bowl.
Combine egg yolks with melted chocolate and mix well.
Add the flour mixture to the chocolate mixture and mix until combined.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold egg whites into the chocolate mixture until no white streaks remain.
Pour the batter into a greased and floured springform pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the edges are set.

title: Raclette (Switzerland)
ingredients: Assorted accompaniments (boiled potatoes, bread, pickles, etc.)
instructions: Preheat the broiler.
Cut the raclette wheel into 1-inch thick slices.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add flour and whisk to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Slowly pour in white wine and heavy cream, whisking constantly.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange sliced raclette on a platter or individual plates.
Serve with the sauce and assorted accompaniments.

title: Sauerbraten (Germany)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine sliced onion and minced garlic.
Add beef pot roast to the bowl and coat with the onion mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk together beef broth, vinegar, water, brown sugar, flour, salt, black pepper, and cloves.
Pour the marinade over the beef and onions, making sure the beef is completely coated.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 days or up to 5 days.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Remove the beef from the marinade and place in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot.
Pour the marinade into the pot and cover with a lid.
Bake for 3-4 hours or until the beef is tender and falls apart easily.

title: Apfelstrudel (Austria)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt.
Add softened butter and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the dough to a large rectangle.
In a separate bowl, mix together granulated sugar, cinnamon sugar, and chopped almonds.
Spread the sugar mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Arrange sliced apples and raisins on top of the sugar mixture.
Roll the strudel into a tight log and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Zürigeschnätzlets (Switzerland)
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge the cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Beat the eggs in a separate bowl.
Dip the floured cutlets in the eggs and then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the veal cutlets and cook until golden brown on both sides.
Transfer the cutlets to a plate and keep warm.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the skillet.
Add the Parmesan cheese and cook until melted.
Stir in lemon juice and beef broth.
Serve the veal cutlets with the creamy sauce spooned over the top.

title: Schnitzel Wiener Art
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Dredge the veal cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured veal cutlets in eggs, making sure they're fully coated.
Dredge the egg-coated veal cutlets in breadcrumbs.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded veal cutlets and cook until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Tafelspitz (Boiled Beef)
instructions: Place the beef in a large pot and add enough cold water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Add the carrots, potatoes, onion, and apple to the pot.
Simmer until the beef is tender, about 2-3 hours.
Strain the broth and discard the solids.
Serve the beef with the broth, horseradish, and mustard.

title: Raclette
ingredients: 1 pound cured meats (such as prosciutto or ham)
instructions: Preheat the broiler.
Place the raclette cheese under the broiler and melt.
Scoop the melted cheese onto the baguette slices.
Serve with cured meats, grapes, and pickled onions.

title: Zurich-Style Chicken Cordon Bleu
instructions: Season the chicken breasts with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Butterfly the chicken breasts and layer with ham and Swiss cheese.
Dredge the stuffed chicken breasts in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured chicken breasts in eggs, making sure they're fully coated.
Dredge the egg-coated chicken breasts in breadcrumbs.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded chicken breasts and cook until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Austrian Apple Strudel
instructions: Make the dough by combining flour, warm water, and salt in a bowl.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Combine the sugar, eggs, berries, and apples in a bowl.
Spread the filling evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the dough over the filling to form a seal.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F for 45 minutes.

title: Sacher Torte
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Butter and flour a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat eggs and sugar until stiff peaks form.
Melt chocolate and butter in a double boiler.
Combine egg mixture and chocolate mixture, then fold in flour.
Pour into prepared pan and bake for 25 minutes.
Let cool completely before serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Dredge cutlets in flour, shaking off excess.
