Add fish and shellfish and cook until lightly browned, 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, fish stock, wine, saffron, fennel seeds, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with toasted bread and aïoli.

title: Coq au Vin

instructions: Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add carrots and celery and cook until tender, 5 minutes.
Add red wine, chicken broth, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add eggplant and cook until tender, 5 minutes.
Add zucchinis and cook until tender, 5 minutes.
Add bell peppers and cook until tender, 5 minutes.
Add garlic and onion and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until tender, 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped basil, if desired.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.

Add apples and cook until tender, 10 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together flour, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add Calvados, if using, and mix to combine.
Roll out puff pastry and place over apples.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown.

title: Crème Brûlée

Sprinkle tops with granulated sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the chicken until browned, about 5 minutes per side.
Remove the chicken and set aside.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Add the cognac and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated.
Add the red wine and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated.
Add the chicken broth, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf.
Return the chicken to the pot and simmer until cooked through.
Add the carrots, celery, and mushrooms to the pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the chicken and vegetables in a rich sauce.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 4 lbs fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and cod)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the tomatoes, fennel, and saffron.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the orange juice and fish broth.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer the broth for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and shellfish to the pot.
Cook until the seafood is cooked through.
Season the bouillabaisse with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Serve the bouillabaisse in bowls, garnished with croutons and rouille.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers.
Cook until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Roll out the puff pastry to fit a 9-inch tart pan.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).

Place the ramekins in a large baking dish and add hot water to come halfway up the sides.
Bake the crème brûlée for 25-30 minutes, or until set.
Let the crème brûlée cool to room temperature.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of sugar over the top of each ramekin.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until browned, then remove.
Add the cognac to the pot and ignite it. Let the flames burn out, then add the onions, carrots, and celery.
Cook until the vegetables are tender, then add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaves.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, and browned chicken. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Serve the chicken and sauce over egg noodles.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and shrimp)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sear the fish and shellfish until browned, then remove.
Add the onion, garlic, leeks, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tomatoes, fish broth, saffron, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
Add the browned fish and shellfish to the pot. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the bouillabaisse with a dollop of rouille and a sprinkle of parsley.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3 pounds apples, peeled, halved, and cored
1 sheet of frozen puff pastry, thawed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large skillet, combine the apples, granulated sugar, butter, flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the apples are caramelized and tender.
Roll out the puff pastry to fit a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
Place the pastry in the tart pan and fill with the apple mixture.
Dot the top of the apples with the heavy cream and sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sear the eggplant, zucchinis, and bell peppers until tender.
Add the onion and garlic to the skillet and cook until the onion is tender.
Add the tomatoes, vegetable broth, thyme, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
Serve the ratatouille hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, granulated sugar, and vanilla extract. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and salt. Temper the egg yolks with the hot cream mixture.
Strain the mixture into 4 ramekins and place in a baking dish. Add hot water to the baking dish to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are set and the centers are still slightly jiggly.
Remove the ramekins from the baking dish and let cool to room temperature.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of granulated sugar over the top of each ramekin. Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch or under the broiler.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pot.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, then add the onions and cook until they are browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cognac and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2 minutes.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Return the chicken to the pot and bring the mixture to a boil.
Cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the carrots, celery, and mushrooms to the pot.
Return the pot to the stovetop and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes.
Serve the Coq au Vin hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and shrimp)
1 tablespoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, leeks, carrots, and celery and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the fish stock, white wine, saffron, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and shellfish to the pot and cook until they are cooked through.
Serve the Bouillabaisse hot, topped with rouille and crostini.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the eggplant and cook until it is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the zucchinis and bell peppers and cook until they are tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season the ratatouille with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the ratatouille hot, garnished with chopped fresh basil leaves if desired.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
In a medium saucepan, combine the sugar, heavy cream, whole milk, and salt.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved.
In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Gradually add the warm cream mixture to the egg yolks, whisking constantly.
Pour the mixture into 4 ramekins or small baking dishes.
Place the ramekins in a large baking dish and add hot water to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are set and the centers are still slightly jiggly.
Remove the ramekins from the water bath and let them cool to room temperature.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until chilled.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of granulated sugar over the top of each ramekin.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch or under the broiler.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3 pounds apples, peeled, halved, and cored
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the apples and cook until they are tender, about 10-12 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the granulated sugar, flour, and salt.
Add the sugar mixture to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Place the pastry over the apples and tuck the edges under the fruit.
Brush the pastry with the beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Bake the tarte for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
Remove the tarte from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Invert the tarte onto a serving plate and serve warm.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
In a large Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the pot and sauté the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Return the chicken to the pot and bring to a boil.
Transfer the pot to the oven and cook, covered, at 300°F for 25-30 minutes.
Add the carrots and celery to the pot and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes.
Serve the chicken and vegetables hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds assorted fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and cod)
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the fish stock, white wine, saffron, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and shellfish to the pot and cook until they are cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Serve the bouillabaisse hot, garnished with lemon slices and croutons.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3-4 Golden Delicious apples, peeled and halved
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a large skillet, combine the sugar, butter, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Add the apple halves to the skillet and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the apples are tender and caramelized, about 20-25 minutes.
Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Place the pastry over the apples and tuck the edges under the fruit.
Bake the tarte for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
Let the tarte cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, and bell pepper to the skillet and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Add the garlic to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper to the skillet.
Simmer the ratatouille for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve the ratatouille hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, granulated sugar, whole milk, and salt.
Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is hot but not boiling.
In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Temper the egg yolks by slowly pouring the hot cream mixture into the egg yolks, whisking constantly.
Pour the mixture into 4-6 ramekins or small baking dishes.
Place the ramekins in a large baking dish and add hot water to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake the crème brûlée for 25-30 minutes, or until set.
Remove the ramekins from the water bath and let cool to room temperature.
Cover the ramekins with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of granulated sugar over the top of each ramekin.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch or under the broiler.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add onion to pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cognac to pot and cook until almost completely reduced, about 2 minutes. Add red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Return chicken to pot and bring to a boil. Cover pot and transfer to the oven. Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Remove pot from oven and stir in carrots and celery. Return pot to stovetop and simmer over medium heat until vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.

title: Crêpes
ingredients: Fresh fruit or whipped cream, for serving
instructions: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, water, sugar, melted butter, salt, and vanilla extract in a large bowl until smooth.
Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour a small amount of batter into pan and tilt to evenly coat the bottom.
Cook crêpe for 1-2 minutes, or until edges start to curl and bottom is light brown. Loosen crêpe with a spatula and flip.
Cook for an additional 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until top is lightly browned. Repeat with remaining batter.

title: Saucisses de Rillio
ingredients: 1 pound sausages, such as andouille or kielbasa
instructions: Cook sausages in a large skillet over medium heat, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 10-12 minutes.
Remove sausages from skillet and set aside. Add onion to skillet and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken broth, white wine, heavy cream, butter, salt, and pepper to skillet. Stir to combine.
Return sausages to skillet and simmer over medium heat until sauce has thickened, about 2-3 minutes. Sprinkle with flour to thicken.

title: Kouign-amann
instructions: Whisk warm milk, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl until yeast is dissolved.
Add flour to bowl and stir to combine. Add melted butter and stir to form a shaggy dough.
Knead dough on a floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Roll out dough to a 1/4-inch thickness. Cut into triangles.
Roll up triangles, starting from the wide end, and curve into a crescent shape. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Far Breton
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk flour, milk, heavy cream, sugar, and salt in a large bowl until smooth.
Add vanilla extract, eggs, and melted butter to bowl and whisk until well combined.
Stir in raisins and prunes.
Pour batter into a 9x13-inch baking dish and smooth top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
In a large Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on both sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the pot.
Add the sliced onion and cook until caramelized, about 10-12 minutes.
Add the garlic, cognac, red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer to the oven.
Braise the Coq au Vin in the preheated oven at 300°F (150°C) for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve the Coq au Vin hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3 pounds apples, peeled, halved, and cored
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the sliced apples, granulated sugar, and salt.
Let the apple mixture sit at room temperature for 15 minutes, until the apples start to release their juice.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the pastry to a 9-inch (23cm) tart pan with a removable bottom.
Arrange the apple mixture in a concentric circle pattern, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Dot the top of the apples with the softened butter.
Fold the edges of the pastry up over the apples, pressing gently to seal.
Bake the Tarte Tatin in a preheated oven at 425°F (220°C) for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
Remove the tart from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Drizzle the heavy cream, Calvados, and vanilla extract over the top of the tart.
Return the tart to the oven and bake for an additional 5-7 minutes, or until the cream is bubbly and slightly caramelized.

title: Tarte Flambée
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups warm water, 2 teaspoons active dry yeast, 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, 1/4 cup lard or vegetable shortening, 1 egg, beaten, for egg wash, 8 ounces Munster cheese, crumbled, 4 ounces bacon, diced, 1 onion, thinly sliced, Salt and pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons butter, 2 cloves garlic, minced, Fresh thyme leaves, chopped (optional)
instructions: Combine warm water and yeast. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt, and melted butter to the yeast mixture. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Let the dough rest for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Spread the Munster cheese, bacon, and onion over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
Fold the border over the filling to form a crust.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
Brush with beaten egg for glaze. Sprinkle with chopped thyme, if desired.

title: Choucroute Garnie
ingredients: 1 pound sauerkraut, drained, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 onion, chopped, 3 cloves garlic, minced, 1 pound smoked pork sausage, such as knockwurst or Metzgerei, sliced, 1 pound smoked bacon, diced, 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank, sliced, Salt and pepper, to taste, 1/4 cup Alsatian mustard, such as Moutarde de Meaux, 2 tablespoons white wine vinegar
2 tablespoons butter, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic. Cook until softened.
Add the sauerkraut, sausage, bacon, and beef. Cook until heated through.
Season with salt, pepper, mustard, and vinegar.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley and butter.

title: Baeckeoffe
ingredients: 1 pound potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced, 1 pound carrots, peeled and thinly sliced, 1 pound onions, thinly sliced, 2 pounds beef, cut into 1-inch pieces, 1 pound bacon, diced, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup Alsatian beer, such as Kronenbourg, 2 tablespoons butter, Salt and pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, carrots, onions, beef, bacon, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, mix beer and butter. Pour over the meat and vegetable mixture.
Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cover with foil and bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the foil and sprinkle with flour. Return to oven and bake for an additional 30 minutes.

title: Tarte aux Kugelhopf
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups warm milk, 2 teaspoons active dry yeast, 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted, 2 large eggs, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1 cup almonds, chopped, Confectioners' sugar, for dusting
instructions: Combine warm milk and yeast. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt, sugar, and melted butter to the yeast mixture. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Let the dough rest for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Transfer the dough to a greased and floured brioche mold or a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool for 10 minutes before removing from mold or pan.

title: Quetschentaart
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, 2 large eggs, 2 tablespoons milk, 2 cups cherry jam, 1 cup sliced almonds
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and sugar.
Add softened butter and mix until crumbly.
Beat in eggs and milk.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Transfer the dough to a greased and floured 9-inch springform pan.
Spread the cherry jam over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
Top with sliced almonds.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool for 10 minutes before removing from pan.

title: Braised Short Ribs in Red Wine
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Season the short ribs with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the short ribs until browned, then set aside.
Add the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the short ribs to the pot and cover with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and braise for 2 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Remove the pot from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Serve the short ribs with the braising liquid spooned over the top.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Sear the chicken until browned, then set aside.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot. Cook until the onion is tender.
Add the mushrooms to the pot and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the bacon, pearl onions, and carrots.
Cover the pot and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve the Coq au Vin hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Bœuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef short ribs or chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the beef until browned, then set aside.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot. Cook until the onion is tender.
Add the carrots and celery to the pot and cook until they are tender.
Add the red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the beef to the pot and add the mushrooms and pearl onions.
Cover the pot and simmer over low heat for 2 1/2 hours, or until the beef is tender.
Serve the Bœuf Bourguignon hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Tarte aux Fromages
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, chilled and cut into small pieces
2 cups cheese, shredded (Comté, Gruyère, or Emmental)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, confectioners' sugar, and salt.
Add the cold butter to the bowl and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually pour in the heavy cream, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together in a ball.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the dough to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
In a small bowl, mix together the shredded cheese and grated cheese.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the dough up over the cheese to form a crust.
Bake the tart for 35-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Poulet en Cocotte
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until browned, then set aside.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot. Cook until the onion is tender.
Add the mushrooms to the pot and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the broth, flour, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the pot and cover with a lid.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve the Poulet en Cocotte hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Salade Lyonnaise
ingredients: 4 cups mixed greens, such as arugula and endive
4 slices of bacon, cooked and crumbled
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens and frisée.
Top the salad with croutons and shaved Comté cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Season the dressing with salt and pepper to taste.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Top the salad with crumbled bacon and serve immediately.

title: Poulet en Daube
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the white wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover the pot and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 30 minutes, then serve hot.

title: Tarte aux Fromages
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Transfer the pastry to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix together the Gruyère, Comté, and Parmesan cheese.
Spread the cheese mixture over the center of the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Brush the edges of the pastry with the beaten egg for a glaze.
Bake the tart for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
Remove from the oven and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

title: Quenelles de Brochet
ingredients: 1 pound pike fish, boned and flaked
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the flaked fish, flour, softened butter, beaten egg, and grated Gruyère cheese.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Using a piping bag or a spoon, shape the mixture into quenelles, about 1 inch in diameter.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add a small amount of oil.
Add the quenelles to the skillet and cook until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Serve the quenelles hot with a side of your choice.

title: Cassoulet
ingredients: 1 pound white beans, such as cannellini or navy beans
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the sliced sausage and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the shredded duck confit and cook until heated through.
Add the white beans, chicken broth, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover the pot and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 30 minutes, then serve hot.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds assorted fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and cod)
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, leeks, carrots, and celery, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the saffron, thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, paprika, and saffron powder, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the fish and shellfish, and cook until they are lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the fish stock and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rouille and cook for 1 minute.
Serve the bouillabaisse hot, garnished with parsley and basil, and topped with croutons.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Heat the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken, and cook until browned on both sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot, and set aside.
Add the cognac to the pot, and ignite the flame.
Once the flames have died down, add the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, flour, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf, and stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the pot, and simmer for 25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the mushrooms and pearl onions to the pot, and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve the Coq au Vin hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large bowl, combine the apples, sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice.
Add the melted butter and Calvados to the bowl, and toss to combine.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the pastry to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
Arrange the apple mixture in the pastry-lined tart pan, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the pastry up over the apples, pressing gently to seal.
Bake the tart for 25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic, and cook until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the bell peppers, zucchinis, and eggplants, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth to the skillet, and stir to combine.
Reduce the heat to low, and simmer the ratatouille for 20 minutes, or until the flavors have melded together.
Season the ratatouille with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the ratatouille hot, garnished with parsley and basil.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, granulated sugar, and salt.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is hot but not boiling.
In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Gradually add the hot cream mixture to the egg yolks, whisking constantly.
Strain the mixture into 4 (1/2 cup) ramekins or custard cups.
Place the ramekins in a large baking dish, and add hot water to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake the crème brûlée for 25-30 minutes, or until set.
Remove the ramekins from the water bath, and let cool to room temperature.
Cover the ramekins with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of granulated sugar over the top of each ramekin.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch, or under the broiler.

title: Piperade
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and bell peppers; cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Make 2 wells in the mixture and crack in the eggs.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the eggs are set, about 5 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with Manchego cheese if desired.

title: Tournedos Rossini
instructions: Season the filets with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the filets and cook, turning occasionally, until browned on both sides and cooked to desired doneness, about 8-10 minutes.
Transfer the filets to a plate and keep warm.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the flour to the skillet; cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Gradually add the Madeira wine and beef broth, whisking constantly; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, whisking occasionally, until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the mustard and thyme.
Serve the filets with the sauce spooned over the top, topped with foie gras and truffles if desired.
Garnish with parsley if desired.

title: Garbure
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans (such as cannellini or Great Northern), soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans, broth, ham, bacon, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the beans are tender, about 1 hour.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Magret de Canard
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, mustard, and garlic.
Rub the mixture all over the duck breasts.
Season with thyme, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the duck breasts, skin side down, until browned, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook, skin side up, until the duck is cooked to desired doneness, about 12-15 minutes.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Cassoulet
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans (such as cannellini or Great Northern), soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans, broth, sausage, and duck confit.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the beans are tender, about 1 hour.
Transfer the pot to the oven and bake, uncovered, until the top is golden brown, about 30 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with Gruyère cheese if desired.

title: Ratatouille Provençale
ingredients: 2 large bell peppers, sliced 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss eggplant, zucchinis, and bell peppers with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast in the oven for 30 minutes, or until tender.
In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Combine roasted vegetables with tomato mixture and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped basil if desired.

title: Tarte Provençale aux Fruits
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a 1/4-inch thickness.
Transfer pastry to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
In a bowl, mix together berries, peaches, nectarines, granulated sugar, and vanilla extract.
Arrange fruit mixture in a concentric circle pattern on the pastry.
Brush edges of pastry with beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Soupe au Pistou
ingredients: 2 cups dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
2 cups chopped fresh vegetables (carrots, celery, onions)
instructions: In a large pot, combine soaked kidney beans, chopped vegetables, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
In a blender or food processor, puree soup until smooth.
In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in grated Gruyère cheese until melted.
Add basil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, topped with a dollop of pistou.

title: Daube Provençale
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add beef short ribs and cook until browned on all sides.
Add chopped onions, garlic, carrots, and celery, and cook until tender.
Add red wine, beef broth, tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Transfer Dutch oven to the preheated oven and braise for 2 1/2 hours.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.

title: Tapenade Niçoise
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine olives, capers, green olives, garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Blend until smooth, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve as a dip or spread on crackers or bread.

title: Kouign-amann
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups warm milk, 2 teaspoons active dry yeast, 3 tablespoons granulated sugar, 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted, 1 egg, beaten, 1/2 cup granulated sugar
instructions: In a large bowl, combine warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon sugar. Let it sit for 5 minutes. Add flour, salt, and melted butter. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Add beaten egg and mix until smooth. Knead the dough for 10 minutes. Let it rise for 1 hour. Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch. Fold the dough in thirds, then roll it out to a thickness of 1/4 inch. Repeat the folding and rolling process 3 times. Cut the dough into triangles and roll each triangle into a croissant shape. Place the kouign-amann on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Let it rise for another 30 minutes. Bake in a preheated oven at 425°F for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Steak Tartare
ingredients: 1 pound beef tenderloin, finely chopped, 1 tablespoon finely chopped shallot, 1 tablespoon finely chopped capers, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 2 egg yolks, 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, softened
1 baguette, sliced, 1 lettuce leaf, 1 tomato slice, 1 lemon wedge
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chopped beef, shallot, capers, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Just before serving, stir in egg yolks and softened butter. Divide the steak tartare among plates. Serve with toasted baguette slices, lettuce leaf, tomato slice, and lemon wedge.

title: Crêpes Bretonnes
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1/2 cup water, 2 tablespoons butter, melted, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, 1/4 cup crème fraîche, 1/4 cup granulated sugar
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, eggs, milk, water, melted butter, salt, and sugar. Whisk until smooth. Let it rest for 30 minutes. Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Brush with butter. Pour a small amount of batter into the pan and tilt to coat evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl. Loosen the crêpe with a spatula and flip. Cook for another minute. Repeat with remaining batter. Serve with crème fraîche and granulated sugar.

title: Brebiche Bretonne
ingredients: 4 cups mussels, scrubbed and debearded, 1 pound smoked bacon, diced, 2 tablespoons butter, 1 onion, chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup dry white wine, 1 cup fish stock, 1 tablespoon tomato paste, 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons heavy cream, 2 egg yolks, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 2 slices baguette, toasted
instructions: In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced bacon and cook until crispy. Remove the bacon from the pot and set aside. Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot and cook until softened. Add mussels, white wine, fish stock, tomato paste, flour, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the mussels are open. Stir in heavy cream and egg yolks. Cook for another minute. Serve the brebiche in bowls with toasted baguette slices and chopped parsley.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 4-6 apples, peeled, cored, and halved, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
instructions: In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add granulated sugar and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally. Add halved apples to the skillet and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally. In a small bowl, whisk together flour, heavy cream, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice. Pour the mixture over the apples and cook for 2-3 minutes. Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of 1/4 inch. Place the pastry over the apples and tuck the edges under the skillet. Bake in a preheated oven at 425°F for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown. Let the tarte Tatin cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
2 cups mushrooms, button or cremini, sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
In a large Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on both sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the pot.
Add the sliced onion, carrots, and celery and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cognac and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 25-30 minutes.
Add the browned chicken back to the pot and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve the chicken with the sauce spooned over the top and garnished with mushrooms.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat.
Add the halved apples and cook until they are caramelized and tender, about 20-25 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the granulated sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice.
Sprinkle the sugar mixture evenly over the apples.
Roll out the pie crust and place it over the apples.
Trim the excess crust and crimp the edges to seal the tart.
Cut a few slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Brush the top crust with the beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake the tart for 25-30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.
Remove the tart from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Invert the tart onto a serving plate and serve warm.

title: Steak au Poivre
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Season the steaks with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, mix together the black peppercorns and coriander seeds.
Press the peppercorn mixture onto both sides of the steaks.
Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the steaks and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until a nice crust forms.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook the steaks for 8-12 minutes, or until they reach the desired level of doneness.
Remove the skillet from the oven and add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the heavy cream and cognac, and cook until the sauce has thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve the steaks with the sauce spooned over the top.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced eggplant, zucchini, bell pepper, and onion, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes.
Season the ratatouille with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the ratatouille hot, garnished with fresh herbs, if desired.

title: Bûche de Noël
ingredients: 1 cup chocolate ganache, store-bought or homemade
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, confectioners' sugar, and unsalted butter.
Add the granulated sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract, and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Transfer the dough to a parchment-lined baking sheet and smooth the top.
Bake the dough for 20-25 minutes, or until it is lightly golden brown.
Remove the dough from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a wire rack and let it cool completely.
In a small bowl, whisk together the heavy cream and confectioners' sugar.
Dip the cooled dough in the cream mixture, then roll it up tightly.
Place the rolled dough on a serving plate and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Drizzle the chocolate ganache over the top of the dough and sprinkle with chopped hazelnuts.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 cup red wine, such as Burgundy
8 ounces mushrooms, such as button or cremini
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and transfer to oven.
Bake at 300°F for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Add mushrooms, carrots, and celery to pot and cook for an additional 10 minutes.

title: Bœuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef short ribs, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cups red wine, such as Burgundy
1 cup mushrooms, such as button or cremini
instructions: Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, red wine, broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and transfer to oven.
Bake at 300°F for 2 1/2 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add carrots, celery, and mushrooms to pot and cook for an additional 10 minutes.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a large bowl, combine apples, sugar, and melted butter.
Roll out puff pastry and place in a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
Fill pastry with apple mixture and dot with Calvados, if using.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and apples are tender.
Let cool in pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a plate to serve.

title: Duck L'Orange
ingredients: 1/4 cup Grand Marnier or other orange-flavored liqueur
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a small saucepan, combine orange juice, Grand Marnier, and honey.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season duck breasts with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Sear duck in a skillet over medium-high heat until browned, about 2 minutes per side.
Transfer duck to oven and cook for 12-15 minutes, or until cooked through.
Brush with orange sauce and serve.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add eggplant and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add zucchini, bell pepper, and onion, and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds assorted fish and shellfish, such as mussels, clams, and cod, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add fish stock, water, saffron, fennel seeds, and orange zest. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.
Add fish and shellfish to the pot. Simmer, covered, until cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with croutons and rouille.

title: Salade Lyonnaise
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, lettuce, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and blue cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together oil and vinegar.
Drizzle dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Sprinkle with chervil and tarragon.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Tarte aux Fines Herbes
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Transfer pastry to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix together butter, chervil, tarragon, parsley, and Gruyère cheese.
Spread herb mixture evenly over the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold edges of pastry up over the filling to form a crust.
Bake until pastry is golden brown, about 25 minutes.

title: Cassoulet
ingredients: 1 pound white beans, such as cannellini or navy
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large pot, combine beans and enough cold water to cover. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 10 minutes.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 10 minutes.
Stir in thyme and rosemary. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer beans to a 9x13-inch baking dish. Top with sausage mixture and duck confit.
Bake until casserole is hot and bubbly, about 25 minutes.

title: Quenelles de Brochet
instructions: In a large bowl, combine fish, flour, Gruyère cheese, egg, and melted butter. Mix well to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Using a piping bag, pipe fish mixture into long, thin cylinders.
Poach quenelles in a large pot of simmering water for 5-7 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve with parsley and a side of lemon wedges.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, and thyme. Set aside.
In a large Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, then the sliced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the cognac and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2 minutes.
Add the red wine, chicken broth, and tomato paste. Stir to combine.
Return the chicken to the pot and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and transfer to the oven. Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve the chicken and vegetables hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3-4 Golden Delicious apples, peeled, halved, and cored
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat.
Add the sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sugar is dissolved.
Add the apple halves to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes, or until the apples are tender and caramelized.
Roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Place the pastry over the apples and tuck the edges under the fruit.
Dot the top of the pastry with the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter.
Bake the tarte for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
Remove the tarte from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Invert the tarte onto a serving plate and serve warm.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 2 pounds assorted fish and shellfish (such as mussels, clams, and shrimp)
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, carrots, and celery. Cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the fish and shellfish to the pot and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they start to brown.
Add the fish broth, water, saffron, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through.
Serve the bouillabaisse hot, topped with rouille and croutons.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a medium saucepan, combine the cream, sugar, and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar is dissolved.
In a small bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and vanilla extract.
Gradually add the warm cream mixture to the egg yolks, whisking constantly.
Pour the mixture into 4-6 ramekins or small baking dishes.
Place the ramekins in a large baking dish and add hot water to come halfway up the sides.
Bake the crème brûlée for 25-30 minutes, or until set.
Remove the ramekins from the water bath and let cool to room temperature.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until chilled.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of granulated sugar over the top of each ramekin.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch or under the broiler.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the pie crust and place it in a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, Gruyère cheese, ham, onion, salt, and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture into the pie crust.
Drizzle the melted butter over the top of the quiche.
Bake the quiche for 35-40 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the center is set.
Remove the quiche from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Serve the quiche warm, garnished with fresh herbs.

title: Piperade
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the peppers and onions and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and sausage and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and paprika and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

title: Tournedos Rossini
instructions: Season the filets with salt and pepper.
Sear the filets in a skillet over high heat for 2 minutes per side.
Add the foie gras to the skillet and cook for 30 seconds.
Transfer the filets to a plate and keep warm.
Add the cognac to the skillet and ignite.
Add the broth, wine, and butter to the skillet and simmer until reduced.
Serve the filets with the sauce spooned over the top.

title: Gigot d'Agneau au Moutarde
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Rub the lamb with the mustard, oil, garlic, and rosemary.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Roast the lamb in the oven for 20 minutes per pound, or until cooked to desired doneness.

title: Tarbais Beans
ingredients: 1 pound Tarbais beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes, paprika, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Simmer for 1 hour, or until the beans are tender.

title: Gâteau Basque
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, almonds, and sugar.
Add the butter and eggs to the bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Add the vanilla extract to the dough and mix to combine.
Roll out the dough and place on a baking sheet.
Spread the jam and preserves over the dough.
Roll up the dough and bake for 40 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
2 large zucchinis, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
2 large bell peppers, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, toss eggplant slices with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20-25 minutes.
In another bowl, toss zucchinis and bell peppers with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with salt. Spread on a separate baking sheet and roast for 20-25 minutes.
In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add roasted eggplant, zucchinis, and bell peppers to the skillet. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add diced tomatoes to the skillet and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with chopped basil leaves, if desired.

title: Tarte Provençale
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and cold butter. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ice water, stirring with a fork until dough comes together in a ball.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Transfer dough to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom. Trim edges and press dough into corners.
In a bowl, mix caramelized onions, garlic, Gruyère cheese, and Comté cheese.
Spread onion mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Brush edges with beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until crust is golden brown.

title: Daube Provençale
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a large Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown beef short ribs on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Add red wine, beef broth, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary to the pot. Stir to combine.
Return beef short ribs to the pot and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, or until meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Soupe au Pistou
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic to the pot and cook for an additional minute.
Add diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and heavy cream to the pot. Stir to combine.
Bring the soup to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until heated through.
Stir in chopped basil, parsley, and Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Tarte aux Fruits
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
2 cups mixed berries (such as strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour and cold butter. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work butter into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ice water, stirring with a fork until dough comes together in a ball.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Transfer dough to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom. Trim edges and press dough into corners.
In a bowl, mix granulated sugar, eggs, and mixed berries.
Pour the berry mixture into the pastry-lined tart pan.
In a small bowl, mix cornstarch and lemon juice. Sprinkle over the berry mixture.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until crust is golden brown.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: Combine mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and Kalamata olives in a large bowl.
Crumb feta cheese over the top of the salad.
In a small bowl, whisk together red wine vinegar, olive oil, and dried oregano.
Drizzle dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush eggplant slices with olive oil and season with salt.
Bake eggplant slices in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.
In a large skillet, cook ground lamb over medium-high heat until browned.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet and cook until softened.
Stir in tomato puree and dried oregano.
In a separate saucepan, heat bechamel sauce over low heat.
Assemble the moussaka by layering eggplant slices, lamb mixture, and bechamel sauce in a baking dish.
Top with grated kefalograviera cheese and bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Greek Stuffed Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a small bowl, combine crumbled feta cheese, chopped parsley, chopped dill, and minced garlic.
Season with dried oregano, salt, and pepper to taste.
Stuff each chicken breast with the feta mixture.
Bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine chopped spinach, crumbled feta cheese, chopped parsley, chopped dill, and minced garlic.
Season with dried oregano to taste.
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Place the spinach mixture in the center of the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Brush the edges of the pastry with beaten egg.
Fold the pastry over the filling, pressing edges to seal.
Bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Loukoumades
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, warm water, olive oil, honey, sugar, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and ground cardamom.
Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 375°F (190°C).
Fry small balls of dough in the hot oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Gyro
ingredients: 1 pound lamb or beef, thinly sliced
Tomato, onion, and cucumber, thinly sliced
instructions: In a large bowl, combine sliced lamb or beef, olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix well to combine.
Thread lamb or beef onto skewers, if using.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Cook gyro meat for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Warm pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating them in the oven for a few minutes.
Assemble gyros by slicing cooked meat and serving it in pita breads with tzatziki sauce, tomato, onion, and cucumber.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1 large eggplant, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, cook sliced eggplant over medium heat until golden brown on both sides.
In a separate skillet, cook chopped onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add ground lamb or beef to the skillet and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Stir in tomato puree and cook for a few minutes.
In a separate saucepan, heat bechamel sauce over low heat.
To assemble moussaka, create a layer of eggplant slices in the bottom of a baking dish, followed by a layer of meat sauce, and then a layer of bechamel sauce.
Repeat this process until all ingredients are used, finishing with a layer of bechamel sauce on top.
Sprinkle kefalograviera cheese over the top of the bechamel sauce.
Bake moussaka in the preheated oven for 30-40 minutes, or until golden brown and set.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and Kalamata olives.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Top salad with crumbled feta cheese.
Serve immediately.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine spinach, feta cheese, Parmesan cheese, parsley, dill, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together olive oil and beaten egg.
Layer phyllo dough in a baking dish, brushing each layer with olive oil and egg mixture.
Spoon spinach mixture into the center of the phyllo dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold phyllo dough over the spinach mixture, brushing edges with olive oil and egg mixture.
Bake spanakopita in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and set.

title: Tzatziki Sauce
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine Greek yogurt, diced cucumber, garlic, lemon juice, and dried dill.
Mix well to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Greek Salad
ingredients: 4 cups mixed greens, such as romaine, arugula, and/or spinach
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and olives.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and dried oregano.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Top with crumbled feta cheese and serve.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush the eggplant slices with olive oil and season with salt.
Grill or broil the eggplant until tender.
In a large skillet, cook the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned.
Stir in the tomato puree and bring to a simmer.
In a large baking dish, create a layer of eggplant slices.
Top with the meat sauce and a layer of bechamel sauce.
Repeat the layers two more times, ending with a layer of bechamel sauce.
Top with Parmesan cheese and bake until golden brown.

title: Greek Stuffed Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a small bowl, mix together the olive oil, garlic, feta cheese, parsley, dill, and scallions.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Make a horizontal incision in each chicken breast to create a pocket.
Stuff each chicken breast with the feta cheese mixture.
Bake until the chicken is cooked through and the filling is heated through.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, mix together the spinach, garlic, feta cheese, Parmesan cheese, parsley, and dill.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil and egg.
Layer the phyllo dough in a large baking dish, brushing with the olive oil mixture between each layer.
Top with the spinach mixture and fold the phyllo dough over to create a triangle.
Bake until the phyllo is golden brown and the filling is heated through.

title: Galaktoboureko
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium saucepan, whisk together the milk, sugar, and cornstarch.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in the melted butter, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Layer the phyllo dough in a large baking dish, brushing with melted butter between each layer.
Top with the custard mixture and fold the phyllo dough over to create a triangle.
Bake until the phyllo is golden brown and the custard is set.
Top with chopped walnuts and serve.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds eggplant, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook eggplant slices in a single layer on a baking sheet, drizzling with olive oil and seasoning with salt and pepper.
Brown lamb or beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and cook until softened.
Stir in tomato puree and cook for 1-2 minutes.
In a large baking dish, create a layer of eggplant slices, followed by a layer of meat mixture, and then a layer of bechamel sauce.
Repeat this process two more times, ending with a layer of bechamel sauce on top.
Sprinkle kefalograviera cheese over the top layer of bechamel sauce.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the casserole is hot and bubbly.

title: Greek Salad
ingredients: 4 cups mixed greens (such as arugula, spinach, and lettuce)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion.
Top with crumbled feta cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Drizzle dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine spinach, feta cheese, kefalograviera cheese, scallions, dill, and parsley.
Stir in olive oil and beaten egg.
Layer phyllo dough in a large baking dish, brushing each layer with butter or olive oil.
Spoon spinach mixture onto the phyllo dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the phyllo dough up over the filling, then roll the dough into a tight log.
Place the log seam-side down in the baking dish and brush with butter or olive oil.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the phyllo dough is golden brown and the filling is hot and bubbly.

title: Grilled Octopus
ingredients: 4 octopus tentacles, cleaned and patted dry
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, and oregano.
Brush the mixture onto both sides of the octopus tentacles.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Grill the octopus for 2-3 minutes per side, or until it is cooked through and slightly charred.

title: Tiropita
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine feta cheese, kefalograviera cheese, scallions, dill, and parsley.
Stir in beaten egg.
Layer phyllo dough in a large baking dish, brushing each layer with olive oil.
Spoon cheese mixture onto the phyllo dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the phyllo dough up over the filling, then roll the dough into a tight log.
Place the log seam-side down in the baking dish and brush with olive oil.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the phyllo dough is golden brown and the filling is hot and bubbly.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the chopped mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together the red wine vinegar and olive oil.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Sprinkle the dried oregano over the top of the salad and serve.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, sauté the chopped onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add the ground lamb to the skillet and cook until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
In a separate saucepan, combine the tomato puree and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
In a large baking dish, create a layer of eggplant slices. Top with a layer of the meat mixture, followed by a layer of the tomato sauce.
Repeat the layers, finishing with a layer of bechamel sauce on top.
Sprinkle the grated kefalograviera cheese over the top of the bechamel sauce and bake for 30-40 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Grilled Octopus
ingredients: 4 octopus tentacles, cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, and lemon zest.
Add the octopus pieces to the bowl and toss to coat with the marinade.
Grill the octopus for 2-3 minutes per side, or until charred and cooked through.
Serve the grilled octopus with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the spinach, feta cheese, kefalograviera cheese, chopped dill, and chopped scallions.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Place a sheet of phyllo dough on a flat surface and brush with melted butter.
Repeat the process of layering the phyllo dough and brushing with butter until all of the dough is used, finishing with a layer of phyllo on top.
Spoon the spinach mixture into the center of the phyllo dough and fold the edges of the dough over the filling to form a triangle.
Brush the top of the spanakopita with melted butter and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Galaktoboureko
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, chopped pistachios, cinnamon, and ground cloves.
Place a sheet of phyllo dough on a flat surface and brush with melted butter.
Repeat the process of layering the phyllo dough and brushing with butter until all of the dough is used, finishing with a layer of phyllo on top.
Spoon the milk custard into the center of the phyllo dough and fold the edges of the dough over the filling to form a triangle.
Brush the top of the galaktoboureko with melted butter and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion.
Crumb feta cheese over the top of the salad.
Drizzle olive oil over the salad and sprinkle with garlic.
Add vinegar and oregano, and toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush eggplant slices with olive oil and season with salt.
Bake eggplant slices for 20-25 minutes or until tender.
In a large skillet, sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add lamb and cook until browned, breaking into small pieces.
Stir in tomato sauce and cook for 5 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, heat bechamel sauce over low heat.
In a 9x13 inch baking dish, create a layer of eggplant slices.
Top with lamb and tomato sauce mixture, followed by bechamel sauce.
Sprinkle with kefalograviera cheese and bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine spinach, feta cheese, parmesan cheese, dill, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour and melted butter.
Add beaten egg to flour mixture and stir to combine.
Roll out puff pastry and cut into a circle or square shape.
Place spinach mixture in center of pastry and brush edges with egg wash.
Fold pastry over filling and press edges to seal.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Grilled Octopus
ingredients: 1 large octopus, cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, and oregano.
Add octopus pieces to bowl and toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Grill octopus for 2-3 minutes per side or until tender and slightly charred.
Serve immediately.

title: Tiropita
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine feta cheese, parmesan cheese, parsley, and garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour and melted butter.
Add beaten egg to flour mixture and stir to combine.
Layer phyllo dough in a 9x13 inch baking dish, brushing with melted butter between layers.
Top with cheese mixture and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: Combine chopped mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion in a large bowl.
Top with crumbled feta cheese.
In a small bowl, whisk together red wine vinegar and olive oil.
Pour the dressing over the salad and sprinkle with dried oregano.
Toss to combine and serve.

title: Spanakopita (Spinach and Feta Pie)
ingredients: 1 package frozen spinach, thawed and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Combine spinach, feta cheese, Parmesan cheese, and chopped dill in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, salt, and black pepper.
Add the dry mixture to the spinach mixture and stir until well combined.
Add the melted butter and eggs to the spinach mixture and stir until well combined.
Roll out the pie crust and place it in a 9-inch pie dish.
Pour the spinach mixture into the pie crust.
Bake for 40-50 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/4-inch thick rounds
1 cup bechamel sauce (see below for recipe)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush eggplant slices with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Grill or bake eggplant slices until tender.
In a large skillet, combine tomato sauce and dried oregano.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes.
Spread a layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Arrange a layer of eggplant slices on top of the tomato sauce.
Spread a layer of bechamel sauce on top of the eggplant.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and dried thyme.
Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used up.
Top with a layer of bechamel sauce and Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 30-40 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Greek Stuffed Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Butterfly the chicken breasts and season with salt and pepper.
Combine feta cheese, parsley, dill, garlic, and oregano in a small bowl.
Divide the feta mixture among the chicken breasts.
Roll up the chicken breasts and secure with toothpicks.
Place the chicken on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes or until cooked through.

title: Galaktoboureko (Custard Pie in Phyllo Dough)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Combine custard and chopped walnuts in a small bowl.
Cut the phyllo dough into 4 equal pieces.
Place a piece of phyllo dough on a flat surface and brush with butter.
Place a spoonful of the custard mixture in the center of the phyllo dough.
Fold the phyllo dough over the filling and brush with butter.
Repeat with the remaining phyllo dough and custard mixture.
Place the galaktoboureko on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Greek Moussaka
ingredients: 1 cup bechamel sauce (see below for recipe)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Sauté eggplant slices in olive oil until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Cook ground lamb, onion, and garlic in a large skillet until the lamb is browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in tomato puree, oregano, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, eggs, and milk. Mix well.
In a 9x13-inch baking dish, create a layer of eggplant slices, followed by a layer of the lamb mixture, and then a layer of the ricotta mixture.
Repeat the layers, ending with a layer of eggplant on top.
Spread bechamel sauce over the top layer of eggplant.
