Add garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, garam masala, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens, about 15-20 minutes.
Add the grilled chicken to the saucepan and simmer until the chicken is coated in the sauce.
Serve the chicken hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the spinach, garlic, and 1/4 cup water until smooth.
In a large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat. Add cumin and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the spinach puree and cook, stirring constantly, for 2-3 minutes.
Add the paneer, garam masala, salt, and black pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until the paneer is coated in the spinach sauce.
Add the heavy cream and lemon juice. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Serve the palak paneer hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Sri Lankan Hoppers (Appam)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt.
Gradually add the water to the flour mixture and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan or a hopper pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of oil into the pan and tilt to coat the bottom.
Pour 1/4 cup of the batter into the pan and tilt to form a circular shape.
Cook the hopper for 2-3 minutes, until the bottom is golden brown.
Loosen the hopper with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook the other side for 1-2 minutes, until it is lightly browned.
Serve the hopper hot with coconut milk and chopped cilantro.

title: Nepali Momo (Dumplings)
ingredients: 1/2 cup ground meat (beef, pork, or chicken)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Gradually add the oil and water to the flour mixture and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Heat a non-stick pan or a steamer over medium heat.
Steam the momos for 10-15 minutes, until they are cooked through.

title: Indian Basmati Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer until the water runs clear.
In a large saucepan, combine the rice and water.
Add the ghee and salt to the saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer the rice for 15-20 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Serve the basmati rice hot.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee or oil, garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add chicken to the marinade and mix until coated.
Grill chicken until cooked through.
Heat butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste.
Simmer sauce until thickened.
Add cooked chicken to the sauce and simmer until heated through.

title: Sri Lankan Hoppers (Appam)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine rice flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and sugar.
Gradually add lukewarm water and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Add coconut milk and mix until combined.
Add beaten egg and mix until smooth.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Brush pan with vegetable oil.
Pour a small amount of batter into the pan and tilt to spread evenly.
Cook until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Loosen the hopper with a spatula and flip over to cook the other side.

title: Nepali Momo (Dumplings)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, warm water, and salt.
Mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and press edges to seal.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the momos until golden brown.
Serve with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce, vinegar, and ghee or oil.

title: Pakistani Biryani
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, and cayenne pepper (if using).
Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add rice and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice is cooked.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in frozen peas and carrots.

title: Indian Chana Masala
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, and cayenne pepper (if using).
Cook for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas and cook until browned.
Add diced tomatoes and vegetable broth.
Simmer until the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt to taste.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee or oil, garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, if using.
Grill the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
In a large saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and stir to coat.
Simmer the chicken in the sauce for 5-10 minutes, or until heated through.
Serve the chicken in the sauce over basmati rice, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Sag Aloo
ingredients: 1 small bunch of fresh cilantro, chopped
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the diced potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are tender, about 10-12 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach and cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the spices are fragrant.
Stir in the chopped cilantro.
Serve the Sag Aloo hot over basmati rice or with naan bread.

title: Biryani
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and corn)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the spices are fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender.
In a large saucepan, combine the rice and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and fluffy.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the cooked chicken and vegetable mixture.
Transfer the Biryani to a serving dish and garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Dhokla
ingredients: 1 cup split red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed and drained
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the lentils and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Drain the lentils and transfer them to a blender or food processor.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, baking soda, and salt to the blender.
Blend until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and stir in the lemon juice.
Pour the mixture into a greased 8-inch square baking dish or a non-stick Dhokla pan.
Steam the Dhokla for 15-20 minutes, or until it is set and firm to the touch.
Remove the Dhokla from the steamer and let it cool for a few minutes.
Cut the Dhokla into small squares and serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Rogan Josh
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the diced lamb or beef and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are tender.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the spices are fragrant.
Add the Kashmiri red chili powder and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Serve the Rogan Josh hot over basmati rice or with naan bread, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne pepper (if using); cook for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in tomato puree and season with salt to taste.
Serve over basmati rice, garnished with cilantro.

title: Sri Lankan Fish Ambulthiyal
ingredients: 4 fish pieces (mackerel or sardines), cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tbsp mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: In a blender, combine tamarind paste and water; blend until smooth.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic, onion, and green chilies; cook until onion is translucent.
Add fish pieces and cook until browned on both sides.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, and tamarind paste mixture.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Nepali Dal Bhat
instructions: Rinse lentils and soak in water for 30 minutes.
Drain and rinse lentils, then combine with 2 cups water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Heat oil in a separate saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until onion is translucent.
Stir in cumin and coriander; cook for 1 minute.
Add cooked lentils and season with salt to taste.
Serve with basmati rice and garnished with cilantro.

title: Pakistani Kebabs
ingredients: 1 lb lamb or beef, finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chopped meat, onion, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne pepper (if using); mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Form meat mixture into small patties or skewers.
Grill for 4-6 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges and your favorite sides.

title: Indian Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add spinach leaves and cook until wilted.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Add paneer cubes and cook until heated through.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, lemon juice, garam masala, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, if using.
Grill the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until it is cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth and heavy cream, and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the tomato paste.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and stir to coat.
Simmer the sauce for 2-3 minutes, or until it has thickened slightly.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and serve the chicken in the sauce over basmati rice.

title: Sag Aloo (Spinach and Potato Curry)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes, or until they are tender.
Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes, or until they are softened.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the spinach and cook, stirring occasionally, until it has wilted.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the butter and stir until melted.
Serve the curry over basmati rice, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Biryani (Mixed Rice with Meat and Spices)
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and cauliflower)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes, or until it is softened.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is cooked through.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are tender.
In a separate saucepan, bring the rice and water to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender.
To assemble the biryani, layer the cooked rice and chicken mixture in a large saucepan.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve.

title: Palak Paneer (Spinach and Cheese Curry)
ingredients: 1 pound paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes, or until they are softened.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the spinach and cook, stirring occasionally, until it has wilted.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the paneer and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is coated in the spinach mixture.
Add the butter and stir until melted.
Serve the curry over basmati rice, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Dosa (South Indian Fermented Crepe)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons chutney (such as coconut or tomato)
instructions: Rinse the rice and dal, and soak them in water for 4-5 hours.
Drain and grind the rice and dal into a smooth batter.
Add the fenugreek seeds, yeast, and salt to the batter, and mix well.
Cover the batter and let it ferment for 12-24 hours.
Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of the batter into the pan and tilt to coat the bottom.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl.
Loosen the dosa with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the other side is lightly browned.
Serve the dosa with chutney and garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onions and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken; cook until browned, about 6 minutes.
In a large saucepan, combine rice and water. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and cover.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, cayenne pepper, and salt to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the spice mixture to the saucepan with the rice. Stir to combine.
Transfer the chicken mixture to the saucepan with the rice. Stir to combine.
Cover the saucepan and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Garnish with cilantro and yogurt.

title: Sri Lankan Pittu
instructions: In a large bowl, combine puffed rice flour, coconut milk, water, coconut, cilantro, salt, baking soda, and baking powder.
Mix well to combine.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until it forms a smooth ball.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on desired size.
Shape each piece into a long, thin cylinder.
Place the cylinders on a steamer basket lined with parchment paper.
Steam the pittu over boiling water for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Pakistani Karahi
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 cups mixed vegetables (bell peppers, carrots, potatoes)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onions and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken; cook until browned, about 6 minutes.
Add mixed vegetables; cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, and salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in yogurt.
Garnish with cilantro.

title: Indian Chana Masala
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onions and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, cayenne pepper, and salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas; cook for 2 minutes.
Add water and tomato puree; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until the chickpeas are tender.
Stir in yogurt.

title: Nepali Momo (Dumplings)
ingredients: 1/2 cup ground meat (beef, buffalo, or chicken)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda.
Gradually add lukewarm water; mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape.
Seal the edges with a fork or your fingers.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the momos until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee, garam masala, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, if using.
Grill the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes per side.
In a large saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the grilled chicken to the sauce and stir to coat.
Simmer the sauce for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Serve the chicken in the sauce over basmati rice, garnished with cilantro and naan bread.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the spinach leaves until smooth.
Heat the ghee in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, garam masala, salt, and black pepper.
Add the pureed spinach and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the broth and heavy cream and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the paneer to the sauce and stir to coat.
Simmer the sauce for 2-3 minutes, or until the paneer is heated through.
Stir in the butter and serve the palak paneer over basmati rice or with naan bread.

title: Sri Lankan Hoppers
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, coconut milk, warm water, and salt.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Heat a small non-stick skillet or hopper pan over medium heat.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on the size of hopper you want to make.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Place a disk of dough in the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl.
Loosen the hopper with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the other side is lightly browned.
Serve the hoppers hot with a sprinkle of grated coconut and chopped cilantro.

title: Bengali Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, such as cod or tilapia, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Add the fish to the saucepan and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Add the curry paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the fish broth and coconut milk and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and serve the fish curry over steamed rice.

title: Nepali Gorkhali Lamb
ingredients: 1 pound lamb or beef, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the ghee in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, garam masala, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the lamb to the saucepan and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the yogurt and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the lamb is cooked through.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and serve the Gorkhali lamb over steamed rice.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt mixture for 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
In a large saucepan, heat the ghee or oil over medium heat.
Add the spices and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the tomato puree, chicken broth, and heavy cream.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until thickened.
Stir in the butter and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Sri Lankan Hoppers (Appam)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flours, salt, sugar, and yeast.
Gradually add the lukewarm water and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the batter rise for 2-3 hours.
Heat a non-stick pan or appam pan over medium heat.
Brush the pan with ghee or oil.
Pour a small amount of the batter into the pan and tilt to form a circular shape.
Cook the hopper for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl.
Loosen the hopper with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Nepali Gorkhali Lamb
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder or shank, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the ghee or oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, spices, and cumin seeds, and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the lamb and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the broth, tomato puree, and yogurt.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 1 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with rice or roti.

title: Pakistani Kebabs (Seekh Kebab)
ingredients: 10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground meat, onion, cilantro, mint, garlic, spices, salt, and pepper.
Mix well with your hands until just combined.
Do not overmix.
Thread the meat mixture onto the bamboo skewers.
Brush the skewers with lemon juice and ghee or oil.
Grill the kebabs over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve hot with chutney or raita.

title: Bangladeshi Fish Curry (Bhapa Ilish)
ingredients: 1 lb fish fillets (such as hilsa or tilapia), cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, spices, and mustard paste, and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the fish and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the water, yogurt, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through.
Season with black pepper to taste.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with rice or roti.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee or oil, garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper. Add the chicken and mix until coated.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Remove the chicken from the marinade, allowing any excess to drip off. Grill the chicken until cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
In a large saucepan, combine the diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the heavy cream and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken to the saucepan and stir to coat with the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Sag Aloo
instructions: Heat the ghee or oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until they start to brown, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne pepper (if using) and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the mustard greens and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the greens are wilted, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Bengali-Style Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish (such as cod or tilapia), cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper (if using) and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the fish and cook, stirring occasionally, until opaque, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and fish broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the fish is cooked through and the sauce has thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the mustard oil (if using). Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the spinach leaves until smooth.
Heat the ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper (if using) and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the paneer and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach puree and water to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the paneer is coated in the spinach sauce, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Dal Makhani
ingredients: 1 cup kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 cup black lentils, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine the kidney beans and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer until the beans are tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Heat the ghee or oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper (if using) and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the black lentils and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the cooked kidney beans and heavy cream to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the dal has thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee or oil, garam masala, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the marinade and mix until coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
In a large saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened slightly, about 10-15 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken back into the sauce and stir to coat.
Simmer for a few minutes until the chicken is fully coated in the sauce.
Serve hot over basmati rice.

title: Sri Lankan Pittu
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the rice flour and salt.
Gradually add in the coconut milk and water, stirring with a fork until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until it is smooth and pliable.
Shape the dough into small cylindrical shapes, about 5-6 inches long and 1 inch in diameter.
Heat a pittu maker or a metal steamer basket over boiling water.
Place the pittu into the steamer and steam for 10-12 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve with coconut sambal and lunu miris (onion and chili relish).

title: Nepali Dal Bhat
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Rinse the lentils and soak them in water for 30 minutes.
Drain and rinse the lentils again, then combine them with 4 cups of water in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the lentils are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Heat the ghee or oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), and salt.
Add the cooked lentils to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Cook for a few minutes until the flavors have melded together.
Serve with basmati rice and a variety of side dishes.

title: Pakistani Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat the ghee or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the saucepan and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened slightly, about 10-15 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Indian Naan Bread
ingredients: Toppings (optional): cilantro, garlic, cumin seeds, or poppy seeds
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, warm water, salt, sugar, and yeast.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Divide the dough into 6-8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a ball and then flatten slightly into an oval shape.
Place the naan on the skillet or griddle and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until lightly browned and puffed.
Flip the naan and cook for another minute, or until lightly browned on the other side.
Serve hot, topped with desired toppings.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper.
Add the chicken to the bowl and mix until coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Grill the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
In the same grill or grill pan, add ghee or oil and swirl to coat.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and heavy cream.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the sauce has thickened.
Add the cooked chicken back to the sauce and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Sag Aloo (Spinach and Potato Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, or until they start to brown.
Add the cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach leaves and cook until wilted.
Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Dosa (Savory Rice and Lentil Crepe)
ingredients: 1 cup split red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed and drained
1 cup basmati rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Soak the lentils and rice in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain and rinse the lentil-rice mixture, then transfer to a blender.
Add fenugreek seeds, salt, and baking soda to the blender.
Blend until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and let it ferment for 24 hours.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of the fermented mixture onto the skillet.
Tilt the skillet to evenly coat the bottom with the mixture.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the edges start to curl.
Loosen the dosa with a spatula and fold it in half.
Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Biryani (Mixed Rice Dish)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and drained
2 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and cauliflower)
2 cups cooked chicken or lamb, shredded
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 1 minute.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add the cooked chicken or lamb and stir to combine.
In a separate saucepan, combine the basmati rice and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and fluffy.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the cooked vegetable mixture.
Transfer the biryani to a serving dish and garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Korean-Style Kimchi Fried Rice
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and cauliflower)
Chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds (for garnish)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Push the vegetables to one side of the skillet.
Add a little more oil if necessary, then pour in the beaten eggs.
Scramble the eggs until cooked through, then mix with the vegetables.
Add the cooked rice to the skillet, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Stir-fry the rice with the vegetables and eggs for about 5 minutes.
Add the chopped kimchi, soy sauce, and Gochujang to the skillet.
Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes, until the kimchi is evenly distributed.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Marinate the chicken in yogurt mixture for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Grill or bake the chicken until cooked through.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they start to brown.
Add garlic, garam masala, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and tomato paste. Stir to combine.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Serve the chicken in the sauce, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Combine spinach, garlic, and onion in a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach puree and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the paneer and cook until it starts to melt.
Stir in heavy cream and lemon juice. Simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Serve the palak paneer hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Sag Aloo
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they start to brown.
Add garlic, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until they start to soften.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted.
Serve the sag aloo hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Dosas
instructions: Soak the rice and dal in water for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Drain and rinse the rice and dal. Grind into a smooth batter.
Add yeast, salt, and fenugreek seeds to the batter. Mix well.
Cover the batter and let it ferment for 12-14 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or dosa pan over medium heat.
Brush the pan with oil. Pour a small amount of batter into the pan and spread it thinly.
Cook the dosa for 2-3 minutes, or until it starts to brown. Flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.

title: Rogan Josh
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they start to brown.
Add garlic, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the broth, wine (if using), tomato paste, and chili powder. Stir to combine.
Simmer the rogan josh for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Serve the rogan josh hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until they start to brown, about 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add ginger paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, cayenne pepper, and garam masala powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until they start to break down, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in butter until melted.
Garnish with cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
instructions: Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add spinach and cook until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Add cumin powder, coriander powder, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add paneer and cook until coated in the spinach mixture.
Stir in heavy cream until heated through.
Garnish with cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Nihari
ingredients: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until they start to brown, about 5 minutes.
Add beef or lamb shanks and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add ginger paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, cayenne pepper, and garam masala powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until they start to break down, about 5 minutes.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in butter until melted.
Garnish with cilantro and serve over basmati rice.

title: Kebabs
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
10-12 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, garam masala powder, cumin powder, salt, and black pepper.
Add chicken and mix until coated in the marinade.
Thread chicken onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Heat oil in a large grill pan over medium-high heat.
Add skewers and cook until chicken is cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with chutney or raita.

title: Samosas
ingredients: Filling ingredients: 1 cup cooked and mashed potatoes, 1 cup cooked and mashed peas, 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, salt, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and baking powder.
Add ghee or oil and mix until the dough comes together.
Gradually add lukewarm water and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until it becomes pliable.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon or two of the filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a triangle or a cone shape, and press the edges together to seal.

title: Bengali-Style Chicken Rezala
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they're lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, and cayenne pepper; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chicken; cook until it's browned on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and cilantro; cook for 1 minute.
Season with salt to taste.

title: Shorshe Ilish (Mustard Fish Curry)
ingredients: 2 pounds hilsa or any other fish of your choice, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they're lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add mustard paste; cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the fish; cook until it's browned on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the mustard oil, mustard seeds, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Macher Jhol (Fish Curry)
ingredients: 2 pounds any fish of your choice, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they're lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add mustard seeds; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the fish; cook until it's browned on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Luchi (Fried Bread)
instructions: Combine flour, ghee or oil, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Gradually add the lukewarm water; mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth; let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 6-8 equal portions; shape each portion into a ball.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat; fry the luchi until they're golden brown, about 1-2 minutes per side.

title: Bengali-Style Egg Curry (Ande Jhol)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they're lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add mustard seeds; cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the eggs; cook until they're heated through, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Fish Ambulthiyal
ingredients: 1 kg fish (mackerel or sardine), cut into small pieces
instructions: Marinate the fish pieces in a mixture of tamarind paste, mustard oil, garlic, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, turmeric powder, and red chili powder for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the marinated fish until it's cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh curry leaves.

title: Egg Hoppers
instructions: Mix the rice flour, coconut milk, water, and salt in a bowl to form a smooth batter.
Add the eggs to the batter and mix well.
Heat a non-stick pan and brush it with ghee or oil.
Pour a small amount of the batter into the pan and tilt it to form a circular shape.
Cook until the edges start to curl and the surface is dry.
Flip the hopper over and cook for another minute.

title: Gotu Kola Mallung
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the gotu kola leaves and sauté until they're wilted.
Add the shredded coconut, carrot, and beetroot to the pan and sauté until they're well combined.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Kirata Deviled Potatoes
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Mash the boiled potatoes in a bowl and add the sautéed garlic-ginger mixture, grated coconut, and salt.
Mix well to combine.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Sri Lankan Pittu
instructions: Mix the rice flour, coconut milk, water, and salt in a bowl to form a smooth batter.
Heat a pittu maker or a steamer and brush it with ghee or oil.
Pour a small amount of the batter into the pittu maker and steam until it's cooked through.
Serve hot with a side of coconut sambal or other accompaniments.

title: Sarson Ka Saag
instructions: Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin, coriander, garam masala, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add onion and garlic, and sauté until onion is translucent.
Add chopped greens and cook until they are wilted.
Blend the mixture in a blender until smooth.
Return the mixture to the pan and add heavy cream.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes or until the saag thickens.

title: Murgh Makhani
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin, coriander, garam masala, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add onion and garlic, and sauté until onion is translucent.
Add chicken and cook until it is browned on all sides.
Add tomatoes, heavy cream, and tomato puree, and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin, coriander, garam masala, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add onion and garlic, and sauté until onion is translucent.
Add tomatoes, tomato puree, and water, and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Add soaked kidney beans and simmer for another 15-20 minutes or until the beans are tender.

title: Gujia
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 1 tablespoon hot water
instructions: Mix flour, ghee or oil, and sugar to make a dough.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of khoya or mawa, paneer, pistachios, and almonds in the center of the circle.
Fold the dough into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Fry the gujias in hot oil until golden brown.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and serve.

title: Punjabi Sarson Ka Achaar
ingredients: 1/2 cup mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add ginger and garlic, and sauté for another minute.
Add chopped mustard greens and cook until they are wilted.
Add vinegar, water, and cooked greens mixture to a saucepan.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the achaar thickens.

title: Gujarati Handvo
ingredients: 2 cups semolina, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup grated coconut, 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro, 1/4 cup chopped green chilies, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala powder, 1 teaspoon cumin seeds, Salt, to taste, 1 cup curd, 1 cup water
instructions: Soak semolina in water for 2 hours. Drain and mix with flour, coconut, cilantro, chilies, turmeric, red chili, garam masala, cumin seeds, and salt.
Add curd and mix well.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan and grease it with oil.
Pour the mixture and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Increase heat to medium and cook until the handvo is golden brown and firm.
Serve hot with chutney or sauce.

title: Khaman Dhokla
ingredients: 1 cup fermented dhokla batter, 1 cup water, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 teaspoon ginger paste, 1 teaspoon green chutney, 1 teaspoon mustard oil, Salt, to taste, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, 1 tablespoon grated ginger
instructions: Mix dhokla batter, water, lemon juice, ginger paste, green chutney, and salt in a bowl.
Grease a non-stick pan with oil and pour the mixture.
Steam for 15-20 minutes.
Mix mustard oil and chopped cilantro in a bowl.
Unmold the dhokla and cut it into small pieces.
Serve with mustard oil mixture and grated ginger.

title: Undhiyu
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as beans, eggplant, okra, and potato), 2 tablespoons oil, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon cumin seeds, 1 teaspoon mustard seeds, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 1 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, Salt, to taste, 2 tablespoons tamarind paste, 2 tablespoons date syrup
instructions: Heat oil in a non-stick pan and add garlic, cumin seeds, and mustard seeds.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until they are tender.
Mix coriander, cumin, turmeric, red chili, and salt in a bowl.
Add the spice mixture and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix tamarind paste and date syrup in a bowl.
Add the tamarind-date mixture and cook for 5 minutes.

title: Gujarati Dal
ingredients: 1 cup split red lentils, 2 cups water, 2 tablespoons ghee, 1 small onion, chopped, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 teaspoon cumin seeds, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, Salt, to taste, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
instructions: Soak lentils in water for 2 hours. Drain and cook with 2 cups water.
Heat ghee in a non-stick pan and add onion and garlic.
Add cumin seeds and cook until fragrant.
Mix coriander, cumin, and salt in a bowl.
Add the spice mixture and cook for 2 minutes.
Add cooked lentils and mix well.

title: Dhokla
ingredients: 1 cup fermented dhokla batter, 1 cup water, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 teaspoon ginger paste, 1 teaspoon green chutney, Salt, to taste, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, 1 tablespoon grated ginger
instructions: Mix dhokla batter, water, lemon juice, ginger paste, green chutney, and salt in a bowl.
Grease a non-stick pan with oil and pour the mixture.
Steam for 15-20 minutes.
Mix chopped cilantro and grated ginger in a bowl.
Unmold the dhokla and cut it into small pieces.
Serve with cilantro-ginger mixture.

title: Sadya Thali
instructions: Cook basmati rice and set aside.
Heat ghee in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk, yogurt, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Simmer the mixture for 10 minutes.
Serve the mixture over basmati rice and garnish with curry leaves and coriander leaves.

title: Erissery
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add red beans and pumpkin. Cook until tender.
Add coconut milk, grated coconut, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Simmer the mixture for 10 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Idiyappam with Chicken Curry
ingredients: For Chicken Curry: 1 cup boneless chicken, cut into small pieces
instructions: Mix idiyappam flour, lukewarm water, grated coconut, coconut oil, and salt to form a dough.
Knead the dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add chicken and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk, water, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Simmer the mixture for 10 minutes.
Steam idiyappam and serve with chicken curry.

title: Pachadi
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add cucumber and cook until tender.
Add yogurt, grated coconut, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Simmer the mixture for 5 minutes.
Serve chilled.

title: Inji Curry
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and sauté cumin seeds.
Add grated ginger and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk, grated coconut, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Simmer the mixture for 5 minutes.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Sadam (Steaming Hot Tamil Nadu Style Rice)
instructions: Heat 2 cups of water in a large vessel and bring to a boil.
Add 1 tsp of ghee and salt to taste.
Add 1 tsp of cumin seeds for flavor.
Add the rinsed basmati rice and cook until the water is absorbed.
Serve hot.

title: Kootu (Mixed Vegetable Curry)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, beans, and potatoes)
2 cups cooked and mashed toor dal
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
Add garlic and onion and sauté until onion is translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and sauté until they are tender.
Add toor dal, coconut milk, turmeric powder, and red chili powder.
Simmer until the flavors are well combined.

title: Pongal (Sweet and Savory Rice Pudding)
instructions: Heat ghee in a large vessel and add cumin seeds.
Add raw rice and split red gram and sauté until they are lightly browned.
Add milk, water, salt, jaggery powder, and cardamom powder.
Simmer until the rice and dal are cooked and the mixture thickens.
Serve hot.

title: Paruppu Vadai (Lentil Fritters)
instructions: Soak toor dal in water for 2 hours.
Grind the soaked dal with rice flour, cumin seeds, asafoetida powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder.
Shape the mixture into small patties.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the patties until they are golden brown.
Serve hot.

title: Sambar (Lentil-based Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, beans, and potatoes)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin seeds and coriander seeds.
Add mixed vegetables and sauté until they are tender.
Add toor dal, tamarind paste, water, turmeric powder, and red chili powder.
Simmer until the flavors are well combined.
Serve with rice.

title: Chicken Rezala
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic and cook for another minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add spices, salt, vinegar, and yogurt. Mix well.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve.

title: Beguni (Eggplant Fritters)
instructions: Mix together gram flour, spices, and baking soda.
Add lemon juice and mix well.
Dip eggplant slices in the mixture and coat evenly.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the eggplant slices until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Mishti Doi (Sweet Yogurt)
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Mix together yogurt, sugar, milk powder, cardamom powder, and saffron.
Heat ghee in a pan over low heat.
Add the yogurt mixture and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Chill in the refrigerator before serving.
Garnish with crushed cardamom and serve.

title: Kosha Mangsho (Bengali-Style Lamb Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic and cook for another minute.
Add lamb and cook until browned on all sides.
Add spices, salt, and yogurt. Mix well.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes or until the lamb is tender.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve.

title: Shukto (Mixed Vegetable Dish)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as eggplant, pumpkin, and plantain)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic and cook for another minute.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add spices and salt. Mix well.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the flavors have melded together.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve.

title: Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until they start to brown.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they are browned.
Add ginger paste, garlic paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, and garam masala powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and slit green chilies. Cook until the tomatoes are soft.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot over basmati rice.

title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 1 cup paneer (Indian cheese), cut into small cubes
instructions: In a blender, puree spinach leaves, garlic, and onion until smooth.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add cumin powder, coriander powder, and garam masala powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach puree and cook until it thickens.
Add paneer cubes and cook until they are coated in the spinach sauce.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot over basmati rice or with naan bread.

title: Biryani
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until they are lightly browned.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they are browned.
Add ginger paste, garlic paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, and garam masala powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and slit green chilies. Cook until the tomatoes are soft.
Add basmati rice and mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a large pot and cook over low heat until the rice is cooked.

title: Seekh Kebabs
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together ground meat, chopped onions, garlic, cumin powder, coriander powder, and garam masala powder.
Season with salt to taste.
Thread the mixture onto the bamboo skewers.
Grill the skewers over medium heat until they are cooked through.
Serve hot with chutney or raita.

title: Gulab Jamun
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together milk powder, flour, salt, and baking soda.
Add lukewarm milk and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until it is smooth and pliable.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Crumble the dough into small balls and fry until they are golden brown.
Drain the fried dough on paper towels.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and serve hot.

title: Bengali Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 pound fresh fish (such as bhetki or pomfret), cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they are lightly browned.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add fish and cook until it is coated with the spice mixture.
Add yogurt, cilantro, mustard paste, poppy seeds paste, and ghee or oil.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Shukto (Mixed Vegetable Dish)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add ghee or oil and let it melt.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add bitter gourd, drumstick, brinjal, and plantain.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the vegetables are cooked through.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Khichuri (Lentil and Rice Dish)
ingredients: 1 cup split red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add ghee or oil and let it melt.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice and lentils and stir well.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until the rice and lentils are cooked through.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Mishti Doi (Sweet Yogurt)
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 1 tablespoon hot water
instructions: In a pan, combine sugar and water over medium heat.
Cook until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat and let it cool.
Add yogurt, cardamom powder, and saffron to a bowl.
Pour the sugar syrup over the yogurt mixture.
Mix well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Garnish with pistachios and serve chilled.

title: Bengali-Style Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they are lightly browned.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until it is coated with the spice mixture.
Add yogurt, cilantro, mustard paste, and ghee or oil.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Lamprais
ingredients: 1 pound beef or lamb, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add beef or lamb, cook until browned.
Add curry powder, cumin, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, stir well.
Add rice to the pan, stir well.
Add water to the pan, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and cook until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice mixture with a fork.
Transfer the rice mixture to a serving dish.
Arrange sliced eggs on top of the rice mixture.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and mint.

title: Kottu Roti
ingredients: 2 cups roti bread, torn into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add torn roti bread, cook until crispy and golden brown.
Add shredded cabbage, carrots, onions, and tomatoes, cook until vegetables are tender.
Add garlic, curry powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, stir well.
Make a well in the center of the pan, pour beaten eggs into the well.
Scramble the eggs until cooked through.
Mix the eggs with the vegetable mixture.
Transfer the mixture to a serving dish.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Dhal Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add curry powder, cumin, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, stir well.
Add lentils to the pan, stir well.
Add water to the pan, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and cook until lentils are cooked and liquid is absorbed.
Stir the curry occasionally to prevent burning.
Transfer the curry to a serving dish.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.

title: Pittu
instructions: Mix coconut milk, rice flour, water, and salt in a bowl until a smooth batter forms.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Pour the batter into a pittu mold or a metal colander with small holes.
Steam the pittu for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked through.
Transfer the pittu to a serving dish.
Garnish with grated coconut and chopped cilantro.

title: Hoppers (Appam)
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, water, salt, and baking powder in a bowl until a smooth batter forms.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Pour the batter into a hopper mold or a non-stick pan greased with oil.
Cook the hopper for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges start to curl.
Loosen the hopper with a spatula, flip it over, and cook for another minute.
Transfer the hopper to a serving dish.
Garnish with grated coconut and chopped cilantro.

title: Sarson Ka Saag with Makki di Roti
instructions: Heat ghee or oil in a pan and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped greens and sauté until wilted.
Add water and buttermilk, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the greens are cooked and the mixture thickens.
Make makki di roti by mixing makki di atta with water to form a dough, and then rolling it out into small balls and flattening them into thin rotis.
Heat ghee or oil in a pan and cook the rotis until they are golden brown and puffed up.

title: Chole (Spicy Chickpea Curry)
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add tomato puree and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the chickpeas are cooked and the mixture thickens.
Add lemon juice and season with salt.

title: Saag Aloo (Spinach and Potato Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add potatoes and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add spinach and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the potatoes are cooked and the mixture thickens.

title: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into small pieces
instructions: Mix together yogurt, lemon juice, ghee or oil, garam masala, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add chicken to the marinade and mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook until it is cooked through and slightly charred.

title: Gobhi Aloo (Cauliflower and Potato Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add cauliflower and potatoes, and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the cauliflower and potatoes are cooked and the mixture thickens.

title: Gujarati-Style Undhiyu
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables, such as eggplant, okra, and potatoes
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon ghee in a pan over medium heat.
Add ginger paste, garlic paste, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder. Saute for 1 minute.
Add mixed vegetables, coconut, peanuts, and sesame seeds. Mix well.
Add salt, lemon juice, and remaining ghee. Mix well and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Dhokla
ingredients: 1 cup split chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: In a bowl, mix chickpeas, yogurt, water, Eno fruit salt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder.
Stir well and cook in a steamer for 15-20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Cut into squares and serve with lemon juice and cilantro.

title: Handvo
ingredients: 1 cup split chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: In a bowl, mix chickpeas, carrots, zucchini, coconut, cilantro, sesame seeds, peanuts, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder.
Add salt and lemon juice. Mix well.
Pour into a greased mold and steam for 20-25 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with chutney or raita.

title: Khakhra
instructions: In a bowl, mix whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, salt, baking powder, cumin, and coriander.
Add ghee or oil and mix well.
Gradually add water and knead into a soft dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll out into thin sheets and cook in a non-stick pan or griddle until crispy.

title: Gujarati-Style Undhiyu Farsaan
ingredients: Filling ingredients (such as dates, figs, and nuts)
instructions: In a bowl, mix gram flour, water, salt, baking soda, cumin, and coriander.
Add ghee or oil and mix well.
Gradually add water and knead into a soft dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll out into thin sheets and fill with desired filling ingredients.

title: Sadya-Style Pulissery
instructions: Grind the grated coconut, rice flour, turmeric powder, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds, and cayenne pepper into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the ground paste, cook until the mixture turns golden brown.
Add the thick coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and add the thin coconut milk, stir well.
Season with salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steaming rice.

title: Kerala-Style Fish Fry
instructions: Marinate the fish pieces in a mixture of gram flour, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and add the marinated fish pieces, cook until golden brown.
Add lemon juice and ghee, stir well.
Serve hot with steaming rice.

title: Kerala-Style Vegetable Stew
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrots, potatoes, green beans, and peas)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds and coriander seeds, let them sizzle.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk, grated coconut, turmeric powder, and red chili powder, stir well.
Season with salt and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve hot with steaming rice.

title: Kerala-Style Appam
instructions: Mix rice flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in a bowl.
Add coconut milk and mix until a smooth batter is formed.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan and pour a ladle of the batter, spread it evenly.
Cook until the appam is golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with steaming rice and curry.

title: Kerala-Style Parippu
instructions: Rinse the split red lentils and soak them in water for 30 minutes.
Drain the water and cook the lentils in 2 cups of water until tender.
Add turmeric powder and cumin seeds, stir well.
Season with salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steaming rice and curry.

title: Sambhar
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin and coriander seeds.
Add chopped onion and sauté until it turns golden brown.
Add garlic and sauté for a minute.
Add mixed lentils, water, turmeric powder, sambar powder, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the lentils are cooked.

title: Paruppu Rasam
instructions: Heat cumin and coriander seeds in a pan.
Add chopped onion and sauté until it turns golden brown.
Add garlic and sauté for a minute.
Add split red gram, water, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the gram is cooked.

title: Kootu
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin and coriander seeds.
Add chopped onion and sauté until it turns golden brown.
Add garlic and sauté for a minute.
Add mixed vegetables, water, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the vegetables are cooked.

title: Idiyappam with Coconut Milk Sauce
instructions: Mix idiyappam flour and water to form a dough. Knead for 5 minutes.
Steam the dough for 10 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pan and add coconut milk. Bring to a boil.
Add cardamom powder and salt. Simmer for 2 minutes.

title: Pongal
instructions: Heat cumin and coriander seeds in a pan.
Add chopped onion and sauté until it turns golden brown.
Add garlic and sauté for a minute.
Add raw rice, split red gram, water, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the rice and gram are cooked.

title: Bengali Fish Curry
ingredients: 500g fish pieces (mackerel or any white fish), boneless and skinless
instructions: Marinate fish pieces in a mixture of 1 tablespoon mustard oil, 1 tablespoon mustard paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons mustard oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let it crackle.
Add onions and sauté until they turn translucent.
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala powder, and cayenne pepper. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add marinated fish pieces and cook until they are 3/4 done.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they are mushy.
Add 2 cups of water and bring the curry to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with steaming hot rice.

title: Bengali Rasgulla
instructions: Boil milk in a large pan and add sugar, cardamom powder, and baking soda. Boil until the milk thickens and forms a smooth, creamy paste.
Add lemon juice and stir well. The milk will curdle and separate into curds and whey.
Line a strainer with cheesecloth or a clean muslin cloth. Place the curds in the strainer and let the excess water drain.
Once the curds have cooled, knead them well and mix in the crumbled paneer.
Divide the mixture into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat ghee or oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Fry the rasgullas until they are golden brown.
Soak the fried rasgullas in a sugar syrup made by dissolving sugar in water for at least 30 minutes.

title: Bengali Jhol Muri
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard paste and let it crackle.
Add onions and sauté until they turn translucent.
Add tomatoes and sauté until they are mushy.
Add chopped cilantro, green chilies, cumin powder, and coriander powder. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add puffed rice and salt to taste. Mix well.
Add lemon juice and mix well.
Garnish with sliced eggs or chicken, if using. Serve immediately.

title: Bengali Luchi
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Add ghee or oil and mix well.
Gradually add lukewarm water and knead the dough for 5-7 minutes or until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat ghee or oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Fry the luchis until they are golden brown.

title: Bengali Kosha Mangsho
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let it crackle.
Add onions and sauté until they turn translucent.
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala powder, and cayenne pepper. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add lamb or mutton pieces and cook until they are 3/4 done.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they are mushy.
Add 2 cups of water and bring the curry to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the meat is tender.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with steaming hot rice.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Cook spaghetti in boiling salted water until al dente.
In a skillet, cook pancetta over medium heat until crispy.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and Parmesan cheese.
Add cooked spaghetti to the bowl and toss with egg mixture.
Add pancetta to the bowl and toss until combined.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with parsley.

title: Chicken Parmesan
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt, oregano, and basil.
Dredge chicken in flour, then in breadcrumbs.
Heat a skillet with oil over medium heat.
Fry chicken breasts until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer chicken to a baking dish.
