Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and set.

title: Mujaddara
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Rinse the lentils and soak them in water for 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley.

title: Shawarma
ingredients: 1 pound thinly sliced lamb or beef
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the oil, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add the sliced meat and mix to coat.
Grill or broil the meat for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Warm the pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating in the oven for 5 minutes.
Assemble the shawarma by slicing the meat and serving it in the pita breads with tahini sauce.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 1 cup pita bread, toasted and cubed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, feta cheese, parsley, mint, and pita bread.
In a small bowl, whisk together the oil and lemon juice.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to coat.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Kunafeh
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large bowl, combine the phyllo dough, ricotta cheese, confectioners' sugar, and melted butter. Mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
Sprinkle with pistachios and rose water. Serve warm.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 cups mixed vegetables (such as carrots, zucchini, and bell peppers)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onions and bell peppers, cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper, cook for 1 minute.
Add cherry tomatoes, cook for 5 minutes.
Make 4 wells in the vegetables, crack an egg into each well.
Cook until the whites are set, about 5-7 minutes.

title: Kubbeh (Bulgur and Meatballs)
ingredients: 1 cup fine bulgur, rinsed and drained
instructions: In a large bowl, combine bulgur, beef, onion, garlic, egg, parsley, mint, salt, and black pepper, mix well.
Divide mixture into 8 portions, shape each portion into a ball.
Flatten each ball slightly into a disk.
Dredge disks in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat, cook until golden brown, about 4-5 minutes on each side.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Drain chickpeas, transfer to a blender.
Add garlic, lemon juice, tahini, and salt, blend until smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in olive oil and water.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

title: Sabich (Eggplant Omelette)
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
instructions: Dredge eggplant slices in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip in beaten egg, then coat in cornstarch mixture.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat, cook until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes on each side.
In a bowl, mix parsley, cilantro, Parmesan cheese, salt, and black pepper.
Place a cooked eggplant slice on a plate, top with a spoonful of the herb mixture.

title: Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice and Meat Casserole)
ingredients: 1 pound boneless lamb or beef, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add lamb or beef, cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic, cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add rice, water, parsley, mint, salt, and black pepper, stir to combine.
Transfer mixture to a large saucepan, cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed.

title: Masgouf
ingredients: 1 whole carp (about 2 pounds), scaled and cleaned
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Rinse the fish under cold water, pat dry with paper towels.
Mix together garlic, sumac, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Brush the fish with olive oil and sprinkle the spice mixture evenly.
Grill the fish for 10-12 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Kubbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur in water for 30 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Mix together ground meat, onion, parsley, mint, salt, and black pepper.
Add the meat mixture to the soaked bulgur and mix well.
Divide the mixture into small balls and flatten slightly.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the kubbeh until golden brown and crispy, about 5 minutes per side.

title: Gormeh Sabzi
ingredients: 1 pound lamb or beef, cut into small pieces
1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned.
Add the parsley, cilantro, dill, and dried lime.
Add the kidney beans and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.

title: Shawarma
ingredients: 1 pound thinly sliced lamb or beef
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned and cooked through.
Mix together garlic, sumac, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Brush the meat with the spice mixture and cook for an additional minute.
Warm the pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating in the oven.
Assemble the shawarma by placing the meat in the pita breads and topping with tzatziki sauce.

title: Machboos
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook until softened.
Add the cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper.
Add the rice and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.

title: Fesenjan (Chickpea and Pomegranate Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add broth, walnuts, cinnamon, cardamom, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in pomegranate molasses and butter.
Add chickpeas and cook for an additional 10 minutes.

title: Tahdig (Crispy Fried Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and drained
1 teaspoon ground saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
instructions: Rinse rice in a fine mesh strainer until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add rice and stir to coat with oil.
Add water, saffron, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until water is absorbed.
Increase heat to medium-high and cook, stirring constantly, until rice is crispy and golden brown.

title: Khoresh-e Bademjan (Eggplant Stew)
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Add eggplant and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add tomato puree, broth, tomato paste, olive oil, pomegranate molasses, cinnamon, turmeric, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.

title: Baklava (Nuts and Honey Pastry)
instructions: Thaw phyllo dough according to package instructions.
Layer phyllo dough in a large baking dish, brushing with melted butter.
Sprinkle nuts, sugar, flour, cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, and salt over phyllo dough.
Repeat layering phyllo dough and nuts until all ingredients are used.
Cut baklava into diamond shapes and bake at 350°F for 30-40 minutes.
Drizzle honey over baklava while still warm.

title: Kebabs (Grilled Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 10-12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Combine lamb or beef, onion, garlic, oil, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Mix well with hands until just combined.
Thread lamb or beef mixture onto skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired level of doneness.

title: Doner Kebab
instructions: Preheat a vertical spit or a grill to medium-high heat.
Thread the sliced beef onto skewers or onto the spit.
Cook the beef for 10-15 minutes, or until it's nicely charred and cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the sliced onions in olive oil until they're softened and lightly caramelized.
Mix the pomegranate molasses, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Brush the mixture onto the cooked beef and onions.
Warm the pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating them in the oven for a few minutes.
Assemble the kebabs by slicing the beef and onions and serving them in the pita breads with a dollop of yogurt, if desired.

title: Menemen
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper, and cook until they're softened.
Add the diced tomato and cook for a few minutes, until it's softened and lightly caramelized.
Make four wells in the egg mixture and crack an egg into each well.
Cook the eggs until they're set, then fold them over to create a scramble-like texture.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.

title: Lahmacun
instructions: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil and warm water, and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes, until it's smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on the size you prefer for your lahmacun.
Roll out each piece of dough into a thin circle.
Mix the minced lamb or beef, chopped onion, garlic, tomato paste, parsley, mint, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Spread a tablespoon or two of the meat mixture onto each dough circle, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the dough up over the filling to create a crust.
Bake the lahmacun in a preheated oven at 400°F (200°C) for 10-15 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Thaw the phyllo dough according to the package instructions.
Mix the chopped walnuts, granulated sugar, flour, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves in a small bowl.
Layer the phyllo dough in a 9x13-inch baking dish, brushing each layer with melted butter.
Sprinkle a layer of the walnut mixture onto the phyllo dough, followed by another layer of phyllo dough and butter.
Repeat the layering process until all the ingredients are used up, finishing with a layer of phyllo dough on top.
Bake the baklava for 45-50 minutes, or until the phyllo dough is golden brown and the filling is caramelized.
Drizzle the honey over the baklava and serve hot.

title: Kofte
instructions: Combine the minced lamb or beef, chopped onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, paprika, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a large bowl.
Mix the ingredients together with your hands until they're just combined.
Do not overmix the kofte mixture.
Shape the mixture into small patties or balls.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook the kofte for 4-5 minutes on each side, or until they're cooked through and lightly browned.
Serve the kofte hot with a side of rice and salad.

title: Kibbeh Bil Sanieh
instructions: Soak the bulgur in water for 10 minutes.
Drain the bulgur and mix with ground meat, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Form into small balls.
Dip each ball into the beaten egg and then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the kibbeh until golden brown.

title: Fatayer Bi Zait
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out the puff pastry and cut into squares.
Place a spoonful of spinach, cheese, parsley, and mint in the center of each square.
Brush the edges with water and fold the pastry to form a triangle.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Shawarma
ingredients: 1 pound thinly sliced lamb or beef
instructions: Marinate the meat in a mixture of olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, paprika, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Grill the meat until cooked through.
Warm the pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating in the oven for 5 minutes.
Assemble the shawarma by placing the meat in the pita bread and topping with tzatziki sauce.

title: Mujaddara
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and lentils and stir to combine.
Add 4 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes or until the rice and lentils are cooked.

title: Baklawa
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Layer the phyllo dough in a baking dish, brushing each layer with melted butter.
Sprinkle a layer of nuts and a layer of sugar mixture (flour, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt) on top of the phyllo.
Repeat the layers until all the ingredients are used up, finishing with a layer of phyllo on top.
Cut the baklawa into diamond shapes and bake for 45-50 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Shawarma Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips
Tzatziki sauce, for serving (store-bought or homemade)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, garlic, allspice, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the bowl and mix to coat.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, if using.
Bake the chicken for 20-25 minutes, or until cooked through.
Warm the pita breads by wrapping them in foil and heating in the oven for 5 minutes.
Assemble the shawarma by slicing the cooked chicken and serving it in the pita breads with tzatziki sauce.

title: Ma'amoul Cookies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, confectioners' sugar, and salt.
Add the softened butter and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and pliable.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin sheet.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal.
Brush the tops with the beaten egg and sprinkle with shredded coconut, if desired.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 1 cup toasted pita bread, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, toasted pita bread, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil and lemon juice.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Sprinkle the chopped parsley and mint over the top.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Kibbeh Balls
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground bulgur, parsley, mint, scallions, garlic, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Mix the ingredients together until just combined.
Add the beaten eggs and mix until the mixture comes together.
Knead the mixture for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and pliable.
Divide the mixture into small balls, about 1 1/2 inches in diameter.
Roll each ball between your hands to shape into a perfect sphere.
Dredge the kibbeh balls in flour to coat.

title: Gormeh Sabzi Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb or beef, cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the lamb or beef and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the dried parsley, fenugreek, and dill, and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the dried lime juice, beef broth, water, cinnamon, cumin, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

title: Chicken Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (3-4 lbs), cut into 8 pieces
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the chilies, garlic, almonds, raisins, cocoa powder, cinnamon, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Heat the lard or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a large Dutch oven or saucepan.
Add the chili puree to the skillet and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth to the skillet and bring to a boil.
Pour the chili mixture over the chicken and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the chicken is cooked through, about 25-30 minutes.
Stir in the crema and chocolate until melted.
Serve the chicken hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or in a preheated oven until charred and blistered.
Peel the peppers and cut a slit down one side to create a pocket.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Stuff each pepper with the onion mixture, queso fresco, cilantro, scallions, cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper.
In a shallow dish, beat the eggs and mix with the flour and milk.
Dip each stuffed pepper in the egg mixture, coating completely.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the peppers until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve the peppers hot, topped with the shredded queso fresco.

title: Enchiladas Rojas
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken or beef and cook until heated through.
In a separate pan, warm the tortillas over medium heat for about 30 seconds on each side.
To assemble the enchiladas, lay a tortilla flat and spoon some of the chicken mixture onto the center of the tortilla.
Roll the tortilla up and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas and chicken mixture.
Pour the enchilada sauce over the rolled tortillas and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F for about 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Sopes
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the masa harina and warm water until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until smooth and pliable.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces and shape into balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle, about 1/8 inch thick.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and cook the sopes for about 30 seconds on each side, or until lightly browned.
Top each sope with refried beans, cheese, cilantro, scallions, salt, and pepper.

title: Tamales
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together the masa harina and lard until a dough forms.
Gradually add the broth and mix until the dough is smooth and pliable.
Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces and shape into balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle, about 1/8 inch thick.
Place a tablespoon of the filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal the tamale.
Steam the tamales over boiling water for about 1-2 hours, or until the dough is tender and the filling is heated through.

title: Chicken Mole Enchiladas
ingredients: 1/4 cup mole paste, store-bought or homemade
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add chicken and cook until browned.
In a blender, combine mole paste, cilantro, garlic, cinnamon, cumin, ancho chili, and cayenne pepper. Blend until smooth.
Add chicken broth to blender and blend until well combined.
In a large saucepan, warm the mole mixture over medium heat.
Add heavy cream and stir to combine.
Dip each tortilla into the mole sauce and fill with shredded chicken.
Roll up and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour remaining mole sauce over the top and sprinkle with queso fresco.

title: Carne Asada Tacos
ingredients: 1 pound flank steak, sliced into thin strips
instructions: In a large zip-top plastic bag, combine lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Add steak to the marinade and seal the bag. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Remove steak from marinade and cook until browned.
Warm tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos by placing a few slices of steak onto a tortilla, then topping with cilantro, onion, and tomato.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 4 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
instructions: In a bowl, combine queso fresco, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Stuff each poblano pepper with the cheese mixture.
In a shallow dish, mix together flour and Parmesan cheese.
Dip each stuffed pepper into the flour mixture, then the egg, and finally the milk, coating completely.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry peppers until golden brown.
Drain peppers on paper towels and serve.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: In a bowl, combine masa harina and warm water. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes. Divide into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat lard or shortening in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry sopes until golden brown.
Top each sope with chorizo, refried beans, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Sprinkle with queso fresco and serve.

title: Tamales
instructions: In a bowl, combine masa harina and lard or shortening. Mix until a dough forms.
Gradually add chicken broth, mixing until the dough is pliable.
In a separate bowl, combine chicken, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Spread a thin layer of dough onto a corn husk, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Place a spoonful of the chicken mixture onto the center of the dough.
Fold the sides of the corn husk over the filling, then roll the tamale up and secure with a strip of corn husk.
Steam the tamales for 1-2 hours, or until the dough is tender.

title: Tacos al pastor
ingredients: 1 pound boneless pork shoulder, thinly sliced
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together orange juice, lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper.
Add the sliced pork to the marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove the pork from the marinade and cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.

Knead dough for 5 minutes and let rest for 30 minutes.
Heat lard or shortening in a skillet and cook Sopes until crispy.
Top Sopes with refried beans, queso fresco, onion, and cilantro.

title: Tamales
instructions: Mix masa harina and lard or shortening to form a dough.
Add broth to the dough and mix until smooth.
Spread a thin layer of dough on a tamale leaf.
Add shredded meat and fold tamale leaf to form a package.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame, or in the oven, until charred.
Peel the peppers and remove the seeds.
Stuff each pepper with the cheese, then coat with the beaten eggs.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the stuffed peppers until golden brown.
Serve hot.

title: Carne Asada Tacos
ingredients: Optional toppings: diced onions, cilantro, salsa, avocado
instructions: In a large ziplock bag, combine lime juice, garlic, and oregano.
Add the steak and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the steak to desired doneness.
Slice the steak thinly and serve with warm tortillas and desired toppings.

title: Chili Colorado
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank
instructions: Rehydrate the ancho and guajillo chilies in hot water, then chop.
Cook the beef in a large pot until tender.
Add the onion, garlic, cumin, and paprika to the pot and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the rehydrated chilies to the pot and cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: Make the dough by combining the masa harina and warm water, then knead in the lard or shortening.
Shape the dough into small patties.
Heat a skillet and cook the chorizo until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Top each patty with the cooked chorizo, refried beans, onion, and cilantro.

title: Tres Leches Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish and set aside.
Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the softened butter and eggs to the bowl and mix until just combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Poke holes all over the top of the cake with a skewer or fork.
Pour the evaporated milk, condensed milk, and heavy cream over the top of the cake.
Refrigerate the cake for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Mole Poblano
instructions: Roast the chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat, turning frequently, until fragrant.
Grind the chilies, almonds, and raisins in a spice grinder or blender until well combined.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the cinnamon, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the chicken broth to the skillet and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the chicken until cooked through.
Stir in the mole paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Serve the chicken in the sauce.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Stuff each pepper with the cheese mixture and secure with toothpicks.
Dip each pepper in the flour, then the egg, and finally the milk.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the peppers until golden brown and crispy.
Drain the peppers on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Enchiladas Rojas
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat.
Add the onion, cilantro, and jalapeno to the skillet and cook until the onion is softened.
Add the cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken or beef to the skillet and cook until heated through.
In a separate pan, warm the tortillas over medium heat.
Assemble the enchiladas by dipping each tortilla in the tomato sauce and filling with the meat mixture.
Roll the tortillas and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining tomato sauce over the enchiladas and top with cheese.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: Combine the masa harina and lard in a large bowl and stir until well combined.
Gradually add the warm water to the bowl and stir until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and divide into 8 equal pieces.
Shape each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the sopes until golden brown and crispy.
Top each sop with the onion, cilantro, cheese, and chorizo.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for garnish
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the pork to the pot and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the orange juice, lime juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the pork until tender.
Shred the pork with two forks and heat in the pot until crispy.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by spooning the pork onto a tortilla and garnishing with radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro.

title: Arroz a la Tumbada (Mixed Rice)
ingredients: 1 pound cooked shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add shrimp, pork, and chorizo; cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice and stir to combine.
Add beef broth, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 20 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro if desired.

title: Pescado Zarandeado (Grilled Fish with Spicy Mixture)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a blender or food processor, blend garlic, ginger, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Rub the mixture evenly onto both sides of the fish fillets.
Brush grill with oil to prevent sticking.
Grill the fish for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve hot and enjoy.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso (Stuffed Peppers with Cheese)
instructions: Roast the peppers over an open flame or in a 400°F oven until charred.
Peel the peppers and remove seeds.
In a bowl, combine queso fresco, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Stuff each pepper with the cheese mixture.
Dip the stuffed peppers in the beaten egg and then coat in flour.
Fry the peppers in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot and enjoy.

title: Sopes de Chorizo y Frijoles (Chorizo and Bean Sopes)
instructions: In a bowl, combine masa harina and warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and shape into balls.
Roll out each ball into a thin circle.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the sopes for 30 seconds on each side.
Top each sope with chorizo, beans, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Serve hot and enjoy.

title: Tacos de Carnitas (Braised Pork Tacos)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for garnish
instructions: In a large Dutch oven, heat lard or oil over medium heat.
Add pork and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add orange and lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Cover the pot and braise the pork for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender.
Shred the pork with two forks and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by spooning the pork onto a tortilla and garnishing with radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
2 dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 dried guajillo chili, stemmed and seeded
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add pork, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper. Cook until pork is browned.
Add ancho and guajillo chilies, cook for 2 minutes.
Add hominy and chicken broth, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Shred pork with two forks, serve with lime wedges, onion, and cilantro.

title: Sopes de Chorizo y Frijoles
instructions: Combine water, sugar, and yeast, let sit for 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt, and shortening, knead until dough forms.
Let dough rise for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Punch down dough, divide into 6-8 pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place on a baking sheet, bake for 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook chorizo in a pan until browned.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add pinto beans, cook for 2 minutes.
Top sopes with chorizo mixture and cilantro.

title: Tinga de Pollo
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into small pieces
1 medium chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, diced
instructions: In a large pan, heat oil over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add chicken, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook until chicken is browned.
Add chipotle pepper, cook for 1 minute.
Shred chicken with two forks, set aside.
Warm tortillas by wrapping in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos by spooning tinga onto a tortilla, topping with lettuce, tomatoes, and cilantro.

title: Sopa de Elote
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until onion is translucent.
Add corn, cook for 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and queso fresco, cook for 2 minutes.
Season with cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with cilantro.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until charred.
Peel off skin, cut a slit down one side to create a pocket.
Stuff each pepper with queso fresco mixture.
In a shallow dish, mix egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper.
Dip each stuffed pepper into egg mixture, coating completely.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry peppers until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Sopes de Chorizo y Frijoles
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Knead masa harina and melted lard until pliable.
Divide dough into 6-8 equal pieces.
Shape each piece into a disk, about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chorizo, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned.
Add onion, cilantro, lime juice, garlic, and cumin. Cook 1 minute.
Place a sopes disk in the skillet and top with chorizo mixture, beans, and a sprinkle of cheese.
Bake in the oven for 15-20 minutes, until crispy.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso
ingredients: 4 poblano chilies, roasted, peeled, and stemmed
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
In a bowl, combine cooked onion, queso fresco, and cilantro.
Stuff each poblano with the queso mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk together egg, flour, milk, and cumin.
Dip each stuffed poblano in the egg mixture, coating completely.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the coated poblanos until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add lard and cook pork, browning on all sides.
Add onion, garlic, cilantro, lime juice, tomato paste, and cumin. Cook 1 minute.
Transfer pork to a plate and cover with foil.
Simmer sauce over low heat for 10-15 minutes.
Shred pork with two forks and add back to the sauce.
Warm tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos with pork, a sprinkle of onion and cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Empanadas de Epazote y Queso
instructions: In a bowl, combine flour and salt.
Add melted lard and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until smooth.
Divide dough into 6-8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of queso fresco and a sprinkle of epazote in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling, forming a half-circle, and press edges to seal.
Brush tops with beaten egg and water mixture.

title: Chili Colorado con Carne Asada
ingredients: 2 pounds beef flank steak, sliced into thin strips
1 cup dried red chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add beef and cook, browning on all sides.
Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add onion and garlic to the pot and cook until onion is translucent.
Add chilies, beef broth, cumin, and oregano to the pot.
Simmer sauce over low heat for 10-15 minutes.
Add beef back to the pot and simmer for another 10-15 minutes.
Warm tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos with beef, a sprinkle of onion and cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Mole Negro
instructions: Toast the chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant.
Grind the chilies, almonds, and raisins in a spice grinder until smooth.
In a blender, combine the chili mixture, chocolate, flour, cinnamon, cumin, cayenne pepper, and salt. Blend until smooth.
Heat the lard or oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the chili mixture to the saucepan and cook, stirring constantly, until the mole thickens.
Stir in the cilantro and serve the mole over chicken or turkey.

title: Tlayudas
ingredients: 1/2 cup sliced cooked chicken or beef
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place the tortillas on a baking sheet and bake for 5-7 minutes, or until crispy.
Spread the refried beans over the tortillas.
Top the beans with the cheese, radishes, cilantro, epazote, chicken or beef, scallions, and onion.
Drizzle the tortillas with oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the tlayudas immediately.

title: Sopa de Tortilla
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tortilla pieces and cook, stirring constantly, until they are lightly toasted.
Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and cheese until melted and smooth.
Season with cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper to taste.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 1/2 cup sliced cooked chicken or beef
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until charred.
Peel the peppers and cut a slit down one side to create a pocket.
Stuff each pepper with the queso fresco, cilantro, epazote, and chicken or beef.
Dip each pepper in the beaten eggs and then coat in flour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers until golden brown.
Serve the chiles rellenos hot.

title: Tamales
instructions: Soak the corn husks in water for 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the masa harina and chicken broth. Mix until a dough forms.
Add the lard or oil and mix until the dough is smooth.
Spread a thin layer of dough onto the center of a corn husk.
Add a spoonful of the cheese, chicken or beef, cilantro, and epazote to the center of the dough.
Fold the sides of the corn husk over the filling and then roll the tamale up.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast and peel the poblano peppers.
In a blender, blend the crema, walnuts, pomegranate seeds, queso fresco, raisins, cinnamon, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Stuff each poblano pepper with the filling and place them in a baking dish.
Drizzle the tops with vegetable oil and sprinkle with cilantro.
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes or until the filling is heated through.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
2 cups mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the chilies and almonds in a dry skillet.
Blend the chilies, almonds, raisins, chocolate, cinnamon, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, and black pepper until smooth.
Heat the lard or oil in a saucepan and add the blended mixture.
Simmer the mixture for 10-15 minutes or until thickened.
Stir in the chicken broth and shredded chicken.
Serve over chicken or enchiladas.

title: Chili Colorado
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank
2 dried red ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 dried red guajillo chili, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak the dried chilies in hot water for 20 minutes.
Grind the chilies and garlic in a blender.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the chili-garlic mixture.
Add the beef and cook until browned.
Add the oregano, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the mixture for 10-15 minutes or until the beef is tender.
Stir in the beef broth and serve over rice.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: Chopped onion, cilantro, and lime wedges for garnish
instructions: Grill the pork shoulder and slice it into thin strips.
In a blender, blend the orange juice, lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Grill the pork in the marinade until coated.
Warm the tortillas on the grill.
Assemble the tacos with the pork, onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
ingredients: Refried beans, shredded cheese, and diced onion for garnish
instructions: Grill the chorizo and slice it into thin rounds.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the onion and garlic.
Add the chorizo and cook until browned.
Add the cilantro, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Warm the tortillas on the grill.
Assemble the sopes with the chorizo mixture, refried beans, shredded cheese, and diced onion.

title: Papadzules (Stuffed Tortillas with Hard-Boiled Eggs and Pumpkin Seed Sauce)
ingredients: 1/4 cup crumbled queso fresco (or feta cheese)
instructions: Soak the dried tortillas in water for 30 minutes.
Heat a dry griddle or comal over medium heat.
Cook the tortillas on both sides until they're slightly charred.
Spread a spoonful of pumpkin seed sauce on each tortilla.
Place a few slices of hard-boiled egg on top of the sauce.
Sprinkle with cilantro, cheese, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Fold the tortillas in half and serve.

title: Sopa de Limas (Lime Soup)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the lime juice, chicken broth, and heavy cream.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Chiles Rellenos (Stuffed Peppers)
ingredients: 4 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
1 cup queso fresco (or feta cheese), crumbled
instructions: Cut a slit in each pepper to create a pocket.
Stuff each pepper with cheese, cilantro, and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until softened.
Add the epazote and cook for 1 minute.
Add the stuffed peppers and cook until the cheese is melted.

title: Tikin Xic (Grilled Fish with Citrus and Spices)
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (such as snapper or tilapia)
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together the orange and lime juice.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika to the bowl.
Season the fish with salt and pepper.
Brush the fish with the citrus marinade.
Grill the fish for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Panuchos de Cochinita Pibil (Fried Tortillas with Slow-Cooked Pork)
ingredients: 1 pound slow-cooked pork (such as cochinita pibil)
1/4 cup crumbled queso fresco (or feta cheese)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the tortilla wedges and cook until crispy and golden.
Add the slow-cooked pork to the skillet and cook until heated through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with cilantro, cheese, and onion.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Stuff each pepper with cheese and roll in flour.
Dip in beaten eggs and coat in melted butter.
Pan-fry until golden and serve with bechamel sauce.

title: Beef Tacos (Tacos de Carne)
ingredients: Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for garnish
instructions: Sear beef in lard until browned.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add taco seasoning and simmer until beef is tender.
Serve in tortillas with desired toppings.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
ingredients: Shredded cheese, sour cream, and cilantro for toppings
instructions: Cook chorizo in lard until browned.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Place a spoonful of refried beans on each tortilla.
Top with chorizo mixture and desired toppings.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: Shredded cabbage, radishes, and lime wedges for garnish
instructions: Sear pork in lard until browned.
Add hominy, broth, chilies, garlic, and cumin.
Simmer until flavors are combined.
Serve with desired toppings.

title: Chilaquiles con Huevo
ingredients: Shredded cheese, sour cream, and cilantro for toppings
instructions: Fry tortillas in lard until crispy.
Add salsa and simmer until tortillas are coated.
Scramble eggs and serve over tortillas and sauce.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Stuff each pepper with queso fresco mixture and coat with egg wash.
Dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Serve with bechamel sauce.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Make masa dough and shape into thick disks.
Top each disk with chorizo, beans, cheese, and onion.
Bake until crispy and golden brown.

title: Enchiladas Rojas
instructions: Dip each tortilla in enchilada sauce.
Fill with chicken or beef and roll up.
Place seam-side down in baking dish.
Cover with more sauce and cheese.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1 pound boneless pork shoulder, thinly sliced
instructions: Marinate pork in orange and lime juice mixture.
Grill or cook in skillet until caramelized.
Warm tortillas by wrapping in foil and heating in oven.
Assemble tacos with pork, onion, cilantro, and pineapple.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Stuff each pepper with picadillo mixture.
Top with walnut sauce and pomegranate seeds.
Garnish with onion and cilantro.

title: Sopa de Tortilla
ingredients: 6 corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add tortilla strips, cook until crispy.
Add beef, broth, cumin, and paprika, stir to combine.
Simmer until heated through, season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Arroz a la Tumbada
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add rice, cook until lightly toasted.
Add water, shrimp, pork, tomatoes, broth, and oregano, stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add pork, cook until browned on all sides.
Add chilies, broth, tomatoes, and water, stir to combine.
Simmer until pork is tender, season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Stuff each pepper with cheese mixture.
Dip in flour, then beaten egg, then milk.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, season with salt and pepper.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat lard in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add pork, cook until browned on all sides.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Simmer until pork is tender, shred with two forks.
Warm tortillas, assemble tacos with pork, onion, and cilantro.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven.
Peel the skin off the peppers and cut a slit down one side to remove seeds.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of cheese, onion, and epazote.
Dip each stuffed pepper in the beaten egg and then coat with flour.
Fry the peppers in hot oil until golden brown.

title: Sopes de Chapulines
instructions: Mix together masa harina and warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls and flatten each ball into a disk.
Fry the disks in hot oil until crispy.
Top each sopes with a spoonful of refried beans, chopped onion, cilantro, and chapulines.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 dried ancho chilies, rehydrated and chopped
instructions: Saute the onion and garlic in oil until softened.
Add the chopped ancho chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Add the shredded pork, hominy, cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper.
Simmer the pozole for 30 minutes.
Serve the pozole hot with a squeeze of lime juice and a sprinkle of onion and cilantro.

title: Tacos de Carne Asada
ingredients: Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for serving
instructions: Marinate the flank steak in lime juice, garlic, oregano, and cumin for at least 30 minutes.
Grill the steak over medium-high heat until cooked to desired level of doneness.
Slice the steak into thin strips.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by placing a few slices of steak onto a tortilla and topping with radish, lime juice, and cilantro.

title: Tortas de Milanesa
ingredients: Lettuce, tomato, and mayonnaise for serving
instructions: Dredge the pork cutlets in flour, then dip in the beaten egg and finally coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry the pork cutlets in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Assemble the tortas by placing a few slices of pork onto a bolillo roll and topping with lettuce, tomato, and mayonnaise.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 4 large poblano chilies, roasted and peeled
instructions: Cut a slit in each poblano and remove seeds and membranes.
Stuff each poblano with queso fresco mixture.
Beat eggs and mix with milk.
Dip stuffed poblano in egg mixture and then coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry poblano in hot oil until golden brown.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: Mix masa harina and warm water to form dough.
Knead dough and divide into 6-8 pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Fry tortilla in hot oil until crispy.
Top tortilla with chorizo, cheese, onion, and cilantro.

title: Tacos de Carne Asada
ingredients: Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for garnish
instructions: Marinate steak in lime juice mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Grill steak until medium-rare.
Slice steak into thin strips.
Warm tortillas by wrapping in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos with steak, radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro.

title: Enchiladas Rojas
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet and fry tortillas until crispy.
Dip fried tortilla in enchilada sauce.
Roll tortilla and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Repeat with remaining tortillas and sauce.
Top with cheese, onion, and cilantro and bake until cheese is melted.

title: Chilaquiles con Huevo
instructions: Fry tortilla quarters in hot oil until crispy.
Soak fried tortilla in chicken broth.
Heat oil in a large skillet and fry onion, garlic, and cumin.
Add soaked tortilla to skillet and stir to combine.
Make a well in the center of the skillet and pour in eggs.

title: Tlayudas con Carnitas y Salsa Roja
ingredients: 6 tlayudas (crunchy tostadas made from corn tortillas)
1/2 cup salsa roja (red sauce made with dried arbol chilies, garlic, and oregano)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Warm tlayudas by placing them in the oven for 5-7 minutes.
Spread carnitas over tlayudas.
Top with salsa roja, onion, and cilantro.
Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Mole Negro con Pollo
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add mole negro, cumin, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.

title: Tamales de Elote
instructions: Soak corn husks in water for at least 30 minutes.
Grind corn kernels in a molcajete or blender until smooth.
Combine masa harina, broth, lard or shortening, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Add ground corn and mix until a dough forms.
Spread a thin layer of dough onto a corn husk, leaving a 1-inch border.
Add onion and cilantro on top of the dough.

title: Sopes de Chorizo y Frijoles
instructions: Combine masa harina and warm water in a large bowl.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth.
Heat lard or shortening in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add chorizo and cook until browned.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Top sopes with chorizo mixture, beans, and cilantro.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until charred.
Peel off skin and cut a slit down one side of each pepper.
Fill each pepper with cheese mixture.
Beat eggs and mix with milk and flour.
Dip cheese-filled peppers in egg mixture and coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry peppers in hot oil until golden brown.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast and peel the poblano peppers.
In a blender, puree the almonds, raisins, walnuts, and sesame seeds.
In a large skillet, heat the shortening over medium heat.
Add the pureed mixture to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the crema, queso fresco, cilantro, mint, parsley, pomegranate seeds, cinnamon, allspice, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Stuff each poblano pepper with the crema mixture and top with the pureed mixture.
Place the stuffed peppers in a baking dish and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 tablespoons ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
2 tablespoons mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
2 tablespoons pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the almonds, raisins, and sesame seeds to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the ancho, mulato, and pasilla chilies to the skillet and cook for 10 minutes.
In a blender, puree the chilies and spice mixture.
In a large saucepan, combine the pureed mixture, chicken broth, milk, cinnamon, allspice, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil and then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the crema and cilantro.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the pork to the Dutch oven and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the orange and lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and black pepper to the Dutch oven.
Cover the Dutch oven and transfer to the oven.
Bake at 300°F for 2 1/2 hours.
Shred the pork with two forks and warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by spooning the pork onto a tortilla and garnishing with cilantro, radishes, and lime wedges.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the masa harina and warm water.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and then cover with plastic wrap.
Heat the lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chorizo to the skillet and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the onion and cilantro to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and shape into disks.
Heat a dry griddle or skillet over medium heat and cook the disks for 30-45 seconds on each side.
Top each disk with a spoonful of the chorizo mixture, a sprinkle of queso fresco, and a dollop of crema.

title: Tamales de Elote
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the masa harina and warm water.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and then cover with plastic wrap.
In a blender, puree the corn kernels, queso fresco, cilantro, scallions, and epazote.
In a large saucepan, combine the pureed mixture, shortening, chicken broth, crema, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil and then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and shape into disks.
Place a spoonful of the corn mixture onto the center of each disk and fold the dough over to form a triangle.
Steam the tamales for 1 hour.

title: Papadzules
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the tortilla halves until crispy and golden.
In a bowl, mix together the pumpkin seeds, mayonnaise, and crema.
Assemble the papadzules by spreading the pumpkin seed mixture on a fried tortilla half, topping with an egg slice, and folding the tortilla in half.
Serve warm.

title: Sopa de lima (Lime Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the lard or oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Brown the pork pieces until crispy on all sides.
Add the onions and garlic and cook until the onions are translucent.
Pour in the broth and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the pork is tender.
Stir in the cilantro, lime juice, and cumin.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Poc Chuc
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, sliced into thin pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the orange and lime juice, garlic, cilantro, and onion.
Add the sliced pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry the marinated pork until crispy and golden.
Serve hot.

title: Panuchos de cochinita pibil
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, marinated in citrus juice and spices
instructions: Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Grill or pan-fry the marinated pork until crispy and golden.
Split the tortillas in half and fry until crispy.
Assemble the panuchos by topping a fried tortilla half with a slice of pork, pickled onion, cilantro, sour cream, and mayonnaise.

title: Tres leches cake (Pastel de tres leches)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add the softened butter and mix until a dough forms.
Beat in the eggs and vanilla extract.
Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
Poke holes all over the top of the cake with a skewer.
Pour the evaporated milk, heavy cream, and condensed milk over the top of the cake.
Let the cake sit at room temperature for 30 minutes to allow the milk to absorb.
Serve chilled.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat the lard or oil over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and jalapeno and cook for 1 minute.
Add the pork and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the hominy, cumin, oregano, cayenne pepper, and salt. Stir to combine.
Add the beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2 hours.
Shred the pork with two forks and add back to the pot.
Serve the pozole hot, topped with shredded cabbage, radish, and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until charred.
Peel the peppers and cut a slit down one side to remove the seeds.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of queso fresco, cheese, onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Dip each stuffed pepper in the beaten egg and then coat in flour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the peppers until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve the chiles rellenos hot, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.

title: Sopes de Chorizo
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, combine the masa harina and warm water. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until pliable.
Divide the dough into 6-8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk.
Heat the lard or shortening in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chorizo and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through.
Top each sopa with a spoonful of the chorizo mixture, some onion, garlic, and cilantro, and a sprinkle of queso fresco.

title: Tacos de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and cilantro for garnish
instructions: In a large Dutch oven, heat the lard or oil over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the orange and lime juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Cover the pot and simmer the pork for 2-3 hours, or until tender and easily shredded.
Shred the pork with two forks and fry in the pot until crispy.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by spooning the carnitas onto a tortilla and garnishing with radishes, lime, and cilantro.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until charred.
Peel the peppers and cut a slit down one side to remove the seeds.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of onion, cilantro, garlic, walnuts, pecans, raisins, parsley, mint, and queso fresco.
Drizzle the honey over the filling and sprinkle with additional cilantro.
Serve the chiles en nogada hot, garnished with additional parsley and mint if desired.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
2 pounds beef brisket or shank, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then set aside.
Add more oil if necessary and cook the sausage until browned.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the soaked and drained black beans, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Add the browned beef and sausage, then add enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Serve with rice, farofa, and sliced oranges.

title: Churrasco
ingredients: 1 pound flank steak or skirt steak
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together oil, garlic, lime juice, cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper.
Rub the mixture on both sides of the steak.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Thread the steak onto the skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill the skewers for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired doneness.
Let rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Aji de Gallina
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine aji amarillo pepper paste and heavy cream.
Blend until smooth.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add the shredded chicken and cook until heated through.
Stir in the aji amarillo cream and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the chicken mixture over boiled potatoes and hard-boiled eggs.
Garnish with Parmesan cheese and cilantro.

title: Ceviche Clásico
ingredients: 1 pound raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 pound raw fish (such as halibut or sea bass), cut into small pieces
instructions: In a large bowl, combine shrimp and fish.
Pour in the lime juice and let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Stir in the chopped onion, cilantro, and garlic.
Add the diced mango and stir gently.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.

title: Choclo con Queso
ingredients: 1 cup grated queso fresco or feta cheese
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, combine the corn kernels, queso fresco, and cilantro.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Pour the butter mixture over the corn mixture and stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Feijoada (Brazilian Black Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
1 pound smoked sausage, such as linguiça, sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef, then remove and set aside.
Add the sausage and cook until browned, then remove and set aside.
Add the onions, garlic, and bell pepper, and cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add the cumin and oregano, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, beef, sausage, broth, and cachaça (if using).
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Churrasco-Style Grilled Skirt Steak (Uruguay)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds skirt steak, preferably flank steak
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat the grill to high heat.
Season the steak with salt, black pepper, and paprika.
Grill the steak for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired level of doneness.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve with chimichurri sauce spooned over the top.

title: Ceviche de Camarones (Peruvian Shrimp Ceviche)
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Cut the shrimp into small pieces and place in a large bowl.
Pour the lime juice over the shrimp and let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Add the onion, cilantro, and jalapeño to the bowl and stir to combine.
Stir in the avocado and season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.

title: Locro (Argentine Corn and Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and bell pepper, and cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add the cumin and paprika, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, corn, and broth, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth.
Stir in the heavy cream (if using) and season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Sopa de Ajiaco (Colombian Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces, such as thighs and legs
2 medium yuca roots, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons aji amarillo pepper paste (see note)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, cumin, and paprika, and cook until the onion is softened.
Add the chicken and cook until browned, then remove and set aside.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and yuca to the pot and cook until the vegetables are slightly tender.
Add the broth, chicken, and aji amarillo paste to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight
1 pound dried beef brisket or shank, soaked overnight
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove the browned beef and set aside.
Add the oil to the pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soaked black beans, beef broth, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the browned beef and smoked sausage, and cook for an additional 30 minutes.

title: Ceviche Clásico
ingredients: 1 pound raw white fish, such as halibut or sea bass
1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped
instructions: Cut the fish into small pieces and place in a bowl.
Pour the lime juice over the fish and mix well.
Add the onion, cilantro, and jalapeño to the bowl and mix well.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Just before serving, stir in the diced avocado.
Season with salt to taste.

title: Churrasco
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat a grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together the oil, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Brush the mixture onto both sides of the steak.
Grill the steak for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired level of doneness.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain.

title: Aji de Gallina
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a blender or food processor, blend the aji amarillo paste, Parmesan cheese, and garlic until smooth.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the blended mixture to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the heavy cream and stir to combine.
Add the shredded chicken to the skillet and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the chicken mixture over the cooked white rice.

title: Chimichurri
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a blender or food processor, blend the parsley, oregano, and garlic until well combined.
With the blender or food processor running, slowly pour in the red wine vinegar and olive oil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the chimichurri to a bowl and serve immediately, or store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound beef brisket or shank, cut into large pieces
2 pounds smoked sausage, such as linguiça or chorizo, sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
instructions: In a large pot, combine the soaked black beans and enough cold water to cover them by 2 inches. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour.
In a large Dutch oven, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove the beef from the pot and set it aside.
Add the sausage to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the cumin and oregano to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the browned beef and the black beans and their cooking liquid to the pot. Add the beef broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Season the feijoada with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Ceviche de Camarones
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the shrimp and lime juice. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until the shrimp are opaque and cooked through.
Just before serving, stir in the onion, cilantro, jalapeño, and garlic. Season the ceviche with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the ceviche in small glasses or bowls, garnished with diced avocado, tomato, and a lime wedge.

title: Churrasco
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
10-12 wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the lime juice, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Add the flank steak to the bowl and marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat. Thread the marinated steak onto the skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill the skewers for 5-7 minutes per side, or until the steak is cooked to your desired level of doneness.
Let the skewers rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Aji de Gallina
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
1/4 cup aji amarillo pepper puree (see note)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set it aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the skillet. Add the aji amarillo pepper puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the heavy cream to the skillet and bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the Parmesan cheese until melted. Season the sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Add the cooked chicken to the skillet and stir to coat with the sauce.
Serve the chicken over cooked white rice, garnished with a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese and a dollop of the aji amarillo sauce.

title: Chimichurri
instructions: In a food processor, combine the parsley, oregano, and garlic. Process until the mixture is well chopped.
With the processor running, slowly pour in the red wine vinegar and olive oil. Process until the mixture is well combined.
Season the chimichurri with salt and black pepper to taste.
Transfer the chimichurri to a serving bowl and serve with grilled meats, such as steak or chorizo.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound smoked pork neck or shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 pounds beef brisket or shank, cut into large pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Brown the pork and beef in batches in the oil, then set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté the onions and garlic until softened.
Add the soaked beans, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the browned meat, along with 4 cups of water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 2 hours, or until the beans are tender.
Serve with rice, farofa, and sliced oranges.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef strips (such as sirloin or ribeye)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the tomato and bell peppers, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef back in, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Serve with French fries, and top with a fried egg.

title: Churrasco
ingredients: 1 pound skirt steak or flank steak
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat a grill to high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together the garlic, oil, lemon juice, and oregano.
Rub the mixture on both sides of the steak, then season with salt and pepper.
Grill the steak for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired level.
Let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve with grilled onions and tomatoes.

title: Ceviche
ingredients: 1 pound raw white fish (such as halibut or snapper)
1 cup mixed citrus juice (such as lime, lemon, and orange)
instructions: Cut the fish into small pieces and place in a large bowl.
Add the onion, garlic, and tomato to the bowl with the fish.
Pour the citrus juice over the fish mixture, and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the fish to 'cook' in the acid.
Garnish with cilantro before serving.

title: Choclo con Carne
ingredients: 1 pound beef strips (such as sirloin or ribeye)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the beef and cook until browned, then set aside.
Add more oil if needed, then sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the corn kernels and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the beef broth, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the browned beef back in, and stir to combine.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro.

title: Feijoada (Brazilian Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound smoked pork neck or bacon, cut into large pieces
2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat.
Add the onions and garlic and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add the beef and pork and cook until browned.
Add the beans, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Add enough water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
Serve with rice, farofa, and sliced oranges.

title: Ceviche (Peruvian Raw Fish Salad)
ingredients: 1 pound raw white fish, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the fish, lime juice, onion, cilantro, garlic, and ají amarillo pepper.
Mix well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with crispy corn kernels and sweet potato.

title: Asado de Tira (Argentine Beef Short Ribs)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Season the short ribs with salt and pepper.
Grill the short ribs for 5 minutes per side, or until browned.
Transfer the short ribs to a large Dutch oven.
Add the oil, onions, and garlic and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add the wine, broth, tomato paste, and oregano.
Bring to a boil, then cover and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 2 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.

title: Chivito (Uruguayan Sandwich)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Grill the steak to desired doneness.
Assemble the sandwich with the steak, mayonnaise, ham, cheese, tomato, lettuce, and onion.
Serve immediately.

title: Locro (Andean Corn and Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
2 pounds beef or pork, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add the onions and garlic and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add the beef and cook until browned.
Add the corn, beans, broth, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour.
Serve with crusty bread and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
2 pounds smoked sausage, such as linguiça or chorizo, sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
instructions: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onions and cook until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the soaked black beans, beef broth, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the sliced smoked sausage and continue to simmer for another 30 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro.

title: Ceviche de Camarones
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped
instructions: Combine the shrimp and lime juice in a bowl.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the shrimp to 'cook' in the lime juice.
Just before serving, stir in the chopped onion, cilantro, and jalapeño.
Fold in the diced avocado.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

title: Chimichurri
instructions: Combine the parsley, oregano, and garlic in a bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar and olive oil.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the herb mixture and stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

title: Pisco Sour
