instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add mixed vegetables and cooked chicken. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan. Add a little more oil if needed.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side of the pan and scramble them.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables and cooked rice.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and kecap manis. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with chopped scallions (if using).

title: Thai-Style Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 pound fish (e.g. cod, tilapia), cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add garlic, ginger, and lemongrass paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add fish sauce, coconut milk, turmeric powder, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add the fish pieces and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a steamer basket.
Steam for 5-7 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Banh Xeo (Sizzling Pancake)
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, and water in a bowl. Stir to combine.
Add chopped mint and scallions. Mix well.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened.
Pour the rice flour mixture into the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add cooked pork, fish sauce, soy sauce, lime juice, and sugar. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Use a spatula to lift and fold the edges of the pancake towards the center.
Cook for another 2-3 minutes or until the pancake is crispy and golden brown.

title: Singaporean Chili Crab
ingredients: 1 whole crab (about 1 pound), cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large pan over high heat.
Add garlic, ginger paste, and chili paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Add crab pieces and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add tomato paste, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), sugar, and white pepper. Stir to combine.
Mix cornstarch and water in a small bowl. Add to the wok and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Pho
ingredients: 1 pound beef brisket or chuck, sliced
1/4 cup chopped fresh herbs (such as basil, mint, and cilantro)
instructions: In a large stockpot, combine beef bones, ginger, garlic, and onion.
Pour in beef broth and water, and add fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cinnamon, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1-2 hours.
Add sliced beef and cook for an additional 30 minutes.
Strain broth and discard solids.
Serve hot, garnished with herbs, bean sprouts, and lime wedges.

title: Filipino Adobo
ingredients: 1 pound pork or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and onion and cook until fragrant.
Add pork or chicken and cook until browned.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, fish sauce, bay leaf, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and corn)
1 cup cooked chicken or beef, diced
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add cooked chicken or beef and stir to combine.
Push vegetables to one side of the pan.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble until cooked.
Mix eggs with vegetables and add cooked rice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and kecap manis.
Stir-fry until combined and heated through.

title: Malaysian Satay
ingredients: 1 pound chicken or beef, cut into thin strips
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger.
Add chicken or beef and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread marinated meat onto skewers.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.

title: Thai Khao Soi
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as cabbage, carrots, and bean sprouts)
2 cups boiled chicken or beef, sliced
2 cups braising liquid (such as beef broth or coconut milk)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and onion and cook until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add boiled noodles and stir to combine.
Add braising liquid, fish sauce, soy sauce, and lime juice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Add sliced chicken or beef and stir to combine.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Vietnamese Pho
ingredients: 1 pound beef brisket or chuck, sliced
instructions: Combine beef bones, ginger, garlic, onion, star anise, cinnamon sticks, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, and black pepper in a large stockpot.
Pour in beef broth and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding solids.
Bring the broth to a boil and cook for 10 minutes.
Cook the sliced beef in boiling water for 3-5 minutes, or until cooked to desired tenderness.
Assemble the pho by placing a portion of noodles in a bowl, followed by slices of beef, and ladling the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with cilantro, scallions, lime wedges, bean sprouts, and jalapenos.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and onion and cook until softened.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, fish sauce, bay leaf, and black pepper.
Pour in chicken broth and water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add potatoes, carrots, and green beans, and cook for an additional 20 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as peas, carrots, and corn)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan.
Add a little more oil to the other side of the pan, and pour in the beaten eggs.
Scramble the eggs until cooked through, then mix with the vegetables.
Add cooked rice to the pan, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Stir-fry the rice with the vegetables and eggs for about 5 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, rice vinegar, and black pepper.
Transfer the nasi goreng to a serving platter, garnished with green onions, cilantro, and lime wedges.

title: Malaysian Roti Canai
instructions: Combine flour, salt, sugar, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Add ghee or oil and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the roti for 1-2 minutes on each side, until golden brown and puffed.
Brush with ghee or oil and serve hot.

title: Singaporean Chili Crab
ingredients: 1 whole crab (about 1 pound), cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and onion and cook until softened.
Add ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add chili paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add crab pieces and cook until pink and cooked through.
Stir in tomato sauce and water, and bring to a boil.
Thicken the sauce with cornstarch and cook for 2 minutes.
Push the crab to one side of the wok, and scramble in the beaten eggs.
Mix the eggs with the crab and sauce, and cook for 1 minute.
Serve hot, garnished with green onions and cilantro.

title: Vietnamese Pho
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or chuck, sliced
instructions: Combine beef bones, ginger, garlic, onion, star anise, and cinnamon stick in a large stockpot.
Pour in beef broth and water, and bring to a boil.
Skim off any impurities, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook for 1 hour, then strain broth and discard solids.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cinnamon, cumin, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper to the broth.
Return broth to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Cook rice noodles according to package instructions.
Slice beef into thin strips and cook in a skillet until browned.
Assemble pho by placing noodles in a bowl, then adding beef and broth.
Garnish with cilantro, basil, bean sprouts, lime wedges, and jalapeños.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, then remove from skillet.
Add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until softened.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, fish sauce, black pepper, salt, and cayenne pepper to skillet.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Return chicken to skillet and add bay leaf.
Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in parsley and serve.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as carrots, peas, and corn)
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Push vegetables to one side of skillet.
Add a little more oil to other side of skillet, then pour in eggs.
Scramble eggs until cooked through, then mix with vegetables.
Add cooked chicken, soy sauce, oyster sauce, kecap manis, black pepper, salt, and cayenne pepper to skillet.
Stir-fry until combined, then stir in cooked rice.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with green onions, garlic, and cilantro.

title: Malaysian Roti Canai
instructions: Combine flour, ghee, lukewarm water, salt, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Divide dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until edges start to curl.
Flip and cook for another minute, or until golden brown.

title: Thai Green Curry with Shrimp
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (such as bell peppers, Thai basil, and bamboo shoots)
1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add green curry paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add shrimp and cook until pink and cooked through.
Stir in Thai basil, cilantro, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Serve with lime wedges, peanuts, and steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Banh Mi
instructions: Grill the pork until charred, then set aside.
Spread the mayonnaise and sriracha on the bottom half of the baguette.
Add the pickled carrots, cucumber, radish, and cilantro on top.
Place the grilled pork on top.
Drizzle with soy sauce and cover with the top half of the baguette.

title: Filipino Adobo Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until browned.
Add the vinegar, soy sauce, pepper, and salt.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., peas, carrots, corn)
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan.
Add a little more oil if necessary and scramble the eggs on the other side.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables.
Add the rice, soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using).

title: Malaysian Roti Canai
instructions: Combine the flour, ghee or oil, and salt in a bowl.
Gradually add the lukewarm water and knead the dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4-6 pieces, depending on desired size.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the roti until puffed and golden.

title: Thai Coconut Soup (Tom Kha)
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger and sauté until fragrant.
Add the curry paste and lemongrass and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk and chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add the mushrooms and simmer until tender.
Stir in the coconut cream, fish sauce, and lime juice.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 1 cup pandan leaves, tied in a knot
instructions: Rinse the rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In a large pot, combine the rice, coconut milk, pandan leaves, pandan sticks, salt, and water.
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the pandan leaves and pandan sticks. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve.

title: Roti Canai
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, and baking powder.
Gradually add the ghee or oil and mix until the dough comes together.
Add the lukewarm water and knead the dough for 10 minutes.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece into a thin circle. Cook in a hot skillet for 1-2 minutes on each side.

title: Ayam Masak Merah
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the coconut milk, chicken broth, tomato paste, soy sauce, sugar, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Kuih Talam
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, water, palm sugar, grated coconut, salt, and pandan extract.
Mix until the dough comes together. Knead for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a rectangle.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the kuih until golden brown on both sides.

title: Sambal Sotong
ingredients: 1 cup squid, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook until fragrant.
Add the squid and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the sambal oelek, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 1.5 kg, cut into 8 pieces
Chili sauce and sliced chili for garnish
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine mesh sieve until the water runs clear. Drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger paste and sauté until fragrant.
Add the chicken stock, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and pandan extract to the saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Add the rice to the saucepan and stir to combine. Cook for 18-20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and fluffy.
Meanwhile, marinate the chicken pieces in a mixture of soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and cornstarch for at least 30 minutes.
Poach the chicken in boiling water for 10-12 minutes or until cooked through.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry until browned on all sides.
Serve the chicken with the fragrant rice and chili sauce on the side.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked prawns and chicken. Stir-fry until combined.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil to the wok. Stir-fry for another minute.
Add the rice noodles to the wok and stir-fry until combined and heated through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Chili Crab
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger paste and sauté until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce, crab broth, chili sauce, soy sauce and sugar to the wok. Bring to a boil.
Add the crab to the wok and stir to combine. Cook for 5-7 minutes or until the crab is cooked through.
Mix the cornstarch with a little water and add to the wok. Stir to combine and cook for another minute.
Add the beaten eggs to the wok and stir to combine. Cook until the eggs are set.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with steamed rice and lime wedges on the side.

title: Kaya Toast
instructions: Combine the sugar, coconut milk, water and salt in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until the kaya thickens.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the butter until melted.
Add the beaten eggs to the saucepan and stir to combine.
Toast the bread until lightly browned.
Spread a layer of butter on each slice of toast, then a layer of kaya.
Serve immediately and enjoy.

title: Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 pound fish (mackerel or snapper), cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a blender, combine coconut milk, fish stock, fish sauce, ginger, lemongrass, garlic, turmeric, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth.
In a saucepan, combine blended mixture and palm sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add coconut cream and stir to combine.
Place a rice flour wrapper in a steamer basket. Spoon a small amount of fish mixture onto the center of the wrapper.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle and press the edges together to seal.
Repeat with remaining wrappers and filling.
Steam the amok for 10-12 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and the wrappers are tender.
Serve with steamed rice and garnished with cilantro and mint.

title: Bai Mon (Cambodian-Style Stir-Fried Eggplant)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add eggplant and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger. Cook until onion is translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add lemongrass, fish sauce, palm sugar, fish stock, turmeric, cumin, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in cilantro and mint.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Laotian Grilled Fish with Spicy Dipping Sauce (Pla Kaipen)
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (mackerel or tilapia), skin removed
instructions: Marinate the fish in a mixture of fish sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, and chilies for at least 30 minutes.
Grill the fish until cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix together cilantro, mint, palm sugar, and black pepper for the dipping sauce.
Serve the grilled fish with the spicy dipping sauce.

title: Laotian-Style Stuffed Chicken (Kaipen Khao Piak Sen)
instructions: Rice the sticky rice and mix with fish sauce, lime juice, garlic, and ginger.
Stuff each chicken breast with the rice mixture.
Secure the filling with toothpicks, if needed.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken until cooked through.

title: Laotian-Style Stir-Fried Vegetables (Pad Pak)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (bell peppers, carrots, broccoli, onions)
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry until tender.
Season with soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, and black pepper.

title: Laphet Thoke (Burmese Tea Leaf Salad)
instructions: Soak fermented tea leaves in hot water for 10 minutes.
Drain and chop tea leaves into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add peanuts, sesame seeds, and fried garlic, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Combine tea leaves, peanut mixture, soy sauce, sugar, and lime juice in a bowl.
Toss well and season with salt to taste.

title: Mohinga (Burmese Fisherman's Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound fish (such as catfish or tilapia), cut into small pieces
1 cup mixed vegetables (such as bean sprouts, carrots, and potatoes)
instructions: Mix rice flour and fish sauce in a bowl to form a thick paste.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add fish paste and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add fish broth and bring to a boil.
Add fish and vegetables, and cook until the fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and garnish with cilantro and egg slices.

title: Shan-Style Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast or thighs, cut into small pieces
1 cup mixed vegetables (such as bean sprouts, carrots, and potatoes)
instructions: Cook noodles according to package instructions.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through.
Add chicken broth, water, and mixed vegetables, and bring to a boil.
Add cooked noodles and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, fish sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.

title: Kyi Ye (Burmese Fried Rice)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as peas, carrots, and corn)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Push vegetables to one side of the pan and add a little more oil.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble until cooked through.
Combine eggs and vegetables, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add cooked rice and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.
Season with soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), salt, and pepper to taste.

title: Burmese-Style Grilled Chicken
instructions: Mix garlic, ginger, soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add chicken to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Let chicken marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and grill until cooked through.
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Bun Cha Ha Noi
ingredients: 1 cup fresh herbs, such as mint, basil, and cilantro
instructions: Grill the pork until charred and cooked through.
Soak the rice paper wrappers in water for 5 minutes.
Assemble the dish by placing a piece of pork, some herbs, and pickled carrots and daikon on a wrapper.
Fold the wrapper to enclose the filling and serve with nuoc cham sauce.

title: Pho Bo
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or chuck, sliced
instructions: Simmer the beef bones in a large pot for 1 hour.
Add the beef, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, star anise, and cinnamon to the pot.
Simmer for another 30 minutes or until the beef is tender.
Serve the pho hot with herbs, bean sprouts, and lime wedges on the side.

title: Goi Cuon
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Soak the spring roll wrappers in water for 5 minutes.
Assemble the spring rolls by placing a piece of pork, shrimp, cabbage, carrots, and herbs on a wrapper.
Fold the wrapper to enclose the filling and serve with nuoc cham sauce.

title: Banh Xeo
instructions: Mix the rice flour, coconut milk, and water to form a batter.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add the oil.
Pour the batter into the skillet and top with scallions, cilantro, shrimp, and pork.
Cook for 2-3 minutes or until the edges start to curl and the bottom is golden brown.

title: Com Tam
instructions: Cook the broken rice according to package instructions.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add the oil.
Add the onions and scallions to the skillet and cook until softened.
Add the pork, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and lime juice to the skillet and stir to combine.

title: Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaf, and black pepper. Stir well.
Simmer for 30 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.

title: Sinangag (Filipino Fried Rice)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., peas, carrots, green beans)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble until cooked. Then mix with vegetables.
Add cooked rice and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, breaking up any clumps with a spatula.

title: Lechon Kawali (Crispy Fried Pork Belly)
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, garlic, black pepper, and salt in a bowl. Add pork belly and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Remove pork from marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Fry pork until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.

title: Lumpia (Filipino Spring Rolls)
ingredients: 1 package spring roll wrappers (usually found in the frozen food section or at Asian grocery stores)
instructions: Combine cabbage, carrots, onions, chicken, and garlic in a bowl.
Dip a spring roll wrapper in water and place on a flat surface.
Place about 1 tablespoon of the cabbage mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Fold the bottom half of the wrapper over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll up the wrapper to form a tight cylinder.
Repeat with remaining wrappers and filling.

title: Tinola (Filipino Ginger Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add onion and ginger and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Add chicken broth and water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.

title: Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 2 cups cooked Indonesian fried rice, broken into small pieces
1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, peas, carrots)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Push the onion and garlic mixture to one side of the pan.
Add a little more oil if necessary, then pour in the beaten eggs.
Scramble the eggs until cooked through, breaking them up with a spatula as they cook.
Mix the eggs with the onion and garlic mixture.
Add the mixed vegetables, cooked Indonesian fried rice, soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Stir-fry everything together until well combined and heated through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with chopped scallions and fried shallots.

title: Gado-Gado
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots, cucumber)
1 cup tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed vegetables, cooked chickpeas, and tofu cubes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the peanut sauce, soy sauce, and lime juice.
Heat the oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour the peanut sauce mixture over the onion and garlic, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour the peanut sauce mixture over the mixed vegetables, and toss to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with chopped scallions.

title: Sate Ayam
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into small pieces
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, kecap manis, garlic, ginger, coriander powder, cumin powder, and turmeric powder.
Add the chicken pieces to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated chicken onto the bamboo skewers.
Brush the grill or grill pan with oil to prevent sticking.
Grill the sate for 5-7 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve hot with peanut sauce or kecap manis for dipping.

title: Bakwan Jagung
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the corn kernels, shredded cabbage, shredded carrots, flour, cornstarch, grated coconut, chopped scallions, and chopped cilantro.
Add the beaten eggs to the bowl and mix well to combine.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Using a spoon, drop the mixture into the hot oil and fry until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the bakwan on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Soto Betawi
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket or beef shank, cut into large pieces
instructions: In a large pot, combine the beef bones and beef pieces.
Add the beef broth, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the coconut milk to the pot and stir to combine.
Heat the oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and sliced ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the bean sprouts, shredded cabbage, and sliced rice noodles to the pot.
Stir to combine and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
Serve the soto hot, garnished with chopped scallions and fried shallots.

title: Nasi Lemak
instructions: Rinse the rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and pandan extract, bring to a boil.
Add rice and water, stir and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and cook until the rice is cooked.
Serve with fried anchovy, cucumber, peanuts and sambal sauce.

title: Ayam Percik
instructions: Grill the chicken until cooked.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, water, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder and chili powder.
Bring to a boil and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Serve the chicken with the sauce.

title: Roti Canai
instructions: Mix flour, ghee or oil, salt, sugar and yeast.
Gradually add lukewarm water and knead the dough until smooth.
Rest the dough for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll out into thin circles.
Heat a non-stick pan and cook the roti until golden brown.

title: Sambal Sotong
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add chilies and cook until they turn dark brown.
Add squid and cook until it turns opaque.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder and salt.
Stir well and add vinegar.

title: Kuih Lapis
instructions: Mix rice flour, corn flour, coconut milk, water, salt and sugar.
Heat oil in a pan and pour in the mixture.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown.
Beat eggs and add vanilla extract.
Pour the egg mixture over the rice mixture and cook until golden brown.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless chicken breast or thighs, skin removed
instructions: Poach the chicken in the warmed chicken stock for 30 minutes.
Prepare the rice by combining it with water, pandan leaves, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), sugar, salt, and black pepper in a saucepan.
Cook the rice over high heat until it boils, then reduce the heat to low and cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer the rice for 15-20 minutes, or until it is cooked and fluffy.
Serve the poached chicken with the fragrant rice and chili sauce (optional)

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
instructions: Heat the wok or large skillet over high heat and add the vegetable oil.
Stir-fry the onion and garlic until they are softened.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked prawns to the wok, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), sugar, salt, and black pepper to the wok, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Push the vegetables and prawns to one side of the wok, and add a little more oil to the other side.
Pour the beaten eggs into the wok, and scramble them until they are cooked through.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables and prawns, and stir-fry for another minute.
Serve the Char Kway Teow hot, garnished with chopped scallions.

title: Kaya Toast
instructions: Combine the coconut milk, sugar, eggs, and melted butter in a saucepan.
Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and turns a deep golden brown.
Toast the bread until it is lightly browned, then spread the softened butter on each slice.
Top each slice of bread with a spoonful of the kaya jam.
Serve the Kaya Toast hot, with fried or poached eggs on top (if desired)

title: Laksa
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
instructions: Heat the wok or large skillet over high heat and add the vegetable oil.
Stir-fry the onion, garlic, and ginger until they are softened.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked prawns to the wok, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the laksa broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), sugar, salt, and black pepper to the wok, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Push the vegetables and prawns to one side of the wok, and add a little more oil to the other side.
Pour the beaten eggs into the wok, and scramble them until they are cooked through.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables and prawns, and stir-fry for another minute.
Serve the Laksa hot, garnished with chopped scallions and a sprinkle of laksa paste (optional)

title: Roti Prata
ingredients: 1/2 cup ghee or vegetable oil, for brushing
instructions: Combine the flour, warm water, salt, sugar, and yeast in a bowl.
Knead the dough for 10-15 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on how large you want your roti to be.
Roll out each piece of dough into a thin circle.
Brush the roti with ghee or vegetable oil, and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side, until it is lightly browned and puffed up.
Serve the Roti Prata hot, with a variety of fillings such as chicken, beef, or vegetables.

title: Fish Amok
ingredients: 2 pounds fish fillets (such as snapper or tilapia), cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a blender or food processor, puree the coconut milk, fish sauce, ginger, garlic, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the fish and cook until opaque, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the coconut milk mixture and water to the saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a steamer basket and steam for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro.

title: Nom Banh Chok
ingredients: 2 cups fish balls or fish cakes, sliced
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package instructions.
In a blender or food processor, puree the coconut milk, oil, garlic, and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the fish balls and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts, cilantro, and mint to the saucepan.
Pour in the coconut milk mixture and stir to combine.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and pepper to the saucepan.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, then serve over the noodles.

title: Bai Mon
ingredients: 2 cups mixed greens (such as lettuce, spinach, and watercress)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, chicken, onion, cucumber, and carrots.
In a small bowl, whisk together the oil, garlic, fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
Serve immediately.

title: Nom Prahok
ingredients: 1 cup sliced fish balls or fish cakes
instructions: In a blender or food processor, puree the prahok and water.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the garlic and ginger to the saucepan and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the prahok mixture to the saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Serve the prahok mixture in banana leaves with the fish balls, bean sprouts, and cilantro.

title: Kuy Teav
instructions: In a large pot, combine the bones and broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1-2 hours.
Cook the noodles according to the package instructions.
In a blender or food processor, puree the oil, garlic, and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the beef or pork to the saucepan and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and cilantro to the saucepan.
Pour in the broth and stir to combine.
Serve the beef or pork over the noodles.

title: Laotian Grilled Fish with Spicy Dipping Sauce (Pla Kaipen)
ingredients: 4 fish fillets (such as catfish or tilapia), skin removed
instructions: Grill the fish fillets over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side.
In a blender, combine fish sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, cilantro, mint, chilies, palm sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Blend until smooth and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve the grilled fish with the spicy dipping sauce.

title: Sticky Rice with Coconut Milk and Palm Sugar (Khao Niew)
ingredients: 2 cups glutinous rice (also known as sticky rice)
instructions: Rinse the sticky rice and soak it in water for at least 4 hours.
Drain the rice and cook it in a steamer basket over boiling water for 15-20 minutes.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, palm sugar, water, and salt.
Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring until the palm sugar dissolves.
Add the cooked sticky rice to the coconut milk mixture and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Serve the sticky rice hot, topped with unsalted butter and chopped coconut flakes if desired.

title: Laotian-Style Fried Noodles (Khao Soi)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as bean sprouts, carrots, and green onions)
1 cup cooked chicken or pork, diced
instructions: Cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry until the onion is translucent.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked chicken or pork and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the cooked noodles, soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Stir-fry everything together for 2-3 minutes and serve hot.

title: Laotian-Style Grilled Pork Skewers (Mok Pa)
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for at least 30 minutes
instructions: In a blender, combine fish sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, cilantro, mint, chilies, palm sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Blend until smooth and adjust seasoning to taste.
Thread the pork cubes onto the bamboo skewers.
Grill the skewers over medium heat for 5-7 minutes per side, brushing with the marinade during the last minute of cooking.
Serve the grilled pork skewers hot with sticky rice or noodles.

title: Laotian-Style Vegetable Curry (Kaipen)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as eggplant, bell peppers, and carrots)
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry until the onion is translucent.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, curry paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Stir-fry everything together for 2-3 minutes and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve the vegetable curry hot with sticky rice or noodles.

title: Mohinga
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until fragrant.
Add fish balls; cook until browned.
Add fish stock, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cumin, coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook noodles according to package instructions.
Serve mohinga over noodles with fried shallots, eggs, and fish balls.

title: Laphet Thoke
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cumin, coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper; stir to combine.
Add pickled tea leaves, fried noodles, boiled peanuts, and chickpeas.
Stir-fry until well combined.
Transfer to a serving dish; garnish with cilantro and scallions.

title: Shan Style Fried Noodles
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic; sauté until fragrant.
Add boiled chicken and shrimp; cook until heated through.
Add mixed vegetables; stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cumin, coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Stir-fry until well combined.
Add fried noodles; stir-fry until coated with sauce.

title: Burmese Chicken Curry
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless chicken breast or thighs
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions, garlic, and ginger; sauté until fragrant.
Add chicken; cook until browned.
Add coconut milk, chicken broth, curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar; stir to combine.
Garnish with cilantro; serve over rice.

title: Kyay Oh
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., carrots, green beans, bell peppers)
instructions: Mix rice flour and water to form a dough; knead for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add boiled chicken or fish and mixed vegetables; stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cumin, coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Stir-fry until well combined.
Shape dough into small balls; flatten slightly.
Wrap each ball around a portion of the filling; serve hot.

title: Bun Bo Hue
ingredients: 1 pound beef bones, 1 pound beef brisket or chuck, sliced
2 tablespoons fish sauce, 2 tablespoons lime juice
2 teaspoons ground cumin, 1 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper
2 cups rice noodles, 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint leaves
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro leaves, 2 cups bean sprouts
instructions: Bring beef broth, water, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, cinnamon, cumin, and cayenne pepper to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add beef bones and brisket, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove beef bones and brisket, and slice into thin strips.
Cook rice noodles according to package instructions.
Assemble bowls with noodles, beef, herbs, and bean sprouts.

title: Goi Cuon
ingredients: 1 package spring roll wrappers, 1 pound ground pork
1/2 cup chopped shrimp, 1/2 cup chopped carrots
1/2 cup chopped cucumber, 1/4 cup chopped fresh mint leaves
2 tablespoons fish sauce, 2 tablespoons lime juice
instructions: Prepare ingredients and assemble spring roll wrappers with ground pork, shrimp, carrots, cucumber, mint, fish sauce, lime juice, honey, and scallions.
Dip fingers in water and wet edges of spring roll wrapper.
Roll up spring rolls tightly, and serve with peanut sauce.

title: Banh Xeo
ingredients: 1 cup rice flour, 1/2 cup water, 1/4 cup coconut milk
1/2 cup shredded coconut, 1/2 cup chopped shrimp
1/2 cup chopped pork, 1/4 cup chopped fresh scallions
2 tablespoons fish sauce, 2 tablespoons lime juice
instructions: Mix rice flour, water, and coconut milk to make batter.
Heat a non-stick skillet and add batter, tilting to form a round pancake.
Add shredded coconut, shrimp, pork, and scallions to the pancake.
Cook until the bottom is crispy, then flip and cook the other side.

title: Canh Chien Ga
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
1 cup fish sauce, 1 cup coconut milk
2 cups water, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1 tablespoon fish sauce
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet and sauté chicken until browned.
Add onion and garlic and stir-fry until onion is translucent.
Add fish sauce, coconut milk, water, sugar, and fish sauce, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through.

title: Com Tam
ingredients: 1/4 cup chopped fresh scallions, 2 tablespoons fish sauce
instructions: Cook broken rice according to package instructions.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar to make sauce.
Assemble bowls with broken rice, scallions, and sauce.

title: Adobo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add pork or chicken and cook until browned.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, patis, black pepper, and bay leaves.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 30 minutes or until the meat is tender.

title: Sinangag (Filipino Fried Rice)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g. peas, carrots, corn)
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until tender.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan.
Add more oil if necessary and scramble in the eggs.
Mix the eggs with the vegetables.
Add cooked rice and stir-fry until combined.

title: Lechon Kawali (Crispy Fried Pork Belly)
instructions: Boil pork belly in vinegar, water, garlic, black pepper, and salt until tender.
Let cool and refrigerate overnight.
Cut into large pieces and coat with flour.
Deep-fry until crispy and golden brown.

title: Lumpia (Filipino Spring Rolls)
instructions: Combine ground pork, cabbage, carrots, green onions, and garlic in a bowl.
Add soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using) and mix well.
Place a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Fold the bottom half of the wrapper over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll up.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Deep-fry until crispy and golden brown.

title: Tinola (Filipino Ginger Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and sauté until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Pour in chicken broth and water, then bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked.
Add patis and fish oil, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., peas, carrots, corn)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add mixed vegetables; stir-fry until tender.
Push vegetables to one side of the wok.
Add a little more oil to the empty side; pour in beaten eggs.
Scramble eggs until cooked through.
Mix eggs with vegetables.
Add cooked rice to the wok; stir-fry until combined with eggs and vegetables.
Season with soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using).

title: Gado-Gado
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (e.g., bean sprouts, cabbage, carrots)
1 cup cooked tofu, cut into small pieces
1/4 cup crispy fried shallots (store-bought or homemade)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine mixed vegetables, tofu, and boiled peanuts.
Add mixed greens on top.
Drizzle peanut sauce over the salad.
Top with sliced hard-boiled eggs and crispy fried shallots.

title: Sate Ayam
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, coriander powder, cumin powder, and cayenne pepper (if using); blend until smooth.
Thread chicken onto bamboo skewers.
Grill or broil skewers until cooked through.
Brush skewers with marinade during the last few minutes of cooking.

title: Martabak
ingredients: 1 cup diced vegetables (e.g., onions, cabbage, carrots)
1 cup diced cooked chicken or beef
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, warm water, salt, and sugar; mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth.
Divide dough into 2-3 equal pieces; roll out each piece into a thin circle.
Heat a non-stick pan or martabak pan over medium heat.
Add a little oil to the pan; cook martabak until crispy and golden brown.
Brush with beaten eggs; add diced vegetables and cooked meat on one half of the martabak.
Fold the other half over the filling; cook until the other side is crispy and golden brown.

title: Sop Buntut
ingredients: 2 pounds beef oxtail, cut into large pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add beef oxtail; cook until browned on all sides.
Add beef broth, water, soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), and sugar.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer until beef is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add water, fish stock, Tom Yum paste, fish sauce, and coconut milk.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until they are pink and cooked through.
Stir in lime juice and cilantro.
Serve hot.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 2 inches piece of fresh ginger, grated
1 pound beef or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup potatoes, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they are softened.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add curry paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef or chicken and cook until browned.
Add potatoes, broth, coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in cilantro and peanuts.
Serve hot.

title: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Heat oil in a large bowl over medium heat.
Add garlic and chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Add mixed vegetables and cook until they are slightly softened.
Add papaya and cook until it is slightly softened.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Stir in peanuts and cilantro.
Serve hot.

title: Satay
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat oil in a large bowl over medium heat.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken and cook until it is browned.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder, coconut milk, fish sauce, and lime juice.
Stir to combine.
Thread chicken onto bamboo skewers.
Grill or broil until chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Khao Soi
ingredients: 2 inches piece of fresh ginger, grated
1 pound beef or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until they are softened.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add curry paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef or chicken and cook until browned.
Add broth, coconut milk, and noodles.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in cilantro and peanuts.
Serve hot.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 cups mixed vegetables (bell peppers, Thai basil, chilies)
instructions: In a large pot, combine water, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and garlic.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add ginger, shrimp, Tom Yum paste, fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and Thai chili peppers.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes or until the shrimp are pink and cooked through.
Add mixed mushrooms and vegetables, and simmer for 2-3 minutes or until tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro leaves.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, carrots, green onions)
instructions: Cook rice noodles according to package instructions, then set aside.
In a large wok or frying pan, heat oil over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic, and stir-fry until the onion is translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and cooked shrimp, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.
Pour the sauce mixture over the vegetables and shrimp, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked noodles, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes or until the noodles are well coated with the sauce.
Sprinkle ground peanuts over the top, and serve hot with lime wedges and cilantro leaves.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 pound beef or chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, and stir-fry until the onion is translucent.
Add ginger and curry paste, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, beef or chicken, potatoes, peanuts, palm sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, and lime juice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes or until the meat and potatoes are cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro leaves.

title: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (tomatoes, long beans, chilies)
instructions: In a large mortar and pestle, combine papaya, ginger, garlic, palm sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and Thai chili peppers.
Pound the mixture until it is well combined and slightly crushed.
Add mixed vegetables and peanuts, and pound until the vegetables are slightly crushed.
Transfer the mixture to a serving bowl, and garnish with chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately, with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Satay
ingredients: 1 pound chicken or beef, cut into thin strips
20 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken or beef, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread marinated meat onto bamboo skewers, leaving a small space between each piece.
Grill for 5-7 minutes per side, or until the meat is cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped peanuts and cilantro leaves.

Add tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, soy sauce, and rice vinegar. Stir-fry for 1 minute.

title: Tom Yum Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.

title: Massaman Curry

title: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)

title: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)

instructions: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large saucepan.

instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.

2 cups mixed vegetables (such as tomatoes, chilies, and carrots)
instructions: In a large mortar and pestle, pound garlic and ginger until smooth.
Add palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice. Pound until well combined.
Add mixed vegetables and pound until slightly crushed.
Add papaya and pound until slightly crushed.

title: Pad Thai

instructions: Cook noodles according to package instructions.

title: Khao Soi

title: Tom Yum Soup
ingredients: 2 cups chicken broth, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, 4-6 mushrooms (button or cremini), sliced, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 tablespoon grated ginger, 2 cups mixed seafood (shrimp, mussels, clams), 2 tablespoons Tom Yum paste, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, 1 tablespoon lime juice, 1 tablespoon palm sugar, 2 kaffir lime leaves, 2-3 Thai chilies
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces, 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, 2-3 Thai basil leaves, chopped, Salt, to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add garlic, ginger, and Thai chilies; cook for 1 minute.
Add mixed seafood; cook until it turns opaque. Add chicken and cook until it's no longer pink.
Add Tom Yum paste, fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Add mushrooms and simmer for another 3-4 minutes or until they're tender.
Stir in cilantro and basil. Season with salt to taste. Serve hot.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 1 cup rice noodles, 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 1 onion, thinly sliced, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 cup mixed vegetables (bean sprouts, carrots, green onions), 1 cup cooked shrimp, 1 cup cooked chicken, 2 tablespoons tamarind paste, 2 tablespoons palm sugar, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon ground white pepper, Salt, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped peanuts, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, 2 tablespoons lime wedges
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 5-7 minutes or according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a large wok or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic; cook until onion is translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and cooked shrimp and chicken. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, palm sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Pour the mixture into the wok or frying pan and stir to combine.
Add cooked noodles and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes or until everything is well combined. Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with peanuts and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, 2 cloves garlic, minced, 1 tablespoon grated ginger, 2 tablespoons Massaman curry paste, 2 cups coconut milk, 1 cup beef or pork, cut into bite-sized pieces, 1 cup potatoes, peeled and cubed, 1 cup peanuts, 2 tablespoons fish sauce, 1 tablespoon palm sugar, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon ground coriander, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, Salt, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil, 2-3 Thai chilies, sliced
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add Massaman curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add beef or pork and cook until it's browned. Add potatoes and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and add fish sauce, palm sugar, soy sauce, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and salt. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
