Add flour, salt, and olive oil. Mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Roll out dough to a thickness of about 1/4 inch.
Place in a deep-dish pizza pan and top with pizza sauce, mozzarella cheese, cheddar cheese, and toppings.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until crust is golden brown and cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Texas-Style Brisket
instructions: Preheat smoker to 225-250°F (110-120°C).
In a small bowl, mix together chili powder, cumin, brown sugar, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Rub spice mixture all over the brisket, making sure to coat evenly.
Place brisket in smoker and cook for 4-5 hours, or until tender and easily shredded.
After 4 hours, brush brisket with beef broth and barbecue sauce.
Continue cooking for an additional 30 minutes to 1 hour, until glaze is caramelized and brisket is tender.

title: New Orleans-Style Gumbo
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, celery, and garlic. Cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add sausage and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until browned, 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth, thyme, oregano, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Serve over cooked rice.

title: Classic Cheeseburger
ingredients: Lettuce, tomato, pickles, and any other desired toppings
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Form the ground beef into 4 patties.
Season the patties with salt and pepper.
Grill the patties for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked to desired doneness.
Meanwhile, toast the buns on the grill or in a toaster.
Assemble the burgers with cheese, lettuce, tomato, pickles, and any other desired toppings.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the clams, clam juice, milk, and potatoes.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the thyme and season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces (legs, thighs, wings, and breasts)
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour the buttermilk into a separate large bowl.
Dip each piece of chicken into the buttermilk, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch.

title: New York-Style Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a medium bowl, mix together the graham cracker crumbs and sugar.
Add the melted butter and stir until the crumbs are evenly moistened.
Press the crumb mixture into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese until smooth.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the sugar and vanilla extract.

title: Texas-Style BBQ Brisket
instructions: Preheat the smoker to 225-250°F.
In a small bowl, mix together the chili powder, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the brisket.
Place the brisket in the smoker, fat side up.
Smoke the brisket for 4-5 hours, or until tender and easily shredded with a fork.
During the last 30 minutes, brush the brisket with beef broth.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Dill Sauce
instructions: Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add salmon fillets and sear for 3-4 minutes per side.
In a bowl, mix together dill, garlic, and lemon juice.
Add heavy cream and stir until combined.
Serve salmon with dill sauce spooned over the top.

title: Wild Mushroom Risotto
ingredients: 4 cups mixed wild mushrooms (such as chanterelle and oyster)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add Arborio rice and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add white wine and cook until absorbed.
Add warmed broth, 1 cup at a time, stirring constantly.

title: Coho Smoked Salmon Dip
instructions: In a bowl, mix together smoked salmon, sour cream, mayonnaise, lemon juice, dill, and horseradish.
Stir until combined and smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve with crackers or vegetables.

title: Roasted Salmon with Fennel and Carrots
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper.
In a bowl, toss fennel and carrots with olive oil.
Arrange fennel and carrots in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Place salmon fillets on top of fennel and carrots.
Roast in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until cooked through.

title: Clam Chowder with Smoked Bacon
instructions: In a large pot, cook bacon over medium heat until crispy.
Remove bacon from pot and set aside.
Add butter to pot and cook until melted.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add clams, clam juice, and heavy cream to pot.

title: Classic New York-Style Pastrami on Rye
instructions: Preheat a griddle or skillet over medium heat.
Butter the rye bread slices.
Place the rye bread slices on the griddle and toast until lightly browned.
Assemble the sandwiches with pastrami, onion, and mustard.
Serve immediately.

title: New York-Style Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Prepare the crust with graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth.
Add eggs, sugar, and vanilla extract to the cream cheese mixture.
Pour the cheesecake batter into the prepared crust.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes.

title: Knish Filling (Potato and Onion)
instructions: Boil the potatoes and onion until tender.
Drain the potatoes and onion and mash.
Add butter, flour, and chicken broth to the mashed potatoes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cannoli Siciliani (New York-Style)
instructions: Fill the cannoli shells with ricotta cheese mixture.
Dust the filled cannoli with confectioners' sugar.
Top the cannoli with candied fruit and pistachios.

title: New York-Style Black and White Cookies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and vanilla extract to the butter mixture.
Divide the dough in half and roll into balls.
Bake for 15-20 minutes.

title: Fried Chicken and Waffles
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, such as legs and thighs
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each piece of chicken into the buttermilk, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken until golden brown and cooked through.
While the chicken is cooking, preheat a waffle iron according to the manufacturer's instructions.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Pour about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the center of the waffle iron and cook until the waffles are golden brown.
Serve the fried chicken with the waffles and your favorite syrup.

title: Grits and Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a large saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the grits and reduce heat to low.
Cook the grits, stirring constantly, until they are smooth and creamy.
Stir in the butter, cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink and just cooked through.
Remove the shrimp from the skillet and set aside.
Add the butter to the skillet and melt.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the heavy cream and bring to a simmer.
Return the shrimp to the skillet and toss with the cream sauce.
Serve the shrimp over the grits and garnish with parsley.

title: Biscuits and Gravy
ingredients: 1 lb sausage, such as andouille or kielbasa, sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut the cold butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times.
Roll the dough out to about 1 inch thickness.
Cut out biscuits with a biscuit cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place the biscuits on a baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the biscuits are baking, cook the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove the sausage from the skillet and set aside.
Add the butter to the skillet and melt.
Add the flour and whisk to make a roux, cooking for 1-2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the beef broth and bring to a simmer.
Return the sausage to the skillet and cook until the gravy has thickened.
Serve the gravy over the biscuits.

title: Fried Green Tomatoes
ingredients: 4 large green tomatoes, sliced 1/4 inch thick
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each tomato slice into the buttermilk, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the tomato slices until golden brown and crispy.
Drain the fried tomatoes on paper towels.
Serve the fried tomatoes with remoulade sauce.

title: Sweet Potato Casserole
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a large saucepan, bring the sliced sweet potatoes to a boil in enough water to cover.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Drain the sweet potatoes and mash in a large bowl.
Add the sugar, flour, salt, and pepper to the bowl and stir to combine.
Add the melted butter, heavy cream, eggs, and vanilla extract to the bowl and stir until just combined.
Pour the sweet potato mixture into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the casserole is set and the top is lightly browned.
Remove the casserole from the oven and top with marshmallows.
Return the casserole to the oven and bake for an additional 5-10 minutes, or until the marshmallows are golden brown.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
Add clams, clam juice, milk, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
Add potatoes and cook until tender.
Serve hot.

title: Maine Blueberry Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix blueberries, sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Roll out pie crust and fill with blueberry mixture.
Dot top with butter pieces.
Roll out remaining pie crust and use to cover pie.
Crimp edges and cut a few slits in top.

title: Boston Baked Beans
ingredients: 1 pound dried navy beans, soaked overnight
1 pound smoked bacon, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°F.
Drain and rinse beans, transfer to a large Dutch oven.
Add bacon, onion, ketchup, sugar, molasses, mustard, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Cover and bake for 6 hours, or until beans are tender.
Serve hot.

title: Cape Cod Lobster Rolls
ingredients: Lettuce, tomato, and pickles for garnish
instructions: Mix lobster meat, butter, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and chives in a bowl.
Split buns in half and toast until lightly browned.
Fill buns with lobster mixture and garnish with lettuce, tomato, and pickles.
Serve immediately.

title: Vermonter Apple Crisp
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix apples, sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl.
Transfer to a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Mix oats, brown sugar, and butter in a bowl until crumbly.
Top apple mixture with oat mixture and bake for 35-40 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Fried Chicken Tenders with Creamy Coleslaw
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast or tenders, cut into strips
1 cup all-purpose flour, seasoned with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each chicken strip into the buttermilk, coating completely, then roll in flour mixture to coat.
Heat 1/2-inch vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add coated chicken to skillet and fry until golden brown and cooked through.
In a separate bowl, mix together shredded cabbage, carrots, mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Serve chicken tenders with coleslaw

title: Classic Midwestern Beef Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef to pot and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic to pot and cook until onion is translucent.
Add beef broth, red wine, carrots, potatoes, thyme, and rosemary to pot.
Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Crispy Pan-Fried Walleye Fillets
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, panko breadcrumbs, and Parmesan cheese.
In a separate dish, beat eggs.
Dip each fish fillet into eggs, coating completely, then roll in flour mixture to coat.
Heat 1/2-inch vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add coated fish to skillet and fry until golden brown and cooked through.

title: German-Style Potato Salad
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender.
Drain potatoes and let cool.
In a large bowl, whisk together oil, apple cider vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Add cooled potatoes, diced eggs, and chopped parsley to bowl.
Toss to combine and serve.

title: Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
instructions: In a large pot, sauté chopped onion, garlic, carrots, and celery in a little bit of oil until tender.
Add chicken to pot and cook until browned.
Add chicken broth and thyme to pot.
Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add egg noodles to pot and cook until tender.
Serve hot.

title: Brisket with BBQ Sauce
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket, trimmed of excess fat
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
In a small bowl, mix together chili powder, brown sugar, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the brisket.
Place the brisket in a large Dutch oven or a heavy-duty roasting pan.
Add beef broth to the pan, covering the brisket.
Bake for 3 hours, or until the brisket is tender.
After 3 hours, brush the brisket with BBQ sauce.
Return the brisket to the oven and bake for an additional 30 minutes.

title: Chicken Fried Steak with Creamy Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 1 pound beef steaks, cut into thin steaks
instructions: Season the steaks with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Dredge the steaks in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured steaks in buttermilk, then coat in flour again.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the steaks until golden brown and cooked through.
While the steaks are cooking, boil the chopped potatoes until tender.
Drain the potatoes and mash with butter and heavy cream.
Serve the fried steaks with creamy mashed potatoes.

title: Texas-Style Beef Fajitas
ingredients: Optional toppings: avocado, sour cream, shredded cheese, cilantro
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together lime juice, garlic, oregano, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the beef strips to the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over high heat.
Add the beef strips to the skillet and cook until browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the sliced onion and bell peppers to the skillet and cook until tender.
Warm the flour tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the fajitas by placing the beef and vegetable mixture onto a tortilla and adding desired toppings.

title: Green Chile Stew
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Add the beef stew meat to the pot and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the chopped green chilies, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper to the pot.
Pour in the beef broth and water, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro if desired.

title: Texas-Style Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into small pieces
2 cups shredded cheese (Cheddar or Monterey Jack)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper to the skillet and cook for an additional minute.
In a separate pan, warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the enchiladas by placing a portion of the chicken mixture onto a tortilla and rolling it up.
Place the rolled enchiladas seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the enchilada sauce over the rolled enchiladas and sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: California Avocado Salad
ingredients: 1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine diced avocado, red onion, and chopped jalapeño.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, garlic, and cumin.
Pour the lime juice mixture over the avocado mixture and toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped cilantro, if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Santa Maria Style Tri-Tip
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together olive oil, garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Rub the tri-tip roast with the spice mixture, making sure to coat all surfaces.
Grill the tri-tip for 4-5 minutes per side, or until it reaches desired level of doneness.
Let the tri-tip rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: California-Style Grilled Fish Tacos
ingredients: 4 white fish fillets (such as cod or tilapia)
Sliced radishes, lime wedges, and sour cream (optional)
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together lime juice, garlic, and oregano.
Brush the fish fillets with the lime juice mixture and season with salt and pepper.
Grill the fish for 3-4 minutes per side, or until it flakes easily with a fork.
Warm the tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble the tacos by placing a piece of fish on each tortilla and topping with cilantro, radishes, lime wedges, and sour cream, if desired.

title: California-Style Fried Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces (such as legs, thighs, and wings)
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together buttermilk and hot sauce.
Add the chicken pieces to the buttermilk mixture and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
In a separate bowl, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Remove the chicken from the buttermilk mixture and dredge in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per batch.

title: California-Style Green Chile Stew
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef stew meat and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the green chilies, tomatoes, beef broth, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1-2 hours, or until the beef is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro, if desired.

title: Gumbo
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron pot over medium-high.
Add sausage and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove sausage and set aside.
Add chicken to pot and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside with sausage.
Add onions, celery, and garlic to pot and cook until vegetables are tender.
Add thyme, oregano, cayenne pepper, paprika, salt, and pepper to pot and stir to combine.
Add rice, chicken broth, and water to pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until rice is cooked and liquid has been absorbed.
Stir in filé powder, if using.
Return sausage and chicken to pot and simmer until heated through.
Serve hot, garnished with scallions and parsley.

title: Beignets
instructions: Combine yeast and warm water in a large bowl and let sit for 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt, sugar, and oil to bowl and mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes and place in a greased bowl, covered with plastic wrap.
Let dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Preheat oil in a deep frying pan to 375°F.
Punch down dough and roll out to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into 2-inch squares and fry in batches until golden brown.
Drain beignets on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Red Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 lb dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Combine beans, sausage, onion, garlic, thyme, oregano, cayenne pepper, paprika, salt, and pepper in a large pot.
Add water to pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, until beans are tender.
Serve over cooked rice.

title: Fried Catfish
instructions: In a shallow dish, combine flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dredge catfish in flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Dip flour-coated catfish in buttermilk, then coat in flour mixture again.
Heat oil in a large skillet to 375°F.
Fry catfish in batches until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Bananas Foster
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high.
Add brown sugar to skillet and cook, stirring constantly, until caramelized.
Add bananas to skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until caramelized.
Flambé rum in skillet and cook until reduced.
Stir in vanilla extract.
Serve bananas over ice cream, topped with heavy cream.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Dill Sauce
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skin removed (6 oz each)
instructions: Season salmon with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon for 3-4 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix dill, sour cream, lemon juice, mustard, and honey in a bowl.
Serve salmon with dill sauce spooned over the top.

title: Roasted Dungeness Crab with Garlic Butter
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix butter, garlic, and lemon zest in a bowl.
Stuff each crab shell with butter mixture.
Place crabs in a baking dish and roast for 10-12 minutes, or until heated through.
Serve crabs with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Smoked Salmon Pâté
instructions: Mix smoked salmon, cream cheese, lemon juice, and mustard in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Serve chilled, garnished with chopped dill if desired.

title: Grilled Halibut with Lemon-Herb Butter
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Mix butter, lemon zest, parsley, and garlic in a bowl.
Season halibut with salt and pepper.
Grill halibut for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through.
Serve with lemon-herb butter spooned over the top.

title: Cranberry-Orange Relish
instructions: Combine cranberries, sugar, orange juice, and orange zest in a bowl.
Mix well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Stir in chopped parsley before serving.

title: Classic New York Style Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Prepare crust by mixing crumbs and sugar, then add melted butter and mix until combined.
Press crust into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cream cheese until smooth, then add eggs one at a time.
Add sugar, vanilla extract, and sour cream, mix until combined.
Pour filling into crust and bake for 55-60 minutes.
Let cool completely before serving.

title: Knish Filling (Potato and Onion)
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, then drain and mash.
Sauté onion in oil until softened.
Add mashed potatoes, salt, pepper, and garlic powder, mix until combined.
Let cool before using as knish filling.

title: New York-Style Pastrami on Rye
instructions: Assemble sandwiches by spreading mustard on bread, then adding pastrami, pickles, and coleslaw.
Serve immediately.

title: Jewish Deli-Style Brisket
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear brisket until browned, then set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic until softened.
Add beef broth, red wine, brown sugar, thyme, salt, and pepper, mix until combined.
Return brisket to pot and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until tender.
Let rest before slicing.

title: Matzo Ball Soup
instructions: Whisk eggs and matzo meal in a bowl.
Add chopped dill, parsley, salt, and pepper, mix until combined.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Using a spoon, drop egg mixture into pot and cook until browned and puffed.
Add chicken broth to pot and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Fried Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces (legs, thighs, wings, breasts)
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate shallow dish.
Dip each piece of chicken into the buttermilk, then coat in the flour mixture.
Dip the floured chicken into the beaten eggs, then coat in the flour mixture again.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch.
Drain the chicken on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Biscuits and Gravy
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces
2 cups sausage gravy (see below for sausage gravy recipe)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead a few times until it comes together.
Roll the dough out to about 1-inch thickness and use a biscuit cutter to cut out biscuits.
Place the biscuits on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve the biscuits with sausage gravy spooned over the top.

title: Sausage Gravy
instructions: In a large skillet, cook the sausage over medium-high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Remove the cooked sausage from the skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Leave the drippings in the skillet and add the flour.
Whisk the flour into the drippings to make a roux, cooking for 1-2 minutes.
Slowly pour in the milk, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until it thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return the cooked sausage to the gravy and serve over biscuits.

title: Collard Greens
instructions: In a large pot or Dutch oven, cook the chopped onion and minced garlic in the bacon drippings over medium heat until the onion is softened.
Add the chopped collard greens to the pot, stirring to combine with the onion and garlic.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover the pot and cook until the greens are tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Serve the collard greens hot, garnished with a splash of vinegar if desired.

title: Sweet Potato Pie
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, cooked and mashed
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, whisk together the mashed sweet potatoes, sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger.
Beat in the heavy cream and eggs until well combined.
Stir in the melted butter.
Pour the filling into an unbaked pie crust.
Bake the pie for 45-50 minutes, or until the filling is set and the crust is golden brown.
Serve the pie warm, topped with whipped cream if desired.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and garlic; cook until softened.
Add clams, clam juice, and thyme; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add milk and potatoes; cook until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Maine Lobster Rolls
instructions: Cut lobster meat into chunks.
Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice, and Dijon mustard in a bowl.
Add lobster meat to bowl and toss to coat.
Assemble rolls with lobster mixture, lettuce, and tomato.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add butter and eggs; mix until smooth.
Pour batter into a greased and floured pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown.

title: New England Boiled Dinner
instructions: Place corned beef in a large pot or Dutch oven.
Add potatoes, carrots, turnips, and garlic.
Add enough water to cover the ingredients.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add cabbage and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes.

title: Cape Cod Cranberry Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Mix cranberries, sugar, and flour in a bowl.
Add butter and mix until crumbly.
Roll out dough and fill with cranberry mixture.
Brush with egg wash and bake for 40-50 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Midwestern Beef Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds beef stew meat, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic and cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a boil, then cover and transfer to oven.
Bake at 300°F for 2 1/2 hours, or until beef is tender.

title: Amish Chicken and Noodles
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Cook noodles according to package instructions.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic and cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth and milk. Bring to a simmer and cook until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in cooked noodles and thyme. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Midwestern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken pieces (legs, thighs, wings, breasts)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour buttermilk into a separate large bowl.
Dip chicken pieces into buttermilk, then coat in flour mixture.
Heat about 1/2-inch oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.

title: German-Style Potato Salad
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes.
Drain potatoes and let cool.
In a large bowl, mix together mayonnaise, parsley, dill, mustard, and chives.
Add cooled potatoes to bowl and toss to combine.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Wisconsin-Style Beer Cheese Soup
instructions: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly add beer and chicken broth, whisking constantly.
Bring to a simmer and cook until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and cheese. Cook until cheese is melted and soup is smooth.

title: Chicken Fried Steak
ingredients: 1 pound beef top round, cut into 1-inch thick steaks
1 cup all-purpose flour, seasoned with salt and pepper
instructions: Season the steaks with salt and pepper.
Dredge the steaks in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured steaks in buttermilk, coating completely.
Dredge the steaks in flour again, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the steaks until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot with your favorite sides.

title: Texas-Style Brisket
ingredients: 2 pounds beef brisket, trimmed of excess fat
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Season the brisket with salt, pepper, chili powder, brown sugar, cumin, and smoked paprika.
Place the brisket in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot.
Pour the beef broth and barbecue sauce over the brisket.
Cover the pot with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise the brisket for 3-4 hours, or until tender and easily shredded.
Slice the brisket against the grain and serve.

title: Southern-Style Sweet Potato Casserole
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, cook the sweet potatoes until tender.
Drain the sweet potatoes and mash in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, salt, and pepper.
Add the melted butter, heavy cream, eggs, and vanilla extract to the sugar mixture.
Pour the sugar mixture over the mashed sweet potatoes and stir until combined.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Top with marshmallows and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Spicy Texas-Style Chili
ingredients: 1 can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until translucent.
Add the minced garlic and diced jalapeno and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chili powder, cumin, oregano, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.
Stir to combine and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes and kidney beans.
Simmer the chili for 30 minutes, or until the flavors have melded together.
Serve hot with your favorite toppings.

title: Texas-Style Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a large skillet, cook the chicken over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through.
In a separate pan, warm the tortillas over medium heat for 30 seconds on each side.
To assemble the enchiladas, lay a tortilla flat and spoon some of the chicken down the center.
Roll the tortilla and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas and chicken.
Pour the enchilada sauce over the rolled tortillas and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: California Avocado and Bacon Salad
instructions: In a large bowl, combine diced avocado, crumbled bacon, and thinly sliced red onion.
Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice and Dijon mustard.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Grilled Tri-Tip with Chimichurri
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Season tri-tip with salt and pepper.
Grill tri-tip for 5-7 minutes per side, or until it reaches desired level of doneness.
In a food processor, combine parsley, oregano, and garlic.
Process until well combined, then add red wine vinegar and olive oil.
Process until smooth, then season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Homemade Guacamole
ingredients: 1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine diced avocado, chopped red onion, and chopped jalapeño pepper.
Stir in chopped cilantro and lime juice.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.

title: California-Style Fish Tacos
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish (such as halibut or mahi-mahi)
Shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, and shredded cheese for garnish
instructions: In a large bowl, combine fish, lime juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, and cumin.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill fish for 3-4 minutes per side, or until it reaches desired level of doneness.
Warm tortillas by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and microwaving for 20-30 seconds.
Assemble tacos by placing cooked fish onto a tortilla, then topping with shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, and shredded cheese.

title: California-Style Grilled Steak Fajitas
ingredients: Shredded cheese and sour cream for garnish
instructions: In a large bowl, combine steak, lime juice, garlic, oregano, and cumin.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill steak for 5-7 minutes per side, or until it reaches desired level of doneness.
Grill sliced onion and bell peppers for 3-4 minutes per side, or until they are tender.
Slice steak into thin strips, then serve with grilled onion and bell peppers, along with warm tortillas.

title: Gumbo Z'Herbes
ingredients: 2 cups mixed herbs (such as parsley, basil, thyme, and oregano)
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large cast-iron pot over medium-high.
Add onion, celery, and carrot; cook until vegetables are tender.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add mixed herbs, oregano, thyme, cayenne pepper, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add sausage and chicken; cook until browned.
Add chicken broth, water, and filé powder (if using); bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions and crusty bread on the side.

title: Beignets
instructions: Combine yeast, flour, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Gradually add warm water, sugar, and melted butter; mix until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes; place in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat oil in a deep frying pan to 375°F.
Punch down dough and roll out to 1/2-inch thickness.
Cut into 2-inch squares and fry in batches until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Jambalaya
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron pot over medium-high.
Add onion, celery, and bell pepper; cook until vegetables are tender.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add sausage and chicken; cook until browned.
Add rice, chicken broth, paprika, thyme, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Crawfish Etouffee
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron pot over medium-high.
Add onion, celery, and carrot; cook until vegetables are tender.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add paprika, thyme, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add crawfish tails and cook until pink and tender.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions and crusty bread on the side.

title: Bananas Foster
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high.
Add brown sugar and cook for 2 minutes.
Add bananas and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until caramelized.
Add rum and cook for 1 minute.
Add cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Serve bananas over vanilla ice cream and flambé with a match.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the remaining onion for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended vegetables, thyme, curry powder, salt, pepper, and bay leaf; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover, and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, until tender.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and berbere; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon.
Heat the olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides; set aside.
Cook the onion in the pot for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives; simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in half the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the bread, curry powder, jam, lemon juice, raisins, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and level the top.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the beef; place the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
ingredients: 8 green cooking bananas, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the bananas, stock, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes, until the bananas are tender.
Mash the bananas lightly in the pot and serve warm.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the bell pepper and crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes, thyme, curry powder, salt, and bay leaf; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover, and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in 1/2 cup milk, then squeeze it out and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the meat and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the soaked bread, jam, curry powder, turmeric, lemon juice, raisins, and salt.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and press it down evenly.
Beat the eggs with the remaining 1/2 cup milk and pour over the meat; arrange the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the topping is set and golden.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wat (Spiced Red Lentils)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh or oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and berbere; cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, water or stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Season the chicken with salt and brown it on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35–40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the preserved lemon, olives, cilantro, and parsley; simmer uncovered for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Ghanaian Groundnut Soup with Chicken
instructions: Season the chicken with the salt.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, then stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with 1 cup of the stock until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the remaining stock.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the whole Scotch bonnet pepper.
Simmer gently, partially covered, for 35–45 minutes, until the chicken is tender; do not break the pepper.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 3–5 minutes, then remove the pepper and serve.

title: Senegalese Chicken Yassa
instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, pepper, and salt; coat the chicken and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Remove the chicken and reserve the marinade; cook the onions in oil over medium heat until soft and golden.
Brown the chicken in the same pot, then return the onions and add the reserved marinade and stock.
Cover and simmer for 35–45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the olives and serve hot with rice.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot
instructions: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat, stirring often, until softened and lightly browned.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and thick.

title: Nigerian Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded for less heat
instructions: Blend the bell pepper, tomatoes, and Scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened; stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture and cook for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Stir in the stock, thyme, curry powder, bay leaf, and salt; bring to a boil.
Add the rice and stir once; cover tightly and cook on low heat for 25–30 minutes, until tender.
Fluff the rice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and peel sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides; set aside.
Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, and salt; stir for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon peel and olives; simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with couscous or bread.

title: Ghanaian Red Red
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the black-eyed peas in a pot with the water; bring to a boil, then simmer for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Heat the palm oil in a separate pot over medium heat; cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and Scotch bonnet; cook until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Add the cooked peas and their cooking liquid; season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the pepper and serve with fried plantains.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
instructions: Blend the bell pepper and crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomato mixture, thyme, curry powder, salt, pepper, and bay leaf; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Egusi Soup (Nigeria)
ingredients: 1 pound beef, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Boil the beef in a pot until tender, about 30 minutes, reserving the cooking stock.
Mix the ground egusi with 1/2 cup water to make a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and cook the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the egusi paste in small spoonfuls and cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Add the beef, stock, crayfish, red pepper, salt, and ground shrimp, if using.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Serve hot with fufu or rice.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, berbere, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and water or stock, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the lentils are soft and thick, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the salt and serve with injera or rice.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and peel sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot or tagine over medium heat.
Brown the chicken pieces on both sides, then transfer them to a plate.
Cook the onion in the pot until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock and salt.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Add the preserved lemon and olives, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Scatter the cilantro over the tagine and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in 1/4 cup of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the soaked bread, chutney, curry powder, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and press it down evenly.
Beat the eggs with the remaining 1/4 cup milk and pour over the meat.
Place the bay leaves on top and bake until the custard is set and golden, about 30 minutes.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the bell pepper and crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato mixture, curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and chicken stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Let stand covered for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and berbere and cook for 1 minute.
Mix in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick, about 25 minutes.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken thighs, bone-in and skin removed
1 preserved lemon, rind rinsed and thinly sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, and turmeric; cook for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the preserved lemon and olives and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in 1/2 cup milk, then squeeze it lightly and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and ground beef; cook until the beef is browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the curry powder, apricot jam, lemon juice, raisins, soaked bread, reserved milk, 1 egg, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and smooth the top.
Whisk the remaining 2 eggs with 3/4 cup milk and pour over the beef mixture.
Place the bay leaves on top and bake until the custard is set and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Ugali (East African Maize Meal)
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually pour in the maize meal while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and continue stirring until the mixture thickens.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring firmly every few minutes, until smooth and stiff.
Shape the ugali into a mound and serve warm.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, rinsed and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, and salt; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and turn to coat with the spices.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon and olives and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and parsley, then serve.

title: Senegalese Chicken Yassa
instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, black pepper, salt, and crushed red pepper in a bowl.
Add the chicken and onions, toss to coat, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Lift the chicken from the marinade and set the onions and marinade aside.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions and cook until softened and lightly golden.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the marinade and stock.
Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes; serve with rice.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentil Stew)
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook slowly until very soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the berbere and tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and thick.

title: Ghanaian Red Red (Black-Eyed Peas in Tomato Sauce)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the black-eyed peas and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, until the peas are tender; drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.
Heat the palm oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic, ginger, and chili pepper.
Add the crushed tomatoes and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cooked peas and reserved cooking liquid, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Fry or bake the plantain slices until golden and serve alongside the stew.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it gently and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic, curry powder, and turmeric and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the soaked bread, raisins, apricot jam, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and smooth the top.
Whisk the eggs with the reserved milk and pour over the meat; place the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the remaining onion until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture, thyme, curry powder, salt, pepper, and bay leaf; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Fluff the rice and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wat (Spiced Red Lentils)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh or oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and berbere and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, water or stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered until the lentils are soft and thick, 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve warm with injera or rice.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock and preserved lemon.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it gently and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, raisins, jam, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Crumble the soaked bread into the meat mixture and stir well.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and smooth the top.
Whisk the eggs with the reserved milk and pour over the meat; place the bay leaves on top.
Bake until the topping is set and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
instructions: Cut the peeled bananas into large chunks and set aside.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, bell pepper, and curry powder; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the bananas, stock, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the bananas are tender, about 30 minutes.
Mash a few banana pieces into the sauce to thicken it, then serve warm.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
instructions: Blend the bell pepper and crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomato mixture, thyme, curry powder, ginger, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, berbere, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water or stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.
Serve hot, traditionally with injera.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives

instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.

Cook the onion until softened, then stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and saffron.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Scatter with cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic, curry powder, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the soaked bread, raisins, chutney, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and smooth the top.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the meat; place the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
ingredients: 8 green cooking bananas, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and salt; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the bananas and pour in the stock.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes, until the bananas are tender.
Mash a few banana pieces into the sauce and stir gently.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the remaining onion until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture, thyme, curry powder, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and stock, stir, and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh or oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the berbere and tomato paste; stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water or stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon; cook for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon and olives, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in half the milk, then squeeze it lightly and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder; cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the soaked bread, apricot jam, raisins, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and bake for 20 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk, pour over the meat, and bake for 20–25 minutes, until set and golden.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
ingredients: 8 green cooking bananas, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and bell pepper; cook for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Add the bananas, salt, pepper, and stock.
Cover and simmer for 25–35 minutes, until the bananas are tender.
Mash a few banana pieces into the sauce to thicken it.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp discarded and rind sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, turmeric, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and turn to coat with the spices.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the preserved lemon, olives, cilantro, parsley, and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, then serve.

title: Ghanaian Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, pierced but left whole
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, curry powder, paprika, and Scotch bonnet.
Simmer the tomato mixture for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the rice, stock, salt, and black pepper.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentil Stew)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh or unsalted butter
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook slowly until very soft and golden, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the berbere and tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered until the lentils are soft and thick, about 25 minutes.
Serve hot with injera or flatbread.

title: Senegalese Chicken Yassa
instructions: Whisk together the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, black pepper, and salt.
Toss the chicken and onions with the marinade; cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and reserve the onions and marinade.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onions and bay leaf; cook until the onions are soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the reserved marinade and stock.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes; serve with rice.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then squeeze it gently and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook until soft, about 8 minutes; add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the curry powder, soaked bread, apricot jam, lemon juice, raisins, salt, and black pepper.
Spoon the mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the meat mixture.
Place the bay leaves on top and bake until set and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Jollof Rice (West Africa)

instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.

Stir in the rice and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice and serve.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat; brown the chicken on both sides, then transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and cinnamon; cook for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon and olives; simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot (Spiced Red Lentils)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh or unsalted butter
instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the onion and cook slowly until very soft, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and berbere; cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve.

title: Ugali (East African Maize Meal)
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually sprinkle in the maize meal, whisking to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and stir firmly with a wooden spoon for 8–10 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Cover and cook for 3 minutes, then turn the ugali onto a plate.
Shape it with a spoon and serve hot.

title: Senegalese Thieboudienne (Fish and Rice)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into 4 pieces
1 carrot, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Pound the parsley and garlic with a pinch of salt; rub the mixture into the fish and let it stand for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the fish briefly on both sides; transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste.
Cook for 5 minutes, then add the water, carrot, cabbage, eggplant, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender; remove them and set aside.
Return the fish to the pot and simmer gently for 10 minutes, then remove it.
Add the rice to the broth, cover, and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Serve the rice topped with the fish and vegetables.

title: West African Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the bell pepper and crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes, thyme, curry powder, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the berbere, garlic, ginger, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered until the lentils are soft and thick, about 25 minutes.
Serve hot, traditionally with injera.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, rind rinsed and sliced
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.

Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 40 minutes.

Stir in the cilantro and serve.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in half of the milk, then squeeze out the excess and crumble it.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.

Bake until the topping is set and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
instructions: Cut the peeled bananas into large chunks and place them in a bowl of water.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.

Drain the bananas and add them to the pot with the stock, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the bananas are tender, about 30 minutes.
Mash a few pieces into the sauce and serve hot.

title: West African Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the remaining onion for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture, thyme, curry powder, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover, and cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Fluff the rice, remove the bay leaf, and serve.

Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.

Mix in the soaked bread and transfer the mixture to a baking dish.

title: Senegalese Thieboudienne
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish, cut into 4 pieces
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 cup cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Mix the parsley, garlic, and chili paste; make small cuts in the fish and rub the mixture into them.

Return the fish to the pot and cook gently for 10 minutes, until just cooked; remove the fish and vegetables and keep warm.
Stir the rice into the cooking liquid, cover, and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender.
Serve the rice with the fish and vegetables.

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh or oil in a saucepan over medium heat.

Stir in the garlic, ginger, berbere, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water or stock, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered until the lentils are soft and thick, about 25 minutes.
Stir occasionally and add a little water if the lentils become too thick.
Serve hot with injera or rice.

title: South African Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess milk and reserve it.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, apricot jam, raisins, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and soaked bread.

title: Ugandan Matoke (Stewed Green Bananas)
ingredients: 8 green cooking bananas, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.

Add the bananas, stock, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the bananas are tender, about 25 minutes.
Lightly mash some of the bananas into the sauce and serve hot.

instructions: Melt the niter kibbeh in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook slowly until soft and golden, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and berbere, and cook for 1 minute.
Mix in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, stock, and salt; bring to a boil.

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft; add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
