Spoon the mixture into a baking dish and press it down evenly.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the meat; place the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the topping is set and golden.

title: Ghanaian Kelewele (Spiced Fried Plantain)
instructions: Cut the plantains into bite-sized cubes.
Mix the ginger, cayenne, cinnamon, cloves, salt, and water in a bowl.
Toss the plantain cubes in the spice mixture until coated.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the plantains in batches for 3 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Couscous with Lamb and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
2 turnips, peeled and cut into chunks
1 cup chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion, tomato paste, harissa, coriander, paprika, turmeric, and salt; stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water and chickpeas. Cover and simmer until the lamb and chickpeas are nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the carrots and turnips; simmer for 15 minutes, then add the potatoes and zucchini and cook until tender.
Prepare the couscous according to its package directions, then fluff it with the butter.
Pile the couscous on a serving platter and arrange the lamb and vegetables on top. Spoon over some broth and serve the remaining broth alongside.

title: Ojja with Merguez
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and brown the merguez; transfer them to a plate.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, harissa, caraway, paprika, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and water. Simmer for 10 minutes, then return the merguez to the skillet.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook until the whites are set.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve hot with bread.

title: Lablabi (Chickpea Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
4 thick slices day-old bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Put the chickpeas and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming the surface.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chickpeas are very tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Poach the eggs in the chickpea broth until the whites are set, or cook them separately to your liking.
Divide the bread among bowls and ladle chickpeas and broth over it.
Top each bowl with an egg, olive oil, harissa, parsley, and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Brik à l’Œuf
instructions: Lay one pastry sheet flat and place 1 tablespoon parsley and 1 tablespoon capers near the center.
Crack an egg onto the filling and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Fold the pastry into a half-moon, keeping the filling enclosed, and press the edges together.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Slide in one brik and fry, spooning hot oil over the top, until crisp and golden, about 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Drain briefly and serve at once with lemon wedges; repeat with the remaining pastry and filling.

title: Slata Mechouia (Grilled Vegetable Salad)
ingredients: 1 small yellow onion, peeled and halved
instructions: Grill the peppers, tomatoes, onion, and garlic over a flame or under a broiler, turning until charred and softened.
Place the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and remove their seeds.
Peel the tomatoes and garlic. Finely chop all the grilled vegetables together, or pulse briefly for a coarse texture.
Stir in the olive oil, salt, caraway, and lemon juice.
Spread the salad on a plate and garnish with the hard-boiled eggs and olives.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into pieces
1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced
instructions: Mix the chicken with the onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, pepper, saffron, salt, and olive oil.
Arrange the chicken in a tagine or heavy pot and add the water.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, turning the chicken once, until cooked through.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and parsley and serve with bread.

title: Harira
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
1/2 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
1/4 cup vermicelli, broken into short pieces
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and celery until softened.
Add the chickpeas, lentils, cilantro, parsley, ginger, turmeric, pepper, cinnamon, tomatoes, broth, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for about 1 hour, until the chickpeas and lentils are tender.
Whisk the flour with the cold water until smooth, then stir it into the soup.
Add the vermicelli and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup thickens and the pasta is tender.

title: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
ingredients: 1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion, ginger, turmeric, pepper, half the salt, and 6 cups of water; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, then add the chickpeas, carrots, turnips, cabbage, and tomatoes.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then add the zucchini and pumpkin and cook until all the vegetables are tender.
Put the couscous in a large bowl, stir in the remaining oil and salt, and pour over 1 cup boiling water; cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the couscous topped with the lamb and vegetables, ladle broth over it, and finish with cilantro.

title: Zaalouk (Moroccan Eggplant and Tomato Salad)
instructions: Prick the eggplants with a fork and roast them at 425°F for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until very soft.
Let the eggplants cool slightly, then peel and roughly chop the flesh.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne, and salt; cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the eggplant and mash it with a spoon as it cooks for 10 to 15 minutes, until thick.
Mix in the cilantro and lemon juice, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Bissara (Fava Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried split fava beans, rinsed
instructions: Put the fava beans, water, and garlic in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 60 to 75 minutes, skimming the surface as needed, until the beans are very soft.
Blend the beans and cooking liquid until smooth, adding a little hot water if the soup is too thick.
Return the soup to the pot and stir in the cumin, paprika, and salt.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with cayenne.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and bread.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin removed
instructions: Toss the chicken with lemon juice and salt; set aside for 20 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, until soft and deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Add the niter kibbeh and oil, then stir in the berbere and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and turn to coat in the onion mixture.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Pierce the eggs lightly, add them to the pot, and simmer for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Misir Wat
instructions: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the niter kibbeh and oil, then stir in the berbere and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the lentils, water, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick, about 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Gomen
ingredients: 2 pounds collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Wash the collard greens well and drain them.
Heat the niter kibbeh and oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the greens, water, and salt; cover and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 35 minutes.
Uncover and cook briefly if needed to reduce excess liquid.

title: Shiro Wat
instructions: Cook the onion in a dry pot over medium-low heat until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the niter kibbeh and oil, then stir in the berbere and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Whisk the shiro powder with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Pour the mixture into the pot, add the remaining water and salt, and stir well.
Simmer gently, stirring frequently, until smooth and thick, about 20 minutes.

title: Atakilt Wat
ingredients: 1 pound green cabbage, cut into wedges and sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, carrots, water, and salt; cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, cover, and cook until all the vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes, stirring gently once or twice.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, whole or chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the remaining onion until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture, thyme, curry powder, salt, bay leaf, and Scotch bonnet; simmer until thick and reduced, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, then cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender, about 25 minutes.
Fluff the rice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Egusi Soup with Spinach
ingredients: 1 cup ground egusi, or melon seeds
1 pound beef, cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 pound stockfish, soaked and cut into pieces
instructions: Simmer the beef and stockfish with the seasoning cube and salt until tender; reserve the stock.
Mix the ground egusi with 1/2 cup water to make a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the egusi paste in small portions and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, stockfish, crayfish, Scotch bonnet, and 3 cups reserved stock; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.

title: Efo Riro
ingredients: 1 pound assorted beef, cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 pound smoked fish, cleaned and flaked
1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Simmer the beef with the seasoning cube and salt until tender; reserve 1 cup of the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and Scotch bonnet until smooth.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft.
Add the blended mixture and simmer until thick and reduced, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the beef, smoked fish, crayfish, and reserved stock; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until just wilted, about 3 minutes.

title: Moi Moi
ingredients: 2 cups peeled black-eyed peas, soaked for 30 minutes
1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Drain the peas and blend them with the bell pepper, onion, Scotch bonnet, and water until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a bowl and stir in the oil, salt, and seasoning cube.
Spoon the batter into greased heatproof containers and place half an egg in each portion.
Set the containers in a large pot with enough water to reach halfway up their sides.
Cover and steam gently until firm, about 45 minutes, adding hot water as needed.
Cool slightly before serving.

title: Akara
ingredients: 2 cups peeled black-eyed peas, soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Drain the peas and blend them with a little water into a thick, smooth batter.
Transfer the batter to a bowl and beat by hand until light and airy, about 5 minutes.
Fold in the onion, Scotch bonnet, and salt.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and fry in batches until golden brown, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Red Red (Beans Stew with Fried Plantain)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, picked over and rinsed
6 cups water, plus more as needed
1/2 teaspoon ground dried chili, or to taste
instructions: Put the peas and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until tender, about 45–60 minutes; drain, reserving a little cooking liquid.
Heat the palm oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, ginger, crayfish, chili, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down and the oil begins to show at the edges.
Add the cooked peas and a splash of reserved liquid. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring gently, until thick and well seasoned.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet and fry the plantain slices until golden on both sides. Serve with the beans stew.

title: Waakye (Rice and Beans)
ingredients: 1 cup dried black-eyed peas, picked over and rinsed
2 dried sorghum leaves, rinsed, or 1 teaspoon baking soda
instructions: Put the peas, water, and sorghum leaves in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the peas are just tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Add the rice and salt, adding a little hot water if needed so the rice is covered by about 1 inch of liquid.
Cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Remove the sorghum leaves, fluff gently, and serve with stew, shito, or your favorite waakye accompaniments.

title: Groundnut Soup with Chicken
ingredients: 1 teaspoon ground chili, or to taste
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, onion, ginger, and chili in a large pot. Add 1 cup water, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes with the peanut butter and 1 cup of the water or stock until smooth.
Pour the mixture into the pot and add the remaining water or stock. Stir well and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the eggplant, if using, and simmer uncovered for 35–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the soup is rich. Serve with rice balls or fufu.

title: Kontomire Stew with Boiled Yam
ingredients: 1 pound cocoyam leaves, finely chopped, or 10 ounces frozen chopped spinach
1 pound yam, peeled and cut into chunks
1 smoked mackerel, skin and bones removed and flaked
1/2 cup cooked egusi, or 2 tablespoons ground egusi mixed with 3 tablespoons water
1 teaspoon ground dried chili, or to taste
instructions: Put the yam in a pot, cover with water, and boil until fork-tender, about 20–25 minutes. Drain and keep warm.
If using cocoyam leaves, steam them with a splash of water until tender, about 10 minutes. Set aside.
Heat the palm oil in a saucepan. Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste.
Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil shows at the edges. Stir in the egusi and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the leaves, smoked mackerel, chili, and salt. Simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, stirring carefully. Serve with the boiled yam.

title: Kelewele (Spiced Fried Plantain)
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon ground chili, or to taste
instructions: Cut the plantains into bite-size cubes and place them in a bowl.
Mix the ginger, chili, cloves, salt, and water. Toss with the plantain and leave to season for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 inch of vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium heat.
Fry the plantain in batches until deep golden and crisp at the edges, turning occasionally, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on a paper towel and serve warm, on its own or with roasted peanuts.

title: Thieboudienne (Fish and Rice)
ingredients: 2 lb whole fish, cut into 4 pieces
1 small cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Pound the parsley, garlic, nététou, and salt into a paste; cut slits in the fish and rub the paste into them.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the fish on both sides; remove and set aside.
Add the onion and tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring. Add the grated tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and add the carrots, cassava, eggplant, cabbage, and Scotch bonnet. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes; remove them and set aside.
Return the fish to the pot and simmer gently for 8 minutes. Remove the fish and keep the broth hot.
Add the rinsed rice to the broth, cover, and cook over low heat until tender, about 25 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Serve the rice with the fish and vegetables, with broth spooned over the top.

title: Yassa Poulet (Senegalese Lemon-Onion Chicken)
instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, black pepper, and salt. Coat the chicken and onions with the mixture and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Lift the chicken from the marinade and reserve the onions and marinade.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add the onions and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot. Add the reserved marinade, water, Scotch bonnet, and olives.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes. Remove the pepper before serving.
Serve hot with white rice.

title: Mafé (Peanut Stew with Beef)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 sweet potato, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes.
Return the beef to the pot and add the water. Cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with 1 cup of hot cooking liquid until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Add the carrots, sweet potato, cabbage, and Scotch bonnet. Simmer uncovered until the vegetables and beef are tender and the sauce is thick, about 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with rice.

title: Domoda (Senegalese Peanut and Tomato Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef stew meat, cut into cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add the onion and cook until softened. Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot and add the water. Cover and simmer until nearly tender, about 40 minutes.
Mix the peanut butter with a ladleful of hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the lemon juice.
Add the carrots, potato, and Scotch bonnet. Simmer uncovered until the beef and vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pepper and serve with rice.

title: Thiéré Bassé (Millet Couscous with Meat and Vegetables)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the lamb with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the lamb. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer until the lamb is nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the carrots, cassava, cabbage, eggplant, and Scotch bonnet. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, place the millet couscous in a heatproof bowl and sprinkle it with 1/2 cup water. Let it stand for 10 minutes, then steam it over the simmering stew until fluffy and tender, about 20 minutes.
Serve the millet couscous topped with the lamb, vegetables, and broth.

title: Ugali
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add the maize flour, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Keep stirring and pressing the mixture against the sides of the pot until it thickens and pulls away from the sides, about 8–10 minutes.
Shape into a mound and serve hot with sukuma wiki, stew, or nyama choma.

title: Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 large bunch collard greens, stems removed and leaves thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and salt, and cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the collard greens and water, cover, and cook until tender but still bright green, about 8–12 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve with ugali.

title: Githeri
ingredients: 2 cups dried maize kernels, soaked overnight
1 cup dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
6 cups water, plus more as needed
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked maize and beans.
Put them in a large pot with the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the maize and beans are tender, about 1 1/2–2 hours; add water if needed.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until softened, then stir in the potato and salt.
Add the mixture to the pot and simmer until the potato is tender and the githeri is thick, about 15–20 minutes.

title: Irio
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups corn kernels, fresh or frozen
instructions: Put the potatoes and peas in a pot with the water and salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the corn and cook for 5 minutes, then drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Add the butter and mash everything together, leaving some texture; add a splash of reserved water if needed.
Serve hot with stew or grilled meat.

title: Kenyan Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, and tomato paste, and cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the beef stock, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the carrots and potatoes, cover, and simmer until the vegetables are tender and the beef is soft, about 25–30 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve with rice, chapati, or ugali.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Soak the bread in half the milk, then mash it with a fork.
Cook the onion in a little oil until soft. Add the beef and cook until browned.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, salt, jam, chutney, vinegar, and mashed bread. Spoon into a baking dish.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the meat. Arrange the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the topping is set and golden.

title: Boerewors and Pap with Tomato-Onion Relish
instructions: Bring 3 cups of the water and the salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Mix the maize meal with the remaining cup of cold water, then stir it into the boiling water.
Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and cooked through.
Meanwhile, grill or pan-fry the boerewors over medium heat, turning until browned and cooked through.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan and cook the onion until soft. Add the tomatoes, vinegar, and sugar, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the pap with the boerewors and tomato-onion relish.

title: Chakalaka
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened.
Stir in the carrots, tomatoes, curry powder, paprika, and salt.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the baked beans and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

title: Cape Malay Chicken Curry
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onions until soft.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, and cumin, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and turn to coat it in the spices. Cook until lightly browned.
Add the tomatoes, potatoes, water, and salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 35–40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the potatoes are tender.

title: Melktert
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and bake the pastry shell for 10 minutes.
Warm the milk with the cinnamon stick in a saucepan; remove the stick before it boils.
In a bowl, whisk the sugar, flour, cornstarch, and egg yolks with a little of the warm milk until smooth.
Whisk the mixture into the saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick. Stir in the butter and vanilla.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them gently into the custard.
Pour the filling into the pastry shell, dust with ground cinnamon, and bake for 20 minutes. Cool before serving.

title: Lablabi (Chickpea Soup)
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the chickpeas and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chickpeas are very tender, about 1½ to 2 hours; add water if needed.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, harissa, and salt, then simmer for 10 minutes.
If using eggs, crack them into the soup and poach until just set.
Divide the bread among bowls and ladle the hot chickpeas and broth over it.
Finish each bowl with olive oil and lemon juice.

title: Ojja Merguez
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and brown the merguez for 5 minutes.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, harissa, caraway, and paprika; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt, then simmer until thickened, about 12 minutes.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set, about 5 minutes; scatter parsley over the top.

title: Couscous with Lamb and Vegetables
ingredients: 1½ pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion and cook until softened, then stir in the tomato paste, paprika, coriander, caraway, and salt.
Pour in the 6 cups water and bring to a boil; cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and turnips and cook for 15 minutes, then add the potatoes, zucchini, and chickpeas and simmer until tender.
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and butter, then serve topped with the lamb and vegetables and spoon over broth.

title: Brik with Egg and Tuna
ingredients: 4 sheets malsouka or spring roll wrappers
instructions: Lay a wrapper flat and place one quarter of the tuna, capers, and parsley near the center.
Sprinkle with a little salt and carefully crack an egg on top.
Fold the wrapper into a half-moon, keeping the filling inside.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slide in one brik and fry until golden and crisp, about 1 to 2 minutes per side; repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Slata Mechouia (Grilled Pepper and Tomato Salad)
instructions: Grill the peppers, tomatoes, onion, and garlic, turning often, until their skins are charred and the vegetables are soft.
Place the vegetables in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and seed the peppers and peel the tomatoes and garlic.
Finely chop the vegetables together, or pulse briefly in a food processor.
Stir in the olive oil, salt, and lemon juice.
Arrange the salad on a plate and garnish with the eggs and olives.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind cut into strips
instructions: Mix the chicken with the onions, garlic, spices, olive oil, cilantro, parsley, and salt.
Arrange the chicken and onion mixture in a tagine or heavy pot, then add the water.
Cover and simmer gently for 50 to 60 minutes, turning the chicken once, until tender and cooked through.
Add the olives and preserved lemon rind; simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Serve hot with bread, spooning the sauce over the chicken.

title: Harira
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
1/2 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
1/2 pound lamb stew meat, cut into small cubes
1/2 cup water, for the flour mixture
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the lamb and onion for 5 minutes.
Add the celery, cilantro, parsley, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, pepper, and salt; stir for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, lentils, grated tomatoes, tomato paste, and 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for about 1 hour, until the chickpeas and meat are tender.
Whisk the flour with 1/2 cup water until smooth, then stir it gradually into the soup.
Add the vermicelli and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the soup thickens and the vermicelli is cooked.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Beef and Prune Tagine
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Put the beef, onions, olive oil, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, pepper, saffron, and salt in a heavy pot.
Add the water, cover, and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the prunes and honey, then simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce is glossy and thick.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and almonds before serving.

title: Zaalouk (Smoky Eggplant and Tomato Salad)
instructions: Steam the eggplant cubes for 15 to 20 minutes, until very soft, then drain well.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, pepper, and salt; cook for 8 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the eggplant and mash it into the tomato mixture with a spoon.
Cook over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the cilantro and lemon juice, then serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Moroccan Carrot Salad with Cumin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds carrots, peeled and cut into coins
instructions: Boil the carrots in salted water for 10 to 12 minutes, until tender but not falling apart; drain.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet and cook the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, and black pepper.
Add the carrots and toss gently to coat; cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and mix in the lemon juice and cilantro.
Serve warm or chilled.

title: Doro Wat
instructions: Marinate the chicken in lemon juice and salt for 30 minutes, then drain.
Cook the onions in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring often, until soft and deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the niter kibbeh, berbere, tomato paste, garlic, and ginger; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and turn to coat it in the spice mixture.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, turning them once.

title: Misir Wot
instructions: Cook the onions in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring often, until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the niter kibbeh, berbere, garlic, and ginger; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, water, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and thick, about 30 minutes.
Add a little water if needed to reach a spoonable consistency.

title: Shiro Wot
instructions: Cook the onion in a heavy pot over medium heat until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the oil, niter kibbeh, berbere, and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Whisk the shiro powder with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Gradually stir the shiro mixture and remaining water into the pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often, and cook until thick and glossy, about 20 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Gomen
ingredients: 2 pounds collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Wash the collard greens well and drain them.
Cook the onion in a heavy pot over medium heat until soft, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the greens, water, and salt, then cover the pot.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender, about 35 minutes.
Uncover and cook until any excess liquid has evaporated.

title: Kik Alicha
instructions: Bring the split peas and water to a boil in a pot, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the peas are tender, about 45 minutes.
Cook the onion in a separate pan with the niter kibbeh until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute.
Add the onion mixture and salt to the peas.
Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy, about 10 minutes.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the remaining onion until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the blended mixture and cook, stirring often, until thickened and reduced.
Add the stock, thyme, curry powder, salt, pepper, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the rice, cover tightly, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 pound beef, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Season the beef with salt and the stock cube, then simmer with the stock until tender.
Mix the ground egusi with 1 cup of water to make a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the egusi paste in small spoonfuls and cook for 5 minutes, turning gently.
Add the beef, stockfish, beef stock, crayfish, and chili pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Efo Riro
ingredients: 3 red bell peppers, seeded and chopped
1/2 pound beef, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Blend the bell peppers, tomatoes, and Scotch bonnet until mostly smooth.
Season the beef with salt and the stock cube, then simmer with a little water until tender.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft.
Add the blended pepper mixture and simmer until thick and reduced, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the beef, smoked fish, and crayfish; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and well combined.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve.

title: Moi Moi
ingredients: 2 cups peeled black-eyed peas, soaked for 1 hour
instructions: Drain the soaked peas and rub them between your hands to remove any remaining skins.
Blend the peas with the bell pepper, onion, Scotch bonnet, and water until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a bowl and stir in the oil, salt, and stock cube.
Spoon the batter into greased heatproof ramekins and place half an egg in each portion.
Set the ramekins in a large pot with hot water reaching halfway up their sides.
Cover the pot and steam over medium-low heat until the moi moi is firm, about 50 minutes.
Cool slightly before serving.

title: Akara
ingredients: 2 cups peeled black-eyed peas, soaked for 1 hour
instructions: Drain the peas and rub them between your hands to remove any remaining skins.
Blend the peas, onion, Scotch bonnet, and water into a thick, smooth batter.
Pour the batter into a bowl and beat it briskly for 3 minutes until light and airy.
Stir in the salt.
Heat the oil in a deep pot over medium heat.
Scoop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and fry in batches, turning, until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Red Red (Bean Stew with Fried Plantain)
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, picked over and rinsed
6 cups water, plus more for soaking
instructions: Soak the peas in water overnight, then drain.
Put the peas in a pot with 6 cups fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 45 to 60 minutes; drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.
Heat the palm oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, dried shrimp, salt, and cayenne; simmer until thick, about 10 minutes.
Add the cooked peas and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and fry the plantain slices until golden on both sides. Serve with the bean stew.

title: Ghanaian Jollof Rice
instructions: Blend the bell pepper with the crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Add the blended tomato mixture and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the stock, curry powder, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Add the whole Scotch bonnet.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the Scotch bonnet, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Groundnut Soup with Chicken
ingredients: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: Season the chicken with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Blend the onion, ginger, and garlic with 1 cup of the water or stock.
Pour the blended mixture into the pot and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with 2 cups of the remaining water or stock until smooth, then add it to the pot with the rest of the liquid.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the whole Scotch bonnet. Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked and the soup is rich.
Remove the pepper and serve the soup hot with rice or fufu.

title: Waakye (Rice and Beans)
instructions: Put the peas, water, and baking soda in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 to 40 minutes, until the peas are nearly tender.
Stir in the rice, salt, and vegetable oil. Add a little water if needed so the rice is just covered.
Cover the pot and cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the waakye, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve with stew or shito.

title: Kontomire Stew with Boiled Yam
ingredients: 1 pound fresh cocoyam leaves, washed and chopped, or 10 ounces frozen chopped spinach, thawed
1 pound white yam, peeled and cut into chunks
1 smoked mackerel fillet, skin and bones removed and flaked
instructions: Put the yam in a pot, cover with water, and boil for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender. Drain and keep warm.
Put the cocoyam leaves or spinach in a pot with 1 cup water. Cover and cook until soft, about 10 minutes; drain well and chop finely if using leaves.
Heat the palm oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Stir in the cooked leaves, flaked mackerel, dried shrimp, salt, and Scotch bonnet. Simmer for 10 minutes, adding a splash of water if the stew is too thick.
Remove the pepper and serve the stew with the boiled yam.

title: Thieboudienne (Fish and Rice)
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish, cut into 4 pieces
instructions: Pound the parsley, garlic, salt, pepper, and half the Scotch bonnet into a rough paste.
Make a slit in each fish piece and rub in the paste; set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the fish briefly on both sides; remove and set aside.
Cook the onion in the pot until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down, then pour in the water and add the bay leaf.
Add the carrots, cabbage, eggplant, and turnip; simmer until just tender, then remove the vegetables.
Return the fish to the pot and simmer gently until cooked through; remove it and keep warm.
Stir the tamarind paste into the broth, then add the rinsed rice and the remaining Scotch bonnet.
Cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and has absorbed the broth, stirring once or twice.
Serve the rice with the fish and vegetables.

title: Yassa Poulet (Lemon-Onion Chicken)
instructions: Mix the onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, black pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Add the chicken and turn to coat; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Lift the chicken from the marinade and reserve the onion mixture.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add the onions and marinade to the pot and cook, stirring, until the onions soften and begin to caramelize.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the bay leaf, Scotch bonnet, and water.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in salted water until tender; drain if needed.
Serve the chicken and onions over the rice.

title: Mafé (Peanut Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they soften and release their juices.
Whisk the peanut butter with a cup of stock until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the remaining stock.
Return the beef to the pot and add the sweet potatoes, carrots, cabbage, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the beef and vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, taking care not to break the Scotch bonnet if you want a milder stew.
Serve hot with cooked rice.

title: Thiakry (Millet Couscous with Yogurt)
instructions: Put the millet couscous in a heatproof bowl and pour over 1 cup boiling water.
Cover and let stand for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork and allow it to cool.
Whisk together the yogurt, sour cream, milk, sugar, vanilla, and nutmeg.
Stir the cooled couscous and raisins into the yogurt mixture.
Chill for at least 30 minutes and serve cold.

title: Accara (Black-Eyed Pea Fritters)
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: Soak the black-eyed peas in plenty of water overnight, then drain.
Rub the peas between your hands in a bowl of water to loosen their skins; skim off the skins and repeat until most are removed.
Drain the peas well and blend them with the onion, Scotch bonnet, salt, pepper, and water until thick and smooth.
Beat the batter vigorously for 2 minutes to make it airy.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil, working in batches, and fry until golden and cooked through, turning as needed.
Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate and serve hot.

title: Ugali
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy saucepan; add the salt if using.
Reduce the heat and gradually stir in the maize meal, breaking up lumps.
Cook, stirring and folding firmly with a wooden spoon, until thick and pulling away from the sides, about 8–10 minutes.
Turn onto a plate and serve hot.

title: Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens (sukuma wiki), stems removed and leaves thinly sliced
instructions: Warm the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Stir in the sliced greens, water, and salt.
Cover and cook for 5–8 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender but still green.

title: Githeri
ingredients: 2 cups dried maize kernels, soaked overnight and drained
2 cups dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the maize, beans, and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the maize and beans are tender, about 1 1/2–2 hours; add water if needed.
Heat the oil in a separate pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until saucy, then stir in the potato and salt.
Add the cooked maize and beans with a little of their cooking liquid; simmer until the potato is tender and the flavors come together.

title: Kenyan Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef in batches; set it aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot until softened, then add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Return the beef to the pot and add the stock, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer until tender, about 20–25 minutes.

title: Chapati
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for rolling
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus extra for cooking
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl; stir in 1 tablespoon oil and the warm water to make a soft dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth, about 8 minutes; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a thin circle, dusting with flour as needed.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and cook each chapati until bubbles appear and brown spots form, about 1–2 minutes per side.
Brush lightly with oil if desired and keep covered in a clean towel until serving.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it out and reserve the milk.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the soaked bread, jam, chutney, raisins, lemon juice, and salt.
Spoon the mixture into a greased baking dish and smooth the top. Beat the eggs with the reserved milk and pour over the mince.
Place the bay leaves on top and bake for 35–40 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.

title: Boerewors and Pap with Tomato and Onion Relish
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan. Gradually whisk in the maize meal.
Cover and cook over low heat for 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pap is thick and cooked through. Stir in the butter.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the relish for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Grill or pan-fry the boerewors over medium heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through. Serve with the pap and relish.

title: Samp and Beans
instructions: Rinse the samp and beans, cover generously with cold water, and soak overnight.
Drain and place in a large pot with fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 2–3 hours until tender, adding hot water if needed.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the onion, salt, and pepper into the samp and beans. Simmer for 10 minutes more.
Stir in the butter and serve hot.

title: Chakalaka
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Stir in the curry powder and paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the carrots, tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Cover partially and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the mixture is thick.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve warm or chilled as a relish.

title: Malva Pudding
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium baking dish.
Beat the sugar and egg until pale and thick. Beat in the apricot jam.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Stir the vinegar, melted butter, and milk into the egg mixture.
Fold in the dry ingredients until just combined. Pour the batter into the baking dish.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until risen and deeply golden.
While the pudding bakes, heat the cream, butter, sugar, and hot water in a saucepan, stirring until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot sauce over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven. Let it soak for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and Vegemite.
Simmer until thickened, then cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Spoon in the filling and top with puff pastry. Seal the edges and cut a small vent in each pie.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually beat in the caster sugar until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Spoon the meringue onto the tray and shape into a round with a shallow centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar and spread it over the cooled pavlova.
Top with kiwifruit, strawberries, and passionfruit pulp.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Stir the bicarbonate of soda into the boiling water, then mix it into the butter mixture.
Pour the butter mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoonfuls of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving room to spread.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until golden, then cool on the trays.

title: New Zealand Lamb Roast
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Make small cuts in the lamb and tuck in the garlic slices.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Place the lamb in a roasting pan and roast for 30 minutes per 500 g, or until cooked to your liking.
Add the potatoes to the pan for the final 60 minutes, turning them once.
Transfer the lamb and potatoes to a platter to rest for 15 minutes.
Skim excess fat from the pan juices, stir in the flour, then gradually whisk in the stock.
Simmer the gravy until smooth and thickened, then serve with the lamb and potatoes.

title: New Zealand Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
ingredients: ½ cup caster sugar, for the hokey pokey
instructions: Line a small tray with baking paper.
Heat the ½ cup caster sugar and golden syrup in a saucepan until bubbling and amber-coloured.
Remove from the heat, quickly stir in the bicarbonate of soda, and pour onto the tray. Cool completely, then break into small pieces.
Whisk the egg yolks with the remaining caster sugar until pale.
Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until steaming, then slowly whisk into the yolks.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook over low heat, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in the vanilla and chill the custard until cold.
Churn in an ice-cream maker according to its instructions, folding in the hokey pokey pieces near the end. Freeze until firm.

title: Australian Lamingtons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time and add the vanilla.
Fold in the flour in two batches, alternating with the milk.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then cut it into 16 squares.
Whisk the icing sugar and cocoa with the boiling water until smooth.
Dip each cake square in the chocolate icing, then roll it in coconut and leave it to set.

title: New Zealand Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar gradually, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray into a 20 cm round, making a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside with the door closed.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the cooled pavlova with cream, kiwifruit, and strawberries.

title: Australian Meat Pie
ingredients: 500 g beef chuck, cut into 1 cm cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a 20 cm pie tin with the shortcrust pastry.
Spoon in the cooled filling and cover with the puff pastry, pressing the edges to seal.
Trim the pastry, cut a small vent in the top, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: New Zealand Hāngī-Style Roast
ingredients: 1 kg kumara, peeled and cut into chunks
600 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
500 g pumpkin, seeded and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and place a large roasting pan in the oven to warm.
Toss the pork, chicken, kumara, potatoes, pumpkin, and onions with the oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the meat and vegetables in the hot pan and pour the stock around them.
Cover the pan tightly with a lid or foil and roast for 3 hours, until the meat is tender and the vegetables are soft.
Remove the cover and roast for 20 minutes to brown the top.
Rest the meat for 10 minutes, then serve with the vegetables and pan juices.

title: Australian Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, then rub in the butter until the mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Make a well in the centre and add the milk and water.
Mix with a butter knife until a soft dough forms, adding a little flour if it is sticky.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and shape it into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
Cool slightly before slicing and serving.

title: Australian Lamingtons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.
Fold in the flour alternately with the milk until just combined.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely, then cut into squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl. Stir in the boiling water and extra butter until smooth.
Dip each cake square in the chocolate icing, then roll it in desiccated coconut. Set on a rack to dry.

title: New Zealand Hāngī-Style Roast
ingredients: 1 kg kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
500 g pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Rub the lamb with oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the kūmara, potatoes, pumpkin, and onions in a large roasting pan. Pour in the stock.
Place the lamb on top and cover the pan tightly with foil.
Roast for 4 hours, until the lamb is tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the vegetables and pan juices.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Grease four individual pie tins.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Add the mince and brown, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually stir in the stock, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and Vegemite.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes, until the filling is thick. Cool slightly.
Line the pie tins with shortcrust pastry and divide the filling among them.
Cut puff pastry lids to fit. Place them over the filling, press the edges to seal, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the pastry is golden.

title: New Zealand Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add the sugar, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture into a 20 cm circle on the tray, making a slight dip in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form. Spoon it over the pavlova and top with kiwifruit and strawberries.

title: Australian Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Combine the flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Add the milk and water and mix to form a soft dough. Knead gently until just smooth.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and place it on the tray. Cut a deep cross into the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped on the base.
Cool slightly before serving.

title: Australian Meat Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef and garlic; cook, breaking up the mince, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes, stirring, until thick. Cool the filling.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Spoon in the filling and cover each pie with puff pastry. Press the edges to seal and trim excess pastry.
Brush with beaten egg and cut a small slit in each pie.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: New Zealand Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar gradually, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray and shape it into a round with a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside with the door closed.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread it over the cooled pavlova.
Top with kiwifruit and strawberries before serving.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.
Fold in the flour alternately with the milk until just combined.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then cut it into squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl. Stir in the melted butter and boiling water to make a smooth icing.
Dip each cake square in the icing, then roll it in coconut.
Place the lamingtons on a rack to set.

title: New Zealand Hāngī-Style Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 1.2 kg boneless pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
1 kg kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F).
Toss the pork with the oil, salt, and pepper.
Place the kūmara, potatoes, carrots, and onion in a large roasting pan.
Arrange the pork over the vegetables and pour the stock into the pan.
Sprinkle with rosemary and cover the pan tightly with a lid or foil.
Roast for 3 hours, until the pork is very tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Remove the cover and roast for 15 minutes more to brown the pork lightly.
Serve the pork with the vegetables and pan juices.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F) and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut, and brown sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir the baking soda into the boiling water, then mix it into the melted butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving space between each.
Flatten the balls slightly and bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden.
Cool on the trays for a few minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick. Cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a pie dish with shortcrust pastry and add the filling.
Cover with puff pastry, seal the edges, and cut a small steam vent. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar gradually, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar, and vanilla.
Shape the meringue into a high round with a shallow hollow in the center.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside until cool.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the cooled pavlova with cream, kiwifruit, and strawberries.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water, then stir it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoonfuls into balls and place them on the trays, leaving room to spread.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden. Cool on the trays.

title: New Zealand Hāngī-Style Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 kg boneless pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
700 g kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Place the kūmara, potatoes, carrots, and onion in a large roasting dish.
Arrange the pork on top and pour the water around the vegetables.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and roast for 3 hours, until the pork is tender.
Remove the foil and roast for 15 minutes to brown the pork lightly.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: New Zealand Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
ingredients: ½ cup caster sugar, for the hokey pokey
instructions: Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until steaming, but do not boil.
Whisk the egg yolks with ¾ cup sugar in a bowl.
Gradually whisk the hot cream mixture into the yolks, then return it all to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard lightly coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the vanilla, cool the custard, then chill until cold.
Line a tray with baking paper. Heat ½ cup sugar and the golden syrup in a saucepan until bubbling and amber.
Remove from the heat, quickly stir in the baking soda, and pour onto the tray. Cool completely, then break into small pieces.
Churn the chilled custard in an ice-cream maker, folding in the hokey-pokey pieces near the end. Freeze until firm.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar gradually, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray in a round, making a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread it over the cooled pavlova.
Top with kiwifruit and strawberries before serving.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda in the boiling water, then stir it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving room to spread.
Flatten each ball slightly and bake for 12–15 minutes until golden.
Cool on the trays for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

title: Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and Vegemite.
Simmer for 10–15 minutes until thick, then let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Divide the filling among the tins and cover each with puff pastry.
Trim and seal the edges, cut a small slit in each top and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed and golden.

title: New Zealand Hāngī
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
1.5 kg lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
1 kg kumara, peeled and cut into chunks
1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
500 g pumpkin, seeded and cut into chunks
1 large banana leaf or several cabbage leaves
instructions: Season the pork and lamb with salt.
Arrange the kumara, potatoes and pumpkin in a large roasting pan or deep casserole.
Place the meat and cabbage on top, then add the water.
Cover the food with the banana leaf or cabbage leaves.
Seal the pan tightly with foil and a lid.
Bake at 160°C for about 4 hours, until the meat is tender and the vegetables are cooked through.
Carefully remove the cover and serve the meat and vegetables together.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a square cake tin with baking paper.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale and creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.
Fold in the flour alternately with the milk until just combined.
Spoon the batter into the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then cut it into 16 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl, then stir in the melted butter and boiling water to make a smooth icing.
Dip each cake square in the icing, then roll it in coconut.
Place the lamingtons on a wire rack to set.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan-forced) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar gradually, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray in a round, making a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form and spread it over the pavlova.
Top with the kiwifruit and strawberries before serving.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan-forced) and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda in the boiling water, then stir it into the butter mixture.
Pour the butter mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving room to spread.
Flatten each ball slightly and bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden.
Leave the biscuits on the trays for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a rack to cool.

title: New Zealand Lamb Roast
ingredients: 1.5 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced).
Make small cuts over the lamb and tuck the garlic slices into them.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Place the potatoes in a roasting pan and set the lamb on top.
Roast for about 1 hour 45 minutes, or until cooked to your liking, turning the potatoes once.
Transfer the lamb and potatoes to a platter, cover loosely with foil and rest for 15 minutes.
Pour off most of the fat from the pan and place the pan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour, then gradually whisk in the stock and simmer until thickened.
Carve the lamb and serve with the potatoes and gravy.

title: Australian Meat Pie
ingredients: 500 g beef chuck, cut into 1 cm cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced).
Heat the oil in a saucepan and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, tomato sauce and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the filling is thick.
Cool the filling completely.
Line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry and divide the filling among them.
Cover with puff pastry, press the edges to seal and trim away excess pastry.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and cut a small vent in each pie.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden.

title: New Zealand Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
ingredients: ½ cup caster sugar, for the hokey pokey
2 tablespoons golden syrup, for the hokey pokey
1 teaspoon bicarbonate of soda, for the hokey pokey
instructions: Line a small tray with baking paper.
Heat ½ cup caster sugar and the golden syrup in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until dissolved.
Let the mixture bubble for 3–4 minutes until golden, then remove it from the heat and quickly stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
Pour the honeycomb onto the tray, leave it to cool and set, then break it into small pieces.
Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk the egg yolks and remaining ¾ cup sugar in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the hot cream mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon; do not boil.
Stir in the vanilla and chill the custard until cold.
Churn in an ice-cream maker according to its instructions, folding in the hokey pokey pieces near the end.
Freeze until firm before serving.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste.
Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick. Cool the filling.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a pie dish with the shortcrust pastry.
Spoon in the cooled filling and cover with the puff pastry. Trim and seal the edges, then cut a small slit in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Shape the meringue into a 20 cm circle on the tray, making a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the pavlova with cream, kiwifruit, and strawberries just before serving.

title: New Zealand Lamb Roast
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Make small cuts in the lamb and insert the garlic slices.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the potatoes, carrots, and onion in a roasting pan and pour in the water.
Place the lamb on top of the vegetables and roast for about 1 hour 45 minutes, or until cooked to your preference.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving. Serve with the roasted vegetables.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut, and brown sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Stir the baking soda into the boiling water, then mix it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls and place them on the trays, leaving room to spread.
Flatten slightly and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden. Cool on the trays.

title: New Zealand Cheese Rolls
ingredients: 12 slices white sandwich bread, crusts removed
instructions: Place the cheese, onion, evaporated milk, butter, mustard powder, and salt in a saucepan.
Heat gently, stirring, until the cheese melts and the mixture thickens. Stir in the parsley and cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over each bread slice.
Roll up each slice tightly and place seam-side down on the tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.

title: Australian Lamingtons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla.
Fold in the flour alternately with the milk until just combined.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely, then cut into 16 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl. Stir in the boiling water and extra butter until smooth.
Dip each cake square in the icing, let excess drip off, then roll in coconut. Leave on a rack until set.

title: New Zealand Pavlova
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add the caster sugar, beating until glossy and stiff.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray in a 20 cm circle, making a slight dip in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form. Top the pavlova with cream, kiwifruit and strawberries just before serving.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and beef stock. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Mix the cornflour with the cold water, stir it into the mince and simmer until thick. Cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line four individual pie tins with shortcrust pastry and fill with the cooled mixture.
Cut puff pastry lids to fit, place them over the filling and press the edges to seal. Brush with beaten egg and cut a small slit in each lid.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden.

instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Pat the pork dry and rub it with oil, salt and pepper.
Arrange the kūmara, potatoes and onions in a deep roasting pan. Set the pork on top.
Pour the stock around the vegetables and sprinkle the rosemary over everything.
Cover the pan tightly with a lid or foil and roast for 3 hours, until the pork is very tender.
Uncover and roast for 20–30 minutes to brown the pork. Rest for 15 minutes before serving with the vegetables and pan juices.

title: Australian Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and lightly grease a baking tray.
Combine the flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Make a well in the centre and pour in the milk. Mix with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently until smooth. Shape into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on the tray and brush with the extra milk. Cut a cross about 1 cm deep into the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped. Cool slightly before serving.

title: Australian Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
