Simmer gently for 60–75 minutes until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick; cool the filling.
Line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry and divide the filling among them.
Cover each pie with puff pastry, press the edges to seal and cut a small slit in each top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes until golden.

title: Hokey Pokey Ice Cream
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with ¼ cup of the sugar in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the cream, milk and remaining ½ cup sugar in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Gradually whisk the hot cream mixture into the yolks, then return everything to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in the vanilla, transfer the custard to a bowl and chill until completely cold.
Line a small tray with baking paper and warm the golden syrup in a saucepan until bubbling.
Stir in the bicarbonate of soda, pour the foaming mixture onto the tray and let it cool until hard.
Break the hokey pokey into small pieces and fold them into the chilled custard.
Churn in an ice-cream maker according to its instructions, then freeze until firm.

title: Lamb Roast with Garlic and Rosemary
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Make small cuts all over the lamb and tuck in the garlic slivers.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Place in a roasting pan and pour the water into the pan.
Roast for about 1 hour 45 minutes, basting occasionally, until cooked to your liking.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: West Australian Fish and Chips
ingredients: 800 g firm white fish fillets, cut into 4 portions
1 cup plain flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Soak the potato chips in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Heat the oven to 120°C and heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 160°C.
Fry the chips in batches for 5 minutes, then drain on a rack.
Whisk the flour, beer, baking powder and salt into a smooth batter.
Raise the oil temperature to 180°C.
Dust the fish with flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches for 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Fry the chips again for 2–3 minutes until crisp, then serve with the fish and lemon.

title: Kangaroo Steaks with Bush Tomato Chutney
instructions: Bring the kangaroo steaks to room temperature and pat dry.
Rub with olive oil, salt and pepper.
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat and cook the steaks for 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Transfer the steaks to a plate and rest for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in the pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Stir in the bush tomato chutney and warm through.
Serve the steaks with the chutney.

title: Sausage Sizzle with Onions
instructions: Heat a barbecue hotplate or large frying pan to medium heat.
Add the oil and cook the onions, stirring, for 10–12 minutes until soft and golden.
Cook the sausages, turning often, for 12–15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Place each sausage on a slice of bread.
Top with onions, tomato sauce and mustard.

title: Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the milk and mix gently to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape into a round loaf.
Place on the tray, brush with milk and cut a cross in the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Tasmanian scallop pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the fish stock and milk; simmer until thickened.
Add the scallops, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Cook gently for 2 minutes, then cool slightly.
Line a pie dish with one sheet of pastry and spoon in the filling.
Cover with the second pastry sheet, seal the edges and cut a small slit in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.

title: Tasmanian wallaby stew
ingredients: 750 g wallaby meat, cut into 3 cm cubes
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Toss the wallaby with the flour, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and brown the meat in batches; set aside.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the casserole until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the meat to the casserole and add the stock, bay leaf and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 30–40 minutes, until the meat and potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme sprig, then serve hot.

title: Tasmanian curried scallop mornay
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven grill to medium-high.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the flour and curry powder; cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Stir in half the cheese, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Add the scallops and cook gently for 2 minutes.
Spoon into a shallow ovenproof dish and scatter over the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese.
Grill for 3–5 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

title: Tasmanian lamb roast with mint sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Rub the lamb with olive oil, salt and pepper, then make small cuts and tuck in the garlic and rosemary.
Place the lamb in a roasting pan and pour the water into the pan.
Roast for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Roast for about 1 hour and 20 minutes, or until cooked to your liking, basting occasionally.
Transfer the lamb to a board, cover loosely with foil and rest for 20 minutes.
For the mint sauce, stir the sugar into the boiling water until dissolved.
Mix in the mint and vinegar, then serve with the sliced lamb.

title: Tasmanian apple and berry crumble
ingredients: 5 Tasmanian apples, peeled, cored and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Toss the apples and blackberries with the caster sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Spoon the fruit into a baking dish.
Mix the oats, flour and brown sugar in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until the mixture forms coarse crumbs.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Hangi-Inspired Chicken and Vegetables
ingredients: 500 g kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Put the chicken, kūmara, potatoes, carrots and cabbage in a large roasting dish.
Sprinkle with salt and add the water. Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Remove the foil and roast for 10 minutes to brown the chicken slightly.

title: Pāua Fritters
instructions: Mix the pāua, onion, eggs, flour, parsley, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon the mixture into the pan to make small fritters, flattening them gently.
Cook for 2–3 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through.

title: Rewena Paraoa (Māori Bread)
ingredients: ¾ cup warm water, plus more as needed
instructions: Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the rewena starter and warm water, then mix to form a soft dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes, adding a little flour or water if needed.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover and leave in a warm place until doubled in size, about 4–6 hours.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a greased baking tray. Cover and rise for 30 minutes.
Bake at 200°C for 30–35 minutes, until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Bacon and Egg Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C. Grease a 20 cm pie dish and line it with one sheet of pastry.
Scatter the bacon, onion and peas over the pastry-lined dish.
Crack the eggs into the dish, keeping the yolks whole where possible. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover with the second pastry sheet, press the edges to seal and cut a small slit in the top.
Brush the pastry with milk and bake for 35–40 minutes, until puffed and golden.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water, then stir it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls, place them on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden. Cool on the trays.

title: Māori Hāngī-Style Roast Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and put the pork and vegetables in a large covered roasting dish.
Rub the pork with oil and salt, then arrange the vegetables around it.
Pour the water into the dish and cover tightly with a lid or foil.
Roast for 3½ to 4 hours, until the pork is tender and the vegetables are cooked.
Serve hot with the cooking juices.

title: New Zealand Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, tomato sauce and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a pie tin with shortcrust pastry and add the filling.
Cover with puff pastry, seal the edges and cut a small slit in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden.

title: Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar, cornflour and vanilla.
Shape the meringue into a 20 cm round on the tray, leaving a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form, spoon it over the pavlova and top with kiwifruit and strawberries.

title: Afghan Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cream the butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift in the flour and cocoa, then mix until combined.
Fold in the cornflakes without crushing them too much.
Place heaped tablespoonfuls on the tray and bake for 15 minutes.
Mix the icing sugar, cocoa and hot water into a smooth icing.
Ice the cooled biscuits and top each with a walnut half.

title: Whitebait Fritters
instructions: Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Gently fold in the whitebait.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in small portions of the mixture and cook for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until set and lightly golden.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Canterbury Roast Lamb
ingredients: 1.5 kg floury potatoes, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Pat the lamb dry and make small cuts all over it.
Push garlic slices into the cuts, then rub the lamb with rosemary, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Put the lamb in a roasting dish and roast for about 1 hour 30 minutes, or until cooked to your liking. Rest under foil for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, parboil the potatoes for 8 minutes and drain well. Toss with dripping or oil.
Roast the potatoes alongside the lamb for 60–75 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Cook the peas in boiling water until tender, then drain and serve with the lamb and potatoes.

title: Southland Cheese Rolls
instructions: Put the evaporated milk, butter, onion, mustard powder, salt and pepper in a saucepan.
Warm gently, stirring, until the butter melts and the onion softens. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in the cheese until melted and thick. Cool until spreadable.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the cheese mixture over the bread and roll each slice up tightly.
Place the rolls seam-side down on a baking tray and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden.

title: Māori Boil-Up
ingredients: 1.2 kg pork bones or meaty pork ribs
500 g floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
½ small cabbage, cut into wedges
250 g watercress or silverbeet, roughly chopped
instructions: Put the pork, water, salt and onion in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover partly and simmer for 1½ hours, until the pork is tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes, then stir in the watercress or silverbeet.
Cook for 3–5 minutes more, until the greens are tender. Taste the broth and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Whitebait Fritters
instructions: Whisk the eggs, flour, milk, salt and pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Gently fold in the whitebait.
Heat the butter and oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in small rounds of batter and cook for 2–3 minutes, until set and golden underneath.
Turn carefully and cook for 1–2 minutes more. Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Pavlova with Kiwifruit
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the mixture is glossy and stiff.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Pile the meringue onto the tray and shape it into a round with a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool inside with the door closed.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Top the cooled pavlova with cream, kiwifruit and strawberries just before serving.

title: Sydney-Style Barramundi with Lemon and Parsley
ingredients: 1 lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges
instructions: Pat the barramundi dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the fillets skin-side down for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp.
Turn and cook for 2–3 minutes, until just cooked through.
Add the lemon juice and parsley, then serve with lemon wedges.

title: Aussie Meat Pie
ingredients: 500 g beef chuck, cut into 1 cm cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock.
Mix in the tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and Vegemite.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick; cool completely.
Preheat the oven to 200°C and line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry.
Fill the pastry shells with the beef mixture and top with puff pastry.
Trim and seal the edges, brush with beaten egg, and cut a small slit in each lid.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.

title: Sausage Rolls
ingredients: 500 g beef and pork sausage mince
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the sausage mince, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, tomato sauce and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl.
Cut each pastry sheet in half lengthways and divide the filling into four log shapes.
Place a log along one edge of each pastry strip, roll up and seal the seam underneath.
Cut each roll into four pieces and place them on the tray.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until puffed and golden and the filling is cooked through.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir the bicarbonate of soda into the boiling water, then mix it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until combined.
Roll tablespoonfuls into balls, place them on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden, then cool on the trays.

title: Pavlova with Cream and Passionfruit
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the vinegar and cornflour.
Spoon the mixture into a 20 cm circle on the tray and make a slight dip in the centre.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the pavlova with cream, passionfruit and strawberries just before serving.

title: Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and Vegemite.
Simmer until thick, then cool the filling completely.
Line a pie tin with shortcrust pastry and spoon in the filling.
Cover with puff pastry, seal the edges and cut a small steam vent.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until golden.

title: Sausage Rolls
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, egg, tomato sauce and thyme in a bowl.
Cut each pastry sheet in half lengthways and shape the mince mixture into logs along the centre of each piece.
Roll the pastry around the filling and place seam-side down.
Cut each log into rolls and arrange them on the tray.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed and cooked through.

title: Lamb Roast with Mint Sauce
ingredients: ½ cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Make small cuts in the lamb and tuck in the garlic slices.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Place in a roasting pan with 1 cup water and roast for about 1 hour 45 minutes, or until cooked to your liking.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving.
For the mint sauce, stir the mint and sugar together, add the boiling water and vinegar, and leave for 15 minutes.
Serve the carved lamb with the mint sauce and pan juices.

title: Chicken Parmigiana
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Place the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan in separate shallow dishes.
Coat each piece of chicken in flour, egg and breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a pan and brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes on each side.
Arrange the chicken on the tray, spoon over the tomato sauce and scatter with mozzarella.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the cheese is golden.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Shape the mixture into a round on the tray, making a shallow dip in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside until completely cool.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the pavlova with cream, kiwifruit, strawberries and passionfruit pulp before serving.

title: Queensland Prawn Curry
ingredients: 500 g green prawns, peeled and deveined
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, coconut milk and salt, then simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 4–5 minutes, until pink and just cooked through.
Serve hot with cooked rice.

title: Moreton Bay Bug Mornay
ingredients: 4 cooked Moreton Bay bugs, split lengthways
instructions: Remove the bug meat from the shells, chop it roughly and set the shells aside.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until thick and smooth.
Stir in the cheese, white pepper and bug meat.
Spoon the mixture into the shells, top with breadcrumbs and parsley, and grill until golden.

title: Queensland Pumpkin Scones
ingredients: ½ cup mashed cooked pumpkin, cooled
¼ cup milk, plus extra for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Sift the flour, sugar and salt into a bowl, then rub in the butter until the mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Mix the pumpkin, egg and milk in a jug.
Add the pumpkin mixture to the flour and stir gently until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured bench, pat it to 2 cm thick and cut into rounds.
Place the scones close together on the tray, brush with milk and bake for 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.

title: Lamb and Macadamia Damper
ingredients: ½ cup roasted macadamias, roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Combine the flour and salt in a bowl, then rub in the butter until crumbly.
Stir in the macadamias and rosemary.
Add the milk and mix until a soft dough forms.
Shape into a round loaf and place on the tray; cut a cross in the top and brush with milk.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.

title: Golden Syrup Dumplings
instructions: Rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the milk to make a soft dough, then roll into 8 small balls.
Combine the water, golden syrup, sugar, extra butter and lemon juice in a wide saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the dumplings, cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, turning them once.
Serve the dumplings with the syrup.

title: Noongar Kangaroo and Bush Tomato Stew
ingredients: 700 g kangaroo shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the kangaroo with salt and pepper, then toss it with the flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the kangaroo in batches; set aside.
Cook the onion and carrots in the pot until softened, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste.
Return the kangaroo to the pot and add the stock, bush tomato powder and rosemary.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the meat is tender.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve hot.

title: Swan River Marron with Lemon Butter
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil.
Add the marron and cook for 6–8 minutes, until just cooked through.
Melt the butter in a small pan and stir in the lemon juice, parsley and garlic.
Split the cooked marron lengthwise and season lightly with pepper.
Spoon over the lemon butter and serve straight away.

title: West Australian Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 firm white fish fillets, about 180 g each
1 cup plain flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Soak the potato chips in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and dry well.
Heat the oil to 150°C and fry the chips for 5 minutes; drain on paper towel.
Whisk the flour, beer, baking powder and salt into a smooth batter.
Dust the fish lightly with flour, then coat each fillet in batter.
Raise the oil to 180°C and fry the fish until golden and cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Fry the chips again until crisp and golden, then serve with the fish and lemon wedges.

title: West Australian Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the milk and enough water to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a round loaf.
Place on the tray and cut a shallow cross on top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.

title: West Australian Lamingtons
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour alternately with the milk until just combined.
Spread the batter in the tin and bake for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then cut it into squares.
Whisk the icing sugar and cocoa with the boiling water and melted butter.
Dip each cake square in the chocolate icing, roll it in coconut and leave to set.

title: Tasmanian Scallop Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the flour, then gradually whisk in the milk until smooth and thickened.
Add the scallops, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper; cook gently for 2 minutes.
Spoon the filling into a pie dish and cover with pastry. Trim and seal the edges, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden.

title: Tasmanian Wallaby Stew
ingredients: 800 g wallaby shoulder, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Toss the wallaby in flour, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and brown the meat in batches; set aside.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the casserole until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the meat to the casserole and add the stock, bay leaf and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 2–2½ hours, until the meat is tender.

title: Tasmanian Curried Scallop Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a pie dish with the pastry.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the flour and curry powder, then gradually whisk in the milk and fish stock.
Cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens; season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the scallops and parsley, then spoon the filling into the pastry case.
Cover with a pastry lid, seal the edges and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.

title: Tasmanian Leatherwood Honey Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 20 cm cake tin.
Beat the butter and honey until creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour and cinnamon alternately with the milk.
Spoon the batter into the tin and smooth the top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

title: Tasmanian Apple and Blackberry Crumble
ingredients: 4 Tasmanian apples, peeled, cored and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Toss the apples and blackberries with the sugar and lemon juice, then spread in a baking dish.
Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the oats, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit is bubbling.

title: Auckland-Style Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 thick fillets firm white fish, such as tarakihi or hoki
1 cup plain flour, plus extra for dusting
4 large agria potatoes, cut into chips
instructions: Soak the potato chips in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 150°C. Fry the chips in batches for 5 minutes, then drain.
Whisk the flour, beer, baking powder, and salt into a smooth batter.
Dust the fish lightly with flour, dip it in the batter, and fry at 180°C until golden and cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Fry the chips again at 180°C until crisp and golden. Drain and season with salt.
Serve hot with lemon and malt vinegar.

title: Māori Hāngī-Style Chicken and Vegetables
ingredients: 4 large banana leaves, rinsed, or 2 sheets baking paper and foil
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Arrange the kūmara, potatoes, carrots, and cabbage on the leaves or baking paper, then place the chicken on top.
Sprinkle with water and wrap everything into a tightly sealed parcel.
Place the parcel in a roasting dish and bake at 160°C for about 2 hours, until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Open carefully and serve with the cooking juices.

title: Boil-Up with Pork Bones and Doughboys
ingredients: 1 kg pork bones or pork hocks
2 kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the pork, water, salt, and onion in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 1½ hours, skimming the surface as needed.
Stir the flour and water together to make a soft dough, then shape into 8 dumplings.
Add the potatoes and kūmara to the pot and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the dumplings and cabbage, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the watercress and cook for 3 minutes, then serve the broth, meat, and vegetables together.

title: Pavlova with Kiwifruit
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form, then add the sugar gradually, beating until glossy and stiff.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar, and vanilla.
Spoon the meringue into a thick round on the tray and make a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, spread it over the pavlova, and top with kiwifruit and strawberries.

title: Afghan Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cream the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy.
Sift in the flour and cocoa, then fold in the cornflakes.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls, place on the tray, and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15 minutes, then cool on the tray.
Mix the icing sugar, cocoa, and hot water into a thick icing.
Ice each biscuit and top with a walnut half.

title: Roast Lamb with Mint Sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Make small cuts in the lamb and tuck in the garlic. Rub with oil, salt, and pepper.
Place in a roasting dish and roast for about 1 hour 30 minutes, or until cooked to your liking.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving.
Stir the mint, boiling water, vinegar, and sugar together; serve with the lamb.

title: Hāngī-Style Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
500 g kūmara, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Arrange the pork, pumpkin, kūmara, potatoes, and onion in a large covered roasting dish.
Pour in the stock and season with salt and pepper.
Cover tightly and bake for 3 hours, until the pork is tender and the vegetables are cooked.
Serve hot with the cooking juices.

title: Whitebait Fritters
instructions: Whisk the eggs, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Gently fold in the whitebait.
Heat the butter and oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in small portions of the mixture and cook for 2 minutes on each side, until just set and golden.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Rewena Paraoa
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add the potato starter and warm water, then mix to form a soft dough.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 minutes, until smooth.
Place in a greased bowl, cover, and leave in a warm place until doubled in size, about 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Shape the dough into a round loaf and place on a greased baking tray.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Cool before slicing.

title: Pavlova with Kiwi Fruit
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the mixture is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar, and vanilla.
Pile the mixture onto the tray and shape into a round mound.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until softly peaked, spread it over the pavlova, and top with kiwifruit and strawberries.

title: Lamb Roast with Mint Sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C. Make small cuts in the lamb and tuck in the garlic.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then place it in a roasting tin.
Roast for about 1 hour 30 minutes, or until cooked to your liking, basting occasionally.
Mix the mint, vinegar, sugar, and boiling water. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with mint sauce.

title: Southland Cheese Rolls
ingredients: 12 slices white sandwich bread, crusts removed
instructions: Put the onion, cheese, evaporated milk, butter, mustard powder, and salt in a saucepan.
Warm over low heat, stirring, until the cheese melts and the mixture thickens. Cool slightly.
Spread the cheese mixture over the bread slices and roll them up tightly.
Place the rolls seam-side down on a baking tray.
Bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: Hokey Pokey
instructions: Line a small tin with baking paper.
Put the sugar and golden syrup in a saucepan and stir over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil and cook without stirring for 4–5 minutes, until the mixture turns golden.
Remove from the heat and quickly stir in the baking soda; the mixture will foam up.
Pour into the tin and leave to set, then break into pieces.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form, then gradually beat in the caster sugar until thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla.
Pile the mixture onto the tray, shape into a round, and make a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar, spread it over the pavlova, and top with kiwifruit and strawberries.

title: Anzac Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut, and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water and stir it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and mix well.
Roll tablespoonfuls into balls, place them on the trays, and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until golden, then cool on the trays.

title: Sydney Rock Oysters with Lemon
instructions: Arrange the oysters on a bed of ice or a chilled plate.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and cracked pepper.

title: Sausage Sizzle
instructions: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and browned.
Cook the sausages on a barbecue or in a separate pan, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Place each sausage on a slice of bread, top with onion, and add tomato or barbecue sauce.

title: Meat Pie with Tomato Sauce
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick, then cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line four pie tins with shortcrust pastry and divide the filling among them.
Cover with puff pastry, press the edges to seal, brush with beaten egg, and cut a small slit in each top.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden. Serve with tomato sauce.

title: Chicken Parmigiana
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Coat each piece in flour, dip it in egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the chicken in batches until golden on both sides; transfer to a baking tray.
Mix the passata with oregano and spoon it over the chicken.
Top with mozzarella and Parmesan, then bake for 12–15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the cheese is bubbling.

title: Pavlova with Cream and Fruit
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form, then add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until glossy and thick.
Gently fold in the vinegar and cornflour.
Spoon the mixture onto the tray in a round, making a slight hollow in the centre.
Bake for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and let the pavlova cool completely inside.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form, spread it over the pavlova, and top with the kiwifruit, strawberries, and passionfruit.

title: Lamb Roast with Vegetables
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Pat the lamb dry, then rub it with olive oil, garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Put the potatoes, carrots and onions in a roasting pan and pour in the water.
Set the lamb on top of the vegetables and roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce the oven to 180°C and roast for about 1 hour 15 minutes, or until cooked to your liking.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving; serve with the roast vegetables.

title: Meat Pie
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock.
Add the tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and Vegemite; simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a pie dish with shortcrust pastry and spoon in the filling.
Cover with puff pastry, trim and seal the edges, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden.

title: Sausage Rolls
ingredients: 500 g beef and pork sausage mince
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the sausage mince, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, tomato sauce and herbs in a bowl.
Cut each pastry sheet in half and divide the filling into four long portions down the centre of the pastry pieces.
Roll the pastry around the filling and place each roll seam-side down.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and cut into smaller rolls.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until puffed, golden and cooked through.

title: ANZAC Biscuits
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and line two trays with baking paper.
Combine the oats, flour, coconut and brown sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small saucepan.
Stir the bicarbonate of soda into the boiling water, then mix it into the butter mixture.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Roll tablespoons of mixture into balls, place them on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until golden, then cool on the trays.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Spoon the meringue onto the tray and shape it into a round with a shallow hollow in the centre.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form and spread it over the pavlova.
Top with kiwifruit, strawberries and passionfruit just before serving.

title: Queensland Prawn and Mango Salad
ingredients: 500 g cooked Queensland prawns, peeled and deveined
1 large ripe mango, peeled and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Arrange the salad leaves, cucumber, mango and avocado on a platter.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, sweet chilli sauce, salt and pepper.
Add the prawns to the platter and drizzle with dressing just before serving.

title: Damper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the milk to make a soft dough, then knead lightly on a floured bench.
Shape into a round loaf and place on the tray.
Brush with extra milk and cut a shallow cross in the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Lamb Roast with Pumpkin and Potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Make small cuts in the lamb and push in the garlic slivers.
Rub the lamb with olive oil, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Place the lamb in a roasting pan and roast for 45 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and potatoes, turning them in the pan juices.
Roast for another 45–60 minutes, until the lamb is cooked to your liking and the vegetables are tender.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Meat Pie with Tomato Sauce
ingredients: ½ cup tomato sauce, to serve
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until softened.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a pie dish with the shortcrust pastry.
Spoon in the filling and cover with puff pastry; press the edges together and cut a small vent in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden.
Serve hot with tomato sauce.

title: Pavlova with Passionfruit
instructions: Heat the oven to 120°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
Add the caster sugar gradually, beating until the meringue is thick and glossy.
Fold in the vinegar and cornflour.
Pile the meringue onto the tray and shape into a round with a shallow centre.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Beat the cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form.
Top the pavlova with cream, passionfruit pulp and kiwi slices before serving.

title: Cottage Pie
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the minced beef and cook until browned.
Stir in the tomato purée and flour, then add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 25 minutes until thickened; season to taste.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the beef mixture into an ovenproof dish and spread the mash over it.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until golden on top.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix quickly to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a round loaf.
Place on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 200°C and bake for 25–30 minutes more.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale until smooth and thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the mustard, cheese and Worcestershire sauce.
Season with black pepper and let the mixture cool slightly.
Toast the bread on one side, then spread the cheese mixture over the untoasted sides.
Grill until bubbling and golden.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 800 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into chunks
700 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Season the flour with salt and pepper, then toss the lamb in it.
Heat the oil in a casserole and brown the lamb in batches; set aside.
Cook the onion and carrots in the casserole for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the casserole and add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Arrange the potato slices over the top, overlapping them, and brush with melted butter.
Cover and bake for 1 hour, then uncover and bake for 45–60 minutes until the potatoes are golden and the lamb is tender.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 900 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Meanwhile, cook the cabbage in a little boiling water for 5–7 minutes, then drain well.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pan; mash until smooth.
Warm the milk with the spring onions, then stir it into the potatoes with the butter.
Fold in the cabbage and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, with an extra knob of butter if desired.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the lamb and brown it, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomato purée and flour, then add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened; season to taste.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and spread the mash over it.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix briefly to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a round loaf.
Place it on the tray and cut a deep cross into the top.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 300 g waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Mix the flour with a pinch of salt, then rub in the butter and lard until crumbly.
Add the cold water gradually and bring the mixture together into a dough.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, potatoes, swede, and onion; season generously.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Roll out the dough and cut out four circles, about 20 cm across.
Divide the filling among the circles, placing it in the center of each.
Brush the edges with beaten egg, fold each circle over, and crimp the edges firmly.
Brush the pasties with egg and bake for 45–50 minutes, until golden and cooked through.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale until smooth and thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cheese, and pepper.
Toast the bread lightly on both sides.
Spread the cheese mixture over the toast.
Grill until bubbling and golden, then serve hot.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
While the potatoes cook, simmer the cabbage in a little water for 5–7 minutes, until tender; drain well.
Warm the milk with the spring onions in a small saucepan.
Mash the potatoes with the butter and warm milk mixture.
Fold in the cabbage and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, with an extra knob of butter if desired.

title: Cottage Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook until softened.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and a little salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes, until thickened.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spoon the beef mixture into a baking dish and spread the mashed potatoes over it.
Sprinkle with cheddar and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Irish Colcannon
ingredients: 2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain.
While the potatoes cook, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a pan. Add the cabbage and cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Warm the milk with the scallions in a small saucepan.
Mash the potatoes with the warm milk and scallions until smooth.
Fold in the cabbage and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with the remaining butter melted over the top.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook until thick and smooth.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cayenne, cheddar, and black pepper until the cheese melts.
Toast the bread on both sides and arrange it on a baking sheet.
Spread the cheese mixture over the toast and broil until golden and bubbling, about 2 to 3 minutes.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook until softened.
Add the lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, stock, rosemary, and a little salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and spread the mashed potatoes over it.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling.

title: Irish Soda Bread
ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and lightly flour a baking sheet.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Mix quickly with a fork until a soft dough forms, then turn it onto a lightly floured surface.
Knead gently just enough to bring the dough together, then shape it into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on the baking sheet and cut a deep cross across the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped on the bottom.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: 900 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Add the thyme, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and spread the mashed potatoes over it.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Irish Soda Bread
ingredients: 450 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix quickly until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a round loaf without kneading much.
Place the loaf on the tray and cut a deep cross into the top.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 200°C and bake for 25–30 minutes more.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Welsh Cawl
ingredients: 700 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into chunks
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, then set it aside.
Add the onion and leeks to the pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot and add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the carrots and parsnips and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for 20–25 minutes until the meat and vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 300 g beef skirt, cut into small cubes
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the butter and lard until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cold water a little at a time until a firm dough forms. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, potatoes, swede, onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Divide the dough into four pieces and roll each into a circle about 20 cm wide.
Place the filling down the center of each circle, leaving a border around the edge.
Brush the edges with beaten egg, fold the pastry over the filling, and crimp to seal.
Place the pasties on the tray, brush with the remaining egg, and bake for 45–50 minutes until golden.

title: Irish Colcannon
ingredients: 900 g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Meanwhile, cook the cabbage in a pan of boiling water for 4–5 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Warm the milk with half the butter and the spring onions in a small saucepan.
Mash the potatoes until smooth, then mix in the warm milk mixture and cabbage.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the remaining butter melting on top.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomato purée and flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 25 minutes until thickened, then season and spoon into a baking dish.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter, milk, salt, and pepper.
Spread the mash over the lamb filling and bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until golden.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in most of the buttermilk.
Mix quickly to form a soft dough, adding the remaining buttermilk if needed.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and cut a deep cross on top.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 200°C and bake for 25–30 minutes more, until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 thick cod fillets, about 150 g each
150 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chips
instructions: Soak the chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pan to 140°C and fry the chips for 5–7 minutes until softened but pale; drain.
Whisk the flour and baking powder with the sparkling water to make a smooth batter.
Dust the fish with flour, dip each fillet in the batter, and fry at 180°C for 6–8 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Fry the chips again at 180°C for 3–5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain the fish and chips, season with salt, and serve with malt vinegar.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale and cook until smooth and thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cheese, and black pepper.
Toast the bread on one side, then arrange it toasted-side down on a baking tray.
Spread the cheese mixture over the untoasted sides and grill until bubbling and golden.

title: Bangers and Mash
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and cook the sausages, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Melt 25 g of the butter in a separate pan and cook the onions over low heat until soft and golden.
Stir the flour into the onions, then gradually add the beef stock and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the remaining butter, milk, salt, and pepper.
Serve the sausages over the mash with onion gravy.

title: Cottage Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the beef and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the beef mixture into a baking dish and spread the mash over it.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Irish Soda Bread
ingredients: 450 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and lightly flour a baking tray.
Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently shape it into a round loaf.
Place the loaf on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped on the base. Cool before slicing.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale until smooth, then simmer until thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cheese, and black pepper.
Toast the bread on one side, then arrange it toasted-side down on a baking tray.
Spread the cheese mixture over the untoasted sides and grill until bubbling and golden.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 900 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into chunks
800 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then toss it with the flour.
Heat the oil in a large ovenproof casserole and brown the lamb in batches. Set it aside.
Add the onions and carrots to the casserole and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the casserole. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaf, and bring to a simmer.
Layer the potato slices over the top, overlapping them. Brush with melted butter and cover with a lid.
Bake for 2 hours, then remove the lid and bake for 30 minutes more until the potatoes are golden and tender.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 900 g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, melt 25 g of the butter in a pan. Add the cabbage and cook gently for 5–7 minutes until soft.
Add the spring onions and milk to the cabbage and warm through.
Drain the potatoes and mash until smooth.
Stir the cabbage mixture and remaining butter into the potatoes. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 25 minutes until thickened; season with salt and pepper.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and spread the mash over it.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes, until golden on top.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and dust a baking sheet with flour.
Whisk together the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Make a well in the centre and pour in the buttermilk.
Mix briefly into a soft dough, then turn it onto a floured surface and shape into a round.
Place on the baking sheet and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 200°C and bake for 25–30 minutes more, until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale until smooth and thick.

instructions: Toss the strawberries with the sugar and leave for 15 minutes to release their juices.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Fold most of the strawberries and crushed meringue into the cream.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and lightly flour a baking tray.

Place the loaf on the tray and cut a deep cross into the top.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.

title: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy

Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C and season the beef with salt and pepper.

Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, Guinness, stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook in the oven for 2½–3 hours, until the beef is tender.
Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
4 medium potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
3 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb in batches.
Add the onion, potatoes, carrots, stock, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then scatter over the parsley to serve.

title: Boxty
ingredients: 2 cups raw potatoes, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Squeeze excess liquid from the grated potatoes.
Mix the grated potatoes with the mashed potatoes, flour, salt, and baking powder.
Stir in enough buttermilk to make a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through, adding butter as needed.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lb floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a pan and cook the cabbage with a splash of water until tender.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the milk and remaining butter.
Fold in the cabbage and scallions, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, with an extra knob of butter if desired.

title: Coddle
ingredients: 8 oz thick-cut bacon, cut into pieces
2 lb potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Brown the sausages in a skillet, then cut them into large pieces.
Layer the sausages, bacon, onion, and potatoes in a lidded ovenproof pot.
Pour in the stock and add the black pepper.
Cover and bake for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the potatoes are tender.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and lightly flour a baking sheet.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix just until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead lightly for a few seconds.
Shape into a round loaf and place on the baking sheet.
Cut a deep cross in the top and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a rack before slicing.

title: Ulster Fry
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the sausages and bacon, turning occasionally, until cooked through and browned; set aside and keep warm.
Fry the tomatoes cut-side down until softened, then turn briefly and set aside.
Add the butter and fry the soda bread and potato bread until golden on both sides.
Fry the eggs to your liking and season with salt and pepper.
Serve everything hot together.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 900 g lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
700 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
750 ml water or light lamb stock
instructions: Put the lamb, potatoes, carrots and onions in a large heavy pot.
Pour in the water or stock and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a gentle boil, skimming any foam from the surface.
Cover and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Boxty
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash until smooth.
Squeeze excess liquid from the grated raw potatoes using a clean tea towel.
Mix the mashed potato, grated potato, flour, egg, buttermilk and salt into a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter and cook small pancakes for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter as needed, and serve warm.

title: Belfast Bap
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and oil, then mix into a dough.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover and leave to rise for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Divide into 6 pieces and shape into round rolls; place on a greased baking tray and flatten slightly.
Cover and leave to rise for 30 minutes while the oven heats to 220°C.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly golden and hollow-sounding when tapped; cool on a rack.

title: Soda Farls
instructions: Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix quickly to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead very briefly.
Shape into a round about 2 cm thick and cut into four farls.
Heat a dry, heavy frying pan or griddle over medium-low heat.
Cook the farls for about 8 minutes per side, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Cool slightly, then split and serve.

title: Yorkshire Pudding
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Divide the oil among 12 muffin-tin cups and heat the tin in the oven until the oil is very hot.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter. Rest it for 20 minutes.
Carefully pour the batter into the hot tin, filling each cup about halfway.
Bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the oven, until risen and deeply golden.

title: Parkin
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Mix the oatmeal, flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.
Gently warm the treacle, golden syrup, butter and sugar in a pan until melted; do not boil.
Stir the warm mixture into the dry ingredients, then mix in the egg and milk.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50–60 minutes, until set. Cool in the tin, then wrap and leave for a few days before cutting for a stickier texture.

title: Yorkshire Curd Tart
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Roll out the pastry and line a 20 cm tart tin.
Beat the curd cheese, sugar, melted butter and egg until combined.
Stir in the currants, nutmeg and rosewater.
Spoon the filling into the pastry case and bake for 25–30 minutes, until lightly golden and just set.
Cool before serving.

title: Yorkshire Fat Rascals
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the sugar, currants, mixed peel, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Beat the egg with the milk, then mix into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Shape into 8 thick rounds and place on the tray. Press 3 almonds onto each round to make a face.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, until risen and golden. Cool on a rack.

title: Yorkshire Lamb and Potato Pie
ingredients: 500 g stewing lamb, cut into 2 cm pieces
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Heat the oil in a flameproof casserole and brown the lamb in batches. Set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pan until softened. Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Return the lamb to the pan, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until tender.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until soft. Drain, then mash with the butter, milk, salt and pepper.
Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and spread the mashed potato over the top.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the potato is golden and the filling is bubbling.

title: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the potatoes in a pan of salted water and bring to a boil; simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the sausages over medium heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Transfer the sausages to a plate. Add the onions to the pan and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually stir in the stock and Worcestershire sauce, then simmer until thickened.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and warm milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve the sausages and mash with the onion gravy.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the lamb and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the flour and tomato purée, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened, then stir in the peas and season.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the lamb mixture into a baking dish and cover with the mash.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges.

title: Toad in the Hole
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the oil in a medium baking dish and heat it in the oven for 5 minutes.
Add the sausages to the hot dish and bake for 10 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the flour with a pinch of salt, then whisk in the eggs, milk and water until smooth. Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Carefully pour the batter around the sausages and return the dish to the oven.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the batter is well risen and golden. Do not open the oven during cooking.
Season with black pepper and serve hot.

title: Bubble and Squeak
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain and mash roughly.
Cook the cabbage in a little boiling water for 4–5 minutes until just tender; drain well.
Mix the cabbage into the potatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the potato mixture and press it down into an even layer. Cook for 8–10 minutes until the underside is crisp and golden.
Turn portions over and cook for another 6–8 minutes until crisp on the other side.

title: Eton Mess
instructions: Whip the cream with the caster sugar and vanilla until it forms soft peaks.
Lightly crush half the strawberries and half the raspberries with a fork.
Fold the crushed fruit and most of the remaining berries into the cream.
Gently fold in the crushed meringue, keeping some pieces chunky.
Spoon into serving glasses or bowls and top with the reserved berries.
Serve straight away, before the meringue softens.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 300 g beef skirt, cut into small cubes
instructions: Rub the lard and butter into the flour and salt until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the cold water a little at a time and bring together into a firm dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef, potatoes, swede, onion, salt and pepper.
Divide the pastry into four and roll each piece into a round about 20 cm across.
Pile the filling on one half of each round, leaving a border. Brush the border with beaten egg.
Fold the pastry over the filling and crimp the edges firmly to seal.
Brush the pasties with egg and bake for 45–55 minutes, until golden and cooked through.

title: Stargazy Pie
ingredients: 400 g whole pilchards or sardines, cleaned and headed
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Simmer the potatoes in water for 8–10 minutes, then drain.
Put the potatoes and onion in a pie dish. Add the fish stock, cream, parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Lay the fish over the filling with their tails toward the centre and heads pointing upward at the rim.
Roll out the pastry, cover the dish, and cut small openings so the fish heads remain visible above the crust.
Trim and crimp the pastry edges, then brush the pastry with beaten egg.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling bubbles.

title: Cornish Hevva Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, currants, mixed spice and baking powder.
Beat the egg with the milk, then mix it into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Shape the dough into a round about 2 cm thick and place it on the tray.
Mark a criss-cross pattern across the top with a knife and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden. Cool before slicing.

title: Cornish Saffron Buns
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm milk for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, sugar, salt and yeast in a large bowl.
Rub in the butter, then stir in the currants and mixed peel.
Add the saffron milk, warm milk and beaten egg. Mix to a soft dough.
Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth, then cover and leave to rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Divide into 12 buns and place on a lined baking tray. Cover and leave to rise for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden.

title: Cornish Clotted Cream Fudge
instructions: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Put the sugar, golden syrup, butter and clotted cream in a heavy-based saucepan.
Heat gently, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved and the butter has melted.
Bring to a steady boil and cook, stirring often, until the mixture reaches 116°C on a sugar thermometer.
Remove from the heat and leave for 5 minutes. Stir in the vanilla.
Beat the mixture until it thickens and loses its glossy sheen.
Pour into the tin, smooth the top and leave to set before cutting into squares.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 700 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into chunks
900 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan.
Season the lamb, then brown it in the dripping in a flameproof casserole. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pan until softened. Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Return the lamb to the pan and add the carrots. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30 minutes.
Arrange the potato slices in overlapping layers on top. Brush with melted butter and season.
Cover and bake for 1 hour, then uncover and bake for 45 minutes until the potatoes are golden and the lamb is tender.

title: Lancashire Butter Pie
instructions: Rub the cold diced butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Stir in enough cold water to make a firm pastry.
Wrap the pastry and chill it for 30 minutes.
Melt 40 g butter in a pan and cook the onions gently until soft but not browned.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Roll out two-thirds of the pastry and line a 23 cm pie dish.
Layer the potatoes and onions in the dish, seasoning as you go. Pour over the stock.
Roll out the remaining pastry, cover the pie, and seal the edges. Cut a small steam hole and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until the pastry is golden.

title: Eccles Cakes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Stir in the brown sugar, currants, cinnamon, and lemon zest, then leave the filling to cool.
Cut the pastry into eight 12 cm circles. Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each.
Gather the pastry edges over the filling and pinch to seal. Turn each cake over and flatten gently with a rolling pin.
Brush with milk, snip three small cuts in the top, and sprinkle with granulated sugar.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack before serving.

title: Parkin
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C fan and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oatmeal, flour, ginger, and baking powder in a bowl.
Warm the butter, treacle, golden syrup, and sugar in a saucepan over low heat until melted. Do not boil.
Pour the warm mixture into the dry ingredients and stir well.
Beat the egg with the milk, then mix it into the batter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45–55 minutes until firm in the centre.
Cool in the tin, then wrap and leave for a few days to soften before cutting.

title: Lancashire Cheese and Onion Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain and mash roughly.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onions gently until soft and sweet.
Stir the onions, Lancashire cheese, milk, and mustard powder into the potatoes. Season and leave to cool slightly.
Roll out half the pastry and line a 23 cm pie dish. Spoon in the filling and level the top.
Roll out the remaining pastry, cover the pie, and seal the edges. Make a small steam hole and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the pastry is golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 300 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the haddock in a pan with the milk and bay leaf; bring just to a gentle simmer.
Poach for 5–7 minutes, until the fish flakes easily. Lift out the fish and strain the milk into a jug.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion gently until soft.
Add the potatoes and strained milk. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Flake the haddock into the soup, removing any bones, and warm through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the parsley, and serve.

title: Stovies
ingredients: 700 g floury potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
300 g cooked roast beef or lamb, chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the dripping or butter in a heavy pot over a medium heat.
Add the onion and cook gently until soft.
Layer in the potatoes and chopped meat, seasoning lightly with salt and pepper.
Pour in the stock, cover, and bring to a simmer.
Cook gently for 35–45 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and starting to break down; stir carefully once or twice.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Mince and Tatties
ingredients: 900 g floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and add a pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil and cook for 15–20 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, brown the mince in a saucepan, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mince is tender and the gravy has thickened; season to taste.
