Drain the potatoes and mash with the milk and butter until smooth.
Serve the mince and gravy with the mashed potatoes.

title: Rumbledethumps
ingredients: 800 g floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and add a pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil and cook for 15–20 minutes, until tender; drain well.
Melt half the butter in a pan and cook the onion gently until soft.
Add the cabbage and cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring, until tender.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining butter, then fold in the cabbage and onion; season to taste.
Spoon into an ovenproof dish, scatter the cheese over the top, and bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes, until golden.

title: Cranachan
instructions: Toast the oats in a dry frying pan over a medium heat, stirring often, until lightly golden; leave to cool.
Crush half the raspberries with the caster sugar and leave for 5 minutes.
Whip the cream until softly thickened, then fold in the honey and whisky.
Layer the cream, toasted oats, crushed raspberries, and remaining whole raspberries in glasses.
Chill briefly or serve straight away.

title: Welsh Cawl
ingredients: 500 g lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the stock, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the swede, carrots, and potatoes; simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the leeks and cook for 10 minutes, until the vegetables and lamb are tender.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Toast the bread on one side and arrange it, untoasted side up, on a baking tray.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat and stir in the flour to make a paste.
Gradually whisk in the ale and cook until smooth and thick.
Stir in the mustard powder, Worcestershire sauce, and cheese until melted.
Remove from the heat and beat in the egg yolk.
Spoon the cheese mixture over the untoasted sides of the bread.
Grill until bubbling and golden, then serve immediately.

title: Glamorgan Sausages
instructions: Melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the leek over low heat until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the leek with the cheese, breadcrumbs, parsley, mustard powder, and one beaten egg.
Shape the mixture into 8 sausage-shaped pieces.
Put the flour and remaining beaten egg in separate shallow bowls.
Roll each sausage in flour, dip it in egg, then roll it in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the sausages, turning often, until golden and hot through.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve.

title: Welsh Cakes
instructions: Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, currants, and mixed spice.
Add the egg and enough milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface to about 5 mm thick.
Cut into rounds using a 6 cm cutter.
Cook the cakes in batches on a lightly greased griddle or heavy frying pan over medium-low heat for about 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Sprinkle with caster sugar while warm.

title: Bara Brith
instructions: Put the dried fruit in a bowl, pour over the hot tea, and leave to soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan and line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper.
Stir the brown sugar into the soaked fruit and tea.
Mix in the flour and mixed spice, then stir in the beaten egg and milk.
Spoon the batter into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
4 large potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb in batches.
Add the onions and water or stock, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and carrots, season with salt and pepper, and simmer until the lamb and vegetables are tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lb floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
½ small green cabbage, finely shredded
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes, then drain.
While the potatoes cook, simmer the cabbage in a little water until tender, about 8 minutes, and drain well.
Warm the milk and half the butter in a small saucepan.
Mash the potatoes with the warm milk, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the cabbage and scallions, top with the remaining butter, and serve.

title: Boxty
ingredients: 1 lb waxy potatoes, peeled and grated
2 tbsp butter, melted, plus extra for frying
instructions: Boil the floury potatoes until tender, then drain and mash until smooth.
Squeeze excess liquid from the grated potatoes using a clean towel.
Combine the mashed and grated potatoes with the flour and salt.
Stir in the milk and melted butter to make a thick batter.
Heat a little butter in a frying pan and cook spoonfuls of batter over medium heat, about 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.

title: Bacon and Cabbage
ingredients: 1 small green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Put the bacon in a pot and cover with the water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, or until tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until tender.
Slice the bacon and serve with the potatoes and cabbage, topped with butter and parsley.

title: Soda Bread
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and lightly flour a baking sheet.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in most of the buttermilk.
Mix lightly until a soft dough forms, adding the remaining buttermilk if needed.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a round loaf without kneading much.
Place on the baking sheet, cut a deep cross on top, and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until browned and hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Ulster Fry
instructions: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the sausages, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 12–15 minutes.
Add the bacon and puddings; fry until the bacon is cooked and the puddings are browned on both sides.
Melt half the butter in a second pan and fry the potato farls and soda farls until golden on both sides.
Add the remaining butter and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve everything hot.

title: Champ
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, until tender, then drain well.
Warm the milk with the spring onions in a small saucepan for 2 minutes.
Mash the potatoes with the butter and warm milk mixture until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 800 g lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Arrange half the potatoes in a large casserole dish, then add the lamb, carrots, and onions.
Season with salt and pepper, pour in the stock, and cover with the remaining potatoes.
Cover the dish and bake for 2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

title: Boxty
instructions: Boil the 500 g of potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash.
Squeeze excess liquid from the grated potatoes using a clean tea towel.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the mashed and grated potatoes, egg, and buttermilk to make a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through, adding butter as needed.

title: Apple and Blackberry Crumble
ingredients: 500 g cooking apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Put the apples, blackberries, caster sugar, and water in a baking dish and mix gently.
Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir the oats and brown sugar into the crumble mixture.
Scatter the topping over the fruit and bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Yorkshire Pudding
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter; leave it to rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the oil among 8 holes of a muffin tin and heat in the oven until very hot.
Pour the batter into the hot tin, filling each hole about halfway.
Bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the oven door, until well risen and golden.

title: Parkin
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oatmeal, flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.
Gently warm the butter, treacle, syrup and sugar in a saucepan until melted; do not boil.
Stir the warm mixture into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg with the milk, then stir it into the batter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50–60 minutes, until firm in the middle.
Cool in the tin, then wrap and leave for a few days to soften before cutting.

title: Yorkshire Curd Tart
instructions: Rub the flour and diced butter together until they resemble breadcrumbs; stir in 2 tbsp sugar.
Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to bring the pastry together.
Chill the pastry for 30 minutes, then roll it out and line a 23 cm tart tin.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and bake the pastry case blind for 15 minutes; remove the baking paper and weights.
Beat the curd cheese, 75 g sugar, melted butter and egg until combined.
Fold in the currants, nutmeg and lemon zest.
Pour the filling into the pastry case and bake for 25–30 minutes, until lightly golden and set.
Cool before serving.

title: Yorkshire Tea Loaf
instructions: Put the dried fruit in a bowl, pour over the hot tea and leave to soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper.
Stir the flour, sugar and mixed spice into the soaked fruit and tea.
Mix in the beaten egg until evenly combined.
Spoon the mixture into the tin and bake for 60–70 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.

title: Yorkshire Lamb and Barley Stew
ingredients: 700 g boneless lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then brown it in batches; set aside.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the stock, stirring to lift any browned bits from the pot.
Return the lamb to the pot and add the barley, bay leaf and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lamb and barley are tender.
Remove the bay leaf, taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Toad in the Hole
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pour the oil into a roasting tin and add the sausages.
Roast the sausages for 15 minutes, turning once, until browned and the tin is very hot.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter.
Pour the batter around the sausages and bake for 25–30 minutes, without opening the oven, until puffed and golden.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes, until tender; drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb and brown it, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the flour and tomato purée, then add the stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 20 minutes; stir in the peas and season.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Spoon the filling into a baking dish, spread the mash over it and rough up the top with a fork.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Beef and Ale Stew
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Toss the beef with the flour and a generous pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; set it aside.
Add the onion, carrots and celery to the pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato purée, then pour in the ale and stock, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot and add the bay leaves and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 2–2½ hours, until the beef is tender. Remove the bay leaves before serving.

title: Bubble and Squeak
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes, until tender; drain and roughly mash.
Mix the potatoes with the cooked cabbage and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Press the mixture into the pan and cook for 8–10 minutes, until the underside is crisp and golden.
Turn it over in sections and cook for another 8–10 minutes, until browned and hot throughout.

title: Eton Mess
instructions: Whip the cream with the icing sugar and vanilla until it forms soft peaks.
Reserve a few strawberry slices for topping and gently fold the rest into the cream.
Fold in most of the crushed meringue, keeping a little for the top.
Spoon into serving glasses and finish with the reserved strawberries and meringue.
Serve straight away.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 300 g beef skirt, cut into small pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Rub the lard and butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cold water a little at a time and bring the dough together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef, potato, swede and onion; season well.
Divide the dough into four pieces and roll each into a circle about 23 cm wide.
Spoon the filling down the centre of each circle, leaving a border. Brush the edges with beaten egg.
Fold the pastry over the filling and crimp the edges firmly.
Brush the pasties with egg and bake for 45–50 minutes, until golden and cooked through.

title: Stargazy Pie
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
25 g butter, plus extra for greasing
6 fresh sardines, cleaned, heads left on
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and butter a shallow pie dish.
Put the potatoes, onion, milk, cream and bay leaf in a pan. Simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender. Lift out the bay leaf and drain, reserving the liquid.
Arrange the potato and onion in the dish with the butter, parsley, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Lay the sardines over the filling with their heads pointing towards the edge of the dish.
Roll out the pastry and cover the dish, leaving the fish heads visible through small openings. Press the pastry edges to seal.
Brush the pastry with beaten egg and bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Cornish Heavy Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Rub the butter and lard into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the caster sugar, currants, mixed spice and baking powder.
Beat the egg with the milk, then mix it into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Pat the dough into a round about 2 cm thick and place it on the tray.
Sprinkle with demerara sugar and bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and firm.
Cool on the tray before cutting into wedges.

title: Cornish Saffron Buns
instructions: Warm the milk gently and steep the saffron in it for 10 minutes, until the milk turns golden.
Mix the flour, sugar, salt and yeast in a large bowl.
Rub the butter into the flour mixture, then stir in the currants and mixed peel.
Pour in the saffron milk and beaten egg. Mix to a soft dough.
Knead for 8–10 minutes, then cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Divide into 12 buns and place on a lined baking tray. Cover and prove for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden.

title: Cornish Clotted Cream Fudge
instructions: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Put the sugar, milk, golden syrup, clotted cream and butter in a heavy-based saucepan.
Heat gently, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.
Bring to a steady boil and cook, stirring often, until the mixture reaches 116°C on a sugar thermometer.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla. Beat until the mixture thickens and loses its shine.
Pour into the tin and leave to cool completely before cutting into squares.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 700 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into chunks
900 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Melt the butter or dripping in a large ovenproof casserole and brown the lamb in batches; set aside.
Cook the onions and carrots in the casserole until softened, then stir in the flour.
Return the lamb, add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Arrange the potato slices in overlapping layers over the meat and brush with melted butter.
Cover and bake for 1½ hours, then uncover and bake for 30–40 minutes until the potatoes are golden and the lamb is tender.

title: Butter Pie
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a pan and gently cook the onions until soft and sweet.
Stir the flour into the onions, then gradually add the stock and simmer until thickened.
Fold in the potatoes and season with salt and pepper; leave the filling to cool slightly.
Line a pie dish with half the pastry, add the filling, then cover with the remaining pastry and seal the edges.
Brush the top with beaten egg, make a small steam hole, and bake for 30–35 minutes until golden.

title: Lancashire Cheese and Onion Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onions gently until soft; cool slightly.
Line a pie dish with half the pastry.
Mix the cheese, eggs, cream, mustard, onions, salt and pepper, then spoon into the pastry case.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal the edges, and cut a small steam hole.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and set.

title: Lancashire Parkin
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a 20 cm square cake tin.
Mix the oatmeal, flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.
Gently warm the butter, treacle, golden syrup and sugar in a pan until melted; do not boil.
Stir the warm syrup mixture into the dry ingredients.
Mix in the egg and milk until smooth, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 50–60 minutes until firm; cool in the tin and wrap to mature for a few days before cutting.

title: Lancashire Eccles Cakes
ingredients: 50 g mixed candied peel, finely chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Mix the currants, candied peel, brown sugar, melted butter, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Roll the pastry to about 3 mm thick and cut out 12 rounds, about 10 cm across.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each round, gather the edges over the filling and pinch to seal.
Turn each cake over, flatten gently with a rolling pin, and snip three small cuts in the top.
Brush with egg white, sprinkle with granulated sugar, and bake for 15–20 minutes until crisp and golden.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 2 medium floury potatoes, peeled and diced
300 grams undyed smoked haddock, skin removed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and milk, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the haddock and simmer gently until it flakes easily, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper.
Scatter over the parsley and serve hot.

title: Stovies
ingredients: 750 grams potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
300 grams cooked roast beef, cut into bite-sized pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the dripping in a heavy pot over low heat and cook the onions until soft.
Layer in the potatoes and beef, seasoning each layer lightly with salt and pepper.
Pour in the stock, cover, and simmer gently until the potatoes are tender, about 45 minutes.
Stir roughly so some potatoes break down and thicken the juices, then serve.

title: Scotch Broth
ingredients: 200 grams lamb neck or stewing lamb, diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion, carrots, and leek, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the barley and stock, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and cover.
Simmer gently until the lamb and barley are tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the cabbage and cook for 5 minutes; season and serve.

title: Haggis, Neeps and Tatties
ingredients: 500 grams floury potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Cook the haggis according to the packet instructions, usually by simmering it gently in water.
Boil the swede in salted water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and mash with half the butter.
Boil the potatoes until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash with the milk and remaining butter.
Season both mashes with salt and pepper.
Serve the haggis with the neeps and tatties.

title: Cranachan
instructions: Toast the oats in a dry frying pan over medium heat until golden, stirring often; set aside to cool.
Whip the cream until softly thickened, then fold in the honey and whisky.
Gently fold in most of the raspberries and toasted oats.
Spoon into glasses and top with the remaining raspberries and oats.

title: Cawl
ingredients: 2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
2 parsnips, peeled and cut into chunks
500 g stewing lamb, cut into pieces
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb, carrots, parsnips, water or stock, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and swede and simmer for 30 minutes, until tender.
Stir in the cabbage and cook for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the ale until smooth and thick.
Stir in the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and cheese until the cheese melts.
Remove from the heat and mix in the egg yolk.
Toast the bread lightly, spread the cheese mixture over it, and grill until bubbling and golden.

title: Glamorgan Sausages
instructions: Mix the cheese, breadcrumbs, spring onions, parsley, mustard, and 1 egg in a bowl.
Shape the mixture into 8 sausage-shaped portions.
Beat the remaining egg in a shallow bowl and put the flour on a plate.
Roll each sausage in flour, dip it in beaten egg, then coat it in any remaining breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the sausages over medium heat, turning until golden on all sides.

title: Welsh Cakes
instructions: Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the sugar, currants, and mixed spice.
Add the beaten egg and enough milk to make a firm dough.
Roll the dough out to 5 mm thick and cut into rounds.
Grease a griddle or heavy frying pan lightly with butter and heat over medium-low heat.
Cook the cakes in batches for about 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.

title: Bara Brith
instructions: Put the dried fruit in a bowl, pour over the hot tea, and leave to soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 160°C and line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper.
Stir the sugar into the soaked fruit and tea.
Fold in the flour and mixed spice, then mix in the beaten egg.
Spoon the mixture into the tin and bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the water, salt, cinnamon, cloves, and pepper. Simmer until the liquid is nearly gone.
Mix in the mashed potatoes and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 30 to 35 minutes.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the flour and salt, then cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough holds together. Chill for 20 minutes.
Roll out the dough and cut circles to fit a 12-cup muffin tin. Press the rounds into the cups.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, and vanilla until smooth.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells, then pour in the filling, stopping just below the rims.
Bake until the pastry is golden and the filling is set, about 20 to 25 minutes. Cool before removing.

title: Montreal-Style Bagels
instructions: Stir the warm water, honey, and yeast together; let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.
Mix in the egg and oil. Add the flour and salt, then knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Cover the dough and let rise until puffy, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces. Roll each into a rope and join the ends to form a ring.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Bring the 8 cups of water and 1/4 cup honey to a gentle boil.
Boil the bagels in batches for about 45 seconds per side, then drain.
Dip the bagels in sesame seeds and place on a baking sheet.
Bake until golden brown, about 15 to 18 minutes.

title: Split Pea Soup
ingredients: 1 pound dried green split peas, rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the split peas, ham hock, water, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered until the peas are tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the ham hock and bay leaf. Shred the meat, discard the bone, and return the meat to the pot.
Stir in the salt and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve hot.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, powdered sugar, and milk until smooth. Spread over the chilled base.
Chill until the filling is firm, about 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the filling and chill until set.
Cut into bars with a warm knife.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled, cooked, and mashed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook until the meat is browned.
Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, cloves, savory, salt, pepper, and broth. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Fit one crust into a 9-inch pie plate and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Donair
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine the beef, salt, pepper, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, cayenne, oregano, and thyme. Knead firmly until smooth and sticky.
Shape the mixture into a compact loaf and bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until cooked through. Cool, then slice thinly.
Whisk the evaporated milk, condensed milk, vinegar, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder until thickened; chill until ready to serve.
Warm the pita breads. Fill with sliced meat, tomato, and onion, then drizzle generously with the sauce.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Combine the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough just holds together. Shape into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles; press them into a muffin tin.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt until smooth. Divide the raisins among the pastry shells.
Pour the filling into the shells, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges. Cool before removing from the tin.

title: Poutine
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the potatoes into fries and toss with the oil and salt.
Spread the fries on a baking sheet and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef broth and chicken broth. Add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper, then simmer until thickened, about 8 minutes.
Divide the hot fries among serving plates and top with cheese curds.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds. Serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Whisk the melted butter, granulated sugar, and cocoa in a heatproof bowl over simmering water. Slowly whisk in the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened butter and custard powder until smooth. Beat in the icing sugar and milk until creamy.
Spread the custard layer evenly over the chilled base and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the custard layer and chill until firm.
Cut into squares with a warm knife and serve.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook until the meat is browned.
Stir in the water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Mix in the mashed potatoes and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one pastry crust and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 35–40 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Hodge Podge
ingredients: 2 cups new potatoes, halved if large
2 cups green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Put the potatoes and carrots in a large pot with the water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the green beans, peas, and cauliflower. Simmer until all the vegetables are tender, about 6–8 minutes.
Drain, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.
Return the vegetables to the pot. Stir in the butter, cream, pepper, and enough reserved liquid to make a light sauce.
Warm gently without boiling and serve.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the fries with the oil and salt, spread on a baking sheet, and bake until crisp and golden, turning once, about 35–40 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef broth, then add the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and pepper.
Simmer, whisking, until the gravy thickens, about 5 minutes.
Divide the hot fries among serving plates and scatter the cheese curds over them.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds. Serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
For the base, whisk the melted butter, granulated sugar, and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat. Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the pan and chill for 20 minutes.
For the filling, beat the softened butter and custard powder until smooth. Beat in the icing sugar and milk, then spread over the base. Chill until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining tablespoon of butter. Spread over the filling and chill until set.
Cut into small squares with a warm knife and serve.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Combine the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water just until the dough comes together. Shape into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles to line a standard muffin pan.
Whisk together the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and remaining salt until smooth. Stir in the raisins.
Fill each pastry shell about two-thirds full with the mixture.
Bake until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling, about 18–22 minutes. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the pork, beef, and water; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and sage. Simmer until the liquid is absorbed.
Mix in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, then cut a few slits in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Stir in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened butter, custard powder, and milk until smooth. Gradually beat in the powdered sugar.
Spread the custard layer over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tablespoon butter, spread over the custard layer, and chill until set.
Cut into squares with a warm knife.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Combine the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water just until the dough comes together. Shape into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles to line a muffin pan.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells.
Whisk together the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Pour the filling into the shells, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling. Cool before removing from the pan.

title: Pea Soup (Soupe aux pois)
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the split peas, water, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the ham hock. Shred the meat, discard the bone and skin, and return the meat to the pot.
Simmer until the peas are very soft and the soup reaches the desired thickness.
Season with salt, remove the bay leaf, and serve hot.

title: Pouding chômeur
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Combine the brown sugar and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then remove from the heat.
Beat the softened butter and granulated sugar until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture alternately with the milk, mixing just until combined.
Pour the hot brown-sugar syrup into the baking dish. Carefully spoon the batter evenly over the syrup.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the cake is golden and set. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the pork, beef, and water. Cook, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the liquid is nearly gone.
Stir in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Top with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Combine the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through.
Serve warm with cream or ice cream, if desired.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the water and 2 tablespoons oil until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently until smooth.
Pat the dough into a round about 3/4 inch thick.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the bannock for 8–10 minutes per side, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Cool briefly, then slice and serve.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt.
Spread the fries on a baking sheet and bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock. Add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper, then simmer until thickened.
Divide the hot fries among serving plates and scatter the cheese curds over them.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds. Serve immediately.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Whisk the melted butter, granulated sugar, and cocoa in a heatproof bowl. Whisk in the beaten egg.
Set the bowl over a saucepan of gently simmering water and stir until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and almonds.
Press the mixture firmly into the prepared pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat the softened butter and custard powder until smooth. Gradually beat in the powdered sugar and milk.
Spread the filling evenly over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the filling.
Chill until the topping is set, then cut into squares with a warm knife.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork, beef, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory.
Cook, stirring and breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through; cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with half the pastry and add the cooled filling.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden.

title: Montreal-Style Bagels
ingredients: 4 cups bread flour, plus more for kneading
instructions: Stir the warm water, sugar, and yeast together and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour and salt, then knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and bring a large pot of water to a boil; stir in the honey.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a rope, and join the ends to form bagels.
Boil the bagels in batches for about 1 minute per side, then drain.
Brush with beaten egg, coat with sesame seeds, and bake on a lined sheet for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt the first 1/2 cup butter with the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and almonds, then press firmly into the pan.
Beat the softened 1/2 cup butter with the custard powder, confectioners’ sugar, and milk until smooth; spread over the base and chill until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining 2 tablespoons butter and spread over the chilled filling.
Refrigerate until set, then cut into bars.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt, then cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in enough ice water to make the dough hold together; wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface.
Cut out rounds and fit them into a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk together the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells and pour in the filling, leaving room at the top.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges; cool before removing.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Combine the berries, sugar, water, lemon juice, and cornstarch in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook, stirring gently, until the filling thickens; cool slightly.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with half the pastry and spoon in the filling; dot with butter.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 15 minutes.
Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and bubbling; cool before slicing.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 kg russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the fries with oil and salt, spread on a baking sheet, and bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer, stirring, until the gravy thickens.
Divide the hot fries among plates and top with cheese curds.
Pour hot gravy over the fries and curds. Serve immediately.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled, boiled, and mashed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the pork and beef. Cook, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink; drain excess fat if needed.
Stir in the broth, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, then cut a few vents in the top. Brush with egg wash.
Bake for 35–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 20 cm (8-inch) square pan with parchment paper.
Whisk the melted butter, sugar, cocoa, egg, and vanilla in a heatproof bowl. Set over simmering water and stir until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened butter and custard powder until smooth. Beat in the icing sugar and milk until creamy.
Spread the custard layer over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tablespoon butter. Spread over the custard layer.
Chill until the chocolate is set, then cut into bars with a warm knife.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Arrange the tart shells on a baking sheet.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Divide the raisins among the tart shells, then pour in the filling, filling each shell about two-thirds full.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Cool the tarts in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Pea Soup with Salt Pork
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the peas and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat and let stand for 1 hour.
Drain the peas and return them to the pot with fresh water to cover by about 5 cm (2 inches).
Add the salt pork, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 1½–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Mash some of the peas against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Taste and add salt as needed. Serve hot.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled, boiled, and mashed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and water. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 9-inch pie plate with one pastry crust and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few steam vents.
Brush the top with egg wash and bake for 35–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Donair
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine the beef, salt, oregano, flour, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne. Knead until well mixed and firm.
Shape the meat into a compact loaf and bake on a rack for about 1 hour, turning once. Cool slightly, then slice thinly.
Whisk the evaporated milk and sugar until the sugar dissolves. Slowly whisk in the vinegar and chill the sauce.
Warm the pita breads. Fill with sliced meat, tomato, and onion, then drizzle with the sweet sauce.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potatoes with oil and salt, spread on a baking sheet, and bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock. Add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper, then simmer until the gravy thickens.
Divide the hot fries among serving plates and scatter cheese curds over them.
Pour hot gravy over the fries and curds. Serve immediately.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Combine the flour and salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water just until the dough comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles to line a muffin tin.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and salt until smooth. Stir in the raisins.
Fill the pastry shells about two-thirds full with the mixture.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges. Cool before removing from the tin.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Whisk the melted butter, sugar, and cocoa in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water. Whisk in the egg until thick, about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press firmly into the prepared pan.
Beat the softened butter and custard powder until smooth. Beat in the icing sugar and milk until creamy, then spread over the base. Chill until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining butter. Spread over the chilled filling and refrigerate until set.
Cut into squares with a warm knife and serve.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and water. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mix in the mashed potato and cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place one pastry round in a pie plate and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden.

title: Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the peas, water, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, partially covered, for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the ham hock and bay leaf. Pull the meat from the hock, chop it, and return it to the pot.
Season with salt and simmer until the peas are soft and the soup is thick, about 15 minutes more.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press the mixture firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened 1/2 cup butter with the custard powder, powdered sugar, and milk until smooth.
Spread the custard layer over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the custard layer and chill until set.
Cut into squares with a warm knife.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and arrange the tart shells on a baking sheet.
Beat the butter and brown sugar until creamy.
Beat in the eggs, corn syrup, vanilla, vinegar, and salt until combined.
Divide the raisins among the tart shells, then pour in the filling, filling each shell about two-thirds full.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Cool in the pan before serving.

title: Montreal-Style Bagels
ingredients: 4 cups bread flour, plus more for kneading
instructions: Stir the warm water, 2 tablespoons honey, and yeast together. Let stand for 5 minutes, until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the yeast mixture and knead until a smooth, firm dough forms, about 10 minutes.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces. Roll each piece into a rope and join the ends to form a ring.
Cover the rings and let them rest for 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Bring 8 cups water and 1/4 cup honey to a boil. Boil the bagels in batches for 1 minute per side, then drain.
Brush the bagels with egg white and dip them in sesame seeds.
Bake on a parchment-lined baking sheet for 15–20 minutes, until deeply golden.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork, beef, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory.
Simmer, stirring and breaking up the meat, until cooked through and most liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with half the crust and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining crust, seal and vent the edges, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Hodge Podge
ingredients: 2 cups green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Put the potatoes, carrots, water, and salt in a large pot.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and peas, then simmer until all the vegetables are tender, about 8–10 minutes.
Drain off most of the cooking liquid, leaving a few tablespoons in the pot.
Stir in the butter, cream, and pepper, and warm gently without boiling.
Serve hot.

title: Newfoundland Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 4 cups cold water, plus more for soaking
instructions: Rinse the salt cod and soak it in cold water in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours, changing the water several times.
Break the hard bread into pieces and soak it in cold water for 1 hour, then drain.
Place the cod in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer until it flakes easily, about 10 minutes.
Drain the cod and flake it, removing any bones.
Put the drained bread in a pot with 1/2 cup water and heat gently until soft and warmed through.
Fry the salt pork in a skillet until crisp and golden; reserve the rendered fat.
Serve the cod and bread with butter and crisp salt pork, spooning a little rendered fat over each portion.

title: Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the split peas, ham bone, water, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 2–2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the ham bone and bay leaf. Pull the meat from the bone, chop it, and return it to the pot.
Mash some of the peas against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Season with salt to taste and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Whisk the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in enough ice water to form a dough.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out the dough and cut 12 rounds. Press them into the cups of a muffin tin.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells, then pour in the filling, filling each shell about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the garlic, water, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is mostly absorbed; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one crust and spoon in the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush the crust with beaten egg.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden; rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Blueberry Grunt
instructions: Combine the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a large covered skillet or saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, without lifting the lid.
Serve warm with cream or ice cream, if desired.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt, then spread them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth; add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, whisking, until the gravy thickens.
Divide the hot fries among serving plates and scatter the cheese curds over them.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds; serve immediately.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir in the water and 1/4 cup oil until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently until smooth.
Pat the dough into a 1-inch-thick round.
Heat 1 inch of oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Fry the dough round for 6 to 8 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Arrange the tart shells on a baking sheet and divide the raisins among them.
Beat the butter and brown sugar in a bowl until smooth.
Beat in the eggs, corn syrup, vanilla, and salt until combined.
Pour the filling into the tart shells, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook until the meat is browned.
Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and water. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mix in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Fit one crust into a 9-inch pie plate and add the filling. Cover with the second crust, seal the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40–45 minutes, until golden.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press the mixture into a parchment-lined 8-inch square pan and chill.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, powdered sugar, and milk until smooth. Spread over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tablespoon butter. Spread over the filling, chill until set, then cut into bars.

title: Pea Soup (Soupe aux pois)
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the peas, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, water, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 2–2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are soft.
Remove the ham hock. Shred the meat, discard the bone and skin, and return the meat to the pot.
Season with salt and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and serve.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water a tablespoon at a time, mixing just until the dough comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles. Fit them into a muffin pan.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt until combined. Divide the raisins among the pastry shells and pour in the filling.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15–18 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling. Cool before removing from the pan.

title: Pouding chômeur
instructions: Beat the softened butter and granulated sugar until light. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl. Add to the butter mixture in batches, alternating with the milk.
Spread the batter in a greased 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Combine the maple syrup, cream, and brown sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot syrup mixture carefully over the batter. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40–45 minutes, until the cake is golden and set. Serve warm.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potatoes with oil and salt, spread on a baking sheet, and bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in both broths and the Worcestershire sauce. Simmer, whisking, until the gravy thickens, about 5 minutes.
Divide the fries among serving plates, top with cheese curds, and pour hot gravy over them. Serve immediately.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled, cooked, and mashed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook until the meat is browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the water, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt, and pepper. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the mashed potato and let the filling cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 9-inch pie plate with half the pastry and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia-Style Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Place the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with water, and boil until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash.
Meanwhile, simmer the cod in lightly salted water until it flakes easily, about 8 minutes. Drain well and flake the fish.
Cook the onion in the butter until soft, about 5 minutes. Mix it with the potatoes, fish, salt, and pepper; cool until firm enough to shape.
Form the mixture into 8 patties. Dip each patty in beaten egg, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the patties for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and heated through.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.

Melt the first 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat. Whisk in the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press the mixture firmly into the pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, powdered sugar, and milk until smooth. Spread over the chilled base and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the custard layer and chill until set. Cut into bars.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough holds together. Shape into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 rounds. Fit them into a muffin tin.
Whisk together the brown sugar, corn syrup, egg, melted butter, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Divide the raisins among the pastry shells and pour in the filling, leaving room at the top.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set but still slightly soft in the center. Cool before removing from the pan.

title: Tourtière (Québec Pork Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the pork, beef, water, spices, salt, and pepper. Simmer, stirring, until the meat is cooked and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and flute the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Hodge Podge
ingredients: 2 cups green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer until nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and peas. Simmer until all the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Drain off most of the water, leaving about 1/2 cup in the pot.
Stir in the milk, cream, salt, and pepper. Warm gently without boiling.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Newfoundland Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 4 cups cold water, plus more for soaking
4 cups hard bread (hard tack), broken into pieces
instructions: Rinse the salt cod and soak it in cold water in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours, changing the water several times.
Soak the hard bread in cold water until softened, about 30 minutes, then drain.
Place the cod in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer gently until it flakes, about 10 minutes. Drain and flake the fish.
Place the softened bread in a pot with fresh water. Simmer until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain well.
Cook the salt pork in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Remove the scraps and reserve the rendered fat.
Serve the cod and bread together, topped with butter and hot rendered salt-pork fat.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/4 cup vegetable oil, plus 2 tablespoons for the skillet
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir in the water and 1/4 cup oil until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Pat the dough into a 1-inch-thick round and cut a few shallow slashes across the top.
Heat the remaining oil in a heavy skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the bannock for 8–10 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Cool slightly, then cut into wedges and serve.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and place the tart shells in a muffin tin.
Beat the butter and brown sugar until creamy. Beat in the eggs, corn syrup, and vanilla.
Stir in the flour and salt, then fold in the raisins.
Divide the filling among the tart shells, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the pork, beef, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory.
Simmer, stirring often, until the meat is cooked and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Stir in the mashed potato and let the filling cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spoon the filling into one pie crust and cover with the second crust.
Seal and crimp the edges, cut a few vents in the top, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until golden.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the fries with vegetable oil and spread them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp; season with salt.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and whisk in the flour.
Cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the beef broth.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and black pepper, and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Divide the fries among plates, top with cheese curds, and pour hot gravy over them.

title: Nova Scotia Blueberry Grunt
instructions: Combine the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk together the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, until the dumplings are cooked through.
Serve warm.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until thickened; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts, then press the mixture into the pan.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, powdered sugar, and milk until smooth.
Spread the filling over the base and chill until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tablespoon butter, spread it over the filling, and chill until set.
Cut into squares.

title: Pea Soup with Salt Pork
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Put the split peas and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add the salt pork, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and black pepper.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and salt pork; dice the pork and return it to the pot if desired.
Stir the soup well, adjust the consistency with water if needed, and serve hot.

title: Tourtière (Québec Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the pork, beef, and onion; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and water.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has mostly evaporated; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Fit one crust into a 9-inch pie plate and add the filling.
Top with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few steam vents.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts; press firmly into the pan and chill.
Beat the softened 1/4 cup butter with the custard powder, icing sugar, and milk until smooth.
Spread the custard layer over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tablespoon butter; spread over the custard layer.
Chill until set, then cut into bars with a warm knife.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Combine the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl; cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough holds together; shape into a disk and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll out the dough and cut 12 circles to line a muffin pan.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and 1/4 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Pour the filling into the shells, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt; spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock; add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Simmer, whisking, until the gravy thickens, about 5 minutes.
Divide the fries among serving plates and scatter the cheese curds over them.
Pour the hot gravy over the fries and curds; serve immediately.

title: Split Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed and picked over
instructions: Combine the split peas, water, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover partially.
Simmer for 1 1/2–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are soft and the soup is thick.
Remove the ham hock and bay leaf; discard the bay leaf.
Take the meat from the ham hock, chop it, and return it to the pot.
Season with salt to taste and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Jiggs’ Dinner with Pease Pudding
ingredients: 1 cotton pudding bag or clean cheesecloth
1 small turnip, peeled and cut into chunks
4 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1.5 kg salt beef, soaked overnight and rinsed
instructions: Put the split peas in the pudding bag and tie it loosely, leaving room for them to swell.
Place the salt beef and onion in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 hour, skimming as needed.
Add the pea bag to the pot and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the turnip, carrots, potatoes, and cabbage. Simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Remove the pea pudding bag, mash the peas with a fork, and serve with the sliced salt beef and vegetables.

title: Toutons with Molasses
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and leave until foamy, about 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast mixture and butter, then knead until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Pinch off pieces of dough and flatten them into small rounds.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the rounds in batches until puffed and golden on both sides.
Serve warm with molasses.

title: Fish and Brewis
ingredients: 450 g salted cod, soaked overnight and rinsed
1 cup water, plus more for soaking
instructions: Break the hard bread into pieces and soak it in cold water overnight.
Drain the bread, cover it with fresh water, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain again.
Put the soaked cod in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer gently until it flakes, about 10 minutes. Drain and flake the fish.
Fry the salt pork in a skillet until crisp and its fat has rendered.
Stir the butter into the hot hard bread and serve it with the flaked cod, crisp pork, and rendered fat.

title: Cod au Gratin
ingredients: 500 g cod fillets, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Arrange the cod in a buttered baking dish.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk. Cook, stirring, until smooth and thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the cod and sprinkle with the cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake until bubbling and golden and the fish flakes easily, about 25 minutes.

title: Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 3 tablespoons cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Put the blueberries, 0.5 cup sugar, and water in a deep skillet or saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Mix the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Rub in the butter until the mixture is crumbly.
Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries. Cover tightly and cook gently for 15–18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Serve warm, spooning the blueberry sauce over the dumplings.

title: Tourtière du Lac-Saint-Jean
ingredients: 1 pound boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
8 cups peeled potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Mix the pork, beef, pork shoulder, onions, salt, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves; cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a deep roasting pan with pastry, leaving overhang.
Spread the potatoes in the pastry-lined pan, then add the meat mixture.
Pour in enough stock to come nearly to the top of the filling.
Cover with the pastry lid, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a small steam vent.
Brush the pastry with egg wash and bake for 30 minutes.
Reduce the oven to 275°F (135°C), cover the pan loosely with foil, and bake for 6 to 7 hours, adding hot stock if the filling looks dry.
Rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Pâté chinois
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain.
Mash the potatoes with the butter, warm milk, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish, then layer on the corn kernels and cream-style corn.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes, until hot and lightly browned.

title: Pea soup with ham
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Combine the split peas, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, water, savory, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partly covered for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the ham hock and bay leaf. Pull the meat from the bone, chop it, and return it to the pot.
Mash some of the peas against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Cretons
instructions: Combine the pork, milk, onion, salt, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves in a heavy saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring and breaking up the pork.
Reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for about 1 hour, stirring often, until the mixture is very soft and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the breadcrumbs and cook for 5 minutes.
Spoon into a container, cool, cover, and refrigerate until firm. Serve chilled on toast.

title: Pouding chômeur
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter an 8-inch square baking dish.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar until light, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour mixture alternately with the milk, just until combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared dish.
Warm the maple syrup and cream together in a saucepan, then carefully pour the mixture over the batter.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the cake is set and the sauce bubbles around the edges.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving warm.

title: Ontario Peameal Bacon Sandwiches
ingredients: 4 peameal bacon slices, about 1/2 inch thick
