instructions: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the peameal bacon for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Toast the cut sides of the rolls in the skillet.
Spread each roll with mustard, add a slice of peameal bacon, and serve.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 package (14 ounces) refrigerated double pie crust
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork, beef, water, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and savory.
Simmer, stirring and breaking up the meat, until cooked through and most of the liquid has evaporated, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 9-inch pie plate with one crust and add the filling.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cut the pie crust into rounds and fit them into a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk together the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and salt.
Divide the raisins among the pastry shells and pour in the filling, filling each shell about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer the tarts to a rack.

title: Maple Baked Beans
ingredients: 1/2 pound salt pork, cut into small pieces
instructions: Rinse the beans and soak them overnight in 6 cups of water.
Drain the beans, put them in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer until just tender, about 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Drain the beans, reserving 2 cups of cooking liquid.
Put the beans, salt pork, and onion in a bean pot or covered casserole.
Whisk the maple syrup, ketchup, mustard, salt, pepper, and reserved cooking liquid together; pour over the beans.
Cover and bake for 4 hours, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if the beans become dry.
Uncover for the final 30 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the top is browned.

title: Peach and Blueberry Cobbler
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Toss the peaches and blueberries with 1/3 cup sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch; spread in a baking dish.
Whisk the flour, remaining 1/4 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the milk and melted butter just until combined.
Spoon the batter over the fruit, leaving small gaps for steam to escape.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the fruit bubbles and the topping is golden.
Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Nova Scotia Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb cooked salt cod, soaked and flaked
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water, changing the water several times, until mild enough to eat; drain and flake.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter.
Mix the potatoes with the cod, onion, egg, and pepper; chill until firm.
Shape into patties and coat lightly with breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil over medium heat until browned on both sides and hot through.

title: Hodge Podge
ingredients: 1 lb new potatoes, scrubbed and halved
2 cups green or yellow beans, trimmed
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the water and potatoes; cover and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the beans and carrots and simmer until nearly tender, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the peas, cream, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently until all the vegetables are tender, then serve with some of the broth.

title: Rappie Pie
instructions: Put the chicken, quartered onion, water, salt, and pepper in a pot; simmer until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken and onion, strain and reserve the broth, and shred the chicken.
Finely grate the potatoes, then squeeze them through a clean cloth to remove the liquid.
Measure the squeezed potato pulp and stir in an equal volume of hot reserved broth, adding it gradually until loose and spoonable.
Spread half the potato mixture in a greased baking dish; scatter over the chicken and chopped onion, then cover with the remaining potato mixture.
Drizzle with melted butter and bake at 375°F for about 2 hours, until deeply golden and set.

title: Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen wild blueberries
instructions: Put the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide pot; bring to a simmer.
Mix the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries, leaving space between them.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through.

title: Oatcakes
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Grind the oats briefly until coarse, then mix with the flour, brown sugar, baking soda, and salt.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles crumbs.
Stir in the cold water to make a firm dough, adding a little more if needed.
Roll the dough 1/4 inch thick and cut into rounds or squares.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until crisp and lightly browned; cool on a rack.

title: Chicken Fricot
instructions: Put the chicken, water, salt, pepper, and bay leaves in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Skim the surface, lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 1 hour.
Lift out the chicken, remove the meat from the bones, and return the meat to the pot.
Add the onion, carrots, and potatoes; simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering broth, cover, and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

title: Rappie Pie
ingredients: 4 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Put the chicken and onion in a pot, cover with water, and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Remove the chicken, strain and reserve 4 cups of broth, then pull the meat from the bones and season it with salt and pepper.
Press the grated potatoes through a clean cloth over a bowl, reserving the potato starch and discarding the liquid.
Stir the potato starch back into the grated potatoes, then gradually mix in the boiling broth until smooth.
Spread half the potato mixture in a buttered baking dish, add the chicken, and cover with the remaining potato mixture.
Pour the melted butter over the top and bake at 375°F for about 2 hours, until deeply golden and crisp on top.

title: Acadian Seafood Chowder
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp; remove it and leave 1 tablespoon of drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened.
Add the potatoes, fish stock, water, and bay leaf; simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the haddock and scallops and simmer gently until just cooked through.
Stir in the lobster, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley and bacon, and serve hot.

title: New Brunswick Dulse with Brown Bread
ingredients: 1 cup dried dulse, rinsed and patted dry
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and grease a baking sheet.
Whisk together the whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, oats, baking soda, and salt.
Stir the buttermilk and molasses together, then add them to the dry ingredients and mix just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface, shape it into a round loaf, and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped; cool before slicing.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the dulse, and cook briefly until crisp; serve alongside the brown bread.

title: Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 3 tablespoons cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Put the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide pot and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries release their juices.
Whisk together the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries, leaving a little space between them.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.

title: Manitoba Bison and Barley Stew
ingredients: 1 pound bison stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the bison on all sides, working in batches if needed.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic.
Pour in the broth and add the barley, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for about 1 1/2 hours, until the bison and barley are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Perogies with Potato and Cheddar
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain well.
Mash the potatoes with the cheddar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and pepper. Let the filling cool.
Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Add the egg, sour cream, and melted butter; stir until a dough forms.
Knead the dough briefly, cover, and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut out 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Cook the perogies in batches in boiling water until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain.
Fry the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until golden. Add the oil and boiled perogies; fry until lightly browned, then serve with the onion.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups Saskatoon berries, fresh or frozen
1 tablespoon butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Combine the berries, 3/4 cup sugar, flour, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Spoon the filling into one pie crust and dot with the butter.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top. Brush with milk and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 350°F and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles.
Cool the pie before slicing so the filling can set.

title: Lake Winnipeg Pickerel with Dill Butter
instructions: Pat the pickerel dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge the fillets lightly in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the fillets for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and just cooked through.
Transfer the fish to plates. Melt the butter in the skillet, then stir in the lemon juice and dill.
Spoon the dill butter over the fish and serve immediately.

title: Manitoba Cabbage Rolls
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Remove the cabbage core. Carefully lower the cabbage into the water and peel off leaves as they soften; set aside 12 large leaves.
Mix the beef, pork, rice, onion, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick rib from each cabbage leaf. Place about 1/4 cup filling near the base, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Stir the crushed tomatoes, tomato juice, brown sugar, and lemon juice together in a bowl.
Spread a little sauce in a baking dish. Arrange the rolls seam-side down, pour the remaining sauce over them, and cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the cabbage is tender and the filling is cooked through.

title: Alberta Beef and Barley Soup
ingredients: 1 pound Alberta beef stewing meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef on all sides, working in batches if needed.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the broth, barley, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the beef and barley are tender.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Prairie Chicken and Dumplings
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and add the chicken, sage, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and dumpling salt in a bowl. Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering stew. Cover tightly and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check that the dumplings are cooked through, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 4 cups Saskatoon berries, fresh or thawed
1 tablespoon butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Fit one pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
In a bowl, toss the berries with the granulated sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and cinnamon.
Spoon the filling into the crust and dot with butter. Cover with the second crust, seal the edges, and cut vents in the top.
Brush the crust with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
Cool for at least 3 hours before slicing.

title: Alberta Beef and Bison Chili
ingredients: 1 can (19 ounces) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef and bison and cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Add the onion and bell pepper; cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, kidney beans, broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat. Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Stir in the graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts. Press the mixture firmly into the pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, icing sugar, and milk until smooth. Spread evenly over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with 2 tablespoons butter. Spread over the filling and chill until set.
Let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes, then cut into bars with a warm knife.

title: Pacific Salmon with Maple and Cedar
ingredients: 1 cedar plank, soaked in water for 1 hour
1 whole salmon side, about 2 lb, pin bones removed
instructions: Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates lightly.
Stir together the maple syrup, mustard, and lemon juice.
Season the salmon with salt and pepper, then brush with the maple mixture.
Place the soaked plank on the grill until it begins to smoke, about 3 minutes.
Set the salmon skin-side down on the plank, close the lid, and cook until it flakes easily, 15–20 minutes.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Melt 1/2 cup butter with the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat.
Whisk in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 2 minutes; remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Mix in the graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts, then press firmly into the pan.
Beat the softened butter with the custard powder, icing sugar, and milk until smooth; spread over the base and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with 1 tbsp butter, spread it over the custard layer, and chill until set before cutting into squares.

title: West Coast Spot Prawn Boil
instructions: Bring the water, salt, lemon, and bay leaves to a boil in a large pot.
Add the potatoes and simmer until nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Add the corn and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook just until pink and opaque, 2–3 minutes.
Drain and serve with melted butter and parsley.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Stir in the water and 2 tbsp oil until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for 1 minute.
Pat into a 1-inch-thick round and cut a few slashes across the top.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the bannock until golden and cooked through, about 8–10 minutes per side, adjusting the heat as needed.

title: Wild Mushroom and Barley Soup
instructions: Heat the butter and oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and begin to brown, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the barley, broth, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the barley is tender, 45–55 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Jiggs' Dinner with Pease Pudding
ingredients: 8 cups cold water, plus more for soaking
1 small head green cabbage, cut into wedges
4 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
2 medium turnips, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Rinse the split peas, put them in the cheesecloth, and tie it into a loose pouch.
Soak the salt beef in cold water overnight in the refrigerator, changing the water once if you prefer it less salty.
Put the beef in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 1 hour, skimming as needed.
Add the pea pouch and simmer for 1 hour more, keeping the pouch submerged.
Add the turnip and carrots; simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and simmer until all the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pea pouch, mash the peas with a fork, and serve with sliced beef and vegetables.

title: Fish and Brewis
instructions: Break the hard bread into pieces, cover with cold water, and soak overnight.
Rinse the salt cod and soak it in cold water overnight in a separate bowl, changing the water once.
Drain the bread, cover it with fresh water, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes; drain again.
Put the cod in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer gently until it flakes, about 10 minutes; drain.
Fry the salt pork in a skillet until crisp and golden. Stir in the butter.
Serve the bread and cod together, topped with the hot pork scraps and drippings.

title: Toutons
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water and oil, then mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead for about 5 minutes, cover, and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Roll the dough about 1/2 inch thick and cut into rounds.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Fry the rounds in batches until puffed and golden on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve warm with molasses.

title: Newfoundland Style Cod au Gratin
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds cod fillets, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a shallow baking dish.
Arrange the cod in the dish.
Melt the butter in a saucepan; cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper, then stir in half the cheese.
Pour the sauce over the cod and scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Mix the breadcrumbs with melted butter, sprinkle over the dish, and bake until bubbling and golden, about 30 minutes.

title: Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen Newfoundland blueberries
instructions: Put the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, and water in a wide saucepan; bring to a simmer.
Mix the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through, about 15 minutes; do not lift the lid while they cook.
Serve warm, spooning berries and syrup over the dumplings.

title: Tourtière du Lac-Saint-Jean
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
6 cups peeled potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork, beef, chicken, salt, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves; cook, stirring, until the meat is lightly browned.
Let the meat mixture cool, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Stir the potatoes into the chilled meat mixture.
Line a deep, oven-safe pot with half the pastry, leaving an overhang. Fill with the meat and potato mixture, then pour in enough stock to just cover.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a small vent in the center. Brush with egg wash.
Bake for 30 minutes, then lower the oven to 250°F (120°C) and bake for about 6 hours, adding hot stock through the vent if the filling looks dry.
Let rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Pâté chinois
ingredients: 2 cans (14 ounces each) whole-kernel corn, drained
2 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain well.
Mash the potatoes with the butter, milk, and 1/2 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened, then add the beef, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Layer the cream-style corn and drained corn over it.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly on top, making ridges with a fork.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until bubbling and lightly golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Pea soup with ham
ingredients: 1 pound dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Put the split peas, water, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, savory, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skimming any foam, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover partially and simmer for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are very soft.
Remove the ham hock. Pull off the meat, discard the bone and skin, and dice the meat.
Stir the ham meat and cooked ham into the soup. Add salt to taste.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, adding water if the soup is thicker than you like. Remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Cretons
instructions: Combine the pork, milk, onion, salt, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves in a heavy saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, breaking up the pork with a spoon.
Reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for about 1 hour, stirring often, until the pork is very soft and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the breadcrumbs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the mixture is thick and spreadable.
Spoon into a clean container, cool, cover, and refrigerate until firm. Serve chilled on toast.

title: Maple sugar pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edge.
Whisk the maple syrup, brown sugar, cream, eggs, flour, melted butter, and salt until smooth.
Pour the filling into the crust.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still has a slight wobble.
Cool completely before slicing so the filling can set.

title: Peameal Bacon Sandwich
ingredients: 1 boneless peameal bacon roast, about 1 kg
instructions: Slice the peameal bacon into 1 cm-thick pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the slices for 3–4 minutes per side, until hot and browned.
Split and toast the kaiser rolls.
Spread the rolls with Dijon mustard and fill with the hot peameal bacon.

title: Tourtière (Québec-Style Meat Pie)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the pork, beef, potato, spices, salt, pepper, and water.
Simmer, stirring and breaking up the meat, until cooked through and most of the liquid has evaporated, about 25 minutes. Cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a 23 cm pie plate with pastry and add the filling.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 35–40 minutes.

title: Ontario Butter Tarts
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and place the pastry shells in a muffin tin.
Whisk the brown sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, egg, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Divide the raisins among the shells and pour in the filling, leaving room at the top.
Bake until the pastry is golden and the filling is just set, about 18–22 minutes.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

title: Maple-Baked Beans
ingredients: 2 cups dried navy beans, picked over and rinsed
115 g salt pork, cut into cubes
instructions: Put the beans in a large bowl, cover with cold water, and soak overnight.
Drain the beans, place them in a pot, and cover with fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender but still holding their shape, about 45–60 minutes. Drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 150°C. Put the beans and onion in a covered baking dish.
Stir the maple syrup, brown sugar, ketchup, mustard, salt, pepper, and reserved liquid together, then pour over the beans.
Tuck in the salt pork, cover, and bake for 4 hours, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if dry.
Uncover and bake for 30 minutes, until thick and browned on top.

title: Peach Melba
instructions: Bring the granulated sugar and water to a simmer in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Halve and pit the peaches, then poach them in the syrup for 5–8 minutes, until tender. Cool and peel.
Blend the raspberries with the icing sugar and lemon juice, then strain out the seeds.
Place a scoop of ice cream in each serving dish and add two peach halves.
Spoon raspberry sauce over the peaches and serve.

title: Nova Scotia Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb cooked salt cod, soaked and flaked
2 cups peeled potatoes, cut into chunks
instructions: If the salt cod is very salty, soak it in cold water in the refrigerator, changing the water several times; drain and flake it.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Mix the potatoes, cod, onion, egg, and pepper; chill until firm enough to shape.
Form into 8 patties and coat lightly with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the patties over medium heat until golden on both sides and hot through.

title: Hodge Podge
ingredients: 2 cups green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cups wax beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Put the potatoes and carrots in a large pot and cover with water; simmer until nearly tender.
Add the green beans and wax beans and cook until tender-crisp.
Add the peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Drain off most of the water, leaving about 1 cup in the pot.
Stir in the milk, cream, butter, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Nova Scotia Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen wild blueberries
3 tbsp cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Combine the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide, heavy pot; bring to a simmer.
Mix the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries, leaving small gaps for steam.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
Serve warm with cream or vanilla ice cream.

title: Rappie Pie
instructions: Put the chicken, water, halved onion, 1 teaspoon salt, and pepper in a pot; simmer until the chicken is cooked and tender.
Remove the chicken and onion; strain and reserve the broth. Shred the chicken and keep it warm.
Grate the potatoes finely, then squeeze them in a clean cloth over a bowl to collect the liquid.
Let the potato liquid settle, pour off the clear water, and return the starch at the bottom to the grated potatoes.
Gradually stir hot broth into the potatoes until they form a thick, moist mixture; stir in the melted butter and remaining salt.
Spread half the potato mixture in a greased baking dish, add the shredded chicken and chopped onion, then cover with the remaining potato mixture.
Scatter the diced salt pork over the top and bake at 375°F for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until deeply golden and set.

title: Nova Scotia Oatcakes
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pulse the oats in a food processor until coarsely ground, or crush them with a rolling pin.
Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar, salt, and baking soda in a bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture is crumbly.
Stir in the boiling water to make a firm dough; add a little more water if needed.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut into squares or rounds.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until lightly browned; cool on the baking sheet.

title: Acadian Chicken Fricot
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into pieces
instructions: Put the chicken, 10 cups water, salt, pepper, onion, and bay leaf in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 1 hour.
Lift out the chicken. Strain the broth if desired, return it to the pot, and bring it to a simmer.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and celery; simmer until nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Remove the chicken meat from the bones and return the meat to the pot.
Whisk the flour with 1/2 cup cold water until smooth, then stir it into the simmering broth.
Cook, stirring, until the broth thickens and the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes; stir in the parsley and serve.

title: Acadian Chicken and Dumplings (Poutines à Trou)
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Bring the chicken broth, carrot, celery, and pepper to a simmer in a large pot; cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken.
Drop tablespoon-sized pieces of dough into the gently simmering broth, leaving space between them.
Cover and simmer without lifting the lid until the dumplings are cooked through, about 15 minutes.

title: New Brunswick Salmon Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound skinless salmon fillet, cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and stock; bring to a boil, then simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the milk, cream, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Stir in the dill and serve hot.

title: Acadian Baked Beans (Fèves au Lard)
ingredients: 8 cups cold water, plus more for soaking
1/2 pound salt pork, cut into cubes
instructions: Rinse the beans, cover them with 8 cups cold water, and soak overnight.
Drain the beans and put them in a large pot; cover with fresh water and simmer until the skins begin to split, about 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 300°F.
Drain the beans, reserving 2 cups of their cooking liquid, and put the beans in a covered baking dish with the onion and salt pork.
Stir the molasses, brown sugar, mustard, salt, and pepper into the reserved liquid, then pour it over the beans.
Add the boiling water, cover, and bake until tender and richly flavored, about 5 hours; check occasionally and add hot water if needed.

title: New Brunswick Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen wild blueberries
instructions: Put the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide, heavy pot.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until crumbly, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries, leaving small gaps for steam.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through, about 15 minutes; do not lift the lid while they cook.

title: Manitoba Farmer Sausage and Cabbage
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sausage and brown for 4 to 5 minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion, cabbage, and carrots to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the broth and stir in the dill and pepper.
Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Return the sausage to the skillet and heat through.

title: Tourtière (French-Canadian Meat Pie)
ingredients: 1 double-crust pie pastry, for a 9-inch pie
instructions: Combine the pork, beef, onion, water, salt, cinnamon, cloves, and pepper in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 25 minutes, breaking up the meat as it cooks.
Stir in the breadcrumbs and let the filling cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a 9-inch pie plate with the bottom pastry and spoon in the cooled filling.
Cover with the top pastry, seal and crimp the edges, and cut a few vents.
Brush the top with milk and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Perogies with Potato, Cheddar, and Onion
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain well.
Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Mash the potatoes with the cheddar, cooked onion, and black pepper; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the egg, sour cream, and water, and stir into a dough.
Knead the dough briefly until smooth, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut into 3-inch rounds.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the perogies in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; lift out with a slotted spoon.
Serve with melted butter and sour cream.

title: Saskatoon Berry Bannock
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms, then gently fold in the berries.
Pat the dough into a 1-inch-thick round on the baking sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Cool slightly before cutting into wedges.

title: Creamy Wild Rice Soup
instructions: Combine the wild rice, broth, and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat, and simmer until the rice is tender, about 45 to 55 minutes; drain any excess liquid.
Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, celery, carrot, and mushrooms; cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk, then add the thyme, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently until thickened, about 8 minutes; do not boil.
Stir in the cooked wild rice and heat through.

title: Alberta Beef and Barley Soup
ingredients: 1 pound stewing beef, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef on all sides.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the broth, barley, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the beef and barley are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Prairie Chicken and Dumplings
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 6 minutes.
Add the broth, chicken, sage, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop tablespoonfuls of dough onto the simmering stew, leaving space between them.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through.

title: Alberta Beef Hash
ingredients: 4 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the onion and potatoes, then season with salt and pepper.
Add the broth, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender and the edges are browned.
Stir in the parsley and serve.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 1 double-crust pie pastry, for a 9-inch pie
4 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
1 tablespoon butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Fit one pastry crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
In a bowl, toss the berries with 3/4 cup sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and cinnamon.
Spoon the berry filling into the crust and dot with butter. Cover with the second crust, seal the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush the top crust with milk and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles.
Cool for at least 3 hours before slicing.

title: Perogy Casserole
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain.
Mash the potatoes with the sour cream, butter, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Cook the lasagna noodles according to package directions; drain.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Spread a little milk in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Layer noodles, mashed potatoes, cheddar, and onion; repeat, finishing with noodles and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for 10 minutes more, until bubbling and golden.

title: Salmon Candy
ingredients: 2 pounds skin-on salmon fillet, pin bones removed
instructions: Cut the salmon into 1-inch-wide strips.
Whisk the brown sugar, maple syrup, soy sauce, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss the salmon with the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for 8 hours.
Rinse the salmon briefly and pat it dry. Arrange the pieces on a rack and let them air-dry until tacky, about 1 hour.
Heat a smoker to 180°F and add the soaked alder chips.
Smoke the salmon until firm and glossy, about 3 hours, then cool before serving.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Combine the melted butter, sugar, and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat. Stir in the egg and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Remove from the heat and mix in the graham cracker crumbs, coconut, and walnuts.
Press the mixture firmly into the pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Beat the softened butter, custard powder, and milk until smooth. Gradually beat in the icing sugar.
Spread the custard layer over the chilled base and refrigerate until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining butter. Spread it over the custard layer.
Chill until set, then cut into squares with a warm knife.

title: West Coast Smoked Salmon Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the fish stock, then add the potatoes. Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the milk and cream and warm gently without boiling.
Fold in the smoked salmon, dill, pepper, and salt. Heat through and serve topped with the bacon.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir in the water and oil until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently just until smooth.
Pat the dough into a 1-inch-thick round and cut it into 8 wedges.
Heat 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the wedges in batches until golden and cooked through, about 4 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels.

title: BC Spot Prawns with Garlic Butter
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds live or fresh spot prawns, shells on
instructions: Rinse the prawns under cold water and drain well.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, taking care not to brown it.
Add the prawns and cook, turning once, until pink and just opaque, about 2 minutes per side.
Stir in the lemon juice, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately with the garlic butter from the pan.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
instructions: Grind the allspice berries, then blend with the sugar, peppers, scallions, garlic, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, soy sauce, lime juice, and salt.
Rub the marinade over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium, or heat an oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes; or roast for 40–50 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, cooked and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, lime juice, and salt; set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and stir in the brown sugar until it bubbles and darkens.
Add the chicken and turn to coat; brown for 6–8 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, onion, and garlic.
Add the coconut milk, stock, scallions, and thyme; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the steak with salt.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the steak on both sides.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, beef stock, tomato paste, vinegar, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the steak is very tender, about 2½–3 hours.
Transfer the steak to a plate and shred it with two forks.
Return the shredded beef to the pot and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes; remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, salt, pepper, thyme, garlic, onion, sour orange juice, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Remove the pork and reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and golden, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of cold water until smooth.
Season the fish with the lime juice, ½ teaspoon of salt, and black pepper; set aside.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion, tomato, and thyme until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the remaining 3 cups of water and the remaining salt; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornmeal mixture gradually and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir the butter into the cou-cou and keep warm.
Steam the fish over the simmering tomato mixture until opaque and cooked through, about 8–10 minutes.
Serve the fish with the cou-cou.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded for less heat
1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, Scotch bonnet, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, spices, salt, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken skin-side down, turning occasionally, until deeply browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, cooked and drained
2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, salt, and black pepper; set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the brown sugar until dark amber.
Add the chicken carefully and turn to coat; brown for 5 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, onion, and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir to coat in the seasonings.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, then add the carrot and hot pepper sauce.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and let stand covered for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, brown sugar, turmeric, and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water and oil; knead until a soft dough forms, then cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Drain the soaked chickpeas and simmer them in 3 cups fresh water until tender, about 45 minutes; drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.
Heat a little oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until softened.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin, geera, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas and reserved cooking liquid; simmer until thick, then stir in the cilantro.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a thin round.
Fry the rounds in hot oil until puffed and lightly golden, about 30 seconds per side; drain.
Sandwich spoonfuls of chickpeas between two fried dough rounds and top with tamarind chutney.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Add the whole Scotch bonnet, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot, add the water, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour; remove the pork and reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
ingredients: 4 flying fish fillets, about 6 oz each
instructions: Rub the fish with lime juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper; set aside for 15 minutes.
Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a saucepan and add the okra; simmer until tender, about 8 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal with the remaining 2 cups of water until smooth.
Gradually stir the cornmeal mixture into the okra and cooking water.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 10 minutes; stir in the butter and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion, tomato, bell pepper, garlic, and thyme until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the fish and a splash of water, cover, and simmer until the fish flakes easily, about 8–10 minutes.
Serve the flying fish with the cou-cou.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill or oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grill the chicken over medium heat, turning occasionally, for 35–45 minutes, or bake until browned and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 lb bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Toss the chicken with green seasoning, lime juice, and salt; marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and cook until dark amber.
Add the chicken and turn to coat; brown for 5 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, onion, and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Pour in the coconut milk and stock, then add the carrot, scallions, Scotch bonnet, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and fluff gently before serving.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1½-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme, cloves, salt, and pepper; cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot and add the water.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 60–75 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Drain the pork and pat the pieces dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Mix the cornmeal with 1 cup of water until smooth; set aside.
Season the fish with lime juice, ½ teaspoon salt, and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion, tomato, thyme, and scallions for 3 minutes.
Add the fish and cook gently for 4–6 minutes, turning once, until opaque and flaky.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water and the remaining salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal mixture. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10–15 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the butter and serve the cou-cou with the fish and sauce.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the salt pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the onion and bell pepper; cook for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and sofrito and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, oregano, and pigeon peas.
Add the rice, broth, and salt; stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20–25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fold in the olives, cover, and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded for less heat
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, pepper, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium heat and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
instructions: Toss the chicken with green seasoning, lime juice, salt, and pepper; marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the brown sugar.
Cook until the sugar bubbles and turns deep amber.
Add the chicken and brown it, turning to coat in the caramel.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, onion, and garlic.
Add coconut milk and stock, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the parsley.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Season the fish with lime juice, half the salt, and the black pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and tomato until softened.
Add 1/2 cup water, thyme, and hot pepper sauce; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently until cooked through, about 8–10 minutes.
For the cou-cou, bring 3 cups of water and the remaining salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Add the okra and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Whisk the cornmeal with the remaining 1 cup of water until smooth.
Gradually stir the cornmeal mixture into the pan and cook, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the butter and serve with the fish and sauce.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme, salt, pepper, and cloves in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot and add the water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Drain the pork and pat it dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the steak with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the steak on both sides.
Add the onion, bell peppers, garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the steak is very tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the steak and shred it with two forks.
Return the shredded steak to the pot, stir in the olives, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded for less heat
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, salt, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until charred in spots and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
½ tsp salt, or to taste
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water and oil, then knead until a soft dough forms.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Heat a little oil in a saucepan and cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and cumin, then add the chickpeas and water.
Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas; stir in cilantro and salt.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten each into a thin round, and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides.
Serve the chickpeas spooned between pairs of fried breads.

title: Jamaican Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 lb salted cod, soaked overnight and drained
1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: Place the soaked cod in a saucepan, cover with fresh water, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drain the cod, remove any skin and bones, and flake it into pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion, tomato, bell pepper, scallions, Scotch bonnet, and thyme until softened.
Add the flaked cod and black pepper; cook for 3 minutes.
Gently fold in the ackee and cook until heated through, taking care not to break it up.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: ½ cup sliced pimiento-stuffed green olives
instructions: Season the steak with salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the steak on both sides.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, broth, olives, capers, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently until the steak is tender, about 2½ hours.
Transfer the steak to a plate and shred it with two forks.
Return the shredded beef to the pot and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and cook for 2 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the gandules, tomato sauce, adobo, and oregano.
Add the rice, broth, olives, and bay leaf; stir once to combine.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce the heat to low.
Cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat, rest covered for 5 minutes, and fluff with a fork.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, pepper, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium, or heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes; or roast it for 40–45 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 lb bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces
2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, lime juice, salt, and pepper; set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and cook until dark amber.
Add the chicken and turn to coat. Brown for 5–7 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, onion, and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Pour in the coconut milk and stock, then stir in the ketchup and thyme.
Add the pumpkin and whole Scotch bonnet. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the thyme and pepper. Fluff the rice and serve.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the steak with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the steak on both sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and bell peppers to the pot; cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, wine, tomato paste, cumin, oregano, and bay leaves.
Return the steak to the pot. Cover and simmer gently for 2½–3 hours, until fork-tender.
Transfer the steak to a plate and shred it with two forks. Return the meat to the sauce and stir in the olives.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and stir in the cilantro before serving.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 3 cups medium-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the salt pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, sazón, oregano, pigeon peas, rice, broth, salt, and olives; stir well.
Bring to a boil and cook uncovered until most of the liquid has evaporated and small steam holes appear in the rice, about 8–10 minutes.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Fluff the rice gently and serve.

title: Barbadian Flying Fish with Cou-Cou
ingredients: 1 lb flying fish fillets, or other firm white fish fillets
instructions: Rub the fish with lime juice, salt, and black pepper; set aside for 10 minutes.
Dust the fish lightly with flour. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the fillets for 3–4 minutes per side, until cooked through. Set aside.
Add the onion and tomato to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the water, tomato paste, thyme, and cayenne; simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the fish to the skillet and spoon the sauce over it. Keep warm.
For the cou-cou, bring 3 cups of the water to a boil in a saucepan. Add the okra and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Whisk the cornmeal with the remaining 1 cup water until smooth. Slowly stir it into the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 10 minutes. Stir in the butter.
Serve the cou-cou with the fish and sauce.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, and pepper into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
1 cup dried split chickpeas, soaked overnight
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl; add warm water and oil and knead into a soft dough.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Drain the chickpeas and simmer them with onion, garlic, curry powder, cumin, turmeric, salt, and water until tender, about 1 hour; mash lightly.
Divide the dough into 16 balls, cover, and rest for 15 minutes.
Flatten each ball into a thin round and fry in hot oil until puffed and lightly golden on both sides.
Sandwich a spoonful of chickpeas between two fried rounds and drizzle with tamarind sauce.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the ham and cook for 3 minutes; stir in the sofrito and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, sazón, oregano, pigeon peas, broth, salt, and olives; bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook over low heat for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Fluff the rice gently and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, pepper, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot, add the water, and simmer until tender, about 1 hour.
Drain the pork and pat it dry; remove the whole pepper.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 5 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of water until smooth.
Simmer the okra, remaining water, and salt in a saucepan until tender, about 8 minutes.
Slowly stir in the cornmeal mixture and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 10 minutes; stir in the butter.
Rub the fish with lime juice, salt, and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet; cook the onion, tomato, and thyme for 3 minutes.
Add the fish and 1/2 cup water, cover, and simmer until the fish flakes easily, about 8 minutes.
Serve the fish with the cou-cou.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
instructions: Rinse the kidney beans, cover with the water, and soak overnight.
Drain the beans, then simmer them in fresh water until nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, rice, scallions, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Remove the scallions, thyme stems, and whole pepper before serving.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh dasheen leaves or spinach, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the greens, okra, coconut milk, water, scallions, thyme, Scotch bonnet, and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the greens are very tender, about 30 minutes.
Remove the thyme stems and whole pepper.
Blend until smooth, or mash to a chunky consistency, then serve hot.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the ham for 3 minutes.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, oregano, cumin, salt, rice, pigeon peas, broth, olives, and bay leaf; stir well.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Let stand covered for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and serve.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, turmeric, and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water and oil, then knead until a soft dough forms; cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Heat a little oil in a saucepan and stir in the curry powder and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas, water, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes, lightly mashing some of the chickpeas.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten them into thin rounds, and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides.
Spoon chickpeas onto one fried dough round, top with another round and mango chutney, and serve warm.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the steak with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the steak on both sides; transfer it to a plate.
Cook the onion and bell peppers in the pot until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and oregano, then add the tomatoes, broth, wine, and bay leaf.
Return the steak to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until very tender, about 2 hours.
Shred the steak with two forks, stir in the olives, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend the allspice, thyme, Scotch bonnet, scallions, garlic, onion, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, cinnamon, salt, pepper, and oil into a thick marinade.
Make shallow cuts in the chicken and coat it with the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
1 cup dried yellow split peas, soaked overnight
instructions: Combine the flour, yeast, turmeric, cumin, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Add the warm water and 2 tablespoons oil; knead until soft and smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 hour.
Drain the split peas and simmer them in 3 cups water until tender, about 45 minutes; drain.
Mash the peas with the garlic, cumin, salt, and cayenne into a thick filling.
Divide the dough into 16 balls, cover, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Flatten each ball into a thin round and fry in hot oil until puffed and lightly browned on both sides.
Sandwich a spoonful of pea filling and tamarind sauce between two fried rounds.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the salt pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas and rice until evenly coated.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the cilantro before serving.

title: Jamaican Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water for 8 hours, changing the water several times.
Drain the cod, place it in a pot of fresh water, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drain, remove any skin and bones, and flake the fish.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, tomato, bell pepper, scallions, Scotch bonnet, and thyme; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flaked cod and black pepper; cook for 3 minutes.
Gently fold in the ackee and heat through without breaking it up, about 3 minutes.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, garlic, onion, scallions, Scotch bonnet, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot and add the water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Remove the pork and pat the pieces dry; reserve the cooking liquid for another use.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and deeply browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Grind the allspice berries and peppercorns into a coarse powder.
Blend with the scallions, onion, Scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, and salt.
Rub the marinade over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Grill over medium heat, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
instructions: Rub the chicken with the green seasoning and let it stand for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the brown sugar, and cook until dark and bubbling.
Add the chicken and stir to coat; cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the onion, garlic, and pigeon peas; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, coconut milk, broth, carrot, and salt; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the cilantro.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Season the fish with the lime juice, half the salt, and half the pepper; set aside for 15 minutes.
Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan and add the okra.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal, then cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter and remaining salt; keep warm.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and tomato until softened.
Add the thyme, remaining pepper, and fish; cover and cook gently until the fish flakes, about 8 minutes.
Serve the flying fish with the cou-cou.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the salt pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, and garlic; cook until softened.
Add the sofrito, pigeon peas, rice, adobo, annatto, and olives; stir to coat the rice.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1½-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, onion, garlic, lime juice, orange juice, salt, pepper, and thyme in a bowl.
Add the whole Scotch bonnet and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot; add the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 45 minutes; remove the pork and discard the pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and golden, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, and salt into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium heat and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and green seasoning.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and add the sugar.
Cook the sugar until it bubbles and turns deep brown.
Add the chicken and stir to coat; brown for 5 minutes.
Stir in the onion, garlic, and ketchup, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, pigeon peas, coconut milk, stock, and carrot.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the scallions and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Place the beef in a pot, cover with water, and simmer until tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the beef and shred it with two forks; reserve 1 cup of cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, broth, wine, cumin, oregano, bay leaves, and reserved cooking liquid.
Stir in the shredded beef and simmer until the sauce thickens, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the olives and remove the bay leaves before serving.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Combine the pork, lime juice, orange juice, onion, garlic, peppers, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot and add the water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour; drain well.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and golden, about 4 to 6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans, then place them in a pot with the water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the beans are nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, rice, scallions, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and fluff the rice before serving.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, allspice, thyme, salt, pepper, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium heat, or preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes; or bake for 40–50 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, and green seasoning.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; add the sugar and cook until dark amber.
Add the chicken and stir to coat; brown for 5–7 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, coconut milk, stock, carrot, scallions, and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25–30 minutes.
Fluff gently and serve.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Mix the cornmeal with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil with the okra and salt; cook until the okra is tender.
Gradually stir in the cornmeal mixture, then cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter and keep the cou-cou warm.
Season the fish with lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet; cook the onion, tomato, and garlic until softened.
Add the fish and stock; cover and simmer until the fish flakes easily, about 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and serve the fish with the cou-cou.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, salt, pepper, thyme, cloves, Scotch bonnet, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 60–75 minutes.
Remove the pork and reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid; pat the pork dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain the pork and serve with the reserved cooking liquid for dipping.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and salt pork; cook for 4 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the tomato sauce, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the pigeon peas, rice, broth, olives, and bay leaf; stir once.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20–25 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded for less heat
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, pepper, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium heat, or heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes; or bake until cooked through, about 45–55 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, cumin, and salt; add warm water and 1 tablespoon oil, then knead into a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Drain the chickpeas and simmer them with the onion, garlic, curry powder, cumin, salt, and 3 cups water until tender, about 1 hour; stir in the cilantro.
Divide the dough into 16 balls, cover, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Pat each ball into a thin round and fry in hot oil until puffed and lightly golden on both sides.
Sandwich spoonfuls of chickpeas between two fried rounds and serve warm.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the salt pork until lightly browned.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, broth, and olives, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 Scotch bonnet peppers, pierced with a knife
instructions: Combine the pork, lime juice, orange juice, onion, garlic, peppers, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot, add the water, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the pork is tender, about 1 hour; remove the pork and pat it dry.
