Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of water until smooth and set aside.
Rub the fish with lime juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and the black pepper; set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion, tomato, bell pepper, and garlic until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, then add the fish and cook gently until it flakes, about 8 minutes.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil in a heavy pot; gradually whisk in the cornmeal mixture.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 10–15 minutes; stir in the butter.
Serve the cou-cou with the flying fish and its sauce.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, seeded for less heat
instructions: Blend the scallions, onion, peppers, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, and oil into a rough paste.
Coat the chicken with the paste, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 30–40 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 1 lb dasheen leaves or spinach, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and scallions; cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the dasheen leaves or spinach, okra, coconut milk, water, thyme, salt, pepper, and whole Scotch bonnet.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the leaves and okra are very tender, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pepper and blend or mash the mixture to your preferred texture.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, then serve.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Mix the cornmeal with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil in a saucepan; add the okra and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Gradually stir in the cornmeal mixture, then cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter and keep the cou-cou warm.
Season the fish with lime juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet; cook the onion, tomato, and thyme until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the fish and 1/2 cup water; cover and simmer until the fish flakes easily, about 8 minutes.
Serve the fish and sauce with the cou-cou.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 1 packet (about 1 oz) sazón seasoning with annatto
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and ham; cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the sazón, cumin, pigeon peas, rice, broth, salt, and olives.
Bring to a boil, then stir once and cover the pot tightly.
Reduce the heat to low and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes; fluff before serving.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme, salt, pepper, and cloves in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot; add the water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the pork is tender, about 1 hour; drain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until crisp and browned, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, Scotch bonnet, garlic, thyme, spices, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, salt, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water and oil; knead until a soft dough forms.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 hour.
Mix the chickpeas with the curry powder, garlic, cumin, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Simmer the chickpeas for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and tender.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a thin round.
Fry the dough rounds in hot oil for about 30 seconds per side, until puffed and golden.
Sandwich the chickpeas and chutney between two fried rounds to serve.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of cold water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water, butter, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal mixture and cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until thick and smooth, about 20 minutes.
Season the fish with lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the tomato, tomato paste, fish stock, and thyme; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently until cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Serve the flying fish with the cou-cou.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the salt pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, adobo, oregano, bay leaf, and pigeon peas; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, water, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Cook uncovered until most of the water is absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently and serve.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 1½ lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 lb calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Toss the beef with the lime juice, salt, and pepper; let it stand for 10 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Pour in the beef stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the squash, carrots, potatoes, cabbage, celery, macaroni, and thyme.
Add the whole Scotch bonnet and simmer until the vegetables and pasta are tender, about 25 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and stir in the parsley before serving.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 small Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Blend the scallions, pepper, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, salt, and oil into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 1 lb dasheen leaves or spinach, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the leaves, okra, coconut milk, water, thyme, salt, and pepper; add the whole pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the leaves and okra are tender, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pepper and blend the mixture until smooth or partly chunky.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, then serve.

title: Haitian Griot
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, lime juice, onion, garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot and add the water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Drain the pork and pat the pieces dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until deeply golden and crisp, about 4–6 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Puerto Rican Arroz con Gandules
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the tomato sauce, adobo, oregano, and sazón; cook for 1 minute.
Add the gandules, rice, water, and salt, and stir once.
Bring to a boil and cook uncovered until most of the water has evaporated and small steam holes appear, about 8 minutes.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Fluff gently with a fork and serve.

title: Barbadian Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of water until smooth and set aside.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a boil in a saucepan.
Add the okra and 1 teaspoon of salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Slowly stir in the cornmeal mixture and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter and keep the cou-cou warm.
Rub the fish with the lime juice, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and the black pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the tomato and thyme and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the fish and cook gently until opaque and flaky, about 5 minutes per side.
Serve the fish with the cou-cou.

title: Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and drained
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the salt pork and cook until browned.
Stir in the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes. Add the tomato sauce, sazón, oregano, and cumin; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, water, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Cook uncovered until most of the water has evaporated and small steam holes appear in the rice.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20 minutes. Fluff gently before serving.

title: Mofongo
ingredients: 3 green plantains, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the plantain pieces in batches for 5 to 7 minutes, until tender but not browned. Drain well.
Pound the garlic and salt together in a pilón or sturdy bowl. Add the pork cracklings and pound until combined.
Add the fried plantains a few pieces at a time, pounding until chunky and well mixed.
Stir in the olive oil and enough warm broth to bring the mixture together. Shape into mounds and serve hot.

title: Pollo Guisado
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches, then set aside.
Add the sofrito to the pot and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the tomato sauce, sazón, and oregano.
Return the chicken to the pot. Add the olives, potatoes, and water; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 40 to 45 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through. Stir in the cilantro.

title: Pasteles de Yuca
ingredients: 2 pounds yuca, peeled and finely grated
1 pound boneless pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
8 banana leaves, cut into 10-inch squares and warmed
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the pork and cook until browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce, oregano, and olives. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the pork is tender; cool slightly.
Mix the grated yuca and green banana with the sofrito, achiote oil, and salt.
Lay out a banana leaf square and brush lightly with achiote oil. Spread about 1/2 cup of the yuca mixture in the center.
Add a spoonful of pork filling, fold the leaf into a packet, and tie securely with twine. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Boil the packets in salted water for 45 minutes. Drain, unwrap, and serve hot.

title: Tembleque
instructions: Whisk 1 cup of the coconut milk with the cornstarch until smooth.
Pour the remaining coconut milk into a saucepan. Add the sugar, salt, and cinnamon stick; bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk in the cornstarch mixture. Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling, about 5 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla.
Pour into a lightly dampened mold or serving cups. Cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set. Sprinkle with ground cinnamon before serving.

title: Griot (Haitian Fried Pork)
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, scallions, Scotch bonnet, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Transfer the pork and marinade to a pot, add the water, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 60 to 75 minutes.
Remove the pork and pat it dry; reserve the cooking liquid for another use.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until deeply browned and crisp, about 5 to 7 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Diri ak Pwa (Rice and Beans)
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, rinsed
instructions: Put the beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours; reserve 3 cups of cooking liquid and drain the beans.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion, garlic, and scallions until softened.
Add the beans, thyme, Scotch bonnet, reserved cooking liquid, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover, and cook over low heat until the liquid is absorbed, about 18 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Soup Joumou (Haitian Pumpkin Soup)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 lb calabaza or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Toss the beef with the lime juice and let it stand for 10 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the squash and water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the squash and beef are very tender, about 1 hour.
Mash the squash into the broth or blend a portion and return it to the pot.
Add the carrots, potatoes, cabbage, celery, thyme, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the macaroni and cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and serve hot.

title: Legim (Haitian Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and thyme.
Add the eggplant, chayote, cabbage, carrots, water, salt, and pepper.
Place the Scotch bonnet on top, cover, and cook over low heat until the vegetables are very soft, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and mash the vegetables lightly, leaving some texture.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve with rice.

title: Mayi Moulen ak Pwa (Cornmeal with Beans)
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, rinsed
instructions: Put the beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours; keep the beans and cooking liquid in the pot.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the onion, garlic, and scallions until softened.
Stir the aromatics, thyme, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper into the beans.
Slowly whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Cover and cook over low heat, stirring often, until thick and tender, about 20 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and serve warm.

title: La Bandera Dominicana (Rice, Beans, and Stewed Chicken)
ingredients: 2 cups cooked red kidney beans, with 1 cup cooking liquid
instructions: Season the chicken with lime juice, oregano, half the salt, and half the garlic; let it stand for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot and brown the chicken on all sides. Add half the onion and bell pepper, then cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomato sauce. Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed.
In a separate pot, heat the remaining oil and cook the remaining garlic and onion for 1 minute. Add the rice, water, and remaining salt.
Bring the rice to a boil, cover, and cook on low until tender, about 18 minutes. Let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing.
Simmer the beans with their cooking liquid and the remaining bell pepper until thickened. Stir in the cilantro.
Serve the chicken with the rice and beans.

title: Mangú with Los Tres Golpes
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the plantains in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss the onion with the vinegar and let it stand for 10 minutes. Heat 2 tablespoons oil and cook the onion until soft.
Drain the plantains, reserving 1 cup of cooking water. Mash with the butter, adding warm water a little at a time until smooth and soft.
Fry the cheese in a skillet until golden on both sides. Set aside.
Fry the salami slices until browned, then set aside. Add the remaining frying oil and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the mangú with the fried cheese, salami, eggs, and cooked onions.

title: Sancocho de Siete Carnes
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into chunks
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 pound smoked pork ribs, cut into pieces
1 pound beef short ribs, cut into pieces
1 pound pork sausage, cut into chunks
1 pound goat meat, cut into chunks
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound yautía, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound auyama (calabaza), peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Rinse the meats with lime juice. Season with salt, oregano, half the onion, half the pepper, and half the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Brown the beef, pork, ribs, goat, and sausage in batches; add the chicken and cook briefly.
Add the remaining onion, pepper, and garlic. Pour in the water, add the cilantro, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until the meats are nearly tender, about 1 hour, skimming the surface as needed.
Add the plantain, yuca, yautía, corn, and vinegar. Simmer until the root vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add the auyama and simmer until soft, about 15 minutes. Remove the cilantro bundle and adjust the salt.
Serve hot, with rice and lime wedges if desired.

title: Pastelón de Plátano Maduro
ingredients: 6 ripe plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the plantains in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash with the butter.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, then add the garlic and oregano.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread half the mashed plantains in a greased baking dish.
Layer the beef over the plantains, sprinkle with half the cheese, and cover with the remaining plantains.
Pour the beaten eggs over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake until set and golden, about 25 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Habichuelas con Dulce
ingredients: 1 pound dried red kidney beans, picked over
1 pound sweet potato, peeled and cut into small cubes
instructions: Rinse the beans and soak them in water overnight. Drain and place them in a pot with 8 cups fresh water.
Add the cinnamon stick and cloves. Simmer until the beans are very soft, about 1 hour.
Remove the cinnamon and cloves. Blend the beans with their cooking liquid until smooth, then strain into a large pot.
Stir in the evaporated milk, coconut milk, sugar, salt, and nutmeg. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the sweet potato and raisins. Cook gently until the potato is tender and the mixture is creamy, about 25 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the vanilla. Serve warm or chilled with milk cookies on top.

title: Cou-cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Rub the flying fish with lime juice, rinse, and pat dry.
Season the fish with green seasoning and black pepper; set aside for 20 minutes.
Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 3 cups water and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal mixture; cook over low heat, stirring often, until thick and smooth, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the butter and keep the cou-cou warm.
Heat the oil in a skillet; cook the onion, garlic, thyme, tomato, and Scotch bonnet until softened.
Add the fish and 1/2 cup water; cover and simmer gently until the fish flakes, about 10 minutes.
Serve the flying fish and sauce with the cou-cou.

title: Bajan Macaroni Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated cheddar cheese, for topping
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender; drain well.
Stir the butter into the hot macaroni until melted.
Mix in the cheddar, evaporated milk, ketchup, mustard, hot pepper sauce, black pepper, paprika, and beaten egg.
Spoon the mixture into a greased baking dish and scatter the topping cheese over it.
Bake until set and golden on top, about 35 minutes; rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bajan Pepperpot
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Season the beef and pork with green seasoning, salt, and black pepper; refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the meat in batches; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic in the pot until softened.
Return the meat to the pot; add cloves, cinnamon, Scotch bonnet, stock, and brown sugar.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently until the meat is very tender, about 2 hours.
Stir in the lime juice, remove the whole pepper, and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Bajan Fish Cakes
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 8 hours or overnight, changing the water once.
Drain the cod, place it in a saucepan with fresh water, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain and flake, removing skin and bones.
Whisk the flour and baking powder in a bowl; gradually whisk in 1/2 cup water to make a thick batter.
Fold in the flaked cod, scallions, parsley, hot pepper sauce, and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop tablespoonfuls of batter into the oil and fry in batches until golden, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Bajan Stew Chicken
instructions: Rub the chicken with lime juice, rinse, and pat dry.
Season the chicken with green seasoning, salt, and black pepper; marinate for at least 1 hour.
Sprinkle the brown sugar into a heavy pot over medium heat and cook until it melts and turns dark amber.
Carefully stir in the oil, then add the chicken and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Add the onion and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, stock, thyme, bay leaf, and carrot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 40 minutes.
Taste the gravy and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Bahamian Peas and Rice
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, cooked and drained
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot until crisp; leave about 1 tablespoon of fat in the pot.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Add the pigeon peas, rice, and water; stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

title: Bahamian Boiled Fish
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish steaks, such as grouper
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the fish with salt, black pepper, and lime juice; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the potatoes, whole hot pepper, and water; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Gently add the fish and simmer until it flakes easily, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot with the broth.

title: Bahamian Chicken Souse
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken wings, split at the joints
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, black pepper, and 2 tablespoons lime juice; let it stand for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the chicken lightly on all sides.
Add the onion, potatoes, carrot, whole hot pepper, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the chicken and vegetables are tender, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the remaining lime juice and taste for seasoning.
Serve hot with Johnny cake or toasted bread.

title: Bahamian Cracked Conch
ingredients: 1 pound conch meat, cleaned and tenderized
instructions: Cut the tenderized conch into bite-size pieces and season with salt, black pepper, and paprika.
Set the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow bowls.
Dredge each piece in flour, dip it in egg, then coat it with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Fry the conch in batches until golden, about 2 minutes per batch; drain on a rack or paper towels.
Serve with lime juice.

title: Bahamian Johnny Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8-inch round cake pan.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the milk and stir just until a soft dough forms.
Press the dough evenly into the prepared pan and prick the top lightly with a fork.
Bake until golden and cooked through, about 35 minutes; cool slightly before slicing.

title: Jamaican Brown Stew Chicken
ingredients: 2 lb chicken pieces, skin on or off
instructions: Season the chicken with browning sauce, salt, pepper, thyme, scallions, onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Lift the chicken from the marinade and reserve the vegetables.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the tomato and whole Scotch bonnet.
Cover and simmer for 35–45 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Remove the Scotch bonnet before serving, if desired.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, rinsed
instructions: Put the beans and water in a pot and simmer until the beans are tender, about 1–1 1/2 hours; add water if needed.
Add the coconut milk, scallions, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the rice and bring the pot to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20–25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the scallions and Scotch bonnet, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Jamaican Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced (optional)
instructions: Soak the saltfish in cold water for several hours or overnight, changing the water once or twice.
Drain the fish, cover it with fresh water, and simmer for 10 minutes. Drain, remove any bones, and flake the fish.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, scallions, tomato, thyme, black pepper, and Scotch bonnet, if using.
Cook for 4–5 minutes, until the vegetables soften.
Stir in the flaked saltfish and cook for 2 minutes.
Fold in the ackee gently and warm through for 3–4 minutes without mashing it.

title: Jamaican Steamed Cabbage
ingredients: 1 medium green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, scallions, and garlic; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage, carrot, water, salt, pepper, thyme, and whole Scotch bonnet, if using.
Cover and steam for 8–12 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender but not mushy.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and serve.

title: Jamaican Festival Dumplings
instructions: Whisk together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Pour in the milk and mix until a soft dough forms, adding water a little at a time if needed.
Knead briefly until smooth, then divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a short oval.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the dumplings in batches, turning often, for 5–7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Trinidad Pelau
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
1 cup pigeon peas, cooked or canned and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning and salt; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Add the sugar and let it caramelize until deep amber.
Add the chicken carefully and stir to coat. Brown for 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, carrot, and ketchup.
Add the coconut milk and stock. Stir in the chadon beni and scallions, then place the whole pepper on top.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pepper, fluff the pelau, and serve.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 pound dasheen leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Put the dasheen leaves, pumpkin, okra, onion, scallions, chadon beni, garlic, coconut milk, water, and salt in a large pot.
Add the whole Scotch bonnet pepper without breaking it.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the vegetables and leaves are very soft, about 45 minutes.
Remove the pepper. Blend or whisk the mixture until smooth, taking care with the hot liquid.
Stir in the butter and simmer for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Doubles
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
1 cup dried split chickpeas, soaked overnight
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Add the warm water and oil, then knead until soft.
Cover the dough and let it rise for 1 hour.
Drain the soaked chickpeas. Simmer them with the onion, garlic, curry powder, cumin, salt, and water until tender, about 1 hour; mash lightly.
Divide the dough into small balls, cover, and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet. Stretch each ball into a thin round and fry briefly on both sides until cooked but still soft.
Sandwich a spoonful of chickpeas between two fried bara. Serve with tamarind sauce and cucumber chutney.

title: Trinidad Curry Chicken
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 medium potato, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning and salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the curry powder and cumin with 2 tablespoons of water. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to make a paste.
Add the garlic and chicken. Stir well and cook until the chicken is coated and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the water and potato. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the potato is tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir in the chadon beni and simmer uncovered until the gravy reaches your preferred consistency.

title: Trinidad Macaroni Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a baking dish.
Boil the macaroni in salted water until just tender. Drain well.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the onion over medium heat.
Mix the macaroni with the onion, cheddar, evaporated milk, eggs, mustard, black pepper, and salt.
Spoon the mixture into the baking dish and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until set and golden on top. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the steak with salt and pepper.
Simmer the steak in water until tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours; reserve 1/2 cup cooking liquid.
Let the steak cool slightly, then shred it into strips.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce, broth, reserved cooking liquid, and bay leaf.
Add the shredded beef and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Stir in the olives and serve.

title: Moros y Cristianos
instructions: Put the beans, water, and bay leaf in a pot and simmer until tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours; reserve 2 cups of bean liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion and bell pepper until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, and tomato paste; stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, cooked beans, salt, and 2 cups reserved bean liquid.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the pot rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice and stir in the vinegar before serving.

title: Picadillo a la Habanera
ingredients: 1 large russet potato, peeled and diced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, then stir in the garlic.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Add the wine and simmer until reduced by about half.
Stir in the tomato sauce, olives, capers, raisins, and potato.
Cover and simmer gently until the potato is tender and the sauce thickens, about 25 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Picadillo-Stuffed Tostones
instructions: Peel the plantains and cut them into 1-inch pieces.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the plantain pieces for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly golden; drain them.
Flatten each piece to about 1/2 inch thick with a tostonera or the bottom of a cup.
Fry the flattened plantains again until crisp and golden; drain and sprinkle with salt.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and ground beef; cook until the beef is browned.
Stir in the cumin, tomato sauce, and olives; simmer for 8 minutes.
Spoon the picadillo over the tostones and serve hot.

title: Yuca con Mojo
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh or frozen yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the yuca in a pot and cover with cold water; add the salt.
Bring to a boil and cook until the yuca is tender and begins to split, about 25 to 35 minutes.
Drain the yuca and remove any tough central fibers.
Warm the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat.
Add the garlic and cook gently for 1 minute without browning it.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the sour orange juice, lime juice, and onion.
Pour the mojo over the hot yuca and let it stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Arroz con Gandules
ingredients: 2 cups medium-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the achiote oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sofrito and ham; cook for 4 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the tomato sauce, gandules, adobo, oregano, and olives.
Add the rice and water; stir once and bring to a boil.
Boil uncovered until most of the water has evaporated and small steam holes appear.
Cover, lower the heat, and cook for 20 minutes. Fluff before serving.

title: Mofongo
ingredients: 3 green plantains, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the plantain pieces in batches for 5 to 7 minutes, until tender but not browned; drain well.
Mash the garlic and salt in a mortar.
Add the fried plantains a few pieces at a time and mash until chunky.
Mix in the pork cracklings and enough warm broth to hold the mixture together.
Shape into balls or mound in a bowl, and serve warm.

title: Pollo Guisado
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken with adobo.
Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in batches; set aside.
Add the sofrito, onion, and bell pepper; cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce and oregano, then return the chicken to the pot.
Add the potatoes, olives, and chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken and potatoes are tender.

title: Pasteles de Masa
ingredients: 2 pounds green plantains, peeled and chopped
2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
10 banana leaves, cut into 10-inch squares and warmed
instructions: Blend the bananas, yautía, and plantains with the milk and achiote oil until smooth; set the masa aside.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and brown the pork.
Stir in the sofrito, tomato sauce, olives, and adobo; cook for 5 minutes, then cool the filling.
Brush a banana leaf square lightly with achiote oil.
Spread about 1/2 cup masa on the leaf and place a spoonful of pork filling in the center.
Fold the leaf into a secure packet and tie with kitchen twine; repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Boil the pasteles in salted water for 50 to 60 minutes, then drain and unwrap to serve.

title: Tembleque
instructions: Whisk 1 cup of the coconut milk with the cornstarch until smooth.
Pour the remaining coconut milk into a saucepan and whisk in the sugar and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk in the cornstarch mixture and cook, stirring constantly, until thick and glossy, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour into a lightly rinsed mold or serving cups, cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Sprinkle with cinnamon before serving.

title: Griot (Haitian Fried Pork)
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the pork, sour orange juice, onion, garlic, scallions, Scotch bonnet, thyme, salt, and pepper in a pot.
Add the water, cover, and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Remove the pork and reserve the cooking liquid; discard the Scotch bonnet.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pork in batches until deeply golden and crisp, about 5 minutes per batch.
Serve hot with pikliz and rice or fried plantains.

title: Diri ak Pwa (Rice and Beans)
ingredients: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, rinsed
instructions: Simmer the beans in the water until tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours; reserve 3 cups of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the scallions and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans, reserved cooking liquid, thyme, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice and coconut milk, then place the whole Scotch bonnet on top.
Cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Remove the Scotch bonnet, fluff the rice, and serve.

title: Soup Joumou (Haitian Pumpkin Soup)
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 lb calabaza squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Toss the beef with sour orange juice, salt, and pepper; let it stand for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the squash and broth; simmer until the squash is very soft, about 30 minutes.
Mash the squash into the broth, then add the carrots, potatoes, cabbage, celery, and thyme.
Simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, following the package time.
Stir in the lime juice and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Pikliz (Haitian Spicy Pickled Vegetables)
instructions: Combine the cabbage, carrot, onion, Scotch bonnet, salt, and peppercorns in a clean jar.
Pour in the vinegar and water until the vegetables are covered.
Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving.
Keep refrigerated and use a clean fork to serve.

title: Haitian Legim (Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Steam the eggplant, chayote, and cabbage until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the steamed vegetables, spinach, thyme, salt, pepper, and water.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mash the vegetables roughly with a spoon and cook uncovered until thick, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice and serve with rice.

title: La Bandera Dominicana
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for the rice
1 can (15 ounces) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1/2 cup vegetable oil, for frying the plantains
instructions: Season the chicken with lime juice and adobo; let it rest for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken on all sides, then set it aside.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic to the pot; cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce and cilantro, return the chicken, cover, and simmer until cooked through, about 25 minutes.
For the rice, heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot. Add the rinsed rice, salt, and water; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Simmer the beans with chicken broth and oregano until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Heat the frying oil in a skillet and fry the plantain slices until golden on both sides. Serve with the chicken, rice, and beans.

title: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for frying the salami
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for frying the cheese
8 ounces frying cheese, cut into 1/2-inch slices
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for frying the eggs
instructions: Put the plantains in a pot, cover with water, add the salt, and boil until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain the plantains, reserving 1/2 cup cooking water. Mash with the butter and warm water until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet. Cook the onion with the vinegar until soft and lightly browned; set aside.
In the same skillet, fry the salami slices until browned on both sides.
Fry the cheese slices until golden on both sides, adding the tablespoon of oil if needed.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil to your preferred doneness.
Serve the mashed plantains topped with the onions, alongside the salami, cheese, and eggs.

title: Sancocho Dominicano
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into chunks
1 pound yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound yautía, peeled and cut into chunks
1 green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken and beef with lime juice, salt, and oregano.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Brown the beef, then add the chicken and brown lightly.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic; cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the meat begins to soften, about 45 minutes.
Add the corn, yuca, yautía, and plantain. Simmer until the root vegetables are nearly tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and cilantro; simmer until everything is tender and the broth has thickened, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the sour orange juice, taste for salt, and serve hot.

title: Habichuelas Guisadas
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper; cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and oregano; cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, chicken broth, and potato. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender and the broth is thick, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro, salt, and pepper. Serve with white rice.

title: Pastelón de Plátano Maduro
ingredients: 6 ripe plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil the plantains in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash with the butter.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, then add the garlic.
Add the ground beef, oregano, and black pepper; cook until browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce and water. Simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Spread half the mashed plantains in a greased baking dish. Add the beef filling and half the cheese.
Top with the remaining plantains, pour the beaten eggs over the top, and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake until set and golden, about 25 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Cou-cou and Flying Fish
instructions: Rinse the flying fish and rub with lime juice; rinse again and season with Bajan seasoning and black pepper.
Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 3 cups water and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Pour in the cornmeal mixture, stirring constantly; cook over low heat, stirring, until thick and smooth, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the butter and keep warm.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until softened.
Add the tomato, tomato paste, thyme, and 1 cup water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the seasoned fish and simmer gently until cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Serve the flying fish and sauce with the cou-cou.

title: Bajan Macaroni Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a baking dish.
Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender; drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the mustard, pepper sauce, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, nutmeg, and evaporated milk.
Remove from the heat and stir in 1 1/2 cups of the cheese.
Let the sauce cool slightly, then mix in the beaten eggs and cooked macaroni.
Spoon into the baking dish and top with the remaining cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake until golden and set, about 35 minutes; rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bajan Fish Cakes
ingredients: 1 pound salted cod, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the soaked cod in a saucepan, cover with fresh water, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain and flake, removing any bones.
Whisk the flour and baking powder in a bowl.
Stir in the onion, scallions, parsley, pepper sauce, black pepper, and flaked cod.
Add the water gradually to make a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and fry in batches until golden, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Bajan Pepperpot
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into chunks
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Season the beef and pork with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the meat in batches; set aside.
Cook the onion in the pot until softened, then add the garlic and brown sugar.
Stir in the tomato paste, cassareep, thyme, cinnamon, and cloves.
Return the meat to the pot and add the stock and whole Scotch bonnet.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently until the meat is very tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Remove the Scotch bonnet and skim excess fat before serving.

title: Bajan Pudding and Souse
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
1 banana leaf, softened over a flame
instructions: Put the pork shoulder and trotters in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until the meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours; drain and reserve the meat.
Mix the cucumber, onion, parsley, lime juice, water, and pepper sauce in a bowl.
Add the warm pork to the lime mixture and let it marinate while the pudding cooks.
Mix the sweet potato, white potato, grated onion, flour, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Spoon the pudding mixture onto the banana leaf, wrap securely, and tie with kitchen string.
Simmer the wrapped pudding in water with the cloves for about 1 hour, until firm.
Unwrap and slice the pudding, then serve with the pork souse and its cucumber-lime dressing.

title: Bahamian Peas and Rice
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, cooked and drained
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until browned.
Add the onion and bell pepper; cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, salt, black pepper, and crushed red pepper.
Add the pigeon peas, rice, and water; stir once and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

title: Bahamian Boiled Fish
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish steaks, such as grouper
instructions: Season the fish with salt, black pepper, and lime juice; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the potatoes, carrot, water, thyme, and whole Scotch bonnet; bring to a simmer.
Cook until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Gently add the fish and simmer until it flakes easily, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice and serve the broth with the fish and vegetables.

title: Bahamian Chicken Souse
ingredients: 2 pounds chicken wings or legs, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, black pepper, and lime juice; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken lightly on all sides.
Add the onion, bell pepper, potatoes, carrot, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the chicken and vegetables are tender, about 35 minutes.
Add the whole Scotch bonnet during the last 10 minutes of cooking; remove it before serving if desired.
Stir in the fresh lime juice and serve hot with the broth.

title: Bahamian Johnny Cake
ingredients: 1/4 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a baking pan with the oil.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Rub the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk until a soft dough forms.
Knead briefly on a floured surface, then press the dough into the prepared pan.
Bake until golden and cooked through, about 30 minutes; cool slightly before slicing.

title: Bahamian Guava Duff
ingredients: 3 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 tablespoon flour, for dusting the guava
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar together in a bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Toss the guava paste with the tablespoon of flour.
Roll the dough into a rectangle and scatter the guava paste over it.
Roll up the dough, pinch the seam closed, and wrap it securely in parchment and foil.
Place the wrapped roll in a large pot of gently simmering water and cook for 1 hour.
Unwrap carefully, slice, and serve warm.

title: Jamaican Brown Stew Chicken
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, browning sauce, soy sauce, onion, scallions, garlic, and half the Scotch bonnet; cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Lift the chicken from the seasoning and reserve the marinade.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the chicken on all sides.
Add the reserved seasoning and tomato; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, add the carrot and whole Scotch bonnet, then cover and simmer for 35–45 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning; remove the Scotch bonnet before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
instructions: Rinse the kidney beans, then soak them overnight and drain.
Put the beans and water in a pot; bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 1–1 1/2 hours.
Add the coconut milk, scallions, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the rinsed rice and bring the pot back to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20–25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and remove the Scotch bonnet.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Rinse the saltfish, then soak it in cold water for several hours or overnight, changing the water once or twice.
Drain the fish, cover it with fresh water, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain, remove any bones, and flake it.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook the onion, bell pepper, scallions, tomato, Scotch bonnet, thyme, and black pepper for 4–5 minutes.
Add the flaked saltfish and cook for 2 minutes.
Gently fold in the ackee and cook just until heated through, taking care not to mash it.

title: Jamaican Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lb goat meat, cut into pieces
instructions: Toss the goat with the curry powder, salt, pepper, onion, scallions, garlic, and ginger; cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the goat in batches.
Add the seasoning from the bowl and cook for 2 minutes, stirring often.
Add the water, thyme, and whole Scotch bonnet; cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the goat is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, until tender and the gravy thickens.
Taste and adjust the seasoning; remove the Scotch bonnet before serving.

title: Jamaican Festival
instructions: Whisk together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg, and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and mix to form a soft dough; add a little flour if it is sticky.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and roll each into a short tapered log.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the festivals in batches for 4–5 minutes, turning until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Pelau
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas, cooked or canned and drained
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, half the salt, and black pepper; let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and cook until it bubbles and turns deep amber.
Add the chicken carefully and turn to coat. Brown for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, carrot, coconut milk, stock, ketchup, scallions, and remaining salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 30 to 35 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.

title: Doubles
ingredients: 3/4 cup warm water, plus more as needed
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, cumin, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Add warm water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Work in 2 tablespoons oil, cover the dough, and let it rise for 1 hour.
For the channa, heat 1 tablespoon oil in a saucepan. Cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chickpeas, cumin, geera, salt, and water. Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the mixture.
Divide the dough into small balls and rest them, covered, for 15 minutes.
Heat a shallow layer of oil in a skillet. Stretch each ball into a thin round and fry briefly on both sides until cooked but still soft.
Sandwich a spoonful of channa between two bara. Serve with tamarind sauce and pepper sauce.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 pound dasheen leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Put the dasheen leaves, pumpkin, okra, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme, whole pepper, coconut milk, water, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 45 to 60 minutes, until the leaves and pumpkin are very soft.
Remove the thyme stems and whole pepper, taking care not to break the pepper if you want mild callaloo.
Blend with a stick blender, or mash thoroughly, until smooth and creamy.
Stir in the butter and adjust the salt. Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Curry Chicken
ingredients: 1 cup water, plus more as needed
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Season the chicken with green seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Mix the curry powder and cumin with 2 tablespoons water to make a paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the curry paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn to coat in the curry. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 cup water and the potatoes. Cover and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the potatoes are tender.
Uncover and simmer briefly to thicken the gravy, adding a little water if needed.

title: Bake and Shark
instructions: Season the shark with lime juice, salt, and black pepper; set aside for 15 minutes.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Gradually whisk in the water to make a smooth batter.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C). Dip each shark fillet in the batter and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and cooked through.
Drain the fish on a paper towel-lined plate.
Split each bake and fill it with a shark fillet, cabbage, tomato, and cucumber.
Serve with tamarind sauce and pepper sauce.

title: Ropa Vieja
instructions: Season the flank steak with salt and pepper.
Place the steak in a pot, cover with water, and simmer until tender, about 1 1/2 hours. Reserve 1/2 cup cooking liquid.
Let the steak cool slightly, then shred it into long strands.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the wine, tomato sauce, broth, reserved cooking liquid, and bay leaf.
Add the shredded beef and simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the olives and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Arroz con Pollo
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on both sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine and tomato sauce; simmer for 2 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in the rice, broth, and saffron. Nestle the chicken into the rice mixture and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Scatter the peas and olives over the rice, cover, and cook for 5 more minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Moros y Cristianos
ingredients: 1 cup dried black beans, rinsed and picked over
2 cups reserved black bean cooking liquid
instructions: Put the black beans, water, and bay leaf in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until tender, 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the salt and set aside 2 cups of the bean cooking liquid. Drain the beans, reserving them.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft, about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, and oregano; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the vinegar, rinsed rice, reserved beans, bean liquid, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce the heat to low. Cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the pot stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff gently before serving.

title: Picadillo a la Habanera
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, olives, raisins, and capers.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered until thick and fragrant, about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

title: Yuca con Mojo
ingredients: 2 pounds yuca, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces
instructions: Place the yuca in a pot and cover with water. Add the salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the yuca is tender and begins to split, about 25 minutes. Drain and discard any tough fibers from the centers.
Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat.
Add the garlic and cook gently until fragrant, about 2 minutes; do not let it brown.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the sour orange juice, lime juice, oregano, and pepper.
Arrange the yuca on a serving plate and spoon the warm mojo over it.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the pork.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock and add the soy sauce and sugar; bring to a simmer.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cold cooked rice, clumps broken up
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the eggs and scramble until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the ham and shrimp for 1 minute.
Add the peas and rice; stir-fry until the rice is hot and separated.
Return the eggs to the wok and add the soy sauce and salt.
Toss in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil; simmer for 3 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the sugar until amber.
Add the pork and stir to coat.
Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced, about 15 minutes.

title: Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing)
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl; stir in the boiling water and cold water until a rough dough forms.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a thin rectangle.
Brush each rectangle with sesame oil and scatter scallions over it.
Roll each rectangle into a rope, coil it into a spiral, then flatten into a round pancake.
Heat a little neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Pan-fry each pancake for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or tilapia, about 1 1/2 lb (680 g), cleaned
2-inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Pat the fish dry and make 2 diagonal slashes on each side.
Rub the fish with salt and Shaoxing wine; place half the ginger and scallions in its cavity.
Set the fish on a heatproof plate and scatter the remaining ginger over it.
Place the plate in a steamer over boiling water, cover, and steam for 8 to 12 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily.
Carefully pour off the liquid on the plate and drizzle the soy sauce over the fish.
Scatter the scallions on top and heat the neutral oil until shimmering.
Pour the hot oil over the scallions and serve immediately.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tablespoons doubanjiang (fermented broad bean chili paste)
1 tablespoon fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) boneless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch cubes
2 tablespoons light soy sauce, for the sauce
1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, for the sauce
2 teaspoons cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
8 dried red chilies, cut in half and seeded
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir together the remaining soy sauce, black vinegar, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and cornstarch mixture.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until thickened, then stir in the peanuts and serve.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs; transfer to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and cooked through; transfer to the plate.
Heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the ham and peas for 1 minute.
Add the rice and break up any clumps; stir-fry until hot.
Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok, then add the soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Stir in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
2 tablespoons rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the sugar until lightly caramelized.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Add the ginger, scallions, and star anise; stir briefly, then pour in the Shaoxing wine, soy sauces, and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve hot.

title: Scallion Pancakes
ingredients: ¼ cup all-purpose flour, for the filling
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, then stir in the boiling water and cold water until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the sesame oil with the ¼ cup flour to make a paste.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a thin rectangle.
Spread each rectangle with the paste and sprinkle with scallions.
Roll each rectangle into a tight log, coil it into a spiral, and roll the spiral into a 7-inch round.
Heat a little neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook each pancake for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a simmer, add the tofu, and simmer for 2 minutes; drain gently.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then bring to a simmer.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions before serving.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch pieces
2 tbsp light soy sauce, for the sauce
8 dried red chilies, cut in half and seeded
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir together the remaining soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, chicken stock, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peanuts and scallions, then serve.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 3 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the sugar until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Add the ginger, scallions, and star anise; stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; remove the star anise and serve.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or branzino, about 1½ lb, cleaned and scaled
2-inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Pat the fish dry and rub it inside and out with the salt and Shaoxing wine.
Place half the ginger on a heatproof plate and set the fish on top; scatter the remaining ginger over the fish.
Set the plate in a steamer over boiling water, cover, and steam for 8 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Carefully pour off the liquid that has collected on the plate and scatter the scallions over the fish.
Heat the soy sauce, water, and sugar in a small saucepan until hot, then pour over the fish.
Heat the oil until shimmering and carefully drizzle it over the scallions and fish.
Serve immediately.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
ingredients: 1 tbsp Sichuan preserved mustard greens, finely chopped
1 tbsp chili oil, plus more to taste
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package directions; drain and divide among bowls.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned and crisp.
Add the ginger, garlic, and preserved mustard greens; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Whisk the sesame paste, soy sauce, black vinegar, chili oil, sugar, and chicken stock until smooth.
Pour the sauce into the wok and simmer for 1 minute.
Spoon the pork mixture and sauce over the noodles.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, toss, and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 14 ounces soft tofu, cut into ¾-inch cubes
1 tablespoon fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the pork.
Stir in the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
2 tablespoons rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 3 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the sugar until amber.
Add the pork and stir to coat.
Add the soy sauces, rice wine, water, ginger, scallions, star anise, and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve with rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch cubes
8 dried red chilies, cut in half and seeded
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the rice wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, stock, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peanuts and scallions, then serve hot.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a wok over high heat and scramble the eggs until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add 1 teaspoon oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and cooked through; transfer to the plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the barbecue pork and peas for 1 minute.
Add the chilled rice and break up any clumps; stir-fry until hot.
Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok, then add the soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Toss in the scallions and stir-fry briefly before serving.

title: Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Ban Mian)
instructions: Stir together the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling water according to package directions; drain.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the scallions and fry slowly, turning occasionally, until browned and crisp; remove the scallions.
Carefully stir the soy sauce mixture into the hot oil and simmer for 30 seconds.
Toss the noodles with the scallion oil sauce, top with the crisp scallions and sesame seeds, and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then bring to a simmer.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
8 dried red chilies, cut in half and seeded
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the vinegar, sugar, water, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch to make the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns; stir-fry briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peanuts and serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil for 3 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the sugar and cook until melted and amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Add the water, ginger, scallions, star anise, cinnamon, and salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally, until tender.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve hot.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or branzino, about 1 1/2 lb, cleaned and scaled
1 piece fresh ginger, about 2 inches, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Pat the fish dry and make 3 shallow diagonal cuts on each side.
Rub the fish inside and out with the salt and Shaoxing wine. Place half the ginger and scallions inside and the rest on top.
Set the fish on a heatproof plate in a steamer over boiling water.
Cover and steam for 8 to 12 minutes, depending on the fish’s thickness, until the flesh flakes easily.
Carefully pour off the liquid that collected on the plate and remove the cooked ginger and scallions.
Mix the soy sauce with the water and pour it over the fish; top with fresh ginger and scallions.
Heat the neutral oil and sesame oil until shimmering, then carefully drizzle over the fish and serve.

title: Hand-Pulled Noodles with Scallion Oil
instructions: Mix the flour, warm water, and salt until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces, roll each into a thick rope, coat with a little oil, cover, and rest for 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add the scallions and cook until deeply golden; remove the scallions.
Stir the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar into the scallion oil; keep warm.
Stretch each dough rope by pulling and gently bouncing it against the work surface until thin, then tear into long noodles.
Boil the noodles for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked; drain and toss with the scallion sauce and sesame oil.
Finish with sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and warm for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the stock and soy sauce, then gently stir in the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and scallions, then serve.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch cubes
8 dried red chilies, cut in half and seeded
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, stock, and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat; briefly fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and cook until glossy and thickened, then toss in the peanuts and serve.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and scramble the eggs until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink.
Add the char siu, peas, and carrots; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice and break up any clumps as you stir-fry until hot.
Return the eggs to the wok; add the soy sauce, salt, and scallions and toss well.
Serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the rock sugar until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Add the ginger, scallions, star anise, Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve hot.

title: Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Ban Mian)
