instructions: Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package directions; drain and reserve ½ cup cooking water.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the scallions and fry, turning occasionally, until deep golden and crisp; remove them with a slotted spoon.
Stir the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar into the hot oil until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, adding a little reserved cooking water if needed.
Top with the fried scallions and sesame seeds, then serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and warm for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the pork.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then gently stir in the tofu.
Simmer for 5 minutes, carefully turning the tofu once.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve hot.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and cooked through; transfer to the plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the ham and peas for 1 minute.
Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until hot.
Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok; add the soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Stir-fry until evenly combined, then fold in the scallions and serve.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Boil for 3 minutes, skim the surface, then drain and rinse the pork.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; add the sugar and stir until melted and amber.
Add the pork carefully and stir to coat.
Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, water, ginger, star anise, and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; remove the spices and serve.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or similar white fish, about 1 1/2 lb, cleaned and scaled
1 piece fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Pat the fish dry and make 2 shallow diagonal cuts on each side.
Rub the fish with salt and Shaoxing wine, then place half the ginger inside and on top.
Set the fish on a heatproof plate and steam over boiling water for 8–10 minutes, until just cooked.
Carefully pour the steaming liquid off the plate and discard the ginger.
Scatter the remaining ginger and scallions over the fish.
Heat the neutral oil until shimmering, then carefully pour it over the aromatics.
Warm the soy sauce with the water, pour it around the fish, and serve immediately.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
ingredients: 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Whisk the sesame paste, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and chicken stock in a bowl until smooth.
Cook the noodles according to the package directions; add the greens during the final minute, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the pork.
Add the doubanjiang, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Divide the sesame sauce among serving bowls and add the hot noodles.
Top with the pork, greens, scallions, and ground Sichuan peppercorns; toss before eating.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 14 oz (400 g) soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain gently.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.

Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, and serve with rice.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 oz (85 g) peeled shrimp, roughly chopped

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)

title: Peking-Style Roast Duck
ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 5 lb (2.3 kg), giblets removed

Set the duck on a rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered for at least 8 hours to dry the skin.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix the maltose, hot water, and vinegar; brush the mixture over the duck skin.
Roast the duck on the rack for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C) and roast for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until cooked through and crisp.
Rest the duck for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with pancakes, cucumber, scallions, and hoisin sauce.

title: Hot and Sour Soup

Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes without breaking the cubes.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and add it gradually; simmer until the sauce thickens.
Finish with the ground Sichuan peppercorns, scallions, and sesame oil.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Break up the chilled rice so no large clumps remain.

instructions: Toss the chicken with the light soy sauce, rice wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Mix the dark soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, water, and remaining 1 teaspoon cornstarch in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy and thickened. Stir in the peanuts and serve.

title: Peking-Style Roast Duck
ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 5 lb (2.3 kg), giblets removed
instructions: Pat the duck very dry, then rub the skin and cavity with the salt and five-spice powder.
Dissolve the maltose in the boiling water, stir in the vinegar, and brush the mixture over the duck skin.
Place the duck uncovered on a rack in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours to dry the skin.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Roast the duck on a rack for 20 minutes, breast side up.
Reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C) and roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest for 15 minutes.
Carve the duck and serve with pancakes, hoisin sauce, scallions, and cucumber.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) skin-on pork belly, cut into 1½-inch pieces
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse the pork.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the sugar and cook until melted and amber.
Add the pork and stir to coat. Add the ginger, scallions, star anise, and cinnamon.
Stir in the rice wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally, until tender.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced. Serve hot.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 4 oz (115 g) small shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Break up the chilled rice with your fingers to separate the grains.
Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the eggs and scramble until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and cooked through.
Add the ham and peas and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir-fry until hot and evenly separated.
Return the eggs to the wok. Add the soy sauce, salt, white pepper, and scallions; toss well and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 14 oz (400 g) soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 tsp chili oil, or to taste
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and simmer for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, then gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Top with Sichuan pepper, chili oil, and scallions; serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) boneless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch pieces
2 tbsp light soy sauce, for the sauce
8 dried red chilies, snipped and seeded
instructions: Mix the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch; marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir together the remaining soy sauce, dark soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and water.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat; add the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peanuts and serve hot.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) pork belly, cut into 1½-inch pieces
2 tbsp rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork belly in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 5 minutes; drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and melt the sugar until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Add the ginger, scallions, star anise, cinnamon, Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve hot.

title: Scallion Pancakes
ingredients: ¼ cup neutral cooking oil, for frying
instructions: Combine the flour and salt in a bowl; stir in the boiling water, then add the cold water and mix into a dough.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Brush each circle with sesame oil and sprinkle with scallions.
Roll each circle into a log, coil the log into a spiral, tuck the end underneath, and roll it into a 7-inch pancake.
Heat a little neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry each pancake for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
ingredients: 4 oz (115 g) firm tofu, cut into thin strips
4 oz (115 g) shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and sliced
1 tsp chili oil, or to taste
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
instructions: Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a pot.
Add the tofu, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, black vinegar, white pepper, and chili oil.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and pour it slowly into the soup, stirring until slightly thickened.
Drizzle in the eggs while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Turn off the heat and stir in the scallions and sesame oil; serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block (14 oz) soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tablespoon fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
2 teaspoons Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and cook for 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.
Add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, then gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Top with ground Sichuan peppercorns and scallions; serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into ¾-inch cubes
8 dried red chilies, halved and seeds removed
instructions: Toss the chicken with the light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch; set aside for 15 minutes.
Mix the dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, stock, and remaining cornstarch in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and cook until glossy and thickened; stir in the peanuts and serve.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
2 tablespoons rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Place the pork in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil; simmer for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; add the sugar and stir until melted and amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat in the caramel.
Add the ginger, scallions, star anise, Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, and water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; serve hot.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 oz peeled small shrimp, patted dry
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a wok over high heat; add the eggs and scramble until just set, then transfer to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and cooked through; transfer to the plate.
Heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the rice, breaking up clumps, for 3 minutes.
Add the roast pork and peas; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok; add the soy sauce and salt and toss well.
Stir in the scallions and serve immediately.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or branzino, about 1½ lb, cleaned and scaled
3-inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Pat the fish dry and make 2 shallow diagonal cuts on each side.
Rub the fish inside and out with the salt and Shaoxing wine; place half the ginger and scallions in the cavity.
Set the fish on a heatproof plate and scatter the remaining ginger over it.
Steam over vigorously boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily.
Carefully pour off the liquid on the plate and discard the ginger from the cavity.
Scatter the remaining scallions over the fish; heat the soy sauce and water until hot and pour over the fish.
Heat the oil until shimmering and carefully drizzle it over the fish; serve at once.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer and warm the tofu cubes for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the ground pork until browned.
Stir in the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic, and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Add the stock, soy sauce, and sugar, then bring to a simmer.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.
Top with Sichuan peppercorns and scallions, then serve hot.

title: Beijing Zhajiangmian
instructions: Stir the sweet bean sauce, soybean paste, water, and sugar together in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork until browned.
Add the sauce mixture and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Cook the noodles according to package directions, then drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls and spoon the pork sauce over them.
Top with cucumber, bean sprouts, and scallions; toss before eating.

title: Dongpo Pork
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the pork belly for 5 minutes; drain.
Tie each pork cube with kitchen twine, if desired, to help it hold its shape.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and arrange the ginger and scallions on the bottom.
Place the pork in the pot, skin-side down, and add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, sugar, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 2 hours, turning the pork once halfway through.
Transfer the pork to a serving dish and spoon the cooking liquid over it.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 3 cups cold cooked rice, preferably day-old
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add another teaspoon of oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink; transfer to the plate with the eggs.
Heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the ham and peas for 1 minute.
Add the rice and break up any clumps; stir-fry until heated through.
Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok, then add the soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Stir-fry for 1 minute, fold in the scallions, and serve.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
ingredients: 4 oz firm tofu, cut into thin strips
1/2 cup bamboo shoots, cut into thin strips
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and thinly sliced
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer in a pot.
Add the tofu, bamboo shoots, and shiitake mushrooms; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, black vinegar, and white pepper.
Stir the cornstarch slurry, then drizzle it into the soup while stirring; simmer until lightly thickened.
Slowly pour in the beaten egg while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil.
Garnish with scallions and serve hot.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs until just set; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the shrimp, ham, and carrots for 2 minutes.
Add the peas and rice; break up the rice and stir-fry until hot.
Return the eggs to the wok, add scallions, salt, and white pepper, and toss well before serving.

title: Lion’s Head Meatballs (Hong Shao Shizi Tou)
ingredients: 500 g ground pork, preferably with some fat
instructions: Mix the pork with egg, water, light soy sauce, ginger, scallions, cornstarch, salt, and white pepper until sticky.
Shape the mixture into 4 large meatballs.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet and brown the meatballs on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the stock, dark soy sauce, and rock sugar to the skillet, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Return the meatballs to the skillet, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Nestle the cabbage leaves around the meatballs and simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes, until tender.

title: Braised Gluten Puffs with Mushrooms (Sikao Youmianjin)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Soak the shiitake mushrooms in warm water until soft, then remove the stems and slice the caps.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, briefly blanch the gluten puffs, and drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the mushrooms for 1 minute.
Add the gluten puffs, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and water.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, turning the puffs once so they absorb the sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce lightly thickens; garnish with scallions.

title: Jinling Salted Duck
instructions: Toast the salt and Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan until fragrant, then cool and crush lightly.
Rub the duck all over, including the cavity, with the salt mixture; refrigerate for 12 hours.
Rinse the duck and drain well.
Bring the water, star anise, cassia, ginger, and scallions to a gentle simmer in a large pot.
Lower in the duck and simmer gently for 45–55 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Let the duck cool in the broth, then lift it out, chill, and chop into serving pieces.

title: Squirrel-Shaped Mandarin Fish (Songshu Guiyu)
ingredients: 1 whole mandarin fish, about 700 g, scaled and gutted
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Fillet the fish while keeping the head attached, then score the flesh in a crosshatch pattern without cutting through the skin.
Season the fish with salt and white pepper, dip it in beaten egg, and coat it thoroughly with cornstarch.
Heat the oil to 180°C (350°F); carefully fry the fish, curved flesh-side outward, until crisp and golden, then drain.
In a small saucepan, combine ketchup, sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and water; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy and thick.
Arrange the fish with its head at one end, pour the hot sauce over it, and scatter with pine nuts.

title: Dongpo Pork (东坡肉)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, skin on, cut into 2-inch cubes
1/3 cup rock sugar or granulated sugar
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and arrange the scallions and ginger on the bottom.
Set the pork on top, skin side down, and add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, sugar, and water.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 2 hours, turning the pork once.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and the pork is tender.

title: West Lake Vinegar Fish (西湖醋鱼)
ingredients: 1 whole freshwater carp, about 2 lb, cleaned and scaled
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer with the ginger and 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine.
Add the fish and poach gently until just cooked through, about 8 to 10 minutes, turning carefully once.
Transfer the fish to a serving platter.
In a small saucepan, combine the remaining Shaoxing wine, water, sugar, vinegar, and soy sauce; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until lightly thickened, then pour the sauce over the fish.

title: Longjing Shrimp (龙井虾仁)
ingredients: 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss the shrimp with the salt, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch; chill for 15 minutes.
Steep the tea leaves in the hot water for 2 minutes, then strain and reserve the tea and leaves separately.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the shrimp until pink and nearly cooked.
Add 3 tablespoons of the brewed tea and the sugar; toss until the shrimp are just cooked.
Stir in the reserved tea leaves and serve immediately.

title: Ningbo Tangyuan (宁波汤圆)
ingredients: 3/4 cup warm water, plus 1 to 2 tablespoons as needed
3 tbsp lard or unsalted butter, softened
instructions: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over low heat until fragrant, then cool and grind finely.
Mix the ground sesame with the sugar and lard until it forms a thick filling; chill for 20 minutes.
Gradually mix the warm water into the rice flour until a soft, smooth dough forms.
Divide the dough into 16 portions, flatten each, add a little filling, and seal into balls.
Bring the water to a boil, add the tangyuan, and simmer gently until they float; cook for 1 more minute and serve with some cooking water.

title: Zhejiang Braised Bamboo Shoots (油焖笋)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh bamboo shoots, peeled and sliced
instructions: If using fresh bamboo shoots, boil the slices for 10 minutes, then drain.
Heat the neutral oil in a wok and stir-fry the bamboo shoots for 3 minutes.
Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and cook until the liquid is nearly gone; finish with sesame oil.

title: Fujian Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Zao Rou)
ingredients: 1½ lb pork belly, cut into 1½-inch pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and melt the rock sugar over low heat until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat; stir in the ginger and scallions.
Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, water, and star anise.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 75–90 minutes, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and the pork is tender.

title: Fujian Oyster Omelet (Hai Li Jian)
instructions: Whisk the sweet potato starch with the water until smooth.
Beat the eggs with the scallions, white pepper, and salt.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oysters and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the starch mixture and cook until it begins to set, then pour the eggs over it.
Cook until the bottom is golden; flip in sections and cook until the eggs are set.
Serve hot with sweet chili sauce.

title: Fujian Fish Ball Soup (Yu Wan Tang)
ingredients: 12 oz firm white fish fillet, skinless and cut into chunks
4 napa cabbage leaves, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Chill the fish chunks for 15 minutes, then pulse in a food processor until finely ground.
Add the egg white, potato starch, and salt; process until the mixture is smooth and springy.
Bring the chicken stock and ginger to a gentle simmer.
With wet hands, shape the fish mixture into small balls and drop them into the simmering stock.
Cook for 5–7 minutes, until the fish balls float and are cooked through.
Add the napa cabbage and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the scallions, white pepper, and sesame oil; serve hot.

title: Fujian Peanut Noodles (Ban Mian)
ingredients: ½ cup hot noodle cooking water
instructions: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Cook the noodles according to the package directions; reserve ½ cup cooking water before draining.
Whisk the hot cooking water into the peanut sauce until smooth and pourable.
Toss the hot noodles with the sauce until evenly coated.
Top with scallions and sesame seeds, and serve immediately.

title: Fujian Oyster and Seaweed Soup (Hai Li Zi Cai Tang)
instructions: Rinse the dried laver briefly and drain it well.
Bring the chicken stock and ginger to a simmer in a saucepan.
Add the Shaoxing wine and oysters; simmer gently for 2–3 minutes, until the oysters are just cooked.
Stir in the laver, salt, and white pepper; simmer for 30 seconds.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and scallions.
Serve hot.

title: Hunan-Style Stir-Fried Pork with Chili (Xiao Chao Rou)
instructions: Mix the pork with the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine; let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat a wok over high heat and add 1 tablespoon oil. Stir-fry the pork until just cooked, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, black beans, bell pepper, and chilies. Stir-fry until fragrant and crisp-tender.
Return the pork to the wok and toss everything together for 1 minute.

title: Steamed Pork with Preserved Mustard Greens (Mei Cai Kou Rou)
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, cut into thick slices
1 cup preserved mustard greens, soaked and chopped
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Mix the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar. Coat the pork with the mixture.
Heat the oil and briefly stir-fry the mustard greens with the ginger.
Arrange the pork in a heatproof bowl and cover it with the mustard greens and scallions.
Steam over medium heat for 90 minutes, until the pork is very tender.

title: Hunan Steamed Fish Head with Chopped Chilies (Duo Jiao Yu Tou)
ingredients: 1 large fish head, about 2 lb, split and cleaned
instructions: Place the fish head on a heatproof plate and rub it with the Shaoxing wine.
Scatter the ginger and garlic over the fish, then spread the chopped chilies on top.
Steam over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Heat the oil until shimmering and pour it over the fish. Drizzle with soy sauce and finish with scallions.

title: Hunan Cured Pork with Smoked Tofu and Garlic Scapes
ingredients: 8 oz Hunan-style cured pork, thinly sliced
6 oz garlic scapes, cut into 2-inch lengths
instructions: Simmer the cured pork in water for 10 minutes to soften and reduce its saltiness; drain.
Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the pork until its edges begin to render.
Add the garlic, chilies, smoked tofu, and garlic scapes. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and water, then stir-fry until the scapes are crisp-tender and the liquid has mostly evaporated.

title: Hunan Sour-Spicy Potato Slivers
ingredients: 2 dried red chilies, broken in half
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thin slivers and rinse them in cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the dried chilies and garlic and stir briefly until fragrant.
Add the potatoes and salt. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, keeping the potatoes moving.
Add the vinegar and soy sauce and toss until the potatoes are just tender but still crisp. Garnish with scallions.

title: Huangshan Stinky Mandarin Fish (Chou Guiyu)
ingredients: 1 whole mandarin fish, about 1½ pounds, cleaned and patted dry
1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
instructions: Rub the fish inside and out with salt and leave it in a cool place for 1–2 days, until it develops the characteristic pungent aroma; rinse and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wok and brown the fish on both sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Fry the ginger, garlic, scallions, and chili briefly in the wok.
Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, water, and sugar; bring to a simmer.
Return the fish to the wok, cover, and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Uncover and spoon the sauce over the fish before serving.

title: Hui-Style Braised Pork Belly
ingredients: 1½ pounds pork belly, cut into 1½-inch cubes
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and melt the rock sugar over low heat until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat it in the caramel.
Stir in the ginger, scallions, Shaoxing wine, soy sauces, star anise, and cinnamon.
Add the water and bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 1½ hours, turning the pork occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced; remove the spices before serving.

title: Huangshan Bamboo Shoots with Cured Pork
ingredients: 8 ounces cured pork belly, thinly sliced
instructions: Soak the dried bamboo shoots overnight, changing the water once, then rinse and cut into bite-size pieces.
Blanch the bamboo shoots in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the cured pork and cook until its fat begins to render.
Stir in the bamboo shoots and Shaoxing wine, then add the stock, water, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes, until the shoots are tender.
Scatter the scallions over the top and serve hot.

title: Luzhou Roast Duck
ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 4 pounds, patted dry
instructions: Rub the duck inside and out with salt, white pepper, Shaoxing wine, and soy sauce.
Refrigerate uncovered overnight to dry the skin.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Stir the honey, rice vinegar, and five-spice powder together, then brush the mixture over the duck.
Place the duck on a rack over a roasting pan and pour the water into the pan.
Roast for 20 minutes, lower the oven to 350°F (175°C), and roast for about 1 hour more, until the skin is crisp and the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Anhui Steamed Tofu with Dried Shrimp
ingredients: 14 ounces firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the dried shrimp in the warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and reserve the soaking water.
Arrange the tofu in a heatproof dish.
Mix the shrimp, reserved soaking water, soy sauce, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, and ginger; spoon the mixture over the tofu.
Set the dish in a steamer over boiling water, cover, and steam for 10 minutes.
Scatter the scallion and chili over the tofu and serve warm.

title: Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐)
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into ¾-inch cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper, plus more to taste
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and simmer for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the pork and stir-fry until browned.
Stir in the doubanjiang and black beans; fry until the oil turns red, about 1 minute.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir-fry briefly. Pour in the stock, then add the soy sauce and sugar.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 4–5 minutes, turning the pieces carefully.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and drizzle it into the wok; simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and scallions, then serve with rice.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork (回锅肉)
instructions: Place the pork belly in a saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 25–30 minutes, until just cooked through.
Cool the pork until easy to handle, then slice it thinly.
Heat a wok over medium heat. Add the pork and stir-fry until the edges curl and some fat renders; remove excess fat if needed.
Add the doubanjiang and sweet bean paste and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the leek and bell pepper; stir-fry until the vegetables are just tender.
Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar. Toss well and serve hot.

title: Sichuan Dry-Fried Green Beans (干煸四季豆)
ingredients: 1 lb green beans, trimmed and dried well
2 tbsp preserved mustard greens, rinsed and chopped
2 dried red chilies, broken in half
instructions: Heat a wok over medium-high heat and add the oil and green beans.
Stir-fry for 8–10 minutes, turning often, until the beans are blistered and tender; transfer to a plate.
Add the pork to the wok and stir-fry until browned and crumbly.
Add the preserved mustard greens, garlic, ginger, and dried chilies; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return the beans to the wok. Add the soy sauce and sugar and toss until evenly coated.
Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and serve.

title: Sichuan Fish-Fragrant Eggplant (鱼香茄子)
ingredients: 1 lb Chinese eggplant, cut into 3-inch batons
2 scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
¾ cup water or unsalted stock
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender, adding the remaining oil as needed; set aside.
Add the doubanjiang to the wok and stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallion whites; stir-fry for about 30 seconds.
Pour in the water or stock, then add the soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar.
Return the eggplant to the wok and simmer for 3–4 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and add it to the sauce; cook until glossy and lightly thickened.
Scatter the scallion greens over the eggplant and serve with rice.

title: Sichuan Spicy Cold Noodles (凉面)
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package directions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with a little sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Blanch the mung bean sprouts in boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and cool.
In a bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, vinegar, chili oil, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, and warm water.
Divide the noodles and sprouts among bowls and pour the sauce over them.
Toss well, then finish with sesame seeds, scallions, and Sichuan pepper.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass, about 1½ pounds, cleaned and patted dry
3 scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, plus 1 scallion finely shredded
instructions: Score both sides of the fish and rub with the salt.
Place half the ginger and scallions on a heatproof plate; set the fish on top and scatter the remaining ginger and scallions over it.
Steam over vigorously boiling water for 8–10 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily.
Carefully pour off the liquid on the plate and discard the cooked scallions and ginger.
Drizzle the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine over the fish, then top with the shredded scallion.
Heat the oil until shimmering and carefully pour it over the scallion before serving.

title: Cantonese Clay Pot Rice with Chinese Sausage
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked, stems removed, and sliced
instructions: Combine the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Put the rice and water in a clay pot and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 8 minutes.
Arrange the sausage and mushrooms over the rice, cover, and cook for 12–15 minutes, until the rice is tender and a crisp layer forms at the bottom.
Turn off the heat and let the pot stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the rice, scatter with scallions, and gently mix before serving.

title: Char Siu (Cantonese Barbecue Pork)
ingredients: 1½ pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into long strips
½ teaspoon red food coloring, optional
instructions: Stir together the hoisin, honey, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, five-spice powder, and optional food coloring.
Coat the pork with the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a roasting pan with foil; set a rack over the pan.
Arrange the pork on the rack and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.
Brush with the remaining marinade and roast for another 10–15 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, then slice thinly.

title: Beef Chow Fun
ingredients: 12 ounces fresh wide rice noodles, separated
8 ounces flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, the cornstarch, and Shaoxing wine; marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir together the dark soy sauce and remaining 1 tablespoon light soy sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef until just browned; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce, and toss gently over high heat until the noodles are hot and lightly colored.
Return the beef to the wok; add the bean sprouts and scallions and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes, until the sprouts are just tender.

title: Winter Melon Soup with Dried Scallops
ingredients: 1½ pounds winter melon, peeled, seeded, and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Rinse the dried scallops and soak them in ½ cup warm water for 30 minutes; reserve the soaking liquid and shred the scallops.
Bring the chicken stock, reserved soaking liquid, ginger, and shredded scallops to a boil in a pot.
Add the winter melon and salt, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes, until the melon is translucent and tender.
Remove the ginger, scatter the scallions over the soup, and serve hot.

title: Shandong-Style Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
ingredients: 1 cup warm water, plus more as needed
2 tablespoons neutral oil, for boiling water
instructions: Mix the flour with warm water until a shaggy dough forms; knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle the cabbage with half the salt, let stand for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the pork, cabbage, scallions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, remaining salt, and white pepper.
Roll the dough into a rope and cut into 30 pieces; roll each piece into a thin round wrapper.
Put a spoonful of filling in each wrapper, fold, and pinch the edges closed.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the neutral oil; boil the dumplings in batches until they float and the wrappers look translucent, about 5 minutes.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Potatoes
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds pork belly, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 pound waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot; add the sugar and cook until it melts and turns amber.
Add the pork and toss to coat; stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Add the ginger, star anise, water, and scallions; bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered until tender and the sauce is glossy, about 20 minutes.

title: Shandong Sweet-and-Sour Carp
ingredients: 1 whole carp, about 2 pounds, cleaned and scaled
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Pat the carp dry and make diagonal cuts on both sides; rub with salt and dust with cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep skillet and fry the fish carefully until golden and crisp on both sides; transfer to a serving platter.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil; stir-fry the scallions, ginger, and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and water; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens, then pour it over the fish.

title: Shandong Braised Eggplant with Garlic
ingredients: 2 pounds Chinese eggplant, cut into 2-inch batons
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Toss the eggplant with salt and let stand for 15 minutes; pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet and cook the eggplant in batches until lightly browned and tender; set aside.
Add the garlic and ginger to the skillet and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water; return the eggplant and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the cornstarch slurry and stir until the sauce clings to the eggplant; finish with scallions.

title: Shandong-Style Scallion Pancakes
instructions: Mix the flour and salt; stir in the boiling water, then add the cold water and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces; roll each into a thin rectangle and brush with sesame oil.
Scatter scallions over each rectangle, roll it up from the long side, coil it into a spiral, and flatten gently into a pancake.
Heat a little neutral oil in a skillet and pan-fry each pancake over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice (扬州炒饭)
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and cook the shrimp until pink; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and scramble the eggs until just set.
Add the rice and stir-fry, breaking up clumps, until hot and separated.
Stir in the ham, peas, shrimp, salt, and white pepper; toss until heated through.
Add the scallions, toss briefly, and serve.

title: Lion’s Head Meatballs (狮子头)
ingredients: 500 g ground pork with about 30% fat
1 tablespoon light soy sauce, for braising
instructions: Mix the pork, water chestnuts, ginger, scallions, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, salt, egg, and cornstarch until sticky.
Divide into 4 portions and shape each into a large ball, tossing it gently between your hands to compact it.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and brown the meatballs on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Line a heavy pot with the cabbage leaves and set the meatballs on top.
Pour in the stock and braising soy sauce; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 2 hours, spooning broth over the meatballs occasionally.

title: Salted Duck (盐水鸭)
instructions: Toast the salt and Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan until fragrant; cool completely.
Rub the mixture all over the duck and inside its cavity, then refrigerate uncovered for 12 hours.
Rinse the duck and place it in a pot with the scallions, ginger, star anise, Shaoxing wine, and water.
Bring the liquid just to a simmer, skim it, and cook gently for 45 minutes, turning the duck once.
Turn off the heat, cover, and let the duck steep in the broth for 2 hours.
Cool, carve into pieces, and serve at room temperature.

title: Braised Gluten with Peanuts (四喜烤麸)
ingredients: 500 ml mushroom soaking liquid or water
instructions: Soak the wheat gluten, shiitake mushrooms, and wood ear mushrooms in warm water until soft; drain and reserve the mushroom soaking liquid.
Cut the gluten into bite-size pieces, squeeze out excess water, and pat dry.
Boil the peanuts for 10 minutes and drain; slice the shiitake mushrooms and tear the wood ear into pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the gluten until lightly golden on several sides.
Add the ginger, mushrooms, wood ear, and peanuts; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauces, sugar, Shaoxing wine, and soaking liquid; simmer uncovered until the sauce is nearly absorbed, stirring occasionally.

title: Squirrel-Shaped Mandarin Fish (松鼠鳜鱼)
ingredients: 1 whole mandarin fish, about 700 g, cleaned and filleted with the head reserved
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Cut a crosshatch pattern into the flesh side of each fish fillet without cutting through the skin; season with salt, Shaoxing wine, and white pepper.
Dip the fillets and fish head in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with cornstarch, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a wok or deep pot.
Hold each fillet skin-side down and carefully lower it into the oil, curling it into a flower shape; fry until crisp and golden. Fry the head until crisp as well, then drain.
For the sauce, simmer the sugar, vinegar, tomato paste, soy sauce, and 100 ml water in a saucepan.
Add the pineapple and peas, stir in the cornstarch mixture, and cook until glossy and thick.
Arrange the fried fish and head on a platter and pour the hot sauce over the fish just before serving.

title: Dongpo Pork (Dongpo Rou)
ingredients: 1½ lb pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the pork, and simmer for 5 minutes; drain and rinse.
Arrange the scallions and ginger in a heavy pot, then place the pork on top, skin side down.
Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, rock sugar, and water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 2 hours, turning the pork once.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and the pork is very tender.

title: West Lake Beef Soup (Xihu Niurou Geng)
ingredients: 4 oz soft tofu, cut into small cubes
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
instructions: Mix the beef with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch.
Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a saucepan, then add the tofu.
Stir in the beef and simmer for 3 minutes, breaking it up gently.
Stir the cornstarch slurry, then drizzle it into the soup while stirring until lightly thickened.
Slowly pour in the egg white while stirring gently.
Season with salt and white pepper, then stir in the cilantro and serve.

title: Zhejiang-Style Braised Bamboo Shoots (Youmen Chun Sun)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh spring bamboo shoots, peeled and sliced
instructions: If the bamboo shoots are fresh, boil them in water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and add the bamboo shoots.
Stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the rock sugar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and cook until the sauce is nearly reduced; finish with sesame oil.

title: Ningbo Rice Cakes with Shepherd’s Purse (Cai Zhi Nian Gao)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh Chinese rice cakes, sliced
6 oz shepherd’s purse, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the ground pork until no longer pink.
Add the Shaoxing wine and shepherd’s purse; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the rice cakes, light soy sauce, salt, and water.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring once to keep the cakes from sticking.
Uncover and stir-fry until the rice cakes are soft and the liquid has mostly been absorbed.

title: Hangzhou Pian Er Chuan Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 cup pickled mustard greens, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and stir-fry the pork until it changes color.
Add the Shaoxing wine, shiitake mushrooms, and pickled mustard greens; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring it to a boil; simmer for 8 minutes.
Season with the light soy sauce and salt.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle the hot soup and toppings over them, and garnish with scallions.

title: Fujian Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Zao Rou)
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tablespoons Fujian red rice wine lees
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the pork pieces on all sides.
Stir in the ginger, scallion, red rice wine lees, soy sauce, wine, and sugar.
Add the water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60 to 75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and glossy.

title: Fujian Fish Ball Soup
ingredients: 8 oz firm white fish fillet, skin removed
4 oz napa cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Chop the fish finely, then pound or process it into a sticky paste.
Mix in the tapioca starch, salt, and white pepper until smooth.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer and add the mushrooms and cabbage.
Shape small fish balls with two spoons and drop them into the simmering stock.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the fish balls float and are cooked through.
Finish with sesame oil and scallions.

title: Fuzhou Oyster Pancake
instructions: Whisk the sweet potato starch with the water until smooth.
Stir in the oysters, scallions, white pepper, and salt.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and pour in the oyster mixture.
Cook until the underside is crisp and the starch mixture is mostly set, about 4 minutes.
Pour the beaten eggs over the pancake and cook until set.
Flip carefully and cook until crisp and golden on the second side.

title: Fujian Red Wine Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 cup Fujian red rice wine lees
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown the pieces lightly on all sides.
Stir in the red rice wine lees, water, salt, and sugar.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Add the scallions and simmer uncovered for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Fuzhou Litchi Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Season the pork with salt and white pepper, then coat each piece in potato starch.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry the pork in batches until crisp and cooked through; drain.
Stir the vinegar, sugar, ketchup, soy sauce, and water together in a bowl.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil from the pan and stir-fry the bell pepper for 1 minute.
Add the pineapple and sauce mixture, then bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.
Toss in the fried pork just before serving.

title: Hunan-Style Stir-Fried Pork with Long Green Peppers (Xiangjiao Chao Rou)
ingredients: 8 oz long green peppers, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and lightly mashed
instructions: Toss the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and dark soy sauce; set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat a wok over high heat, add 1 tablespoon oil, and stir-fry the peppers with the salt until blistered and tender-crisp; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the pork until browned and just cooked through.
Add the garlic and black beans; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return the peppers to the wok and toss everything together for 1 minute before serving.

title: Hunan Steamed Pork with Preserved Mustard Greens (Mei Cai Kou Rou)
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 cup preserved mustard greens, rinsed, squeezed dry, and chopped
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and simmer the pork belly for 15 minutes; drain and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the pork until lightly browned on all sides.
Stir in the garlic, preserved mustard greens, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Transfer the mixture to a heatproof bowl and pour in the water.
Cover and steam over medium heat for 90 minutes, until the pork is tender.

title: Hunan Spicy Smoked Tofu with Celery
ingredients: 6 oz celery, thinly sliced on the diagonal
2 dried red chilies, cut in half
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the dried chilies, garlic, and black beans; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the smoked tofu and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the celery, soy sauce, and water; stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the celery is crisp-tender.

title: Hunan-Style Fish Head with Chopped Chilies (Duo Jiao Yu Tou)
ingredients: 1 large fish head, about 2 lb, split and cleaned
instructions: Pat the fish head dry and arrange it cut-side up on a heatproof plate.
Rub the fish with the Shaoxing wine and scatter the ginger and scallions over it.
Spread the chopped chilies evenly over the fish and drizzle with the soy sauce.
Steam over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Heat the oil until shimmering and carefully drizzle it over the fish before serving.

title: Hunan Sour-and-Spicy Potato Slivers (Suan La Tu Dou Si)
ingredients: 2 dried red chilies, cut into short pieces
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks and rinse them under cold water; drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the dried chilies and garlic for 20 seconds.
Add the potato matchsticks and salt; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water and black vinegar, then stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender but still crisp.
Toss in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Huangshan Stinky Mandarin Fish (Chou Guiyu)
ingredients: 1 whole mandarin fish, about 1½ pounds, cleaned
instructions: Rub the fish inside and out with salt and leave it for 30 minutes; rinse and pat dry. (Traditional fermentation takes longer, so this is a home-style version.)
Heat the oil in a wide pan and sear the fish on both sides until lightly golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, and chilies; stir briefly.
Pour in the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and water. Cover and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes, turning the fish once.
Scatter over the scallions and simmer uncovered for 1 minute; serve with the sauce.

title: Hui-Style Braised Pork with Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tablespoon rock sugar or brown sugar
8 ounces cooked bamboo shoots, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a pot; add the sugar and stir until melted and amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat. Stir in the ginger, both soy sauces, and Shaoxing wine.
Add the water, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the bamboo shoots and simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce is glossy.

title: Hefei Salted Duck
ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 4 pounds, thawed and patted dry
instructions: Toast the salt and peppercorns in a dry pan until fragrant, then crush the peppercorns lightly.
Rub the mixture all over the duck and inside the cavity. Refrigerate uncovered for at least 8 hours.
Rinse the duck briefly and place it in a pot with the ginger, scallions, and water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skim the surface, and cook partially covered for about 1 hour, until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F.
Let the duck rest in the cooking liquid for 20 minutes, then drain and chop into serving pieces.

title: Stir-Fried Hairy Tofu with Chili
ingredients: 12 ounces fermented hairy tofu, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Pat the tofu dry carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok or skillet over medium heat. Add the tofu and pan-fry until golden on several sides.
Add the ginger, garlic, and chilies; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce and water, then gently turn the tofu to coat and heat through.
Top with scallions and serve hot with rice.

title: Wuhu Rice Noodles with Shrimp
instructions: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package directions; drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the ginger and garlic and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until just pink, about 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, bean sprouts, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and salt. Toss over high heat until hot and evenly seasoned.
Stir in the scallions and serve immediately.

title: Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐)
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu, cut into ¾-inch cubes
2 tbsp Sichuan doubanjiang (fermented broad-bean chili paste)
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu, and warm it for 2 minutes; drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the pork and stir-fry until browned.
Add the doubanjiang and black beans; stir-fry until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Stir in the garlic and ginger, then add the stock and soy sauce.
Gently add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes, turning it carefully in the sauce.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and drizzle it into the wok; simmer until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with the scallions and remaining Sichuan pepper and serve with rice.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork (回锅肉)
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot with the ginger and one scallion. Cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes.
Lift out the pork and let it cool until easy to handle; slice it thinly.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the pork and stir-fry until the edges curl and some fat renders.
Push the pork aside. Add the doubanjiang and sweet bean sauce to the rendered fat and stir until fragrant.
Add the bell pepper and leek; stir-fry until just tender.
Toss everything together with the soy sauce and remaining scallion, then serve hot.

title: Fish-Fragrant Eggplant (鱼香茄子)
ingredients: 1 lb Chinese eggplant, cut into 2-inch batons
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the eggplant in batches until tender and lightly browned; set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the doubanjiang, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Return the eggplant to the wok and pour in the sauce mixture. Toss to coat.
Stir the cornstarch mixture, add it to the wok, and cook until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the eggplant.
Scatter over the scallions and serve with rice.

title: Sichuan Dry-Fried Green Beans (干煸四季豆)
ingredients: 1 lb green beans, trimmed and patted dry
1 tbsp preserved mustard greens, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the green beans and stir-fry until blistered and tender, 7 to 9 minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the ground pork. Stir-fry until browned and crumbly.
Add the doubanjiang, preserved mustard greens, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry until fragrant.
Return the beans to the wok, add the soy sauce, and toss until everything is well combined and hot.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Sour and Spicy Shredded Potatoes (酸辣土豆丝)
ingredients: 2 dried red chilies, torn in half
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks and rinse them in cold water until the water runs mostly clear; drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir until fragrant.
Add the garlic and potatoes; stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, keeping the potatoes moving.
Add the vinegar and salt, then stir-fry until the potatoes are just tender but still crisp.
Toss in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Steamed Pork with Salted Fish
ingredients: 30 g Chinese salted fish, finely chopped
instructions: Combine the pork with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and oil.
Spread the pork in a shallow heatproof dish and scatter the salted fish and ginger over it.
Steam over boiling water for 12–15 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.
Scatter the scallion on top and serve with rice.

title: Cantonese Steamed Egg with Dried Scallops
ingredients: 2 dried scallops, soaked until soft and shredded
instructions: Beat the eggs gently with the salt and warm water, then strain into a shallow heatproof bowl.
Scatter the shredded scallops over the egg mixture and cover the bowl with foil.
Steam over low heat for 10–12 minutes, until just set.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil, then garnish with scallion.

title: Beef Chow Fun
ingredients: 200 g beef flank, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, cornstarch, and Shaoxing wine; let it stand for 10 minutes.
Separate the rice noodles gently. Mix the dark soy sauce with the remaining 1 tablespoon light soy sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the beef until nearly cooked; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and onion; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce, tossing gently until hot and evenly colored.
Return the beef to the wok and add the bean sprouts and scallions; toss for 1 minute and serve.

title: Cantonese White-Cut Chicken
instructions: Rub the chicken inside and out with salt and set it aside for 20 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the ginger and scallion lengths; lower in the chicken breast-side up.
Return the water to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 35 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74°C; transfer the chicken to cool before chopping.
Mix the minced ginger and sliced scallion in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil until shimmering, pour it over the ginger and scallion, and serve as a dipping sauce with the chicken.

title: Winter Melon Soup with Dried Shrimp
ingredients: 500 g winter melon, peeled, seeded, and cut into chunks
instructions: Bring the chicken stock, dried shrimp, and ginger to a boil in a pot.
Add the winter melon and return the soup to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the melon is tender and translucent.
Season with salt and white pepper, then garnish with scallion.

title: Shandong Scallion-Braised Sea Cucumber
ingredients: 4 dried sea cucumbers, rehydrated and cleaned
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Simmer the rehydrated sea cucumbers in fresh water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok and brown the scallions on all sides; set aside.
Add the sea cucumbers and Shaoxing wine, then stir in both soy sauces, sugar, and stock.
Return the scallions and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.

title: Jinan Sweet-and-Sour Yellow River Carp
ingredients: 1 whole carp, about 2 pounds, cleaned and scored
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 3 tablespoons water
instructions: Pat the carp dry and rub it with the salt.
Coat the fish lightly with cornstarch, including the scored cuts.
Heat the oil in a wok and carefully fry the fish until crisp and cooked through; drain.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon oil, then briefly fry the ginger and garlic.
Add the water, sugar, vinegar, and soy sauce; bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy, then pour the sauce over the fish.

title: Shandong Braised Pork with Potatoes
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and melt the sugar until amber.
Add the pork and turn to coat; stir in the soy sauces and Shaoxing wine.
Add the ginger, scallions, and water, then cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, until tender and the sauce is reduced.

title: Shandong Pork and Cabbage Dumplings
instructions: Mix the flour and warm water into a dough; knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Salt the cabbage, let it stand for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the pork with the scallions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, and cabbage.
Roll the dough into a rope and cut it into 24 pieces; roll each piece into a thin round wrapper.
Place filling in each wrapper, fold, and pinch the edges closed.
Boil the dumplings in batches until they float and the wrappers are tender, about 5 minutes.

title: Shandong Braised Eggplant with Garlic
ingredients: 2 medium Chinese eggplants, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the eggplant over medium-high heat until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water, then pour into the wok.
Cover and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once, until the eggplant is tender.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce lightly thickens.
Finish with the sliced scallions.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive container and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove beef from the marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved marinade, sugar, and beef stock; cover and simmer gently for about 3 hours, until tender.
Transfer the beef to a platter. Stir crushed gingersnaps into the cooking liquid and simmer until thickened; slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a clean kitchen towel.
Mix the potato and onion with eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in small portions of the mixture and flatten into pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels and serve with applesauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Place the veal cutlets between sheets of parchment and gently pound until about 1/4 inch thick.
Season the cutlets with salt.
Set flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing them in.
Heat clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the cutlets one at a time, gently shaking the pan, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk flour, milk, egg yolks, granulated sugar, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold them into the batter with the raisins.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the underside is golden and the top is nearly set, about 5 minutes.
Turn the pancake in large sections and cook the other side until golden.
Tear it into bite-size pieces with two forks and cook briefly until lightly browned.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum preserves.

title: Swiss Rösti
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 10 minutes; drain and cool completely, or refrigerate overnight.
Peel the potatoes and coarsely grate them into a bowl.
Season the grated potatoes with salt and pepper and toss gently.
Heat butter and oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and press them into an even, compact cake.
Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the underside is crisp and golden.
Invert the rösti onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side for 8 to 10 minutes.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, wine, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive container and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the beef daily.
Remove beef from the marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved marinade and vegetables. Cover and simmer gently for about 3 hours, turning the beef occasionally, until tender.
Transfer the beef to a plate. Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan and skim off excess fat.
Whisk flour with a little cold water, stir it into the liquid, and simmer until thickened. Add sugar and crushed gingersnaps; stir until smooth.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of parchment and gently pound to about 1/4 inch thick.
Season the cutlets with salt.
Set flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, then coat it lightly with breadcrumbs without pressing them on.
Heat clarified butter or oil in a large skillet to about 350°F.
Fry the cutlets one at a time, gently shaking the skillet, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain briefly on a wire rack and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into bite-size cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch in a bowl.
Pour wine and lemon juice into the pot and warm over medium-low heat until steaming.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring constantly until each addition melts before adding more.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; keep the fondue gently bubbling.
Serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes and onion into a clean kitchen towel.
Gather the towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer the potato mixture to a bowl and stir in eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon about 1/4 cup of mixture into the skillet for each pancake and flatten gently.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden; drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with applesauce.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Soak the raisins in rum or warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Whisk flour, milk, egg yolks, sugar, and salt until smooth; fold in the raisins.
In a clean bowl, beat egg whites to soft peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the bottom is set and golden, then bake at 375°F for about 8 minutes until puffed and cooked through.
Tear the pancake into bite-size pieces with two forks.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet and toss the pieces briefly until lightly caramelized.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with plum compote.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive bowl and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat daily.

Transfer beef to a plate. Stir flour and brown sugar into the cooking liquid, then add crushed gingersnaps and simmer until thickened.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel

Set flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn

ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch.
Pour wine and lemon juice into the pot and warm over medium-low heat until steaming.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring continuously until melted before adding more.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; keep warm over low heat without boiling.
Dip bread cubes into the fondue and serve.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion using the large holes of a box grater.
Wrap the grated mixture in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Stir the potato mixture with eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in 1/4-cup portions and flatten into pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding oil as needed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk egg yolks with flour, milk, granulated sugar, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold them into the batter.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Scatter raisins over the top and cook until the underside is golden and the top is nearly set, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to a 400°F (200°C) oven and bake until puffed and cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Tear the pancake into bite-size pieces with two forks and return the skillet to low heat for 1 minute.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum preserves.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine the vinegar, water, onion, carrot, peppercorns, bay leaves, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place the beef in a nonreactive dish and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning the beef daily.
Remove the beef and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add 2 cups of the reserved marinade and the beef broth. Cover and simmer gently for 2½ to 3 hours, turning occasionally, until tender.
Transfer the beef to a plate. Stir the brown sugar and crushed gingersnaps into the cooking liquid and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of plastic wrap and pound to about ⅛ inch thick.
Set the flour, beaten eggs mixed with milk, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.
Season the cutlets with salt and pepper, then coat each in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs without pressing the crumbs firmly.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet to about 350°F.
Fry the cutlets one at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, gently shaking the skillet, until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty bread, cut into cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch.
Heat the wine and lemon juice in the pot until steaming but not boiling.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring steadily until each addition melts before adding the next.
Stir in the kirsch and nutmeg; keep the fondue gently warm.
Dip the bread cubes into the fondue and serve.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion using the large holes of a box grater.
Wrap the grated mixture in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Stir the potatoes and onion together with the eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in ¼-cup portions of the mixture and flatten into pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding oil as needed.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with the flour, milk, granulated sugar, and salt until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold them into the batter.
Melt the butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Scatter the raisins over the batter and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the bottom is set and golden.
Turn the pancake in large sections and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into bite-size pieces and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum preserves.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, wine, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive bowl and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning the beef once daily.
Remove beef from the marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides. Add the reserved vegetables and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the reserved marinade, cover, and simmer gently for 3 to 3½ hours, turning the beef occasionally, until tender.
Transfer beef to a plate. Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan and whisk in flour, sugar, and crushed gingersnaps.
Simmer the sauce for 5 to 10 minutes until thickened. Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: German Käsespätzle
instructions: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, salt, and nutmeg into a thick, smooth batter; let it rest for 15 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through a spätzle maker or colander into the water.
Cook the spätzle until they float, about 2 to 3 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 15 minutes.
Heat butter in a large ovenproof skillet. Add a layer of spätzle, sprinkle with cheese, and repeat the layers.
Cover and cook over low heat until the cheese melts, about 5 minutes, or briefly broil until bubbling.
Top with caramelized onions and chives; serve hot.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 cup clarified butter or vegetable oil
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of parchment and gently pound to about ⅛ inch thick.
Set flour in one shallow dish, whisk eggs with milk in a second dish, and place breadcrumbs in a third dish.
Season cutlets with salt and pepper. Coat each in flour, dip in egg, then coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing them in.
Heat clarified butter or oil in a large skillet to about 350°F (175°C).
Fry the cutlets one or two at a time, gently shaking the skillet, until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain briefly on a wire rack or paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Austrian Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for brushing
6 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl. Stir in warm water, oil, and lemon juice; knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Brush the dough with oil, cover, and rest for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Toss apples with sugar, cinnamon, and raisins. Toast breadcrumbs in 2 tablespoons of melted butter until golden.
Roll the dough on a floured cloth, then gently stretch it with your hands until very thin.
Brush the dough with some remaining melted butter and sprinkle with toasted breadcrumbs and walnuts, leaving a border around the edges.
Spread the apple mixture over one end of the dough. Fold in the sides and use the cloth to roll the dough into a log.
