Place seam-side down on a baking sheet, brush with remaining butter, and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden. Cool slightly before slicing.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into bite-size cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Pour wine and lemon juice into the pot and warm over medium heat until steaming, but do not boil.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch. Add the cheese to the pot a handful at a time, stirring in a steady figure-eight motion until melted.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper. Keep the fondue warm over a low flame, stirring occasionally.
Serve with bread cubes for dipping.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, cloves, peppercorns, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive bowl and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove beef from the marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade and vegetables.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of marinade. Cover and simmer gently for 2½ to 3 hours, until tender, turning occasionally.
Transfer beef to a plate. Whisk flour into a little cold water, then stir it into the cooking liquid with broth, sugar, and crushed gingersnaps.
Simmer the sauce until thickened, season to taste, and serve with sliced beef.

title: Bavarian Pretzels (Brezeln)
ingredients: ⅔ cup food-grade lye, following package safety directions
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water; let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, fine salt, butter, and yeast mixture until a dough forms. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Divide dough into 8 pieces. Roll each into a long rope and shape into pretzels.
Place pretzels on a lined tray and refrigerate uncovered for 30 minutes.
Wearing protective gloves and eye protection, carefully dissolve lye in water in a nonreactive container. Dip each pretzel for about 10 seconds, then place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Sprinkle with coarse salt and bake at 425°F (220°C) for 12 to 15 minutes, until deep brown.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of plastic wrap and pound to about ⅛ inch thick.
Set flour, beaten eggs mixed with milk, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.
Season cutlets with salt and pepper. Coat each in flour, dip in egg, then coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing them on.
Heat clarified butter or oil in a large skillet to about 350°F (175°C).
Fry cutlets one at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, gently shaking the pan so the coating puffs.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into bite-size cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch.
Heat wine and lemon juice in the pot over medium heat until steaming, but not boiling.
Add cheese a handful at a time, stirring steadily until each addition melts before adding more.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; keep the fondue gently warm.
Serve with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Swiss Rösti
instructions: Boil potatoes whole and unpeeled for 10 to 12 minutes, until just barely tender. Drain and cool completely, preferably overnight in the refrigerator.
Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes; season with salt and pepper.
Heat butter and oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add potatoes and press into an even layer. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp.
Invert the rösti onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side for 8 to 10 minutes.
Slide onto a serving plate, cut into wedges, and serve hot.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, cloves, peppercorns, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive bowl and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the beef daily.
Remove beef from marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides.
Pour in 2 cups of reserved marinade and the beef broth. Cover and simmer gently for about 3 hours, until tender.
Transfer beef to a plate. Whisk flour with a little cold water, stir it into the pot, and simmer until thickened.
Stir in sugar and crushed gingersnaps; simmer until the sauce is smooth. Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of parchment and pound to about 1/4 inch thick.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Put flour, eggs beaten with milk, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing them on.
Heat clarified butter or oil in a large skillet to about 350°F (175°C).
Fry cutlets one at a time, gently shaking the skillet, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on a rack and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into bite-size cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch.
Heat wine and lemon juice in the pot over medium heat until steaming but not boiling.
Add the cheese by handfuls, stirring constantly until each addition melts before adding the next.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; heat gently until smooth and creamy.
Set the pot over a fondue burner and serve with bread cubes for dipping.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion into a clean kitchen towel.
Squeeze out as much liquid as possible, then transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Stir in eggs, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon in 1/4-cup portions and flatten into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden; drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with applesauce.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk egg yolks, flour, milk, granulated sugar, salt, and vanilla until smooth.
In a separate bowl, beat egg whites to soft peaks; gently fold them into the batter.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Scatter raisins over the batter and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the top is mostly set.
Turn the pancake over in large pieces and cook for 2 minutes.
Tear it into bite-size pieces with two forks and cook, tossing, until lightly browned.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with plum jam.

title: Bavarian Schweinebraten (Roast Pork)
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Pat the pork dry and score the skin.
Mix the salt, pepper, and caraway; rub over the pork, working some into the scored skin.
Heat the oil in a roasting pan and brown the pork on all sides. Set it skin side up.
Add the onions, carrots, and celery around the pork. Pour in the stock and beer without wetting the skin.
Roast uncovered for about 2½ hours, basting the vegetables occasionally, until the pork is tender.
Transfer the pork to a board and rest for 15 minutes. Strain and skim the pan juices, then serve as gravy.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil, for frying
instructions: Pound the cutlets between sheets of parchment until about ⅛ inch thick; season with salt and pepper.
Put the flour in one shallow dish, whisk the eggs with the milk in a second, and place the breadcrumbs in a third.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then cover lightly with breadcrumbs without pressing them on.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet to about 330°F (165°C).
Fry the cutlets one at a time for 2–3 minutes per side, gently shaking the pan so the coating puffs and browns.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 loaf crusty bread, cut into bite-size cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with the cornstarch.
Warm the wine and lemon juice in the pot over medium heat until steaming but not boiling.
Add the cheese by handfuls, stirring steadily until each addition melts before adding the next.
Stir in the kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; keep the fondue gently warm.
Dip the bread cubes into the fondue and serve.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: ½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes and onion into a clean kitchen towel.
Gather the towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer the potato mixture to a bowl and stir in the eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon in ¼-cup portions and flatten into thin pancakes; fry for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce.

title: Swiss Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (Veal in Cream Sauce)
instructions: Season the veal with salt and pepper, then toss it with the flour and shake off excess.
Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Brown the veal in batches for about 1 minute per side; transfer to a plate.
Add the mushrooms and onion to the skillet and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Pour in the wine and simmer until reduced by half; stir in the cream and simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the veal and any juices to the skillet and warm gently for 1–2 minutes without boiling.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley, then serve hot.

title: German Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, cloves, peppercorns, and salt in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then cool completely.
Place beef in a nonreactive bowl and pour the cooled marinade over it. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning the beef once daily.
Remove beef from the marinade and pat dry; strain and reserve the marinade.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides. Remove the beef and stir flour into the pot.
Gradually stir in 2 cups reserved marinade and the broth. Add brown sugar and raisins, then return the beef to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently for 3 hours, turning occasionally, until tender.
Stir in crushed gingersnaps and simmer until the gravy thickens. Slice the beef and serve with gravy.

title: German Kartoffelpuffer
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes and onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the grated vegetables with eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon heaping tablespoons of the mixture into the skillet and flatten into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with applesauce.

title: Austrian Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Place each cutlet between sheets of parchment and pound to about 1/4 inch thick.
Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Set flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three shallow dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then cover with breadcrumbs without pressing them in.
Heat clarified butter in a large skillet to about 330°F (165°C).
Fry the cutlets one at a time, gently shaking the pan, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk flour, milk, egg yolks, granulated sugar, and salt until smooth.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold them into the batter with the raisins.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter.
Cook until the bottom is golden and the top is beginning to set, about 5 minutes.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes, until puffed and cooked through.
Tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces with two forks and return the skillet to low heat briefly.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with plum preserves.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 1 lb crusty bread, cut into cubes
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with the cut sides of the garlic; discard the garlic.
Toss the grated cheeses with cornstarch.
Pour wine and lemon juice into the pot and warm over medium heat until steaming.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring continuously until melted before adding more.
Stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper; keep the fondue warm over low heat.
Serve immediately with bread cubes for dipping.

title: Berner Platte
ingredients: 4 smoked sausages, such as Saucisson bernois
500 g dried green beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Put the pork shoulder, bacon, marrow bones, onions, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a large pot and cover with water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skim the surface, and cook for about 1 hour.
Add the soaked beans and cook until tender, about 45 minutes.
In a separate pot, simmer the sauerkraut until tender, about 40 minutes.
Add the potatoes and sausages to the meat pot; simmer until the potatoes are tender and the sausages are heated through.
Drain the beans and toss with butter and salt.
Arrange the meat, sausages, beans, sauerkraut, and potatoes on a warm platter; serve with some cooking broth.

title: Berner Rösti
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until just tender, about 20 minutes; cool completely, preferably overnight.
Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes, then mix with the salt.
Heat the clarified butter in a heavy frying pan over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and press them into an even cake; sprinkle the water around the edge.
Cook until a golden crust forms underneath, about 10 minutes.
Turn the rösti onto a plate, slide it back into the pan, and cook the other side until golden and crisp.

title: Älplermagronen
ingredients: 500 g waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the potatoes for 5 minutes.
Add the macaroni and cook until both are tender; drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Return the potatoes and macaroni to the pot; stir in the cream, Gruyère, pepper, and nutmeg over low heat until creamy.
Add a splash of reserved cooking water if needed to loosen the mixture.
Meanwhile, fry the onions in butter over medium-low heat until deeply golden and sweet.
Serve the macaroni topped with the fried onions, with applesauce alongside.

title: Berner Zibelechueche
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Rub the cold butter into the flour and salt until crumbly.
Mix in the egg yolk and cold water; bring the dough together, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Cook the onions in butter over medium-low heat until soft and lightly golden; let cool.
Roll out the dough and line a 26 cm tart tin, then prick the base with a fork.
Scatter the onions, bacon, and Gruyère over the pastry.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, pepper, and nutmeg; pour over the filling.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until set and golden; rest briefly before slicing.

title: Berner Honiglebkuchen
instructions: Heat the honey, sugar, and milk gently in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves; cool until lukewarm.
Mix the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves in a large bowl.
Stir the honey mixture, egg, and kirsch into the dry ingredients to make a firm dough.
Cover and rest the dough at room temperature for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Roll the dough about 1 cm thick, cut into rectangles, and place on the tray.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until lightly browned, then cool on a rack.
Whisk the egg white with the powdered sugar and brush a thin glaze over the cooled lebkuchen.

title: Weißwurst with Sweet Mustard and Pretzels
instructions: Heat the water in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Add the Weißwürste and poach gently for 10–12 minutes; do not let the water boil.
Serve hot with sweet mustard and pretzels.

title: Bavarian Potato Salad
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 20 minutes; drain and peel while warm.
Slice the potatoes into a large bowl.
Warm the broth with the onion, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper, then pour it over the potatoes.
Fold gently and leave for 20 minutes so the potatoes absorb the dressing.
Stir in the oil and chives, then taste and adjust the seasoning.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, stretchy batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and press the batter through a Spätzle maker into the water.
When the Spätzle float, lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Layer the hot Spätzle with the grated cheese in a warm serving dish.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion until golden; spoon it over the Spätzle and finish with chives.

title: Schweinebraten with Dark Beer Gravy
ingredients: 1.5 kilograms boneless pork shoulder, rind scored
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Rub the pork with salt, pepper, and caraway seeds.
Heat the oil in a roasting pan and brown the pork on all sides.
Add the onions and carrots, then pour in the beer and stock around the meat.
Roast uncovered for about 2 hours, basting occasionally, until tender and cooked through.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes; strain and reduce the pan juices to make gravy, then slice and serve.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 1 tablespoon melted butter, plus extra for brushing
750 grams tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Mix the flour, egg, oil, water, and melted butter into a smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190°C and mix the apples with the raisins, sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Roll the dough thinly on a floured cloth, then gently stretch it until nearly translucent.
Sprinkle the breadcrumbs over the dough and spread the apple mixture over one half, leaving a border.
Use the cloth to roll the dough around the filling and tuck in the ends.
Place seam-side down on a baking tray, brush with melted butter, and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden.

title: Berliner Kartoffelsuppe (Berlin Potato Soup)
ingredients: 1 small celery root, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery root; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the potatoes, stock, and marjoram. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Mash some of the potatoes in the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the sausage and simmer for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then serve sprinkled with parsley.

title: Königsberger Klopse (Meatballs in Caper Sauce)
instructions: Mix the beef, pork, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper. Shape into 12 meatballs.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a large pot.
Add the meatballs and simmer gently for 15 minutes, until cooked through. Remove them with a slotted spoon and reserve the stock.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 500 ml of the reserved stock and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the cream, capers, and lemon juice. Return the meatballs to the sauce and warm gently before serving.

title: Eisbein mit Sauerkraut (Cured Pork Knuckle with Sauerkraut)
ingredients: 150 ml dry white wine or water
instructions: Put the pork knuckle in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Add the onion, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 2½ to 3 hours, until very tender.
Meanwhile, melt the lard or butter in a saucepan. Add the apple and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the sauerkraut, wine, and caraway. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain the pork knuckle and serve hot with the sauerkraut.

title: Senfeier mit Kartoffeln (Eggs in Mustard Sauce with Potatoes)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes, until tender; drain.
Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Cook for 9 minutes, then cool, peel, and halve them.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer, whisking, until smooth and thickened.
Stir in the mustard, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Add the eggs to the sauce and warm gently. Serve with the potatoes and dill.

title: Berliner Pfannkuchen (Jam-Filled Berlin Doughnuts)
ingredients: 150 g smooth raspberry or plum jam
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the milk, egg yolks, butter, and salt. Knead for about 8 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and shape them into smooth balls. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 170°C.
Fry the doughnuts in batches for about 2 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a small nozzle with jam and pipe jam into each doughnut.
Roll the warm doughnuts in sugar and serve.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
instructions: Bring the vinegar, water, onions, carrot, leek, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and sugar to a boil, then cool completely.
Put the beef in a non-reactive bowl, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the beef and pat it dry; strain and reserve the marinade and vegetables.
Season the beef with salt and pepper, then brown it on all sides in the oil in a heavy pot.
Add the reserved vegetables and cook for 5 minutes; sprinkle in the flour and stir.
Pour in 500 ml of the reserved marinade and the stock, cover, and simmer gently for about 2½ hours, turning occasionally, until tender.
Transfer the beef to a board; stir the raisins and gingerbread into the sauce and simmer until thickened.
Season the sauce, slice the beef, and serve with the sauce.

title: Himmel un Ääd (Heaven and Earth)
ingredients: 800 g floury potatoes, peeled and cubed
500 g tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the apples with 2 tbsp water and the sugar until soft, about 10 minutes; mash roughly.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the warm milk and 1 tbsp butter; season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining butter in a pan and cook the onion slowly until golden and soft.
Heat the oil in a separate pan and fry the blood sausages over medium heat until browned and hot throughout.
Serve the mashed potatoes and apples together, topped with the onions and blood sausage.

title: Rheinischer Döppekooche
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Grate the potatoes into a bowl and squeeze out excess liquid using a clean cloth.
Mix the potatoes with the onion, bacon, eggs, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pour the oil into a heavy ovenproof pot and heat it in the oven until shimmering.
Carefully add the potato mixture and spread it evenly; bake uncovered for about 1 hour 15 minutes, until crisp and cooked through.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve.

title: Rheinischer Sauerampfer-Suppe
ingredients: 400 g fresh sorrel, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion over medium-low heat until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the sorrel and cook until wilted.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the stock, stirring; simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth, then return it to the pan.
Whisk the cream and egg yolks together, then stir in a ladle of hot soup.
Remove the pan from the heat and slowly stir in the cream mixture; do not boil.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg, then serve hot.

title: Rheinische Mutzenmandeln
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add the eggs, butter, rum, and lemon zest; knead briefly to make a smooth dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1 cm thick and cut into small diamond shapes.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 170°C.
Fry the dough pieces in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden; drain on paper towels.
While still warm, toss the mutzenmandeln in the coating sugar.

title: Schwäbische Linsen mit Spätzle und Saitenwürstle
ingredients: 250 g brown or green lentils, rinsed
1 small piece of celery root, diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: For the Spätzle, mix flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, elastic batter; beat until glossy, then rest for 10 minutes.
Melt butter in a saucepan and cook onion, carrot, and celery for 4 minutes.
Stir in lentils, bay leaf, and stock; simmer until the lentils are tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Whisk flour with a little cold water, stir it into the lentils, and simmer for 3 minutes. Season with vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press or scrape the batter into the water in batches; lift out the Spätzle when they float and keep warm.
Warm the sausages gently in hot water without boiling. Serve with the lentils and Spätzle.

title: Käsespätzle
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, elastic batter; beat well and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook the onions slowly until deeply golden, about 15–20 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press or scrape the batter into the water in batches; lift out the Spätzle when they float.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Layer Spätzle and grated cheese in a buttered baking dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake until the cheese melts and the top is lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Top with the browned onions and season with pepper.

title: Maultaschen in der Brühe
ingredients: 100 g finely chopped spinach, squeezed dry
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Mix flour, 2 eggs, water, and salt into a firm dough. Knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt butter and cook the onion until soft; cool briefly.
Mix pork, spinach, cooked onion, 1 egg, breadcrumbs, parsley, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Roll the dough thinly into a rectangle. Spoon filling in a strip along one long side, leaving space between portions.
Fold the dough over the filling, press around each portion to seal, and cut into rectangular dumplings.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Cook the Maultaschen for 10–12 minutes, until cooked through.
Serve in hot broth sprinkled with chives.

title: Zwiebelrostbraten mit Bratkartoffeln
ingredients: 2 beef rump steaks, about 200 g each
600 g waxy potatoes, cooked and chilled
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Toss onion slices with flour and shake off the excess.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet and fry the onions in batches until crisp and golden; drain and season with salt.
Slice the chilled potatoes. Heat oil and butter in a large skillet and fry the potatoes until browned and crisp, turning occasionally; season with salt and pepper.
Season the steaks with salt and pepper. Heat a separate skillet with 1 tablespoon oil and sear the steaks for 2–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness and preferred doneness.
Transfer the steaks to a warm plate to rest. Stir mustard and beef stock into the steak pan and simmer briefly, scraping up the browned bits.
Serve each steak with pan sauce, crisp onions, and Bratkartoffeln; sprinkle the potatoes with parsley.

title: Schwäbischer Kartoffelsalat
ingredients: 250 ml beef or vegetable stock, hot
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 20–25 minutes; drain and let them cool just enough to handle.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly into a large bowl.
Warm the stock with the onion, vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Pour the warm dressing over the potatoes and gently fold together. Let stand for 20 minutes so the potatoes absorb the dressing.
Fold in the oil and chives. Taste and adjust the seasoning; serve slightly warm or at room temperature.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 thin veal cutlets, about 5 ounces each
1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil, for frying
instructions: Pound the cutlets gently until evenly thin, then season both sides with salt.
Put the flour in one shallow dish, whisk the eggs with the milk in a second, and place the breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, and coat it lightly with breadcrumbs without pressing them on.
Heat the clarified butter or oil in a large skillet to about 340°F (170°C).
Fry the cutlets one at a time, gently shaking the pan, until golden on both sides and cooked through, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain briefly on a rack or paper towels and serve at once with lemon wedges.

title: Tafelspitz with Apple-Horseradish Sauce
ingredients: 3 pounds beef rump or top round, tied if needed
2 teaspoons fine salt, plus more to taste
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small celery root, peeled and cut into chunks
1 leek, trimmed and cut into chunks
1 tart apple, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Place the beef in a large pot and add the cold water and salt.
Bring slowly to a gentle simmer, skimming any foam from the surface.
Meanwhile, brown the cut sides of the onion in a dry skillet until deeply golden.
Add the onion, carrots, celery root, leek, bay leaf, and peppercorns to the pot.
Simmer very gently, uncovered, until the beef is tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours; do not let the broth boil hard.
Mix the horseradish, grated apple, lemon juice, and sour cream; season to taste.
Lift out the beef, slice it across the grain, and serve with the vegetables, some strained broth, and the apple-horseradish sauce.

title: Käsespätzle
ingredients: 1/2 cup water, plus more as needed
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, salt, and nutmeg into a thick, elastic batter; beat until bubbles form, adding a little water if needed.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and set a bowl of cold water nearby.
Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or colander into the boiling water in batches.
When the noodles float, scoop them into the cold water, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat until deeply golden, about 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a baking dish and layer in the drained noodles and cheeses.
Bake until the cheese is melted and bubbling, about 15 minutes, then top with the onions and chives.

title: Wiener Erdäpfelsalat
ingredients: 1 teaspoon fine salt, or to taste
instructions: Place the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer until tender when pierced, about 20 to 25 minutes, then drain and let cool just enough to handle.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly into a large bowl.
Scatter the chopped onion over the warm potatoes.
Whisk the hot broth with the vinegar, oil, mustard, salt, and pepper, then pour it over the potatoes.
Fold gently and let the salad stand for at least 30 minutes so the potatoes absorb the dressing.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then sprinkle with chives before serving.

title: Marillenknödel
ingredients: 1 pound ripe apricots, washed and patted dry
8 ounces farmer cheese or well-drained quark
1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Mix the farmer cheese, egg, softened butter, flour, semolina, and salt into a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Slit each apricot, remove the pit, and place a sugar cube inside; close the fruit around it.
With floured hands, wrap each apricot in dough and seal it completely.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer and cook the dumplings in batches for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet and toast the breadcrumbs until golden; stir in the sugar and cinnamon.
Lift the dumplings out with a slotted spoon, drain briefly, and roll them in the cinnamon breadcrumbs before serving.

title: Tiroler Gröstl
ingredients: 500 g waxy potatoes, boiled in their skins and cooled
300 g cooked beef or leftover roast, thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices.
Heat the butter in a large skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef and caraway; fry briefly, then add the potatoes.
Fry, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are golden and crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with parsley. Fry the eggs separately and serve one on each portion.

title: Tiroler Speckknödel
instructions: Place the bread in a large bowl.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion and speck until the onion is soft. Let cool slightly, then add to the bread.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, parsley, salt, and pepper; pour over the bread and mix gently.
Leave the mixture to rest for 15 minutes, then mix in the flour. Shape into 8 firm dumplings with damp hands.
Simmer the dumplings gently in salted water for 15–20 minutes, until cooked through.
Serve in hot beef broth.

title: Kasspatzln
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, sticky batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through a spaetzle maker into the water in batches.
When the spaetzle float, lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a wide pan. Add the spaetzle and both cheeses, stirring until melted and creamy.
In a separate pan, cook the onions in the remaining butter until deeply golden.
Top the spaetzle with the onions and chives, and serve hot.

title: Tiroler Kaspressknödel
ingredients: 3 tablespoons butter or oil, for frying
instructions: Place the bread and grated cheese in a large bowl.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Add it to the bowl.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, parsley, salt, and pepper; pour over the bread mixture and leave for 15 minutes.
Mix in the flour. Shape the mixture into 8 balls, then flatten each into a patty.
Heat the frying butter or oil in a skillet and fry the patties over medium heat until golden on both sides and cooked through.
Serve in hot beef broth.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Whisk the egg yolks with the milk, flour, granulated sugar, vanilla sugar, and salt until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and gently fold them into the batter with the raisins.
Melt the butter in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Pour in the batter and cook until the underside is golden.
Turn the pancake in large pieces and cook the other side until set. Tear it into bite-sized pieces with two forks.
Dust with confectioners' sugar and serve warm with plum jam.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) beef or veal stock
instructions: Season the veal with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over high heat. Brown the veal quickly in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet. Cook the onion and mushrooms until softened and lightly browned.
Stir in the flour, then add the wine and stock, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced.
Stir in the cream and simmer until the sauce thickens. Add the lemon juice.
Return the veal and any juices to the skillet and warm through without boiling. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Zürcher Birchermüesli
instructions: Stir the oats, milk, and lemon juice together in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Fold in the grated apples and yogurt.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the oat mixture with the condensed milk.
Top with hazelnuts and raspberries before serving.

title: Rösti
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until just tender, about 15 to 20 minutes. Drain, cool, and refrigerate until completely cold.
Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat. Add the potatoes and press them into an even cake.
Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, loosening the edges occasionally, until the underside is golden and crisp.
Invert the rösti onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side until golden and crisp. Serve hot.

title: Älplermagronen
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the potatoes and macaroni and cook until both are tender. Drain well.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion over medium-low heat until golden and soft.
Warm the cream and milk in a saucepan. Stir in the Gruyère, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until the cheese melts.
Toss the drained potatoes and macaroni with the cheese sauce.
Top with the golden onions and serve with applesauce.

title: Zuger Kirschtorte
ingredients: 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, for syrup
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line two 9-inch (23 cm) cake pans with parchment.
Beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup sugar until pale and thick. Fold in the flour and ground almonds.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks. Fold them gently into the yolk mixture.
Divide the batter between the pans and bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool completely.
Simmer the water and 1/2 cup sugar until dissolved. Cool, then stir in the kirsch.
Whip the cream with 2 tbsp powdered sugar until firm. Brush the cake layers generously with the kirsch syrup.
Spread whipped cream between the layers and over the top and sides. Press the toasted almonds onto the sides and dust the top with powdered sugar. Chill before serving.

title: Berner Platte
ingredients: 4 smoked sausages, such as cabbage sausages
500 g dried green beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Put the pork shoulder, bacon, onions, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a large pot and cover with water.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 1 hour, skimming as needed.
Add the soaked beans and cook until tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut and potatoes; simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add the sausages and pork chops for the last 15 minutes, cooking until heated through and done.
Arrange the meats and vegetables on a platter and serve hot.

title: Älplermagronen with Apple Purée
ingredients: 500 g waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Put the apples, water, and sugar in a small saucepan and simmer until soft, about 15 minutes; mash into a purée.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes.
Add the macaroni to the potatoes and cook until both are tender; drain.
Return the macaroni and potatoes to the pot, stir in the cream and Gruyère, and warm gently until creamy.
Cook the onions in butter over medium-low heat until deeply golden, about 15 minutes.
Spoon the onions over the macaroni and serve with the apple purée.

title: Berner Rösti
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until just tender, about 20 minutes; drain and cool completely.
Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and shape into a compact cake.
Cook until the underside is golden and crisp, about 15 minutes.
Invert onto a plate, slide back into the skillet, and cook the other side until crisp, about 10 minutes.

title: Zibelechueche (Bernese Onion Tart)
instructions: Mix the flour and salt, rub in the cold butter, then add the water and bring the dough together.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Cook the onions in butter over low heat until soft and lightly golden, about 20 minutes; cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, cream, Gruyère, nutmeg, salt, and pepper together, then stir in the onions.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Roll out the dough and line a 26 cm tart pan; prick the base with a fork.
Pour in the onion filling and bake until set and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Berner Honiglebkuchen
instructions: Warm the honey, sugar, and water in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves; let cool until lukewarm.
Mix the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and lemon zest in a large bowl.
Pour in the honey mixture and stir until a soft dough forms.
Cover and let the dough rest in a cool place for at least 12 hours.
Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Roll the dough out to about 1 cm thick and cut into rectangles.
Brush with milk and bake until firm and lightly browned, about 15 minutes.

title: Weißwurst with Pretzels and Sweet Mustard
instructions: Heat the water until steaming but not boiling.
Add the Weißwürste and let them warm gently for 10–12 minutes.
Serve the sausages hot with pretzels and sweet mustard.

title: Schweinebraten with Beer Gravy
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Score the pork rind, then rub the pork with salt, caraway, and pepper.
Put the onions and carrots in a roasting pan and set the pork on top, rind-side up.
Pour the beer and stock around the pork, taking care not to wet the rind.
Roast for about 2 hours, basting occasionally, until tender and the rind is crisp.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, then strain and season the pan juices as gravy.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, sticky batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a simmer.
Press or scrape the batter into the water in small batches; cook until the spätzle float, then lift them out.
Heat the oven to 180°C and butter an ovenproof dish.
Layer the spätzle and cheese in the dish, then bake for 10 minutes until the cheese melts.
Fry the onions in oil until golden and scatter them over the spätzle before serving.

title: Bayerischer Kartoffelsalat
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain and let them cool enough to handle.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly into a large bowl.
Whisk the hot stock with the vinegar, oil, mustard, onion, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the potatoes and fold gently; let stand for 20 minutes to absorb.
Sprinkle with chives and serve at room temperature.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus extra for brushing
800 g tart apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Mix the flour, egg, oil, water, and salt into a smooth dough; knead until elastic.
Brush the dough with oil, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190°C and mix the apples with raisins, sugar, and cinnamon.
On a floured cloth, roll and stretch the dough into a very thin rectangle.
Brush the dough with melted butter and sprinkle with breadcrumbs, leaving a border.
Spread the apple mixture over one end, fold in the sides, and roll up using the cloth.
Place seam-side down on a baking tray, brush with the remaining butter, and bake for 40–45 minutes until golden.

title: Berliner Kartoffelsuppe (Berlin-Style Potato Soup)
ingredients: 600 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the bacon until lightly crisp.
Add the onion, carrot, and leek; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the potatoes, stock, marjoram, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and mash some of the potatoes in the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the sausage and warm through; season with salt and pepper.
Serve with parsley scattered over the top.

title: Königsberger Klopse (Meatballs in Caper Sauce)
ingredients: 400 g ground veal or a mixture of veal and pork
instructions: Soak the bread roll in the milk, then squeeze out the excess milk and crumble it.
Mix the bread with the ground meat, onion, egg, salt, and pepper; shape into 8 meatballs.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer and cook the meatballs for 15 minutes, without boiling hard.
Lift out the meatballs and keep them warm; reserve 400 ml of the cooking stock.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the reserved stock and cream; simmer until smooth and lightly thickened.
Stir in the capers, lemon juice, and sugar, then return the meatballs to the sauce and warm gently.

title: Eisbein mit Sauerkraut (Cured Pork Knuckle with Sauerkraut)
ingredients: 100 ml dry white wine or water
instructions: Put the pork knuckle in a large pot with the onion, carrot, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Cover with cold water, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook partially covered for about 2½ hours, until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the lard in a saucepan and stir in the sauerkraut and grated apple.
Add the wine or water and caraway; cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lift the knuckle from the pot and let it drain briefly.
Serve the pork with the sauerkraut and boiled potatoes or peas.

title: Berliner Leber (Berlin-Style Liver with Apples and Onions)
ingredients: 2 apples, cored and cut into rings
instructions: Pat the liver dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Lightly coat the liver slices in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet; fry the onions until golden, then set them aside.
Add the remaining oil and butter; fry the apple rings until tender and lightly browned, then set them aside.
Fry the liver in batches for about 2 minutes per side, keeping the centers slightly pink.
Arrange the liver with the apples and onions, and finish with parsley.

title: Berliner Pfannkuchen (Jelly Doughnuts)
instructions: Combine the flour, yeast, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the milk, egg yolks, butter, salt, and vanilla; knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and shape each into a smooth ball.
Set the balls on a floured tray, cover, and let rise for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep pot and fry the doughnuts in batches for about 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain on a rack and roll in sugar while still warm.
Fill a piping bag with jam and inject a little into the side of each doughnut.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef rump or bottom round
instructions: Put the vinegar, water, onions, carrot, leek, bay leaves, cloves, peppercorns, and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil; let cool completely.
Place the beef in a nonreactive bowl, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the beef and pat it dry; strain and reserve the marinade and vegetables.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the reserved vegetables and cook briefly, then dust with the flour.
Pour in 500 ml of the reserved marinade and the beef stock; cover and simmer gently for about 2½ hours, turning occasionally, until tender.
Remove the beef and keep it warm; strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan.
Stir the golden syrup and raisins into the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes; season with salt.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce, potato dumplings, and red cabbage.

title: Himmel un Ääd (Heaven and Earth)
ingredients: 800 g floury potatoes, peeled and chopped
500 g tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the apples with 2 tablespoons water, the sugar, and lemon juice until soft; mash roughly and keep warm.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and milk; season with salt and pepper.
Toss the onions with the flour.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onions over medium heat until golden and crisp; transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, fry the blood sausages gently until browned and heated through, turning carefully.
Serve the mashed potatoes and apples together, topped with the sausages and fried onions.

title: Rheinischer Döppekooche
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze out excess liquid with a clean kitchen towel.
Mix the potatoes with the onions, bacon, eggs, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pour the oil into a heavy ovenproof pot and heat it in the oven for 5 minutes.
Carefully add the potato mixture and smooth the top.
Bake uncovered for about 1 hour 30 minutes, until the top is deeply golden and crisp and the center is set.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve.

title: Rheinischer Endiviensalat mit Kartoffeln
ingredients: 1 large head curly endive, washed and thinly sliced
100 ml warm beef or vegetable stock
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes; drain, peel while warm, and slice.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, warm stock, sugar, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the warm potato slices and toss gently; let them absorb the dressing for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the bacon and onion until the bacon is crisp.
Pour the hot bacon, onion, and pan drippings over the potatoes and toss.
Fold in the sliced endive just before serving, while the potatoes are still warm.

title: Rheinische Rievkooche (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: 4 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more as needed
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes and squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a clean kitchen towel.
Mix the potatoes with the onion, eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon in small mounds of the mixture and flatten each into a thin pancake.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding more oil as needed.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce.

title: Maultaschen (Swabian Filled Pasta)
ingredients: 3 tablespoons water, plus more as needed
4 ounces spinach, cooked and squeezed dry
1 stale bread roll, soaked in water and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix the flour, 2 eggs, salt, and water into a firm dough; knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Let it cool.
Finely chop the spinach, then mix it with the onion, pork, beef, bread roll, egg, parsley, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Roll the dough thinly into a rectangle. Spoon the filling in a line along one side, fold the dough over it, and press the edges to seal. Cut into large rectangles.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Cook the Maultaschen in batches for 10–12 minutes, until cooked through.

title: Linsen mit Spätzle und Saitenwürstle
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a saucepan and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the broth. Add the lentils and bay leaf; simmer until the lentils are tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the vinegar, salt, and pepper, and keep the lentils warm.
For the Spätzle, beat the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, elastic batter.
Press the batter through a Spätzle maker into a pot of boiling salted water. When the noodles float, lift them out and drain.
Melt the remaining butter and toss it with the Spätzle. Warm the Saitenwürstle gently in hot water, then serve with the lentils and noodles.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a thick, elastic batter; beat until small bubbles form.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions slowly until deeply golden and soft.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through a Spätzle maker into the water in batches.
When the Spätzle float, remove them with a slotted spoon and drain.
Heat the butter in a large pan. Add the Spätzle and cheese in layers, tossing gently until the cheese melts.
Top with the onions and black pepper, and serve hot.

title: Schwäbischer Kartoffelsalat
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 20–25 minutes. Drain, cool just enough to handle, and peel.
Slice the warm potatoes thinly into a large bowl and add the onion.
Whisk together the hot broth, vinegar, oil, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the potatoes and gently fold until they absorb it. Let the salad stand for at least 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with chives and serve at room temperature.

title: Zwiebelrostbraten
ingredients: 4 beef sirloin steaks, about 6 ounces each
instructions: Season the steaks with salt and pepper, then dust lightly with flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over high heat. Sear the steaks for 2–3 minutes per side, or to your preferred doneness; transfer to a warm plate.
Add the butter and onions to the skillet. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until golden and soft, about 15 minutes.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the broth and mustard, then simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return the steaks and any juices to the pan briefly to warm through. Serve topped with the onions and sauce.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 4 veal cutlets, about 5 oz each, pounded thin
1 cup clarified butter or neutral oil, for frying
instructions: Set out the flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs in three shallow dishes.
Season the cutlets with salt and pepper, then coat each in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs without pressing the crumbs firmly.
Heat the clarified butter in a large skillet until hot but not smoking.
Fry the cutlets in batches for 2–3 minutes per side, gently shaking the pan so the fat washes over them.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve at once with lemon wedges.

title: Tafelspitz
ingredients: 3 lb beef rump or top round, in one piece
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small celery root, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Place the beef in a large pot and cover with the cold water; bring slowly to a gentle simmer.
Skim the surface, add the salt, and simmer uncovered for 1 hour.
Char the cut sides of the onion in a dry skillet, then add the onion, vegetables, peppercorns, and bay leaves to the pot.
Simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beef is tender; avoid a hard boil.
Lift out the beef and slice across the grain. Strain the broth and serve the meat with some broth and chopped chives.

title: Wiener Erdäpfelsalat
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender, about 20–25 minutes.
Drain, cool just enough to handle, then peel and slice the potatoes into a bowl.
Stir together the hot broth, onion, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the warm potatoes and toss gently; leave for 20 minutes to absorb.
Fold in the oil and chives, adjust the seasoning, and serve at room temperature.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, milk, salt, and nutmeg into a thick, sticky batter; beat until glossy.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Push the batter through a spätzle maker or colander into the water.
When the spätzle float, cook for 1 minute more, then lift them out and drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium heat until deeply golden, about 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a baking dish and layer in the spätzle and cheese, seasoning with pepper between layers.
Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted, then top with the onions.

title: Marillenknödel
ingredients: 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Mix the farmer cheese, egg, softened butter, flour, and semolina into a soft dough; chill for 30 minutes.
Press a sugar cube into the cavity of each apricot.
With floured hands, divide the dough into 8 portions and wrap one portion around each apricot, sealing it completely.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer and cook the dumplings for 12–15 minutes, turning once.
Melt the remaining butter in a skillet, stir in the breadcrumbs, and toast until golden.
Mix the 2 tablespoons sugar with the cinnamon, then roll the drained dumplings in the buttery crumbs and serve warm.

title: Tiroler Gröstl
ingredients: 1 lb cooked potatoes, cooled and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the potatoes and cook, turning occasionally, until browned.
Stir in the beef, marjoram, salt, and pepper; cook until heated through and crisp in places.
In a separate pan, fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the Gröstl topped with fried eggs and parsley.

title: Tiroler Speckknödel
instructions: Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion and speck until the onion is soft; cool slightly.
Place the bread in a bowl and mix in the onion, speck, parsley, eggs, milk, flour, salt, and pepper.
Let the mixture stand for 15 minutes, then shape it into 8 firm dumplings with damp hands.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and cook the dumplings for 15–18 minutes, without boiling hard.
Serve the dumplings in the broth.

title: Kaspressknödel
ingredients: 6 cups beef or vegetable broth, for serving
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and cook the onion until soft; cool slightly.
Combine the bread, cheese, onion, eggs, milk, parsley, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl; rest for 15 minutes.
Shape the mixture into 8 flat patties, pressing them firmly together.
Melt the remaining butter in a skillet and fry the patties over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot in warm broth, or enjoy them plain with a green salad.

title: Tiroler Kiachl
instructions: Stir the yeast and 1 teaspoon of the sugar into the lukewarm milk and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, egg yolks, melted butter, salt, rum, and yeast mixture into a soft dough.
Knead until smooth, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces, shape into balls, and rest covered for 15 minutes.
Stretch each ball into a thin round with a thicker rim.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the rounds one at a time until golden on both sides.
Drain briefly and serve with lingonberry jam.

title: Tiroler Schlipfkrapfen
ingredients: 1 lb starchy potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter until soft, then mix it into the potatoes with the chives and pepper.
Mix the flour, egg, water, oil, and salt into a smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch rounds.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each round, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Cook the dumplings in gently boiling salted water for 4–5 minutes, until they float and are tender.
Brown the serving butter and pour it over the dumplings; finish with chives.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the veal with salt and pepper, then dust lightly with flour.
Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a pan over high heat. Brown the veal quickly in batches and set aside.
Add the remaining butter and onion to the pan; cook until softened.
Add the mushrooms and cook until their liquid evaporates.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer until reduced by half.
Add the stock and cream, then simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return the veal to the pan and warm gently without boiling.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley, adjust the seasoning, and serve.

title: Rösti
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, about 15 minutes; drain and cool completely.
Peel the cooled potatoes and grate them coarsely.
Season the grated potatoes with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and press them into an even cake.
Cook until the underside is golden and crisp, about 10 minutes.
Invert the rösti onto a plate, slide it back into the pan, and cook the other side until golden.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

title: Zürcher Chäschüechli
instructions: Rub the flour and salt into the butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Mix in the egg yolk and cold water; bring the dough together without overworking it.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roll out the dough and line 8 small tart tins; prick the bases with a fork.
Divide the grated cheeses among the pastry shells.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, nutmeg, and pepper; pour over the cheese.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and golden. Serve warm.

title: Älplermagronen
ingredients: 400 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more for the cooking water
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the macaroni and cook until both are tender; drain well.
Return the macaroni and potatoes to the pot. Stir in the cheese, cream, milk, nutmeg, and pepper.
Warm gently, stirring, until the cheese melts and the mixture is creamy.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet; cook the onions slowly until deeply golden.
Spoon the macaroni into bowls and top with the onions.
Serve with applesauce on the side.

title: Birchermüesli
instructions: Stir the oats, milk, and lemon juice together in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Fold in the grated apples, yogurt, and condensed milk.
Add the strawberries, hazelnuts, and raisins.
Serve chilled.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter over medium heat until soft and golden. Stir it into the potatoes with the cheese and pepper.
Combine the flour and salt. Add the egg, warm water, and oil; knead until a smooth dough forms. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches for 3–4 minutes, until they float. Serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Brown the chicken on both sides, then transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Add the broth gradually, stirring until smooth. Return the chicken to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 35–40 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then mix it into the pot off the heat.
Cook the noodles according to package directions and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes, until softened.
Add the beets and tomato paste; cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the dill and adjust the seasoning. Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Mămăligă with Cheese and Sour Cream
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the butter. Spoon into bowls and top with feta and sour cream.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches. Transfer to a plate.
Add the onions and cook until deeply golden, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, and garlic; cook for 30 seconds.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the broth and caraway seeds, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Mix the flour with the cold water until smooth. Stir it into the goulash and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or well-drained cottage cheese
1 medium onion, thinly sliced, for serving
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash.
Cook the diced onion in butter until soft and golden. Mix it with the potatoes, cheese, and pepper; cool the filling.
Combine the flour and salt. Add the egg, warm water, and melted butter, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 minutes more. Drain.
Fry the sliced onion in oil until golden. Serve the pierogi topped with fried onion and sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides. Transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft. Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the paprika and flour, then add the broth gradually.
Add the tomato, bell pepper, and chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 35 to 45 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions and drain.
Stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then mix it into the pot off the heat. Serve the chicken and sauce over noodles.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Put the beef, water, bay leaves, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and carrot until softened, then stir in the beets and tomato paste.
Add the cabbage and potatoes to the broth and simmer until nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the beet mixture, vinegar, sugar, and black pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and dill. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then remove the bay leaves.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Romanian Mămăligă
ingredients: 1 cup crumbled feta or Romanian telemea cheese
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until thick and pulling away from the sides, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the butter.
Spoon the mămăligă into bowls and top with cheese and sour cream.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
4 cups bread dumplings, sliced, for serving
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until deeply golden, about 12 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika, tomato paste, and garlic.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the broth, caraway seeds, and bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Mix the flour with the cold water until smooth. Stir it into the goulash and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the marjoram, remove the bay leaves, and serve with sliced bread dumplings.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or dry-curd cottage cheese
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the chopped onion in butter until soft and golden. Stir it into the potatoes with the cheese, pepper, and salt; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the egg, warm water, and sour cream; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; remove with a slotted spoon.
Fry the sliced onion in butter until golden. Serve the pierogi topped with onion and melted butter.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the broth, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, cook the beets, onion, and carrot in a skillet over medium heat until softened, about 10 minutes.
Stir the tomatoes, tomato paste, vinegar, and sugar into the vegetables; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage to the beef broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the beet mixture, salt, and pepper; simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the garlic and dill. Rest the soup for 10 minutes, then serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft, about 8 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika.
Stir in the flour and broth until smooth, then return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions; drain.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Stir the sour cream into the sauce, then return the chicken and warm gently without boiling.
Serve over noodles and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Romanian Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head sour cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: Rinse the cabbage leaves and trim away any thick ribs. Chop any torn leaves and set aside.
Cook the onion in oil until softened. Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then cool slightly.
Combine the onion and rice with the pork, beef, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Place a portion of filling near the base of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Scatter the chopped cabbage and bacon in a large pot. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in layers.
Mix the tomato paste, diced tomatoes, and water; pour over the rolls. Add water if needed to nearly cover them.
Cover and simmer gently until the cabbage and rice are tender, about 2 hours.

title: Czech Bramboráky (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes into a bowl and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the potatoes with the egg, flour, garlic, marjoram, salt, pepper, and milk.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon the potato mixture into the skillet and flatten each portion into a thin pancake.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden; add more oil as needed.
Drain the pancakes on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or dry-curd cottage cheese
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden. Stir it into the potatoes with the cheese and pepper; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add the egg, oil, and warm water, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain and serve with butter and sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft. Remove from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Add the broth, tomato, and bell pepper, stirring to combine. Return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes.
Stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then stir the mixture into the pot without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: If using beef, simmer it in the broth until tender, about 1 1/2 hours; remove and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the beets and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the broth and add the beef, if using, and potatoes. Simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the cabbage is tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the dill and serve with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale
ingredients: 1 large head sour cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: If the cabbage leaves are very salty, rinse them and trim away the thick ribs.
Cook the onion in the oil until soft. Cool slightly, then mix with the pork, beef, rice, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Line a heavy pot with any torn cabbage leaves. Arrange the rolls seam-side down and scatter the bacon between layers.
Mix the tomato paste, tomato juice, and water; pour over the rolls. Add water if needed to nearly cover them.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the cabbage and rice are tender.

title: Russian Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then toss with the flour.
Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet. Brown the beef in batches and set aside.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the skillet until softened and lightly browned.
Add the beef broth and mustard, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Return the beef to the skillet and simmer gently until just cooked through.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the sour cream.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions. Serve the stroganoff over the noodles, garnished with parsley.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden.
Mix the potatoes, farmer cheese, onion, pepper, and salt for the filling.
Combine the flour and salt, then mix in the egg, warm water, and melted butter to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch rounds.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and firmly pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes.
Serve warm with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, for the sauce
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft, about 8 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and 1 tablespoon flour.
Add the broth and return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the remaining 1 tablespoon flour, then stir in a little hot sauce from the pot.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot and warm gently without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the beets and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the broth and potatoes, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper, and dill; adjust the seasoning to taste.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the cabbage head until the leaves loosen, about 5 minutes.
Separate 12 large leaves, trim their thick ribs, and reserve the remaining cabbage.
Cook the onion in the oil until soft, then cool slightly.
Mix the onion with the pork, rice, salt, pepper, thyme, and dill.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Finely shred the reserved cabbage and spread half in the bottom of a heavy pot.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down over the shredded cabbage and tuck in the bacon slices.
Cover with the remaining shredded cabbage, then pour in the passata and water.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked, about 2 hours.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
4 cups bread dumplings, sliced, for serving
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions and cook until deeply golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, caraway, and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot and add the broth and garlic.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Whisk the flour with the cold water until smooth, then stir it into the goulash.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the parsley and serve with sliced bread dumplings.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter over medium heat until soft and golden.
Mix the mashed potatoes with farmer cheese, onion, salt, and pepper; let the filling cool.
Combine flour and salt in a bowl. Add the egg, warm water, and oil; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch rounds.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; remove with a slotted spoon.
Serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour for sour cream mixture
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Pour in the broth, stirring to make a smooth sauce, then return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with 1 tablespoon flour, then stir in a few spoonfuls of hot sauce.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot and warm gently without boiling.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrot until softened.
Add the beets and tomato paste; cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes, reduce the heat, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper; simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
