Stir in the garlic and dill, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Mămăligă
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until thick and pulling away from the sides, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the butter.
Spoon into bowls and top with feta and sour cream.

title: Czech Svíčková na Smetaně
ingredients: 2 pounds beef sirloin or top round
1 small celery root, peeled and chopped
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the butter, carrots, parsnip, celery root, and onion; cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and add the bay leaves and allspice; return the beef to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the beef and keep it warm. Discard the bay leaves and allspice.
Blend the vegetables and cooking liquid until smooth, then return the sauce to the pot.
Stir in the lemon juice, sugar, cream, and finishing butter; warm gently and season to taste.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce, bread dumplings, lemon, and cranberry preserves.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter over medium heat until soft and golden.
Mix the mashed potatoes with the farmer cheese, onion, and black pepper; cool the filling.
Combine the flour and salt, then mix in the egg, warm water, and oil to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and firmly pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, caraway seeds, and garlic; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste and bell pepper, then return the beef to the pot.
Pour in the broth, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered until tender, about 20 minutes.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook the onion and carrot until softened.
Add the beet and tomato paste; cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage, vinegar, salt, and pepper; simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the dill and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Separate the cabbage leaves and trim away thick ribs; reserve the smaller leaves and any trimmings.
Cook the onion in oil over medium heat until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the pork, beef, rice, onion, thyme, paprika, and black pepper in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Chop the reserved cabbage trimmings and spread half over the bottom of a large pot.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot; scatter the bacon and remaining trimmings between the layers.
Mix the tomato passata with the water and pour it over the rolls.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked through, about 2 hours.

title: Czech Bramboráky (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze out excess liquid with a clean kitchen towel.
Mix the potatoes with the egg, flour, garlic, marjoram, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon the potato mixture into the skillet and flatten each portion into a thin pancake.
Fry until golden and crisp, about 3 minutes per side; add more oil as needed.
Drain the pancakes on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 cup farmer cheese or dry-curd cottage cheese
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Mix the mashed potatoes with the cheese, onion, and pepper; let the filling cool.
Combine the flour and salt, then mix in the egg and warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch circles.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; drain.
Pan-fry in vegetable oil until lightly browned, and serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, for the sauce
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the lard in a Dutch oven and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Stir in the broth, return the chicken to the pot, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the remaining tablespoon of flour, then stir in a little hot cooking liquid.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot and warm gently without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions and serve with the paprikash.

title: Russian Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a skillet and sear the beef in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, onion, and mushrooms to the skillet and cook until softened and browned.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Add the broth and mustard, scraping up browned bits, and simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the beef to the skillet and simmer gently until just cooked through.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the sour cream.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions, then serve topped with the beef mixture and parsley.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the beets and tomato paste; cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the broth and beef, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 60 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, salt, and pepper; simmer for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the dill and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Mămăligă
ingredients: 1 cup crumbled feta or Romanian telemea cheese
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until thick and creamy, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the butter until melted.
Spoon into bowls and top with crumbled cheese and sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden. Stir it into the potatoes with the farmer cheese, salt, and pepper; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the egg, warm water, and oil; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch rounds. Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and firmly pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain and serve with butter and sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken on both sides. Transfer it to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft. Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the paprika and flour, then add the broth.
Return the chicken to the pot. Cover and simmer gently until cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Stir a few spoonfuls of hot cooking liquid into the sour cream, then stir the mixture into the pot. Warm gently without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions. Serve the chicken and sauce over noodles, sprinkled with parsley.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef stew meat, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion and carrot until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beet and tomato paste; cook, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Add the beef broth and beef. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and cabbage. Simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then stir in the dill.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream in each bowl.

title: Romanian Mămăligă
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until thick and pulling away from the sides, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the butter and transfer the mămăligă to a serving plate.
Serve warm with crumbled feta and sour cream.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches. Transfer it to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until deeply golden, about 15 minutes. Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, and garlic.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the beef broth, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the caraway seeds and bay leaves, cover, and simmer until tender, about 2 hours.
Stir in the marjoram and vinegar. Remove the bay leaves and serve hot.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
1 cup farmer cheese or dry cottage cheese
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat until golden. Mix it with the potatoes, cheese, and black pepper; cool the filling.
Combine the flour and salt. Add the egg, warm water, and melted butter, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch rounds. Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and pinch the edges closed.
Cook the pierogi in batches in simmering salted water until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain and serve, or pan-fry until golden.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken on both sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, about 6 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Stir in the broth, return the pot to medium heat, and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the water. Stir a spoonful of hot sauce into the sour cream, then stir the mixture into the pot without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions, drain, and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Put the beef, water, bay leaves, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the beets, onion, and carrot for 8 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and 1/2 cup of broth.
Add the cabbage and potatoes to the beef broth. Simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the beet mixture, vinegar, sugar, and black pepper. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the dill, and serve with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale
ingredients: 1 large head pickled cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: Rinse the cabbage leaves and trim away any thick ribs. Chop any small or torn leaves and set aside.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then cool slightly.
Mix the pork, beef, onion and rice mixture, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place about 2 tablespoons of filling on each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Scatter the chopped cabbage and bacon in the bottom of a heavy pot. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in layers.
Whisk the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, and broth together, then pour over the rolls. Cover and simmer gently for 2 1/2 hours, until the cabbage and filling are tender.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
8 slices Czech-style bread dumplings, for serving
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, then set it aside.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until deep golden, about 12 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika, tomato paste, and garlic.
Return the pot to medium heat. Add the beef, broth, and caraway seeds, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the beef is tender, about 2 hours. Stir in the marjoram.
Mix the flour and cold water until smooth. Stir it into the goulash and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken. Serve with bread dumplings.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or dry-curd cottage cheese
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter until soft and golden, then mix it with the potatoes, cheese, and pepper.
Mix the flour and salt; add the egg and warm water, and knead until a smooth dough forms. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Stir in the broth, return the chicken to the pot, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions. Stir the sour cream into the sauce off the heat and serve the chicken over the noodles.

title: Russian Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet over high heat and sear the beef in batches. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and cook the onion and mushrooms until softened and browned.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the broth and mustard. Simmer until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions. Return the beef to the skillet and warm through.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the sour cream. Serve over the noodles.

title: Romanian Sarmale
ingredients: 1 large head sour cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then cool slightly.
Mix the pork, beef, onion mixture, thyme, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Spread some tomato sauce in a large pot. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in layers, adding bacon between layers.
Pour the remaining tomato sauce and water over the rolls. Cover and simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked, about 2 hours.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Place the beef and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the beets, onion, and carrot until softened, about 8 minutes; stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Add the cabbage, potatoes, beet mixture, salt, pepper, and bay leaf to the broth.
Simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 25 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and stir in the dill.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion until golden.
Stir the onion, farmer cheese, and black pepper into the mashed potatoes; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the egg and warm water, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and firmly pinch the edges closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes; drain.
Fry the pierogi in vegetable oil until lightly golden, and serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft, about 8 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Add the broth and return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes.
Stir a little hot cooking liquid into the sour cream, then stir the mixture into the pot without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to package directions and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the beets and tomato paste; cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper; simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the kidney beans and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the dill and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Separate the cabbage leaves and trim away thick ribs; reserve any torn leaves and chop them.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Cool slightly.
Mix the pork, rice, onion, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling near the base of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Scatter the chopped cabbage and bacon in the bottom of a large pot.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in layers in the pot.
Mix the tomato paste, tomato juice, and water; pour over the rolls.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked, about 2 hours.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Add the onions and cook until deeply golden, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, caraway seeds, and tomato paste.
Return the beef to the pot and pour in the broth.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Whisk the flour and cold water together, then stir into the goulash.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until thickened; stir in the parsley and serve with bread.

title: Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrots; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the beets and tomato paste; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and potatoes, bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, salt, pepper, and dill.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Mix the potatoes with the farmer cheese, onion, pepper, and salt; cool the filling.
Combine the flour and salt in a bowl; add the warm water, egg, and melted butter, then knead until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch rounds.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and firmly seal the edges.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes.
Drain and serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, about 6 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the stock and return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour, then stir in a ladleful of hot cooking liquid.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot and warm gently without boiling.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions and serve with the chicken and sauce.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Rinse the cabbage leaves and trim away any thick ribs.
Cook the onion in the oil until soft, about 5 minutes; let cool slightly.
Mix the pork, beef, rice, onion, salt, pepper, thyme, and dill in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Scatter the bacon in the bottom of a large pot and arrange the rolls seam-side down.
Pour the tomato passata and chicken stock over the rolls.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked, about 2 hours.
Serve hot with some of the cooking liquid.

title: Czech Beef Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; set it aside.
Add the onions and cook until deeply golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, caraway, and garlic.
Return the beef to the pot and pour in the stock.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Mix the flour with the cold water until smooth, then stir it into the goulash.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Stir in the marjoram and serve with sliced bread dumplings.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook the onion in butter over medium heat until golden. Stir into the potatoes with the farmer cheese and pepper.
Mix the flour and salt. Add the egg, warm water, and sour cream; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain.
Fry the pierogi in vegetable oil until lightly browned, and serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides. Transfer to a plate.
Cook the onions in the pot until soft, about 8 minutes. Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Add the broth and stir until smooth. Return the chicken to the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F, about 35 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat. Stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then stir the mixture into the pot. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beets and tomato paste; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the beef broth and beef. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and cabbage. Simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Stir in the dill and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Mămăligă
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, until thick and pulling away from the sides, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the butter and remove from the heat.
Spoon into bowls and top with feta cheese and sour cream.

title: Russian Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Cook the egg noodles in salted boiling water according to the package directions; drain.
Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet and sear the beef in batches until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Cook the onion and mushrooms until softened and browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually add the beef broth and mustard, stirring until smooth.
Simmer until the sauce thickens, about 3 minutes. Return the beef and any juices to the skillet and warm through.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sour cream. Serve over the noodles with parsley.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or dry curd cottage cheese
2 tablespoons butter, for frying the onion
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Fry the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden. Stir it into the potatoes with the cheese and pepper; cool the filling.
Mix the flour and salt. Add the egg, warm water, and melted butter, then knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Boil the pierogi in batches until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Drain and serve with melted butter and sour cream.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches and set aside.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 8 minutes. Stir in the paprika, caraway, and garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste, then return the beef and its juices to the pot. Add the broth and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Add the carrots, potatoes, bell pepper, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 30 minutes.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the beets and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the dill and adjust the seasoning. Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head fermented cabbage, separated into leaves
instructions: Rinse the cabbage leaves if very salty, then trim away thick stems. Chop any small or torn leaves.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes; cool slightly.
Mix the onion and rice with the pork, paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Spread chopped cabbage scraps in a heavy pot. Arrange the rolls seam-side down, layering them with the bacon.
Mix the passata and water and pour over the rolls. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours, until the cabbage and rice are tender.

title: Russian Blini
ingredients: 2 tablespoons melted butter, plus more for the pan
2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill, for serving
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in a large bowl. Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth.
Cover the batter and let it rise in a warm place until bubbly, about 1 hour.
Whisk in the egg yolk, melted butter, and sour cream. Beat the egg white until soft peaks form, then gently fold it into the batter.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat. Cook small ladlefuls of batter until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes.
Flip and cook until golden on the other side, about 1 minute. Serve warm with smoked salmon and dill.

title: Polish Pierogi Ruskie
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 cup farmer cheese or dry-curd cottage cheese
1 teaspoon salt, plus more for the cooking water
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash.
Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden; stir it into the potatoes with the cheese, pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt.
Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Add the egg, warm water, and melted butter; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch rounds. Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the pierogi in batches in salted water until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes. Serve with sour cream.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches; set it aside.
Add the onions and cook until softened. Stir in the paprika, caraway, and garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste, bell pepper, and tomatoes, then return the beef to the pot.
Add the stock, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered until the beef and potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beets, tomato paste, and vinegar; cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage, salt, pepper, and sugar. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and dill. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve with sour cream.

title: Romanian Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Let it cool slightly.
Combine the pork, beef, rice, onion, salt, pepper, and thyme in a bowl.
Trim thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Line a heavy pot with any torn cabbage leaves and half the bacon. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in the pot and add the remaining bacon.
Mix the tomato paste, tomato juice, and water; pour over the rolls. Cover and simmer gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the rice and meat are cooked.

title: Russian Blini
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, for the pan
instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and let stand for 5 minutes.
Whisk the all-purpose flour, buckwheat flour, and salt in a large bowl. Add the egg yolks, milk mixture, and melted butter; whisk until smooth.
Cover the batter and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat. Cook small ladles of batter until bubbles appear, then flip and cook until golden. Serve with sour cream and smoked salmon.

title: Bryndzové halušky (Potato dumplings with sheep cheese)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more as needed
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely into a bowl and stir in the salt.
Mix in the flour until you have a thick, sticky dough.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press small pieces of dough through a halušky maker or coarse grater into the water.
Cook the dumplings until they rise to the surface, then simmer for 2 more minutes. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Stir the bryndza and sour cream together, loosening with a spoonful of cooking water if needed.
Toss the hot dumplings with the cheese mixture.
Fry the bacon until crisp and spoon it and its fat over the dumplings. Sprinkle with chives and serve.

title: Kapustnica (Sauerkraut soup)
ingredients: 1 pound sauerkraut, drained and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the sausage and smoked pork and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the sauerkraut, mushrooms, bay leaves, caraway, paprika, and pepper.
Pour in the stock and add the prunes. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves and taste, adding salt if needed.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Segedínsky guláš (Pork and sauerkraut stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the lard in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches. Transfer the pork to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, scraping up browned bits.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika and caraway.
Return the pork to the pot and add the sauerkraut and stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 75 to 90 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Whisk the sour cream and flour together, then stir into the stew. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with bread or dumplings.

title: Lokše (Potato flatbreads)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
4 tablespoons melted butter or duck fat
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain and cool completely.
Peel and finely grate the potatoes into a large bowl.
Mix in the salt and flour a little at a time to form a soft dough that is not sticky.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a thin circle on a well-floured surface.
Cook each flatbread in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side, until browned in spots.
Brush the hot lokše with melted butter or duck fat and stack under a clean towel to keep warm.

title: Šúľance s makom (Potato dumplings with poppy seeds)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain, cool, and peel.
Finely grate the potatoes into a bowl and mix with the flour, egg, and salt.
Knead briefly to make a soft dough, adding a little flour if it is sticky.
Roll portions of dough into ropes about 1/2 inch thick, then cut into 2-inch pieces and roll each piece into a small dumpling.
Cook the dumplings in batches in gently boiling salted water. Remove them with a slotted spoon when they float, then drain.
Melt the butter and toss it with the dumplings.
Mix the ground poppy seeds with the powdered sugar and sprinkle generously over the dumplings before serving.

title: Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head sour cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves; chop any small or torn leaves.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the rice and paprika, then remove from the heat and cool.
Combine the pork, beef, onion mixture, thyme, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Line a heavy pot with chopped cabbage and bacon. Arrange the rolls snugly in the pot, then tuck in the bay leaf.
Pour in the tomatoes and water or stock. Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the rice and meat are cooked.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Smântână (Polenta with Cheese and Sour Cream)
ingredients: 1 cup crumbled Romanian telemea or feta
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Whisk in the cornmeal gradually so no lumps form.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes, until thick and tender.
Stir in the butter and spoon the polenta into bowls.
Top with crumbled cheese and sour cream.

title: Ciorbă de Perișoare (Sour Meatball Soup)
ingredients: 1/2 cup sauerkraut brine or lemon juice, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped fresh lovage or dill
instructions: Mix the pork, rice, egg, salt, and pepper, then shape into small meatballs.
Heat the oil in a soup pot and cook the onion, carrot, celery, and bell pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and tomato puree and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and gently add the meatballs. Simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in sauerkraut brine or lemon juice to taste and simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve with parsley and lovage or dill.

title: Fasole cu Ciolan (White Beans with Smoked Ham Hock)
ingredients: 1 lb dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the beans and ham hock in a large pot and cover with the water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then add the bay leaves and simmer gently for about 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika.
Add the vegetables to the pot and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, until the beans are tender.
Remove the ham hock, discard the skin and bone, shred the meat, and return it to the pot.
Season with pepper, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Papanași (Romanian Cheese Doughnuts)
ingredients: 1 lb dry farmer cheese or well-drained ricotta
1 cup all-purpose flour, plus extra for shaping
instructions: Mix the cheese, eggs, sugar, vanilla, and lemon zest in a bowl.
Stir in the flour, baking powder, and salt just until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough into 8 portions. Shape each into a ring with a small hole, and make 8 small dough balls from the centers.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rings and dough balls in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Set a dough ball on each ring and serve with sour cream and sour cherry preserves.

title: Pierogi Ruskie (Potato and Farmer’s Cheese Dumplings)
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more for the filling
1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
8 ounces Polish twaróg or dry farmer’s cheese, crumbled
1 medium onion, thinly sliced, for serving
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain well.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet and cook the diced onion until soft and golden.
Mash the potatoes with the cheese, cooked onion, salt, and pepper; let the filling cool.
Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add the egg and warm water, then knead until smooth; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 3-inch rounds. Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Cook the pierogi in batches in gently boiling salted water until they float, then cook 2 minutes longer; lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the sliced onion in 2 tablespoons butter until golden and serve over the pierogi.

title: Bigos (Hunter’s Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound sauerkraut, drained and roughly chopped
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in boiling water for 20 minutes; strain and reserve the soaking liquid, then chop the mushrooms.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches; set it aside.
Add the kielbasa and onion to the pot and cook until the onion softens.
Stir in the sauerkraut, cabbage, mushrooms, prunes, and tomato paste.
Return the pork to the pot. Add the wine, reserved mushroom liquid, stock, bay leaves, allspice, caraway, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender and the flavors are well blended.
Serve hot; if time allows, cool and refrigerate overnight, then reheat gently the next day.

title: Gołąbki (Cabbage Rolls with Pork and Rice)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Remove the cabbage core and boil the whole cabbage, peeling off softened leaves as they loosen; drain and cool.
Cook the rice in salted water until just tender; drain and cool.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft; let it cool slightly.
Mix the rice, onion, pork, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick rib from each cabbage leaf. Put a portion of filling near the base, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Arrange the rolls seam-side down in a buttered baking dish. Pour over the passata and stock.
Cover and bake at 350°F (175°C) for about 1 hour, until the pork is cooked through and the cabbage is tender.

title: Żurek (Sour Rye Soup with Sausage and Egg)
instructions: Put the stock, kielbasa, onion, garlic, bay leaves, and allspice in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes, then remove and discard the onion, garlic, bay leaves, and allspice.
Stir in the rye sour starter and marjoram; simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour and a ladleful of hot soup until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.
Add the horseradish, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel, and halve them.
Serve the soup with kielbasa and a halved egg in each bowl.

title: Placki Ziemniaczane (Polish Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Drain off excess liquid, leaving the starch settled at the bottom; stir the starch back into the grated mixture.
Mix in the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter and flatten each portion into a thin pancake; fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and repeat, adding more oil as needed.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Borshch with Beef
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the beef and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, and simmer for about 1 hour, until tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, then add the beets and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the tomato paste, vinegar, sugar, and a splash of broth. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf to the beef pot; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and beet mixture. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the dill, and rest for 10 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

title: Varenyky with Potato and Onion
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 1/2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions until golden. Stir half into the potatoes with the butter, salt, and pepper.
Whisk the warm water, egg, and salt. Gradually mix in the flour to make a soft dough; knead for 5 minutes, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut into 3-inch rounds.
Put a spoonful of filling on each round, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Boil the varenyky in batches in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes after they float. Drain and serve with the remaining onions and sour cream.

title: Holubtsi (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Core the cabbage and simmer it, peeling off leaves as they soften. Drain and trim the thick ribs.
Cook the rice in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and carrot until soft. Cool slightly, then mix with the rice, pork, salt, pepper, and dill.
Place about 2 tablespoons of filling on each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Arrange the rolls seam-side down in a heavy pot. Mix the crushed tomatoes with the broth and pour over the rolls.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the cabbage is tender and the pork is cooked through.

title: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl. Drain off excess liquid, leaving the starch at the bottom.
Stir the potato mixture with the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon the mixture into the skillet and flatten each mound into a thin pancake.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Add more oil as needed.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Uzvar (Dried Fruit Compote)
instructions: Rinse the dried fruit under cool water.
Put the apples, pears, and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the prunes and raisins and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Remove from the heat and let the uzvar cool until warm.
Stir in the honey and chill or serve at room temperature.

title: Borscht
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the beet and tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth and potatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the cabbage is tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and dill. Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Pelmeni
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
instructions: Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Add the egg and water and knead until a firm, smooth dough forms. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the pork, beef, grated onion, black pepper, and 1 teaspoon salt.
Roll the dough thinly on a floured surface. Cut into 3-inch rounds.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the center of each round. Fold into a half-moon, pinch the edges closed, then bring the corners together and pinch.
Bring the water and boiling salt to a boil. Add the pelmeni in batches and stir gently.
Once they float, cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the filling is cooked through. Drain and serve with butter and sour cream.

title: Syrniki
ingredients: 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Mash the farmer cheese in a bowl. Mix in the egg, sugar, vanilla, salt, and flour until combined.
Dust your hands and work surface with flour. Shape the mixture into 8 small, thick patties and lightly coat them with flour.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the patties in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with sour cream.

title: Shchi
ingredients: 1 pound boneless beef chuck, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef, water, salt, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the beef, cut it into bite-size pieces, and return it to the pot.
Add the potatoes and cabbage. Simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the black pepper and dill. Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Buckwheat Kasha with Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 cup buckwheat groats, rinsed and drained
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the buckwheat, cover, and simmer over low heat until tender and the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir the cooked buckwheat into the mushrooms. Add the remaining butter and black pepper and warm through.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Draniki (Belarusian Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Stir in the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in the potato mixture and flatten each portion into a thin pancake.
Fry for 3–4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Machanka with Blini
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tbsp sunflower oil, for blini batter
instructions: Whisk together the blini flour, egg, milk, salt, and oil until smooth; rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet and cook thin blini, turning once, until golden; keep warm.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a saucepan and brown the pork on all sides.
Add the sausage and onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in 2 tablespoons flour, then gradually whisk in the stock.
Simmer for 30–40 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the sour cream, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Serve the machanka with the blini for dipping.

title: Kholodnik (Cold Beet Soup)
ingredients: 3 medium beets, cooked, peeled, and grated
instructions: Combine the beets, cucumber, radishes, dill, and green onions in a large bowl.
Pour in the kefir and cold water, then stir in the salt.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
Serve cold, topped with a halved hard-boiled egg.

title: Babka (Belarusian Baked Potato Pudding)
ingredients: 1 tbsp butter, for greasing the baking dish
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until browned; add the onion and cook until soft.
Finely grate the potatoes and drain off excess liquid.
Mix the potatoes with the bacon, onion, egg, sour cream, salt, and pepper.
Spread the mixture in the baking dish.
Bake for 60–75 minutes, until set and browned on top.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Kletski (Potato Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and finely grated
1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more as needed
1 tbsp salt, for the cooking water
instructions: Place the grated potatoes in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the potatoes with the egg, flour, and salt to make a soft dough.
Bring the water and 1 tablespoon salt to a gentle boil.
With damp hands, shape the dough into small dumplings.
Lower the dumplings into the water in batches and simmer for 8–10 minutes, until they rise and are cooked through.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and toss with melted butter and dill.

title: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikás csirke)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the lard in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, then add the chicken and turn to coat.
Add the salt, bell pepper, tomato, and water. Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream and flour together in a bowl. Stir in a ladleful of hot cooking liquid, then mix the cream into the pot.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling. Serve with nokedli or boiled potatoes.

title: Beef Goulash (Gulyásleves)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the lard in a large pot and cook the onions until soft and golden.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and caraway seeds.
Add the beef and salt, and stir until the meat is coated.
Return the pot to low heat and cook, stirring, until the beef releases its juices.
Add the broth, cover, and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots, potatoes, pepper, and tomato. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.

title: Cabbage Rolls (Töltött káposzta)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Carefully remove the cabbage leaves and blanch them until pliable, about 2 minutes; drain.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft. Let it cool slightly.
Mix the onion with the pork, rice, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Put a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Spread half the sauerkraut in a large pot. Arrange the rolls seam-side down on top, then cover with the remaining sauerkraut.
Pour in the water or broth. Cover and simmer gently until the rice and pork are cooked through, about 1 1/2 hours.
Serve the rolls with the sauerkraut and sour cream.

title: Hungarian Stuffed Peppers (Töltött paprika)
instructions: Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds and membranes.
Mix the pork, rice, onion, salt, and pepper. Loosely fill each pepper with the mixture.
Put the crushed tomatoes and water in a large pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stand the peppers in the pot, cover, and simmer gently until the filling is cooked and the peppers are tender, about 1 hour.
In a small saucepan, heat the oil and stir in the flour. Cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in a ladleful of tomato broth.
Stir the flour mixture and sugar into the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes and serve the peppers with their sauce.

title: Hungarian Plum Dumplings (Szilvás gombóc)
ingredients: 2 pounds starchy potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
12 small ripe plums, pitted and halved
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth; cool completely.
Mix the potatoes with the egg, flour, and salt to form a soft dough.
Mix the cinnamon and granulated sugar. Put one sugar cube inside each plum half and dust with a little cinnamon sugar.
On a floured surface, roll the dough about 1/2 inch thick and cut it into 12 squares. Wrap a plum in each square and seal the dough around it.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Cook the dumplings in batches until they rise to the surface, then cook for 3 more minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet and toast the breadcrumbs until golden. Roll the drained dumplings in the crumbs and serve warm.

title: Svíčková na smetaně (Beef with Creamy Root-Vegetable Sauce)
ingredients: 2 lb beef sirloin or chuck roast
1 small celery root, peeled and chopped
instructions: Season the beef with salt. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the bacon, onion, carrots, parsnip, and celery root to the pot. Cook until lightly browned.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the broth, bay leaves, peppercorns, and allspice. Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 2 to 3 hours.
Remove the beef and keep it warm. Discard the bay leaves and whole spices, then blend the vegetables and cooking liquid until smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the blended sauce and simmer until smooth and thickened.
Stir in the cream, vinegar, and sugar. Season with salt and adjust the sweet-sour balance to taste.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce, warm bread dumplings, lemon, and cranberry preserves.

title: Vepřo knedlo zelo (Roast Pork with Dumplings and Cabbage)
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Rub the pork with garlic, caraway, salt, and pepper.
Place the onion and water in a roasting pan. Set the pork on top, cover, and roast until tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Uncover for the final 30 minutes to brown.
For the dumplings, combine the warm milk and yeast. Stir in the flour, egg, and dumpling salt to make a soft dough. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Shape the dough into two logs. Simmer them in salted water, uncovered, for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once. Remove and slice.
Heat the lard in a large pan. Add the cabbage and sugar and cook until softened, about 15 minutes. Stir in the vinegar and season with salt.
Slice the pork and serve with the pan juices, cabbage, and dumplings.

title: Bramboračka (Czech Potato and Mushroom Soup)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the broth until smooth.
Add the potatoes, carrot, mushrooms, marjoram, caraway, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley, and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Čočka na kyselo (Lentils with a Tangy Onion Gravy)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups brown or green lentils, rinsed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the lentils, water, and bay leaf in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 25 to 35 minutes. Drain, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until golden. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the reserved lentil liquid. Simmer until the gravy thickens, then stir in the lentils.
Season with vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper, balancing the tang to taste.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the eggs to your liking. Serve the lentils topped with fried eggs.

title: Ovocné knedlíky (Czech Fruit Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 cup farmer cheese or dry curd cottage cheese
instructions: Mix the flour, cheese, egg, softened butter, and salt into a soft dough. If it is sticky, dust lightly with flour.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces. Flatten each piece, place a plum or apricot in the center, and seal the dough around the fruit.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings and simmer until they float, then cook for 3 more minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the 3 tablespoons of butter in a skillet. Add the breadcrumbs and toast until golden.
Lift out the dumplings and drain briefly. Serve with toasted breadcrumbs, powdered sugar, and sour cream.

title: Bryndzové halušky (Potato dumplings with sheep cheese)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more as needed
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and mix with the flour and salt to make a thick, sticky batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press small bits of batter through a halušky maker or colander into the water.
Cook the dumplings until they float, then simmer for 2 minutes and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Stir the bryndza and sour cream together, then toss with the hot dumplings.
Fry the bacon until crisp and spoon it and its drippings over the dumplings. Sprinkle with chives.

title: Kapustnica (Sauerkraut soup)
ingredients: 1 lb sauerkraut, drained and roughly chopped
1/2 oz dried porcini mushrooms, rinsed and soaked in 1 cup hot water
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the sausage and pork; cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the sauerkraut, caraway, paprika, bay leaves, and pepper.
Add the stock and the mushrooms with their soaking liquid. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves and serve the soup with sour cream.

title: Segedínsky guláš (Pork and sauerkraut stew)
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 lb sauerkraut, drained and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches; set it aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft, then remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika and caraway.
Return the pork to the pot and add the sauerkraut and stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the pork is tender.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour, stir it into the stew, and simmer for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Lokše (Potato griddle cakes)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain, cool, peel, and mash until smooth.
Mix the potatoes with the flour and salt to make a soft dough.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces and roll each piece thinly on a floured surface.
Cook each round in a dry hot skillet for about 1 minute per side, until brown spots appear.
Brush the warm lokše with melted butter and stack them under a clean towel to keep soft.

title: Šúľance s makom (Potato dumplings with poppy seeds)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain, cool, peel, and mash until smooth.
Mix the potatoes with the flour, egg, and salt to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough into long ropes about 1/2 inch thick and cut into 2-inch pieces; roll each piece into a small tapered dumpling.
Cook the dumplings in batches in boiling salted water until they float, then simmer for 1 minute and drain.
Toss with the melted butter. Mix the poppy seeds and sugar, sprinkle over the dumplings, and serve warm.

title: Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 large head sour cabbage, leaves separated
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Mix the pork, rice, onion, thyme, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves and place a spoonful of filling on each leaf.
Fold in the sides and roll each leaf snugly around the filling.
Line a heavy pot with any torn cabbage leaves and half the bacon.
Arrange the rolls in the pot, layering with the remaining bacon and bay leaves.
Pour in the passata and water, cover, and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the rice and cabbage are tender.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Smântână (Polenta with Cheese and Sour Cream)
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Whisk in the cornmeal gradually to prevent lumps.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the butter.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with telemea and sour cream.

title: Ciorbă de Perișoare (Sour Meatball Soup)
instructions: Mix the pork, rice, egg, half the onion, salt, and pepper, then shape into small meatballs.
Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a large pot.
Add the carrot, celery, bell pepper, and remaining onion; simmer for 10 minutes.
Lower the meatballs gently into the soup and simmer for 20 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the passata and borș, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then stir in the parsley before serving.

title: Fasole cu Ciolan (Beans with Smoked Ham Hock)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the beans, ham hock, bay leaves, and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the beans are nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Stir in the paprika and passata, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetable mixture and pepper to the bean pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the ham hock, pull the meat from the bone, and return the meat to the pot.

title: Papanași (Fried Cheese Doughnuts)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
1/2 cup sour cherry preserves, for serving
instructions: Mix the cheese, eggs, sugar, and vanilla in a bowl.
Stir in the flour, baking powder, and salt until a soft dough forms.
With floured hands, shape the dough into 8 rings and 8 small balls.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rings and balls in batches until golden brown, turning once; drain on paper towels.
Serve each ring topped with sour cream, sour cherry preserves, and a small dough ball.

title: Pierogi ruskie (potato and farmer’s cheese dumplings)
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain well.
Cook the diced onion in 2 tablespoons butter until soft and golden.
Mash the potatoes with the farmer’s cheese, cooked onion, pepper, and salt to taste; let the filling cool.
Mix the flour, warm water, egg, and salt into a soft dough. Knead briefly, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out circles about 3 inches wide.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Cook the pierogi in batches in gently boiling salted water until they float, then cook for 2 more minutes.
Drain and serve with melted butter and sour cream.

title: Bigos (hunter’s stew)
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Pour the boiling water over the dried mushrooms and soak for 20 minutes; reserve the soaking liquid and chop the mushrooms.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and brown the pork in batches. Set it aside.
Add the onion and sausage to the pot and cook until the onion softens.
Stir in the sauerkraut, cabbage, prunes, tomato paste, bay leaves, juniper, marjoram, and pepper.
Return the pork to the pot. Add the mushrooms, strained soaking liquid, wine, and stock.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until tender and richly flavored.
Remove the bay leaves and serve hot; the flavor improves after chilling and reheating.

title: Żurek (sour rye soup)
ingredients: 2 cups bottled żurek starter (sour rye starter)
instructions: Place the kielbasa, stock, onion, carrot, bay leaf, and allspice in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 25 minutes, then remove the onion, bay leaf, and allspice berries.
Stir in the żurek starter and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with a ladleful of hot soup, then stir it back into the pot.
Add the horseradish, marjoram, and pepper; taste and adjust the seasoning.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel, and halve them.
Serve the soup with an egg in each bowl and sprinkle with dill.

title: Gołąbki (cabbage rolls with pork and rice)
instructions: Cook the rice in salted water until just tender, then drain and cool.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Remove the cabbage core and loosen the leaves in the boiling water as they soften.
Cook the onion in butter until translucent, then let it cool.
Mix the pork, rice, onion, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick rib from each cabbage leaf. Place a portion of filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Arrange the rolls seam-side down in a covered baking dish.
Mix the passata and stock, pour over the rolls, and cover the dish.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the cabbage is tender and the filling is cooked through.
Serve with the tomato sauce and chopped dill.

title: Placki ziemniaczane (Polish potato pancakes)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Squeeze out and discard excess liquid, leaving any potato starch settled at the bottom; return the starch to the grated mixture.
Stir in the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in the mixture and flatten each portion into a thin pancake.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding oil as needed.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Borshch with Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Put pork and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a skillet. Cook beets with vinegar and sugar for 8 minutes.
Add onion and carrot to the skillet and cook until softened. Stir in tomato paste and a splash of broth.
Add potatoes to the pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in cabbage and the beet mixture. Add salt, pepper, and bay leaves; simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in garlic and dill. Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with sour cream.

title: Chicken Kyiv
instructions: Mix butter, parsley, garlic, and a pinch of salt. Shape into a small log, wrap, and chill until firm.
Pound each chicken breast between sheets of parchment until about 1/4 inch thick.
Cut the chilled butter into four pieces. Place one on each breast, fold in the sides, and roll tightly to enclose the butter.
Season the chicken with remaining salt and pepper. Coat each piece in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Chill for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 325°F (165°C). Fry the chicken, turning carefully, until golden, about 8 minutes.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake at 350°F (175°C) until cooked through, about 10 minutes. Rest briefly before serving.

title: Varenyky with Potato and Cheese
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
1 tbsp salt, for the cooking water
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Cook onion in butter until golden. Stir into the potatoes with farmer cheese and pepper; cool the filling.
Mix flour and salt in a bowl. Add egg and warm water, then knead until a smooth dough forms. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Place a spoonful of filling on each, fold over, and pinch the edges firmly closed.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook varenyky in batches, stirring gently, until they float; simmer for 2 more minutes.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve with sour cream.

title: Holubtsi (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Core the cabbage and simmer it in a large pot of boiling water. Remove softened leaves one by one and trim their thick ribs.
Cook rice in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook onion and carrot until softened. Cool slightly, then mix with rice, pork, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll snugly.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a covered baking dish. Mix tomato sauce with broth and pour over the rolls.
Cover and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the filling is cooked through. Serve with sour cream.

title: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion finely into a bowl.
Squeeze out excess liquid, then stir in the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon the mixture into the skillet and flatten each portion into a small pancake.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and deeply golden. Add more oil as needed between batches.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Borscht
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the beef and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet and cook the beets for 5 minutes.
Add the onion and carrot and cook until softened, then stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Add the potatoes and cabbage to the broth and simmer until nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the beet mixture, salt, and pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve with dill and sour cream.

title: Pelmeni
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
instructions: Mix the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg with the cold water, pour into the flour, and knead until a firm, smooth dough forms.
Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, pepper, and remaining salt in a separate bowl.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out rounds about 3 inches wide.
Place a teaspoon of filling in each round, fold over, and pinch the edges tightly; join the corners to form a dumpling.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add the pelmeni in batches.
Cook until they float, then simmer for 3 more minutes; drain and serve with butter and sour cream.

title: Buckwheat Kasha with Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 cup buckwheat groats, rinsed and drained
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Stir in the buckwheat, cover, and simmer over low heat until tender and the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet.
Cook the onion until soft, then add the mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Fold the mushrooms and onion into the buckwheat with the remaining butter and black pepper.
Cover and let stand for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Syrniki
ingredients: 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Mash the farmer cheese in a bowl until mostly smooth.
Mix in the egg, sugar, vanilla, flour, and salt.
Dust a work surface with flour and shape the mixture into a thick log.
Cut the log into 8 rounds and lightly coat each round with flour.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the syrniki in batches until golden on both sides and set in the center, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve warm with sour cream.

title: Shchi (Cabbage Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the beef and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion and carrot until softened.
Add the cabbage, potatoes, tomato, salt, pepper, and bay leaves to the broth.
Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the cooked onion and carrot and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves and serve with dill and sour cream.

title: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Drain off excess liquid, then stir in the egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in small portions and flatten into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Machanka with Pancakes
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tbsp sunflower oil, for pancakes, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the pancake flour, egg, milk, salt, and oil into a smooth batter; rest for 15 minutes.
Cook thin pancakes in a lightly oiled skillet, turning once; keep warm.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot and brown the pork shoulder on all sides.
Add the bacon, sausage, and onion; cook until the onion softens.
Sprinkle in 2 tablespoons flour and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 35–40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the sour cream, salt, and pepper; warm gently without boiling.
Serve the machanka with the pancakes.

title: Kolduny (Potato Dumplings with Meat)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion; drain off excess liquid.
Mix the grated mixture with the egg, flour, and half the salt.
Season the ground pork with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Place a spoonful of potato mixture in your palm, add a teaspoon of pork, and cover with more potato mixture; shape into an oval dumpling.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat and brown the dumplings on both sides.
Cover the skillet and cook for 15–20 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Serve with sour cream.

title: Babka (Baked Potato Casserole)
ingredients: 1 tbsp butter, for the baking dish
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a baking dish.
Fry the bacon in a skillet until crisp; add the onion and cook until soft.
Finely grate the potatoes and stir in the egg, milk, salt, pepper, bacon, and onion.
Spread the mixture in the prepared dish.
Bake for 60–70 minutes until set and golden on top.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with sour cream.

title: Kulesh (Millet and Pork Soup)
ingredients: 1/2 lb pork shoulder, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a soup pot over medium heat.
Brown the pork pieces for 5–7 minutes.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the stock, potatoes, millet, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 35–40 minutes until the pork and millet are tender.
Stir in the dill and serve hot.

title: Gulyásleves (Hungarian Goulash Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the lard in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef and cook, stirring, until its surface is no longer pink.
Take the pot off the heat; stir in the paprika, caraway, and salt.
Add the broth or water, return the pot to the heat, and simmer covered until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the carrots, potatoes, pepper, and tomato. Simmer until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 25 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then scatter with parsley and serve hot.

title: Csirkepaprikás (Chicken Paprikash)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
instructions: Season the chicken with salt.
Heat the lard in a wide pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer it to a plate.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft, then remove the pot from the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the broth and bell pepper, then return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 35 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour and a ladleful of hot cooking liquid until smooth.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot and warm gently without boiling. Serve with nokedli or egg noodles.

title: Lecsó (Pepper and Tomato Stew)
ingredients: 4 Hungarian wax peppers or mild yellow peppers, seeded and sliced
instructions: Heat the lard in a skillet or heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
If using sausage, add it and cook for 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, and salt. Cover and simmer gently until the peppers are tender and the tomatoes form a saucy stew, about 20 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with bread, or spoon over rice.

title: Töltött Káposzta (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 12 large sauerkraut leaves, rinsed and drained
instructions: Mix the pork, rice, onion, salt, pepper, and paprika in a bowl.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Place a portion of filling near the base of each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll it up.
Spread half the sauerkraut in a heavy pot and scatter over half the bacon.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot, then cover with the remaining sauerkraut and bacon.
Pour in the water or broth. Cover and simmer gently until the rice and filling are cooked, about 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Serve the rolls with sauerkraut and a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Nokedli (Hungarian Egg Dumplings)
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Whisk the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and water, then stir just until a sticky batter forms.
Working in batches, press the batter through a spaetzle maker or colander into the boiling water.
