Cook the dumplings until they rise to the surface, then simmer for 1 more minute.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and toss with butter. Serve alongside paprikash or stew.

title: Svíčková na smetaně (Marinated Beef with Creamy Root-Vegetable Sauce)
ingredients: 2 lb beef sirloin or top round, tied
1 small celery root, peeled and chopped
instructions: Season the beef with salt. Heat the lard in a heavy pot and brown the beef on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the bacon, carrots, parsnip, celery root, and onion to the pot. Cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the sugar and vinegar, then add the bay leaves, peppercorns, allspice, and broth.
Return the beef to the pot. Cover and simmer gently until tender, about 2 to 2½ hours, turning the meat occasionally.
Transfer the beef to a board and remove the whole spices. Blend the vegetables and cooking liquid until smooth.
Stir the cream into the sauce and simmer gently. If needed, knead the butter and flour together and whisk small pieces into the sauce to thicken; season with salt.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce, bread dumplings, cranberry sauce, and lemon slices.

title: Vepřo knedlo zelo (Roast Pork with Dumplings and Sauerkraut)
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Rub the pork with salt, pepper, caraway, and garlic.
Scatter the onion in a roasting pan, set the pork on top, and pour in the water.
Cover and roast for 2 hours, basting occasionally. Uncover and roast for 30 to 45 minutes more, until browned and tender.
Transfer the pork to a board and rest for 10 minutes. Strain or spoon off excess fat from the pan juices, then serve them alongside the sliced pork.
While the pork roasts, warm the lard in a saucepan. Add the sauerkraut and sugar, cover, and cook gently for 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir the flour with 2 tbsp cold water until smooth. Stir it into the sauerkraut and cook for 3 minutes, until lightly thickened.
Steam or briefly simmer the dumpling slices until hot. Serve with the pork and sauerkraut.

title: Bramboráky (Czech Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: ½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes into a bowl. Squeeze out and discard most of the liquid.
Mix in the eggs, flour, garlic, marjoram, salt, pepper, and milk to make a thick batter.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter and spread each portion into a thin pancake. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Kulajda (Creamy Dill, Mushroom, and Potato Soup)
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in the warm water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and strain the soaking liquid through a fine sieve.
Melt the butter in a large pot. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and strained mushroom liquid. Add the mushrooms, potatoes, bay leaf, and caraway.
Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Whisk a little hot soup into the cream, then stir the cream mixture into the pot. Simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Add the vinegar and dill; season with salt and pepper.
Poach the eggs separately until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft. Serve one egg in each bowl of soup.

title: Ovocné knedlíky (Czech Fruit Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
12 small plums, pitted, or 12 hulled strawberries
½ cup sour cream, for serving
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain, cool until easy to handle, then peel and rice or mash finely.
Mix the potatoes with the flour, egg, and salt just until a soft dough forms.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
On a floured surface, divide the dough into 12 pieces. Flatten each piece, wrap it around a plum or strawberry, and pinch the seams closed.
Lower the dumplings into the water in batches. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring gently once so they do not stick.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet. Add the breadcrumbs and toast until golden; stir in the sugar and cinnamon.
Lift out the dumplings and drain briefly. Roll them in the buttered crumbs and serve with sour cream.

title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelette)
ingredients: 6 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, then stir in the potatoes and onion.
Heat the reserved oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook until the edges are set, about 6 minutes, then invert the tortilla onto a plate.
Slide it back into the skillet and cook the other side for 3–4 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 small green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
50 grams day-old white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt to a blender.
Blend until smooth, adding the cold water as needed.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil and blend until creamy.
Strain if desired, then chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 800 grams waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-centimeter cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Toss the potatoes with 3 tablespoons olive oil and the salt, then roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and both paprikas.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, vinegar, and sugar.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Spoon the sauce over the roasted potatoes and serve hot.

title: Gambas al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)
ingredients: 500 grams large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with the salt.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and just cooked through.
Stir in the parsley and lemon juice, then serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: Warm the milk in a saucepan with the cinnamon stick and lemon zest until steaming; do not boil.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the milk steep for 10 minutes, then discard the cinnamon and zest.
Whisk the egg yolks, 100 grams sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Gradually whisk the warm milk into the yolk mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Divide the custard among 4 shallow dishes and chill for at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle each serving with the remaining sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch just before serving.

title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelet)
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, then stir in the warm potatoes and onion.
Heat the reserved oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the edges are set, then invert the tortilla onto a plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the skillet and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until set throughout.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 2 pounds ripe tomatoes, cored and chopped
1 small green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
2 slices stale white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess water.
Place the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, and water in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar as needed.
Chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 pound bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 pound green beans, trimmed and cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium-high heat.
Season the chicken and rabbit with salt and pepper, then brown them on all sides.
Add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the grated tomato and paprika and cook until the tomato thickens, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the warm stock and add the saffron; bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice and white beans, then arrange the rosemary on top.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes, then reduce the heat and cook for 8 to 10 minutes more without stirring, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the rosemary, rest the paella for 5 minutes, and serve.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the potatoes with 3 tablespoons olive oil and the salt, then spread them on a baking sheet.
Roast for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened, then stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and cayenne.
Add the crushed tomatoes, vinegar, and sugar; simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Spoon the sauce over the hot potatoes and serve.

title: Gambas al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season them with the salt.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and chile and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until pink and just cooked through.
Pour in the sherry and simmer for 1 minute.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 700 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion, season with salt, and cook gently for 20–25 minutes until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tbsp of the oil.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, then stir in the warm potatoes and onion. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Heat the reserved oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the egg mixture and cook until the edges set.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side until just set.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 kg ripe tomatoes, cored and roughly chopped
1 medium cucumber, peeled and roughly chopped
1 small green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
50 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil.
Add cold water until the gazpacho reaches your preferred consistency.
Chill for at least 2 hours, then stir and serve cold.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
2 tbsp olive oil, for the sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes with 3 tbsp olive oil and salt.
Spread the potatoes on a baking tray and roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and cayenne.
Add the crushed tomatoes and sherry vinegar. Simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Spoon the sauce over the hot potatoes and serve.

title: Gambas al Ajillo
ingredients: 500 g raw large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and chile and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and just cooked through.
Stir in the parsley and lemon juice, then serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Crema Catalana
ingredients: 2 tbsp granulated sugar, for the topping
instructions: Warm the milk in a saucepan with the lemon peel, orange peel, and cinnamon stick until steaming. Remove from the heat and steep for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks, 150 g sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Strain the milk, then gradually whisk it into the egg mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Pour into 6 shallow ramekins and cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle each custard with the topping sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch just before serving.

title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelet)
ingredients: 700 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion, season with salt, and cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl, fold in the potato mixture, and let stand for 5 minutes.
Heat the reserved oil in the skillet, add the egg mixture, and cook over medium-low heat until the edges are set.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side until set.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 small green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
50 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
120 ml cold water, plus more as needed
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil.
Add cold water to reach your preferred consistency, then blend again.
Chill for at least 2 hours and serve cold.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
2 tablespoons olive oil, for the sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the potatoes with 3 tablespoons olive oil and salt, spread on the tray, and roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and tender.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and both paprikas for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes and vinegar, simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Arrange the potatoes on a serving plate and spoon over the brava sauce.
Serve with mayonnaise on the side or drizzled over the potatoes.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 800 g chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into pieces
200 g green beans, trimmed and cut into 4 cm lengths
150 g butter beans, cooked and drained
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Warm the stock in a saucepan and steep the saffron in it.
Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit on all sides, then move them to the edges of the pan.
Add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the grated tomatoes and paprika.
Cook until the tomato mixture thickens, then add the hot saffron stock, butter beans, and salt.
Bring to a boil, add the rice evenly across the pan, and stir once to distribute it.
Add the rosemary and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, then lower the heat and cook for 8–10 minutes more without stirring, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the paella for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Croquetas de Jamón (Spanish Ham Croquettes)
ingredients: 150 g finely diced Spanish serrano ham
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth, then cook for 8–10 minutes until very thick.
Stir in the ham, nutmeg, and salt, then spread the mixture in a shallow dish.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until firm.
Shape the chilled mixture into small cylinders, dip each in beaten egg, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the olive oil to 180°C in a deep pan and fry the croquettes in batches for 2–3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Tortilla Española

Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the garlic and chili and cook gently for 1–2 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Increase the heat to medium-high, add the shrimp, and cook for 1–2 minutes per side until pink and just cooked through.
Pour in the sherry and simmer for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with lemon wedges and crusty bread.

title: Fabada Asturiana
ingredients: 500 g dried large white beans, soaked overnight and drained
200 g cured pork belly, cut into large pieces
instructions: Put the beans, pork belly, chorizo, morcilla, onion, garlic, bay leaf, and paprika in a large heavy pot.
Add the cold water, ensuring the beans are covered by about 3 cm.
Bring slowly to a gentle simmer, skimming off any foam; do not let the pot boil hard.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 2½–3 hours, adding a little cold water if needed to keep the beans covered.
When the beans are tender, add the salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the onion, garlic, and bay leaf; slice the meats and sausages.
Serve the beans hot with the sliced meats and sausages.

title: Spanish Tortilla (Tortilla de Patatas)
ingredients: 6 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon olive oil, for the pan
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl, then stir in the potatoes and onion. Rest for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook for 5–7 minutes, until the edges are set. Cover the skillet with a plate, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide it back into the skillet.
Cook for 3–5 minutes more, until set, then rest briefly before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 small green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
50 grams stale white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it gently.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, and cold water until smooth.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve for a smoother texture, if desired.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Stir well and serve cold.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 500 grams chicken thighs, cut into pieces
150 grams flat green beans, trimmed and cut into pieces
100 grams butter beans, cooked and drained
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken and rabbit and brown them on all sides.
Stir in the green beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the grated tomatoes and cook until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, saffron, and salt, then add the warm stock and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, add the rice, and spread it evenly across the pan. Add the butter beans.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes, then reduce the heat and cook for 8–10 minutes more without stirring, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the rosemary, cover loosely, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 800 grams waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-centimeter cubes
instructions: For the sauce, heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and both paprikas.
Add the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, vinegar, and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan to 175°C.
Fry the potatoes in batches for 6–8 minutes, until golden and tender. Drain on paper towels.
Spoon the warm sauce over the potatoes and serve.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick and lemon peel in a saucepan until steaming. Remove from the heat and steep for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks, 80 grams of sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel from the milk, then slowly whisk the warm milk into the egg mixture.
Pour the mixture back into the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Do not let it boil.
Divide the custard among 4 shallow dishes and chill for at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle each dish with 1 tablespoon of sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch until crisp and golden.
Let the sugar topping harden for a few minutes before serving.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 700 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion; cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, then stir in the warm potatoes and onion.
Heat the reserved oil in the skillet and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook over low heat until the edges are set, about 6–8 minutes.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook the other side for 3–4 minutes.
Rest briefly, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 small cucumber, peeled and roughly chopped
1 small green bell pepper, seeded and roughly chopped
50 g stale white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it gently.
Put the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt in a blender.
Blend until smooth, then gradually blend in the olive oil.
Add cold water until the gazpacho reaches your preferred consistency.
Strain if desired, cover, and chill for at least 2 hours.
Stir well and serve cold.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 400 g bomba or other short-grain rice
700 g chicken thighs, cut into pieces
200 g flat green beans, trimmed and cut into lengths
100 g garrofó or large lima beans, cooked
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit on all sides, then push them toward the edges.
Add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and cook until reduced, about 5 minutes.
Add the paprika, saffron, and salt; stir briefly.
Pour in the warm stock and add the garrofó and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then scatter the rice evenly across the pan.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes, then reduce the heat and cook for another 8–10 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and the stock is absorbed.
Remove from the heat, cover loosely, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tablespoon olive oil, for the sauce
instructions: Simmer the potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden and crisp, about 6–8 minutes; drain on paper towels.
For the sauce, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes; add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in both paprikas and the tomato paste, then add the crushed tomatoes, vinegar, and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth if desired.
Serve the potatoes hot with the sauce spooned over them.

title: Croquetas de Jamón
ingredients: 100 g finely chopped Spanish cured ham
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth.
Cook, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture is very thick.
Stir in the ham, nutmeg, and salt.
Spread the mixture in a shallow dish, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until firm.
Shape the mixture into small cylinders.
Dip each croquette in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat the frying oil to 180°C and fry the croquettes in batches until golden, about 2–3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Cocido Madrileño
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and put them in a large pot with the beef, ham bone, and chicken.
Cover with cold water, bring to a gentle simmer, and skim the foam.
Add the chorizo, morcilla, and chickpeas; simmer gently for about 2 hours, adding water as needed.
Add the carrots and potatoes and cook until tender, about 30 minutes.
Cook the cabbage separately in some of the broth until tender.
Strain broth for soup, bring it to a boil, add the noodles, and cook until tender.
Serve the noodle soup first, followed by the chickpeas, vegetables, and meats.

title: Callos a la Madrileña
ingredients: 2 lb beef tripe, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Put the tripe and beef foot in a pot, cover with water, bring to a boil, and drain.
Return them to the pot with fresh water and the bay leaf; simmer until tender, about 2½ hours.
Warm the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in the paprika and jamón, then add the mixture to the pot.
Add the chorizo and morcilla and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season to taste and serve hot with bread.

title: Tortilla de Patatas
ingredients: 1½ lb potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently until soft but not browned, about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt and fold in the potatoes and onion.
Heat 1 tablespoon reserved oil in a nonstick skillet and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook until the edges set, then invert onto a plate and slide back into the skillet.
Cook the other side until just set, then rest briefly before serving.

title: Huevos Rotos con Patatas
ingredients: 1½ lb potatoes, peeled and cut into thick fries
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet and fry the potatoes in batches until golden and tender.
Drain the potatoes and season with salt.
Fry the eggs in a little of the same oil until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny.
Arrange the potatoes on a platter and lay the jamón over them.
Top with the eggs and break the yolks just before serving.

title: Sopa de Ajo
ingredients: 6 oz day-old rustic bread, thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and gently cook the garlic until fragrant.
Add the jamón and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the paprika, then add the bread and toss to coat.
Pour in the broth, bring to a simmer, and cook for 15 minutes.
Season to taste and crack the eggs into the soup.
Cover and simmer until the egg whites are set, about 4 minutes.

title: Sopa de ajo (Castilian garlic soup)
ingredients: 4 ounces day-old country bread, thinly sliced
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook gently until golden, not browned.
Stir in the paprika, then add the bread and turn it to coat.
Pour in the broth, season with salt, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Crack the eggs into the soup and simmer until the whites set, about 3 minutes.
Serve hot, with one egg in each bowl.

title: Judiones de La Granja
ingredients: 1 pound dried judión or large butter beans
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Put the beans in a pot and cover with fresh cold water by 2 inches.
Add the onion and bay leaf, bring slowly to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer gently for 1 hour, skimming as needed; add a splash of cold water if the beans boil hard.
Add the chorizo, morcilla, and pancetta, and simmer until the beans are tender, about 1 hour more.
Warm the olive oil in a small pan, stir in the paprika, and mix this into the beans.
Season with salt and let the stew rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Cochinillo asado (roast suckling pig)
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and set a rack inside a roasting pan.
Rub the pig with the lard and salt, then place it skin-side down on the rack.
Pour the water into the pan, keeping it below the rack.
Roast for 1 hour 30 minutes, basting occasionally with the pan juices.
Turn the pig skin-side up and roast until the skin is crisp and deeply golden, about 45 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carve and serve.

title: Tortilla de patatas
ingredients: 1½ pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion, season with salt, and cook gently until soft, about 20 minutes; do not brown them.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl, then fold in the warm potatoes and onion; rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the reserved oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and add the egg mixture.
Cook until the edges set, then invert onto a plate and slide the tortilla back into the pan.
Cook the other side until set but still tender inside, about 3 minutes, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Bacalao a la tranca
ingredients: 1½ pounds salt cod, soaked and desalted
instructions: Pat the desalted cod dry and cut it into serving pieces.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the cod skin-side down and cook gently for 4 minutes; turn and cook until just flaky, about 3 minutes more.
Transfer the cod to a warm serving plate.
Add the garlic to the skillet and cook until lightly golden.
Remove the skillet from the heat, stir in the paprika and vinegar, and spoon the sauce over the fish.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately.

title: Fabada Asturiana
ingredients: 1 pound dried fabes (large white beans), soaked overnight
4 ounces lacón (cured pork shoulder), soaked overnight if very salty
1 small onion, peeled and left whole
instructions: Drain the beans and put them in a heavy pot with the onion, lacón, salt pork, and enough cold water to cover by about 2 inches.
Bring slowly to a boil, skim the surface, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer.
Add the chorizo, morcilla, and paprika; simmer gently for about 2½ to 3 hours, adding a little cold water if the beans become exposed.
Shake the pot occasionally instead of stirring so the beans stay whole.
When the beans are tender and the broth is rich, taste and add salt only if needed; rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Pote Asturiano
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight
1 pound collard greens (berza), stems removed and leaves chopped
1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the beans and place them in a large pot with the salt pork and lacón; cover generously with cold water.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the chopped greens, potatoes, chorizo, morcilla, and paprika.
Simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, until the beans and potatoes are tender and the broth is thick.
Taste for salt, let the pot rest briefly, and serve hot.

title: Cachopo Asturiano
ingredients: 2 large veal cutlets, about 6 ounces each, pounded thin
4 slices mild melting cheese, such as Havarti or young Manchego
instructions: Lay one veal cutlet flat and cover it with the ham and cheese, leaving a small border around the edges.
Top with the second cutlet and press the edges firmly together; season both sides with salt and pepper.
Coat the stuffed cutlets in flour, dip them in beaten egg, then cover completely with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat; fry the cachopo for about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels, cut in half, and serve hot.

title: Chorizo a la Sidra
ingredients: 4 Asturian chorizo links, about 1 pound total
instructions: Prick each chorizo several times with a fork and place them in a small saucepan.
Pour in the cider and add the bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, turning the chorizo once.
Slice the chorizo and serve warm with some of the cider cooking liquid.

title: Arroz con Leche Asturiano
ingredients: 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, for the top
instructions: Put the rice, water, and salt in a heavy saucepan and simmer until the water is nearly absorbed.
Add the milk, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel; cook over very low heat, stirring frequently, for 1½ to 2 hours, until creamy.
Stir in the sugar and butter and cook for 10 minutes more; add the anise liqueur if using.
Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon peel, then spoon the rice pudding into a serving dish.
Sprinkle the top with sugar and caramelize it with a kitchen torch, or serve without caramelizing.

title: Salmorejo cordobés
ingredients: 1 kg ripe tomatoes, cored and roughly chopped
200 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool, peel, and chop them.
Blend the tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
Add the bread and blend until thick and creamy.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil.
Chill for at least 1 hour, then serve topped with chopped egg and jamón.

title: Gazpacho andaluz
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water until softened, then squeeze it gently.
Blend the tomatoes, pepper, cucumber, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
Pour in the olive oil while blending.
Add cold water until the gazpacho reaches your preferred consistency.
Chill for at least 2 hours and stir before serving.

title: Espinacas con garbanzos
instructions: Toast the bread in 1 tablespoon of olive oil until golden, then set aside.
Fry the garlic in the remaining oil until lightly golden.
Blend the toasted bread, garlic, cumin, paprika, vinegar, and a splash of water into a paste.
Wilt the spinach in a pot over medium heat, adding a little water if needed.
Stir in the chickpeas, bread paste, remaining water, and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring gently, and serve warm.

title: Patatas a lo pobre
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes, pepper, onion, garlic, and salt.
Cover and cook gently for 25–30 minutes, turning carefully now and then, until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the lid and cook for a few minutes if you prefer the edges lightly golden.
Drain off excess oil and serve hot.

title: Tortillitas de camarones
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, all-purpose flour, water, and salt into a thin batter.
Stir in the shrimp, onion, and parsley.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Drop in small spoonfuls of batter and spread each into a thin round.
Fry in batches until crisp and golden on both sides, then drain on paper towels.

title: Pa amb tomàquet
instructions: Toast the bread lightly, if desired.
Rub each slice with the cut garlic, if using.
Rub the cut side of a tomato over each slice until the bread is juicy and coated.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt.

title: Escalivada
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place the peppers, eggplant, and onion on a baking tray and roast, turning once, until soft and charred, about 40–50 minutes.
Cover the vegetables with a clean towel and let them cool until easy to handle.
Peel the peppers and eggplant; peel the onion. Remove the pepper seeds and tear all the vegetables into strips.
Arrange on a plate, season with salt, and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Trinxat de la Cerdanya
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small green cabbage, cored and sliced
instructions: Put the potatoes and cabbage in a large pot, cover with water, and add the salt.
Bring to a boil and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes; drain well.
Mash the potatoes and cabbage together until roughly combined.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the pancetta until browned; add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mashed vegetables and pepper to the skillet. Press into a thick cake and cook until browned underneath, about 5 minutes.
Turn the mixture in sections and cook until browned in places, then serve hot.

title: Fricandó de vedella amb bolets
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in the warm water for 20 minutes; strain and reserve the soaking liquid, keeping any grit behind.
Season the beef with salt and pepper, then lightly coat each slice in flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until soft, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Add the stock, reserved mushroom liquid, bay leaf, and mushrooms.
Return the beef to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until tender, about 1 hour.
Crush the almonds and toasted bread with the parsley and 2 tablespoons of the cooking liquid to make a paste.
Stir the paste into the pot and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

title: Crema catalana
instructions: Warm the milk with the cinnamon stick and lemon zest in a saucepan until steaming; remove from the heat and steep for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks, 1/2 cup sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Strain the warm milk and gradually whisk it into the egg mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Divide among four shallow ramekins and chill until set, at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle 1 teaspoon sugar over each ramekin and caramelize with a kitchen torch just before serving.

title: Bacalao al pil-pil
ingredients: 1 lb salted cod, soaked in cold water for 36–48 hours, changing the water several times
2 dried guindilla chiles, or 1 small dried red chile
instructions: Drain the cod and pat it dry. Cut it into serving pieces and remove any remaining bones.
Warm the oil in a wide skillet over low heat. Add the garlic and chile and cook until the garlic is pale gold; remove them with a slotted spoon.
Place the cod skin-side down in the oil and cook gently for about 8 minutes, turning once, until just tender. Transfer it to a plate.
Let the oil cool until warm, then swirl the skillet steadily to emulsify the oil and the cod’s released juices into a glossy sauce.
Return the cod to the skillet and warm gently in the sauce. Top with the garlic, chile, and parsley.

title: Marmitako
ingredients: 1½ lb fresh albacore tuna, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and peppers and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf. Pour in the fish stock and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth has thickened slightly.
Season the tuna with salt and pepper, add it to the pot, and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes, until just cooked. Serve hot.

title: Piperrada
ingredients: 3 ripe tomatoes, peeled, seeded, and chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and peppers and cook, stirring occasionally, until very soft, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the mixture is thick and jammy.
Make four shallow wells in the vegetables and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft, about 5 minutes.
Serve with toasted bread.

title: Alubias de Tolosa
ingredients: 1 lb dried black beans from Tolosa, picked over
1 small yellow onion, peeled and left whole
1 small green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
instructions: Rinse the beans and place them in a pot with the cold water, 1 tablespoon oil, and the whole onion. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer gently, uncovered, for about 2½ hours, adding a little cold water if needed to keep the beans just covered. Do not stir; gently shake the pot instead.
Add the salt and pork ribs and simmer for 30 minutes, until the beans and meat are tender.
Add the morcilla and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove the onion and discard it.
Meanwhile, boil the cabbage in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes. Drain it. Warm the remaining oil in a skillet, cook the garlic until pale gold, and toss with the cabbage.
Serve the beans with the ribs, morcilla, and cabbage.

title: Gâteau Basque with cherry preserves
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add 1 egg and the vanilla, then mix just until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough into two portions, one slightly larger than the other. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Press the larger dough portion over the bottom and up the sides of a buttered 9-inch tart pan.
Spread the cherry preserves over the dough, leaving a narrow border. Roll out the remaining dough and lay it over the filling; press the edges together to seal.
Beat the remaining egg with the water and brush it over the top. Score a light crosshatch pattern with a fork.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until deep golden. Cool completely before slicing.

title: Galician-Style Octopus (Pulpo á Feira)
ingredients: 1 whole octopus, about 3 pounds, cleaned and thawed if frozen
instructions: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil.
Dip the octopus into the boiling water three times, then lower it into the pot.
Simmer gently until tender, about 45 to 60 minutes; check the thickest part with a knife.
Add the potatoes during the last 20 to 25 minutes and cook until tender.
Drain the octopus and potatoes, then slice the octopus and cut the potatoes into thick rounds.
Arrange on a platter, sprinkle with salt and both paprikas, and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Galician-Style White Bean and Greens Soup (Caldo Gallego)
ingredients: 1 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 bunch turnip greens, tough stems removed and leaves chopped
1 small onion, peeled and left whole
instructions: Put the beans, water, ham hock, and onion in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently until the beans are nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the greens and cook until soft, about 10 minutes.
Remove the ham hock and onion; shred any meat from the hock and return it to the pot.
Stir in the olive oil, season with salt, and serve hot.

title: Galician-Style Empanada with Tuna and Peppers
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
2 cans tuna in olive oil, 5 ounces each, drained
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, and yeast in a bowl; stir in the warm water and ¼ cup olive oil.
Knead until smooth, cover, and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions and peppers over medium-low heat until very soft, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, tuna, and chopped eggs; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Divide the dough into two pieces and roll each into a rectangle.
Place one rectangle on a baking sheet, spread the filling over it, and leave a border around the edges.
Cover with the second rectangle, seal the edges, and cut a small vent in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 35 to 40 minutes.

title: Galician Clams with White Wine (Almejas a la Marinera)
ingredients: 2 pounds small clams, scrubbed and purged
½ cup water or fish stock
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide, lidded pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 6 minutes; stir in the garlic and paprika.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and water or stock, stirring until the sauce is smooth; simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the clams, cover, and cook until they open, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Discard any clams that remain closed, stir in the parsley, and serve with bread.

title: Galician Almond Cake (Tarta de Santiago)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, for greasing the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Whisk the eggs and granulated sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in the ground almonds, lemon zest, and cinnamon.
Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake until golden and a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool completely, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 200 g flat green beans, trimmed and cut into pieces
150 g garrofó beans, fresh or thawed
instructions: Season the chicken and rabbit with salt. Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan and brown the meat well.
Add the green beans and garrofó; cook for a few minutes. Stir in the grated tomato and cook until it thickens.
Add the paprika and saffron, then pour in the water. Simmer for about 30 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt. Add the rice, spreading it evenly across the pan.
Cook over high heat for 8 minutes, then lower the heat and cook for about 10 minutes more without stirring.
Add the rosemary for the final few minutes. Rest the paella for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Arròs al Forn (Oven-Baked Rice)
ingredients: 250 g pork ribs, cut into pieces
800 ml meat or chicken stock, hot
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Warm the olive oil in an ovenproof casserole and brown the pork ribs with a pinch of salt.
Stir in the paprika and rice, then add the chickpeas and hot stock.
Arrange the potato and tomato slices on top and set the whole garlic head in the center.
Bake for about 25 minutes, until the rice has absorbed the stock and is tender.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Fideuà
ingredients: 400 g firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan. Brown the noodles, stirring, until golden; transfer them to a plate.
Cook the squid in the same pan for a few minutes. Add the garlic and grated tomato and cook until thickened.
Stir in the paprika, then pour in the hot fish stock and add the noodles. Season with salt.
Simmer until the noodles are nearly tender and most of the stock has been absorbed.
Add the fish and prawns and cook until just done and the noodles are dry, about 5 minutes.
Rest briefly and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Esgarraet
ingredients: 150 g salted cod, soaked and flaked
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C. Roast the peppers, turning occasionally, until charred and soft.
Cover the peppers in a bowl and let them steam until cool enough to handle.
Peel and seed the peppers, then tear the flesh into strips and place it in a serving dish.
Add the flaked cod, garlic, and olives.
Pour over the olive oil and let the salad stand for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Bunyols de Carabassa (Pumpkin Fritters)
ingredients: 500 g peeled pumpkin, cut into chunks
instructions: Steam or boil the pumpkin until very tender, then drain it well and mash until smooth.
Dissolve the yeast and tablespoon of sugar in the warm water. Let it stand for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt into the pumpkin, then stir in the yeast mixture to make a thick, sticky batter.
Cover and leave the batter in a warm place for about 1 hour, until risen and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep pan. Drop small portions of batter into the oil and fry, turning once, until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels and roll in the serving sugar while warm.

title: Cocido Madrileño
instructions: Soak the chickpeas in plenty of water overnight, then drain.
Put the beef, chicken, ham bone, and chickpeas in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to a gentle simmer, skimming the surface.
Simmer for 2 hours, adding water as needed to keep the ingredients covered.
Add the carrots, potato, chorizo, and morcilla. Simmer for 30 minutes, then add the cabbage and cook until tender.
Strain some broth into a separate pot, season it, and cook the noodles in it until tender.
Serve the noodle soup first, followed by the chickpeas, vegetables, and meats.

title: Callos a la Madrileña
ingredients: 2 lb beef tripe, cleaned and cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Place the tripe and ham bone in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Drain and rinse.
Return the tripe and ham bone to the pot with fresh water and the bay leaf. Simmer until the tripe is tender, about 2 hours.
Warm the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Add the garlic and paprika, then stir in the crushed tomatoes.
Add the tomato mixture, chorizo, and morcilla to the tripe. Simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with bread.

title: Huevos Rotos con Patatas
ingredients: 4 large potatoes, peeled and cut into thick fries
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Fry the potatoes in batches until tender and golden. Drain and season with salt.
Arrange the potatoes on a serving plate and scatter the jamón over them.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Set the eggs over the potatoes and ham, then break the yolks just before serving.

title: Sopa de Ajo Madrileña
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pot and gently fry the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the bread and stir until it absorbs the oil and begins to toast.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, and pour in the chicken broth.
Simmer for 15 minutes, breaking up the bread slightly, and season with salt.
Crack the eggs into the soup and simmer until the whites set and the yolks remain soft.

title: Bocadillo de Calamares
ingredients: 1 lb squid, cleaned and cut into rings
instructions: Pat the squid rings dry and season them with salt.
Put the flour in a bowl and toss the squid in it until lightly coated. Shake off excess flour.
Heat the olive oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry the squid in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until crisp and lightly golden. Drain on paper towels.
Split the baguette rolls and fill them generously with the fried squid. Serve immediately.

title: Sopa Castellana (Castilian Garlic Soup)
ingredients: 4 ounces day-old country bread, cut into small cubes
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the garlic until lightly golden.
Add the bread and stir until it absorbs the oil and begins to toast.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, then pour in the stock and add salt.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Crack the eggs into the soup and simmer until the whites set and the yolks are still soft, about 3 minutes.

title: Judiones de La Granja (White Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound dried large white beans, soaked overnight
8 ounces Spanish chorizo, cut into thick slices
8 ounces morcilla, cut into thick slices
4 ounces salt pork or pancetta, diced
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a pot with the water, onion, and bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the beans are nearly tender, about 1½ hours.
In a skillet, warm the olive oil and cook the salt pork until lightly browned.
Stir in the paprika, then add the mixture, chorizo, and morcilla to the beans.
Simmer gently until the beans are tender and the broth is rich, 30 to 45 minutes; season with salt.

title: Cochinillo Asado (Roast Suckling Pig)
ingredients: 1 suckling pig, about 8 pounds, split lengthwise
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and set a rack inside a large roasting pan.
Rub the pig all over with the lard and salt, then place it skin-side down on the rack.
Pour the water into the pan and roast for 1 hour, adding a little water if the pan dries out.
Turn the pig skin-side up and roast until the meat is tender and the skin is crisp, about 1½ hours.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Lechazo Asado (Castilian Roast Lamb)
ingredients: 1 bone-in leg of milk-fed lamb, about 5 pounds
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and place the lamb in a roasting dish, skin-side down.
Rub the lamb with the salt and pour the water into the dish.
Roast for 1 hour, basting occasionally with the pan juices.
Turn the lamb skin-side up and roast until browned and tender, about 45 minutes more.
Rest for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the pan juices.

title: Tortilla de Patatas (Spanish Potato Omelet)
ingredients: 1½ pounds waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a deep skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook gently, stirring occasionally, until soft but not browned, about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl, then fold in the warm potatoes and onion.
Heat the reserved oil in a nonstick skillet, add the mixture, and cook until the underside is set.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate, slide it back into the skillet, and cook until set through, about 3 minutes.

title: Fabada Asturiana
ingredients: 500 g dried Asturian fabes or other large white beans, soaked overnight
150 g salt-cured pork belly or panceta
1 small onion, peeled and left whole
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a large pot with the onion and enough fresh cold water to cover by about 5 cm.
Bring to a gentle boil, skim the surface, then add the chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, paprika, and olive oil.
Simmer very gently, uncovered, for about 2½ to 3 hours, adding a little cold water if needed to keep the beans covered.
Avoid stirring; instead, gently shake the pot now and then so the beans stay whole.
When the beans are tender, taste the broth and add salt only if needed. Rest for 15 minutes, then serve with pieces of the meats.

title: Pote Asturiano
ingredients: 250 g dried white beans, soaked overnight
300 g chopped collard greens or Asturian berza
300 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
150 g salt-cured pork belly, cut into pieces
instructions: Drain the beans and add them to a large pot with the pork belly and enough cold water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the chorizo, morcilla, greens, potatoes, and paprika.
Simmer for another 45 to 60 minutes, until the beans and potatoes are tender and the broth has thickened.
Taste, adjust the salt, and let the pot stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Merluza a la Sidra
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cider and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring to make a smooth sauce.
Season the hake lightly and nestle it into the sauce. Cover and cook gently for 5 minutes.
Add the clams, cover again, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the hake is just cooked and the clams have opened.
Discard any clams that remain closed, scatter with parsley, and serve with the sauce.

title: Cachopo Asturiano
ingredients: 2 large thin veal steaks, about 180 g each
2 slices semi-cured cheese, such as Manchego or local Asturian cheese
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Lay one veal steak flat and top it with the ham and cheese, leaving a small border around the edges.
Place the second steak on top and press the edges together; season both sides with salt and pepper.
Coat the stuffed steak in flour, dip it in beaten egg, then cover it completely with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan to about 170°C.
Fry the cachopo for 4 to 5 minutes per side, turning carefully, until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on a rack or paper towels, then cut into portions and serve hot.

title: Arroz con Leche Asturiano
ingredients: 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, for the top
instructions: Put the milk, lemon peel, cinnamon stick, and salt in a heavy saucepan and bring just to a simmer.
Stir in the rice and cook over very low heat for about 1½ hours, stirring frequently so it does not catch.
Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon stick, then stir in the sugar and butter.
Cook for 10 to 15 minutes more, stirring, until creamy; add a splash of milk if it becomes too thick.
Spoon into a shallow dish, sprinkle the top with granulated sugar, and caramelize it with a kitchen torch before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
50 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
250 ml cold water, plus more as needed
instructions: Soak the bread in a little cold water until softened, then squeeze out the excess.
Blend the tomatoes, pepper, cucumber, garlic, bread, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
With the blender running, gradually pour in the olive oil.
Blend in cold water until the gazpacho is as thin as you like.
Chill for at least 2 hours and serve cold.

title: Salmorejo Cordobés
ingredients: 1 kg ripe tomatoes, cored and chopped
200 g day-old white bread, crusts removed
50 g finely chopped jamón serrano, for serving
instructions: Soak the bread in the chopped tomatoes for 10 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, bread, garlic, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
Pour in the olive oil gradually while blending until thick and creamy.
Chill for at least 1 hour.
Serve cold, topped with chopped egg and jamón.

title: Espinacas con Garbanzos
ingredients: 400 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and fry the bread and garlic until golden; transfer to a mortar.
Pound the bread and garlic with the cumin, paprika, and vinegar into a rough paste.
Add the chickpeas and water to the pan and stir in the paste.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the spinach and salt, then cook until the spinach has wilted and the chickpeas are tender, about 5 minutes.

title: Patatas a lo Pobre
ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Combine the potatoes, onion, peppers, oil, garlic, and salt in a wide frying pan.
Cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, turning gently every few minutes.
Uncover and cook for 5 to 10 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and lightly golden at the edges.
Remove the garlic and serve warm.

title: Tortillitas de Camarones
ingredients: 100 g small peeled shrimp, chopped if large
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, all-purpose flour, water, and salt into a thin batter.
Stir in the shrimp, onion, and parsley.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Drop tablespoons of batter into the hot oil and spread each into a thin round.
Fry for 1 to 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden, then drain on paper towels.

title: Pa amb tomàquet
instructions: Toast the bread until crisp at the edges.
If using, rub each slice lightly with the garlic.
Rub the cut side of a tomato over each slice, letting the pulp soak into the bread.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.

title: Escalivada
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place the peppers, eggplant, and onion on a baking tray and roast, turning once, until softened and charred, about 40–50 minutes.
Cover the vegetables with a clean towel and let them cool until easy to handle.
Peel the peppers and eggplant, remove the pepper seeds, and tear the vegetables into strips.
Arrange the vegetables on a platter, drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, and season with salt.

title: Esqueixada de bacallà
ingredients: 12 ounces salt cod, soaked in cold water for 24–36 hours with the water changed several times
instructions: Drain the soaked cod, remove any skin or bones, and pull it into bite-size flakes.
Combine the cod, tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, and olives in a serving bowl.
Dress with the olive oil and vinegar and toss gently.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Fricandó de vedella
ingredients: 2 pounds thinly sliced beef chuck or top round
1 ounce dried moixernons or dried chanterelles
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain and reserve the soaking liquid.
Season the beef with salt and pepper, dust it with flour, and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until soft, then stir in the garlic.
Pour in the wine and simmer for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot and add the stock, mushrooms, and ½ cup of the reserved mushroom liquid.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender, about 1½ hours, adding a little water if needed.
Stir in the parsley and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Crema catalana
ingredients: ½ cup granulated sugar, plus 4 teaspoons for the tops
instructions: Warm the milk with the lemon zest and cinnamon stick until steaming; remove from the heat and let it infuse for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks, ½ cup sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Remove the zest and cinnamon, then slowly whisk the warm milk into the yolk mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened; do not let it boil.
Divide the custard among four shallow dishes and cool, then refrigerate until set.
Sprinkle each dish with 1 teaspoon sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch just before serving.

title: Bacalao al pil-pil (Salt Cod in Garlic Oil)
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) salt cod, desalted and cut into 4 pieces
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the refrigerator for 24–36 hours, changing the water several times; drain and pat dry.
Warm the olive oil, garlic, and chile in a wide pan over low heat until the garlic is golden; remove the garlic and chile.
Add the cod skin-side up and cook gently for about 5 minutes, without letting the oil sizzle hard.
Turn the cod skin-side down and cook until just opaque and tender, about 5 minutes more; transfer to a plate.
Let the oil cool until warm, then whisk it in the pan in small circles until it thickens into a glossy sauce.
Return the cod to the pan and spoon the pil-pil sauce over it; serve with the reserved garlic and chile.

title: Marmitako (Basque Tuna and Potato Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) fresh tuna, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 lb (900 g) potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat; cook the onion and green pepper until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and stir to coat; pour in the fish stock and season with salt.
Simmer gently until the potatoes are tender and the broth is slightly thickened, about 20 minutes.
Add the tuna and simmer just until it turns opaque, 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Gilda Pintxos (Anchovy, Olive, and Pepper Skewers)
instructions: Thread one olive, one folded guindilla pepper, and one anchovy onto each small skewer.
Arrange the skewers on a plate and drizzle with the olive oil.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Piperrada (Basque Pepper and Tomato Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the onion and peppers and cook, stirring occasionally, until very soft, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt; simmer until thick and saucy, about 15 minutes.
Make four shallow wells in the vegetables and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft, about 5–7 minutes.

title: Txangurro a la Donostiarra (Donostia-Style Stuffed Spider Crab)
ingredients: 1 cooked spider crab, about 2 lb (900 g), meat picked and shell reserved
1 small leek, white part only, finely chopped
1 small ripe tomato, peeled and finely chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat; cook the onion and leek until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the tomato and salt and cook until the mixture is thick, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the crab meat and brandy; simmer for 2 minutes, then remove from the heat and mix in the parsley.
Spoon the mixture into the cleaned crab shell and sprinkle with breadcrumbs; dot with butter.
Broil until the top is golden and bubbling, about 3–5 minutes; serve hot.

title: Galician Octopus (Pulpo á Feira)
ingredients: 1 whole octopus, about 3 pounds, cleaned and frozen, then thawed
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil without adding salt.
Dip the octopus into the boiling water three times, lifting it out between dips, then lower it into the pot.
Simmer gently for 35 to 45 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the thickest part of a tentacle.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender; drain and peel.
Rest the octopus in its cooking water for 10 minutes, then cut the tentacles into bite-size pieces.
Slice the potatoes onto a platter and arrange the octopus on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and coarse salt; serve warm.

title: Galician-Style Clams (Almejas a la Gallega)
ingredients: 2 pounds small clams, scrubbed and soaked in cold salted water for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and paprika, stirring for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and water and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the drained clams, cover, and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until they open.
Discard any clams that remain closed, stir in the parsley, and serve with bread.

title: Galician Caldo (Caldo Galego)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound turnip greens or collard greens, washed and chopped
1 ounce salted pork fat or panceta, diced
1 teaspoon fine salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the beans, pork hock, pork fat, and water in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the beans are nearly tender.
Remove the pork hock, cut the meat from the bone, and return the meat to the pot.
Add the potatoes and greens and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until tender.
Season with salt to taste and let the caldo rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Galician Empanada with Tuna (Empanada de Atún)
ingredients: 2 cans tuna in olive oil, 5 ounces each, drained
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl; add 1/4 cup olive oil and the yeast mixture, then knead until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise for 1 hour.
Heat the remaining 1/4 cup olive oil in a pan and cook the onions and pepper over low heat until soft, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, tuna, and chopped eggs; cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into a rectangle.
Place one rectangle on a baking sheet, spread the filling over it, and cover with the other rectangle; seal the edges and cut a small vent in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden.

title: Galician Almond Cake (Tarta de Santiago)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, for the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 9-inch round cake pan.
Whisk the eggs and granulated sugar until pale and slightly thickened.
Fold in the ground almonds, lemon zest, and cinnamon until evenly mixed.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool the cake completely, then dust with confectioners' sugar before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 200 g flat green beans, trimmed and cut into lengths
150 g garrofó beans, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan and salt the meat lightly.
Brown the rabbit and chicken well on all sides.
Add the green beans and garrofó; cook for a few minutes.
Stir in the grated tomato and cook until its liquid evaporates.
Add the paprika and saffron, then pour in the water and add salt.
Simmer for about 30 minutes, adding the rosemary for the final 10 minutes.
Add the rice and spread it evenly; do not stir again.
Cook over a steady heat for about 16–18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Arroz al Horno
ingredients: 300 g pork ribs, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Warm the olive oil in an ovenproof casserole and brown the pork ribs and sausage.
Add the paprika and rice; stir briefly to coat the grains.
Add the chickpeas and broth, then season with salt.
Arrange the potato and tomato slices over the rice and place the garlic head in the center.
Bake for about 20 minutes, until the rice has absorbed the broth and the top is browned.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Fideuà
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a paella pan and briefly brown the prawns; remove them.
Cook the squid in the same pan until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and grated tomato; cook until thickened.
Stir in the paprika and saffron, then add the noodles and toast them for 1 minute.
Pour in the hot fish stock and season with salt.
Add the fish and prawns, spreading them over the noodles.
Simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, until the noodles are tender and most of the stock is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Esgarraet
ingredients: 200 g salt cod, desalted and flaked
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Roast the peppers, turning occasionally, until blistered and soft, about 30–40 minutes.
Cover the peppers and let them cool, then peel and remove the seeds.
Tear the pepper flesh into strips and place it in a serving dish.
Add the flaked cod, garlic, olives, and olive oil.
Let the salad stand for at least 20 minutes before serving with bread.

title: All i Pebre de Anguila
ingredients: 1 kg eel, cleaned and cut into pieces
700 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Fry the bread, almonds, garlic, and ñoras in the olive oil until lightly golden; remove them.
Crush the fried ingredients with the paprika and a pinch of salt to make a paste.
Add the potatoes and water to the pan and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the paste and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the eel and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the potatoes and eel are cooked.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve hot.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and salt; cook, stirring often, for 35–45 minutes until deeply caramelized.
Stir in the sugar and flour; cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in the stock, bay leaf, and thyme; simmer for 25 minutes, then remove the herbs.
Toast the baguette slices until crisp.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top with bread and Gruyère, and broil until the cheese is bubbling and golden.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic and bell pepper; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the zucchini, tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Brown the chicken in batches, then transfer it to the plate.
Add the butter, onion, and carrots; cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock; stir in the tomato paste, bay leaf, and thyme.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot; cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme stems; sprinkle with parsley before serving.

title: Beef Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, adding olive oil as needed; transfer it to the plate.
Add the chopped onion and carrots; cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot; sprinkle with flour and stir to coat.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook in a 325°F (165°C) oven for 2 hours.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms; cover and cook for 45 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Discard the bay leaf and thyme stems; sprinkle with parsley before serving.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish and chill it for 15 minutes.
Line the crust with parchment and pie weights; bake for 15 minutes, then remove the weights and parchment.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain it on paper towels.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the crust, then pour in the egg mixture.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the center is just set and the top is golden.
Let the quiche rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the eggplant until lightly browned, about 6 minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add the zucchini and cook until lightly browned, about 4 minutes; transfer to the plate.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the basil and serve warm.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the sugar and flour; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Add the stock and thyme; simmer for 25 minutes.
Heat the broiler and toast the baguette slices until crisp.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls and top each with baguette and Gruyère.
Broil until the cheese is melted and browned, about 3 minutes.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 4 pounds, cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat until crisp; transfer to a plate.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then dust with flour.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the olive oil, onion, and carrots; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, then add the thyme and bacon.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer uncovered until tender, about 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate and chill while preparing the filling.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the crust.
Pour the egg mixture into the crust.
Bake until the center is just set and the top is golden, 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Crêpes Suzette
ingredients: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus 2 tablespoons for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar, and salt until smooth.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat and pour in enough batter to coat the bottom thinly.
Cook each crêpe until lightly golden, about 1 minute per side; repeat with the remaining batter.
Mix the softened butter, sugar, and orange zest in a bowl.
Melt the orange butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Stir in the orange juice and lemon juice; simmer for 2 minutes.
Fold each crêpe into quarters and place it in the sauce, turning to coat.
Pour in the orange liqueur and simmer briefly before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; remove and set aside.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat, working in batches; set aside.
Add the carrots, pearl onions, and garlic; cook for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up browned bits; add the bouquet garni.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter, then stir them into the pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni, adjust the seasoning, and serve.

Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain it on a paper towel.
Melt the butter in the skillet and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Scatter the bacon, onion, and Gruyère in the crust; pour the egg mixture over them.
Bake until the filling is just set and golden, about 30 to 35 minutes; rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and salt; cook, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the sugar and flour; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Add the stock and pepper; simmer for 25 minutes.
Toast the baguette slices until crisp.
Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls, top with toast and Gruyère, and broil until the cheese is bubbling.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes; add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the eggplant and remaining oil; cook until lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the zucchini and bell peppers; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the vegetables are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Coq au Vin
