instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat, working in batches, then set aside.
Add the olive oil, onion, and carrots; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook uncovered for 15 minutes, until tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Beef Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, then set it aside.
Add the olive oil, chopped onion, and carrots; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot, cover, and bake for 2 hours.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms; cover and bake for 1 hour more, until the beef is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Crêpes Suzette
ingredients: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus 2 tablespoons for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar, and salt until smooth.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered nonstick skillet over medium heat; add a thin layer of batter and swirl to coat.
Cook each crêpe until lightly golden on both sides; stack and keep warm.
Mix the softened butter with the sugar and orange zest.
Melt the orange butter in a large skillet over medium heat; stir in the orange juice and lemon juice.
Fold each crêpe into quarters and place it in the sauce; turn to coat and warm through.
Pour in the orange liqueur and carefully ignite, if desired; serve once the flames subside.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes and let them sit for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot and brown the eggplant; transfer to a plate.
Add 1 tablespoon oil and cook the zucchini until lightly browned; transfer to the plate.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion and bell peppers until softened.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Line the pie crust with parchment and pie weights; bake for 12 minutes, then remove the weights.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the crust.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper; pour into the crust.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the filling is set and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat, working in batches; set aside.
Add the olive oil, onion, and carrots; cook until softened, then stir in the garlic.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions, salt, and sugar; cook, stirring often, for 35–45 minutes until deeply caramelized.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits from the pot.
Add the beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf; simmer for 25 minutes, then remove the bay leaf.
Heat the broiler and toast the baguette slices until golden.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top with baguette and Gruyère, and broil until bubbling and browned.

title: Crêpes Suzette
ingredients: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar, and salt until smooth.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Lightly butter a skillet and heat it over medium heat.
Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirl to coat the pan, and cook until the edges lift; flip and cook briefly.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the crêpes.
Melt the 1/2 cup butter with the 1/2 cup sugar in a large skillet.
Stir in the orange juice and zest and simmer for 2 minutes.
Fold each crêpe into quarters, add to the sauce, and warm for 1 minute per side.
Stir in the Grand Marnier and serve immediately.

title: French Onion Soup
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and sugar; cook, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine and scrape up any browned bits from the pot.
Stir in the stock, thyme, and bay leaf; simmer for 25 minutes, then remove the bay leaf and season to taste.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top with toasted baguette and Gruyère, and broil until the cheese is bubbling and golden.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Brown the chicken in batches in the bacon fat and olive oil; set aside.
Add the onion and carrots and cook until softened; stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, then stir in the tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaf.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, sauté the mushrooms in the butter until browned; stir them into the pot for the last 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Toss the eggplant with half the salt and let it stand for 20 minutes; pat dry.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large pot and brown the eggplant in batches; set aside.
Add the remaining oil, onion, and bell peppers; cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, remaining salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant to the pot and simmer gently until all the vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch tart pan and prick the base with a fork.
Line the crust with parchment and pie weights; bake for 15 minutes, then remove the weights and parchment.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the crust, then pour in the egg mixture.
Bake until the filling is set and golden, about 30 minutes; rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Crêpes Suzette
ingredients: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
2 tablespoons Grand Marnier or other orange liqueur
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar, and salt until smooth; rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Lightly butter a skillet and heat over medium heat.
Pour in a small ladleful of batter, swirling to form a thin crêpe; cook until lightly golden on both sides.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the crêpes on a plate.
Melt the 1/2 cup butter with the 1/2 cup sugar in a large skillet over medium heat.
Stir in the orange juice and zest; simmer until slightly syrupy.
Fold each crêpe into quarters, add to the sauce, and turn to coat.
Pour in the orange liqueur and warm briefly; serve immediately.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and salt; cook, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 40 minutes.
Stir in the sugar and flour; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and scrape up any browned bits.
Pour in the beef stock, add the pepper, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Toast the baguette slices until crisp.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top with baguette and Gruyère, and broil until bubbly and golden.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Brown the chicken in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the butter, onion, and carrots; cook until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Sauté the mushrooms in a separate pan until browned, then stir them into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, discard the bay leaf, and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds; transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Add another tablespoon of oil and cook the eggplant until lightly browned; transfer to the bowl.
Add the remaining oil and cook the zucchini until lightly browned.
Return the onion mixture and eggplant to the pot; add the tomatoes, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Beef Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 pounds boneless beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, adding olive oil as needed; set aside.
Cook the chopped onion and carrots until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot, cover, and cook in a 325°F (165°C) oven for 2 hours.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms; cook uncovered for 45 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the seasoning, and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Line the pie crust with parchment and pie weights; blind-bake for 15 minutes, then remove the weights.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the crust.
Pour the egg mixture into the crust.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the filling is just set and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Galettes de blé noir (Buckwheat Crêpes)
ingredients: 2 cups cold water, plus more as needed
1 tablespoon salted butter, for the pan
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour and salt in a bowl.
Gradually whisk in the cold water until smooth, then whisk in 1 egg.
Cover and rest the batter in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Thin the batter with a little water if needed; it should pour easily.
Heat a crêpe pan over medium-high heat and rub it with a little butter.
Pour in a ladleful of batter and quickly tilt the pan to make a thin galette.
Cook until the edges lift, then turn the galette.
Add ham, cheese, and an egg; fold the edges inward and cook until the cheese melts and the egg is set.

title: Kouign-Amann
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salted butter, for the pan
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, yeast, and lukewarm water into a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes, cover, and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Roll the cold butter between sheets of parchment into a square and chill until firm.
Roll the dough into a square, place the butter in the center, and fold the dough over it to enclose.
Roll into a rectangle, sprinkle with one-third of the sugar, and fold into thirds.
Turn the dough a quarter-turn, roll it out again, and repeat the sugaring and folding twice more.
Chill the folded dough for 30 minutes, then roll it into a thick square and tuck the corners underneath.
Place in a buttered cake pan and let rise for 30 minutes.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 35–40 minutes, until deeply golden and caramelized; turn out while warm.

title: Far Breton aux pruneaux
ingredients: 2 tablespoons salted butter, melted, plus more for the dish
instructions: Soak the prunes in the rum for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a baking dish.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, and salt until combined.
Whisk in the flour, then gradually whisk in the milk and melted butter until smooth.
Scatter the prunes in the dish and pour the batter over them.
Bake for 50–60 minutes, until puffed and golden with a set center.
Cool before slicing; the far will settle as it cools.

title: Cotriade Bretonne
ingredients: 2 leeks, white and light-green parts sliced
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound firm white fish, cut into large pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and leeks and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, stock, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the mussels and shrimp, cover, and cook until the mussels open and the shrimp are pink, about 4–5 minutes; discard unopened mussels.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the parsley.
Serve hot with toasted bread.

title: Saucisses de Molène aux algues
ingredients: 1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with salted water, and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes; drain.
Prick the sausages lightly and simmer them in water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the sausages and brown them on all sides.
Pour in the wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the cream, dulse, and pepper; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Serve the sausages and seaweed cream with the boiled potatoes.

title: Poulet Vallée d’Auge
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3½ pounds, cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy pot; brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer to a plate.
Add the shallots, apples, and mushrooms; cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the cider and Calvados, if using, and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 35–40 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the crème fraîche and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes; adjust the seasoning and serve.

title: Moules à la Normande
instructions: Discard any mussels that are cracked or remain open when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the shallots for 3 minutes.
Add the cider and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover, and cook for 5–7 minutes, shaking the pot once, until they open.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the crème fraîche, parsley, and pepper.
Discard any mussels that stayed closed, then serve with the cooking broth.

title: Tripes à la Mode de Caen
ingredients: 3 pounds cleaned beef tripe, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 calf’s foot, split, or 1 tablespoon powdered gelatin
2 leeks, white and pale green parts sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C).
Layer the tripe, calf’s foot, carrots, onions, leeks, and garlic in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Add the cider, stock, bouquet garni, salt, and pepper; the liquid should nearly cover the ingredients.
Cover tightly and cook in the oven for 8 hours, until the tripe is very tender.
Remove the bouquet garni and calf’s foot; skim excess fat and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes or crusty bread.

title: Tarte Normande aux Pommes
ingredients: 3 medium firm apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Arrange the apple slices in the pastry shell.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, crème fraîche, Calvados, vanilla, and flour until smooth.
Pour the filling over the apples.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until the filling is set and golden.
Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.

title: Teurgoule (Norman Cinnamon Rice Pudding)
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Rinse the rice and drain it well.
Stir the rice, milk, sugar, cinnamon, and salt together in a deep ovenproof dish.
Bake uncovered for 3½–4 hours, until the top is deeply browned and the rice is very tender.
Cool slightly before serving warm, or chill and serve cold.

title: Choucroute Garnie
instructions: Warm the duck fat in a large heavy pot and soften the onion over medium heat.
Add the sauerkraut, Riesling, stock, bay leaf, and juniper berries; stir together.
Nestle in the smoked pork loin, cover, and simmer gently for 1½ hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 25 minutes.
Add the smoked sausages and frankfurters for the final 10 minutes, then serve everything hot.

title: Tarte Flambée (Flammekueche)
ingredients: 5 ounces smoked bacon, cut into small lardons
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat the oven and a baking stone or heavy baking sheet to 500°F.
Mix the flour and salt; add the water and oil and knead until smooth.
Roll the dough very thin and place it on parchment.
Stir together the crème fraîche and fromage blanc, then spread it over the dough.
Scatter on the onion and bacon and season with pepper.
Bake until the edges are crisp and browned, about 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Baeckeoffe
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 bottle dry Alsatian white wine, such as Riesling
2 pounds waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Combine the beef, lamb, pork, wine, half the onions, garlic, parsley, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F and layer half the potatoes in a heavy covered casserole.
Add the marinated meat and its liquid, then cover with the remaining onions and potatoes.
Cover tightly and bake until the meat is very tender, about 3 hours.

title: Kugelhopf
instructions: Soak the raisins in the kirsch or warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk with a spoonful of the sugar; let stand until foamy.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, eggs, yeast mixture, and salt until a soft dough forms.
Beat in the softened butter a little at a time, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the raisins, cover, and let rise until doubled, about 1½ hours.
Butter a kugelhopf mold and place an almond in each groove; fill the mold with the dough.
Let rise until the dough reaches near the rim, then bake at 350°F until golden and cooked through, about 40 minutes.
Cool briefly, turn out of the mold, and dust with confectioners’ sugar.

title: Tarte aux Quetsches
ingredients: ½ cup unsalted butter, cold and diced
2 pounds Italian prune plums, halved and pitted
2 tablespoons granulated sugar, for the fruit
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Rub the butter into the flour and sugar until crumbly; mix in the egg yolk and cold water to form a dough.
Roll out the dough and fit it into a 10-inch tart pan.
Arrange the plum halves upright in close rows over the pastry.
Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon and sprinkle it over the plums.
Bake until the pastry is golden and the fruit is tender, about 40 to 45 minutes.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
2 cups Burgundy or other dry red wine
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
In a Dutch oven, cook the bacon until browned; remove it and leave the fat in the pot.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat and oil, then set it aside.
Cook the chopped onion and carrots until softened; stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot. Add the wine, stock, garlic, and bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for about 2½ hours, until the beef is tender.
Sauté the mushrooms and pearl onions in butter until browned, then add them to the pot for the final 30 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni, adjust the seasoning, and serve.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 chicken, about 4 pounds, cut into 8 pieces
3 cups Burgundy or other dry red wine
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; remove it and reserve the fat.
Brown the chicken in batches in the bacon fat and butter, then set it aside.
Cook the onion and carrot until softened. Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot. Add the wine, stock, and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked through.
Sauté the mushrooms and pearl onions in a little butter; add them to the pot for the final 20 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni, scatter with parsley, and serve.

title: Jambon Persillé
ingredients: 2 pounds cooked ham, cut into small cubes
1 pound unsalted cooked pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
instructions: Put the onion, carrot, celery, and bouquet garni in a saucepan with 3 cups water; simmer for 30 minutes, then strain.
Measure 2 cups of the broth and stir in the gelatin until dissolved.
Mix the ham and pork with the parsley, garlic, vinegar, and pepper.
Stir the broth mixture and white wine into the meat.
Pack the mixture firmly into a loaf pan or terrine and pour in enough liquid to cover.
Cover and refrigerate overnight until set.
Slice cold and serve with mustard or cornichons.

title: Gougères
ingredients: 7 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1½ cups grated Gruyère or Comté cheese
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Bring the water, butter, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Take the pan off the heat, add the flour all at once, and stir until a smooth dough forms.
Return the pan to low heat and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the dough pulls away from the sides.
Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Stir in the cheese, pepper, and nutmeg.
Drop tablespoonfuls of dough onto the baking sheet, leaving space between them.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden; serve warm.

title: Œufs en Meurette
ingredients: 2 cups Burgundy or other dry red wine
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Cook the bacon in a saucepan until crisp; remove it and reserve the fat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook until softened. Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, add the bouquet garni, and simmer until reduced by about one-third.
Strain the sauce, return it to the pan, and whisk in the butter; season to taste.
Bring a skillet of water and the vinegar to a gentle simmer. Crack in the eggs and poach for 3 to 4 minutes.
Place a poached egg on each slice of toast and spoon over the warm sauce.
Scatter the reserved bacon on top and serve immediately.

title: Quenelles de brochet with Nantua sauce
ingredients: 150 g crayfish tails, cooked and peeled
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Arrange the quenelles in a buttered baking dish and bake for 20 minutes.
Melt the remaining butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the crème fraîche, crayfish, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the quenelles and bake for 10 minutes more, until bubbling.

title: Salade lyonnaise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Toast the bread and rub each slice with the cut garlic clove.
Fry the lardons in a skillet until crisp; reserve the warm fat.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, olive oil, and 1 tablespoon of the warm lardon fat; season with pepper.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes.
Toss the frisée with the dressing and divide among plates.
Top with lardons and poached eggs, and serve with the garlic toast.

title: Tablier de sapeur
ingredients: 600 g beef tripe, cooked and trimmed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Cut the tripe into four broad pieces.
Mix the wine and mustard, add the tripe, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Drain the tripe and season with salt and pepper.
Coat each piece in flour, dip in beaten egg, then cover with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the tripe for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Cervelle de canut
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Stir the fromage blanc and crème fraîche together until smooth.
Mix in the chives, parsley, shallot, vinegar, olive oil, and garlic.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving with bread or boiled potatoes.

title: Poulet au vinaigre
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 1.5 kg, cut into 8 pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy pan; brown the chicken on all sides, then set it aside.
Add the shallots and cook until softened.
Pour in the vinegar and simmer until reduced by about half.
Return the chicken to the pan and add the stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the crème fraîche and mustard, then simmer uncovered for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with rice or potatoes.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
2 cups Burgundy or other dry red wine
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven; remove and set aside.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat and oil, then set it aside.
Cook the onion and carrots until softened. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, scraping up browned bits, then stir in the stock, tomato paste, garlic, and bouquet garni.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot. Cover and simmer gently for about 2½ hours, until the beef is tender.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter and stir them into the stew for the last 15 minutes. Remove the bouquet garni and adjust the seasoning.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3½ lb, cut into 8 pieces
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven; remove and set aside.
Brown the chicken pieces in the bacon fat and oil, working in batches. Set aside.
Cook the chopped onion and carrots until softened. Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up the browned bits. Add the bouquet garni, bacon, and chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms in butter, then add them to the pot for the last 15 minutes. Remove the bouquet garni and adjust the seasoning.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Prick the pastry shell with a fork and chill it for 15 minutes.
Line the shell with parchment and pie weights. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the weights, and bake for 5 minutes more.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until lightly crisp; drain it well.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, pepper, and salt.
Scatter the bacon in the pastry shell and pour in the egg mixture.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the filling is just set and lightly golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Rub a shallow baking dish with the cut sides of the garlic, then butter the dish.
Slice the potatoes thinly and evenly; do not rinse them.
Bring the milk, cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Layer the potatoes in the dish and pour the warm cream mixture over them.
Bake uncovered for 60–75 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden.
Let the gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: French Onion Soup
ingredients: 8 slices baguette, about ½ inch thick
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat.
Add the onions, sugar, and salt. Cook slowly, stirring often, for 40–50 minutes, until deeply golden and soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Add the wine and scrape the bottom of the pot.
Pour in the beef stock, add the bouquet garni, and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes. Season with pepper and remove the bouquet garni.
Heat the broiler. Toast the baguette slices until crisp.
Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, top each with baguette and Gruyère, and broil until the cheese is bubbling and browned.

title: Poulet au pot (Chicken and vegetables in broth)
ingredients: 2 onions, peeled, one studded with 2 cloves
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley stems, and bay leaf)
instructions: Put the chicken, water, carrots, leeks, turnips, onions, celery, bouquet garni, salt, and peppercorns in a large pot.
Bring just to a simmer, skimming the surface, then cover and cook gently for about 1½ hours, until the chicken is tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes, until tender.
Lift out the chicken and vegetables; strain the broth if desired.
Serve the broth first with toast, then serve the chicken and vegetables.

title: Garbure (Cabbage and bean soup)
ingredients: ½ green cabbage, cored and sliced
2 cups cooked white beans, such as Tarbais beans
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley stems, and bay leaf)
instructions: Warm the duck fat in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garlic and cabbage and cook until the cabbage begins to soften, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans, stock, duck leg, potato, bouquet garni, and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, partially covered, for about 1 hour.
Remove the bouquet garni and duck leg; pull the meat from the bone and return it to the soup.
Serve hot with country bread.

title: Confit de canard (Duck confit)
instructions: Rub the duck legs all over with the salt.
Place them in a dish with the garlic, thyme, bay leaves, and peppercorns; cover and refrigerate for 12 to 24 hours.
Wipe the salt and seasonings from the duck legs and pat them dry.
Arrange the legs snugly in a heavy ovenproof pot and pour in enough melted duck fat to cover them.
Cover and cook in a 275°F oven for about 3 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Serve warm, or cool the legs in the fat and refrigerate them for later.

title: Cassoulet toulousain
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley stems, and bay leaf)
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the soaked beans in a pot with the halved onion, carrot, bouquet garni, and stock.
Bring to a simmer and cook gently for about 1 hour, until the beans are nearly tender; remove the onion, carrot, and bouquet garni.
Heat the duck fat in a heavy ovenproof pot and brown the pork shoulder on all sides.
Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beans and their cooking liquid, then add the sausages and duck confit legs.
Scatter the breadcrumbs over the top and bake uncovered at 325°F for about 2 hours, breaking the crust and pushing it back into the beans a few times.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Tourin à l’ail (Garlic soup)
ingredients: 12 garlic cloves, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Melt the duck fat in a saucepan over low heat.
Add the onions and garlic and cook gently for 10 minutes without browning.
Pour in the stock, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar.
Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl, then slowly whisk in a ladleful of hot soup.
Take the pot off the heat and stir the egg mixture into the soup without boiling it.
Serve over toasted country bread.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Salt the eggplant lightly and leave it in a colander for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat half the olive oil in a large heavy pot and brown the eggplant in batches; set aside.
Add a little more oil and cook the zucchini until lightly browned; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion and peppers until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot and simmer gently, uncovered, for 35 to 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the basil, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Aïoli Provençal
instructions: Pound the garlic and salt to a smooth paste in a mortar.
Whisk in the egg yolks until combined.
Add the olive oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly until the mixture thickens.
Continue adding the oil in a thin stream while whisking.
Whisk in the lemon juice and warm water until smooth.
Cover and chill until serving; keep refrigerated and use within 1 day.

title: Soupe au Pistou
ingredients: 1 cup green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup cooked white beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, green beans, zucchini, water, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Stir in the white beans, pasta, and grated tomatoes; simmer until the pasta is cooked.
Pound the garlic and basil together, then mix in the Parmesan and extra-virgin olive oil to make the pistou.
Remove the soup from the heat and stir in the pistou just before serving.

title: Daube Provençale
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Combine the beef, wine, onion, carrots, garlic, orange zest, bay leaf, and thyme in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Remove the beef and vegetables from the marinade and pat the beef dry; reserve the marinade.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven and brown the beef in batches.
Add the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste.
Pour in the reserved marinade and add the salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer very gently for 3 hours, until the beef is tender.
Stir in the olives during the final 15 minutes and serve with polenta or potatoes.

title: Pissaladière
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat.
Add the onions, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; cook gently for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into a 10-by-14-inch rectangle and place it on the baking sheet.
Remove the bay leaf and spread the onions evenly over the dough.
Arrange the olives and anchovy fillets over the onions, then drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the crust is golden; serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Galettes de sarrasin (Buckwheat Crêpes)
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour and salt in a bowl.
Gradually whisk in the water, then beat in the egg until smooth.
Cover and rest the batter in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Heat a crêpe pan over medium-high heat and lightly grease it with butter.
Pour in a thin layer of batter and cook until the edges lift; flip briefly.
Add ham, grated cheese, and an egg to the center of each galette.
Fold the edges inward and cook until the cheese melts and the egg is set.

title: Kig ha farz
ingredients: 500 g beef chuck, cut into large pieces
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 small green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Put the beef, pork hock, carrots, leeks, cabbage, onions, cloves, and bouquet garni in a large pot.
Cover with water, bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 2½ hours.
Mix the buckwheat flour, wheat flour, and salt in a bowl.
Beat the egg with the milk and stir it into the flour to make a thick dough.
Wrap the dough securely in a clean cloth, leaving room for it to expand.
Lower the wrapped dough into the simmering broth and cook for 2 hours.
Mash the softened butter with the cold water to make beurre blanc-style sauce.
Unwrap and crumble the farz; serve it with the meats, vegetables, broth, and butter sauce.

title: Cotriade bretonne (Breton Fish Stew)
ingredients: 1 kg mixed firm white fish, cut into chunks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and leeks and cook until softened without browning.
Add the potatoes, fish stock, wine, and bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the fish and mussels, cover, and simmer gently until the fish is cooked and the mussels open, about 6 minutes.
Discard any mussels that remain closed.
Season with salt and pepper, scatter with parsley, and serve hot with the broth.

title: Far breton aux pruneaux (Prune Far)
ingredients: 40 g salted butter, melted, plus extra for the dish
instructions: Soak the prunes in the rum for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a deep baking dish.
Whisk the flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the eggs, then gradually add the milk until the batter is smooth.
Stir in the melted butter and vanilla.
Scatter the prunes in the baking dish and pour the batter over them.
Bake for 50–60 minutes, until deeply golden and just set in the center.
Cool before slicing.

title: Palets bretons (Breton Butter Biscuits)
instructions: Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and creamy.
Beat in the 3 egg yolks.
Whisk the flour and baking powder together, then mix them into the butter mixture to form a soft dough.
Shape the dough into a log, wrap it, and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 170°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Slice the dough into rounds about 1 cm thick and place them on the tray.
Brush the tops with beaten egg yolk.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, until golden, then cool on the tray.

title: Poulet Vallée d’Auge
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3½ lb, cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy casserole; brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the shallots and thyme to the casserole and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the Calvados and carefully ignite it, or let it bubble until reduced.
Add the cider and stock, return the chicken, cover, and simmer gently for 35 minutes.
Add the apples and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the apples are tender.
Stir in the crème fraîche and warm gently before serving.

title: Moules à la Normande
ingredients: 4 lb fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
instructions: Discard any mussels that are cracked or remain open when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the shallots until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the cider and pepper and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover, and cook for 5–7 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until they open.
Stir in the crème fraîche and parsley.
Discard any mussels that have not opened and serve at once with the cooking broth.

title: Tripes à la Mode de Caen
ingredients: 3 lb prepared beef tripe, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 beef foot, split by the butcher
instructions: Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C).
Put the tripe and beef foot in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Add the carrots, leeks, onion, garlic, cider, wine, stock, bouquet garni, salt, and pepper.
Bring the liquid just to a simmer on the stove, then cover the pot tightly.
Cook in the oven for 8 hours, until the tripe is very tender.
Remove the bouquet garni and beef foot; take any meat from the foot and return it to the pot.
Skim excess fat and serve hot.

title: Tarte Normande aux Pommes
ingredients: 3 firm apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Arrange the apple slices in the pastry shell.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until smooth, then whisk in the crème fraîche, Calvados, vanilla, and melted butter.
Pour the mixture over the apples.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until the filling is set and golden.
Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.

title: Teurgoule (Norman Rice Pudding)
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Rinse the rice and drain it well.
Stir the rice, sugar, cinnamon, and salt together in a deep ovenproof dish.
Pour in the milk and stir once.
Bake uncovered for 4–5 hours, until a deep brown skin forms and the pudding is thick and tender.
Let it cool slightly before serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Choucroute garnie
ingredients: 2 pounds sauerkraut, drained and rinsed briefly
1 pound smoked pork loin or kassler
instructions: Melt the fat in a large heavy pot and soften the onion over medium heat.
Stir in the sauerkraut, Riesling, stock, bay leaf, and juniper berries.
Nestle in the smoked pork, cover, and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
Add the sausages to the sauerkraut for the last 10 minutes, until heated through.
Serve the sauerkraut and meats with the potatoes.

title: Tarte flambée (Flammekueche)
ingredients: 5 ounces smoked bacon, cut into small lardons
instructions: Heat the oven to 500°F, or as hot as it will go, with a baking sheet or pizza stone inside.
Mix the flour and salt, then add the water and oil and knead until smooth.
Roll the dough very thin on parchment paper.
Mix the crème fraîche and fromage blanc, season with pepper, and spread over the dough.
Scatter the onion and bacon evenly over the top.
Slide the tart onto the hot baking surface and bake until the edges are crisp and browned, about 8 to 12 minutes.

title: Baeckeoffe
ingredients: 1 pound boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 bottle (750 ml) dry Alsatian white wine
2 pounds waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
1 cup all-purpose flour, for sealing the lid
instructions: Combine the meats, wine, onions, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and refrigerate the meat mixture for at least 8 hours, or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F and arrange half the potatoes in a deep ovenproof casserole.
Add the drained meat and onions, then pour in enough marinade to come about halfway up the dish.
Cover with the remaining potatoes.
Mix the flour with a little water to make a firm paste and press it around the casserole rim; fit the lid on top to seal.
Bake for 3 hours, until the meat is tender.
Break the flour seal at the table and serve hot.

title: Quiche alsacienne
ingredients: 6 ounces smoked bacon, cut into lardons
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Line the pastry shell with parchment and baking weights, then blind-bake for 15 minutes; remove the weights and bake 5 minutes more.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until lightly browned, then drain on paper towels.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper together.
Scatter the bacon in the pastry shell and pour in the egg mixture.
Bake until just set in the center and golden at the edges, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Kougelhopf
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, for the mold
instructions: Soak the raisins in the kirsch or warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Butter a 10-inch kougelhopf mold and place an almond in each groove at the base.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the milk and eggs and knead until a soft dough forms.
Knead in the softened butter a little at a time, then work in the drained raisins.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Spoon the dough into the mold, cover, and let rise until it reaches near the rim, about 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F and bake until deep golden and cooked through, about 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool in the mold for 10 minutes, turn out onto a rack, and dust with confectioners' sugar.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven; transfer it to a plate.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, then set it aside.
Add the butter and olive oil, then cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Stir in the garlic and flour; cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot. Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, and bouquet garni.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 2½ hours, until the beef is tender.
Sauté the mushrooms and pearl onions in a little butter, then add them to the pot for the final 30 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3½ pounds, cut into 8 pieces
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven and set it aside.
Brown the chicken pieces in the bacon fat; set them aside.
Add the butter and oil, then cook the onion and carrot until softened.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot. Add the wine, stock, and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked through.
Sauté the mushrooms and pearl onions in butter, then add them to the pot for the final 20 minutes.
Remove the bouquet garni, check the seasoning, and serve with the sauce.

title: Œufs en Meurette
ingredients: 1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Toast the bread slices and keep them warm.
Cook the bacon in a saucepan until crisp, then set it aside.
Add the butter, onion, and carrot to the pan; cook until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock, add the bouquet garni, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Strain the sauce, return it to the pan, and season with salt and pepper.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar.
Poach the eggs one at a time for about 3 minutes, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Place an egg on each toast, spoon the wine sauce over it, and scatter with bacon.

title: Gougères
ingredients: 6 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Bring the water, butter, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the flour all at once.
Return the pan to low heat and stir until the dough forms a ball and pulls away from the sides.
Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Stir in the Gruyère, pepper, and nutmeg.
Drop tablespoonfuls of dough onto the baking sheet, spacing them apart.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and golden; serve warm.

title: Jambon Persillé
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless cooked ham, cut into ½-inch cubes
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the pork hocks, onion, carrot, garlic, and bouquet garni in a pot with the water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for about 2½ hours, until the meat is tender.
Strain the broth and measure 2 cups; discard the vegetables and bouquet garni.
Remove the meat from the hocks and dice it, discarding the bones and skin.
Stir the vinegar and gelatin into the hot broth until dissolved.
Mix the cooked hock meat with the ham, parsley, and chives; season with salt and pepper.
Pack the mixture into a loaf pan and pour in enough broth to cover it.
Chill for at least 8 hours, until set, then slice and serve cold.

title: Quenelles de brochet with Nantua sauce
ingredients: 4 large pike quenelles, about 150 g each
30 g butter, for the baking dish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Butter a baking dish and arrange the quenelles in it.
Warm the béchamel with the crème fraîche and crayfish butter, stirring until smooth. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the quenelles and scatter the crayfish tails on top.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the quenelles are puffed and the sauce is bubbling. Serve hot.

title: Salade lyonnaise
ingredients: 1 head frisée, washed and torn into bite-size pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Toast the bread, rub each slice with the cut side of the garlic, and set aside.
Fry the lardons in a skillet until browned and crisp. Keep them warm and reserve 1 tablespoon of the fat.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, oil, reserved bacon fat, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft.
Toss the frisée with the warm lardons and dressing. Divide among plates and top each with a poached egg and a slice of garlic toast.

title: Saucisson brioché
ingredients: 250 g all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
1 egg yolk, beaten with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and mix until a dough forms.
Knead in the softened butter a little at a time until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1½ hours.
Bring a saucepan of water to a simmer. Add the sausage and warm it for 10 minutes, then drain and pat it dry. Remove its casing.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Roll the dough into a rectangle large enough to wrap the sausage.
Wrap the sausage in the dough, seal the seam, and place it seam-side down in a greased loaf pan. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes.
Brush with the egg yolk mixture and bake for 35–40 minutes, until deeply golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Cervelle de canut
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Stir the fromage blanc and crème fraîche together until smooth.
Mix in the chives, parsley, shallot, vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavors can mingle.
Serve cold with crusty bread or boiled potatoes.

title: Tarte à la praline rose
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the sugar and egg yolk. Add the cold water and bring the dough together without overworking it.
Roll out the dough and line a 24 cm tart pan. Prick the base and chill for 20 minutes.
Line the shell with baking paper and pie weights. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the weights, and bake for 5 minutes more.
Put the crushed pralines and cream in a saucepan. Heat gently, stirring, until the pralines melt and the mixture thickens slightly.
Pour the filling into the tart shell and bake for 15–20 minutes, until bubbling. Cool completely before slicing.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
2 cups Burgundy or other dry red wine
1 bouquet garni (thyme, parsley, and bay leaf)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Pat the beef dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven; transfer it to a plate and brown the beef in the rendered fat and olive oil in batches.
Add the onion and carrots and cook until softened, then stir in the flour.
Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up the browned bits; stir in the tomato paste, garlic, bouquet garni, bacon, and beef.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2½ hours, until the beef is tender.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter, stir them into the stew, and simmer for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Soupe à l’oignon gratinée
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat.
Add the onions and sugar; cook, stirring often, for 40–50 minutes until deeply golden and soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then add the wine and scrape the bottom of the pot.
Add the stock, bay leaf, thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer uncovered for 30 minutes.
Heat the broiler and ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls.
Top each bowl with toasted baguette and Gruyère, then broil until the cheese is bubbling and browned.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and fit the crust into a 9-inch tart pan.
Line the crust with parchment and pie weights; blind-bake for 15 minutes, then remove the weights and bake for 5 minutes more.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until lightly crisp, then drain it and scatter it over the crust.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour the custard into the crust and bake for 30–35 minutes, until just set in the center.
Rest the quiche for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Poulet rôti aux herbes
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Pat the chicken dry and rub it all over with butter, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Put the lemon, garlic, thyme, and rosemary in the cavity; tie the legs together if desired.
Arrange the potatoes in a roasting pan and set the chicken on top.
Roast for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375°F (190°C) and roast for about 1 hour more, basting once, until the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes before carving; serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

title: Crêpes sucrées
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted unsalted butter, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk in the eggs, then gradually whisk in the milk until smooth.
Stir in the melted butter and vanilla; rest the batter for 30 minutes.
Lightly butter a nonstick skillet and warm it over medium heat.
Pour in about ¼ cup batter, swirl to coat the pan thinly, and cook until the edges lift and the underside is lightly golden.
Flip and cook for about 30 seconds; repeat with the remaining batter, buttering the pan as needed.

title: Garbure Gasconne
ingredients: 1 small green cabbage, cored and chopped
1 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the beans, ham hock, garlic, bouquet garni, and water in a large pot; bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Lower the heat and simmer for 1 hour, or until the beans are nearly tender.
Add the cabbage, carrots, turnips, and leeks; simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Warm the duck legs separately, remove their bones if desired, and stir the meat into the soup.
Season to taste and serve hot.

title: Poulet au Pot Gascon
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Set the chicken in a large pot with the onion, garlic, bouquet garni, and water.
Bring to a gentle boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots, leeks, turnips, and cabbage; simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook until the chicken and vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes more.
Lift out the chicken and vegetables, season the broth to taste, and serve the broth first, followed by the chicken and vegetables.

title: Confit de Canard
instructions: Rub the duck legs with the salt, garlic, thyme, and bay leaves.
Cover and refrigerate for 12 to 24 hours.
Wipe the seasoning from the legs and pat them dry.
Warm the duck fat in a heavy ovenproof pot; add the legs, fully submerging them.
Cook uncovered in a 250°F oven until the meat is very tender, about 3 hours.
Serve hot, or cool the legs in the fat and refrigerate for later.

title: Cassoulet Toulousain
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Simmer the beans in fresh water until just tender, about 45 minutes; drain and reserve.
Brown the sausage in a heavy pot, then set it aside.
Cook the salt pork, onion, and carrots in the pot until softened; stir in the garlic and tomatoes.
Add the beans, stock, bouquet garni, and sausage; simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Nestle the duck legs into the beans and bake uncovered at 325°F for 1 hour.
Scatter the breadcrumbs over the top and bake until golden and bubbling, about 20 minutes more.
Remove the bouquet garni, season to taste, and serve hot.

title: Tourin à l’Ail
ingredients: 2 tablespoons duck fat or olive oil
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the duck fat in a pot and cook the onion over low heat until soft, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook gently for 2 minutes without browning it.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 25 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the vinegar in a bowl; slowly whisk in a ladle of hot soup.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the egg mixture without boiling the soup.
Season to taste and serve over toasted country bread.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the zucchini and bell pepper; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, herbes de Provence, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Soupe au pistou
ingredients: 1 cup green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 cup small pasta, such as ditalini
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrots; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, green beans, zucchini, water, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the pasta and white beans; simmer until the pasta is cooked, following the package timing.
Meanwhile, pound the basil and garlic together in a mortar, then work in the Parmesan and 1/4 cup olive oil to make the pistou.
Take the soup off the heat and stir in the pistou just before serving.

title: Daube provençale
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 strip orange zest, about 3 inches long
1 bouquet garni (thyme, bay leaf, and parsley)
instructions: Put the beef, wine, onion, carrots, garlic, orange zest, and bouquet garni in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Remove the beef and vegetables from the marinade; pat the beef dry and reserve the marinade.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven and brown the beef in batches.
Return the beef to the pot. Stir in the tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the reserved marinade and add the vegetables and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer very gently for 3 hours, until the beef is tender.
Stir in the olives for the last 15 minutes of cooking. Remove the bouquet garni and serve.

title: Pissaladière
ingredients: 1 pound pizza dough, at room temperature
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide pan over low heat.
Add the onions, thyme, salt, and pepper. Cook slowly, stirring often, for 35 to 45 minutes, until soft and golden but not browned.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Roll the dough into a rectangle and place it on an oiled baking sheet.
Spread the onions evenly over the dough, leaving a narrow border.
Arrange the anchovies and olives over the onions; drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the crust is golden. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Aïoli provençal
ingredients: 2 large egg yolks, at room temperature
1 pound carrots, peeled and cut into sticks
instructions: Put the egg yolks, mashed garlic, mustard, and salt in a bowl and whisk until smooth.
Add the olive oil a few drops at a time, whisking constantly. Once the mixture thickens, add the oil in a thin, steady stream.
Whisk in the lemon juice and taste for seasoning. Keep the aïoli chilled.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes; drain.
Steam or boil the carrots and green beans separately until tender, then drain.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them under cold water, and peel.
Arrange the vegetables and eggs on a platter and serve with the aïoli for dipping.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some of the oil, season with salt, and roast on baking sheets for 20 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic and ground meat and cook until browned.
Stir in the wine, tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes, until thickened.

Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick, then remove from the heat and stir in the nutmeg, eggs, and half the cheese.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, and top with the remaining eggplant. Pour over the béchamel and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook the spinach in a large pan until wilted. Drain well and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with the scallions, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil. Layer 6 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each sheet lightly with oil.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo. Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40–45 minutes, until crisp and golden. Rest briefly before serving.

title: Dolmades (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 jar (16 ounces) grape leaves in brine, rinsed and drained
instructions: Carefully separate the grape leaves and trim any tough stems.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the dill, mint, parsley, pepper, and half the lemon juice.
Place a grape leaf vein-side up on a work surface. Add about 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining filling and leaves.
Line a heavy pot with a few unused grape leaves. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in snug layers.
Pour in the broth, remaining oil, and remaining lemon juice. Place a heatproof plate on top to hold the rolls in place.
Cover and simmer gently for 45–50 minutes, until the rice is tender. Cool slightly before serving.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange the potatoes in a large roasting pan and place the chicken thighs on top.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, broth, oregano, salt, and pepper. Pour the mixture over the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 60–75 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken is browned and cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over the chicken and potatoes before serving.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1/4 cup olive oil, plus more for serving
instructions: Place the soaked beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add the olive oil, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, bay leaf, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Stir in the salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the soup thickens slightly.
Remove the bay leaf and serve hot with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil, arrange on baking sheets, and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic and ground meat and brown.
Stir in the wine, tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, pepper, and half the salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.

Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick, then remove from the heat and whisk in the egg, cheese, and remaining salt.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Pour the béchamel over the top and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook the spinach in a large skillet until wilted. Drain well and squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine the spinach, scallions, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and black pepper in a bowl.
Brush a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Layer 6 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each lightly with oil.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo. Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40–45 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool slightly before serving.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 6 ounces feta cheese, cut into a slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and olives on a serving platter.
Place the feta slab on top of the vegetables.
Whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, oregano, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the salad and serve immediately.

title: Dolmades (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 jar (16 ounces) grape leaves in brine, rinsed and drained
1/4 cup olive oil, plus 2 tablespoons for the pot
instructions: Separate the grape leaves and trim any tough stems.
Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the dill, mint, parsley, salt, pepper, and juice of 1 lemon.
Place a grape leaf vein-side up. Add about 1 teaspoon of filling near the stem, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line a pot with any torn grape leaves. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in tight layers and drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Pour in the broth and remaining lemon juice. Place a heatproof plate over the rolls to keep them submerged.
Cover and simmer gently for 45–50 minutes until the rice is tender. Cool before serving.

title: Greek Lemon Potatoes
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange the potatoes in a single layer in a roasting pan.
Whisk together the olive oil, chicken broth, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour the mixture over the potatoes and toss to coat.
Roast for 60–75 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until golden and tender. Spoon the pan juices over them before serving.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some olive oil and roast until tender, about 20 minutes.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ground meat and brown.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, wine, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thickened.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Stir in half the cheese and the beaten egg.
Layer the eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish. Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake until golden and bubbling, about 35 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Wilt the spinach in a pan over medium heat. Cool, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with the scallions, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil. Layer in 6 phyllo sheets, brushing each lightly with oil.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil. Score the top into portions.
Bake until crisp and golden, about 40 minutes. Cool slightly before serving.

title: Fasolada
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add the onion, carrots, celery, tomatoes, tomato paste, water, bay leaves, and olive oil.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered until the beans are tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes more, then remove the bay leaves and serve.

title: Pastitsio
ingredients: 12 ounces tubular pasta, such as bucatini
1 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese, divided
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Cook the pasta in salted water until just al dente, then drain.
Cook the onion in a pan over medium heat until soft. Add the garlic and beef, and brown the meat.
Stir in the tomatoes, wine, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thickened.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Stir in the nutmeg, half the cheese, and the beaten eggs.
Spread the pasta in a baking dish and spoon the meat sauce over it. Pour the béchamel on top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake until golden and set, about 40 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Tzatziki
instructions: Place the grated cucumber in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Stir the yogurt, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
Fold in the cucumber until evenly combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 200 g feta cheese, in one block
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, bell pepper, and olives in a serving bowl.
Place the feta block on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, then sprinkle with oregano and salt.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 500 g fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook the spinach in a large pan over medium heat until wilted; drain and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with scallions, dill, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil and layer in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1 cm rounds
100 g grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil and roast on baking sheets for 20 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until softened.
Add the lamb and garlic; cook until the meat is browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk and cook until thickened; remove from the heat and whisk in the eggs and half the cheese.
Layer the eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, then spread the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden, then rest for 20 minutes before cutting.

title: Avgolemono Chicken Soup
instructions: Place the chicken, water, carrot, celery, onion, salt, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer for about 1 hour, until the chicken is tender.
Remove the chicken and vegetables; strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Pull the chicken meat from the bones and set it aside.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the orzo, and cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl.
Slowly whisk 2 cups of hot broth into the egg mixture, then stir it back into the pot.
Add the chicken and warm gently without boiling; serve hot.

title: Dolmades (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
instructions: Blanch the grape leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the rice, dill, mint, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Place a grape leaf flat with the veined side up; add about 1 teaspoon of filling near the stem end.
Fold the sides over the filling and roll it up snugly.
Line a pot with any torn grape leaves and arrange the dolmades seam-side down in layers.
Pour in the broth and remaining olive oil; place a heatproof plate on top to keep the rolls in place.
Cover and simmer gently for 45–50 minutes, until the rice is tender; cool slightly before serving.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 200 g feta cheese, cut into a slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and olives on a serving platter.
Drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, then season with salt and oregano.
Place the feta on top and sprinkle with a little more oregano.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 500 g fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cook the spinach in a large pan until wilted, then drain and squeeze out excess moisture.
Mix the spinach with scallions, dill, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil and layer in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread the filling evenly over the phyllo.
Layer the remaining phyllo on top, brushing each sheet with oil, and tuck in the edges.
Score the top into portions and bake for 45–50 minutes until golden.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, sliced into 1 cm rounds
1/2 cup grated Kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil and roast on baking sheets for 20 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the lamb and garlic, and cook until the lamb is browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk and cook until the sauce thickens; stir in nutmeg and let cool slightly.
Whisk the egg into the sauce, then stir in half the cheese.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Dolmades (Stuffed Vine Leaves)
ingredients: 250 g vine leaves in brine, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until softened.
Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then mix in the dill, mint, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Lay a vine leaf vein-side up and trim away its stem.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll it snugly.
Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line a pot with any torn vine leaves and arrange the rolls seam-side down in close layers.
Pour over the lemon juice and broth, then place a heatproof plate on top to hold the rolls in place.
Cover and simmer gently for 50–60 minutes, until the rice is tender.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 300 g dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the soaked beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes; drain.
Heat the olive oil in the pot and cook the onion, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours until the beans are tender.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Horiatiki (Greek Village Salad)
ingredients: 200 g feta cheese, in one slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, bell pepper, and olives in a serving bowl.
Add the feta slab on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, then sprinkle with oregano and salt.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Spanakopita (Spinach and Feta Pie)
ingredients: 500 g fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cook the spring onions in olive oil over medium heat until softened.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted; cool and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with feta, eggs, dill, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with melted butter and layer in 4 phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Spread the filling evenly over the pastry.
Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden.

title: Moussaka

Salt and black pepper, to taste
75 g grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

Gradually whisk in the warm milk and simmer until thick; cool slightly, then whisk in the egg and half the cheese.
Layer the eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, then spread the béchamel on top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)

instructions: Put the beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes; drain.

title: Pastitsio (Greek Baked Pasta)

instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and cook the pasta in salted water until just tender; drain.

Gradually whisk in the warm milk and simmer until thick; cool slightly, then whisk in the egg and half the cheese.
Spread the pasta in a baking dish and spoon the meat sauce over it.
Pour the béchamel over the meat and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40–45 minutes until golden, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Moussaka

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil and roast on a baking sheet until tender, about 20 minutes.
