title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh spinach, washed and chopped
1 package (16 ounces) frozen phyllo dough, thawed
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted. Let cool, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine the spinach mixture, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, nutmeg, and pepper in a bowl.
Brush a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each sheet lightly with melted butter.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo. Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Score the top into portions with a sharp knife. Bake until crisp and golden, about 45 minutes. Rest briefly before serving.

title: Horiatiki (Greek Village Salad)
ingredients: 7 ounces feta cheese, in one slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, and olives in a serving bowl.
Place the feta slab on top of the vegetables.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, oregano, and a pinch of salt.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and serve immediately.

title: Fasolada (Greek Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, bay leaf, and 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the beans are tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir in the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes more, then remove the bay leaf and serve.

title: Pastitsio
ingredients: 12 ounces tubular pasta, such as bucatini or ziti
Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Cook the pasta in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic and ground meat; cook until browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, wine, oregano, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thickened.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the beaten eggs, then stir the egg mixture and half the cheese into the saucepan.
Toss the pasta with a little béchamel and spread it in a baking dish. Spoon the meat sauce over the pasta, then spread the remaining béchamel on top.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake until golden and set, about 45 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated Kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some of the olive oil and roast for 20 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic and ground meat; cook until browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the beaten eggs, then stir the egg mixture and half the cheese into the sauce.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat mixture over it, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Pour the sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40 minutes, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted. Drain well and cool.
Mix the spinach with the scallions, dill, parsley, salt, pepper, feta, and eggs.
Brush a baking dish with melted butter. Layer 6 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each sheet with butter.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo.
Top with the remaining 6 sheets, brushing each with butter. Score the top into portions.
Bake for 40–45 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool slightly before serving.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 4 pounds, cut into pieces
2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange the chicken and potatoes in a large roasting pan.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, broth, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour the mixture over the chicken and potatoes, turning them to coat.
Roast for 75–90 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving with the pan juices.

title: Fasolada
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot and cover with the water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes. Drain and return the beans to the pot with fresh water to cover.
Add the onion, carrots, celery, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaves, and olive oil.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partly covered for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Stir in the salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaves and serve warm.

title: Tzatziki
instructions: Toss the grated cucumber with the salt and let it drain in a strainer for 15 minutes.
Squeeze the cucumber firmly to remove excess liquid.
Stir together the yogurt, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill, and pepper.
Fold in the cucumber. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant with some of the oil and roast on baking sheets until tender, about 25 minutes.
Heat the remaining oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and meat; brown the meat.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, half the salt, and half the pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thickened; cool slightly and whisk in the egg and half the cheese.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, then add the remaining eggplant. Pour the sauce on top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) until golden and bubbling, about 40 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion and scallions until soft, then add the spinach and cook until wilted and most liquid has evaporated. Cool.
Stir the dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and pepper into the spinach mixture.
Brush a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with oil. Layer 6 phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each with oil.
Spread the filling evenly over the phyllo. Layer the remaining 6 sheets on top, brushing each with oil.
Tuck in the edges, score the top into portions, and sprinkle with water. Bake until crisp and golden, about 45 minutes.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 7 ounces feta cheese, cut into a slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, bell pepper, and olives on a serving platter.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper together.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables.
Place the feta on top and sprinkle with oregano. Serve immediately.

title: Dolmades (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 jar (16 ounces) grape leaves, drained and rinsed
instructions: Separate the grape leaves and trim any tough stems. Set aside 4 leaves to line the pot.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the dill, mint, parsley, pepper, and half the lemon juice. Remove from the heat and let the filling cool slightly.
Place a grape leaf vein-side up. Add about 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining filling and leaves.
Line a heavy pot with the reserved leaves and arrange the rolls seam-side down in snug layers.
Pour in the broth, remaining olive oil, and remaining lemon juice. Place a heatproof plate on top to hold the rolls down.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice is tender, about 50 minutes. Cool in the pot before serving.

title: Avgolemono Chicken Soup
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 3 pounds), cut into pieces
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, carrots, celery, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 1 hour.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Strain the broth and return it to the pot. Remove the meat from the bones and shred it.
Bring the broth to a boil. Add the orzo and cook until tender according to the package directions.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 cups of hot broth to temper the mixture.
Lower the soup to a gentle heat. Slowly stir in the egg mixture; do not boil.
Stir in the shredded chicken, pepper, and dill. Serve hot.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with olive oil and arrange them on baking sheets.
Roast the eggplant for 20 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon olive oil until soft. Add the garlic and ground meat; cook until browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes, until thickened.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the eggs, then stir the egg mixture and half the cheese into the saucepan.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat mixture over it, then add the remaining eggplant.
Pour the sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40 minutes, until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook the spinach in a large pan until wilted. Drain well and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with the scallions, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and black pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil. Layer in 6 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with oil.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil. Tuck in the edges and score the top into portions.
Bake for 45–50 minutes, until crisp and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Horiatiki (Greek Village Salad)

instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and olives on a serving platter.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, oregano, and salt together.
Place the feta slab on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and serve.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes. Drain.
Heat the olive oil in the pot. Add the onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and crushed tomatoes.
Add the beans, water, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cover partially.
Simmer for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beans are tender, adding water if needed.
Stir in the salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the soup.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the parsley, and serve with olive oil and crusty bread.

title: Pastitsio
ingredients: 12 ounces tubular pasta, such as bucatini
1 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Cook the pasta in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ground meat. Brown the meat.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thickened.

Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the eggs, then stir the egg mixture and half the cheese into the saucepan.
Toss the pasta with a few spoonfuls of the sauce and spread it in a baking dish.
Spread the meat sauce over the pasta, then pour the remaining white sauce on top. Sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 45 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some of the olive oil and arrange them on baking sheets.
Roast the eggplant for 20 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ground meat; cook until browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, cinnamon, nutmeg, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth and thick.
Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the beaten eggs, then stir the egg mixture and half the cheese into the saucepan.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Pour the white sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden. Rest for 20 minutes before slicing.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and scallions until soft.
Add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Squeeze excess liquid from the spinach, then mix it with the dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with melted butter. Layer 6 phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each sheet with butter.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo.
Layer the remaining phyllo sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Tuck in the edges and score the top into portions.
Bake for 40–45 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Greek Horiatiki Salad
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
7 ounces feta cheese, cut into a slab
instructions: Arrange the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, and olives on a serving platter.
Place the feta slab on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Sprinkle with oregano and salt. Serve immediately.

title: Dolmades

instructions: Separate the grape leaves and set aside any torn leaves to line the pot.

Cover and simmer gently for 45–50 minutes, until the rice is tender. Cool before serving.

title: Fasolada

instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot and add the olive oil, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes, broth, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cover partially.
Simmer for 1 1/2–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender.
Stir in the salt and black pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley, and serve warm.

Stir in the feta, eggs, dill, and pepper.

Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo.
Top with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Score the top into portions and bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: Moussaka

instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil and arrange them on baking sheets.
Roast the eggplant for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ground lamb.

Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Squeeze the cucumber firmly to remove excess liquid.
Stir together the yogurt, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill, and remaining salt.
Fold in the cucumber and chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil, season with salt, and roast on baking sheets for 20 minutes, turning once.

Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick, then stir in the nutmeg and half the cheese.
Let the sauce cool slightly, then whisk in the egg.
Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spoon over the meat sauce, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Spread the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 40 minutes, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.

Toss the pasta with a few spoonfuls of béchamel and spread it in a baking dish. Add the meat sauce, then spread the remaining béchamel over the top.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake for 45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, chicken broth, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.

Place the chicken thighs skin-side up among the potatoes and pour the remaining mixture over everything.
Roast for 55–65 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over the chicken and potatoes before serving.

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some of the oil and arrange them on baking sheets.

Layer half the eggplant in a baking dish, spread the meat sauce over it, and top with the remaining eggplant.
Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Bake for 45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 20 minutes before serving.

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large pan. Cook the onion until soft, then add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted.
Transfer the spinach mixture to a colander and press out excess liquid. Let it cool.
Stir in the scallions, dill, parsley, salt, pepper, feta, and eggs.
Brush a baking dish with oil. Layer 6 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each with oil and butter.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo. Layer the remaining 6 sheets on top, brushing each with oil and butter.
Tuck in the edges, score the top into portions, and bake for 40–45 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut along the scored lines and serve.

title: Pastitsio
ingredients: 1 cup grated Kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese, divided
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Cook the pasta in salted water until just tender, then drain.

Remove the sauce from the heat. Whisk a little sauce into the beaten eggs, then stir the egg mixture and 1/2 cup of cheese into the saucepan.
Toss the pasta with a few spoonfuls of béchamel and spread it in a baking dish. Top with the meat sauce.
Spread the remaining béchamel over the meat and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Arrange the potatoes in a roasting pan and place the chicken on top, skin side up.

title: Fasolada (Greek Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the drained beans in a large pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes, water or broth, bay leaf, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then stir in the parsley.
Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread and olives.

title: Kotopita (Epirus Chicken Pie)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the chicken, water, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 1 hour.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth. When cool enough to handle, remove the meat from the bones and shred it.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the rice, 2 cups of strained broth, pepper, and cinnamon; simmer until the rice is partly cooked and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Mix the rice with the shredded chicken and season to taste. Let the filling cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush a baking dish with butter and layer in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Spread the filling over the phyllo. Top with the remaining sheets, brushing each with butter, and tuck in the edges.
Score the top into portions and bake until deeply golden, about 50 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Alevropita (Epirus Flour Pie)
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, plus 2 tablespoons for the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Pour 2 tablespoons olive oil into a large shallow baking pan and heat the pan in the oven for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour, water, milk, eggs, salt, and 1/4 cup olive oil into a thin, smooth batter.
Carefully pour the batter into the hot pan. Scatter the feta over the top and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake until puffed, crisp at the edges, and golden, about 30 minutes.
Cool for a few minutes, cut into squares, and serve warm.

title: Pita me Horta (Wild Greens Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound mixed wild greens, such as nettles, chicory, and dandelion greens
instructions: Wash the greens well, remove tough stems, and chop them. Blanch sturdy greens in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry; leave tender greens raw.
Mix the greens with the scallions, dill, parsley, salt, pepper, half the olive oil, and feta.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush a baking dish with oil and layer in half the phyllo sheets, brushing each lightly with oil.
Spread the greens filling evenly over the phyllo. Cover with the remaining sheets, brushing each with oil, and tuck in the edges.
Score the top and bake until crisp and golden, about 45 minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Gigantes Plaki (Baked Giant Beans)
ingredients: 1 pound dried giant lima beans or gigantes beans
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Put the beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer until tender but still holding their shape, about 60 to 90 minutes. Drain, reserving 1 cup of cooking water.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Warm the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, salt, pepper, oregano, and reserved cooking water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Combine the beans and sauce in a baking dish. Cover and bake for 45 minutes, then uncover and bake until the sauce thickens, about 20 minutes more.
Stir in the parsley, adjust the seasoning, and let the beans rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Trahanas Soup with Feta
ingredients: 6 cups water or light chicken stock
instructions: Bring the water or stock to a boil in a saucepan.
Stir in the trahanas and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
Cook, stirring often, until the trahanas is soft and the soup is creamy, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in the butter, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and top with crumbled feta. Serve with toasted bread.

title: Plastos (Thessalian Cornmeal Pie)
ingredients: 3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for the pan
1 pound wild greens or spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and oil a large shallow baking pan.
Mix the greens, scallions, dill, and feta in a bowl.
Whisk the cornmeal, warm water, salt, and olive oil into a loose batter.
Spread half the batter thinly over the pan.
Scatter the greens mixture evenly over the batter.
Spoon the remaining batter over the greens and spread it as thinly as possible.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 50–60 minutes, until golden and crisp at the edges.

title: Spetsofai (Thessalian Sausage and Peppers)
ingredients: 1 pound Greek country sausage, sliced into thick rounds
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat.
Brown the sausage for 5–6 minutes, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the peppers and onion and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper.
Return the sausage to the pan and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

title: Batzina (Thessalian Zucchini Pie)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil, for the baking pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and oil a large shallow baking pan.
Toss the grated zucchini with the salt and let it stand for 10 minutes.
Squeeze the zucchini firmly to remove excess liquid.
Whisk the eggs, yogurt, and olive oil in a large bowl.
Stir in the zucchini, feta, kefalotyri, and black pepper.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Spread the mixture in the pan and bake for 45–55 minutes, until set and deeply golden.

title: Trahanas Soup with Feta
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Pour in the stock and bring it to a boil.
Stir in the trahanas and salt.
Lower the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring often, until creamy and tender.
Season with black pepper and serve topped with feta.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the soaked beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes; drain.
Return the beans to the pot and add the onion, carrots, celery, tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, water, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partially covered for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Stir in the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer for another 10 minutes and remove the bay leaves before serving.

title: Fava Santorinis
ingredients: 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, for serving
instructions: Put the split peas, water, chopped onion, and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer gently until the peas are very soft, about 50 minutes.
Stir in the salt and lemon juice, then mash or blend until smooth.
Spoon onto a plate and drizzle with the remaining olive oil; serve with sliced red onion and capers.

title: Tomatokeftedes
ingredients: 3 large ripe tomatoes, finely chopped and drained
instructions: Mix the tomatoes, onion, mint, parsley, and oregano in a bowl.
Stir in the flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper until a thick batter forms.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden; drain briefly and serve warm.

title: Patatato of Amorgos
ingredients: 1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and lamb; brown the lamb on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the crushed tomatoes, wine, oregano, cinnamon, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and water, then simmer uncovered until the potatoes and lamb are tender and the sauce is thick, about 35 minutes.

title: Kremmydopita (Cycladic Onion Pie)
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onions with the salt over low heat until very soft and golden, about 30 minutes.
Let the onions cool, then mix with the pepper, dill, feta, and eggs.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush a baking dish with melted butter.
Layer 4 sheets of phyllo in the dish, brushing each with butter.
Spread the onion mixture over the phyllo, then top with the remaining 4 sheets, brushing each with butter.
Tuck in the edges, score the top lightly, and bake until crisp and golden, about 35 minutes.

title: Melopita of Sifnos
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh unsalted mizithra cheese or ricotta, drained
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, for the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 9-inch round baking pan.
Mash the cheese in a bowl until smooth.
Whisk in the honey and eggs, then mix in the semolina and cinnamon.
Pour the mixture into the pan and bake until set and lightly browned, about 50 minutes.
Cool until just warm, then drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.

title: Dakos (Cretan Barley Rusk Salad)
instructions: Set the rusks on two plates and sprinkle each with a little water to soften slightly.
Spoon the grated tomato over the rusks and season lightly with salt.
Top with myzithra, capers, and oregano.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve at once.

title: Horta (Boiled Wild Greens)
ingredients: 500 g mixed wild greens or dandelion greens, trimmed and washed
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.
Add the greens and boil until tender, 8 to 15 minutes depending on the greens.
Drain well, reserving a little cooking water if desired.
Serve warm or at room temperature with olive oil and lemon.

title: Briam (Cretan-Style Baked Vegetables)
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
2 medium zucchini, cut into thick rounds
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Arrange the potatoes, zucchini, and onion in a baking dish.
Mix the grated tomatoes with olive oil, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour the tomato mixture over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Cover the dish with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake until the vegetables are tender and browned, about 30 minutes more.

title: Cretan Gamopilafo (Wedding Rice with Lamb Broth)
ingredients: 2 teaspoons fine sea salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the lamb, water, onion, and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming the surface.
Lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer until the lamb is very tender, about 2 hours.
Lift out the lamb and strain the broth; return 750 ml broth to the pot and bring it to a boil.
Stir in the rice and simmer, stirring often, until tender and creamy, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and clarified butter, then taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the rice hot with the lamb alongside.

title: Kalitsounia with Myzithra and Honey
ingredients: 250 g all-purpose flour, plus extra for rolling
instructions: Mix the flour, water, olive oil, and salt into a smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mash the myzithra with the egg and sugar until combined.
Roll the dough thinly and cut out 10 cm rounds.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center of each round and pinch the edges into small pleats around it.
Bake on a lined tray at 180°C until golden, about 25 minutes.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon before serving.

title: Bougatsa with Semolina Custard
ingredients: 50 g unsalted butter, melted, plus extra for brushing
instructions: Heat the milk and sugar in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk the semolina into the milk and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Beat the eggs with the vanilla, then slowly whisk in a ladleful of hot semolina mixture.
Stir the egg mixture back into the saucepan and cook gently for 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in 50 g butter; let the custard cool slightly.
Brush a baking dish with butter and layer in half the filo, brushing each sheet with butter.
Spread the custard over the filo and cover with the remaining buttered sheets.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon before serving.

title: Soutzoukakia Smyrneika
ingredients: 1 slice stale bread, soaked in water and squeezed dry
2 tablespoons olive oil, plus extra for frying
instructions: Mix the beef, onion, garlic, bread, cumin, salt, and pepper until combined.
Shape the mixture into oblong meatballs and chill for 20 minutes.
Lightly dust the meatballs with flour and brown them in olive oil; set aside.
Add the wine to the pan and simmer for 1 minute, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in the tomatoes, sugar, and cinnamon and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Return the meatballs to the pan, cover, and simmer gently for 30 minutes, turning once.
Serve hot with rice or crusty bread.

title: Spanakorizo
ingredients: 1 kg fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
2 cups hot water or vegetable stock
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion and spring onions until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the spinach in batches and stir until wilted.
Stir in the rice, dill, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the hot water or stock and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 20–25 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Gigantes Plaki
ingredients: 500 g dried butter beans, soaked overnight
1½ cups cooking liquid from the beans
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and place them in a pot with fresh water and the bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until just tender, about 45–60 minutes; reserve 1½ cups cooking liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrots until softened.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, sugar, parsley, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Place the beans in a baking dish and pour the tomato sauce and reserved cooking liquid over them.
Bake uncovered at 180°C for 45–55 minutes, until tender and lightly browned on top.
Let the beans rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bougatsa-Style Cheese Pie (Tirobougatsa)
instructions: Mix the feta, ricotta, eggs, and black pepper in a bowl.
Brush a baking dish with melted butter and layer in 4 filo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Spread the cheese filling evenly over the filo.
Top with the remaining 4 filo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Tuck in the edges, brush the top with butter, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve warm.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the beans in a large pot, cover with water, and boil for 10 minutes; drain.
Add the olive oil, onion, carrots, celery, tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaf, and 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered until the beans are tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir in the salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Remove the bay leaf, scatter parsley over the soup, and serve with bread.

title: Spanakorizo (Spinach and Rice)
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the spinach in batches and stir until wilted.
Stir in the rice, water, dill, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gemista (Tomato and Pepper Stuffed with Rice)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers, keeping the tops as lids; scoop out the tomato pulp and chop it.
Warm 1/4 cup olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the chopped tomato pulp, rice, parsley, mint, salt, and pepper; cook for 3 minutes.
Fill the tomatoes and peppers about two-thirds full and replace their lids.
Arrange them snugly in a baking dish, pour in the water, and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 45 minutes; uncover and bake until tender and lightly browned, about 30 minutes more.

title: Briam (Greek Roasted Vegetables)
ingredients: 2 medium zucchini, cut into thick rounds
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Put the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, and onion in a large baking dish.
Mix the grated tomatoes, olive oil, parsley, oregano, salt, pepper, and water; pour over the vegetables.
Toss to coat and spread the vegetables in an even layer.
Bake uncovered for about 1 hour, turning the vegetables once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving with bread.

title: Chicken Avgolemono Soup
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 1 hour.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth; return 8 cups broth to the pot.
Bring the broth to a simmer, add the rice, and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Shred some chicken meat and add it to the soup.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl; slowly whisk in 1 cup hot broth.
Take the pot off the heat and gradually stir in the egg mixture; do not boil the soup afterward.
Season with black pepper and additional salt to taste.

title: Horiatiki (Village Salad)
ingredients: 200 g Greek feta, in one piece
instructions: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, pepper, and olives in a serving bowl.
Season lightly with salt and drizzle with the vinegar and olive oil.
Lay the feta on top and sprinkle it with oregano.
Serve at once with bread for dipping in the juices.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 500 g dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1.5 litres water, plus more as needed
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the drained beans in a large pot and cover with fresh water by 5 cm.
Bring to a boil, cook for 10 minutes, then drain and discard the water.
Return the beans to the pot with the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes, olive oil, bay leaves, and 1.5 litres water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered until the beans are tender, about 1½ to 2 hours; add water if needed.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaves, and serve warm.

title: Briam (Oven-Roasted Vegetables)
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
2 medium zucchini, cut into thick rounds
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Arrange the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, and onion in a large baking dish.
Mix the grated tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and water; pour over the vegetables.
Cover the dish with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for 35 to 45 minutes more, until tender and browned, turning the vegetables once.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving with bread.

title: Manestra (Orzo with Tomato)
ingredients: 750 ml hot water or vegetable stock
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes and hot water or stock, then season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, stir in the orzo, and lower the heat.
Simmer, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and the sauce is creamy, about 10 to 12 minutes; add a splash of hot water if it thickens too much.
Serve hot with grated cheese.

title: Ladera-Style Green Beans with Potatoes
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and grated tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the green beans, potatoes, water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans and potatoes are tender and the sauce is reduced.
Stir in the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Pastitsada Corfiot Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 lb, cut into serving pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Grated kefalotyri or Parmesan, for serving
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, paprika, sugar, and chicken. Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 50 minutes.
Cook the pasta in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Serve the chicken and rich sauce over the pasta, with grated cheese.

title: Sofrito Corfiot Beef
ingredients: 2 lb beef top round, cut into thin slices
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then lightly coat each slice in flour.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Add the garlic and parsley to the pot and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the wine and vinegar, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot and add the water. Cover and simmer gently until very tender, about 1 1/2 hours, turning the slices occasionally.
Taste the sauce for seasoning and serve hot with mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

title: Bourdeto Corfiot Fish Stew
ingredients: 2 lb firm white fish, such as scorpionfish or cod, cut into pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Season the fish lightly with salt and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onions over medium-low heat until soft and golden, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, and pepper flakes; cook for 1 minute.
Add the wine, water, and vinegar, and simmer for 10 minutes to make a thick sauce.
Nestle the fish pieces into the sauce, cover, and simmer gently until just cooked through, about 10 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness.
Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning; serve with bread to soak it up.

title: Bianco Corfiot Fish
ingredients: 2 lb firm white fish, such as sea bass or cod, cut into serving pieces
1 1/2 lb waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into thick slices
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Season the fish with salt and pepper.
Layer the potatoes in a wide pot and scatter the garlic over them.
Drizzle with olive oil and add the water; cover and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 20 minutes.
Place the fish on top of the potatoes, cover, and simmer gently until the fish flakes easily, about 10 minutes.
Pour in the lemon juice and gently shake the pot to combine it with the cooking juices.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately.

title: Tsigarelli Corfiot Greens
ingredients: 2 lb mixed wild greens or chard, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the greens by handfuls, stirring as they wilt.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the greens are tender and the sauce has thickened, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, taste for seasoning, and serve warm with bread.

title: Pita me Horta (Wild Greens Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound mixed wild greens, such as dandelion, chicory, and nettles, washed and chopped
1/3 cup olive oil, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Blanch the greens in boiling water for 2 minutes; drain well and squeeze out excess water.
Mix the greens with scallions, dill, parsley, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with oil and layer in half the phyllo, brushing each sheet lightly with oil.
Spread the greens filling evenly over the phyllo.
Layer the remaining phyllo on top, brushing each sheet with oil; tuck in the edges and score the top.
Sprinkle the water over the pie and bake for 45–55 minutes, until golden and crisp.

title: Fasolada (White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the drained beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes; drain.
Return the beans to the pot with 8 cups water, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaves, and olive oil.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partially covered for about 1 hour, until the beans begin to soften.
Stir in the tomato paste and crushed tomatoes.
Simmer for 30–45 minutes, until the beans are tender and the broth is thick.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaves, and serve hot.

title: Bourdeto (Spicy Fish Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish, cut into large pieces
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook for 8–10 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, and red pepper flakes; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes, water, salt, and black pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Nestle the fish pieces into the sauce and cover the pot.
Simmer gently for 12–15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily; avoid stirring so the pieces stay whole.

title: Alevropita (Flour-and-Feta Pie)
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, plus more for the pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Whisk the flour, water, eggs, olive oil, and salt into a smooth, thin batter.
Oil a large shallow baking pan and pour in the batter.
Scatter the feta and oregano evenly over the top.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until puffed and deeply golden at the edges.
Cool for 5 minutes, cut into squares, and serve warm.

title: Kotosoupa Avgolemono (Chicken Soup with Egg and Lemon)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, salt, and pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and vegetables; strain the broth back into the pot.
Add the rice to the broth and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until tender.
Remove the meat from the chicken, discard the bones, and return the meat to the soup.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice in a bowl.
Slowly whisk 2 cups of hot broth into the egg mixture, then pour it back into the pot while stirring.
Warm the soup gently without boiling, adjust the seasoning, and serve.

title: Spetzofai (Thessalian Sausage and Pepper Stew)
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Brown the sausage slices, then transfer them to a plate.
Add the onion and peppers to the pan and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, and red pepper flakes; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt, and black pepper, then return the sausage to the pan.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the peppers are tender.

title: Trahanas with Feta
ingredients: 4 cups water or light chicken stock
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the trahanas and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water or stock, add the salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until creamy.
Stir in the feta and butter, then serve hot.

title: Lamb with Greens and Avgolemono
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into serving pieces
1 kg mixed wild greens, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, cover, and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the greens, salt, and pepper; cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice in a bowl. Slowly whisk in a ladle of hot broth, then stir the mixture into the pot off the heat.
Let the stew stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Plastos (Cornmeal Pie with Greens)
ingredients: 500 g chopped spinach or mixed greens
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and oil a 30 cm baking dish with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil.
Mix the greens, spring onions, feta, and dill in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the cornmeal, warm water, salt, and remaining olive oil into a pourable batter.
Pour half the batter into the dish and spread the greens filling evenly over it.
Pour the remaining batter over the filling and spread it gently to cover.
Bake for 50–60 minutes, until golden and firm. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
ingredients: 300 g dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the drained beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain again.
Add the olive oil, onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste, then add the beans, bay leaf, and water.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover loosely, and simmer for 1.5–2 hours until the beans are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the broth.

title: Fava Santorinis (Yellow Split Pea Purée)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the split peas, chopped onion, water, bay leaf, salt, and 1 tablespoon olive oil in a pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer gently until the peas are very soft, about 50 minutes; add a little water if needed.
Remove the bay leaf and blend or mash the peas until smooth. Stir in the lemon juice and season to taste.
Spoon into a shallow dish and drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Top with sliced red onion and capers; serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Tomatokeftedes (Santorini Tomato Fritters)
ingredients: 2 cups ripe Santorini tomatoes, finely chopped and drained
instructions: Mix the tomatoes, onion, mint, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Stir in the flour and baking powder until you have a thick, spoonable batter; let it rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Drop heaping tablespoons of batter into the hot oil and flatten them slightly.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Revithada (Slow-Baked Chickpeas of Sifnos)
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Put the chickpeas and sliced onions in a covered ovenproof pot or clay pot.
Add the olive oil, salt, pepper, and water; stir gently.
Cover tightly and bake until the chickpeas are tender and creamy, about 5 to 6 hours, checking once to make sure there is enough liquid.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve warm with bread.

title: Patatato (Amorgos Lamb and Potato Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the lamb on all sides, working in batches if needed.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Add the potatoes and water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the lamb and potatoes are tender and the sauce is rich, about 1 hour and 30 minutes.

title: Aegean Chickpea and Herb Salad
instructions: Put the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, feta, and parsley in a serving bowl.
Whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently.
Let the salad stand for 10 minutes before serving so the flavors can mingle.

title: Dakos (Cretan Barley-Rusk Salad)
instructions: Sprinkle the rusks lightly with water to soften their surfaces without making them soggy.
Spoon the grated tomato over the rusks and season with salt.
Top with mizithra, olives, oregano, vinegar, and olive oil.
Let stand for 5 minutes, then serve.

title: Briam (Cretan Roasted Vegetables)
ingredients: 1 pound zucchini, cut into thick rounds
1 large red onion, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange the potatoes, zucchini, eggplant, and onion in a large baking dish.
Stir together the grated tomatoes, olive oil, water, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper; pour over the vegetables.
Cover the dish with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 30 to 40 minutes more, until tender and browned, turning the vegetables once.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Chochlioi Boubouristi (Cretan Fried Snails)
ingredients: 1 pound cleaned edible snails, shells intact
instructions: Rinse the snails thoroughly and drain them well.
Spread the coarse salt in a heavy skillet and heat over medium heat.
Place the snails in the skillet with their openings facing down and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the olive oil and rosemary; cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring gently.
Pour in the vinegar and add the pepper; cook for 2 minutes more.
Serve hot, with bread for the pan juices.

title: Gamopilafo (Cretan Wedding Rice)
ingredients: 1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
instructions: Put the chicken, lamb, water, and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming the surface.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, until the meat is tender.
Transfer the meat to a plate and strain the broth into a clean pot.
Measure 6 cups of broth into the pot and bring it to a boil; add the rice.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and creamy.
Stir in the lemon juice, butter, and pepper; serve the rice with the meat.

title: Stamnagathi with Eggs (Cretan Wild Greens and Eggs)
ingredients: 1 pound stamnagathi or dandelion greens, trimmed and washed
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the greens.
Boil for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender; drain well.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and add the greens and salt.
Make four small wells in the greens and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are to your liking.
Finish with lemon juice and black pepper, then serve warm.

title: Bougatsa with Semolina Custard
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Warm the milk and sugar in a saucepan until steaming. Whisk in the semolina and salt, then cook, stirring, until thick.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl. Slowly whisk in a ladle of hot semolina mixture, then stir the egg mixture back into the saucepan.
Cook the custard for 1 minute, stirring, then remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla. Let it cool slightly.
Layer half the phyllo in the dish, brushing each sheet with melted butter. Spread the custard over it.
Top with the remaining phyllo, brushing each sheet with butter. Tuck in the edges and score the top lightly.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until crisp and golden. Dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon before serving.

title: Soutzoukakia Smyrneika
instructions: Combine the beef, onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, cumin, salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons of the wine.
Shape the mixture into about 12 oval meatballs. Chill for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet and brown the meatballs on all sides. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, water, and remaining wine to the skillet. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Return the meatballs to the skillet, cover, and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes, turning them once, until cooked through and the sauce is thick.

title: Giouvarlakia Avgolemono
ingredients: 8 cups water or light chicken stock
instructions: Mix the beef, rice, onion, parsley, half the egg, salt, and pepper. Shape into small balls.
Bring the water or stock to a gentle boil with the carrot and olive oil.
Add the meatballs one at a time. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer gently for 35–40 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Whisk the flour with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot and simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk the remaining egg with the lemon juice. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then remove the pot from the heat and stir in the egg-lemon mixture.
Let the soup stand for 2 minutes without boiling, then serve.

title: Gigantes Plaki
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Cover the beans with fresh water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim, and simmer for 45–60 minutes, until nearly tender. Drain and reserve 2 cups of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Warm the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion, carrots, and celery for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir the beans into the tomato mixture and transfer everything to a baking dish. Add the reserved cooking liquid.
Cover and bake for 40 minutes. Uncover and bake for 20–30 minutes more, until tender and saucy. Sprinkle with parsley.

title: Spanakorizo
ingredients: 500 g fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
2 cups hot water or vegetable stock
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and scallions for 5 minutes, until softened.
Add the spinach in batches, stirring until wilted. Stir in the dill and parsley.
Add the rice, hot water or stock, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice, and let stand covered for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 1 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush the eggplant slices with some olive oil, season with salt, and roast on baking sheets until tender and browned, about 20 minutes.
Warm the remaining olive oil in a pan. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ground meat; brown the meat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the wine, tomatoes, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk; cook until thick. Remove from the heat and whisk in the eggs, nutmeg, and half the cheese.
Layer the eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish. Spread the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until golden and bubbling, about 40 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Wilt the spinach in a large pan over medium heat. Let it cool, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the spinach with the scallions, dill, parsley, feta, eggs, and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil. Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each sheet lightly with oil.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the phyllo. Layer the remaining sheets on top, brushing each with oil.
Score the top into portions and bake until crisp and golden, 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Fasolada
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the drained beans in a large pot and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add the onion, carrots, celery, tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaves, and 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partially covered until the beans are tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir in the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the broth is rich and slightly thickened.
Remove the bay leaves, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Pastitsio
ingredients: 12 ounces tubular pasta, such as bucatini
1 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese, divided
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Cook the pasta in salted water until just shy of al dente; drain.
Cook the onion in a pan until soft. Add the garlic and ground beef; cook until browned.
Stir in the wine, tomatoes, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Toss the pasta with the beaten eggs and half the cheese. Spread it in a greased baking dish, then spoon the meat sauce over it.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute; gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook until thick, then season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread the béchamel over the meat sauce and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Bake until browned and bubbling, about 40 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

title: Gemista
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers, keeping the tops as lids. Scoop the tomato pulp into a bowl and set the hollow vegetables in a baking dish.
Chop or blend the tomato pulp. Mix it with the rice, onion, garlic, parsley, mint, salt, pepper, and 1/4 cup olive oil.
Fill each tomato and pepper about two-thirds full, leaving room for the rice to expand. Replace the lids.
Arrange the potato wedges around the vegetables. Pour the water and remaining olive oil into the dish.

Cover loosely with foil and bake for 1 hour. Uncover and bake until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned and the rice is cooked, about 30 minutes more. Let rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Ladera: Green Beans with Potatoes
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound ripe tomatoes, grated, or 1 can (14 ounces) crushed tomatoes
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, green beans, potatoes, tomatoes, water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 45–55 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans and potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Fasolada: Greek White Bean Soup
ingredients: 1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the drained beans in a large pot with the water. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot with 10 cups fresh water, the onion, carrots, celery, tomatoes, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partly covered for about 1 hour, until the beans are nearly tender.
Stir in the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20–30 minutes more, until the beans are soft and the broth has thickened.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust the seasoning, and serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Briam: Roasted Summer Vegetables
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 large red onion, cut into wedges
1 pound ripe tomatoes, grated, or 1 can (14 ounces) crushed tomatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Put the eggplant, zucchini, potatoes, and onion in a large roasting pan.
Mix the tomatoes, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and water, then pour over the vegetables and toss well.
Roast uncovered for 60–75 minutes, turning the vegetables once or twice, until tender and browned at the edges.
Scatter the parsley over the top and let the briam rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Horta: Boiled Wild Greens with Lemon
ingredients: 2 pounds tender wild greens or dandelion greens, washed well and tough stems removed
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.
Add the greens and boil for 8–15 minutes, depending on their tenderness, until soft but not falling apart.
Drain the greens well and arrange them on a serving plate.
Dress with olive oil and lemon juice, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Hilopites with Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 3 pounds), cut into pieces
12 ounces hilopites (Greek egg pasta), or small egg noodles
1/2 cup grated kefalotyri or Parmesan cheese
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, working in batches if needed.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, water, cinnamon stick, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer gently for 45–55 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Lift the chicken onto a plate and keep it warm. Remove the cinnamon stick and bring the sauce to a steady simmer.
Add the hilopites and cook according to the package directions, stirring often and adding a little hot water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Return the chicken to the pot and warm through. Serve with grated cheese.

title: Pastitsada (Corfiot Beef in Spiced Tomato Sauce)
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into large chunks
1 pound thick pasta, such as bucatini
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until soft, about 8 minutes; stir in the garlic.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, cloves, paprika, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Return the beef to the pot. Cover and simmer gently until very tender, about 2 hours, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if the sauce gets too thick.
Cook the pasta in salted water according to the package directions, then drain.
Remove the cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf. Serve the beef and sauce over pasta, topped with grated cheese.

title: Sofrito (Veal with Parsley and Garlic)
ingredients: 2 pounds veal shoulder, cut into thin slices
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, and pepper on a plate, then lightly coat the veal slices.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium-high heat. Brown the veal in batches and set aside.
Add the garlic to the pan and cook for about 30 seconds, taking care not to let it burn.
Pour in the white wine and stock, scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the parsley and vinegar.
Return the veal to the pan, cover, and simmer gently until tender, about 1 hour. Turn the slices once or twice and add a splash of water if needed.
Serve with mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

title: Bourdeto (Spicy Fish Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish, such as scorpionfish or cod, cut into portions
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onions until soft and translucent, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add the water and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 15 minutes.
Lay the fish portions in the sauce in a single layer. Cover and simmer gently until the fish is just cooked through, 10 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve hot with bread.

title: Bianco (Corfiot Fish with Garlic and Lemon)
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish, cut into thick portions
1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into thick slices
instructions: Arrange the potatoes in a wide, heavy pot and place the fish on top.
Scatter the garlic over the fish and potatoes. Add the olive oil, salt, pepper, and water.
Cover and simmer gently until the potatoes are almost tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the lemon juice, cover again, and cook until the fish flakes easily and the potatoes are tender, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Shake the pot gently to mingle the sauce without breaking up the fish. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Tsigarelli (Wild Greens with Garlic and Tomato)
ingredients: 2 pounds mixed wild greens, such as dandelion greens, chard, and nettles, washed and roughly chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the greens in handfuls, turning them as they wilt.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt, pepper, and water. Cover and simmer gently until the greens are tender, 25 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the vinegar and taste for seasoning. Serve warm with bread.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot; fry the onions until deep golden, then set half aside.
Add the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaves to the pot and fry briefly.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, then add the chicken, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, yogurt, and salt.
Cook, stirring, until the chicken is coated and beginning to brown; mix in the cilantro and mint.
Boil the rice in salted water until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken, top with the reserved onions, cover tightly, and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then gently combine the rice and chicken before serving.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Add the tomatoes and cook until soft and thick.
Stir in the chickpeas and water; simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Mix in the garam masala and amchur, then simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer it to cold water and drain.
Blend the spinach with the green chili into a smooth puree.
Heat the ghee in a pan and brown the paneer cubes; remove and set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pan until soft, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomato, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook until the tomato breaks down.
Stir in the spinach puree and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer, garam masala, and cream; simmer gently for 3 minutes and serve.

title: Sri Lankan Dhal Curry
instructions: Put the lentils, onion, garlic, turmeric, curry powder, chili powder, water, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and cook until the seeds pop.
Pour the spiced oil over the dhal, stir, and serve.

title: Nepali Momo
instructions: Mix the flour and water into a smooth, firm dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, cabbage, cilantro, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and oil.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12–15 minutes, until the wrappers are tender and the filling is cooked through.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Drain the soaked chickpeas and place them in a pot with 6 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 60–90 minutes; drain and reserve 1 cup cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes soften, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the cilantro and lemon juice. Serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and 1 teaspoon salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Warm the milk and soak the saffron in it.
Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy pot. Fry the onions until golden; remove half and set aside.
Add the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and bay leaf to the pot. Add the marinated chicken and cook for 8 minutes, turning occasionally.
Drain the rice. Bring 3 cups water and the remaining salt to a boil in a separate pot. Add the rice and cook for 5 minutes, then drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender. Rest for 10 minutes, then gently fluff and serve.

title: Bangladeshi Masoor Dal
ingredients: 2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds and dried chilies and cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic and fry until golden.
Pour the spiced oil mixture into the cooked lentils and stir well.
Simmer for 2 minutes, garnish with cilantro, and serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Milk Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Season the fish with the salt and turmeric and set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, and green chili. Cook until the onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, coriander, and fenugreek. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add the coconut milk and water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, until just cooked through.
Stir in the lime juice, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 cup bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, ground cumin, turmeric, and chili powder. Cook until the tomatoes soften, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, water, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the black-eyed peas and simmer for 5 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
500 g bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
instructions: Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot, then fry the onions until golden; set aside half for garnish.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and salt; simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Boil the rice in the water until it is about 70 percent cooked, then drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken, topping it with cilantro, mint, reserved onions, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes; gently mix before serving.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then cool it in cold water and blend into a puree.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the cumin until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the spinach puree and water, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the cumin until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until thick and soft.
Stir in the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and amchur, then garnish with cilantro.

title: Sri Lankan Red Lentil Dhal
ingredients: 1 dried red chili, broken in half
instructions: Combine the lentils, onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the dried chili, curry leaves, and cinnamon, and fry for 30 seconds.
Pour the spiced oil over the dhal and stir before serving.

title: Nepali Chicken Momo
ingredients: 3/4 cup water, plus more as needed
instructions: Mix the flour with the water and knead into a smooth, firm dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, cabbage, cilantro, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, oil, cumin, coriander, and salt in a bowl.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin 3-inch round.
Place about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of each round and pleat the edges closed.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the filling is cooked through.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cans (15 ounces each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and chili powder; cook until the tomato softens.
Add the chickpeas, water, and salt. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash some chickpeas to thicken the sauce, then stir in the cilantro and lemon juice.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and 1 teaspoon salt. Set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions until deep golden; remove half for garnish.
Add the marinated chicken and cook for 8 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add the cilantro and mint, then spread the drained rice over the chicken.
Add the water, remaining salt, and ghee. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes, then gently fluff and serve with the reserved onions.

title: Dal Tadka
ingredients: 1 cup yellow split pigeon peas (toor dal), rinsed
instructions: Combine the dal, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot.
