Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer until the dal is very soft, about 35 minutes.
Mash the dal until creamy, adding a little water if needed.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and dried chili.
When the seeds begin to pop, add the garlic and cook until golden.
Add the tomato and chili powder; cook until the tomato softens.
Pour the spiced ghee mixture over the dal, stir, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Milk Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, coriander, and chili powder.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, add the salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until just cooked through.
Stir in the lime juice and garnish with cilantro.

title: Nepali Chicken Momo
instructions: Mix the flour and water to form a firm dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, cabbage, cilantro, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, cumin, pepper, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the wrappers are tender and the filling is cooked through.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
500 g bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
A few saffron strands soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
instructions: Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden; reserve half for garnish.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves, then stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, and salt; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and cook until the chicken is partly tender and the sauce thickens.
In a separate pot, boil the rice in salted water until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken; top with the reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the rice is fully cooked.
Gently fluff and serve hot.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then cool it in cold water and drain.
Blend the spinach into a smooth puree.
Heat the oil or ghee in a pan and fry the cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the spinach puree and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala, then simmer gently for 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the cumin seeds; let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, ground coriander, turmeric, ground cumin, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the chickpeas and water, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice; simmer for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Dhal
instructions: Put the lentils, half the onion, garlic, green chili, turmeric, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When the seeds begin to pop, add the remaining onion, curry leaves, and chili flakes; fry until the onion is golden.
Pour the seasoned oil over the lentils and stir before serving.

title: Nepali Vegetable Momo
ingredients: 1 cup warm water, plus more as needed
instructions: Mix the flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons oil in a bowl; gradually add warm water and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the cabbage, carrot, onion, cilantro, garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, 1/2 teaspoon salt, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon oil in a bowl.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin 3-inch circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, then pleat and pinch the edges closed.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 10–12 minutes, until the wrappers are glossy and cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
500 g bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
1 pinch saffron, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk (optional)
instructions: Boil the rice in salted water until about three-quarters cooked; drain and set aside.
Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot, then fry the onions until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken; cook until the chicken is lightly browned.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, and salt; cook until the chicken is nearly done and the sauce thickens.
Layer the rice over the chicken, then sprinkle with cilantro, mint, and saffron milk if using.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice and chicken are fully cooked.
Gently fluff and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer it to cold water and drain.
Blend the spinach into a smooth puree.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomato softens.
Add the spinach puree and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala, then simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Parippu (Red Lentil Curry)
instructions: Put the lentils, onion, garlic, green chili, turmeric, water, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the curry leaves and cumin, then cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the spiced oil over the lentils, stir, and serve hot with rice.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 1 cup bamboo shoots, rinsed and sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and add the fenugreek seeds.
When the seeds darken, add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, cumin, coriander, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot with rice.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
1 pinch saffron soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
instructions: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden; remove half for garnish.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked.
In a separate pot, bring the water to a boil, add the rice, and cook until it is about three-quarters done; drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken, then top with the reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes; gently fluff and serve.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and amchur powder; simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Pakistani Aloo Gosht
ingredients: 1 pound bone-in lamb or beef pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until golden.
Add the meat and ginger-garlic paste; brown the meat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes break down.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer until the meat is tender, about 60 to 90 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook uncovered until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Sri Lankan Parippu (Red Lentil Curry)
instructions: Combine the lentils, onion, green chili, turmeric, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the lentils are soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the curry leaves and cinnamon, then pour the tempering over the lentils.
Stir and serve hot.

title: Nepali Momo
instructions: Mix the flour and water to form a smooth, firm dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, cabbage, cilantro, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, oil, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the filling is cooked through.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with half the salt; add the rice and cook until about three-quarters done, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden; remove half for garnish.
Add the chicken, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, turmeric, chili powder, and remaining salt; cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and mint, then spread the chicken mixture evenly in the pot.
Layer the drained rice and reserved onions over the chicken.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender.
Gently fluff the rice and serve.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the cumin seeds.
When the seeds sizzle, add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the cilantro and serve.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and blend into a smooth puree.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and tomato; cook until the tomato softens.
Add the turmeric, garam masala, salt, and spinach puree; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the paneer and cream, then simmer gently for 4 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Dhal
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When they begin to pop, add the onion, garlic, green chili, curry leaves, and chili flakes; fry until the onion is golden.
Pour the fried seasoning over the lentils, stir, and serve.

title: Nepali Vegetable Momo
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for the filling
instructions: Mix the flour, water, oil, and salt to form a smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the cabbage, carrot, scallions, ginger, soy sauce, pepper, and filling oil in a bowl.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin 3-inch circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange the momos in an oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the wrappers look slightly translucent and the filling is hot.
Serve immediately.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
500 g bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, and half the salt.
Add the rice and cook until about 70 percent tender; drain and set aside.
Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot, then fry the onions until golden. Remove half for garnish.
Add the chicken and ginger-garlic paste; cook until the chicken is lightly browned.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and remaining salt; simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked and the sauce is thick.
Spread the rice over the chicken, then top with the reserved onions, mint, and cilantro.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Gently fluff and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds.
When the seeds sizzle, add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the spinach, and blanch for 2 minutes.
Drain the spinach, cool it under cold water, and blend into a smooth purée.
Heat the oil and butter in a pan and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until soft and golden, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the spinach purée and water, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer gently for 4 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve warm.

title: Sri Lankan Dhal Curry
instructions: Combine the lentils, onion, garlic, green chili, turmeric, curry powder, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When the seeds pop, add the curry leaves and cinnamon stick; fry for 30 seconds.
Pour the spiced oil over the lentils, stir, and serve hot with rice.

title: Nepali Momo
instructions: Mix the flour with enough water to make a firm, smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the chicken, onion, cilantro, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, oil, cumin, salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons water.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin circle about 8 cm wide.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the wrappers are tender and the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with tomato achar or another dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot; fry the onions until golden, then set aside half for garnish.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Boil the water, add the rice, and cook until it is about three-quarters done; drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken, topping with reserved onions, cilantro, and mint.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, then gently mix and serve.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Add the tomatoes and cook until soft and thick.
Add the chickpeas and water; simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and amchur; garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and blend into a smooth purée.
Heat the oil and butter in a pan; cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the spinach purée and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Dhal
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, chili powder, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and cook until they begin to pop.
Add the onion, garlic, and curry leaves; fry until the onion is golden.
Pour the fragrant oil mixture into the dhal, stir, and serve.

title: Nepali Vegetable Momo
instructions: Mix the flour and 3/4 cup water; knead into a smooth dough, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the cabbage, carrot, onion, cilantro, oil, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and soy sauce in a bowl.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in each circle, then pleat and seal the edges.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over simmering water for 12–15 minutes, until the wrappers are cooked through; serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Pressure-cook the chickpeas with 5 cups water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and reserve 3 cups cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and add the cumin seeds.
When the seeds sizzle, add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften, about 7 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and reserved cooking liquid, then simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the cilantro and lemon juice, then serve.

title: Chicken Karahi
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat and add the cumin seeds.
Add the chicken and salt; cook, turning, until lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the coriander, chili powder, and turmeric.
Add the tomatoes, ginger, and garlic; cover and cook over medium heat until the chicken is tender, about 25 minutes.
Uncover and cook over high heat, stirring, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Stir in the green chilies and garam masala, then cook for 2 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Bangladeshi Masoor Dal
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then simmer uncovered until the lentils are soft, about 20 minutes.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan until shimmering.
Add the dried chili and cumin seeds; cook for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic and fry until golden.
Pour the seasoned oil and aromatics into the lentils and stir well.
Simmer for 2 minutes, garnish with cilantro, and serve with rice.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Sambol
instructions: Combine the onion, chili flakes, and salt in a bowl and crush together with your fingers or a mortar until the onion softens.
Add the grated coconut and mix thoroughly.
Stir in the lime juice and warm water.
Taste and adjust the salt or lime juice, then serve at room temperature.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 1 cup bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
1 cup black-eyed peas, cooked and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and add the cumin and fenugreek seeds.
When the seeds sizzle, add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, and water, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the black-eyed peas and simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
A pinch of saffron soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with half the salt and the whole spices. Add the rice and cook until about three-quarters done, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden. Set aside half for garnish.
Add the chicken and ginger-garlic paste to the pot; cook until the chicken is lightly browned.
Stir in the tomatoes, yogurt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and remaining salt. Simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked and the sauce thickens.
Layer the rice over the chicken. Scatter the cilantro, mint, reserved onions, and saffron milk on top.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through. Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix and serve.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the chickpeas and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 60–90 minutes; drain and reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add the chickpeas and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice. Serve hot.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, then transfer it to cold water and drain.
Blend the spinach with the green chili into a smooth purée.
Heat the ghee in a pan and fry the paneer cubes until lightly golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion until soft. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, cumin, turmeric, and salt. Cook until the tomato breaks down.
Stir in the spinach purée and water. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer for 3 minutes. Stir in the cream and serve.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Dhal
instructions: Put the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the lentils are soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds and cook until they begin to pop.
Add the onion, garlic, green chili, curry leaves, and chili flakes. Cook until the onion is soft and lightly golden.
Pour the spiced oil mixture into the lentils and stir well. Simmer for 2 minutes, then serve.

title: Nepali Vegetable Momos
ingredients: 3/4 cup water, plus more as needed
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Gradually add the water and knead into a smooth, firm dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the cabbage, carrot, onion, cilantro, soy sauce, ginger, cumin, pepper, and oil in a bowl.
Divide the dough into small balls. Roll each into a thin round about 3 inches wide.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each round. Pleat and pinch the edges together to seal.
Arrange the momos in a lightly oiled steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 10–12 minutes, until the wrappers look slightly translucent and the filling is hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden; set aside half.
Add the chicken, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt, lemon juice, cilantro, mint, and half the fried onions. Cover and simmer until the chicken is nearly tender.
In another pot, bring the water to a boil with the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, and salt. Add the drained rice and cook until just tender, then drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken. Sprinkle with garam masala and the remaining onions.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes. Gently mix before serving.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then cool and blend into a puree.
Heat the oil or ghee in a pan and cook the cumin until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until soft. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the spinach puree and water. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed (about 3 cups)
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the cumin until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the chickpeas and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Dhal
instructions: Put the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the onion, garlic, green chili, cumin, and curry leaves. Cook until the onion is soft.
Pour the seasoning mixture into the lentils, stir, and serve.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes
1 cup bamboo shoots, drained and sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the cumin until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until the onion softens.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, and water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth has thickened slightly.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
1/4 teaspoon saffron threads soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
instructions: Heat the oil and ghee in a heavy pot; fry the onions until golden, then remove half and set aside.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; simmer until the chicken is partly cooked.
Boil the rice in salted water until just underdone, then drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken and top with reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender.
Gently fluff and serve.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and add the cumin seeds; cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chickpeas and water; simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice; serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Dhal Curry
instructions: Put the lentils, onion, garlic, green chili, turmeric, fenugreek, water, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and cook until the seeds pop.
Pour the tempering over the dhal, stir, and serve.

title: Bangladeshi Shorshe Ilish
ingredients: 2 green chilies, plus 2 slit chilies for cooking
instructions: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend the mustard seeds with 2 green chilies and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub the hilsa with turmeric and salt.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it just begins to smoke, then let it cool slightly.
Add the mustard paste and water; stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and slit chilies; cover and cook gently for 8–10 minutes, turning the fish once.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 1 cup bamboo shoots, rinsed and sliced
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and add the cumin seeds; cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until softened, then stir in the garlic and ginger.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, cumin, and coriander; cook until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, black-eyed peas, water, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Simmer the chickpeas in the water until tender, about 60–90 minutes; drain and reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a pot and toast the cumin seeds for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chickpeas and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the cilantro and lemon juice before serving.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and 1 teaspoon salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy pot. Fry the onions until deep golden; remove half and set aside.
Add the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and cumin seeds to the pot and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the marinated chicken and cook for 8 minutes, turning to coat it in the spices.
Drain the rice. In a separate pot, bring the water and remaining salt to a boil, then cook the rice for 5 minutes; drain while the grains are still firm.
Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and lemon juice.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender. Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix and serve.

title: Bangladeshi Masoor Dal
ingredients: 2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds and dried chilies and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and garlic and fry until golden.
Pour the sizzling spiced oil over the cooked lentils and stir.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Coconut Sambol
instructions: Pound the onion, chilies, chili powder, and salt together in a mortar until crushed and well combined.
Add the grated coconut and pound briefly to mix.
Stir in the lime juice and taste, adjusting the salt or lime if needed.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 1 cup bamboo shoots, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a pot until shimmering. Add the fenugreek seeds and dried chilies; cook until the seeds darken.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, bamboo shoots, tomatoes, turmeric, cumin, and salt; stir to coat.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth is flavorful.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, and half the salt.
Add the rice and cook until about three-quarters done; drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions until golden. Remove half for garnish.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the chicken, yogurt, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, and remaining salt.
Cook until the chicken is nearly tender and the sauce is thick.
Layer the rice over the chicken and scatter the cilantro, mint, and reserved onions on top.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender.
Gently mix and serve hot.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, drained, or 1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala, cilantro, and lemon juice.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then transfer it to cold water and drain.
Blend the spinach into a smooth puree.
Heat the oil in a pan and lightly brown the paneer cubes; remove and set aside.
Add the onion to the pan and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, cumin, turmeric, coriander, chili powder, and salt; cook until the tomato softens.
Stir in the spinach puree and water, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and garam masala; simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve hot.

title: Sri Lankan Parippu (Red Lentil Curry)
instructions: Put the lentils, onion, garlic, green chili, turmeric, salt, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the mustard seeds and cook until they begin to pop.
Add the curry leaves and chili flakes, then cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the spiced oil over the lentils, stir, and serve hot with rice.

title: Nepali Aloo Tama
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes
1 cup bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the fenugreek seeds and cook until they darken and become fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric, chili powder, and potatoes; stir to coat.
Add the bamboo shoots, tomatoes, water, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot with rice.

title: Chicken Karahi
instructions: Heat the oil in a karahi or heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until lightly browned.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, salt, chili flakes, coriander, and cumin.
Add the tomatoes, cover, and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the tomatoes break down, about 25 minutes.
Uncover and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens and oil separates at the edges.
Add the green chilies and garam masala; cook for 2 minutes.
Top with fresh ginger and cilantro, and serve hot.

title: Aloo Keema
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink.
Stir in the salt, coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder.
Add the potatoes, water, and tomato; cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook until the mixture is thick and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the green chilies and cilantro, then serve.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cans (15 ounces each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato, salt, coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder; cook until the tomato softens.
Stir in the chickpeas and water, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Masoor Dal
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the lentils are soft, about 20 minutes; stir occasionally.
Lightly mash the lentils and adjust the consistency with a little water if needed.
Heat the ghee in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and dried chili; cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and garlic and fry until golden, then stir in the chili powder.
Pour the hot tempering over the lentils, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Chicken Pulao
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Heat the oil or ghee in a heavy pot and fry the onion until golden.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, salt, cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf.
Add the yogurt and cook, stirring, until it is absorbed into the chicken.
Drain the rice and add it to the pot with the water and green chilies.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 18 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the pulao rest, covered, for 10 minutes; fluff gently before serving.

title: Shorshe Ilish (Hilsa in Mustard Sauce)
instructions: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then blend with 1 green chili and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Season the fish with turmeric and half the salt.
Heat the mustard oil until shimmering, then lower the heat.
Stir in the mustard paste, remaining salt, and water; simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the fish and remaining chili, cover, and cook gently for 8–10 minutes, turning once.

title: Masoor Dal with Garlic and Dried Chili
instructions: Put the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot and bring to a boil.
Skim any foam, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan.
Add the garlic, dried chilies, and cumin seeds; fry until the garlic is golden.
Pour the hot seasoning into the lentils and stir before serving.

title: Aloo Bhorta (Mashed Potato with Mustard Oil)
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes, until tender.
Drain well and mash the potatoes while warm.
Mix in the onion, green chilies, mustard oil, cilantro, and additional salt to taste.
Shape into a mound and serve warm with rice.

title: Chingri Malai Curry (Prawns in Coconut Milk)
ingredients: 500 grams large prawns, peeled and deveined
instructions: Season the prawns with turmeric and half the salt.
Heat the mustard oil and quickly fry the prawns for 1 minute; transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the ginger paste, cumin, chili powder, remaining salt, cardamom, and cinnamon; stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the prawns to the pan and cook gently for 4–5 minutes, until just cooked.

title: Khichuri (Rice and Lentils)
instructions: Dry-toast the mung dal in a pot over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant; set aside.
Heat the mustard oil in the pot and fry the onion until golden.
Add the ginger paste, turmeric, cumin seeds, bay leaf, and green chilies; stir for 30 seconds.
Add the toasted dal, rice, salt, and water; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and porridge-like.
Rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Sri Lankan Red Rice and Parippu (Lentil Curry)
instructions: Put the lentils, water, onion, garlic, chile, turmeric, curry powder, curry leaves, and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 3–5 minutes until creamy.
Serve hot with cooked red rice.

title: Pol Sambol (Coconut Sambol)
instructions: Pound the onion, chiles, Maldive fish, and salt together until finely crushed.
Add the grated coconut and pound or mix until evenly combined.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt and heat.
Serve fresh with rice, hoppers, or bread.

title: Kiribath (Coconut Milk Rice)
instructions: Put the rice, water, and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat, and cook until the rice is soft and most of the water is absorbed, about 15–20 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook gently, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Press the rice onto a lightly oiled plate, flatten the top, and let it cool slightly before cutting into squares or diamonds.

title: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 pound bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
1 tablespoon Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
instructions: Toss the chicken with the curry powder, turmeric, pepper, and salt.
Heat the coconut oil in a pot; add the onion, garlic, ginger, chile, curry leaves, and cinnamon, and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir for 3–4 minutes to coat it in the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, cover, and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Taste and adjust the salt, then serve with rice.

title: Polos (Young Jackfruit Curry)
ingredients: 2 pounds canned young green jackfruit, drained and cut into chunks
1 tablespoon Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a pot and cook the onion, garlic, ginger, chile, and curry leaves until fragrant.
Stir in the turmeric, curry powder, and salt.
Add the jackfruit, coconut milk, and water; stir gently to coat.
Cover and simmer for 30–40 minutes, stirring carefully now and then, until the jackfruit is tender and the sauce is thick.
Taste for seasoning and serve with rice.

title: Sarson da Saag
ingredients: 1 lb mustard greens, washed and chopped
instructions: Add the mustard greens, spinach, and water to a pot. Cover and simmer until very soft, about 45 minutes.
Mash the greens with a potato masher, or pulse briefly with an immersion blender.
Stir in the maize flour and salt, then simmer for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Cook the onion, ginger, garlic, and green chili until the onion is golden.
Stir the tempering into the greens and serve hot with makki di roti.

title: Makki di Roti
instructions: Mix the maize flour and salt in a bowl.
Add warm water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Pat each ball into a round between damp hands or between sheets of parchment.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and cook each roti until browned on both sides, turning once.
Brush lightly with ghee and serve warm.

title: Punjabi Chole
instructions: Soak the chickpeas in 6 cups of water overnight, then drain.
Add the chickpeas, 4 cups fresh water, and tea bag to a pressure cooker. Cook until tender, then remove the tea bag.
Heat the mustard oil in a pot. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the tomatoes, coriander, cumin, amchur, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and salt.
Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add the cooked chickpeas and their cooking liquid. Simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with bhature or rice.

title: Punjabi Rajma
instructions: Soak the kidney beans in 5 cups of water overnight, then drain.
Pressure-cook the beans with 4 cups of fresh water until completely tender.
Heat the ghee in a pot. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Cook until thick and the oil separates.
Add the cooked beans and their cooking liquid. Simmer for 25 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken the curry.
Stir in the garam masala, garnish with cilantro, and serve with steamed rice.

title: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
instructions: Whisk the yogurt, 1/2 cup chickpea flour, 4 cups water, turmeric, and salt until smooth.
Pour into a pot and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently. Cook for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
For the pakoras, mix 1 cup chickpea flour, onion, chili powder, and salt. Add water gradually to make a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a deep pan. Drop in spoonfuls of batter and fry until golden; drain on paper towels.
Add the pakoras to the simmering kadhi and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried red chilies, and asafoetida; cook briefly until fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the kadhi and serve hot with rice.

title: Gujarati Dal
instructions: Combine the toor dal and water in a pot and simmer until soft, about 30 minutes.
Mash the dal lightly, then stir in the tomato, turmeric, ginger, green chili, jaggery, lemon juice, and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, adding water if needed to make a thin, pourable dal.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried red chili, and peanuts.
When the seeds crackle and the peanuts turn golden, pour the tempering into the dal.
Simmer for 2 minutes and finish with cilantro.

title: Undhiyu
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh fenugreek leaves, finely chopped
1 cup chopped surti papdi or flat beans
instructions: Mix the fenugreek leaves, chickpea flour, turmeric, coriander, cumin, chili powder, sugar, salt, and 2 tablespoons oil into a firm dough.
Shape the dough into small oval muthia and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a heavy pot. Add the carom seeds and asafoetida.
Add the yam, eggplant, potatoes, green beans, papdi, and pigeon peas; stir to coat with the spices.
Add the water, cover, and cook over low heat until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 20 minutes.
Nestle the muthia into the vegetables, cover, and cook until the muthia are cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Gently stir in the coconut, cilantro, and lemon juice before serving.

title: Khandvi
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, yogurt, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture becomes thick and leaves the sides of the pan, about 10 minutes.
Spread the hot mixture immediately into a very thin layer on the backs of several greased plates or on a clean counter.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, then cut into strips and roll each strip up tightly.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds and sesame seeds; when they pop, add the green chili.
Pour the tempering over the rolls and garnish with coconut and cilantro.

title: Gujarati Kadhi
instructions: Whisk the yogurt, chickpea flour, and water together until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring often.
Stir in the ginger, green chili, jaggery, and salt; simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried red chili, and asafoetida.
When the seeds crackle, pour the tempering into the kadhi.
Simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with cilantro.

title: Thepla
instructions: Combine the flour, fenugreek leaves, yogurt, 1 tablespoon oil, coriander, cumin, turmeric, chili powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add water a little at a time and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into 10 balls and roll each into a thin round, dusting with flour as needed.
Cook each thepla on a hot skillet, brushing with a little oil and turning until golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm or cool completely before packing.

title: Kerala Matta Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice several times until the water is mostly clear.
Bring the rice, water, and salt to a boil in a large pot.
Cover partly and simmer for 35–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the grains are tender.
Drain any remaining water and serve warm.

title: Kerala Parippu Curry
ingredients: 1 cup split yellow moong dal, rinsed
instructions: Combine the dal, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan and simmer until very soft, about 25 minutes.
Grind the coconut, green chilies, and cumin with 2 tablespoons water to make a coarse paste.
Stir the coconut paste into the cooked dal and simmer for 5 minutes, adding water if needed for a loose curry.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When they pop, add the dried red chilies and curry leaves and fry briefly.
Pour the tempering over the dal and serve with rice.

title: Avial
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables, cut into batons (carrot, green beans, ash gourd, and drumstick)
instructions: Put the vegetables, turmeric, salt, and 1/2 cup water in a wide pot.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the vegetables are tender but still hold their shape, about 12 minutes.
Grind the coconut, green chilies, and cumin with a little water to make a coarse paste.
Stir the paste into the vegetables and cook gently for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and fold in the yogurt.
Drizzle with coconut oil, add the curry leaves, and cover for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Kaalan
ingredients: 2 cups raw plantain, peeled and cubed
2 cups firm green yam, peeled and cubed
instructions: Put the plantain, yam, turmeric, salt, and 1 cup water in a saucepan.
Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Grind the coconut, green chilies, and cumin with a little water to make a smooth paste.
Stir the paste into the vegetables and simmer for 4 minutes.
Lower the heat and mix in the yogurt; warm gently without letting the curry boil.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan and add the mustard and fenugreek seeds.
When the mustard seeds pop, add the dried red chilies and curry leaves and fry briefly.
Pour the tempering over the curry and serve with rice.

title: Kerala Fish Curry
ingredients: 500 g firm fish, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a clay pot or saucepan over medium heat.
Add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then add the curry leaves and onion.
Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the ginger and garlic.
Add the chili powder, turmeric, and coriander powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Mix the tamarind paste with the water and salt, then pour it into the pot.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the fish pieces and simmer gently until just cooked, about 8–10 minutes.
Rest the curry for 10 minutes before serving with rice.

title: Ven Pongal
ingredients: 1/4 cup split yellow moong dal, rinsed
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pot until fragrant, then add the rinsed rice, water, turmeric, and salt.
Cook covered over low heat until the rice and dal are very soft, stirring occasionally and adding a little hot water if needed.
Heat the ghee in a small pan; fry the cashews until golden.
Add the pepper, cumin, ginger, and curry leaves to the ghee and sizzle briefly.
Stir the seasoning and cashews into the pongal and serve hot.

title: Sambar
ingredients: 1/2 cup split pigeon peas (toor dal), rinsed
2 cups water, plus more as needed
1 cup mixed vegetables, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Cook the toor dal with 2 cups water and turmeric until completely soft, then mash it.
Simmer the tamarind pulp with the onion, tomato, vegetables, sambar powder, and salt until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the mashed dal and enough water for a stew-like consistency; simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add the dried chile and curry leaves, then pour the seasoning into the sambar and serve.

title: Lemon Rice
ingredients: 2 cups cooked rice, cooled and separated
1 dried red chile, broken in half
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then stir in the chana dal and peanuts and fry until golden.
Add the dried chile, curry leaves, turmeric, and salt; stir for a few seconds.
Add the rice and toss gently until evenly coated and hot.
Turn off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Cabbage Poriyal
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a pan; add the mustard seeds and let them pop.
Stir in the urad dal and fry until pale golden, then add the dried chile and curry leaves.
Add the cabbage, water, and salt; cover and cook over medium-low heat until tender, stirring once or twice.
Uncover and cook until any excess water evaporates.
Stir in the grated coconut and serve as a side dish.

title: Rasam
ingredients: 1 small lemon-size ball tamarind, soaked in 1 cup warm water
instructions: Squeeze the soaked tamarind in its water and strain the liquid into a saucepan.
Add the crushed tomato, turmeric, rasam powder, salt, and 2 cups water.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 8 minutes, until the raw tamarind smell fades; do not let it boil hard.
Heat the ghee in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then add the dried chile and curry leaves.
Pour the seasoning into the rasam, stir in the cilantro, and serve hot.

title: Shukto
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled and cut into batons
1 medium raw banana, peeled and cut into batons
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into batons
1 tablespoon poppy seeds, soaked and ground
1 tablespoon mustard seeds, soaked and ground
instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a pot and lightly fry the bitter gourd; set it aside.
Add panch phoron and bay leaf to the pot, then add the potato, banana, sweet potato, and drumstick.
Stir in ginger, salt, and sugar, then add water and simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Mix in the ground poppy seeds and mustard seeds, then simmer until the vegetables are cooked.
Add milk and ghee, return the bitter gourd to the pot, and simmer briefly before serving.

title: Aloo Posto
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind them with one green chili into a smooth paste.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until shimmering, then add the nigella seeds and the remaining green chili.
Add the potatoes and salt, and stir to coat them in the oil.
Add the poppy seed paste and water, cover, and cook over low heat until the potatoes are tender.
Uncover and cook until the sauce clings to the potatoes; serve with rice.

title: Cholar Dal
ingredients: 1 cup chana dal, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Put the dal, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot and simmer until tender but still holding its shape.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan; add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.
Add the cumin seeds, then stir in the coconut and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the spice mixture into the dal and add the sugar and green chilies.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then serve with luchi or rice.

title: Dimer Jhol
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel, and lightly score them.
Rub the eggs and potatoes with some turmeric and salt.
Heat the mustard oil and fry the eggs until lightly golden; remove them, then fry the potatoes until golden.
Add cumin seeds and bay leaf to the pan, then cook the onion until golden.
Stir in the ginger, tomato, remaining turmeric, ground cumin, coriander, and chili powder; cook until thick.
Add the potatoes and hot water, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Add the eggs and garam masala, simmer for 2 minutes, and serve with rice.

title: Mishti Doi
ingredients: 2 tablespoons plain yogurt with live cultures
instructions: Bring the milk to a gentle boil in a heavy pot, stirring often.
Simmer, stirring, until the milk reduces by about one-third.
In a small pan, cook the sugar over low heat until it turns amber, then carefully stir it into the hot milk.
Cool the milk until it is warm to the touch, then whisk in the yogurt.
Pour into a clay pot or small bowls, cover, and leave in a warm place until set, about 8 to 12 hours.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
1-inch piece fresh ginger, cut into matchsticks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy karahi or skillet over medium-high heat. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle briefly.
Add chicken and brown for 6–8 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste, salt, chili powder, coriander, and ground cumin; cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook until the chicken is tender and the tomato sauce is thick and clings to it.
Stir in green chilies, ginger, cilantro, and garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes and serve hot.

title: Aloo Keema
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until golden.
Add ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste, salt, chili powder, turmeric, coriander, and cumin; cook for 1 minute.
Add potatoes and water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender.
Uncover and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated and the meat is fragrant.
Stir in green chilies and cilantro, then serve with roti or rice.

title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the soaked chickpeas and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until tender, about 60–90 minutes; drain and reserve 1 cup cooking water.
Heat oil in a separate pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes; cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Stir in salt, coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas and reserved cooking water. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Stir in garam masala, dried fenugreek, and cilantro. Serve with naan or rice.

title: Masoor Dal
instructions: Combine lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skimming any foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Mash the lentils lightly and add a little hot water if you prefer a thinner dal.
Heat ghee in a small pan. Add cumin seeds and dried chilies; let them sizzle briefly.
Add onion and cook until golden, then add garlic and chili powder and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the hot tempering over the dal, garnish with cilantro, and serve with rice or roti.

title: Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
2 tbsp warm milk mixed with a pinch of saffron
instructions: Mix chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, salt, chili powder, turmeric, coriander, and garam masala. Set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry onions until deep golden. Remove half for garnish.
Add cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf to the pot. Stir briefly, then add the marinated chicken and tomatoes.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is partly cooked and the sauce is thick.
In another pot, bring water to a boil. Add soaked rice and cook for 5–6 minutes, until about three-quarters cooked; drain.
Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with green chilies, reserved onions, cilantro, mint, and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then gently fluff and serve.

title: Shorshe Ilish (Hilsa in Mustard Sauce)
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then grind with the green chilies and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Rub the hilsa with turmeric and salt; set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it just begins to smoke, then let it cool slightly.
Stir in the mustard paste, remaining water, and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish, cover, and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.

title: Cholar Dal (Bengal Gram with Coconut)
ingredients: 1 cup split Bengal gram (chana dal), rinsed and soaked for 1 hour
instructions: Drain the dal and simmer it with the water and turmeric until tender but still holding its shape, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan; fry the coconut until golden, then remove and set aside.
Add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and cumin seeds to the pan and stir until fragrant.
Add the cooked dal and its cooking liquid, salt, sugar, and green chilies; simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the fried coconut and serve hot.

title: Aloo Posto (Potatoes with Poppy Seed Paste)
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then grind into a thick, smooth paste.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan and add the nigella seeds.
Add the potatoes, turmeric, and salt; stir to coat.
Add the poppy seed paste, green chilies, and water, then cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.

title: Masoor Dal with Garlic Tarka
instructions: Combine the lentils, water, and turmeric in a pot and bring to a boil.
Skim any foam, lower the heat, and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the salt and lightly mash the lentils to your preferred consistency.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan; add the garlic, dried chilies, and cumin seeds and fry until the garlic is golden.
Pour the hot seasoning over the dal, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Bangladeshi Chicken Curry
instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot until it just begins to smoke, then reduce the heat.
Add the onions and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the ginger paste, garlic paste, turmeric, coriander, cumin, chili powder, and salt; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until coated in the spices and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and water, cover, and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the green chilies and garam masala, then simmer uncovered for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Sri Lankan Parippu (Red Lentil Curry)
instructions: Put the lentils, water, turmeric, and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until the lentils are soft, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan; add the mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add the onion, chile, curry leaves, and fenugreek; cook until the onion is soft.
Pour the seasoned oil over the lentils and stir gently.

title: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds bone-in chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Toss the chicken with the curry powder, turmeric, chili powder, salt, and lime juice; set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, ginger, chile, curry leaves, and cinnamon; stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring, until coated and lightly browned.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

title: Pol Sambol (Coconut Sambol)
ingredients: 1 dried red chile, soaked in warm water and drained
instructions: Pound the dried chile and salt together in a mortar until finely crushed.
Add the onion and chili powder and pound to a coarse paste.
Mix in the grated coconut until evenly colored.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt before serving.

title: Kiribath (Coconut Milk Rice)
instructions: Put the rice and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat, and cook until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the salt and coconut milk.
Cover and cook over low heat for 5 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Press the rice into a shallow tray, smooth the top, and let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting into pieces.

title: Sri Lankan Beetroot Curry
ingredients: 2 medium beetroots, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, chile, and curry leaves; stir for 1 minute.
Add the beetroot, turmeric, and salt, then stir to coat.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer until the beetroot is tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes.

title: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
ingredients: 500 g mustard greens, washed and chopped
¾ cup warm water, or as needed
instructions: Put the mustard greens, spinach, green chilli, ginger, 2 cloves of garlic, and salt in a pot with 1 cup water.
Cover and simmer until the greens are very soft, about 45 minutes.
Mash the greens with a wooden masher, stir in the maize flour, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a pan; add the cumin seeds, onion, and remaining garlic, and cook until golden.
Stir the onion mixture into the greens and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the maize flour for the rotis with warm water to make a soft dough; divide into 6 balls.
Pat each ball into a thick round between damp hands or sheets of parchment.
Cook each roti on a hot griddle, turning until browned spots appear; finish with the remaining ghee and serve with the saag.

title: Punjabi Chole
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the chickpeas, water, and tea bags in a pot; simmer until the chickpeas are tender, about 1½ to 2 hours, then discard the tea bags.
Heat the ghee in a pan and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then stir in the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add the cooked chickpeas with 2 cups of their cooking liquid and simmer for 20 minutes, lightly mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the amchur and garam masala; simmer for 2 minutes and finish with cilantro.

title: Punjabi Rajma
ingredients: 1½ cups dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the kidney beans and water in a pressure cooker and cook until very tender, about 25 minutes at pressure; let the pressure release naturally.
Heat the oil in a pot and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until golden; stir in the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt; cook until thick and glossy.
Add the cooked beans and their cooking liquid; simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally and mashing a few beans into the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro, then serve hot.

title: Aloo Gobi
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pan and add the cumin seeds.
Add the onion and cook until lightly golden; stir in the ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt; cook until the tomatoes soften.
Stir in the potatoes and cauliflower until coated with the masala.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro and serve.

title: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
ingredients: 1 medium onion, finely chopped, for pakoras
¼ cup water, or as needed
instructions: Whisk the yogurt, ⅓ cup chickpea flour, water, turmeric, and salt until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot; add cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, sliced onion, ginger, garlic, and dried chilli, and cook until the onion is golden.
Pour in the yogurt mixture, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring often.
For the pakoras, mix the remaining chickpea flour with the finely chopped onion, baking powder, and enough water to make a thick batter.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan; drop in spoonfuls of batter and fry until golden, turning once. Drain on a paper towel.
Add the pakoras to the kadhi and simmer for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the chilli powder over the kadhi and serve hot.

title: Gujarati Dal
instructions: Combine the dal and water in a pressure cooker and cook until soft, about 3 whistles; mash until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, and dried chile; let them sizzle.
Stir in turmeric, ginger, green chile, and curry leaves, then add the cooked dal and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, adding water if needed to make a pourable dal.
Stir in jaggery and lemon juice. Finish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Thepla
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely chopped fresh fenugreek leaves
1 tablespoon oil, plus more for cooking
instructions: Mix the flour, fenugreek, yogurt, oil, spices, and salt in a bowl.
Add water a little at a time and knead into a soft dough. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a thin circle, dusting with flour as needed.
Cook each thepla on a hot skillet, turning and brushing lightly with oil, until browned spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm or cool completely before packing.

title: Undhiyu
ingredients: 1 cup chopped surti papdi, or flat beans
instructions: Mix the fenugreek leaves, chickpea flour, cilantro, coconut, ginger-green chile paste, coriander, turmeric, chile powder, and half the salt. Shape into small muthia dumplings.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Add carom seeds and asafoetida.
Add the yam, sweet potato, potatoes, eggplant, green beans, flat beans, pigeon peas, and remaining salt; toss to coat.
Add water, cover, and cook over low heat until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 25 minutes.
Add the muthia, cover, and cook until the dumplings and vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes. Serve hot.

title: Khandvi
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, yogurt, water, turmeric, and salt until smooth.
Cook the mixture in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until very thick and glossy, about 10 minutes.
Quickly spread the hot mixture into a thin layer over the backs of two greased baking sheets. Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Cut the set layer into strips and roll each strip into a tight coil.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, and green chile; pour the tempering over the rolls.
Garnish with coconut and cilantro.

title: Gujarati Kadhi
instructions: Whisk the yogurt and chickpea flour until smooth, then gradually whisk in the water.
Pour into a saucepan and stir in turmeric, ginger, green chile, jaggery, and salt.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring often, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried chile, and curry leaves; let them sizzle.
Pour the tempering into the kadhi and simmer for 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Kerala Matta Rice and Parippu Curry
ingredients: 1/2 cup split yellow moong dal, rinsed
3 cups water, plus more for cooking rice
instructions: Cook the matta rice in plenty of water until tender, then drain.
Pressure-cook the moong dal with turmeric and 2 cups water until soft; mash lightly.
Grind the coconut, green chili, and cumin with a little water into a coarse paste.
Stir the coconut paste and salt into the dal; simmer for 5 minutes, adding water to make a thick curry.
Heat the coconut oil; splutter the mustard seeds, then add dried chilies and curry leaves.
Pour the seasoning over the curry and serve with the rice.

title: Avial
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables, cut into batons (such as yam, carrot, green beans, and raw banana)
instructions: Put the vegetables in a pan with turmeric, salt, and 1/2 cup water.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the vegetables are tender but still hold their shape.
Grind the coconut, green chilies, and cumin coarsely with a splash of water.
Fold the coconut mixture into the vegetables and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the yogurt.
Drizzle with coconut oil, add the curry leaves, and cover for a few minutes before serving.

title: Kerala Fish Molee
ingredients: 500 grams firm white fish, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the fish with turmeric and half the salt; set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and soften the onion, ginger, and green chilies.
Add the tomatoes and curry leaves; cook until the tomatoes begin to soften.
Pour in the thin coconut milk, add the remaining salt and pepper, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish in a single layer and simmer gently until just cooked, turning the pieces once if needed.
Stir in the thick coconut milk and lime juice; warm through without boiling, then serve.

title: Puttu with Kadala Curry
ingredients: 1 cup dried black chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
1/2 cup grated fresh coconut, toasted until golden
instructions: Rinse the soaked chickpeas and pressure-cook them with turmeric and 3 cups water until tender.
Mix the puttu flour and salt; sprinkle in water gradually and rub with your fingers until the mixture is moist and crumbly, not doughy.
Layer the flour mixture in a puttu steamer, packing a little grated coconut between layers, and steam for 8 to 10 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan and splutter the mustard seeds.
Add the onion, ginger, green chilies, and curry leaves; cook until the onion softens.
Add the tomato, coriander powder, and chili powder; cook until the tomato breaks down.
Add the cooked chickpeas with enough cooking liquid for a thick curry, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the toasted coconut and serve the curry with the steamed puttu.

title: Appam with Vegetable Stew
ingredients: 2 cups raw rice, soaked for 4 hours
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water with a pinch of sugar and leave until foamy.
Drain the soaked rice and blend it with the cooked rice, grated coconut, and enough water to make a smooth batter.
Stir the yeast mixture, remaining sugar, and salt into the batter; cover and ferment in a warm place until bubbly, about 6 hours.
For the stew, heat the coconut oil and soften the onion, ginger, green chilies, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and curry leaves.
Add the carrot, cauliflower, and potato with the thin coconut milk; cover and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the thick coconut milk and warm gently without boiling; keep the stew warm.
Stir the fermented batter; thin it with a little water if needed so it pours easily.
Pour a ladleful into a hot appam pan, swirl to coat the sides, cover, and cook until the lacy edges are crisp and the center is set.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve the appams with the vegetable stew.

title: Ven Pongal
ingredients: 1 teaspoon whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pot over low heat until fragrant, then add the rinsed rice, water, turmeric, and salt.
Cook covered until the rice and dal are very soft, stirring occasionally and adding a little hot water if needed.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews until golden.
Add the cumin, pepper, ginger, and curry leaves to the ghee; fry briefly until fragrant.
Pour the tempering and cashews over the pongal, mix well, and serve hot.

title: Murungakkai Sambar
instructions: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze and strain the juice.
Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric and 1 1/2 cups water until soft; mash it smooth.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and add the mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, dried chili, and curry leaves.
When the mustard seeds pop, add the onion and cook until softened; stir in the tomato and drumsticks.
Add the tamarind juice, sambar powder, salt, and 1 cup water; simmer until the drumsticks are tender.
Stir in the mashed dal and simmer gently for 5 minutes, adding water if needed.
Finish with chopped cilantro and serve hot with rice.

title: Keerai Masiyal
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach or amaranth leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Put the greens, onion, green chilies, turmeric, salt, and 1/2 cup water in a pot.
Cover and cook over medium heat until the greens are completely tender.
Mash the greens with a wooden masher until soft, then stir in the cooked toor dal.
Heat the sesame oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
When the seeds pop, add the dried red chilies and fry briefly.
Pour the tempering over the greens, stir, and serve with rice.

title: Kara Kuzhambu with Brinjal
instructions: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze and strain the juice.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and add the mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
