When the mustard seeds pop, add the asafoetida, curry leaves, and onion; cook until the onion softens.
Add the brinjals and tomato and cook for 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Stir in the sambar powder, turmeric, and salt, then add the tamarind juice and 1 cup water.
Simmer uncovered until the brinjals are tender and the gravy has thickened, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the jaggery, simmer for 1 minute, and serve with rice.

title: Coconut Chutney
ingredients: 1/2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: Grind the coconut, roasted gram, green chilies, ginger, salt, and water until smooth.
Transfer the chutney to a serving bowl and adjust the thickness with a little water if needed.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When the seeds pop, add the dried red chili and curry leaves; fry briefly.
Pour the tempering over the chutney and serve with idli or dosa.

title: Shukto
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled and cut into batons
1 medium raw banana, peeled and cut into batons
instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a pot until it just begins to smoke, then let it cool slightly.
Fry the bitter gourd until lightly browned; lift it out and set aside.
Add the panch phoron and bay leaf to the pot. When fragrant, stir in the ginger paste.
Add the potato, raw banana, drumsticks, and eggplant; stir gently for 2 minutes.
Mix in the poppy seed paste, mustard paste, sugar, and salt, then pour in the water.
Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the fried bitter gourd and simmer for 2 minutes.
Finish with ghee and crushed radhuni; serve warm with rice.

title: Aloo Posto
ingredients: 500 grams potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-centimeter cubes
instructions: Soak the poppy seeds in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Grind the poppy seeds with 1 green chili and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until shimmering.
Add the nigella seeds and the remaining green chili, slit lengthwise.
Add the potatoes and salt; stir to coat in the oil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Add the poppy seed paste and water, then cover and cook until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Shorshe Ilish
instructions: Soak both kinds of mustard seeds in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Grind the mustard seeds with 1 green chili, a pinch of salt, and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub the hilsa steaks with turmeric and the remaining salt.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it just begins to smoke, then cool for a minute.
Stir the mustard paste with the water and pour it into the pan.
Add the fish and remaining green chilies; spoon sauce over the steaks.
Cover and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, turning the fish once with care.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Cholar Dal
ingredients: 1 cup chana dal, rinsed and soaked for 1 hour
instructions: Drain the soaked dal and add it to a pot with the water and turmeric.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer until tender but still holding its shape, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the salt and sugar.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan; add the bay leaf, cumin seeds, and dried red chilies.
When the spices sizzle, add the ginger and ground cumin; cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the tempering into the dal and stir gently.
Add the grated coconut and garam masala; simmer for 3 minutes.
Serve with luchi or steamed rice.

title: Luchi
instructions: Combine the flour and salt in a bowl, then rub in the ghee.
Add the warm water gradually and knead into a firm, smooth dough.
Cover and rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Divide into 12 balls and roll each into a small, even circle.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan until a small piece of dough rises quickly to the surface.
Slide in one luchi and gently press it with a slotted spoon until it puffs.
Turn once and fry until pale golden, then drain on paper towels.
Repeat with the remaining dough and serve hot.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, for the pasta water
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the salt, and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; turn off the heat.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolk, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the skillet and toss with the guanciale.
Remove the skillet from the heat and quickly stir in the egg mixture, adding a little pasta water until creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 L chicken or beef stock, kept warm
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm stock.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a heavy saucepan; cook the onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are lightly toasted.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has evaporated.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more.
After about 15 minutes, stir in the saffron and its liquid; continue cooking until the rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano; season with salt and serve.

title: Pesto alla Genovese
ingredients: 50 g fresh basil leaves, washed and dried
instructions: Crush the garlic and salt in a mortar until smooth.
Add the pine nuts and crush until finely ground.
Add the basil a handful at a time and pound gently into a paste.
Mix in the Parmigiano and Pecorino.
Pour in the olive oil gradually, stirring until the pesto is smooth.
Toss with freshly cooked pasta, loosening with a little pasta water if needed.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
ingredients: 600 ml whole milk, for the béchamel
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the beef and pork; cook until browned, breaking up the meat as it cooks.
Pour in the wine and simmer until it has evaporated.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, 250 ml milk, salt, and pepper; simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 600 ml milk; simmer, stirring, until thickened, then season with nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Spread a little béchamel in a baking dish, then layer lasagne sheets, meat sauce, béchamel, and Parmigiano.
Repeat the layers, finishing with béchamel and Parmigiano.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling; rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine the cooled espresso and Marsala in a shallow dish.
Briefly dip each ladyfinger in the coffee mixture and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers; repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Toss the hot spaghetti with the guanciale and its rendered fat.
Add the egg mixture, tossing quickly and adding pasta water a little at a time until creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Margherita Pizza
ingredients: 200 g canned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed
250 g fresh mozzarella, drained and torn
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm water and let stand for 5 minutes.
Combine the flour and salt, then add the yeast mixture and olive oil.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise until doubled, about 1½ hours.
Heat the oven to its highest setting, ideally with a pizza stone inside.
Divide the dough in half and stretch each piece into a thin round.
Spread crushed tomatoes over each round and add the mozzarella.
Bake one pizza at a time until the crust is puffed and browned, about 7–10 minutes.
Top with basil and a drizzle of olive oil before serving.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 litres hot beef or chicken stock
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot stock for 10 minutes.
Warm the remaining stock in a saucepan and keep it hot over low heat.
Cook the onion gently in the olive oil and 20 g butter until soft but not browned.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are lightly toasted.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has evaporated.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is absorbed.
After about 10 minutes, stir in the saffron and its soaking liquid.
Continue adding stock until the rice is creamy and al dente, about 18 minutes total.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano.
Season with salt and serve immediately.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 1 large eggplant, cut into 2 cm cubes
Salt, for the pasta water and seasoning
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes and leave them in a colander for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender; set aside.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes; season with salt.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain, reserving ½ cup of pasta water.
Add the pasta and eggplant to the tomato sauce, tossing with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Stir in half the basil and ricotta salata.
Serve topped with the remaining basil and ricotta salata.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with 70 g sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites with the remaining 30 g sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold the egg whites gently into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine the cooled espresso and Marsala in a shallow bowl.
Dip each ladyfinger briefly into the espresso and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolk, Pecorino Romano, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss to coat.
Pour in the egg mixture, tossing quickly; loosen with a little reserved pasta water until glossy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 L chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot stock for 10 minutes.
Warm the remaining stock in a saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Heat the olive oil and 30 g of butter in a heavy pot; cook the onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are lightly toasted.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has been absorbed.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next.
After about 15 minutes, stir in the saffron and its soaking liquid; continue cooking until the rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano; season with salt and serve.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
ingredients: 500 ml whole milk, for the béchamel
50 g unsalted butter, for the béchamel
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the ground beef and pork; cook until browned, breaking up the meat.
Pour in the wine and simmer until it has mostly evaporated.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and 250 ml milk; season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the ragù gently for 1½ to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 500 ml milk; simmer until thickened, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Spread a thin layer of ragù in a baking dish, then layer lasagna sheets, ragù, béchamel, and Parmesan; repeat, finishing with béchamel and Parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and golden; rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 2 medium eggplants, cut into 2 cm cubes
4 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for frying
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the eggplant with salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes; pat dry.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender; set aside.
In the same skillet, gently cook the garlic until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes and oregano; season with salt and pepper, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente; reserve ½ cup pasta water and drain.
Toss the pasta with the tomato sauce, adding pasta water as needed; fold in the eggplant and basil.
Serve topped with ricotta salata.

title: Tiramisù
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with 70 g of sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy; gradually add the remaining 30 g sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the egg whites into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine the cooled espresso and Marsala, if using, in a shallow dish.
Briefly dip each ladyfinger in the coffee and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers; repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining cream.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours; dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk the eggs, yolk, Pecorino Romano, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss; let it cool for about 30 seconds.
Stir in the egg mixture, tossing quickly and adding pasta water a little at a time until creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 L chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot
instructions: Soak the saffron in the warm water for 10 minutes.
Warm the olive oil and half the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft but not browned.

Mix in the Parmigiano-Reggiano and Pecorino Sardo.
Pour in the olive oil gradually, stirring until the pesto is smooth.
Toss with freshly cooked pasta, loosening with a little pasta water if needed.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, salt it, and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss.
Pour in the egg mixture, tossing quickly; add a little pasta water until glossy and creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 liters chicken or vegetable stock, kept warm
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm stock.
Warm the remaining stock in a saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a heavy pot; cook the onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast it lightly.
Pour in the wine and stir until it is absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to absorb before adding more.
After about 15 minutes, stir in the saffron and its liquid; continue cooking until the rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano; season with salt and serve.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the beef and pork; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Pour in the wine and simmer until mostly evaporated.
Stir in the tomatoes, milk, salt, and pepper; simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Cook the lasagna sheets according to package directions if needed, then drain.
Spread a thin layer of béchamel in a baking dish; add a layer of pasta, ragù, béchamel, and Parmigiano.
Repeat the layers, finishing with béchamel and Parmigiano.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 25 minutes; uncover and bake for 15 minutes more.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Ossobuco alla Milanese
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge them lightly in flour.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a heavy pot; brown the shanks on both sides and set aside.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery; cook until softened.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the stock and tomatoes, then return the shanks to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, turning the shanks occasionally, until tender.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley, and garlic to make the gremolata.
Serve the shanks with their sauce, topped with gremolata.

title: Panzanella
ingredients: 300 g stale rustic bread, cut into bite-size pieces
400 g ripe tomatoes, cut into chunks
instructions: Place the bread in a large bowl and sprinkle with a little water; let it soften briefly, then gently squeeze out excess moisture.
Add the tomatoes, red onion, and cucumber to the bread.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper together.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently.
Fold in the basil and let the salad rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove the skillet from the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss to coat.
Take the skillet off the heat, add the egg mixture, and toss quickly, loosening with pasta water until creamy.
Serve immediately with additional Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 L chicken or beef stock, kept warm
instructions: Steep the saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm stock.
Warm the olive oil and half the butter in a saucepan; cook the onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast it lightly.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has mostly evaporated.
Add warm stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often and allowing each addition to absorb before adding the next.
After about 10 minutes, stir in the saffron and its soaking liquid.
Continue adding stock until the rice is creamy and al dente, about 18 minutes total.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmesan; season with salt and serve.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
ingredients: 1.2 L whole milk, for the béchamel
100 g unsalted butter, for the béchamel
100 g all-purpose flour, for the béchamel
A pinch of freshly grated nutmeg
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the beef and pork; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Pour in the wine and simmer until mostly evaporated.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, 250 ml milk, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; simmer gently for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 1.2 L milk; simmer until thickened, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Spread a little béchamel in a baking dish.
Layer lasagna sheets, ragù, béchamel, and Parmesan; repeat, finishing with béchamel and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake until golden, about 20 minutes more.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Pesto alla Genovese
ingredients: 50 g fresh basil leaves, washed and dried
instructions: Place the garlic and a pinch of salt in a mortar and crush to a paste.
Add the pine nuts and crush until smooth.
Add the basil a handful at a time, grinding gently until it forms a green paste.
Mix in the Parmesan and Pecorino.
Pour in the olive oil gradually, stirring until the pesto is smooth.
Taste and adjust the salt; toss with cooked pasta or refrigerate in a sealed container.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine the cooled espresso and Marsala, if using, in a shallow dish.
Briefly dip each savoiardo in the espresso and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the biscuits.
Add a second dipped-biscuit layer and cover with the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Dust generously with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; turn off the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino Romano, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the skillet and toss with the guanciale and its fat.
Remove the skillet from the heat and quickly stir in the egg mixture, adding pasta water a little at a time until creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1.2 liters chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot
instructions: Soak the saffron in the warm water for 10 minutes.
Warm the olive oil and half the butter in a saucepan; cook the onion gently until soft.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has been absorbed.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding more.
Stir in the saffron and its soaking water when the rice is nearly tender.
Cook until the rice is creamy and al dente, about 16–18 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano; season with salt and serve.

title: Pesto alla Genovese
ingredients: 50 g fresh basil leaves, washed and thoroughly dried
20 g Pecorino Sardo or Pecorino Romano, finely grated
instructions: Place the garlic and coarse salt in a mortar and crush to a paste.
Add the pine nuts and crush until smooth.
Add the basil leaves a few at a time and pound gently until a bright green paste forms.
Mix in the grated cheeses.
Pour in the olive oil gradually, stirring until the pesto is smooth.
Toss with freshly cooked pasta, loosening with a little pasta water if needed.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
ingredients: 700 ml whole milk, for the béchamel
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the ground beef and pork; cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Pour in the wine and simmer until mostly evaporated.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and 250 ml milk; season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the ragù gently, partially covered, for 1½–2 hours, stirring occasionally.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 700 ml milk; simmer, stirring, until thickened. Season with salt and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Spread a little ragù in a baking dish, then layer lasagne sheets, ragù, béchamel, and Parmesan.
Repeat the layers, finishing with béchamel and Parmesan.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until bubbling and golden; rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine the cooled espresso with the Marsala, if using.
Briefly dip each savoiardo into the espresso and arrange a layer in a dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the biscuits.
Add a second layer of dipped biscuits and cover with the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Dust generously with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salt, for the pasta water
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the salt, and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; turn off the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss to coat.
Remove the skillet from the heat, add the egg mixture, and toss quickly, loosening with pasta water until creamy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
instructions: Soak the saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm stock.
Warm the butter and olive oil in a heavy saucepan; cook the onion until soft, without browning.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
Pour in the wine and stir until it has evaporated.
Add warm stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often and letting each addition absorb before adding more.
After about 10 minutes, stir in the saffron and its soaking liquid.
Continue adding stock until the rice is creamy and al dente, about 18 minutes total.
Remove from the heat, stir in the Parmesan, and season with salt.
Rest for 2 minutes, then serve.

title: Ribollita
ingredients: 250 g dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight and drained
300 g cavolo nero or kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
250 g stale Tuscan bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Place the soaked beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer until tender, about 60 minutes; reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock, cooked beans, and enough reserved bean liquid to make a hearty soup.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then add the greens and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the bread.
Simmer gently until the bread softens and thickens the soup, about 10 minutes.
Let the soup cool, refrigerate overnight, then reheat gently before serving.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a heavy Dutch oven; brown the shanks on all sides, then transfer them to a plate.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook until softened.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock, bay leaf, and lemon zest.
Return the shanks to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until very tender, about 2 hours, turning once.
Mix the parsley and garlic, then sprinkle over the shanks before serving.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and thick.
Fold the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip each ladyfinger briefly into the cooled espresso and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the biscuits.
Add a second layer of espresso-dipped ladyfingers and cover with the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.
Dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Tagliatelle al Ragù Bolognese
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Mound the flour on a work surface, make a well, and add the eggs.
Beat the eggs with a fork, gradually drawing in flour; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot and cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add both meats and cook, breaking them up, until no longer pink.
Pour in the wine and simmer until evaporated; stir in the tomato paste and milk.
Simmer gently, partially covered, for at least 2 hours, adding a little water if needed; season with salt and pepper.
Roll the dough thin, cut into tagliatelle, and cook in salted boiling water until al dente.
Toss the pasta with the ragù and serve with Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Tortellini in Brodo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 litres homemade capon or chicken broth
instructions: Make a well in the flour, add the eggs, and knead until smooth; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Cook the pork loin in a small pan until just done, then cool completely.
Finely chop the pork, prosciutto, and mortadella; mix with the cheese, egg yolk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin and cut it into small squares, about 4 cm wide.
Place a little filling in the center of each square, fold into a triangle, seal the edges, and join the two corners around a fingertip.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil and cook the tortellini until tender, about 3–5 minutes.
Serve the tortellini hot in their broth.

title: Lasagne Verdi alla Bolognese
ingredients: 100 g cooked spinach, squeezed dry and finely chopped
instructions: Mix the pasta flour, eggs, and spinach; knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in 60 g flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer, stirring, until the béchamel is smooth and thick; season with salt and nutmeg.
Roll the pasta thin and cut into sheets; blanch each sheet briefly in boiling salted water, then cool on a clean towel.
Spread a little béchamel in a baking dish, then layer pasta, ragù, béchamel, and Parmigiano.
Repeat the layers, finishing with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until browned and bubbling; rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Crescentine (Gnocco Fritto)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water and leave for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt, then add the yeast mixture and lard.
Knead until smooth and elastic; cover and let rise for about 2 hours.
Roll the dough about 3 mm thick and cut into diamond shapes.
Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the dough pieces in batches, turning once, until puffed and golden.
Drain briefly and serve warm with prosciutto, salami, and soft cheese.

title: Piadina Romagnola
instructions: Combine the flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Rub in the lard, then add the water gradually and knead until smooth.
Cover and rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each into a thin round about 3 mm thick.
Cook each piadina in a hot, dry skillet for 1–2 minutes per side, pricking any large bubbles.
Serve warm, folded around squacquerone cheese, prosciutto, or other fillings.

title: Bagna Cauda
ingredients: 12 anchovy fillets, rinsed and patted dry
8 garlic cloves, peeled and thinly sliced
1 small head Savoy cabbage, cut into wedges
1 small fennel bulb, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange the cabbage, peppers, celery, carrots, and fennel on a platter.
Put the anchovies, garlic, and olive oil in a small saucepan over very low heat.
Cook gently for about 15 minutes, stirring often, until the garlic is soft and the anchovies dissolve; do not let the mixture brown.
Stir in the butter until melted, then keep the sauce warm over very low heat.
Dip the raw vegetables into the warm sauce at the table.

title: Agnolotti del Plin
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 pound mixed roasted veal, pork, and rabbit, finely chopped
1 cup cooked Swiss chard, squeezed dry and finely chopped
instructions: Mound the flour on a work surface, make a well, and add the eggs and olive oil.
Beat the eggs with a fork, gradually drawing in flour, then knead until smooth; wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the chopped meats, chard, Parmigiano-Reggiano, nutmeg, salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll the dough into thin sheets and place small mounds of filling in a line along each sheet.
Fold the dough over the filling, press around each mound to seal, and pinch between the mounds to form small parcels.
Cut between the pinches and set the agnolotti on a floured towel.
Boil the agnolotti in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and are tender.
Melt the butter with the sage in a skillet; drain the agnolotti and toss gently in the butter.
Serve with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Risotto al Barolo
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon fine salt, or to taste
instructions: Warm the butter and olive oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes, until the grains are glossy.
Pour in the Barolo and stir until it has nearly evaporated.
Add the hot broth a ladleful at a time, stirring often and allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more.
Cook until the rice is creamy but still slightly firm, about 16 to 18 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the Parmigiano-Reggiano and finishing butter.
Taste for salt and serve immediately.

title: Vitello Tonnato
ingredients: 2 tablespoons capers, drained, plus 1 tablespoon for garnish
instructions: Put the veal, carrot, celery, onion, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt in a saucepan and cover with cold water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 1 hour, until the veal is tender.
Let the veal cool in its cooking liquid, then remove and refrigerate until cold.
Blend the mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons capers, anchovies, lemon juice, and olive oil until smooth.
Slice the chilled veal thinly and arrange it on a platter.
Spoon the sauce over the veal and garnish with the remaining capers.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Bonet
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and set a 9-inch loaf pan inside a roasting pan.
Cook 1/2 cup sugar with the water in a small saucepan until it becomes a deep amber caramel.
Pour the caramel into the loaf pan and tilt to coat the bottom.
Warm the milk in a saucepan; whisk in the cocoa until smooth, then remove from the heat.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, remaining 1/2 cup sugar, crushed amaretti, rum, and vanilla in a bowl.
Gradually whisk the warm cocoa milk into the egg mixture.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-lined pan and set the roasting pan in the oven.
Add hot water to the roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the loaf pan.
Bake for about 55 minutes, until just set, then cool and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a serving plate, and serve chilled.

title: Pasta alla gricia
ingredients: 180 g guanciale, cut into short strips
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, salt it lightly, and cook the rigatoni until al dente.
Meanwhile, put the guanciale in a cold skillet and cook over medium-low heat until the fat renders and the pieces are golden.
Add the black pepper to the skillet and stir briefly.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain the rigatoni.
Toss the pasta with the guanciale and a splash of pasta water, off the heat.
Stir in the Pecorino a little at a time, adding more pasta water as needed for a creamy sauce, and serve at once.

title: Pasta e ceci
ingredients: 250 g ditalini or other small pasta
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan and gently cook the onion and celery until soft.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, and rosemary; stir for a minute.
Add the chickpeas and broth, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the rosemary and garlic. Mash some of the chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the broth.
Stir in the pasta and cook until al dente, adding a little hot water if the soup gets too thick.
Season with salt and pepper, rest for a few minutes, and serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Saltimbocca alla romana
ingredients: 8 thin slices veal, about 500 g total
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Lay a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf on each piece of veal, then secure with a toothpick.
Season lightly with pepper and dust the veal side with flour.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Cook the veal prosciutto-side down for about 2 minutes, then turn and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the wine and simmer until the sauce reduces slightly and the veal is cooked through.
Remove the toothpicks and serve with the pan sauce.

title: Carciofi alla romana
ingredients: 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Prepare a bowl of water with the juice of half the lemon.
Trim the artichokes, remove tough outer leaves and choke, and rub the cut surfaces with lemon; keep them in the lemon water.
Mix the mint, parsley, garlic, salt, pepper, and 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Open the artichoke leaves gently and tuck the herb mixture inside each one.
Stand the artichokes upright in a snug saucepan and add the water and remaining olive oil.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 to 45 minutes, until tender when pierced with a knife.

title: Maritozzi con la panna
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, warm milk, orange zest, vanilla, and salt until a rough dough forms.
Knead in the softened butter a little at a time until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1½ to 2 hours.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and shape each into an oval bun; arrange on a lined baking sheet.
Cover and let rise until puffy, about 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden, then brush with warm honey and cool completely.
Whip the cold cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Split each bun lengthwise without cutting all the way through and fill generously with cream.

title: Risi e Bisi
ingredients: 1 cup carnaroli or vialone nano rice
4 cups hot chicken or vegetable broth
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a saucepan; cook the onion until soft.
Add the peas and a ladle of broth; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, until the rice is creamy and just tender, about 16–18 minutes.
Stir in the remaining butter, Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper. Serve slightly looser than risotto.

title: Sarde in Saor
ingredients: 1 pound fresh sardines, cleaned and butterflied
instructions: Season the sardines with salt and lightly coat them in flour.
Heat half the oil in a skillet and fry the sardines in batches until golden; drain on paper towels.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet and cook the onions over low heat until soft and pale golden.
Stir in the vinegar, water, bay leaf, raisins, and pine nuts; simmer for 2 minutes.
Arrange the sardines and onion mixture in layers in a dish, spooning the liquid over them.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours before serving at room temperature.

title: Bigoli in Salsa
ingredients: 12 ounces bigoli or thick whole-wheat spaghetti
6 anchovy fillets packed in oil, drained
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over low heat until very soft, about 20 minutes.
Add the anchovies and stir until they dissolve into the onions.
Pour in the wine and simmer until almost evaporated; season with pepper and little or no salt.
Drain the pasta, reserving a little cooking water, and toss it with the sauce, adding water if needed.

title: Fegato alla Veneziana
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Cook the onions with the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter over low heat until very soft and lightly golden, about 25 minutes.
Raise the heat, add the liver, and cook briefly, turning once, until just browned outside and still tender.
Add the wine and simmer for 1 minute.
Stir in the remaining butter and parsley; season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, traditionally with soft polenta.

title: Baccalà Mantecato
ingredients: 1 pound dried salt cod, soaked in cold water for 24–36 hours with frequent water changes
instructions: Drain the soaked cod and place it in a saucepan with fresh water and the bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the fish flakes easily, about 20 minutes; drain and remove skin and bones.
Flake the cod into a bowl and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon or hand mixer.
Add the olive oil and warm milk gradually while beating, until the mixture is pale and creamy.
Mix in the garlic and parsley, season with pepper, and serve on toasted bread or polenta.

title: Orecchiette with Turnip Greens
ingredients: 1 pound turnip greens, trimmed and washed
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more for the pasta water
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the turnip greens and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the orecchiette to the pot and cook until al dente, following the package timing.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a skillet. Add the garlic, anchovies, and red pepper flakes; stir until the anchovies dissolve.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a small dry pan until golden.
Drain the pasta and greens, reserving a cup of cooking water. Toss them with the anchovy oil, adding a splash of cooking water if needed.
Serve with the toasted breadcrumbs.

title: Fave e Cicoria
ingredients: 1 cup dried split fava beans, rinsed
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more for the greens
instructions: Cover the fava beans with fresh water in a saucepan and add the onion and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently until the beans are very soft, about 1 hour; add hot water as needed.
Remove the bay leaf and mash the beans with a wooden spoon until creamy. Stir in 3 tablespoons of olive oil and the salt.
Boil the chicory in a separate pot of salted water until tender, about 10 minutes, then drain well.
Serve the chicory beside the fava purée and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

title: Tiella Barese with Rice, Potatoes, and Mussels
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Put the mussels in a covered pot over medium heat until they open, about 5 minutes. Strain and reserve the liquid; discard any mussels that stay closed.
Grease a baking dish with a little olive oil. Layer in half the potatoes and onion, then half the tomatoes, parsley, and garlic.
Scatter over half the rice and arrange half the mussels, still in their half shells, on top.
Repeat the layers with the remaining ingredients. Season with salt and pepper, then sprinkle with Pecorino.
Pour in the reserved mussel liquid and enough water to come about halfway up the layers. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Bake until the rice is tender and the top is golden, about 50 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Puddica with Onion and Olives
instructions: Stir the yeast into the warm water and leave for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons of olive oil; knead until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in 1 tablespoon of olive oil over low heat until soft and lightly golden, about 20 minutes. Stir in the olives, oregano, and pepper.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Oil a baking pan and press the dough into it.
Spread the onion mixture over the dough and drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Bake until golden, about 25 minutes.

title: Cartellate with Vincotto
instructions: Combine the flour and salt in a bowl. Pour in the warm wine and olive oil, then knead until the dough is smooth and firm.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin and cut it into strips about 1 inch wide and 12 inches long.
Pinch each strip together at intervals and roll it into a rose shape, pressing the end to seal.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the cartellate in batches until crisp and golden, then drain on paper towels.
Warm the vincotto gently in a small saucepan. Dip or drizzle it over the cartellate and finish with orange zest.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 1 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more for pasta water
instructions: Toss the eggplant with 1 teaspoon salt and leave in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat dry.
Bring the water and pasta salt to a boil. Cook the pasta until al dente, then reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet. Fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender; set aside.
Warm the remaining olive oil in the skillet. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes. Discard the garlic, then stir in the basil and eggplant.
Add the pasta and a splash of reserved pasta water; toss to coat. Serve with ricotta salata.

title: Sarde a Beccafico
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds fresh sardines, cleaned, butterflied, and filleted
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Oil a small baking dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Combine the breadcrumbs, pecorino, raisins, pine nuts, parsley, lemon zest, salt, pepper, and 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Place a spoonful of filling on each sardine fillet and roll it up from tail to head. Arrange the rolls snugly in the dish.
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and bake for 15–18 minutes, until the sardines are cooked and the tops are golden.
Serve warm with lemon wedges.

title: Caponata
ingredients: 1 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
1/3 cup green olives, pitted and halved
instructions: Toss the eggplant with 1 teaspoon salt and leave in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet. Cook the eggplant in batches until browned and tender; set aside.
Add the remaining olive oil and cook the onion and celery for 6–8 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, capers, olives, vinegar, and sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant to the skillet and simmer for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt.
Cool to room temperature, then scatter with pine nuts and basil before serving.

title: Pasta con le Sarde
ingredients: 1 pound fresh sardines, cleaned, filleted, and chopped
1 can (2 ounces) anchovy fillets in oil, drained
1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more for pasta water
instructions: Steep the saffron in the warm water for 10 minutes.
Bring the water and pasta salt to a boil. Cook the bucatini until al dente; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a large skillet. Cook the onion over medium heat until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the anchovies and stir until they break down. Add the sardines and cook for 3 minutes, gently breaking them into pieces.
Stir in the saffron water, raisins, pine nuts, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Toss the pasta with the sardine sauce, adding reserved pasta water as needed. Serve topped with toasted breadcrumbs.

title: Cassatelle di Ricotta
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Mix the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, and salt. Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the egg and wine, mixing until a firm dough forms. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Stir together the ricotta, 1/3 cup sugar, and cinnamon until smooth.
Roll the dough thinly on a lightly floured surface. Cut out 4-inch circles.
Place a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold over, and press the edges firmly together. Seal with a fork.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 350°F. Fry the cassatelle in batches until golden, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Spaghetti alle vongole
ingredients: 1 kg small clams, scrubbed and rinsed
1 small handful fresh parsley, finely chopped
instructions: Soak the clams in cold salted water for 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil with the garlic and red pepper flakes in a wide pan.
Add the clams and wine, cover, and cook until the clams open, about 4 to 6 minutes; discard any that remain closed.
Lift the clams out briefly and remove most from their shells, if desired. Keep the cooking liquid in the pan.
Drain the spaghetti, reserving a cup of pasta water, and add it to the pan with the clam liquid.
Toss over medium heat until the pasta is al dente, adding a splash of pasta water if needed. Stir in the clams and parsley and serve.

title: Pasta e patate
ingredients: 320 g short pasta, such as tubetti
500 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
1.2 litres hot water or light vegetable broth
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion, celery, and carrot until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the potatoes and hot water or broth. Season lightly with salt.
Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes, breaking a few pieces against the pot to thicken the broth.
Add the pasta and cook, stirring often, until al dente; add hot water if the mixture gets too thick before the pasta is done.
Turn off the heat and stir in the provola and Parmigiano until creamy. Rest for a few minutes, then finish with black pepper.

title: Parmigiana di melanzane
ingredients: 1.2 kg eggplants, sliced lengthwise about 5 mm thick
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices lightly and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat them dry.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan. Fry the eggplant in batches until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Warm the olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic, and cook briefly. Add the passata and a pinch of salt; simmer for 20 minutes, then remove the garlic.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a little sauce in a baking dish and add a layer of eggplant.
Top with sauce, mozzarella, Parmigiano, and basil. Repeat the layers, finishing with sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and browned. Let it rest for at least 20 minutes before serving.

title: Gnocchi alla sorrentina
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan and gently cook the garlic until fragrant.
Add the passata and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, then remove the garlic and stir in half the basil.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the gnocchi in batches; remove them with a slotted spoon as they rise to the surface.
Toss the gnocchi with the tomato sauce, mozzarella, and half the Parmigiano.
Transfer to a baking dish, scatter the remaining Parmigiano over the top, and bake for 10 to 15 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned. Finish with the remaining basil.

title: Pizza di scarola
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1 tablespoon for brushing
2 large heads escarole, washed and roughly chopped
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, for the filling
50 g pitted black olives, roughly chopped
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, and water until a rough dough forms. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil and the salt, then knead until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise until doubled, about 1 to 1½ hours.
Cook the escarole in a covered pot with a little water until wilted. Drain very well and squeeze out excess liquid.
Warm 3 tablespoons olive oil in a pan. Add the garlic and anchovies and stir until the anchovies dissolve.
Add the escarole, olives, capers, pine nuts, and raisins. Cook for 5 minutes, season with black pepper, and cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Divide the dough into two pieces, one slightly larger, and roll both out.
Line an oiled 26 cm round pan with the larger piece. Add the filling, cover with the remaining dough, and seal the edges.
Brush the top with olive oil, prick it in a few places, and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Cool slightly before slicing.

title: Ribollita
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
1 small bunch Tuscan kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
1 pound ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 1 (14-ounce) can whole tomatoes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
6 ounces stale country bread, torn into chunks
instructions: Drain the beans, cover with fresh water, and simmer until tender, about 1 hour; reserve the cooking liquid.
Warm the olive oil in a large pot. Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste, then add the kale, cabbage, tomatoes, beans, reserved bean liquid, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently until the vegetables are very tender, about 45 minutes. Remove the rosemary sprig.
Stir in the bread and simmer until it softens and thickens the soup. Let stand, then reheat before serving with olive oil.

title: Pappa al Pomodoro
ingredients: 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
1 1/2 pounds ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped, or 1 (28-ounce) can whole tomatoes
4 cups water or light vegetable broth
8 ounces stale Tuscan country bread, torn into pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over low heat. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant without browning the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, water or broth, and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes as they cook.
Stir in the bread and simmer gently until it breaks down into a thick, soft soup, about 15 minutes.
Remove the garlic if desired, stir in the basil, and season with salt and pepper. Serve warm with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Panzanella
ingredients: 8 ounces stale country bread, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound ripe tomatoes, cut into chunks
1 cucumber, peeled if desired and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: If the bread is very hard, sprinkle it with the water and let it soften slightly; otherwise, use it as is.
Soak the red onion in the red wine vinegar for 10 minutes.
Combine the bread, tomatoes, cucumber, and onion with its vinegar in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil, basil, salt, and pepper, then toss well.
Let the salad stand for 20 minutes so the bread absorbs the juices. Toss again and serve at room temperature.

title: Pici all’Aglione
ingredients: 1 (28-ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1/4 cup finely grated Pecorino Toscano, optional
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat. Add the garlic and cook gently until soft and fragrant, without letting it brown.
Add the red pepper flakes and tomatoes. Season with salt and simmer until the sauce thickens, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the red wine vinegar. Cook the pici in the boiling water until tender, then reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Toss the pici with the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed. Serve with Pecorino if desired.

title: Schiacciata all’Uva
ingredients: 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the pan and top
1 pound black seedless grapes, washed and dried
instructions: Stir the yeast and 2 tablespoons sugar into the lukewarm water and let stand until foamy, about 10 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons olive oil, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Oil a rimmed baking sheet. Divide the dough in half and press one half into the pan.
Scatter half the grapes over the dough. Cover with the remaining dough, press it out, and scatter the rest of the grapes on top.
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil, sprinkle with 2 tablespoons sugar and rosemary if using, and bake at 400°F until golden, about 30 minutes.

title: Tagliatelle al Ragù Bolognese
ingredients: 300 g “00” flour, plus extra for dusting
250 ml beef or chicken broth, as needed
instructions: Mound the flour on a work surface, make a well, and add the eggs. Beat with a fork, gradually drawing in flour, then knead until smooth. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Warm the oil in a heavy pot. Cook the pancetta, onion, carrot, and celery over low heat until soft.
Add the beef and pork. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and no longer pink.
Pour in the wine and simmer until evaporated. Stir in the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Simmer gently, partially covered, for at least 2 hours, adding broth as needed. Stir in the milk toward the end.
Roll the dough thinly, cut into tagliatelle, and cook in salted boiling water until al dente.
Toss the drained pasta with the ragù and serve with Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Tortellini in Brodo
ingredients: 250 g “00” flour, plus extra for dusting
A pinch of freshly grated nutmeg
1.5 litres homemade capon or chicken broth
instructions: Make a smooth dough with the flour and eggs. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Cook the pork loin in a little broth until tender, then cool completely.
Finely mince the pork loin, prosciutto, and mortadella. Mix with the Parmigiano, egg yolk, nutmeg, and a little salt.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into small squares, about 4 cm wide.
Place a small dab of filling in the center of each square. Fold into a triangle, press the edges closed, then wrap the corners around a finger and join them.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil. Add the tortellini and cook until they float and the pasta is tender, about 3–5 minutes.
Serve the tortellini hot in their broth.

title: Lasagne Verdi alla Bolognese
ingredients: 300 g “00” flour, plus extra for dusting
A pinch of freshly grated nutmeg
instructions: Wilt the spinach in a covered pan with a little water. Cool, squeeze very dry, and finely chop.
Combine the spinach, 300 g flour, and eggs. Knead until smooth, wrap, and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Stir in 60 g flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk; simmer until thick. Season with salt and nutmeg.
Roll the dough into thin sheets and cut to fit your baking dish. Briefly cook the sheets in boiling salted water, then lay them on clean towels.
Spread a little béchamel in the baking dish. Layer pasta, ragù, béchamel, and Parmigiano, repeating until the ingredients are used.
Finish with béchamel and Parmigiano. Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Crescentine Modenesi
ingredients: Neutral oil or lard, for frying
instructions: Mix the flour and yeast in a bowl. Add the water, softened lard, and salt; knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1–2 hours.
Roll the dough about 5 mm thick and cut into squares or diamonds.
Heat oil or lard in a deep pan to 175°C.
Fry a few pieces at a time, turning once, until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, traditionally with cured meats and soft cheese.

title: Zuppa Inglese
ingredients: 200 g sponge cake or savoiardi biscuits
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth.
Heat 500 ml milk with the vanilla until steaming. Slowly whisk it into the egg mixture.
Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, whisking, until thick. Divide the custard between two bowls.
Whisk the cocoa and 2 tablespoons milk into one portion of custard. Cover both custards and cool.
Briefly dip pieces of sponge cake or savoiardi in the Alchermes and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread over a layer of vanilla custard, then chocolate custard. Repeat the layers, finishing with custard.
Cover and chill for at least 3 hours before serving.

title: Bagna Cauda
ingredients: 6 garlic cloves, peeled and thinly sliced
1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
1 small celery root, peeled and cut into sticks
instructions: If using salted anchovies, rinse them well and remove the bones.
Put the garlic and olive oil in a small saucepan over very low heat; cook gently until the garlic is soft, not browned.
Add the anchovies and stir until they dissolve into the oil.
Stir in the butter and keep the sauce warm over very low heat.
Arrange the vegetables on a platter and serve with the warm sauce for dipping.

title: Agnolotti del Plin with Roast Meat Filling
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
8 ounces cooked roast beef, finely chopped
4 ounces cooked roast pork, finely chopped
1/2 cup cooked spinach, squeezed dry and finely chopped
1/2 teaspoon fine salt, plus more for pasta water
instructions: Mound the flour on a work surface, make a well, and add the eggs; gradually work the flour into the eggs until a dough forms.
Knead for about 8 minutes until smooth, adding a little water if needed; wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the roast meats, spinach, Parmigiano, egg yolk, nutmeg, and salt for the filling.
Roll the dough into thin sheets and place small mounds of filling along one edge, leaving space between them.
Fold the dough over the filling, press out the air, and pinch between the mounds to seal; cut into small agnolotti.
Boil the agnolotti in salted water until they float and are tender, about 3 minutes.
Melt the butter with the sage in a skillet, then toss in the drained agnolotti and serve.

title: Tajarin with Butter and Sage
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
instructions: Put the flour on a work surface, make a well, and add the yolks, whole egg, and salt.
Mix until a dough forms, adding water a little at a time if needed; knead until smooth, about 10 minutes.
Wrap the dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin, dust it lightly with flour, and cut it into narrow ribbons.
Boil the tajarin in salted water for 1 to 2 minutes, until just tender.
Meanwhile, melt the butter with the sage in a skillet; add a little pasta water to make a glossy sauce.
Drain the pasta, toss it with the butter sauce, and finish with Parmigiano.

title: Risotto al Barolo
ingredients: 5 cups hot beef or vegetable stock
1/2 teaspoon fine salt, or to taste
instructions: Warm the butter and olive oil in a heavy saucepan and cook the onion gently until soft.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes, coating each grain in fat.
Pour in the Barolo and stir until it has nearly evaporated.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is mostly absorbed before adding the next.
Cook until the rice is creamy and tender but still firm at the center, about 16 to 18 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the Parmigiano and finishing butter; season with salt and serve immediately.

title: Bunet (Piedmontese Chocolate Amaretti Pudding)
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and set a loaf pan inside a larger baking dish.
Cook 1/2 cup of the sugar with the water in a small saucepan until it turns amber; pour the caramel into the loaf pan and tilt to coat the bottom.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining 1/2 cup sugar, cocoa, crushed amaretti, milk, rum, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-lined pan and set the larger dish in the oven.
Pour hot water into the larger dish to come halfway up the sides of the loaf pan.
Bake until the pudding is set around the edges with a slight wobble in the center, about 50 minutes.
Cool, refrigerate for at least 4 hours, then loosen the edges and turn out onto a serving plate.

title: Bucatini all’Amatriciana
ingredients: 150 g guanciale, cut into short strips
400 g canned peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it lightly.
Warm the oil in a skillet; add the guanciale and cook gently until crisp and its fat has rendered.
Add the chili, if using, then stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Cook the bucatini until just shy of al dente; reserve a cup of pasta water and drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed.
Take the skillet off the heat, mix in most of the Pecorino, and serve with the rest.

title: Pasta alla Carbonara
ingredients: 150 g guanciale, cut into small strips
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it lightly.
Cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium-low heat until golden and crisp; turn off the heat.
Whisk the yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and black pepper in a bowl.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente; reserve a cup of pasta water and drain.
Add the hot spaghetti to the guanciale and toss.
Off the heat, stir in the egg mixture quickly, loosening with a little pasta water until glossy.
Serve at once with extra Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Cacio e Pepe
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it sparingly.
Toast the black pepper in a wide skillet over low heat for about 1 minute.
Cook the pasta until just shy of al dente; reserve 2 cups of starchy pasta water.
Add a ladle of pasta water to the skillet and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Add the pasta and toss until al dente, adding more water as needed.
Take the skillet off the heat and let it cool for a few seconds.
Gradually toss in the Pecorino, adding small splashes of pasta water until a creamy sauce forms.
Serve immediately with more black pepper.

title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
ingredients: 8 thin slices veal, about 600 g total
instructions: Lay a sage leaf and a slice of prosciutto on each veal slice; secure with a toothpick.
Lightly dust the veal side with flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Cook the veal prosciutto-side down for 1–2 minutes, then turn and cook for about 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer briefly until the sauce is lightly reduced.
Season with black pepper and serve with the pan sauce.

title: Carciofi alla Romana
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Fill a bowl with cold water and squeeze in the juice of half the lemon.
Trim the artichokes, remove the tough outer leaves, cut off the tips, and trim the stems; place them in the lemon water.
Mix the parsley, mint, garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Open the artichoke leaves gently and press some herb mixture between them.
Arrange the artichokes stem-up in a snug saucepan; add the oil, water, and remaining lemon half.
Cover and cook over low heat for 35–45 minutes, until the hearts are tender when pierced.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the cooking juices.

title: Risi e Bisi
ingredients: 1 cup vialone nano or other risotto rice
4 cups chicken or vegetable broth, kept warm
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt 2 tablespoons butter with the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the peas and a ladleful of warm broth; simmer until the peas are nearly tender.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add warm broth a ladleful at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next.
Cook until the rice is creamy and just tender, about 16–18 minutes; keep it looser than a typical risotto.
Stir in the remaining butter, Parmigiano-Reggiano, parsley, salt, and pepper. Serve hot.

title: Sarde in Saor
ingredients: 1 pound fresh sardines, cleaned, butterflied, and patted dry
1/2 cup olive oil, plus more as needed for frying
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more for the sardines
instructions: Season the sardines lightly with salt and pepper, then dredge them in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet and fry the sardines in batches until golden, about 2 minutes per side; drain on paper towels.
Add the onions to the skillet and cook gently until soft and lightly golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, water, raisins, pine nuts, sugar, and salt; simmer for 3 minutes.
Layer the sardines and onion mixture in a shallow dish, spooning the liquid over them.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours before serving, preferably at room temperature.

title: Bigoli in Salsa
ingredients: 12 ounces bigoli or thick whole-wheat spaghetti
6 salted anchovy fillets, rinsed and finely chopped
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over low heat and add the onions.
Cook the onions slowly until very soft but not browned, about 20 minutes; add a splash of water if they begin to stick.
Stir in the anchovies and cook until they melt into the onions.
Pour in the wine and simmer until almost evaporated; season with pepper.
Cook the bigoli in the boiling water until al dente, then drain, reserving 1/2 cup pasta water.
Toss the pasta with the onion and anchovy sauce, adding a little pasta water if needed. Serve hot.

title: Fegato alla Veneziana
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the onions and cook gently, stirring often, until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the liver in a single layer, working in batches if needed.
Cook briefly, about 1 minute per side, until just browned outside and still tender inside.
Stir in the vinegar, parsley, salt, and pepper, then remove from the heat.
Serve immediately with soft polenta or crusty bread.

title: Baicoli
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading
instructions: Stir the yeast into the lukewarm milk with a pinch of the sugar and let stand until foamy, about 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add the yeast mixture, butter, and egg; knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Divide the dough in half and shape each half into a narrow loaf about 12 inches long.
Place the loaves on a lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise until puffy, about 30 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) until lightly golden, about 20 minutes; cool completely.
Slice the loaves very thinly and arrange the slices on baking sheets.
Bake at 300°F (150°C), turning once, until crisp and pale golden, about 25 minutes; cool completely before storing.

title: Orecchiette with Cime di Rapa
ingredients: 1 kg cime di rapa, trimmed and washed
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the cime di rapa and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the orecchiette to the same pot and cook until al dente, following the package timing.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a pan; add the garlic, anchovies, and chili, and cook gently until the anchovies dissolve.
Drain the pasta and greens, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss them with the oil mixture, adding a splash of cooking water if needed, and serve.

title: Focaccia Barese
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the pan and topping
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl; add the yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Knead until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise until doubled, about 1½ hours.
Oil a round baking pan generously and press the dough into it; let rise for 30 minutes.
Press the tomatoes and olives into the dough, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with oregano and salt.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) until golden, about 25–30 minutes.

title: Tiella Barese with Rice, Potatoes, and Mussels
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Open the mussels in a covered pot over medium heat; strain and reserve their liquid, then remove the mussel meat from the shells.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Oil a baking dish and scatter in the onion and half the tomatoes.
Layer in half the potatoes, rice, mussels, parsley, and Pecorino; season lightly with salt and pepper.
Add the remaining tomatoes and potatoes, then drizzle with olive oil.
Pour in the reserved mussel liquid and enough water to just reach the top layer of potatoes.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes; uncover and bake until the potatoes are tender and the top is browned, about 15 minutes more.

title: Pasta e Ceci alla Pugliese
ingredients: 250 g dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
250 g short pasta, such as ditalini
1.2 liters water, plus more as needed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Put the chickpeas, onion, celery, garlic, rosemary, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chickpeas are tender, about 1½–2 hours.
Remove the rosemary and garlic; season the chickpeas with salt and pepper.
Stir in the pasta and cook until al dente, adding hot water if the pot becomes too thick.
Turn off the heat, stir in the olive oil, and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Pasticciotto Leccese
ingredients: 100 g granulated sugar, for the custard
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, 100 g sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Heat the milk until steaming; slowly whisk it into the yolk mixture, then return everything to the pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick; stir in the vanilla and cool completely.
Rub the lard into the flour, 180 g sugar, and baking powder until crumbly; mix in the eggs and lemon zest to make a dough.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes; heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Press dough into greased oval molds, fill with custard, and cover with a dough lid; seal the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 25–30 minutes.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 1 large eggplant, cut into ¾-inch cubes
1 (28-ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
½ teaspoon fine salt, plus more for the eggplant
½ cup fresh basil leaves, torn
instructions: Toss the eggplant with salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes; pat dry.
Heat ⅓ cup olive oil in a large skillet and fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender. Transfer to a plate.
Warm the remaining olive oil with the garlic in the skillet. Add the tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes, then remove the garlic and stir in the basil.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve ½ cup pasta water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the tomato sauce and a splash of pasta water. Fold in the eggplant and serve with ricotta salata.

title: Pasta con le Sarde
ingredients: 1 small fennel bulb, fronds reserved and bulb finely chopped
12 ounces fresh sardine fillets, cleaned and chopped
¼ teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm water
⅓ cup pine nuts, lightly toasted
½ teaspoon fine salt, plus more for the pasta water
instructions: Cook the chopped fennel in salted boiling water until tender, about 8 minutes. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and reserve the water for the pasta.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the anchovies until they dissolve.
Add the sardines and cook gently for 3 minutes. Stir in the fennel, saffron and soaking water, raisins, pine nuts, and salt; simmer for 8 minutes.
Boil the bucatini in the reserved fennel water until al dente, then drain, reserving ½ cup cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the sardine sauce, adding cooking water as needed. Finish with toasted breadcrumbs and chopped fennel fronds.

title: Caponata
ingredients: 1 large eggplant, cut into ¾-inch cubes
¼ cup green olives, pitted and halved
instructions: Toss the eggplant with salt and leave it to drain for 30 minutes; pat dry.
Heat ⅓ cup olive oil in a skillet and fry the eggplant in batches until browned and tender. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Cook the onion and celery over medium heat until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, and capers; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar and sugar, then add the eggplant. Simmer for 5 minutes and adjust the salt.
Cool to room temperature, scatter with pine nuts, and serve.

title: Sarde a Beccafico
ingredients: 12 butterflied sardines, heads and backbones removed
¼ cup raisins, soaked in warm water and drained
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Toast the breadcrumbs in 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet until golden. Transfer to a bowl.
Stir the raisins, pine nuts, parsley, lemon zest, salt, and pepper into the breadcrumbs.
Place a spoonful of filling on each sardine and roll it up, skin side out.
Arrange the rolls snugly in an oiled baking dish, placing a bay leaf between groups of rolls.
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until the sardines are cooked through.

title: Pasta e Ceci alla Siciliana
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook until soft, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and rosemary and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Mash about one-third of the chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Stir in the pasta, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Simmer until the pasta is tender, stirring often and adding a little water if needed.
Remove the rosemary sprig and serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Spaghetti alle vongole
ingredients: 1 kg small clams, scrubbed and rinsed
instructions: Soak the clams in cold salted water for 20 minutes, then rinse and drain them.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just shy of al dente.
Warm the oil, garlic, and red pepper flakes in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add the clams and wine, cover, and cook until the clams open, about 4 minutes; discard any that remain closed.
Lift the clams into a bowl and strain the cooking liquid to remove any grit.
Drain the spaghetti, reserving a cup of pasta water, and add it to the pan with the clam liquid.
Toss over medium heat until the pasta is al dente, adding a splash of pasta water if needed.
Stir in the clams and parsley, then serve immediately.

title: Pasta e patate
ingredients: 320 g short pasta, such as pasta mista
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes
1.2 litres hot water or light vegetable broth
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion, celery, and carrot until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
