Add the potatoes, Parmesan rind, and hot water or broth; season lightly with salt.
Cover partly and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and cook, stirring often, until tender; add hot water as needed to keep the mixture creamy.
Remove the Parmesan rind and stir in the grated Parmesan and black pepper.
Let the pasta rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Polpette al sugo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
800 g canned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess milk.
Mix the bread with the beef, egg, Parmesan, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into 16 small meatballs.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion until soft.
Add the tomatoes and water, season with salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Gently place the meatballs in the sauce, cover partly, and simmer for 35 minutes, turning them once.
Stir in the basil and serve the meatballs with the sauce.

title: Parmigiana di melanzane
ingredients: 1 kg eggplants, cut lengthwise into 5 mm slices
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil with the garlic in a saucepan; add the passata and simmer for 25 minutes, then remove the garlic and season with salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan and fry the eggplant in batches until golden; drain on paper towels.
Heat the oven to 190°C.
Spread a little tomato sauce in a baking dish, then layer eggplant, sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan, and basil.
Repeat the layers, finishing with sauce and Parmesan.
Bake for 35 minutes until bubbling and browned, then rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Migliaccio napoletano
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a 24 cm round cake pan.
Bring the milk, water, butter, and citrus zests to a simmer in a saucepan.
Whisk in the semolina in a steady stream and cook, stirring, until thick, about 5 minutes; remove the zests and cool.
Beat the ricotta and sugar until smooth, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mix in the vanilla and limoncello, if using, then fold in the cooled semolina mixture.
Pour into the pan and bake until set and golden, about 50 minutes.
Cool completely, dust with powdered sugar, and cut into slices.

title: Ribollita
ingredients: 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
1 bunch Tuscan kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
1 small Savoy cabbage, cored and sliced
2 cups cooked cannellini beans, drained, with 1 cup cooking liquid reserved
6 slices stale country bread, torn into pieces
1 teaspoon fine salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the kale, cabbage, beans, bean liquid, and broth. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the greens are tender, about 45 minutes.
Stir in the bread and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until it softens and thickens the soup.
Season with salt and pepper. Let cool, then refrigerate overnight if you can.
Reheat gently, adding a little water if needed. Serve hot with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Pappa al Pomodoro
ingredients: 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
2 pounds ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped, or 1 can (28 ounces) whole peeled tomatoes
4 cups water or light vegetable broth
8 ounces stale unsalted country bread, torn into pieces
1 teaspoon fine salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over low heat. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally and breaking up the tomatoes.
Pour in the water or broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the bread and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the bread breaks down into a thick, soft soup.
Remove the garlic cloves. Stir in the basil and black pepper, then taste and adjust the salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature with olive oil drizzled over each bowl.

title: Pici all’Aglione
ingredients: 1 can (28 ounces) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 teaspoon fine salt, plus more for the pasta water
1/4 cup pasta cooking water, as needed
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over low heat. Add the garlic and cook gently until soft and fragrant, without browning, about 8 minutes.
Add the red pepper flakes and tomatoes. Season with salt and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the pici in the boiling water until just tender, following the package timing. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Add the pici to the sauce and toss over low heat. Loosen with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Serve hot, with an extra drizzle of olive oil.

title: Panzanella
ingredients: 8 ounces stale country bread, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 pound ripe tomatoes, cut into chunks
1/2 teaspoon fine salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the bread in a large bowl. Sprinkle with the water and 1 tablespoon of the vinegar and toss lightly.
Let the bread stand for 10 minutes, then gently squeeze out excess liquid if it is very wet.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion.
Whisk the remaining vinegar with the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Pour over the salad and toss gently.
Fold in the basil and let the salad rest for 20 minutes before serving. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

title: Cantucci
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
1 cup whole almonds, toasted and cooled
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, orange zest, and vanilla. Stir the wet mixture into the dry ingredients until a firm dough forms.
Fold in the almonds. Divide the dough in half and shape each portion into a log about 2 inches wide on a lightly floured surface.
Brush the logs with beaten egg white and bake for 25 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool for 10 minutes.
Cut the logs diagonally into 1/2-inch slices. Lay the slices cut-side down on the baking sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes, turn the slices over, and bake for another 8 to 10 minutes until crisp. Cool completely.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup silken tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Warm the dashi in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming; do not boil.
Whisk the miso with a ladleful of warm dashi until smooth, then stir it into the saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame and heat gently for 2 minutes.
Divide among bowls and garnish with scallions.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Pat the chicken dry and make a few shallow cuts in the thicker parts.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, for 5 minutes.
Turn the chicken and cook for 4 minutes, until nearly cooked through.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce is glossy and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain for 20 minutes.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 15 minutes; turn off the heat and rest for 10 minutes without lifting the lid.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Place a portion of warm rice in your palm, add a little umeboshi paste, and shape into a triangle around the filling.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Beat the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and salt until combined.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt the pan to cover the bottom.
When the egg is mostly set, roll it toward one end of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, pour in another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg mixture is used, rolling the layers together.
Rest briefly, then slice into pieces.

title: Japanese Vegetable Tempura
ingredients: 1 small sweet potato, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
instructions: Pat the vegetables dry and chill them while preparing the batter.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Whisk the egg with the ice-cold water, then lightly stir in 3/4 cup flour; leave the batter lumpy.
Dust the vegetables with the remaining flour.
Dip a few vegetables at a time in the batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until crisp and pale gold.
Drain on a wire rack and serve promptly with tentsuyu.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not let it boil.
Add the tofu and wakame, and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a little hot dashi in a small bowl, then stir it into the saucepan.
Serve hot, topped with green onions.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular or nonstick skillet and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture; when nearly set, roll it to one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg mixture is used, then cook the roll briefly on each side.
Cool slightly and slice into pieces.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot; bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Take a handful of warm rice, add a small amount of umeboshi paste in the center, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger.
Pat the chicken dry and heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, for 5 minutes; turn and cook for 4 minutes.
Pour the sauce into the skillet and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy, about 5 minutes.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Soba Noodles with Dipping Sauce
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the soba according to the package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold water; drain well.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a simmer, then remove it from the heat and chill until cool.
Divide the noodles among serving plates and serve with the dipping sauce, green onions, and wasabi.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until hot but not boiling.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Place the miso in a small bowl, whisk in a ladleful of hot dashi, then stir the mixture into the saucepan.
Warm gently without boiling, sprinkle with scallions, and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and prick the skin lightly with a fork.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 6–8 minutes, until browned; turn and cook for 4 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then remove from the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Divide the warm rice into 6 portions; flatten each portion, add a little umeboshi paste, and shape into a triangle around the filling.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or small skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg toward one side of the pan, then oil the exposed pan lightly.
Pour in another thin layer, lifting the cooked roll so egg flows underneath; roll again when nearly set.
Repeat with the remaining mixture, then let the omelet rest briefly before slicing.

title: Soba Noodles with Dipping Sauce
instructions: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a simmer, stir until the sugar dissolves, then cool it completely.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the soba according to package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold water until cool.
Divide the noodles among plates and serve with the dipping sauce, scallions, and wasabi.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup soft tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not let it boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm for 2 minutes.
Scoop a little hot dashi into a bowl and whisk in the miso until smooth.
Stir the miso mixture into the saucepan, then serve topped with scallions.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and salt until combined.
Lightly oil a nonstick pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg toward one side of the pan, then oil the exposed surface.
Pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg flows underneath; cook and roll again.
Repeat with the remaining mixture, then slice the omelet into pieces.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot and let soak for 20 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt; divide the rice into 6 portions.
Flatten each portion, add a little umeboshi paste to the center, and shape into a triangle around the filling.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and trim any excess fat.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, for 5 minutes; turn and cook for 4 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy, about 5 minutes.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Soba Noodles with Dipping Sauce
instructions: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then simmer for 1 minute; chill until cool.
Boil the soba in a large pot of water according to the package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold running water.
Divide the soba among plates and serve with the chilled dipping sauce, scallions, and wasabi.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup soft tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in water until softened, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Remove a little hot broth, whisk it with the miso until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.
Warm gently without boiling, scatter with scallions, and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and salt.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg toward one end of the pan, oil the exposed pan, and slide the roll back.
Repeat with the remaining egg, rolling each layer around the previous one.
Cook briefly until set, then slice and serve.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot and let soak for 30 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt; take a portion of rice and place umeboshi paste in the center.
Shape the rice into a triangle and wrap with a strip of nori.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl.
Pat the chicken dry and heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, until browned; turn and cook until nearly done.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Hiyayakko (Chilled Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block silken tofu, about 14 ounces, chilled
instructions: Drain the tofu gently and cut it into serving-size pieces.
Arrange the chilled tofu on a plate.
Top with scallions, ginger, and bonito flakes.
Drizzle with soy sauce just before serving.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup silken tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Add the wakame and tofu; simmer for 2 minutes.
Place the miso in a small bowl, whisk in a ladleful of hot stock, then stir the mixture back into the saucepan.
Warm gently without boiling, then garnish with scallions and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, sugar, mirin, and soy sauce until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture; when nearly set, roll it to one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat with the remaining mixture, rolling each layer around the existing omelet.
Cook briefly on all sides, then slice and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar together in a small bowl.
Pat the chicken dry and heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, until browned; turn and cook until nearly done.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy and reduced.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine rice and water in a pot; cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let the rice steam, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt; place a scoop of warm rice in your palm and add a little umeboshi to the center.
Enclose the filling with rice and shape into a triangle; repeat with the remaining rice.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Agedashi Tofu
instructions: Drain the tofu and pat it dry; cut it into 8 pieces.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin together for 2 minutes to make the sauce.
Heat the oil in a pot to 350°F (175°C).
Coat each tofu piece lightly with potato starch and fry in batches until crisp and pale golden.
Drain the tofu on a rack or paper towels and arrange it in serving bowls.
Pour the warm sauce around the tofu and top with scallions and grated daikon.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a little hot dashi in a small bowl, then stir it into the saucepan.
Serve immediately, topped with green onions.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and pierce the skin lightly with a fork.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes, then turn and cook for 4 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until glossy and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Slice and serve with the reduced sauce.

title: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan and soak for 20 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt; shape a portion of rice around a little umeboshi paste into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, soy sauce, and sugar until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular or nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to spread it evenly.
When the surface is nearly set, roll the egg toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan lightly, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until the mixture is used, then cook the roll briefly on all sides.
Cool slightly, slice, and serve.

title: Soba Noodles with Dipping Sauce
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the soba according to the package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold running water; drain well.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a simmer, then remove it from the heat and chill until cool.
Divide the noodles among serving plates.
Serve with the dipping sauce, green onions, and wasabi.

instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not boil.
Add the tofu and wakame, and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a ladleful of hot dashi until smooth, then stir it into the pan.
Serve hot, topped with scallions.

title: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)

Combine the rice and water in a pot; cover and bring to a boil.
