Wet your hands and rub them with salt; place a scoop of warm rice in your palm and make a hollow in the center.
Fill the hollow with umeboshi, cover with rice, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar until combined.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular or nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to coat the bottom.
When the egg is nearly set, roll it toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan lightly, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the mixture is used, then cook the roll briefly to set.
Cool slightly and cut into slices.

title: Chicken Yakitori
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
8 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Thread the chicken and scallions alternately onto the skewers.
Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Grill the skewers over medium-high heat, turning often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Brush the skewers with sauce during the last few minutes of grilling.
Serve hot with any remaining sauce.

title: Soba Noodles with Dipping Sauce
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil and cook the soba according to the package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold running water.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan; bring to a simmer, then cool the dipping sauce.
Divide the noodles among serving plates.
Serve with the dipping sauce, scallions, and wasabi on the side.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Ladle a little hot stock into a bowl and whisk in the miso until smooth.
Stir the miso mixture into the saucepan, remove from the heat, and serve topped with scallions.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes; remove from the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Take a handful of warm rice, place some umeboshi in the center, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Chicken Yakitori
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
8 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened; set aside.
Thread the chicken and scallions alternately onto the skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until the chicken is cooked through.
Brush the skewers with the sauce during the final 2 minutes of grilling and serve.

title: Tonkatsu
ingredients: 4 boneless pork loin cutlets, about 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Season the pork cutlets on both sides with salt and pepper.
Place the flour, beaten eggs, and panko in separate shallow dishes.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly with panko.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the cutlets in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack, slice, and serve with tonkatsu sauce.

title: Tamago-yaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and salt in a bowl until combined.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular or nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to coat the surface.
When the egg is mostly set, roll it toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan lightly, pour in another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg mixture is used, rolling each layer around the previous one.
Cook briefly to set, then transfer to a board, cool slightly, and slice.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a little hot stock until smooth, then stir it into the saucepan.
Warm gently without boiling, top with scallions, and serve.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with salt; shape a portion of warm rice around a little umeboshi paste into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tonkatsu
ingredients: 4 boneless pork loin chops, about 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Pat the pork dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Coat each chop in flour, dip it in beaten egg, then press it into the panko.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the chops in batches for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack, slice, and serve with tonkatsu sauce.

title: Teriyaki Chicken
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce thickens and coats it.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it to serve.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Beat the eggs with the sugar, mirin, soy sauce, and water.
Lightly oil a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or small nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg to one side, oil the exposed pan, and pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg runs underneath.
Repeat until all the egg is used, then cook the roll briefly on all sides.
Cool slightly, slice, and serve.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Place the miso in a small bowl, whisk in a ladleful of hot dashi until smooth, then stir it into the saucepan.
Warm the soup without boiling, garnish with scallions, and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and trim any excess fat.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down, if applicable, for 5 to 6 minutes; turn and cook for 4 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until cooked through and the sauce is glossy and thick.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, dashi, soy sauce, sugar, and salt until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular tamagoyaki pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg toward one side of the pan, oil the exposed surface, and move the roll to the far side.
Add another thin layer of egg, lifting the roll so egg flows underneath; cook until nearly set and roll again.
Repeat with the remaining egg mixture, then cook the roll briefly on all sides.
Cool slightly, slice, and serve.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain for 20 minutes.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Divide the rice into 8 portions; place umeboshi paste in the center of each and shape into a triangle around the filling.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Japanese Pickled Cucumber (Kyuri no Sunomono)
instructions: Thinly slice the cucumbers and toss them with the salt.
Let stand for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the excess liquid.
Stir together the rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumbers with the dressing and chill for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not let it boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a ladleful of hot dashi until smooth, then stir it into the pan.
Serve hot, topped with scallions.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and pierce the skin several times with a fork.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken skin-side down until browned, about 6 minutes.
Turn the chicken and cook until nearly done, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Slice and serve with the reduced sauce.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes; remove from the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt.
Take a handful of warm rice, make an indentation, add a little umeboshi paste, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs, sugar, mirin, dashi, and soy sauce until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular or nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to cover the bottom.
When the egg is nearly set, roll it toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, pour in another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows beneath it.
Repeat until all the mixture is used, then cook the roll briefly on each side.
Cool slightly, slice, and serve.

title: Soba Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Cook the soba in boiling water according to the package directions.
Drain and rinse the noodles under cold water; set aside.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a simmer in a saucepan.
Divide the soba between bowls and ladle the hot broth over it.
Garnish with scallions and nori, then serve immediately.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Warm the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not boil.
Whisk the miso with a little warm dashi in a small bowl until smooth, then stir it into the saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame; warm gently for 2 minutes without boiling.
Divide among bowls and top with scallions.

title: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)
ingredients: 3 tablespoons umeboshi paste or flaked cooked salmon
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes; turn off the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with salt.
Take a portion of warm rice, make a hollow in the center, add a little filling, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the chicken dry and trim any excess fat.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat; add the chicken and cook for 5–6 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Pour the sauce into the skillet and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce thickens and coats it, about 3 minutes.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
instructions: Beat the eggs with the dashi, sugar, and soy sauce until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular or nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg; when it is just set, roll it toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, pour in another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
When the new layer is just set, roll it around the existing omelet; repeat until all the egg is used.
Let the omelet rest briefly, then slice into pieces.

title: Japanese Vegetable Tempura
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Whisk the egg with the ice-cold water; add the flour and stir lightly, leaving some small lumps.
Pat the vegetables dry and dust them lightly with flour.
Dip the vegetables in the batter, letting excess drip off.
Fry in batches for 2–3 minutes until crisp and pale golden; turn as needed.
Drain on a wire rack and serve immediately with tentsuyu.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup soft tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until steaming; do not boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a ladleful of hot dashi until smooth, then stir it into the pan.
Add the scallions and serve immediately.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Pat the chicken dry and cut each thigh into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes per side.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until glossy and thickened, 3 to 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain for 15 minutes.
Combine the rice and water in a pot; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt; shape a handful of rice into a triangle around a small amount of umeboshi paste.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Beat the eggs with the dashi, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar.
Lightly oil a rectangular or small nonstick skillet and heat over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg; when mostly set, roll it to one side of the pan.
Oil the empty part of the pan, pour in another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Roll the new layer around the existing roll; repeat until all the egg is used.
Cook briefly to set, then slice and serve.

title: Soba Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Cook the soba in boiling water according to the package directions; drain and rinse under cold water.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Divide the noodles between two bowls and pour the hot broth over them.
Top with scallions and nori, then serve.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi in a saucepan until hot but not boiling.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a little hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pan.
Warm without boiling, top with green onions, and serve.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let the rice steam, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands, rub them with salt, and shape a portion of rice into a triangle around a little umeboshi paste.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Pat the chicken dry and heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Pour the sauce into the skillet and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce thickens and coats it.
Slice the chicken and serve with the remaining glaze.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and salt.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg to one side, oil the exposed pan, and pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg is cooked, then shape the roll and slice.

title: Soba Noodle Soup
instructions: Cook the soba noodles according to the package directions, then drain and rinse briefly under cool water.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a simmer in a saucepan.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pour the hot broth over them.
Top with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame; simmer for 2 minutes.
Place the miso in a small bowl, whisk in a ladleful of hot broth, then stir the mixture into the saucepan.
Warm gently without boiling, top with scallions, and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and trim any excess fat.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken for 5–7 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce thickens and coats it.
Slice the chicken and spoon the sauce over it.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, sugar, and soy sauce until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular skillet and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and cook until nearly set.
Roll the egg toward one side of the pan, oil the exposed surface, then move the roll back to the opposite side.
Pour in another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg flows beneath it; cook and roll again.
Repeat with the remaining mixture, then cool slightly and slice.

title: Onigiri
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot and let stand for 20 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes; fluff the rice.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt. Shape a small portion of rice around a little umeboshi paste into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Soba Noodle Soup
instructions: Cook the soba in a pot of boiling water according to the package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse briefly under cold water.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a simmer in a saucepan.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pour the hot broth over them.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately.

title: Hakata Mizutaki
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 lb, cut into serving pieces
1 small head napa cabbage, cut into chunks
1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Put the chicken, water, and kombu in a large pot and bring slowly to a gentle simmer.
Remove the kombu just before the water boils, then skim the surface.
Simmer the chicken uncovered for 1½ hours, skimming occasionally, until the broth is rich and the meat is tender.
Add the cabbage, tofu, leeks, and shiitake; simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Add the mizuna and cook for 1 minute.
Serve the chicken and vegetables with ponzu, green onion, and lemon.

title: Hakata Goma Saba
ingredients: 1 lb sashimi-grade mackerel fillet, skin removed and thinly sliced
1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Grind the sesame seeds coarsely in a mortar.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Toss the mackerel gently with the sesame dressing and chill for 10 minutes.
Serve over rice or on a small plate, topped with green onion and nori.

title: Hakata Udon with Gobō Tempura
ingredients: 1 large burdock root, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the udon according to the package directions; drain and rinse briefly.
Bring the dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt to a simmer; keep the broth hot.
Whisk the tempura flour and ice-cold water just until combined.
Dip small bundles of burdock matchsticks in the batter.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry the burdock in batches until crisp and lightly golden; drain well.
Divide the udon among bowls, pour over the hot broth, and top with burdock tempura and green onion.

title: Chicken Mizutaki Zosui
ingredients: 1½ cups cooked short-grain rice, rinsed briefly
instructions: Bring the broth and shredded chicken to a gentle boil in a pot.
Add the rice, salt, and soy sauce; simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drizzle in the beaten egg and cook until just set.
Turn off the heat and scatter the green onion over the porridge.

title: Karashi Mentaiko Tamagoyaki
ingredients: 1 oz karashi mentaiko, roe removed from the sac
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, soy sauce, and sugar.
Warm a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt the pan to cover the bottom.
When the egg is nearly set, place some mentaiko along one edge and roll the egg over it.
Push the roll to one side, oil the pan lightly, and add another thin layer of egg.
Lift the roll so uncooked egg flows underneath, then roll again; repeat until the egg mixture is used.
Cook briefly to set, then slice into pieces and serve warm.

title: Goya Champuru
ingredients: 1 medium bitter melon (goya), halved, seeded, and thinly sliced
7 ounces firm tofu, drained and patted dry
instructions: Toss the bitter melon with salt and let it stand for 10 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Tear the tofu into rough chunks and dry-fry in a skillet until lightly browned; set aside.
Heat the oil in the skillet and cook the pork until browned.
Add the bitter melon and stir-fry until crisp-tender.
Return the tofu to the skillet and add the soy sauce.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set; finish with bonito flakes.

title: Rafute (Okinawan Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Place the pork in a pot, cover with water, and simmer for 10 minutes; drain and rinse.
Put the pork in a clean pot with the dashi and ginger.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the pork is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the awamori, soy sauce, and brown sugar.
Simmer uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes, turning the pork occasionally, until the sauce is glossy.

title: Okinawa Soba
ingredients: 2 tablespoons soy sauce, for the pork
1 sheet beni shoga (red pickled ginger), sliced
instructions: Simmer the pork belly in water until tender, about 45 minutes; drain and slice.
Warm the brown sugar and 2 tablespoons soy sauce in a small pan, add the pork, and simmer until glazed.
Bring the dashi to a simmer and season with 2 tablespoons soy sauce and the salt.
Cook the noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls.
Pour the hot broth over the noodles and top with glazed pork, scallions, and beni shoga.

title: Jimami Tofu (Peanut Tofu)
ingredients: 1 cup raw peanuts, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Blend the peanuts with the water until smooth, then strain through a fine cloth or sieve into a saucepan.
Whisk the kuzu starch and salt into the peanut liquid until no lumps remain.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until very thick and glossy, about 10 minutes.
Pour into a lightly oiled dish and chill until firm, at least 2 hours.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, and dashi for 2 minutes to make a sauce.
Cut the chilled tofu into pieces and serve with the sauce and ginger.

title: Ninjin Shirishiri (Okinawan Carrot Stir-Fry)
instructions: Shred the carrots into thin matchsticks using a slicer or coarse grater.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and stir-fry the carrots until softened but still slightly crisp.
Add the tuna, soy sauce, mirin, and salt; toss to combine.
Push the mixture to one side, pour the eggs into the empty space, and scramble until nearly set.
Fold the eggs through the carrots and cook until just set.

title: Hiroshima-Style Okonomiyaki
ingredients: 2 tablespoons okonomiyaki sauce, plus more for serving
instructions: Whisk the flour and dashi into a smooth batter.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle over medium heat and spread a thin circle of batter.
Layer on the cabbage, bean sprouts, tenkasu, and green onion; drizzle with a little batter.
Lay the pork belly on top and cook until the base is set, about 4 minutes.
Carefully flip the pancake and cook until the pork is browned and the cabbage has softened.
Fry the yakisoba noodles beside the pancake, stir in 2 tablespoons okonomiyaki sauce, and shape the noodles into a round.
Set the pancake on the noodles, then fry the egg and place it on top.
Flip the assembled okonomiyaki so the egg is on top; brush with more sauce and finish with aonori and bonito flakes.

title: Kaki-no-Dotenabe (Hiroshima Oyster Miso Hot Pot)
ingredients: 1/2 napa cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces
1 bunch shungiku (chrysanthemum greens), cut into 2-inch lengths
1 package (8 ounces) firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Rinse the oysters gently and drain them well.
Mix the hatcho miso and white miso with the mirin and sake to make a thick paste.
Spread the miso paste around the inside rim of a donabe or heavy pot.
Pour the dashi into the pot without washing the miso down from the rim.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer and add the cabbage, tofu, and enoki mushrooms.
As the vegetables cook, stir a little miso from the rim into the broth to season it.
Add the oysters and shungiku and simmer gently until the oysters are just cooked through.

title: Anago Meshi (Conger Eel Rice)
ingredients: 2 cooked conger eel fillets (about 10 ounces total)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain it.
Cook the rice with 2 cups water in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small saucepan and simmer until slightly syrupy.
Brush the eel fillets with some of the sauce and broil or grill until hot and lightly glazed.
Slice the eel into strips.
Spoon the rice into bowls, arrange the eel on top, and drizzle with the remaining sauce.
Sprinkle with sansho pepper and serve.

title: Hiroshima Oysters with Ponzu
instructions: Rinse the oysters gently and pat them dry.
Coat each oyster lightly with potato starch and shake off any excess.
Bring the water and sake to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Poach the oysters in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until just opaque and plump.
Drain the oysters and let them cool slightly.
Serve with ponzu, grated daikon, and sliced green onion.

title: Hiroshima Lemon Nabe
ingredients: 1 pound skinless cod fillets, cut into chunks
1/2 napa cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces
1 package (8 ounces) firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin in a donabe or heavy pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the napa cabbage, tofu, mushrooms, and leek.
Simmer until the vegetables begin to soften, about 8 minutes.
Add the cod and cook gently until it flakes easily, about 5 minutes.
Lay the lemon slices over the hot pot and simmer for 1 minute.
Serve hot, taking care not to simmer the lemon for too long, so the broth stays bright.

title: Zunda Mochi
ingredients: 1 cup shelled edamame, fresh or frozen
2 tablespoons water, plus more as needed
instructions: Boil the edamame until tender, then drain and remove any tough skins.
Mash the edamame with the sugar, salt, and water until chunky or smooth, as you prefer.
Boil the mochi until soft, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Drain the mochi and coat it generously with the zunda mixture.

title: Sendai Miso Yaki Onigiri
ingredients: 2 cups Japanese short-grain rice, rinsed and cooked
instructions: Mix the miso, mirin, and sugar in a small bowl.
Wet your hands and shape the rice into 4 firm triangles.
Brush a thin layer of oil over a skillet and heat it over medium heat.
Toast the onigiri for 2 to 3 minutes per side until lightly crisp.
Brush the tops with miso mixture and cook briefly, turning once, until fragrant and glazed.

title: Harako Meshi
ingredients: 1 pound salmon fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Combine the soy sauce, sake, mirin, sugar, and water in a saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes; lift it out and set aside.
Strain the cooking broth into a rice cooker, add the rinsed rice, and cook according to the cooker directions, adding water if needed to reach the usual level.
Fluff the rice and fold in the cooked salmon.
Serve topped with salmon roe and mitsuba.

title: Sendai-style Imoni
ingredients: 1 pound taro, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 pound konnyaku, torn into bite-size pieces
instructions: Rinse the konnyaku and boil it for 2 minutes, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a simmer in a pot and add the taro and konnyaku.
Cook until the taro is almost tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the beef, leek, soy sauce, sake, and sugar; simmer until the beef is cooked and the leek is tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot.

title: Oysters with Sendai Miso Hot Pot
ingredients: 12 ounces shucked oysters, rinsed and drained
1/2 pound firm tofu, cut into cubes
1/4 head napa cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces
4 shiitake mushrooms, stems removed and caps sliced
instructions: Whisk the miso, sake, and sugar with a ladleful of dashi until smooth.
Bring the remaining dashi to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the cabbage, leek, shiitake mushrooms, and tofu; simmer until the vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in the miso mixture and add the oysters.
Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, just until the oysters are cooked through, and serve hot.

title: Shōgayaki (Ginger Pork)
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, ginger, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork in a single layer and cook until nearly done, turning once.
Pour in the sauce and cook, turning the pork, until glazed and cooked through.
Serve with shredded cabbage.

title: Nikujaga (Beef and Potato Simmer)
ingredients: 1 lb potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the beef until it just changes color.
Add the potatoes, onion, and carrot, and stir briefly.
Pour in the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Bring to a simmer, skim off any foam, and cover loosely.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the broth has reduced.

title: Tamagoyaki (Rolled Japanese Omelet)
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, sugar, and soy sauce.
Lightly oil a rectangular pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to spread it.
When nearly set, roll the egg toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg is used, then cook the roll briefly on each side.
Transfer to a board, cool slightly, and slice.

title: Miso Shiru (Tofu and Wakame Miso Soup)
ingredients: 7 oz silken tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a saucepan.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm gently for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and whisk the miso into the soup until dissolved.
Serve topped with scallions.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls with Salted Salmon)
ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt, plus more for shaping
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot and let stand for 20 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Season the salmon with salt and broil or pan-cook until done; flake it and remove any bones.
Wet your hands and sprinkle them with salt. Place a scoop of warm rice in your palm, add salmon to the center, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori.

title: Osaka-Style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Whisk the flour, dashi, and eggs into a smooth batter.
Fold in the cabbage until evenly coated.
Heat the oil on a griddle or large skillet over medium heat.
Spread half the batter into a thick round and arrange half the pork on top.
Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, flip, and cook until browned and cooked through; repeat with the remaining batter and pork.
Brush with okonomiyaki sauce, drizzle with mayonnaise, and finish with aonori and bonito flakes.

title: Takoyaki
ingredients: 6 ounces cooked octopus, cut into small pieces
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, dashi, eggs, and soy sauce into a thin batter.
Heat and oil a takoyaki pan over medium heat, filling each cup with batter and letting some spill over the edges.
Add octopus, pickled ginger, green onion, and tenkasu to each cup.
As the batter sets, turn each ball with skewers, tucking in the loose batter; keep turning until round and golden.
Serve hot with takoyaki sauce, mayonnaise, aonori, and bonito flakes.

title: Kitsune Udon
instructions: Simmer 1 cup dashi with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons mirin, and sugar.
Add the aburaage and simmer for 8 minutes, turning once; set aside in the broth.
Bring 4 cups dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to a gentle simmer.
Cook the udon according to the package directions and divide among four bowls.
Pour the hot broth over the noodles and top each bowl with aburaage and green onion.

title: Buta no Shogayaki
instructions: Mix the ginger, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork in batches and sear until nearly cooked through.
Pour in the ginger sauce and turn the pork until coated and glazed.
Serve with shredded cabbage and bowls of rice.

title: Osaka-Style Butajiru
ingredients: 8 ounces thinly sliced pork belly, cut into bite-size pieces
1 small daikon, peeled and cut into thin half-moons
1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin half-moons
1/2 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork until it begins to brown.
Add the daikon, carrot, and onion and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the dashi, bring to a simmer, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, dissolve the miso in a ladleful of broth, and stir it back into the pot.
Serve hot, topped with green onion.

title: Yudofu (Kyoto-Style Simmered Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block (14 ounces) soft tofu, cut into large cubes
instructions: Wipe the kombu with a damp cloth, leaving its white surface intact.
Place the kombu and water in a pot and let stand for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and warm gently over low heat until steaming; do not let the water boil.
Lift the tofu into small bowls and serve with ponzu, scallions, and ginger.

title: Nishin Soba (Herring Soba)
ingredients: 2 dried herring fillets, about 5 ounces total
instructions: Rinse the herring and simmer it with water, sake, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, sugar, and 2 tablespoons mirin for 15 minutes.
Cook the soba according to the package directions, then rinse briefly and drain.
Heat the dashi with the remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 2 tablespoons mirin until steaming.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pour over the hot broth.
Top each bowl with a herring fillet and sliced scallions.

title: Obanzai: Komatsuna and Aburaage Simmered in Dashi
ingredients: 1 bunch komatsuna, about 10 ounces, cut into 2-inch lengths
1 piece aburaage, about 1 ounce, blanched and cut into strips
instructions: Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a gentle simmer in a small pot.
Add the aburaage and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the komatsuna and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until tender but still green.
Serve warm or at room temperature with a little of the cooking broth.

title: Kyo-imo no Taitan (Kyoto Taro Simmer)
ingredients: 1 pound taro roots, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Rub the peeled taro with the salt, rinse well, and drain.
Place the taro and dashi in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Cover and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, until the taro is tender.
Let the taro cool in the broth for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Kyo-tsukemono: Shibazuke-Style Eggplant Pickles
ingredients: 1 tablespoon red shiso leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Toss the eggplant with the salt and leave it for 30 minutes.
Squeeze the eggplant gently to remove excess liquid.
Mix the ume plum vinegar, shiso, and sugar in a bowl.
Add the eggplant and toss well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Ishikari Nabe (Salmon and Miso Hot Pot)
ingredients: 1 lb salmon, cut into bite-size pieces
2 potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
8 oz firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Bring the dashi, sake, potatoes, onion, and carrot to a simmer in a large pot.
Cook until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir a ladleful of hot broth into the miso, then return the mixture to the pot.
Add the cabbage, tofu, and salmon; simmer gently until the salmon is cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Top with butter and scallions, and serve hot.

title: Zangi (Hokkaido-Style Fried Chicken)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, sake, ginger, and garlic in a bowl.
Add the chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Stir the beaten egg into the chicken, then coat each piece with potato starch.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C) in a heavy pot.
Fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Hokkaido Butter Corn Ramen
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the ground pork until browned.
Warm the broth in a saucepan; whisk in the miso and soy sauce.
Boil the ramen noodles according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide the noodles between two bowls and pour over the broth.
Top with pork, corn, butter, scallions, and nori.

title: Kabocha Nimono (Simmered Kabocha Squash)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb kabocha squash, seeded and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Arrange the kabocha pieces skin-side down in a saucepan in a single layer.
Add the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and sake.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Remove the lid and simmer briefly until the liquid is slightly reduced.
Let the squash rest in the broth for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Hokkaido Salmon Chan Chan Yaki
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb salmon fillet, cut into 4 portions
instructions: Mix the miso, sugar, sake, and mirin in a small bowl.
Spread the cabbage, onion, carrot, and mushrooms in a large skillet.
Set the salmon portions on top and spread the miso mixture over them.
Dot with butter, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Gently mix the vegetables with the sauce and serve.

title: Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen
ingredients: 8 cups water, plus more for blanching
instructions: Cover the bones and trotters with water, bring to a boil, and cook for 10 minutes; drain and rinse them well.
Put the bones, trotters, onion, ginger, garlic, and 8 cups water in a large pot. Simmer vigorously for 8 to 10 hours, adding water as needed, until the broth is rich and cloudy.
Strain the broth and season each serving bowl with 1 tablespoon tare.
Cook the noodles according to their package directions and divide them among the bowls.
Pour hot broth over the noodles and top with chashu, ramen egg, green onion, and sesame seeds.

title: Motsunabe
ingredients: 1 lb beef or pork offal, cleaned and cut into bite-size pieces
1 bunch garlic chives, cut into 2-inch lengths
1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, blanch the offal for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse it.
Mix the dashi, soy sauce, miso, sake, and mirin in a wide pot.
Add the offal, cabbage, tofu, garlic, and chile. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the garlic chives and cook for 2 minutes, until just wilted.
Add the champon noodles to the remaining broth and simmer until tender.

title: Goma Saba (Mackerel with Sesame Soy Sauce)
ingredients: 1 lb very fresh sashimi-grade mackerel, skin removed and thinly sliced
1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Grind the sesame seeds coarsely in a mortar.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and grated ginger.
Gently toss the mackerel with the sesame sauce and chill for 10 minutes.
Serve topped with green onion and nori.

title: Karashi Mentaiko Tamagoyaki
instructions: Beat the eggs with the dashi, soy sauce, and sugar.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium-low heat and pour in a thin layer of egg.
When the egg is nearly set, place a strip of mentaiko near one edge and roll the egg around it.
Push the roll to one side, oil the pan lightly, and add another thin layer of egg, lifting the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until the egg mixture is used, then cook the roll briefly on all sides and slice.

title: Hakata Zoni
ingredients: 4 tbsp dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and drained
instructions: Bring the dashi, soy sauce, sake, and salt to a gentle simmer.
Add the taro, carrot, and shiitake mushrooms and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the yellowtail and simmer gently until just cooked, about 4 minutes.
Grill or toast the mochi until puffed and lightly browned.
Divide the mochi and mizuna among bowls, ladle in the hot soup and toppings, and serve.

title: Gōyā Champurū
ingredients: 1 medium gōyā (bitter melon), halved, seeded, and sliced
instructions: Toss the gōyā with salt, rest for 10 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Wrap the tofu in a clean towel and press gently to remove excess water; tear it into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and brown the tofu; transfer it to a plate.
Stir-fry the pork until cooked through, then add the gōyā and cook until just tender.
Return the tofu to the pan; add the awamori and soy sauce and toss together.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set; finish with bonito flakes.

title: Rafutē (Okinawan Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 800 g pork belly, in one piece
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot, cover with water, and simmer gently for 1 hour; drain and let it cool enough to handle.
Cut the pork into thick slices.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and briefly brown the pork on both sides.
Add the awamori, dashi, ginger, and brown sugar; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, then add the soy sauce.
Continue simmering gently for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, turning the pork occasionally, until tender and glossy.

title: Ninjin Shirishiri
instructions: Shred the carrots into thin strips with a shirishiri slicer or box grater.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Add the carrots and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until softened but not mushy.
Add the soy sauce, mirin, and salt; toss to coat.
Push the carrots to one side, pour the eggs into the pan, and scramble until just set.
Mix the eggs through the carrots and finish with bonito flakes.

title: Jūshī (Okinawan Mixed Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups short-grain rice, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup hot water, for soaking the mushrooms
1 3/4 cups dashi, including the mushroom soaking liquid
instructions: Soak the shiitake in the hot water until soft; reserve the soaking liquid, discard the stems, and dice the caps.
Put the rice in a rice cooker and add the pork, shiitake, carrot, and konnyaku.
Stir the soy sauce, awamori, mirin, and salt into the dashi and mushroom soaking liquid; add enough to make 1 3/4 cups total liquid.
Pour the seasoned liquid into the rice cooker without stirring the rice.
Cook on the regular rice setting; when done, let stand for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently and serve.

title: Mimigā (Pork Ear with Cucumber)
instructions: Place the pork ear in a pot, cover with water, add 1 teaspoon salt, and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes until tender.
Drain the pork ear, cool it, and slice it into very thin strips.
Toss the cucumber with 1 teaspoon salt and let stand for 10 minutes; rinse briefly and squeeze out excess water.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar in a bowl.
Add the pork ear and cucumber and toss to coat.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and chill briefly before serving.

title: Hiroshima-Style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Whisk the flour, water, and salt into a thin batter.
Heat a large griddle or skillet over medium heat and grease with a little oil.
Spread a thin circle of batter, then layer on cabbage, bean sprouts, and pork belly.
Cook until the bottom is golden, then carefully flip and cook until the pork is done.
Stir-fry the noodles with a little oil on the griddle and shape them into a circle.
Set the cabbage pancake on top of the noodles.
Fry the eggs beside the pancake, break the yolks, and set the pancake on top of the eggs.
Brush with okonomiyaki sauce and finish with mayonnaise, aonori, and bonito flakes.

title: Kaki no Dote-nabe (Oyster Miso Hot Pot)
ingredients: 1/2 pound firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 bunch shungiku or chrysanthemum greens, trimmed
instructions: Mix the red miso, white miso, mirin, and sake into a smooth paste.
Spread the miso paste around the inside rim of a heavy pot.
Add the dashi, ginger, tofu, cabbage, and shiitake mushrooms.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the oysters and shungiku and simmer gently until the oysters are just cooked through.
Stir some of the miso from the pot’s rim into the broth to season it, then serve hot.

title: Anago Meshi (Conger Eel Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with the water in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger in a small saucepan.
Simmer the sauce until slightly syrupy, about 5 minutes.
Brush the eel with some sauce and broil or grill briefly until heated and lightly caramelized.
Spoon the rice into bowls and arrange the eel on top.
Drizzle with the remaining sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Hiroshima Takana Rice
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with the water.
Heat the sesame oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped takana and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce and sesame seeds, then remove from the heat.
Fold the takana mixture into the hot rice.
Serve topped with strips of nori.

title: Hiroshima-style Gansu (Fried Fish Cake)
ingredients: 1 pound boneless white fish fillets, such as cod
instructions: Pat the fish dry and finely mince it, or pulse it in a food processor until smooth.
Mix the fish with the onion, carrot, salt, pepper, cornstarch, and egg.
Shape the mixture into 8 oval patties.
Coat each patty in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently so they adhere.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the patties in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Sendai-Style Zunda Mochi
ingredients: 2 cups shelled edamame, fresh or frozen
2 tablespoons water, plus more as needed
8 pieces kirimochi or other plain mochi
instructions: Boil the edamame until tender, about 5 minutes; drain and slip off any tough skins.
Pound or pulse the edamame with the sugar and salt until coarsely mashed, adding water a little at a time until thick and spoonable.
Boil the mochi according to its package directions until soft, then drain.
Spoon the zunda over the warm mochi and serve.

title: Sendai Miso-Yaki Onigiri
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Sendai miso or other dark miso
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear, then cook it according to the package directions.
Mix the miso, mirin, and sugar in a small bowl.
With damp hands, shape the warm rice into 4 firm triangular rice balls.
Brush a skillet lightly with oil and toast the rice balls over medium heat until lightly crisp on both sides.
Brush the tops with miso mixture and cook briefly, miso-side up, until fragrant; turn and cook the other side briefly.

title: Harako Meshi (Salmon and Salmon Roe Rice)
ingredients: 300 grams salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear and drain well.
Combine the soy sauce, sake, mirin, sugar, and dashi in a saucepan; bring to a simmer.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 4 minutes; lift out the salmon and reserve the broth.
Put the rice in a rice cooker or pot and add enough reserved broth to reach the usual level for 2 cups of rice; cook until tender.
Flake the salmon into large pieces and arrange it over the cooked rice with the ikura and mitsuba before serving.

title: Sendai Seri Nabe
ingredients: 300 grams chicken thigh, cut into bite-size pieces
1 bunch Sendai seri (Japanese parsley), roots scrubbed clean and separated from stems and leaves
1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 package shirataki noodles, rinsed and drained
instructions: Bring the dashi, soy sauce, sake, mirin, and salt to a simmer in a hot pot.
Add the chicken and simmer until nearly cooked through, skimming any foam.
Add the tofu and shirataki and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the seri roots and simmer until tender, about 2 minutes.
Add the seri stems and leaves and cook just until wilted; serve hot from the pot.

title: Sendai Abura-fu Donburi
ingredients: 4 pieces Sendai abura-fu (fried wheat gluten), cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a skillet and bring to a simmer.
Add the onion and abura-fu and simmer until the onion is soft and the abura-fu has absorbed some broth, about 6 minutes.
Pour the beaten eggs evenly over the mixture and cover the skillet.
Cook over low heat until the eggs are softly set, about 2 minutes.
Spoon over bowls of hot rice and finish with mitsuba or scallions.

title: Shōgayaki (Ginger Pork)
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, ginger, and sugar.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the pork in a single layer and cook until no longer pink, turning once.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, turning the pork to coat, until glossy.
Serve hot with rice and shredded cabbage.

title: Nikujaga (Beef and Potato Stew)
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook just until its color changes.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and dashi.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Let stand for a few minutes before serving.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and mirin without making them foamy.
Lightly oil a rectangular omelet pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt the pan to spread it.
When the egg is mostly set, roll it toward one end of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the egg is used, then gently brown the roll on all sides.
Rest briefly, then slice into pieces.

title: Miso Shiru (Tofu and Wakame Miso Soup)
ingredients: 7 oz silken tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water until softened, then drain.
Bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm gently without boiling.
Ladle a little hot dashi into a bowl and dissolve the miso in it.
Stir the miso mixture back into the pot and turn off the heat.
Top with scallions and serve.

title: Onigiri (Salted Rice Balls)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Combine the rice and water in a pot and let soak for 20 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and rub a little salt onto your palms.
Shape warm rice into triangles, using gentle pressure.
Wrap each rice ball with a strip of nori and serve.

title: Osaka-Style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Whisk the flour, dashi, and eggs into a smooth batter.
Fold in the cabbage until evenly coated.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add half the batter and shape it into a thick round.
Lay half the pork belly over the top and cook for 5 minutes, until the underside is golden.
Flip carefully and cook for 5 minutes more, until the pork is browned and the center is cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining oil, batter, and pork belly.
Spread okonomiyaki sauce and mayonnaise over each pancake, then finish with aonori and bonito flakes.

title: Takoyaki
ingredients: 6 ounces cooked octopus, cut into small pieces
instructions: Whisk the flour, dashi, eggs, and soy sauce into a thin batter.
Heat a takoyaki pan over medium heat and brush each well generously with oil.
Pour batter into the wells, filling them slightly over the tops.
Add a piece of octopus, a little beni shoga, green onion, and tenkasu to each well.
As the edges set, use a pick to turn each ball a quarter turn, tucking in loose batter. Keep turning until the balls are round and golden all over.
Serve hot with takoyaki sauce, mayonnaise, aonori, and bonito flakes.

title: Kitsune Udon
instructions: Put 1 cup dashi, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Add the aburaage and simmer gently for 8 minutes, turning once; set aside in the seasoned liquid.
In a separate pot, combine 4 cups dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook the udon according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide the noodles among four bowls and ladle the hot broth over them.
Top each bowl with a piece of seasoned aburaage and sliced green onion.

title: Osaka-Style Buta no Shogayaki
instructions: Mix the ginger, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 2 minutes.
Add the pork in a single layer and cook until lightly browned, turning once.
Pour in the ginger sauce and simmer, turning the pork, until the sauce lightly coats it and the meat is cooked through.
Serve with shredded cabbage.

title: Osaka-Style Oden
ingredients: 4 daikon rounds, peeled and 1 inch thick
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the daikon, and simmer for 15 minutes; drain.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and salt in a large pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the daikon, eggs, aburaage, ganmodoki, chikuwa, and konnyaku.
Cover partially and simmer very gently for 45 minutes, without letting the broth boil hard.
Turn off the heat and let the ingredients rest in the broth for at least 15 minutes before serving.

title: Kyoto-Style Obanzai: Simmered Herring and Eggplant (Nishin nasu)
ingredients: 2 dried Japanese herring, rehydrated and cut into pieces
2 Japanese eggplants, cut into thick rounds
instructions: Place the herring, dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and sake in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the eggplant and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Let the dish cool briefly in the broth so the flavors settle, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Kyo-fu Shira-ae (Kyoto-Style Tofu and Vegetable Salad)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, about 300 g, drained
100 g spinach, blanched and squeezed dry
1 small carrot, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Boil the konnyaku for 2 minutes, drain, and set aside.
Blanch the carrot briefly, then drain and cool.
Toast the sesame seeds and grind them finely.
Mash the tofu until smooth, then mix in the sesame, miso, sugar, and soy sauce.
Fold in the spinach, carrot, and konnyaku until evenly coated.

title: Yudofu (Kyoto Hot Pot Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block silken tofu, about 400 g, cut into large cubes
instructions: Place the kombu and dashi in a pot and warm gently for 10 minutes without boiling.
Remove the kombu and add the tofu.
Heat gently until the tofu is warmed through, about 5 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, and mirin in a small bowl.
Serve the tofu hot with the dipping sauce, scallions, and ginger.

title: Kyoto-Style Dashimaki Tamago
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar until combined.
Lightly oil a rectangular tamagoyaki pan and heat it over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture and tilt the pan to cover the base.
When nearly set, roll the egg toward one side of the pan.
Oil the exposed pan, add another thin layer, and lift the roll so the egg flows underneath.
Repeat until all the mixture is used, then gently shape the omelet and slice to serve.

title: Saba-zushi (Kyoto-Style Pressed Mackerel Sushi)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with the water.
Mix the vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved.
Spread the hot rice in a wide bowl and fold in the vinegar mixture; cool to room temperature.
Lay the kombu over the mackerel and rest it for 30 minutes, then remove the kombu.
Shape the rice into a compact oblong and place the mackerel skin-side up over it.
Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and press under a light weight for 1 hour.
Unwrap and slice with a damp knife.

title: Ishikari Nabe (Salmon and Miso Hot Pot)
ingredients: 8 oz firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Bring the dashi and sake to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the potatoes and daikon; simmer until nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir the miso into a ladleful of hot broth, then return it to the pot.
Add the cabbage, onion, tofu, and salmon; simmer gently until the salmon is cooked through.
Top with butter and scallions, and serve hot.

title: Chan Chan Yaki (Miso-Grilled Salmon and Vegetables)
instructions: Mix the miso, sugar, sake, and mirin in a small bowl.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and melt half the butter.
Add the cabbage, onion, carrot, and bean sprouts; cook for 3 minutes.
Set the salmon on top of the vegetables and spread the miso mixture over it.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the salmon is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Add the remaining butter and gently mix the vegetables with the sauce before serving.

title: Hokkaido Butadon (Pork Rice Bowl)
ingredients: 1 lb boneless pork loin, thinly sliced
instructions: Stir the soy sauce, sugar, mirin, and sake together in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the pork in batches until browned and cooked through; transfer to a plate.
Pour the sauce into the skillet and simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the pork to the skillet and turn to coat it in the sauce.
Serve over rice and garnish with scallions.

title: Hokkaido Cream Stew with Corn and Potatoes
ingredients: 2 potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, potatoes, and chicken; cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir until it coats the ingredients.
Gradually stir in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the chicken and vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the milk and corn; simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Hokkaido Kabocha Korokke (Pumpkin Croquettes)
ingredients: 1 lb kabocha squash, seeded and cut into chunks
instructions: Steam the kabocha until very tender, about 15 minutes, then mash it in a bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft; mix it into the kabocha.
Season with salt and pepper, then shape the mixture into 8 small oval patties.
Coat each patty in flour, dip it in beaten egg, and cover it with panko.
Heat the frying oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the croquettes in batches until golden, about 3 minutes per side; drain and serve hot.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Mix the beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar; set aside for 10 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately in boiling water, then drain and season lightly with salt.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and cook the carrot and zucchini separately until just tender; set aside.
Cook the beef in the same pan until browned and cooked through.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef on top.
Add an egg, gochujang, and sesame seeds to each bowl; mix before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
