ingredients: 1 cup aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the kimchi, kimchi brine, gochugaru, and gochujang; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth and garlic, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Top with scallions and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi
instructions: Mix the grated pear, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and black pepper.
Add the beef, onion, and scallions; toss to coat and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet or grill pan over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood and Scallion Pancake)
instructions: Whisk the flour, potato starch, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Stir the seafood into the batter.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Arrange half the scallions in the skillet and pour half the batter over them.
Cook until the underside is golden, about 4 minutes, then flip and cook until crisp and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining oil, scallions, and batter.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds for dipping; serve with the pancakes.

title: Japchae
instructions: Mix the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, and the garlic; set aside.
Cook the noodles according to package directions, drain, and cut into manageable lengths.
Blanch the spinach, drain, and squeeze out excess water.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a skillet and cook the beef until done; transfer to a bowl.
Add the remaining oil and cook the carrot, onion, and mushrooms until tender; transfer to the bowl.
Toss the noodles with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Combine the noodles, beef, vegetables, and spinach; sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Mix the beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar; set aside for 10 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately, drain, and season lightly with salt and sesame oil.
Heat a little vegetable oil and cook the carrot and zucchini separately until tender.
Cook the beef in a pan until browned, then fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide rice among bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef on top.
Top each bowl with an egg, gochujang, and sesame seeds; mix before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 300 g aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
200 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the kimchi, onion, garlic, gochugaru, and gochujang; cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Top with green onions and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi
instructions: Combine the grated pear and onion with soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and pepper.
Add the beef and green onions; toss to coat and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Haemul Pajeon
ingredients: 1 bunch Korean chives or scallions, cut into 10 cm lengths
instructions: Whisk the flour, potato starch, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Arrange the chives in a layer in a hot skillet with 1 tablespoon oil.
Scatter the seafood over the chives and pour the batter evenly on top.
Cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, until the bottom is crisp and golden.
Flip carefully, add another tablespoon of oil, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds for dipping.
Cut the pancake into pieces and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Japchae
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Mix the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, and half the garlic.
Blanch the spinach, drain, and gently squeeze out excess water.
Heat the vegetable oil and cook the beef until browned; remove from the pan.
Cook the carrot, pepper, and mushrooms in the same pan until tender.
Boil the noodles according to package directions, then drain.
Toss the noodles with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic.
Add the beef, vegetables, and spinach; toss until evenly combined and heated through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
ingredients: 2 cups aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat and brown the pork belly.
Add the kimchi and onion; cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the kimchi juice, broth, gochugaru, gochujang, and garlic.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Top with scallions and sesame oil; serve hot.

title: Bulgogi (Korean Marinated Beef)
instructions: Combine the grated pear, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and black pepper.
Add the beef, onion, and scallions; toss to coat and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches, stirring, until browned and cooked through, about 3 minutes per batch.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)
instructions: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Mix the beef with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic.
Heat 1 teaspoon vegetable oil in a skillet and cook the beef until browned; set aside.
Cook the carrot and zucchini separately in a little oil until tender-crisp; season lightly with salt.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately, drain, and season with a pinch of salt and sesame oil.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the remaining oil.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the beef and vegetables on top.
Add an egg and a spoonful of gochujang to each bowl; sprinkle with sesame seeds and mix before eating.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood and Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 1 bunch scallions, trimmed and cut to fit the pan
6 ounces mixed seafood, thawed and patted dry
instructions: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds for dipping sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spread half the scallions in the skillet and scatter half the seafood over them.
Pour half the batter evenly over the scallions and seafood.
Cook for 4 minutes, then flip and cook until crisp and cooked through, about 3 minutes more.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients and oil; serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Tteokguk (Korean Rice Cake Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound Korean oval rice cake slices, soaked in cold water for 10 minutes and drained
instructions: Bring the beef broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add the beef, soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and black pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Drain the rice cakes and add them to the pot.
Simmer until the rice cakes are tender and float, about 5 minutes.
Slowly pour in the beaten eggs and cook for 1 minute without stirring.
Ladle into bowls and top with crumbled seaweed and scallions.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately; drain and season each with a little sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry the carrot and mushrooms separately in vegetable oil until tender.
Season the beef with soy sauce and stir-fry until cooked through.
Fry the eggs to your preference.
Mix the gochujang with the sugar and 1 teaspoon water.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef on top.
Add an egg and the gochujang mixture to each bowl; sprinkle with sesame seeds and mix before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the kimchi, gochugaru, gochujang, and garlic; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the onion and broth, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Top with scallions and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 600 g beef rib-eye or sirloin, thinly sliced
1 small Asian pear, peeled and grated
instructions: Mix the pear, onion, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and garlic in a bowl.
Add the beef and toss to coat; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or grill pan over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and scallions; serve hot.

title: Haemul Pajeon
ingredients: 1 bunch scallions, cut to fit the pan
150 g mixed seafood, thawed and patted dry
instructions: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds for dipping.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Pour in half the batter and spread it into a thin round.
Arrange half the scallions and seafood over the batter; press lightly.
Cook until the underside is golden, about 4 minutes, then flip and cook until crisp and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining oil, batter, scallions, and seafood; serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 6 dried anchovies, heads and guts removed
1 sheet dried kelp, about 10 cm square
instructions: Simmer the water, anchovies, and kelp for 10 minutes to make a broth; remove the anchovies and kelp.
Stir the gochujang, gochugaru, sugar, and soy sauce into the broth.
Add the rice cakes and simmer, stirring often, until tender and the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.
Add the scallions and hard-boiled eggs; simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to package directions.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately; drain and season each with a little sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry the carrot and zucchini separately in vegetable oil until just tender.
Season the beef with soy sauce and sugar, then stir-fry until cooked through.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef on top.
Add an egg, gochujang, sesame oil, and sesame seeds to each bowl; mix before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 300 g aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the kimchi, onion, garlic, gochugaru, and gochujang; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth and soy sauce, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the green onions and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi
instructions: Whisk together the grated pear, grated onion, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and black pepper.
Add the beef and green onions; toss to coat and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood and Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 200 g mixed seafood, thawed and patted dry
1 bunch scallions, trimmed and cut to fit the pan
instructions: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and gochugaru in a small bowl for dipping.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Arrange half the scallions in the pan, scatter half the seafood over them, and pour over half the batter.
Cook until the underside is golden, about 4 minutes; flip carefully and cook until crisp and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining oil, scallions, seafood, and batter.
Cut into pieces and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Japchae
instructions: Cook the dangmyeon according to package directions, drain, and snip into shorter lengths.
Blanch the spinach, drain, and season with 1 teaspoon sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Mix the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, and the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and cook the beef until browned; set aside.
Stir-fry the carrot, onion, and mushrooms until tender, then set aside.
Scramble the beaten egg in the skillet, then slice it into thin strips.
Toss the noodles with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Add the beef, vegetables, spinach, and egg; toss well and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Daegu-Style Makchang Gui (Grilled Beef Abomasum)
ingredients: 1 lb cleaned beef makchang, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Mix the doenjang, gochujang, rice wine, garlic, and sesame oil; toss with the makchang and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and brush it lightly with neutral oil.
Grill the makchang, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 10–15 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and scallions, and serve hot.

title: Daegu-Style Yukgaejang (Spicy Beef and Scallion Soup)
ingredients: 2 cups fernbrake, soaked and cut into short lengths
instructions: Simmer the brisket in the water until tender, about 1½ hours, skimming the surface as needed.
Remove the beef, strain the broth, and shred the beef when cool enough to handle.
Heat the neutral and sesame oils in a pot; briefly stir-fry the gochugaru and garlic over low heat.
Add the broth, shredded beef, soup soy sauce, salt, sprouts, fernbrake, and scallions.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stir in the black pepper, and serve hot.

title: Sujebi (Hand-Torn Dough Soup)
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Mix the flour, water, salt, and oil into a smooth dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Bring the stock to a boil and add the potato and onion.
Pinch off small pieces of dough and stretch them thinly into the simmering stock.
Add the zucchini, soup soy sauce, and garlic; simmer until the dough and vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Gochu Twigim (Stuffed and Fried Green Chiles)
ingredients: ½ cup firm tofu, drained and mashed
instructions: Slit each chile lengthwise and remove the seeds.
Mix the tofu, pork, garlic, scallion, salt, and pepper; fill each chile with the mixture.
Lightly coat the stuffed chiles in flour, then dip them in beaten egg.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the chiles, turning gently, until golden and the filling is cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Nabak Kimchi (Light Radish and Cabbage Water Kimchi)
ingredients: 1 lb Korean radish, peeled and cut into thin squares
½ small napa cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Toss the radish and cabbage with the salt and leave for 30 minutes; drain off the liquid.
Whisk the glutinous rice flour into 1 cup water and simmer, stirring, until lightly thickened; cool completely.
Mix the rice paste with 6 cups water, garlic, and ginger.
Add the radish, cabbage, red chile, and scallions to the seasoned water.
Cover and ferment at room temperature for 1–2 days, then refrigerate and serve chilled.

title: Gangwon Gamja Ongsimi (Potato Dough Soup)
instructions: Grate the potatoes, then squeeze the pulp through a clean cloth over a bowl; let the starchy liquid settle for 10 minutes.
Pour off the liquid and mix the settled starch back into the potato pulp with a pinch of salt.
Bring the stock to a boil and add the onion and zucchini.
Shape the potato mixture into small balls and drop them into the soup.
Simmer until the dumplings float and are cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Season with soup soy sauce, garlic, and salt; finish with scallions and sesame oil.

title: Gangwon Gamja Jorim (Braised Potatoes)
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and add the potatoes; cook, stirring, for 3 minutes.
Add the water, soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, and garlic.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes, turning them occasionally.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce becomes glossy and coats the potatoes.
Stir in the sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Gangwon Chwinamul Muchim (Seasoned Aster Greens)
ingredients: 300 g fresh chwinamul (aster greens), tough stems trimmed
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the greens for 1 minute.
Drain, rinse under cold water, and squeeze out excess water.
Cut the greens into bite-size lengths.
Mix the doenjang, garlic, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Add the greens and toss well; adjust with soy sauce if needed, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Gangwon Makguksu (Buckwheat Noodles)
instructions: Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package directions.
Drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water until chilled; drain well.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, gochugaru, and garlic.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and sesame seeds.
Serve topped with cucumber, pear, and boiled egg.

title: Gangwon Hwangtae-gui (Grilled Dried Pollock)
ingredients: 2 dried pollock fillets, rehydrated and patted dry
instructions: Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, gochugaru, garlic, and sesame oil.
Brush the pollock fillets lightly with vegetable oil.
Grill or pan-cook over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Brush both sides with the sauce and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, turning carefully, until lightly charred and hot.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Gwangju-Style Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 2 cups well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
200 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork until lightly browned.
Add the kimchi, onion, garlic, gochugaru, and gochujang; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes; scatter scallions over the stew before serving.

title: Namdo-Style Tteokgalbi
instructions: Combine the beef, pork, onion, scallions, garlic, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and pepper.
Knead the mixture until sticky, then shape it into 8 flat oval patties.
Heat the neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the patties for 4–5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Rest for 3 minutes before serving.

title: Gwangju-Style Yukjeon
ingredients: 300 g thinly sliced beef, cut into palm-size pieces
instructions: Season the beef on both sides with salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl and stir in the scallion.
Dredge each beef piece lightly in flour, then dip it in the egg.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the beef in batches for 1–2 minutes per side, until the egg coating is set and lightly golden.

title: Mugeunji Deunggalbijjim (Braised Aged Kimchi and Pork Ribs)
ingredients: 1 kg pork back ribs, cut into pieces
500 g aged napa cabbage kimchi, left in large pieces
instructions: Rinse the ribs and place them in a pot with water to cover; boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Return the ribs to the pot with the kimchi, onion, garlic, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, and 4 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 70–80 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Add the scallions and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Hongeo Samhap
ingredients: 300 g boiled pork belly, thinly sliced
instructions: Arrange the skate, pork belly, and kimchi on a serving platter.
Sprinkle the kimchi with sesame seeds and drizzle it with sesame oil.
Serve each bite by pairing a slice of skate with pork belly and kimchi.

title: Daejeon-Style Dubu Dureubuchim (Pan-Fried Tofu with Chive Soy Sauce)
ingredients: 1 block (14 ounces) firm tofu, drained and patted dry
instructions: Cut the tofu into 1/2-inch-thick slices.
Stir together the chives, soy sauce, water, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and gochugaru.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the tofu until golden on both sides.
Arrange the tofu on a plate and spoon the chive sauce over it.

title: Kongnamul Muchim (Seasoned Soybean Sprouts)
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the sprouts in a pot with 1/2 cup water and cover.
Bring to a boil and steam for 5 minutes without lifting the lid.
Drain the sprouts and let them cool until easy to handle.
Toss with the salt, garlic, scallions, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and gochugaru.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Gochujang Jjigae with Zucchini and Potato
ingredients: 1 medium potato, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
7 ounces firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a small pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 2 minutes.
Stir in the gochujang and doenjang, then add the stock.
Add the potato and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tofu and simmer for 2 minutes.
Scatter the scallion over the stew and serve hot.

title: Daejeon-Style Kalguksu (Knife-Cut Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1/2 medium potato, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, and water into a firm dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Dust the dough with flour and roll it into a thin sheet.
Fold the sheet loosely and cut it into thin noodles; shake the noodles apart.
Bring the stock to a boil and add the potato and onion.
Add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Add the zucchini, soy sauce, and garlic and simmer until the noodles are tender, about 3 minutes.
Finish with the scallions and sesame oil.

title: Kimchi Bokkum Bap (Kimchi Fried Rice)
instructions: Break up the cold rice with a spoon.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and stir-fry the kimchi for 3 minutes.
Mix in the kimchi juice and gochujang.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry until hot and evenly coated.
Stir in the sesame oil and top with scallion and sesame seeds.

title: Kimchi-jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
ingredients: 2 cups aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
200 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork belly until lightly browned.
Add the kimchi, gochugaru, and garlic; cook for 3 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the water or stock and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and scallions, then simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Doenjang-jjigae (Soybean Paste Stew)
ingredients: 100 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a small pot and sauté the onion and potato for 2 minutes.
Stir in the doenjang and garlic.
Gradually pour in the stock, stirring to dissolve the paste.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tofu and green chili; simmer for 3 minutes and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi (Marinated Beef)
instructions: Mix the grated pear, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic in a bowl.
Add the beef and onion, toss to coat, and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches, spreading it out so it browns instead of steams.
Return all the beef to the skillet, toss with the scallions, and finish with sesame seeds.

title: Japchae (Glass Noodles with Vegetables)
ingredients: 200 g dried dangmyeon (sweet potato glass noodles)
instructions: Marinate the beef with 1 teaspoon soy sauce and 1/2 teaspoon sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the package directions, drain, and cut them into manageable lengths.
Blanch the spinach, rinse under cold water, squeeze dry, and set aside.
Heat the neutral oil in a skillet and cook the beef until browned; transfer to a large bowl.
Cook the carrot, onion, and mushrooms in the same skillet until tender, then add them to the bowl.
Add the noodles, spinach, remaining soy sauce and sesame oil, sugar, and garlic; toss well.
Warm everything together in the skillet for 2 minutes and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Mandu (Korean Dumplings)
ingredients: 150 g firm tofu, pressed and crumbled
instructions: Squeeze excess liquid from the chopped cabbage and crumbled tofu.
Mix the pork, tofu, cabbage, garlic chives, scallions, soy sauce, sesame oil, and pepper in a bowl.
Place about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of each wrapper; moisten the edge with water, fold, and seal.
Heat the neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat and arrange the dumplings flat-side down.
Cook until the bottoms are golden, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and cover the skillet; steam for 5 to 6 minutes, until the filling is cooked through.
Remove the lid and cook until the remaining water evaporates; serve hot.

title: Dwaeji Gukbap (Pork and Rice Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder or pork belly
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
1 tsp Korean red pepper flakes, for serving
instructions: Put the pork bones and pork in a large pot, cover with water, and boil for 5 minutes; drain and rinse the meat and pot.
Return the bones and pork to the pot with 12 cups fresh water, onion, garlic, and ginger.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for 2½ to 3 hours, adding water if needed.
Remove the pork, slice it thinly, and strain the broth; season the broth with salt.
Put cooked rice and sliced pork in bowls, ladle over hot broth, and serve with scallions, saeujeot, and red pepper flakes.

title: Milmyeon (Busan Wheat Noodles in Chilled Broth)
ingredients: 12 oz dried wheat noodles for milmyeon
1 tbsp Korean mustard, or to taste
8 oz cooked beef brisket, thinly sliced
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package directions, then rinse thoroughly under cold water and drain.
Stir the chilled broth with rice vinegar and sugar; taste and adjust the seasoning.
Divide the noodles among bowls and pour the chilled broth over them.
Top with cucumber, pear, brisket, and egg, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Serve with Korean mustard and additional vinegar at the table.

title: Eomuk Tang (Busan Fish Cake Soup)
ingredients: 8 oz Korean fish cake sheets, cut into wide strips
1 piece dried kelp, about 4 by 4 inches
6 dried anchovies, heads and guts removed
1 small Korean radish, peeled and cut into ½-inch slices
instructions: Add water, kelp, anchovies, and radish to a pot and bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer for 10 minutes, remove the kelp and anchovies, and continue simmering until the radish is tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and salt, then add the fish cake and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add scallions and sesame oil, simmer for 1 minute, and serve hot.

title: Dongnae Pajeon (Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 1 bunch scallions, trimmed and cut to fit the pan
4 oz small shrimp, peeled and deveined
4 oz squid, cleaned and cut into thin rings
instructions: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, cold water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds in a small bowl for dipping.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat, arrange half the scallions in the pan, and scatter over half the shrimp and squid.
Pour over half the batter and cook until the underside is deeply golden and crisp, about 4 minutes.
Flip carefully, add a little more oil around the edge, and cook until the seafood is done and the second side is golden.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Godeungeo Gui (Grilled Mackerel)
instructions: Pat the mackerel dry and rub both sides with salt; rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush lightly with oil.
Grill the mackerel skin-side down until crisp and browned, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Turn carefully and cook the other side until the flesh flakes easily, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and rice.

title: Jeonju-Style Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Mix the beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and garlic; let it stand for 10 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately, drain, and season each with a little salt and sesame oil.
Sauté the zucchini, carrot, and mushrooms separately in a little vegetable oil until tender; season lightly with salt.
Cook the beef in a skillet until browned, then fry the eggs to your liking.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the beef and vegetables on top.
Add an egg, gochujang, and sesame seeds to each bowl; mix before eating.

title: Kongnamul Guk (Soybean Sprout Soup)
instructions: Bring the anchovy-kelp stock to a boil in a pot.
Add the soybean sprouts and garlic, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes without lifting the lid.
Season with soup soy sauce and salt.
Stir in the scallions and sesame oil; add gochugaru if desired.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu (450 g), drained and sliced into 1 cm slabs
instructions: Mix the water, soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, and garlic in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and brown the tofu on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the tofu and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, turning the slices once.
Stir in the scallion and sesame oil, then scatter sesame seeds over the top.
Serve warm with rice.

title: Hwangtae-gui (Grilled Dried Pollock)
ingredients: 2 dried pollock fillets (about 150 g total), rehydrated and patted dry
instructions: Soak the dried pollock in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, gochugaru, garlic, and sesame oil.
Brush the pollock lightly with vegetable oil and grill over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Brush both sides with the sauce and grill for 1 to 2 minutes more, until lightly charred and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Jeonju Moju (Spiced Rice Wine)
instructions: Combine the water, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, brown sugar, and jujubes in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 minutes.
Strain the spiced liquid into a clean pot and stir in the makgeolli and honey.
Warm over low heat without boiling, then serve hot.

title: Jeju Hairtail Stew (Galchi Jorim)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh hairtail, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 small Korean radish, cut into thick half-moons
instructions: Arrange the radish in a shallow pot and lay the hairtail and onion on top.
Mix the water, chili flakes, soy sauce, fish sauce, garlic, and ginger; pour over the fish.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, spooning the broth over the fish.
Add the scallions and simmer for 2 minutes, until the radish is tender and the broth is savory.

title: Jeju Pork and Buckwheat Noodles (Gogi Guksu)
instructions: Put the pork, water, onion, and garlic in a pot and bring to a boil.
Skim the surface, then simmer for 45–60 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Remove the pork and strain the broth; season the broth with soy sauce and salt.
Cook the noodles according to the package directions, then drain and rinse briefly.
Slice the pork and divide it and the noodles among bowls; ladle hot broth over them.
Finish with scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Jeju Abalone Porridge (Jeonbokjuk)
ingredients: 2 fresh abalones, cleaned and thinly sliced
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then soak it for 30 minutes and drain.
Warm the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the abalone for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Lower the heat and simmer for 35–45 minutes, stirring often, until the rice breaks down and the porridge is creamy.
Season with salt and serve topped with scallion and sesame seeds.

title: Jeju Seaweed Soup with Sea Urchin (Seongge Miyeokguk)
instructions: Soak the miyeok in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the miyeok for 2 minutes.
Add the water, soy sauce, and garlic; bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 25 minutes, until the seaweed is tender.
Gently stir in the sea urchin and simmer for 2 minutes; season with salt and serve.

title: Jeju Buckwheat Pancakes with Chives (Bingtteok-style Jeon)
ingredients: 1 cup garlic chives, cut into 2-inch lengths
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour, water, egg, and salt into a smooth, thin batter.
Stir the garlic chives into the batter.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame seeds in a small bowl for dipping.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in a thin layer of batter and cook for 2–3 minutes, until the edges lift and the underside is browned.
Flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more; repeat with the remaining batter and oil.
Cut into pieces and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Daegu-Style Makchang Gui (Grilled Pork Intestines)
instructions: Rinse the makchang well and pat dry.
Mix the doenjang, garlic, soju, sesame oil, and black pepper; coat the makchang and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and brush it with neutral oil.
Grill the makchang, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 15–20 minutes.
Slice into bite-size pieces and scatter with scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Daegu-Style Spicy Beef Soup (Yukgaejang)
ingredients: 1 cup fernbrake (gosari), soaked and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Simmer the brisket in the water until tender, about 1 hour; remove the beef and reserve the broth.
Shred the beef into bite-size strands.
Mix the gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil; toss with the beef, gosari, and scallions.
Return the seasoned mixture to the broth and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and mushrooms; simmer until tender, about 10 minutes, then season with salt.

title: Kongnamul Bap (Rice with Soybean Sprouts)
ingredients: 8 oz soybean sprouts, rinsed and drained
1 tbsp soy sauce for the seasoning sauce
instructions: Place the rinsed rice and water in a pot and arrange the soybean sprouts on top.
Cover and bring to a boil; lower the heat and cook until the rice is tender, about 15 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the ground beef in a skillet with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic until browned.
Mix the scallions, remaining soy sauce, gochugaru, and sesame seeds to make a seasoning sauce.
Fluff the rice and sprouts, top with the beef, and serve with the sauce.

title: Ojingeo Bokkeum (Spicy Stir-Fried Squid)
ingredients: 1 lb cleaned squid, cut into rings and tentacles
1 medium carrot, cut into thin strips
instructions: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic.
Heat the neutral oil in a skillet over high heat and stir-fry the onion and carrot for 2 minutes.
Add the squid and sauce; stir-fry just until the squid turns opaque, about 2–3 minutes.
Add the scallions and sesame oil and toss briefly.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot with rice.

title: Gamja Jorim (Soy-Braised Potatoes)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb small waxy potatoes, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Rinse the potatoes and drain well.
Heat the neutral oil in a pot and stir-fry the potatoes for 3 minutes.
Add the water, soy sauce, sugar, corn syrup, and garlic; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the liquid becomes glossy and coats the potatoes; finish with sesame oil and sesame seeds.

title: Gangwon Potato Ongsimi Soup (Gamja Ongsimi-guk)
ingredients: 3 medium starchy potatoes, peeled and finely grated
instructions: Set a fine sieve over a bowl and drain the grated potatoes, saving the liquid.
Let the potato liquid stand until the starch settles, then pour off the water and mix the starch into the grated potato with salt.
Stir in the potato starch and shape the mixture into small balls.
Bring the stock to a boil and add the potato balls.
When they rise, add zucchini, onion, soup soy sauce, and garlic; simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Finish with scallions and sesame oil, and serve hot.

title: Gangwon Buckwheat Memiljeonbyeong
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, water, and salt into a thin, smooth batter.
Mix cabbage, kimchi, garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil for the filling.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and pour in a thin layer of batter.
Cook until the edges look dry, flip, and cook briefly on the other side.
Place a strip of filling across the pancake and roll it up in the skillet.
Cook seam-side down until lightly golden, then slice and serve.

title: Gangwon Corn Makgeolli Ppyeong (Steamed Corn Cake)
ingredients: 2 cups fresh corn kernels, finely ground
instructions: Mix warm water, makgeolli, sugar, and yeast; let stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in ground corn, flour, salt, and vegetable oil to make a thick batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until bubbly, about 1 hour.
Line a small steamer pan with parchment and spread in the batter.
Steam over boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes, until set in the center.
Cool slightly, cut into pieces, and serve warm.

title: Gangwon Dried Pollock Soup (Hwangtae-guk)
ingredients: 120 grams dried pollock, torn into bite-size pieces
1 small potato, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Rinse the dried pollock briefly and squeeze out excess water.
Heat sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the pollock for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add potato, onion, garlic, and soup soy sauce, then simmer until the potato is tender.
Pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream and let them set briefly.
Add scallions and black pepper, then serve hot.

title: Gangwon Potato Jeon (Gamja-jeon)
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Drain the mixture through a sieve, reserving the liquid; let the liquid stand until the starch settles.
Pour off the water and stir the settled starch and salt into the grated mixture.
Mix in the potato starch.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and spoon in small portions of the mixture.
Flatten each portion and fry until crisp and golden on both sides; serve hot.

title: Gwangju-Style Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 2 cups aged napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
200 g firm tofu, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork until lightly browned.
Add the kimchi, gochugaru, and garlic; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and scallions, then simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gwangju-Style Aehobak Namul
ingredients: 1 large Korean zucchini (aehobak), cut into half-moons
instructions: Toss the zucchini with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then gently squeeze out excess liquid.
Heat the perilla oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and zucchini and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until tender.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Muguk (Korean Radish Soup)
ingredients: 250 g Korean radish, cut into thin matchsticks
instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the beef until no longer pink.
Add the radish and soup soy sauce; stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil, skimming any foam.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, until the radish is tender.
Stir in the garlic, scallions, and black pepper, then simmer for 2 minutes.

title: Kongnamul Muchim (Seasoned Soybean Sprouts)
instructions: Put the sprouts and water in a pot and sprinkle with the salt.
Cover and steam over medium heat for 7 minutes without lifting the lid.
Drain the sprouts and let them cool until just warm.
Toss with the garlic, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and scallion.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Gochujang Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)
ingredients: 400 g firm tofu, cut into 1 cm slices
instructions: Pat the tofu dry with a clean towel.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and pan-fry the tofu for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Mix the water, gochujang, soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, and garlic.
Pour the sauce over the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes, turning the slices once.
Scatter over the scallion and sesame seeds, then serve with rice.

title: Daejeon-Style Spicy Kalguksu
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Stir in the gochugaru, garlic, soup soy sauce, and salt.
Add the potato, zucchini, and clams; simmer until the clams open and the vegetables soften.
Shake excess flour from the noodles, add them to the pot, and cook until tender, stirring gently.
Top with scallions and serve hot.

title: Kongnamulbap (Bean Sprout Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups short-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Mix the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the garlic, and 1 teaspoon sesame oil.
Put the rice and water in a rice cooker, then spread the soybean sprouts and seasoned beef over the top.
Cook on the regular rice setting; let it rest for 10 minutes after cooking.
Mix the scallions, gochugaru, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, sesame seeds, and 1 tablespoon sesame oil for the sauce.
Gently mix the rice and sprouts, then serve with the sauce.

title: Dubu Dureubuchigi (Pan-Fried Tofu)
instructions: Drain the tofu and pat it dry, then cut it into 1 cm-thick slices.
Stir together the soy sauce, water, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, scallion, and sesame seeds.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Pan-fry the tofu until golden on both sides.
Spoon the seasoning sauce over the tofu and serve warm.

title: Baechu Doenjang Guk (Cabbage Soybean-Paste Soup)
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Whisk in the doenjang and gochujang until dissolved.
Add the cabbage and garlic; simmer for 10 minutes, until the cabbage is tender.
Add the tofu and simmer for 3 minutes more.
Stir in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Gamja Jorim (Braised Potatoes)
ingredients: 500 g small potatoes, scrubbed and halved
instructions: Heat the neutral oil in a skillet and brown the potatoes lightly for 4 minutes.
Add the water, soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, and garlic.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce turns glossy and coats the potatoes.
Finish with sesame oil and sesame seeds.

title: Kimchi-jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
ingredients: 2 cups well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a small pot and cook the pork belly until lightly browned.
Add kimchi and onion; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in gochugaru and gochujang, then pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add tofu and simmer for 5 minutes. Top with scallions and serve hot.

title: Doenjang-jjigae (Soybean Paste Stew)
instructions: Bring the broth to a simmer in a small pot.
Dissolve the doenjang in the broth.
Add potato and onion; simmer for 8 minutes.
Add zucchini and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Add tofu and green chili; simmer for 3 minutes. Scatter scallion on top and serve.

title: Bulgogi (Korean Marinated Beef)
ingredients: 450 g thinly sliced beef ribeye or sirloin
instructions: Mix the grated pear, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic in a bowl.
Add beef and onion; toss to coat and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the beef in batches for 2–3 minutes per batch, until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and scallions; serve with rice.

title: Pajeon (Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 1 bunch scallions, trimmed and cut into 10 cm lengths
instructions: Whisk flour, cold water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Fold the scallions into the batter.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium heat and pour in the batter, spreading it evenly.
Cook for 3–4 minutes per side, adding the remaining oil when flipping, until golden and crisp.
Mix soy sauce and rice vinegar for dipping; cut the pancake into pieces and serve.

title: Gyeran-jjim (Korean Steamed Eggs)
instructions: Whisk the eggs, broth, salt, and fish sauce until combined.
Pour the mixture into a small heatproof bowl or earthenware pot.
Set the bowl in a pot with a little simmering water, cover, and steam over low heat for 10–12 minutes, until just set.
Top with scallion and sesame oil, then serve warm.

title: Busan-Style Dwaeji Gukbap (Pork and Rice Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder or pork leg, thinly sliced
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Simmer the pork bones in the water for 1 hour, skimming any foam.
Add the pork and garlic, then simmer for 25 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Season the broth with salt and fish sauce.
Divide the rice among bowls and ladle the hot pork and broth over it.
Top with scallions, sesame seeds, and gochugaru; adjust the seasoning to taste.

title: Milmyeon (Busan Wheat Noodles in Chilled Broth)
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package directions, then rinse thoroughly under cold water and drain.
Stir the chilled broth with the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and gochugaru.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pour the broth over them.
Top with pear, cucumber, and egg, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Dongnae Pajeon (Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 1 bunch scallions, trimmed and cut to fit the pan
4 ounces small shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Whisk the all-purpose flour, rice flour, water, egg, and salt into a smooth batter.
Arrange the scallions in a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and scatter the shrimp and squid over them.
Pour the batter evenly over the scallions and seafood.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the bottom is golden and crisp, then carefully flip and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame seeds together and serve alongside the pancake.

title: Eomuk Bokkeum (Busan Fish Cake Stir-Fry)
ingredients: 12 ounces Korean fish cakes, sliced into strips
instructions: Stir the soy sauce, rice syrup, gochujang, and water together in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the fish cakes and sauce, then stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce lightly coats everything.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil.
Finish with sesame seeds and scallion.

title: Agujjim (Spicy Braised Monkfish)
ingredients: 2 pounds monkfish, cut into large pieces
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water
1 bunch water dropwort or chrysanthemum greens, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Mix the gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and fish sauce into a paste.
Bring the water to a simmer in a wide pot and add the monkfish and seasoning paste.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, turning the fish carefully once.
Add the bean sprouts, water dropwort, and scallions; cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Jeonju-Style Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice in a rice cooker or saucepan until tender.
Mix the beef with soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, and sugar; set aside for 10 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts and spinach separately, drain, and season each lightly with salt.
Heat a little vegetable oil in a pan and cook the zucchini, carrot, and mushrooms separately until tender; set aside.
Cook the beef in the pan until browned and cooked through.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the remaining vegetable oil.
Divide rice among four bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef over it.
Top each bowl with an egg, gochujang, sesame oil, and sesame seeds; mix before eating.

title: Kongnamul Guk (Soybean Sprout Soup)
instructions: Bring the anchovy-kelp stock to a boil in a pot.
Add the soybean sprouts and garlic, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes without opening the lid.
Season with soup soy sauce and salt.
Stir in the scallions and sesame oil.
Serve hot, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, about 450 g, drained and sliced into 1 cm slabs
instructions: Pat the tofu dry with paper towels.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet and pan-fry the tofu until golden on both sides; remove and set aside.
Mix the water, soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, and garlic.
Return the tofu to the skillet and pour the sauce over it.
Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, turning the tofu once, until the sauce reduces slightly.
Finish with scallion, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.

title: Hobak Jeon (Korean Zucchini Pancakes)
ingredients: 1 medium Korean zucchini, cut into 7 mm rounds
instructions: Sprinkle the zucchini rounds with salt and let them stand for 10 minutes.
Pat the rounds dry, then lightly coat each one in flour.
Dip each round in beaten egg.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the zucchini in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and tender.
Mix the soy sauce and rice vinegar for dipping, then serve the jeon with sesame seeds.

title: Sigeumchi Namul (Seasoned Spinach)
ingredients: 300 g fresh spinach, trimmed and washed
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the blanching salt.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, then transfer it to cold water.
Drain well and gently squeeze out excess water; cut into bite-size lengths.
Toss the spinach with garlic, soup soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve at room temperature.

title: Jeju Mungge Mulhoe (Raw Sea Squirt in Chilled Soup)
ingredients: 8 oz fresh sea squirt, cleaned and sliced
1 small ice cube tray of ice, for serving
instructions: Whisk the water, vinegar, gochujang, and sugar until smooth.
Add the sea squirt and cucumber to a bowl.
Pour in the chilled soup and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Add ice and serve immediately.

title: Jeju Momguk (Pork and Gulfweed Soup)
ingredients: 1 oz dried gulfweed ( 모자반 ), rinsed and soaked
8 oz pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Drain the soaked gulfweed and cut it into shorter lengths.
Put pork and water in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming any foam.
Simmer for 25 minutes, then stir in the doenjang and garlic.
Add the gulfweed and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Season with salt and finish with scallions.

title: Jeju Bingtteok (Buckwheat Pancakes with Radish)
instructions: Toss the radish with sesame oil, salt, and sesame seeds; set aside.
Whisk the buckwheat flour, water, and salt into a thin batter.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and pour in a thin layer of batter.
Cook until set, flip, and cook briefly on the other side.
Place some radish filling across each pancake, roll it up, and serve.

title: Jeju Godeungeo Jorim (Braised Mackerel with Radish)
ingredients: 1 lb mackerel fillets, cut into portions
8 oz daikon radish, cut into thick half-moons
instructions: Arrange the radish in a shallow pot and place the mackerel on top.
Mix the water, soy sauce, gochugaru, garlic, and sugar; pour over the fish.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, spooning sauce over the fish occasionally.
Add the scallion and simmer for 2 more minutes.

title: Jeju Gogi-guksu (Pork Noodle Soup)
instructions: Put the pork, water, and garlic in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming any foam.
Lower the heat and simmer for 45 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Remove the pork, slice it thinly, and season the broth with salt.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot according to the package directions; drain and divide among bowls.
Pour hot broth over the noodles, top with pork and scallions, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Hummus
instructions: Cover the chickpeas with plenty of water and soak overnight.
Drain the chickpeas, then simmer with the baking soda in fresh water until very tender, about 60–90 minutes.
Drain the chickpeas and reserve a few for garnish.
Blend the tahini and lemon juice until smooth.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt, and chickpeas; blend until smooth.
With the blender running, add the cold water gradually until creamy.
Spoon into a serving dish and garnish with olive oil, parsley, and reserved chickpeas.

title: Tabbouleh
instructions: Combine the bulgur, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt in a bowl; let stand for 20 minutes.
Stir in the parsley, mint, tomatoes, and scallions.
Taste and adjust the lemon juice and salt before serving.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper; cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt, and black pepper; simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set, about 6–8 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve warm.

title: Mujadara
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Combine the lentils and water in a pot; simmer until almost tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain the lentils, reserving 2 cups of the cooking liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Add the rice, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper to the lentils.
Pour in the reserved cooking liquid and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Fluff the lentils and rice, then serve topped with the caramelized onions.

title: Baba Ghanoush
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Prick the eggplants several times and place them on a baking sheet.
Roast, turning once, until collapsed and tender, about 40–50 minutes.
Cool the eggplants, then peel them and drain the flesh in a sieve for 10 minutes.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt.
Spoon into a serving dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish with parsley and serve.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Add the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt to a food processor.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the processor running, add the cold water and blend until creamy.
Spoon into a serving bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika.

title: Tabbouleh
ingredients: 2 cups finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
instructions: Place the bulgur in a bowl and pour the boiling water over it.
Cover and let stand for 15 minutes, then drain any excess water and fluff with a fork.
Combine the parsley, mint, tomatoes, and scallions in a large bowl.
Whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Add the bulgur and dressing to the herbs and vegetables; toss well.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and red pepper flakes; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Make 6 small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the egg whites are set.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Combine the lentils and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are partly tender; drain and reserve 2 cups of the cooking liquid.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onions and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden; set aside half for serving.
Add the cumin and coriander to the skillet and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir in the lentils, rice, reserved cooking liquid, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and top with the reserved onions.

title: Fattoush
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Brush the pita rounds with 1 tablespoon olive oil and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp; cool and break into pieces.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic, sumac, salt, and pepper.
Combine the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, scallions, mint, and parsley in a large bowl.
Add the dressing and toss to coat.
Add the pita pieces just before serving and toss lightly.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
instructions: Blend the tahini and lemon juice until smooth.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt, and chickpeas; blend until thick and creamy.
With the blender running, add the cold water a little at a time until smooth.
Spoon into a serving dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Sprinkle with paprika and serve.

title: Tabbouleh
ingredients: 2 cups finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
instructions: Place the bulgur in a bowl and pour the boiling water over it.
Cover and let stand for 15 minutes, then drain any excess water and fluff with a fork.
Combine the parsley, mint, tomatoes, and scallions in a large bowl.
Add the bulgur, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper; toss well.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Mujadara
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Combine the lentils and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are partly tender; drain, reserving 2 cups cooking liquid.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onions, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper into the lentils.
Add the reserved cooking liquid, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve with the onions on top.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 6 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili flakes; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Make six wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
