Add the chicken and turn to coat it thoroughly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Arrange the chicken on a lined baking sheet.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until cooked through and browned at the edges.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly and serve.

title: Baba Ganoush
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Prick the eggplants several times with a fork and place them on a baking sheet.
Roast for 35 to 45 minutes, turning once, until very soft and collapsed.
Let the eggplants cool, then peel them and drain the flesh in a colander for 10 minutes.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt.
Spoon into a serving bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and garnish with parsley and paprika.

title: Mansaf
ingredients: 1 lb jameed, soaked and blended with 4 cups warm water
instructions: Put the lamb and onion in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the lamb is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Strain the jameed mixture into a saucepan. Add 2 cups of lamb broth and simmer gently, stirring often.
Transfer the lamb to the jameed sauce and simmer for 20 minutes. Season with salt.
Melt 2 tbsp ghee in a pot. Stir in the rice and turmeric, add 4 cups of water and salt, cover, and cook until the rice is tender, about 15 minutes.
Lay the shrak bread on a large platter and spoon over a little jameed sauce. Spread the rice over the bread and arrange the lamb on top.
Pour some sauce over the lamb and rice. Garnish with almonds, pine nuts, and parsley, and serve the remaining sauce alongside.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the eggplant and cauliflower with the oil and roast on a baking sheet until golden, about 25 minutes.
Put the chicken and onion in a pot with 6 cups water. Bring to a boil, skim, and simmer until the chicken is cooked, about 35 minutes. Strain and reserve 5 cups broth.
Mix the allspice, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Drain the rice and stir in half of the spice mixture.
Arrange the chicken in the bottom of a heavy pot. Layer the eggplant and cauliflower over it, then add the rice. Pour in the broth and remaining spice mixture.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 30 minutes.
Let the pot rest for 10 minutes. Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a serving platter, and garnish with almonds.

title: Musakhan
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put the chicken in a roasting pan and season with the allspice, salt, and pepper.
Roast the chicken until cooked through and golden, about 45 minutes.
While the chicken roasts, warm the olive oil in a wide pan. Add the onions and cook over medium-low heat until very soft, about 25 minutes.
Stir the sumac into the onions and season with a little more salt if needed.
Set the breads on a baking sheet and spread the onion mixture over them. Spoon on some pan juices and bake for 5 minutes to warm.
Place the chicken over the breads, scatter with pine nuts, and serve warm.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Put the lentils in a pot with 3 cups water. Bring to a boil and simmer until nearly tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a pan. Cook the onions over medium heat, stirring often, until deeply browned and crisp at the edges, about 25 minutes. Set aside half for topping.
Drain the lentils if needed. Add the rice, cumin, salt, pepper, and 4 cups water to the pot with the lentils.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Let the pot rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
Spoon the reserved onions over the mujadara and serve warm.

title: Warak Enab
ingredients: 1 jar grape leaves, about 60 leaves, rinsed and stems removed
instructions: Mix the rice, ground lamb, tomatoes, parsley, 2 tbsp lemon juice, salt, pepper, allspice, and olive oil in a bowl.
Lay a grape leaf veined-side up. Put about 1 tsp filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot with the potato slices. Pack the rolls seam-side down in snug layers over the potatoes.
Pour the water and 1/4 cup lemon juice over the rolls. Place a heatproof plate on top to keep them in place.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat until the rice and meat are cooked, about 1 hour.
Let the pot rest for 10 minutes. Carefully drain any excess liquid, then turn the rolls onto a platter and serve warm.

title: Musakhan
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Season the chicken with salt, pepper, and allspice, and roast until cooked through, about 40–50 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the onions slowly in olive oil until very soft and golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the sumac into the onions and spoon in a little chicken roasting juice.
Lay the breads on a tray and spread the onions over them.
Arrange the chicken on top and bake for 8–10 minutes to warm the bread.
Scatter with pine nuts and serve warm.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the eggplant, cauliflower, and potatoes with olive oil and roast until browned, 25–30 minutes.
Put the chicken, onion, cinnamon, cardamom, allspice, turmeric, salt, pepper, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth; measure 4 cups broth.
Arrange the chicken and roasted vegetables in layers in a heavy pot, then spread the drained rice over the top.
Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender, about 25 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carefully invert the pot onto a large platter.

title: Mujaddara
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Simmer the lentils in 3 cups water until just tender, about 20 minutes; drain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Cook the onions in olive oil over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 30 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, salt, and pepper into the lentils.
Add enough reserved liquid and water to make 2 cups, then pour it into the pot.
Cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Fold in half the onions and serve topped with the rest.

title: Maftoul with Chicken and Chickpeas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pot and brown the chicken on all sides.
Add the onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, allspice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Add the chickpeas and broth, bring to a boil, then simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 35 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and keep it warm; strain the broth if desired.
Steam the maftoul over the simmering broth until tender, following the package timing, usually 20–25 minutes.
Serve the maftoul topped with chicken and chickpeas, with broth spooned over it.

title: Qidreh
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 cups short-grain rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the garlic, cumin, allspice, cardamom, pepper, salt, and water or broth.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the lamb is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the chickpeas and drained rice, adding broth if needed so the rice is just covered.
Cover tightly and bake until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 35–40 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff gently, and serve.

title: Shakshuka
ingredients: 1 small loaf crusty bread, for serving
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are as runny or firm as you like, 5 to 8 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with bread.

title: Israeli Chopped Salad
instructions: Combine the tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, and parsley in a bowl.
Add the olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss well and serve immediately.

title: Mujadara
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the lentils are almost tender, about 15 minutes; drain, reserving 2 cups of the cooking liquid.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until deeply golden, 25 to 30 minutes. Transfer half to a plate for serving.
Add the cumin, salt, and pepper to the pot, then stir in the rice and lentils.
Pour in the reserved cooking liquid and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Let stand covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve topped with the reserved onions and yogurt.

title: Israeli Couscous with Roasted Vegetables
ingredients: 1 large red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 small red onion, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the bell pepper, zucchini, and onion with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the salt, and the black pepper.
Spread the vegetables on a baking sheet and roast until tender and browned, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the couscous and toast, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth and remaining salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until tender, about 10 minutes.
Fluff the couscous and stir in the roasted vegetables and lemon juice.
Top with mint and feta before serving.

title: Baked Fish with Chraime-Style Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into portions
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Warm the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, cumin, and cayenne; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, water, and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Nestle the fish portions into the sauce and spoon some sauce over the top.
Bake until the fish flakes easily, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on thickness.
Finish with cilantro and lemon juice, then serve with bread or rice.

title: Masgouf (Iraqi Grilled Carp)
ingredients: 1 whole carp, about 3 lb, cleaned and butterflied
instructions: Rinse the carp and pat it dry.
Rub the fish with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Set the fish upright, skin side toward a wood fire, and grill slowly for 45–60 minutes, turning as needed, until cooked through.
Grill the tomato and onion slices until softened.
Serve the fish hot with grilled vegetables and lemon wedges.

title: Quzi (Lamb and Rice)
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Put the lamb, onion, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, allspice, salt, pepper, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 1½–2 hours until the lamb is tender.
Lift out the lamb and strain the broth; measure 3 cups broth for the rice.
Melt 2 tablespoons ghee in a pot, add the drained rice, and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the broth, cover, and cook on low for 15–20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Brown the lamb under a broiler or in a hot oven.
Fry the almonds and raisins in the remaining ghee, then spoon them over the rice with the lamb.

title: Dolma (Iraqi Stuffed Vegetables)
instructions: Mix the rice, ground meat, onion, tomato paste, pomegranate molasses, salt, pepper, allspice, and parsley.
Fill the zucchini, eggplants, and peppers loosely with the mixture, leaving room for the rice to expand.
Arrange the tomato slices in the bottom of a heavy pot and place the stuffed vegetables snugly on top.
Pour in the water and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 60–75 minutes, until the vegetables and filling are cooked.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carefully turn the pot onto a serving platter.

title: Shorbat Adas (Iraqi Lentil Soup)
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric, then add the lentils, salt, pepper, and water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Blend until smooth, or mash lightly for a textured soup.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Timman Bagilla (Rice with Dill and Broad Beans)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
2 cups shelled broad beans, fresh or frozen
instructions: Drain the rice.
Heat the oil in a pot and add the broad beans; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice, dill, salt, pepper, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15–20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 lb stewing beef, cut into cubes
1/2 cup chopped chives or green onion tops
3 dried Persian limes, pierced with a knife
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until golden.
Stir in the turmeric, then add the beef and brown on all sides.
Add the beans, water, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, sauté the parsley, cilantro, chives, and fenugreek in a little oil until fragrant and dark green.
Stir the herbs and pierced dried limes into the pot.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the beef and beans are tender and the stew is thick.

title: Zereshk Polo ba Morgh
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
1 cup dried barberries, picked over and rinsed
1/4 tsp ground saffron, bloomed in 2 tbsp hot water
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the chicken on both sides.
Add the onion and turmeric; cook until the onion softens.
Add the salt, pepper, and water. Cover and simmer for 35 to 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Add a little oil and water to the rice pot, return the rice, cover with a clean towel and lid, and steam over low heat for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt the butter in a small pan. Add the barberries and sugar and cook gently for 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir a spoonful of cooked rice into the saffron water.
Serve the rice topped with saffron rice and barberries, with the chicken and its sauce alongside.

title: Kuku Sabzi
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely chopped green onion tops
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the turmeric, salt, pepper, and baking powder.
Fold in the parsley, cilantro, dill, and green onion tops.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and spread it evenly.
Cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the center is set.
Cut into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Adas Polo
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Combine the lentils and water in a saucepan and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until just tender; drain.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until golden. Stir in the turmeric and cinnamon.
Layer the rice and lentils in the pot, seasoning with salt and pepper as you go.
Cover with a clean towel and lid, then steam over low heat for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt the butter in a small pan, add the raisins, and cook for 1 minute.
Serve the rice and lentils topped with the onions and warm raisins.

title: Khoresh Bademjan
ingredients: 1 lb stewing beef, cut into cubes
2 large eggplants, peeled in stripes and sliced lengthwise
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying eggplant
2 dried Persian limes, pierced with a knife
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices lightly and set aside for 20 minutes; pat dry.
Heat oil in a pot and cook the onion until golden.
Add the turmeric and beef, and brown the beef on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the water, salt, pepper, and dried limes.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the beef is nearly tender.
Fry the eggplant slices in a separate pan until golden on both sides; drain on paper towels.
Add the eggplant and tomatoes to the stew and simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, until tender.

title: Mercimek Çorbası (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water or stock, salt, cumin, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the lentils are very soft, about 25 minutes.
Blend until smooth, adding a little water if the soup is too thick.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the dried mint and Aleppo pepper, and drizzle over the soup before serving.

title: İmam Bayıldı (Olive Oil–Braised Eggplant)
instructions: Peel alternating strips from each eggplant and make a lengthwise slit without cutting all the way through.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large pan and brown the eggplants on all sides; set aside.
Add the remaining olive oil and cook the onions over medium-low heat until soft, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomatoes, then cook until the tomatoes soften, about 5 minutes.
Mix in the parsley, salt, sugar, and black pepper.
Arrange the eggplants in a baking dish with their slits facing up, and spoon the onion mixture into each slit.
Pour the water around the eggplants, cover the dish, and bake at 350°F (175°C) until very tender, about 50 minutes.
Let cool to room temperature before serving.

title: Kuru Fasulye (Turkish White Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the drained beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer until nearly tender, about 45 minutes; drain.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, 5 cups water, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently until the beans are fully tender and the broth is rich, about 45 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Karnıyarık (Stuffed Eggplant with Ground Beef)
instructions: Peel alternating strips from the eggplants and make a lengthwise slit in each.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a pan and brown the eggplants all over; transfer them to a baking dish.
Add the remaining olive oil to the pan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in half the tomatoes, the parsley, salt, and black pepper; cook for 3 minutes.
Fill the slits in the eggplants with the beef mixture.
Whisk the tomato paste into the water and pour it around the eggplants; scatter the remaining tomatoes on top.
Bake uncovered at 375°F (190°C) until the eggplants are tender, about 35 minutes.

title: Bulgur Pilavı (Turkish Bulgur Pilaf)
ingredients: 1 cup coarse bulgur, rinsed and drained
2 cups hot water or vegetable stock
instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the bulgur, hot water or stock, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat until the liquid is absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions)
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until the lentils are partly tender.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, salt, and pepper into the lentils.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, until the rice and lentils are tender and the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then serve topped with the caramelized onions.

title: Kibbeh Bil Sanieh (Baked Kibbeh)
instructions: Rinse the bulgur, cover it with cold water, and soak for 15 minutes; drain and squeeze it dry.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the chopped onion until soft.
Add half the beef, the pine nuts, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then set aside.
Process the drained bulgur with the remaining beef, allspice, cinnamon, remaining salt, and pepper until the mixture holds together.
Oil a baking dish and press half the kibbeh mixture into an even layer.
Spread the cooked filling over it, then cover with the remaining kibbeh mixture and smooth the surface with wet hands.
Score the top into diamonds, drizzle with neutral oil, and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35 to 40 minutes, until browned.

title: Fasolia bi Zeit (Green Beans in Olive Oil)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds green beans, trimmed and cut in half
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the green beans, crushed tomatoes, salt, pepper, cinnamon, and water.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 35 to 45 minutes, until the beans are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Shorbat Adas (Lebanese Red Lentil Soup)
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the carrot, potato, lentils, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the water or broth and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils and vegetables are very soft.
Blend until smooth, adding a little water if needed, then stir in the lemon juice and serve.

title: Fattoush
instructions: Toast or bake the pita pieces until crisp, then set aside to cool.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic, sumac, and salt.
Combine the romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, scallions, parsley, and mint in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss well.
Add the crisp pita just before serving and toss once more.

title: Mujaddara (Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions)
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils in a pot with 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes. Set aside half for serving.
Add the rice, cumin, allspice, 1 teaspoon salt, pepper, and remaining 1 cup water to the lentils. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the rice and lentils are tender and the water is absorbed, about 20 minutes. Rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff the mujaddara and serve topped with the reserved onions.

title: Shakriyeh (Lamb in Yogurt Sauce)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Put the lamb, onion, bay leaf, water, and 1 teaspoon salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the lamb is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Strain the lamb, reserving 2 cups of broth. Discard the onion and bay leaf.
Whisk the yogurt, cornstarch, egg white, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt in a heavy pot until smooth.
Set the pot over medium-low heat and stir constantly until the yogurt just begins to simmer and thickens, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the lamb and 1 cup reserved broth. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, adding more broth if needed.
Melt the butter in a small skillet. Add the garlic and mint and cook for 30 seconds, then stir into the yogurt sauce and serve.

title: Kibbeh bil Sanieh (Baked Kibbeh)
instructions: Cover the bulgur with cold water and soak for 15 minutes. Drain well, pressing out excess water.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet. Cook the chopped onion until soft, then add the pine nuts and cook until lightly golden.
Add 1/2 pound ground beef, cumin, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned; set aside.
Combine the drained bulgur with the remaining 1/2 pound ground beef, grated onion, allspice, cinnamon, remaining 1 teaspoon salt, and water. Knead until evenly blended.
Press half the bulgur mixture into an oiled baking dish. Spread the cooked filling over it, then cover with the remaining bulgur mixture and smooth the top.
Score the surface into diamonds and brush with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Bake at 375°F (190°C) until browned and cooked through, about 35 minutes.

title: Yalanji (Vegetarian Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 jar grape leaves, about 8 ounces, rinsed and drained
instructions: Mix the rice, tomato, onion, parsley, mint, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, salt, pepper, and allspice in a bowl.
Line the bottom of a wide pot with the potato slices and a few torn grape leaves.
Place a grape leaf vein-side up. Put about 1 teaspoon filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll snugly. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Arrange the rolls tightly in the pot, seam-side down, in layers.
Mix the water with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice. Pour over the rolls and place a heatproof plate on top to keep them in place.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender, about 50 minutes. Cool before serving.

title: Fattet Hummus (Chickpeas with Yogurt and Toasted Bread)
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, drained, with 1 cup cooking liquid reserved
2 pita breads, torn into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pita pieces with the olive oil and bake until crisp and golden, about 10 minutes.
Warm the chickpeas in a saucepan with the reserved cooking liquid and cumin. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt until smooth. Thin with a little warm chickpea liquid if needed.
Spread the toasted pita in a serving dish and spoon the warm chickpeas and some cooking liquid over it.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the chickpeas.
Melt the butter in a small skillet, add the pine nuts, and cook until golden. Spoon the butter and pine nuts over the dish and finish with parsley.

title: Mansaf
ingredients: 2 cups plain jameed sauce or reconstituted jameed
instructions: Put the lamb and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Add the onion, reduce the heat, and simmer until the lamb is tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Whisk the jameed sauce, yogurt, and cornstarch until smooth; warm in a separate pot, stirring constantly.
Add the cooked lamb and enough strained broth to loosen the sauce; simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Cook the rice with the turmeric, salt, and 1 tablespoon ghee until tender.
Toast the almonds and pine nuts in the remaining ghee until golden.
Lay the shrak bread on a large platter, spoon on some sauce, and mound the rice over it.
Arrange the lamb on the rice, pour over more sauce, and finish with the nuts and parsley.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Season the chicken with allspice, cinnamon, turmeric, and 1 teaspoon salt.
Brown the eggplant and cauliflower in oil in batches; set aside.
Put the chicken and onion in a pot, cover with broth, and simmer until the chicken is nearly tender, about 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth; measure 4 cups broth, adding water if needed.
Layer the eggplant and cauliflower in the bottom of a clean heavy pot, then add the chicken and drained rice.
Pour in the measured broth and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carefully invert the pot onto a serving platter; garnish with almonds and parsley.

title: Mujaddara
instructions: Bring the lentils and water to a boil in a pot, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in olive oil over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, salt, and pepper into the lentils.
Cover and simmer until the rice and lentils are tender and the water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Fold in half the onions and spoon the rest over the top before serving.

title: Warak Dawali
ingredients: 35 grape leaves, rinsed and stems trimmed
instructions: Mix the rice, ground lamb, tomatoes, parsley, mint, salt, allspice, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a grape leaf vein-side up and put about 1 tablespoon filling near the stem end.
Fold in the sides and roll snugly; repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line a heavy pot with the potato slices and arrange the rolls tightly on top, seam-side down.
Mix the water, lemon juice, and olive oil, then pour over the rolls.
Place a heatproof plate on top to hold the rolls in place; cover the pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until the rice and meat are cooked, about 1 hour.

title: Musakhan
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Rub the chicken with 2 tablespoons olive oil, allspice, salt, and pepper; roast until cooked through and browned, about 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the onions with the remaining olive oil over medium-low heat until soft and golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the sumac and lemon juice into the onions.
Spread the onion mixture over the flatbreads and bake for 8 minutes to warm and crisp the edges.
Set a chicken quarter on each flatbread and spoon over any pan juices.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet until golden and scatter over the chicken before serving.

title: Musakhan
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the chicken with 2 tablespoons oil, allspice, salt, and pepper; roast until cooked through, about 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in the remaining oil over medium-low heat until very soft, about 25 minutes.
Stir the sumac into the onions and season to taste.
Spread the onions over the bread and arrange the chicken on top.
Bake for 8 minutes, then scatter with pine nuts and serve.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Simmer the chicken and onion in a pot of water with 1 teaspoon salt until the chicken is nearly tender, about 25 minutes; reserve the broth.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower with olive oil and roast until browned, about 25 minutes.
Fry the eggplant in vegetable oil until golden, then drain.
Mix the rice with the remaining salt, allspice, cinnamon, and pepper.
Layer the chicken, cauliflower, eggplant, and rice in a heavy pot; pour in 4 cups of reserved broth.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender, about 30 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, invert onto a platter, and top with toasted almonds.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Simmer the lentils in 4 cups water until just tender, about 20 minutes.
While the lentils cook, fry the onions in olive oil over medium heat, stirring often, until deep golden; set aside half for garnish.
Add the rice, cumin, salt, and pepper to the lentils and stir.
Cover and cook over low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff gently, and top with the reserved onions.

title: Warak Dawali
ingredients: 35 grape leaves, rinsed and stems trimmed
instructions: Mix the rice, lamb, tomatoes, parsley, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and allspice in a bowl.
Place a small spoonful of filling near the stem end of each grape leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Line the bottom of a pot with potato slices and arrange the rolls snugly on top, seam-side down.
Drizzle with olive oil and pour in the water and 1/4 cup lemon juice.
Place a heatproof plate over the rolls, cover the pot, and simmer gently until the rice and lamb are cooked, about 60 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Maftoul with Chickpeas and Chicken
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pot and brown the chicken on all sides.
Add the onion, cumin, allspice, salt, and pepper; cook until the onion softens.
Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Remove the chicken and stir the maftoul and chickpeas into the broth.
Cover and simmer until the maftoul is tender, about 20 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
Serve the maftoul with the chicken and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Shakshuka
ingredients: 1 small loaf crusty bread, for serving
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set, 5 to 8 minutes.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve with bread.

title: Israeli Chopped Salad
instructions: Combine the tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, and parsley in a bowl.
Add the olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss well and serve fresh.

title: Majadra (Lentils and Rice with Onions)
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the lentils are just tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper into the lentils.
Cover and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 18 minutes.
Fold in half the onions and pile the remaining onions on top before serving.

title: Sabich
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Arrange the eggplant rounds on a baking sheet, brush with 1/4 cup olive oil, and season with 3/4 teaspoon salt.
Roast until tender and browned, turning once, about 25 minutes.
Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 9 minutes, then cool, peel, and slice them.
Warm the pita breads and spread hummus inside each one.
Fill each pita with eggplant, sliced egg, tomato, cucumber, and parsley.
Drizzle with tahini sauce and amba, then serve.

title: Chicken Soup with Matzah Balls
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 4 pounds), cut into pieces
3 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 teaspoon salt for the matzah balls
instructions: Put the chicken and cold water in a large pot and bring slowly to a boil, skimming off foam.
Add the carrots, celery, onion, dill, salt, and pepper.
Reduce the heat and simmer gently until the chicken is cooked and the broth is flavorful, about 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs, vegetable oil, water, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the matzah meal and refrigerate the mixture for 30 minutes.
Bring a separate pot of salted water to a simmer. With damp hands, shape the mixture into 1-inch balls.
Cover and simmer the matzah balls until tender and cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Strain the soup if desired, return the carrots and broth to the pot, and serve with chicken and matzah balls.

title: Masgouf (Iraqi Grilled Carp)
ingredients: 1 whole carp, about 3 pounds, cleaned and butterflied
instructions: Rinse the carp and pat it dry.
Rub the fish with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Grill it skin-side down over medium charcoal heat, turning once, until the flesh flakes easily, about 25–35 minutes.
Serve with tomato and onion slices and lemon wedges.

title: Quzi (Lamb and Rice)
instructions: Put the lamb, onion, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper in a pot with the water or broth.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer until the lamb is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the lamb and strain the broth; measure 3 cups broth for the rice.
Bring the measured broth to a boil, add the rice, cover, and cook on low until tender, about 15 minutes.
Fry the almonds in oil until golden, then add the raisins and cook for 1 minute.
Arrange the rice and lamb on a platter and scatter the almonds and raisins over the top.

title: Dolma (Stuffed Vegetables)
ingredients: 2 bell peppers, tops removed and seeded
instructions: Mix the rice, lamb, onion, tomato paste, parsley, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Fill each vegetable loosely with the rice mixture, leaving room for it to expand.
Pack the vegetables snugly in a heavy pot.
Stir the water and lemon juice together and pour them into the pot.
Cover and simmer gently until the vegetables and rice are tender, about 60–75 minutes.

title: Tashreeb Dajaj (Chicken and Bread Stew)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 40 minutes.
Place the torn bread in a serving dish and ladle the hot broth and chicken over it.

title: Bamia (Okra and Lamb Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound lamb stew meat, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the lamb is nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the okra and simmer gently until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve hot.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
1 pound stewing beef, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Drain the beans and simmer them in fresh water until almost tender, about 40 minutes; drain.
Heat half the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until golden.
Add the beef, turmeric, salt, and pepper; brown the beef on all sides.
Stir in the beans, dried limes, and water. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, fry the chopped herbs in the remaining oil over medium-low heat until dark green and fragrant, about 15 minutes.
Stir the herbs into the pot and simmer until the beef and beans are tender and the stew is fragrant, about 1 hour more.
Taste and add lime juice as needed; serve with steamed rice.

title: Fesenjan
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, and turmeric.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the chicken and brown it on both sides; transfer it to a plate.
Stir the ground walnuts into the pot and toast gently for 2 minutes.
Add the water and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses and sugar; simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender, about 30 minutes.
Taste for a balance of sweet and tart, then serve with steamed rice.

title: Zereshk Polo ba Morgh
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Season the chicken with turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until golden.
Add the chicken and brown it on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the water. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 40 minutes.
Boil the soaked rice in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, until the grains are tender outside but firm inside; drain.
Add a little oil and water to the rice pot, spoon in the rice, cover, and steam over low heat for about 35 minutes.
Rinse the barberries briefly. Melt the butter in a small pan, add the barberries and sugar, and cook gently for 1 minute.
Stir the saffron water into a cup of cooked rice. Spoon the saffron rice and barberries over the steamed rice, and serve with the chicken and its sauce.

title: Adas Polo
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Simmer the lentils in water until just tender, about 20 minutes; drain.
Boil the soaked rice in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, until tender outside but firm inside; drain.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan and cook the onion until golden and crisp at the edges.
Add the cinnamon, cumin, salt, pepper, raisins, and dates; stir for 1 minute, then remove from the heat.
Add a little oil and water to the rice pot. Layer in rice and lentils, then cover and steam over low heat for about 35 minutes.
Melt the butter and stir in the saffron water.
Spoon the onion and dried-fruit mixture over the rice, drizzle with saffron butter, and serve.

title: Kuku Sabzi
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Whisk the eggs with turmeric, salt, pepper, and baking powder.
Fold in the parsley, cilantro, scallions, dill, walnuts, and barberries.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof skillet and pour in the egg mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cook over medium-low heat until the edges begin to set, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake until the center is set and the top is lightly browned, 15 to 20 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, cut into wedges, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Mercimek Çorbası (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cumin; cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, water or stock, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are very soft.
Blend the soup until smooth, adding a little water if it is too thick.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the dried mint, and drizzle over the soup.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: İmam Bayıldı (Stuffed Eggplant with Onion and Tomato)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Peel alternating lengthwise strips from each eggplant and cut a deep lengthwise slit without cutting through the other side.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a skillet and brown the eggplants on all sides; transfer them to a baking dish.
Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat until soft, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Season with salt and sugar, then stir in the parsley.
Gently open the slits in the eggplants and fill them with the onion mixture.
Pour the water into the baking dish, cover with foil, and bake for 45 minutes, until the eggplants are tender.
Cool to room temperature before serving.

title: Kuru Fasulye (Turkish White Bean Stew)
ingredients: 1 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the soaked beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer for 30 minutes; drain.
Heat the olive oil in the pot and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the grated tomato, beans, water, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 60 to 75 minutes, until the beans are tender and the broth is rich.
Taste and adjust the salt, then let the stew rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Karnıyarık (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Peel alternating lengthwise strips from the eggplants and cut a deep lengthwise slit in each one.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a skillet and brown the eggplants; place them in a baking dish.
Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet and cook the onion until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in half the tomato, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Open each eggplant slit and divide the meat filling among them. Top with the remaining tomato.
Pour the water into the baking dish, cover with foil, and bake for 35 minutes, until the eggplants are tender.
Uncover and bake for 10 more minutes before serving.

title: Bulgur Pilavı (Turkish Bulgur Pilaf)
ingredients: 1 cup coarse bulgur, rinsed and drained
2 cups hot water or vegetable stock
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the bulgur and grated tomato and stir to coat.
Pour in the hot water or stock, then add the salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the bulgur is tender.
Turn off the heat and let the pilaf rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Onions)
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils and 3 cups of water in a pot; bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the rice, cumin, 1 cup water, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper. Cover and simmer until the rice and lentils are tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes.
Stir half the onions into the lentils and rice. Taste and add the remaining salt if needed.
Spoon into a serving dish and top with the remaining onions.

title: Kibbet Batata (Potato Kibbeh)
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1/4 cup olive oil, plus more for the baking dish
1 tablespoon olive oil, for the pine nuts
instructions: Cover the bulgur with cold water and soak for 10 minutes, then drain well and squeeze out excess water.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash until smooth.
Mix the potatoes with the bulgur, grated onion, salt, cumin, and pepper.
Oil a baking dish and press the mixture into it. Score the top into diamonds and drizzle with 1/4 cup olive oil.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until the top is golden, about 35 minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in 1 tablespoon olive oil until golden and scatter over the kibbeh before serving.

title: Fasolia bi Zeit (Green Beans in Olive Oil)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds fresh green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the green beans, tomatoes, salt, pepper, and water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat until the beans are tender and the sauce has thickened, about 35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Shish Barak (Lamb Dumplings in Yogurt Sauce)
instructions: Mix the lamb, onion, cinnamon, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. Fold into a half-moon and pinch the edges closed, then join the two corners.
Arrange the dumplings on a baking sheet and bake at 375°F (190°C) until lightly golden, about 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, cornstarch, and water together in a saucepan until smooth. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce simmers and thickens.
Add the dumplings to the yogurt sauce and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Warm the olive oil in a small skillet, add the garlic and dried mint, and cook for 30 seconds. Stir into the sauce and serve.

title: Tabbouleh
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Put the bulgur in a bowl with the lemon juice and let it soften for 15 minutes.
Add the parsley, mint, tomatoes, and scallions; toss well.
Pour in the olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Toss again and let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Mujaddara (Lentils and Rice with Onions)
ingredients: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
instructions: Put the lentils in a pot with 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply golden, about 25 minutes. Set aside.
Add the rice, remaining 1 cup water, cumin, salt, and pepper to the lentils. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, about 18 minutes.
Let the pot rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently.
Serve topped with the golden onions.

title: Shakriyeh (Yogurt and Meat Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef stew meat, cut into cubes
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the beef, water, onion, bay leaves, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer until the meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Strain the broth and reserve 2 cups. Discard the onion and bay leaves.
Whisk the yogurt, cornstarch, egg white, and 2 tablespoons water in a heavy pot until smooth.
Stir continuously over medium-low heat until the yogurt is hot and just beginning to simmer; do not let it boil hard.
Add the reserved broth and cooked meat. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, and season to taste.
Warm the olive oil in a small skillet. Add the garlic and mint and cook for 30 seconds, then stir into the stew with the white pepper.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Yabrak (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 jar (16 ounces) grape leaves, drained and rinsed
instructions: Mix the lamb, rice, salt, pepper, allspice, and 2 tablespoons lemon juice in a bowl.
Trim any tough stems from the grape leaves. Place a leaf vein-side up and put about 1 tablespoon filling near the stem end.
Fold in the sides and roll snugly into a small cylinder. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
Line a heavy pot with the tomato slices and crushed garlic. Arrange the rolls tightly in layers, seam-side down.
Pour in the water and 1/4 cup lemon juice. Set a heatproof plate on top of the rolls to keep them in place.
Bring to a gentle boil, cover, and simmer over low heat until the rice and meat are cooked, about 1 hour.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Kibbeh Bil Sanieh (Baked Kibbeh)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon olive oil, for the pan
instructions: Cover the bulgur with cold water and soak for 20 minutes, then drain very well.
For the filling, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet. Cook the finely chopped onion until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add half the beef, half the salt, half the pepper, and half the allspice. Cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the pine nuts and set the filling aside.
Process the drained bulgur, remaining beef, chopped onion, and remaining salt, pepper, and allspice until smooth and pliable.
Oil a baking dish. Press half the kibbeh mixture into an even layer, spread the filling over it, then cover with the remaining kibbeh mixture.
Score the top into diamonds and brush with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until browned and cooked through, about 35 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Fatteh Hummus (Chickpeas with Yogurt and Toasted Bread)
ingredients: 2 pita breads, split and cut into squares
1/2 cup chickpea cooking liquid or water
instructions: Spread the pita squares on a baking sheet and toss with the olive oil. Bake at 375°F (190°C) until crisp and golden, about 10 minutes.
Warm the chickpeas with the chickpea liquid in a small saucepan. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Put the toasted pita in a serving dish and spoon the warm chickpeas over it.
Pour the yogurt mixture evenly over the chickpeas and bread.
Melt the butter in a small skillet and toast the almonds until golden. Stir in the paprika.
Spoon the butter and almonds over the fatteh, sprinkle with parsley, and serve right away.

title: Guacamole
instructions: Halve and pit the avocados, then scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the avocado with a fork until chunky.
Stir in the onion, tomatoes, chile, cilantro, lime juice, and salt.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve promptly.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Fry the tortilla wedges in batches in hot oil until crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Toast the guajillo chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with the tomatoes, onion, garlic, broth, and salt until smooth.
Simmer the sauce in a skillet for 8 minutes.
Add the crisp tortillas and toss gently until coated and slightly softened.
Serve topped with queso fresco, crema, and cilantro.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
instructions: Place the chicken, onion half, garlic, and salt in a saucepan and cover with water.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the chicken is done, about 20 minutes; reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.
Shred the chicken with two forks.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotle chiles, oregano, and reserved cooking liquid until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the sliced onion until softened.
Add the tomato mixture and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread refried beans on the tostadas, then top with chicken tinga, lettuce, and queso fresco.

title: Pinto Bean Soup
ingredients: 1 pound dried pinto beans, rinsed and picked over
instructions: Combine the beans, water, onion, and garlic in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir in the salt once the beans are tender.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the cumin and tomatoes until the tomatoes soften, about 5 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the soup topped with cilantro.

title: Mexican Rice
ingredients: 2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and toast the rice, stirring, until lightly golden.
Carefully stir in the tomato mixture and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and salt, then bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Stir in the peas, cover again, and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
ingredients: 2 canned chipotle chiles in adobo, minced
instructions: Place the chicken in a saucepan, cover with water, and simmer until cooked through, about 18 minutes. Transfer to a plate and shred with two forks.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, chipotle chiles, oregano, and cumin; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken and cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Spread refried beans over the tostadas. Top with chicken tinga, lettuce, queso fresco, and crema.

title: Pork Carnitas
ingredients: 3 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Put the pork in a heavy pot and season with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Add the orange juice, orange halves, water, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat until the pork is tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the pork and discard the bay leaf and orange halves. Shred the meat into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork in batches until browned and crisp at the edges.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over. Place in a covered bowl for 10 minutes.
Peel the peppers, make a lengthwise slit in each, and remove the seeds. Fill each pepper with cheese and secure the slit with a toothpick.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and broth until smooth. Pour into a saucepan and simmer for 10 minutes to make the sauce.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Beat the yolks with the salt, then gently fold them into the whites.
Spread the flour on a plate and coat each pepper lightly. Dip each pepper in the egg mixture.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers, turning once, until golden; drain on paper towels.
Serve the peppers warm with the tomato sauce.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 cans hominy, 15 ounces each, drained and rinsed
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Put the pork, water, onion halves, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 hour.
Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry skillet for 20 seconds per side. Cover with hot water and soak for 15 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with 1 cup of their soaking liquid, oregano, and cumin until smooth. Strain the mixture.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the chile sauce for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Remove the onion halves from the pot. Add the chile sauce and hominy, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve the pozole with cabbage, radishes, lime wedges, and tostadas.

title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Put the tomatillos, serrano chiles, onion, and garlic in a saucepan. Cover with water, bring to a simmer, and cook until the tomatillos turn olive green, about 8 minutes.
Drain the vegetables and blend with the cilantro, salt, and broth until smooth.
Pour the salsa into a saucepan and simmer for 10 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable. Divide the shredded chicken among them and roll each tortilla around the filling.
Arrange the enchiladas seam-side down in a baking dish. Pour the salsa over them and top with crema and queso fresco.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until bubbling, about 15 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
ingredients: 2 canned chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, chipotle peppers, oregano, and cumin; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the broth, chicken, and salt. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and shred it with two forks.
Simmer the sauce until slightly thickened, then stir in the shredded chicken.
Top the tostada shells with chicken tinga, lettuce, crema, and queso fresco.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Place the tomatillos and serrano chiles in a saucepan, cover with water, and simmer until softened, about 8 minutes.
Drain the tomatillos and chiles; blend with the onion, garlic, cilantro, salt, and 1/2 cup water until smooth.
Simmer the salsa in a saucepan for 5 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll it up, and arrange seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the salsa over the enchiladas and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes.
Serve with crema and queso fresco.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in pork shoulder, cut into chunks
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 cans (25 ounces each) hominy, drained and rinsed
instructions: Combine the pork, water, onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water until soft, about 20 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with the oregano, cumin, and 1 cup of soaking water until smooth; strain the sauce.
Remove the pork from the pot, discard the bones, and shred the meat.
Stir the chile sauce and hominy into the broth; simmer for 30 minutes.

Pour in the tomato mixture and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer until the sauce thickens, about 8 minutes.
Spoon the chicken mixture onto tostada shells and top with lettuce, queso fresco, and crema.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over.
Place the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel, slit, and remove the seeds.
Fill each pepper with 1/4 cup of Oaxaca cheese and secure the opening with a toothpick if needed.
Spread the flour on a plate and lightly coat each pepper.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold in the yolks and salt.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Dip each pepper in the egg mixture and fry, turning once, until golden on both sides.
Warm the tomato sauce and serve it over the fried peppers.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded
2 cans (15 ounces each) hominy, drained and rinsed
instructions: Combine the pork, water, onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the pork is tender, about 1 1/2 hours, skimming the surface as needed.
Meanwhile, soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Blend the chiles with 1 cup of broth from the pot and the oregano until smooth; strain the mixture into the pot.
Add the hominy and simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the pork, shred it into bite-size pieces, and return it to the pot.
Serve hot with cabbage, radishes, and lime wedges.

title: Tres Leches Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9-by-13-inch baking pan.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup of the sugar until pale and thick; mix in the milk and vanilla.
Fold the flour mixture into the yolk mixture until just combined.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add the remaining 1/4 cup sugar, and beat to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the egg whites into the batter and spread it in the pan.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 25 minutes; cool completely.
Whisk together the evaporated milk, condensed milk, and 1/2 cup heavy cream.
Pierce the cake all over with a fork and slowly pour the milk mixture over it.
Refrigerate the cake for at least 4 hours.
Beat the chilled heavy cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla until soft peaks form, then spread it over the cake before serving.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
ingredients: 2 canned chipotle peppers in adobo, minced
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then stir in the tomatoes, chipotles, oregano, cumin, and broth.
Simmer for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Add the chicken and salt. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Shred the chicken in the skillet and stir it into the sauce.
Spoon the tinga onto tostada shells and top with lettuce, queso fresco, and crema.

title: Poblano Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over.
Place the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel them and make a small slit in each.
Remove the seeds and fill each pepper with Oaxaca cheese.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold in the yolks and salt.
Dredge the peppers in flour and coat them in the egg mixture.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the peppers until golden on all sides.
Warm the tomato sauce with the water and serve it over the peppers.

title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Simmer the tomatillos and serrano chiles in water until tender, about 8 minutes, then drain.
Blend the tomatillos and chiles with the onion, cilantro, and salt until smooth.
Simmer the sauce in a saucepan for 5 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry skillet so they are pliable.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll it up, and place it seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the green sauce over the enchiladas, then top with crema and cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until hot and bubbling, about 20 minutes.

title: Sopa de Tortilla
ingredients: 4 corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a skillet and fry the tortilla strips until crisp, then drain them on paper towels.
Heat the remaining oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes begin to break down.
Stir in the cumin, broth, and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with tortilla strips, avocado, queso fresco, and crema.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Pico de Gallo
instructions: Combine the tomatoes, onion, jalapeños, and cilantro in a bowl.
Stir in the lime juice and salt.
Let the salsa rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Guacamole
instructions: Cut the avocados in half, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the avocado with a fork until chunky.
Fold in the onion, tomato, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, and salt.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve promptly.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
ingredients: 2 canned chipotle chiles in adobo sauce
instructions: Place the chicken, salt, and onion half in a saucepan and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and shred it; reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, and reserved liquid until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the sliced onion for 4 minutes.
Add the tomato mixture and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread refried beans over the tostada shells and top with the chicken mixture, lettuce, and queso fresco.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Char the poblano chiles over a flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over.
Place the chiles in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel them and make a slit down each side.
Remove the seeds and fill each chile with 1/4 cup cheese; secure the openings with toothpicks if needed.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold in the yolks and salt.
Spread the flour on a plate and lightly coat each chile.
Dip each chile in the egg mixture to coat.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the chiles, turning once, until golden.
Drain briefly and serve with warm tomato sauce.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
3 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 cans (25 ounces each) hominy, drained and rinsed
instructions: Put the pork, neck bones, water, onion halves, garlic, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Meanwhile, soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with 1 cup of their soaking water until smooth, then strain.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the chile purée for 5 minutes.
Remove the pork and bones from the pot; discard the bones and shred or chop the pork.
Discard the onion halves, then stir the chile purée, hominy, oregano, and cumin into the broth.
Return the pork to the pot and simmer for 30 minutes; serve with cabbage, radishes, and lime wedges.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 1 cup of the chicken broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the fideo noodles and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly golden.
Pour in the tomato mixture and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining broth and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Stir in the cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, oregano, and cumin; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chipotle chiles, broth, and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend the tomato mixture until smooth, then return it to the skillet.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer for 8 minutes, until heated through and coated in sauce.
Spread refried beans on each tostada. Top with chicken tinga, lettuce, queso fresco, crema, and avocado.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cans (15 ounces each) hominy, drained and rinsed
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Put the pork, water, onion halves, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Transfer the dried chiles to a bowl and cover with hot water. Soak for 20 minutes, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the oregano, cumin, and 1 cup of broth from the pot until smooth. Strain the sauce.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the chile sauce for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the hominy and chile sauce to the pot. Simmer for 30 minutes, then remove the onion halves and garlic.
Serve the pozole with cabbage, radishes, lime wedges, chopped onion, and tostadas.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 8 ounces Oaxaca cheese, cut into 4 strips
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over.
Place the chiles in a covered bowl for 15 minutes. Peel off the skins, make a lengthwise slit, and remove the seeds.
Stuff each chile with a strip of Oaxaca cheese and secure the slit with a toothpick if needed.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, broth, and 1/2 teaspoon salt until smooth. Simmer the sauce in a saucepan for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Beat in the yolks, salt, and pepper just until combined.
Dredge each chile in flour, then coat it with the egg mixture.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the chiles, turning once, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Serve the chiles with the warm tomato sauce.

title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Place the tomatillos and serrano chiles in a saucepan, cover with water, and simmer for 8 minutes, until softened.
Drain the tomatillos and chiles. Blend with the onion, garlic, cilantro, salt, and chicken broth until smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a saucepan. Add the salsa and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir the shredded chicken into 1/2 cup of the salsa and keep warm.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable. Fill each with chicken and roll up.
Arrange the enchiladas seam-side down in a baking dish. Cover with the remaining salsa and queso fresco.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes. Drizzle with crema before serving.

title: Mole Poblano with Chicken
ingredients: 3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 slice white bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked. Reserve the broth.
Toast the ancho, pasilla, and mulato chiles in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side. Cover with hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet. Toast the sesame seeds and almonds until golden, then transfer to a blender.
Fry the raisins, tortilla pieces, and bread pieces briefly in the same skillet. Add them to the blender with the cinnamon, cloves, pepper, and drained chiles.
Add 2 cups chicken broth to the blender and blend until very smooth.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a pot. Carefully cook the chile mixture for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the Mexican chocolate and simmer for 15 minutes, adding reserved broth as needed to make a thick sauce.
Add the cooked chicken and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve with extra sesame seeds if desired.

title: Tacos de Tinga de Pollo
instructions: Simmer the chicken with half the onion, 1 garlic clove, salt, and enough water to cover until cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate; reserve 1/2 cup cooking liquid. Shred the chicken.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, remaining garlic, and reserved cooking liquid until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the sliced onion until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the blended sauce and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the shredded chicken and cook until hot and coated.
Warm the tortillas and fill with tinga. Serve with crema and queso fresco.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Simmer the tomatillos and serrano chiles in water until the tomatillos turn olive green, about 8 minutes; drain.
Blend the tomatillos and chiles with the onion, garlic, cilantro, salt, and 1/2 cup water until smooth.
Simmer the salsa in a saucepan for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Briefly dip each tortilla in the oil until pliable, then drain on paper towels.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, roll it up, and arrange seam-side down on plates.
Spoon warm salsa over the enchiladas and top with crema and queso fresco.

title: Pozole Rojo de Cerdo
ingredients: 1 pound dried white hominy, soaked overnight and drained
2 pounds bone-in pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 small head green cabbage, finely shredded
instructions: Put the hominy, pork, onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Add water to cover by 2 inches and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the hominy is tender and the pork pulls apart easily, 2 to 3 hours; skim foam as needed.
Soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water until soft, about 15 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with the oregano, cumin, and 1 cup soaking water until smooth; strain into the pot.
Simmer the pozole for 20 minutes. Remove the pork, shred it, and return it to the pot.
Serve with cabbage, radishes, lime wedges, and tostadas.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos
ingredients: 2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Arrange the tortilla wedges on a baking sheet and bake until crisp, about 15 minutes, turning once.
Toast the guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side, then soak in hot water for 10 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes until soft, about 8 minutes. Blend with the drained chiles, onion, garlic, salt, and broth.
Simmer the salsa in a skillet for 8 minutes.
Fry the eggs in a little oil to your preferred doneness.
Add the crisp tortilla wedges to the salsa and toss until coated but still slightly crisp. Serve with eggs, crema, queso fresco, and sliced onion.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 1 cup of the chicken broth until smooth; strain if desired.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the fideo and stir until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Carefully pour in the tomato mixture and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining broth and salt. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the noodles are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve topped with queso fresco.

title: Arroz a la tumbada
ingredients: 1 pound mixed firm fish and shrimp, cut into pieces
1 cup long-grain rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the tomato, onion, and garlic; cook until softened.
Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the fish stock, bell pepper, bay leaf, oregano, and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered until the rice is nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the fish and shrimp. Simmer gently until they are just cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Picadas veracruzanas
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for the griddle
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt until a soft dough forms. Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and press each into a small, thick disk.
Cook the disks on a lightly oiled hot griddle for about 1 minute per side, until set but still soft.
While each disk is warm, pinch up its edge to make a rim.
Add a little oil to the griddle and fry the picadas briefly on both sides.
Top with salsa roja or salsa verde, queso fresco, and onion.

title: Pescado a la veracruzana
instructions: Season the fish fillets with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, jalapeños, bay leaf, oregano, and water. Simmer until the tomatoes break down into a sauce, about 10 minutes.
Nestle the fish into the sauce, cover, and cook gently until opaque and flaky, 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and serve the fish with plenty of sauce.

title: Caldo de camarón
ingredients: 2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Simmer the shrimp shells in the water for 10 minutes. Strain the broth and discard the shells.
Toast the guajillo chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water until soft, about 10 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the tomatoes, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Heat the oil in a soup pot. Carefully pour in the blended mixture and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the strained broth, potatoes, carrots, and salt. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink and just cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the cilantro and serve with lime.

title: Camarones al mojo de ajo
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season them with the salt and pepper.
Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook gently until fragrant, about 1 minute; do not let it brown.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for about 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque.
Stir in the lime juice and cilantro, then remove the skillet from the heat.
Serve hot with lime wedges and the garlic butter from the pan.

title: Corundas de Michoacán
ingredients: 2 cups warm water, plus more as needed
12 fresh corn husks, softened in hot water
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt until you have a soft, pliable dough; add water a little at a time if it feels dry.
Divide the dough among the softened corn husks and shape each portion into a small triangle, folding the husk around it.
Arrange the corundas in a steamer, cover, and steam for 60 to 75 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Let them rest for 10 minutes, then unwrap and serve with crema and salsa verde.

title: Uchepos (Fresh-Corn Tamales)
ingredients: 6 cups fresh corn kernels, cut from about 8 ears
12 fresh corn husks, softened in hot water
instructions: Blend the corn kernels until mostly smooth, leaving a little texture.
Stir in the masa harina, butter, sugar, and salt until evenly combined.
Spoon the mixture into the softened corn husks and fold the sides and ends closed.
