Steam the tamales for 50 to 60 minutes, until the filling is set and pulls away from the husk.
Rest for 10 minutes before unwrapping and serving with crema.

title: Sopa Tarasca
ingredients: 4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 cups cooked pinto beans, with 1 cup cooking liquid
1/2 cup vegetable oil, for frying tortilla strips
instructions: Soak the ancho chiles in the hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with 1 cup of the soaking water until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes; add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, chile purée, broth, and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, then blend until smooth and return to the pot.
Fry the tortilla strips in the remaining oil until crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with crema, queso fresco, and tortilla strips.

title: Morisqueta Michoacana
ingredients: 4 cups cooked pinto beans, with 1 cup cooking liquid
instructions: Combine the rice, water, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 18 minutes; rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the beans and their cooking liquid, tomatoes, serrano, and oregano. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until thick and saucy.
Spoon the beans over the rice and finish with queso fresco.

title: Carnitas estilo Michoacán
ingredients: 3 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 cup chopped white onion, for serving
1 cup chopped fresh cilantro, for serving
instructions: Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Melt the lard in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the pork, water, orange halves, onion, and garlic.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook for 45 to 60 minutes more, turning the pork as it browns, until tender and crisp at the edges.
Discard the orange, onion, and garlic. Serve the carnitas in warm tortillas with chopped onion and cilantro.

title: Carne Asada Sonorense
ingredients: 2 lb thin-cut beef flap meat or skirt steak
instructions: Pat the beef dry, then rub it with lime juice, oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat a grill or cast-iron skillet until very hot.
Cook the beef in batches for 2 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and just cooked through.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes, then slice it across the grain.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, lime, and salsa.

title: Gallina Pinta
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 lb beef shank, cut into pieces
1 cup dried pinto beans, rinsed and picked over
2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the beef, beans, corn, onion, garlic, salt, and water in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours.
Check that the beans, corn, and beef are tender; add water during cooking if needed.
Remove the onion and garlic, taste, and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with cilantro, green onions, radishes, and lime.

title: Caldo de Queso Sonorense
ingredients: 2 green Anaheim chiles, roasted, peeled, seeded, and sliced
2 large russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
8 oz queso fresco, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and roasted chiles; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, broth, oregano, and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Lower the heat and stir in the milk and queso fresco; warm gently without boiling.
Taste for salt and serve with cilantro.

title: Frijoles Maneados
ingredients: 4 cups cooked pinto beans with 1 cup of their cooking liquid
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Mash the beans with their cooking liquid until mostly smooth.
Melt the lard in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans and salt, then stir and cook until thick and creamy, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the cheese until melted and stretchy.
Serve hot with warm flour tortillas.

title: Coyotas de Piloncillo
ingredients: 1 tbsp all-purpose flour, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in the shortening, then gradually mix in the warm water to make a soft dough.
Cover the dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Mix the piloncillo with 1 tablespoon flour. Divide the dough into 16 balls and roll each into a thin round.
Place filling on 8 rounds, leaving a border. Top with the remaining rounds and press the edges firmly closed.
Brush the tops with beaten egg, sprinkle with sugar, and prick each coyota once with a fork.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool before serving.

title: Tlayudas with Black Beans and Tasajo
ingredients: 1 cup cooked black beans, lightly mashed
1 cup salsa de chile de árbol
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tasajo until browned and cooked through; set aside.
Warm the black beans in a small saucepan until spreadable.
Spread asiento over each tlayuda, then spread with black beans.
Top with quesillo and heat on a griddle until the tortilla is crisp and the cheese melts.
Add tasajo and cabbage, fold in half, and serve with salsa.

title: Mole Coloradito with Chicken
instructions: Simmer the chicken in water until tender, about 35 minutes; reserve 3 cups of broth.
Toast the chiles briefly on a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast the sesame seeds, then toast the bread until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic on a skillet.
Blend the drained chiles, charred vegetables, bread, sesame seeds, cinnamon, cloves, and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the blended sauce for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add the remaining broth and salt; simmer for 20 minutes, then add the chicken and simmer for 10 minutes more.

title: Sopa de Guías
ingredients: 2 ears fresh corn, cut into rounds
1 pound squash blossoms, cleaned and roughly chopped
1 pound tender squash vines and leaves, chopped
1/2 cup fresh masa, mixed with 1/2 cup water
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth, add the corn, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the squash vines, leaves, and zucchini; simmer until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the squash blossoms and salt, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir the masa mixture into the soup and simmer until lightly thickened, about 5 minutes.

title: Memelas with Black Beans and Quesillo
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt into a soft dough; rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and press each into a thick oval.
Cook the ovals on a hot dry griddle for about 2 minutes per side.
While each memela is still warm, pinch up a shallow rim around the edge.
Spread with asiento and mashed beans, then return to the griddle until hot.
Top with quesillo and salsa roja, and serve warm.

title: Higaditos Oaxaqueños
ingredients: 1 pound chicken livers, trimmed and finely chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, tomato, oregano, and cumin; cook for 3 minutes.
Add the ground pork and chicken livers and cook, breaking them up, until no longer pink.
Pour in the broth, add the salt, and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, then slowly drizzle them into the simmering broth while stirring.
Cook for 2 minutes, until the egg forms soft ribbons, and serve hot.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 6 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup sesame seeds, plus 1 tablespoon for garnish
4 cups chicken broth, plus more as needed
instructions: Toast the chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 20 seconds per side; soak them in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil. Fry the tortilla and bread until golden; transfer to a plate. Toast the sesame seeds and almonds until golden, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Cook the raisins, onion, and garlic until softened; add the coriander, anise, peppercorns, cloves, and cinnamon, and toast briefly.
Blend the chiles, fried tortilla and bread, toasted seeds and almonds, raisins, onion, garlic, spices, and 2 cups broth until very smooth.
Pour into a large pot and simmer gently, stirring often, for 20 minutes. Add the chocolate, salt, and remaining broth; simmer until glossy and thick, about 20 minutes, adding broth if needed.
Add the cooked chicken and simmer until heated through. Serve with sesame seeds.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 1 cup walnuts, peeled if possible, soaked in water for 4 hours
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered all over. Cover for 10 minutes, then peel, make a slit in each, and remove the seeds carefully.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, add the garlic and pork, and cook until the pork is browned.
Stir in the apple, pear, plantain, raisins, almonds, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Cook until the fruit softens and the filling is fragrant; cool slightly.
Drain the walnuts. Blend them with the crema, milk, goat cheese, and sugar until smooth; chill the sauce.
Fill each poblano with the cooled meat mixture and arrange on a platter. Spoon walnut sauce over the chiles and garnish with pomegranate seeds and parsley.

title: Tinga Poblana
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 canned chipotle chiles in adobo, chopped
instructions: Put the pork in a pot, cover with water, season with salt, and simmer until tender, about 1 hour. Drain, reserving 1/2 cup cooking liquid, and shred the pork.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, oregano, bay leaf, and broth. Simmer until the tomatoes break down, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the shredded pork and reserved cooking liquid. Simmer until saucy and well combined, about 10 minutes; remove the bay leaf.
Spoon the tinga onto tostadas and top with queso fresco, crema, and avocado.

title: Cemitas Poblanas
ingredients: 4 thin slices beef milanesa, about 1 pound total
1/4 cup chopped fresh papalo, or 2 tablespoons chopped cilantro
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Dredge each slice in flour, dip in beaten egg, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the beef in batches until golden and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side; drain on paper towels.
Split the cemita rolls and spread the bottom halves with refried beans.
Layer each roll with a breaded beef cutlet, avocado, quesillo, pickled jalapeños, and papalo.
Close the rolls and serve while the cutlets are still crisp.

title: Rajas con Crema
instructions: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered. Cover for 10 minutes, then peel, seed, and slice into strips.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the poblano strips and corn; cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Stir in the crema and salt. Simmer gently until warmed through, about 3 minutes; do not boil.
Sprinkle with queso fresco and serve warm with tortillas.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
1/2 cup sour orange juice, or 1/4 cup orange juice mixed with 1/4 cup lime juice
1/2 tsp kosher salt, for the onion
instructions: Blend the achiote paste, orange juice, lime juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Put the pork in a bowl, pour over the marinade, and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Line a Dutch oven with banana leaves, leaving enough overhang to fold over the pork.
Add the pork and marinade, fold the leaves over the top, and cover the pot tightly.
Bake until the pork is very tender, about 3 1/2 hours. Shred the pork in its juices.
Toss the onion with sour orange juice and salt; let it pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Serve the pork in warm tortillas with pickled onion.

title: Sopa de Lima
ingredients: 2 limes, juiced, plus lime wedges for serving
instructions: Put the chicken, water, half onion, garlic, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the chicken is cooked, about 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken and strain the broth. Shred the chicken and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a soup pot. Cook the chopped onion, tomato, and bell pepper until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the broth, oregano, and black pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken and lime juice.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a skillet and fry the tortilla strips until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Serve the soup hot, topped with crisp tortilla strips and lime wedges.

title: Papadzules
ingredients: 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, and boil for 10 minutes. Cool, peel, and chop them.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly browned. Cool completely.
Grind the seeds to a fine meal in a blender or spice grinder. Add the warm broth gradually and blend until smooth. Season with salt.
Warm the pumpkin-seed sauce gently in a saucepan, stirring often; do not let it boil. Add a little warm broth if it becomes too thick.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the tomato and onion until soft, about 8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas until pliable. Dip each tortilla in the pumpkin-seed sauce, fill with chopped egg, and roll up.
Arrange the tortillas on a platter, spoon over more sauce, and top with the tomato mixture.

title: Frijol con Puerco
ingredients: 1 lb dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the beans, pork, water, half onion, and garlic in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partially covered.
Cook until the beans and pork are tender, 1 1/2 to 2 hours, adding hot water if needed to keep everything covered.
Stir in the salt and simmer for 10 minutes more. Remove the onion and garlic if desired.
Mix the chopped tomato, finely chopped onion, habanero, and cilantro in a small bowl to make a fresh salsa.
Ladle the beans, pork, and broth into bowls. Serve with the salsa and lime wedges.

title: Poc Chuc
ingredients: 2 lb pork loin, sliced into 1/2-inch-thick cutlets
1/2 cup fresh sour orange juice, or 1/4 cup orange juice mixed with 1/4 cup lime juice
1 red onion, cut into thick rings
instructions: Whisk the sour orange juice, garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Add the pork and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Brush the onion and tomatoes lightly with oil.
Grill the onion and tomatoes until softened and charred in spots, turning as needed. Set aside.
Grill the pork in batches until browned and cooked through, about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Chop the grilled onion and tomatoes and toss with the cilantro and any resting juices from the pork.
Serve the pork with the grilled salsa and warm tortillas.

title: Birria de Res Estilo Jalisco
ingredients: 3 lb beef chuck roast, cut into large pieces
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Char the tomatoes and onion in the skillet; blend them with the drained chiles, garlic, vinegar, cumin, oregano, cloves, peppercorns, cinnamon, and salt until smooth.
Put the beef in a large pot and pour the chile sauce over it. Add the water and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently for 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender; skim excess fat as it cooks.
Shred the beef and serve it in bowls with broth, tortillas, onion, cilantro, and lime.

title: Torta Ahogada
ingredients: 4 birote salado rolls, or sturdy crusty rolls
1 1/2 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1/2 cup thinly sliced pickled red onion
instructions: Put the pork, onion, garlic, salt, and water in a pot. Cover and simmer for about 2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Drain the pork, reserving a little cooking liquid, and shred it with two forks.
Boil the tomatoes until soft. Toast the árbol chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then blend them with the tomatoes, garlic, oregano, vinegar, salt, and 1/2 cup water until smooth.
Simmer the tomato-chile sauce for 10 minutes; add a splash of pork cooking liquid if it is too thick.
Split the rolls and spread the bottoms with refried beans. Fill with shredded pork and close the rolls.
Pour the sauce over the tortas to taste and top with pickled red onion.

title: Carne en Su Jugo
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Brown the beef in batches in the bacon fat, then return all the beef to the pot.
Simmer the tomatillos and serranos in water for 8 minutes, until the tomatillos turn olive green. Drain and blend with the garlic, chopped onion, and 1 cup broth.
Pour the blended sauce and remaining broth over the beef. Add salt and simmer for 35 to 45 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Stir in the pinto beans and cooked bacon; simmer for 5 minutes and adjust the salt.
Serve with cilantro, chopped onion, radishes, lime, and warm tortillas.

title: Pozole Rojo de Cerdo
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
2 cans (25 oz each) white hominy, drained and rinsed
2 teaspoons salt, plus more to taste
5 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Put the pork, neck bones, water, halved onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the drained chiles with the oregano, cumin, pepper, and 1 cup of the soaking water until smooth; strain the sauce into the pot.
Add the hominy and simmer for 45 minutes, until the pork is tender and the broth is flavorful.
Remove the pork, discard bones, and return the meat to the pot in bite-size pieces. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with cabbage, radishes, chopped onion, lime, and tostadas.

title: Enchiladas Tapatías
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Boil the tomatoes until soft. Toast the guajillo chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the drained chiles with the tomatoes, garlic, onion, oregano, salt, and 1/2 cup water until smooth; strain the sauce into a shallow bowl.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Briefly dip each tortilla in the sauce, then fry it in the oil for a few seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll it up, and arrange the enchiladas on a serving platter.
Spoon the remaining sauce over the enchiladas and top with queso fresco, crema, sliced onion, and lettuce.

title: Chilaquiles Verdes
instructions: Arrange the tortilla wedges on a baking sheet and bake at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, until crisp, or fry them in the oil until golden.
Boil the tomatillos and serrano chiles in water for 8 minutes, then drain.
Blend the tomatillos and chiles with the onion, garlic, cilantro, broth, and salt until smooth.
Simmer the salsa in a skillet for 5 minutes.
Add the tortilla wedges and chicken, and toss gently until coated and heated through.
Serve with crema, queso fresco, and sliced onion.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, thinly sliced
instructions: Cover the guajillo chiles with hot water and soak for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the achiote, orange juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, and salt.
Coat the pork with the marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork in batches until browned and cooked through.
Add the pineapple and cook for 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, fill with pork and pineapple, and top with onion and cilantro. Serve with lime.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 cans (25 ounces each) hominy, drained and rinsed
instructions: Put the pork, neck bones, water, half the onion, 2 garlic cloves, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Meanwhile, soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with the remaining garlic, oregano, and 1 cup of soaking water until smooth; strain the sauce.
Remove the pork, discard the bones, and shred the meat. Strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Stir in the chile sauce and hominy, then simmer for 30 minutes. Return the pork to the pot and heat through.
Serve with shredded cabbage, radishes, lime wedges, and tostadas.

title: Enchiladas de Mole Poblano
ingredients: 8 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side, taking care not to burn them; cover with hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and toast the sesame seeds, almonds, raisins, and tortilla separately until fragrant or lightly golden.
Blend the drained chiles with the toasted sesame seeds, almonds, raisins, tortilla, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, chocolate, and 2 cups of broth until smooth.
Pour the sauce into a large pot. Add the remaining broth and salt, then simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring often.
Warm the tortillas on a skillet until pliable, fill each with chicken, and fold in half.
Spoon mole over the enchiladas and garnish with queso fresco and sesame seeds.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and 1 cup of chicken broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and toast the fideo noodles, stirring, until golden brown.
Pour in the tomato mixture and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining broth and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Pescado a la Veracruzana
ingredients: 4 firm white fish fillets, about 6 ounces each
instructions: Season the fish with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomatoes, olives, capers, jalapeños, oregano, bay leaf, and water.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Nestle the fish into the sauce, cover, and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Arroz a la Tumbada
ingredients: 1 pound medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 pound firm white fish, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and rice; stir for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, oregano, cumin, and salt.
Pour in the fish stock and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the fish, shrimp, and mussels. Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the rice is tender, the seafood is cooked, and the mussels open.
Discard any mussels that remain closed. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with lime.

title: Picadas Jarochas
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt in a bowl until a soft dough forms. Rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Press each ball into a small, thick tortilla.
Cook the tortillas on a hot dry griddle for about 1 minute per side, until set but still pliable.
While each tortilla is warm, pinch the edges to make a raised rim.
Heat the oil in a skillet and shallow-fry the picadas until lightly golden on both sides. Drain briefly.
Spread each picada with warm beans and salsa. Top with queso fresco and onion.

title: Caldo de Mariscos
ingredients: 1 pound red potatoes, cut into chunks
1 pound firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and tomatoes; cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the oregano.
Add the fish stock, potatoes, carrots, and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the fish, shrimp, and mussels. Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the seafood is cooked and the mussels open.
Discard any mussels that remain closed. Stir in the cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Camarones al Coco
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails left on
instructions: Season the shrimp with salt and pepper.
Set out the flour, beaten eggs, and a mixture of coconut and panko in separate shallow bowls.
Coat each shrimp in flour, dip it in egg, then press it into the coconut mixture.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the shrimp in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Stir together the mayonnaise, lime juice, and cilantro. Serve the shrimp with the sauce.

title: Michoacán-Style Carnitas
ingredients: 3 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Put the pork, salt, orange halves, water, and bay leaf in a heavy pot.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the pork is tender, about 2 hours; turn the pieces occasionally.
Uncover and cook until the liquid evaporates and the pork browns in its rendered fat, turning to crisp several sides.
Add a little lard if the pot becomes dry before the pork is browned.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, and lime.

title: Sopa Tarasca
ingredients: 2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 cups cooked pinto beans, with 1 cup bean broth
4 corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and lightly fry the tortilla strips until crisp; drain and set aside.
In the same skillet, toast the ancho chiles briefly, then soak them in hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, soaked chiles, beans, and bean broth until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a pot and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add the chicken broth and salt; simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Serve with crema, queso fresco, tortilla strips, and avocado.

title: Uchepos with Cream and Salsa
ingredients: 6 cups fresh sweet corn kernels, cut from about 8 ears
12 corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
instructions: Blend the corn, milk, sugar, salt, and melted butter into a coarse, thick batter.
Drain the corn husks and spoon about 1/3 cup batter onto each husk.
Fold the sides of each husk over the batter, then fold up the bottom.
Stand the uchepos upright in a steamer basket over simmering water.
Cover and steam until set, about 1 hour; check that the water does not run dry.
Unwrap and serve warm with crema, queso fresco, and salsa.

title: Corundas with Pork Chile Verde
ingredients: 12 large corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
1 1/2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt; beat in the lard until the dough is light and spreadable.
Spread a thin layer of dough over each drained corn husk and fold it into a triangle-shaped packet.
Steam the packets over simmering water for about 1 hour, until the masa is firm.
Meanwhile, simmer the pork in a pot with enough water to cover until tender, about 45 minutes; drain.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos until softened, about 8 minutes.
Blend the tomatillos and chiles with the onion, garlic, chicken broth, and salt.
Pour the salsa over the pork and simmer for 20 minutes; stir in the cilantro.
Serve the corundas with the pork chile verde.

title: Charanda-Style Red Enchiladas
ingredients: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak the guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water for 15 minutes.
Boil the tomatoes until softened, about 8 minutes.
Blend the chiles, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, salt, and 1/2 cup soaking water until smooth; strain the sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a saucepan and cook the sauce for 10 minutes.
Lightly fry each tortilla in a little oil until pliable, then dip it in the warm sauce.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll it up, and arrange on a plate.
Spoon over more sauce and top with queso fresco, sliced onion, and crema.

title: Carne asada sonorense
ingredients: 2 pounds thin-cut beef flap meat or skirt steak
instructions: Season the beef with lime juice, salt, and pepper; let it sit for 20 minutes while the grill heats.
Grill the green onions over medium-high heat until softened and lightly charred; set aside.
Grill the beef over high heat for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Rest the beef for 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Serve with warm flour tortillas, grilled onions, lime wedges, and salsa verde.

title: Gallina pinta
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 pound beef shank, cut into pieces
1 cup dried pinto beans, rinsed and picked over
instructions: Put the beef, beans, hominy, onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot with 3 quarts of water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer gently for about 3 hours, until the beans, hominy, and beef are tender.
Remove the onion and garlic; discard them, or mash the garlic and stir it back into the broth.
Taste and adjust the salt, then stir in the oregano and cilantro.
Serve hot with lime wedges.

title: Caldo de queso sonorense
ingredients: 2 Anaheim green chiles, roasted, peeled, seeded, and chopped
2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
12 ounces queso fresco, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the roasted chiles and potatoes, then add the chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the milk and warm gently without boiling; season with salt and pepper.
Add the queso fresco and serve as soon as it is warmed through.

title: Frijoles maneados
ingredients: 4 cups cooked pinto beans with 1 cup of their cooking liquid
instructions: Mash the cooked beans with their cooking liquid until mostly smooth.
Melt the lard in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the beans and salt; cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cheese until melted and stretchy.
Serve hot with flour tortillas.

title: Coyotas sonorenses
ingredients: 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt; cut in the shortening until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the warm water gradually and knead just until a soft dough forms; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix the piloncillo with 1 tablespoon flour for the filling.
Divide the dough into 24 balls and roll each into a thin round; place a spoonful of filling on 12 rounds, cover with the remaining rounds, and seal the edges.
Brush the tops with beaten egg, prick each coyota once with a fork, and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly golden.

title: Mole Coloradito
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste
instructions: Toast the chiles briefly in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes and drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet; cook the onion, tomatoes, and garlic until softened and lightly charred.
Toast the bread, sesame seeds, and almonds separately in the remaining oil until golden.
Blend the chiles, vegetables, bread, sesame seeds, almonds, cinnamon, cloves, oregano, and 1 cup broth until very smooth.
Cook the sauce in a heavy pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 15 minutes.
Stir in the remaining broth, chocolate, and salt; simmer for 20 minutes until thick and glossy.
Add the cooked chicken and simmer gently for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Tlayudas with Beans and Quesillo
ingredients: 1/2 cup salsa de chile de árbol
instructions: Warm the lard in a skillet and cook the mashed beans with the salt for 5 minutes.
Spread a layer of beans over each tlayuda tortilla.
Top with quesillo, cabbage, and tomato.
Toast each tlayuda in a dry skillet or on a comal over medium heat until crisp and the cheese melts.
Add avocado and salsa, fold in half, and serve hot.

title: Sopa de Guías
ingredients: 1 pound squash blossoms, rinsed and roughly chopped
1 pound tender squash vines and leaves, chopped
1 ear fresh corn, kernels cut off
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a soup pot and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the squash vines, zucchini, and corn; simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the squash blossoms and salt, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the quesillo and serve as soon as it begins to soften.

title: Memelas with Black Beans and Salsa
instructions: Mix the masa harina, warm water, and salt until a soft dough forms; rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and press each into a thick oval about 1/4 inch thick.
Cook the ovals on a hot comal for about 2 minutes per side.
Pinch up a low rim around each warm memela, then spread with mashed beans.
Return the memelas to the comal and cook until lightly browned and heated through.
Top with salsa, queso fresco, and onion; serve warm.

title: Tejate
ingredients: 1 tablespoon toasted mamey seed, finely ground
1 teaspoon dried rosita de cacao, crushed
2 tablespoons granulated sugar, or to taste
instructions: Combine the masa, cacao nibs, mamey seed, and rosita de cacao in a bowl.
Gradually work in 1 cup cold water with your hands until the mixture is smooth and well combined.
Add the remaining water a little at a time, rubbing and lifting the mixture to create a foamy surface.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Serve cold over ice, spooning some of the foam into each glass.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 tablespoons sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
instructions: Toast the chiles briefly in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes; drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet. Fry the onion and garlic until softened, then add the tomatoes and cook until collapsed.
In the same skillet, toast the tortilla, raisins, almonds, and sesame seeds until lightly browned.
Blend the chiles, onion mixture, toasted ingredients, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, and 2 cups broth until very smooth.
Heat the remaining oil in a heavy pot. Carefully pour in the blended sauce and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining broth, chocolate, and salt. Simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring often.
Add the cooked chicken and simmer until heated through. Serve with sesame seeds.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Char the poblanos over a flame or under a broiler, turning until blistered. Cover for 10 minutes, then peel, slit, and remove seeds.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the pork, beef, onion, and garlic until the meat is browned and the onion is soft.
Add the tomatoes, pear, apple, peach, raisins, almonds, cinnamon, and salt. Simmer until the fruit is tender and the filling is fairly dry; cool slightly.
Blend the walnuts, milk, crema, queso fresco, and sugar until smooth. Chill the sauce.
Fill each poblano with the meat mixture and arrange on a platter.
Spoon the walnut sauce over the chiles and garnish with pomegranate seeds and parsley.

title: Cemitas Poblanas
ingredients: 4 cemita rolls or sesame-topped crusty rolls
4 thin slices beef milanesa, about 1 pound total
1/2 pound Oaxaca cheese, pulled into strands
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Dredge each slice in flour, dip in egg, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the beef until crisp and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side; drain.
Split the rolls and spread the bottom halves with refried beans.
Layer on the milanesa, Oaxaca cheese, avocado, and papalo.
Stir the chopped chipotles into the mayonnaise and spread on the top halves of the rolls.
Close the cemitas and serve right away.

title: Tacos Árabes
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, thinly sliced
instructions: Whisk the yogurt, lime juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add the pork and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or griddle over high heat. Cook the pork in batches until browned and cooked through.
Warm the flour tortillas on a dry skillet.
Fill each tortilla with pork and top with onion, cilantro, and chipotle salsa.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Molotes Poblanos de Papa y Requesón
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the mashed potatoes, requesón, epazote, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cool the filling.
Divide the masa into 8 balls. Press each into an oval between sheets of plastic.
Place filling down the center of each oval, fold the masa over, and pinch the edges closed to make a sealed oblong.
Heat the frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry the molotes in batches until golden, turning once; drain.
Serve topped with salsa verde, lettuce, queso fresco, and crema.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ingredients: 3 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
2 banana leaves, softened over a flame
1/2 cup fresh lime juice, for the pickled onion
1/2 teaspoon salt, for the pickled onion
instructions: Blend the achiote paste, orange juice, lime juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, and salt until smooth.
Coat the pork with the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Line a Dutch oven with banana leaves, leaving enough overhang to fold over the pork.
Add the pork and marinade, fold the leaves over it, and cover the pot tightly.
Bake until the pork is very tender, about 3 to 3 1/2 hours; shred it in its juices.
Toss the sliced onion with the lime juice and salt. Let it stand for at least 30 minutes, then serve with the pork.

title: Papadzules
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon salt, for the tomato sauce
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until fragrant; do not let them brown deeply.
Cool the seeds, then grind them finely in a blender or spice grinder.
Blend the ground seeds with 1 cup water and 1/4 teaspoon salt until smooth. Add a little more water if needed for a pourable sauce.
Heat the oil in a saucepan. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the tomatoes, epazote, and 1/4 teaspoon salt; simmer until the tomatoes break down into a sauce. Remove the epazote.
Warm the tortillas until pliable. Dip each in the pumpkin-seed sauce, fill with chopped egg, and roll up.
Arrange the rolls on plates, spoon over more pumpkin-seed sauce, and top with tomato sauce.

title: Sopa de Lima
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
4 limas dulces or Key limes, thinly sliced
6 corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
instructions: Put the chicken, water, halved onion, garlic, and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, and simmer until the chicken is cooked, about 30 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Strain the broth and return it to the pot; shred the chicken when cool enough to handle.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet. Cook the chopped onion until soft, then add the tomato and bell pepper and cook until tender.
Stir the vegetables and oregano into the broth. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, then add the shredded chicken and lime slices.
Heat the remaining oil in a skillet and fry the tortilla strips until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Serve the soup hot, topped with crisp tortilla strips.

title: Huevos Motuleños
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Warm the refried beans in a small saucepan over low heat.
Heat a little oil in a skillet and fry the tortillas one at a time until lightly crisp but still pliable; drain briefly.
In the same skillet, cook the eggs sunny-side up, in batches if needed.
Spoon beans over each tortilla and place one egg on top.
Combine the tomatoes, onion, habanero, and salt to make a quick salsa.
Spoon the salsa over the eggs and finish with peas and queso fresco.

title: Frijol con Puerco
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
2 pounds bone-in pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the beans, pork, water, halved onion, and garlic in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, until the beans and pork are tender, about 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Stir in the salt during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Add hot water if needed to keep the beans covered.
Remove the onion and garlic. Taste the broth and adjust the salt.
Mix the tomatoes, chopped onion, habanero, cilantro, and lime juice for the fresh garnish.
Serve the beans and pork in bowls with plenty of broth, topped with the tomato mixture.

title: Birria de res estilo Jalisco
ingredients: 3 pounds beef chuck roast, cut into large pieces
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried pasilla chile, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chiles briefly in a dry skillet, turning often; do not let them burn.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the onion, garlic, tomatoes, cumin, oregano, cloves, vinegar, salt, and 1 cup beef broth until smooth.
Strain the chile sauce into a large pot and add the beef, remaining broth, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently for about 3 hours, until the beef is very tender; skim excess fat if desired.
Shred the beef and serve it in the broth with warm tortillas, onion, cilantro, and lime.

title: Tortas ahogadas
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into large pieces
1/2 teaspoon salt for the chile sauce
1/2 cup water for the chile sauce
1 cup thinly sliced pickled red onion
instructions: Put the pork, salt, oregano, bay leaf, and water in a pot; cover and simmer for about 2 hours, until tender.
Remove the pork and shred it, reserving a little cooking liquid to keep it moist.
Toast the árbol chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the tomatoes, garlic, cumin, salt, vinegar, and water until smooth; strain the sauce.
Split the bolillos and spread the insides with refried beans.
Fill the rolls with shredded pork, place them in shallow bowls, and spoon chile sauce over them to taste.
Top with pickled onion and serve immediately.

title: Carne en su jugo
ingredients: 1 pound thinly sliced beef steak, cut into small strips
1 cup pinto beans, cooked and drained
1 cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems
1/2 cup chopped white onion, for serving
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp; leave about 1 tablespoon of fat in the pot.
Add the beef and cook, stirring, until browned.
Blend the tomatillos, quartered onion, garlic, cilantro, jalapeños, and 1 cup of beef broth until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture into the pot and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the remaining broth, salt, pepper, and cooked pinto beans.
Cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Serve hot with chopped onion, cilantro, radishes, and lime.

title: Pozole rojo de cerdo
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into chunks
2 cans (25 ounces each) white hominy, drained and rinsed
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Put the pork, neck bones, water, onion halves, garlic, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Toast the dried chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the oregano and 1 cup of cooking broth until smooth; strain into the pot.
Add the hominy and simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the pork, discard the bones, and return the meat to the pot in bite-size pieces.
Serve with cabbage, radishes, chopped onion, tostadas, and lime.

title: Tacos de barbacoa de res
ingredients: 3 pounds beef cheek or beef chuck roast
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the drained chiles with the onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, vinegar, salt, and water until smooth.
Place the beef in a covered roasting pan or Dutch oven and coat it with the chile mixture; add the bay leaves.
Cover tightly and cook at 300°F for about 4 hours, until the beef pulls apart easily.
Shred the beef and mix it with the cooking juices.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, and lime.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook until the beef is browned, then let the filling cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each pastry disc. Fold over and press the edges closed with a fork.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Season the beef with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet or wok over high heat. Sear the beef in batches, then set it aside.
Add the onion, tomatoes, and chili to the skillet. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the beef to the skillet. Add the soy sauce and vinegar, and toss briefly.
Fold in the fries and cilantro. Serve immediately with cooked rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Soak the black beans in water overnight, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion until softened, then stir in the garlic.
Add the pork shoulder, sausage, ham hock, drained beans, bay leaves, salt, pepper, and 8 cups fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2 1/2–3 hours, until the beans and meat are tender.
Remove the ham hock, discard the bone, shred the meat, and return it to the pot.
Serve the feijoada with rice and orange wedges.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth. Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the corn mixture, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk, queso fresco, salt, and pepper. Warm gently without boiling.
Serve topped with avocado slices and cilantro.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned.
Let the filling cool, then stir in the chopped eggs.
Place filling on each dough round, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Arrange on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until golden.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the pork shoulder.
Add the sausage and bacon; cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add the beans, bay leaf, water, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2–3 hours until the beans and pork are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
1 red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow chili pepper, seeded and sliced
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Toss the beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat and sear the beef in batches.
Add the onion, tomatoes, chili, and garlic; stir-fry briefly until just tender.
Stir in the remaining soy sauce and cilantro.
Fold in the fries and serve immediately.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and top with the eggs, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn and milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and cumin; cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the potatoes and chicken broth, bring to a boil, and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes in the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk and queso fresco; heat gently without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve topped with avocado and cilantro.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then let the mixture cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Spoon filling onto each dough round, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Arrange on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Heat a skillet or wok over high heat and add the vegetable oil.
Stir-fry the beef in batches until browned, then transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and tomatoes to the skillet and stir-fry briefly until just tender.
Return the beef to the skillet; add soy sauce and vinegar and toss to coat.
Fold in the fries and cilantro, then serve immediately with cooked rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Soak the beans in water overnight, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion until softened; add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sausage and pork shoulder and brown lightly.
Stir in the beans, 8 cups fresh water, cumin, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Remove the bay leaves and serve the stew with rice and orange slices.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn with the milk until coarsely puréed.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk and queso fresco, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, topped with avocado slices and cilantro.

title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Place filling on each pastry round, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Soak the beans in water overnight, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion until softened; add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sausage and pork shoulder and brown lightly.
Stir in the beans, 8 cups fresh water, bay leaf, salt, pepper, and orange halves.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and orange halves, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds very fresh firm white fish, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 ají amarillo chile, seeded and finely chopped
1 ear corn, cooked and cut into rounds
1 medium sweet potato, cooked and sliced
instructions: Place the fish in a glass or ceramic bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Add the red onion, lime juice, and ají amarillo; toss gently to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 10–15 minutes, until the fish turns opaque at the edges.
Stir in the cilantro and taste for seasoning.
Serve immediately with corn and sweet potato.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and top with the eggs, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth, then cook in a saucepan with the butter, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25–30 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso
instructions: Mix the warm water and salt in a bowl.
Gradually stir in the cornmeal, then knead in the butter until a soft dough forms.
Fold in 1 cup of the cheese and let the dough rest for 5 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the arepas during the last minute of cooking, then serve warm.

title: Argentinian Beef Empanadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the beef, scallions, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the beef, until browned; cool the filling.
Stir in the chopped eggs.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper. Moisten the edges, fold over, and press to seal.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and soaked overnight
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Brown the pork shoulder, then transfer it to a plate.
Cook the bacon and sausage in the pot until lightly browned. Add the onion and cook until softened; stir in the garlic.
Return the pork to the pot. Add the beans, bay leaf, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for about 2 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with orange wedges.

title: Peruvian Chicken Causa
ingredients: 2 pounds yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain and mash until smooth.
Mix the lime juice, aji amarillo paste, oil, and salt into the warm potatoes. Cool the mixture.
Combine the shredded chicken, mayonnaise, and red onion in a bowl.
Press half the potato mixture into a serving dish. Add the chicken mixture and avocado slices.
Spread the remaining potato mixture over the top and chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet. Cook the beef and onion until browned and softened.
Stir in the cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish.
Arrange the egg quarters, olives, and shredded chicken over the beef.
Blend the corn, milk, and butter until mostly smooth. Spread the corn mixture over the filling.
Sprinkle the sugar over the top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35–45 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso
instructions: Combine the warm water and salt in a bowl. Gradually stir in the cornmeal until a soft dough forms.
Knead in the mozzarella and butter until evenly combined. Rest the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a thick, flat round.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through.
Remove from the heat and stir in the chopped eggs and olives. Cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Place a spoonful of filling on each dough round, fold over, and seal the edges with a fork.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake until golden, about 20 minutes.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow chili pepper, seeded and sliced
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Sear the beef in batches until browned, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Stir-fry the onion and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar. Cook for 1 minute, keeping the tomatoes fairly firm.
Return the beef to the skillet and toss everything together until heated through.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with the French fries and rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the beans and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the beans are nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, then stir in the garlic.
Add the sausage and pork to the skillet and brown lightly.
Stir the meat mixture, bay leaf, salt, and pepper into the beans.
Simmer until the beans are creamy and the pork is tender, about 1 hour, adding water if needed.
Serve hot with white rice and orange slices.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened, then add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins over the top.
Blend the corn and milk until mostly smooth. Transfer to a saucepan and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 8 minutes.
Stir the butter into the corn mixture, then spread it over the filling. Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake until the topping is golden and the filling is bubbling, about 30 minutes.

title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are very tender, about 20 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk, cheese, salt, and pepper. Cook gently until the cheese melts; do not boil.
Serve topped with avocado and cilantro.

title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Place filling on each dough disc, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
1 medium red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow chili pepper, seeded and sliced
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Season the beef with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until crisp; drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat and sear the beef in batches.
Add the onion and chili; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar; toss briefly until the tomatoes begin to soften.
Fold in the fries and cilantro, then serve immediately with rice.

title: Brazilian Moqueca de Peixe
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks
instructions: Toss the fish with lime juice, salt, and pepper; marinate for 15 minutes.
Layer the onion, peppers, tomatoes, and fish in a large pot.
Pour in the coconut milk and palm oil.
Cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in the cilantro and green onions, then serve with rice.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 6 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and arrange the eggs, olives, chicken, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn with the milk until coarse, then cook with the butter, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso

Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the arepas for 5–6 minutes per side, until golden.
Top with the remaining cheese and cook briefly until melted.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then cool.
Stir the chopped eggs into the filling.
Place filling in the center of each wrapper, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Put the beans and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet; cook the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the sausage and pork to the skillet and brown lightly.
Stir the meat mixture, bay leaves, salt, and pepper into the beans.
Simmer partly covered for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans and meat are tender and the broth is thick.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 pound fresh firm white fish, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 ají amarillo pepper, seeded and finely chopped

instructions: Boil the sweet potato until tender, about 15–20 minutes; drain and set aside.

Place the fish in a glass bowl and toss with the lime juice, onion, ají amarillo, salt, and pepper.
Refrigerate for 10–15 minutes, until the fish turns opaque at the edges.
Stir in the cilantro and serve immediately with sweet potato and corn.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 6 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish, then top with the eggs, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat until thickened.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.

Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a 1/2-inch-thick disk.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.

Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

instructions: Season the beef with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Sear the beef in batches, then set aside.
Add the onion and chili pepper; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar. Cook briefly, keeping the tomatoes intact.
Return the beef to the pan and toss to combine. Stir in the cilantro.
Serve immediately with French fries and rice.

title: Brazilian Moqueca de Peixe
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into chunks
2 tablespoons dendê oil or olive oil
instructions: Toss the fish with lime juice, salt, and pepper; let marinate for 15 minutes.
Layer the onion, bell peppers, and tomatoes in a large pot.
Arrange the fish over the vegetables and pour in the coconut milk.
Cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Drizzle with dendê oil and sprinkle with cilantro.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Top with eggs, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until coarsely puréed.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Ajiaco
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound papas criollas or small yellow potatoes
2 ears fresh corn, cut into pieces
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes, skimming as needed.
Remove the chicken and set aside. Strain out the onion if desired.
Add the russet and Yukon Gold potatoes to the broth. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring until some potatoes break down and thicken the soup.
Add the small yellow potatoes, corn, and guascas. Simmer for 20–25 minutes, until tender.
Shred the chicken, discard the bones, and return the meat to the pot. Heat through.
Serve with cream, capers, and avocado on the side.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned. Let the filling cool, then stir in the chopped eggs.
Place a spoonful of filling on each pastry disc, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Fry the potatoes in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain and set aside.
Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat and sear the beef in batches.
Add the onion and chili pepper; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar; toss briefly until the tomatoes just begin to soften.
Fold in the fries and cilantro, then serve immediately with cooked rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1/2 pound smoked pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, sausage, pork shoulder, bay leaves, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Season with salt and pepper; remove the bay leaves.
Serve hot with white rice and orange wedges.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and top with the egg slices, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso
instructions: Mix the cornmeal, warm water, salt, and melted butter in a bowl.
Let the dough rest for 5 minutes, then knead until smooth.
Knead in 1 cup of the cheese.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the arepas during the last minute of cooking, then serve warm.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned; cool slightly.
Stir in the chopped eggs and chill the filling until cool.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each pastry disc. Fold over and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, rinsed and soaked overnight
8 ounces smoked pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
In a large pot, cook the bacon over medium heat until browned. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the garlic, pork shoulder, sausage, beans, bay leaf, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with rice, if desired.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 pound very fresh firm white fish, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 ají amarillo pepper, seeded and finely chopped
1 medium sweet potato, cooked and sliced
1 ear corn, cooked and cut into rounds
instructions: Place the fish in a chilled glass bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Add the red onion, lime juice, and ají amarillo; gently toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 10–15 minutes, until the fish turns opaque at the edges.
Stir in the cilantro and taste for seasoning.
Serve immediately with sweet potato slices and corn.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or thawed corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned, then spread the mixture in a baking dish.
Arrange the egg quarters, olives, and raisins over the beef.
Blend the corn with the milk until coarse. Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso
instructions: Mix the warm water and salt in a bowl. Gradually stir in the cornmeal until a soft dough forms.
Knead in the cheese and butter until evenly combined. Rest the dough for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the oil in a skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Serve warm.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned, then let the filling cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Place filling on each pastry round, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Arrange on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Season the beef with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef in batches.
Add the onion, tomatoes, and chili; stir-fry briefly, keeping the vegetables firm.
Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar, then toss in the fries and cilantro.
Serve hot with cooked white rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Add the beans, pork shoulder, sausage, bacon, onion, garlic, bay leaves, and water to a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Stir occasionally and add water if needed to keep the ingredients covered.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer uncovered until the broth thickens slightly.
Serve with white rice and orange slices.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the beef and onion until browned and softened.
Stir in the cumin, salt, and pepper, then spread the mixture in a baking dish.
Arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins over the beef filling.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Venezuelan Arepas
instructions: Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the cornmeal and knead until a soft dough forms; rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a thick disk.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Split the arepas and fill with mozzarella and avocado.

title: Argentine Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned.
Remove from the heat and stir in the chopped eggs. Let the filling cool.
Spoon filling onto the pastry discs, fold them in half, and crimp the edges closed.
Arrange on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes until golden.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned; set aside.
Add the onion to the skillet and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar; cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the skillet and toss with the cilantro.
Serve immediately with French fries and cooked rice.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and rinsed
instructions: Soak the black beans in water overnight, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, sausage, and pork; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the beans, bay leaves, and 8 cups fresh water; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2–3 hours until the beans and pork are tender, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the parsley, and serve with white rice.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the ground beef, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and top with the egg slices, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes until golden.

title: Venezuelan Arepas
instructions: Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the cornmeal and knead until a soft dough forms; rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a thick, smooth disc.
Heat the oil on a griddle over medium heat.
Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
