Transfer to a 350°F (175°C) oven and bake for 10 minutes until cooked through.
Split each arepa and fill with shredded mozzarella cheese.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
ingredients: 1/2 cup green olives, pitted and chopped
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned; let cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs and olives.
Place a spoonful of filling on each dough disc. Fold over and firmly crimp the edges.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 pound very fresh firm white fish, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 ají amarillo pepper, seeded and finely chopped
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the sweet potato in salted water until tender, about 15–20 minutes; drain and set aside.
Boil the corn until tender, about 8–10 minutes; drain and set aside.
Place the fish in a glass bowl and season with salt.
Add the onion, lime juice, ají amarillo, and cilantro; gently toss.
Refrigerate for 5–10 minutes, until the fish is just opaque on the outside.
Serve immediately with the sweet potato and corn.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, rinsed and soaked overnight
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Brown the sausage, bacon, and pork shoulder in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Return the meats to the pot. Add the beans, bay leaves, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 2–3 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with rice.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 6 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the corn mixture and cook, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Venezuelan Arepas
instructions: Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the cornmeal until a soft dough forms. Rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden.
Transfer the arepas to a 350°F (175°C) oven and bake for 10 minutes, until cooked through.
Mix the chicken, mayonnaise, and mashed avocado.
Split each arepa and fill with the chicken mixture.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until browned, then cool.
Stir in the chopped eggs.
Place filling in the center of each dough round, fold over, and crimp the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 pound fresh firm white fish, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 small aji amarillo pepper, seeded and finely chopped
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the sweet potato until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and set aside.
Boil the corn until tender, about 8 minutes; drain and set aside.
Toss the fish with salt, lime juice, onion, and aji amarillo in a glass bowl.
Refrigerate for 10–15 minutes, until the fish turns opaque at the edges.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with the sweet potato and corn.

title: Brazilian Moqueca de Peixe
ingredients: 2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks
instructions: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until softened.
Layer the bell peppers and tomatoes over the onion, then arrange the fish on top.
Pour in the coconut milk and red palm oil.
Cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 6 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish and top with the eggs, olives, and raisins.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Spread the corn mixture over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Colombian Arepas de Queso
instructions: Mix the cornmeal and salt in a bowl.
Gradually stir in the warm water and melted butter until a soft dough forms.
Knead in the grated cheese and let the dough rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and shape each into a 1/2-inch-thick round.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.

title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the chopped eggs, then cool the filling completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spoon filling onto the center of each wrapper, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Arrange the empanadas on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until golden brown.

title: Brazilian Moqueca de Peixe
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon dendê oil or red palm oil
instructions: Toss the fish with lime juice, salt, and pepper. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and bell peppers and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Layer the fish over the vegetables and pour in the coconut milk.
Cover and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, until the fish is just cooked through.
Stir in the cilantro, parsley, and dendê oil. Serve hot.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 medium red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow chili pepper, seeded and sliced
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Toss the beef with soy sauce, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Spread the potato fries on a baking sheet and bake for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet or wok over high heat. Sear the beef in batches until browned, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet. Stir-fry the onion and chili for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef and its juices to the skillet. Toss briefly with the cilantro.
Fold in the fries and serve immediately with white rice.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 6 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned and cooked through.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Arrange the egg slices, olives, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn and milk until mostly smooth. Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture and basil, and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 8 minutes.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Colombian Ajiaco
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound yellow potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound small waxy potatoes, peeled and sliced
1/2 cup guascas leaves, fresh or dried
instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, skimming as needed.
Remove the chicken and set aside. Strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Add the russet potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until they begin to break down.
Add the yellow and waxy potatoes, corn, and guascas. Simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the broth is thick.
Remove the chicken from the bones, shred the meat, and return it to the pot. Heat through.
Serve hot with cream, capers, and avocado on the side.

title: Ají de Gallina
instructions: Simmer the chicken in the broth until cooked through, about 20 minutes. Remove, reserve the broth, and shred the chicken.
Soak the bread in the evaporated milk, then blend until smooth.
Boil the potatoes until tender, about 20 minutes; peel and slice them.
Heat the oil in a pan. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, ají amarillo, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Stir in the bread mixture and 1 cup of reserved broth. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken, walnuts, and Parmesan. Stir and simmer until creamy, adding broth as needed.
Serve over rice with potatoes, egg halves, and olives.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 medium red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 yellow ají amarillo, seeded and sliced
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Season the beef with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet or wok over high heat. Sear the beef in batches, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Stir-fry the onion and ají amarillo for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce, and vinegar; toss briefly so the tomatoes soften but hold their shape.
Return the beef to the pan and toss over high heat for 1 minute. Stir in the cilantro.
Fold in the fries, or serve them alongside the beef. Serve immediately with rice.

title: Papa a la Huancaína
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain, cool slightly, peel, and slice.
Blend the queso fresco, evaporated milk, ají amarillo, crackers, oil, and salt until smooth and pourable.
Arrange lettuce leaves on a serving platter and place the potato slices on top.
Pour the huancaína sauce over the potatoes.
Garnish with the egg halves and olives. Serve at room temperature.

title: Causa Limeña de Pollo
ingredients: 2 pounds yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash until smooth.
While the potatoes are warm, mix in the ají amarillo, lime juice, oil, and salt. Cool the mash.
Mix the chicken with the mayonnaise and parsley.
Press half the potato mixture into a serving dish. Arrange the avocado slices over it, then spread the chicken mixture on top.
Cover with the remaining potato mixture and smooth the surface. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Serve on lettuce leaves, cut into portions.

title: Arroz con Pollo Peruano
ingredients: 1 yellow ají amarillo, seeded and chopped
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot. Brown the chicken on both sides, then transfer to a plate.
Blend the cilantro with the beer and chicken broth until smooth.
In the same pot, cook the onion and garlic over medium heat until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the ají amarillo.
Add the cilantro mixture and browned chicken. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Stir in the rice, peas, and carrot. Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff the rice and serve with the chicken.

title: Ajiaco Santafereño
ingredients: 2 ears corn, cut into 3 pieces each
1 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
2 guascas sprigs or 2 tablespoons dried guascas
instructions: Put the chicken, water, corn, scallions, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, skimming the surface as needed.
Remove the chicken and scallions. Add all the potatoes and guascas to the pot.
Simmer for 35 to 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes soften and thicken the broth.
Shred the chicken and return it to the pot; simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with cream, capers, and avocado.

title: Bandeja Paisa
ingredients: 1 cup dried red beans, soaked overnight and drained
1/2 lb pork belly, cut into strips
2 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced lengthwise
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, for frying plantains
instructions: Put the beans and water in a pot; bring to a boil, then simmer until tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Season with salt.
Cook the pork belly in a skillet over medium heat until browned and crisp, turning occasionally; set aside.
Season the ground beef with cumin, salt, and pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the beef, breaking it up, until browned.
Fry the plantain slices in oil until golden on both sides; drain on paper towels.
Fry the eggs to your liking and warm the arepas.
Serve the beans, pork belly, beef, rice, plantains, eggs, arepas, and avocado together.

title: Sancocho de Gallina
ingredients: 1 whole hen, about 4 lb, cut into serving pieces
1 lb yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and halved
instructions: Place the hen, water, scallions, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the hen is nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the corn and plantains; simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the yuca and potatoes; simmer until all the vegetables and hen are tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and adjust the seasoning.
Serve in bowls with lime wedges.

title: Arepas de Choclo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or thawed sweet corn kernels
instructions: Blend the corn, milk, sugar, and salt until mostly smooth, leaving a little texture.
Transfer to a bowl and stir in the masarepa and melted butter; rest for 5 minutes.
Shape the mixture into 8 small, thick patties.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-low heat and cook the patties for 5 to 7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Split each arepa while warm and tuck in mozzarella slices; serve as the cheese softens.

title: Empanadas Colombianas
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for the filling
instructions: Put the potatoes in a small pot, cover with water, and boil until tender; drain and mash lightly.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet. Add the beef, scallions, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook until the beef is browned.
Stir the potatoes into the beef mixture and let the filling cool.
Mix the masarepa, warm water, salt, and 1 tablespoon oil until a soft dough forms; rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 10 balls. Press each ball between plastic sheets into a thin round.
Place a spoonful of filling on one half of each round, fold over, and seal the edges firmly.
Heat frying oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the empanadas in batches until crisp and golden, about 4 minutes; drain before serving.

title: Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 8 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Spoon the beef mixture into a baking dish and arrange the chicken, eggs, olives, and raisins over it.
Blend the corn with the milk and basil until mostly smooth.
Cook the corn mixture in a saucepan, stirring, until thick; season with salt.
Spread the corn topping over the filling and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25–30 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Porotos Granados
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen cranberry beans
2 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the garlic and paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, pumpkin, tomatoes, stock, and oregano.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the beans and pumpkin are tender, about 35 minutes.
Stir in the corn and basil and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Cazuela de Vacuno
ingredients: 700 g beef shank or chuck, cut into 4 pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add the water, onion, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin, corn, and carrots; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the rice and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve each bowl with cilantro.

title: Charquicán
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika, and beef; cook until the beef is browned.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin, stock, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Mash the mixture roughly with a wooden spoon, leaving some chunks.
Stir in the peas and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with a fried egg.

title: Empanadas de Pino
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl; stir in the melted butter and warm water to form a dough.
Knead until smooth, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onions until soft and lightly golden.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook until browned, then cool the filling.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a round about 18 cm wide.
Place filling in the center of each round with an egg wedge, olive, and a few raisins.
Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges, folding them into a firm crimp.
Place on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes, until golden.

title: Arepas de Maíz Pilado
instructions: Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the cornmeal and knead until a soft dough forms; rest for 5 minutes.
Divide into 6 portions and shape each into a thick, smooth disc.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and cook the arepas for 5–7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Split and fill with cheese, shredded meat, or your favorite filling.

title: Pabellón Criollo
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans, drained and rinsed
2 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced diagonally
instructions: Season the steak with half the salt and the pepper.
Simmer the steak in water until tender, about 1 1/2 hours; reserve 1/2 cup cooking liquid and let the steak cool slightly.
Shred the steak into thin strands.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet and sauté the onion and bell pepper until soft; add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the shredded steak and reserved cooking liquid; cook until the meat is lightly browned and juicy.
Warm the beans with the cumin and remaining salt in a saucepan.
Serve with the cooked rice.
Fry the plantain slices in hot vegetable oil until golden on both sides, then serve alongside.

title: Hallacas
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
1 pound beef chuck, cut into small cubes
1/2 pound chicken breast, cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot; brown the pork and beef in batches.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, scallions, and sweet pepper; cook until softened.
Stir in the chicken, capers, olives, raisins, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add a little water if needed and simmer until the meats are tender and the stew is thick; cool completely.
Mix the cornmeal with the warm broth and annatto oil to make a smooth, pliable dough.
Lay out a banana-leaf piece and spread a thin circle of dough over it.
Spoon some cooled filling onto the dough, fold the leaf to enclose it, and tie securely with twine.
Repeat with the remaining dough, filling, and leaves.
Boil the hallacas for about 45 minutes, then drain and serve warm.

title: Asado Negro
instructions: Season the beef with salt, pepper, and Worcestershire sauce; let it stand for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef on all sides; transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Stir in the brown sugar and cook until it melts and turns dark amber.
Carefully add the red wine, scraping up the browned bits; stir in the broth and tomato paste.
Return the beef to the pot, cover, and simmer gently until tender, about 2 1/2 hours, turning occasionally.
Remove the beef and slice it thinly; simmer the sauce until glossy and spoon it over the meat.

title: Cachapas con Queso
ingredients: 8 ounces queso de mano or mozzarella, sliced
instructions: Blend the corn, milk, cornmeal, sugar, salt, and melted butter until the mixture is thick but still slightly textured.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and melt a little butter in it.
Pour in about 1/2 cup batter and spread it into a thick round.
Cook until the underside is golden and the top begins to set, about 4 minutes; flip and cook for 2–3 minutes more.
Place cheese on one half, fold the cachapa over it, and cook briefly until the cheese softens.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot.

title: Locro de Papa
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
6 cups water or light chicken stock
instructions: Warm the achiote oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes; stir in the garlic and cumin.
Add the potatoes and water or stock. Salt lightly, bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are very tender, about 25 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk and queso fresco and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Serve hot with avocado slices.

title: Llapingachos
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 cup grated mozzarella or queso fresco
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes; drain well.
Mash the potatoes until smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon achiote oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Mix the onion, cheese, and salt into the mashed potatoes. Cool until easy to handle.
Shape the mixture into 8 thick patties and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil and remaining achiote oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties in batches until browned on both sides and heated through.
Serve with peanut sauce.

title: Encebollado de Pescado
ingredients: 1 pound albacore tuna, cut into large chunks
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1 pound yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the tuna, water, halved onion, tomatoes, cumin, and salt in a pot. Bring to a gentle boil and cook until the tuna is just done, about 10 minutes.
Lift out the tuna and strain the broth, pressing the tomatoes through the strainer. Return the broth to the pot.
Add the yuca and simmer until tender, about 25 minutes. Remove any tough fibers and break the yuca into bite-size pieces.
Toss the sliced red onions with the lime juice and a pinch of salt; let them stand for 15 minutes, then stir in the cilantro and oil.
Flake the tuna and return it to the broth with the yuca. Warm gently and adjust the salt.
Serve the soup topped with the onion relish, with cooked plantains on the side.

title: Seco de Pollo
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1 cup naranjilla juice or unsweetened orange juice
2 cups cooked white rice, for serving
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin, and achiote.
Add the tomatoes, juice, cilantro, and stock; scrape up any browned bits and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken to the pot. Cover and simmer gently until tender and cooked through, about 40 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with white rice.

title: Fanesca
ingredients: 2 cups cooked bacalao, desalted and flaked
1 pound pumpkin, peeled, cooked, and mashed
Salt and black pepper to taste
2 ripe plantains, sliced and fried, for garnish
instructions: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the milk, bacalao, beans, peas, corn, rice, and mashed pumpkin. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often.
Cook uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring frequently so the milk does not scorch.
Stir in the queso fresco and cream; simmer gently for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with hard-boiled egg and fried plantain.

title: Chivito al Plato
ingredients: 2 beef tenderloin steaks, about 6 ounces each
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potato fries with half the oil and a pinch of salt, then bake until golden, about 30 minutes.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; set aside. Fry the eggs in the bacon fat and set aside.
Season the steaks with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a skillet and sear the steaks for 2–3 minutes per side, or to your preferred doneness.
Top each steak with ham and mozzarella. Cover the skillet briefly until the cheese melts.
Mix the mayonnaise and ketchup. Serve each steak with a fried egg, bacon, tomato, olives, fries, and the sauce.

title: Choripán with Chimichurri
instructions: Mix the parsley, garlic, vinegar, olive oil, oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper. Let the chimichurri stand while the sausages cook.
Grill the chorizos over medium heat, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Split and lightly toast the bread rolls on the grill.
Place a sausage in each roll and spoon chimichurri over the top.

title: Torta Frita
instructions: Stir the flour and salt together in a bowl. Rub in the lard.
Add the warm water gradually and knead until a smooth, soft dough forms. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and shape each into a disk about 1/4 inch thick. Make a small hole in the center of each disk.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C). Fry the disks in batches until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with sugar while warm.

title: Pascualina (Spinach and Egg Pie)
ingredients: 1 pound fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9-inch pie dish and line it with one sheet of puff pastry.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the spinach and cook until wilted. Let the mixture cool and squeeze out excess liquid.
Stir the spinach mixture together with the ricotta, Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Spread it in the pastry-lined dish.
Make four small wells in the filling and crack one egg into each well.
Cover with the second pastry sheet, seal the edges, and cut a few vents in the top. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake until the pastry is puffed and golden, about 40 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Arroz con Leche
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water and drain.
Combine the rice, water, cinnamon stick, and lemon zest in a saucepan. Simmer until most of the water is absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Add the milk and sugar. Cook gently, stirring often, until the rice is tender and the mixture is creamy, about 30 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon zest. Stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm or chilled, dusted with ground cinnamon.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 1 pound dried black beans, picked over and soaked overnight
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the sausage and pork shoulder; transfer to a plate.
Cook the bacon in the pot until browned, then add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the garlic, beans, bay leaves, browned meats, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the beans and pork are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve with rice, sautéed collard greens, and orange slices.

title: Moqueca Baiana
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Toss the fish with the lime juice, salt, and pepper; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the dendê oil and vegetable oil in a wide pot over medium heat.
Layer in the onion, peppers, and tomatoes, then arrange the fish on top.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Sprinkle with cilantro and scallions, and serve with rice.

title: Pão de Queijo
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine the tapioca starch and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Bring the milk and oil to a boil, then pour over the starch and stir until combined; let cool slightly.
Mix in the egg, then knead in both cheeses until a sticky dough forms.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and arrange them on the baking sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until puffed and lightly golden.

title: Galinhada
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Cook the onion in the pot until soft, then add the garlic and tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, turmeric, and rinsed rice.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff gently and stir in the parsley.

title: Brigadeiros
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
instructions: Combine the condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 8 to 12 minutes, until thick and the mixture pulls away from the pan.
Scrape the mixture onto a buttered plate and let it cool completely.
Grease your hands with butter and roll the mixture into 1-inch balls.
Roll each ball in chocolate sprinkles and place in small paper cups.

title: Empanadas Salteñas
ingredients: 2 tablespoons beef fat or neutral oil
instructions: Heat the fat in a skillet and cook the onions until soft.
Add the beef and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, oregano, chili flakes, and broth; simmer until the liquid is mostly absorbed, then cool the filling.
Fold in the chopped eggs and olives.
Spoon filling onto each wrapper, moisten the edges, fold over, and seal with a firm crimp.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F until golden, about 20 minutes.

title: Locro
ingredients: 1 pound dried white corn, soaked overnight
1 pound dried white beans, soaked overnight
1 pound beef chuck, cut into cubes
1/2 pound pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Drain the soaked corn and beans and put them in a large pot with the beef, pork, onion, and water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer gently for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the sausage and pumpkin and simmer until the corn and beans are tender and the pumpkin begins to break down, about 1 hour.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, and salt; add a little water if the stew becomes too thick.
For the topping, warm the oil in a small pan and stir in the chili flakes.
Serve the locro hot with the chili oil and sliced green onions.

title: Milanesa a la Napolitana
ingredients: 4 beef top-round cutlets, about 1/4 inch thick
instructions: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Put the flour in one shallow dish, beat the eggs with the parsley and garlic in a second, and put the breadcrumbs in a third.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the cutlets in batches until crisp and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side; drain on paper towels.
Arrange the cutlets on a baking sheet and top each with tomato sauce, ham, and mozzarella.
Broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling, then serve hot.

title: Carbonada Criolla
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes and broth, scraping up any browned bits from the pot.
Add the sweet potato, potatoes, pumpkin, corn, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef and vegetables are tender, about 1 hour; add a splash of water if needed.
Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.

title: Alfajores de Maicena
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then beat in the egg yolks and vanilla.
Whisk together the cornstarch, flour, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture and mix just until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut out rounds; place them on the baking sheets.
Bake until set but still pale, 10 to 12 minutes, then cool completely.
Spread dulce de leche on the underside of half the cookies and sandwich with the remaining cookies.
Roll the edges in grated coconut and let the filling settle before serving.

title: Ají de Gallina
instructions: Simmer the chicken in water until cooked through; reserve 2 cups of broth and shred the chicken.
Soak the bread in the evaporated milk, then blend it with the walnuts until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft. Add the garlic, ají amarillo, and cumin; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the bread mixture and reserved broth. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the shredded chicken and Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper, then simmer until creamy and heated through.
Serve over rice, garnished with hard-boiled egg and olives.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 pound beef sirloin, cut into strips
1 medium red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 pound russet potatoes, cut into fries
instructions: Fry the potatoes in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat a wok or skillet over high heat and add the oil.
Sear the beef in batches until browned, then transfer it to a plate.
Stir-fry the onion and tomato briefly, keeping them firm. Add the soy sauce, vinegar, and ají amarillo.
Return the beef and its juices to the pan. Toss briefly with the cilantro.
Fold in the fries and serve immediately with rice.

title: Papa a la Huancaína
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain, cool slightly, peel, and slice.
Blend the queso fresco, ají amarillo, evaporated milk, crackers, oil, and salt until smooth.
Arrange the lettuce on a serving plate and place the potato slices on top.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes and garnish with egg halves and olives.

title: Causa Limeña de Pollo
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain, peel while warm, and mash until smooth.
Mix the mashed potatoes with the ají amarillo, lime juice, oil, and salt. Let cool.
Combine the shredded chicken with the mayonnaise.
Press half the potato mixture into a serving dish. Layer on the avocado and chicken.
Cover with the remaining potato mixture and smooth the top. Chill for at least 30 minutes, then garnish with parsley.

title: Arroz con Pollo
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides; set it aside.
Blend the cilantro with the chicken broth until smooth.
In the same pot, cook the onion until soft. Add the garlic and ají amarillo; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cilantro mixture and water, then bring to a simmer.
Stir in the rice, peas, and carrot. Nestle the chicken pieces into the rice and cover the pot.
Cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through. Add the bell pepper during the last 10 minutes.

title: Ajiaco Santafereño
ingredients: 2 ears corn, cut into 3 pieces each
1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 cup chopped fresh cilantro, for serving
instructions: Put the chicken, water, corn, scallions, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes, skimming as needed.
Remove the chicken and scallions. Add the papa criolla and both kinds of potatoes to the pot; simmer until the potatoes soften and begin to thicken the broth, about 30 minutes.
Stir in half the guascas and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove the chicken meat from the bones and return it to the pot.
Stir in the remaining guascas and cook for 5 minutes. Serve hot with cream, cilantro, capers, and avocado.

title: Bandeja Paisa
ingredients: 1 cup dried red beans, picked over and rinsed
6 cups water, plus more for soaking
1/4 pound pork belly, cut into pieces
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon vegetable oil for the beef
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of water overnight, then drain.
Put the beans, 6 cups fresh water, pork belly, salt, and cumin in a pot. Simmer until tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Cook the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon oil until soft. Stir them into the beans and simmer for 10 minutes; season to taste.
Combine the rice and 2 cups water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until tender, about 15 minutes.
Cook the ground beef in 1 teaspoon oil until browned; season with salt. Fry the plantain slices in 2 tablespoons oil until golden on both sides.
Fry the eggs and warm the arepas. Serve the beans and rice with beef, plantains, eggs, bacon, arepas, and avocado.

title: Sancocho de Gallina
ingredients: 1 whole stewing hen, about 4 pounds, cut into pieces
1 pound yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
2 green plantains, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the hen and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until the meat is beginning to soften, about 1 hour.
Add the onion, scallions, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the corn, plantains, and yuca. Cook until tender, about 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook until tender, about 20 minutes. Stir in the cilantro and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with lime wedges and a little broth in each bowl.

title: Arepas de Choclo
instructions: Blend the corn, milk, sugar, and salt until the mixture is coarse but mostly combined.
Transfer to a bowl and stir in the cornmeal and melted butter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-low heat and melt a little of the cooking butter.
Spoon the batter into 4-inch rounds. Cook until golden underneath, about 5 minutes, then flip and cook the other side.
Split each arepa, fill with mozzarella, and cook briefly until the cheese melts. Serve warm.

title: Empanadas Colombianas
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus more for frying
1 tablespoon vegetable oil for the filling
1 cup cooked potatoes, peeled and finely diced
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beef, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook until browned, then stir in the potatoes and let the filling cool.
Mix the cornmeal, warm water, salt, and 1 tablespoon oil until a soft dough forms. Rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Press each ball between pieces of plastic into a thin round.
Place a spoonful of filling on one half of each round, fold over, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry the empanadas in batches until crisp and golden, about 3 to 4 minutes. Drain and serve hot.

title: Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
4 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the beef and onion and cook until the beef is browned and the onion is soft.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Set the meat mixture aside.
Blend the corn, milk, and basil until mostly smooth. Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the corn mixture, and cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Spread the beef mixture in a baking dish. Arrange the eggs, olives, and raisins on top.
Cover evenly with the corn mixture and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until golden and bubbling, about 25 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Porotos Granados
ingredients: 4 cups fresh or frozen cranberry beans
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, and oregano and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth, and pumpkin. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the beans and pumpkin are tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the corn and basil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Mash a few beans and pumpkin pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.

title: Charquicán
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, and paprika. Cook, breaking up the meat, until browned.
Stir in the potatoes, pumpkin, broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Mash the vegetables lightly with a spoon, leaving some pieces intact.
Stir in the peas and corn and cook for 5 minutes. Serve topped with a fried egg.

title: Cazuela de Vacuno
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef short ribs or beef shank, cut into serving pieces
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the beef, water, onion, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin, corn, and carrots. Simmer until the vegetables are almost tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the rice and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve each bowl with beef, broth, and vegetables, topped with cilantro.

title: Sopaipillas
ingredients: 1 cup cooked pumpkin, mashed and cooled
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for frying
instructions: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add the pumpkin and oil. Mix until a dough forms, adding warm water a little at a time if needed.
Knead the dough briefly until smooth. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough to about 1/4 inch thick and cut into 3-inch rounds. Prick each round once with a fork.
Heat 1 inch of oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C). Fry the rounds in batches until puffed and golden, about 1 minute per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Pabellón Criollo
instructions: Place the steak in a pot, cover with water, and simmer until tender, about 1½ hours.
Let the steak cool slightly, then shred it into thin strands.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet and cook the onion and bell pepper until soft.
Add the garlic and crushed tomatoes; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the shredded beef, water, salt, and pepper. Simmer until saucy, about 15 minutes.
Warm the black beans and cooked rice separately.
Heat the remaining oil in a skillet and fry the plantain slices until golden on both sides.
Serve the beef with rice, beans, and fried plantains.

title: Arepas de Maíz
ingredients: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, for the pan
instructions: Stir the warm water and salt together in a bowl.
Gradually mix in the cornmeal until a soft dough forms.
Rest the dough for 5 minutes, then knead until smooth.
Divide into 8 portions and shape each into a 1/2-inch-thick disk.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat.
Cook the arepas until browned, about 5 minutes per side.
Transfer to a 400°F oven and bake until cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Cool briefly, split open, and fill as desired.

title: Hallacas
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless beef chuck, cut into small pieces
1 pound boneless pork shoulder, cut into small pieces
1 pound chicken thighs, boneless and diced
20 banana leaves, cleaned and cut into large squares
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot and brown the beef, pork, and chicken in batches.
Add the onions, bell pepper, and garlic; cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes, wine, capers, raisins, olives, salt, cumin, and pepper.
Simmer gently until the meats are tender and the stew is thick, about 1½ hours; cool completely.
Mix the cornmeal with the warm broth and annatto oil to make a soft, spreadable dough.
Lay a banana leaf square flat and spread a thin layer of dough over the center.
Spoon some cooled stew onto the dough and fold the leaf into a neat packet.
Tie each packet securely with kitchen twine.
Boil the hallacas in a large pot of water for about 45 minutes.
Drain and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Asado Negro
ingredients: 3 pounds beef eye of round, tied
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Stir in the brown sugar and cook until dark and caramelized, watching closely so it does not burn.
Carefully add the wine, broth, and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up browned bits.
Return the beef to the pot and add the bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently, turning the beef occasionally, until very tender, about 2½ hours.
Remove the beef and rest it for 10 minutes; simmer the sauce until thickened.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Cachapas de Maíz
ingredients: 8 ounces queso de mano or mozzarella, sliced
instructions: Blend the corn, milk, cornmeal, sugar, and salt until mostly smooth but still slightly textured.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Pour in about 1/2 cup batter and spread it into a thick round.
Cook until the edges look set and the underside is golden, about 4 minutes.
Flip and cook the other side until golden, about 3 minutes.
Place cheese on one half, fold the cachapa over, and cook briefly until the cheese softens.
Repeat with the remaining batter and butter; serve warm.

title: Locro de papa
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the achiote oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and water or broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are very tender, about 25 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the milk, queso fresco, and salt. Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Serve hot with avocado and cilantro.

title: Encebollado de pescado
ingredients: 1 pound albacore tuna, cut into large chunks
1 pound yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the tuna, water, halved onion, tomatoes, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and salt in a pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until the tuna is just cooked, about 10 minutes.
Lift out the tuna and strain the broth into a bowl. Discard the cooked vegetables.
Return the broth to the pot, add the yuca, and simmer until tender, about 25 minutes. Remove the yuca and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Toss the sliced red onions with lime juice and cilantro. Let them stand while the soup finishes.
Flake the tuna into large pieces and return it to the broth with the yuca. Warm gently for 2 minutes.
Serve with the marinated onion, avocado, a drizzle of oil, and white rice on the side.

title: Llapingachos
ingredients: 2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon of achiote oil in a skillet. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Mix the onion and queso fresco into the mashed potatoes. Let the mixture cool until easy to handle.
Shape the potato mixture into 8 thick patties. Chill for 15 minutes so they hold together.
Heat the vegetable oil and remaining achiote oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties in batches until browned and crisp on both sides, about 4 minutes per side.
Serve with warm peanut sauce, avocado, and a fried egg.

title: Fanesca
ingredients: 1 cup dried salted cod, soaked overnight and drained
6 cups water, plus more as needed
instructions: Simmer the cod in 6 cups of water until tender, about 15 minutes. Lift it out, reserve the cooking liquid, and flake the fish, removing any bones.
Heat the achiote oil in a large pot. Cook the onion until soft, then stir in the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the reserved fish liquid, beans, lentils, corn, peas, pumpkin, squash, and rice. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the milk and queso fresco. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, adding a little water if the soup is too thick.
Fold in the flaked cod and cilantro and warm through for 3 minutes.
Serve topped with hard-boiled egg and fried plantain.

title: Seco de pollo
instructions: Heat the achiote oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, and achiote and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and brown it lightly on all sides.
Pour in the naranjilla juice, tomatoes, and broth. Add the cilantro and salt.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened, about 45 minutes. Turn the chicken once or twice while it cooks.
Serve with white rice and fried plantain slices.

title: Chivito al Plato
ingredients: 2 beef sirloin steaks, about 6 ounces each
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Season the steaks with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the steaks for 3–4 minutes per side, or until done to your liking.
Top each steak with ham and mozzarella; cover the skillet briefly until the cheese melts.
Fry the eggs in the same skillet until the whites are set.
Serve each steak with mayonnaise, an egg, tomato, olives, and french fries.

title: Torta Frita
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Rub in the lard until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the warm water gradually and knead until a soft dough forms.
Cover and rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Divide into 8 pieces and flatten each into a round; make a small hole in the center.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the rounds in batches until golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Milanesa a la Napolitana
ingredients: 4 thin beef cutlets, about 5 ounces each
½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
instructions: Season the cutlets with salt and pepper.
Put the flour, eggs whisked with water, and breadcrumbs in separate shallow dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and fry the cutlets in batches until golden and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and place the cutlets on a baking sheet.
Spoon tomato sauce over each cutlet, add ham and mozzarella, and bake until the cheese melts, about 5 minutes.

title: Pascualina
ingredients: 10 ounces fresh spinach, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 9-inch pie dish.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted; let the mixture cool, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Stir in the salt, pepper, nutmeg, ricotta, Parmesan, and 1 egg.
Line the pie dish with one sheet of pastry and spoon in the filling.
Make 3 shallow wells in the filling and carefully crack an egg into each well.
Cover with the second pastry sheet, seal and trim the edges, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until golden, and rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Chajá
instructions: Combine the water and granulated sugar in a small saucepan and bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from the heat, stir in the sherry, and let the syrup cool.
Beat the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla until soft peaks form.
Slice the sponge cake horizontally into 2 layers and brush the cut sides with the cooled syrup.
Spread dulce de leche over the bottom layer, then add half the whipped cream and half the peaches.
Set the top layer in place and cover the cake with the remaining whipped cream and peaches.
Press the crumbled meringue over the top and sides; chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Feijão Carioca (Everyday Brazilian Pinto Beans)
ingredients: 1 pound dried pinto beans, picked over and rinsed
8 cups water, plus more for soaking
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of water overnight, then drain and rinse.
Put the beans in a pot with 8 cups fresh water and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in a ladleful of beans and mash them lightly.
Scrape the onion mixture into the pot. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.

title: Moqueca Baiana (Bahian Fish Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into large pieces
instructions: Season the fish with the lime juice, salt, and pepper. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Layer the onion, bell pepper, and tomatoes in a wide pot.
Arrange the fish over the vegetables and pour in the coconut milk.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Stir in the dendê oil, cilantro, and scallions. Serve hot.

title: Galinhada (Brazilian Chicken and Rice)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
instructions: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the peas and parsley. Cover and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Pão de Queijo (Brazilian Cheese Bread)
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Bring the milk, oil, and salt to a boil in a small saucepan.
Put the tapioca starch in a bowl. Pour in the hot milk mixture and stir until evenly moistened. Let cool for 10 minutes.
Mix in the egg, then knead in the Parmesan until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them on the baking sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until puffed and lightly golden.

title: Brigadeiros (Brazilian Chocolate Truffles)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
instructions: Grease a plate and set it aside. Add the condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter to a saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the bottom of the pan, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Spread the mixture on the greased plate and let it cool completely.
Grease your hands lightly with butter. Roll the mixture into 1-inch balls and coat each one in chocolate sprinkles.

title: Empanadas Salteñas
ingredients: 2 tablespoons beef fat or neutral oil
1 small red bell pepper, finely chopped
2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced small
instructions: Cook the potatoes in boiling salted water until just tender; drain and cool.
Heat the fat in a pan and cook the onions and bell pepper until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika, chili, and salt; cook until the beef is just browned.
Stir in the potatoes and scallions, then cool the filling completely and mix in the chopped eggs.
Put a spoonful of filling on each pastry round, fold over, and seal the edges with a firm crimp.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 220°C (425°F) until golden, about 15–20 minutes.

title: Locro
ingredients: 250 g dried white corn kernels, soaked overnight
200 g dried white beans, soaked overnight
500 g beef chuck, cut into chunks
250 g pork belly, cut into pieces
250 g pork ribs, cut into pieces
1 large butternut squash, peeled and diced
instructions: Drain the soaked corn and beans.
Put the corn, beans, beef, pork belly, ribs, chorizo, onion, leek, and bay leaves in a large pot; cover with water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the squash, paprika, cumin, and salt; simmer until the squash breaks down and the corn is tender, about 45 minutes.
For the sauce, warm the oil in a small pan and stir in the crushed red pepper; cook briefly, then remove from the heat.
Serve the locro hot with the red pepper sauce and sliced scallions.

title: Milanesa a la Napolitana
ingredients: 4 beef top-round cutlets, about 150 g each
½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
instructions: Pound the cutlets until evenly thin, then season both sides with salt and pepper.
Place the flour, beaten eggs mixed with milk, and breadcrumbs in separate shallow dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs to cover well.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and fry the cutlets in batches until golden on both sides; drain on paper towels.
Arrange the cutlets on a baking sheet, spread with tomato sauce, and top with mozzarella, Parmesan, and oregano.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) until the cheese is melted and bubbling, about 8 minutes.

title: Carbonada Criolla
ingredients: 600 g beef chuck, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches; set it aside.
Cook the onion and bell pepper in the same pot until softened, then add the tomatoes.
Return the beef to the pot and stir in the potatoes, sweet potatoes, pumpkin, carrot, stock, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef and vegetables are tender, about 50 minutes; add a little water if needed.
Stir in the corn and dried apricots and cook for 10 more minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot.

title: Chimichurri
ingredients: ½ cup fresh parsley leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Combine the parsley, garlic, oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Stir in the red wine vinegar and warm water.
Slowly mix in the olive oil until combined.
Let the chimichurri stand for at least 30 minutes before serving with grilled meat.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let stand for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper; mix gently.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and flour to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and cream, then simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
2 lb green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage wedges in a large pot.
Add a layer of lamb, sprinkle with some flour, salt, and peppercorns, then repeat the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pork Patties)
instructions: Combine the pork, onion, egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Beat the mixture until smooth and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Shape the mixture into oval patties using a spoon.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb salmon fillet, skinned and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat.
Add the leek and carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fish stock; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and cream and simmer gently until the salmon is cooked, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the dill, and serve.

title: Icelandic Skyr Cake (Skyrterta)
instructions: Mix the graham cracker crumbs with the melted butter and press into the base of a springform pan.
Chill the crust while preparing the filling.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let it soften for 5 minutes.
Beat the skyr with the sugar, vanilla, and lemon juice.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form, then fold it into the skyr mixture.
Warm the softened gelatin gently until dissolved, then stir it into the filling.
Spread the filling over the crust and chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Swedish Köttbullar (Meatballs)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set them aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 8 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a large pot, sprinkling flour, peppercorns, and salt between the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pan-Fried Meat Patties)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Chill the mixture for 15 minutes so it firms up.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties with a spoon and fry in batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
1 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the leek for 4 minutes, until softened.
Add the potatoes, carrot, stock, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the salmon and cream, then simmer gently for 5 minutes, until the salmon is just cooked.
Stir in the dill and serve.

title: Icelandic Plokkfiskur (Fish and Potato Mash)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and roughly mash.
Poach the cod in simmering water for 6 to 8 minutes, until it flakes easily; drain and flake it into pieces.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk.
Simmer until the sauce thickens, then season with salt and pepper.
Fold in the potatoes and fish and heat gently until warmed through.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the milk and breadcrumbs together and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium heat and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer them to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and cream, then simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 8 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 medium green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage wedges in a large heavy pot, sprinkling each layer with salt and peppercorns.
Sprinkle the flour over the layers and pour in the water.
Cover and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is very tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper until smooth and slightly sticky.
Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties using a spoon and place them in the skillet.
Fry for 5 to 7 minutes per side, turning once, until browned and cooked through.

title: Finnish Karjalanpiirakka (Karelian Rice Pies)
instructions: Bring the rice and water to a boil in a saucepan and cook until the water is absorbed.
Add the milk and 1 teaspoon salt; simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is thick and tender, about 45 minutes. Cool the porridge.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup water, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt into a firm dough.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a thin oval.
Spoon rice porridge down the center of each oval, leaving a border around the edges.
Fold and pleat the edges over the filling, leaving the center exposed.
Bake on a hot baking sheet at 475°F (245°C) for 10 to 15 minutes, until lightly browned.
Mix the melted butter and 1/2 cup milk, then brush the hot pies with the mixture.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Whisk together the egg, milk, and vanilla, then stir into the flour mixture to make a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough to 1/4-inch thickness and cut into diamond shapes.
Make a short slit in the center of each diamond, then pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the kleinur in batches, turning once, until golden; drain on paper towels.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl; let stand for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, onion, egg, allspice, salt, and pepper; mix gently.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 10 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 medium green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Sprinkle the lamb with the flour and salt.
Layer half the cabbage in a large pot, then add half the lamb and peppercorns.
Repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes, if desired.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk and melted butter.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and brush each well with butter.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter.
Cook until the bottoms are golden, turning each pancake with a skewer to cook all sides.
Serve warm with jam and powdered sugar.

title: Finnish Karelian Pies (Karjalanpiirakat)
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for egg butter
instructions: Bring 2 cups water to a boil; add the rice and simmer until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the milk and salt; simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is thick and tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir in 2 tablespoons butter and cool the rice porridge.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and 1/2 cup water into a firm dough.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each piece into a thin oval.
Spoon rice porridge down the center of each oval, leaving a border on both sides.
Fold the edges over the filling and crimp them into a pleated shape.
Bake at 475°F (245°C) for 12 to 15 minutes, until the crust is lightly browned.
Mix the chopped eggs with the softened butter and serve with the warm pies.

title: Icelandic Skyr Cake
instructions: Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 2 tablespoons sugar.
Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan and chill.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let it bloom for 5 minutes.
Warm the bloomed gelatin gently until dissolved; do not boil.
Whisk the skyr with 1/2 cup sugar, vanilla, and lemon juice.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it into the skyr mixture.
Stir a spoonful of the skyr mixture into the dissolved gelatin, then fold the gelatin mixture into the filling.
Spread the filling over the crust and chill for at least 4 hours, until set.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the soaked bread, onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt the remaining butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; cook through, then set aside.
Whisk the flour into the skillet drippings, gradually add the broth, and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the cream, return the meatballs to the skillet, and simmer for 5 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a large pot, sprinkling each layer with salt, peppercorns, and a little flour.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk and melted butter; stir into the dry ingredients.
Stir in the baking soda.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and butter each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter and cook until the edges set.
Turn each pancake with a skewer and cook until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with raspberry jam and powdered sugar.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 leek, white and light green parts, sliced
1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the leek until softened.
Add the fish stock and potatoes; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the salmon and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until just cooked.
Stir in the cream, salt, pepper, and dill; heat through without boiling.
Serve hot.

title: Icelandic Skyr Cake
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 2 tablespoons sugar; press into the base of a 9-inch springform pan.
Bake the crust for 8 minutes, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk the skyr, cream, 1/2 cup sugar, eggs, vanilla, flour, and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until just set in the center.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage wedges in a large pot, sprinkling each layer with salt, peppercorns, and a little flour.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and butter each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter and cook until the edges begin to set.
Turn each pancake with a skewer and cook until golden and cooked through.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Finnish Karjalanpiirakat (Karelian Pasties)
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for the egg-butter spread
instructions: Combine the rice and water in a saucepan and simmer until the water is absorbed.
Add the milk and salt; simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is soft and thick, about 40 minutes.
Stir in 2 tablespoons butter and let the porridge cool.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and cold water into a firm dough.
Roll the dough into a log and cut it into 12 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a thin oval and place a spoonful of rice porridge in the center.
Fold and pleat the edges over the filling, leaving the center open.
Bake on a parchment-lined tray at 450°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until lightly browned.
Mix the softened butter with the chopped hard-boiled eggs and serve with the warm pasties.

title: Icelandic Skyr Cake
instructions: Mix the graham cracker crumbs with the melted butter and 2 tablespoons sugar.
Press the mixture into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let it soften for 5 minutes.
Warm the gelatin gently until dissolved, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk the skyr with 1/2 cup sugar, vanilla, and lemon juice.
Whip the heavy cream to soft peaks and fold it into the skyr mixture.
Stir a spoonful of the skyr mixture into the gelatin, then fold the gelatin mixture into the filling.
Spread the filling over the crust and chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let stand for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat until soft; cool slightly.
Combine the breadcrumb mixture, onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper.
Shape into small meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in 2 tablespoons butter in batches, then set aside.
Stir the flour into the pan drippings and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the pan and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 large head green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage in a large pot.
Add some lamb, peppercorns, salt, and flour; repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk and melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and butter each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter.
Cook until the edges set, turning each pancake with a skewer to brown all sides.
Serve warm, traditionally with jam and powdered sugar.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and soften the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the fish stock and potatoes; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, pepper, and dill; warm through without boiling.
Serve hot.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Beat the eggs with the milk and melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out to about 1/4 inch thick and cut into strips.
Cut a slit in the center of each strip and pull one end through to make a twist.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the twists in batches until golden, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve cooled.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Combine the breadcrumbs and milk; let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium heat and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 10 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 medium green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange half the cabbage in a large pot.
