Add half the lamb, sprinkle with half the salt, peppercorns, and flour, then repeat the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk and melted butter, then stir into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and brush each well with butter.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter and cook until the bottoms are golden.
Turn each pancake with a skewer and cook until golden and cooked through.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 leek, white and light-green parts sliced
1 pound salmon fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and soften the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the fish stock and potatoes; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, and pepper; warm through without boiling.
Stir in the dill and serve.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Rub in the butter, then mix in the egg and milk to form a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough to 1/4-inch thickness and cut into strips about 1 inch wide and 4 inches long.
Make a slit lengthwise in the center of each strip, then pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once; drain on paper towels.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together; let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper.
Shape into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 3 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a large pot, sprinkling each layer with salt and peppercorns.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
If using flour, whisk it with a little cold water, stir it into the stew, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk and melted butter; stir into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and butter each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter.
Cook until the edges set, turning each pancake with a skewer to brown all sides.
Serve warm with jam and powdered sugar.

title: Finnish Karelian Pies (Karjalanpiirakat)
ingredients: 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
instructions: Combine the rice and water in a saucepan; simmer until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the milk and salt; simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is soft and the porridge is thick, about 45 minutes.
Stir in 2 tablespoons butter and let the rice filling cool.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and water into a firm dough.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each piece into a thin oval on a floured surface.
Spoon rice filling down the center of each oval, leaving the edges uncovered.
Pinch and pleat the edges over the filling.
Bake at 475°F for 10 to 15 minutes, until the crust is browned.
Beat the egg with 1/2 cup softened butter and 1/2 cup milk; brush over the hot pies.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cardamom, and salt.
Beat the eggs with the milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut it into diamond-shaped strips.
Cut a slit in the center of each strip, then pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Fry the kleinur in batches, turning once, until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and cool before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a bowl; let stand for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, pepper, soaked breadcrumbs, and onion until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer them to a plate.
Stir the flour into the skillet drippings and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until the gravy thickens.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 3 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into serving pieces
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage in a large pot.
Add a layer of lamb, then sprinkle with some salt, peppercorns, and flour.
Repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Chill the mixture for 15 minutes so it firms up.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties using a spoon and place them in the skillet.
Fry in batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Serve warm with potatoes or rye bread.

title: Finnish Karjalanpiirakat (Karelian Pies)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt, for the rice filling
instructions: Bring the rice and milk to a simmer with 1 teaspoon salt; cook gently, stirring often, until thick and soft, about 45 minutes. Cool the filling.
Mix the water and 1 teaspoon salt in a bowl; stir in the rye flour and all-purpose flour to make a firm dough.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a thin oval on a floured surface.
Spoon rice filling down the center of each oval, leaving a border around the edges.
Pinch and pleat the edges over the filling, leaving the center exposed.
Bake on a hot baking sheet at 475°F (245°C) for 12 to 15 minutes, until the crust is firm and lightly browned.
Mix the egg with the softened butter and brush over the hot pies.
Brush the pies with melted butter and cover with a clean towel until soft.

title: Icelandic Skyr
ingredients: 1/4 cup plain skyr with live cultures
instructions: Heat the milk slowly to 185°F (85°C), stirring to prevent scorching.
Cool the milk to 110°F (43°C).
Whisk a little warm milk into the skyr, then stir the mixture back into the pot.
Mix the rennet with the water and gently stir it into the milk.
Cover and leave undisturbed in a warm place for 8 to 12 hours, until set.
Line a colander with clean cheesecloth and set it over a bowl.
Spoon the curds into the cloth and drain in the refrigerator for 4 to 8 hours, until thick.
Whisk the skyr smooth and refrigerate until ready to serve.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl; let stand for 5 minutes.
Add beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper; mix gently.
Shape into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in broth and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 medium green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage wedges in a large pot.
Dust lamb with flour and arrange half over the cabbage.
Sprinkle with half the peppercorns and salt.
Repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom in a bowl.
Whisk egg yolks, buttermilk, and melted butter in a separate bowl.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and brush each well with butter.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter.
Cook until the edges set, turning each pancake with a skewer to brown all sides.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Finnish Karjalanpiirakka (Karelian Pasties)
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for egg butter
instructions: Rinse the rice, then simmer it with 2 cups water until the water is absorbed.
Add milk and salt; simmer gently, stirring often, until the rice is thick and tender, about 45 minutes. Cool.
Mix rye flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and 3/4 cup water to form a firm dough.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a thin oval.
Spoon rice filling down the center of each oval, leaving the edges uncovered.
Fold and crimp the edges over the filling.
Bake on a hot baking sheet at 475°F (245°C) for 12 to 15 minutes.
Stir chopped eggs into softened butter and serve the pasties warm with egg butter.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cardamom, and salt in a bowl.
Beat eggs with milk and melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients to make a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut into diamonds.
Cut a slit in the center of each diamond and pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once; drain on paper towels.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Combine the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl; let soak for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper until combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer to a plate.
Sprinkle the flour into the skillet and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the cream, return the meatballs to the skillet, and simmer until cooked through.
Serve with lingonberry jam.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 3 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage in a large pot.
Add some lamb, peppercorns, salt, and flour; repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender; drain.
Serve the stew hot with the potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pan-Fried Meat Patties)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties using a spoon and fry in batches.
Cook for about 5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Creamy Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 leek, white and light green parts thinly sliced
1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the leek and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, fish stock, and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, and white pepper; warm through without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the dill, and serve.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt in a large bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Whisk the egg and milk together, then stir them into the dry ingredients to form a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough on a floured surface to about 1/4 inch thick and cut into diamond shapes.
Cut a slit in the center of each diamond, then pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur in batches, turning once, until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and cool slightly before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let stand for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper; mix gently.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 10 minutes.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange a layer of cabbage wedges in a large pot.
Dust the lamb with flour and place some pieces over the cabbage.
Sprinkle with peppercorns and salt; repeat the layers, ending with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom in a bowl.
Whisk the egg yolks, buttermilk, and melted butter in a second bowl.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and brush each well with butter.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter.
Cook until the edges set, turning each pancake with a skewer to brown it all over.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Creamy Salmon Soup)

instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the leek and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and stock; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are almost tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, pepper, and dill; warm without boiling.
Serve hot.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cardamom, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the egg, milk, sour cream, and melted butter in a second bowl.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients to form a soft dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and roll it about 1/4 inch thick.
Cut the dough into diamond shapes, make a slit in the center of each, and pull one end through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur in batches, turning once, until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let stand for 5 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat until soft; cool slightly.
Combine the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper.
Roll the mixture into small meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in batches in 2 tablespoons butter; transfer to a plate.
Stir the flour into the pan drippings and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the pan and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)

1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage wedges in a large pot, seasoning each layer with salt and peppercorns.
Sprinkle the flour over the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pork Meatballs)

Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
Shape into oval patties using a spoon dipped in water.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties in batches for 5 to 7 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and soften the leek for 5 minutes.

Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)

Rub the butter into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg with the milk and stir it into the flour mixture to form a dough.
Roll the dough out to about 1/4 inch thick and cut into diamond shapes.

Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and cool before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, egg, salt, allspice, pepper, and soaked breadcrumbs.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and cream, then simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 medium green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a large pot, sprinkling flour, salt, and peppercorns between the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes.

title: Danish Frikadeller (Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
Shape it into oval patties with a spoon.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 5 to 7 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the leek and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fish stock, then bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the salmon and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until just cooked.
Stir in the cream, salt, pepper, and dill; warm through without boiling.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Rub in the butter, then mix in the egg and milk to form a soft dough.
Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough to 1/4-inch thickness and cut into diamonds.
Make a slit in each diamond and pull one end through to twist the dough.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once, then drain on paper towels.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let stand for 10 minutes.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft; cool slightly.
Combine the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, beef, pork, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt the remaining butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; set aside.
Stir the flour into the skillet drippings, then gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream.
Simmer the sauce until thickened, return the meatballs to the skillet, and cook until done.

title: Norwegian Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 large head green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage wedges in a large pot, sprinkling each layer with salt, peppercorns, and flour.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve hot, with some cooking broth in each portion.

title: Danish Æbleskiver
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cardamom.
Whisk the egg yolks with the buttermilk, melted butter, and vanilla; stir into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the batter.
Heat an æbleskiver pan over medium heat and butter each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter and cook until the bottoms are golden.
Turn each pancake with a skewer and cook until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm, dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto (Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the leek until softened.
Add the fish stock, potatoes, and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, pepper, and dill; warm through without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Icelandic Kleinur (Twisted Doughnuts)
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture is crumbly.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and vanilla, then stir into the flour mixture to form a dough.
Knead briefly, cover, and chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough to about 1/4 inch thick and cut into diamond shapes; make a slit in the center of each.
Pull one pointed end through the slit to twist each piece.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Bergen Fish Soup (Bergens fiskesuppe)
ingredients: 500 g cod fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g salmon fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan and soften the leek and carrot for 3 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then gradually whisk in the fish stock.
Simmer for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the milk and cream and heat gently without boiling.
Whisk the egg yolk with the vinegar and sugar; stir in a ladle of hot soup, then mix it back into the pot.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, until just cooked.
Season with salt and white pepper, stir in the dill, and serve hot.

title: Persetorsk (Pressed and salted cod)
ingredients: 1 kg cod fillet, skinless and pin-boned
instructions: Mix the salt and sugar, then rub the mixture over the cod.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours, turning the fish once.
Rinse the cod briefly and cut it into serving portions.
Bring the water and vinegar to a gentle simmer in a wide pan.
Add the cod and poach gently for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes easily.
Lift out the fish, dot with butter, and sprinkle with chives.

title: Raspeballer with Salted Lamb
ingredients: 500 g salted lamb, cut into pieces
instructions: Put the salted lamb in a pot, cover with water, and simmer gently for about 90 minutes.
Finely grate all the potatoes and squeeze out some of their liquid.
Mix the potatoes with the barley flour, all-purpose flour, and salt to make a firm dough.
With wet hands, shape the dough into 8 balls.
Carefully add the balls to the lamb pot and simmer for 40–45 minutes, without boiling hard.
Fry the bacon in a pan until crisp, then stir in the butter.
Serve the dumplings with the lamb and bacon fat.

title: Lapskaus (Bergen-style meat and root vegetable stew)
ingredients: 600 g beef chuck, cut into 2 cm cubes
instructions: Brown the beef in butter in a heavy pot, working in batches if needed.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the bay leaves, and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, carrots, rutabaga, leek, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 35–40 minutes, until the meat and vegetables are tender and the stew is thick.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the parsley, and serve hot.

title: Skillingsboller (Bergen cinnamon buns)
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, cardamom, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
Add the lukewarm milk, butter, and egg; knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Roll the dough into a rectangle and spread it with the filling butter.
Mix the filling sugar and cinnamon, sprinkle it evenly over the dough, then roll it up from a long side.
Slice into 12 buns and place them cut-side up on a lined baking tray.
Cover and rise for 30 minutes while the oven heats to 200°C.
Brush the buns with beaten egg and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Cover and chill the mixture for 20 minutes.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties with a spoon and fry in batches for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Stegt Flæsk med Persillesovs (Crispy Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb pork belly, sliced 1/4 inch thick
1/4 teaspoon fine salt, for the sauce
1/8 teaspoon black pepper, for the sauce
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Season the pork belly with salt and pepper, lay it in a single layer, and roast for 25–35 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15–20 minutes, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer, stirring, until smooth and thickened.
Stir the parsley, salt, and pepper into the sauce, then serve with the pork and potatoes.

title: Æbleflæsk (Apples with Pork)
ingredients: 8 oz thick-cut bacon, cut into 1-inch pieces
4 medium tart apples, cored and cut into wedges
instructions: Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until browned and crisp, about 8 minutes.
Transfer the bacon to a plate, leaving about 2 tablespoons of fat in the skillet.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the apples and pepper and cook for 8–10 minutes, turning gently, until tender but still holding their shape.
Return the bacon to the skillet, stir in the thyme, and serve warm.

title: Hønsekødssuppe (Danish Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
2 medium yellow onions, peeled and halved
1 leek, white and light-green parts sliced and rinsed
instructions: Put the chicken, water, carrot chunks, onion, celery, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skimming any foam, and cook uncovered for 75–90 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth; discard the cooked vegetables and seasonings.
Let the chicken cool slightly, then remove the meat from the bones and tear it into bite-size pieces.
Return the broth to the pot, add the sliced carrots and leek, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook according to its package directions; stir in the chicken and parsley before serving.

title: Risalamande (Danish Rice Pudding with Almonds)
instructions: Put the rice, milk, vanilla bean, sugar, and salt in a heavy saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often, then cover and cook over low heat for 35–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and creamy.
Remove the vanilla bean and scrape its seeds into the pudding; cool the pudding completely.
Stir in the chopped almonds.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and gently fold it into the cold rice pudding.
Chill until ready to serve, with warm cherry sauce spooned over each portion.

title: Stegt flæsk med persillesovs (Crispy Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
ingredients: 1½ lb (700 g) pork belly, sliced about ¼ inch thick
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15–20 minutes; drain and keep warm.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Arrange pork belly on a rack over a baking sheet, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20 minutes.
Turn the slices and roast until crisp and browned, about 15–20 minutes more.
Melt butter in a saucepan. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer, stirring, until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in parsley and season with salt and pepper. Serve the pork with potatoes and parsley sauce.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, veal, onion, flour, egg, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Cover and chill the mixture for 20 minutes.
Heat butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties using a spoon, and fry in batches for 5–6 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot, traditionally with potatoes, gravy, or cabbage.

title: Hønsekødssuppe (Danish Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 1½ tsp salt, plus more to taste
1 leek, white and light-green parts thinly sliced
instructions: Put the chicken, water, chopped vegetables, bay leaves, peppercorns, and salt in a large pot.
Bring just to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for 1½ hours, until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth. Discard the cooked vegetables and return the broth to the pot.
Remove the chicken meat from the bones and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Add the sliced carrots and leek to the broth and simmer until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the soup dumplings and chicken; simmer until the dumplings are heated through. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

title: Brunede Kartofler (Caramelized Potatoes)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, about 15–20 minutes. Drain, cool, and peel.
Sprinkle the sugar evenly into a large skillet and heat over medium heat until it melts and turns amber; do not stir.
Add the butter and swirl the pan until melted.
Add the potatoes and salt. Turn gently to coat them in caramel.
Cook for 8–10 minutes, turning often, until glossy and evenly browned.

title: Æblekage (Danish Apple Cake Dessert)
ingredients: 2 lb (900 g) tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar, for the crumbs
instructions: Put the apples, ¼ cup sugar, water, and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the apples soften into a chunky purée, about 15 minutes. Cool completely.
Melt the butter in a skillet. Add the breadcrumbs and remaining sugar, and toast over medium heat, stirring, until crisp and golden. Cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Layer the apple mixture and toasted crumbs in a serving bowl or glasses, finishing with crumbs.
Top with whipped cream and serve chilled.

title: Lohikeitto (Finnish Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 1 leek, white and light-green parts, sliced
1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and soften the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, stock, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, and white pepper; warm without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the dill, and serve.

title: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian Hot Pot)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Put the beef, pork, and onion in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Add the salt, peppercorns, bay leaves, and water.
Cover and bake for 3 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes if you want the meat browned on top.

title: Hernekeitto (Finnish Split Pea Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried green split peas, rinsed
instructions: Put the split peas and water in a large pot and soak overnight.
Add the onion and ham hock, then bring the pot to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas break down and the meat is tender.
Lift out the ham hock, remove the meat from the bone, and return the meat to the soup.
Stir in the marjoram, salt, and pepper. Serve with mustard.

title: Lihapullat (Finnish Meatballs)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a bowl and let stand for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat until soft, then let it cool.
Mix the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, beef, egg, salt, allspice, and pepper until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Heat the remaining butter in a skillet and fry the meatballs in batches, turning, until browned and cooked through, about 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Pannukakku (Finnish Oven Pancake)
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Whisk the eggs and milk together in a large bowl.
Add the flour, sugar, and salt, and whisk until smooth.
Melt the butter in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish in the oven.
Pour the batter into the hot dish and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Let it settle for a few minutes, then cut into squares and serve.

title: Kjötsúpa (Icelandic lamb soup)
ingredients: 1 lb bone-in lamb shoulder or neck, cut into chunks
instructions: Put the lamb, water, and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the onion, barley, and thyme. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots, rutabaga, and potatoes. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage and cook until the vegetables and lamb are tender, about 10 minutes.
Season with pepper and additional salt if needed; serve hot.

title: Plokkfiskur (Icelandic fish stew)
ingredients: 1 lb potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and roughly mash.
Simmer the fish in a little water until opaque and flaky, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain and break into large flakes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth and thickened.
Fold in the potatoes and fish. Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg, and warm gently without boiling.
Serve with rye bread.

title: Lifrarpylsa (Icelandic liver sausage)
ingredients: 4 cleaned sausage casings, about 8 inches each
instructions: Rinse the casings and soak them in cold water while preparing the filling.
Mix the liver, suet, oats, milk, onion, salt, pepper, and allspice in a large bowl.
Fill each casing loosely with the mixture, leaving room for it to expand, and tie the ends securely.
Place the sausages in a pot of gently simmering water and cook for about 2 hours; do not let the water boil hard.
Cool the sausages before slicing. Pan-fry slices until browned, or serve them chilled.

title: Rúgbrauð (Icelandic dark rye bread)
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°F (95°C). Grease a covered 2-quart oven-safe pot or loaf pan.
Whisk together the rye flour, all-purpose flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Stir in the buttermilk and golden syrup until a thick, even batter forms.
Spoon the batter into the prepared pot and cover it tightly with its lid or foil.
Bake for 8 hours, until the loaf is firm and dark. Cool before slicing.

title: Kleinur (Icelandic twisted doughnuts)
ingredients: 4 tbsp cold butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt.
Rub the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Beat the egg with the milk, add it to the bowl, and mix just until a soft dough forms.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1/4 inch thick. Cut into diamonds, make a slit in each, and pull one point through the slit to twist.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the kleinur in batches until golden, turning once, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and cool slightly before serving.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Mix in the onion, egg, salt, allspice, and ground meat until just combined.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet and brown the meatballs in batches; transfer them to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and flour to the skillet and stir for 1 minute.
Whisk in the beef stock and cream, then simmer until thickened.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer for 5 minutes, until cooked through.

title: Raggmunk with Lingonberries
instructions: Whisk the flour with a little of the milk until smooth.
Whisk in the remaining milk, egg, and salt to make a thin batter.
Coarsely grate the potatoes and stir them into the batter.
Melt a little butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in portions of the potato mixture and flatten into thin pancakes.
Fry for 3–4 minutes on each side until crisp and golden, adding butter as needed.
Serve hot with lingonberry preserves.

title: Gravlax (Cured Salmon)
ingredients: 700 g skin-on salmon fillet, pin bones removed
1 large bunch fresh dill, roughly chopped
instructions: Pat the salmon dry and check that all pin bones are removed.
Mix the salt, sugar, and white pepper.
Spread the mixture over the flesh side of the salmon, then cover it with the dill.
Wrap the salmon tightly and place it in a dish, skin side down.
Refrigerate for 36–48 hours, turning the salmon every 12 hours and spooning the cure back over it.
Scrape off the dill and cure, then slice the salmon thinly across the grain.

title: Ärtsoppa (Swedish Yellow Pea Soup)
ingredients: 500 g dried yellow split peas, rinsed
1 onion, peeled and studded with 2 whole cloves
instructions: Put the peas and water in a large pot and soak overnight.
Add the ham hock and clove-studded onion to the pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then lower the heat.
Cover partially and simmer for 1 1/2–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas are soft.
Remove the ham hock and onion; discard the onion and cloves.
Pull the meat from the hock, chop it, and return it to the soup.
Stir in the marjoram, thyme, salt, and pepper, then simmer for 10 minutes.

title: Janssons Frestelse (Jansson’s Temptation)
ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, plus extra for the dish
125 g Swedish anchovy-style sprats, drained and chopped
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and butter a baking dish.
Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onions gently until soft but not browned.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, followed by the onions and chopped sprats.
Add the remaining potatoes and pour over the cream and milk.
Scatter the breadcrumbs over the top and dot with a little butter.
Bake for 50–60 minutes, until tender and golden on top.

title: Ärtsoppa (Swedish Yellow Pea Soup)
ingredients: 500 g dried yellow peas, rinsed and soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked peas and put them in a large pot with the water, onion, and ham hock.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer gently for about 90 minutes, until the peas are tender.
Remove the ham hock and onion. Discard the onion, cut the meat from the hock, and return the meat to the pot.
Stir in the thyme, marjoram, salt, and white pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve hot with Swedish mustard.

title: Pytt i panna (Swedish Hash)
ingredients: 500 g waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
250 g cooked beef or leftover roast, diced
instructions: Boil the diced potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain and dry them well.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan. Fry the potatoes until golden and crisp, turning occasionally.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the beef and ham and fry until heated through.
Season with salt and pepper.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan and serve one over each portion of hash, with pickled beetroot.

title: Raggmunk med fläsk (Potato Pancakes with Pork)
ingredients: 400 g thinly sliced salted pork belly
instructions: Whisk the flour with a little of the milk until smooth, then whisk in the remaining milk, egg, and salt.
Coarsely grate the potatoes and stir them into the batter.
Fry the pork in a pan over medium heat until browned and crisp; keep warm.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan. Add a thin layer of batter and fry each pancake until golden on both sides and cooked through.
Serve the raggmunk with the pork and lingonberry jam.

title: Fiskgratäng med räkor (Fish Gratin with Shrimp)
ingredients: 600 g cod fillets, cut into portions
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Arrange the cod in a buttered baking dish and season with salt and white pepper.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and cream.
Simmer the sauce, stirring, until smooth and thickened. Stir in the dill and pour over the fish.
Scatter the shrimp, grated cheese, and breadcrumbs over the top.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the top is golden.

title: Kåldolmar (Swedish Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Remove the cabbage leaves one at a time and blanch them until pliable, about 2 minutes each.
Mix the beef, pork, rice, onion, milk, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in a buttered baking dish.
Brush the rolls with melted butter and dark syrup, then pour the beef stock around them.
Cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes, until browned and cooked through.

title: Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
1 large head green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage wedges in a large pot, sprinkling flour, salt, and peppercorns between the layers.
Pour in the water and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the cabbage is soft.
Serve hot, with boiled potatoes if desired.

title: Kjøttkaker i Brunsaus (Norwegian Meat Cakes with Brown Gravy)
instructions: Mix the milk and breadcrumbs in a bowl and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, onion, salt, and pepper; mix gently and shape into 8 oval patties.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a skillet and brown the patties on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook until golden brown.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream, then simmer until smooth and slightly thickened.
Return the patties to the skillet, cover, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until cooked through.

title: Lapskaus (Norwegian Beef and Root Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and brown the beef in batches.
Return all the beef to the pot and add the stock and onion.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, carrots, rutabaga, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 35 to 45 minutes, until the beef and vegetables are tender and the broth is thick.

title: Raspeballer (Potato Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 tsp salt for the cooking water
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix the grated potatoes with the flour and salt to make a firm dough.
Shape the dough into 8 dumplings, tucking a little diced bacon into the center of each if desired.
Bring the water and cooking-water salt to a gentle boil in a large pot.
Lower the dumplings into the water and simmer gently for 35 to 45 minutes, until cooked through.
Serve with the remaining bacon, fried until crisp.

title: Rømmegrøt (Sour Cream Porridge)
instructions: Simmer the sour cream in a heavy saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the flour a little at a time and cook, stirring, until the butter begins to separate.
Spoon off the separated butter and keep it warm for serving.
Gradually whisk the warm milk into the porridge until smooth.
Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy; add the salt.
Serve warm with the reserved butter, sugar, and cinnamon.

title: Bergen Fish Soup (Bergensk fiskesuppe)
ingredients: 500 g cod or haddock, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g salmon, cut into bite-size pieces
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Bring the fish stock to a gentle simmer; add the carrots and leek and cook until just tender.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in a ladle of hot stock at a time until smooth, then stir the mixture into the soup.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked, about 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, sour cream, vinegar, and sugar; warm without boiling.
Season with salt and white pepper, and finish with chives.

title: Persetorsk (Pressed Cod)
instructions: Mix the salt and sugar, then rub the mixture over the cod.
Cover and refrigerate the cod for 2 hours, turning it once.
Rinse the cod briefly and pat it dry.
Bring the water, onion, bay leaf, and peppercorns to a simmer in a wide pan.
Add the cod and poach gently for 8–12 minutes, until it flakes easily.
Lift out the fish, dot with butter, and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Raspeballer with Salted Lamb
ingredients: 500 g salted lamb or cured mutton, cut into pieces
1 rutabaga, peeled and cut into chunks
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Put the salted lamb in a pot, cover with the water, and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Grate the floury and raw potatoes; squeeze out excess liquid from the grated mixture.
Mix the potatoes with the barley flour, all-purpose flour, and salt to make a firm, sticky dough.
Shape the dough into balls with wet hands.
Add the rutabaga and carrots to the lamb pot, then gently lower in the dumplings.
Simmer uncovered for 35–40 minutes, until the dumplings are cooked through.
Serve the dumplings with the lamb and vegetables, with cooking broth on the side.

title: Lapskaus (Bergen-Style Meat and Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 600 g beef chuck, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches.
Return all the beef to the pot, add the stock, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, skimming if needed.
Add the potatoes, carrots, rutabaga, leek, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 30–40 minutes, until the meat and vegetables are very tender.
Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the stew, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve with parsley sprinkled over the top.

title: Skillingsboller (Cinnamon Buns)
ingredients: 75 g butter, softened, for the filling
75 g granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, cardamom, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
Add the lukewarm milk, softened butter, and egg; knead until smooth and elastic, about 8–10 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Roll the dough into a rectangle and spread it with the filling butter.
Mix the filling sugar and cinnamon, then sprinkle it evenly over the dough.
Roll up the dough, cut it into 12 slices, and place the slices on lined baking trays.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes while the oven heats to 200°C.
Brush the buns with beaten egg and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties with a spoon and fry in batches for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Flæskesteg (Danish Roast Pork with Crackling)
ingredients: 4 lb pork loin roast with skin, scored into narrow strips
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Rub salt into the scored skin, working it between the cuts.
Place the roast skin-side up in a roasting pan, leveling it with crumpled foil if needed.
Tuck the bay leaves and peppercorns into the pan and pour in the water.
Roast for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C) and roast until the center reaches 145°F (63°C), about 1 hour more.
If the crackling is not crisp, briefly broil it while watching closely.
Rest the roast for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Hakkebøf med Bløde Løg (Beef Patties with Soft Onions)
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then shape it into four thick patties.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook the onions, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden, about 20 minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and raise the heat to medium-high.
Cook the patties for 4–5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Pour the broth into the skillet and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the onions to the pan and spoon the broth and onions over the patties.

title: Æblekage (Danish Layered Apple Dessert)
ingredients: 4 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and diced
instructions: Put the apples, water, half the sugar, and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat until the apples are soft, about 15 minutes; mash lightly and cool.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the breadcrumbs and remaining sugar, and toast until golden, stirring often.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Layer the cooled apples and toasted crumbs in serving glasses or a bowl.
Top with whipped cream and small spoonfuls of red currant jelly.

title: Brændende Kærlighed (Mashed Potatoes with Bacon and Onions)
ingredients: 2 lb potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer until tender, about 15–20 minutes, then drain.
Mash the potatoes with the warm milk, 2 tablespoons butter, salt, and pepper; keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, then transfer it to a plate, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the onions to the skillet and cook until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir the bacon back into the onions and season to taste.
Spoon the mashed potatoes onto plates, top with the bacon and onions, and finish with parsley.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs)
instructions: Mix the pork, onion, egg, milk, flour, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Shape the mixture into oval patties with a spoon and fry in batches for 5–6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Stegt Flæsk med Persillesovs (Crispy Pork with Parsley Sauce)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb pork belly, cut into 1/4-inch slices
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Season the pork slices with salt and pepper and arrange them on a rack set over a baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes, turn the slices, then roast for 15–20 minutes more until crisp.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15–20 minutes, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer until smooth and thickened.
Stir in the parsley and salt, then serve the sauce with the pork and potatoes.

title: Brunede Kartofler (Danish Caramelized Potatoes)
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain, cool, and peel.
Spread the sugar evenly in a skillet and heat over medium heat until it melts and turns amber; do not stir.
Add the butter and salt, stirring carefully until combined.
Add the potatoes and turn them gently in the caramel until glossy and heated through, about 8–10 minutes.

title: Gule Ærter (Danish Yellow Pea Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb dried yellow split peas, rinsed
instructions: Put the peas in a large pot with the water and soak overnight; drain and rinse.
Add the peas, ham hock, onion, carrots, leek, thyme, and bay leaf to the pot with 8 cups fresh water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer partly covered for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the peas are soft and the ham is tender.
Lift out the ham hock, discard the bay leaf, and shred the meat, discarding the bone and skin.
Stir the ham back into the soup and season with salt and pepper.

title: Æblekage (Danish Apple Cake)
ingredients: 2 lb tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Put the apples and water in a saucepan and simmer, covered, until soft, about 15 minutes.
Mash the apples with the sugar and cinnamon, then let the purée cool.
Melt the butter in a skillet and toast the breadcrumbs over medium heat until golden.
Layer the apple purée and toasted breadcrumbs in a serving bowl, finishing with breadcrumbs.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve with whipped cream.

title: Lohikeitto (Finnish Salmon Soup)
ingredients: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 pound salmon fillet, skin removed and cut into chunks
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and soften the leek for 5 minutes.
Add the stock, potatoes, and carrot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, salt, and white pepper; warm without boiling.
Scatter the dill over the soup and serve.

title: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian Hot Pot)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Layer the beef, pork, lamb, and onions in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Add the salt, peppercorns, bay leaves, and water.
Cover and bake until the meat is very tender, about 3 1/2 hours.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt before serving.

title: Hernekeitto (Finnish Pea Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound dried green split peas, rinsed
instructions: Put the peas, water, ham hock, and onion in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover partly and simmer until the peas have broken down and the ham is tender, about 2 hours; stir occasionally.
Remove the ham hock, take the meat off the bone, and return the meat to the pot.
Stir in the salt, marjoram, and pepper. Serve with a little mustard.

title: Pyttipannu (Finnish Hash)
ingredients: 1 pound cooked potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
8 ounces cooked beef or ham, diced
instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and meat; season with salt and pepper.
Cook, turning occasionally, until browned and hot throughout, about 10 minutes.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan to your liking. Serve them on top of the hash with parsley.

title: Mustikkapiirakka (Finnish Blueberry Pie)
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9-inch pie dish.
Mix the flour, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl. Rub in the butter, then mix in the egg to make a soft dough.
Press the dough evenly into the pie dish and slightly up the sides.
Scatter the blueberries over the crust.
Whisk the sour cream, egg yolk, sugar, and vanilla, then pour the mixture over the blueberries.
Bake until the filling is set and the crust is golden, about 40 minutes. Cool before serving.

title: Kjötsúpa (Icelandic Lamb Soup)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into pieces
instructions: Put the lamb, water, and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Lower the heat and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the onion, carrots, rutabaga, potatoes, barley, cabbage, thyme, and pepper.
Simmer for 35–45 minutes, until the lamb and vegetables are tender.
Remove the lamb bones, pull the meat into bite-size pieces, and return the meat to the soup.

title: Plokkfiskur (Icelandic Fish Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and roughly mash.
Simmer the fish in a little water for 6–8 minutes, until it flakes easily; drain and flake it.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the warm milk.
Cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens; season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Fold in the fish and potatoes and warm gently without boiling.
Scatter with chives and serve hot.

title: Hangikjöt með uppstúf (Smoked Lamb with White Sauce)
instructions: Put the smoked lamb in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for about 1 hour, or until heated through and tender; let it rest in the cooking liquid.
Boil the potatoes in a separate pot until tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer, stirring, until smooth and thick.
Season the sauce with white pepper, nutmeg, and salt to taste.
Slice the lamb and serve with potatoes and white sauce.

title: Rúgbrauð (Icelandic Rye Bread)
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°F (95°C) and grease a lidded oven-safe pot or loaf pan.
Whisk together the rye flour, all-purpose flour, oats, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and brown sugar.
Stir in the buttermilk and golden syrup until you have a thick batter.
Spoon the batter into the prepared pot or pan and cover tightly with a lid or foil.
Bake for 8 hours, until the bread is firm and cooked through.
Cool before slicing.

title: Lummur (Icelandic Skillet Pancakes)
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter, plus more for the pan
instructions: Mix the flour, oats, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg, milk, and melted butter in another bowl.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined; let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat.
Drop in small rounds of batter and cook until bubbles appear and the edges look set.
Flip and cook until golden on the other side.
Serve warm, traditionally with butter or jam.

title: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
instructions: Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together and let stand for 10 minutes.
Soften the onion in 1 tablespoon butter, then let it cool.
Mix the meats, egg, salt, white pepper, allspice, soaked breadcrumbs, and onion just until combined.
Shape into small meatballs with damp hands.
Fry the meatballs in batches in 2 tablespoons butter until browned and cooked through; transfer to a plate.
Stir the flour into the pan drippings and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream; simmer until smooth and thickened.
Return the meatballs to the pan and warm through.

title: Salmon Pudding (Laxpudding)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon butter, plus extra for the baking dish
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a baking dish.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, then add half the salmon and onion; sprinkle with some dill.
Repeat with the remaining potatoes, salmon, onion, and dill, finishing with potatoes.
Whisk together the eggs, milk, cream, salt, and white pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the layers and dot with butter.
Bake for 50–60 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Pea Soup with Pancakes (Ärtsoppa och pannkakor)
ingredients: 1 yellow onion, peeled and left whole
3 tablespoons melted butter, plus more for the pan
instructions: Put the peas, water, ham hock, and whole onion in a large pot; bring to a boil and skim any foam.
Cover partly and simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours, until the peas are soft.
Remove the ham hock and onion; discard the onion, shred the meat, and return the meat to the pot.
Stir in the marjoram, thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
For the pancakes, whisk the flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk in the eggs and milk until smooth, then stir in the melted butter.
Cook thin pancakes in a lightly buttered skillet, turning once, until golden on both sides.
Serve the soup hot, followed by the pancakes.

title: Jansson’s Temptation (Janssons frestelse)
ingredients: 2 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
1 tablespoon butter, plus extra for the baking dish
1 can (4 ounces) Swedish anchovy-style sprats, drained and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and butter a baking dish.
Soften the onions in 1 tablespoon butter over medium-low heat.
Arrange half the potatoes in the dish, then add the onions and sprats.
Top with the remaining potatoes.
Mix the cream and milk and pour over the potatoes.
Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and bake for 50–60 minutes, until tender and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Swedish Cinnamon Buns (Kanelbullar)
ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for the filling
1/2 cup granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Stir the yeast into the lukewarm milk and let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix in the sugar, salt, cardamom, and flour; knead until a dough forms.
Knead in 1/3 cup softened butter until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour.
Mix the filling butter, sugar, and cinnamon.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread with the filling, and fold it in half lengthwise.
Cut into strips, twist each strip, and shape into buns; place on lined baking sheets.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes while heating the oven to 400°F.
Brush the buns with beaten egg, sprinkle with pearl sugar, and bake for 10–12 minutes until golden.

title: Ärtsoppa (Swedish Yellow Pea Soup)
ingredients: 8 cups water, plus more for soaking
instructions: Rinse the peas and soak them in plenty of cold water overnight; drain.
Put the peas, 8 cups fresh water, onion, and ham hock in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the peas are soft.
Remove the ham hock, take the meat from the bone, chop it, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the marjoram, thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer for 5 minutes and serve with mustard.

title: Pytt i panna (Swedish Hash)
ingredients: 1 lb waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
8 oz cooked beef or leftover roast, cut into small cubes
8 oz cooked ham, cut into small cubes
instructions: Boil the potato cubes in salted water until just tender, about 8 minutes; drain and let them dry.
Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden and crisp, then set aside.
Cook the onion in the skillet until softened; add the beef and ham and fry until browned.
Return the potatoes to the skillet, season with salt and pepper, and toss until hot.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan and serve one on each portion with pickled beetroot.

title: Raggmunk med fläsk (Potato Pancakes with Pork)
ingredients: 12 oz thick-cut bacon or salted pork, sliced
instructions: Whisk the flour and salt with half the milk until smooth, then whisk in the remaining milk and egg.
Grate the potatoes and stir them into the batter just before frying.
Fry the bacon or pork in a skillet until crisp and cooked through; keep warm.
Melt a little butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and add a thin layer of batter.
Fry each pancake for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through, adding butter as needed.
Serve the pancakes with the pork and lingonberry jam.

title: Kålpudding (Swedish Cabbage and Meat Bake)
ingredients: 1 medium green cabbage, about 2 lb, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Simmer the cabbage wedges in salted water for 5 minutes, drain, and chop them roughly.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the cabbage and syrup, and cook until lightly golden.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, milk, breadcrumbs, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Layer half the cabbage in a baking dish, spread the meat mixture over it, and cover with the remaining cabbage.
Pour the beef stock around the edges and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until cooked through and browned on top.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with lingonberry jam.

title: Fiskgratäng med räkor (Fish Gratin with Shrimp)
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated Swedish Västerbotten cheese or sharp cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and butter a shallow baking dish.
Season the fish with salt and white pepper, arrange it in the dish, and bake for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cream; simmer until smooth and thick, then stir in the lemon juice and dill.
Fold the shrimp into the sauce, pour it over the fish, and scatter the cheese and breadcrumbs on top.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and the topping is golden.

title: Fårikål (Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder or neck, cut into chunks
1 large green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a heavy pot, sprinkling each layer with flour, salt, and peppercorns.
Pour in the water and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the cabbage is soft.
Serve hot, with boiled potatoes if desired.

title: Kjøttkaker med Brun Saus (Norwegian Meat Cakes with Brown Gravy)
instructions: Mix the beef, pork, onion, potato starch, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and milk until well combined.
Shape the mixture into 8 oval patties.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet and brown the patties on both sides; transfer to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet, stir in the flour, and cook until golden brown.
Whisk in the beef stock and simmer until smooth and thickened.
Return the patties to the skillet, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, until cooked through.

title: Lapskaus (Norwegian Beef and Root Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb stewing beef, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and brown the beef in batches.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the beef stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, carrots, rutabaga, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft and the stew is thick.

title: Raspeballer (Potato Dumplings)
ingredients: 4 oz salt pork, cut into 8 cubes
1 teaspoon salt, for the cooking water
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and press out excess liquid.
Mix the potatoes with both flours and 1 teaspoon salt to make a firm dough.
Shape the dough into 8 balls, placing a cube of salt pork in the center of each.
Bring the water and remaining salt to a gentle boil in a large pot.
Lower the dumplings into the water and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve hot.

title: Rømmegrøt (Sour Cream Porridge)
instructions: Bring the sour cream to a gentle simmer in a heavy saucepan and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the flour gradually and cook until the butterfat begins to separate.
Spoon off the separated butter and set it aside.
Whisk in the warm milk a little at a time until smooth.
Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy; stir in the salt.
Serve warm with the reserved butter, sugar, and cinnamon.

title: Vietnamese Phở Bò
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until blackened in spots.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds in a dry pot for 1 minute.
Add bones, brisket, water, onion, and ginger to the pot; bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add toasted spices, fish sauce, sugar, and salt; simmer gently for 3 hours.
Remove the brisket when tender, cool slightly, and slice thinly; strain the broth and keep it hot.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Top noodles with sliced brisket and raw sirloin; ladle hot broth over the meat.
Serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, scallions, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside; simmer the sauce for 10 minutes until slightly reduced.
Heat oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return chicken to the pot, add brown sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken with the reduced sauce and steamed rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add shallots, garlic, chili, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add chicken and rice, breaking up any clumps as you stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt; cook until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the rice topped with fried eggs and scallions, with cucumber on the side.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, coriander, and cumin into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add beef and stir to coat with the paste.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, coconut milk, water, tamarind, and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in toasted grated coconut and cook until the oil separates and the beef is dark and coated.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb firm white fish, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Whisk coconut milk, egg, fish sauce, palm sugar, curry paste, and salt in a bowl.
Fold the fish into the coconut mixture and let it stand for 10 minutes.
Line four small heatproof bowls with banana leaf squares and divide the cabbage among them.
Spoon the fish mixture into the bowls and top with Thai basil and sliced lime leaf.
Set the bowls in a steamer over simmering water, cover, and steam for 20 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Serve warm with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until blackened in spots.
Rinse the bones and brisket, then place them in a large pot and cover with 4 quarts of water.
Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then add the charred onion and ginger.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander in a dry pan; add them to the pot.
Simmer gently for 3 hours, adding water as needed. Remove the brisket when tender, cool it, and slice it thinly.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot, and season with fish sauce, sugar, and salt.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide them among bowls.
Top with sliced brisket and raw sirloin, ladle over boiling broth, and serve with sprouts, basil, lime, scallions, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to concentrate it.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on all sides.
Return the chicken to the pot and simmer in the sauce for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and rice, breaking up any clumps as you stir-fry.
Add the kecap manis and soy sauce, then toss until the rice is evenly coated and hot.
Heat the remaining oil in a separate pan and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the rice topped with fried eggs, scallions, cucumber, and tomato.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, chilies, and turmeric with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and cinnamon; stir to coat.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, then add the tamarind paste and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Remove the lemongrass, galangal, and cinnamon stick before serving.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups banana-leaf pieces, softened in hot water
2 stalks lemongrass, tender inner parts chopped
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, chili, turmeric, and water into a smooth kroeung paste.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar, and salt.
Fold the fish pieces gently into the coconut mixture.
Line small bowls or ramekins with softened banana leaves and brush them lightly with oil.
Divide the fish mixture among the lined bowls.
Steam over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the custard is set and the fish is cooked through.

title: Vietnamese Pho Ga
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, turning until blackened in spots.
Put the chicken and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off foam.
Add the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds, and salt. Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken. Strain the broth, return it to the pot, and stir in the fish sauce.
Shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones. Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and drain.
Divide the noodles and chicken among bowls. Ladle hot broth over them and serve with scallions, cilantro, bean sprouts, and lime wedges.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1/2 cup Filipino cane vinegar or rice vinegar
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot. Bring to a boil without stirring.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Remove the chicken and set it aside. Simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the pot and turn it in the sauce. Serve with the sauce and sliced scallions.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large wok over high heat. Beat the eggs with the salt, scramble until just set, and transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the shallots, garlic, and chilies for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp paste and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Add the rice, kecap manis, and soy sauce. Stir-fry until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Return the eggs to the wok and break them into pieces as you stir. Serve topped with scallions and cucumber.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and tied in knots
2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, and turmeric with the oil into a smooth paste.
Put the beef, spice paste, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, and salt in a heavy pot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook uncovered over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Continue cooking and stirring as the sauce reduces and thickens, until it coats the beef and turns dark brown, about 30 to 45 minutes.
Remove the lemongrass and serve the rendang hot.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
1 teaspoon palm sugar or brown sugar
2 cups thinly sliced banana leaves, for lining
1 red chili, thinly sliced, for garnish
instructions: Line four small heatproof bowls with banana leaves and divide the sliced cabbage among them.
Whisk together the coconut milk, egg, fish sauce, sugar, curry paste, and rice flour until smooth.
Fold the fish and sliced kaffir lime leaves into the coconut mixture.
Spoon the mixture into the lined bowls.
Steam the bowls over simmering water until the fish is opaque and the custard is set, about 20 minutes.
Garnish with sliced chili and serve hot.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until lightly blackened.
Add beef bones, brisket, water, onion, and ginger to a large pot; bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add star anise, cinnamon, cloves, fish sauce, and salt; simmer gently for 3 hours.
Remove the brisket, let it cool, and slice it thinly; strain the broth and keep it hot.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide them among serving bowls.
Top with sliced brisket and raw sirloin, then ladle hot broth over the meat.
Serve with bean sprouts, lime, Thai basil, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside; simmer the sauce until slightly reduced.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the pot and simmer in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice and sliced scallions.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add shallots, garlic, chili, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt; stir-fry until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side and heat the remaining oil in the empty space.
Crack in the eggs and scramble until just set, then mix them into the rice.
Serve with sliced scallions and cucumber.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
