4 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef and stir until coated with the paste.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, coconut milk, water, and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 2 to 3 hours, stirring often, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Remove the lemongrass and serve with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, cut into bite-size pieces
1/4 cup finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
2 stalks lemongrass, tender inner parts chopped
instructions: Blend lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, turmeric, and chili into a smooth kroeung paste.
Whisk the paste with coconut milk, egg, fish sauce, palm sugar, and salt.
Fold in the fish and half of the kaffir lime leaves.
Line small heatproof bowls with napa cabbage and divide the fish mixture among them.
Steam the bowls over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the custard is set.
Garnish with the remaining kaffir lime leaves and serve with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Phở Gà
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until lightly blackened.
Put the chicken and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming the surface.
Add the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, fish sauce, sugar, and salt.
Simmer gently for 35–45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and strain the broth.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Pour hot broth over the noodles and top with chicken, bean sprouts, basil, scallions, and lime.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in or boneless
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside; simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to reduce slightly.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the reduced sauce over the chicken and stir in the brown sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then serve with rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, kecap manis, soy sauce, salt, and pepper; stir-fry until hot and evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side and add the remaining oil to the cleared space.
Crack in the eggs and scramble until just set, then mix them into the rice.
Stir in the scallions and serve hot.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef and stir to coat it with the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and water; add the lemongrass, lime leaves, tamarind, and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Remove the lemongrass and serve with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, chili, and turmeric into a smooth paste.
Whisk the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a bowl.
Stir the spice paste and half of the lime leaves into the coconut mixture.
Fold in the fish pieces.
Line four small bowls with banana leaf and divide the fish mixture among them.
Steam for 20–25 minutes, until the custard is set and the fish is cooked through.
Garnish with the remaining lime leaves and serve with rice.

title: Vietnamese Phở Gà (Chicken Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons fish sauce, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Char the onion and ginger over a flame or under a broiler until lightly blackened.
Place the chicken and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off foam.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute, then add them to the pot.
Add the charred onion and ginger. Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through, about 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken, let it cool, and pull the meat from the bones. Return the bones to the pot and simmer the broth for 45 minutes more.
Strain the broth and season it with fish sauce, sugar, and salt.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide them among serving bowls.
Top with chicken, hot broth, scallions, and cilantro. Serve with lime, bean sprouts, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside. Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to concentrate the flavor.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce, add the brown sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve with rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, shallots, garlic, and chilies to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and shrimp paste and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until hot.
Stir in the kecap manis, soy sauce, salt, scrambled eggs, and scallions.
Serve topped with fried shallots and cucumber slices.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and tied in knots
2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
2-inch piece fresh galangal, peeled and chopped
4 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, and turmeric into a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the spice paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef and lemongrass and stir until the beef is coated with the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Stir in the toasted coconut, salt, and lime leaves. Continue cooking for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 cup thinly sliced red bell pepper
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, lime zest, turmeric, and salt into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Place the cabbage and bell pepper in a heatproof dish or individual bowls.
Fold the fish pieces into the coconut mixture and spoon it over the vegetables.
Steam, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is opaque and the custard is just set.
Scatter the basil leaves over the top and serve hot with rice.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
ingredients: 10 cm piece fresh ginger, halved lengthwise
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan or under a broiler until lightly blackened.
Rinse the bones and brisket, cover with water in a large pot, bring to a boil, and simmer for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Return the bones and brisket to the pot with 4 liters fresh water. Add the charred onion and ginger; simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming as needed.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds until fragrant. Add them to the broth and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove the brisket when tender and let it cool; slice it thinly. Strain the broth, then season with fish sauce, salt, and sugar.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls. Top with brisket and raw sirloin.
Bring the broth to a boil and ladle it over the noodles and beef. Serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside. Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to concentrate it.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, add the brown sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve with rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, shallots, garlic, and chili to the wok; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and shrimp paste and stir-fry until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the rice, kecap manis, and soy sauce. Toss over high heat until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Stir in the egg and scallions. Serve with cucumber and fried shallots.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
8 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, coriander, and cumin into a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
Place the paste, beef, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, turmeric leaf, and salt in a heavy pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook uncovered over low heat for 2 hours, stirring regularly.
Continue cooking for 30 to 60 minutes, stirring more often as the liquid reduces and the beef becomes tender.
Cook until the sauce is thick, dark, and clinging to the beef. Remove the lemongrass and serve with rice.

title: Singaporean Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 300 g jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
2 tablespoons chicken fat or neutral oil
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt and let it stand for 15 minutes. Rinse off the salt.
Place the chicken in a pot and cover with water. Add the ginger, crushed garlic, and scallions.
Bring the water just to a boil, then lower the heat and poach gently for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes, then drain and brush with sesame oil.
Heat the chicken fat in a saucepan. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.
Cut the chicken into serving pieces. Serve with the rice, cucumber, soy sauce, and chili sauce.

title: Vietnamese Phở Bò
instructions: Broil the onion and ginger, cut sides up, until charred, about 5 minutes.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander in a dry pot until fragrant.
Add the beef bones, brisket, charred onion and ginger, and 12 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming the surface.
Remove the brisket when tender, cool it, and slice thinly. Strain the broth; season it with fish sauce, sugar, and salt.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide them among bowls with the brisket and raw sirloin.
Bring the broth to a boil, pour it over the noodles and beef, and serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside. Simmer the sauce uncovered until slightly reduced, about 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the pot and turn it in the sauce. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then transfer them to a plate.
Heat the remaining oil. Fry the shallots, garlic, and chilies for 1 minute.
Stir in the shrimp paste, then add the rice and break up any clumps.
Add the kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt. Stir-fry until the rice is hot and evenly seasoned.
Fold in the scrambled eggs and scallions. Serve with cucumber and fried shallots.

title: Malaysian Laksa Lemak
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
instructions: Soak or cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions; drain and divide among bowls.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the laksa paste and fry for 2 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the chicken stock and coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the chicken and tofu puffs. Simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and sugar. Ladle the soup over the noodles.
Top with bean sprouts and mint, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Line four small heatproof bowls with banana leaves, folding the edges to form cups.
Mix the coconut milk, coconut cream, kroeung paste, egg, fish sauce, and sugar until smooth.
Fold the fish into the coconut mixture.
Divide the cabbage among the banana-leaf cups, then spoon in the fish mixture.
Set the cups in a steamer over simmering water. Cover and steam until the fish is opaque and the custard is set, about 20 minutes.
Garnish with sliced kaffir lime leaves and serve hot.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
ingredients: 2 lb beef bones, preferably marrow and knuckle bones
instructions: Rinse the bones and brisket, then place them in a large pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil for 10 minutes; drain and rinse the bones and pot.
Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until blackened in spots.
Return the bones and brisket to the pot with 4 quarts fresh water. Add the charred onion and ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds.
Bring to a gentle simmer, skimming the surface. Cook for 3 hours, removing the brisket when tender, then slice it thinly.
Continue simmering the broth for another 2 hours. Strain it, then season with fish sauce, salt, and sugar.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide them among serving bowls.
Top with sliced brisket and raw sirloin. Pour boiling broth over the meat and noodles.
Serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, scallions, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1/2 cup Filipino cane vinegar or rice vinegar
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside. Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. Garnish with scallions and serve with rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Pound or finely chop the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste into a rough paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the paste for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir-fry, breaking up clumps, for 3 minutes.
Stir in the kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt. Cook for 2 minutes, tossing until evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side of the wok. Scramble the eggs in the open space, then mix them through the rice.
Stir in the scallions and serve with cucumber and crispy fried shallots.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 inches fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
2 lemongrass stalks, tender inner parts chopped
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, lemongrass, chilies, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes, until the meat is browned on the outside.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Add the lime leaves, salt, and palm sugar.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Continue cooking and stirring until the oil separates and clings to the beef. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
1/2 cup thinly sliced red bell pepper
1 banana leaf, softened, or 4 heatproof ramekins
instructions: Whisk together the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, and palm sugar until smooth.
Fold in the fish, cabbage, bell pepper, and half of the lime leaves.
Line a steamer basket with the softened banana leaf, or divide the mixture among ramekins.
Spoon the fish mixture into the leaf or ramekins and cover loosely.
Steam over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the custard is set.
Garnish with the remaining lime leaves and cilantro. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Phở Bò
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until blackened in spots.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander in a dry pot for 1 minute.
Add the beef bones, brisket, onion, ginger, and 10 cups water; bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Simmer gently for 2 hours, removing the brisket when tender and slicing it thinly.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot, and season with fish sauce, sugar, and salt.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Top with brisket and raw sirloin, ladle over hot broth, and serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside; simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to reduce slightly.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce, stir in the brown sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, and chili; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Push the aromatics to one side, pour in the eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the chicken and rice, breaking up any rice clumps as you stir-fry.
Stir in the kecap manis, soy sauce, coriander, and salt; cook until the rice is hot.
Top with scallions and fried shallots, and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the spice paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef, lemongrass, lime leaves, and cinnamon; stir to coat the meat.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, add the salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Remove the lemongrass and cinnamon stick, then serve with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
1 stalk lemongrass, tender inner part finely minced
4 banana-leaf cups or small ovenproof ramekins
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and arrange the banana-leaf cups or ramekins in a baking dish.
Whisk together the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, sugar, curry paste, lemongrass, rice flour, and salt.
Fold in the fish, cabbage, spinach, and half the lime leaves.
Divide the mixture among the cups and place them in the baking dish.
Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the cups, then bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until set.
Sprinkle with the remaining lime leaves and serve hot with rice.

title: Vietnamese Phở Gà (Chicken Noodle Soup)
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, turning until blackened in spots.
Put the chicken and water in a large pot and bring to a gentle boil, skimming off foam.
Add the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds, fish sauce, and salt. Simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Strain the broth and return it to the pot; keep it hot. When cool enough to handle, remove the chicken meat from the bones and slice it.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide noodles and chicken among bowls. Ladle hot broth over them and serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
4 cups cooked white rice, for serving
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced slightly.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 2 minutes. Serve with rice and scallions, if using.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Break up the cold rice with a fork and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add the shallots, garlic, and chili; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, kecap manis, soy sauce, salt, and white pepper. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until hot and evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side of the wok. Crack in the eggs and scramble until just set, then mix them through the rice.
Stir in the scallions and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Malaysian Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 2 pandan leaves, tied in a knot (optional)
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan leaves, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the anchovies for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp, then transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, toast the peanuts for 2 minutes, stirring, then set aside.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool under cold water, peel, and halve.
Serve the coconut rice with anchovies, peanuts, eggs, sambal, and cucumber, on banana leaves if desired.

title: Burmese Mohinga (Fish Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and tied in a knot
instructions: Put the fish, water, lemongrass, and turmeric in a pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Lift out the fish and lemongrass. Flake the fish and set aside; keep the cooking liquid as broth.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir the onion mixture and fish sauce into the broth. Whisk the rice flour with 1 cup cold water, then stir it into the pot.
Simmer the soup for 10 minutes, stirring often, until lightly thickened. Add the flaked fish and heat through.
Cook the rice vermicelli according to package directions and drain. Divide among bowls, ladle soup over the noodles, and garnish with egg, lime, and cilantro.

title: Vietnamese Phở Gà (Chicken Noodle Soup)
instructions: Char the onion and ginger over a flame or under a broiler until lightly blackened.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds in a dry pot for 1 minute.
Add the water, chicken, onion, ginger, toasted spices, fish sauce, and salt to the pot.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer gently for 60 minutes, until the chicken is cooked.
Remove the chicken and let it cool; strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Pull the chicken meat from the bones and keep it warm.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and divide among serving bowls.
Pour hot broth over the noodles and top with chicken, scallions, cilantro, and bean sprouts; serve with lime wedges.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Combine the vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Add the chicken and bring the mixture to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside; simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with scallions.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chili, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in the kecap manis and soy sauce until the rice is evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side, pour the eggs into the empty side, and scramble until just set.
Mix the eggs into the rice and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Serve topped with scallions and fried shallots, with cucumber on the side.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and tied in knots
4 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
Put the paste, beef, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, turmeric leaf, and salt in a heavy pot.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring well, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick, dark coating.
Remove the lemongrass and lime leaves before serving.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
2 tablespoons finely sliced red bell pepper
2 stalks lemongrass, tender inner parts finely chopped
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallot, garlic, galangal, turmeric, and oil into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar, and salt.
Fold the fish into the coconut mixture.
Divide the cabbage among four heatproof bowls or banana-leaf cups, then spoon the fish mixture on top.
Steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the custard is just set.
Garnish with red bell pepper and makrut lime leaves before serving.

title: Vietnamese Phở Bò (Beef Noodle Soup)
instructions: Parboil the bones for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan until browned.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds until fragrant.
Add bones, brisket, charred aromatics, toasted spices, and water to a pot; simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming as needed.
Remove the brisket when tender, let it cool, and slice it thinly.
Strain the broth, then season it with fish sauce and sugar.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide them among bowls.
Top with brisket and raw sirloin, ladle over boiling broth, and serve with sprouts, basil, lime, scallions, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside; simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, stir in the sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through.
Push the mixture to one side, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the rice, kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt; stir-fry until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Stir in the scallions and serve with cucumber slices and fried eggs.

title: Malaysian Laksa Lemak
instructions: Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions, drain, and divide among bowls.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the laksa paste for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the chicken and turn to coat it in the paste.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken, shred it, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar; heat gently without boiling.
Add the tofu puffs and warm them in the broth for 3 minutes.
Ladle the broth over the noodles and top with chicken, bean sprouts, egg, and mint; serve with lime.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Line a heatproof bowl or banana-leaf cup with the sliced cabbage.
Whisk together the coconut milk, kroeung paste, egg, fish sauce, palm sugar, rice flour, and salt.
Fold the fish and half the lime leaves into the coconut mixture.
Spoon the mixture over the cabbage and sprinkle with the remaining lime leaves and chili.
Steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the custard is set.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
ingredients: 1/2 pound raw beef sirloin, thinly sliced
instructions: Char the onion and ginger under a broiler or over a flame until browned.
Rinse the bones and brisket, then simmer them in 4 quarts of water for 10 minutes; drain and rinse.
Return the bones and brisket to a clean pot with 4 quarts of water; simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming the surface.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds, then add them with the onion and ginger to the broth.
Simmer for 1 hour more; remove the brisket when tender, cool it, and slice it thinly.
Season the broth with fish sauce, sugar, and salt; strain it and keep it hot.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide them among bowls with the sliced brisket and raw sirloin.
Ladle boiling broth over the noodles and beef; serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, scallions, and chilies.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set aside; simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to concentrate it.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with scallions and serve with steamed rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and rice, breaking up any clumps as you stir-fry.
Stir in the kecap manis, soy sauce, salt, and white pepper; cook until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Push the rice to one side, add the remaining oil, and scramble the eggs in the cleared space.
Fold the eggs and scallions through the rice and cook for 1 minute more.
Serve hot with cucumber slices.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and tied in knots
6 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric, and oil into a smooth spice paste.
Heat the paste in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef and stir until coated with the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and water; add the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook uncovered for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the tamarind paste, palm sugar, and salt.
Continue cooking for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring more often as the sauce thickens, until the beef is tender and the oil separates.
Remove the lemongrass and serve with steamed rice.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, tender inner parts chopped
2 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, turmeric, and chilies into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste with half the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar, lime juice, and salt.
Fold the fish into the mixture and let it stand for 15 minutes.
Line a steamer-safe dish with the cabbage and spoon the fish mixture over it.
Steam, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is opaque and set.
Warm the remaining coconut milk and spoon it over the amok.
Garnish with kaffir lime leaves and basil; serve with steamed rice.

title: Vietnamese Phở Bò
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry skillet over medium-high heat until blackened in spots.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander in a dry pot for 1 minute.
Add the beef stock, charred onion, ginger, brisket, fish sauce, sugar, and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer gently for 2½ hours, skimming the surface as needed.
Remove the brisket, slice it thinly, and strain the broth; return the broth to the pot and keep it hot.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide the noodles, brisket, and raw sirloin among bowls; pour the hot broth over them.
Serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, jalapeños, and scallions.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside; simmer the sauce for 10 minutes more.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Pour the sauce into the skillet, add the sugar, and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Push the aromatics to one side, crack in the eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the rice, kecap manis, soy sauce, and salt; stir-fry until the rice is hot and evenly coated.
Stir in the scallions and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1½-inch cubes
8 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, and turmeric with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef and stir to coat it in the paste.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, cinnamon, coconut milk, water, tamarind, and salt; bring to a gentle boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick and dark.
Cook until the oil separates and clings to the beef, then remove the lemongrass and cinnamon stick before serving.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Whisk together the coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar, and kroeung paste until smooth.
Fold in the fish, cabbage, and spinach.
Soften the banana leaf squares over a flame or in hot water, then shape each into a small cup and secure the corners with toothpicks.
Divide the fish mixture among the banana-leaf cups and top with sliced kaffir lime leaves.
Steam the cups over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked and the custard is set.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, turning until blackened in spots.
Put the beef bones and brisket in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and brisket.
Return the bones and brisket to the pot with 4 quarts fresh water. Add the charred onion and ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 3 hours, skimming the surface occasionally. Remove the brisket when tender, cool it, and slice thinly.
Strain the broth, stir in the fish sauce and salt, and keep it hot. Cook the rice noodles according to package directions and drain.
Divide noodles and brisket among bowls. Add the raw sirloin, pour over hot broth, and serve with scallions, basil, bean sprouts, and lime wedges.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Add the chicken and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Remove the chicken and set it aside. Simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Indonesian Nasi Goreng
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice, kecap manis, and soy sauce. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking up clumps, until hot.
Heat the remaining oil in a skillet and fry the eggs to your preferred doneness.
Divide the rice among plates and top each serving with a fried egg. Serve with scallions, cucumber, and tomato.

title: Malaysian Beef Rendang
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and tied in knots
2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chilies, turmeric, and coriander with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the spice paste and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beef, lemongrass, and lime leaves. Stir to coat the beef with the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the toasted coconut and salt. Continue cooking for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring more often, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef. Remove the lemongrass before serving.

title: Cambodian Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups thinly sliced banana leaves, softened in hot water
1 stalk lemongrass, tender inner part finely chopped
instructions: Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, and turmeric with 2 tablespoons of water into a smooth paste.
Whisk the coconut milk, egg, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a bowl. Stir in the spice paste and fish.
Line four small heatproof bowls with the softened banana leaves, leaving enough overhang to fold over.
Divide the fish mixture among the bowls and fold the leaves over to cover. Steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and the custard is set.
Garnish with lime leaves and chili, then serve hot.

title: Nasi Lemak
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan leaves, and salt in a rice cooker; cook until tender.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, and peel.
Fry the anchovies in a little oil until crisp; drain.
Warm the sambal and roast the peanuts if needed.
Serve the coconut rice with eggs, anchovies, peanuts, cucumber, and sambal.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 2 Chinese chives, cut into 5 cm lengths
instructions: Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and oyster sauce in a small bowl.
Heat a wok until very hot and add the oil.
Stir-fry the garlic, prawns, and Chinese sausage until the prawns are nearly cooked.
Add the noodles and sauce; toss over high heat until evenly coated.
Push the noodles aside, scramble the eggs in the wok, then toss everything together.
Add the bean sprouts and chives; stir-fry briefly and serve hot.

title: Rendang Ayam
ingredients: 8 dried red chillies, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, and turmeric into a smooth paste.
Put the paste, chicken, coconut milk, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves in a heavy pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often, and cook until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the kerisik, turmeric leaf, and salt.
Continue cooking gently, stirring frequently, until the sauce is dark and clings to the chicken.

title: Asam Laksa
ingredients: 5 dried red chillies, soaked and drained
1 cup pineapple, cut into thin strips
instructions: Simmer the mackerel in the water until cooked; remove the fish and reserve the broth.
Cool the fish, remove the bones, and flake the flesh.
Blend the chillies, shallots, galangal, and shrimp paste into a paste.
Simmer the paste, lemongrass, tamarind, salt, and sugar in the reserved broth for 20 minutes.
Add the flaked fish and simmer for 5 minutes; remove the lemongrass.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles and top with cucumber, onion, pineapple, mint, Vietnamese mint, and prawn paste.

title: Kangkung Belacan
ingredients: 500 g water spinach (kangkung), trimmed and washed
instructions: Pound or blend the garlic, shallots, chillies, and shrimp paste into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry the paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the water spinach and water; toss until the leaves wilt and the stems are crisp-tender.
Add the sugar, toss once more, and serve immediately.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
2 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt and set aside for 15 minutes.
Bring the water, crushed garlic, sliced ginger, and pandan leaves to a gentle boil in a pot large enough to hold the chicken.
Lower the chicken into the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes, until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and rest it; reserve the broth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and fry the rice with the minced garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add 3 cups of reserved broth, cover, and cook the rice over low heat until tender, about 15 minutes.
Mix the minced ginger, minced garlic, lime juice, and a little broth for a dipping sauce; mix the chili with soy sauce for another sauce.
Chop the chicken and serve with the rice, dipping sauces, and extra broth.

title: Laksa Lemak
ingredients: 200 g dried rice vermicelli, soaked and drained
2 tablespoons dried shrimp, soaked and drained
instructions: Blend the dried shrimp, shallots, garlic, chilies, coriander, and turmeric into a paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the paste for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring until fragrant.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, and stock; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and salt, then simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Add the prawns and fish cake and cook until the prawns turn pink.
Blanch the vermicelli and bean sprouts in hot water, then divide them among serving bowls.
Ladle the hot laksa broth, prawns, and fish cake over the noodles and garnish with laksa leaves.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 2 Chinese chives, cut into 5 cm lengths
instructions: Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water in a small bowl.
Loosen the rice noodles gently so they do not break.
Heat a wok over high heat and add the oil.
Fry the garlic and Chinese sausage for 30 seconds, then add the prawns and stir-fry until nearly cooked.
Push the ingredients aside, crack in the eggs, and scramble briefly.
Add the noodles and sauce, tossing over high heat until the noodles are hot and evenly coated.
Add the bean sprouts and chives; toss for 30 seconds and serve immediately.

title: Kaya Toast with Soft-Boiled Eggs
ingredients: 2 tablespoons salted butter, chilled and thinly sliced
instructions: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil, then remove it from the heat.
Lower the eggs into the hot water, cover, and leave for 7 minutes.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Spread kaya on two slices of toast and layer the butter over the kaya.
Top with the remaining toast, cut into halves, and serve warm.
Crack the eggs into small bowls and season with soy sauce and white pepper.

title: Sambal Kangkong
ingredients: 500 g water spinach (kangkong), rinsed and cut into 8 cm lengths
5 dried red chilies, soaked until soft
instructions: Pound or blend the dried chilies, fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, and belacan into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the paste for 4 to 5 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the sugar and water.
Add the kangkong and stir-fry over high heat until just wilted, about 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat, stir in the lime juice, and serve hot.

title: Fish Amok
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish, cut into bite-size pieces
2 tbsp kroeung, finely pounded lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, kaffir lime zest, garlic, and shallot
2 cups thinly sliced banana leaves, for lining
instructions: Line small heatproof bowls or a steamer basket with banana leaves.
Whisk coconut milk, kroeung, egg, fish sauce, and palm sugar until smooth.
Fold in the fish and divide among the lined bowls.
Steam over simmering water for 20–25 minutes, until the fish is just cooked and the custard is set.
Scatter with sliced kaffir lime leaf and serve with rice.

title: Samlor Korkor
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
2 tbsp kroeung, finely pounded lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, and shallot
1 tbsp prahok, or fermented fish paste
instructions: Bring the water or broth to a boil in a large pot and add the pork.
Stir in the kroeung and prahok, then simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add the papaya, pumpkin, and eggplant; simmer until nearly tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the long beans, roasted rice powder, fish sauce, and salt.
Cook for 5–7 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender, and serve hot with rice.

title: Nom Banh Chok (Khmer Noodles with Fish Gravy)
ingredients: 2 tbsp kroeung, finely pounded lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, and shallot
1 tbsp prahok, or fermented fish paste
instructions: Simmer the fish in the water until cooked through, about 8 minutes; lift it out and reserve the broth.
Flake the fish, removing any bones.
Return the broth to a simmer and stir in the kroeung and prahok.
Add the flaked fish and coconut milk; simmer gently for 10 minutes, then season with fish sauce and salt.
Divide rice noodles among bowls, ladle over the fish gravy, and serve with bean sprouts, cucumber, and mint.

title: Bai Sach Chrouk (Grilled Pork with Rice)
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, garlic, and oil in a bowl.
Add the pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Combine the rice and water in a pot; bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Grill or sear the pork over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, until cooked through and lightly charred.
Serve the pork over rice with sliced cucumber.

title: Kuy Teav (Pork Rice Noodle Soup)
instructions: Cover the pork bones with water in a pot and bring to a boil; skim off any foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 1 hour, then strain the broth and season it with fish sauce, salt, and sugar.
Soak the rice noodles according to the package directions, then drain.
Divide noodles and sliced pork among bowls; pour the hot broth over them and let the pork cook in the broth for 2–3 minutes.
Top with bean sprouts, scallions, and cilantro, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Khao Niew (Lao Sticky Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice several times until the water is mostly clear.
Cover with plenty of water and soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and place it in a sticky-rice steaming basket.
Set the basket over a pot of boiling water, cover, and steam for 20 minutes.
Flip the rice in the basket and steam for 10 to 15 minutes more, until tender.
Transfer to a covered serving basket and serve warm.

title: Tam Mak Hoong (Lao Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 pound green papaya, peeled and shredded
1 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic and chiles in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the long beans and pound lightly to bruise them.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce, padaek, and lime juice; pound and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the tomatoes and gently pound until they release some juice.
Add the shredded papaya and toss, pounding lightly until the dressing coats it well.
Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sour, sweet, and spicy; serve promptly.

title: Larb Gai (Lao Chicken Larb)
instructions: Toast uncooked sticky rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring until golden; cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Place the chicken and water in a pan over medium heat.
Cook, stirring and breaking up the chicken, until fully cooked and no longer pink.
Remove from the heat and stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, toasted rice powder, and chile flakes.
Fold in the shallot, mint, cilantro, and green onions.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Or Lam (Lao Herb and Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
1 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tablespoon chopped rice paddy herb, if available
instructions: Put the beef, water, and lemongrass in a pot and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, skim the surface, and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the padaek and fish sauce.
Add the eggplant, pumpkin, and long beans; simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the dill, rice paddy herb, and roasted sticky rice powder.
Simmer for 2 minutes, taste for seasoning, and serve hot with sticky rice.

title: Mok Pa (Lao Steamed Fish in Banana Leaves)
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, tender inner parts finely sliced
4 large banana-leaf pieces, softened over a flame
instructions: Combine the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and chiles in a bowl.
Add the fish, fish sauce, and padaek; mix gently to coat.
Fold in the dill and scallions.
Divide the mixture among the banana-leaf pieces and fold each into a secure packet.
Place the packets in a steamer over boiling water.
Cover and steam for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked through; serve hot.

title: Mohinga
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
2 tablespoons rice flour mixed with 1/2 cup water
instructions: Simmer the fish in the water with the lemongrass until cooked, about 10 minutes; lift out the fish and strain the broth.
Flake the fish, removing bones, and set aside.
Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in a little oil until soft; stir in turmeric and paprika.
Add the strained broth, fish sauce, and flaked fish; simmer for 10 minutes.
Whisk the chickpea flour with a little broth, then stir it into the pot. Add the rice-flour mixture and simmer until the soup thickens slightly.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle soup over the noodles and serve with eggs, cilantro, lime, and fried onions.

title: Ohn No Khao Swe
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Cook the noodles according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft; add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, paprika, and chickpea flour; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Pour in the broth and coconut milk, then add the fish sauce.
Simmer until the chicken is tender and cooked through, about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Divide noodles among bowls and ladle the chicken curry over them.
Serve with lime, fried onions, cilantro, and eggs.

title: Lahpet Thoke (Tea Leaf Salad)
instructions: Place the tea leaves in a small bowl and mix with the fish sauce, lime juice, oil, and chili flakes.
Put the cabbage and tomatoes in a large serving bowl.
Add the dressed tea leaves, peanuts, sesame seeds, fried garlic, and fried peas.
Toss thoroughly just before serving.

title: Burmese Chicken Curry
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Mix the chicken with the turmeric, paprika, chili powder, fish sauce, and salt; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onions over medium heat until deeply golden, about 12 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and its marinade; stir and cook until the pieces are lightly browned.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes, stirring now and then.
Uncover and simmer briefly to thicken the sauce to your liking.

title: Shan-Style Tofu Noodles
ingredients: 1 block (14 ounces) firm tofu, drained and mashed
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, turmeric, salt, and 1 cup of water in a saucepan until smooth.
Stir in the mashed tofu and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and creamy, about 8 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and divide among bowls.
Warm the vegetable broth in a separate pot.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the garlic until fragrant; stir in the soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Spoon the tofu mixture over the noodles and add hot broth to each bowl.
Top with the garlic mixture, scallions, cilantro, peanuts, and chili oil.

title: Cá Kho Tộ (Caramelized Clay-Pot Fish)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb catfish steaks, cut into pieces
instructions: Toss the fish with the fish sauce and black pepper; set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the sugar and water in a heavy pot until deep amber, then carefully stir in the oil.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the fish and turn gently to coat with the caramel.
Pour in the coconut water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook for 25–30 minutes, turning the fish once, until tender and the sauce is glossy.
Scatter the scallions over the fish and serve with steamed rice.

title: Canh Chua Cá (Vietnamese Sour Fish Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb catfish or white fish, cut into chunks
1/4 cup chopped rice paddy herb or cilantro
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a pot.
Stir in the tamarind, fish sauce, and sugar.
Add the tomatoes and pineapple and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently until nearly cooked, about 5 minutes.
Add the okra and celery and cook until just tender.
Heat the oil in a small pan and fry the garlic until golden; stir it into the soup.
Add the bean sprouts and herbs, then turn off the heat and serve.

title: Thịt Kho Trứng (Braised Pork and Eggs)
ingredients: 2 lb pork belly, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water, and peel.
Heat the sugar and water in a pot until amber; carefully stir in the coconut water.
Add the pork, shallots, garlic, fish sauce, pepper, and 1 cup water.
Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the peeled eggs and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, turning the eggs occasionally.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Gỏi Cuốn (Fresh Spring Rolls)
ingredients: 12 cooked medium shrimp, peeled and halved lengthwise
8 oz cooked pork belly, thinly sliced
instructions: Cook the vermicelli according to the package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water.
Stir the hoisin sauce, peanut butter, and water together in a small bowl; sprinkle with peanuts.
Dip one rice paper wrapper briefly in warm water and lay it flat on a board.
Place lettuce, herbs, vermicelli, pork, and bean sprouts near the lower edge.
Fold the sides over the filling, roll once, add two shrimp halves with their cut sides facing up, then roll tightly to seal.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Bún Bò Huế (Spicy Lemongrass Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb pork hocks, cut into pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into lengths
instructions: Place the beef, pork hocks, water, bruised lemongrass, and onion in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Skim the surface, reduce the heat, and simmer until the meat is tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the meat, slice it, and strain the broth; return the broth to the pot.
Stir the fish sauce, shrimp paste, and sugar into the broth and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Heat the oil in a small pan; fry the minced lemongrass and chili flakes for 1 minute, then stir the mixture into the broth.
Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions and divide it among bowls.
Top with sliced meat, hot broth, cabbage, bean sprouts, and cilantro.

title: Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and set aside; simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Sinigang na Baboy
ingredients: 2 pounds pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 bunch water spinach, cut into 3-inch lengths
1 packet tamarind soup base, about 1.4 ounces
instructions: Put the pork and water in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the onion and tomatoes; simmer until the pork is tender, about 60 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and fish sauce.
Add the radish and eggplant; simmer until just tender, about 8 minutes.
Add the water spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.

title: Pancit Bihon
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and cook the chicken until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and onion; cook until fragrant and softened.
Add the carrot, cabbage, broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce; bring to a simmer.
Add the drained noodles and toss until they absorb the broth and are tender.
Top with green onions and serve.

title: Laing
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the pork belly until browned and some fat has rendered.
Add the onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until softened.
Stir in the shrimp paste, coconut milk, and coconut cream.
Add the dried taro leaves and whole chilies; press the leaves gently into the liquid without stirring.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the leaves are tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir carefully and serve with rice.

title: Kare-Kare
ingredients: 2 pounds beef shank, cut into pieces
instructions: Put the beef, water, and onion in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Cover and simmer until the beef is tender, about 2 hours; reserve the broth and discard the onion.
Whisk the peanut butter and rice flour with 2 cups of reserved broth until smooth.
Return the beef and peanut mixture to the pot and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Add the green beans, eggplant, and banana blossom; cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Serve with shrimp paste on the side.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
instructions: Crush the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the paste for 1 minute.
Add the eggs and scramble until just set.
Add the rice, sweet soy sauce, and salt; stir-fry until hot and evenly coated.
Stir in the scallions and serve with cucumber.

title: Sayur Lodeh
ingredients: 1 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the shallots, garlic, and chilies until softened.
Stir in the coriander and shrimp paste and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the thin coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the chayote and long beans; simmer until nearly tender, about 8 minutes.
Add the tofu, thick coconut milk, salt, and palm sugar; simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.

title: Rendang Daging
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilies, ginger, galangal, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth spice paste.
Put the beef, spice paste, lemongrass, lime leaves, coconut milk, water, salt, and palm sugar in a heavy pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring often.
Cook for 2½ to 3 hours, until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick, dark coating.
Remove the lemongrass and lime leaves before serving.

title: Soto Ayam
instructions: Simmer the chicken in the water for 30 minutes, skimming the surface as needed.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and coriander into a paste.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the paste for 3 minutes.
Stir the paste, lemongrass, lime leaves, and salt into the chicken broth; simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and return it to the broth.
Divide the rice and bean sprouts among bowls, ladle over the soup, and top with egg and scallions; serve with lime.

title: Gado-Gado
ingredients: 1 cup boiled potato, cut into chunks
8 ounces firm tofu, fried and cubed
instructions: Grind the peanuts, garlic, and chilies into a coarse paste.
Mix in the tamarind, palm sugar, salt, and warm water until you have a thick dressing.
Blanch the cabbage and bean sprouts separately until just tender, then drain.
Arrange the cabbage, bean sprouts, cucumber, potato, tofu, and eggs on a platter.
Spoon the peanut dressing over the vegetables and finish with fried shallots.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 2 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
instructions: Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan leaves, and salt in a rice cooker; cook until fluffy.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool them, and peel.
Fry the anchovies in a little oil until crisp; drain.
Serve the rice with eggs, anchovies, peanuts, cucumber, and sambal.

title: Chicken Rendang
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric, and belacan into a paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste until fragrant, about 8 minutes.
Add the chicken and lemongrass; stir to coat.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, then add the salt. Simmer gently, stirring often, until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the turmeric leaves and cook until the rendang is dark and nearly dry.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 2 stalks Chinese chives, cut into 5 cm lengths
instructions: Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, chili paste, and fish sauce in a small bowl.
Heat a wok until very hot and add the oil. Fry the garlic and lap cheong briefly.
Add the prawns and stir-fry until nearly cooked.
Add the noodles and sauce; toss over high heat until hot and evenly coated.
Push the noodles aside, scramble the eggs in the wok, then toss them through.
Add the bean sprouts and chives; stir-fry briefly and serve at once.

title: Asam Laksa
ingredients: 2 tablespoons tamarind pulp, mixed with 1/2 cup water and strained
1 cup pineapple, cut into small pieces
instructions: Simmer the mackerel in the water until cooked; lift out the fish and reserve the broth.
Remove the fish bones and flake the flesh.
Blend the soaked chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, and belacan into a paste.
Fry the paste in a little oil until fragrant, then add it to the reserved broth with the lemongrass and tamarind slices.
Add the tamarind water, salt, and sugar; simmer for 20 minutes, then stir in the flaked fish.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle over the hot broth. Top with cucumber, onion, pineapple, mint, and sliced chili.

title: Kuih Seri Muka
ingredients: 200 g glutinous rice, rinsed and soaked for 2 hours
2 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
4 pandan leaves, blended with 3 tablespoons water and strained
instructions: Drain the glutinous rice and mix it with the first measure of coconut milk and the salt.
Steam the rice with the pandan leaves for 25 minutes, then press it firmly into a lined 20 cm square pan.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, second measure of coconut milk, rice flour, tapioca flour, and pandan juice until smooth.
Strain the pandan mixture over the rice layer.
Steam over low heat for 30 minutes, keeping the lid wrapped in a cloth to prevent water from dripping onto the custard.
Cool completely before cutting into squares.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
2 tablespoons chicken fat or neutral oil
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
4 cups water, or enough to cover the chicken
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt and set aside for 15 minutes.
Bring the water, garlic, and ginger to a gentle simmer in a pot. Add the chicken breast-side down, cover, and simmer gently until cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and plunge it briefly into a bowl of ice water, then drain. Reserve the cooking broth.
Heat the chicken fat in a saucepan. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes; add the pandan, if using, and 2½ cups of reserved broth.
Cover and cook the rice until tender, about 15 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes.
Mix the minced ginger with a pinch of salt and the minced chilli with lime juice.
Carve the chicken and serve with the rice, ginger sauce, chilli sauce, and light soy sauce.

title: Laksa Lemak
ingredients: 200 g dried rice vermicelli, soaked and drained
200 g dried thick rice noodles, soaked and drained
2 tablespoons dried shrimp, rinsed and soaked
1 teaspoon chilli paste, or to taste
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
2 tablespoons chopped laksa leaves or Vietnamese mint
instructions: Blend the dried shrimp, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, coriander, turmeric, and chilli paste with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the paste over medium heat until fragrant and the oil begins to separate, about 8 minutes.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Stir in the coconut milk and salt; simmer gently for 10 minutes without boiling hard.
Add the fish cakes and prawns. Simmer until the prawns are just cooked, about 3 minutes.
Blanch the rice vermicelli, thick rice noodles, and bean sprouts separately in hot water; drain well.
Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among bowls. Ladle over the hot laksa broth, prawns, and fish cakes.
Top with chopped laksa leaves and serve immediately.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 500 g fresh flat rice noodles, separated
2 stalks Chinese chives, cut into 5 cm lengths
1 teaspoon chilli paste, or to taste
instructions: Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and chilli paste in a small bowl.
Heat a wok until very hot. Add 1 tablespoon of oil and sear the prawns until nearly cooked; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and fry the Chinese sausage until lightly browned. Add the garlic and stir-fry briefly.
Add the noodles and sauce mixture. Toss over high heat until the noodles are hot and evenly coated.
Push the noodles aside, crack in the eggs, and scramble until just set; fold them through the noodles.
Return the prawns to the wok. Add the bean sprouts and chives, toss briefly, and serve hot.

title: Sambal Kang Kong
ingredients: 500 g water spinach (kang kong), trimmed and cut into 8 cm lengths
4 dried red chillies, soaked and drained
1 tablespoon dried shrimp, rinsed and soaked
½ teaspoon salt, or to taste
instructions: Pound or blend the dried shrimp, dried and fresh chillies, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the paste over medium heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add the water and sugar, then stir to combine.
Add the water spinach and toss over high heat until wilted but still crisp, about 2–3 minutes.
Season with salt and serve immediately.

title: Pandan Chiffon Cake
ingredients: 6 large eggs, separated and at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C. Use an ungreased 20 cm chiffon cake pan.
Whisk the egg yolks with 50 g of the sugar until pale. Whisk in the coconut milk, oil, and pandan extract.
Sift in the cake flour and salt, then whisk just until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar until foamy. Gradually add the remaining 100 g sugar and beat to firm, glossy peaks.
Fold one-third of the egg whites into the yolk mixture to lighten it, then gently fold in the rest.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake until risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean, about 50–55 minutes.
Invert the pan immediately and let the cake cool completely before unmoulding.

title: Samlor Korko (Khmer Vegetable and Fish Soup)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons kroeung (lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, shallot, and kaffir lime zest paste)
8 ounces firm white fish, cut into chunks
1 cup green papaya, peeled and sliced
1 cup water spinach, cut into short lengths
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the kroeung for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the fish and turn gently to coat it in the paste.
Add the pumpkin, papaya, eggplant, water, prahok, and fish sauce.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the water spinach and ground rice; simmer for 2 minutes and serve hot.

title: Bai Sach Chrouk (Grilled Pork with Rice)
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, garlic, and oil; coat the pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Combine the rice and water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low until tender, about 15 minutes.
Toss the cucumber and carrot with the rice vinegar and sugar.
Grill or broil the pork, turning once, until browned and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve the pork over rice with the pickled vegetables.

title: Amok Trey (Steamed Fish Curry)
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Place the napa cabbage in the bottom of a heatproof dish or several banana-leaf cups.
Whisk the kroeung, coconut milk, egg, fish sauce, and palm sugar until smooth.
Fold in the fish and half of the kaffir lime leaves.
Spoon the mixture over the cabbage and cover loosely.
Steam over simmering water until the fish is just cooked and the custard is set, about 20 minutes.
Top with the remaining lime leaves and chili before serving.

title: Nom Banh Chok (Khmer Rice Noodles with Fish Gravy)
instructions: Simmer the catfish in the water until cooked, about 10 minutes; remove the fish and reserve the cooking liquid.
Flake the fish, removing any bones.
Return the liquid to the pot and stir in the kroeung, prahok, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the flaked fish and coconut milk; simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Divide the rice noodles among bowls and top with bean sprouts, cucumber, banana blossom, and mint.
Ladle the hot fish gravy over the noodles and serve.

title: Khor Sach Chrouk (Caramel-Braised Pork)
ingredients: 1½ pounds pork belly, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Melt the palm sugar with the water in a heavy pot over medium heat until it turns deep amber.
Carefully add the pork and stir to coat it in the caramel.
Add the fish sauce, soy sauce, garlic, eggs, water, and star anise.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently until the pork is tender, about 1½ hours.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is glossy and reduced to your liking.
Serve with steamed rice and sliced green onions.

title: Khao Niew (Lao Sticky Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice several times, until the water is mostly clear.
Cover with plenty of water and soak for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and spread it in a bamboo sticky-rice basket or steamer lined with cheesecloth.
Steam over simmering water for 20 minutes.
Turn the rice over and steam for 10 to 15 minutes more, until tender and glossy.
Serve warm in a covered sticky-rice basket.

title: Tam Mak Hoong (Lao Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 small green papaya, peeled and julienned
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a large mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the dried shrimp and palm sugar; pound lightly to combine.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and padaek, and stir with the pestle.
Add the tomato and gently bruise it to release its juices.
Add the papaya and pound lightly while tossing with a spoon until well coated.
Taste and adjust the lime, fish sauce, and padaek; serve right away.

title: Larb Gai (Lao Chicken Larb)
instructions: Put the chicken and water in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook, stirring and breaking up the meat, until fully cooked and no longer pink.
Remove from the heat and stir in the toasted rice powder, fish sauce, lime juice, and chili flakes.
Fold in the shallot, scallions, mint, and cilantro.
Taste and adjust the lime, fish sauce, and chili to your liking.
Serve warm or at room temperature with lettuce leaves and sticky rice.

title: Or Lam (Luang Prabang Herb and Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1 pound beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and cut into lengths
1 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Bring the beef and water to a boil in a large pot, skimming any foam.
Add the lemongrass and shallots; simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the padaek, eggplant, pumpkin, and long beans.
Simmer until the vegetables are tender and the broth is flavorful, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the dill, Thai basil, toasted rice powder, and Sichuan pepper.
Simmer for 2 minutes, then taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Mok Pa (Lao Steamed Fish in Banana Leaves)
ingredients: 1 pound white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces
4 large banana-leaf squares, softened over a flame
instructions: Combine the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and chilies in a bowl.
Add the fish, fish sauce, dill, Thai basil, and scallions; toss gently.
Divide the mixture among the banana leaves.
Fold each leaf into a secure packet and tie with kitchen string or a strip of banana leaf.
Steam the packets over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked through.
Open carefully and serve hot with sticky rice.

title: Mohinga
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
1 cup thinly sliced banana stem, optional
instructions: Simmer the catfish in the water with the lemongrass until just cooked, about 10 minutes. Lift out the fish and strain the broth; flake the fish.
Heat a little oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the broth, fish sauce, flaked fish, and banana stem, if using. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk the chickpea flour with 1 cup cool water, then stir it into the soup. Simmer until lightly thickened.
Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions and divide among bowls. Ladle soup over it and serve with eggs, cilantro, and lime.

title: Ohn No Khao Swè (Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, paprika, and turmeric; stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and cook, stirring, until the chicken is coated in the spices.
Stir in the coconut milk and chicken stock. Simmer gently for 25 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Whisk the chickpea flour with 1/2 cup cool water and stir it into the soup. Simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.
Cook the egg noodles according to the package directions. Divide them among bowls, ladle soup over them, and top with red onion, cilantro, and lime.

title: Burmese Tomato and Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds firm white fish, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring, until they soften and break down, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce and water, then bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish in a single layer. Cover and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish is just cooked.
Scatter cilantro over the curry and serve with steamed rice.

title: Lahpet Thoke (Fermented Tea Leaf Salad)
ingredients: 1 small green chili, finely sliced, optional
instructions: Taste the tea leaves; if they are very salty or bitter, rinse briefly and squeeze dry.
Put the tea leaves, cabbage, tomato, peanuts, sesame seeds, fried garlic, and split peas in a large bowl.
Drizzle with the oil, lime juice, and fish sauce.
Toss thoroughly just before serving, then add the chili if you like.

title: Burmese Chicken Potato Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and fish sauce. Cook, turning the pieces, until coated and lightly browned.
Add the potatoes and water. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the potatoes are soft.
Uncover and simmer for a few minutes if you want a thicker sauce. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with steamed rice.

title: Cơm tấm sườn nướng (Broken Rice with Grilled Pork Chop)
ingredients: 2 pork shoulder chops, about 1 inch thick
1 tablespoon neutral oil, for scallion oil
2 tablespoons fish sauce, for dipping sauce
1/4 cup warm water, for dipping sauce
1 clove garlic, minced, for dipping sauce
1 Thai chile, finely sliced, for dipping sauce
instructions: Mix the fish sauce, honey, sugar, lemongrass, garlic, and oil. Coat the pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Combine the rinsed rice and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook over low heat until tender, about 15 minutes; rest covered for 10 minutes.
Stir-fry the scallions in 1 tablespoon oil for about 30 seconds to make scallion oil.
Grill or broil the pork, turning once, until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes per side.
Stir the dipping-sauce fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, warm water, garlic, and chile until the sugar dissolves.
Serve the pork over broken rice with cucumber, scallion oil, and dipping sauce.

title: Phở gà (Chicken Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon fish sauce, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Char the onion and ginger in a dry skillet or under a broiler until blackened in spots.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander in a dry pot until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the water, chicken, charred onion and ginger, and toasted spices. Bring to a gentle simmer and skim the surface.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 45 minutes. Remove the chicken, cool slightly, and pull the meat from the bones.
Return the bones to the pot and simmer the broth for 1 hour. Strain, then season with fish sauce and salt.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package directions and divide among bowls.
