Top the noodles with chicken, sliced onion, and scallions. Pour over hot broth and serve with cilantro, lime, bean sprouts, chiles, and basil.

title: Canh chua cá (Vietnamese Sweet-and-Sour Fish Soup)
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tablespoons chopped rice-paddy herb or cilantro
instructions: Bring the water and tamarind concentrate to a simmer in a pot.
Add the fish sauce, sugar, tomatoes, and pineapple. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked, about 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small skillet and cook the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the okra and celery to the soup and simmer for 3 minutes. Stir in the bean sprouts and fried garlic.
Taste and adjust the sweet, sour, and salty balance with sugar, tamarind, or fish sauce.
Serve hot, topped with rice-paddy herb or cilantro and sliced chile.

title: Bún thịt nướng (Grilled Pork Vermicelli Bowls)
ingredients: 1 Thai chile, finely sliced, for dressing
instructions: Mix the fish sauce, sugar, honey, lemongrass, garlic, and oil. Toss with the pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the vermicelli according to the package directions. Rinse with cool water and drain well.
Stir together the dressing fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, warm water, garlic, and chile until the sugar dissolves.
Grill or broil the pork, turning as needed, until browned and cooked through.
Divide the noodles among bowls. Add cucumber, bean sprouts, mint, cilantro, and grilled pork.
Spoon the dressing over the bowls and finish with roasted peanuts.

title: Bánh xèo (Crispy Vietnamese Turmeric Crepes)
ingredients: 8 ounces small shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tablespoons fish sauce, for dipping sauce
1/4 cup warm water, for dipping sauce
1 clove garlic, minced, for dipping sauce
1 Thai chile, finely sliced, for dipping sauce
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric, salt, coconut milk, and water until smooth. Stir in the scallions and rest the batter for 20 minutes.
Stir the dipping-sauce fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, warm water, garlic, and chile until the sugar dissolves.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a nonstick skillet. Cook some pork and shrimp until nearly done, then add a few onion slices.
Pour in enough batter to make a thin crepe, swirling the pan to coat. Cover and cook over medium heat until the edges crisp.
Scatter mung bean sprouts over one half of the crepe. Fold the other half over and cook uncovered until crisp and golden.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients and oil. Serve with lettuce, mint, cilantro, and dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine the chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes without stirring.
Turn the chicken, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through.
Remove the chicken and simmer the sauce until slightly reduced.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides.
Return the chicken to the sauce and serve with rice.

title: Sinigang na Baboy
ingredients: 2 lb pork ribs, cut into pieces
1 bunch water spinach, cut into lengths
1 packet tamarind soup base, about 1.4 oz
instructions: Put the pork and water in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Add the onion and tomatoes, then simmer for 60 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and fish sauce.
Add the radish and eggplant and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the water spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until just wilted.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot.

title: Pancit Bihon
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water for 8 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the chicken until no longer pink.
Add the garlic and onion and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the carrot, cabbage, broth, soy sauce, fish sauce, and pepper; bring to a simmer.
Add the drained noodles and toss until they absorb the broth and become tender.
Scatter the scallions over the noodles and serve.

title: Laing
instructions: Place the pork belly in a pot over medium heat and cook until its fat renders and the pieces begin to brown.
Add the garlic, onion, and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and fish sauce and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the dried taro leaves without stirring; cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Stir carefully, add the coconut cream and chilies, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Chicken Tinola
ingredients: 1 green papaya, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook, turning, until lightly browned.
Stir in the fish sauce and pepper, then add the water.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the papaya and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the chili leaves and cook for 1 minute before serving.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
instructions: Pound the shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the paste until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry until just softened.
Add the rice, sweet soy sauce, fish sauce, and salt; toss until hot and evenly colored.
Stir in the scallions. Fry the eggs separately and serve on top.

title: Sayur Lodeh
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the shallots, garlic, and chili until softened.
Stir in the coriander and turmeric, then add the lemongrass.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the tofu, green beans, and chayote; simmer until nearly tender, about 8 minutes.
Add the cabbage and coconut milk. Simmer gently until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and palm sugar, and remove the lemongrass before serving.

title: Soto Ayam
instructions: Simmer the chicken in the water until cooked through, about 30 minutes. Lift out the chicken and reserve the broth.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the paste until fragrant, about 4 minutes.
Add the broth, lemongrass, lime leaves, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Shred the chicken and return it to the broth. Simmer for 5 minutes, then remove the lemongrass and lime leaves.
Divide the rice and bean sprouts among bowls, ladle the soup over them, and top with scallions. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Tempeh Orek
ingredients: 14 ounces tempeh, cut into thin strips
instructions: Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the tempeh in batches until golden and crisp. Drain and set aside.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Fry the shallots, garlic, and chilies until fragrant.
Stir in the sweet soy sauce, tamarind water, salt, and water.
Add the tempeh and toss until coated and the sauce has mostly reduced.
Serve warm with rice.

title: Perkedel Kentang
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth.
Heat the neutral oil in a small skillet and sauté the shallots and garlic until soft.
Mix the sautéed aromatics, white pepper, salt, and celery leaves into the potatoes.
Shape the mixture into 8 small, flat patties and let cool until firm.
Dip each patty in beaten egg. Heat the frying oil in a skillet and fry the patties until golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
2 Thai bird’s eye chilies, lightly crushed
12 ounces large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer in a pot.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer until pink and just cooked, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and chili paste.
Remove from the heat and garnish with cilantro before serving.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 ounces firm tofu, cut into small cubes
8 ounces medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tablespoons palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Stir together the fish sauce, tamarind paste, sugar, and rice vinegar.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and cook the tofu until golden.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until nearly cooked through.
Push the ingredients to one side, add the eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the noodles and sauce; toss until the noodles are tender and coated.
Add the bean sprouts and green onions; toss briefly.
Serve topped with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry with Chicken
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
1 teaspoon palm sugar or brown sugar
1 small Thai eggplant, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Stir in half the coconut milk and simmer until fragrant and slightly thickened.
Add the chicken and stir until coated with the curry mixture.
Pour in the stock and remaining coconut milk; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant, fish sauce, and sugar; simmer until the chicken is cooked and the eggplant is tender.
Stir in the bell pepper and basil; cook for 1 minute.
Serve hot with jasmine rice and sliced chili, if desired.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 pound green papaya, peeled and shredded
2 tablespoons palm sugar or brown sugar
1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice; pound lightly to combine.
Add the long beans and tomatoes; gently bruise them with the pestle.
Add the shredded papaya and toss or pound gently until coated.
Taste and adjust the balance of lime, fish sauce, and sugar.
Top with roasted peanuts and serve immediately.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tablespoon palm sugar or brown sugar
1 pound waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Stir in half the coconut milk, then add the beef and coat it in the curry mixture.
Add the stock, fish sauce, tamarind paste, sugar, cinnamon, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and remaining coconut milk; simmer until the beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the peanuts and remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaves.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 300 g medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 stalks lemongrass, trimmed and cut into 5 cm pieces
1 tablespoon Thai roasted chili paste (nam prik pao)
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook until tender.
Add shrimp and cook until pink and just cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce and roasted chili paste.
Remove from the heat, stir in lime juice, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 150 g firm tofu, cut into small cubes
2 green onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Stir together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden.
Add shrimp and garlic; stir-fry until the shrimp are nearly cooked.
Push the ingredients to one side, add the eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add the drained noodles and sauce; toss until the noodles are tender and coated.
Stir in bean sprouts and green onions, then serve with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry Chicken (Gaeng Keow Wan Gai)
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the green curry paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat with the curry paste.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and chicken stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add eggplant, bamboo shoots, and kaffir lime leaves; simmer until the chicken is cooked and the eggplant is tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in Thai basil and red chilies, then serve hot.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 300 g green papaya, peeled and shredded
75 g green beans, cut into 4 cm lengths
instructions: Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add dried shrimp and peanuts; pound lightly to break them up.
Add palm sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and tamarind water; stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add green beans and lightly pound to bruise them.
Add tomatoes and gently press until they release some juice.
Add shredded papaya and toss or pound lightly until coated with dressing.
Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, and sweet before serving.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
ingredients: 700 g beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
300 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the Massaman curry paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir to coat with the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and beef stock; add bay leaves and cinnamon.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 1½ hours until the beef is nearly tender.
Add potatoes and onion; simmer uncovered until the vegetables and beef are tender.
Stir in fish sauce, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and peanuts; simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 300 g large shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
3 Thai bird’s eye chilies, lightly crushed
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until just pink, about 2 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and roasted chili paste.
Remove from the heat, stir in lime juice, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Rice Noodles)
ingredients: 2 green onions, cut into 3 cm pieces
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Mix the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat; add garlic and tofu and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add shrimp and cook until nearly done.
Push everything to one side, add eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add drained noodles and tamarind mixture; toss until the noodles are tender and coated.
Add bean sprouts and green onions; toss briefly.
Serve with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry with Chicken
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until the oil begins to separate.
Add the chicken and stir to coat.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and chicken stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the bell pepper, fish sauce, and palm sugar; simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in basil and kaffir lime leaves, then serve with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 300 g green papaya, peeled and shredded
4 green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
instructions: Pound the chilies and garlic in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the dried shrimp and peanuts; pound lightly.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice; stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the green beans and tomatoes; gently pound to bruise them.
Add the shredded papaya and toss, pounding lightly to mix and soften.
Taste and adjust the balance of lime, fish sauce, and sugar before serving.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
ingredients: 700 g beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until the oil begins to separate.
Add the beef and stir to coat with the curry mixture.
Add the beef stock and remaining coconut milk; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1½ hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the potatoes and onion; simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, until tender.
Stir in fish sauce, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and peanuts; serve with jasmine rice.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, cut into 5 cm pieces and bruised
3 Thai bird's eye chilies, lightly crushed
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and shrimp; simmer until the shrimp are just cooked.
Stir in the fish sauce and roasted chili paste.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lime juice, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Rice Noodles)
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Mix the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok; stir-fry the garlic and tofu for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook until nearly done, then push everything to one side.
Pour the eggs into the wok and scramble; add the noodles, sauce, and dried shrimp.
Stir-fry until the noodles are tender and coated with sauce.
Toss in the bean sprouts and green onions, then serve with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry with Chicken (Kaeng Khiao Wan Gai)
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until the oil begins to separate.
Add the chicken and stir to coat with the curry mixture.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and bamboo shoots; simmer until the chicken and eggplant are cooked.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then stir in the lime leaves and basil.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 300 g green papaya, peeled and shredded
4 long beans, cut into 4 cm pieces

Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sour, and sweet flavors; serve immediately.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 lb waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
2 tbsp palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until fragrant.
Add the beef and turn to coat in the curry mixture.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and beef stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook until the beef is beginning to soften, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and onion; simmer until the beef and potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the peanuts, fish sauce, tamarind, and sugar.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Stir together the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat; cook the tofu and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook until just pink, then push everything to one side.
Pour in the eggs and scramble until set.
Add the noodles and sauce; toss until the noodles are tender and coated.
Fold in the bean sprouts and green onions; serve with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the chili paste and fish sauce.
Add the shrimp and simmer until pink and cooked through.
Remove the pot from the heat; stir in the lime juice and chilies.
Serve topped with cilantro.

title: Green Curry with Chicken
ingredients: 400 g chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until fragrant and slightly thickened.
Add the chicken and stir to coat with the curry mixture.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant, bamboo shoots, fish sauce, sugar, and lime leaves; simmer until the chicken is cooked and eggplant is tender.
Stir in the basil and red chilies, then serve with steamed rice.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 300 g green papaya, peeled and shredded
50 g long beans, cut into 4 cm pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice; pound until the sugar dissolves.
Add the long beans and dried shrimp; lightly pound to bruise the beans.
Add the tomatoes and gently pound until they release some juice.
Add the papaya and toss or pound lightly until coated with the dressing.
Serve topped with roasted peanuts.

title: Massaman Curry with Beef
ingredients: 500 g beef chuck, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir to coat.
Pour in the stock and remaining coconut milk; add the cinnamon and cardamom.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and onion; simmer until tender and the beef is soft.
Stir in the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar; simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with roasted peanuts.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 300 g large shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
3 Thai bird’s eye chilies, lightly crushed
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink and just cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce and chili paste, then remove from the heat.
Add lime juice, taste and adjust seasoning, and garnish with cilantro.

title: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Rice Noodles)
ingredients: 200 g medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
100 g firm tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat; stir-fry garlic and tofu for 1 minute.
Add shrimp and cook until nearly done.
Push everything to one side, pour in eggs, and scramble until set.
Add drained noodles and sauce; toss until the noodles are tender and coated.
Stir in bean sprouts and green onions, then remove from the heat.
Serve topped with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Green Chicken Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan Gai)
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a saucepan and heat over medium heat.
Stir in the curry paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add eggplant, bamboo shoots, and kaffir lime leaves; simmer until the chicken is cooked and eggplant is tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in basil and red chilies, then serve with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 cup long beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until coarsely crushed.
Add palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice; pound until the sugar dissolves.
Add long beans and dried shrimp; lightly pound to bruise the beans.
Add tomatoes and gently crush them to release their juice.
Add shredded papaya and toss or pound lightly until coated with dressing.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with peanuts.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
ingredients: 700 g beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
300 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add curry paste and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef and stir to coat with the paste.
Pour in coconut milk and beef stock; add bay leaves and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add potatoes and onion; simmer uncovered until the beef is tender and potatoes are cooked, about 30 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and peanuts; adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve hot with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken)
ingredients: 2 cups cooked jasmine rice, for serving
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the garlic and chilies; stir-fry briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry, breaking it up, until cooked through.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water.
Add the basil and toss just until wilted.
Serve over jasmine rice, topped with fried eggs if desired.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, cut into short lengths and lightly bruised
instructions: Bring the stock to a boil in a pot.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer until nearly tender.
Add the shrimp and cook until just pink and opaque.
Turn off the heat; stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and roasted chili paste.
Taste and adjust the sour, salty, and spicy balance, then serve topped with cilantro.

title: Gaeng Keow Wan Gai (Green Curry Chicken)
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 small Thai eggplant, cut into wedges
2 cups cooked jasmine rice, for serving
instructions: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a saucepan and heat until it begins to separate.
Stir in the curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and bamboo shoots; simmer until the chicken is cooked and the eggplant is tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then stir in the basil and red chilies.
Serve hot with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tam Thai (Thai Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 200 g green papaya, peeled and shredded
4 green beans, cut into short lengths
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice; pound or stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the green beans and dried shrimp; bruise them lightly with the pestle.
Add the tomatoes and press gently to release some juice.
Add the shredded papaya and toss, pounding lightly to mix without crushing it completely.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with roasted peanuts.

title: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)
ingredients: 150 g boneless chicken, cut into small pieces
instructions: Break up the cold rice so there are no large clumps.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through.
Push the chicken to one side, crack in the egg, and scramble until just set.
Add the rice, soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar; toss over high heat until hot.
Toss in the tomato and scallions, then remove from the heat.
Serve topped with cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Khao Soi Gai (Northern Thai Curry Noodles with Chicken)
ingredients: 1 cup vegetable oil, for frying noodles
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until glossy.
Add chicken thighs and turn to coat in the curry.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and chicken stock; simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Fry a handful of dried noodles in hot vegetable oil until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Boil the remaining dried noodles and fresh noodles separately until tender, then drain.
Divide cooked noodles among bowls and ladle chicken curry over them.
Top with crispy noodles, shallot, pickled mustard greens, and coriander; serve with lime.

title: Nam Prik Ong (Northern Tomato and Pork Relish)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the chilies, garlic, shallots, soybean paste, shrimp paste, and salt into a rough paste.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the paste until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink.
Stir in the tomatoes and fish sauce.
Simmer until the tomatoes soften and the mixture thickens, about 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve with sticky rice, cucumber, and blanched long beans.

title: Sai Ua (Northern Thai Herb Sausage)
ingredients: 500 g ground pork with some fat
instructions: Mix the pork with fish sauce, salt, sugar, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, coriander, spring onion, and curry paste.
Stuff the mixture loosely into the sausage casings and tie the ends.
Prick the sausages lightly to release trapped air.
Grill over medium heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Rest briefly, slice, and serve warm.

title: Kaeng Hang Le (Northern Pork Belly Curry)
ingredients: 700 g pork belly, cut into 3 cm pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the curry paste, curry powder, and turmeric until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and stir to coat evenly.
Stir in the ginger and garlic.
Add fish sauce, tamarind paste, palm sugar, dark soy sauce, and water.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently until the pork is tender, about 1 hour 30 minutes.
Stir in the peanuts and simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Taste and balance the sour, salty, and sweet flavors before serving.

title: Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao (Rice Noodles with Northern Pork and Tomato Broth)
ingredients: 250 g pork ribs, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste, soybean paste, and shrimp paste until fragrant.
Add the pork ribs and ground pork; cook, stirring, until the pork begins to brown.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook until softened.
Pour in the pork stock, season with fish sauce and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer until the ribs are tender, about 45 minutes.
Briefly blanch the rice vermicelli in hot water and drain.
Place noodles in bowls and ladle the hot broth, pork, and tomatoes over them.
Top with bean sprouts, coriander, and spring onion; serve with lime.

title: Som Tam Lao (Isan Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the palm sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, and padaek; pound lightly to combine.
Add the green beans and tomatoes, then bruise them gently with the pestle.
Add the papaya and peanuts; toss and pound lightly until evenly dressed.
Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, sweet, and spicy. Serve right away.

title: Larb Moo (Isan Minced Pork Salad)
instructions: Heat the water in a pan over medium heat.
Add the pork and cook, stirring and breaking it up, until cooked through.
Remove from the heat and stir in the toasted rice powder, lime juice, fish sauce, and chili flakes.
Fold in the shallot, scallions, mint, cilantro, and sawtooth coriander.
Taste and adjust the seasoning; serve warm with sticky rice and raw vegetables.

title: Gai Yang (Isan Grilled Chicken)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 stalks lemongrass, tender lower parts chopped
instructions: Pound the garlic, lemongrass, and white peppercorns into a coarse paste.
Stir in the fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and oil.
Rub the marinade over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and oil the grates lightly.
Grill the chicken, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving with sticky rice and dipping sauce.

title: Tom Saep (Isan Spicy Pork Rib Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork ribs, cut into pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
instructions: Put the ribs and water in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal.
Reduce the heat, cover partly, and simmer until the ribs are tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and chili flakes.
Turn off the heat and mix in the cilantro and sawtooth coriander.
Taste and adjust the sour, salty, and spicy flavors before serving hot.

title: Khao Niao (Isan Sticky Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice several times until the water is mostly clear.
Cover the rice with plenty of water and soak for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and place it in a lined sticky-rice steamer basket.
Steam over boiling water for 20 minutes, then turn the rice over.
Steam for another 10–15 minutes, until tender and glossy.
Transfer to a covered basket or bowl and serve warm.

title: Phuket-Style Hokkien Mee
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok and fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry until lightly browned, then add the shrimp and squid.
Stir in the light soy sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the noodles and cabbage; simmer until the noodles are tender and the seafood is cooked.
Crack in the eggs and stir gently until just set.
Season with white pepper and serve topped with spring onions.

title: Nam Prik Kung Siap (Phuket Dried Shrimp Chili Dip)
ingredients: 150 g long beans, cut into lengths
instructions: Toast the dried shrimp in a dry pan until fragrant, then set aside.
Char the chilies, shallots, and garlic in the pan until softened and lightly blackened.
Pound the shrimp paste, chilies, shallots, and garlic into a coarse paste in a mortar.
Add the dried shrimp and pound until combined but still textured.
Stir in the lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Serve with cucumber and long beans for dipping.

title: Gaeng Som Pla (Southern Sour Fish Curry)
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish, cut into chunks
200 g green papaya, peeled and sliced
8 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the chilies, garlic, shallots, shrimp paste, and turmeric into a smooth curry paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the paste until fragrant.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Stir in the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the papaya and simmer until nearly tender.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked through.
Taste and adjust the sour, salty, and sweet balance before serving.

title: Moo Hong (Phuket Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 800 g pork belly, cut into large chunks
instructions: Pound the garlic, peppercorns, and coriander seeds into a rough paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and brown it on all sides.
Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the star anise, cinnamon, and water; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the pork is tender and the sauce is glossy.
Remove the spices and serve with steamed rice.

title: Oh Aew (Phuket Banana and Jelly Dessert)
instructions: Cook the soaked red beans in fresh water until tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the oh aew jelly powder into 1 litre of water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring, and simmer until the mixture is clear.
Pour into a shallow dish and chill until firmly set, then cut into cubes.
Simmer the palm sugar with 250 ml water until dissolved; cool the syrup.
Divide the jelly, red beans, and banana among serving bowls.
Top with crushed ice and drizzle with palm sugar syrup.

title: Ayutthaya Boat Noodles (Kuay Teow Ruea)
ingredients: 1 cup water spinach, cut into 2-inch lengths
instructions: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package directions, then drain.
Bring the pork stock to a simmer; stir in the soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, soybean paste, and roasted rice.
Add the pork and liver and simmer until just cooked through.
Blanch the bean sprouts and water spinach briefly in the broth, then divide them among serving bowls.
Add noodles to the bowls and ladle in the hot broth, pork, and liver.
Top with fried garlic, cilantro, and Thai basil; serve with lime and chili flakes.

title: Ayutthaya Grilled River Prawns
ingredients: 1 tbsp fish sauce, for dipping sauce
1 tbsp palm sugar, for dipping sauce
1 tbsp chopped shallot, for dipping sauce
1 tsp chopped fresh chili, for dipping sauce
instructions: Pound the cilantro roots and garlic into a rough paste, then mix with the fish sauce, oil, and white pepper.
Cut the prawns lengthwise along the back without separating the halves; remove the vein and brush with the seasoning paste.
Heat a charcoal grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill the prawns shell-side down until the shells turn red and the flesh is nearly opaque, then turn briefly to finish cooking.
Mix the lime juice, tamarind pulp, dipping-sauce fish sauce, palm sugar, shallot, and chili.
Serve the prawns hot with the dipping sauce.

title: Ayutthaya-Style Tamarind Prawn Soup (Tom Yum Goong Nam Sai)
ingredients: 1 lb medium shrimp, peeled and deveined, shells reserved
2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Simmer the shrimp shells in the water for 10 minutes, then strain and return the stock to the pot.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until tender.
Add the shrimp and simmer just until pink and opaque.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, tamarind juice, and crushed chilies.
Top with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Nam Prik Kapi with Fried Mackerel and Vegetables
instructions: Rub the mackerel with salt and brush with oil.
Grill or pan-fry the mackerel over medium heat until cooked through and browned on both sides.
Pound the shrimp paste, chilies, and garlic in a mortar until coarse.
Add the palm sugar, lime juice, and fish sauce; pound and stir until combined.
Arrange the cucumber, long beans, eggplant, and cabbage on a platter.
Serve the nam prik kapi with the mackerel and vegetables.

title: Ayutthaya Boat Noodle-Style Braised Beef with Rice
ingredients: 1½ lb beef shank, cut into 1½-inch pieces
instructions: Rinse the rice, combine it with the water in a saucepan, and cook covered until tender.
Bring the beef stock to a simmer with the star anise, cinnamon, garlic, and cilantro roots.
Add the beef, fish sauce, soy sauce, and palm sugar; cover and simmer gently until the beef is very tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the spices and adjust the broth seasoning to taste.
Divide the rice and bean sprouts among bowls, then spoon over the beef and broth.
Finish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Khao Yam Pak Tai (Southern Thai Rice Salad)
ingredients: 1 cup finely shredded young coconut, toasted
1 cup thinly sliced green beans or winged beans
1/2 cup thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves
1/4 cup toasted dried shrimp, pounded finely
instructions: Warm the budu with palm sugar over low heat until the sugar dissolves; cool and stir in lime juice.
Arrange the rice, vegetables, pomelo, herbs, coconut, and dried shrimp on a platter.
Drizzle with the budu dressing and toss everything together just before eating.

title: Gaeng Som Pla (Southern Sour Fish Curry)
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish, cut into pieces
200 g green papaya, peeled and cut into batons
6 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the dried chilies, fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, and salt into a smooth curry paste.
Bring the water to a boil and stir in the curry paste.
Add the papaya and cauliflower; simmer until nearly tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked; serve hot with rice.

title: Kua Kling Moo (Dry Southern Pork Curry)
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry, breaking it into small pieces.
Cook until the pork is done and the mixture is fairly dry.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in the lime leaves, lemongrass, turmeric, and chilies; cook for 1 minute and serve with rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Gaeng Tai Pla (Southern Fish-Gut Curry)
ingredients: 400 g firm fish fillets, cut into chunks
2 tablespoons tai pla (fermented fish entrail sauce)
instructions: Bring the water and tai pla to a boil, then strain out any solids.
Return the broth to the pot and stir in the curry paste.
Add the pumpkin, eggplant, and bamboo shoots; simmer until nearly tender.
Add the fish and cook gently until just done.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then add the lime leaves and chilies. Serve hot with rice.

title: Khanom Jeen Nam Ya Tai (Rice Noodles with Southern Fish Curry)
ingredients: 500 g fresh khanom jeen rice noodles
100 g long beans, cut into short pieces
instructions: Simmer the mackerel in the water until cooked; lift it out and reserve the broth.
Remove any bones and flake the fish finely.
Bring the broth and coconut milk to a gentle simmer; stir in the curry paste.
Add the flaked fish and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then stir in the lime leaves.
Serve the curry over rice noodles with cucumber, bean sprouts, long beans, and cabbage.

title: Kai Yang Isan-Style Grilled Chicken
instructions: Pound the garlic, lemongrass, peppercorns, and coriander roots into a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and oil.
Rub the marinade all over the chicken and under the skin; cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Grill over medium-low heat, turning occasionally, until cooked through and the juices run clear, about 45–60 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then chop into serving pieces.

title: Larb Moo (Isan Pork Salad)
instructions: Toast uncooked rice in a dry pan until golden, then grind it into a coarse powder if you do not have toasted rice powder ready.
Put the pork and water in a pan and cook over medium heat, breaking up the meat, until fully cooked.
Remove from the heat and stir in fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chili flakes, and toasted rice powder.
Fold in the shallot, scallions, mint, and cilantro.
Taste and adjust with more lime or fish sauce; serve warm with sticky rice and raw vegetables.

title: Som Tam Thai (Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies lightly in a mortar.
Add the dried shrimp and palm sugar; pound until the sugar is mostly dissolved.
Stir in lime juice and fish sauce.
Add the long beans and tomatoes and gently bruise them with the pestle.
Add the papaya and carrot; toss and pound lightly until coated with dressing.
Top with peanuts and serve promptly.

title: Tom Saep (Isan Spicy Pork Rib Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork ribs, cut into serving pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and add the ribs, lemongrass, and galangal.
Skim the surface, lower the heat, and simmer until the ribs are tender, about 1 hour.
Add the kaffir lime leaves and shallots; simmer for 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and roasted chili powder.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then finish with cilantro and sawtooth coriander.

title: Moo Ping (Thai Grilled Pork Skewers)
ingredients: 10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Pound the garlic and white pepper together into a paste.
Mix the paste with coconut milk, fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and oil.
Add the pork and toss to coat; cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Thread the pork onto the soaked skewers.
Grill over medium heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 8–12 minutes.

title: Khao Soi Kai (Northern Thai Chicken Curry Noodles)
ingredients: 1 cup cooked egg noodles, for frying
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook until the oil begins to separate.
Add the chicken and turn to coat in the curry.
Pour in the stock, fish sauce, and palm sugar; simmer until the chicken is tender.
Cook the fresh noodles according to the package directions.
Fry the cooked noodles in a little oil until crisp, then drain.
Serve the curry and chicken over noodles with crisp noodles, shallots, mustard greens, lime, and cilantro.

title: Nam Ngiao (Northern Thai Pork and Tomato Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 250 g pork ribs, cut into small pieces
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and pork ribs; cook, breaking up the ground pork.
Stir in the fermented soybean paste, stock, tomatoes, fish sauce, and sugar.
Simmer until the ribs are tender and the tomatoes have softened.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, then divide among bowls.
Ladle the soup over the noodles and top with bean sprouts, cilantro, scallions, and lime.

title: Sai Ua (Northern Thai Herb Sausage)
ingredients: 500 g ground pork with some fat
1 meter natural pork sausage casing, rinsed
instructions: Mix the pork, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, cilantro stems, scallions, curry paste, fish sauce, salt, and sugar.
Knead the mixture until evenly combined and slightly sticky.
Stuff the mixture loosely into the casing and twist into links.
Grill the sausages over medium heat, turning often, until cooked through and browned.
Rest briefly, then slice and serve.

title: Kaeng Ho (Northern Thai Leftover Curry Stir-Fry)
ingredients: 1 cup cooked green beans, cut into short lengths
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok and fry the curry paste and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add the pork, cabbage, bamboo shoots, and green beans; stir-fry until hot.
Add the glass noodles, fish sauce, and soy sauce.
Toss until the noodles are heated through and have absorbed the seasonings.
Stir in the lime leaves and cilantro, then serve.

title: Nam Prik Ong (Northern Thai Tomato and Pork Relish)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons nam prik ong curry paste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in the tomatoes, fish sauce, and sugar.
Simmer, stirring often, until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens.
Top with cilantro and serve with cucumber, blanched cabbage, and sticky rice.

title: Pad Kra Pao Gai (Thai Basil Chicken)
ingredients: 2 Thai bird’s eye chilies, finely chopped
2 cups cooked jasmine rice, for serving
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat.
Add the garlic and chilies; stir-fry briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry, breaking it into small pieces, until cooked through.
Stir in the oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and water.
Add the basil and toss just until wilted.
Serve over jasmine rice with a fried egg.

title: Tom Kha Gai (Chicken Coconut Soup)
ingredients: 200 g boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
2 Thai bird’s eye chilies, lightly crushed
instructions: Bring the coconut milk and chicken stock to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and mushrooms; simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the fish sauce, sugar, and chilies.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Serve topped with cilantro.

title: Som Tam Thai (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 2 long beans, cut into 2 cm pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the dried shrimp and palm sugar; pound until combined.
Add the long beans and lightly bruise them with the pestle.
Stir in the lime juice and fish sauce.
Add the papaya, carrot, and tomatoes; lightly pound and toss until coated.
Top with peanuts and serve immediately.

title: Gaeng Keow Wan Gai (Green Curry Chicken)
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a pot and heat until it begins to simmer.
Stir in the curry paste and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the paste.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and bamboo shoots; cook until the chicken and eggplant are tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in the basil and lime leaves, then garnish with the red chili and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Khao Tom Moo (Thai Pork Rice Soup)
instructions: Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a pot.
Mix the ground pork with the fish sauce and soy sauce.
Add the pork to the simmering stock in small pieces and cook until done.
Stir in the cooked rice and simmer for 3 minutes.
Heat the oil in a small pan and fry the garlic until golden.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with ginger, green onions, cilantro, fried garlic, and white pepper.

title: Khao Soi Gai (Northern Thai Curry Noodles with Chicken)
ingredients: 1 cup cooked egg noodles, for frying
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Stir in the coconut milk, then add the chicken drumsticks and turn to coat.
Add the stock, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Simmer gently until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Deep-fry the cooked noodles until crisp and drain on paper towels.
Boil the fresh noodles until tender and divide among bowls.
Ladle the curry and chicken over the noodles. Top with crispy noodles, shallots, mustard greens, and cilantro; serve with lime.

title: Nam Prik Ong (Northern Thai Tomato and Pork Relish)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons nam prik ong curry paste
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add the curry paste and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink.
Stir in the tomatoes, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Simmer until thick and the tomatoes break down, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro and serve warm with cucumber and pork rinds.

title: Gaeng Hung Lay (Northern Thai Ginger Pork Curry)
ingredients: 750 grams pork shoulder, cut into 3-centimeter cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the curry paste and curry powder until aromatic.
Add the pork and stir until coated.
Pour in the water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar.
Cover and simmer gently until the pork is very tender, about 1 hour 30 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
Add the ginger, shallots, garlic, and peanuts. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, then serve with steamed rice.

title: Sai Ua (Northern Thai Herb Sausage)
ingredients: 500 grams ground pork, preferably with some fat
instructions: Mix the pork with the curry paste, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, cilantro, fish sauce, salt, and turmeric until evenly combined.
Rinse the casing and fit it over a sausage-stuffing nozzle.
Fill the casing with the pork mixture, taking care not to pack it too tightly, and twist into links.
Grill the sausages over medium-low heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Rest briefly, then slice and serve with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Khao Niao (Northern Thai Steamed Sticky Rice)
instructions: Rinse the sticky rice several times until the water is mostly clear.
Cover the rice with plenty of water and soak for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and place it in a sticky-rice steaming basket.
Set the basket over a pot of boiling water, cover, and steam for 20 minutes.
Turn the rice over and steam for another 10 minutes, until tender and glossy.
Transfer to a covered serving basket and serve warm.

title: Som Tam Isan
ingredients: 1 tablespoon fermented fish sauce (pla ra), optional
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the palm sugar and pound until it dissolves.
Add the long beans and tomatoes; gently bruise them with the pestle.
Stir in the fish sauce, fermented fish sauce, and lime juice.
Add the papaya and peanuts, then pound and toss until evenly dressed.
Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sour, and spicy before serving.

title: Larb Moo
instructions: Toast uncooked sticky rice in a dry pan over medium heat until golden, then grind it into a coarse powder.
Put the pork and water in a pan and cook over medium heat, breaking the meat into small pieces, until just cooked through.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, and toasted rice powder.
Fold in the shallots, mint, cilantro, and scallions.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Gai Yang Isan
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 tablespoon chopped cilantro roots or stems
instructions: Pound the garlic, white peppercorns, and cilantro roots into a rough paste.
Mix the paste with the fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, and oil.
Rub the marinade all over the chicken and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and cook the chicken, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then serve with sticky rice and dipping sauce.

title: Nam Tok Neua
instructions: Rub the steak with the vegetable oil and grill or sear it over high heat to your preferred doneness.
Rest the steak for 10 minutes, then slice it thinly across the grain.
Toss the warm steak with the fish sauce, lime juice, toasted rice powder, and chili flakes.
Fold in the shallots, mint, and cilantro.
Taste and adjust the lime and fish sauce, then serve with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Tom Saep Isan
ingredients: 1 pound pork ribs, cut into small pieces
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into pieces
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a pot and add the pork ribs.
Skim the surface, then add the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Simmer gently until the pork is tender, about 45 to 60 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, and toasted rice powder.
Add the cilantro and sawtooth herb, taste, and adjust the sour and salty balance before serving.

title: Phuket-Style Hokkien Mee (Fried Yellow Noodles)
ingredients: 400 g fresh thick yellow wheat noodles
150 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined
instructions: Blanch the noodles briefly in boiling water, drain, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic and pork belly; stir-fry until the pork is lightly browned.
Add the prawns and stir-fry until just pink.
Push everything to one side, crack in the eggs, and scramble until softly set.
Add the noodles, cabbage, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and stock. Toss until hot and the cabbage is tender.
Season with white pepper and scatter with spring onion before serving.

title: Nam Prik Kung Sia (Phuket Dried-Shrimp Chili Relish)
instructions: Rinse the dried shrimp and pat them dry.
Pound the chilies, garlic, and shallots in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the dried shrimp and pound until broken into small pieces.
Stir in the lime juice, palm sugar, fish sauce, and warm water.
Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, and sweet; serve with raw vegetables and rice.

title: Gaeng Som Pla (Southern Sour Fish Curry)
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish, cut into 4 cm pieces
200 g green papaya, peeled and cut into batons
6 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the dried chilies, bird’s eye chilies, garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste into a smooth curry paste.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot and stir in the curry paste.
Add the papaya and simmer until nearly tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Taste for a sharp, salty, lightly sweet balance and serve hot with rice.

title: Moo Hong (Phuket Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 800 g pork belly, cut into 4 cm pieces
instructions: Pound the garlic, peppercorns, and coriander roots into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and brown it on all sides.
Stir in the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, vinegar, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1½ to 2 hours, turning the pork occasionally, until tender.
Uncover and simmer briefly to thicken the sauce; serve with steamed rice.

title: Oh Aew (Phuket Banana-and-Jelly Dessert)
ingredients: 1 litre water, for cooking the beans
instructions: Whisk the oh-aew powder into 1 litre of water in a saucepan until dissolved.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring, then pour into a shallow dish and chill until set.
Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water, and simmer until tender; drain.
Simmer the palm sugar with 100 ml water until dissolved, then cool the syrup.
Cut the set jelly into small pieces and divide among serving bowls.
Add the red beans, banana, crushed ice, and palm-sugar syrup; serve immediately.

title: Ayutthaya Boat Noodles (Kuay Teow Reua)
instructions: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package directions; drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the garlic and soybean paste until fragrant.
Add the pork stock, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, and palm sugar; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the pork and cook just until tender.
Divide noodles and bean sprouts among bowls, then ladle the hot broth and pork over them.
Finish with ground toasted rice, Thai basil, and fried garlic.

title: Ayutthaya-Style River Prawn Grilled with Chili-Lime Seafood Sauce
ingredients: 2 whole freshwater river prawns, about 12 ounces each
2 Thai bird’s eye chilies, finely chopped
instructions: Rinse the prawns and pat them dry; split them lengthwise through the shell, keeping the halves attached.
Season the cut sides lightly with salt.
Grill the prawns cut-side up over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, then turn and grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir together the lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, chilies, garlic, and cilantro.
Serve the hot prawns with the chili-lime sauce.

title: Gaeng Phet Ped Yang (Red Curry with Roast Duck)
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the red curry paste for 1 minute.
Add 1 cup coconut milk and simmer, stirring, until the oil begins to separate.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the duck and pineapple; simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and kaffir lime leaves and cook for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the chili and Thai basil; serve with steamed rice.

title: Miang Kham (Betel Leaf Bites)
instructions: Simmer the palm sugar, fish sauce, and water in a small pan until syrupy; cool the sauce.
Arrange the betel leaves on a platter with the dried shrimp, peanuts, coconut, ginger, shallot, lime, and chilies.
Spoon a little sauce onto each leaf, fold it into a small parcel, and eat in one bite.

title: Khao Chae (Rice in Jasmine-Scented Water)
instructions: Rinse the rice, then cook it with 1 1/2 cups water until tender.
Spread the rice on a tray and rinse gently with the remaining 4 1/2 cups water to remove excess starch; drain well and chill.
Mix the pork with the rice flour and 1/4 cup water; shape into small balls and fry in the vegetable oil until golden. Drain.
Heat the neutral oil in a pan, add the beaten eggs and fish sauce, and cook as a thin omelet; cool and slice into strips.
Divide the chilled rice among bowls and pour over the chilled jasmine-scented water; add ice cubes.
Serve with the fried pork balls, egg strips, cucumber, and green mango on the side.

title: Hat Yai-Style Fried Chicken
instructions: Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce, white pepper, coriander, garlic, and rice flour; coat the chicken and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and fry the shallots until golden; lift them out and drain.
Fry the chicken in batches until deep golden and cooked through, about 12–15 minutes per batch.
Drain the chicken and serve topped with the fried shallots.

title: Khao Yam Pak Tai (Southern Thai Rice Salad)
ingredients: 1 cup finely shredded young coconut, toasted
1 cup thinly sliced pomelo or tart green mango
1/2 cup finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
1/2 cup dried shrimp, pounded or finely chopped
instructions: Warm the budu with the palm sugar in a small pan until the sugar dissolves; cool and stir in the lime juice.
Arrange the rice, coconut, lemongrass, pomelo, bean sprouts, kaffir lime leaves, dried shrimp, toasted coconut, and long beans in a large bowl.
Pour over the budu dressing and toss well just before serving.

title: Gaeng Som Pla (Southern Sour Fish Curry)
ingredients: 500 g firm white fish, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon fish sauce, plus more to taste
200 g green papaya, peeled and sliced
1 cup green beans, cut into short lengths
6 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the dried and fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, and salt into a smooth curry paste.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot and whisk in the curry paste.
Add the papaya and green beans; simmer until nearly tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the fish and simmer gently until just cooked, about 5 minutes; adjust the sour and salty flavors before serving.

title: Khua Kling Moo (Dry Southern Pork Curry)
ingredients: 1/2 cup thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves
8 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
instructions: Pound the dried and fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, black peppercorns, shrimp paste, and turmeric into a coarse curry paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and stir-fry the paste until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink and the mixture is nearly dry.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then stir-fry until the pork is dry and coated in the paste.
Fold in the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves and cook for 1 minute before serving.

title: Khanom Jeen Nam Ya Tai (Southern Fish Curry with Rice Noodles)
ingredients: 500 g mackerel or other oily fish
8 dried red chilies, soaked and drained
1 cup long beans, cut into short lengths
instructions: Simmer the fish in the water until cooked; lift it out, cool slightly, and remove the bones.
Pound the chilies, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, shrimp paste, and turmeric into a smooth paste.
Flake the fish finely and stir it into the curry paste.
Bring the cooking water and coconut milk to a gentle simmer; add the fish mixture and cook for 15 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, then serve the curry over rice noodles with bean sprouts, cucumber, and long beans.

title: Larb Isan (Spicy Minced Pork Salad)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon roasted chili flakes, or to taste
1 head cabbage, cut into wedges, for serving
1 bunch long beans, cut into lengths, for serving
instructions: Toast the uncooked sticky rice in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, then cool and grind coarsely.
Cook the pork with the water in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until fully cooked.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, and sugar, if using.
Fold in the shallot, scallions, mint, cilantro, and ground toasted rice.
Taste and adjust the lime, fish sauce, or chili, then serve with cabbage and long beans.

title: Tam Mak Hoong (Isan Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 pound green papaya, peeled and shredded
2 fresh Thai bird's-eye chilies, or to taste
1 tablespoon fermented fish sauce (pla ra), optional
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a large mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the long beans and dried shrimp, if using, and lightly pound to bruise them.
Add the fish sauce, fermented fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar; stir to dissolve the sugar.
Add the tomatoes and gently pound until they release some juice.
Add the papaya and carrot, then pound and toss together until well coated and lightly softened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve promptly.

title: Gai Yang Isan (Isan Grilled Chicken)
ingredients: 2 pounds bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro roots or stems
instructions: Pound the garlic, cilantro, and peppercorns into a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with the fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, and oil.
Make a few shallow cuts in the chicken and rub the marinade all over it.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Grill over medium heat, turning often, until browned and cooked through, about 35–45 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Moo Ping (Isan-Style Grilled Pork Skewers)
ingredients: 8 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Stir together the fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, garlic, white pepper, coconut milk, and oil.
Add the pork and toss to coat; cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Thread the pork slices onto the soaked skewers.
Grill over medium heat, turning and brushing with any remaining marinade, until browned and cooked through, about 8–12 minutes.
Serve hot with sticky rice.

title: Tom Saep Isan (Hot and Sour Pork Rib Soup)
ingredients: 2 pounds pork ribs, cut into pieces
2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into lengths
1 teaspoon roasted chili flakes, or to taste
2 tablespoons chopped fresh sawtooth coriander, optional
instructions: Put the ribs and water in a pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal, and shallots.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the ribs are tender, about 1 1/2–2 hours.
Remove the lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves if desired.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, and chili flakes.
Taste and adjust the sour, salty, and spicy balance, then finish with cilantro and sawtooth coriander.

title: Nam Ngiao (Northern Thai Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 250 g pork ribs, cut into small pieces
100 g dried red beans, soaked overnight and boiled until tender
instructions: Soak the vermicelli in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the ground pork and pork ribs; cook until the pork is no longer pink.
Stir in the fermented soybean paste and tomatoes, then cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the stock, boiled beans, fish sauce, and salt; simmer until the ribs are tender, about 45 minutes.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water until tender, then drain and divide among bowls.
Ladle the soup over the noodles and finish with cilantro, green onion, and fried garlic.

title: Sai Ua (Northern Thai Herb Sausage)
ingredients: 500 g ground pork with some fat
instructions: Combine the pork, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, cilantro stems, green onion, curry paste, shrimp paste, fish sauce, and salt.
Mix and knead until the seasonings are evenly distributed and the mixture feels sticky.
Shape the mixture into 8 small sausage patties.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

title: Khao Soi Kai (Chiang Mai Curry Noodles with Chicken)
instructions: Boil half of the fresh egg noodles until tender, then drain and divide between bowls.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the chicken drumsticks and turn to coat with the curry mixture.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock; simmer until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Cook the remaining fresh noodles until tender, then drain.
Ladle the chicken curry over the boiled noodles and top with crispy noodles, shallots, cilantro, pickled mustard greens, and lime.

title: Kaeng Khae Kai (Northern Thai Herb and Chicken Curry)
ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 cup mixed Thai herbs, such as cha-om, basil, and dill
instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until coated and lightly browned.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, long beans, and bamboo shoots; simmer until the chicken and vegetables are cooked.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Stir in the mixed herbs just before serving.

title: Nam Prik Ong (Northern Thai Tomato and Pork Dip)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons nam prik ong curry paste
2 cups blanched vegetables, such as cabbage and long beans
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the ground pork and cook, breaking it into small pieces.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer until soft and saucy, about 12 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in the cilantro and green onion.
Serve warm with cucumber, blanched vegetables, and pork cracklings.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; leave the batter slightly lumpy.
Heat a lightly buttered griddle over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the griddle.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until golden, about 1 minute more.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter with a pastry cutter or fingertips until the mixture has pea-sized pieces.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it into a 1-inch-thick rectangle. Fold it in half and pat it out again twice.
Cut out biscuits with a 2 1/2-inch cutter and place them close together on the baking sheet. Gather scraps and cut more biscuits.
Brush the tops with buttermilk and bake until risen and golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups chopped clams, with their juices
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice and water. Add the potatoes, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams and cream; heat gently without boiling. Season with pepper and salt.
Remove the bay leaf. Serve topped with the bacon and parsley.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl. Add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk, letting excess drip off, then coat thoroughly in the seasoned flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F, filling the pot no more than halfway.
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until deep golden and cooked through, about 12 to 16 minutes per batch. The thickest part should reach 165°F.
Drain on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Classic American Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
3 pounds tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Whisk the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon sugar in a bowl. Cut in the cold butter until pea-sized pieces remain.
Add ice water 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing just until the dough holds together. Divide into two disks, wrap, and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Roll out one disk and fit it into a 9-inch pie plate. Add the apple filling and dot with butter.
Roll out the remaining dough, place it over the filling, and trim and crimp the edges. Cut several vents in the top.
Brush the crust with the egg wash. Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375°F and bake until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles, 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 cups chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; remove and set aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and reserved clam juice.
Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it 1 inch thick.
Cut out biscuits and place them close together on the baking sheet.
Bake until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Midwestern Meatloaf
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a loaf pan.
Mix the beef, breadcrumbs, milk, onion, egg, salt, pepper, and 1/4 cup ketchup in a large bowl.
Shape the mixture into a loaf and place it in the pan.
Stir the remaining ketchup with the brown sugar and mustard.
Spread the ketchup mixture over the loaf.
Bake until cooked through, about 60 to 70 minutes; rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the crust
4 packages (8 ounces each) cream cheese, softened
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and wrap the outside of a 9-inch springform pan in foil.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese and 1 1/4 cups sugar until smooth.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the sour cream, vanilla, and flour.
Pour the filling over the crust and set the pan in a roasting pan; add hot water halfway up the springform pan sides.
Bake until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly, about 70 minutes.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Texas Beef Chili
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened; stir in the garlic.
Add the chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook for 30 seconds.
Return the beef to the pot and stir in the tomatoes, broth, and tomato paste.
Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook over low heat until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Uncover and simmer until the chili reaches your preferred thickness.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; remove and set aside.
Add the onion and celery to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice and water, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and reserved clam juice; simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the milk, cream, clams, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the reserved bacon.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
6 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture has pea-size pieces.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and fold it over itself 3 times.
Pat the dough to 1-inch thickness and cut out biscuits.
Place the biscuits on the baking sheet and bake until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Midwestern Tater Tot Hotdish
ingredients: 1 can (10.5 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Brown the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium heat; drain excess fat.
Stir in the soup, milk, corn, green beans, salt, and pepper.
Spread the mixture in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Arrange the tater tots in an even layer over the beef mixture.
Bake until the tots are crisp and the filling is bubbling, about 40 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheddar and bake until melted, about 5 minutes.

title: Louisiana-Style Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat.
Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, until the roux is deep brown, about 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and sausage and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the chicken, stock, Cajun seasoning, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered until the chicken is tender, about 35 minutes.
Add the okra and simmer until tender, about 10 minutes; remove the bay leaves.
Serve over cooked rice and garnish with parsley.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
ingredients: 4 packages (8 ounces each) cream cheese, softened
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press firmly into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth; add the remaining sugar and flour and beat until combined.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing just until incorporated.
Mix in the sour cream, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly, about 60 to 70 minutes.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups chopped clams, drained, juices reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; remove and set aside.
Cook the onion in the bacon fat until softened, about 5 minutes.
