Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water.
Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the reserved bacon.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently fold it over itself 4 times.
Pat the dough 3/4 inch thick and cut out biscuits.
Place biscuits on the baking sheet and bake until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Kansas City-Style Barbecue Ribs
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F and line a roasting pan with foil.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Rub the spice mixture over the ribs and place them in the pan, meat-side up.
Cover tightly with foil and bake until tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and brush the ribs with barbecue sauce.
Grill the ribs, turning and basting, until glazed and lightly charred, 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Classic American Apple Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and fit one crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Spoon the filling into the crust and dot with butter.
Cover with the second crust, seal and crimp the edges, and cut vents in the top.
Brush the crust with milk and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375°F and bake until golden and bubbling, 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Midwestern Green Bean Casserole
ingredients: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) cut green beans, drained
1 can (10.5 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Stir together the green beans, mushroom soup, milk, pepper, and 2/3 cup fried onions in a casserole dish.
Bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until hot and bubbling.
Stir the casserole and top with the remaining fried onions.
Bake for 5 more minutes, until the onions are golden.

title: Classic Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the griddle
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
Heat a buttered griddle over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the griddle.
Cook until bubbles form on top and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until golden, about 1 minute more.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 (6.5-ounce) cans chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water. Add the potatoes and thyme.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, cream, pepper, and salt. Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Serve topped with the bacon and parsley.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter with a pastry cutter or fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Pat it to about 1 inch thick, fold it in half, and pat it thick again. Repeat once.
Cut out biscuits with a 2 1/2-inch cutter, pressing straight down. Place them close together on the baking sheet.
Brush the tops lightly with buttermilk and bake until tall and golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Texas-Style Beef Chili
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, then set it aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, cayenne, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the broth, tomatoes, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover partially and simmer until the beef is tender and the chili has thickened, about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
6 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Whisk the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon sugar in a bowl. Cut in the cold butter until pea-size pieces remain.
Add the ice water 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing until the dough just holds together. Divide in half, shape into disks, wrap, and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Roll one dough disk into a circle and fit it into a 9-inch pie plate. Add the apple filling and dot with the butter pieces.
Roll out the remaining dough and place it over the filling. Trim and crimp the edges, then cut several vents in the top.
Brush the crust with the egg wash. Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and bake until golden and bubbling, 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool the pie for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk with 1 teaspoon salt and the black pepper in a large bowl.
Add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour with the remaining salt, paprika, and garlic powder in a shallow dish.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dredge each chicken piece in the flour mixture, pressing to coat well.
Fry the chicken in batches for 12 to 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Drain on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice, reserved clam liquid, and water.
Add the potatoes and thyme; bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the clams, cream, salt, and pepper; simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon.

title: Midwestern Beef Meatloaf
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Combine the beef, breadcrumbs, onion, eggs, milk, 1/4 cup ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Mix gently until just combined, then shape into a loaf in a baking dish.
Spread the remaining ketchup over the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 pound dried red kidney beans, rinsed and soaked overnight
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat; brown the sausage, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, sausage, broth, bay leaves, thyme, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender.
Mash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth; remove the bay leaves.
Serve over the cooked rice.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the crust
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
Combine the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press firmly into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese and remaining sugar until smooth.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed after each addition.
Mix in the sour cream, vanilla, and flour until just combined.
Pour the filling over the crust and smooth the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, fold it over itself a few times, and pat it 1 inch thick.
Cut out biscuits, place them on the baking sheet, and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juices reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water, then add the potatoes and reserved clam juices.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon.

title: Kansas City–Style Barbecue Ribs
ingredients: 2 racks pork baby back ribs, about 4 pounds total
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne.
Remove the membrane from the ribs and rub the spice mixture over both sides.
Place the ribs meat-side up on the baking sheet, cover tightly with foil, and bake for 2 1/2 hours.
Heat a grill to medium and brush the ribs with barbecue sauce.
Grill the ribs for 5 to 10 minutes, turning and brushing with more sauce, until lightly charred.

title: Classic Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, about 3 1/2 pounds, cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl; add the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Whisk the flour, paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and cayenne in a shallow dish.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk, let excess drip off, and coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F.
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked to 165°F at the thickest part, about 12 to 16 minutes per batch.
Drain the chicken on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: New York–Style Cheesecake
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the crust
4 packages (8 ounces each) cream cheese, softened
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press the mixture firmly into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then let it cool.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then beat in the remaining sugar, sour cream, vanilla, and flour.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low just until combined.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours before serving.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the griddle
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, and melted butter.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients just until combined; leave some small lumps.
Heat a buttered griddle over medium heat.
Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the griddle and cook until bubbles form on top.
Flip and cook until golden and cooked through; serve warm.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate.
Cook the onion in the bacon fat until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice, reserved clam liquid, and water.
Add the potatoes and thyme; simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams and cream; heat gently without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, top with bacon, and serve.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently pat it 1 inch thick.
Cut out biscuits and place them close together on the baking sheet.
Brush the tops with buttermilk and bake until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Classic Meatloaf
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a loaf pan.
Combine the beef, breadcrumbs, milk, egg, onion, salt, pepper, 1/4 cup ketchup, and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl.
Mix gently and shape the mixture into a loaf in the pan.
Spread the remaining ketchup over the top.
Bake until the center reaches 160°F, about 1 hour.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Apple Pie
ingredients: 6 cups peeled and sliced tart apples
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with one crust.
Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Pile the apple filling into the crust and dot with butter.
Cover with the second crust, seal the edges, and cut several vents in the top.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375°F and bake until golden and bubbling, 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool before slicing.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; leave some small lumps.
Heat a buttered skillet over medium heat. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake into the pan.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until golden, about 1 minute more.
Serve warm.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups chopped clams, drained, with juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water. Add the potatoes and thyme.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, pepper, salt, and reserved clam juice to taste. Heat gently without boiling for 5 minutes.
Serve topped with the cooked bacon.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl. Add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne in a shallow dish.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk, letting excess drip off, and coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and cooked through, about 15 to 20 minutes per batch.
Drain on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Classic Macaroni and Cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender. Drain.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook, stirring, until thickened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the dry mustard, salt, pepper, and cheddar until the cheese melts.
Fold in the macaroni and transfer the mixture to the prepared dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with 1 tablespoon melted butter and sprinkle over the macaroni.
Bake until bubbling and golden on top, about 20 minutes.

title: Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
1 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Whisk 2 1/2 cups flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon granulated sugar in a bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture has pea-size pieces. Stir in ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until the dough holds together.
Divide the dough in half, shape into disks, wrap, and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Roll out one disk and line a 9-inch pie plate. Add the apple filling and dot with 1 tablespoon butter.
Roll out the second disk, place it over the filling, and crimp the edges. Cut several vents in the top crust.
Brush the crust with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles, 35 to 45 minutes. Cool before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; remove and set aside.

Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and clam juice; bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the reserved bacon.

title: Classic American Apple Pie

title: Texas Beef Chili

instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened; stir in the garlic.
Add the chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste, beef broth, diced tomatoes, and browned beef.
Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook over low heat until the beef is tender and the chili thickens, about 2 hours.

Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Roll out one dough disk and fit it into a 9-inch pie plate; add the apple filling and dot with butter.
Roll out the remaining dough, place it over the filling, and crimp the edges; cut several vents in the top.
Brush the crust with beaten egg and bake for 20 minutes.
Reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and bake until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool the pie before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the butter, onion, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice, water, and reserved clam liquid.
Add the potatoes, salt, and pepper; bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams and cream; simmer gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Serve topped with bacon and parsley.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
6 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently pat it into a 1-inch-thick rectangle; fold it in half twice, patting it back down each time.
Cut out biscuits with a 2 1/2-inch cutter and place them close together on the baking sheet.
Brush the tops with buttermilk and bake until golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Texas-Style Beef Chili
ingredients: 3 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes; stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Return the beef to the pot and add the broth and tomatoes; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer until the beef is tender, about 2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Whisk the masa harina with the cold water, stir it into the chili, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.

title: Midwestern Green Bean Casserole
ingredients: 1 pound fresh green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 can (10.5 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil; cook the green beans until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes, then drain.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden, about 8 minutes.
Whisk the soup, milk, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Stir in the green beans, cooked onion, and 2/3 cup of the fried onions.
Spread the mixture in the baking dish and bake for 25 minutes.
Scatter the remaining fried onions over the top and bake until golden, about 5 minutes more.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 1 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
3 pounds Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Whisk the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon granulated sugar in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until pea-size pieces remain; add ice water 1 tablespoon at a time until the dough holds together.
Divide the dough into two disks, wrap, and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F and place a baking sheet on the lower rack.
Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Roll out one dough disk and fit it into a 9-inch pie plate; add the apple filling and dot with butter.
Roll out the second disk, lay it over the filling, and trim and crimp the edges; cut several vents in the top.
Brush the crust with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake on the heated sheet for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 375°F and bake until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles, 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool the pie for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; leave some lumps.
Heat a buttered skillet over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the skillet.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until golden, about 1 minute more.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, fold it over itself 3 times, and pat it 3/4 inch thick.
Cut into rounds and place on a baking sheet, touching slightly. Brush the tops with buttermilk.
Bake until risen and golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups chopped clams, with their juice
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice and water. Add the potatoes, thyme, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams and cream and warm gently for 3 to 5 minutes; do not boil.
Season with salt and serve topped with bacon and parsley.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl. Add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whisk the flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne in a shallow dish.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk, let excess drip off, and coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and cooked through, 15 to 18 minutes. Keep the oil near 325°F.
Transfer to a wire rack and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
6 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Whisk the flour, salt, and 1 teaspoon sugar in a bowl. Cut in the cold butter until pea-sized pieces remain.
Add the ice water a tablespoon at a time, tossing until the dough just holds together. Divide in half, shape into disks, wrap, and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the apples with 3/4 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Roll out one disk and line a 9-inch pie plate. Add the apple filling and dot with butter.
Roll out the second disk, place it over the filling, and seal and crimp the edges. Cut several vents in the top.
Brush the crust with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake until golden and bubbling, 35 to 45 minutes. Cool before slicing.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake into the skillet.
Cook until bubbles form on top and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook until golden, about 1 minute more.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
3/4 cup cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter with a pastry cutter or fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface, gently pat it to 1-inch thickness, and fold it in half twice.
Pat the dough to 1-inch thickness and cut out biscuits without twisting the cutter.
Place the biscuits close together on the baking sheet and brush the tops with buttermilk.
Bake until risen and golden, 12 to 15 minutes.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 (6.5-ounce) cans chopped clams, drained, juices reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and thyme. Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, reserved clam juices, cream, pepper, and salt. Heat gently without boiling, until warmed through.
Stir in the parsley and reserved bacon, then serve.

title: Classic Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients: 3 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese, divided
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 2-quart baking dish.
Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender. Drain.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook, stirring, until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the dry mustard, salt, pepper, and 2 1/2 cups cheddar until melted.
Add the macaroni and stir to coat. Transfer the mixture to the baking dish.
Combine the breadcrumbs with 1 tablespoon melted butter and sprinkle over the macaroni with the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar.
Bake until bubbling and golden, about 20 minutes.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the crust
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar, for the filling
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Wrap the outside of a 9-inch springform pan with two layers of foil.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar. Press firmly into the bottom of the pan.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then set aside to cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese and 1 1/4 cups sugar until smooth. Mix in the sour cream.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low just until incorporated. Mix in the vanilla, flour, and lemon juice.
Pour the filling over the crust. Set the pan in a larger roasting pan and add hot water to reach halfway up its sides.
Bake until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly, about 65 to 75 minutes.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake rest inside for 1 hour.
Remove the pan from the water bath, cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours before serving.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juice reserved
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the butter, onion, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice, reserved clam juice, and water.
Add the potatoes and bring to a simmer; cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, cream, salt, and pepper; heat gently without boiling.
Serve topped with the bacon and parsley.

title: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl; add the chicken and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Combine the flour, paprika, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and cayenne in a shallow dish.
Remove each chicken piece from the buttermilk, letting excess drip off, and coat thoroughly in the seasoned flour.
Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 325°F (163°C).
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked to 165°F (74°C), about 12–18 minutes depending on the piece.
Drain on a wire rack and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Texas-Style Beef Chili
ingredients: 2 1/2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches; transfer to a plate.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes; stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano, and cayenne.
Return the beef to the pot and add the broth, tomatoes, tomato paste, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook over low heat until the beef is tender, about 2 hours.
Whisk the masa harina with the cold water and stir it into the chili.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, then taste and adjust the seasoning.

title: Kansas City-Style Barbecue Ribs
ingredients: 2 racks (about 4 pounds total) pork baby back ribs
instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C) and line a baking sheet with foil.
Remove the thin membrane from the bone side of each rack.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne; rub over both sides of the ribs.
Place the ribs meat-side up on the baking sheet, cover tightly with foil, and bake until tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, whisk the ketchup, vinegar, molasses, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce in a saucepan.
Simmer the sauce over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Heat a grill to medium or set the oven to broil; brush the ribs generously with sauce and cook until lightly charred, turning once.
Brush with more sauce and rest for 10 minutes before cutting into portions.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
ingredients: 4 packages (8 ounces each) cream cheese, softened
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (163°C) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press firmly into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth; gradually beat in the remaining 1 1/4 cups sugar and the flour.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed after each addition.
Mix in the sour cream, vanilla, and lemon zest until just combined.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly, about 60–70 minutes.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours before serving.

title: Salmon Chowder
ingredients: 4 cups fish stock or clam juice
1 pound skinless salmon, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock, then add the potatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the milk and cream. Add the salmon, salt, and pepper, and simmer gently until the salmon is just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the dill, and serve.

title: Dungeness Crab Louie
ingredients: 1 pound cooked Dungeness crab meat, picked over
instructions: Whisk the mayonnaise, chili sauce, lemon juice, horseradish, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Divide the lettuce among four plates.
Top each plate with crab, tomatoes, avocado, eggs, and cucumber.
Spoon the dressing over the salads and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Marionberry Cobbler
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Place the marionberries in a 9-inch baking dish and toss with 1/4 cup sugar and the lemon juice.
Whisk the flour, remaining 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the milk, melted butter, and vanilla until just combined.
Spoon the batter evenly over the berries.
Bake until the topping is golden and the filling bubbles, 35 to 40 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Dutch Baby with Hood River Apples
ingredients: 3/4 cup whole milk, at room temperature
2 medium apples, cored and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, granulated sugar, and salt until smooth.

Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add the apples, brown sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice and cook until just tender, about 5 minutes. Transfer the apples to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter to the skillet and place it in the oven until the butter melts and foams.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet and bake until puffed and golden, 18 to 20 minutes.
Top with the apples, dust with powdered sugar, and serve immediately.

title: Oregon Hazelnut-Crusted Steelhead
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds steelhead trout fillet, skin on
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix the hazelnuts, panko, parsley, lemon zest, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Place the steelhead skin-side down on the baking sheet and spread the Dijon mustard over the flesh.
Press the hazelnut mixture onto the mustard-coated fish and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake until the fish flakes easily and the crust is golden, 12 to 16 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

title: New York–Style Bagels
ingredients: 1 tablespoon baking soda, for boiling water
instructions: Mix the flour, malt syrup, yeast, salt, and warm water until a firm dough forms.
Knead for 10 minutes, cover, and let rise until slightly puffy, about 1 hour.
Divide into 8 pieces, shape each into a ring, and let rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F and bring a wide pot of water to a boil; stir in the baking soda.
Boil the bagels for 30 seconds per side, then drain and add sesame seeds if using.
Bake on a parchment-lined sheet until deeply golden, about 20 minutes.

title: New York Deli Chopped Liver
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs, cool them, and peel them.
Heat the schmaltz in a skillet and cook the onions over medium-low heat until deeply golden, about 25 minutes; set aside.
Cook the livers in the same skillet until browned outside and just cooked through, about 4 minutes per side; cool slightly.
Pulse the livers, onions, eggs, salt, and pepper in a food processor until coarsely chopped, adding stock if needed.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve with rye bread.

title: Manhattan Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 cans (6.5 ounces each) chopped clams, drained, juices reserved
instructions: Heat the oil in a soup pot and cook the onion, celery, and carrot until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, clam juice, water, potatoes, reserved clam juices, thyme, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the clams and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with parsley.

title: New York Knish
ingredients: ¼ cup neutral oil, plus more for brushing
2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Mix the flour and salt; stir in the water, oil, and vinegar to form a soft dough.
Knead briefly, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash.
Cook the onions in schmaltz until golden, then fold them into the potatoes with the pepper.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll the dough thinly into a rectangle, spread the filling along one long edge, and roll it up around the filling.
Cut into 8 portions, pinch the ends closed, and place seam-side down on the sheet.
Brush with beaten egg and bake until golden, about 30 minutes.

title: New York–Style Cheesecake
ingredients: ¼ cup granulated sugar, for the crust
4 packages (8 ounces each) cream cheese, softened
1½ cups granulated sugar, for the filling
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and wrap the outside of a 9-inch springform pan in foil.
Combine the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and ¼ cup sugar; press firmly into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then let it cool.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth; mix in the remaining sugar and flour.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed, then mix in the sour cream, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Pour the filling over the crust and set the pan in a roasting pan; add hot water to come halfway up the springform pan.
Bake until the edges are set and the center still wobbles slightly, about 75 minutes.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the cake cool inside for 1 hour; chill for at least 6 hours before serving.

title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl, add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Combine the flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Lift each chicken piece from the buttermilk, let excess drip off, and dredge in the seasoned flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet to 325°F.
Fry the chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked to 165°F at the thickest part, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain on a wire rack and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Shrimp and Grits
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Bring the water, milk, and salt to a simmer in a saucepan.
Whisk in the grits, reduce the heat to low, and cook, stirring often, until creamy and tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Stir the butter and cheddar into the grits and keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving 1 tablespoon of drippings in the skillet.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook until pink and just opaque, about 2 minutes per side.
Stir in the scallions, lemon juice, and black pepper, then spoon the shrimp and bacon over the grits.

title: Southern Collard Greens with Smoked Ham Hock
ingredients: 2 pounds collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Rinse the collard greens well and drain.
Put the ham hock, onion, garlic, and chicken broth in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the collard greens, vinegar, red pepper flakes, and salt.
Cover and simmer until the greens are tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the ham hock, pull off the meat, chop it, and stir it back into the greens before serving.

title: Skillet Cornbread
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and place a 10-inch cast-iron skillet inside to heat.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg, buttermilk, and melted butter in a separate bowl.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients just until combined.
Carefully add the bacon drippings to the hot skillet and swirl to coat.
Pour in the batter and bake until golden and a toothpick comes out clean, about 18 to 22 minutes.

title: Peach Cobbler
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the peaches with 1/4 cup sugar, lemon juice, and cinnamon, then spread them in a baking dish.
Whisk the flour, remaining 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the milk until the batter is just combined.
Pour the melted butter over the peaches, then spoon the batter evenly on top without stirring.
Bake until the topping is golden and the peaches are bubbling, about 40 to 45 minutes.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
2 cups chopped clams, with their liquor
instructions: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice and water, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and thyme; simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams and their liquor, milk, cream, pepper, and salt. Heat gently without boiling until steaming hot.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon.

title: Maple Baked Beans
ingredients: 1 pound dried navy beans, picked over and rinsed
4 ounces salt pork, cut into small pieces
instructions: Cover the beans with 6 cups of water and soak overnight.
Drain the beans, put them in a pot, and add the remaining 2 cups water and baking soda.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the beans are just tender, about 45 minutes; drain and reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Place the onion in a bean pot or covered baking dish. Add the beans, maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, vinegar, salt, pepper, and salt pork.
Pour in the reserved cooking liquid, cover, and bake for 4 hours, checking occasionally and adding hot water if the beans look dry.
Uncover for the final 30 minutes, until the top is browned and the sauce is thick.

title: Yankee Pot Roast
ingredients: 1 large yellow onion, cut into wedges
4 medium carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Pat the roast dry and season it with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the roast on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the broth, tomato paste, and thyme.
Return the roast to the pot, cover, and bake for 2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes around the roast. Cover and bake until the meat and vegetables are tender, about 1 hour more.
Transfer the roast and vegetables to a platter and keep warm.
Whisk the flour and cold water together, then stir the mixture into the pot juices. Simmer on the stovetop until thickened, about 3 minutes; serve as gravy.

title: Johnnycakes
ingredients: 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for the griddle
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal, salt, and sugar in a heatproof bowl.
Stir in the boiling water and let the mixture stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in the milk until the batter is thick but spoonable.
Heat a buttered griddle over medium heat.
Spoon the batter onto the griddle to make small cakes and cook until the edges look set, about 4 minutes.
Flip and cook until browned and cooked through, about 3 minutes more. Serve warm with butter or maple syrup.

title: Blueberry Buckle
ingredients: 1/4 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease an 8-inch square baking pan.
Whisk together 2 cups flour, the baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, cream the softened butter and granulated sugar until fluffy. Beat in the egg.
Add the flour mixture in three additions, alternating with the milk, mixing just until combined.
Fold in the blueberries and spread the batter in the prepared pan.
Mix the brown sugar, remaining 1/3 cup flour, and cinnamon. Cut in the cold butter until crumbly, then sprinkle over the batter.
Bake until golden and a tester inserted in the center comes out clean, 40 to 45 minutes. Cool before serving.

title: Midwestern Beef Pot Roast
ingredients: 1 large yellow onion, cut into wedges
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Season the roast with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the roast on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the broth and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up browned bits.
Return the roast to the pot and add the thyme. Cover and roast for 2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes. Cover and cook until the beef is fork-tender, about 1 hour more.
Remove the thyme sprigs and serve the beef with the vegetables and cooking juices.

title: Tater Tot Hotdish
ingredients: 1 can (10.5 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Brown the ground beef and onion in a skillet over medium heat. Drain excess fat and season with salt and pepper.
Stir together the soup and milk, then mix with the green beans and cooked beef.
Spread the mixture in the baking dish and sprinkle with cheddar.
Arrange the tater tots in an even layer on top.
Bake until bubbling and the tots are golden, about 45 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Wisconsin Beer-Battered Fried Cheese Curds
instructions: Pat the cheese curds dry and let them sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Whisk 3/4 cup flour, beer, egg, baking powder, and salt in a bowl until just combined.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 375°F.
Toss the curds with the remaining 1/4 cup flour, then dip them in the batter in small batches.
Fry the curds until lightly golden, about 1 minute per batch. Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
Serve hot.

title: Swedish Meatballs with Egg Noodles
instructions: Combine the breadcrumbs and milk in a large bowl and let stand for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, pork, egg, allspice, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix gently and shape into 1-inch meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in a large skillet over medium heat, turning as needed. Transfer them to a plate.
Cook the egg noodles in salted water according to the package directions, then drain.
Melt the butter in the skillet. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and cream. Simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer until cooked through, about 8 minutes. Serve over the noodles.

title: Dutch Apple Pie
ingredients: 6 medium tart apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Toss the apples with granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, and lemon juice. Spoon into the crust.
Mix the topping flour and brown sugar in a bowl. Cut in the cold butter until coarse crumbs form.
Sprinkle the topping evenly over the apples.
Bake until the apples are tender and the topping is golden, about 50 minutes. Cover the crust edges with foil if they brown too quickly.
Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

title: Texas-Style Chili con Carne
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, then set it aside.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, chile powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the broth and crushed tomatoes, bring to a simmer, and cover.
Cook gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender.
Whisk the masa harina with the cold water, stir it into the chili, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until thickened.

title: Chicken-Fried Steak with Cream Gravy
ingredients: 4 beef cube steaks, about 6 ounces each
1/2 cup vegetable oil, plus more as needed
instructions: Place the cube steaks between sheets of parchment and pound them to about 1/4 inch thick.
Combine 1 1/2 cups flour, 1 teaspoon salt, pepper, and paprika in a shallow dish. In another dish, whisk the eggs with 1/2 cup milk.
Dredge each steak in the seasoned flour, dip it in the egg mixture, then dredge it in flour again.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the steaks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; keep warm.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of drippings. Whisk in 2 tablespoons flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in 2 cups milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick, then season with salt and pepper and serve over the steaks.

title: Texas Barbecue Beef Brisket
ingredients: 1 cup oak or pecan wood chunks
instructions: Trim the brisket, leaving about 1/4 inch of fat on top.
Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Rub the mixture evenly over the brisket.
Heat a smoker to 250°F and add the wood chunks.
Place the brisket fat-side up in the smoker. Cook until the thickest part reaches about 165°F, roughly 6 to 8 hours.
Wrap the brisket tightly in butcher paper and return it to the smoker.
Continue cooking until the thickest part is tender when probed, usually at 200 to 205°F.
Rest the wrapped brisket in a cooler or warm oven for at least 1 hour. Slice across the grain to serve.

title: Texas Pinto Beans
ingredients: 1 pound dried pinto beans, rinsed and picked over
8 cups water, plus more as needed
instructions: Put the beans in a large pot and cover with the water. Soak overnight, then drain.
Return the beans to the pot. Add 8 cups fresh water, the onion, garlic, and ham hock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed.
When the beans are tender, remove the ham hock and pull off any meat. Stir the meat back into the pot.
Season with salt, pepper, and cumin. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Texas Buttermilk Cornbread
ingredients: 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted, plus 1 tablespoon for the skillet
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put a 10-inch cast-iron skillet in the oven with 1 tablespoon butter.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the egg, buttermilk, and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined.
Carefully swirl the hot skillet so the butter coats the bottom. Pour in the batter.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: California Fish Tacos
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, such as rockfish or cod, cut into strips
instructions: Toss the fish with cumin, chili powder, salt, and olive oil.
Cook the fish in a hot skillet for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until opaque and flaky.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet.
Fill each tortilla with fish, cabbage, and cilantro; drizzle with crema and serve with lime wedges.

title: California-Style Cobb Salad
instructions: Arrange the romaine on a large platter.
Top with rows of chicken, avocado, tomatoes, bacon, eggs, and blue cheese.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper together.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad just before serving.

title: Sonoma Chicken with Garlic and Rosemary
ingredients: 6 garlic cloves, peeled and lightly crushed
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the chicken skin-side down and cook until deeply browned, about 7 minutes; turn and brown the other side for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, rosemary, wine, and broth to the skillet.
Bake at 400°F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest part.

title: Santa Maria-Style Tri-Tip
instructions: Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, and oregano; rub the mixture all over the tri-tip.
Let the meat stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high and brush the grates with olive oil.
Grill the tri-tip, turning occasionally, until browned and an instant-read thermometer registers 130°F for medium-rare, about 25 to 35 minutes.
Rest the roast for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.

title: California Avocado and Citrus Salad
ingredients: 2 ripe California avocados, peeled and sliced
instructions: Arrange the arugula on a serving platter.
Top with the avocado, orange segments, and red onion.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper together.
Spoon the dressing over the salad and serve immediately.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, until the roux is a deep brown, about 25 to 35 minutes.
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, and celery. Cook until softened, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the sausage and chicken; stir to coat. Gradually pour in the stock, stirring to dissolve the roux.
Add the bay leaves, thyme, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the scallions and parsley, taste and adjust the seasoning, and serve over rice.

title: Red Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 pound dried red kidney beans, rinsed and picked over
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Soak the beans in the water overnight, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and sausage and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, ham hock, bay leaves, thyme, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Pour in 8 cups fresh water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partially covered, until the beans are tender, about 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Stir occasionally and add water if needed.
Mash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken the mixture. Remove the bay leaves and ham hock; shred any meat from the hock and return it to the pot.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve over rice topped with scallions.

title: Crawfish Étouffée
ingredients: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 pounds peeled crawfish tails, thawed and drained
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring often, until the roux is golden brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery. Cook until softened, about 7 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Whisk in the seafood stock, tomato paste, paprika, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the crawfish tails and simmer gently until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the scallions, parsley, and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve over rice.

title: Jambalaya
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
1 can (14.5 ounces) diced tomatoes, with juices
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage, then transfer it to a plate.
Brown the chicken in the pot, then transfer it to the plate with the sausage.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery. Cook until softened, about 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic.
Stir in the rice and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, thyme, paprika, cayenne, salt, and black pepper.
Return the sausage and chicken to the pot. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce the heat to low.
Cook without lifting the lid until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, fluff with a fork, and top with scallions.

title: Shrimp Creole
ingredients: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, seafood stock, bay leaf, paprika, thyme, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens, about 25 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer until pink and just cooked through, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the parsley, scallions, and lemon juice; taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve over rice.

title: Dungeness Crab Cakes
ingredients: 1 pound cooked Dungeness crab meat, picked over for shell
1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, plus 1/2 cup for coating
instructions: Gently mix the crab, egg, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, 1/2 cup panko, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Shape into 8 patties and coat lightly with the remaining panko.
Chill the patties for 20 minutes.
Heat the butter and oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and heated through.

title: Salmon with Maple-Mustard Glaze
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the maple syrup, mustard, soy sauce, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Place the salmon skin-side down on the baking sheet and season with salt and pepper.
Brush the glaze over the salmon.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.

title: Marionberry Cobbler
ingredients: 4 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter an 8-inch baking dish.
Toss the berries with 1/2 cup sugar, lemon juice, and cornstarch, then spread in the dish.
Whisk the flour, remaining 1/4 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Rub the butter into the flour mixture until crumbly, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the berries, leaving small gaps.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the topping is golden and the filling bubbles.

title: Oregon Hazelnut Oatmeal Cookies
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and both sugars until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt, then stir into the butter mixture.
Fold in the oats and hazelnuts.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the sheets and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden.

title: Pacific Northwest Salmon Chowder
ingredients: 4 cups fish stock or low-sodium chicken broth
1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 pound skinless salmon, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and celery and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock, then add the potatoes, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the salmon and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until just cooked.
Stir in the milk, cream, salt, and pepper and warm without boiling.
Remove the bay leaf and stir in the dill before serving.

title: New York Deli-Style Matzo Ball Soup
instructions: Whisk the eggs, schmaltz, water, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Stir in the matzo meal, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Bring the broth, carrots, and celery to a simmer in a large pot.
With damp hands, shape the chilled mixture into 1-inch balls.
Drop the matzo balls into the simmering broth, cover, and cook gently for 30 minutes.
Stir in the dill and serve hot.

title: New York-Style Cheesecake
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, for the crust
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, for the filling
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix the graham crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar, then press firmly into the pan bottom.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes and let it cool slightly.
Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then mix in the remaining sugar and flour.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the sour cream, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Pour the filling over the crust and bake for 65 to 75 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off the oven, crack the door, and leave the cake inside for 1 hour.
Cool completely, then chill for at least 6 hours before slicing.

title: New York Deli Potato Salad
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until tender but not falling apart, then drain.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the warm potatoes, celery, and red onion, and fold gently to coat.
Stir in the dill and chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

title: New York-Style Black-and-White Cookies
ingredients: 2 tablespoons boiling water, plus more as needed
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and granulated sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the dry ingredients in batches, alternating with the sour cream.
Drop 1/4-cup portions of dough onto the sheets, spacing them apart, and flatten each slightly.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until the bottoms are lightly golden, then cool completely.
Whisk the confectioners' sugar, boiling water, and corn syrup into a smooth glaze, adding a little more water if needed.
Spread glaze over half of each cookie; whisk the cocoa into the remaining glaze and spread it over the other halves.
Let the icing set before serving.

title: New York Diner-Style Chopped Cheese
ingredients: 4 hero rolls or soft sub rolls
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until softened.
Add the ground beef, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking it into small pieces, until browned and cooked through.
Divide the beef into four portions in the skillet and top each portion with a slice of American cheese.
Stir each portion until the cheese melts through the beef.
Spread mayonnaise inside the rolls and fill them with the cheesy beef, tomato, and lettuce.
Serve hot.

title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk and hot sauce in a large bowl, add the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Whisk the flour, paprika, garlic powder, pepper, and salt in a shallow dish.
Let excess buttermilk drip from each chicken piece, then dredge it in the seasoned flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F.
Fry the chicken in batches until golden and cooked through, about 12 to 16 minutes per batch; drain on a wire rack.

title: Shrimp and Grits
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a saucepan, then slowly whisk in the grits.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook, stirring often, until tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Stir the cheese and 1 tablespoon of butter into the grits; keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp, then transfer it to a plate and leave 1 tablespoon of drippings in the skillet.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook until pink, about 2 minutes per side.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds; add the lemon juice, remaining butter, and bacon.
Spoon the shrimp mixture over the grits and garnish with green onions.

title: Southern Collard Greens
ingredients: 2 pounds collard greens, stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes; stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the collard greens in batches, stirring until they begin to wilt.
Pour in the broth and stir in the vinegar, sugar, red pepper flakes, and black pepper.
Cover and simmer gently until the greens are tender, about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

title: Buttermilk Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture has pea-size pieces.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface, fold it over itself 4 times, and pat it to 1-inch thickness.
Cut out biscuits and place them close together on the baking sheet.
Bake until risen and golden, about 12 to 15 minutes.

title: Pecan Pie
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie plate.
Whisk the corn syrup, brown sugar, eggs, melted butter, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Arrange the pecans in the pie crust and pour the filling over them.
Bake until the center is just set, about 50 to 60 minutes; cover the crust edges with foil if they brown too quickly.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 cups peeled russet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
2 cups chopped clams, with their juices
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; transfer it to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.
Add the onion and celery and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the clam juice, then add the potatoes, bay leaf, and thyme.
Simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in the clams, milk, and cream; heat gently without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and serve topped with bacon.

title: New England Baked Beans
ingredients: 8 cups water, plus more for soaking
4 ounces salt pork, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Rinse the beans and soak them overnight in 8 cups of water.
Drain the beans, place them in a pot, cover with fresh water, and add the baking soda.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the beans are just tender, about 30 minutes; drain, reserving the cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 300°F. Place the onion in the bottom of a bean pot or covered Dutch oven.
Stir the molasses, brown sugar, mustard, salt, and pepper into 2 cups of boiling water.
Add the beans and salt pork to the pot, then pour in the molasses mixture; add enough reserved bean liquid to just cover the beans.
Cover and bake for 5 hours, checking occasionally and adding reserved liquid if the beans look dry.
Uncover for the final 30 minutes to brown the top.

title: Johnnycakes
ingredients: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, plus more for the griddle
instructions: Whisk the cornmeal and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Stir in the boiling water and butter, then let the mixture stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in the milk to make a thick batter.
Heat a buttered griddle over medium heat.
Drop the batter onto the griddle in 2-tablespoon portions and spread each into a small round.
Cook until the edges look dry and the underside is golden, about 4 minutes; flip and cook until golden on the other side.

title: New England Boiled Dinner
ingredients: 1 pound carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 1/2 pounds small Yukon Gold potatoes, halved
1 small green cabbage, cut into 6 wedges
instructions: Place the corned beef in a large pot and add the water, bay leaf, peppercorns, and onion.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then cover and simmer gently until nearly tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage wedges and cook until the vegetables and beef are tender, about 15 minutes more.
Slice the corned beef across the grain and serve with the vegetables and cooking broth.

title: Blueberry Grunt
ingredients: 3 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
instructions: Combine the blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar, water, and lemon juice in a wide covered skillet.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk the flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then stir in the milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the simmering berries.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through, about 15 minutes; do not lift the lid while they cook.
Serve warm with cream or vanilla ice cream.

title: Midwestern Beef and Vegetable Pot Roast
ingredients: 1 large yellow onion, cut into wedges
4 medium russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Season the roast with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the roast on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion and carrots to the pot and cook for 3 minutes.
Return the roast to the pot. Add the broth and thyme, then cover and bake for 2 hours.
Add the potatoes, cover, and bake until the beef and vegetables are tender, about 1 hour more.

title: Tater Tot Hotdish
ingredients: 1 can (10.5 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.
Brown the ground beef and onion in a skillet over medium heat. Drain excess fat and season with salt and pepper.
Stir together the soup and milk, then mix with the beef and green beans in the baking dish.
Sprinkle the cheddar over the mixture and arrange the tater tots in an even layer on top.
Bake until bubbling and the tater tots are golden, about 45 minutes.

title: Wisconsin Beer-Battered Fish Fry
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, plus 1/2 cup for dredging
instructions: Pat the fish dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Whisk 1 cup flour with the baking powder in a bowl. Whisk in the beer and egg until just combined.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 350°F.
Dredge each fillet in the remaining flour, then dip it in the batter.
Fry the fish in batches until crisp and cooked through, about 4 minutes per side. Drain on a rack and serve with lemon.

title: Classic Midwest Chicken and Noodles
instructions: Combine the chicken, broth, salt, and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Add the carrots, celery, and onion to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the chicken meat from the bones and shred it, discarding the skin and bones.
Add the noodles to the pot and cook until tender, following the package time.
Stir in the chicken and parsley, warm through, and serve.

title: Rhubarb Crisp
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8-inch square baking dish.
Toss the rhubarb with the granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, and cinnamon. Spread it in the dish.
Stir together the oats, 3/4 cup flour, brown sugar, and salt. Mix in the melted butter until crumbly.
Scatter the oat mixture evenly over the rhubarb.
Bake until the fruit is bubbling and the topping is golden, about 40 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Texas-Style Beef Chili
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches, then return it to the pot.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and cook over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender.

title: Chicken-Fried Steak with Cream Gravy
ingredients: 4 beef cube steaks, about 6 ounces each
instructions: Season the steaks with the salt and pepper.
Mix the flour and paprika in a shallow dish.
Whisk the eggs and 1/4 cup milk in a second shallow dish.
Dredge each steak in the flour, dip it in the egg mixture, then coat it again in flour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Fry the steaks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through; drain on a rack.
Pour off the oil, leaving 3 tablespoons of drippings in the skillet.
Whisk in the gravy flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 2 cups milk; simmer, stirring, until thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve the gravy over the steaks.

title: Texas-Style Smoked Brisket
ingredients: 1 whole packer beef brisket, 10 to 12 pounds
1 cup oak or pecan wood chunks
instructions: Trim the brisket, leaving about 1/4 inch of fat on the fat cap.
Mix the salt, pepper, and garlic powder; coat the brisket evenly on all sides.
Heat a smoker to 250°F and add the wood chunks.
Place the brisket fat-side up in the smoker and cook until the thickest part reaches about 165°F, around 6 to 8 hours.
Wrap the brisket tightly in butcher paper and return it to the smoker.
Continue cooking until a probe slides easily into the thickest part, usually at 200 to 205°F.
Rest the wrapped brisket in an insulated cooler for at least 1 hour.
Slice across the grain and serve.

title: Texas Pinto Beans
ingredients: 1 pound dried pinto beans, picked over and rinsed
instructions: Put the beans in a large pot and cover with the water.
Add the ham hock, onion, garlic, and cumin.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover partially and simmer for 2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender; add water if needed.
Remove the ham hock, pull off any meat, and stir the meat back into the beans.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Texas Peach Cobbler
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the peaches with 1/4 cup sugar, the cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Stir together the flour, baking powder, salt, and remaining 1/2 cup sugar.
Whisk in the milk until just combined.
Pour the melted butter into a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, then spread the batter over it without stirring.
Spoon the peaches and their juices evenly over the batter.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Let the cobbler cool for 15 minutes before serving.

title: California-Style Fish Tacos
ingredients: 1 pound firm white fish, such as cod, cut into strips
instructions: Toss the fish with cumin, chili powder, and salt.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the fish for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until opaque and flaky.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet.
Fill the tortillas with fish and cabbage, then drizzle with crema and top with cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: California Avocado Toast
instructions: Toast the sourdough until golden.
Mash the avocado with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the avocado over the toast.
Top with cotija and red pepper flakes.

title: Santa Maria-Style Tri-Tip
instructions: Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Rub the mixture over the tri-tip.
Let the meat stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high and brush the grates with olive oil.
Grill the tri-tip for 5 to 7 minutes per side, then move it to indirect heat and cook until it reaches 130°F for medium-rare.
Rest the roast for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.

title: California Cobb Salad
instructions: Arrange the romaine on a serving platter.
Top with rows of chicken, eggs, avocado, tomatoes, bacon, and blue cheese.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper until combined.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad just before serving.

title: California-Style Mission Burrito
ingredients: 1 cup carne asada, cooked and sliced
instructions: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable.
Divide the beans, rice, carne asada, cheese, pico de gallo, sour cream, and avocado between the tortillas, placing the fillings in the center.
Fold in the sides of each tortilla, then roll tightly from the bottom.
Place each burrito seam-side down in a skillet and toast over medium heat until lightly golden.

title: Chicken and Andouille Gumbo
