ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Brown the sausage in a heavy pot over medium heat; transfer to a plate.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, brown it in the pot, and set aside.
Add the oil and flour. Stir constantly over medium-low heat until the roux is a deep chocolate brown.
Stir in the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Gradually stir in the stock.
Return the sausage and chicken to the pot. Add bay leaves, thyme, and cayenne.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Stir in green onions and parsley, then serve over rice.

title: Red Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 pound dried red kidney beans, rinsed and picked over
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the sausage; transfer it to a plate.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, sausage, water or stock, bay leaves, thyme, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered until the beans are tender, about 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Add water as needed.
Mash some beans against the side of the pot and stir to thicken. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve over rice and top with sliced green onions.

title: Shrimp Étouffée
ingredients: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 1/2 pounds medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook, stirring, until the roux is golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the seafood stock. Add the paprika, cayenne, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently until the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook just until pink and opaque, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the green onions, parsley, and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot over rice.

title: Crawfish Étouffée
ingredients: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 pounds cooked crawfish tails, thawed and drained
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until soft, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and flour; cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the seafood stock, then stir in the tomato paste, paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently until the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.
Fold in the crawfish tails and cook gently until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the green onions, parsley, and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve over rice.

title: Jambalaya
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage, then transfer it to a plate.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it in the pot; transfer it to the plate.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and rice; cook for 1 minute.
Add the stock, tomatoes, bay leaves, thyme, paprika, cayenne, sausage, and chicken. Stir well.
Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and let it stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, fluff the rice, and stir in the green onions. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken or beef, shredded
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté the chopped onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet peppers until soft.
Stir in curry powder and thyme, cooking for one minute.
Add the blended tomatoes and peppers; cook until the oil separates from the mixture.
Pour in the stock, bay leaves, and salt; bring to a boil.
Add the washed rice and stir well to prevent sticking.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice with a fork and mix in the cooked meat.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and ground
1 large yam or 3 cups cassava flour
2 cups beef or chicken, cubed and boiled
instructions: Boil yams in salted water until soft, then pound in a mortar until smooth and stretchy, or mix cassava flour with water and knead until smooth.
In a large pot, heat palm oil and fry the ground crayfish and onions until fragrant.
Add the ground egusi seeds, garlic, and ground pepper; stir for 2 minutes.
Gradually add the stock and some of the boiled water, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer the soup for 20 minutes until it thickens.
Add the boiled meat and chopped greens, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with fufu.

title: Suya Spiced Meat Skewers
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, thinly sliced
instructions: Combine ground peanuts, flour, ginger, garlic, cayenne, and salt to make the suya spice blend.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly over the sliced meat, ensuring it is well coated.
Let the marinated meat rest for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Thread the meat slices onto metal or soaked wooden skewers.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the skewers for 3-4 minutes per side until the meat is charred and cooked through.
Garnish with fresh onion slices, tomatoes, and cilantro before serving.

title: Pounded Yam and Ewedu Soup
instructions: Boil yams in a small amount of water until very soft, then drain and pound with a pestle until smooth and elastic.
In a separate pot, heat palm oil and sauté the onion and garlic.
Add the ground crayfish, ginger, salt, and black pepper, stirring for one minute.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the washed ewedu leaves and cook for 10 minutes until the soup thickens.
Serve the pounded yam in bowls with a spoonful of soup on top.

title: Amala and Ewedu Soup
ingredients: 1 cup smoked fish or beef, chopped
instructions: Gradually add warm water to the cassava flour while stirring vigorously to form a smooth, thick paste.
Cook the amala over low heat, stirring constantly, until it pulls away from the sides of the pot and becomes firm.
In a separate pot, heat palm oil and sauté the onion, garlic, and ginger.
Add the ground crayfish, salt, and black pepper, then pour in the stock.
Add the washed ewedu leaves and bring to a simmer, cooking for 10 minutes.
Stir in the smoked fish or beef and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve the amala alongside the ewedu soup.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, washed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and fry until translucent.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the blended tomatoes and peppers; simmer until the mixture reduces and thickens.
Add thyme, curry powder, bay leaves, salt, and pepper; stir well.
Add the washed rice and stir to coat every grain with the sauce.
Pour in the stock slowly, ensuring the rice is just covered.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Do not lift the lid while cooking. Once the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, fluff with a fork.
Garnish with grated hard-boiled eggs before serving.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and crushed
2 cups spinach or garden cress, chopped
1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed and boiled
1 cup yam, plantain, or cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: In a large pot, heat palm oil over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and fry until soft.
Stir in the blended peppers and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the crushed egusi seeds and fry for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Pour in the stock gradually, stirring until the soup thickens to a desired consistency.
Add the boiled meat, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or garden cress and cook until wilted.
Meanwhile, boil the yam, plantain, or cassava chunks until very soft.
Mash the boiled starches into a smooth, stretchy dough by hand.
Serve the fufu immediately with a ladle of hot egusi soup.

title: Wakye
ingredients: Fried fish, spaghetti, and gari for serving
instructions: Wash the rice, red beans, and sorghum flour thoroughly.
In a large pot, heat vegetable oil and fry the chopped onions until soft.
Add the blended tomatoes and peppers; cook until the oil separates from the sauce.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for another minute.
Add the washed rice, beans, sorghum, water, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until beans and rice are soft and well-integrated.
Remove from heat and let it steam for 10 minutes.
Serve warm alongside fried fish, spaghetti, and gari.

title: Suya Spiced Meat Skewers
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, thinly sliced
instructions: In a bowl, mix peanut butter, cumin, coriander, cloves, ginger, cayenne, garlic, salt, and water until a smooth paste forms.
Coat the sliced meat thoroughly with the spice mixture and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Thread the marinated meat onto skewers.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers, turning frequently, until the meat is cooked through and slightly charred.
Serve hot with sliced onions, tomatoes, and a side of spicy peanut sauce.

title: Egusi and Spinach Stew
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and ground
2 cups spinach or bitter leaf, chopped
1 lb mixed meats (beef, goat, or chicken), cubed
instructions: Heat palm oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions and fry until golden.
Stir in the blended peppers and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the ground egusi seeds and fry for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the stock gradually, stirring until the soup thickens.
Add the mixed meats, ground crayfish, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or bitter leaf and cook until wilted.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Serve hot with fried plantain and rice.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the diced onions until soft.
Add tomato paste and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates.
Stir in the blended tomatoes, garlic, and peppers; cook until the raw tomato smell disappears.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, and stock; simmer for 10 minutes.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot.
Stir well to coat the rice with the sauce, ensuring no dry spots remain.
Cover the pot tightly and cook over low heat for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve hot.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 3 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), soaked in warm water
2 cups peeled and diced green plantains
2 cups peeled and diced yams or cassava
instructions: Boil the plantains, yams, or cassava in salted water until very soft, about 30 minutes.
Mash the boiled roots in a large bowl with your hands or a mortar until smooth and elastic.
In a separate pot, fry the onions, garlic, and pepper until fragrant.
Add the soaked egusi seeds to the pot and fry until the water evaporates.
Pour in the stock, crayfish powder, and salt; bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally to prevent the soup from sticking to the bottom.
Serve the hot egusi soup immediately with a large portion of fufu.

title: Wakato (Spicy Beef Stew)
ingredients: Pounded yam or rice for serving
instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt and let them sit for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and sear the beef on all sides until browned.
Remove the beef and set aside; sauté the onions, garlic, and ginger in the same pot.
Add the chopped tomatoes, scotch bonnet peppers, curry powder, and crayfish; cook until the sauce thickens.
Return the beef to the pot and add the beef stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot with pounded yam or rice.

title: Egusi Soup with Cowpeas
ingredients: 1 cup dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight
1/2 cup fresh spinach or kale, chopped
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger, and peppers into a smooth paste.
In a large pot, fry the blended paste with a little oil until the raw smell is gone.
Add the soaked black-eyed peas, egusi seeds, stock, and crayfish powder.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chopped spinach or kale and cook for another 10 minutes.
Taste the soup and adjust the salt and pepper to your preference.
Serve hot with fufu, banku, or garri.

title: Mafe (Groundnut Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed
1 cup roasted groundnuts (peanuts), blended into a thick paste
Fried plantain or rice for serving
instructions: Sear the meat cubes in oil until browned on all sides.
Remove the meat and sauté the onions, garlic, and ginger until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Stir in the groundnut paste, blending it well with the tomato sauce.
Return the meat to the pot, add the stock, bay leaf, ginger, and cayenne pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick.
Season with salt and serve with fried plantains or white rice.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 2 cups long grain parboiled rice, washed
1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and half the curry powder.
Brown chicken in oil in a large pot, then remove.
Sauté onions and garlic in the same pot until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add blended tomatoes and peppers, cooking down until oil separates.
Return chicken to the pot and add stock, thyme, bay leaves, and remaining spices.
Bring to a boil, then add washed rice.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

title: Tagine with Apricots and Almonds
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Brown the lamb cubes on all sides, then remove.
Sauté onions and garlic until translucent.
Stir in ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, and cumin; cook for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot and add stock, apricots, and salt.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Remove lid and increase heat slightly to thicken the sauce.
Stir in sliced almonds and cook for 2 more minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve.

title: Peanut Stew (Njama Njama)
ingredients: 1 lb beef stew meat, cut into cubes
instructions: Season meat with salt and brown in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove meat and set aside; sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and ground peanuts, cooking for 2 minutes.
Return meat to the pot and add stock, coriander, cumin, and cayenne.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Stir in water and tomato paste again to adjust consistency.
Continue simmering uncovered for 30 minutes until sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving with rice or ugali.

title: Mopane Worm Salad
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or dried mopane worms
instructions: If using dried worms, soak in warm water for 30 minutes, then boil for 10 minutes.
Drain worms well and rinse with cold water; chop into bite-sized pieces.
In a large bowl, combine worms, spinach, cucumber, tomato, and red onion.
Whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, chili flakes, and salt.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Top with fresh coriander and serve immediately.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), soaked and ground
1 lb goat meat or chicken, cubed
instructions: Boil meat until tender, then set aside.
In a separate pot, fry onions, garlic, and ginger until soft.
Add palm oil and stir in the ground egusi seeds, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add the cooked meat, stock, scotch bonnet peppers, and crayfish.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the soup thickens.
Add yam cubes and cook for another 10 minutes until soft.
Stir in fresh spinach or kontomire if using and cook for 3 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 2 cups mixed fried plantains and grilled chicken
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add blended peppers, crushed tomatoes, curry, thyme, and bay leaf.
Simmer sauce until it reduces by half.
Add stock and bring to a boil.
Stir in rice, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for 25 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and fluff with a fork.
Serve with fried plantains and grilled chicken.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 3 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and crushed
2 cups peeled and cubed yam or plantain
2 cups spinach or palm greens, chopped
1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed and boiled
instructions: Boil meat with onion, garlic, ginger, and salt until tender.
Strain meat broth and set broth aside.
Blend yam and plantain with a little water until smooth.
Boil the blended mixture in a pot, stirring constantly until it pulls away from the sides.
In a separate pot, fry egusi seeds in palm oil until fragrant.
Add meat broth, spinach, and salt to the egusi; simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve hot fufu balls with the soup.

title: Suya Skewers
ingredients: 1 lb beef mince or thinly sliced beef
instructions: Grind peanuts into a coarse powder.
Mix beef with peanut powder, ginger, garlic, salt, peppers, and oil.
Let the mixture marinate for 30 minutes.
Thread the seasoned meat onto soaked skewers.
Grill over charcoal or under a broiler until charred and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sliced onions and fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Red Bean and Plantain Stew
ingredients: 2 cups red kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil beans with onion, garlic, ginger, allspice, thyme, and broth until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add plantain slices and cook gently for 15 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve warm as a side dish or with rice.

title: Moroccan-Style Chicken Tagine
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown chicken in olive oil in a tagine pot.
Add onion and garlic; cook until softened.
Stir in spices, apricots, barley, and stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and chopped peppers; sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook until it darkens slightly.
Pour in the blended tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until the liquid reduces.
Add rice, curry powder, thyme, basil, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; stir to coat rice.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover tightly and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Tagine with Chicken and Prunes
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or deep pot over medium heat.
Season chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, cinnamon, ginger, and turmeric.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot and cook until softened, then add garlic.
Return chicken to the pot and add prunes, apricots, and stock.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in sliced almonds and cook for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 4 cups peeled and chopped watermelon seeds (egusi)
1 lb beef, cubed and marinated in ginger and garlic
2 cups cassava flour or plantain flour
instructions: Fry the ground egusi seeds in oil until fragrant, then set aside.
In a separate pot, sauté onions, blended tomatoes, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Add ground crayfish, marinated beef, stock, salt, and ginger; simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the fried egusi seeds and chopped greens; cook until greens wilt.
In a separate pot, boil water and gradually add cassava or plantain flour.
Knead the dough vigorously until smooth and elastic, then portion into balls.
Serve the hot soup with the warm fufu balls.

title: Ginger and Plantain Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat or beef, cubed
instructions: Season the meat with salt, black pepper, and half the grated ginger.
Sauté the meat in a pot until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until soft, then add blended tomatoes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook until the oil separates.
Return the meat to the pot and add stock, remaining ginger, and scotch bonnet.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Stir in palm oil and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Add sliced plantains and cook for 5 minutes until heated through.
Serve hot.

title: Moroccan-Style Spiced Lamb Tagine
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Season lamb with salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, and saffron.
Sear lamb pieces until browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
Sauté onions in the pot until golden, then add garlic.
Return lamb to the pot and add apricots, stock, and dried mint.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours.
Stir in toasted almonds and cook for another 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, soaked for 30 minutes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Drain the soaked rice and set aside.
Sauté the chopped onion, garlic, and tomato paste in oil until fragrant.
Stir in the blended tomatoes and peppers, cooking until the mixture thickens and oil separates.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper, stirring well.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the rice, stir once to combine, then cover tightly.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the frozen peas and cook for 5 more minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and ground
2 cups cubed yam, plantain, or cassava
2 cups spinach or bitter leaf, chopped
1 cup beef or goat meat, cubed and boiled
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Boil the yam, plantain, or cassava until very soft and mash them into a smooth, stretchy dough.
In a large pot, combine the ground egusi, water, onion, tomato paste, and stock.
Add the ground crayfish, ginger, garlic, salt, and seasoning cubes.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent lumps.
Add the boiled meat and spinach, cooking until the greens wilt and the soup thickens.
Season with more salt if needed and serve immediately with fufu.

title: Poulet Yassa
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried or fresh pineapple, chopped
instructions: Marinate chicken thighs with turmeric, ginger, salt, and half the olive oil for 2 hours.
Sauté the sliced onions in olive oil until golden brown and crispy.
Add the pineapple and cook for 5 minutes until caramelized.
Remove half the onions and pineapple to a bowl, set aside.
In the same pot, sear the marinated chicken until golden on all sides.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the reserved onions and pineapple to the pot with the chicken.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with rice and lemon wedges.

title: Moin Moin
instructions: Blanch the green beans and corn for 3 minutes, then drain and chop.
Sauté the onion, ginger, and garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook until the oil separates.
Stir in the stock, salt, pepper, vegetables, and cook for 5 minutes.
In a separate bowl, mix corn flour and water to form a thick batter.
Pour the vegetable mixture into the corn batter and stir gently.
Line a mold or steamer basket with banana leaves and pour in the batter.
Steam for 40-50 minutes until firm.
Unmold onto a plate and serve with groundnut sauce.

title: Kedgeree
ingredients: 1 lb fresh cod or haddock, flaked
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the rice in stock until just tender, then drain and fluff with a fork.
In a pan, melt butter and sauté onions until soft.
Add mustard seeds and curry powder, cooking for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add the flaked fish and peas, stirring gently to coat.
Mix the cooked rice into the fish mixture and heat through.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Garnish with sliced hard-boiled eggs and chopped chives.
Serve hot as a breakfast or light lunch dish.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the chopped onion until soft.
Add the blended tomatoes, peppers, garlic, and tomato paste; cook until the oil separates.
Stir in the curry powder, thyme, salt, and pepper, then add the rice.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover tightly and simmer for 30-40 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and crushed
1 large cow foot or goat meat, boiled and shredded
1 large yam, peeled and cut into chunks
1 large cassava root, peeled and cut into chunks
1 ripe plantain, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the yam, cassava, and plantain in separate pots until soft.
Pound the boiled ingredients together in a mortar until smooth and stretchy.
In a large pot, fry the onions and garlic in palm oil until fragrant.
Add the shredded meat, stock, and crushed egusi seeds.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup thickens to a gravy-like consistency.

title: Pounded Yam and Ewedu
ingredients: 3 large yams, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups fresh spinach (ewedu), washed and chopped
1/2 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the yam chunks in water until very soft and easily mashable.
Mash the yam in a mortar or bowl until it forms a smooth, stretchy dough.
Fry the onions and garlic in palm oil until golden.
Add the ground shrimp, locust beans, and crayfish to the oil.
Stir in the chopped ewedu and stock, cooking for 10 minutes until the greens wilt and the soup thickens.

title: Egusi Stew with Smoked Fish
ingredients: 2 cups smoked fish, cleaned and flaked
1 large cow foot or goat meat, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the meat until tender, then set aside.
In a large pot, fry the onions and peppers in palm oil until soft.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes until it darkens.
Stir in the roasted egusi seeds, dried ginger, salt, and pepper.
Add the stock, the boiled meat, and the flaked smoked fish. Simmer for 20 minutes until the stew is thick.

title: Suya Spices and Skewers
ingredients: 1 pound beef or goat meat, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Mix the ground peanuts, cumin, coriander, ginger, cayenne, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Add the chopped onion and a little water to the spice mix to form a paste.
Rub the spice paste thoroughly onto the sliced meat and let it marinate for at least 1 hour.
Thread the marinated meat onto the soaked wooden skewers.
Grill the skewers over hot charcoal or an open flame, turning frequently, until the meat is charred and cooked through.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in blended peppers and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; stir well.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice, stir gently to coat.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and stir in frozen peas just before serving.

title: Groundnut Soup (Nigerian Style)
ingredients: 2 cups roasted groundnuts (peanuts), blended into paste
1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed and stewed
2 cups spinach or cowpea leaves, chopped
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: In a large pot, sauté the blended onions and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add the stewed meat, tomatoes, and blended peppers; cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the groundnut paste gradually, mixing well to avoid lumps.
Add beef stock and seasoning cubes; bring to a simmer.
Cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the sliced okra and continue simmering for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped leaves and cook for another 5 minutes until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving with fufu or pounded yam.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and ground into powder
1 lb mixed meats (beef, goat, or fish), stewed
2 cups spinach or bitter leaf, chopped
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Sauté chopped onions, ginger, and ground crayfish in oil until soft.
Add blended tomatoes and peppers; cook for 5 minutes.
Gradually stir in the ground egusi powder and mix well.
Pour in water or stock and bring to a boil.
Add the stewed meats and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the chopped greens and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and seasoning cubes to taste.
Serve hot with fufu or garri.

title: Moin Moin
ingredients: 1 cup spinach or cowpea leaves, chopped
instructions: Mix grated corn, grated yam, chopped onions, and greens in a large bowl.
Add ground crayfish, curry powder, ginger, blended peppers, and salt.
Whisk egg whites until stiff peaks form and gently fold into the mixture.
Add beaten egg yolks and mix until well combined.
Grease a steamer basket or mold with oil.
Pour the batter into the mold and steam for 45-60 minutes until firm.
Cool slightly, remove from mold, and slice into wedges.
Serve with hot pepper sauce and soup.

title: Suya Spiced Meat
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, thinly sliced
2 tbsp dried fish, ground into powder
2 tbsp ground peanuts, roasted and ground
Fresh onions and tomatoes for garnish
instructions: In a small bowl, mix all dry spices: ground fish, peanuts, curry, ginger, garlic, nutmeg, cayenne, and salt.
Rub the spice mixture thoroughly onto the sliced meat and let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or over an open fire.
Cook the marinated meat in batches, turning frequently until browned and slightly charred.
Drain excess oil and serve immediately.
Garnish with fresh sliced onions and tomatoes.
Serve with sliced onions, tomatoes, and your favorite spicy sauce.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, washed until water runs clear
2 cups cooked chicken or beef, shredded
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions, garlic, and blended peppers; sauté until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until the oil separates.
Pour in the blended tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add curry powder, thyme, basil, bay leaves, salt, and black pepper; stir well.
Add the washed rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain with the sauce.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Gently fold in the shredded chicken or beef.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Tagine with Lamb and Prunes
ingredients: 1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Add lamb cubes and brown on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until soft and translucent.
Add garlic and spices (cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, cumin, coriander); cook for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Add prunes, raisins, apricots, honey, stock, and water.
Season with salt and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until lamb is tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Swallow Soup (Fufu) with Palm Nut Stew
ingredients: 4 cups palm nut cream or concentrate
1 pound goat meat or beef, cubed
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Boil the cubed meat with onion, garlic, and stock cubes until tender.
In a separate pot, heat palm oil and fry the scotch bonnet pepper slightly.
Add the palm nut cream and beef stock; simmer until smooth.
Stir in the okra and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cooked meat and simmer for another 10 minutes.
For the swallow: mix cassava flour, corn flour, and mashed plantains in a bowl.
Gradually add hot water, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic; let it rest covered for 10 minutes.
Shape the dough into balls and serve immediately with the stew.

title: Pepper Soup with Goat Meat
ingredients: Ginger and garlic slices for serving
instructions: Blanch the meat in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain and rinse to remove scum.
In a large pot, combine meat, onions, garlic, ginger, and blended peppers.
Add water, pepper powder, thyme, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and stock cubes.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Stir in the palm oil and fresh spinach; cook for 2 more minutes.
Remove bay leaves if used; ladle into bowls.
Serve hot with ginger and garlic slices on the side.

title: Suya Spiced Beef Skewers
ingredients: 1 pound lean beef, trimmed and cut into thin strips
1 tablespoon Suya spice mix (or homemade blend of cumin, coriander, pepper)
instructions: Mix flour, Suya spice mix, salt, ginger, garlic powder, cayenne, and oregano in a bowl.
Toss the beef strips in the spice mixture until evenly coated; let marinate for 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated beef onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer over medium-high heat.
Fry the skewers for 3-4 minutes until the outside is golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oil and drain on paper towels.
Arrange on a platter with sliced onions, chopped tomatoes, and coriander.
Serve wrapped in lettuce leaves with your favorite dipping sauce.

title: Jollof Rice
instructions: Sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft.
Add blended peppers and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and puree; simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in stock, thyme, curry powder, and bay leaf.
Add rice, stir to coat, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed
instructions: Soak egusi seeds in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Boil meat with onions, garlic, and ginger until tender; reserve broth.
Blend soaked egusi seeds with some broth until smooth.
Pour blended mixture into the meat pot and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add spinach and cook for another 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil yam or plantain until soft, then pound into a smooth dough.
Serve fufu hot with the soup.

title: Peanut Stew with Chicken
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Sear chicken pieces in oil until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until translucent.
Add garlic, tomato paste, ginger, and cayenne; cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot and stir in ground peanuts.
Add chicken stock and bay leaf; simmer covered for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve.

title: Injera and Wat (Ethiopian Lentil Stew)
ingredients: 1 tsp niter kibbeh (spiced butter) or butter
instructions: Fry grated onions in butter until golden; add garlic and berbere.
Add meat and lentils; stir in water and simmer for 1 hour until lentils are soft.
For injera: Mix flour and yeast with water to form a thin batter.
Let batter ferment for 12-24 hours in a warm place.
Pour batter onto a hot griddle to cook thin circular flatbreads.
Serve wat hot with injera.

title: Suya Spiced Beef Skewers
ingredients: Fresh onions and tomatoes for garnish
instructions: Grind peanuts and spices together to form a coarse paste.
Toss beef slices in the spice paste and let marinate for at least 1 hour.
Thread marinated beef onto skewers.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Grill skewers, turning frequently, until beef is charred and cooked through (about 5-7 minutes).
Garnish with sliced onions and tomatoes before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, washed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat; fry onions until soft.
Add garlic, curry powder, and thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add blended tomatoes and peppers.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes until it reduces and thickens.
Add rice, bay leaves, salt, and pepper; stir well to coat grains.
Pour in the stock; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover tightly and cook for 30-35 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), soaked overnight and drained
4 cups water, plus more if needed
1 lb beef or goat meat, cut into cubes
1 lb yam or cassava, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups spinach or ugu leaves, chopped
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Boil meat with onion, garlic, and seasoning until tender; set aside.
Blend soaked egusi seeds with some of the cooking liquid until smooth.
In a large pot, fry palm oil until it separates from the solids.
Add the egusi paste to the oil and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the meat broth to the soup, stirring to avoid lumps.
Add more water or broth to reach desired consistency; simmer for 20 minutes.
Add chopped spinach and cook until wilted.
Meanwhile, boil yam or cassava chunks until very soft.
Mash the cooked yam in a mortar or with hands until smooth and elastic to serve.

title: Tuwo Shinkafa with Miyan Kuka
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried locust beans (iru), soaked and blended with kolanut
Boiled egg or fried fish for serving
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear; soak for 30 minutes if desired.
Boil rice and water in a heavy-bottomed pot until rice is very soft and mushy.
Stir continuously and mash the rice against the side of the pot to form a thick dough.
Cook on low heat for 15 minutes, adding small amounts of water as needed.
In a separate pot, fry onions in half the palm oil until golden.
Add powdered kolanut, blended locust beans, crayfish, and remaining oil.
Stir in the soup mixture and simmer for 20 minutes, adding water to thin.
Season with salt and flaked dried fish; serve hot with tuwo.

title: Pounded Yam and Ewedu Soup
ingredients: 2 lbs yam, peeled and cut into chunks
1 cup spinach leaves (ewedu), washed and drained
instructions: Boil yam chunks in water until they fall apart easily.
Mash the yam into a smooth, elastic paste using a mortar and pestle.
In a pot, fry onions and ginger in palm oil until fragrant.
Add stock, flaked fish, ground crayfish, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the washed ewedu leaves and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the pounded yam to the soup in small portions, stirring vigorously to incorporate.
Continue stirring until the soup thickens and becomes smooth.
Serve immediately with the pounded yam mixed into the soup.

title: Moin Moin
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Boil the soaked black-eyed peas until very soft; mash slightly.
In a bowl, mix mashed beans with spinach, okra, onions, garlic, and ginger.
Add ground crayfish, palm oil, prekese, salt, and seasoning; mix well.
Pour the mixture into a greased cylindrical mold or lined with banana leaves.
Steam over boiling water for 45-60 minutes until firm.
While steaming, prepare a sauce by sautéing onions and peppers in oil.
Remove the mold and invert onto a plate; slice into wedges.
Serve hot with the spicy vegetable sauce on the side.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add blended tomatoes and peppers; simmer for 10 minutes until oil rises to the top.
Season with curry, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add washed rice and stir to coat evenly.
Pour in stock and add bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Suya Spiced Beef Skewers
ingredients: 1 lb beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds, toasted and ground
instructions: Toast cumin seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind to a powder.
In a bowl, mix ground peanuts, ginger, paprika, ground cumin, black pepper, and salt.
Toss beef strips with the spice mixture and oil; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread marinated beef onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped dried onions.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and crushed
1 lb goat meat or beef, cubed
1 scotch bonnet pepper, chopped (adjust to taste)
1 cup pre-boiled cassava and plantain flour mixture (for fufu)
instructions: Boil meat with onions until tender, then drain and set aside.
In a separate pot, combine crushed egusi seeds, water, chopped tomatoes, scotch bonnet, and ground crayfish.
Simmer the egusi mixture for 20 minutes until thickened.
Stir in palm oil and the cooked meat with its broth.
Season with salt and simmer for another 10 minutes.
While soup simmers, prepare fufu by boiling the cassava and plantain flour mixture and kneading until smooth and elastic.
Serve the soup in a bowl with a portion of fufu on the side.

title: Wakato Beans with Palm Oil
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
In a pot, sauté onions and garlic in a little oil until translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Stir in the palm oil, thyme, and bay leaf; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and enough water or stock to cover them.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until beans are soft.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaf before serving.

title: Maafe Peanut Stew
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and ginger; set aside.
In a large pot, heat oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in blended tomatoes and bell pepper.
Simmer the tomato mixture for 10 minutes until reduced.
Stir in ground peanuts and cook for another 5 minutes, adding a splash of water if too dry.
Add chicken pieces and chicken stock; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce is thick.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, and bell pepper until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add blended tomatoes, scotch bonnet, curry powder, thyme, and bay leaves; simmer for 10 minutes.
Wash rice thoroughly and add to the pot, stirring to coat with the sauce.
Pour in beef stock, add frozen vegetables, and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and steam for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), soaked and ground
1 lb beef cubes, boiled and chopped
1 cup spinach or ugu leaves, chopped
Fufu made from cassava and plantain flour
instructions: Sauté onions, ginger, and garlic in palm oil until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes and peppers, cooking down until soft and oily.
Stir in the ground egusi seeds and beef stock; simmer for 20 minutes.
Add boiled beef cubes and cook for another 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped spinach or ugu leaves and cook until wilted.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot fufu by hand with a ladle of soup.

title: Suya
ingredients: 1 lb beef sirloin, sliced thin against the grain
instructions: Combine ground shrimp, dried fish, onion, ginger, garlic, pepper, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Add sliced beef to the spice mixture and mix well to coat evenly.
Marinate the meat in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Skewer the marinated beef onto bamboo or metal skewers.
Roast the skewers over a charcoal grill, turning frequently until charred and cooked through.
In a separate pan, heat groundnut paste with a little oil to make a smooth peanut sauce.
Serve the Suya skewers with peanut sauce, onion leaves, and lettuce.

title: Egusi Stew
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed and stewed
instructions: Sauté onions, tomatoes, peppers, ginger, and garlic in oil until soft.
Stir in ground crayfish and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the stewed meat and beef stock; simmer until the meat is tender.
Mix the groundnut paste and ground egusi together in a bowl.
Gradually add the paste mixture to the pot, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Continue cooking on low heat for 20 minutes until the stew thickens and oil floats to the top.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Akara
ingredients: 1 tsp dried scotch bonnet pepper, blended
instructions: Drain the soaked black-eyed peas and blend them with onion, scotch bonnet pepper, ginger, salt, and baking powder until smooth.
Add flour and a little water if the mixture is too thick; adjust until it has a thick pancake batter consistency.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil.
Fry the akara, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm as a snack or breakfast item.

title: Palm Wine Fish Stew
ingredients: 1 lb fresh fish (tilapia or snapper), cleaned and cut into pieces
3 cups palm wine or substitute with coconut water and tamarind paste
instructions: Season the fish pieces lightly with salt.
In a large pot, heat oil and sauté the chopped onions until soft.
Add the ginger, garlic, scotch bonnet peppers, and tomato paste; cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the palm wine and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish pieces carefully to the pot.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes until the fish is flaky and the sauce has thickened.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 2 cups mixed chicken or beef, cubed
instructions: Season the meat with salt, pepper, and thyme, then fry until browned.
Sauté onions in oil until soft, then add tomato paste and fry until dark red.
Add blended tomatoes and peppers, cooking down until the oil separates.
Stir in the rice and fry for 2 minutes to coat grains.
Pour in the stock, add bay leaf, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

title: Fufu and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), roasted and ground
2 cups boiled spinach or cowpeas to serve
instructions: Boil water or broth with onions, tomatoes, and crayfish until reduced by half.
Stir in the ground egusi seeds and cook for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add spinach and plantain flour gradually to reach desired thickness.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer for 5 more minutes.
Serve hot alongside pounded fufu made from cassava and plantain.

title: Injera with Wat
instructions: Mix teff flour with 1/2 cup water to form a thick batter and let ferment for 2-3 days.
Sauté onions in oil until soft, then add berbere spice and garlic powder.
Add cooked lentils, chickpeas, potatoes, and 2 cups of water to the spice mixture.
Simmer the wat until thickened and flavors meld, about 20 minutes.
Pour fermented batter onto a hot griddle to cook thin, spongy injera bread.

title: Mafe Peanut Stew
ingredients: 1 lb beef or goat meat, cubed
1/2 cup green beans, cut into pieces
Salt and cayenne pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the meat in a pot over medium heat, then remove and set aside.
Sauté onions in the same pot until translucent, then add tomato paste.
Stir in blended tomatoes, ginger, garlic powder, and salt, cooking for 5 minutes.
Return meat to the pot, add broth and peanut butter, and stir well.
Simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender, then add green beans and cook 10 more minutes.

title: Ugali with Sukuma Wiki
ingredients: 1 bunch kale or collard greens, chopped (sukuma wiki)
instructions: Boil 4 cups of water with salt, turmeric, and garlic powder until simmering.
Gradually whisk in cornmeal to avoid lumps, stirring vigorously until dough forms.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until firm.
In a separate pan, sauté onions in oil until soft, then add blended tomatoes.
Add chopped greens, ginger, and salt; cook until wilted and tender.
Serve hot ugali alongside the sautéed sukuma wiki.

title: Brik à l'Oeuf
ingredients: 4 large tomatoes, grated and squeezed dry
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place one sheet of phyllo on a clean surface, brush with melted butter.
Layer two more sheets of phyllo on top, brushing each with butter.
Place a spoonful of tomato and coriander mixture in the center.
Crack the beaten egg over the filling and season with salt and pepper.
Fold the sides of the phyllo over the filling, then roll tightly into a cigar shape.
Seal the edges with a bit of water.
Place brik seam-side down on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Serve immediately with a dollop of garlic yogurt.

title: Tajine de Poulet aux Prunes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the chicken pieces generously with salt, pepper, cumin, and cinnamon.
Heat olive oil in a clay tagine over medium heat.
Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the sliced onions and garlic until soft and golden.
Return the chicken to the pot and stir to coat with the onion mixture.
Add the prunes and chicken broth to the tagine.
Cover with the cone lid and cook on low heat for 1 hour, checking occasionally.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Chorba Mencha (Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: 1 cup green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add the zucchini, carrots, green beans, and cumin.
Simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender but still crisp.
Stir in the green peas and cook for another 2 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in the fresh parsley and coriander.
Serve hot, often with a slice of lemon on the side.

title: Brik en Graine (Seed Filling)
ingredients: 1/2 cup spiced seed mixture (cumin, coriander, fenugreek)
1/4 cup fine bulgur wheat, cooked and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the cooked bulgur, crushed chickpeas, spices, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Layer two phyllo sheets, brushing each lightly with olive oil.
Spread the seed filling mixture evenly over the sheets, leaving a border.
Fold the phyllo over the filling and roll tightly.
Seal the ends with a little beaten egg.
Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes until crispy.
Cut into slices and serve warm.

title: Mloukhia with Lamb
ingredients: 2 cups fresh jute leaves (mloukhia), washed and chopped
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the ground lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the fenugreek powder and black pepper, stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped jute leaves and stir constantly for about 5-10 minutes until the dark green color turns to a bright green.
Add the chopped coriander and mint.
If the mixture is too thick, add a splash of water.
Season with salt and serve immediately with warm bread.

title: Chicken Tagine with Prunes and Almonds
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm water
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft, then add garlic, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper; stir for one minute.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides, then pour in tomatoes and their juices.
Stir in prunes, soaked saffron water, and sugar; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Sprinkle toasted almonds and cilantro over the top before serving.

title: Spiced Lamb Stew (Msemen Style)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add lamb cubes and brown well on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions until golden, then add garlic and spices; cook for one minute.
Return lamb to the pot, add crushed tomatoes, water, raisins, and almonds.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until lamb is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in fresh parsley, and serve hot.

title: Harira Soup with Chickpeas
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil lamb, lentils, and chickpeas in salted water until tender, about 1.5 hours.
While meat cooks, heat olive oil in a separate pot and sauté onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add crushed tomatoes, turmeric, ginger, dried mint, chopped parsley, and cilantro to the vegetable mix.
Stir in the cooked meat, lentils, chickpeas, and water; bring to a simmer.
Add broken vermicelli noodles and cook for 10 minutes until noodles are soft.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve immediately.

title: Zaalouk with Garlic and Cumin
instructions: Roast eggplant cubes in the oven at 400°F (200°C) for 30 minutes until soft.
In a large pan, heat olive oil and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes, roasted eggplant, cumin, paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper; cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice, cilantro, and parsley.
Let the mixture cool slightly, then serve warm or at room temperature topped with crushed walnuts.

title: Bastilla (Chicken Pie with Honey)
instructions: Mix ground almonds, hazelnuts, butter, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and saffron into a smooth paste.
Layer half of the phyllo sheets in a round baking dish, brushing each with butter.
Spread the nut mixture over the first layer, then add shredded chicken and pour the beaten eggs over everything.
Cover with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Drizzle with warm honey and sprinkle with pistachios before serving.

title: Doro Wat
ingredients: 1/4 cup teff injera, torn into pieces
instructions: Fry the chopped onions in niter kibbeh until golden brown.
Add the berbere spice and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat in the spice mixture.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Add the hard-boiled eggs and torn injera pieces.
Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens to a dark, glossy consistency.

title: Misir Wot
instructions: Fry the onions in niter kibbeh until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and berbere spice, cooking for one minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook until the oil separates slightly.
Add the rinsed lentils and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until lentils are soft.
Season with salt and cook on low until the stew is thick.

title: Shiro Wot
ingredients: 1/4 cup green onions, chopped for garnish
instructions: Fry the finely chopped onions in niter kibbeh until very soft.
Add the berbere spice and fry for 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the chickpea flour to prevent lumps.
Gradually add water while whisking constantly.
Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon.
Cook until the paste thickens significantly and pulls away from the pot sides.

title: Tibs with Onions
ingredients: 1 lb beef sirloin, sliced very thin against the grain
3 large red onions, sliced into thick rings
instructions: Heat niter kibbeh in a large skillet over high heat.
Add the sliced beef in a single layer and sear until browned on both sides.
Add the onion rings and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
Sprinkle the berbere spice and salt over the meat and onions.
Pour in the beef broth and toss quickly to coat.
Remove from heat immediately and garnish with fresh cilantro.

title: Gomen (Collard Greens)
ingredients: 2 bunches collard greens, stems removed and chopped
instructions: Wash the collard greens thoroughly and chop them into bite-sized pieces.
Fry the onions and garlic in niter kibbeh until translucent.
Add the chopped greens to the pan and stir well.
Pour in the chicken broth and cover the pot.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and red pepper flakes and cook until the greens are tender.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, soaked for 30 minutes
2 cups mixed cooked meat or fish
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the chopped onions until soft.
Add the blended peppers and tomatoes, then the tomato paste, and fry for 10 minutes until the raw taste is gone.
Stir in the stock, bay leaves, curry, thyme, and Maggi, bringing it to a boil.
Drain the soaked rice, add it to the pot, and mix well to coat every grain.
Cover tightly with foil and then the lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice gently, stir in the meat or fish, and serve hot.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), soaked and ground
1 lb goat meat or beef, cut into chunks
1 lb smoked fish, descaled and flaked
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
2 cups assorted leafy vegetables (crush leaves first)
instructions: Boil the meat and fish separately until tender, then combine them in a large pot.
In a separate pot, fry the blended tomato, pepper, onion, ginger, and garlic mixture in half the palm oil until the oil separates.
Add the ground egusi to the oil mixture and stir for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock or water and bring to a boil, then add the cooked meat and fish.
Season with salt and seasoning cubes, simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the crushed leafy vegetables and remaining palm oil, cook for another 5 minutes until the soup thickens, then serve.

title: Pounded Yam and Egusi
ingredients: 3 kg yams, peeled and cut into chunks
2 tbsp vegetable oil for the pot
1 lb cassava, peeled and cut (optional, for extra softness)
instructions: Boil the yam chunks (and cassava if using) in water until they are very soft and mushy.
Drain the water completely and transfer the yams to a large mortar.
Add the small amount of water reserved from boiling to the mortar.
Pound the yams vigorously with a pestle until they form a smooth, sticky ball with no lumps.
Shape the pounded yam into a round ball, let it cool slightly, and serve immediately with egusi or light soup.

title: Suya Skewers
ingredients: 1 lb beef, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Mix the ground peanuts, dried ginger, cloves, cumin, salt, cayenne, oil, onion, and tomato paste to make the suya spice mix.
Toss the sliced beef in the spice mix until evenly coated and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated beef slices onto the soaked skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
Heat a griddle or barbecue grill over medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers, turning frequently, until the meat is well-charred on all sides and cooked through.
Serve hot with sliced onions, tomatoes, and your favorite spicy suya sauce.

title: Fried Plantain with Egusi
ingredients: 4 ripe plantains, peeled and cut into thick rounds
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan or pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip the plantain rounds in the salt (and sugar if making sweet plantain).
Carefully lower the plantains into the hot oil in batches.
Fry for 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm alongside egusi soup or as a standalone snack.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long grain parboiled rice, rinsed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions until soft.
Add tomato paste and fry for 2 minutes until it loses its raw smell.
Stir in the blended tomatoes, peppers, curry, thyme, and bay leaves.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Wash the rice thoroughly and add it to the pot, stirring well.
Pour in the chicken stock, ensuring the rice is fully submerged.
Season with salt and pepper, then cover the pot tightly.
Cook over medium heat for about 30-40 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork and serve hot.

title: Fufu and Light Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried cocoyam flour (optional, for authenticity)
500g goat meat or beef, cut into cubes
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Boil the meat with bay leaves, ginger, and garlic until tender.
Blend tomatoes, onion, peppers, and seasonings into a smooth paste.
Heat palm oil in a pot and fry the blended vegetable paste until the raw smell disappears.
Add the cooked meat and its stock to the pot, stirring well.
Season with salt, crayfish, and seasoning cubes, then simmer for 20 minutes.
In a separate bowl, mix cassava flour and cocoyam flour.
Boil water and gradually add the flour mixture while stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon.
Continue stirring until the dough is smooth, non-sticky, and firm enough to pull away from the sides.
Cook on low heat for another 5 minutes, then cool slightly.
Pound the fufu on a board until smooth and stretchy, then serve with the hot light soup.

title: Waakye
ingredients: 1 cup red beans (kidney beans), soaked overnight
1 bunch of dried millet leaves (waakye leaves) or a few drops of liquid food coloring
Boiled fish or meat for serving
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them thoroughly.
Combine rice, beans, millet leaves (or food coloring), water, baking soda, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cover the pot.
Cook for about 20-25 minutes until both rice and beans are tender.
Remove the millet leaves once the rice is cooked.
Fluff the waakye with a fork and serve immediately.
Arrange fried plantain, boiled fish or meat, and spicy pepper sauce on the side.
Enjoy the traditional Ghanaian breakfast or lunch.

title: Banku and Tilapia Stew
instructions: Boil water in a large pot and gradually add corn flour and cassava flour while stirring constantly.
Cook the mixture over medium heat, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon for about 20 minutes until it becomes smooth and stretchy.
Season the banku with salt, then cover to keep warm.
Heat oil in a separate pot and fry the whole tilapia until golden brown on both sides.
Remove the fish and set aside, keeping the fish stock.
In the same pot, fry the blended tomatoes, onions, peppers, and tomato paste until the oil rises to the top.
Add the fish stock, ginger, salt, and seasoning cubes, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the fried tilapia to the stew and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve the hot tilapia stew over a bowl of freshly made banku.

title: Red Red (Black Bean Stew)
ingredients: Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Boil the soaked black-eyed peas until they are soft but not mushy.
Drain the beans and set aside.
Heat palm oil in a pot and fry the blended tomatoes, onions, peppers, and tomato paste until the raw smell disappears.
Add the cooked beans, ground crayfish, ginger, salt, and seasoning cubes to the pot.
Stir well and add a little water if the stew is too thick, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the rich red stew with fried plantain slices and a side of gari.

title: Thieboudienne
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes
1 large white fish, cleaned and cut into pieces
Salt and red pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the rice and set aside.
In a large pot, sauté onions, garlic, ginger, and tomatoes until soft.
Add the fish, carrots, and green beans; season with salt and red pepper.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Stir in the soaked rice, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the spinach and remaining water; cover and cook for another 10 minutes until rice is tender.
In a separate pan, fry the peanut butter with a little water until smooth.
Serve the rice and fish topped with the peanut sauce and fresh coriander.

title: Yassa
ingredients: 1 cup red wine or white wine
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with sliced onions, lemon juice, garlic, wine, salt, and pepper for at least 4 hours or overnight.
In a large pot, melt butter and olive oil over medium heat.
Sauté the marinated chicken and onions until the onions are caramelized and chicken is browned.
Add a splash of wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and onions are soft.
Garnish with fresh coriander, sliced peppers, and boiled potato slices before serving.

title: Couscous with Vegetables
instructions: Bring broth to a boil and add carrots, zucchini, and green beans; cook for 10 minutes.
Add onion, tomatoes, raisins, cumin, ginger, salt, and butter to the simmering vegetables.
Stir in the couscous and remove from heat.
Cover the pot tightly and let it steam for 10 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, ensuring it absorbs all the liquid.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Mafé
ingredients: Salt and red pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in peanut oil over medium-high heat.
Add chopped onions, garlic, and ginger; cook until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add water, ground peanuts, salt, and red pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Stir in green peppers and cook for 5 more minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and parsley before serving.

title: Touss
ingredients: 1/2 cup green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
Salt and red pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the millet thoroughly and soak for 30 minutes.
In a pot, sauté onion, garlic, and carrots in vegetable oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, green beans, salt, and red pepper; cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the soaked millet and add water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and parsley before serving.

title: Nyama Choma with Ugali
ingredients: 1 kg goat meat, cut into chunks
instructions: Season the goat meat with salt, garlic, and kachumbari spice, then marinate for 2 hours.
Boil the maize flour with a little water to form a stiff dough called ugali.
Heat oil in a grill pan over medium-high heat.
Grill the meat until the outside is charred and the inside is cooked through.
Serve the meat hot with the ugali and sliced onions.

title: Matoke (Ripe Banana Stew)
instructions: Peel and slice the ripe plantains into thick rounds.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until oily.
Stir in the plantain slices and coconut milk.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the plantains are tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Irio (Sweet Potato and Beans)
ingredients: 2 cups red sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Boil the soaked black-eyed peas until tender, then drain and mash with butter.
In a separate pot, boil the diced sweet potatoes until soft.
Sauté the onion and garlic in a pan until soft.
Mix the mashed beans into the sweet potato mixture.
Season with salt and pepper and stir well to combine.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Sukuma Wiki with Groundnut Sauce
ingredients: 1 bunch kale or collard greens, chopped
instructions: Blanch the chopped greens in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Grind the roasted groundnuts with water to make a smooth paste.
Sauté the onion and garlic in a pot until fragrant.
Add the peanut paste and stir in the remaining water to create a sauce.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes until it thickens.
Add the blanched greens to the sauce and cook for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and chili powder before serving.

title: Ugali with Mbeirik (Fish Stew)
instructions: Clean the fish and season with salt, turmeric, and chili powder.
Boil the maize flour with water to create a firm ugali dough.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until the oil separates.
Add the fish to the tomato sauce and simmer for 15 minutes.
Serve the fish stew alongside the ugali.

title: Bobotie
instructions: Fry the onions until soft and golden.
Mix the ground beef with turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, coriander, salt, and pepper.
Combine the fried onions with the spiced beef.
Soak the bread pieces in the milk.
Stir the soaked bread, beaten eggs, raisins, and apricot preserves into the beef mixture.
Place the mixture in a greased baking dish.
Cover with foil and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes until golden on top.
Serve warm with rice.

title: Biltong
ingredients: 1kg beef topside or fillet, sliced thinly
instructions: Combine vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, salt, pepper, coriander, cloves, nutmeg, onion, and garlic in a bowl.
Add the sliced beef to the marinade and mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Remove beef from marinade and pat dry with paper towels.
Thread the beef onto a drying rack or hang it in a well-ventilated area.
Leave to dry and cure for 2-3 days, turning occasionally.
Once dried to your desired texture, cut into strips and store in an airtight container.

title: Pap and Chakalaka
instructions: Add boiling water to maize meal gradually while stirring to form a smooth paste.
Cook the pap over low heat, stirring constantly for 20 minutes until thick and smooth.
Heat oil in a pan and fry onions until soft.
Add garlic, curry powder, turmeric, salt, and cook for 1 minute.
Add bell peppers, carrots, green beans, pumpkin, and tomatoes.
Simmer the vegetables for 15-20 minutes until tender.
Stir in raisins just before serving.
Serve the chakalaka alongside the pap.

title: Stew
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot over medium heat.
Remove beef and sauté onions, carrots, and garlic until softened.
Return beef to the pot and add tomato paste, salt, pepper, paprika, mixed spice, and bay leaf.
Stir in tomatoes and water or beef stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2 hours until beef is tender.
Add potatoes and cook for another 30 minutes until potatoes are soft.
Remove bay leaf and serve with pap.

title: Malva Pudding
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Add melted butter, milk, brown sugar, egg, and vanilla to the flour mixture.
Stir until smooth, then pour into a greased loaf tin.
Pour the boiling water over the batter gently.
Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
While pudding bakes, make the sauce by melting condensed milk, butter, flour, sugar, cornflour, and water in a saucepan.
Stir continuously until the sauce thickens.
Let the pudding cool slightly, then pour the warm sauce over it.
Serve warm with custard or cream.

title: Brik Tunisi
ingredients: 1 lb firm white cheese (jben or farmer's cheese)
instructions: Beat the whole eggs and add salt.
Crumble the cheese into the egg mixture.
Separate the egg whites and whip them until stiff peaks form.
Fold the whipped whites gently into the cheese mixture.
Cut each phyllo sheet in half and spread a quarter of the filling in the center.
Fold the sides over the filling to create a packet, then roll it up tightly.
Brush the outside with olive oil and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Chorba Salata
instructions: Soak the bulgur and chickpeas in water for 2 hours, then drain.
In a pot, bring the beef broth to a boil and add the soaked chickpeas.
Simmer for 45 minutes until chickpeas are tender.
Add the soaked bulgur to the pot and cook for another 15 minutes.
Stir in the toasted cumin seeds, salt, parsley, and mint.
Remove from heat and let it cool slightly.
Drizzle with olive oil and squeeze fresh lemon juice before serving.

title: Mloukhia with Lamb
ingredients: 3 cups fresh or frozen spinach leaves (mloukhia)
1/2 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté onions until soft.
Add garlic, lamb, and spices; cook until the meat is browned.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the soaked beans and cover with water; simmer for 1 hour.
Wash the spinach leaves thoroughly, remove stems, and chop coarsely.
Add the chopped spinach to the pot in batches, stirring constantly.
Continue cooking until the spinach breaks down and turns a deep green color.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with bread.

title: Brik Méchouia
instructions: Roast the tomatoes over an open flame until charred, then peel and mash them.
In a pan, cook the ground beef with onions, garlic, cumin, and paprika until browned.
Stir in the mashed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites; beat whites until stiff.
Fold the egg whites into the meat mixture.
Cut phyllo sheets in half, brush with oil, and spread a layer of the meat mixture.
Top with the beaten egg yolks and breadcrumbs, then fold the phyllo into a square.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on both sides.
Cut into squares and serve with salad.

title: Mechoui Lamb
ingredients: 1 whole lamb (approx. 10 lbs), cut into large pieces
instructions: Rub the lamb pieces with olive oil, garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
In a large pot, layer the onions at the bottom, followed by the lamb, then carrots and potatoes.
Pour tomato paste and a little water over the ingredients to create steam.
Cover the pot tightly with a heavy lid or aluminum foil.
Cook over low heat for 3 to 4 hours, adding water if necessary to keep it moist.
Check occasionally to ensure the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Once cooked, remove from heat and let rest for 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with bread.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons and Olives
ingredients: 2 preserved lemons, seeds removed and chopped
1/2 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons hot water
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Add chicken pieces, cumin, ginger, salt, and pepper; cook until the chicken is browned.
Stir in chopped preserved lemons and olives.
Pour in 2 cups of water, then add the saffron water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with bread or couscous.

title: Spiced Lamb and Potato Tagine
ingredients: 1 pound lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until golden brown.
Add lamb cubes, cinnamon, turmeric, and ginger; stir well to coat the meat.
Add potatoes, carrots, and apricots to the pot.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the lamb and vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Msemen (Moroccan Square Pancakes)
ingredients: 1/4 cup honey and orange blossom water, for serving
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl; gradually add warm water and knead until smooth.
Let the dough rest covered for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into a long strip, cut into 4 pieces, and flatten each into a square.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with olive oil.
Place a square on the griddle, cover, and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles form.
Flip, cook 1 more minute, then fold in half and press down firmly.
Cook another minute on the folded side, then fold again to make a triangle.
Repeat until the surface has many golden brown spots.
Serve warm with honey and orange blossom water.

title: Harira Soup
instructions: Sauté onions in olive oil until soft.
Add blended tomatoes, carrots, turmeric, cumin, and saffron; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in cooked chickpeas, lentils, and water or stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add broken vermicelli pasta and cook for another 5 minutes until pasta is soft.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish generously with chopped cilantro and parsley before serving.

title: Couscous with Seven Vegetables and Lamb
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil and brown the lamb with onion, ras el hanout, salt, and pepper.
Add carrots, zucchini, turnip, green beans, and peas; stir to combine.
Pour 1.5 cups of water over the mixture, cover, and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, place couscous in a large bowl and pour boiling water over it.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Drain any excess water from the couscous and toss with melted butter.
Steam the cooked vegetables over the couscous for 2 minutes to infuse flavor.
Serve the vegetables and lamb mixture on top of the fluffy couscous.

title: Doro Wat
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat until it foams.
Add the grated onion and fry until soft and slightly browned.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the berbere and atayit, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Pour in the water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken pieces, cover, and cook for 45 minutes.
Add the hard-boiled eggs and cook uncovered for another 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt before serving.

title: Misir Wot
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a pot until it foams.
Add the grated onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the berbere, atayit, and coriander, mixing well.
Add the rinsed lentils and stir to coat them in the spice.
