Pour in the water, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes or until lentils are tender.
Season with salt and serve hot with injera.

title: Tikil Gomen
ingredients: 4 cups fresh collard greens or kale, chopped
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the grated onion and fry until soft and fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the atayit, coriander, and ginger powder.
Add the chopped greens in batches, stirring to wilt them.
Pour in the water, cover, and cook on low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally and add more water if it dries out too much.

title: Shiro Wot
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a pot until it foams.
Add the grated onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the berbere, atayit, and coriander powder.
Gradually whisk in the chickpea flour to avoid lumps.
Slowly add the water while whisking continuously.
Cook on low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until thickened.

title: Gomen
ingredients: 4 cups fresh spinach or chard, chopped
instructions: Heat the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the grated onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the atayit and coriander powder.
Add the chopped greens in batches, stirring to wilt them.
Pour in the water, cover, and cook on low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally and add more water if it dries out too much.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long grain parboiled rice, washed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the blended peppers, tomato paste, curry, and thyme; cook until the raw smell disappears.
Stir in the blended tomatoes and stock, then add bay leaves, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Wash the rice thoroughly until the water runs clear, then add it to the pot.
Add the fried plantains and mixed vegetables on top of the rice.
Cover the pot tightly and cook over medium heat for about 30-40 minutes until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve hot.

title: Egusi Soup
ingredients: 2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), toasted and ground
1 large sheep or goat meat, cubed
instructions: Boil the meat and chicken until tender, then strain and reserve the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, onions, garlic, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Heat palm oil in a large pot and fry the blended paste until the oil separates and the paste darkens.
Stir in the ground egusi, crayfish powder, salt, and the reserved stock.
Add the cooked meat and chicken pieces to the pot.
Simmer on low heat for at least 45 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add fresh spinach or cocoyam leaves in the last 5 minutes of cooking until wilted.
Serve with steamed fufu or pounded yam.

title: Suya Skewers
ingredients: 500g beef mince or thinly sliced beef
Onion and tomato slices for garnish
instructions: Mix the beef mince with all the dry spices, salt, and chopped onions in a bowl.
Knead the mixture well until the spices are evenly distributed and the meat is tender.
Cover and refrigerate the meat mixture for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to meld.
Thread the seasoned meat onto wooden skewers, pressing firmly to compact.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or fryer over medium-high heat.
Fry the skewers until they are golden brown and crispy on the outside (about 3-4 minutes per side).
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with extra cayenne or salt if desired.
Serve immediately with lettuce leaves, onion, and tomato slices for wrapping.

title: Pounded Yam and Egusi Soup
ingredients: 3 kg yams, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups dried melon seeds (egusi), toasted and ground
1 large sheep or goat meat, cubed
instructions: Boil the yam chunks in water until very soft and easily mashed.
Transfer the boiled yam to a mortar and pound vigorously with a pestle until smooth and elastic.
Boil the meat and chicken until tender, then strain and reserve the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, onions, garlic, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Heat palm oil in a large pot and fry the blended paste until the oil separates.
Stir in the ground egusi, crayfish powder, salt, and the reserved stock.
Add the cooked meat and chicken pieces to the pot.
Simmer on low heat for at least 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add fresh spinach or cocoyam leaves in the last 5 minutes of cooking until wilted.
Serve the soup with the pounded yam.

title: Okra Stew (Okro)
ingredients: 1 kg fresh okra, sliced into rounds
Fresh fish (optional, added at the end)
instructions: Boil the meat until tender, then strain and reserve the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, onions, garlic, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Heat palm oil in a large pot and fry the blended paste until the oil separates and the paste darkens.
Add the stock, crayfish powder, salt, curry, thyme, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Add the cooked meat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced okra to the stew and cook on medium heat for about 15-20 minutes until the okra is tender but still holds its shape.
Stir occasionally to prevent the stew from becoming too thick or burning.
If using fresh fish, add it in the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot with rice or fufu.

title: Jollof Rice
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain parboiled rice, soaked and drained
2 cups mixed vegetables (corn, peas, carrots), blanched
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the blended tomato, pepper, onion mixture and cook until the oil separates and turns red.
Stir in garlic, ginger, curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and sugar, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Wash the soaked rice until the water runs clear, then drain well.
Add the rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain with the sauce.
Pour in the stock, ensuring the liquid level is about 1 cm above the rice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Gently fold in the blanched mixed vegetables.
Let the pot rest off the heat for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork and serving.

title: Waakye
ingredients: 1 cup black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Place the soaked black-eyed peas in a pot with 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Add the sasa leaves and baking soda to the pot, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour until the peas are partially cooked.
Add the rice to the pot with the peas and water.
Season with salt and stir gently.
Cook on low heat, covered, for about 30-40 minutes until both rice and peas are fully tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let it steam for 10 minutes before serving with shito, fried plantain, and boiled eggs.

title: Fufu and Light Soup
ingredients: 1 kg beef or goat meat, cut into pieces
2 cups water stock from the meat
Salt and seasoning cubes to taste
instructions: Combine cassava flour, plantain flour, and 1 cup of water in a bowl.
Knead the mixture vigorously with your hands until it forms a smooth, non-sticky dough, then steam for 20 minutes or until hot and firm.
In a separate pot, sauté the meat with onions, garlic, ginger, and spices until browned.
Add the tomato puree, hot pepper, ground crayfish, and stock.
Simmer the soup on low heat for 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and the meat is tender.
Serve the hot soup immediately with pieces of the steamed fufu.

title: Banku and Tilapia Stew
instructions: Mix corn flour, cassava flour, and salt in a large pot.
Add 1 cup of water and stir quickly over high heat to prevent lumps.
Gradually add the remaining water while stirring continuously until the mixture is smooth and starts to boil.
Reduce heat and cook for 20-30 minutes, stirring constantly until the banku is firm and elastic.
Season the fish with salt, ginger, and garlic, then grill or fry until golden.
In another pot, sauté onions, tomatoes, and peppers in palm oil until the oil turns red.
Add the crayfish and shrimp powder, then stir in the grilled fish.
Simmer the stew for 15 minutes before serving with the banku.

title: Red Red
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked and boiled until tender
1 cup water stock from the peas
instructions: Sauté onions, ginger, and garlic in palm oil until fragrant.
Add the blended tomatoes, peppers, and water stock, then cook until the oil separates.
Stir in the boiled black-eyed peas, salt, and seasoning cubes.
Simmer the stew for 15 minutes on low heat to thicken and blend the flavors.
Fry the sliced plantains in a little oil until golden brown.
Serve the red red stew hot with the fried plantains and a slice of fresh bread.

title: Thieboudienne (Senegalese Rice and Fish)
ingredients: 1 whole red snapper or sea bass, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Fry the fish pieces in oil until golden brown, then set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic in the same oil until soft.
Add the blended tomatoes, bay leaves, ginger, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Rinse the rice thoroughly and add it to the tomato sauce; add water to cover the rice by 2 inches.
Place the fried fish on top of the rice and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook for another 5 minutes until wilted.
Serve hot with a side of fried plantains.

title: Yassa (Chicken with Onions and Lemons)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the chicken with lemon zest, juice, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Layer half the sliced onions in a baking dish and top with the marinated chicken.
Pour the remaining onions over the chicken and drizzle with olive oil.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and onions are caramelized.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with rice.

title: Couscous with Vegetables and Meat
ingredients: Fresh parsley and mint for garnish
instructions: Brown the lamb cubes in a pot with oil, onion, garlic, turmeric, and cumin until golden.
Add the carrots, soaked peas, and chickpeas to the pot; add enough water to cover ingredients by 1 inch.
Simmer the stew for 1 hour until meat is tender and vegetables are soft.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and steam it over the hot stew for 5 minutes.
Mix the steamed couscous into the stew gently.
Stir in the green beans and cook for 3 more minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley and mint before serving.

title: Mafé (Peanut Stew with Chicken)
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 cup roasted peanuts, blended into a paste
instructions: Sauté chicken pieces in oil until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions and garlic until soft and translucent.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until oil separates.
Stir in the peanut paste, bay leaf, ginger, and salt; cook for 2 minutes to remove raw taste.
Return the chicken to the pot and add water to cover the ingredients by 1 inch.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the sauce is thick and chicken is tender.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with rice or boiled yam.

title: Salakieh (Spiced Lentil Soup)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add the rinsed lentils, coriander, cumin, turmeric, salt, and pepper; stir well.
Pour in the water or broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until lentils are soft and soup is thick.
Blend half of the soup with a stick blender for a creamier texture, leaving some chunks.
Stir the blended soup back into the pot and heat through.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

title: Sukuma Wiki with Onions
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped collard greens to the pot.
Season with salt and chili powder.
Cover and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.

title: Ugali (Maize Meal)
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Make a small well in the center of the boiling water.
Gradually pour in the maize flour while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Continue stirring vigorously to prevent lumps from forming.
Once the mixture thickens, reduce the heat to low.
Stir continuously for another 10 minutes until the ugali pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Shape the ugali into a mound and cover to keep warm.

title: Nyama Choma with Kachumbari
ingredients: 1 kg goat meat, cut into large chunks
instructions: Mix garlic, olive oil, salt, and cumin seeds to create a marinade.
Rub the marinade generously over the goat meat chunks.
Let the meat marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat a charcoal grill until the coals are white and hot.
Place the meat on the grill and cook, turning frequently, until the outside is charred and the inside is cooked through.
While the meat cooks, combine diced tomatoes, chopped onion, coriander, and chilies in a bowl.
Drizzle the kachumbari with a little olive oil and salt to taste.
Serve the grilled meat immediately with the fresh salad.

title: Githeri
ingredients: 1 cup dried red maize, soaked overnight
1/2 cup green beans, cut into pieces
instructions: Drain the soaked maize and beans.
Boil the maize and beans in fresh water with salt until they are almost tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the potato, carrot, and green beans to the pot.
Continue cooking until all vegetables are tender.
In a separate pan, sauté the chopped onion and garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add the sautéed mixture to the pot of githeri.
Simmer for another 10 minutes to blend the flavors.
Serve hot as a hearty main dish.

title: Pilipili (Chili Stew)
ingredients: 1 kg beef or goat meat, cubed
instructions: Boil the meat with a little water until it becomes soft.
While the meat cooks, sauté onions, garlic, and ginger in oil until soft.
Add the chopped chilies and tomato paste to the pan, cooking for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce, salt, and coriander powder.
Add the boiled meat and any remaining cooking liquid to the pan.
Simmer the stew on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the flavors meld.
Adjust seasoning with salt if needed and serve with ugali or rice.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: 1 kg mince beef, fried with onions and garlic
2 cups fresh bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Fry the mince beef with onions and garlic until browned.
Mix the beaten eggs, bread, coriander, ginger, curry powder, cinnamon, milk, and salt into a smooth paste.
Combine the beef mixture with the egg paste and dried fruit if using.
Spread the mixture into a greased baking dish.
Top with the mashed apricot jam.
Bake for 45 minutes until the top is golden and the center is set.

title: Pap and Beef Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the beef until browned.
Add onion and garlic, cook until soft.
Stir in tomato paste, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add crushed tomatoes, carrots, potatoes, and stock; simmer for 1 hour until meat is tender.
Meanwhile, mix maize meal with a little cold water to form a lump.
Add the lump to the boiling water and whisk vigorously to prevent lumps.
Cook the pap over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens.
Serve the hot pap alongside the beef stew.

title: Bunny Chow
ingredients: 500g beef or lamb curry, prepared separately
instructions: Prepare the curry by frying onion and garlic, then adding spices and cooking for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, soy sauce, sugar, and salt; simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix maize meal with a little cold water and add to boiling water, whisking until thick.
Let the pap cool slightly, then cut the loaves of bread in half horizontally.
Scrape out the soft center of the bread to create a bowl.
Fill the hollowed-out bread bowls generously with the hot curry.
Serve immediately with a side of pickle if desired.

title: Chakalaka
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and fry onions until translucent.
Add ginger and spices, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add bell peppers, carrots, and cauliflower; cook for 10 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in tomato paste and chopped tomatoes; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add beans and sugar; cook for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot as a relish with pap, rice, or bread.

title: Malva Pudding
ingredients: 2 tbsp flour, mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a 20cm square tin.
Mix flour, sugar, eggs, milk, vanilla, golden syrup, and melted butter until smooth.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 40-45 minutes until golden and springy to touch.
For the sauce, heat milk, butter, sugar, and golden syrup in a saucepan.
Stir in the flour-water mixture to thicken the sauce.
Add vanilla to the sauce and keep warm.
Cut the pudding into squares and serve immediately with the warm sauce poured over.

title: Lamb and Watercress Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
In a large pan, cook the onion until soft, then add the lamb mince and brown thoroughly.
Stir in the spinach and watercress, cooking until wilted.
Mix in the tomato paste and beef stock, simmer for 5 minutes.
Roll out the pastry and place half in a pie dish.
Fill with the lamb mixture and top with the remaining pastry.
Brush the top with beaten egg and cut vents in the lid.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Pavlova with Berries and Meringue
ingredients: 2 cups fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and draw a 20cm circle.
Whip egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar, vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla, whipping until stiff peaks form.
Pour mixture into the circle and smooth the top.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the door slightly ajar for 1 hour.
Cool completely before removing from the paper.
Whip the cream with a little sugar until soft peaks form.
Cover the pavlova with cream and arrange the berries and kiwi on top.
Dust with caster sugar and serve immediately.

title: Hāngī Pork with Root Vegetables
instructions: Season the pork and all vegetables generously with salt and pepper.
Place all ingredients into a large steam basket or pit liner.
Pour the water over the ingredients to create steam.
Cover the basket tightly with wet blankets or heavy-duty foil.
Place the covered basket into a pre-heated earth oven (hāngī) or a very hot oven.
Cook for 3 to 4 hours, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Check that the pork is tender and the vegetables are soft before serving.
Serve directly from the basket with the cooking juices.

title: Fish and Chips with Mushy Peas
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (such as snapper or cod), skin removed
4 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
instructions: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the potato chips in hot oil until golden and crispy; drain on paper towels.
Mix flour, potato flour, baking powder, and cold water to make a smooth batter.
Dredge the fish fillets in the batter and fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through.
Drain the fried fish on paper towels.
Rinse the dried peas and cook them with the onion, carrots, and butter until very soft.
Mash the peas and vegetables with a potato masher until smooth.
Serve the fish and chips immediately with a generous portion of mushy peas.

title: Vegetarian Kūmara and Sweet Potato Hash
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and garlic, sautéing until translucent.
Add the kūmara, regular potatoes, and pumpkin to the pan.
Sprinkle with paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper; stir to coat.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cover the pan and reduce heat to medium-low, cooking for another 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Uncover and increase heat to crisp the edges of the vegetables.
Stir in fresh coriander just before serving.
Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Cumberland Sauce with Roast Chicken
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Stir constantly for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and let cool before serving with roast chicken.

title: Fried Fish and Chips
ingredients: 400g white fish fillets, haddock or cod
instructions: Preheat oven to 200C and bake potatoes for 45 minutes until tender.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Gradually add cold water to make a thick batter.
Dip fish fillets into batter and fry in hot oil until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chips, lemon, and tartar sauce.

title: Hāngī (Geothermal) Pork and Potatoes
instructions: Layer vegetables and pork in a large earth oven pit.
Pour water over the ingredients to create steam.
Cover pit tightly with heated stones and damp earth.
Seal the pit to trap heat for 4-6 hours.
Uncover and serve the tender meat and vegetables with native honey.

title: Vegetable Pie (Aussie Style)
ingredients: 1 egg yolk, beaten with water for glaze
instructions: Sauté onion and vegetables in butter until soft.
Make a roux with flour and butter, then gradually add milk.
Simmer until thick, seasoning with salt and nutmeg.
Pour filling into a pie dish and cover with puff pastry.
Brush top with egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden.

title: Lobster Thermidor
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and stir in flour to make a roux.
Add wine, brandy, cream, and mustard, simmering until thick.
Stir in lobster meat, tarragon, and half the cheese.
Fill lobster shell with mixture and top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 180C for 20 minutes until bubbly and serve with lemon.

title: Meat Pie and Veggie Pie (Australia)
instructions: Cook the ground beef and onions in a pan until browned.
Stir in the beef stock and thyme, then simmer until thickened.
Roll out the pastry and line a pie dish, then add the meat filling.
Place remaining pastry on top, crimp edges to seal, and cut vents.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 40 minutes until golden.

title: Fish and Chips with Malt Vinegar (Australia)
ingredients: 1kg white fish fillets, such as cod or hoki
1 cup potato, cut into thick chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 100°C and bake chips for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep fryer to 180°C.
Mix flour and baking powder in a bowl.
Dip fish fillets in the flour mixture, then fry until golden.
Drain fish on paper towels, serve with baked chips and malt vinegar.

title: Lambs Suckling Pig Roast (New Zealand)
instructions: Season the pig inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with lemon halves, onions, and carrots.
Place the pig in a roasting pan with potatoes around it.
Roast at 180°C for 3-4 hours until tender and golden.
Rest the pig for 20 minutes before carving and serving.

title: Hāngi (New Zealand)
instructions: Dig a pit and line it with stones, then heat them in a fire.
Place vegetables and meat on a banana leaf-lined tray.
Cover the tray with more banana leaves and soil to seal.
Bury the tray in the hot stones and cover with more earth.
Wait 2-3 hours, then dig out the hāngi and serve immediately.

title: Tim Tam Slam (Australia)
instructions: Crush the Tim Tam biscuits into fine crumbs.
Mix the crumbs with warm milk and sugar until smooth.
Pour the mixture into hot coffee or tea.
Stir well and drink while warm for an energy boost.
Optional: Add extra milk for a creamier texture.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 4 cups mashed potatoes, mixed with butter and milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Add lamb, carrots, peas, and thyme; cook until lamb is browned.
Stir in mixed greens and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer mixture to a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and smooth the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Lamingtons
ingredients: 1 pack (500g) sponge cake, cut into squares
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Mix sugar, butter, and baking powder; add eggs and vanilla.
Bake cake squares until lightly golden.
Dip each cake square into vanilla icing.
Roll in a mixture of shredded and desiccated coconut.
Place on baking tray and bake for 10 minutes.
Cool completely before serving.

title: Hāngī (Earth Oven) Lamb
instructions: Prepare hāngi by heating stones in a fire until glowing.
Place vegetables in a basket and cover with leaves.
Add lamb chops to the basket.
Cover basket with more leaves and place on hot stones.
Seal the pit with earth and rocks.
Let it cook for 3-4 hours.
Uncover and serve immediately.

title: Mince Pies
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Sauté onion and carrot in butter until soft.
Add mince, spices, sugar, and dried fruits; cook until mince is browned.
Mix flour and water to make a dough.
Roll out dough and cut into circles.
Fill circles with mince mixture and seal edges.
Brush tops with beaten egg and bake for 20 minutes.
Cool before serving.

title: Kūmara and Potato Chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Slice kūmara and potatoes into thin strips.
Toss vegetables in olive oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Arrange on baking trays in a single layer.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Serve warm or cold with dipping sauce.

title: Lamb and Leek Pie
instructions: Season lamb shoulder and sear in olive oil until browned, then remove.
Sauté onion, garlic, and leeks until soft.
Add lamb mince, tomato paste, stock, and gravy; simmer for 30 minutes.
Let filling cool completely.
Roll out pastry, place in pie dish, add filling, and cover with top pastry.
Brush edges with beaten egg and cut steam vents.
Bake at 200°C for 40 minutes until golden and puffed.

title: Pavlova with Berries
instructions: Whip egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar while whipping until stiff peaks form.
Fold in vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla.
Spoon mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 150°C for 1 hour, then turn off oven and cool inside.
Serve topped with whipped cream and mixed berries.

title: Vindaloo Chicken
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, cut into pieces
4 dried red chilies, soaked and chopped
instructions: Marinate chicken with turmeric, cumin, and half the ginger for 2 hours.
Sauté onions, garlic, and chilies in oil until soft.
Add marinated chicken and cook until browned.
Stir in tamarind paste, tomato paste, stock, and remaining ginger.
Simmer covered for 40 minutes until chicken is tender.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

title: Mince Pies with Custard
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, salt, and butter until crumbly; add water to form dough.
Fry mince, carrots, and onion until soft; stir in raisins, brown sugar, and spice.
Divide dough into balls, flatten, fill with mince mixture, and seal.
Place on baking tray, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 180°C for 25 minutes.
Whisk eggs, milk, and vanilla for custard; pour over warm pies.
Serve immediately.

title: Tamaki Sushi Rolls
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear; cook with water and rice vinegar mixture.
Season rice with sugar and salt; spread on bamboo mat.
Place nori on mat, spread rice evenly, and leave 1-inch border.
Arrange carrot, prawns, chicken, sesame seeds, and mayonnaise in center.
Roll tightly using bamboo mat and press firmly.
Slice into 6 pieces and serve with extra sesame seeds.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 2 cups mashed potatoes, salted and buttered
instructions: Brown the lamb mince in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and cook until soft.
Stir in the peas, carrots, beef stock, and tomato paste.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with the mashed potatoes and flatten the surface.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden.

title: Mince Pies
instructions: Rub the flour and cold butter together until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add sugar and mix until the dough forms a ball.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Cook the beef mince with diced apple, cinnamon, and mixed spice until tender.
Roll out the dough and cut into circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle and fold over to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.

title: Vegemite on Toast
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Spread butter generously on one side of each slice.
Place the buttered sides down on a baking sheet.
Top with a thin layer of Vegemite.
Broil for 1-2 minutes until the Vegemite is slightly bubbly.

title: Kōura (Freshwater Crayfish)
instructions: Melt the butter in a large bowl.
Add lemon juice, chopped parsley, and paprika to the butter.
Toss the cooked kōura in the butter mixture until well coated.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Manuka Honey Scones
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and grease a baking tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and manuka honey in a bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture looks like crumbs.
Stir in the sour cream and egg until a dough forms.
Roll out the dough and cut into rounds.
Place on the tray and bake for 12-15 minutes until golden.

title: Aussie Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Mix cooked beef, vegetables, cornstarch, and soy sauce in a bowl.
Roll out puff pastry and cut into 6 circles.
Spoon filling into pastry circles and fold edges to seal.
Place on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake for 25 minutes until golden.
Let cool for 5 minutes before serving.

title: New Zealand Lamb and Leek Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Sauté leeks in a pan until soft, then add lamb mince and cook until browned.
Stir in flour and beef stock, simmer until thickened.
Roll out puff pastry, place filling in the center, and fold edges over.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30 minutes until pastry is golden and flaky.
Serve hot.

title: Kangaroo Steak with Blueberry Sauce
instructions: Season kangaroo steaks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over high heat and sear steaks for 3 minutes per side.
Remove steaks and let rest for 5 minutes.
In the same pan, add blueberries, balsamic vinegar, and honey.
Simmer for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Slice steaks and serve with blueberry sauce.

title: Kiwi Kiwifruit and Honey Yogurt Parfait
instructions: Layer half the yogurt in glasses.
Add half the kiwifruit and drizzle with honey.
Repeat layers with remaining yogurt and fruit.
Top with granola and chopped mint.
Serve immediately.

title: Aussie BBQ Ribs with Pineapple Glaze
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) for slow roasting.
Baste ribs with a mix of soy sauce and mustard, then roast for 3 hours.
Meanwhile, combine brown sugar, ketchup, and remaining soy sauce in a saucepan.
Simmer glaze for 10 minutes until thickened.
Brush ribs with glaze and grill for 5 minutes per side.
Serve with grilled pineapple chunks.

title: Meat Pie with Flaky Pastry
instructions: Heat butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add beef mince and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in beef stock and Worcestershire sauce; simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roll out pastry and cut into circles to line pie tins.
Fill tins with meat mixture and crimp edges to seal.
Brush tops with beaten egg and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Mix sweetened condensed milk and boiling water in a bowl.
Stir in flour and vanilla until a thick icing forms.
Dip sponge cake cubes into the icing, ensuring they are fully coated.
Roll the iced cubes in chocolate sprinkles.
Place on a wire rack and refrigerate for 1 hour to set.
Roll the iced cubes in coconut flakes.
Serve chilled.

title: Hāngī (Geothermal Roast) Lamb
instructions: Mix softened butter, salt, and crushed garlic in a large bowl.
Place lamb, potatoes, pumpkin, carrots, kumara, and spring onions in a large hāngī pot.
Rub the butter mixture generously over the lamb and vegetables.
Layer the vegetables around the lamb to create a bed.
Cover the pot tightly with dampened hāngī cloths or foil to trap steam.
Place the covered pot over the hot rocks in the earth oven.
Cook for 3-4 hours until the lamb is tender and vegetables are soft.
Remove carefully and let rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Hāngī (Geothermal Roast) Lamb
instructions: Mix softened butter, salt, and crushed garlic in a large bowl.
Place lamb, potatoes, pumpkin, carrots, kumara, and spring onions in a large hāngī pot.
Rub the butter mixture generously over the lamb and vegetables.
Layer the vegetables around the lamb to create a bed.
Cover the pot tightly with dampened hāngī cloths or foil to trap steam.
Place the covered pot over the hot rocks in the earth oven.
Cook for 3-4 hours until the lamb is tender and vegetables are soft.
Remove carefully and let rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Fish and Chips with Malt Vinegar
instructions: Mix flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add ice-cold water gradually to make a thick batter.
Cut fish into portions and season lightly with salt.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 180°C (350°F).
Dip fish pieces into the batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Fry in batches for 4-5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with malt vinegar and lemon wedges.

title: Mutton Bird Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Sauté onion and carrots in a pan until soft.
Add mutton bird mince, peas, tomato paste, and stock; simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer mixture to a pie dish and cover with puff pastry.
Brush pastry with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden and cooked through.

title: Hāngī Lamb and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 kg sweet potatoes, cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat hāngi earth oven to 100°C (212°F) using hot rocks.
Layer vegetables and herbs on the hot rocks.
Place lamb on top of the vegetables.
Cover the pit tightly with wet mats and soil to trap steam.
Cook for 4 hours until lamb is tender and vegetables are soft.
Remove and serve immediately with the cooking juices.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets, such as cod or snapper
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and cayenne pepper in a bowl.
Dip fish fillets first in beaten egg, then in the flour mixture.
Fry potato chips in hot oil until golden and crisp; drain.
Deep fry fish fillets in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Serve fish on a bed of chips with lemon wedges and salt and vinegar.

title: Kaiako's Seafood Chowder
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, celery, and carrots until soft.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw flour taste.
Gradually add seafood stock and milk, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Add potatoes and paprika; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add mixed seafood and cook for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Pāua Salad
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and red onion in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, and mustard.
Season dressing with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Top with sliced pāua meat.
Garnish with fresh dill and serve immediately.

title: Lamb and Leek Pie
instructions: Brown the lamb mince in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions, potatoes, carrots, and leeks; cook until softened.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually add beef stock while stirring.
Simmer until the filling thickens and potatoes are tender.
Roll out pastry and place in a pie dish, filling with the mixture.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal edges, and cut vents.
Bake at 200°C for 45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Māori Hangi
instructions: Dig a pit in the ground and line it with cabbage leaves.
Place hot stones in the pit and cover with more cabbage leaves.
Season the meat and vegetables with salt water and arrange them on the stones.
Cover the pit with earth and let it cook for 3-4 hours.
Uncover and serve the steaming food immediately.

title: Crispy Fish and Chips
instructions: Fry potato chips in oil until golden and crisp, then drain.
Dredge fish fillets in flour, dip in beaten eggs, and coat with panko breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 180°C and fry fish fillets until golden and cooked through.
Drain fish on paper towels and sprinkle with salt.
Serve fish and chips with lemon wedges.

title: Polynesian Coconut Rice
instructions: Combine rice, coconut milk, water, brown sugar, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in shredded coconut and vanilla extract.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Baked Ham with Honey and Mustard Glaze
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Mix honey, mustard, soy sauce, brown sugar, and garlic powder to make the glaze.
Place ham in a baking dish and brush with half the glaze.
Add pineapple chunks and green beans to the dish.
Bake for 2 hours, basting with glaze every 30 minutes.
Increase oven temperature to 400°F (200°C) for the last 10 minutes to caramelize the glaze.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in butter until softened.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Pour in stock and thyme, simmer until chicken is tender.
Stir in cream and season with salt and pepper.
Roll out pastry and fit into a pie dish.
Pour filling into pastry case.
Cover with remaining pastry, crimp edges, and cut vents.
Brush with egg wash and bake for 30-40 minutes until golden.

title: Hāngī Lamb
ingredients: 2 kg pumpkin, cut into large chunks
1 kg sweet potato, cut into large chunks
2 kg kumara, cut into large chunks
instructions: Prepare the hāngī pit and heat stones until very hot.
Place meat in a large iron or steel pot with butter and stock.
Add potatoes, pumpkin, sweet potato, kumara, onions, and garlic around the meat.
Season everything with salt and pepper.
Cover the pot tightly with a metal lid or foil.
Place the pot over the hot stones in the pit.
Cover the entire pit with wet earth and leaves to seal heat.
Cook for 3-4 hours, checking periodically to ensure even cooking.
Remove pot and let rest before serving.

title: Keiki Kūmara
ingredients: 1 kg kūmara (sweet potato), peeled and cubed
instructions: Toast cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Grind seeds into a coarse powder.
Toss kūmara cubes with olive oil, ground spices, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Spread on a baking sheet and roast at 200°C (400°F) for 30 minutes.
Flip the kūmara and continue roasting for another 20 minutes until tender.
Remove from oven and immediately toss with cilantro, mint, and lemon juice.
Serve warm as a side dish.

title: Ahi Poke Bowl
ingredients: 400 g fresh tuna, diced into small cubes
instructions: In a bowl, mix soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, wasabi, ginger, and garlic.
Toss diced tuna with the marinade and let sit for 10 minutes.
Cook rice according to package instructions and keep warm.
Arrange rice in bowls.
Top with marinated tuna, edamame, cucumber, and avocado.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.
Serve immediately.

title: Mutton Stew
instructions: Toss mutton cubes with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown mutton on all sides.
Remove mutton and set aside.
Sauté onions in the same pot until softened.
Add carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Return mutton to the pot and add stock, water, bay leaf, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours.
Add potatoes and continue simmering for 30 minutes until tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

title: Sausage and Potato Campfire
instructions: Bring water to boil in a large pot.
Add potatoes and boil for 10 minutes until tender.
Add sausages to the pot.
Cook for another 15 minutes until sausages are browned and cooked through.
Drain and serve with crusty bread.

title: Hāngī Lamb and Potatoes
ingredients: 2 kg lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
1 kg potatoes, cut into large chunks
instructions: Prepare the hāngī earth oven and heat the rocks until very hot.
Place meat, potatoes, sweet potatoes, kūmara, and herbs in a large woven basket.
Pour beef stock over the vegetables and meat.
Cover the basket tightly with wet leaves or a liner.
Bury the basket in the hot rocks for 3 to 4 hours until meat is tender and vegetables are soft.

title: Vegemite on Toast
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Spread softened butter evenly over both sides of the toast.
Rub one side of each slice with Vegemite.
Top with the buttered side and spread a thin layer of honey on the Vegemite side.
Cut in half and serve immediately.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Dip cake squares into the melted chocolate mixture.
Allow excess chocolate to drip off.
Immediately roll each piece in desiccated coconut to coat completely.
Place on a tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes to set.
Serve chilled.

title: Pavlova with Fresh Fruit
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
1 cup mixed berries and sliced kiwifruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar, vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla while beating until stiff peaks form.
Fold in the whipped cream gently.
Pipe the mixture onto a baking sheet in a mound shape.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Top with fresh fruit before serving.

title: Aussie Meat Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Mix beef, onion, stock, and milk in a bowl until combined.
Roll out dough and cut into 6 circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle, then fold and crimp edges to seal.
Brush tops with beaten egg and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden.

title: New Zealand Lamb Chop with Rosemary
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season lamb chops generously with salt, pepper, and chopped rosemary.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sear chops for 3-4 minutes per side until medium-rare.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Kiwi Pavlova
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form, gradually adding sugar.
Fold in vinegar and vanilla.
Pipe or spread mixture onto a baking sheet to form a circle.
Bake for 1 hour, then cool in oven for another hour.
Top with whipped cream and sliced kiwifruit before serving.

title: Lemon Myrtle Chicken
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and crushed lemon myrtle.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add lemon juice to the pan, then stir in spinach until wilted.
Serve chicken over the lemon myrtle spinach.

title: Shepherd's Pie (Aussie Style)
instructions: Brown lamb, onion, peas, and carrots in a large pan.
Stir in stock and tomato paste, simmer for 10 minutes.
Mash potatoes with butter, salt, and pepper.
Spread meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and smooth the surface.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes until topping is golden.

title: Traditional Aussie Meat Pie
instructions: Brown the beef mince in a pan over medium heat until no longer pink.
Add the chopped onion, carrot, and garlic; cook until softened.
Stir in tomato paste, beef stock, and peas; simmer for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roll out puff pastry and line a pie dish, pressing into edges.
Pour filling into the pastry shell.
Cover with remaining pastry, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits in top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden.

title: Kiwi Pavlova
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, beat egg whites, vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla until foamy.
Gradually add sugar and cream of tartar, beating until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Shape the meringue onto the prepared baking sheet into a circle.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off oven and let cool inside for 1 hour.
Whip cream until soft peaks form.
Gently spread whipped cream over the cooled meringue.
Top with mixed berries and serve immediately.

title: Classic Lamingtons
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in buttermilk.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients until just combined.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Spoon batter into a greased loaf tin.
Bake for 50-60 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Dip each cube in chocolate icing, roll in coconut.
Serve chilled.

title: Hāngī Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 3kg pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
instructions: Layer the pork at the bottom of a large pit or oven-safe vessel.
Arrange potatoes, sweet potatoes, kumara, green beans, pumpkin, and corn on top of the meat.
Scatter spring onions, garlic heads, and water over the vegetables.
Cover tightly with wet newspaper or foil to seal in steam.
Heat the earth oven to 150°C (300°F) using heated stones.
Place the covered vessel on the hot stones and cook for 4-5 hours.
Remove the cover carefully and let steam escape for 10 minutes.
Serve the tender meat and vegetables directly from the vessel.

title: Pavlova with Passionfruit Sauce
ingredients: 4 large egg whites, at room temperature
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, beat egg whites, vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla until foamy.
Gradually add sugar and cream of tartar, beating until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Shape the meringue onto the prepared baking sheet into a circle.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off oven and let cool inside for 1 hour.
Whip cream until soft peaks form.
Mix passionfruit pulp and juice together for the sauce.
Gently spread whipped cream over the cooled meringue.
Drizzle passionfruit sauce over the cream and garnish with mint.

title: Australian Meat Pies
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and cook onion and carrots until soft.
Add beef mince and cook until browned, then stir in stock and tomato paste.
Simmer until liquid reduces and mixture is thick.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roll out pastry and cut into circles, place filling in center, and fold over to seal.
Brush tops with beaten egg and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Let cool slightly before serving.

title: New Zealand Lagenella (Lagenella Stew)
instructions: Brown lamb cubes in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onion and cook until translucent.
Stir in coriander and cumin, then add stock, potatoes, and carrots.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1.5 hours until lamb is tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Aussie Vegemite and Ham Sandwich
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden.
Spread butter on one side of each slice.
Spread Vegemite on the unbuttered side of two slices.
Layer ham on the Vegemite side.
Top with the remaining two slices, buttered side down.
Drizzle with honey and cut in half.

title: Kiwi Pavlova with Fresh Berries
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F).
Whip egg whites until soft peaks form, gradually add sugar and beat until stiff.
Fold in vinegar, cornstarch, and vanilla.
Shape mixture onto a lined baking tray and create a peak in the center.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off oven and leave to cool inside for 1 hour.
Top with whipped cream and fresh berries before serving.

title: New Zealand Pavlova with Passionfruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Beat egg whites until foamy, gradually add sugar and beat until glossy.
Add vinegar, cornflour, and vanilla, then spread onto a baking sheet.
Bake for 1 hour, then cool in the turned-off oven.
Whip cream and spread over the cooled meringue.
Top with passionfruit pulp and serve immediately.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the minced lamb with onion and tomato paste.
Add beef stock and simmer until thickened.
Spread vegetable mixture over the meat base.
Top with mashed potato and bake until golden.

title: Pavlova
instructions: Whip egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Fold in vinegar and spread onto a baking sheet.
Bake at low temperature until dry but marshmallowy.
Cool completely and top with whipped cream and berries.

title: Corned Beef and Cabbage
instructions: Place beef, onion, carrots, and spices in a large pot.
Add water and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Add cabbage wedges and bay leaves.
Cook covered for 3-4 hours until tender.
Remove bay leaves and serve with cabbage.

title: Hāngi
instructions: Dig a pit and layer with hot stones and ash.
Place vegetables and meat in a woven basket.
Cover the basket with more hot stones and soil.
Cook for 3-4 hours until food is tender.
Uncover, fluff the soil, and serve immediately.

title: Lamingtons
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, milk, and eggs to make sponge.
Cut into squares and dip in melted chocolate.
Roll in desiccated coconut immediately.
Melt remaining chocolate with icing sugar and milk for glaze.
Drizzle over finished lamingtons and chill.

title: Western Australian Bush Tomatoes with Salt and Pepper
ingredients: 1 kg fresh bush tomatoes, peeled and halved
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and plunge bush tomatoes for 30 seconds until skin loosens.
Transfer to ice water, then peel and halve the tomatoes.
Toss tomatoes with salt, pepper, and olive oil in a large bowl.
Arrange on a baking tray and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until caramelized.
Serve warm topped with torn basil leaves.

title: Perth Seafood Chowder
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onions until soft.
Add cauliflower and potatoes, stirring for 5 minutes.
Pour in milk and cream, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and white pepper, then garnish with parsley.

title: Rockingham Rock Oysters on the Half Shell
instructions: Scrub oyster shells gently under cold running water to remove debris.
Shuck oysters carefully, keeping the meat in the deeper top shell.
Melt garlic butter and brush lightly over each oyster.
Arrange on a preheated baking sheet at 200°C for 5 minutes until edges curl.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges, salt, and dill.

title: Yanchep Clam Chowder
instructions: Sauté carrots, celery, and onions in a pot until translucent.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw taste.
Add clams and stock, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until clams open.
Stir in milk and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Esperance Salmon with Native Spinach
instructions: Season salmon fillets with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Sear salmon skin-side down in a hot pan for 4 minutes until crisp.
Flip and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Sauté native spinach in the same pan with lemon juice and honey for 3 minutes.
Serve salmon topped with spinach and fresh mint leaves.

title: Cassowary and Pumpkin Stew
ingredients: 1kg cassowary meat, cubed and marinated in Tasmanian peppermint vinegar
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the cassowary meat with salt and pepper, then sear in a large pot until browned.
Add the crushed garlic, thyme, and stock, bringing to a simmer.
Stir in the chopped pumpkin and reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook gently for 2.5 hours until the meat is tender and pumpkin is soft.
Remove thyme stems and adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Tasmanian Sea Bass with Smoked Salmon and Dill
ingredients: 2 whole sea bass, cleaned and scaled
instructions: Score the sea bass skin and rub with half the lemon juice and olive oil.
Grill the fish skin-side down until crispy, about 8 minutes per side.
Whisk the melted butter with lemon zest, dill, and remaining lemon juice.
Serve the fish on a bed of dill, drizzle with the butter sauce, and top with smoked salmon slices.
Garnish with extra dill and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Fried Saltwater Croaker with Saltbush
ingredients: 8 whole saltwater croaker, gutted and cleaned
1 cup flour, mixed with 1 tsp salt
instructions: Mix flour, saltbush, cornstarch, and salt to create a dry coating mix.
Dip each fish fillet into the beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in the saltbush flour mix.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 175°C.
Fry the fish in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden and flaky.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Oyster Stew with Wild Herbs
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and sauté the onion, celery, and fennel until soft.
Add the white wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the oysters gently and cook for just 2 minutes.
Pour in the cream and simmer for another 5 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and white pepper, then garnish with fresh parsley.

title: Baked Potato with Smashed Tasmanian Salmon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and prick the potatoes all over with a fork.
Rub potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then bake for 1 hour until soft.
Meanwhile, marinate the salmon in lemon juice and half the olive oil for 30 minutes.
Bake the salmon skin-side down for 12-15 minutes until cooked through.
Top the baked potatoes with smashed salmon, spring onions, coriander, and a dollop of yogurt.

title: Chicken and Potato Kiekie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Heat oil in a large baking dish over medium-high heat.
Season chicken and potatoes with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden, then flip.
Add onions, garlic, and potatoes around the chicken.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Stir in peas and roast for another 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.

title: Lambs Head Soup
instructions: Place lamb head in a large pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any scum, then reduce heat to simmer for 2 hours.
Add onions, carrots, celery, and bay leaves.
Simmer gently for another 1.5 hours until meat falls off the bone.
Remove meat from bones and shred finely.
Strain broth and return to pot.
Add shredded meat back into broth, season with salt.
Serve hot garnished with fresh coriander.

title: Hāngi Pork and Vegetables
ingredients: 2 kg pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Dig a pit in the ground and line with wet towels or banana leaves.
Pile hot rocks from a fire into the pit.
Place pork, vegetables, onion, and salt in a large earth oven bag or tray.
Add water to steam the tea leaves, then cover tightly.
Bury the tray in the hot rocks and cover with soil.
Wait 4 hours for the food to cook slowly.
Uncover and serve immediately.

title: Manuka Honey and Lemon Chicken
instructions: Mix honey, lemon juice, zest, soy sauce, oil, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Marinate chicken in the mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill or oven to 200°C (400°F).
Grill or bake chicken for 20-25 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Baste with remaining marinade during cooking.
Let rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Ngāi Tahu Style Fish and Chips
ingredients: 1 kg hoki or snapper fillets, skin on
1 kg potatoes, cut into thick chips
instructions: Make a batter by mixing flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, and water until smooth.
Fry potato chips in hot oil until golden and crispy, then drain.
Dredge fish fillets lightly in flour.
Dip fish into the batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Fry fish in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until batter is golden and fish is flaky.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with chips and a side of coleslaw.

title: Hāngi Pork and Potatoes
instructions: Mix beer, coriander, pepper, garlic, and ginger to create a marinade.
Combine pork, potatoes, sweet potatoes, kūmara, and spring onions in a large bowl.
Pour the marinade over the vegetables and meat, toss to coat, and let sit for 2 hours.
Prepare a hāngi pit by piling hot stones and wrapping them in wet hessian.
Place the marinated ingredients in a large cloth-lined pit over the stones.
Cover the pit with earth and seal tightly to trap the steam.
Cook for 3 to 4 hours until the pork is tender and vegetables are soft.
Uncover, let steam escape, and serve immediately.

title: Kūmara Pie with Whipped Custard
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
Gradually fold in the flour and egg yolk to form a smooth dough.
Press the dough into a pie dish to form the base and sides.
Place the kūmara cubes in the pie shell.
Whisk the milk, eggs, vanilla, and 200ml cream together.
Pour the mixture over the kūmara.
In a separate bowl, whisk the remaining cream with 100g sugar and cornstarch until thick.
Pour the custard mixture over the kūmara layer.
Bake for 45 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is set.
Serve warm.

title: Cottage Pie with Corned Beef
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté the onions, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add the ground lamb and corned beef, cooking until browned.
Stir in tomato paste, beef stock, and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer the mixture for 20 minutes until thickened.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the meat mixture in a baking dish.
Use a fork to create a textured surface on the potato layer.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes until the top is golden brown.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Fish and Chips with Kelp Sauce
instructions: Cut the fish into 2cm thick strips.
In a bowl, mix flour, baking powder, and salt.
Dip each fish strip first into the beaten eggs, then into the flour mixture, ensuring it is well coated.
Deep fry the potato chips until golden and crispy.
In a separate pan, fry the fish strips in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Drain the fish and chips on paper towels.
Mix the chopped kelp into the mayonnaise to create the sauce.
Serve the fish and chips with the kelp sauce and lemon wedges.

title: Pāua Salad with Avocado
ingredients: 200g pāua meat, cleaned and sliced thinly
instructions: Wash and dry the mixed salad leaves and place them in a large bowl.
Add the diced cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and avocado to the salad.
Gently toss the vegetables and greens together.
In a small bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss lightly to coat.
Top with the thinly sliced pāua meat.
Sprinkle the chopped coriander over the top.
Serve immediately to prevent the avocado from browning.

title: Lamb and Leek Pie
ingredients: 1 kg New Zealand lamb shoulder, cubed
instructions: Brown the lamb in a large pot with a little oil over medium-high heat.
Add onion and carrots, cook until softened.
Stir in wine and tomato paste, scrape up browned bits.
Add stock and leeks, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 1.5 hours until lamb is tender.
Mash some of the leeks and stock to create a thick gravy.
Add peas and season with salt and pepper.
Roll out pastry and place in a deep pie dish.
Pour lamb mixture into the pastry shell.
Fold pastry over to cover, crimp edges, and cut vents.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden.

title: Fillets of Cod in Cream Sauce
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Sauté shallots in butter until soft.
Deglaze pan with white wine, scraping up browned bits.
Add cream and simmer until slightly thickened.
Season sauce with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Place potatoes on a serving platter.
Season cod fillets with salt and pepper.
Sear cod in a separate pan with a little butter for 2 minutes per side.
Gently fold spinach into the cream sauce.
Arrange cod on potatoes, spoon sauce and spinach over fillets, and garnish with parsley.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry with Rice
ingredients: 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions and keep warm.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and chicken, stir-fry until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil, broccoli, capsicum, and peas to the wok.
Stir-fry vegetables for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return chicken to the wok.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and cornstarch slurry.
Toss quickly until sauce thickens and coats everything.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve over rice.

title: Hāngī-Style Steamed Pork and Root Vegetables
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into chunks
2 kg pumpkin, cut into large chunks
instructions: Preheat a hāngi pit or oven to 180°C with rocks heated for several hours.
Place potatoes, sweet potatoes, kumara, and pumpkin in a large baking dish.
Season vegetables generously with salt, pepper, and rosemary.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil and water.
In a separate bowl, mix pork with honey, butter, and salt.
Arrange pork on top of the vegetables.
Cover the dish tightly with foil or a lid.
Place the dish in the hot pit or oven for 2.5 hours.
Check halfway through; if needed, add a little more water to keep steam going.
Serve hot with the juices from the pot.

title: Fish and Chips with Tartar Sauce
ingredients: 6 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
instructions: Soak potato chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Fry chips in oil at 160°C until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Raise oil temperature to 190°C.
Whisk together plain flour, self-raising flour, and a pinch of salt.
Gradually add cold water to make a thick batter.
Dip fish strips into batter and fry for 3-4 minutes until crispy and cooked through.
Drain fish on paper towels and season with salt.
Mix mayonnaise, capers, lemon juice, and parsley for tartar sauce.
Serve chips and fish with tartar sauce, salt, vinegar, pickles, and onion.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Curry with Naan
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook until browned on all sides, then remove.
In the same pot, sauté onion until soft, then add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in curry paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot, add stock and potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add green beans and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot with naan bread and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Smashed Avocado with Feta and Lime
instructions: Cut avocados in half, remove pits, and scoop flesh into a bowl.
Mash avocados with a fork until chunky.
Stir in olive oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Fold in feta cheese and coriander.
Top with sliced red onion.
Serve immediately on toasted sourdough bread.

title: Barramundi with Lemon Butter Sauce
instructions: Season fillets with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook fillets for 3 minutes per side until flaky.
Remove fish and set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté garlic for 30 seconds.
Add lemon juice, zest, and wine if using; simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in parsley and return fish to the pan to warm through.
Serve with steamed vegetables.

title: Lamb Koftas with Mint Chutney
ingredients: 1 tablespoon fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Mix lamb, grated onion, yogurt, spices, and herbs in a bowl until well combined.
Shape mixture into small oval koftas.
Heat oil in a pan and fry koftas for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Brush with lemon juice during cooking.
Serve hot with mint chutney and naan bread.

title: Sourdough and Veggie Frittata
ingredients: 1/2 cup sourdough bread, torn into chunks
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Sauté zucchini, capsicum, and tomatoes until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in sourdough chunks and pour egg mixture over the vegetables.
Sprinkle with feta and basil.
Cook on stovetop until edges set, then transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C for 10 minutes until puffed and set.
Slice and serve warm.

title: Melbourne-Style Chicken in Red Wine and Tomato Sauce
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear chicken until golden brown on both sides.
Remove chicken and set aside; add onion to the pot and sauté until soft.
Add garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and oregano, then return chicken to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Traditional Melbourne Vegemite Toast with Butter
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden and crisp.
Spread a generous layer of softened butter on each slice of warm toast.
Mix Vegemite with a teaspoon of water or lemon juice to create a smooth paste.
Spread the Vegemite paste evenly over the buttered toast.
Sprinkle with a pinch of paprika if desired and serve immediately.

title: Melbourne Braised Lamb Shanks with Root Vegetables
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season lamb shanks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-based casserole dish over medium-high heat and sear lamb on all sides until browned.
Remove lamb and add carrots, celery, and onions to the pot; sauté until slightly softened.
Return lamb to the pot, then add beef stock, red wine, bay leaves, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours until lamb is tender and falling off the bone.
Remove bay leaves and rosemary sprigs before serving.

title: Classic Melbourne Cabbage Roll with Tomato Sauce
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Plain white bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Remove outer leaves from the cabbage and boil the head until leaves are pliable enough to roll.
In a large pan, cook ground meat with onion and carrots until browned and water evaporates.
Stir in tomato sauce, beef stock, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove cabbage leaves from boiling water and let cool slightly.
Place a spoonful of meat mixture in the center of each leaf, roll tightly, and place in a pot seam-side down.
Pour remaining sauce over the rolls and add torn bread to absorb liquid.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour until cabbage is tender.

title: Melbourne Chicken and Veggie Stir-Fry with Rice
ingredients: 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Marinate chicken slices with half the soy sauce and a splash of sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Cook jasmine rice according to package instructions and keep warm.
Heat a wok or large pan over high heat with a little oil.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, then remove from pan.
Add broccoli, carrots, and bell pepper to the pan; stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return chicken to the pan, add remaining soy sauce and cornstarch slurry.
Toss everything together until the sauce thickens and coats the vegetables.
Serve over rice and garnish with sesame seeds.

title: Sunday Morning Sunday Roast
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Rub the chicken inside and out with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon halves, onion quarters, and garlic cloves.
Tuck rosemary sprigs under the skin and over the top of the chicken.
Place chicken breast-side up on a baking tray lined with paper.
Arrange potato wedges and carrots around the chicken.
Drizzle melted butter over the chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes until the skin is golden and the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before carving and serving.

title: Grandma's Spicy Samosa Pie
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté the chopped onion until soft and translucent.
Add cumin, coriander, and cayenne pepper, stirring for 30 seconds.
Add the mixed vegetables and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Season the vegetable mixture with salt.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface.
Spread a thin layer of yogurt over half of the pastry.
Spoon the hot vegetable mixture over the yogurt and sprinkle with spring onions.
Fold the pastry over to cover, pressing edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

title: Cairns Coconut Curry with Rice
ingredients: 1kg fresh pumpkin or butternut squash, cubed
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the diced onion until soft.
Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot, then add pumpkin cubes.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken stock.
Add fish sauce, brown sugar, and lime juice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 25-30 minutes until pumpkin is tender and chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot over a bed of steaming rice, garnished with fresh coriander.

title: Traditional Bunda Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a bowl, rub the cold butter into the flour and baking powder until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Add ice water gradually and mix until a dough forms; wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out the pastry and press into a 9-inch pie dish.
For the filling, mix sugar, white flour, and baking powder.
Stir in condensed milk, beaten eggs, and self-raising flour until smooth.
Fold in currants and walnuts.
Pour the filling into the pastry case.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until the top is golden and the center is set.
Allow to cool completely before slicing and serving.

title: Freshly Caught Snapper with Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 2 whole red snapper, cleaned and scaled
instructions: Score the snapper fillets or whole fish lightly with a knife.
Season the fish inside and out with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sear the fish skin-side down (or belly down if whole) for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Flip the fish and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Remove fish from the pan and set aside on a warm plate.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add cherry tomatoes and red pepper flakes; cook until tomatoes release their juices.
Pour in white wine and fish stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return the fish to the pan to heat through gently.
Garnish with lemon slices and fresh parsley before serving.

title: Perth-Style Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 kg fresh hake or snapper fillets
instructions: Soak potato chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then dry thoroughly.
Deep fry chips in sunflower oil at 160°C until golden, then increase heat to 180°C.
Mix flour, salt, and paprika in a bowl.
Whisk sparkling water into the flour mixture until a thick batter forms.
Dip fish fillets into the batter and deep fry at 180°C for 4-5 minutes until crisp.
Serve immediately with chips and tartare sauce.

title: Grandma's Chicken and Rice Pilau
instructions: Toast cumin and coriander seeds in a heavy pot until fragrant.
Add ghee, then sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until soft.
Stir in turmeric, salt, and chicken, cooking until browned.
Add rinsed rice and stir to coat with spices.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Add raisins, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Western Australian Fish Pie
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then mash with butter, salt, and pepper.
Place flaked fish in a baking dish and cover with half the mashed potatoes.
Heat milk in a saucepan with flour, salt, and pepper until thickened.
Pour the milk sauce over the fish and potato base.
Top with remaining mashed potatoes.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and grated cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden.

title: Bush Tomato and Lamb Stew
instructions: Brown lamb cubes in olive oil in a large pot.
Add onion and carrots, cooking until softened.
Stir in stock, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add chopped bush tomatoes and spinach, cooking for another 15 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

title: Cape Cod Crab Cakes with Lemon Aioli
instructions: Gently mix crab meat, breadcrumbs, spring onions, egg, mayonnaise, lemon zest, and salt.
Form mixture into 10 patties and chill for 30 minutes.
Set up a breading station with flour, beaten egg (if needed), and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each patty in flour, dip in egg, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 175°C.
Fry patties for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with lemon wedges.

title: Lobster Pie with Thyme and Lemon
ingredients: 2 fresh Tasmanian lobsters, cleaned and chopped
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in butter until soft.
Add lobster pieces, wine, and stock; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in thyme, lemon zest, and half the lemon juice.
Preheat oven to 200°C and roll out pastry.
Place filling in a pie dish, cover with top pastry, and seal edges.
Brush with egg wash and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Fried Salt Cod with Tomatoes and Onions
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry onion slices in olive oil until translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flaked cod and fry gently for 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in parsley and coriander.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Smashed Potatoes with Herbs and Butter
ingredients: 1kg baby potatoes, scrubbed but not peeled
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender but not mushy, about 15 minutes.
Drain well and return to pot; mash while warm with butter, garlic, and rosemary.
Shape into a mound in a serving dish.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with parsley, lemon zest, and seasonings.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Fish and Chips with Fish Sauce and Tartar Sauce
ingredients: 600g firm white fish fillets (snapper or cod), cut into portions
4 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
instructions: Parboil chips for 4 minutes, drain, and fry in hot oil until golden.
Dredge fish in plain flour, dip in egg, then coat in flour mixed with beer.
Fry fish in hot oil until crispy and cooked through.
Whisk together mayonnaise, fish sauce, lemon juice, and parsley for tartar sauce.
Serve chips and fish with the tartar sauce on the side.

title: Pikelet and Fruit Salad with Honey
instructions: Mix dry flours and sugar in a bowl.
Combine egg, milk, water, melted butter, and vanilla; stir into dry mix until smooth.
Heat a griddle pan over medium-low heat and grease lightly.
Spoon batter onto pan to form small rounds and cook until bubbles form.
Flip and cook until golden on both sides.
Arrange pikelets on a plate with fresh fruit and drizzle with honey.

title: Lamb and Leek Pie
ingredients: 1 kg New Zealand lamb shoulder, cubed
instructions: Season lamb with pepper and brown in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove lamb and sauté onions and leeks until soft.
Stir in flour, then gradually add stock and wine, scraping up browned bits.
Return lamb to pot, add thyme, and simmer gently for 2 hours until tender.
Fold in parsley and let the sauce thicken slightly.
Roll out pastry, place in a pie dish, add filling, and cover with top pastry.
Seal edges, cut vents, brush with egg, and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes until golden.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Kōura (Snow Crab) with Mānuka Butter
instructions: Boil water with a splash of vinegar and steam kōura for 6 minutes until bright red.
Immediately plunge into ice water to stop cooking.
In a small bowl, mix softened butter, honey, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Scoop butter mixture onto each crab leg or claw.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and coriander.
Optional: grill the buttered crab for 2 minutes to melt the butter slightly.

title: Pavlova with Kiwifruit and Passionfruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form, then add vinegar, cornstarch, and sugar gradually.
Add vanilla and flour, then fold in gently to create a glossy mixture.
Pipe or spoon onto the tray, creating a crust around the edge and a mound in the center.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the door slightly ajar for 1 more hour.
Cool completely before removing from the tray.
Whip cream until firm peaks form.
Top the pavlova with cream, kiwifruit slices, and passionfruit pulp.
Garnish with mint leaves and serve.

title: Green Lagoon Mussels with Fennel
ingredients: 1 kg fresh mussels, debearded and cleaned
instructions: Rinse mussels under cold water and discard any that are open or broken.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, then sauté fennel and garlic until soft.
Add mussels, wine, and stock, then cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until mussels open.
Discard any mussels that do not open.
Stir in parsley, dill, and black pepper.
Serve hot in bowls with lemon wedges and crusty bread on the side.

title: Hāngī Roast Pork with Sweet Potato
ingredients: 2 kg pork shoulder, trimmed and cubed
instructions: Season pork, vegetables, and garlic with salt, pepper, and rosemary.
Place all ingredients in a large hāngī basket or pit.
Add water to the pit to create steam, then cover tightly with wet clay or foil.
Place the basket over hot rocks in a preheated earth oven for 3-4 hours.
Check that vegetables are tender and pork is falling apart.
Remove carefully and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve with a side of tangy cabbage slaw.

title: Vegetable Hotpot with Beef
instructions: Place beef, vegetables, and potatoes in a large pot.
Add cauliflower, broccoli, and carrots on top.
Pour in boiling beef stock and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in a mixture of water and flour to thicken the gravy slightly.
Serve immediately in a deep dish.

title: Scotch Pie
instructions: Mix flour, butter, and water to form a firm dough, then chill for 30 minutes.
Brown the mince with the onion in a frying pan until cooked through.
Sprinkle the plain flour over the meat and stir to coat.
Add beef stock, salt, and pepper, then simmer until thick and glossy.
