Roll the dough thinly and cut into circles slightly larger than the pie dish.
Press dough into a pie dish, fill with meat, and cover with another circle of dough.
Crimp edges together, cut a slit in the top, and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes.

title: Pumpkin Pie with Cream
instructions: Roast pumpkin cubes in the oven at 180°C until soft, about 20 minutes.
Blend the roasted pumpkin with cream, sugar, spices, salt, and eggs until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a greased pie dish.
Dot with melted butter and bake at 160°C for 45-50 minutes until set.
Allow to cool completely before serving with extra cream.

title: Lamb and Leek Casserole
instructions: Season lamb with salt and pepper, then brown in olive oil in a large pot.
Remove lamb and sauté the leeks until softened.
Return lamb to the pot and add wine, tomato paste, and bay leaves.
Add potatoes, stock, and rosemary.
Cover and simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours until lamb is tender.
Remove bay leaves before serving.

title: Fish and Chips with Malt Vinegar
ingredients: 1kg white fish fillets, such as hoki or snapper
instructions: Soak potato chips in cold water for 30 minutes, then dry thoroughly.
Fry chips in hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Make a batter by mixing flour, baking powder, salt, and ice-cold water.
Dip fish fillets into the batter to coat evenly.
Fry battered fish in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot chips and fish with malt vinegar on the side.

title: Pie Crust
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add ice water gradually until dough comes together.
Chill dough for at least one hour before rolling.

title: Cabbage and Bacon Pie
instructions: Sauté onion and bacon in butter until golden.
Stir in cabbage and cook until soft and moisture has evaporated.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix cabbage mixture with milk and eggs.
Pour into pie dish and cover with top crust.
Cut slits in top and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes.

title: Meat and Potato Pie
instructions: Brown mince and onion in a pot over medium heat.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, stock, and tomato paste.
Simmer for 30 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour mixture into pie dish and cover with top crust.
Bake at 190°C for 35 minutes until crust is golden.

title: Haggis
instructions: Finely chop the sheep's offal.
Mix offal with oatmeal, onion, stock, pepper, and salt.
Stuff mixture into a cleaned sheep's stomach casing.
Tie securely at both ends.
Poach in boiling water with a cinnamon stick for 3 hours.
Slice and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Tartan Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Brown beef and onion in a pot until golden.
Add carrots, peas, and green beans, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix filling with milk and eggs.
Pour into pie dish and cover with top crust.
Cut slits in top and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes.
Let cool slightly before serving.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry with Chilli Sauce
instructions: Mix fish sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, chilli paste, and water in a bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Stir-fry chicken slices until golden and cooked through, then remove from wok.
Add garlic, broccoli, baby corn, and capsicum to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the wok, pour in the sauce, and toss everything together.
Cook for another 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve immediately garnished with fresh coriander leaves.

title: Baked Ham and Cheese Roll-ups
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Lay ham slices flat on a cutting board.
Spread softened butter mixed with rosemary, salt, and pepper over each ham slice.
Place a cheese slice on the buttered ham and roll up tightly.
Place rolls in a baking dish, seam side down.
Brush tops with olive oil and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Let rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Sausage and Potato Bake with Fennel
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
In a large baking dish, toss potatoes, fennel, carrots, and onion with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange sausages on top of the vegetables.
In a small bowl, mix chicken stock, water, tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaf.
Pour the liquid mixture over the sausages and vegetables.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 15 minutes until vegetables are tender and sausages are cooked through.
Remove thyme and bay leaf before serving.

title: Lamb Koftas with Mint Chutney
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground lamb, grated onion, garlic, spices, flour, egg, salt, and pepper.
Mix well until all ingredients are evenly distributed.
Shape the mixture into small oval koftas.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry koftas in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes per side.
While koftas cook, make chutney by blending mint, coriander, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
Drain koftas on paper towels.
Serve hot with mint chutney and pita bread.

title: Fish and Chips with Tartare Sauce
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets, such as snapper or barramundi
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) for chips.
Blanch potato chips in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and spread on a tray.
In a bowl, mix 2 cups flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Gradually add cold water to the flour mixture until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large pot to 175°C (350°F).
Fry potato chips in batches until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Fry fish fillets in the same oil until cooked through and golden, about 3-4 minutes per side.
For tartare sauce, mix mayonnaise with pickles, capers, parsley, and lemon juice.
Serve fish and chips immediately with tartare sauce and lemon wedges.

title: Meat Pies with Vegemite Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Mix browned beef, onions, stock, salt, and melted butter for the filling.
Roll out dough and cut into circles.
Fill circles with meat mixture and crimp edges to seal.
Place on baking tray and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Mix Vegemite and water to make a dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Parmigiana with Frying Sauce
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken in flour, then egg, then breadcrumb mixture.
Fry chicken in olive oil until golden and cooked through.
Heat tomato sauce with onion and garlic.
Place chicken on a plate, top with sauce and cheese.
Broil until cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Pavlova with Berries and Passionfruit
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar while whisking until stiff peaks form.
Add vinegar and cornstarch, then fold in gently.
Spread onto a greased baking tray to form a circle.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off oven and leave for 1 hour.
Top with whipped cream, berries, and passionfruit before serving.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 2 cups diced potatoes, boiled and mashed
instructions: Brown lamb with onions, carrots, and peas in a pot.
Add stock and tomato paste, simmer for 10 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes with butter, salt, and pepper.
Spoon meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and spread evenly.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.

title: Bavarian Sausage with Mustard and Sauerkraut
instructions: Sauté onions in a pan until soft.
Add sauerkraut and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in mustard, vinegar, honey, and salt.
Add sliced sausages and heat through.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Salt and Pepper Squid
ingredients: 500g squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
instructions: Pat the squid rings dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Set up three bowls with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs mixed with salt and pepper.
Dip each squid ring into flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, ensuring it is fully coated.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C.
Fry the coated squid in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with fresh coriander, lettuce, soy sauce, and extra salt and pepper sauce.

title: Pavlova with Raspberry Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and draw a circle about 20cm in diameter.
Whip egg whites until soft peaks form, gradually adding sugar until stiff glossy peaks form.
Fold in vinegar, cornstarch, vanilla, and cream of tartar gently.
Pile the mixture into the circle on the baking sheet and smooth the top.
Bake for 1 hour, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form.
Mix the raspberry pulp with passion fruit pulp to make the sauce.
Top the cooled pavlova with whipped cream, sauce, raspberries, and mint leaves before serving.

title: Slow-Cooked Lamb Shanks with Red Wine
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb shanks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the lamb shanks until browned on all sides.
Remove the lamb and set aside. Add onions, garlic, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook until softened.
Pour in the red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the lamb to the pot, add the stock, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the lamb shanks and let them rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Strain the sauce and return it to the pot, simmering briefly to thicken.
Serve the sliced lamb with the rich red wine sauce and fresh parsley.

title: Sunday Roast Chicken with Damper
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Rub the chicken inside and out with olive oil, butter, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with additional herbs and onions.
Place carrots, potatoes, and remaining onions around the chicken in a roasting tray.
Pour the chicken stock over the vegetables.
Roast for 1.5 to 2 hours, basting occasionally, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
While the chicken roasts, mix flour, sugar, and milk for the damper batter.
Stir in melted butter until a thick dough forms.
Grease a cast-iron skillet and pour in the batter, smoothing the top.
Bake the damper for 30-40 minutes until golden and firm.
Carve the chicken and serve with hot damper and roasted vegetables.

title: Fish and Chips with Satay Sauce
ingredients: 600g firm white fish fillets (snapper or bream), cut into strips
Lettuce leaves and ketchup for serving
instructions: Season the fish strips with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika and cayenne.
Dredge each fish strip in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in the seasoned breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C.
Fry the breaded fish until golden and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
In the same oil, fry the thick-cut potato chips until crispy and golden.
In a small bowl, mix mayonnaise, peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and chili paste to make the satay sauce.
Drain the fish and chips on paper towels.
Serve the fish and chips with the homemade satay sauce, ketchup, and lettuce leaves.

title: Traditional Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in buttermilk and melted butter until a soft dough forms.
Shape into a ball and press a cross on top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and hollow when tapped.

title: Classic English Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown beef with onion and garlic in a large pan; drain excess fat.
Add stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste; simmer for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil potatoes until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
Place meat mixture in a baking dish and top with mashed potatoes.
Sprinkle with peas and bake for 25-30 minutes until bubbly.

title: Traditional Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown lamb cubes in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in stock, thyme, and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add carrots and potatoes; cook covered for another 45 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix diced beef, swede, potatoes, onion, salt, pepper, and flour.
Roll pastry into a large rectangle and cut into 6 squares.
Place filling in the bottom half of each square and fold over.
Crimp edges to seal and cut vents on top.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Traditional Irish Colcannon
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
In a large pot, sauté onion in butter until soft.
Add cabbage or kale and cook until wilted.
Mash potatoes with butter, cream, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Fold the cabbage mixture into the mashed potatoes.
Serve warm, optionally topped with fried bacon bits.

title: Traditional Scones
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Gradually stir in the warm milk until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and gently knead it twice.
Roll out the dough to 1 inch thickness and cut into rounds.
Place on a baking tray, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 400°F for 15-20 minutes until golden.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and fry the onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add the ground lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomato paste and beef stock, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in the peas and corn, season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.
Preheat oven to 400°F and grease a baking dish.
Spread the lamb mixture into the dish and top evenly with the mashed potatoes.
Use a fork to rough up the potato topping, then bake for 25-30 minutes until golden.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 2 lbs white potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 lb smoked haddock fillets, skinned and broken into pieces
1 large leek, white part only, sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and fry the onion and leek until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually add the fish stock.
Add the potatoes and bring to a simmer, then cook for 10 minutes.
Gently add the smoked haddock pieces and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, ensuring the fish is just cooked through.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb pieces with salt and pepper and brown them in a heavy pot.
Remove the meat and set aside, then add the onions to the pot and cook until soft.
Return the meat to the pot and add the stock, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and carrots, then simmer uncovered for another 45 minutes until tender.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme, taste for seasoning, and garnish with parsley.

title: Bangers and Mash
ingredients: Salt, black pepper, and dried thyme to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F and bake the sausages on a tray for 20 minutes until browned.
While baking, make the gravy by frying the onion and garlic in a pot until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then slowly add the beef stock.
Simmer the gravy until it thickens, then season with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Serve the sausages alongside the warm mashed potatoes and pour the gravy over everything.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the lamb mince in a large pan with the onions until golden.
Add carrots, peas, tomato puree, thyme, and stock; simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the diced potatoes until tender, then mash with butter until smooth.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 25 minutes until the topping is golden and bubbling.

title: Full Irish Stew
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb cubes on all sides.
Remove lamb; sauté onions until soft, then return lamb to the pot.
Add carrots, potatoes, salt, pepper, rosemary, and thyme.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer gently for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Remove thyme sprigs before serving.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Mince beef with diced potatoes, swede, carrot, onion, salt, pepper, and sage in a food processor until chunky.
Roll out pastry and cut into large circles.
Place a portion of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold pastry over to create a half-moon shape and crimp edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30-35 minutes until pastry is golden and filling is hot.

title: Sunday Roast Beef
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Rub beef with oil and tie with kitchen string.
Roast for 20 minutes, then add carrots, potatoes, and onion to the roasting tin.
Reduce heat to 180°C (350°F) and roast for 15 minutes per 500g for medium-rare.
Remove beef to a board, cover with foil, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Pour off excess fat, add flour to roasting tin, stir to coat, then add stock and herbs.
Simmer to make gravy, strain, and serve with the beef and roasted vegetables.

title: Ulster Fry Sausages and Bacon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss potato slices in oil, salt, and pepper; spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 30 minutes until crispy.
Meanwhile, fry bacon rashers and sausages in a pan until cooked through.
In the same pan, cook onion slices until soft, then add tomato slices.
Butter the white bread slices and toast them under the grill.
Assemble the fry: place sausage, bacon, tomato, and onion on the toast, top with a fried egg if desired, and serve with roasted potatoes and lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Irish Stew
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb cubes in batches, then remove and set aside.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery to the pot; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot, add the stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes and cook for another 45 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove herbs, and serve.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 1 lb flour, plus extra for dusting
1 large swede or potato, peeled and grated
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water gradually until dough forms; wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a separate bowl, mix beef, grated swede, carrot, onion, and thyme.
Roll out dough into a rectangle, place filling along one long edge.
Fold dough over to create a square, crimp edges with a fork.
Brush with egg wash and cut vents on top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Scottish Haggis
instructions: Fry the diced suet and onion in a pan until soft.
Add the oatmeal, dried fruit, stock, salt, pepper, nutmeg, allspice, and garlic.
Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Stuff the mixture tightly into the sheep's stomach casing.
Tie off both ends securely with kitchen string.
Place in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer gently for 2.5 hours.
Remove, let cool slightly, slice, and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Welsh Rarebit
ingredients: 2 tbsp cold butter, cut into pieces
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Toast the bread slices and rub with cold butter.
In a saucepan over low heat, melt the first 2 tbsp of butter.
Add the cheese, stirring until smooth and melted.
Stir in the beer, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, dry mustard, and cayenne.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Pour the mixture generously over each toast slice.
Broil or grill until the top is bubbling and golden brown.

title: English Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 4 large potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the ground meat with onion and garlic in a large skillet.
Stir in peas, tomato paste, stock, rosemary, and thyme; simmer for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a separate pan, melt butter and whisk in flour.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly until thickened into a sauce.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper.
Place the meat mixture in a baking dish and top with potato slices.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes and bake for 30-35 minutes until potatoes are tender and golden.

title: Traditional Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 2 large swede, grated and squeezed dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Mix beef, swede, potato, and onion in a bowl.
Roll out the bottom crust and place filling along one edge.
Fold pastry over to create a half-moon shape and crimp edges.
Brush with melted butter and bake for 40 minutes until golden.
Cool slightly before serving.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F).
Mix flour, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Add buttermilk and honey, stirring until a dough forms.
Shape into a round loaf and score a deep cross on top.
Bake on a baking sheet for 30-35 minutes until hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets, such as cod
Sea salt and malt vinegar for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a tray with parchment.
Season potatoes with salt and fry in hot oil until golden, then drain.
Dip fish fillets in beaten egg, then coat in flour.
Dip again in egg and then beer batter.
Fry fish in hot oil for 4-5 minutes until crispy and flaky.
Serve chips and fish hot with salt and vinegar.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Heat milk and butter in a saucepan until simmering.
Stir in flour, mustard powder, and salt to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in ale and grated cheese until smooth and thick.
Simmer gently for 2 minutes until bubbling.
Spread Dijon mustard on toasted bread slices.
Pour the cheese sauce over the bread and serve immediately.

title: Scottish Haggis
instructions: Mix all ingredients except stock and casing in a large bowl.
Season thoroughly with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Fill the sheep stomach casing with the mixture, leaving space to expand.
Tie off the ends securely.
Place in a pot with beef stock and simmer gently for 2.5 hours.
Remove, cool slightly, slice, and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Scones with Clotted Cream and Jam
instructions: Sift the flour, sugar, and baking powder into a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add the milk and mix quickly with a knife to form a soft dough.
Turn onto a floured surface, pat into a circle, and cut into 8 wedges.
Bake on a greased tray at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until golden.
Serve warm with clotted cream and jam.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then brown in a large pot with oil.
Add the chopped onions and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for one minute.
Pour in the lamb stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Add the potatoes and carrots, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Bangers and Mash
instructions: Boil the diced potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
Mash the potatoes with butter, milk, sage, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and arrange sausages on a baking sheet.
Roast the sausages for 20 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Simmer beef stock in a pan with a little water to make gravy.
Serve the sausages with the mashed potatoes and gravy.

title: Ulster Fry Full Breakfast
ingredients: Butter and brown sauce for serving
instructions: Fry the bacon, black pudding, and white pudding in a large skillet until crisp.
Scramble the eggs in the same pan with a little butter.
Toast the slices of bread until golden brown.
Pan-fry the tomato and onion slices until lightly browned.
Arrange all items on a large plate with the fried potato.
Serve with butter and brown sauce on the side.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
Salt, pepper, and dried herbs to taste
instructions: Brown the ground lamb in a large pot with chopped onion and carrots.
Add peas, stock, tomato paste, herbs, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer the meat mixture to a baking dish.
Boil the potato slices until tender, then mash with butter, flour, milk, and seasoning.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the meat mixture.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-30 minutes until the topping is golden and bubbly.

title: Traditional Irish Lamb and Cabbage Stew
ingredients: 2 lbs green cabbage, chopped into large wedges
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then brown it on all sides.
Remove the lamb and set aside; add the onion to the pot and sauté until soft.
Return the lamb to the pot, add the carrots and potatoes, and stir to coat.
Pour in the stock and add the thyme; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the cabbage wedges and continue simmering, covered, for another 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.

title: Scottish Haggis
ingredients: 2 lbs sheep pluck (heart, liver, lungs), cleaned
instructions: Wash and chop the sheep pluck finely.
In a large bowl, mix the pluck with oatmeal, chopped onion, suet, stock, salt, pepper, sage, and thyme.
Knead the mixture until it forms a smooth, sticky paste.
Fit the natural sheep stomach casing onto a funnel and fill with the mixture, twisting at the top to seal.
Place the haggis in a pot of boiling water and simmer gently for 3 hours.
Remove, let cool slightly, then slice and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Add the cheese, sherry, stock, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, cayenne, and nutmeg.
Stir continuously until the cheese is completely melted and the sauce is smooth.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Preheat the broiler.
Spread the sauce generously over the toasted bread slices.
Place under the broiler for 2-3 minutes until the top is golden brown and bubbling.
Serve immediately.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Mix flour and cold butter in a food processor until crumbs form; add ice water and knead into a dough.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, toss the beef, potatoes, swede, onion, salt, pepper, and rosemary together.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface into a large rectangle.
Cut the dough into 6 squares; place a quarter of the filling in the center of each.
Fold the dough over to create a half-moon shape, pressing the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and cut slits in the top crust.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 40-45 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Ulster Fry Full Breakfast
ingredients: 4 rashers of back bacon or ham
instructions: Fry the bacon and sausages in a large skillet until crispy and cooked through.
In a separate pan, scramble the eggs with salt and pepper to your liking.
Heat a griddle or skillet and fry the tomato slices until slightly charred.
Toast the buttered bread slices in a toaster or under a broiler until golden.
Warm the tea in a pot.
Arrange all components on a large plate: eggs, bacon, sausages, tomatoes, and toast.
Serve immediately with the hot tea.

title: Traditional Scones
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cubed and cold
1 1/4 cups milk, plus more for brushing
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sift the flour, sugar, and salt into a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter using a pastry cutter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the milk and vanilla just until the dough comes together.
Turn onto a floured surface and gently knead 3-4 times.
Pat the dough into a circle about 1 inch thick and cut into 8 wedges.
Brush tops with milk and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden.
Serve warm with clotted cream and jam.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb with salt and pepper.
Brown the lamb in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat; remove and set aside.
Sauté the onions in the pot until soft, then add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot and add the stock and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and carrots, cover again, and simmer for another 45 minutes until tender.
Discard bay leaves before serving.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 1 pound white fish fillets, such as cod or haddock
2 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
Malt vinegar and salt for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°F (95°C) and place chips on a baking sheet.
Place potatoes in boiling salted water for 10 minutes; drain and fry in oil at 375°F (190°C) for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Increase oil temperature to 375°F (190°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl; stir in eggs to form a batter.
Dip fish fillets into batter and fry in oil for 4-5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Drain fish on paper towels.
Serve chips and fish hot with malt vinegar and salt.

title: Cornish Pasties
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté the beef in a pan until browned; drain excess fat.
In a separate pan, cook the potatoes, carrots, and swede until tender.
Mix the cooked vegetables with the beef, onion, salt, and pepper.
Roll out the pastry on a floured surface into a large rectangle.
Spread the filling over half the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border.
Fold the other half over the filling and seal edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg and cut a small slit in the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden brown.

title: Bangers and Mash
ingredients: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain potatoes and return to the pot; mash with butter, milk, sage, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausages and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through.
Stir in the chopped onion and cook for 2-3 minutes until soft.
Serve the sausages with the mashed potatoes and gravy.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and brown the minced lamb.
Add the onion and carrots, cook until softened.
Stir in peas, stock, tomato purée, and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened, then season.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with the mashed potatoes and smooth the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the topping is golden.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Mix with a wooden spoon until a dough forms.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead lightly for 2 minutes.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Score a deep cross on top with a sharp knife.
Brush with the beaten egg.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 15 minutes, then reduce to 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes.

title: Traditional Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb with salt and pepper.
Brown the lamb in a heavy pot with a little oil.
Remove lamb and sauté the onions until soft.
Return lamb to the pot and add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes and carrots.
Continue simmering for another 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaves and thyme before serving.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Mix flour and cold butter until crumbly, add egg yolk mixture to form a dough.
Chill dough for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Combine meat, potatoes, swede/carrots, onion, and stock in a bowl.
Season filling with salt and pepper.
Roll out half the dough and cut into 4 circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle and fold dough over to create a half-moon shape.
Crimp edges firmly and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Full English Breakfast
ingredients: 2 thick slices of bread or English muffins
2 slices of thick-cut smoked back bacon
instructions: Toast the bread or English muffins.
Fry the bacon and sausages in a large pan until cooked through.
In a separate pan, fry the mushrooms in butter until browned.
Cook the tomatoes cut-side down until the skin blisters.
Fry the eggs to your preferred doneness in the same pan used for sausages.
Warm the ham slices.
Arrange all components on the toast or plate.
Serve with black pepper.

title: Traditional Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Sift flour, salt, baking powder, and sugar into a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Mix quickly with your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Score a deep cross on top with a sharp knife.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 15 minutes, then reduce to 200°C (400°F) for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Classic Cornish Pasty
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Place potatoes and swede in a pot of salted water and boil until just tender, then drain well.
In a bowl, mix the mince, onion, salt, and pepper.
Roll out half the pastry and place it in a 20cm tin, pressing it up the sides.
Add the cooked vegetables and mince mixture, leaving a gap around the edges.
Crumple the remaining pastry over the top to seal, pleating the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and fry the onion until soft.
Add the lamb mince, carrots, and peas, cooking until the meat is browned.
Stir in tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce, flour, and stock, simmering for 5 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and spread evenly.
Spread the mashed potatoes over the top, smoothing the surface.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes until the topping is golden and crispy.

title: English Full English Breakfast
ingredients: 2 rashers of streaky bacon or back bacon
1 tbsp runny honey or brown sauce
instructions: Fry the sausages and black pudding in a pan until cooked through.
In the same pan, fry the bacon and back bacon until crisp.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes to the pan, cooking until the tomatoes are soft.
Butter the bread slices and toast them until golden.
Fry the eggs to your preferred style in a little butter.
Arrange all items on plates, drizzling honey or brown sauce over the bacon as desired.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb cubes with salt and pepper.
Brown the lamb in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat, then remove.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot, add stock, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add carrots and swede, simmer for another 30 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 20-25 minutes until all vegetables are tender.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the ground lamb in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrots, cooking until softened.
Stir in the beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato purée.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Mash the potatoes with butter until smooth and set aside.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Pour the lamb mixture into a baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Use a fork to create a textured surface on the potatoes.
Bake for 25 minutes until the topping is golden brown.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb cubes.
Remove lamb and set aside, then sauté the onions until soft.
Return lamb to the pot and add stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and carrots to the stew.
Cover and simmer for another 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf before serving.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a bowl, mix the beef, potatoes, carrots, swede, and onion.
Season the filling with salt, pepper, and flour, then add stock.
Roll out the pastry on a floured surface into a large square.
Place the filling in the center of the pastry, leaving a border.
Fold the pastry over the filling to create four triangular folds, crimping edges to seal.
Create a vent cut on top and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the pastry is golden and filling is cooked.

title: Scottish Haggis
ingredients: 1 lb heart, liver, and lungs of lamb
1/2 cup dried split peas, soaked overnight
instructions: Clean and chop the lamb organs into small pieces.
Sauté the onion and leeks in a pan until softened.
Add the soaked split peas, stock, and sautéed vegetables to a pot.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes until liquid reduces.
Add the chopped organs, oatmeal, salt, pepper, allspice, and nutmeg.
Mix thoroughly until a thick, uniform paste forms.
Stuff the mixture into the sheep's stomach casing.
Tie securely at both ends and prick with a fork.
Poach in boiling water for 2.5 hours or steam until fully cooked.

title: Full Irish Breakfast
ingredients: 2 tbsp brown sugar (optional, for caramelizing onion)
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the bacon and black/white pudding until crispy and cooked through.
Remove meat items and set aside on paper towels.
In the same pan, cook the sliced onions until deeply caramelized.
Add a little brown sugar if desired to aid caramelization.
Push onions to the side and fry tomato slices until softened.
Crack the eggs into the pan, frying sunny-side up or scrambled as preferred.
Season the eggs with salt and pepper.
Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Arrange all items on a large plate: toast, fried eggs, bacon, black pudding, white pudding, tomato, and onions.

title: Traditional Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the lamb cubes in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock, thyme, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add potatoes and carrots; simmer another 45 minutes until tender.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix beef, potato, swede, carrot, onion, sage, and lard in a bowl.
Roll out pastry and cut into squares; fill each with the meat mixture.
Fold pastry over to create four sides, crimping edges with a fork.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Scone with Clotted Cream and Jam
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet.
Mix flour, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in heavy cream and egg until just combined.
Drop dough by spoonfuls onto the sheet; bake 12-15 minutes.
Serve warm with clotted cream and jam.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 lbs white fish fillets (cod or haddock), cut into strips
4 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
instructions: Parboil potato chips in salted water for 5 minutes; drain and cool.
Deep fry chips in oil at 350°F (175°C) until golden; drain on paper towels.
Whisk flour, cornstarch, and salt with cold water to make batter.
Dip fish strips in batter and deep fry at 375°F (190°C) until crispy.
Serve immediately with chips, salt, and malt vinegar.

title: Scotch Egg
instructions: Peel hard-boiled eggs and chill slightly.
Mix ground pork, thyme, salt, pepper, and half the breadcrumbs.
Wrap each egg tightly in pork mixture, forming a ball.
Roll coated eggs in flour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Deep fry at 350°F (175°C) for 4-5 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Traditional Sunday Roast
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Rub the chicken inside and out with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the quartered onions.
Place chicken in a roasting tin surrounded by carrots, parsnips, and potato wedges.
Roast for 1 hour 30 minutes, basting with butter every 30 minutes.
Pour beef stock into the tin and continue roasting for another 30 minutes until juices run clear.
Let rest for 10 minutes before carving.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrots until soft.
Add the minced lamb and cook until browned.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in stock, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato puree; simmer until thickened.
Add frozen peas and season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spoon the meat mixture into a baking dish.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 minutes until the topping is golden brown.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb cubes with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy pot and sear the lamb in batches until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onions until translucent.
Add carrots and celery, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot, add stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes and cook for another 30-40 minutes until tender.
Remove herbs before serving.

title: Cornish Pasty
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl; rub in cold butter until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add a splash of ice water and knead until a smooth dough forms; chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Sauté onion, potatoes, swede, and carrots until soft but not browned.
Add beef mince and cook until browned; drain excess fat.
Stir in stock, pepper, and half the vegetable mixture into the pot.
Roll out half the dough into a rectangle and place in a baking tin.
Fill with the remaining vegetables and meat, then top with the second half of dough.
Crimp edges to seal, brush with egg wash, and bake for 40 minutes until golden.

title: Full English Breakfast
ingredients: 4 slices back bacon or Canadian bacon
instructions: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the sausages and bacon until crispy and cooked through; remove and keep warm.
In the same pan, fry the mushrooms in butter until golden.
Add the tomatoes cut-side down and grill until the skin blisters.
Scramble the eggs in the pan with a little butter and pepper to your liking.
Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Assemble the plate with sausages, bacon, eggs, mushrooms, tomatoes, and toast.
Serve immediately with black tea.

title: Traditional Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Sauté onion and carrots in a pan until soft.
Add lamb mince, stock, tomato puree, and thyme; simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in peas and cook for another 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spread meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and flatten the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.

title: Irish Colcannon
ingredients: 1kg potatoes, peeled and boiled until tender
1 large leek, white and light green parts only, sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until very soft, then drain.
Mash potatoes with butter, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Sauté sliced leeks in olive oil over medium heat until soft and wilted.
Fold the cooked leeks gently into the mashed potatoes.
Serve warm as a side dish.

title: Classic Cornish Pasty
instructions: Mix beef, swede, carrots, onion, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Roll out one sheet of pastry and cut into circles.
Place half the filling on each circle and fold over to create a half-moon shape.
Crimp the edges securely to seal.
Cut steam vents on the top crust.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 40 minutes until golden.

title: Welsh Rarebit
ingredients: Salt and cayenne pepper to taste
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden and butter them.
In a saucepan, melt butter and stir in stock, cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and cayenne.
Heat gently until cheese melts and sauce is smooth, stirring constantly.
Pour the sauce generously over each toast slice.
Broil under a hot grill for 2-3 minutes until bubbling and slightly browned.

title: Scottish Haggis
instructions: Finely chop onion and sauté in a pan until soft.
Combine lamb liver, heart, suet, onion, oatmeal, salt, pepper, sage, thyme, and stock.
Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Stuff the mixture into a natural or synthetic casing and tie securely.
Poach the haggis in simmering water for 2.5 hours, turning occasionally.
Slice and serve with neeps and tatties (turnip and potato mash).

title: Traditional Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix flour, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Add buttermilk and egg; stir until a soft dough forms.
Shape into a round loaf and place on a baking sheet.
Score the top with an X and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 1 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté diced beef, onion, and flour in a pan until browned.
Add potatoes, swede, salt, pepper, and stock; cook until tender.
Roll out pastry and cut into squares.
Fill each square with the mixture, fold over, and crimp edges.
Brush with egg wash and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown ground lamb with onion and carrots in a large pan.
Stir in tomato paste, stock, and thyme; simmer until thickened.
Season the meat mixture with salt and pepper.
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and spread evenly.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes until topping is golden.

title: Welsh Rarebit
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Butter the toast slices and toast lightly.
In a saucepan, melt butter and whisk in mustard, Worcestershire, and cayenne.
Add cheese, milk, and sherry; simmer until thickened.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Pour the sauce over the toast and broil until bubbling.

title: Scottish Haggis
ingredients: 1 large sheep stomach or natural casing
instructions: Soak oatmeal in stock for 10 minutes.
Sauté lamb and onions in a pan until browned.
Add oatmeal mixture, suet, spices, salt, and pepper to the meat.
Mix well and stuff into the sheep stomach or casing.
Tie securely and simmer in boiling water for 2.5 hours.
Slice and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Traditional Scones
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, cubed and cold
instructions: Sift the flour, sugar, and salt into a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Pour in the milk and stir gently until a soft dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead lightly just a few times.
Pat into a circle, cut into 8 wedges, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until golden.

title: Irish Stew
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb with salt and pepper, then brown in the oil in a large pot.
Remove lamb and add onions, cooking until soft.
Return lamb to the pot and add stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until lamb is tender.
Add carrots and potatoes, then cook another 30 minutes until vegetables are soft.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed if frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix the minced lamb, diced vegetables, thyme, and stock in a bowl.
Roll out the pastry and cut into 4 large squares.
Place filling in the center of each square, leaving a border.
Fold the pastry over to create a half-moon shape and crimp edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and pastry is crisp.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 4 large white fish fillets (cod or haddock)
4 large potatoes, cut into thick chips
4 cups vegetable oil for deep frying
Malt vinegar and salt for serving
instructions: Parboil the potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes, drain, and let cool slightly.
Cut potatoes into strips and deep fry at 375°F (190°C) until golden and crisp.
Mix plain flour, baking powder, and salt for the batter.
Dip fish fillets in batter and deep fry at 375°F (190°C) until golden.
Serve hot chips and fish immediately with malt vinegar and salt.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and carrots in a large pan until soft.
Add ground lamb and cook until browned, then drain excess fat.
Stir in peas, stock, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce; simmer for 10 minutes.
In a separate bowl, mash potatoes with butter, milk, salt, and pepper.
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Create peaks with the back of a spoon and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lbs potatoes, peeled and boiled until tender
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft, then drain and mash with a little butter.
Sauté the chopped cabbage and onion in a pan with the remaining butter and garlic until soft.
Stir the cooked cabbage mixture into the mashed potatoes.
Gradually add the heavy cream, mixing until smooth and creamy.
Season generously with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

title: Barmbrack
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, salt, and dried fruits in a large bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and warm milk, then knead until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Place dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough, shape into a round loaf, and place on a baking tray.
Cover and let rise again for 30 minutes.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.

title: Stew with Colcannon
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Season the lamb chunks with salt and pepper, then brown them in a large pot with oil.
Add the onions, carrots, and tomato paste; cook for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the Guinness and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
Add the potatoes to the stew and cook for another 20-30 minutes until soft.
Serve the stew hot alongside a large portion of colcannon.

title: Irish Soda Bread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, and caraway seeds.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Mix quickly with your hands until a stiff dough forms; do not over-knead.
Shape the dough into a round loaf and place it on the baking sheet.
Score a deep cross on top with a sharp knife.
Brush the top with the beaten egg and bake for 30-35 minutes until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.

title: Boxty (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: 3 tbsp melted butter, plus extra for frying
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins, then peel and grate them while still warm.
Squeeze out as much liquid as possible from the grated potatoes using a clean cloth.
Mix the dry flour, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
Stir the grated potatoes and buttermilk into the dry ingredients to form a thick batter.
Heat a generous amount of butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Scoop spoonfuls of the batter into the pan and flatten slightly with a spatula.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown, flip, and cook the other side for another 3 minutes.
Brush the tops with a little beaten egg for a shiny finish and serve hot.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain well.
Steam the cabbage and onion until soft but not mushy.
Mash the potatoes with the warm milk, butter, and eggs until smooth.
Fold in the cooked cabbage and onion gently.
Season generously with salt and pepper and serve warm.

title: Ulster Fry
ingredients: 4 rashers of thick-cut back bacon, fried
4 poached or fried eggs, to serve
instructions: Heat a generous amount of butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the diced streaky bacon until crisp, then remove and set aside.
In the same fat, cook the onions and red pepper until softened.
Toast the soda bread slices in the pan until golden.
Assemble the plate with toast, fried back bacon, tomato slices, and the honey.
Add the fried eggs and the crispy streaky bacon on top.

title: Barmbrack
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, spices, salt, and dried fruits together in a large bowl.
Add the softened butter, brown sugar, and beaten egg to the dry mix.
Gradually incorporate the yeast mixture until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface until smooth, then place in a greased bowl.
Cover and leave to rise until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Punch down the dough, shape into a loaf or round, and let rise again.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Boxty
ingredients: 4 large potatoes, boiled whole and peeled
instructions: Boil the whole potatoes in their skins until tender, then drain and cool.
Peel the warm potatoes and grate them finely on a box grater.
Mash the grated potatoes thoroughly with the flour, milk, butter, eggs, salt, and pepper.
Knead the mixture briefly until it comes together into a stiff dough.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and roll it out to about 1cm thickness.
Cut into circles or squares and dust with flour.
Fry the boxty in hot oil until golden brown on both sides, then serve.

title: Red Jam with Soda Bread
ingredients: 4 slices of freshly baked soda bread
instructions: Place the chopped onions in a heavy-based saucepan with the sugars and spices.
Add the water and stir to combine.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the onions are very soft and the mixture is dark and jammy.
Remove from heat and allow to cool completely.
Serve the warm red jam alongside thick slices of fresh soda bread with butter.

title: Yorkshire Pudding
ingredients: 500g beef steak joints or ribs, trimmed of fat
instructions: Preheat oven to 220C (425F) and place a tray inside to heat up.
Season the beef joints or ribs with salt and pepper, then roast in the oven for 30 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, and flour together until smooth and free of lumps.
Remove the hot tray from the oven, quickly brush the base with melted butter, and immediately pour in the batter.
Return to the oven for 20-25 minutes until the puddings are puffed up and golden brown.
Slice the roasted beef and serve immediately alongside the hot pudding.

title: Bangers and Mash
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash with warm milk and butter until smooth.
Heat a little oil in a pan, add the sliced onions, and fry until soft and golden.
Place the sausages in the same pan, fry gently for 5 minutes, then cover and cook for 10 minutes until done.
Add the flour to the pan with the onions and sausages, stirring to combine.
Gradually stir in the beef stock to create a thick gravy, simmering for 5 minutes.
Serve the sausages and onion gravy over the mashed potatoes.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the minced lamb in a large pan with the diced onion and carrots.
Sprinkle the flour over the meat and stir for 1 minute to remove the raw taste.
Add the tomato puree, beef stock, and peas, simmering until the sauce thickens.
Preheat oven to 200C (400F).
Place the sliced potatoes in a pan with a knob of butter and a splash of water, cover, and steam until just tender.
Mash the potatoes while hot with the remaining butter until fluffy.
Spoon the meat mixture into an ovenproof dish, top with the mashed potatoes, and bake for 30 minutes until golden.

title: Toad in the Hole
instructions: Preheat oven to 220C (425F) and grease a baking tray or tin.
Arrange the sausages snugly in the bottom of the tin, ensuring they do not touch.
Sprinkle the sausages with a little sea salt.
Whisk the flour, eggs, and milk together until smooth, then season with salt and pepper.
Pour the batter over the sausages, spreading it out to fill the gaps.
Drizzle the melted butter over the top of the batter.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until the batter is crisp, golden brown, and the sausages are cooked through.

title: Steak and Kidney Pie
instructions: Brown the diced steak and kidneys in a large pan with the diced onion.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the beef stock and tomato puree.
Simmer the filling gently for 20 minutes until thickened, removing the bay leaf before cooling.
Preheat oven to 200C (400F).
Roll out the puff pastry and place it over the cooled filling in an ovenproof dish.
Brush the pastry edges with beaten egg and cut vents in the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.

title: Sunday Lamb Roast with Yorkshire Pudding
ingredients: 1 kg Bramley apples, peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Rub lamb with rosemary and garlic, then roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce heat to 180°C (350°F) and roast for another 1.5 hours until tender.
Whisk eggs and milk together, add flour, and leave to rest for 30 minutes.
Pour batter into hot roasting tin with melted butter to make puddings.
Serve lamb with roasted apples and warm Yorkshire puddings.

title: Traditional Sunday Gravy (Ragù alla Bolognese)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown pancetta in a large pot until crisp.
Add onions, carrots, and celery; cook until soft.
Stir in beef and cook until no longer pink.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in wine and reduce by half.
Add grated tomato, milk, and stock; simmer gently for 3 hours.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Steamed Haddock with Mushrooms and Parsley
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Steam haddock fillets over boiling water for 10 minutes.
Sauté mushrooms and garlic in olive oil until golden.
Season fish with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Place fish on serving plates and top with mushrooms.
Sprinkle generously with fresh parsley.
Serve with toasted sourdough bread.

title: Chicken Curry with Spiced Rice
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions.
Fry onion in oil until translucent.
Add spices and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chicken and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and cook until chicken is tender.
Serve over spiced rice with coriander.

title: Fish and Chips with Natural Sauce
instructions: Parboil chips in salted water for 5 minutes; drain and fry until golden.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and egg with water to make batter.
Dip fish in batter and deep fry until crispy and cooked through.
Whisk mayonnaise with lemon juice and salt for sauce.
Serve hot chips and fish with natural sauce.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: sea salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Parboil the potatoes and swede for 10 minutes, then drain.
Brown the beef in a pan with the onion, then mix in the vegetables, seasoning, and a splash of water.
Roll out the pastry and cut into 8 circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle, fold over, and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Cawl
instructions: Sear the lamb cubes in a large pot until browned.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Pour in the lamb stock and bring to a boil.
Add the swede, potatoes, carrots, leek, and rosemary.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer gently for 2 hours until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Sea Trout with Parsley Sauce
instructions: Season the trout fillets with salt and pepper.
Fry the fillets in butter over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Remove fish and keep warm.
In the same pan, add cream, garlic, and lemon juice.
Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened, then stir in half the parsley.
Plate the trout and spoon the sauce over the top.

title: Stargazy Pie
instructions: Parboil the potatoes and turnips until just tender, then drain.
Clean the fish, leaving the heads and tails intact, and stuff them with the vegetables.
Arrange the fish on top of the vegetables in a pie dish.
Cover with pastry, seal the edges, and cut vents in the center.
Push the fish heads through the vents so they stick up like stars.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes.

title: Black Pudding and Bacon Fry-up
instructions: Heat a heavy frying pan with a knob of butter over medium heat.
Cook the bacon until crispy, then remove and set aside.
Add more butter and fry the black pudding slices until the outside is crisp and browned.
Push the black pudding to the side, crack the eggs into the empty space, and scramble gently.
Add the bacon back in, season with pepper, and serve with toast and tomato slices.

title: Traditional Lancashire Hotpot
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Season lamb chunks with salt, pepper, and half the rosemary.
Place lamb and onions in a heavy baking dish and top with sliced sausages.
Stir together tomato soup and stock, then pour over the meat.
Cover the dish with potato slices, overlapping them like shingles.
Season the potatoes with remaining rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 2 to 2.5 hours until the lamb is tender and potatoes are golden.

title: Black Pudding and Lardy Cake
ingredients: 1 lb black pudding, sliced into 1-inch rounds
instructions: Heat a frying pan with oil and fry the black pudding slices until browned on both sides; set aside.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs, salt, and cayenne pepper.
Sift the flour into the egg mixture and stir in the chives until smooth.
Heat the lard in a separate frying pan over medium heat.
Pour the batter over the black pudding slices in the pan.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until the top is set and golden brown.
Flip the cake and cook for another 2-3 minutes until cooked through.

title: Lancashire Cobbler
instructions: Combine currants, brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a saucepan with milk and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in yeast and let stand for 10 minutes until frothy.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl; cut in butter until crumbly.
Beat egg into the yeast mixture, then pour into flour mixture to form a dough.
Roll dough out and place over the fruit mixture in a baking dish.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until the top is golden and firm.

title: Cumberland Sauce with Goose
instructions: Combine red currant jelly, vinegar, orange juice, brown sugar, peppercorns, cloves, and cinnamon stick in a saucepan.
Add water and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and let cool.
Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing on the jelly to extract liquid.
Discard the solids (spices and peppercorns).
Refrigerate until ready to serve with roasted goose or pork.

title: Pease Pottage
instructions: Rinse the dried peas and soak them in cold water for 2 hours.
In a large pot, melt butter and sauté onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add the soaked peas and stock to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until peas are very soft.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in fresh parsley before serving.

title: Scottish Haggis
ingredients: 1 fresh sheep's pluck set (heart, liver, lungs), cleaned
instructions: Rub the cleaned pluck set inside and out with salt, then place in a large bowl.
Add the onion, suet, and water to the pluck set and mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine the oatmeal, spices, and pepper.
Pour the spice mixture over the pluck set and stir until fully incorporated.
Stuff the mixture into a natural casing or a large sausage skin, tying it securely at both ends.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 1 lb fresh haddock fillets, skin removed
instructions: Place the haddock fillets in a large pot and cover with water or stock; simmer until just cooked through, then remove and reserve the liquid.
Add the onion, potatoes, thyme, butter, salt, and pepper to the reserved liquid and bring to a boil.
Stir in the oatmeal and cook for 5 minutes until the broth thickens.
Add the diced potatoes and milk to the pot and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Remove the thyme sprigs and check seasoning before serving hot.

title: Arbroath Smokie
instructions: Mix the salmon, haddock, and cod together in a large bowl.
Add the onion, spices, salt, water, and oatmeal to the fish mixture.
Knead the mixture thoroughly until it forms a smooth, elastic paste.
Shape the paste into small sausages, about 3 inches long.
Smoke the sausages over hickory or applewood until the casing is firm and the interior is cooked through.

title: Neeps and Tatties
instructions: Place the diced swedes in a pot of salted water and boil until tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes to the same pot and boil until both vegetables are soft.
Drain the vegetables well and return them to the pot over low heat.
Stir in the butter, milk, salt, pepper, and lemon juice until everything is creamy and well combined.
Serve immediately as a side dish with haggis or other meats.

title: Scotch Broth
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb neck bones or shanks
instructions: Place the lamb bones in a large pot and cover with cold water; bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour, then add the onion, carrot, turnip, celery, spices, thyme, and bay leaf.
Continue to simmer gently for 2 hours until the vegetables are tender and the meat falls off the bone.
Remove the bones and vegetables, then shred the meat and chop the vegetables into small pieces.
Return the meat and vegetables to the broth and season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

title: Cawl
ingredients: 4 leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Place lamb bones and shoulder in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes to remove scum.
Skim the surface, add fresh water, and simmer gently for 2 hours.
Add swede, carrots, and leeks; cook for another 45 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in cabbage, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 10 more minutes until all vegetables are soft.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Bara Brith
ingredients: 1 cup dried fruits, chopped (figs, raisins, sultanas)
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Grease a loaf pan.
Mix tea, brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Stir in orange juice, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
Sift flour into the mixture and stir until combined.
Fold in dried fruits, apricots, and nuts.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean.
Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.

title: Laverbread and Cakes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak cleaned laver seaweed in salted water for 2 hours, then boil until soft.
Blend the boiled seaweed with some of the cooking water until smooth.
In a large pot, fry pork belly and onion in oil until browned.
Stir in the blended laver mixture and thyme; simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper; cool the mixture completely.
Roll the mixture into small balls or pat into small cakes.
Dip each cake in flour, then egg wash.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with mushy peas and toast.

title: Barm Cake
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk and let sit for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, salt, and butter in a large bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and egg; knead until a soft dough forms.
Fold in walnuts if using.
Place dough on a floured surface and roll out to 1/2 inch thickness.
Cut into small round cakes using a cutter.
Place on a baking sheet and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 15-20 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack before serving.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden and crisp.
In a saucepan, melt butter over low heat.
Whisk in milk, beer, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, and cheese until smooth.
Season with paprika, salt, and pepper; cook until slightly thickened.
Spread the sauce generously over the toasted bread slices.
Broil for 2-3 minutes until bubbly and golden on top.
Garnish with chopped chives and serve immediately.

title: Colcannon
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash with half the butter.
Sauté onion and cabbage in a pan with the remaining butter until softened.
Stir in garlic and cook for one minute until fragrant.
Add the sautéed mixture to the mashed potatoes.
Pour in the heavy cream and season with salt and pepper.
Mix thoroughly until creamy and smooth.

title: Boxty
instructions: Grate the raw potato and squeeze out all excess liquid into a bowl.
Mash the boiled potatoes until smooth and add to the grated potato.
Stir in the flour, salt, and buttermilk until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with butter.

title: Coddled Eggs
instructions: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water by an inch.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 6-7 minutes.
Carefully crack the shell of each egg into a small bowl with a splash of milk.
Melt the butter in a serving dish over low heat.
Gently pour the eggs into the buttered dish.
Sprinkle with pepper, chives, and serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the lamb mince with onions and carrots in a large pan.
Stir in tomato paste, stock, and Worcestershire sauce; simmer for 15 minutes.
Season the meat mixture with salt and pepper, then transfer to a baking dish.
Boil potatoes until tender, then drain and mash with milk and butter.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the meat filling.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes until the topping is golden.

title: Soda Bread
instructions: Mix the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Make a well in the center and pour in the buttermilk.
Stir gently with a wooden spoon just until the dough comes together.
Turn onto a floured surface, knead lightly, and shape into a round loaf.
Place on a baking sheet, score an X on top, and brush with melted butter.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 35-40 minutes until hollow-sounding when tapped.

title: Ulster Fry Bacon and Eggs
ingredients: 1 handful fried onions, homemade or jarred
instructions: Fry the bacon rashers in a heavy pan until crisp and golden.
In the same pan, crack the eggs and fry them sunny-side up until whites are set but yolks are runny.
Remove bacon and eggs, leaving the fat in the pan.
Butter the plate and arrange the toasted bread, bacon, and eggs.
Top with tomato slices and a generous helping of fried onions.
Serve immediately while piping hot.

title: Coleraine Brown Bread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and grease a loaf tin.
Sift the flours, sugar, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.
Make a well in the center and add the milk, beaten egg, and melted butter.
Mix gently until a soft dough forms, being careful not to over-knead.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a loaf.
Place in the tin, smooth the top, and bake for 45-50 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Lamb and Onions in Red Wine Sauce
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the lamb chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large casserole dish and sear the lamb on all sides until browned.
Remove lamb and set aside; fry the onions in the same fat until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour to coat the onions and cook for one minute.
Return the lamb to the pot and pour in the red wine, scraping up any brown bits from the bottom.
Add the beef stock, tomato puree, bay leaf, and rosemary.
Cover and simmer gently for 2.5 hours until the lamb is tender and falling apart.
Remove the herbs and serve with mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

title: Bannock Bread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a baking sheet.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the melted butter and buttermilk, mixing until a soft dough forms.
Fold in the rolled oats if using.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead briefly.
Shape into a flat round or divide into smaller rounds.
Place on the baking sheet, prick the tops with a fork to prevent puffing, and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm with butter and jam or as a side to stew.

title: Creamed Spinach with Bacon
ingredients: 1 large bunch fresh spinach, washed and chopped
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté the diced bacon in a pan until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat.
Add the butter to the pan and melt, then stir in the flour to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth, then simmer until thickened.
Stir in the nutmeg, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Add the chopped spinach to the sauce and cook until wilted and tender.
Return the bacon to the pan and toss everything together.
Serve hot as a side dish with roast potatoes or lamb.

title: Yorkshire Pudding
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Whisk together the flour, eggs, and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Gradually whisk in the cold milk until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
Place chunks of butter into a cast-iron tray and heat in the oven until melted and smoking.
Pour the batter into the tray, filling the gaps between the butter.
Immediately place the tray in the oven and cook for 20-25 minutes until risen and golden.

title: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown the lamb in a large casserole dish with a little oil.
Add the onion and carrots, cooking until soft.
Stir in the tomato purée, rosemary, and stock, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the peas and heat through.
Spread the meat mixture into a baking dish.
Top with the mashed potato, smoothing the surface.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes until the topping is golden.

title: Yorkshire Apple Tart
instructions: Rub the cold butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Mix in the egg to form a dough, then chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough and line a baking tin.
Toss the apple slices in caster sugar and cinnamon, then arrange them in the tin.
Brush the pastry rim with beaten egg.
Sprinkle the brown sugar over the apples and dot with butter.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 40-45 minutes until the apples are tender and pastry is golden.

title: Yorkshire Cullin (Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Sear the lamb cubes in a heavy pot until browned on all sides.
Remove the meat and sauté the onions until soft.
Return the meat to the pot and sprinkle with flour, stirring well.
Add the potatoes, parsnips, carrots, swede, and bay leaf.
Pour in the lamb stock, ensuring everything is covered.
Cover and simmer gently on the hob for 45 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.

title: Yorkshire Black Pudding with Bacon
ingredients: crusty bread or eggs to serve
instructions: Fry the chopped bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp.
Add the onions and cook until they are soft and sweet.
Push the bacon and onions to one side of the pan.
Place the black pudding slices in the empty space and fry until crisp and browned.
Season generously with black pepper.
Serve immediately on crusty bread or alongside fried eggs.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 1.5kg chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate chicken and potatoes with half the spices, oil, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C and roast the marinated chicken and potatoes on a baking tray for 20 minutes.
Heat remaining oil in a large pan and fry onions until soft and golden.
Add garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato puree, stock, remaining spices, and bay leaves; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the roasted chicken and potatoes to the sauce and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Stir in the double cream and simmer gently for 2 minutes without boiling.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot with basmati rice.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 750g lamb or beef mince (if not using the above)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan and cook the minced lamb until browned; drain excess fat.
Add onions, carrots, and celery to the meat and cook until softened.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then add stock, Worcestershire sauce, tomato puree, and bay leaf.
Simmer until thickened, stir in frozen peas, remove bay leaf, and season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Boil diced potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until tender.
Drain potatoes, return to pan, add butter and milk, and mash until smooth.
Transfer the meat mixture to a baking dish, spread evenly, and top with the mashed potatoes.
Create small indentations in the potato topping and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Fish and Chips
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (cod or haddock), skin removed
Large bunch curly kale, stems removed
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Season the fish fillets with salt and pepper.
Mix flour, baking powder, and dried parsley in a bowl; make a well in the center and add beaten eggs and cold water to make a thick batter.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large pan to 180°C.
Dip fish fillets into the batter, letting excess drip off, and place on the baking tray.
Fry the battered fish for 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy.
In the same oil, fry thick-cut chips (potatoes) for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Drain chips on kitchen paper, then return to the hot oven for 10 minutes to crisp.
