Serve the fish and chips immediately with steamed kale, lemon wedges, and malt vinegar.

title: Full English Breakfast
instructions: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the sausages and bacon until cooked through and crispy; remove and keep warm.
In the same pan, fry the mushrooms in butter until golden and softened.
Add tomato slices to the pan and fry for 2-3 minutes until the edges are browned.
Crack the eggs into the pan; poach or scramble them to your liking, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Toast the bread slices in the same pan with a little oil or butter.
Arrange all components on a large plate: sausages, bacon, eggs, mushrooms, tomatoes, and toast.
Serve immediately with black pepper.

title: Bangers and Mash
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil diced potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain potatoes and return to the pot; add butter, milk, garlic, and sage, then mash until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the sausages to the pan and fry for 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
Mix tomato ketchup and brown sauce together in a small bowl.
Serve the sausages and onion mixture over the warm mashed potatoes.
Drizzle with the sauce mixture and sprinkle with black pepper.

title: Cornish Pasty
ingredients: 500g all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, rub in cold butter until crumbly.
Add cold water gradually to form a stiff dough, then chill for 30 minutes.
Combine lamb, swede, potato, ox cheek, onion, thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Roll out dough on a floured surface into a large rectangle.
Place filling in a line down the center, fold dough over to create four quarters, sealing edges with a fork.
Brush with egg wash and cut slits in the top.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 45 minutes until golden and cooked through.

title: Stargazy Pie
ingredients: 400g fresh mackerel, cleaned with heads and tails intact
instructions: Layer sliced potatoes and onion at the bottom of a baking dish.
Place mackerel on top, ensuring heads and tails protrude above the pastry.
Dot with butter and sprinkle with salt, pepper, and cream.
Cover completely with puff pastry, sealing edges.
Brush top with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 40 minutes until pastry is golden and fish eyes are visible.

title: Chowder of the Sea
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry onion, celery, and leek in butter until soft.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add potato, stock, and wine; simmer for 15 minutes.
Poach smoked haddock in a separate pan until just cooked, then flake.
Stir flaked fish into chowder and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat, stir in cream and dill.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Sodden Bread and Butter Pudding
ingredients: 1 loaf of stale Cornish bread, cut into cubes
instructions: Grease a baking dish and arrange bread cubes in a single layer.
Stir together eggs, cream, milk, sugar, vanilla seeds, and raisins.
Pour custard mixture over bread, ensuring all cubes are soaked.
Let stand for 30 minutes to absorb liquid.
Dust lightly with cinnamon and dot with butter.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes until set and golden.

title: Pound Cake with Lemon Zest
instructions: Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one by one, adding a little flour with each to prevent curdling.
Fold in flour, lemon zest, and vanilla extract.
Alternately add milk and remaining flour, starting and ending with flour.
Pour into a greased loaf tin.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 1 hour until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, then dust with icing sugar before slicing.

title: Lancashire Hotpot
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a shallow baking dish.
Place onion slices in the bottom of the dish and arrange lamb chops on top, seasoning with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Mix flour with a little water to make a paste, then stir in the tomatoes and milk to create a smooth sauce.
Pour the sauce over the meat, ensuring it is well covered.
Spread the mashed potato evenly over the top to form a crust.
Bake for 1 hour 45 minutes until the potato is golden and the meat is tender.

title: Scrambled Lancashire Eggs
instructions: Gently fry the chopped onions in butter until soft and golden.
Whisk the eggs, milk, pepper, and nutmeg together in a bowl.
Pour the egg mixture over the onions in the pan and stir gently.
Cook over low heat, stirring slowly to create large, creamy curds.
Stir in the grated Lancashire cheese and continue cooking until just set.
Remove from heat immediately and serve hot.

title: Black Pudding on Toast
ingredients: 4 thick slices of crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Fry the onion slices in olive oil until caramelized and soft.
Toast the bread slices in a toaster or under a grill until golden.
Cook the black pudding slices in a separate pan with a little butter until crisp on both sides.
Scramble the eggs with salt and pepper in the same pan.
Serve the black pudding on the toasted bread, topped with the scrambled eggs and onions.

title: Shepherd's Pie (Lancashire Style)
instructions: Sauté the onions, carrots, and celery in a large pan until softened.
Add the minced lamb and cook until browned, stirring frequently.
Stir in the flour, then add the tomatoes, tomato purée, stock, and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer the filling for 15 minutes until thickened and the meat is cooked through.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spread the mashed potato over the top of the pie.
Bake for 25 minutes until the potato is golden and bubbling.

title: Apple Crumble with Custard
instructions: Toss the diced apples with caster sugar and cinnamon in a baking dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle the demerara sugar over the top of the flour mixture.
Press the crumble topping firmly over the apples.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes until the apples are tender and the topping is crisp.
Serve warm with a generous dollop of double cream or custard.

title: Scotch Broth
ingredients: 2 lbs mixed lamb chops or mutton, cut into chunks
instructions: Place lamb chunks in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes to remove impurities.
Skim off any scum from the surface.
Add potatoes, turnips, swede, carrots, leek, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours until vegetables are tender.
Remove lamb from the pot, slice the meat, and return it to the broth.
Stir in fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Haggis
ingredients: 1 large sheep's stomach, cleaned and tied
instructions: Place the chopped heart, liver, and lung in a large bowl.
Add the suet, oatmeal, onion, salt, pepper, nutmeg, cloves, and ginger.
Mix thoroughly by hand until the mixture is uniform.
Gradually add the beef stock while mixing to achieve a sticky, moldable consistency.
Stuff the mixture tightly into the cleaned sheep's stomach.
Tie off both ends securely with kitchen twine.
Simmer in a pot of salted water for 2.5 to 3 hours until cooked through.
Cool slightly, then slice and serve with neeps and tatties.

title: Cullen Skink
ingredients: 3 lbs fresh mackerel fillets, skin on
4 large potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
2 leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Poach the mackerel fillets in a pot with a little water and thyme until just cooked through.
Remove the fish and let it cool, then flake the meat and set aside.
Discard the fish bones and skin.
In the same pot, sauté the onions in butter until soft.
Add the sliced leeks and cook for another 2 minutes.
Stir in the sliced potatoes and pour in the milk and wine.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the potatoes are tender.
Remove the thyme and bay leaves.
Return the flaked mackerel to the soup and heat gently without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve garnished with parsley.

title: Neeps and Tatties
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with half the butter, milk, and cream until smooth.
Season the mashed potatoes with salt and pepper.
In a separate pot, boil the diced turnips until very tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain the turnips and mash them with the remaining butter, cream, milk, salt, and pepper.
Serve the mashed turnips and mashed potatoes alongside your main haggis dish.
Garnish with fresh chives before serving.

title: Cranachan
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen whipped cream, lightly beaten
1/2 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
instructions: Toast the oatmeal in a dry pan until golden brown, then let it cool.
In a large bowl, whip the cream with vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
Fold in the honey until fully incorporated.
Gently fold in the raspberries, strawberries, toasted oatmeal, cinnamon, and salt.
Divide the mixture evenly among serving glasses.
Top each serving with a dollop of fresh whipped cream.
Serve immediately or chill for a few minutes before serving.

title: Cawl
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the lamb and stock in a large pot and bring to a simmer.
Skim off any scum that rises to the surface.
Add the leeks, swede, carrots, and thyme, then cover and simmer gently for 1.5 hours.
Add the cabbage and potatoes, then cook for another 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

title: Lamprey Pie
ingredients: 500g fresh eel or smoked lamprey fillets
instructions: Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the onion, leek, and carrots until softened.
Add the potatoes and eel to the pan, then pour in the milk and simmer until the liquid reduces and thickens.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper, then transfer to a pie dish.
Roll out the puff pastry and place it over the filling, crimping the edges to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Bara Brith
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F) and grease a 20cm loaf tin.
Mix the flour, brown sugar, spices, and dried fruits in a large bowl.
Cream together the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract.
Fold the dry fruit mixture into the wet mixture until just combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes before turning out onto a wire rack.

title: Pork Sausages with Mushrooms and Onions
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the onions and cook for 5 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the mushrooms and thyme, then cook for another 5 minutes until the mushrooms release their water.
Increase the heat to high, then add the sausages, splitting them open to lay flat.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the sausages are golden and cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve immediately.

title: Welsh Rarebit
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and toast the bread slices until golden.
In a saucepan, melt the butter over low heat and whisk in the milk until it thickens slightly.
Stir in the cheese, mustard powder, dry mustard, salt, Worcestershire sauce, and lemon juice.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then remove from heat and stir in the beaten eggs.
Spread a generous layer of the sauce over each slice of toasted bread.
Place the slices on a baking tray and bake for 5 minutes until the top is bubbly and golden.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and pickled onions on the side.

title: Buttered Taters
ingredients: 6 large russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place sliced potatoes in a large baking dish.
Pour melted butter, sour cream, milk, salt, and pepper over potatoes.
Toss to coat evenly.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until tender.
Sprinkle with chopped chives before serving.

title: Poutine
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C) and bake fries until crispy.
In a saucepan, combine broth, mustard, vinegar, and salt; bring to a simmer.
In a bowl, whisk flour and butter until smooth.
Slowly add the broth mixture to the flour mixture while whisking to make gravy.
Simmer gravy for 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Place hot fries on a plate, top with cheese curds, and pour gravy over everything.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix graham cracker crumbs, 1/3 cup butter, and sugar; press into an 8x8 pan.
In a saucepan, melt 1/2 cup butter with sugar and cocoa powder.
Add milk, cornstarch, and vanilla; cook until thickened.
Pour mixture over crust and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Beat whipped cream with confectioners' sugar until stiff peaks form.
Spread whipped cream over the chilled layer and refrigerate until set.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a bowl, combine meats, onion, garlic, thyme, sage, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
In a saucepan, sauté flour in butter until bubbly.
Add broth and tomato paste to the roux; simmer until thickened.
Spread filling into a pie dish and cover with puff pastry.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until pastry is golden brown.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat Sandwich
instructions: Season brisket with onion, garlic, paprika, pepper, and caraway seeds.
Sear brisket in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Add broth to the pot and braise covered for 3-4 hours until tender.
Slice the meat thinly against the grain.
Toast rye rolls and spread mustard on the inside.
Layer meat, Swiss cheese, and extra onion on the rolls and serve hot.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add meats, cherries, parsley, thyme, cinnamon, and nutmeg; cook until meat is browned and juices reduce.
Stir in apple cider and simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer mixture to a baking dish and cover with thawed puff pastry.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden brown.

title: Poutine
instructions: Fry french fries until golden and crispy; drain on paper towels.
Heat beef gravy in a saucepan over medium heat until simmering.
Toss hot fries with a small amount of vegetable oil to make them glossy.
Immediately sprinkle cheese curds over the hot fries.
Pour hot gravy over the fries and cheese until everything is coated.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk milk, oil, and vanilla.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until a soft dough forms.
Shape dough into a log or individual patties.
Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Place ham in a roasting pan and score the surface in a diamond pattern.
In a saucepan, combine maple syrup, brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and orange juice; simmer until thickened.
Brush the glaze over the ham.
Bake for 15-20 minutes per pound until internal temperature reaches 140°F (60°C).
Brush with remaining glaze during the last 15 minutes of cooking.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix graham cracker crumbs with melted butter and press into the bottom of a lined 8x8 pan.
Beat eggs, sugar, and vanilla until thick and pale; fold in cocoa powder and press over the crust.
Bake for 10 minutes and cool completely.
Whip powdered sugar, softened butter, cream cheese, cocoa, and vanilla until smooth for the topping.
Spread topping over the cooled base and refrigerate for 1 hour to set.

title: Poutine
instructions: Cook frozen french fries according to package directions until crispy.
Pour beef gravy over the hot fries.
Immediately cover with cheese curds.
Serve immediately while hot and gooey.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine meats, onion, apple, flour, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Press mixture into a greased 9-inch pie dish.
Cover with puff pastry, crimping edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until crust is golden brown.

title: Buttered Tater Tots
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Arrange frozen tater tots in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Mix melted butter, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Drizzle the butter mixture over the tater tots and toss to coat.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden and crispy.

title: Maple Glazed Salmon
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in an oven-safe skillet.
In a small saucepan, combine maple syrup, butter, dill, and pepper; simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour the glaze over the salmon.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 12-15 minutes until salmon flakes easily.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, mix milk, oil, molasses, and maple syrup.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until a dough forms.
Shape dough into flat rounds, place on the baking sheet, and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 lbs french fries, cut and cooked
instructions: Cook french fries in oil until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Pour hot beef gravy over the hot fries to warm them slightly.
Immediately cover the fries completely with cheese curds.
Serve immediately while hot and crispy.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 2 lbs ground pork, mixed with veal
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion, carrot, celery, and garlic until softened.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in flour, cranberries, and spices, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add stock and simmer until thickened.
Roll out puff pastry on a baking sheet.
Spread meat mixture into the center of the pastry, leaving a border.
Fold the pastry edges up over the filling and crimp to seal.
Brush with egg wash if desired and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 30-40 minutes until golden.

title: Buttered Taters with Maple Syrup
ingredients: 3 lbs russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss potato wedges in a large bowl with melted butter, maple syrup, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 30 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes until potatoes are tender and edges are caramelized.

title: Newfoundland Cod Cakes
ingredients: 1 lb white fish fillets (cod or haddock), flaked
instructions: Mix flaked fish, mashed potato, onion, egg, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Refrigerate the mixture for 30 minutes to firm up.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Form the mixture into small patties and place in the hot oil.
Fry for 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Saskatoon Berry Buckwheat Pancakes
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
Butter and maple syrup for serving
instructions: Whisk together buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk buttermilk, egg, and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined; do not overmix.
Fold in the Saskatoon berries gently.
Heat a griddle or non-stick pan over medium heat and grease with butter.
Pour batter onto the pan to form pancakes.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set, then flip and cook until golden.
Serve immediately with butter and maple syrup.

title: Poutine
instructions: Cook french fries until golden and crisp, then drain.
Pour vegetable oil over hot fries to seal them.
Top fries with fresh curds cheese.
Pour hot beef gravy over the cheese immediately.

title: Buttered Taters
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender.
Drain and return potatoes to the hot pot.
Add butter and toss to coat evenly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix melted butter, graham crumbs, and cocoa to make the crust.
Press crust firmly into a greased 9x9 inch pan.
Beat eggs, sugar, and vanilla until fluffy.
Fold in chocolate chips and spread over crust.
Chill until set, then cut into squares.

title: Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, then sear in butter until browned.
Remove beef and sauté onions and mushrooms until soft.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in beef broth and return beef to the pan.
Simmer until thickened, then stir in sour cream.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (163°C).
Mix maple syrup, brown sugar, cinnamon, and melted butter.
Pour mixture over the ham in a roasting pan.
Roast for 10-15 minutes per pound until internal temp reaches 140°F.
Let rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Brown the salt pork in a large skillet until crisp, then remove and crumble.
Sauté onions and garlic in the fat until soft.
Add ground pork and veal, cooking until browned.
Sprinkle in thyme, sage, nutmeg, cinnamon, and flour, stirring to coat meat.
Pour in enough beef broth to reach a gravy consistency, simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in beaten eggs and crumbled salt pork.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry and press into a 9-inch pie dish.
Pour meat mixture into crust, cover with remaining dough, and crimp edges.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Poutine
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C).
Bake frozen fries for 20 minutes, shaking basket halfway through, until crispy.
Bring beef broth to a simmer in a saucepan.
Whisk together flour, butter, salt, and pepper in the simmering broth until thickened into gravy.
Place fries in deep bowls.
Immediately cover fries with hot gravy.
Top generously with fresh cheese curds.

title: Buttered Taters
ingredients: 1 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Add potatoes and cook for 15-20 minutes until tender but not falling apart.
Drain potatoes and return to the pot.
Add butter, milk, salt, and pepper to the hot potatoes.
Stir vigorously for 1 minute until butter melts and mixture is creamy.
Garnish with chopped chives before serving.

title: Bannock
ingredients: 1/2 cup vegetable oil or melted butter
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together warm water, milk, and oil.
Pour liquid ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until a dough forms.
Knead briefly on a floured surface for 2 minutes.
Shape dough into balls and flatten with a rolling pin or hands.
Place on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Cut into wedges while warm.

title: Lobster Roll
ingredients: 4 hot dog buns, split and toasted
instructions: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard, and celery.
Fold in the chopped lobster meat, salt, and any lobster broth from the shell.
Toast the hot dog buns on a griddle with butter until golden.
Spoon the lobster mixture onto the bottom half of each bun.
Cover with the top bun and serve immediately.

title: Poutine
instructions: Fry potatoes until crispy and drain on paper towels.
Pour hot beef gravy over the fries.
Immediately sprinkle fresh curds cheese on top.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Buttered Toast with Maple Syrup
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Spread softened butter generously on each slice.
Drizzle maple syrup over the buttered toast.
Serve warm.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Melt butter in a skillet and sauté onion, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add ground meat, apple brandy, thyme, and sage; cook until meat is browned.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Place pastry sheets in a pie dish, fill with meat mixture, and cover with top crust.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until pastry is golden.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Score the ham in a diamond pattern without cutting through the bone.
Mix maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Brush the glaze mixture generously over the entire ham.
Bake at 325°F (160°C) for 15-18 minutes per pound.
Baste with remaining glaze every 30 minutes during cooking.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8x8 inch pan.
Mix graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and eggs in a bowl; press firmly into the pan to form a crust.
Bake crust for 8-10 minutes until set, then cool completely.
In a saucepan, melt butter and chocolate chips until smooth.
Whisk eggs, sugar, cocoa, and milk in a bowl until creamy.
Fold chocolate mixture into the egg mixture until combined.
Pour filling over the cooled crust and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to set.

title: Poutine
instructions: Cook french fries until crispy and drain on paper towels.
Boil frozen peas in a pot of water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add vinegar, salt, and sour cream to the melted butter, whisking until smooth.
Pour the cheese sauce over the hot fries.
Immediately top with cheese curds and serve.

title: Beef Stroganoff
instructions: Toss beef cubes in flour and season with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and mushrooms in the same pan until softened.
Stir in beef broth and return beef to the pan.
Simmer for 15 minutes until beef is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream before serving.

title: Buttered Tater Tots
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Arrange tater tots in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden and crispy.
While tots bake, melt butter in a small saucepan.
Add milk, cheese, garlic powder, and salt to the butter.
Simmer until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Pour sauce over hot tots and toss to coat evenly.

title: Chicken Marengo
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Brown chicken pieces on all sides, then remove.
Sauté onion and garlic in the pot until fragrant.
Add tomato sauce, wine, bay leaf, and chicken back to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Bannock
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir in milk and melted butter until a dough forms.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a flat disc about 1/2 inch thick.
Place discs on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on a wire rack before serving.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb french fries, cut and fried until golden
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and bake fries until crisp.
In a saucepan, combine milk and mustard; heat gently until warm but not boiling.
Place fries in a large bowl and pour melted butter over them.
Immediately top with cheese curds and warm cheese sauce.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 2 lbs ground pork or beef mixture
instructions: Sauté onions, carrots, and celery in butter until soft.
Add meat, garlic, thyme, and allspice; cook until browned.
Stir in currants and flour; simmer for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out pastry and place in a baking dish.
Spread meat mixture evenly into the crust.
Brush edges with beaten egg and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Buttered Taters
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil sliced potatoes in salted water until tender but not mushy.
Drain potatoes well and return to pot.
Stir in melted butter, sour cream, cheese, and green onions.
Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cover and let sit for 5 minutes to absorb flavors before serving.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Score the fat of the ham in a diamond pattern.
Mix maple syrup, mustard, brown sugar, cloves, and cinnamon into a glaze.
Place ham in a roasting pan and bake for 15 minutes per pound.
Remove ham, brush with half the glaze, and return to oven for 10 minutes.
Brush with remaining glaze and bake for another 10-15 minutes until set.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
ingredients: 3 cups fresh saskatoon berries, frozen or fresh
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, mix berries, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and vanilla.
Place bottom crust in a pie dish and fill with berry mixture.
Cover with top crust and crimp edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top crust to vent steam.
Brush crust with beaten egg and bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb french fries, fried until golden
instructions: Fry french fries until crisp and drain on paper towels.
Arrange hot cheese curds over the fries immediately.
Pour hot beef gravy evenly over the fries and curds.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Buttered Taters
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
instructions: Boil potato slices in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain potatoes and return to the hot pot.
Stir in melted butter until potatoes are coated.
Fold in sour cream and chopped chives.
Serve warm as a side dish.

title: Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 lb ham hock or diced ham
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in a pot until softened.
Add ham hock, chicken broth, bay leaf, and peas.
Simmer for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove ham hock, shred meat, and return to pot.
Remove bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.
Puree the soup with an immersion blender until smooth.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and apple in a large skillet until soft.
Add ground pork and beef, cooking until browned.
Stir in thyme, sage, and beef stock; simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer meat mixture to a baking dish.
Cover with thawed puff pastry and trim edges.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/4 cup sugar; press into an 8x8 pan.
Beat eggs, 1/3 cup sugar, and 1/4 cup butter until fluffy.
Stir in milk, cocoa powder, and vanilla.
Pour over crust and chill for 30 minutes.
Whip remaining ingredients for topping until stiff peaks form.
Spread topping over chilled layer and refrigerate until set.

title: Poutine
instructions: Fry frozen french fries until crispy and set aside.
Combine beef broth and butter in a saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Slowly whisk in cheese curds until melted and smooth.
Pour cheese sauce over hot fries.
Sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.

title: Buttered Tater Tots
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Arrange tater tots on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add tots to skillet and toss to coat in butter.
Season with salt, pepper, and green onions.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Score the ham in a diamond pattern without cutting through.
Mix maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, garlic, and ginger.
Pour mixture over the ham.
Bake covered with foil for 3 hours.
Remove foil, increase heat to 400°F (200°C), and bake 15 minutes more until glaze is bubbly.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in butter until soft.
Add ground meats and cook until browned.
Stir in currants, apple juice, and spices.
Simmer mixture for 10 minutes until liquid reduces.
Press pie crust into a pie dish.
Fill with meat mixture and top with puff pastry.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 35-40 minutes until crust is golden.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix softened butter, powdered sugar, cocoa, flour, and vanilla for the crust.
Press mixture firmly into a lined 8x8 pan and chill.
Melt butter and mix with cocoa and coffee for the filling.
Gradually add powdered sugar and nuts to filling.
Spread filling over chilled crust.
Sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Chill for 30 minutes, then cut into squares.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Score the ham surface in a diamond pattern.
Mix maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, and garlic in a bowl.
Brush the glaze generously over the ham.
Roast for 15-18 minutes per pound until internal temperature reaches 140°F (60°C).
Let rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Buttered Peas and Bacon
instructions: Rinse the split peas thoroughly and drain.
Fry the chopped bacon in a large pot until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Add butter to the pot and sauté the onion until soft.
Stir in the rinsed peas, salt, and pepper.
Add 4 cups of water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1-1.5 hours until tender.

title: Poutine
instructions: Fry french fries until golden and crispy; drain on paper towels.
In a saucepan, heat milk and melt 2 tablespoons of butter.
Whisk in flour and cook over medium heat for 1 minute.
Gradually add cold butter cubes while whisking vigorously until smooth.
Season gravy with salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Place fries on a serving platter, top with cheese curds.
Pour hot gravy over fries and curds immediately before serving.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix graham crumbs, 1/3 cup butter, and 2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar for the base.
Press firmly into a lined 8x8 inch pan and chill for 30 minutes.
Beat softened butter, 3/4 cup confectioners' sugar, cocoa, and vanilla for the filling.
Spread filling evenly over the chilled base and chill for 1 hour.
Heat chocolate chips and cream in microwave until melted and smooth.
Pour over filling and chill until set.
Drizzle with melted butter and cut into squares.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté onions, carrots, prunes, and cranberries in butter until softened.
Add ground meats to the pot and cook until browned.
Stir in flour, apple cider, thyme, nutmeg, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Simmer mixture for 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Pour filling into a pie dish and cover with a pastry crust.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until crust is golden brown.
Serve warm.

title: Buttered Roll-Up
instructions: In a large bowl, mix ground beef, ground pork, milk, butter, salt, and pepper until well combined.
In a separate bowl, combine breadcrumbs, egg, chives, parsley, shallots, and Parmesan cheese.
Add the breadcrumb mixture to the meat mixture and mix until fully incorporated.
Shape the mixture into 8 equal patties, flattening them slightly.
Set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and additional breadcrumbs if desired.
Dredge each patty in flour, then dip in egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Fry patties for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot with your favorite condiments.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb extra-sharp white cheddar cheese curds
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Spread frozen fries on a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes, flipping halfway through, until crispy.
Meanwhile, in a saucepan, whisk together flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder, egg, milk, melted butter, beef broth, thyme, and paprika.
Cook the mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens into a gravy.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Place a generous amount of crispy fries on a serving plate.
Top immediately with a mound of fresh cheese curds.
Pour the hot gravy evenly over the fries and cheese curds.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Cut in the lard or shortening until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
In a separate bowl, mix warm water, molasses, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until a dough forms.
Knead the dough briefly on a floured surface until smooth.
Shape the dough into a log, cut into 12 equal pieces, and roll each into a ball.
Place the balls on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly before serving.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add onions, carrots, celery, and garlic; sauté until softened.
Add ground pork, beef, and veal to the skillet and cook until browned.
Stir in prunes, raisins, sugar, brandy, beef broth, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly.
Transfer the mixture to a pie dish.
Cover with a pre-made pie crust or puff pastry.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Maple Syrup Roast Beef
ingredients: 4 large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C) for the first 15 minutes, then reduce to 325°F (160°C).
Mix maple syrup, softened butter, Dijon mustard, salt, pepper, rosemary, and thyme in a small bowl.
Rub the herb mixture generously all over the roast.
Place carrots, potatoes, and onion in a large roasting pan.
Set the roast on top of the vegetables.
Roast for 15 minutes at 450°F, then lower temperature to 325°F.
Roast for an additional 15-20 minutes per pound, or until internal temperature reaches 135°F for medium-rare.
Remove roast from oven and let rest for 20 minutes before slicing.
Drain juices from the pan and serve with the vegetables.

title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients: 12 oz elbow macaroni, cooked al dente
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce.
Transfer to a greased baking dish.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Buttered Taters with Pea Pods
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cut potatoes into large wedges.
Toss potatoes with 4 tbsp butter and salt.
Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 45 minutes until tender.
Steam pea pods for 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
In a saucepan, melt remaining 2 tbsp butter over medium heat.
Add green onions and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in cream and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with white pepper and toss with peas.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 lbs frozen cut potatoes, cooked until crispy
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss frozen potatoes with oil, garlic powder, and salt.
Bake for 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until crispy.
While potatoes bake, combine cheese, broth, vinegar, and garlic powder in a saucepan.
Heat over low heat, stirring until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.
Place hot crispy fries on a serving platter.
Pour cheese gravy generously over the fries.
Serve immediately.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, melt lard over medium heat.
Sauté onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add ground meats and cook until browned, breaking them up with a spoon.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add cranberries, thyme, salt, nutmeg, and stock.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Transfer filling to a baking dish.
Cover with a pastry crust and bake for 45 minutes until golden.

title: French-Style Maple Glazed Salmon
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a small bowl, whisk maple syrup, mustard, soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and pepper.
Pat salmon fillets dry and season lightly with salt.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon skin-side down for 3 minutes until crisp.
Flip salmon and spoon half the glaze over the fish.
Transfer skillet to the oven and bake for 8-10 minutes.
Remove from oven, brush with remaining glaze.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Tourtière
ingredients: 1 lb ground pork, mixed with ground beef
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large pot, sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic until softened.
Add meat mixture and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in cranberries, raisins, broth, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, and butter.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the filling is thick and flavors have melded.
Transfer filling to a baking dish and cover with the puff pastry.
Cut slits in the top of the pastry to vent steam.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add warm water and oil, stirring until a dough forms.
Knead briefly until smooth.
Roll out dough on a floured surface to about 1/2 inch thickness.
Cut into rounds or shapes with a knife or biscuit cutter.
Place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve warm.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb fresh curds cheese or vichy cheese
instructions: Cook french fries according to package instructions until crispy.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Pour in heavy cream, milk, butter, flour, pepper, and salt.
Whisk constantly over medium heat until the cheese sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Add curds cheese to the sauce and stir until melted and creamy.
Place hot fries on a serving platter.
Immediately pour the cheese sauce over the fries.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Maple Glazed Ham
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Scrub the ham clean and place it in a large roasting pan.
In a small bowl, mix maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper.
Brush the glaze generously over the entire surface of the ham.
Cover the ham loosely with foil.
Roast for 3 hours, basting with glaze every 30 minutes.
Remove foil and continue roasting for another 30 minutes until the glaze is caramelized.
Let the ham rest for 15 minutes before slicing.
Serve with the remaining glaze.

title: Pea Soup with Bacon
ingredients: 1 lb bacon, cut into small pieces
1 lb fresh peas or frozen peas
instructions: Render the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crispy, leaving the fat in the pot.
Remove bacon and set aside, crumbing it slightly.
Sauté onion and celery in the bacon fat until soft.
Add peas and broth, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in butter and flour to thicken the soup slightly.
Blend the soup until smooth using an immersion blender.
Stir in heavy cream and return to a gentle simmer.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, topped with crispy bacon bits.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 2 cups sharp white cheddar cheese curds
instructions: Fry French fries until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Pour beef gravy into a saucepan and heat until simmering.
Pour hot gravy over the fries in a large bowl.
Immediately sprinkle cheese curds over the top.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Buttered Tater Tots
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss frozen tater tots with melted butter, garlic powder, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Serve topped with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Chicken and Rice Casserole
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a large bowl, mix cooked rice, diced chicken, peas, soup, and milk.
Transfer mixture to a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Drizzle melted butter over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbly and lightly browned.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in a large skillet until soft.
Add ground pork and beef, cooking until browned.
Stir in flour, beef broth, and thyme; simmer for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place filling between two sheets of puff pastry and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden.

title: Maple Glazed Donuts
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm milk, let sit for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, eggs, vanilla, and maple syrup into the yeast mixture.
Knead dough on a floured surface until smooth and elastic.
Let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Cut into rings, fry in hot butter until golden, and drain on paper towels.

title: Cod Faggots
ingredients: 1 lb fresh Atlantic cod, minced fine
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the minced cod and chopped onion to the fat, cooking gently until the mixture loses its raw smell but is not browned.
Stir in the dill, eggs, bread crumbs, fried bacon, salt, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small oval patties.
Pan-fry the patties in butter or oil until golden brown on both sides.

title: Newfoundland Bannock
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and caraway seeds in a large bowl.
Add the water and melted butter to the dry ingredients.
Stir until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not knead.
Grease a cast-iron skillet or griddle with butter.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough onto the hot skillet and flatten slightly with a spatula.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until bubbles form and the bottom is golden, then flip and cook the other side.

title: Fried Cod with Salt Cod Style Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup salt cod, soaked overnight and well-drained
instructions: Dredge the fresh cod fillets first in flour, then dip in the beaten egg.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry the fillets until golden and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Remove cod and drain on paper towels.
Soak the salt cod in cold water overnight to remove excess salt, then squeeze dry.
Mix the drained salt cod with the mashed potatoes, milk, white pepper, and cayenne.
Serve the fried cod hot alongside the creamy salt cod sauce.

title: Jiggs Dinner (Slow-Cooked Corned Beef and Cabbage)
ingredients: 1 large corned beef brisket, with spices packet
4 carrots, peeled and cut into large chunks
1 head green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Place the corned beef in a large pot and cover with water.
Add the onion, bay leaf, and peppercorns to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 3 hours.
Add the potatoes, carrots, turnips, and rutabaga to the pot and continue cooking for 1.5 hours.
Add the cabbage wedges last and cook for another 30-45 minutes until the meat is tender and vegetables are soft.
Remove the meat, let it rest for 10 minutes, then slice against the grain and serve with the vegetables and cooking juices.

title: Fried Haddock with Mushrooms
instructions: Set up a breading station with flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge haddock fillets in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat butter in a skillet and fry the fillets until golden and flaky.
In the same pan, sauté the sliced mushrooms and chopped onion until browned.
Sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms and cook for 1 minute to remove raw taste.
Slowly whisk in the milk to create a smooth, thick sauce, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the fried haddock topped with the mushroom sauce and garnished with parsley.

title: Poutine
ingredients: 1 lb fresh-cut fries, deep-fried until golden
instructions: Fry the fresh-cut potatoes in vegetable oil until crisp and golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
Pour the hot beef gravy into a saucepan and warm it through until just before boiling.
Drain the fresh curds cheese well and place in a large bowl.
Add the hot fries and warm gravy to the bowl with the cheese.
Toss gently to coat everything evenly and serve immediately.

title: Tourtière
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add ground pork and veal to the skillet; cook until browned and no longer pink.
Stir in flour, thyme, cinnamon, and nutmeg, cooking for 1 minute to remove raw flour taste.
Remove from heat, stir in currants, and let the meat mixture cool slightly.
Transfer filling to the pie dish and cover with the pie dough.
Crimp edges to seal and cut slits in the top crust for steam.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until crust is golden brown.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Poutine au Potimarron
ingredients: 1 kg butternut squash, peeled and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss butternut squash cubes with butter, maple syrup, and cinnamon on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelized.
In a large bowl, combine the warm roasted squash, hot fries, and fresh curds cheese.
Pour the hot beef gravy over the mixture.
Toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Tarte au Sucre
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Press the pie dough into a 9-inch pie plate and prick the bottom with a fork.
In a large bowl, beat the fresh curds cheese until smooth.
Gradually add sugar, flour, milk, and vanilla extract, mixing until well combined.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pie crust.
Brush the edges of the crust with the beaten egg.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until the filling is set and the crust is golden.
Cool on a wire rack before slicing.

title: Mousse au Chocolat
instructions: Melt chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, beat egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Stir the yolk mixture into the melted chocolate.
In another clean bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the chocolate mixture.
Fold in the whipped heavy cream gently.
Spoon into serving dishes and chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Buttered Baked Potatoes
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Prick potatoes all over with a fork and place them directly on the oven rack.
Bake for 60-75 minutes until skins are crispy and insides are fluffy.
Slice potatoes open and spoon melted butter generously over the top.
Sprinkle with garlic powder, salt, pepper, and fresh chives.

title: Swiss Steak with Brown Gravy
ingredients: 1 lb Swiss steak or round steak, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Toss beef cubes with flour, salt, and pepper until lightly coated.
Sear meat in a large pot with a little oil until browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion, carrot, and garlic until softened.
Return meat to the pot and add beef broth, ketchup, tomato paste, and Worcestershire sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until meat is tender.
Whisk remaining flour with a splash of cold water to make a slurry, stir into gravy, and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.

title: Nanaimo Bars
instructions: Mix graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and egg yolks in a bowl; press firmly into the bottom of a 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Beat remaining egg yolks, powdered sugar, softened butter, cocoa, and vanilla until smooth and creamy.
Spread the cream layer evenly over the crust.
Melt chocolate chips and butter with shortening in the microwave or over a double boiler.
Pour the chocolate glaze over the cream layer and let set in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Slice into bars before serving.

title: Bannock Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, and molasses.
Make a well in the center and add milk and oil; stir until a dough forms.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Roll dough into a circle about 1/2 inch thick or shape into a long log.
Place on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Slice into rounds or segments and serve warm.

title: Chicken and Rice Casserole
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and whisk in flour to make a roux.
Slowly stir in chicken broth while whisking to avoid lumps.
Add cooked rice, chicken, peas, corn, salt, pepper, and thyme to the pot.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Transfer mixture to a greased baking dish.
Cover with foil and bake for 20-25 minutes until heated through.

title: Grandma's Nova Scotia Baked Salmon
ingredients: 2 lbs wild Atlantic salmon fillets, skin-on
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Pat salmon dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Place fillets skin-side down in an oiled baking dish.
Top each fillet with garlic, dill, and lemon slices.
Drizzle olive oil over the top.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until fish flakes easily.

title: Salt Cod and Potato Bake
ingredients: 1 lb salt cod, soaked and desalted overnight
4 large russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Melt butter in a large baking dish and sauté onion until soft.
Add soaked cod pieces, potatoes, and carrots to the dish.
Pour in milk and sprinkle with nutmeg.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil, bake uncovered for 15 more minutes until potatoes are tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Smoked Haddock and Cabbage Casserole
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, then gradually add milk.
Stir in celery salt and simmer until thickened.
In a baking dish, layer shredded cabbage and flaked haddock.
Pour the sauce over the fish and cabbage.
Top with cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Halibut with Wild Rice and Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 cup wild rice, cooked according to package
instructions: Season halibut steaks with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Sear halibut in olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side.
Remove fish and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté mushrooms until browned.
Add white wine and scrape up browned bits from the pan.
Return fish to the pan, spoon mushroom sauce over it.
Garnish with lemon juice and serve over wild rice.

title: Stewed Cod with Brown Sugar and Butter
ingredients: 1 lb cod fillets, cut into chunks
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add brown sugar, ginger, and cinnamon; stir until melted and bubbly.
Add water and bring to a simmer.
Gently place cod chunks into the sauce.
Simmer covered for 10-12 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in parsley just before serving.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Acadian Lobster Stew
ingredients: 1 large lobster, live, cleaned and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and celery until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add lobster pieces and cook for 2 minutes until slightly pink.
Stir in potato, fish stock, white wine, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until lobster is fully cooked.
Stir in fresh parsley and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: New Brunswick Whitefish Chowder
ingredients: 1.5 kg fresh whitefish (smelt or flounder), filleted and cubed
instructions: In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat.
Cook onions until translucent, then add flour and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Add potatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Gently fold in the whitefish cubes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in cream, salt, and white pepper.
Serve immediately garnished with fresh dill.

title: Baked Haddock with Lemon and Herbs
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
1/2 cup breadcrumbs, mixed with melted butter
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Place haddock fillets in a greased baking dish.
Mix melted butter, lemon juice, zest, herbs, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Spread the herb mixture over the fish fillets.
Cover the fish with the breadcrumb topping.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until fish flakes easily with a fork.
Serve hot, optionally with boiled potatoes.

title: Pea Soup with Bacon and Ham
ingredients: 1 lb Canadian bacon or ham, diced
instructions: In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat.
Sauté onion and carrots until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute, then slowly stir in broth.
Add diced bacon, ham, and fresh peas.
Simmer for 20 minutes until peas are tender.
Stir in heavy cream and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with extra crumbled bacon.

title: Acadian Skillet Cornbread
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a cast iron skillet.
In a large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk eggs, buttermilk, melted butter, corn, and chives.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Pour batter into the hot skillet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Let cool slightly before serving warm.

title: Manitoba Maple Ham with Glazed Onions
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Place ham in a large roasting pan and add 1/2 cup water to the bottom.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 3 hours.
Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in maple syrup, brown sugar, salt, and pepper.
Remove ham from oven, uncover, and brush generously with onion mixture.
Return to oven uncovered and bake for another 30-45 minutes until glaze is set.
Let rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Saskatoon Berry Buckwheat Pancakes
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh or frozen saskatoon berries, thawed
instructions: Whisk buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg, buttermilk, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir just until combined; lumps are okay.
Fold in the saskatoon berries gently.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and grease lightly with butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto the hot surface.
Cook until bubbles form on top and edges look set, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip and cook until golden brown on the other side, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Prairie Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large skillet, cook chicken over medium-high heat until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, carrots, celery, and garlic; cook until vegetables soften, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the mixture and stir for 1 minute to remove raw flour taste.
Slowly stir in chicken broth and heavy cream until smooth.
Add thyme, salt, and pepper; simmer until slightly thickened.
Transfer mixture to a greased 9-inch pie dish.
Place puff pastry over the top, sealing edges with a fork.
Cut slits in the center of the pastry to let steam escape.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Wild Rice and Barley Soup with Caribou
ingredients: 1 lb caribou meat, trimmed and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat.
Add caribou meat and sear until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and carrots; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in wild rice, barley, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Pour in beef stock and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes until grains are tender and meat is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh parsley.

title: Prairie Skillet Fried Green Tomatoes
ingredients: 4-5 large green tomatoes, sliced 1/2 inch thick
instructions: In a shallow dish, mix flour, cornstarch, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
In another shallow dish, whisk together eggs and buttermilk.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Dip each tomato slice first in the egg mixture, letting excess drip off.
Coat thoroughly in the flour mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Fry slices in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Remove to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Dust lightly with sugar if desired while still warm.
Serve immediately with ranch dressing or sour cream.

title: Classic Alberta Beef Stew
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Toss beef cubes in flour, shaking off excess.
Brown beef in oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened.
Stir in broth, bay leaves, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2.5 hours until beef is tender.
Remove bay leaves before serving.

title: Prairie Chicken and Wild Rice
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, boneless and skinless
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet; cook chicken until golden and cooked through.
Remove chicken; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add wild rice blend and toast for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot and cook covered for 45 minutes.
Stir in peas and cheese until melted.
Garnish with fresh parsley.

title: Manitoba-Style Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Combine milk, melted butter, oil, and egg in a separate bowl.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients; mix until a dough forms.
Roll dough into 1-inch thick circles on a floured surface.
Place circles on a baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm with butter.

title: Smoked Bacon and Potato Casserole
ingredients: 1 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook bacon in a skillet until crispy; drain and reserve fat.
Sauté onion in reserved bacon fat until soft.
Add potatoes to the skillet; cook for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk sour cream, heavy cream, cheese, butter, salt, and pepper.
Pour cream mixture over potatoes and stir to combine.
Transfer to a greased baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until potatoes are tender and topping is bubbly.

title: Root Vegetable and Lentil Stew
instructions: Rinse lentils and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, carrots, and parsnips; cook until softened.
Stir in garlic and sage; cook for 1 minute.
Add lentils and vegetable broth; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in peas and cook for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Baked Salmon with Huckleberries and Potatoes
ingredients: 1.5 lbs Yukon Gold potatoes, sliced thin
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss potato slices with half the melted butter, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Place salmon fillets on the same sheet, seasoning with salt, pepper, and dill.
Drizzle remaining butter and maple syrup over the salmon.
Scatter huckleberries over the fish.
Roast for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are tender and salmon flakes easily.
Serve immediately with extra berries if desired.

title: Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Bagels
instructions: Toast the bagels until golden brown.
Spread a generous layer of cream cheese on each bagel half.
Layer the smoked salmon slices over the cream cheese.
Sprinkle with capers, green onions, and fresh dill.
Add red onion slices if using.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side to squeeze over the top.
Eat immediately while warm.

title: Poutine with Local Beets
ingredients: 1.5 cups beef gravy, homemade or store-bought
instructions: Fry frozen potato wedges in oil until crisp and golden, then drain on paper towels.
While potatoes are hot, toss the sliced beets with melted butter, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the crispy fries on a large serving platter.
Immediately cover the fries with the warm, buttery beet slices.
Pour the hot beef gravy evenly over the potatoes and beets.
Scatter the fresh mozzarella cheese curds on top immediately.
Serve instantly so the cheese stays squeaky.

title: Pacific Halibut with Wild Rice
ingredients: 2 cups wild rice blend, cooked according to package
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season halibut steaks generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the halibut for 3-4 minutes per side until opaque and flaky.
Remove fish from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
In the same pan, stir in cooked wild rice, parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Warm the rice mixture for 1-2 minutes.
Plate the halibut over the wild rice and garnish with fresh chives.

title: Maple Glazed Roast Chicken with Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (3-4 lbs), thawed and patted dry
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Mix maple syrup, butter, thyme, rosemary, garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Rub the mixture all over the chicken, including under the skin.
Toss Brussels sprouts with a little oil, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken breast-side up in a roasting pan with sprouts around it.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, basting with pan juices every 20 minutes.
Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Let rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 1 smoked salt cod, soaked and soaked again for 24 hours
instructions: Place the soaked cod in a large pot with the beef stock, molasses, salt, and pepper.
Add the cabbage, carrots, turnip, potatoes, and onion to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 2 to 3 hours until the fish falls apart and vegetables are tender.
Remove the cod, flake it, and return it to the pot if desired, or serve alongside the vegetables.

title: Bannock
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add water, melted butter, and egg if using; mix until a dough forms.
Pat the dough out on a floured surface and cut into rounds.
Place rounds on a baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm.

title: Scalloped Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat; sauté onion until soft.
Add potatoes, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg; stir to coat.
Transfer mixture to a buttered baking dish.
Beat eggs and pour evenly over the potatoes.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 15 minutes until set and slightly browned on top.

title: Fried Cod with Mushrooms
instructions: Season cod fillets with salt and pepper.
Dredge cod in flour, dip in egg, then place on a plate.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cod for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté mushrooms and garlic until soft.
Add parsley to the mushroom mixture.
Serve fried cod immediately with the mushroom sauce on the side.

title: Newfoundland Mince Pie
ingredients: For filling: 2 cups mixed dried fruit
instructions: Mix flour, shortening, brown sugar, and salt for the crust; add milk until dough forms.
Press dough into a pie dish and chill.
Combine dried fruits, raisins, currants, brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and nutmeg for the filling.
Stir in eggs and milk until thickened; pour into crust.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 45-50 minutes until set.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Pâté au Canard
ingredients: 1 whole duck, deboned and cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sear the duck pieces in a heavy pot until browned on all sides.
Remove duck and sauté onion, carrots, and celery in the rendered fat until soft.
Return duck to the pot, add wine, stock, and bay leaf.
Simmer gently for 2 hours until duck is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove meat from bones and chop finely, discarding the bay leaf.
Mix chopped meat with some of the cooking liquid to create a paste.
Press mixture into a greased loaf pan and chill until firm.
Roll out puff pastry, place the chilled pâté on top, and fold edges over.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Tourtière Traditionnelle
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, beef, onion, sage, parsley, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Gradually mix in apple cider and melted butter until the mixture holds together but is not wet.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface and press it into a 9-inch pie dish.
Spoon the meat mixture evenly into the crust, leaving a 1-inch border.
Brush the border with beaten egg to seal.
Cut small slits in the center of the meat to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Poutine Grise
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh white potatoes, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Boil potato cubes in salted water for 15 minutes until just tender.
Drain potatoes and immediately rinse with cold water to stop cooking.
Dry potatoes thoroughly with a clean kitchen towel.
Fry potatoes in deep oil at 375°F (190°C) until crispy and golden, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Heat beef broth in a pot with butter, salt, and pepper until boiling.
Pour hot broth over a mound of cheese curds to melt them slightly.
Place crispy fries on a serving platter.
Top with the melted cheese curds.
Pour hot brown gravy over the entire dish immediately before serving.

title: Soufflé au Riz
instructions: Cook rice in chicken stock until tender and drain well.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in a saucepan, stir in flour to make a roux.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly until thickened into a creamy sauce.
Stir in cooked rice, Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Beat egg whites with cream of tartar until stiff peaks form.
Fold one-third of egg whites into the rice mixture to lighten it.
Gently fold in the remaining egg whites.
Transfer to a greased soufflé dish and smooth the top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25-30 minutes until risen and golden.

title: Tourte aux Choux
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out one sheet of puff pastry and place it in a 9-inch pie dish.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, milk, melted butter, salt, pepper, eggs, and nutmeg.
Add breadcrumbs to the mixture and stir until combined.
Pour the batter over the pastry base, smoothing the top.
Cover with the second sheet of puff pastry.
Press edges together and crimp to seal.
Cut decorative slits in the top pastry.
Brush the entire pie with an egg wash.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown and puffed.

title: Turtle Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery; sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the turtle meat and stir to coat with vegetables.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, mix berries, sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
Pour filling into the bottom pie crust.
Cover with the top crust and crimp edges.
Brush top with beaten egg.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.

title: Ontario Chicken and Dumplings
instructions: Simmer chicken in water for 1 hour until tender.
Remove chicken; strain broth and discard solids.
Return broth to pot and add carrots, celery, and onion; simmer 15 minutes.
Add shredded chicken back to the pot.
In a separate bowl, mix flour, milk, baking powder, and salt to form dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering soup.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes until dumplings float.

title: Maple Glazed Pork Chops
instructions: Season pork chops with salt and pepper.
Sear chops in a skillet over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side.
Remove chops and set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in maple syrup, brown sugar, and mustard.
Return chops to the pan, bone-side down, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Flip chops and cook until glazed and cooked through.

title: Root Beer Floats with Shortbread
ingredients: 2 vanilla ice cream scoops per serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Cream butter and brown sugar until fluffy.
Beat in vanilla extract.
Gradually mix in flour to form a dough.
Roll dough into small balls and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes until edges are golden.
Serve warm shortbread with a scoop of ice cream and a glass of root beer.

title: Nova Scotia Fish and Chips
ingredients: 2 lbs Atlantic haddock, filleted and patted dry
instructions: Season the fish fillets generously with salt and pepper.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Dredge each fillet in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Fry the fish for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with chips and lemon.

title: Baked Cod in Tomato Sauce (Pescatore Style)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft and translucent.
Stir in diced tomatoes, wine, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and gently stir in the heavy cream.
Place cod fillets into the sauce, skin-side up if available.
Cover and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Sprinkle with parsley and fresh basil before serving.

title: Cape Breton Sweet Potato Hash
ingredients: 3 large sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into small cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss sweet potato cubes with salt, pepper, and thyme on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
In a large skillet, cook ground beef in bacon fat until browned.
Stir in green onions and mix with roasted sweet potatoes.
Top each serving with sour cream and cheddar cheese.
Optional: crack an egg on top and finish under the broiler.

title: Halibut with Maple-Mustard Glaze
instructions: Season halibut steaks with salt and white pepper.
In a small saucepan, combine maple syrup, mustard, and dill; heat until simmering.
Place halibut in a baking dish and pour the glaze over the top.
Add lemon slices around the fish.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 12-15 minutes until fish is opaque.
Dot with butter during the last 2 minutes of cooking.

title: Diggedies with Butter and Molasses
ingredients: 2 lbs large Atlantic hake or cod, cleaned
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Clean the fish and pat them completely dry.
In a bowl, mix melted butter, molasses, flour, and celery salt to form a paste.
Rub the paste generously over the entire surface of each fish.
Place fish on a greased baking sheet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the coating is bubbly and the fish is cooked through.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Côte de Niouche with Creamy Sauce
ingredients: 1 lb pork loin, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, then remove and set aside.
In a shallow dish, mix flour with salt and pepper; dip pork cubes in egg, then coat in flour.
Fry pork cubes in bacon fat until golden brown on all sides; remove and keep warm.
Pour in milk and heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, then stir in the cooked bacon before serving.
Serve immediately with boiled potatoes.

title: Poutine Normande
instructions: Soak potato slices in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Fry potatoes in hot oil until golden and crispy; drain on paper towels.
In a saucepan, melt butter and whisk in flour to make a roux.
Gradually add beef broth while whisking until the sauce thickens.
Season sauce with salt, pepper, and a dollop of sour cream.
Place crispy fries on a plate, top generously with cheese cubes, and pour hot sauce over everything.

title: Tourtière à la Manière de Mon Père
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and diced bacon in a large skillet until soft.
Add ground pork and beef to the skillet; cook until browned and no longer pink.
Stir in breadcrumbs, broth, thyme, salt, and nutmeg; mix well and let cool.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Press puff pastry into a 9-inch pie dish, filling with the meat mixture.
Fold edges of pastry over the filling and crimp to seal.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
Serve hot with maple syrup or butter.

title: Soufflé à la Banane
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 6-cup baking dish.
Whisk egg whites until stiff peaks form; fold in half the sugar.
In another bowl, beat egg yolks with remaining sugar until pale and creamy.
Mix mashed bananas, flour, baking powder, vanilla, and salt into the yolk mixture.
Gently fold the banana mixture into the egg whites until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Tarte au Sucre et au Sirop d'Érable
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface and place in a 9-inch pie dish; trim edges.
In a bowl, beat butter, sugar, maple syrup, and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in heavy cream, cinnamon, and nutmeg until well combined.
Pour filling into the pastry shell and sprinkle with chopped pecans.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until pastry is golden and filling is set.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

title: Manitoba Bannock
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Add water gradually and stir until a soft dough forms.
Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Shape into rounds and place on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
instructions: Toss berries with sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
Pour mixture into the unbaked pie crust.
Cover with a second pie crust or lattice top.
Cut slits in the top crust to vent steam.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45-50 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Stuffed Pork Chops
instructions: Season pork chops with salt and pepper.
Make a slit in the center of each chop.
Mix mashed potatoes with cheese and butter.
Stuff each chop with the potato mixture and secure with toothpicks.
Pan-fry in butter over medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through.

title: Wild Rice Soup
instructions: Drain the soaked wild rice and combine with water in a pot.
Add diced onion and chopped carrots.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and continue simmering until rice is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

title: Prairie Chicken Salad
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cooked and cubed
instructions: Toss mixed salad greens in a large bowl.
Add cubed cooked chicken, dried cranberries, and walnuts.
Drizzle maple syrup vinaigrette over the salad.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately as a light lunch or side dish.

title: Alberta-Style Meat and Potatoes
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into 1-inch cubes
