Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside; sauté onions and garlic in the same pot until soft.
Stir in flour and cook for one minute to remove the raw taste.
Pour in beef broth, ketchup, brown sugar, and thyme, stirring to combine.
Return beef and potatoes to the pot, ensuring everything is submerged.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours until tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Country Breakfast Hash
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss diced potatoes with oil and salt, then spread on a baking sheet and roast for 30 minutes.
While potatoes roast, brown the ground beef in a large skillet with butter.
Add diced onions and bell peppers to the beef and cook until softened.
Remove half of the cooked potato mixture and set aside.
Add the remaining potatoes to the skillet with the beef and vegetables.
Pour milk over the mixture and sprinkle with sage; simmer for 5 minutes until liquid reduces.
Make six small wells in the hash and crack an egg into each well.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the eggs and top with the reserved potatoes.
Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes until egg whites are set.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Smoked Bannock Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C).
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and smoked paprika.
In a separate bowl, mix milk, melted butter, and maple syrup.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until a sticky dough forms.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead briefly until smooth.
Divide dough into eight equal balls and flatten each into a patty about 1/4 inch thick.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium heat with a little oil.
Place bannock patties on the hot surface and cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
Flip carefully and cook for another 3-4 minutes on the other side.
Transfer cooked bannock to a baking sheet and place in the oven for 5 minutes to crisp.
Serve warm, traditionally with butter or maple syrup.

title: Prairie Borscht
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef shank, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place beef chunks in a large pot and cover with cold water; bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Add beef stock, bay leaf, salt, and pepper; reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
In a separate pan, sauté onions in oil until translucent.
Add carrots and cook for 5 minutes, then add grated beets and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir the beet mixture into the beef pot and simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Mash a few of the beets in the pot to thicken the soup slightly.
Remove bay leaf and stir in minced garlic.
Ladle soup into bowls and top generously with sour cream and fresh dill.
Serve hot.

title: Maple-Glazed Pork Chops with Rutabaga Mash
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, brown sugar, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Place pork chops in a baking dish and brush generously with the maple glaze.
Roast in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C).
While pork roasts, boil rutabaga cubes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain rutabaga well and return to the pot; add butter and heavy cream.
Mash the rutabaga until smooth and creamy.
Remove pork chops from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the chops and serve alongside the rutabaga mash, drizzling any remaining glaze over the pork.

title: BC Salmon with Dill and Butter
instructions: Pat the salmon fillets dry and season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
In a skillet over medium heat, melt the butter with the minced garlic.
Place the salmon skin-side down in the skillet and cook for 4-5 minutes without moving.
Flip the salmon and cook for another 3-4 minutes until opaque.
Remove from heat, sprinkle with fresh dill, and let rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Pacific Halibut with Root Vegetables
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the root vegetables in olive oil, salt, pepper, and thyme, then spread on a baking sheet.
Place the halibut steaks on top of the vegetables.
Pour the white wine around the fish.
Roast for 12-15 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork and vegetables are tender.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

title: Vancouver Island Cod Chowder
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion and celery until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually add the milk and water, stirring constantly to avoid lumps, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cod cubes and corn, cooking for 10 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in the heavy cream, season with salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh chives.

title: Alaskan King Crab with Garlic Butter
ingredients: 2 lbs cooked Alaskan king crab legs, meat separated
instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat.
Add the minced garlic and Old Bay seasoning, cooking gently for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice and fresh parsley.
Place the crab meat on a serving platter.
Pour the warm garlic butter over the crab meat.
Garnish with lemon slices and extra sea salt before serving.

title: Nanaimo Bar
instructions: Mix graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 1/3 cup cocoa powder in a bowl.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of a greased 9x9 inch pan to form a crust.
In a separate bowl, whisk together sweetened condensed milk, corn syrup, vanilla, and 1/2 cup cocoa powder.
Stir in the powdered sugar and chocolate chips until well combined.
Spread the filling evenly over the crust.
Drizzle with the melted coconut oil to create a glaze and chill for 2 hours.
Cut into squares and store in the refrigerator.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup green kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Combine soaked beans, rice, coconut milk, scallions, allspice, bay leaf, and salt in a pot.
Add water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until rice and beans are tender.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried shrimp, rehydrated and chopped
1/2 tsp scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and green pepper until softened.
Add dried shrimp and scotch bonnet pepper, cooking for 1 minute.
Stir in chopped callaloo and salt, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until greens are tender.

title: Barbadian Fish and Frying Plantains
ingredients: 1 lb red snapper or whole fish, cleaned and filleted
1 ripe plantain, sliced into thick rounds
instructions: Pat fish dry and season with salt and pepper.
Coat fish fillets lightly in flour.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry plantain slices until golden brown on both sides, then remove.
Cook fish fillets for 3-4 minutes per side until flaky.
Serve fish and plantains with lime juice, cilantro, and onion.

title: Haitian Poulet Saucé
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Mix flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Coat chicken pieces in the flour mixture.
Sear chicken in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Pour in chicken broth, ketchup, brown sugar, tomato paste, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.

title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
ingredients: 1.5 lbs flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Season steak with flour, salt, and pepper.
Brown steak in olive oil in a large skillet, then remove.
Sauté onion, garlic, and bell peppers until soft.
Return steak to the pan, add tomato sauce and beef broth.
Simmer covered for 2 hours until meat is very tender and shreds easily.
Shred meat, stir in pimientos and cilantro, and serve.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 cup scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk all marinade ingredients together in a large bowl.
Add chicken pieces to the marinade, ensuring they are fully coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill or oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cook chicken for 25-30 minutes until cooked through and charred.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo
ingredients: 4 oz salted dulse or 1 tbsp salt
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add scotch bonnet pepper and salted dulse.
Stir in chopped callaloo and okra.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable stock.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes until leaves are tender.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Barbadian Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1/2 cup green bananas or plantains, sliced
1 scotch bonnet pepper, whole or minced
instructions: Combine rice, water, coconut milk, thyme, parsley, garlic, and bay leaf in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add cooked kidney beans, sliced green bananas, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Cover again and cook for another 10 minutes until rice is fluffy.
Remove bay leaf and fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
1/2 cup dried pigeon peas, soaked overnight
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and peppers in a large pot with oil.
Add spices, meats, and soaked beans; stir to coat.
Pour in broth and water, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Add pumpkin and carrots; continue simmering for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Guyanese Fry Jacks
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add water, oil, and milk; stir until a thick dough forms.
Let dough rest for 10 minutes.
Divide dough into small balls and flatten into circles.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry jack cakes until golden brown on both sides.
Season lightly with salt and serve immediately.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Mix allspice, peppers, thyme, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, garlic, and ginger in a bowl to make the rub.
Rub the mixture all over the chicken pieces and let marinate for at least 2 hours.
Preheat grill or oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cook the chicken for 45-60 minutes until skin is charred and meat is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Fried Green Plantains
instructions: Peel plantains and cut them into thick rounds.
In one bowl, mix flour, eggs, cornmeal, and salt.
Dip each plantain slice into the batter, ensuring it is coated evenly.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry plantains in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with lime wedges.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 bunch callaloo or spinach leaves, chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté garlic and scotch bonnet pepper for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped callaloo and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and water, then add salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Drain soaked beans and rinse them.
In a pot, combine rice, beans, water, coconut milk, thyme, garlic, salt, and turmeric.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
ingredients: 1/2 cup salted codfish, desalted and flaked
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in water mixed with vinegar for 2 hours, changing water twice.
Sauté onion, green pepper, scotch bonnet pepper, garlic, and thyme in oil until soft.
Add the flaked codfish to the pot and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the drained ackee gently, being careful not to break the pods.
Season with salt and pepper, then cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with fried dumplings or breadfruit.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, bone-in and skin-on
1/2 cup fresh scotch bonnet peppers, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend peppers, thyme, allspice, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sugar, oil, and lime juice until smooth.
Place chicken in a large bowl and pour the marinade over it; mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken for 12-15 minutes per side until skin is charred and meat is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Soak salted codfish in cold water for 24 hours, changing water 3 times, then drain and flake into small pieces.
Sauté onion, green pepper, garlic, and thyme in butter until soft.
Add scotch bonnet pepper and flaked fish; cook for 5 minutes.
Gently fold in the ackee fruit and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve hot with fresh tomato slices on top.

title: Oxtail Stew
instructions: Season oxtail pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown ground beef and oxtail in oil in a large pot.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until fragrant.
Stir in allspice, cinnamon, and bay leaf.
Mix in ketchup, brown sugar, and beef stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours until meat is tender.
Remove bay leaf before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 lb fresh or frozen kidney beans
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear, then drain.
Boil salted pork, onion, green pepper, garlic, thyme, scotch bonnet, bay leaf, and water in a pot for 30 minutes.
Add beans and rice to the pot.
Simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until rice and beans are tender.
Stir gently to avoid breaking grains.
Serve hot, typically with fried dumplings.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 lb callaloo leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Heat butter and oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper until soft.
Add okra and stir for 2 minutes.
Add callaloo leaves and salt; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh crab meat if using.
Cook for another 5 minutes until leaves are wilted but still vibrant green.
Serve hot with rice and beans.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 3 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and minced
instructions: Combine thyme, peppers, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, oil, allspice, cinnamon, pepper, and lime juice in a blender and puree until smooth.
Place chicken in a large ziplock bag and pour the marinade over it.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat with a cast iron skillet.
Grill chicken for 5 minutes per side, then finish in the skillet for 5 minutes until skin is crispy and juices run clear.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1/2 lb salted saltfish, desalted and flaked
instructions: Rinse callaloo thoroughly and set aside.
In a large pot, sauté onions, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper in oil until soft.
Add the saltfish and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in callaloo, coconut milk, stock, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until callaloo is tender.
Add okra in the last 3 minutes and stir gently before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 2 cups long grain white rice, rinsed
1 lb fresh green pigeon peas, shelled
1/2 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked beans and rinse them.
In a large pot, sauté celery, carrots, garlic, and green onions in oil.
Add rinsed rice, beans, coconut milk, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Pour in stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in pigeon peas and bay leaf, cover, and cook for another 15 minutes until rice is fluffy and peas are tender.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Soak saltfish in water for 24 hours, changing water 3 times, then boil for 10 minutes.
Flake the fish and remove any bones.
Sauté onions, scallions, thyme, and peppers in oil and butter until fragrant.
Add the ackee and flaked saltfish to the pot.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir gently and cook for 5 minutes until heated through.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Oxtail Stew
instructions: Toss oxtail pieces in flour and shake off excess.
Sear oxtail in oil in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Remove meat and sauté onions, carrots, celery, and garlic in the same pot.
Stir in tomato paste, ketchup, brown sugar, bay leaves, thyme, allspice, soy sauce, and vinegar.
Return oxtail to the pot and add stock and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2.5 hours.
Add water if needed to prevent sticking.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until meat falls off the bone.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 cups fresh Scotch bonnet peppers, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend peppers, thyme, ginger, garlic, and allspice into a smooth paste.
Mix the paste with soy sauce, brown sugar, and vinegar to create the marinade.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat the grill or broiler to high heat.
Grill the chicken until the skin is charred and the meat is cooked through, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with rice and peas.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 bunch callaloo leaves, stems removed and chopped
1/2 cup green seasonings (scallions, garlic, ginger, thyme)
1/2 cup saltfish, soaked, desalted, and flaked
instructions: Sauté the green seasonings in olive oil until fragrant.
Add the chopped callaloo leaves and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, salt, and pepper, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the okra, saltfish, and crab meat.
Simmer uncovered for another 5 minutes until the okra is cooked.
Sprinkle with flour just before serving to thicken slightly.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
1/2 cup green seasonings (scallions, garlic, ginger, thyme)
1/2 cup fresh corn, cut from the cob
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain well.
Sauté the green seasonings and okra in vegetable oil until fragrant.
Add the soaked beans, coconut milk, and water to the pot.
Stir in the rice, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the corn and cook for an additional 5 minutes until rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve warm.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1/2 cup salted codfish, soaked, desalted, and flaked
1/2 cup green seasonings (scallions, garlic, ginger, thyme)
1/4 cup fresh corn, cut from the cob
instructions: Sauté the green seasonings and okra in butter until fragrant.
Add the flaked saltfish and stir to combine.
Stir in the drained ackee gently; do not overmix to avoid breaking the eggs.
Add the corn, peas, salt, and pepper.
Cook on low heat for 3-5 minutes until heated through.
Sprinkle with flour just before serving to thicken the sauce.
Serve immediately with fried green bananas.

title: Johnny Cake
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh corn, cut from the cob
instructions: Mix cornmeal, sugar, salt, and grated coconut in a large bowl.
Add melted butter, water, and raisins to the dry ingredients.
Knead the mixture until it forms a stiff dough.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut into circles.
Fry the cakes in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with fresh okra and corn before serving.
Serve warm as a side dish or snack.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 cup scotch bonnet peppers, stemmed and chopped
instructions: Combine all ingredients except chicken in a food processor until a smooth paste forms.
Rub the jerk paste generously over the chicken pieces.
Let the chicken marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken for 10-12 minutes per side until cooked through and charred.

title: Callaloo Soup
ingredients: 1 lb salted pork or ham hock
1 scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Simmer the salted pork in water until tender, then remove and shred the meat.
Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and pepper in oil until fragrant.
Add the chopped callaloo and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and shredded pork; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
1/2 cup green peas, fresh or frozen
1 smoked ham hock or salted pork
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and combine with ham hock, scotch bonnet, thyme, and bay leaf in a pot.
Cover with water and simmer until beans are tender.
Add the rice, green onions, and peas to the pot.
Add enough stock to cover the rice by 2 inches.
Simmer covered on low heat for 20-25 minutes until rice is fluffy and liquid is absorbed.

title: Bakes and Greens
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Toss pork cubes in flour until lightly coated.
Sear the pork in hot oil until browned on all sides.
Remove pork and sauté onion, garlic, and pepper in the same oil.
Return pork to the pot; add ketchup, brown sugar, and water.
Simmer for 1 hour until pork is tender.
Stir in the greens and cook for 5 more minutes until wilted.

title: Griot (Fried Pork)
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into small cubes
instructions: Marinate pork cubes in minced pepper, salt, and garlic for 30 minutes.
Mix flour, baking powder, and cayenne pepper in a bowl.
Toss marinated pork in the flour mixture until evenly coated.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry pork in batches until golden brown and crispy.
Serve immediately with a side of hot sauce or fried plantains.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 3 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and minced
instructions: Combine flour, brown sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, lime juice, scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, thyme, ginger, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to make the jerk paste.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the jerk paste and let marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken for about 15-20 minutes per side until the skin is charred and the meat is cooked through.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Callaloo
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic and scallions and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped callaloo leaves and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in the coconut milk, lime juice, and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer for another 5 minutes until the leaves are tender.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1/2 cup kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic, ginger, scallions, and thyme, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast for 1 minute until lightly browned.
Add the coconut milk, kidney beans, green peas, salt, pepper, and turmeric.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried salted codfish, soaked overnight and flaked
instructions: Pat the flaked salted codfish dry and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the scallions, thyme, garlic, and nutmeg, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the green peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the ackee and salted codfish gently; do not stir too vigorously.
Season with lime juice, salt, and pepper, then cook for another 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Serve immediately, traditionally with fried plantains.

title: Johnny Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, mix the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, melted butter, egg, and thyme if using.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Fold in the scallions if using.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 2 inches apart.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until golden brown and firm to the touch.
Cool on a wire rack and serve warm.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 4 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Combine all ingredients except chicken and oil in a blender or food processor until smooth.
Place chicken in a large bowl and pour the marinade over it.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) or prepare a hot charcoal grill.
Cook chicken for 45-60 minutes until fully cooked and skin is charred.

title: Callaloo
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add scotch bonnet pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in chopped callaloo and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk, water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until tender.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1/2 cup green peas, fresh or frozen
1/2 cup kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and peppers in a pot until fragrant.
Add rice and toast for 1 minute.
Stir in peas, beans, coconut milk, bay leaf, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove bay leaf and fluff with a fork before serving.

title: Fried Green Plantains
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and sliced into thick rounds
instructions: Mix cornstarch, flour, and salt in a shallow bowl.
Dip plantain slices into the flour mixture, coating both sides.
Heat oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Fry plantains in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

title: Bammy (Fried Cassava Bread)
instructions: Mix cassava flour, water, and salt in a bowl to form a thick paste.
Roll the paste into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Place flattened cassava balls into the hot oil.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and season with pepper if desired.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 4 lbs), cut into pieces
1 red scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces in the jerk seasoning mixture for at least 2 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides.
Add the sliced onions and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 45 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Remove from heat and let rest before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Rinse the rice until water runs clear.
Drain the soaked beans and combine with rice, peas, onion, garlic, thyme, bay leaf, and scotch bonnet pepper in a pot.
Add the vegetable broth and curry powder.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook for another 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf and scotch bonnet pepper.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in vegetable oil until translucent.
Add the scotch bonnet pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the okra slices and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the callaloo leaves and pour in the water and fish stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend the reserved okra mixture with water and stir into the soup.
Add coconut milk, thyme, and salt, then simmer for 5 more minutes.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
ingredients: 2 cups dried salted codfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Rinse the soaked codfish thoroughly and flake it into small pieces.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, scotch bonnet, bell pepper, and celery until soft.
Add the curry powder, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the codfish.
Cook for 5 minutes until the fish is lightly browned.
Gently fold in the ackee and cook for 2 minutes without breaking the ackee.
Remove from heat, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve.

title: Grilled Plantains (Maduros)
instructions: Peel the plantains and cut them diagonally into thick slices.
Melt the butter and mix with brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Brush the plantain slices generously with the spiced butter mixture.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Grill the plantains for 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized and slightly charred.
Flip occasionally to ensure even browning.
Serve warm as a side dish or dessert.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 cup fresh scotch bonnet peppers, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, soy sauce, brown sugar, flour, garlic, oregano, and allspice until smooth to form a paste.
Rub the paste generously over all chicken pieces and let marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange chicken in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with foil.
Bake for 45-60 minutes until skin is dark and crisp and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Baste with pan juices halfway through cooking.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 lb salted codfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Soak salted codfish in cold water for 24 hours, changing water every 4 hours, then drain and flake.
Sauté onion, green pepper, and garlic in butter and oil until soft.
Add flaked fish and diced tomatoes; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in drained ackee, parsley, salt, and pepper; cook gently for 3 minutes without breaking ackee.
Serve immediately over white rice.

title: Curry Goat
instructions: Brown goat meat in oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until fragrant.
Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add water, coconut milk, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours until meat is tender.
Stir in pimentos and raisins; cook for 10 more minutes.
Season with salt and serve.

title: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add scotch bonnet pepper, okra, and water; bring to a boil.
Simmer until okra is tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in chopped callaloo leaves and cook for 5 minutes until wilted.
Add crab meat, salt, and pepper; heat through gently.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 lb green kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear; drain well.
Sauté onion, scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add drained beans, water, thyme, and salt; bring to a boil.
Stir in rice, pimentos, and nutmeg; reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes until rice and beans are tender.
Fluff with a fork, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and minced
instructions: Combine all spices, peppers, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sugar, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, oil, and lime juice in a bowl to make the marinade.
Place chicken pieces in a large ziplock bag and pour the marinade over them.
Massage the marinade into the chicken, seal the bag, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill or charcoal fire to medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from the marinade and grill for 6-8 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 165°F and the skin is charred.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 pound fresh green bananas (plantains) or yams, cut into chunks
1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain.
In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and scallions until fragrant.
Add the rice, kidney beans, and chopped green bananas or yams to the pot.
Stir in soy sauce, brown sugar, coconut milk, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Add enough water to cover the ingredients by about 2 inches.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes.
Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and stir in parsley and cilantro before serving.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 bunch callaloo (or spinach/kale), stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium-high heat and sauté garlic and scallions until soft.
Add the chopped callaloo leaves, okra, thyme, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, and water.
Stir in the coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the greens are tender.
Stir in the fresh parsley and cilantro.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 pound dried salted codfish, soaked and desalted
1 pound ripe ackee fruit, drained and rinsed
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water several times, until the saltiness is gone.
Flake the fish into small pieces and set aside.
In a large pot, heat oil over medium heat and sauté scallions, thyme, parsley, and cilantro.
Add the flaked saltfish and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, water, and bay leaf.
Add the ackee fruit and stir gently to combine.
Cook on low heat for 5-10 minutes until the mixture is heated through and slightly thickened.
Remove bay leaf and serve immediately.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a blender or food processor until smooth.
Place chicken in a large bowl and pour marinade over it.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place marinated chicken on a baking sheet and bake for 45-60 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot with rice and peas.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 4 cups fresh callaloo or spinach, chopped
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, green pepper, and garlic; sauté until soft.
Stir in callaloo or spinach and cook for 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk, water, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Simmer for 10 minutes until greens are tender.
Serve as a side dish.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a large pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve warm.

title: Grilled Fish with Mango Chutney
instructions: Mix mango, onion, cilantro, lime juice, brown sugar, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, olive oil, and hot pepper sauce to make chutney.
Season fish fillets with salt and pepper.
Grill fish over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until flaky.
Serve fish topped with warm mango chutney.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Soak salted codfish in cold water overnight, then flake into small pieces.
Sauté onion, green pepper, scallion, thyme, ginger, and garlic in oil until soft.
Add ackee and flaked fish to the pot.
Stir in soy sauce, brown sugar, white vinegar, hot pepper sauce, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Simmer for 10 minutes until liquid thickens.
Serve with white rice.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 cup scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Mix all ingredients except chicken in a food processor to make a paste.
Rub the paste generously over the chicken pieces.
Marinate the chicken in a sealed container for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill or broiler to medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for 20-25 minutes per side until skin is charred and meat is cooked through.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1/2 lb salted saltfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add the saltfish and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the okra and nutmeg.
Add the chopped callaloo leaves and water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until leaves are tender.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup green kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Rinse the rice until water runs clear.
Sauté onion, garlic, and pepper in oil until fragrant.
Add the soaked beans, coconut milk, and thyme to the pot.
Stir in the rice and cooked pigeon peas.
Add water to cover ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water for 24 hours, changing water frequently.
Boil the fish until white and flake it, removing any bones.
Sauté onion, green pepper, and tomatoes in oil until soft.
Add the flaked fish, scallions, and allspice to the pot.
Stir in the drained ackee carefully.
Heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling until heated through.

title: Oxtail Stew
instructions: Season oxtail pieces with salt and coat lightly with flour.
Brown the oxtail in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove meat and sauté onion and garlic in the same pot.
Return meat to the pot and add ketchup, soy sauce, bay leaves, water, and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2 to 3 hours until meat is very tender.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh scotch bonnet peppers, blended
instructions: Mix all ingredients in a bowl to create the jerk marinade.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly with the marinade.
Refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill or broiler to high heat.
Cook chicken until skin is charred and meat is cooked through.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
instructions: Rinse the rice until water runs clear.
In a pot, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add rice, beans (rinsed and drained), thyme, and bay leaf.
Stir in broth, coconut milk, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Remove bay leaf and fluff with a fork.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 3 cups fresh callaloo leaves or spinach, chopped
1/2 tsp dried scotch bonnet pepper, minced
instructions: Sauté onion and green pepper in a large pot until tender.
Add garlic and scotch bonnet pepper, cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the chopped callaloo leaves.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until leaves are wilted.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 3 cups dried salted codfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in water overnight to remove excess salt.
Flake the fish and squeeze out any remaining water.
Sauté onion and scallions in a large skillet.
Add tomato paste, turmeric, and allspice; cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the flaked fish and vegetable broth.
Simmer until the fish is tender.
Gently fold in the ackee fruit and heat through without breaking the pods.

title: Oxtail Stew
instructions: Season oxtail pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown the oxtail in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove meat and sauté onions, carrots, and garlic.
Return meat to the pot and add ketchup, soy sauce, and brown sugar.
Stir in bay leaves and beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Add potatoes and cook for another 30 minutes until soft.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 2 scotch bonnet peppers, seeds removed and minced
instructions: Whisk together flour, sugar, oil, garlic, thyme, allspice, salt, pepper, peppers, and lime juice to make the jerk marinade.
Place chicken in a large bowl, pour marinade over it, and toss to coat thoroughly.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken for about 6-8 minutes per side until the skin is charred and the meat is cooked through.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 cup cooked kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat broth in a large pot over medium heat until simmering.
Stir in rice, peas, beans, condensed milk, green onions, pepper, bay leaf, thyme, and salt.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs, and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 bunch callaloo or spinach, stems removed and leaves chopped
1/2 cup dried salted codfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Sauté onion, scallion, garlic, and pepper in oil in a large pot until fragrant.
Add the chopped greens, codfish, thyme, and salt; stir to combine.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until greens are tender.
Stir in coconut milk if using, cover, and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Season with additional salt if necessary and serve hot.

title: Fried Plantains (Maduros)
ingredients: 4 ripe plantains, peeled and cut into thick rounds
instructions: Cut ripe plantains into thick rounds and sprinkle with salt and nutmeg.
Heat oil in a deep skillet or pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry plantain rounds in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and caramelized.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm as a side dish or dessert.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
ingredients: 1 cup dried salted codfish, soaked overnight and flaked
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in cold water overnight, then drain and flake into small pieces.
Melt butter or oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion, scallion, pepper, garlic, and thyme until soft and fragrant.
Add the flaked fish and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in the ackee and coconut milk if using, then season with salt.
Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until heated through but ackee remains soft.
Serve immediately with boiled white rice.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and bell pepper in olive oil until soft.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in tomato, wine, broth, rice, peas, olives, and capers.
Season with salt and pepper, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Mofongo de Plátano Verde
ingredients: 4 large green plantains, peeled and cut in half
instructions: Boil plantains with garlic and a pinch of salt until tender but not mushy.
Drain well and let cool slightly.
Mash plantains in a mortar with lard until smooth and fluffy.
Stir in pork cracklings, garlic, olive oil, and broth.
Serve warm with shrimp or chicken on top.

title: Sancocho de Gallina
ingredients: 4 medium yuca roots, peeled and cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and celery in a large pot until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned.
Pour in water to cover and bring to a boil.
Add yuca, plantains, yam, potato, carrot, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until all vegetables are tender.

title: Pastelón de Plátano
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Fry plantain slices until golden and set aside.
Mix eggs, milk, flour, sugar, and vanilla in a bowl.
Layer half the plantains in a greased baking dish.
Spread ground beef, rice, and beans over the plantains.
Pour egg mixture over the filling and top with remaining plantains.
Bake for 30 minutes until set and golden.

title: Alcapurrias
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and lard; add water to form a dough.
Combine ground pork, rice, olives, capers, green onions, and adobo.
Shape dough into small balls, flatten, and fill with pork mixture.
Seal the edges tightly and roll into smooth balls.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.

title: Tajine Poulet ak Makak
ingredients: 1 cup dried pigeon peas (makak), soaked overnight
2 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Rinse the soaked pigeon peas and drain them well.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and thyme in palm oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on all sides.
Stir in the scotch bonnet peppers and cook for two minutes.
Add the pigeon peas and chicken broth to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1 hour or until chicken is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

title: Griot ak Pikliz
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/4 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Coat the pork pieces thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat the lard or oil in a deep pot over medium-high heat.
Fry the pork pieces until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
In a separate pot, combine the onion, scallions, tomatoes, carrots, celery, pepper, vinegar, sugar, and thyme.
Simmer the pikliz mixture over medium heat for 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Serve the crispy fried pork with the warm pikliz on the side.

title: Rouj Mo
ingredients: 1/2 cup pigeon peas (makak), cooked until soft
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in vegetable oil until translucent.
Add the cooked pigeon peas, green peas, and diced carrots to the pot.
Stir in the rice, chicken stock, salt, pepper, and bay leaves.
Bring the mixture to a rolling boil, stirring gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and cook for 15-20 minutes.
Do not lift the lid during cooking; fluff with a fork once done and serve.

title: Soup Joumou
ingredients: 2 lbs beef brisket, cut into chunks
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb salted pork belly, rinsed and cut
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the beef, pork shoulder, and salted pork in a large pot with the beef broth.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours until meat is tender.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper until soft.
Add the sautéed vegetables (onion mix, carrots, celery) to the meat pot.
Simmer for another 30 minutes to let flavors meld.
Add the green beans and potato, cooking until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaves, and serve hot.

title: Pa Sezi ak Kousou
instructions: In a bowl, mix the flour, cornmeal, baking powder, and salt.
Add the beaten eggs, milk, and melted butter to the dry ingredients.
Fold in the grated cheese and shredded chicken or ham if using.
Heat oil in a deep skillet over medium heat.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion, scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic in butter until soft.
Spoon the batter into the hot oil to form small cakes.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Serve the fried cakes warm, optionally topped with the sautéed onion mixture.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 1 lb chicken pieces, cut into quarters
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper, then brown in oil until golden.
Add onion and garlic to the pot, sauté until fragrant.
Stir in tomato sauce and chicken broth.
Add the rinsed rice and mix well to coat with liquid.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Mangú
ingredients: 3 cups green plantains, peeled and boiled until soft
instructions: Boil plantains until very tender, then drain well.
Mash the hot plantains in a bowl with butter, garlic, and a pinch of salt.
Add chopped cilantro and mix until smooth and creamy.
Place dollops of mangú on a serving plate.
Top each mound with a spoonful of salted black beans and diced onion.

title: Sancocho de Pollo
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in a large pot with a little oil.
Add chicken pieces and brown them slightly.
Pour in enough water to cover ingredients by two inches.
Add bay leaves, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add yuca, malanga, and plantain slices.
Continue cooking until all vegetables and chicken are tender, about 20 minutes more.

title: Sancocho de Yuca con Yuca
ingredients: 2 lbs yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Place beef brisket in a large pot and cover with water.
Add onion, garlic, bay leaves, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil and simmer until meat is tender, about 1 hour.
Add yuca chunks and green plantain slices to the pot.
Cover and simmer until yuca and plantain are soft, about 30 minutes.
Serve hot with a side of fried plantains if desired.

title: Sofrito con Papas
instructions: Boil diced potatoes in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and bell peppers until softened.
Stir in cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add the boiled potatoes to the skillet and toss to coat with the sofrito.
Cook for another 5 minutes until everything is heated through.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

title: Brown Stew Chicken
ingredients: 1 scotch bonnet pepper, whole (do not crush)
instructions: In a bowl, mix the chicken pieces with flour, thyme, oregano, salt, black pepper, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken pieces on all sides.
Add the sliced onions and green pepper to the pot and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef stock, ketchup, and soy sauce, stirring to combine.
Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 45 minutes or until the chicken is tender.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
ingredients: Fresh hot peppers, sliced, for garnish
instructions: Soak the saltfish in cold water for at least 2 hours, changing the water twice, to remove excess salt.
Flake the fish into large pieces, discarding any bones, and set aside.
In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper, sautéing until soft.
Stir in the flaked fish, nutmeg, and salt, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add the ackee and the 1/4 cup of water, stirring gently to combine.
Cook on low heat for 10 minutes until the ackee grains open up and are fluffy.
Garnish with chopped scallions and sliced hot peppers before serving.

title: Ox Tail Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds beef ox tail, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Season the ox tail pieces with salt and black pepper, then brown them in a pot until sealed.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, garlic, scotch bonnet, thyme, and oregano to the pot.
Pour in the beef stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 2 hours.
In a small bowl, mix the two tablespoons of flour with the tablespoon of water until smooth.
Stir the flour mixture into the stew along with the butter.
Simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the stew thickens and the meat is tender.

title: Baked Green Banana and Fish
ingredients: 1 pound red snapper or mahi-mahi, filleted
instructions: Peel the green bananas and slice them into thick rounds.
In a bowl, mix the flour, salt, and pepper, then stir in the milk to create a batter.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Dip the banana slices into the batter and fry until golden brown on both sides.
In the same skillet, sauté the onion, green pepper, and scotch bonnet pepper until soft.
Place the fish fillets in a baking dish, top with the fried bananas and the sautéed vegetables.
Dot with butter, cover with foil, and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes.

title: Fried Dumplings (Dumplings)
instructions: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, gradually adding warm water until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough briefly and let it rest for 10 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the ground beef, onions, green peppers, scotch bonnet, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Roll out small portions of the dough into thin circles.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture in the center of each circle and fold over to seal.
Heat a skillet with the remaining oil and butter over medium heat.
Fry the dumplings for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.

title: Pepperpot Soup
ingredients: 10 lbs pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
1 bunch saltfish, soaked overnight and desalted
4 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the pork chunks in a large pot over medium-high heat until seared on all sides.
Add the desalted saltfish, chopped onion, scallions, and garlic to the pot and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef stock and add thyme sprigs; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer the meat for 2 hours until tender.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour with a little cold water to create a slurry.
Stir the flour slurry into the simmering soup and cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
Add the cubed sweet potatoes and green bananas; cook for 30 minutes until soft.
Stir in the chopped callaloo and cook for another 10 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste before serving.

title: Baked Cod with Coconut Sauce
ingredients: 4 whole fillets of fresh cod or red snapper
Salt and white pepper to taste
1 lime, cut into wedges for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together coconut milk, pineapple chunks, green onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Place the cod fillets on the prepared baking sheet.
Pour the coconut sauce evenly over the fish fillets.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Cracked Conch with Peppers
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh conch meat, cracked and cleaned
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the bell peppers and cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the cleaned conch meat, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper to the skillet.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chopped cilantro during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
Serve hot with lime wedges on the side.

title: Bahamian Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 6 oz dried salted codfish, soaked and desalted
1/2 cup white rice, cooked and cooled
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Flake the soaked saltfish into small pieces, discarding any bones, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the flaked saltfish and sauté for 3-4 minutes until it begins to brown.
Stir in the fresh ackee gently and cook for 2 minutes, ensuring the eggs are not overcooked.
Mix in the green onions, cooked rice, and thyme leaves.
Season with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lime juice to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with extra scallions and lime wedges.

title: Bahamian Style Pigeon Peas and Corn
ingredients: 2 cups dried pigeon peas, soaked overnight
4 ears of fresh corn, husked and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Drain the soaked pigeon peas and rinse them thoroughly.
In a large pot, heat vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the pigeon peas, bay leaves, thyme, and stock to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the corn chunks and continue simmering for another 30-40 minutes until peas and corn are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaves, stir in fresh scallions, and serve hot.

title: Jerk Chicken
instructions: Blend peppers, thyme, onion, garlic, allspice, paprika, and lime juice to make a paste.
Mix paste with soy sauce, brown sugar, oil, and vinegar.
Rub the mixture all over the chicken pieces.
Marinate the chicken in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven or grill to high heat.
Cook chicken until the skin is charred and the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 2 cups dried salted codfish, soaked and flaked
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in water overnight to remove excess salt, then flake it.
Sauté the onions, garlic, and scotch bonnet peppers in butter and oil until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Stir in the flaked fish, allspice, thyme, and green seasoning.
Gently fold in the ackee, being careful not to break the seeds.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1/2 cup salted pork or ham hock, chopped (optional)
instructions: Boil the chopped callaloo leaves in water with a pinch of salt until tender.
In a separate pot, sauté the onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet peppers in oil.
Add the salted pork, if using, and cook until browned.
Stir in the chopped callaloo, thyme, allspice, and scallions.
Add the water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook on medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors meld.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Sauté the onion, garlic, scotch bonnet peppers, and thyme in oil until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir to coat with the oil and spices.
Pour in the water or stock, add the bay leaf, salt, and allspice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the kidney beans and green seasoning.
Cover and cook for another 10 minutes until the rice is fluffy and liquid is absorbed.

title: Fried Plantains
instructions: Peel the plantains and slice them into thick rounds.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, milk, egg, and cinnamon to make a batter.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each plantain slice into the batter, letting excess drip off.
Fry the slices in batches until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with brown sugar if desired.

title: Callaloo and Spinach
ingredients: 2 bunches callaloo, tough stems removed and leaves chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sauté chopped onion, green pepper, garlic, and scotch bonnet peppers until fragrant.
Add the chopped callaloo and spinach, stirring for a few minutes until slightly wilted.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, then add fresh thyme leaves.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the greens are tender.
Stir in the sliced okra and cook for another 5 minutes until okra is cooked through.
Remove from heat and serve hot with rice and beans.

title: Saltfish and Kidney Beans
ingredients: 1 lb salted codfish, soaked overnight in water
3 cups dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the soaked codfish under cold water and flake it into small pieces, removing any bones.
Place the soaked kidney beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer the beans until they are half-cooked.
In a separate pan, heat olive oil and sauté onion, green onions, garlic, ginger, and scotch bonnet pepper.
Add the flaked codfish to the sautéed vegetables and stir well.
Add the half-cooked beans, vegetable stock, fresh thyme, salt, and pepper to the codfish mixture.
Combine everything and simmer gently for 45 minutes until beans are fully tender and flavors have melded.
Adjust seasoning if needed and serve.

title: Pepperpot Soup
ingredients: 1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
1 lb salted codfish, soaked and flaked
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the beef brisket in a large pot and cover with water; bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Add the soaked pigeon peas and simmer until the meat is tender and beans are soft.
In a small bowl, mix the flour with a little cold water to create a smooth slurry.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet pepper in oil until fragrant.
Stir the flour slurry into the simmering pot of meat and beans.
Add the flaked salted codfish and fresh thyme leaves.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes to thicken the soup slightly.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 2 lbs goat meat, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the goat meat chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy pot and brown the meat on all sides.
Remove meat and set aside; sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and scotch bonnet pepper in the same oil.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, and cumin, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the meat to the pot and add water or stock and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cover to simmer for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer for another 30 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Remove bay leaves, adjust seasoning, and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

title: Grilled Fish with Achiote Marinade
ingredients: 4 whole red snapper or sea bass, cleaned and scaled
Salt and black pepper to taste
1 lemon, cut into wedges for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix achiote paste, minced garlic, chopped onion, scotch bonnet pepper, lime juice, olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Place the whole fish in a large ziplock bag or dish and pour the marinade over them, ensuring they are fully coated.
Refrigerate the marinated fish for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat your grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Remove fish from the marinade (reserve any excess marinade for basting).
Grill the fish for 4-5 minutes per side until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Baste the fish with reserved marinade during the last 2 minutes of grilling.
Serve immediately with grilled lemon wedges and rice and beans.

title: Ropa Vieja
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef flank steak, sliced against the grain
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the sliced beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned on both sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onions, bell peppers, and garlic until soft.
Add the tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaf; return the beef to the pot.
Simmer covered for about 2 hours until the meat is very tender and falls apart easily.
Remove the bay leaf, shred the meat with two forks, and mix it back into the sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with white rice.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown the chicken on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, bell pepper, and garlic until fragrant.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken back to the pot along with the chicken broth, water, and capers.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the peas and continue cooking covered for another 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

title: Mofongo de Plátanos Verdes
ingredients: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut into large chunks
1 tsp annatto oil (achiote) or 1/4 tsp annatto powder
instructions: Boil the plantain chunks in salted water with 1/4 cup water until very soft; drain and mash immediately.
While mashing, heat lard, annatto oil, and remaining water in a heavy-bottomed pot over high heat.
Add the mashed plantains and continue cooking, stirring constantly with a wooden pestle, until the mixture turns dark brown and crispy on the outside.
Once the mofongo is cooked, remove from heat.
Garnish with the pork cracklings, garlic salt, and fresh coconut shavings.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Tostones
ingredients: 6 green plantains, peeled and cut into thick rounds
instructions: Boil the plantain rounds in salted water for 5 minutes until tender but not mushy; drain and let cool slightly.
Press each plantain round flat with a heavy object or press to remove as much air as possible.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dust the flattened plantains lightly with flour and fry in batches until golden brown; remove and drain on paper towels.
Let the fried plantains cool completely.
Press them again to flatten them further, then fry a second time until crisp and dark golden.
Season with salt and serve with lime wedges.

title: Mojito con Ron
ingredients: 5-6 fresh mint leaves, plus more for garnish
instructions: Muddle the mint leaves, lime juice, and sugar gently in a glass to release the oils.
Add the white rum and stir well to dissolve the sugar.
Fill the glass with ice cubes and top with soda water.
Stir gently to combine and chill.
Garnish with a sprig of fresh mint and a slice of lime.
Serve immediately.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm water
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown the chicken on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion, garlic, and bell peppers until soft.
Return chicken to the pot and add bay leaf and vinegar.
Stir in the soaked saffron water and add chicken broth.
Add the rinsed rice and stir well to coat with the liquid.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and mix in the chopped cilantro and parsley before serving.

title: Mofongo de Camarón
ingredients: 4 large green plantains, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces
1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Place plantain pieces in a pot with water, bring to a boil, and cook until very tender (about 15 minutes).
Drain the plantains thoroughly and let them cool slightly.
In a heavy skillet, heat lard over medium-high heat and add crushed garlic.
Fry the garlic until golden, then add the pork cracklings and fry until crisp.
Add the fried garlic and cracklings to a food processor along with the cooled plantains.
Pulse until the mixture forms a coarse, mashed consistency, adding a little butter if needed.
Transfer the mofongo to a warm bowl and create a well in the center.
Melt butter in a separate pan, add achiote and black pepper, then sauté shrimp until pink.
Add capers and olives to the shrimp, then pour the mixture into the well of the mofongo.
Top with chopped green onions and serve immediately.

title: Maduros con Chocolate
ingredients: 1/4 cup chocolate sauce or melted chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cut the ripe bananas in half lengthwise and place them cut-side up in a baking dish.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over low heat.
Stir in the brown sugar, cinnamon, and evaporated milk until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the warm mixture evenly over the bananas in the baking dish.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the bananas are soft and caramelized.
Remove from the oven and immediately drizzle with chocolate sauce.
Dust lightly with powdered sugar before serving warm.

title: Frito Con Mojo
ingredients: 2 lbs white fish fillets (like sea bass or snapper), cut into chunks
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour, salt, pepper, and baking powder.
Dip fish chunks into the flour mixture, shaking off any excess.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat until smoking slightly.
Fry fish chunks in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
In a separate bowl, combine onion, garlic, cilantro, culantro, vinegar, olive oil, oregano, and salt to make the Mojo.
Let the Mojo sit for at least 30 minutes to let flavors meld.
Serve the crispy fish immediately alongside the fresh Mojo sauce for dipping.

title: Sancocho de Pollo
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (approx. 3 lbs), cut into pieces
1 yautia (green cassava), peeled and cut into large chunks
1 green plantain, peeled and cut into large chunks
2 green bananas (plátano verde), peeled and cut into large chunks
1 large yucca root, peeled and cut into large chunks
1 whole garlic bulb, peeled but cloves left intact
instructions: Place chicken pieces in a large pot with water, whole garlic bulb, quartered onion, smashed garlic cloves, oregano, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam that rises to the top, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add the vinegar and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Add the yautia, green plantain, green bananas, and yucca root to the pot.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20-30 minutes until all vegetables are very soft.
Season with salt to taste.
Remove the whole garlic bulb, bay leaf, and onion quarters before serving.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and culantro just before serving.

title: Tambal
ingredients: 2 lbs assorted vegetables (pumpkin, carrots, squash, beans), chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté vegetables with salt and pepper until slightly softened.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Griot
ingredients: 1.5 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
2 cups lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Marinate pork with garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper for 2 hours.
Mix flour and baking powder in a bowl.
Coat pork pieces in the flour mixture.
Heat lard in a deep pot until smoking.
Fry pork in batches until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve with fried plantains.

title: Poulet Ti Mo
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, and garlic in a bowl.
Coat chicken pieces thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat lard in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Fry chicken pieces until golden, about 5 minutes per side.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté onion, green pepper, and tomato in the same pot.
Return chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until cooked through.

title: Legume Risi
ingredients: 1 lb mixed beans (kidney, pinto, navy), soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked beans and rinse again.
In a pot, heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add beans, water, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Add rinsed rice and stir gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 20 minutes.
Let stand covered for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Pikliz
instructions: Wash and chop all vegetables into bite-sized pieces.
Combine vegetables in a large bowl.
Mix lime juice, vinegar, salt, sugar, pepper, and turmeric in a separate bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss well.
Let sit in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Mangu con Queso y Guayaba
ingredients: 3 cups green plantains, peeled and sliced
instructions: Boil plantains in water with salt until soft.
Mash plantains into a smooth, creamy paste.
Fry grated cheese in a pan until golden.
Serve mangu hot with fried cheese and guava on the side.

title: Sancocho de Pollo
instructions: Place chicken pieces in a pot and add water.
Add onion, garlic, bay leaf, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add plantains, yucca, and malanga.
Simmer until vegetables are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in culantro leaves and serve hot.

title: Mofongo de Camarones
instructions: Mash fried plantains with garlic and lard in a mortar until fluffy.
Fry shrimp in olive oil with garlic until pink.
Add water, capers, and olives to the shrimp and simmer.
Fold the shrimp mixture into the mashed plantains.
Top with pork cracklings and serve immediately.

title: La Bandera Dominicana
instructions: Cook rice with water, onion, garlic, and salt until fluffy.
Brown ground beef with onion, garlic, and tomato sauce.
Fry chicken pieces until cooked through.
Fry plantain slices until golden.
Layer rice, meat, chicken, and plantains on a plate.
Top with olives, capers, and grated cheese.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Toast vermicelli noodles in oil until golden.
Add onion and garlic, cook until soft.
Stir in tomato sauce and broth.
Simmer until noodles are tender.
Stir in cheese, capers, and olives.
Serve hot with fresh bread.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
ingredients: 1 lb salted cod, soaked overnight and desalted
1 lb ackee, fresh from the market
1/2 cup scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry the onions, garlic, green pepper, and scotch bonnet in oil until soft.
Add the thyme and ginger, cooking for one more minute.
Crumble the desalted cod into the pan and fry until dry and fragrant.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the ackee gently.
Heat through for 2 minutes without breaking the ackee, then serve.

title: Brown Stew Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, washed and patted dry
instructions: Season chicken with black pepper and nutmeg, then dredge in flour.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken pieces on both sides.
Remove chicken and set aside; add onions, garlic, and peppers to the pot.
Sauté until onions are soft, then return chicken to the pot.
Mix ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, and stock in a bowl and pour over chicken.
Add the bay leaf, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until chicken is tender.

title: Oxtail Curry
instructions: Brown the oxtail pieces in oil until deep golden brown, then remove.
In the same pot, sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and scotch bonnet until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, coriander, and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes.
Return the oxtail to the pot, add coconut milk, stock, and brown sugar.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours until meat is falling off the bone.
Season with salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve with rice.

title: Roasted Pork with Scotch Bonnet Marinade
ingredients: 4 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and minced
instructions: Whisk together peppers, garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, thyme, pepper, paprika, and salt.
Rub the marinade all over the pork and place it in a large roasting pan.
Add the quartered onions to the pan around the pork.
Cover tightly with foil and roast at 325°F for 3 hours.
Remove foil, increase heat to 400°F, and roast for 30 more minutes until the skin is crispy and caramelized.

title: Festival (Sweet Potato Fry)
ingredients: 3 lbs sweet potatoes, peeled and grated
instructions: Mix grated sweet potatoes with nutmeg, cinnamon, baking soda, flour, sugar, milk, and eggs in a large bowl.
Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes to absorb moisture.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Shape the mixture into small rounds or strips using your hands or a mold.
Fry in batches until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Conch Fritters
ingredients: 1 pound fresh conch meat, chopped fine
instructions: Mix the chopped conch with flour, eggs, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Form the mixture into small patties and coat them lightly in the extra flour.
Heat oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry the patties in batches until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with lime wedges.

title: Red Rice and Peas
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
In a large pot, heat the oil and sauté the scallion until soft.
Stir in the ketchup, tomato paste, salt, and turmeric, cooking for one minute.
Add the rice, peas, and water, stirring well to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove from heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 pound salted codfish, soaked overnight and flaked
instructions: Remove all white bones from the flaked saltfish and squeeze out excess water.
Heat oil in a large pan and sauté the onions, green peppers, and bell peppers until soft.
Add the flaked saltfish and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the ketchup, tomato paste, salt, and black pepper.
Gently fold in the drained ackee, being careful not to break the eggs.
Sprinkle with scallions, cover, and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes.

title: Bahamian Potato Salad
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, then drain and cut into cubes while still warm.
In a large bowl, mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, and vegetable oil.
Add the diced celery, green pepper, onion, and scallion to the dressing.
Toss the potato cubes into the mixture and season with salt and pepper.
Refrigerate for at least one hour before serving to let flavors meld.

title: Grilled Bananas with Lime and Sugar
instructions: Peel the bananas and cut them in half lengthwise.
Place the banana halves on a skewer or directly on the grill grates.
Grill over medium heat, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the fruit is soft.
In a small bowl, mix the brown sugar, white sugar, lime juice, butter, cinnamon, and vanilla.
Brush the warm bananas generously with the sugar mixture.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Jerk Chicken
ingredients: 1 large Scotch bonnet pepper, seeds removed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Blend the Scotch bonnet pepper, scallions, thyme, garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, oil, salt, and pepper into a smooth paste.
Rub the spice paste all over the chicken pieces and let it marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat your grill or broiler to medium-high heat.
Dredge the marinated chicken in the flour, shaking off any excess.
Grill the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side until the skin is charred and the meat is cooked through.
Serve hot with fried plantains and rice and peas.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 pound green kidney beans (rye beans), drained and rinsed
1-2 Scotch bonnet peppers, chopped (adjust to taste)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and peppers until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute to remove the raw taste.
Add the rinsed rice, bay leaves, thyme, and kidney beans, stirring to coat everything in the oil.
Pour in the water or stock and coconut milk, then season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

title: Ackee and Saltfish
ingredients: 1 pound salted codfish, soaked and flaked
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in fresh water for 24 hours, changing the water several times until the fish is no longer salty.
Flake the fish into small pieces and set aside.
Melt butter and oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté the onion, green pepper, garlic, and Scotch bonnet peppers until soft.
Add the flaked saltfish and thyme, stirring to combine.
