Pour in the water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the ackee gently, being careful not to break the eggs.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes until the liquid has mostly evaporated and the ackee is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Callaloo Soup
ingredients: 2 bunches callaloo leaves, stemmed and chopped
1/2 cup salted pork or bacon, diced
Salt and black pepper to taste
Fresh hot pepper sauce for serving
instructions: Chop the callaloo leaves into 1-inch pieces and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the diced salted pork until slightly crispy.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and ginger to the pot and sauté until fragrant.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped callaloo, water or stock, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the leaves are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and green seasoning if using.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with hot pepper sauce on the side.

title: Bammy and Stew
ingredients: 1 pound beef or goat meat, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the cassava flour with the boiling water until it forms a thick paste.
Let the paste cool slightly, then knead it with your hands.
Roll the dough into small balls and flatten them into thin, round pancakes.
Fry the bammy pancakes in oil until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
In a separate pot, brown the meat cubes with the onion, pepper, garlic, thyme, flour, and salt.
Add the beef stock, chopped tomatoes, and green seasoning to the meat.
Simmer the stew over low heat for 45 minutes to an hour until the meat is tender.
Serve the fried bammy alongside the hot meat stew.

title: Curry Goat
ingredients: 1.5 lbs goat meat, cut into chunks
2 scotch bonnet peppers, seeded and chopped
instructions: Brown the goat meat in a heavy pot with oil over medium-high heat until sealed.
Add onion, scallions, garlic, and ginger, cooking until softened.
Stir in curry powder, allspice, and scotch bonnet peppers, toasting for one minute.
Pour in the chicken stock and add bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Season with salt and serve with rice and peas.

title: Patties
instructions: Mix the meat, onions, scallions, thyme, pepper, and 2 tbsp flour in a bowl.
Wrap small portions of the filling in plastic wrap and roll into balls.
Combine flour and lard for the dough, adding water gradually to form a soft ball.
Roll out dough circles, place a filling ball in the center, and fold over to seal.
Brush with egg wash and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Cool on a wire rack before serving.

title: Callaloo
ingredients: 1 bunch callaloo or spinach, cleaned and chopped
instructions: Blend onion, scallion, garlic, ginger, pepper, flour, and water until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the chopped callaloo or spinach.
Stir in coconut milk, salt, and nutmeg.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the greens are tender.
Serve hot with fried fish or saltfish.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
instructions: Soak the salted codfish in fresh water for 24 hours, changing the water three times.
Flake the fish and sauté with onion, scallion, garlic, and pepper in oil.
Add allspice and salt, cooking until the fish is dry.
Add the ackee to the fish mixture gently.
Add a little water if needed and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Serve immediately with boiled green bananas or dumplings.

title: Rice and Peas
ingredients: 1 lb kidney beans or gungo peas
instructions: Cook the beans in the chicken stock until tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, onion, scallion, garlic, ginger, and pepper to the pot.
Stir in coconut milk, allspice, bay leaves, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove bay leaves and fluff the rice with a fork before serving.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ingredients: 1 lb chicken pieces, marinated with sofrito
instructions: Sauté onion, bell peppers, and tomatoes in oil until softened.
Add marinated chicken and cook until browned.
Stir in rice, broth, peas, bay leaves, and oregano.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.

title: Sancocho
ingredients: 1 lb yuca, peeled and cut into chunks
1 lb malanga, peeled and cut into chunks
1 lb green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Place all meats in a large pot and add water to cover.
Simmer meats for 1 hour until tender.
Add chopped onion and garlic to the pot.
Add yuca, malanga, and plantain chunks.
Cook for another 45 minutes until vegetables are soft.

title: Ropa Vieja
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, sliced against the grain
instructions: Boil sliced beef until tender, about 1.5 hours.
Sauté onion and bell peppers in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the boiled beef, olives, capers, and vinegar.
Simmer for 10 minutes to blend flavors.

title: Fried Plantains (Platanos Fritos)
ingredients: 3 green plantains, peeled and cut into thick slices
instructions: Heat oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry plantain slices for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle with salt immediately while hot.
Serve as a side dish.

title: Moros y Cristianos
instructions: Cook soaked black beans in salted water until tender.
Drain beans and set aside.
Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato in oil until soft.
Add drained beans, raisins, capers, and olives to the pot.
Stir in rice, vinegar, salt, and cumin.
Cook over low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice absorbs liquid.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into small cubes
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes in soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Stir fry chicken in hot oil until cooked through and remove.
In the same pan, sauté garlic, ginger, and bell pepper until fragrant.
Add vinegar and sugar, stir until dissolved.
Return chicken to the pan and toss to coat.
Stir in peanuts and green onions, cook for 1 more minute.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water, then cut into cubes.
Fry beef mince in oil until browned.
Add doubanjiang and bean paste, stir-fry until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and sugar, simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently add tofu cubes to the sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry until sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with green onions and serve hot.

title: Dim Sum Siu Mai
instructions: Mix pork, shrimp, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, pepper, and ginger in a bowl.
Flatten wonton wrappers and place 1 tablespoon of filling in the center.
Fold the wrapper in half to form a half-moon shape.
Pinch the edges to seal, creating pleats along the top.
Place dumplings in a steamer basket lined with parchment paper.
Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with chili vinegar.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup bell peppers, cut into strips
instructions: Toss pork pieces in cornstarch until evenly coated.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and fry pork until golden, then remove.
In a small bowl, mix vinegar, sugar, and ketchup.
Stir fry onions and bell peppers until slightly softened.
Add pineapple and the pork back into the wok.
Pour in the sauce mixture and stir until thickened and glossy.
Garnish with green onions and serve.

title: Jiaozi (Chinese Dumplings)
ingredients: 1/2 lb cabbage, finely chopped and salted
Vegetable oil for frying or steaming
instructions: Squeeze excess water from salted cabbage and mix with pork and seasonings.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Wet the edge of the wrapper with beaten egg, fold in half, and pleat edges to seal.
Arrange dumplings in a steamer lined with cabbage leaves.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes until cooked.
Alternatively, pan-fry in oil until bottoms are crispy and tops are steamed.
Serve with dipping sauce.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 green bell pepper, cut into strips
1 tsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1 tbsp water
instructions: Toss pork strips in flour and shake off excess.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Fry pork in batches until golden, then remove and drain.
Remove oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the wok.
Stir-fry bell peppers and pineapple for 1 minute.
Whisk together pineapple juice, vinegar, sugar, ketchup, soy sauce, and cornstarch mixture.
Pour sauce into wok and bring to a simmer.
Add fried pork back to the wok.
Toss everything together until coated and sauce thickens.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
instructions: Mix flour and water to form a dough; knead until smooth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Combine pork, shrimp, cabbage, scallions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt in a bowl.
Divide dough into 16 equal pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Wet the edges with beaten egg, fold in half, and pinch to seal.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Arrange dumplings in the pan, seam-side down.
Pour water into the pan until it reaches halfway up the dumplings.
Cover and simmer until water evaporates.
Remove lid, cook until bottoms are golden, then flip and cook until fully done.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tsp cornstarch, dissolved in 1 tbsp water
instructions: Drain tofu and place in a bowl of warm water to prevent breaking.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat.
Add garlic, ginger, and chili flakes; stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute until oil turns red.
Pour in chicken broth, water, soy sauce, and sugar; bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes to the sauce.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes without stirring vigorously.
Stir in cornstarch mixture until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and garnish with chopped scallions.

title: Peking Duck
ingredients: Scallions and cucumber slices for serving
instructions: Rinse the duck inside and out and pat dry thoroughly.
In a bowl, mix rice wine, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and five-spice powder.
Stuff the mixture into the duck cavity and rub the outside with the remaining marinade.
Hang the duck in a cool place for 24 hours to dry the skin.
Blow air into the duck's cavity to puff up the skin.
Brush the duck with water and then with honey.
Roast in a preheated oven at 425°F (220°C) for 1 hour.
Reduce heat to 350°F (175°C) and roast for another 1-1.5 hours, basting occasionally.
Check if skin is crispy and golden; let rest before slicing.

title: Dim Sum Siu Mai
instructions: Mix pork, shrimp, cabbage, scallions, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Add water gradually and mix until the meat becomes sticky.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper.
Fold the wrapper over and pleat the edges to create a boat shape.
Steam the siu mai in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment paper for 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with soy sauce or sweet chili sauce.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into small cubes
instructions: Coat the pork cubes lightly with cornstarch.
Fry the pork in hot oil until golden brown, then remove and drain.
In a saucepan, combine ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and water; simmer until thickened.
Add the pineapple, bell peppers, and green onions to the sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the fried pork to the pan, toss to coat, and serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces in soy sauce and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the chicken in a wok with oil until cooked through, then remove.
In the same wok, stir-fry the red chilies and peanuts until fragrant.
Mix the vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Return the chicken to the wok, pour in the sauce mixture, and toss until glossy.
Garnish with green onions and serve immediately.

title: Dim Sum Steamed Pork Buns
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt; add warm water and knead until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
While rising, mix ground pork, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and pepper.
Punch down the dough, divide into small balls, and flatten each into a circle.
Place a spoonful of pork filling in the center of each circle and pleat the edges.
Let the buns rise again for 30 minutes, then steam in a steamer for 12 minutes.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and stir-fry the ground pork until browned.
Add doubanjiang and cook until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in water, soy sauce, and ground peppercorns; bring to a simmer.
Gently add the tofu cubes and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with a little water and stir into the sauce to thicken.
Remove from heat, drizzle with chili oil, and garnish with green onions.

title: Hot and Sour Noodle Soup
instructions: Boil noodles according to package directions, then drain and set aside.
In a pot, heat sesame oil and add wood ear mushrooms and bamboo shoots.
Add chicken broth, soy sauce, vinegar, and white pepper; bring to a boil.
Stir in tofu and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with water and stir into the soup to thicken.
Add the cooked noodles, garnish with green onions, and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water, then cut into cubes.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and add garlic and ginger; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang and stir for 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Pour in broth and soy sauce, then add tofu cubes gently.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until tofu is heated through.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and garnish with green onions before serving.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 green bell pepper, cut into strips
instructions: Toss pork pieces with cornstarch and water until coated evenly.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and deep-fry pork until golden; remove and drain.
In a saucepan, combine soy sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and sugar; simmer until slightly thickened.
Add pineapple, bell peppers, and bamboo shoots to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Return fried pork to the wok and toss briefly to heat through.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: Soy sauce and vinegar for dipping
instructions: Mix flour and boiling water to form a dough; knead until smooth and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground pork, cabbage, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and white pepper; mix well.
Roll dough into thin sheets and cut into small squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Wet the edges with water, fold in half, and pleat the edges to seal.
Bring a pot of water to a boil; drop dumplings in gently.
Cook until dumplings float to the surface, about 5-7 minutes.
Serve hot with soy sauce and vinegar for dipping.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Rub the duck inside and out with rice wine, soy sauce, and honey.
Blow air into the duck's cavity to inflate it; air-dry overnight in a cool place.
Brush the skin with a mixture of water and cornstarch, then air-dry again.
Roast the duck in a low oven (300°F) until the skin is crisp and golden, about 2-3 hours.
Slice the duck meat thinly, keeping the skin intact.
Warm pancakes and spread hoisin sauce on each.
Add a slice of duck, cucumber, and scallion to each pancake.
Roll the pancake and serve immediately.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 lb dried red chilies, cut into pieces
instructions: Toss chicken pieces with cornstarch, soy sauce, oyster sauce, vinegar, and sugar; set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; add chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and slightly crispy.
Remove chicken and set aside; drain excess oil if needed.
Add celery and bell peppers to the wok; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the wok and add roasted peanuts.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and toss to combine.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Marinate chicken with soy sauce and sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry chicken in hot oil until golden, then remove from pan.
Toast peanuts and chilies in the same pan until fragrant.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return chicken to pan and add stock and cornstarch mixture.
Cook until sauce thickens, then stir in scallions and peanuts.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions: Boil water in a pot, gently place tofu cubes in, and remove once cooked.
Fry ground pork in oil until browned.
Add garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang, stir-fry until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and soy sauce, simmer for 5 minutes.
Add tofu cubes and cook gently for 2 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until sauce thickens.
Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with green onions.

title: Dim Sum Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Chop shrimp into small pieces and mix with bamboo shoots, cornstarch, and sesame oil.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Fold wrapper over filling and pleat edges to seal tightly.
Brush tops with egg white and water mixture.
Steam dumplings in a basket over boiling water for 6-8 minutes.
Arrange on a plate and serve hot.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thinly against grain
instructions: Marinate beef slices with soy sauce, cornstarch, and 1 tbsp oil for 10 minutes.
Blanch broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat, stir-fry beef until browned, remove.
Add garlic and ginger to the wok, stir-fry until fragrant.
Return beef to wok, add oyster sauce, stock, and broccoli.
Toss quickly for 2 minutes until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Finish with sesame oil and green onions, serve immediately.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Toss pork cubes with flour and cornstarch until coated.
Deep fry pork in hot oil until golden brown, then drain.
In a bowl, mix ketchup, pineapple juice, vinegar, sugar, and salt.
Heat oil in a wok, stir-fry bell peppers until tender-crisp.
Add pineapple chunks and green onions, cook for 1 minute.
Pour sauce over vegetables and bring to a boil.
Add fried pork and toss to coat in sauce, serve hot.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Marinate diced chicken with soy sauce, cornstarch, and 1 tbsp oil for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry chicken in a wok with oil until cooked through, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry dried chilies, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and crushed peppercorns in a bowl.
Return chicken to the wok and pour in the sauce mixture, tossing to coat.
Add peanuts and scallions, tossing briefly until everything is hot and well combined.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Mix flour and salt, gradually adding warm water to form a smooth dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Squeeze excess water from chopped cabbage and mix with pork, shrimp, ginger, scallions, sesame oil, soy sauce, pepper, and egg.
Roll dough into thin circles, place filling in the center, and fold into crescent shapes.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Drop dumplings into the boiling water one by one.
Cook until dumplings float to the surface, about 3-4 minutes, then remove and serve.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Fry black beans, garlic, and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add Doubanjiang and bean paste, stir-frying for 1 minute until oily.
Pour in chicken broth, soy sauce, and bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes, covering them with the sauce.
Mix cornstarch with a little water and stir into the sauce until it thickens.
Sprinkle ground Sichuan peppercorns and chopped scallions on top before serving.

title: Pork Belly with Bok Choy
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, sliced into thin strips
1 head bok choy, separated into leaves and stems
instructions: Mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and white pepper to make a marinade.
Toss pork belly strips in the marinade and let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Stir-fry pork belly until browned and crispy, then remove and set aside.
Add garlic and ginger to the wok, stir-frying until fragrant.
Add bok choy stems first, stir-frying for 1 minute, then add leaves.
Return pork to the wok and toss until the vegetables are wilted and coated in sauce.

title: Sweet and Sour Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss shrimp in a mixture of cornstarch and flour until lightly coated.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat until hot.
Fry shrimp in batches until golden and cooked through, then drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, mix ketchup, rice vinegar, sugar, water, soy sauce, and cornstarch.
Stir-fry bell peppers, pineapple, and ginger in the same wok until tender-crisp.
Add the sauce mixture and cook until it thickens slightly.
Add fried shrimp back into the wok, tossing to coat evenly with the sauce.
Garnish with chopped scallions before serving.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Marinate pork in soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Coat marinated pork with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Fry pork until golden and remove.
Stir-fry pineapple, peppers, and onions for 2 minutes.
Mix ketchup, sugar, and vinegar in a bowl.
Add sauce to the wok and bring to a boil.
Return pork to the wok and toss until coated.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 1/2 cup cabbage, finely chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix flour and water to form a smooth dough; knead for 10 minutes.
Combine ground pork, cabbage, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, salt, and scallions.
Roll dough into thin circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle.
Fold circle in half and seal edges with water.
Boil dumplings in salted water for 3-4 minutes.
Drain and serve with dipping sauce.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Fry doubanjiang and black beans in oil until fragrant.
Add minced meat and stir until browned.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes and simmer for 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with a little water and stir into the sauce.
Thicken the sauce until it coats the tofu.
Garnish with scallions and serve hot.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Rub duck inside and out with soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar.
Hang duck in a cool place overnight to dry.
Brush duck with oil and rice flour mixture.
Roast duck at 350°F until skin is crispy and golden.
Slice roasted duck into thin pieces.
Brush bok choy and cucumber with hoisin sauce.
Arrange duck, vegetables, and spring rolls on a platter.
Serve with pancakes for wrapping.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
instructions: Heat chicken broth in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu.
Mix vinegar, soy sauce, white pepper, and cornstarch with water.
Stir the mixture into the pot and simmer for 3 minutes.
Drizzle sesame oil over the soup.
Garnish with chopped scallions.
Serve hot.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork loin, cut into small cubes
instructions: Marinate pork with soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Fry pork in oil until golden, then remove from pan.
Stir fry pineapple, peppers, and onions for 2 minutes.
Mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch, and water in a bowl.
Pour sauce into the pan and simmer until thickened.
Return pork to the pan and toss to coat.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Blanch tofu in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Fry pork with garlic and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add chili bean paste and stir fry for 1 minute.
Dilute soy sauce and water in a small bowl.
Pour liquid into the pan and simmer.
Add tofu gently and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with a little water and stir in to thicken.
Drizzle with sesame oil before serving.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to make a soft dough, then rest for 30 minutes.
Combine pork, cabbage, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Roll dough into small circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle.
Fold and pinch edges to seal the dumpling.
Boil in salted water until they float, about 4 minutes.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Rub the duck inside and out with a mixture of soy sauce, honey, sugar, vinegar, five-spice, and water.
Let the duck rest in the fridge overnight.
Air dry the skin for several hours to crisp it.
Roast the duck at 400°F until the skin is golden and crispy.
Carve the duck into thin slices.
Serve with hoisin sauce, cucumber, and scallions.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Mix pork, cabbage, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a small amount of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Wet the edges and fold into triangles, sealing tightly.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Drop wontons into the boiling broth and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add green onions and serve hot.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Coat the pork pieces in flour and cornstarch mixture.
Fry the coated pork in hot oil until golden brown, then remove.
In a pan, mix soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, and ketchup to make the sauce.
Add pineapple, bell peppers, and onions to the sauce and simmer.
Return the fried pork to the pan and toss until coated with sauce.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water, then cut into cubes.
Heat oil in a pan and stir-fry garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned.
Stir in doubanjiang and bean paste, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in water, soy sauce, and ground Sichuan peppercorns.
Gently add tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Mix pork, cabbage, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Fold the wrapper over and seal the edges by pinching.
Arrange dumplings on a greased baking sheet.
Pan-fry in oil until bottoms are golden, then steam with a lid.

title: Peking Duck
ingredients: Sliced cucumber and scallions for garnish
instructions: Rinse the duck and rub inside with rice wine and soy sauce.
Brush the duck outside with honey and maltose syrup mixture.
Hang the duck in a cool place for 24 hours to dry the skin.
Roast the duck at 350°F (175°C) for about 1.5 hours.
Carve the duck into thin slices and serve with hoisin sauce, cucumber, and scallions.

title: Dim Sum Pork Buns (Har Gow)
ingredients: 1 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined, chopped
instructions: Mix shrimp, pork fat, soy sauce, ginger, and sesame oil.
Combine flour, water, baking powder, and salt to make a smooth dough.
Roll out the dough and cut into small circles.
Place a spoonful of shrimp mixture in the center of each circle.
Wet the edges and fold over to form a pleated bun shape.
Steam the buns for 10 minutes until cooked through.

title: Duck with Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 1 whole Peking duck, roasted and sliced
instructions: Stir-fry garlic in a wok until fragrant.
Add bamboo shoots and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add Shaoxing wine and soy sauce, toss to coat.
Arrange roasted duck slices over the vegetables.
Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with green onions.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into cubes
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and fry ground pork until browned.
Add Doubanjiang and stir-fry until oil turns red.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and ground peppercorns.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry and serve.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Toss pork pieces in cornstarch and deep fry until golden.
In a bowl, mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce.
Stir-fry bell peppers and pineapple in a wok.
Add the fried pork and sauce mixture.
Cook until sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Garnish with green onions before serving.

title: Pork Buns (Roujiamo style)
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, and warm water to form a dough; let rise.
Combine ground pork, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and five-spice powder.
Knead dough into small balls and flatten into buns.
Stuff each bun with the seasoned pork mixture.
Pan-fry buns until bottoms are crispy and tops are fluffy.
Brush with oil and serve hot.

title: Lotus Root Stir-Fry
instructions: Toss julienned lotus root with cornstarch.
Steam the coated lotus root for 5 minutes until tender.
Mix oyster sauce, soy sauce, water, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat sesame oil in a wok and stir-fry lotus root.
Pour in the sauce mixture and cook until thickened.
Garnish with sliced green onions.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Coat pork cubes in cornstarch.
Fry pork in oil until golden and set aside.
Stir fry bell peppers and onions until tender-crisp.
Mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, water, and soy sauce in a bowl.
Combine sauce with pineapple and return pork to the pan.
Simmer until sauce thickens and coats the meat.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1/2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and fry ground pork until browned.
Add doubanjiang and crushed peppercorns, stir for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth, sugar, and soy sauce.
Gently add tofu cubes and bean sprouts.
Simmer for 5 minutes until flavors meld.
Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and warm water to form a dough; knead until smooth.
Combine ground pork, cabbage, scallion, ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Roll dough into small circles and place filling in center.
Fold dough over and seal edges by pinching.
Boil dumplings in salted water until they float.
Pan-fry in oil for a crispy bottom before serving.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Rub duck inside and out with soy sauce, rice wine, and scallions.
Brush duck skin with maltose syrup mixture.
Air-dry duck uncovered in a cool place for 24 hours.
Roast duck at 350°F for 3 hours until skin is crispy.
Carve duck thinly, arranging meat on plates.
Serve with hoisin sauce, cucumber, and thin pancakes.

title: Dim Sum (Har Gow)
instructions: Mix shrimp, bamboo shoots, ginger, sesame oil, and salt.
Place filling in center of dumpling wrapper.
Fold wrapper into a crescent shape and pleat edges.
Brush egg white mixed with cornstarch over dumplings.
Steam dumplings in a lined steamer for 8 minutes.
Serve hot with chili sauce.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 1 lb ground pork, mixed with 1 tsp soy sauce
1/2 cup finely chopped cabbage, salted and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix ground pork, soy sauce, cabbage, ginger, and green onions in a bowl.
Combine flour and salt, gradually adding water to form a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into a long rope, cut into small pieces, and flatten each piece.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper and pleat the edges to seal.
Boil water, add dumplings, and cook until they float, about 3-4 minutes.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup dried red chilies, cut into small pieces
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces with soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat, then add dried chilies, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and slightly browned.
Stir in sugar, vinegar, and crushed Sichuan peppercorns.
Add green onions and roasted peanuts, toss to combine.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch tofu cubes in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok, add minced pork and cook until browned.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang, cooking until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and water, then bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and green onions before serving.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Inflate the duck's stomach with air to separate skin from meat, then rub inside with wine, soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar.
Blanch the duck in hot water for 5 minutes, then dry thoroughly.
Brush the skin with honey and water mixture, then roast at 400°F for 30 minutes.
Lower temperature to 350°F and roast for another 45-60 minutes until skin is crispy.
Carve the duck into thin slices, separating skin from meat.
Warm pancakes, and assemble with duck skin, meat, hoisin sauce, cucumber, and scallions.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and chopped
1/2 cup dried tofu puffs, soaked and chopped
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper, sesame oil, water, and cornstarch slurry in a small bowl.
In a pot, heat chicken broth to a boil, then add garlic and ginger.
Add ground pork, wood ear mushrooms, tofu puffs, and bamboo shoots, cooking until pork is done.
Pour in the sauce mixture and stir until the soup thickens.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, then garnish with green onions.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Duck with Red Dates and Goji Berries
instructions: Rinse the duck and place it in a large pot.
Add the red dates, goji berries, water, wine, and ginger.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Remove duck, slice, and serve with the broth.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Blanch tofu cubes in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the bean paste and doubanjiang until fragrant.
Add garlic and ginger, then stir in the chicken broth.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Gently add the tofu, coat with sauce, and thicken with cornstarch slurry.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 pound pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Coat pork cubes in cornstarch and deep fry until golden; drain.
In a pan, sauté bell peppers and pineapple until tender.
Mix sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and cornstarch to make the glaze.
Add the glaze to the pan and simmer until bubbly.
Toss in the fried pork and stir to coat evenly.

title: Steamed Fish with Scallion Oil
instructions: Score the fish, season with salt and wine, and place ginger inside the cavity.
Steam the fish for 10 minutes per pound.
Remove fish, discard ginger, and pour hot water over the fish.
Arrange scallions and garlic on top of the fish.
Heat sesame oil until smoking, then pour over the scallions.

title: Szechuan Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried chilies, cut into segments
instructions: Toss chicken with soy sauce, sugar, and cornstarch, then set aside.
Stir-fry peanuts and chilies in oil until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add vinegar and mix well.
Remove from heat and serve immediately with peanuts.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 cup dried red chilies, cut in half
instructions: Mix soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt, cornstarch, chicken broth, sesame oil, and rice vinegar in a bowl to make the sauce.
Toss chicken cubes with half of the sauce and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry chicken until golden brown, about 5 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add chilies and peanuts to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the wok and pour in the remaining sauce.
Stir-fry quickly for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Garnish with green onions and sesame oil before serving.

title: Dim Sum Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix shrimp with cornstarch, salt, white pepper, and sugar; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Combine flour, tapioca starch, baking powder, salt, sugar, water, and oil to make a smooth dough.
Roll dough into thin sheets and cut into small squares.
Place a spoonful of shrimp mixture in the center of each square.
Pinch the edges together to seal, leaving a small opening at the top.
Steam dumplings in a bamboo steamer for 8-10 minutes until translucent.
Mix chicken broth, cornstarch, soy sauce, and sesame oil to make a glaze.
Brush the glaze over the steamed dumplings before serving.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Blanch tofu cubes in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Brown ground pork in a wok with oil, then remove and set aside.
Add garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant.
Return pork to the wok and add chicken broth, sugar, salt, sesame oil, and soy sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then add tofu and cook gently for 2 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with water to make a slurry and stir into the pot until thickened.
Sprinkle with green onions and serve hot.

title: Peking Duck
instructions: Inflate the duck with air to separate skin from meat, then dry thoroughly for 24 hours.
Rub duck inside and out with soy sauce, honey, water, five-spice powder, and sesame oil.
Hang the duck upside down in a cool place overnight to dry the skin.
Roast the duck in an oven at 400°F for 45 minutes, then lower to 350°F for 1 hour.
Pour hot water over the skin twice during roasting to crisp it.
Carve the duck into thin slices, separating the skin from the meat.
Warm pancakes and mix cucumber, scallions, hoisin sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar.
Serve duck slices with pancakes and the vegetable mixture.

title: Jiaozi (Chinese Potstickers)
instructions: Mix flour and salt, then gradually add water to form a smooth dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Combine pork, shrimp, cabbage, scallions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, cornstarch, and salt in a bowl.
Roll dough into small circles and place a spoonful of filling in the center.
Fold the dough in half and pleat the edges to seal.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan and place dumplings flat-side down.
Cook on medium heat for 3 minutes until the bottom is golden brown.
Pour water into the pan, cover, and steam for 5-7 minutes until water evaporates.
Remove the lid and cook for another 2 minutes to crisp the bottom before serving.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy sauce and cornstarch for 20 minutes.
Stir-fry chicken in hot oil until cooked through and set aside.
In a separate pan, stir-fry peanuts, chilies, and scallions until fragrant.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar to create the sauce.
Combine chicken and sauce with the vegetable mixture.
Heat through and serve hot.

title: Dumplings (Jiaozi)
ingredients: 100g Napa cabbage, finely chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix pork, cabbage, scallions, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil, then mix well.
Place a wrapper on a flat surface and put a spoonful of filling in the center.
Wet the edge with beaten egg and fold the wrapper in half.
Press edges together to seal and pleat if desired.
Boil water, add dumplings, and cook until they float.
Drain and serve with dipping sauce.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork loin, sliced into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Toss pork slices in cornstarch and deep fry until golden brown.
Remove pork and set aside on paper towels.
In a wok, stir-fry pineapple, bell peppers, and carrots until tender-crisp.
Mix vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and ketchup in a small bowl.
Pour the sauce into the wok and bring to a simmer.
Add the fried pork back into the sauce.
Stir until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Boil water briefly, add tofu cubes, and drain.
Heat oil in a wok, then stir-fry ground pork until browned.
Add garlic and ginger, then stir in doubanjiang.
Pour in vegetable broth and add sugar.
Gently add the tofu cubes to the simmering sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until flavors meld.
Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Finish with sesame oil and serve over rice.

title: Dim Sum Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
instructions: Mix shrimp, bamboo shoots, scallions, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Place a wrapper on a plate and add a small amount of filling.
Fold the wrapper over and pleat the edges to form a purse shape.
Brush the sealed edges with egg white.
Steam the dumplings in a basket over boiling water for 8 minutes.
Serve hot with chili oil or soy dipping sauce.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into small cubes
1/2 cup dried red chilies, cut into pieces
instructions: Mix chicken cubes with soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, and cornstarch; let marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Stir-fry chicken until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry garlic, ginger, and chilies until fragrant.
Add peanuts back to the wok.
Return chicken to the wok and toss to combine.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch tofu cubes in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat.
Stir-fry garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute until oil turns red.
Pour in stock, soy sauce, sugar, and ground peppercorns; simmer for 3 minutes.
Gently add tofu cubes to the sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Coat pork pieces in flour and deep-fry until golden; remove and drain.
In a bowl, mix ketchup, sugar, vinegar, and soy sauce until smooth.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry onions, bell peppers, and pineapple until slightly softened.
Add the fried pork back to the wok.
Pour in the sauce mixture and toss to coat.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry until the sauce thickens.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Dim Sum Shrimp Dumplings (Har Gow)
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Chop shrimp, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts very finely.
Mix chopped ingredients with soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper.
Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Place a wonton wrapper on a damp surface and fill with the shrimp mixture.
Fold the wrapper in half and pleat the edges to seal.
Brush the edges with beaten egg to help seal.
Drop dumplings into boiling water and cook for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve immediately.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir Fry
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thinly against the grain
instructions: Mix beef slices with soy sauce and cornstarch; let marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry beef until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry broccoli for 2 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in oyster sauce, sugar, and beef broth.
Toss everything together for 1 minute until heated through.
Serve over steamed white rice.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Dried Mushrooms (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 10g dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and sliced
5g dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Fry pork belly cubes in oil until golden brown and crispy on edges.
Remove pork and set aside; keep the rendered fat in the wok.
Add rock sugar to the fat and stir until melted into a dark caramel sauce.
Add ginger, star anise, and tangerine peel, stir-frying to release aromas.
Return pork to the wok, pour in soy sauces and cooking wine, and stir to coat.
Add water to just cover the meat, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Add the soaked mushrooms and dried tangerine peel.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until pork is tender and sauce is thick.
Turn up heat to reduce sauce to a glossy glaze before serving.

title: Clear Noodle Soup with Chicken and Ham (Liang Mian)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil.
Add ginger slices and dried shrimp to the boiling water.
Gently slide in the chicken slices and cook until just opaque.
Add ham and pickled mustard greens, simmer for 2 minutes.
Separate noodles and blanch them in the soup water for 30 seconds.
Remove noodles with a strainer and place in a deep bowl.
Pour the hot broth over the noodles.
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with chopped scallions.
Serve immediately while steaming hot.

title: Stir-Fried Shredded Pork with Preserved Egg Yolk (Suan Rou)
ingredients: 300g pork loin, thinly sliced and marinated with soy sauce and cornstarch
3 preserved egg yolks, peeled and halved
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add ginger and garlic, stir-frying for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add marinated pork slices and stir-fry quickly until the meat turns white.
Add scallions and toss for another 10 seconds.
Push ingredients to the side of the wok and crack the preserved egg yolks into the center.
Fry the egg yolks until the surface is set but the inside is still soft.
Mix the egg yolk with the pork and scallions.
Add soy sauce, cooking wine, and sugar, tossing continuously.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately.

title: Sweet and Sour Mandarin Fish (Lyu Yu)
ingredients: 2 whole mandarin fish (approx. 300g each), cleaned and scored
instructions: Score the mandarin fish lightly and season inside and out with salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok to 180°C (350°F).
Fry the fish whole until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove fish and drain excess oil from the wok.
Add ginger, garlic, and tomato paste to the hot oil, stir-frying briefly.
Pour in rice vinegar, rock sugar, and water to create the sauce.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and let it bubble until slightly reduced.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce to a glossy coating.
Return the fried fish to the wok, spoon sauce over them, and garnish with scallions.
Serve hot.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallion (Qing Xian Yu)
ingredients: 1 whole freshwater fish (approx. 500g), cleaned and scaled
20g dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
10g dried tangerine peel, soaked and sliced
instructions: Remove the fish head and tail, keeping the body intact, and score the flesh diagonally.
Stuff the fish cavity with half the ginger slices, dried tangerine peel, and half the scallions.
Place the fish on a steaming rack lined with ginger slices.
Pour cooking wine and soy sauce into the fish cavity.
Steam over boiling water for 10 minutes for a 500g fish.
Remove the fish from the steamer and carefully drain excess liquid.
Discard the used ginger and scallion inside the fish, leaving the infused flavors.
Arrange the remaining julienned ginger and scallion on top of the fish.
Scatter the dried shiitake mushroom slices over the aromatics.
Pour hot water over the aromatics to wilt them slightly, then drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Shrimp with Ginger and Scallions
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Pat shrimp dry and season with salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add ginger slices and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes until pink.
Pour in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil.
Toss in scallions and cook for 1 minute until just wilted.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Black Beans
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Drain soaked black beans and set aside.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Seal pork cubes in the fat until browned on all sides.
Add star anise and cinnamon stick.
Pour in Shaoxing wine and rock sugar, stir to combine.
Add black beans and chicken stock.
Simmer covered on low heat for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Add soy sauce and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken sauce.

title: Clear Broth with Fish Maw and Tofu
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 piece dried fish maw, soaked and cleaned
1 lb fresh cod fillet, sliced thinly
instructions: Combine pork bones, ginger, and garlic in a pot with water.
Bring to a boil, skim scum, then simmer for 45 minutes.
Add fish maw and shiitake mushrooms.
Add tofu cubes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Gently add fish slices one by one.
Cook on low heat for 3 minutes until fish is opaque.
Season with salt and strain before serving.

title: Steamed Dragon Whiskers Fish
ingredients: 1 whole fish (about 1 lb), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Make diagonal cuts on both sides of the fish.
Rub fish inside and out with salt and Shaoxing wine.
Arrange ginger strips and scallions over the fish.
Steam over boiling water for 8 minutes.
Remove fish and pour off excess water.
Drizzle soy sauce and sesame oil over the fish.
Heat oil in a small pan until smoking hot.
Pour hot oil over the scallions and ginger to release aroma.
Serve immediately.

title: Sweet and Sour Glazed Pork
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Marinate pork pieces with 1 tbsp soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Mix vinegar, sugar, remaining soy sauce, and water in a bowl.
Add cornstarch to the sauce mixture and stir well.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry pork until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the sauce mixture and bring to a boil.
Stir-fry quickly until sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Toss in scallions and remove from heat.

title: Oyster Omelet (Xiaolong Dan)
ingredients: 1 cup fresh oyster sauce, diluted with water
instructions: Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Pour in the diluted oyster sauce and spread evenly to form a thin layer.
Pour in the beaten eggs and cook until the edges are set but the center is still slightly runny.
Scatter the oyster meat, bean sprouts, and green onions over the egg layer.
Tilt the pan to distribute the liquid evenly.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.
Slide the omelet onto a cutting board, cut into squares, and serve hot.

title: Minced Pork with Scallions (Chashui)
instructions: In a bowl, combine ground pork, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, and cornstarch.
Mix thoroughly with a fork until the meat is sticky and well-coated.
Fold in half of the green onion and the scallion oil.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add the meat mixture in small batches, spreading it out to form a thin layer.
Fry until the bottom is crispy and golden, then flip.
Remove from heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and sprinkle with the remaining green onion.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Taro (Longyu)
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, cut into large chunks
2 medium taro roots, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Blanch the pork belly chunks in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities, then rinse.
In a heavy pot, combine pork, taro, broth, ginger, garlic, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 1.5 hours until tender.
Skim any excess fat from the surface during cooking.
Adjust seasoning with salt if needed.
Serve the pork and taro with the rich braising liquid poured over the top.

title: Tomato and Egg Stir-fry (Chongdan)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until just set, then remove from the pan.
Add a little more oil to the pan and add the diced tomatoes.
Stir-fry the tomatoes until they break down and release their juices.
Add sugar, salt, and a splash of water to help the sauce thicken.
Return the scrambled eggs to the pan and toss gently to coat.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

title: Stuffed Winter Melon (Donggua Ba)
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and chopped
instructions: Scrape the flesh from the winter melon, leaving a thin wall, and cut into large cubes.
In a bowl, mix ground pork, wood ear, shiitake, green onion, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
Stuff the meat mixture generously into the hollowed-out melon cubes.
Place the stuffed melon cubes in a steamer basket lined with cabbage leaves.
Steam over boiling water for 20-25 minutes until the meat is cooked through and the melon is tender.
Pour a little soy sauce over the top before serving.

title: Sichuan-Style Stir-Fried Pork with Preserved Vegetables
ingredients: 200g preserved mustard greens, cleaned and cut
instructions: Blanch the mustard greens in boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking, then remove.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and crushed peppercorns to the oil and fry until fragrant.
Add the sliced pork and stir-fry quickly until the meat changes color.
Season with salt, sugar, and cooking wine, then add the mustard greens.
Toss everything together for one minute until the greens are wilted.
Drizzle with the cornstarch slurry and stir until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.

title: Mapo Tofu with Ground Pork
instructions: Soak the tofu cubes in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the ground pork until cooked through and browned.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang to the pork, stir-frying until the oil turns red.
Pour in the stock, soy sauce, sugar, and ground Sichuan peppercorns, then simmer for 2 minutes.
Gently slide the tofu cubes into the sauce and cook on low heat for 3 minutes without breaking them.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce to a glossy consistency.
Serve immediately over steamed white rice.

title: Dong'an Chicken (Red-Braised Chicken)
ingredients: 5 dried chili peppers, cut into segments
instructions: Blanch the chicken pieces in boiling water for 3 minutes to remove impurities, then rinse and drain.
Heat oil in a large pot and sear the chicken pieces until lightly browned on all sides.
Remove chicken, then add garlic, ginger, dried chilies, and star anise to the pot and fry for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the pot and add Shaoxing wine, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and sugar.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Increase heat slightly to reduce the sauce until it clings to the chicken pieces.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Hunan Spicy Fish Head Soup
ingredients: 1 large fish head (approx. 800g), cleaned and patted dry
instructions: Soak the tofu skin sheets in warm water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok and sear the fish head on all sides until golden, then remove.
In the same wok, fry the pork belly slices until the fat renders slightly.
Add garlic, ginger, dried chilies, and crushed peppercorns, stir-frying until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the salt, sugar, and seared fish head; simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently stir in the soaked tofu skin sheets and cook for another 2 minutes before serving.

title: Pickled Green Peppers with Beef
ingredients: 300g beef brisket, sliced against the grain
400g pickled green peppers, rinsed and sliced
instructions: Marinate the beef slices with cooking wine and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and quickly stir-fry the beef for 1-2 minutes until just cooked.
Remove the beef and set aside, leaving the oil in the wok.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and ground Sichuan peppercorns to the oil and fry until aromatic.
Add the pickled green peppers and stir-fry for 1 minute to release their acidity.
Return the beef to the wok and toss with the peppers and seasoning (salt and sugar).
Drizzle with the cornstarch slurry and toss quickly until the sauce thickens and the dish is hot.

title: Hong Shao Rou (Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 100g dried bamboo shoots, soaked and sliced
instructions: Stir-fry the pork belly in a wok until golden brown and remove.
In the same wok, fry the bean paste until fragrant, then add ginger, garlic, star anise, and orange peel.
Return the pork to the wok, add mushrooms and bamboo shoots.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, soy sauces, and enough water to cover the meat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Remove lid and simmer on high heat until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.

title: Guo Bao Rou (Double Cooked Pork)
ingredients: 1 green onion, cut into small pieces
instructions: Marinate the sliced pork with soy sauce, white pepper, and half the cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the marinated pork in hot oil until just cooked through and remove.
In a separate pan, stir-fry the sweet bean paste until fragrant.
Add the cooked pork back to the pan with the remaining cornstarch, water, wine, and sugar.
Cook until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Toss with green onions and drizzle with sesame oil before serving.

title: Ma Po Tofu (Spicy Minced Meat Tofu)
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water and cut into cubes.
Stir-fry the ground pork in a wok until browned, then remove.
Add garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant.
Return the pork to the wok and add bean sprouts, soy sauce, sugar, and water.
Add the tofu cubes gently and simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Remove from heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and serve hot.

title: Dong Po Rou (Hairy Belly Pork)
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into large chunks
20g dried larch mushrooms, rehydrated and torn
instructions: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities.
In a clay pot or heavy pot, stir-fry ginger, star anise, orange peel, and red dates until fragrant.
Add the blanched pork, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots.
Pour in soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, rock sugar, and water to cover the ingredients.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer on high heat until the sauce reduces to a thick glaze.

title: Yue Xian Jiao (Steamed Dumplings)
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to form a smooth dough and let it rest.
Mix ground pork, cabbage, shrimp, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and pepper.
Roll out small circles of dough and fill with the meat mixture.
Fold and seal the edges to form pleated dumplings.
Place dumplings on a steamer lined with cabbage leaves.
Steam over boiling water for 12-15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.

title: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu, cut into cubes
2 tablespoons fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry the minced meat until browned, then push to the side.
Add garlic, ginger, doubanjiang, and fermented black beans to the meat.
Stir-fry until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in the broth, sugar, and salt; simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the tofu cubes gently and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry until the sauce thickens.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot over rice.

title: Boiled Pork with Garlic and Chili
ingredients: 3 dried red chilies, cut into small pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork slices in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, and sugar.
Heat neutral oil in a wok until smoking hot.
Pour the hot oil over the pork slices in a serving dish.
Immediately add the minced garlic, dried chilies, and ground Sichuan peppercorns.
Toss the pork gently with the garlic chili oil mixture.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with cilantro before serving.

title: Kunming-style Sour Soup Noodles
ingredients: 300g alkaline wheat noodles, cut into short lengths
instructions: Boil the noodles in salted water until al dente, then drain and rinse with cold water.
In a separate pot, heat oil and stir-fry garlic and pickled mustard greens until fragrant.
Add the broth, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and white pepper; bring to a simmer.
Add the pork slices, bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, and tofu puffs.
Cook for 3 minutes until the meat is just cooked through.
Arrange the noodles in a deep bowl and ladle the hot soup and toppings over them.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns.

title: Spicy Shredded Beef with Celery
ingredients: 400g flank steak, sliced thinly across the grain
instructions: Marinate the beef slices with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 tablespoon cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the beef quickly until just browned; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add more oil and stir-fry garlic and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add the doubanjiang and cook until the oil turns red.
Return the beef to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the julienned celery, sugar, salt, and remaining soy sauce.
Toss everything together for 30 seconds until the celery is tender-crisp.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Shredded Pork with Preserved Vegetables
ingredients: 200g preserved mustard greens, washed and shredded
instructions: Blanch the preserved mustard greens and pickled radish in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the shredded pork and stir-fry until the meat changes color.
Add the mustard greens and pickled radish; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper, and salt.
Toss continuously until the vegetables are wilted and coated in the sauce.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Scallion Oil
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or grouper, cleaned and scored
2 scallions, white and green parts separated
instructions: Season the fish inside and out with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger, and the white parts of scallions.
Place the fish in a steamer basket over boiling water and steam for 8-10 minutes until opaque.
Remove fish and discard ginger and scallion whites.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan until it just begins to smoke, then immediately pour it over the hot fish.
Arrange the scallion greens and garlic on top of the fish.
Sprinkle sugar over the top and serve immediately.

title: Cantonese-Style Braised Pork Belly (Zha Jiang Rou)
instructions: Blanch the pork cubes in boiling water for 2 minutes, then rinse under cold water.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the rock sugar until it melts into a deep amber color.
Add the pork, star anise, ginger, and onion, tossing to coat in the caramel.
Pour in the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 1.5 hours until tender.
Increase heat to reduce the sauce to a glaze, finish with sesame oil, and serve.

title: Wonton Soup with Shrimp and Pork
ingredients: 12 cups chicken or pork bone broth
instructions: Mix ground pork, minced shrimp, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, ginger, salt, and 1 tablespoon of water until sticky.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper and pleat to seal.
Bring broth to a rolling boil in a large pot.
Drop wontons gently into the boiling broth and cook until they float (about 3-4 minutes).
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions and toasted sesame seeds.

title: Char Siu BBQ Pork Buns (Baofu)
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Marinate the pork cubes in hoisin sauce, honey, five-spice powder, soy sauce, sesame oil, and food coloring for at least 2 hours.
Preheat an oven or grill to 400°F (200°C).
Place marinated pork on a baking sheet and broil for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and cooked through.
Divide the baozi dough into 12 pieces and flatten each slightly.
Place a generous amount of pork in the center of each bun, pleat the dough to enclose, and brush with oil.
Steam the buns for 15 minutes until puffy, then brush with a little remaining glaze if desired.

title: Drunken Noodles with Beef and Basil (Pad Kee Mao)
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thinly against the grain
instructions: Soak the dried noodles in warm water for 15 minutes until pliable, then drain and set aside.
Stir-fry the beef in hot oil in a wok until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry garlic, ginger, and chili until fragrant.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water to create a sauce base.
Return the beef to the wok, add the noodles, and toss quickly to coat and heat through.
Remove from heat immediately and toss in the basil and bean sprouts until the basil wilts slightly.

title: Jinan Braised Chicken (Jinan Jian Ji)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1.5 kg), cut into pieces
100g dried lily bulbs, soaked and sliced
instructions: Blanch the chicken pieces in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse with cold water.
Fry the pork belly in a wok until golden brown and remove.
In the same wok, stir-fry the minced scallops, shrimp, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and fry until the surface is slightly browned.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, and rock sugar, stirring to coat.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1 hour until the chicken is tender.
Add the fried pork belly and dried lily bulbs, simmer for another 20 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed before serving.

title: Shandong Sweet and Sour Potatoes (Tang Suan Shu Guo)
ingredients: 500g sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
instructions: Boil the sweet potato wedges in water with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until half-cooked, then drain.
Fry the sweet potatoes in vegetable oil over medium-high heat until golden and crispy, about 8 minutes.
Remove potatoes and set aside; wipe the wok clean.
In the same wok, stir-fry the ginger and garlic until aromatic.
Add the vinegar, rock sugar, and water, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Return the fried sweet potatoes to the wok and toss gently to coat in the glaze.
Drizzle with sesame oil and stir once more before serving hot.

title: Braised Pork with Preserved Vegetables (Cai Xin Rou)
ingredients: 100g Shandong preserved mustard greens, rinsed and cut into strips
50g dried radish, soaked and cut into strips
instructions: Blanch the pork cubes in boiling water for 3 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
In a deep pot, heat oil and fry the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the pork, Shaoxing wine, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, rock sugar, star anise, and cinnamon.
Stir well to coat the pork, then add the chicken stock.
Bring to a boil, skim off any scum, then reduce heat to low.
Braise for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the preserved mustard greens and dried radish, and continue to braise for 15 minutes.
Remove the spices, taste for seasoning, and serve.

title: Stir-Fried Squid with Garlic and Ginger (Jiu Jiao)
ingredients: 300g fresh squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
instructions: Marinate the squid rings with 1 tsp of Shaoxing wine for 10 minutes, then drain.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic and ginger until fragrant but not browned.
Add the squid and the crushed Sichuan peppercorns, stir-frying quickly for 1 minute until the squid turns opaque.
Add the rock sugar, remaining Shaoxing wine, and chicken stock, tossing to combine.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry and stir-fry until the sauce thickens and coats the squid.
Drizzle with sesame oil, give it a final toss, and serve immediately.

title: Shandong Braised Radish with Pork (Luo Bo Shu)
ingredients: 400g white radish, peeled and cut into large chunks
instructions: Blanch the radish chunks in boiling water for 2 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain.
In a wok, fry the pork cubes until browned on all sides, then remove.
Stir-fry the dried shrimp, ginger, and garlic until fragrant.
Return the pork to the wok, add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and rock sugar, mixing well.
Add the chicken stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Add the blanched radish chunks and simmer for 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in the sesame oil before serving.

title: Yangzhou Braised Pork
instructions: Blanch pork cubes in boiling water for 2 minutes, then rinse.
Brown the pork in a wok with oil until golden on all sides.
Add ginger, star anise, rock sugar, and Shaoxing wine; stir until sugar melts.
Pour in chicken stock, soy sauces, and sugar; bring to a simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, mushrooms, peas, carrots, and pickled bamboo shoots.
Cover and braise over low heat for 45 minutes until pork is tender.
Remove star anise and ginger; adjust seasoning with salt.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with cilantro before serving.

title: Jiangsu-style Braised Fish
ingredients: 1 whole freshwater fish (approx. 750g), cleaned and scaled
100g dried beancurd skin, cut into strips
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Score the fish diagonally on both sides and season with salt and ginger.
Fry the fish in oil until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry eggplants, beancurd skin, and lily bulbs until slightly softened.
Add remaining ginger and scallion; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in chicken stock, soy sauces, sugar, Shaoxing wine, and salt; bring to a boil.
Return the fish to the wok, bone-side down, then flip to coat in sauce.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
ingredients: 300g leftover cooked rice, day-old and cooled
instructions: Stir-fry the beaten egg in half the oil until set, then remove and chop into pieces.
In the same wok, stir-fry the diced pork until no longer pink.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the pickled bamboo shoots, shrimp, peas, carrots, and preserved radish for 2 minutes.
Add the day-old rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry over high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Mix in the scrambled egg pieces, salt, white pepper, sugar, and light soy sauce.
Continue stir-frying until the rice grains are hot and separated.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss to combine.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve hot.

title: Hairy Crab with Ginger
ingredients: 2 large hairy crabs, cleaned and steamed until bright red
50g dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
instructions: Remove the meat from the steamed crabs and set aside the shell halves.
Stir-fry the julienned ginger, scallion whites, and pork belly until fragrant.
Add the crab meat and mushrooms; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock, soy sauce, sugar, and salt; bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove from heat and drizzle generously with sesame oil over the crab meat.
Serve the crab meat atop the empty crab shells.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with steamed rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Spinach
ingredients: 400g spinach, washed and cut into 3cm pieces
100g dried black fungus, rehydrated and cut into strips
100g dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and set aside.
Stir-fry the black fungus, lily bulbs, and mushrooms in oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the blanched spinach to the wok; stir-fry for 1 minute to heat through.
Pour in the chicken stock, sugar, and salt; cover and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss to coat the vegetables evenly.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Ham (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 150g dried black wood ear mushrooms, soaked
100g dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and stemmed
1 stalk scallion, tied in a knot
instructions: Stir-fry the pork belly cubes until the surface is golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add rock sugar and a little oil, stir until the sugar melts into a deep red caramel.
Add the fried pork, ham, mushrooms, ginger, and scallion to the caramel, stirring to coat evenly.
Pour in the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and broth.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 90 minutes until the pork is tender.
Increase heat slightly to thicken the sauce until it clings to the meat.

title: Stir-Fried Shrimp with Snow Peas and Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 400g fresh river shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Season the shrimp with a pinch of salt and a drop of oil, then marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until they turn pink and curl.
Remove the shrimp and set aside, leaving the oil in the wok.
Add the garlic, bamboo shoots, and snow peas, stir-frying for 2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return the shrimp to the wok, add Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, and salt, tossing quickly.
Drizzle in the cornstarch slurry and toss until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients.

title: Sweet and Sour Shredded Pork
ingredients: 400g pork loin, thinly sliced against the grain
150g pickled mustard greens, rinsed and shredded
instructions: Boil the sliced pork in water with a little salt for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Mix the rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, salt, and ground Sichuan peppercorns in a bowl to make the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled pork, pickled mustard greens, cucumber, and carrot.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and meat.
Toss gently to combine, then drizzle with sesame oil.
Let it sit for 15 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallion
instructions: Make three diagonal slashes along the fish body for even cooking.
Stuff the fish cavity with half of the ginger slices and scallions.
Rub the outside of the fish with salt, sugar, and the remaining ginger and scallions.
Place the fish in a steamer basket lined with ginger slices.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes depending on size.
Remove the fish, discard the ginger inside the cavity, and pour hot oil over the fish to release aromatics.
Drizzle the soy sauce over the steamed fish and garnish with fresh scallion greens.

title: Zhejiang Style Braised Green Beans with Salted Vegetable
ingredients: 300g green beans, trimmed and cut into 3cm pieces
50g preserved vegetable (Lao Gan Ma or similar), rinsed and cut into strips
1 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped
instructions: Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse in cold water.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry the garlic and fermented black beans until fragrant.
Add the preserved vegetable and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the green beans, salt, sugar, Shaoxing wine, and soy sauce.
Toss quickly for 1-2 minutes until the beans are tender-crisp but still bright green.
Serve immediately.

title: Oyster Omelette (Xian Bai Chao Dan)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Mix the flour with a little water to make a thin batter.
Stir-fry the cabbage slices in hot oil until slightly wilted.
Add the oysters to the cabbage and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the beaten eggs and quickly scramble.
Tilt the pan to coat the mixture evenly, then flip to cook the other side.
Season with salt and white pepper, garnish with green onions, and serve immediately.

title: Red-Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
instructions: Blanch the pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Heat oil in a wok and stir-fry the pork until golden brown.
Add ginger, chili, star anise, rock sugar, soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
Uncover and simmer on medium heat until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.

title: Minced Pork and Tofu Soup (Xiao Ji Rou Tang)
ingredients: 4 cups chicken or pork bone broth
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a pot and stir-fry the ground pork until it changes color.
Add the diced tofu to the pork and stir gently for 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to meld the flavors.
Season with salt, white pepper, and soy sauce.
Stir in sesame oil and chopped green onions before serving.

title: Stir-Fried Sea Cucumber with Scallions (Jiao Qi Xian Bei)
ingredients: 2 large sea cucumbers, cleaned and sliced into rings
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Blanch the sea cucumber rings in boiling water for 30 seconds and drain.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Stir-fry the scallion segments until fragrant.
Add the sea cucumber and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry and toss until the sauce thickens.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot.

title: Braised Tofu with Dried Shrimp (Dried Shrimp Tofu)
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
1/2 cup dried mushrooms, soaked and sliced
instructions: Deep fry the tofu cubes until golden and drain on paper towels.
In a pot, lightly sauté the garlic and Sichuan peppercorns in oil.
Add the dried shrimp and mushrooms and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken stock, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Add the fried tofu cubes and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Serve the tofu and broth in a deep bowl.

title: Stir-Fried Pork with Green Peppers (Qiezi Erjiao Rou)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add ground Sichuan peppercorns and stir for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and chili bean paste; stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add pork slices and cook until the edges turn white.
Pour in cooking wine, soy sauce, and chicken stock.
Add green peppers and stir-fry vigorously until the peppers are tender-crisp.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Sour and Spicy Stewed Duck with Wood Ear (Suanla Wuyin)
ingredients: 1 whole duck (about 4 lbs), cut into pieces
1 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
instructions: Blanch duck pieces in boiling water for 2 minutes, then rinse.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang until fragrant.
Add duck pieces and sear until browned on all sides.
