Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots, wood ear, pickled mustard greens, and radish.
Stir in black vinegar and sugar; simmer for another 10 minutes.
Season with white pepper and serve hot.

title: Mapo Tofu with Ground Pork (Mapo Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block soft tofu (about 14 oz), cut into cubes
1 tbsp Doubanjiang oil or sesame oil
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add salt, and gently blanch tofu cubes for 2 minutes; drain and set aside.
In a wok, heat oil over medium heat and fry ground pork until cooked through; remove pork.
In the same wok, add doubanjiang and fry for 1 minute until red oil appears.
Return pork to the wok, add garlic, and stir-fry.
Pour in chicken stock, sugar, and soy sauce; bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes to the sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns, and garnish with cilantro.
Serve immediately.

title: Spicy Beef with Preserved Vegetables (Xiang La Rou)
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until very hot.
Add sliced beef and stir-fry quickly until just cooked; remove and set aside.
Add garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang to the wok; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add preserved mustard greens and radish; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the wok and stir to combine.
Add beef stock, dark soy sauce, and sugar; simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and serve over rice.

title: Stir-Fried Shrimp with Garlic and Chili (Bao Xiang Xia)
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 dried red chilies, cut into segments
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Season shrimp with a pinch of salt and pepper; set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add garlic, ginger, and dried chilies; stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang and stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add shrimp and stir-fry quickly until they turn pink and opaque.
Pour in cooking wine, soy sauce, chicken stock, and sugar; toss to coat.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Sprinkle with ground Sichuan peppercorns and serve immediately.

title: Anhui Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Fry pork belly cubes in oil until golden and crispy on the outside.
Remove pork and set aside; render the excess fat in the pan.
Add ginger, garlic, chilies, star anise, and cinnamon to the fat and stir-fry until fragrant.
Return pork to the pan and add dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, rock sugar, and Shaoxing wine.
Stir well to coat, then add water or broth until it covers the meat halfway.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Remove the spices before serving.

title: Smoked Fish with Ginger (Xiang You Yu)
ingredients: 1 whole smoked fish, cleaned and gutted
instructions: Place the cleaned fish in a pot with the ginger slices and enough water to cover it.
Add rock sugar and salt to the water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse the flavor.
Remove the fish and let it cool slightly before removing the ginger slices.
Return the fish to the pot and add minced garlic and crushed Sichuan peppercorns.
Simmer on low heat for another 5 minutes until the fish is fully cooked and the broth is aromatic.
Serve hot with the ginger-infused broth.

title: Dried Tofu with Cabbage (Qie Guo Cai)
ingredients: 1 lb dried tofu, rehydrated and sliced
2 large heads of Napa cabbage, chopped
instructions: Soak the dried tofu in warm water until soft, then drain and slice into strips.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the dried tofu and stir-fry for 2 minutes until it browns slightly.
Add the chopped Napa cabbage and stir-fry until the leaves wilt.
Pour in water, soy sauce, rock sugar, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes until the tofu is tender and the cabbage is soft.
Garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Stir-Fried River Snails (Shui Zhen)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs river snails, cleaned and scrubbed
instructions: Boil the cleaned snails in water with a slice of ginger for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a wok and stir-fry garlic, ginger, and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add the snails and stir-fry vigorously for 2 minutes.
Add dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and salt, then toss well to coat.
Continue stir-frying on high heat for 3-4 minutes until the snails are cooked through and glossy.
Garnish with green onion segments and serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Braised Chicken Feet with Celery (Jiao Zi)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken feet, cleaned and trimmed
instructions: Boil the chicken feet in water with ginger for 5 minutes to remove impurities, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a pot and stir-fry garlic, ginger, and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add the chicken feet and rock sugar, stir-frying until they turn golden brown.
Add celery, soy sauce, and water until the ingredients are covered.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 45 minutes until the feet are tender.
Season with salt and stir in sesame oil before serving.

title: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Deep fry the minced pork until crispy and set aside.
In a wok, heat oil and stir-fry the Doubanjiang until fragrant and red oil appears.
Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the doubanjiang water, sugar, and soy sauce, bring to a simmer.
Gently slide the tofu cubes into the sauce.
Simmer gently for 2 minutes without stirring too hard.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Top with the fried pork and sprinkle crushed Sichuan peppercorns.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 2 dried red chilies, cut into segments
1/2 cup green onions, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Mix chicken with cornstarch and a splash of soy sauce, let marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok and stir-fry chicken until cooked through, then remove.
Add more oil and stir-fry the dried chilies until slightly dark.
Add garlic, ginger, and Sichuan peppercorns, stir-fry until fragrant.
Return chicken to the wok and add soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar.
Toss quickly to coat the chicken evenly.
Add the green onions and peanuts, toss briefly to heat through.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Spicy Noodles with Ground Pork
instructions: Boil noodles according to package instructions and drain.
Heat a wok over high heat with chili oil.
Add ground pork and cook until browned and crispy.
Stir in Doubanjiang and garlic, cook until the oil turns red.
Add the cooked noodles and toss to coat thoroughly.
Sprinkle in bean sprouts and sesame oil.
Season with salt and crushed Sichuan peppercorns.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

title: Sichuan Boiled Fish
ingredients: 500g fish fillet (e.g., carp or sea bass), sliced thinly
1/4 cup dried chilies, soaked and cut
instructions: Marinate fish slices with cornstarch, soy sauce, and ginger.
Blanch the fish slices in boiling water for 30 seconds and remove.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, garlic, ginger, and scallions.
Place the fish and sauce mixture in a shallow bowl.
Heat oil until smoking hot, then pour over the bowl to sizzle.
Sprinkle with dried chilies and crushed Sichuan peppercorns.
Serve immediately.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
ingredients: 100g dried tofu skin, cut into strips
instructions: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a pot.
Add wood ear mushrooms, tofu skin, and ground pork; simmer for 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix vinegar, white pepper, soy sauce, sugar, and cornstarch slurry.
Pour the mixture into the boiling soup while stirring.
Slowly drizzle in the beaten egg to create ribbons.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot with chopped green onions on top.

title: Cantonese Braised Pork Belly (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, skin-on, cut into 3-inch blocks
instructions: Blanch the pork belly blocks in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the rock sugar until it melts and turns a deep amber color.
Add the blanched pork, ginger, star anise, and red dates; stir to coat evenly with the caramel.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine and water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the pork is tender but not falling apart.
Add soy sauce and white pepper, then increase heat slightly to reduce the sauce until it clings to the meat.

title: Shrimp and Dried Scallop Noodles (Gao Liang Si)
ingredients: 50g dried scallops, soaked in warm water for 2 hours
instructions: Soak the dried scallops in warm water for 2 hours until soft, then slice thinly.
Boil noodles in salted water for 3 minutes, drain, and toss with a little oil to prevent sticking.
Heat lard in a wok over high heat until smoking, then add garlic and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the prawns and stir-fry until they turn pink, then add the scallops.
Toss in the cooked noodles, soy sauce, salt, white pepper, and sesame oil.
Serve immediately topped with chopped green onions.

title: Steamed Sea Cucumber with Scallions
ingredients: 4 sea cucumbers, cleaned and cut into 3-inch segments
instructions: Scrub the sea cucumbers clean, cut into segments, and blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Mix soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch to make a glaze.
Arrange cucumber segments in a steamer basket lined with cabbage leaves.
Steam over high heat for 8 minutes until the cucumber is tender.
While steaming, heat vegetable oil in a small pan and sauté scallions until fragrant.
Pour the warm scallion oil over the steamed cucumber, then drizzle with the soy sauce glaze and sesame seeds.

title: Mapo Tofu (Guangdong Style)
instructions: Bring chicken stock to a simmer in a pot.
In a separate wok, fry ground pork with garlic and ginger until browned.
Add Doubanjiang and stir-fry until the oil turns red, then add the meat mixture.
Pour in the chicken stock, sugar, and crushed Sichuan peppercorns; simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently slide the tofu cubes into the sauce and simmer for 2 minutes without breaking.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken, then garnish with green onions.

title: Cantonese Egg Tarts (Dan Ta)
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and cold butter; rub together until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add ice water and knead briefly to form a smooth dough; wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a muffin tin with dough rounds.
Whisk milk, eggs, sugar, cornstarch, salt, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the custard mixture into the prepared tart shells until nearly full.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until the edges are golden and the centers are set.

title: Braised Pork Belly with Radish (Hong Shao Rou)
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into 3-inch blocks
1 large daikon radish, cut into chunks
instructions: Fry pork blocks in oil until deep golden brown, then remove.
Sauté ginger, garlic, cinnamon, and star anise in the same oil until fragrant.
Add pork back in, stir-frying to coat with spices.
Pour in soy sauces, rock sugar, and Shaoxing wine, scraping up browned bits.
Add radish chunks and enough water to just cover the meat.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until pork is tender and sauce thickens.
Remove spices, adjust salt if needed, and serve over rice.

title: Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Mian)
ingredients: 200 g green onions (scallions), separated into white and green parts
instructions: Boil noodles in salted water according to package instructions, then drain and rinse with cold water.
In a small pan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat until it smokes slightly.
Add crushed Sichuan peppercorns and stir-fry for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add white parts of scallions and garlic, frying until white parts turn golden.
Pour hot oil over the noodles in a large bowl to coat evenly.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil.
Toss in green scallion parts and serve immediately.

title: Stir-Fried Shrimp with Garlic and Scallion (Xiao Gui Xian)
ingredients: 300 g large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Marinate shrimp with 2 tablespoons of Shaoxing wine for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add shrimp and stir-fry quickly until they turn pink, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add remaining Shaoxing wine, rock sugar, soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Add garlic slices and green onions, stir-frying until fragrant and garlic turns light gold.
Return shrimp to the wok and toss to coat in sauce.
Pour in water and cornstarch slurry, stirring until sauce thickens.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion (Dong Po Yu)
instructions: Grease a large steaming pot with oil and line the bottom with ginger slices.
Place fish on the ginger, drizzle with a little Shaoxing wine.
In a separate bowl, mix rock sugar, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and water.
Pour the sauce mixture over the fish in the steamer.
Cover and steam over high heat for 15-18 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Remove from heat and pour remaining sauce over the top.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve.

title: Sichuan-Style Boiled Shrimp (Shui Zhu Xia)
ingredients: 500 g large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Deep fry Sichuan peppercorns in oil until dark brown and fragrant, then set aside.
In a pot, combine vinegar, rock sugar, water, soy sauce, salt, garlic, and ginger.
Bring the liquid to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Add the shrimp to the simmering broth and cook for 3-4 minutes until just opaque.
Remove shrimp with a slotted spoon and place in a serving bowl.
Pour the hot broth over the shrimp, being careful not to boil them further.
Sprinkle the fried peppercorns and green onions on top before serving.

title: Sauerbraten
instructions: Marinate beef in vinegar, wine, water, onions, carrots, bay leaf, and cloves for 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator.
Remove beef from marinade and discard solids; reserve liquid.
Sear beef in a Dutch oven until browned on all sides.
Add reserved marinade liquid and simmer until meat is tender, about 2 hours.
Mix cornstarch with beef broth and stir into the pot to thicken the sauce.
Serve with fried onions and dumplings.

title: Schnitzel
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry schnitzels until golden brown and crispy, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lemon juice and parsley.

title: Rösti
instructions: Squeeze excess moisture from grated potatoes using a clean kitchen towel.
Mix potatoes, flour, eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Pour potato mixture into the skillet and press down firmly to form a flat cake.
Cook until the bottom is golden and crispy, about 5 minutes.
Flip carefully, top with cheese, and cook until cheese melts and the top is browned.

title: Wiener Schnitzel mit Salat
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in beaten eggs, then coat with panko breadcrumbs.
Heat oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry schnitzels until golden brown and crispy, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper for the salad dressing.
Toss shredded lettuce with dressing and serve alongside tomato slices and schnitzel.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal, sliced thin against the grain
instructions: Sauté diced onion in butter until soft in a large skillet.
Add veal slices and cook until browned on all sides.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and stir to coat.
Stir in cognac and cook for 1 minute.
Add white wine and broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer until slightly reduced, then stir in heavy cream and sour cream.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve with spaetzle.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate beef in vinegar, wine, onions, garlic, bay leaves, salt, and pepper for 3 days in the refrigerator.
Remove meat from marinade and pat dry; dredge in flour.
Brown meat in a large pot with oil over medium-high heat.
Add carrots, sliced onions, and remaining marinade liquid to the pot.
Cover and simmer for 3 hours until meat is tender.
Stir in chopped pickles and beef broth.
Simmer for another 30 minutes until sauce thickens.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and white pepper.
Set up breading station: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon slices and parsley.

title: Fondue Savoyarde
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a fondue pot over low heat.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Mix cornstarch with water and stir into the pot.
Gradually add cheeses, stirring constantly until melted and smooth.
Slowly stir in white wine until fully incorporated.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Serve hot with sliced crusty bread for dipping.

title: Raclette
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender; drain.
In a saucepan, melt butter and heavy cream over low heat.
Add potatoes to the sauce and toss gently.
Season potato mixture with salt, pepper, and chives.
Warm raclette slices on a hot plate or grill.
Serve cheese alongside warm potatoes, ham, lettuce, and rye bread.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal sirloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onions in butter until translucent.
Sprinkle flour over onions and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add wine and broth, stirring to avoid lumps.
Add veal strips and mushrooms; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and simmer until sauce thickens.
Season with salt, pepper, and parsley.
Serve immediately over mashed potatoes or spaetzle.

title: German Schnitzel
ingredients: 2 cups breadcrumbs, mixed with grated Parmesan
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the pounded pork with salt and pepper on both sides.
Set up three shallow dishes with flour, beaten eggs, and the breadcrumb mixture.
Dredge each piece of pork in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, and finally coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Fry the schnitzel for about 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Austrian Tafelspitz
ingredients: 3 lbs beef top round roast, trimmed
instructions: Place the beef roast in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Add the onion, bay leaf, and parsley to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 2-3 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the cabbage, carrots, and potatoes during the last 45 minutes of cooking.
Season the broth with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the meat sliced with the vegetables and broth, accompanied by horseradish and bread.

title: Swiss Rösti
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and grated
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Grate the potatoes and squeeze them firmly in a clean kitchen towel to remove excess moisture.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the grated potatoes to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes start to brown and release their starch (about 10-15 minutes).
Stir in the flour and cook for another minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Remove from heat and let the mixture cool slightly.
Beat the eggs and heavy cream together, then stir into the potato mixture until well combined.
Return the skillet to medium heat, add the egg mixture, and spread it out evenly.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip carefully to cook the other side.
Garnish with chopped chives before serving.

title: German Spätzle
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Gradually add the flour to the wet ingredients, mixing until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Transfer the dough to a traditional spätzle press or a colander with holes.
Boil a large pot of salted water.
Squeeze the dough through the press into the boiling water.
Cook the spätzle for about 3-5 minutes until they float to the surface.
Drain immediately and return them to the pot.
Toss with melted butter and grated Gruyère cheese if using.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Austrian Apple Strudel
ingredients: 4 large apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, toss the sliced apples, raisins, cinnamon, sugar, and lemon juice together.
Brush a large baking sheet with melted butter.
Lay out the phyllo dough on a clean surface and brush with butter, covering with a damp cloth to prevent drying.
Place half the apple mixture in a line across the center of the dough.
Fold the sides of the dough over the filling and roll it up tightly into a log.
Place the strudel seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet and brush the top with more melted butter.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and crisp.
Let cool slightly, then dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Marinate beef in wine, vinegar, broth, onion, garlic, bay leaf, and cloves for 3-5 days in the refrigerator.
Remove beef from marinade and pat dry; discard solids from liquid.
Sear beef in batches in a Dutch oven until browned on all sides.
Add marinade liquid and mushrooms to the pot; bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 3-4 hours until meat is tender.
Whisk flour with butter to make a roux, then stir into the cooking liquid.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes until thickened, then season with salt and pepper.

title: Schnitzel Wiener Art
ingredients: 4 veal or pork cutlets, pounded thin
instructions: Season cutlets generously with salt and pepper.
Set up three stations: flour in a dish, eggs in a shallow bowl, and breadcrumbs in a plate.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry schnitzels for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon slices and lettuce.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal or pork tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Toss veal strips in flour, shaking off excess.
Sauté onion and mushrooms in butter until softened.
Add veal strips and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in wine and broth, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Simmer for 5 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Whisk in heavy cream and simmer for another 2 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and fresh parsley before serving.

title: Apfelstrudel
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix apples, sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice, raisins, and vanilla in a bowl.
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface until thin.
Spread apple mixture along one third of the pastry, leaving a border.
Roll pastry tightly around filling, sealing edges with water.
Place seam-side down on a baking sheet; brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat raclette grill according to manufacturer's instructions.
Place sliced cheese on the hot grill plate and melt until bubbly.
Scrape melted cheese over potatoes, lettuce, and bread.
Arrange pickled herring, red onion, and cornichons on the side.
Serve immediately while cheese is hot and melted.
Provide plates for guests to assemble their own portions.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate beef cubes in a mixture of red wine, vinegar, water, bay leaves, cloves, onions, carrots, sugar, salt, and pepper for at least 24 hours.
Remove meat from marinade, pat dry, and brown in a large pot with a little oil.
Return meat to the pot and add the remaining marinade liquid.
Simmer covered on low heat for 3 to 4 hours until meat is tender.
Remove meat and keep warm. Strain cooking liquid and skim fat.
Mix flour with a little cold water to make a slurry, then stir into the simmering liquid.
Add dried cherries and simmer for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.

title: Schweinebraten mit Knödeln
instructions: Season pork shoulder with salt and pepper.
Sear pork in a large roasting pan with butter until browned on all sides.
Remove pork and sauté onions and carrots in the same pan.
Return pork to the pan, add broth, wine, juniper berries, and bay leaf.
Cover and roast in the oven at 325°F (160°C) for about 3 hours.
Meanwhile, mix flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, and caraway seeds for the dumplings.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove pork, let it rest, then slice. Serve with dumplings and pan juices.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season veal slices with salt and white pepper.
Heat butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear veal slices quickly until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions until translucent.
Add wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in broth, cream, cornstarch mixed with a little water, and flour.
Bring to a simmer and cook until sauce thickens slightly.
Return veal to the pan and heat through for 2 minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 500 g apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss apples with sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and a pinch of salt.
Spread one sheet of pastry on a surface and brush with butter.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs over the pastry, then arrange apple mixture in a line.
Roll up the pastry tightly around the filling, sealing the edges.
Place seam-side down on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm.

title: Züricher Rösti
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Steam grated potatoes for 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid with a clean kitchen towel.
In a bowl, mix potatoes, onions, eggs, milk, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon portions of the mixture into the skillet and flatten into rounds.
Fry for 5 minutes on each side until golden and crispy.
Transfer to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chives.

title: Traditional German Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Set up three stations: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured cutlet into the beaten eggs, letting excess drip off.
Coat the egg-covered cutlet thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the schnitzel for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Austrian Tafelspitz
ingredients: 1 whole beef chuck roast, about 4-5 lbs
1 celery stalk, cut into large pieces
instructions: Place the beef chuck roast in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, skimming any foam that rises to the surface.
Reduce heat to low and add the peppercorns, bay leaf, and onion.
Simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is very tender.
Add the carrots, parsnips, and celery during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Add the cabbage quarters during the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Season the broth with salt to taste before serving.
Carve the meat against the grain and serve with the broth, vegetables, and mustard sauce.

title: Swiss Rösti
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes, peeled and grated
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onions using the coarse side of a grater.
Place the grated potatoes and onions in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out all excess liquid.
Transfer the dried mixture to a large bowl and season generously with salt and white pepper.
Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Form the potato mixture into a flat, even patty in the skillet.
Cook for 10-12 minutes per side, pressing down gently with a spatula, until deeply golden and crispy.
Flip once and cook until the bottom is very crisp, then remove from heat.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: German Sauerkraut
instructions: Finely shred the green cabbage by hand or with a food processor.
Place the shredded cabbage in a large bowl and sprinkle with coarse sea salt.
Add the caraway seeds and sugar to the bowl.
Massage the cabbage with your hands for 10 minutes until it releases its own juices and becomes limp.
Pack the cabbage tightly into a large non-reactive pot or crock.
Pour the water over the cabbage until it is almost completely submerged.
Add the bay leaf and mustard seeds if using.
Cover and let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 weeks, stirring daily to submerge the cabbage.
Once fermented, refrigerate to stop the process and serve.

title: Austrian Kaiserschmarrn
ingredients: 2 tablespoons butter, plus extra for greasing
Fresh strawberries or apple slices, for serving
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks, flour, milk, vanilla, salt, and 1/2 cup sugar together until smooth.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold the beaten egg whites gently into the batter.
Heat a large skillet with a generous amount of butter over medium heat.
Pour the batter into the skillet and cook without stirring for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is set.
Break the cake into large, irregular chunks using a wooden spoon.
Sprinkle the remaining sugar over the top and continue cooking, tossing and pulling the pieces apart until crispy edges form.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve immediately with fruit.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate beef in vinegar, wine, onion, carrots, bay leaves, and cloves for 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator.
Remove meat from marinade and pat dry; discard solids, save liquid.
Sear meat in a large pot with a little oil over medium-high heat until browned on all sides.
Add marinade liquid, brown sugar, flour, and broth to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours until tender.
Strain cooking liquid, skim fat, and thicken with a roux if desired before serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and white pepper.
Set up breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip into beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry schnitzel for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Fondue Bourguignonne
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Combine oil, wine, beef broth, and garlic in a fondue pot over a burner.
Heat mixture until simmering but not boiling vigorously.
Season broth with salt and white pepper.
Place pot over the heat source on the table.
Dip thin slices of beef into the hot broth for 1-2 minutes until cooked through.
Remove meat with tongs and serve immediately with bread cubes.

title: Raclette
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, then peel and slice.
Arrange cheese slices on the top of a raclette grill.
Heat cheese until the bottom side melts.
Scrape melted cheese onto plates.
Serve with boiled potatoes, pickled onions, cucumbers, cured meat, and mushrooms.
Guests can add extra toppings as desired.

title: Spätzle
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, milk, and salt in a large bowl until a smooth dough forms.
Knead briefly, then rest for 10 minutes.
Press dough through a spätzle maker or grate against a cheese grater into simmering water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and rinse briefly with cold water.
Toss cooked spätzle with melted butter, sour cream, and extra butter to prevent sticking.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into large cubes
1 lb onions, thinly sliced for serving
1 lb beef liver, sliced thin for serving
instructions: Combine beef, broth, vinegar, wine, onion, carrots, bay leaf, cloves, and thyme in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2.5 hours.
Remove meat and vegetables; strain the liquid.
Brown the meat slices in a separate pan.
Mix flour and sugar into the strained liquid and simmer until thickened.
Slice the meat against the grain and serve with browned onions and beef liver on the side.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip into beaten eggs, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet until hot but not smoking.
Fry cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels, squeeze lemon over the top, and garnish with parsley.

title: Schweizer Röstihähnli
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 3 lbs), cut into pieces
instructions: Sear chicken pieces in a large roasting pan with half the butter until golden.
Add potatoes, carrots, celery, and onion around the chicken.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour in chicken broth and white wine, then add thyme.
Cover and roast at 350°F (175°C) for 1 hour.
Remove cover, baste with pan juices, and roast another 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Bavarian White Sauce (Weißer Sauc)
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in warm milk, salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.
Continue whisking until the sauce thickens and bubbles, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice and sour cream.
Serve warm over dumplings or noodles.

title: Swiss Fondue
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with garlic.
Melt butter in the pot over low heat.
Add white wine, salt, and pepper; bring to a simmer.
Stir in cornstarch and cook for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Gradually add grated cheeses, stirring constantly until melted and smooth.
Heat through gently without boiling.
Serve with kirsch for flambéing if desired, alongside baguette slices.

title: Schweinshaxe
instructions: Rub the pork knuckle generously with salt and caraway seeds.
Place the knuckle in a large pot with water and lemon halves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours until tender.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Remove the knuckle, pat dry, and roast on a rack for 45 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden.

title: Sachertorte
instructions: Beat egg yolks and powdered sugar until pale and creamy.
Fold in the softened butter and half of the melted chocolate.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form, then fold gently into the batter.
Pour batter into a lined 22cm cake tin and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 40-45 minutes.
While cake cools, spread half the apricot jam over the top.
Whisk remaining chocolate with butter and spread over the jam.
Chill until firm, then glaze with remaining jam.

title: Raclette
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, drain, and cut in half.
Preheat the raclette grill or stove-top pan.
Place a slice of cheese on each potato half or on a hot plate.
Heat the cheese until it melts and bubbles.
Serve immediately with ham, pickled onions, and a pat of butter on the side.
Garnish with fresh parsley before eating.

title: Tiroler Kaiserschmarrn
instructions: Whisk egg whites until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, mix yolks, flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
Fold the egg whites gently into the flour mixture.
Heat butter in an oiled skillet over medium heat.
Pour batter into the skillet and cook until golden on the bottom.
Remove from heat, cut the cake into small pieces with a fork, and toss to coat in butter.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm with raspberries.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500g veal or pork tenderloin, sliced thinly
instructions: Coat the sliced meat in flour and set aside.
Sauté onions in butter until soft and translucent.
Add the mushrooms and cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in the flour-coated meat and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in wine and broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Simmer until the meat is cooked through.
Stir in heavy cream and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve with Spätzle.

title: Sauerbraten
instructions: Combine vinegar, broth, onions, carrots, beer, juniper berries, and bay leaf in a large pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
Strain the liquid and reserve it; discard solids.
Toss beef cubes with flour and fry until browned on all sides.
Return beef and strained liquid to the pot; simmer for 3-4 hours until tender.
Strain the cooking liquid and reduce to make a sauce.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 kg pork tenderloin or veal cutlets
Potato salad or fries for sides
instructions: Pound cutlets to an even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500 g veal fillet or pork loin, thinly sliced
Fried potatoes or spaetzle for serving
instructions: Sauté sliced onions in butter until soft and translucent.
Add veal slices and cook for 3-4 minutes until browned.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and stir to coat.
Pour in wine and broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in sour cream and capers; heat gently without boiling.
Garnish with parsley and serve with fried potatoes or spaetzle.

title: Raclette
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, then drain.
Preheat the raclette grill or melt cheese in a frying pan.
Arrange potatoes, ham, gherkins, and bread on a serving board.
Grill the cheese until bubbly and golden.
Serve by scraping the melted cheese over the potatoes and ham.
Add mustard and chives to taste.

title: Schweizer Käsespätzle
ingredients: 400 g cheese spätzle or homemade spätzle
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Sauté onions in butter until soft, then add sliced sausage and cook until browned.
Mix grated cheeses, sour cream, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Add cooked spätzle to the cheese mixture and toss well.
Transfer to a greased baking dish and spread evenly.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chives before serving.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
1 lb onions, thinly sliced for serving
instructions: Marinate the beef in vinegar, wine, onion, carrots, bay leaves, cloves, sugar, and salt for at least 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Remove meat from marinade, pat dry, and dredge lightly in flour.
Brown the beef in a large pot with a little oil over medium-high heat.
Add the remaining marinade liquid, beer, broth, and bay leaves to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3 hours until tender.
Strain the cooking liquid, reserve the meat, and skim fat from the liquid.
Whisk flour into the reserved liquid to thicken, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Sauté the sliced onions until golden brown.
Slice the beef and serve with the onion gravy, onions, and raisins.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour seasoned with salt and pepper, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each veal cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the floured cutlet into the egg wash, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Fry the schnitzel for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove from oil and drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal scallopini or thin beef slices, cut into strips
salt and white pepper to taste
6 slices French bread or spaetzle for serving
instructions: Toss the meat strips in flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onions until translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat and add the floured meat, cooking quickly for 2-3 minutes until browned.
Stir in wine and broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce reduces by half.
Stir in heavy cream, capers, and parsley.
Simmer for another 2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve hot over French bread or spaetzle.

title: Züricher Röstigrütze
instructions: Combine oats, milk, and cream in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat and stir in sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Fold in walnuts and raisins.
Top each serving with a pat of butter.
Serve warm.

title: Schweizer Käsespätzle
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl to form a thick batter; rest for 30 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Drop small spoonfuls of batter into the boiling water and cook for 2-3 minutes until they float.
Drain the spätzle and return them to the pot.
Melt butter in a large skillet and sauté onions until soft and golden.
Add the grated cheeses to the skillet and stir until melted.
Mix the cooked spätzle into the cheese sauce.
Stir in sour cream and caraway seeds.
Serve immediately.

title: Schweinebraten mit Knödeln
instructions: Season pork with flour, salt, and pepper.
Sear pork in oil in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Remove pork and sauté onions until soft.
Return pork to pot, add broth, and simmer covered for 2.5 hours.
Mix potatoes, eggs, flour, and salt for dumplings.
Form into balls and drop into simmering pork broth.
Let dumplings cook for 15 minutes until fluffy.
Serve pork with gravy, dumplings, and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season flour with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Spätzle
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Press dough through a spätzle press or colander into boiling salted water.
Cook until they float to the surface, about 2 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain.
Toss with melted butter and grated cheese if desired.
Serve hot as a side dish.

title: Fondue Savoyarde
instructions: Melt butter in a heavy fondue pot over low heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add milk while whisking continuously.
Bring to a simmer and cook until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in both cheeses until melted.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Serve immediately with bread for dipping.
Add extra cheese and milk if the fondue becomes too thick.

title: Rösti
instructions: Squeeze excess moisture from grated potatoes using a clean towel.
Mix potatoes, milk, salt, eggs, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spread potato mixture evenly in the skillet.
Cook without touching for 10 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for another 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with chives before serving.
Serve hot with sour cream or Swiss cheese.

title: Schweizer Röstihähnli
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat butter in a large roasting pan over medium heat.
Sauté chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides.
Add potatoes, carrots, onions, and garlic to the pan.
Season everything with salt and pepper.
Pour in enough chicken stock to cover the bottom of the pan.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil, sprinkle grated raclette cheese over the top, and bake for another 15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Tiroler Kaiserschmarren
ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, plus more for greasing the pan
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°F (95°C) and grease a baking sheet.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, salt, and vanilla until pale and creamy.
Stir in flour and milk until smooth.
In a separate bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the egg whites into the yolk mixture.
Heat a large non-stick skillet with a little butter over medium heat.
Pour the batter into the skillet and spread it out thinly.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until edges are set and golden, flipping once.
Cook until the top looks dry but still soft, then remove from heat.
Fold the pancake into a fluffy mound, transfer to the baking sheet, and keep warm in the oven.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve immediately with strawberries.

title: Schnitzel Wiener Art
ingredients: 1/2 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
Salt and white pepper to taste
Potato salad or parsley salad for sides
instructions: Season the pork cutlets on both sides with salt and white pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the cutlet into the egg mixture, letting excess drip off.
Coat the cutlet thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the schnitzel for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove from heat and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and your choice of side salad.

title: Bavarian Weisswurst
ingredients: White bread or pretzels for serving
instructions: Boil a pot of water and add the warm chicken broth.
Gently place the Weisswurst into the warm liquid; do not boil or the sausages will burst.
Poach the sausages for about 10-12 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Remove sausages carefully with a slotted spoon and let them rest for a few minutes.
Slice the sausages horizontally.
Arrange the sliced sausages on a plate with lemon slices and fresh parsley.
Serve immediately with mustard and white bread or pretzels.

title: Österreichische Tafelspitz
ingredients: 1 whole beef top round (Tafelspitz), about 2.5 kg
2 celery stalks, cut into large chunks
Boiled potatoes or applesauce for sides
instructions: Rinse the beef under cold water and pat dry.
Place the beef in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Add the onion, carrots, celery, broth, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low.
Skim off any foam that rises to the surface during the first 10 minutes.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for about 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
Remove the meat from the pot and let it rest for 10-15 minutes.
Carve the meat against the grain into thick slices.
Serve the meat slices with the boiled vegetables, lemon wedge, capers, horseradish sauce, and potatoes or applesauce.

title: Sauerbraten
instructions: Marinate beef in vinegar, broth, sugar, onions, wine, bay leaf, and caraway seeds for 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator.
Remove meat from marinade and pat dry.
Sear beef in hot oil until browned on all sides.
Strain marinade and combine with beef, flour, and additional broth.
Simmer covered in a slow cooker or oven at 325°F for 3 to 4 hours until tender.
Reduce remaining cooking liquid to make a gravy.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and bread crumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, then egg, then bread crumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Raclette
instructions: Melt sliced raclette cheese on a hot raclette grill or in an oven-safe dish under a broiler.
Scrape melted cheese over boiled potatoes, mushrooms, and onions.
In a separate pan, sauté mushrooms and onions in butter until tender.
Reduce white wine and cream in a saucepan until slightly thickened.
Serve hot potatoes and cheese with the mushroom sauce on the side.
Garnish with fresh chives before serving.

title: Apfelstrudel
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Toss apple slices with sugar, cinnamon, flour, vanilla, lemon juice, and melted butter.
Lay out phyllo sheets on a baking sheet, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread apple mixture down the center of the phyllo.
Fold sides of phyllo over filling and roll up tightly.
Brush top with beaten egg and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Chocoflan
instructions: Whisk eggs, sugar, butter, milk, and vanilla together until smooth for the flan base.
Pour flan mixture into a greased baking dish and set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix chocolate cake mix, water, oil, and baking powder in a bowl.
Pour batter over the flan mixture in the baking dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool completely before unmolding to reveal the chocolate cake and caramel flan.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 2 lb beef roast, cut into large cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Marinate the beef in vinegar, wine, onion, carrots, bay leaves, and cloves for at least 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Remove meat from marinade and pat dry; season with salt, pepper, and flour.
Brown the meat in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the marinade liquid, broth, tomato paste, and brown sugar to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3 to 4 hours until meat is tender.
Remove meat and skim fat from the sauce.
Strain the sauce and simmer until slightly thickened.
Slice the meat and serve with sauce, potatoes, and red cabbage.

title: Schnitzel Wiener Art
ingredients: 4 veal cutlets or pork chops, pounded thin
Potato salad or parsley salad for sides
instructions: Season the flour with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Set up three shallow dishes with the seasoned flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, then dip in egg, and finally coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry schnitzels for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oil and drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and a side salad.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season the veal strips with salt and white pepper.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat and sauté the veal until lightly browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the onions until translucent.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the wine and broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cream and mustard until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened.
Return the veal to the pan and heat through for 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve hot over egg noodles or with sautéed mushrooms.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 6 large apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, toss sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and walnuts.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface into a large rectangle.
Spread apricot jam over the pastry to create a seal.
Place the apple mixture in a line along the long edge of the pastry.
Roll the pastry tightly around the filling, sealing the edges with water.
Place seam-side down on a baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving warm.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat the raclette grill or broiler to medium-high heat.
Arrange sliced potatoes, lettuce, chives, tomatoes, and onions on individual serving plates.
Place slices of raclette cheese directly on the hot grill or under the broiler.
Melt the cheese until bubbly and golden.
Scrape the melted cheese over the potatoes and vegetables.
Top with a small amount of butter and breadcrumbs if desired.
Serve immediately while the cheese is still warm and gooey.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1 lb sourdough bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Combine vinegar, broth, cherries, onion, beer, bay leaves, and caraway seeds in a large pot.
Add beef cubes to the liquid and let marinate in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days.
Remove meat from the marinade, reserving the liquid, and pat dry.
Sear the beef cubes in a Dutch oven until browned on all sides.
Pour the reserved marinade over the beef, add brown sugar, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove meat and skim fat from the sauce.
Add torn bread to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken.
Slice the meat and serve with the sauce.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs on three separate plates.
Season veal cutlets with salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the flour-coated cutlet into the beaten eggs.
Coat the wet cutlet thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry schnitzels for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and immediately sprinkle with parsley.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and melted butter.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 lb veal, cut into thin strips
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Toss veal strips with flour, shaking off excess.
Melt butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook veal strips until browned and no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Remove veal from skillet and set aside.
Add onion to the skillet and sauté until translucent.
Stir in white wine and chicken broth, scraping up browned bits.
Bring liquid to a simmer and return veal to the pan.
Whisk cornstarch with cold water until smooth.
Stir the cornstarch mixture into the sauce along with heavy cream.
Simmer until the sauce thickens, then season with salt and white pepper.
Garnish with chives and serve with spaetzle or noodles.

title: Chorwurst with Sauerkraut
ingredients: Boiled potatoes or bread for serving
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add sausages.
Boil sausages for 10 minutes until cooked through.
Remove sausages, drain, and slice into coins.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté diced onion until soft and translucent.
Add sauerkraut, apple cider vinegar, caraway seeds, and salt to the skillet.
Cook the sauerkraut mixture for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add sliced sausage coins to the skillet and mix well.
Heat for another 3-5 minutes to combine flavors.
Serve hot with mustard sauce and boiled potatoes or bread.

title: Fondue au Gratin
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with garlic cloves.
Combine grated Gruyère and Emmental cheese in a bowl.
Whisk wine, kirsch, cornstarch, and cold water together in a jug.
Pour the cheese mixture into the warm fondue pot.
Gradually pour in the wine mixture while whisking constantly.
Stir over low heat until the cheese melts and the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped chives.
Serve immediately with thick slices of rustic bread for dipping.

title: Zopf (Swiss Braided Bread)
ingredients: 1 kg all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, salt, sugar, eggs, and softened butter in a large bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down dough and divide into two equal parts.
Braid the two parts together in a traditional pattern.
Place on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 30 minutes.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Schweinshaxe (Roasted Pork Knuckle)
ingredients: 2 bone-in pork knuckles, about 1.5 kg each
500 g pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon lard or rendered pork fat
instructions: Simmer pork knuckles in water with salt and caraway seeds for 2 hours until tender.
Remove knuckles, drain, and place them skin-side down in a roasting pan.
Add pork shoulder, onions, and potatoes around the knuckle.
Roast at 200°C (400°F) for 1 hour.
Flip the knuckle skin-side up and brush generously with lard.
Roast for another 45-60 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Spätzle (Swabian Dumplings)
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Beat eggs and milk together, then pour into the dry ingredients.
Stir until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not knead.
Grease a large pot or skillet with butter.
Press the dough through a spätzle press directly into boiling salted water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and toss immediately with melted butter.

title: Obazda (Bavarian Cheese Spread)
ingredients: 200 g fresh quark cheese (or fresh farmer's cheese)
100 g fresh mozzarella or mild white cheese, crumbled
instructions: Combine quark, crumbled mozzarella, sour cream, and fresh cream in a bowl.
Whisk vigorously until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
Season with salt, white pepper, and half of the chopped chives.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to let flavors meld.
Serve cold on slices of warm crusty bread.
Garnish with remaining chives just before serving.

title: Leberkase (Bavarian Liver Spread)
instructions: Dice the livers into small cubes and brown them in a heavy pot with a little fat.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Pour in the beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, for about 1 hour until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and let cool completely.
Press the cooled mixture into a loaf pan or container.
Refrigerate for several hours until firm, then slice and serve with mustard.

title: Maultaschen (Swabian Ravioli)
instructions: Mix flour and eggs to make a smooth pasta dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground meats, onion, spinach, cheese, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Roll the dough thin and cut into squares.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Fold into a half-moon shape and seal edges by pressing with a fork.
Drop into a large pot of boiling salted water.
Cook for 10-12 minutes until they float, then drain.
Toss with melted butter and serve with a creamy sauce or gravy.

title: Eierkrem (Egg Cream)
instructions: Heat milk with vanilla bean and sugar in a saucepan until warm.
Whisk eggs with cornstarch and salt in a separate bowl.
Slowly pour warm milk into egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring until thickened.
Strain into a bowl and chill before serving.

title: Berliner Zwiebel (Onion Soup)
instructions: Sauté onions in butter until golden brown and caramelized.
Add sugar and cook for another minute to deepen flavor.
Pour in beef broth and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in sour cream and heat through gently.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Käsespätzle (Cheese Noodles)
instructions: Cook spätzle in boiling salted water until tender, then drain.
Sauté onion in butter until soft and slightly browned.
Add cheeses to onions and melt together over low heat.
Toss cooked spätzle with cheese mixture.
Top with sour cream and a splash of vinegar before serving.

title: Rote Grütze (Red Berry Compote)
instructions: Combine berries, sugar, cinnamon stick, and water in a pot.
Simmer gently until berries are soft and juices are released.
Add cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water to thicken.
Cook until mixture coats the back of a spoon.
Remove cinnamon stick and stir in vanilla before cooling.

title: Kartoffelsalat mit Eisbergsalat (Potato Salad)
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then rinse with cold water.
Whisk vinegar, sugar, mayonnaise, sour cream, onion, salt, and pepper.
Mix warm potatoes with dressing and let cool slightly.
Fold in sliced eggs, carrots, and chives gently.
Chill before serving to let flavors meld.

title: Sauerbraten mit Rotkohl und Knödeln
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into large cubes
instructions: Marinate the beef in wine, broth, onions, garlic, bay leaves, caraway, and juniper for at least 24 hours.
Remove meat and reserve marinade; brown the beef in a pot with fat.
Add the reserved marinade to the pot and simmer until the meat is tender.
In a separate pan, cook the red cabbage with vinegar until soft.
Mix potatoes, eggs, and flour to form a dough, then shape into balls and boil until cooked.
Serve the braised meat with the cabbage and dumplings.

title: Kartoffelpuffer mit Apfelmus
instructions: Squeeze excess moisture from the grated potatoes using a clean cloth.
Mix potatoes, onion, eggs, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture into the pan and fry until golden brown on both sides.
In a small bowl, combine apple sauce, cinnamon, and brown sugar.
Serve the hot potato pancakes with the warm apple mixture.

title: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte
ingredients: 1 cup sour cherries, pitted and halved
instructions: Whip egg whites with half the sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold in the remaining sugar, flour, and kirsch gently.
Bake the batter in a springform pan at 175°C until golden and firm.
Allow the cake to cool, then cut it horizontally into three layers.
Spread whipped cream mixed with vanilla between the layers and on top.
Arrange sour cherries over the cream and pour melted chocolate over the top.
Decorate with chocolate shavings and let set in the fridge.

title: Rheinhessen Rouladen
instructions: Season beef slices with salt, pepper, and mustard, then roll them with bacon, onions, pickles, and kirsch inside.
Sear the rolled beef in a pot with a little oil until browned on all sides.
Sprinkle flour over the seared meat and stir to coat.
Add onions, beef broth, and bay leaf, then cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Strain the sauce and serve the rouladen with the thickened gravy.

title: Linsen mit Speck und Sauerkraut
instructions: Rinse the split peas and soak them overnight.
Fry the diced bacon and onions in a pot until crispy.
Add the soaked peas, broth, sauerkraut, bay leaf, and caraway seeds.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours until peas are soft.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and serve hot.

title: Maultaschen
instructions: Mix the ground pork, spinach, breadcrumbs, and eggs in a bowl until well combined.
Cut the pasta sheets into squares large enough to enclose the filling.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square, fold into a half-moon shape, and seal the edges.
Boil a large pot of salted water and cook the Maultaschen for 8-10 minutes until they float.
In a separate saucepan, melt the butter and add the chicken broth to create a rich sauce.
Serve the Maultaschen in the butter broth, optionally garnished with parsley.

title: Spätzle
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, and baking powder.
Gradually add the flour while mixing until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Wet your Spätzle press and scrape the dough through it directly into a pot of boiling salted water.
Cook for about 3 minutes until the Spätzle float to the surface.
Drain immediately and toss with melted butter to prevent sticking.
Serve warm with the cream sauce and fried onions.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the beef in a large bowl and cover with the vinegar, wine, onion, carrots, bay leaves, and bouquet garni.
Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 days, turning the meat daily.
Remove the meat and brown it in a large pot with a little oil over medium heat.
Add the marinating liquid, the dried sour cherries, beer, and some of the onions and carrots to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Strain the cooking liquid, skim off the fat, and reduce it slightly to make a glaze for the roast.

title: Kässpätzle
instructions: Cook the dried Spätzle according to package directions and drain well.
In a large pan, melt the butter over medium heat and sauté the onion and bacon until golden.
Stir in the cooked Spätzle to coat them with the onion and bacon mixture.
Reduce heat to low and sprinkle the Gruyère and Emmental cheese over the pasta.
Pour in the heavy cream and stir gently until the cheese melts and the dish is creamy.
Season with nutmeg and serve immediately.

title: Zwiebelkuchen
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl, then add the yeast mixture and softened butter to form a dough.
Knead the dough until smooth, let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a baking pan.
Layer half the onions and apples on the bottom of the pan, then roll out the dough and place it over the fruit.
Cover with the remaining onions and apples, dot with butter, and bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
ingredients: 400g pork lard or vegetable oil for frying
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Season the veal cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Set up three stations: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs mixed with flour.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the cutlet into the beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in the breadcrumb mixture.
Heat the oil in a large skillet until smoking hot.
Fry the schnitzel for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges and potato salad.

title: Käseknödel
instructions: Whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the breadcrumbs, shredded cheese, yolks, milk, flour, salt, and pepper.
Mix the breadcrumb mixture gently into the stiff egg whites using a large spoon, being careful not to deflate the whites.
Moisten your hands with cold water and shape the mixture into smooth, round balls about the size of a golf ball.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
Drop the dumplings into the water one by one.
Cook for about 10 minutes until they float to the surface.
Serve hot with a rich beef broth (Brühe) and a pat of butter.

title: Apfelstrudel
ingredients: 6-8 Granny Smith apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Toss the sliced apples with lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla sugar.
Spread the breadcrumbs evenly over one half of each puff pastry sheet.
Arrange the apple mixture in a single layer over the breadcrumbs, leaving a border.
Brush the border with melted butter, then roll the pastry tightly into a log.
Place the strudel seam-side down on a baking sheet and brush the top with melted butter.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream.

title: Fleischtopf
instructions: Season the meat cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Brown the meat in a large heavy pot with a little oil until sealed on all sides.
Remove the meat and sauté the onions, carrots, and celery in the same pot until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for another minute.
Return the meat to the pot and add the broth, water, bouquet garni, and potatoes.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender and falling apart.
Remove the bouquet garni before serving.

title: Zwetschgendatschi
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place the plums in a bowl, toss with sugar and cinnamon, and let sit for 15 minutes.
Spread the flour over one half of each puff pastry sheet and dot with butter.
Arrange the plums on the pastry, cut side up, leaving a border.
Roll the pastry around the plums, tucking the ends underneath to seal.
Place the rolls on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and score a pattern on top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden and puffed.
Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

title: Tyrolean Knödel with Meat Sauce
ingredients: 500g potatoes, peeled and boiled until soft
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes with a fork until smooth but not puréed.
Mix in the eggs, flour, and warm milk to form a stiff dough.
Knead briefly, shape into large balls, and boil in salted water for 15 minutes.
Fry the diced pork fat in a heavy pan until golden.
Add the minced beef and onions, cooking until the meat is browned and onions are soft.
Pour in the beef broth, season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper, and simmer for 2 hours until thick.
Serve the boiled Knödel topped generously with the meat sauce.

title: Käsespätzle with Apples
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, milk, and salt to create a thin batter.
Cut noodles from the batter using a traditional spätzle board or press.
Boil the noodles in salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Sauté the apple and onion slices in half the melted butter until golden.
Toss the warm noodles with the cheese and sautéed apples.
Pour the remaining melted butter over the mixture and stir well.
Sprinkle with caraway seeds and serve immediately.

title: Speck und Äpfel (Bacon and Apples)
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in a large pan until crispy and the fat is rendered.
Add the sliced onions and cook until translucent.
Toss in the apple slices and fry for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of cinnamon.
Drizzle with a little butter and stir to coat.
Remove from heat, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve warm.

title: Obatzda with Rye Bread
instructions: Cut the Camembert into cubes and place in a bowl.
Add the softened butter, cream cheese, salt, cayenne, nutmeg, and paprika.
Mix everything together until smooth and creamy.
Fold in the grated onion gently.
Serve immediately with thick slices of toasted rye bread.

title: Kaiserschmarrn with Apple Compote
instructions: Whisk egg whites until stiff peaks form and set aside.
Beat yolks with flour, milk, salt, and sugar to make a smooth batter.
Fold the egg whites into the batter gently.
Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Pour batter in three batches, cooking until browned on the bottom, then tear into large chunks with a spatula.
Cook until puffed and lightly charred, dusting with powdered sugar.
Meanwhile, sauté apples with sugar and cinnamon until soft for the compote.
Serve the Kaiserschmarrn warm alongside the apple compote.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 1 kg veal fillet, cut into small cubes
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with cold water
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season the veal cubes with salt and white pepper.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and brown the meat quickly on all sides.
Remove the meat and set aside; sauté the mushrooms in the same pan until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and cook for 1 minute to remove the raw taste.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the beef broth and bring to a simmer.
Return the meat to the pan and cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Add capers and chopped chives, taste, and serve hot with Rösti.

title: Chnigen
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix flour, salt, and the foamy milk mixture into a soft dough.
Knead in the melted butter and the beaten egg until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into small squares.
Place a small amount of chocolate and walnuts in the center of each square.
Fold the corners over the filling to form a diamond shape.
Let the Chnigen rise again for 30 minutes.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown and drain on paper towels.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Raclette
instructions: Preheat the raclette grill or stove top until the heating element is hot.
Melt a knob of butter on the grill plate.
Place the cheese slices directly on the hot plate.
Melt the bacon in a separate pan until crispy, then set aside.
Arrange the boiled potatoes, pickled onions, and cucumbers on warm plates.
Grill the cheese until the top side is bubbly and slightly browned.
Scrape the melted cheese onto the potatoes and vegetables.
Top with crispy bacon, a pinch of black pepper, and chopped chives.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Appenzeller Käsespätzle
instructions: Make a well in the flour, add eggs, and knead into a smooth dough.
Roll the dough thin and cut into small strips using a spätzle press or knife.
Boil the spätzle in salted water until they float, then drain.
In a large pan, melt butter and fry the diced onions until translucent.
Add the boiled potatoes and bacon to the onions.
Toss the spätzle into the pan and mix well.
Stir in the grated Appenzeller cheese and let it melt over low heat.
Season with salt and oregano.
Remove from heat, top with crushed walnuts, and serve.

title: Swabian Apple Strudel
ingredients: 500 g apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss apple slices with lemon juice, sugar, raisins, and the cinnamon stick.
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter.
Lay out the phyllo sheets, brushing each layer with butter as you go.
Spread the apple mixture in a line across the center of the pastry.
Roll the pastry tightly around the filling.
Place the strudel seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Brush the top with more melted butter and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly, remove the cinnamon stick, and serve warm with vanilla custard.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500g veal loin, sliced thinly against the grain
salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the sliced veal and cook until browned on both sides.
Pour in the white wine and simmer until the sauce reduces slightly.
Stir in the sour cream, capers, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Simmer gently for 2 minutes without boiling the cream.
Serve immediately over boiled potatoes or spaetzle.

title: Schweizer Röstihähnli
instructions: Pat the chicken pieces dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the lard or butter in a large skillet until smoking hot.
Sear the chicken pieces skin-side down until deeply golden brown.
Flip the pieces and cook until no longer pink inside.
Remove chicken and set aside; add onions to the pan and cook until browned.
Return chicken to the pan, spoon the onion juices over it.
Garnish with chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

title: Züricher Bratwurst mit Senf
instructions: Place the sausages in a large pot with the sliced onion, water, caraway seeds, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Uncover, increase heat, and fry until the liquid evaporates and the sausages are browned.
Serve the sausages on plates topped with the caramelized onions.
Accompany with plenty of yellow mustard and fresh parsley.

title: Gnöchi mit Fleischsoße
instructions: Melt butter in a pot and sauté the onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add the ground beef and pork, cooking until browned.
Stir in the tomato paste, broth, and milk; simmer for 10 minutes.
Season the sauce with nutmeg, salt, and a pinch of basil.
Boil the gnocchi in salted water until they float to the surface.
Drain the gnocchi and toss them gently in the meat sauce.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil leaves.

title: Bündner Nudelsalat
instructions: Cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water according to package directions.
Drain the noodles and rinse with cold water to stop cooking.
In a large bowl, mix mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Add the drained noodles, cheese, sunflower seeds, almonds, cranberries, and raisins to the dressing.
Toss gently until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Serve cold as a hearty lunch or side dish.

title: Schweinshaxe
instructions: Score the skin of the pork knuckle deeply with a sharp knife.
Rub the knuckle generously with coarse salt and let it sit for 2 hours.
Place the knuckle in a large pot with water, stock, caraway seeds, onion, celery, and lemon.
Simmer gently on low heat for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the knuckle and let it cool slightly, then dry the skin thoroughly.
Roast in a very hot oven (250°C/480°F) for 30-40 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.

title: Obatzda
ingredients: 500 g camembert or brie, softened to room temperature
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Cut the softened camembert into chunks and place in a mixing bowl.
Mash the cheese with a fork until it becomes a coarse crumble.
Add the softened butter, cream cheese, lemon juice, crushed garlic, and paprika.
Mix vigorously with a wooden spoon or fork until a smooth, creamy consistency forms.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Spread onto a serving plate or bread slices and serve immediately with pretzels or bread.

title: Käsespätzle
ingredients: 300 g fresh goat cheese (Alpkäse) or Emmental, cubed
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the Spätzle in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain the Spätzle and toss with a little butter to prevent sticking.
In a large skillet, melt half the butter and sauté the sliced onions until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the heavy cream to make a sauce.
