Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes, then stir in the cubed cheese until melted and gooey.
Add the cooked Spätzle to the cheese sauce, season with salt, pepper, and caraway seeds, and toss to coat.

title: Sauerkraut mit Bratwurst
instructions: Fry the onions in pork fat until golden and soft.
Add the sauerkraut, sliced apples, bay leaf, and caraway seeds to the pan.
Stir in the flour to coat the vegetables, then pour in the pork stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the kraut is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Meanwhile, pan-fry the bratwurst in a separate skillet until browned and cooked through.
Slice the bratwurst and serve on top of the sauerkraut.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef chuck or round, cut into large cubes
1 cup dried sour cherries or applesauce
instructions: Place the beef cubes in a large bowl, cover with red wine, and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning daily.
Remove the meat from the marinade, pat dry, and sear in a heavy pot until browned on all sides.
Add the stock, onion, carrots, bay leaves, cloves, juniper berries, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is very tender.
Remove the meat and keep warm. Strain the cooking liquid and return it to the pot.
Stir in the dried sour cherries and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Slice the meat and serve with the rich gravy.

title: Berliner Kartoffelklöße
instructions: Steam the waxy potatoes until very soft, then mash them with a fork, keeping some lumps.
Steam the russet potatoes until soft, then mash them completely smooth.
Mix the smooth mashed potatoes with the breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper.
Gradually add the beaten eggs and the lumpy mashed potatoes, mixing until a dough forms.
Shape the dough into small, smooth rolls or balls.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 10-12 minutes until they float to the surface.
Serve hot with a gravy or roast pork.

title: Käsekrainer with Sauerkraut
instructions: Heat the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until translucent.
Stir in the caraway seeds and cook for another minute.
Add the rinsed sauerkraut and cook for 5 minutes.
Place the cheese-filled sausages on top of the sauerkraut.
Cover the pot and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the sausages are heated through and the cheese has melted.
Season with salt and serve immediately.

title: Sauerbraten with Gschmürz
instructions: Rub the beef roast with salt and pepper and let it sit in the fridge for 24 hours.
Place the roast in a large pot and cover with water; bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Add the wine, vinegar, broth, onions, carrots, garlic, bay leaves, and juniper berries.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 3-4 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and set aside to rest.
Strain the cooking liquid and skim off excess fat.
Simmer the liquid until it reduces to a thick gravy, then pour over the sliced meat.
Serve with spaetzle or dumplings.

title: Bergkäse mit Kartoffeln
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the cubed potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot.
Add the butter and milk to the hot potatoes and stir until the butter melts.
Remove from heat and stir in the grated Alpine cheese until melted.
Fold in the whipped fresh curd cheese gently to maintain its airy texture.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Serve warm, garnished with chopped chives.

title: Linsensuppe mit Speck
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in a large pot until crispy, then remove most of the grease.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and sauté until softened.
Stir in the rinsed lentils, broth, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 45-60 minutes until lentils are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, topped with fresh parsley and a sprinkle of fried bacon bits.

title: Kässpätzle
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and salt in a bowl until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough briefly and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough into a long rope and cut into small pieces into boiling salted water.
Cook for 8 minutes until they float to the surface.
Drain the spätzle and return them to the pot.
Stir in melted butter, cheeses, cream, and pepper until creamy and hot.

title: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Marinate the beef in vinegar, wine, spices, and vegetables for 2-3 days in the fridge.
Remove meat from marinade, pat dry, and sear in a large pot with oil until browned.
Add the remaining marinade liquid, broth, and fresh vegetables to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 3-4 hours until the meat is tender.
Strain the cooking liquid and reserve the meat.
Reduce the liquid in a separate pan, adding bread crumbs, sugar, and ketchup to thicken into a sauce.
Slice the meat and serve with the sauce.

title: Eisbein mit Sauerkraut
ingredients: 1 tbsp apple juice or apple vinegar
instructions: Score the skin of the pork knuckle and rub with salt and pepper.
Boil the knuckle in water with bay leaves, garlic, and caraway seeds for 1 hour.
Reduce heat and simmer gently for another 2 hours until the meat is fork-tender.
In a separate pan, fry the shredded red cabbage in lard until wilted and slightly browned.
Stir in the drained sauerkraut and apple juice to the cabbage.
Remove the knuckle from the bone, slice it, and serve with the cabbage.

title: Lorcher Wurstsuppe
instructions: Sauté the onion and carrots in a pot until translucent.
Add the diced potatoes and broth, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in the flour mixed with a little cold water to thicken slightly.
Add the sliced sausages and boiled pork to the pot.
Pour in the white wine and add caraway seeds.
Simmer for another 10 minutes until flavors meld.
Season with salt and pepper, then garnish with chives.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Combine flour, eggs, and salt to form a smooth dough, then rest for 20 minutes.
Cut small pieces of dough into boiling salted water and cook for 8 minutes.
Drain the spätzle and mix with melted butter, cheeses, cream, and pepper.
Fold in the sour cream gently to create a rich, creamy sauce.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Sauerbraten
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into cubes
instructions: Combine beef broth, red wine, apple juice, juniper berries, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, onion, and carrots in a large pot.
Bring the liquid to a simmer, then add the beef cubes and simmer gently for 3 hours until tender.
In a separate pan, brown the sliced onions in lard until golden.
Add the dried sour cherries, currants, and flour to the browned onions and stir to coat.
Remove the meat from the cooking liquid and slice it thinly against the grain.
Strain the cooking liquid and pour it over the sliced meat and onion mixture.
Simmer the sauce gently for 10 minutes to thicken slightly before serving.

title: Spätzle
instructions: Mix flour, salt, baking powder, and nutmeg in a large bowl.
Beat the eggs in a separate bowl, then gradually add them to the flour mixture.
Stir until a thick, sticky dough forms that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Transfer the dough to a traditional spätzle press or use a colander with holes.
Press the dough through the holes into simmering salted water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the dumplings float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and toss immediately with the melted butter.

title: Schweinshaxe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Scrub the pork knuckle clean and score the skin in a diamond pattern.
Rub the knuckle generously with salt and pepper.
Place the knuckle in a large roasting pan with the onion, carrots, and pork belly.
Pour the water, beer, and beef broth over the ingredients.
Roast uncovered for 2 hours, basting occasionally.
After 2 hours, remove the knuckle and increase the oven temperature to 220°C (425°F).
Add the cubed and whole potatoes to the pan around the knuckle.
Return to the oven for another 45-60 minutes until the skin is crispy and the potatoes are tender.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Käsespätzle
instructions: Fry the diced bacon and ham in a large skillet until crispy.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in the softened butter, grated Emmentaler, and Raclette cheese until melted and combined.
Add the caraway seeds, salt, and pepper to the cheese mixture.
Cook the fresh spätzle according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain the spätzle and toss them immediately into the cheese mixture.
Serve hot, optionally topped with a little extra butter.

title: Maultaschen
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in a pan until soft.
Add the ground pork and veal to the pan and cook until browned.
Stir in the chopped spinach, flour, broth, salt, and nutmeg.
Remove from heat and let the filling cool completely.
Mix the cooled filling with the egg and grated parmesan cheese.
Roll out the pasta sheets thinly on a floured surface.
Cut the pasta into large squares and place a spoonful of filling in the center of each.
Fold the pasta over the filling to create a half-moon shape and seal the edges.
Boil the Maultaschen in salted water for 4-5 minutes until they float.
Drain and serve with a creamy spinach sauce or simply with butter.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip the flour-coated cutlet into the beaten eggs.
Press the egg-coated cutlet into the breadcrumbs to coat evenly.
Heat the oil in a large pan until it shimmers.
Fry the schnitzel for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately with lemon slices and parsley, accompanied by buttered potatoes.

title: Sachertorte
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 8-inch cake pans.
Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla.
Gradually mix in flour to form a smooth batter.
Divide batter between the two pans and bake for 35-40 minutes.
Allow cakes to cool completely, then slice horizontally in half.
Spread half of the dark chocolate over the bottom layer of each cake.
Stack the layers and spread the remaining chocolate on top.
Brush the outside of the cake with apricot jam and let set.

title: Apfelstrudel
instructions: Toss apple slices with raisins, granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface.
Spread the apple mixture in a line down the center of the pastry.
Fold the sides of the pastry over the filling and roll it up tightly.
Place the strudel seam-side down on a baking sheet.
Brush the top with melted butter and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25-30 minutes until golden and puffed.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

title: Käseknödel
instructions: Melt the butter and mix with breadcrumbs, milk, flour, salt, and Parmesan.
Allow the breadcrumb mixture to cool slightly.
Mash the boiled potato until smooth.
Mix the potato, eggs, and Gruyère cheese into the breadcrumb mixture.
Divide the dough into walnut-sized balls and roll them gently.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 5 minutes.
Simmer gently in milk or broth with a piece of butter for another 10 minutes.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Zwiebelrostbraten
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef roast generously with salt and pepper.
Sear the roast in hot oil in a large Dutch oven until browned on all sides.
Remove the roast and set aside; sauté the onions in the same oil until soft.
Return the roast to the pot and add the beef broth and red wine.
Simmer the roast covered for 2-3 hours until tender.
In the last 30 minutes, mix flour, tomato paste, and caraway seeds with a little water.
Stir the paste into the pot and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Slice the roast and serve with the onion gravy.

title: Speckknödel mit Sauce und Wildgemüse
ingredients: 400g potatoes, peeled and boiled until soft
100g fresh dough flour, mixed with a little water
instructions: Boil the potatoes until very soft, then drain and mash them thoroughly.
Knead the flour, eggs, diced Speck, chopped spinach, and walnuts into the mashed potatoes until a firm dough forms.
Roll the dough into small balls and boil them in salted water for about 10 minutes until they float.
Sauté the garlic in butter until fragrant, then add the sliced mushrooms and cook until browned.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, let it reduce, then add the vegetable broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drain the dumplings and serve them immediately with the mushroom sauce.

title: Kaspressknödel mit Schmand und Rosinen
instructions: Mash the quark cheese, butter, eggs, salt, and half of the raisins together in a large bowl.
Gradually add the flour and knead until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Roll the dough into small oval rolls and brush them lightly with melted butter.
Bake the rolls in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 20 minutes until golden brown.
Whisk the sour cream with the remaining raisins, cinnamon, and some of the grated hard cheese.
Serve the warm Kaspressknödel topped with the creamy cheese sauce.

title: Bergknödel mit Speck und Bratkartoffeln
ingredients: 500g potatoes, peeled and sliced for fries
1 liter lard or oil for frying
instructions: Boil the first batch of potatoes until soft, then mash them with the flour, eggs, and diced Speck.
Knead the mixture into a firm dough, roll it into small balls, and boil them for 10 minutes.
Fry the bacon lardons in butter until crispy and set aside.
In the same fat, fry the sliced onions until golden, then add the potato slices and cook until browned.
Drain the boiled dumplings and place them on a warm plate.
Top the dumplings with the crispy bacon and fried potatoes, seasoning with salt and pepper.

title: Tyrolean Apple Strudel (Apfelstrudel)
ingredients: 4 apples, peeled, cored, and sliced thin
instructions: Toss the apples with lemon juice, then mix them with the dried fruits, nuts, sugar, and cinnamon.
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter and lay out one sheet of phyllo dough.
Brush the dough with more melted butter, sprinkle with a little sugar, and place the fruit filling in a line down the center.
Fold the sides of the dough over the filling and roll it up tightly like a cigar.
Brush the top with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Serve warm dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Käsespätzle mit Speck und Sauerkraut
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and warm water to form a smooth dough, then rest it for 30 minutes.
Fry the onion and cubed Speck in oil until golden, then add the sauerkraut and caraway seeds.
Cook the sauerkraut mixture for 5 minutes until the fat renders out.
Roll out the dough and cut it into strips to make Spätzle, boiling them in salted water for 2 minutes.
In a large pan, melt the butter and toast the grated cheese until bubbling.
Toss the drained Spätzle with the sauerkraut mixture and the melted cheese until well coated.
Serve immediately.

title: Rösti
ingredients: 800g potatoes, boiled until tender and drained well
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Peel the boiled potatoes and grate them on a coarse grater.
Place the grated potatoes in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
In a bowl, mix the dry potatoes with the beaten egg, oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add the oil.
Form the potato mixture into a flat round and press it firmly into the pan with a spatula.
Cook for about 5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and cook the other side for another 5 minutes.
Slide onto a plate, top with a pat of butter, and serve immediately.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
ingredients: 500g veal or pork tenderloin, sliced thinly against the grain
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Season the meat slices with salt and white pepper.
In a large pan, sauté the onions until translucent.
Add the sliced meat and cook quickly until browned on all sides.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and stir to coat.
Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the heavy cream and add the sliced mushrooms.
Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until the meat is tender.
Finish with a splash of lemon juice and serve with buttered egg noodles.

title: Spätzle
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, and sugar.
Gradually add the flour to the wet ingredients, mixing until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Knead the dough lightly on a floured surface until smooth, then cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough into a thick rope and press it against a spätzle maker or a fork with holes.
Drop the pieces directly into a pot of boiling salted water.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and rinse briefly under cold water.
Toss with a little oil to prevent sticking and serve warm.

title: Älplermagronen
instructions: Grease a large baking dish with butter.
In a saucepan, combine the sliced apples, cinnamon stick, and a splash of water; simmer until soft, then remove the cinnamon stick.
Boil the macaroni until al dente.
In a separate pot, boil the potatoes until tender, drain, and mash them with half the sour cream, milk, and salt.
Layer the macaroni, potatoes, and apples in the baking dish, mixing well.
Pour the remaining sour cream, milk, and stock over the mixture.
Sprinkle generously with grated cheese and top with a pat of butter.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve warm, optionally dusting the apples with a little sugar.

title: Swiss Cheese Fondue
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
Salt and white pepper to taste
Crackers, bread cubes, or boiled potatoes for serving
instructions: Halve the garlic clove and rub the inside of a fondue pot with it, then discard the clove.
Pour in the wine, milk, and vegetable broth.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer over low heat.
Slowly add the grated cheeses, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture to help thicken the fondue.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Once smooth and slightly thickened, remove from heat.
Serve immediately while warm with bread, crackers, or potatoes.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef chuck in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the carrots, celery, and potatoes; simmer for another 30 minutes.
Stir in the grated beets, tomato paste, and bay leaf; cook for 20 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi
ingredients: 1 cup farmer's cheese or curd cheese
instructions: Mix flour, egg, salt, and warm water to form a smooth dough; knead until elastic.
Boil potatoes until soft, mash them, then mix with cheese, onion, sugar, and salt.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges by pinching.
Boil the pierogi in salted water for 5-7 minutes until they float.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain, and fry in butter until golden brown.
Serve immediately with extra melted butter.

title: Romanian Sarbatoru
instructions: Sear the pork shoulder and belly in a large pot until browned.
Add the onions and cook until translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water or broth, add caraway seeds, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and cabbage; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Check seasoning and adjust if necessary before serving.

title: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
instructions: Place the chopped tomatoes, sliced cucumbers, and red onion in a large bowl.
Add the crumbled white cheese on top of the vegetables.
Sprinkle with fresh parsley, salt, pepper, and oregano.
Drizzle with olive oil and toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately as a side dish or appetizer.

title: Hungarian Goulash
instructions: Render the lard in a large pot and brown the pork cubes over medium heat.
Add the diced onions and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the paprika and caraway seeds; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the broth, add the bay leaf, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes and bell pepper; continue simmering for 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve hot.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onions and carrots in oil until soft.
Add grated beets and tomato paste, cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil.
Add red cabbage and simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot topped with sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, water, and egg to form a smooth dough, then rest for 30 minutes.
Combine mashed potatoes, cheese, chives, and salt for the filling.
Roll dough thin and cut into squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square and fold to seal.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, then drain and toss with melted butter.

title: Russian Borsch (Beet Soup)
instructions: Brown the meat in a pot and remove.
Sauté onions and carrots in the same pot.
Return meat to the pot, add water, bay leaf, and vinegar, then simmer for 1 hour.
Add beets and continue cooking until vegetables are soft.
Remove bay leaf, season, and serve with sour cream and dill.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Mix minced pork, ground pork, rice, onion, tomato sauce, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water until pliable.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, roll tightly, and place in a pot.
Cover with water, add salt, and simmer for 2 hours.
Serve hot, optionally fried in oil for crispiness.

title: Hungarian Goulash
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add onions and garlic, cook until softened.
Stir in paprika, caraway seeds, and broth, then simmer for 1 hour.
Add potatoes and continue cooking until meat and potatoes are tender.
Remove from heat, stir in sour cream, and serve with bread.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: 2 lbs red beets, peeled and grated
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef and pork in a large pot with oil until no longer pink.
Add onions and cook until softened, then add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the grated beets, carrots, and potatoes.
Pour in the beef broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in fresh dill, and serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi
ingredients: 2 tbsp bacon fat or butter for frying
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, water, and melted butter to form a soft dough; knead until smooth and cover to rest.
In a pan, sauté onions in butter until soft, then add mushrooms and cook until browned.
Mash the potatoes and mix with the cheese and mushroom mixture; let cool completely.
Roll dough thin and cut into squares, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and fold to seal.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, then pan-fry in bacon fat until golden and serve with chives.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Remove outer leaves from the cabbage and blanch in boiling water until soft; save the broth.
Mix meats, rice, onions, tomato paste, paprika, salt, and half the dill in a bowl.
Wrap a mixture onto each softened cabbage leaf, rolling tightly from the base to the tip.
Place rolls seam-side down in a large pot, cover with the reserved broth and remaining oil.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2 hours until cabbage is tender and rolls are cooked through; garnish with dill.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Render the bacon in a large pot, remove and set aside, leaving the fat.
Sauté onions and garlic in the bacon fat until translucent, then add the beef and brown well.
Stir in paprika, caraway seeds, and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute to release flavors.
Return bacon to the pot, add red wine and beef broth, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2 hours, adding cubed potatoes in the last 45 minutes until tender.

title: Bulgarian Banitsa
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, ricotta, feta, oregano, and salt in a bowl to make the filling mixture.
Brush a sheet of phyllo with melted butter, sprinkle with walnuts, and spread a layer of the egg mixture.
Repeat layers until all phyllo is used, folding edges slightly to create a square loaf.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and bake for 40 minutes until golden and puffed.
Slice into wedges and serve warm.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion until soft, then add beets, carrots, and potatoes.
Pour in beef broth and add bay leaf.
Simmer covered for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot topped with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Pierogi
ingredients: 1 cup farmer cheese or curd cheese
instructions: Mix flour, water, egg, and salt to form a soft dough; knead until smooth.
Wrap dough in plastic and rest for 30 minutes.
Mash potatoes, mix with cheese, scallions, and butter for filling.
Roll dough thin and cut into squares.
Place filling in center of each square, fold, and seal edges.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float.
Drain and serve with melted butter and salt.

title: Zalivanik
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, sour cream, baking powder, and sugar into a smooth batter.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Pour batter into a greased baking dish.
Sprinkle poppy seeds and sugar evenly over the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before slicing into squares.

title: Kutia
instructions: Soak wheat berries in water overnight.
Drain and boil wheat berries until very soft and mushy.
In a separate bowl, blend poppy seeds with a little water into a paste.
Mix wheat berries, poppy paste, honey, nuts, raisins, and caraway seeds.
Stir well and serve warm or at room temperature.
Traditionally eaten during Christmas Eve.

title: Varenyky with Sour Cream
instructions: Make dough with flour, water, egg, and salt; rest for 30 minutes.
Mix sauerkraut, sugar, and caraway seeds for filling.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Place filling on each circle, fold, and seal edges.
Boil in salted water until they float.
Drain and serve immediately with melted butter and sour cream.

title: Dumplings with Sour Cream
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add boiling water gradually to form a soft dough.
Knead briefly and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thin and cut into small squares.
Fry onions in butter until soft, then mix with sour cream, dill, and melted butter.
Place filling on dough squares, fold, and seal edges.
Boil dumplings in salted water for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Serve hot with extra sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Make dough by mixing flour, salt, and warm water until smooth.
Let dough rest for 1 hour.
Steam or boil potatoes, mash, and mix with cottage cheese, egg, onion, and salt.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Place spoonful of filling in center of each circle.
Fold over and crimp edges to seal.
Boil pierogi in salted water for 3 minutes, then again after they float.
Toss in melted butter before serving.

title: Borscht with Beetroot
instructions: Sauté onions and carrots in oil until soft.
Add beetroots and cook for 5 minutes.
Add broth, water, tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Ukranian Borsch
instructions: Brown beef in a large pot.
Add onions and carrots, cook until softened.
Stir in beets, broth, cabbage, tomatoes, tomato paste, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Check seasoning and serve with sour cream.

title: Russian Blini
ingredients: Cottage cheese and sour cream mixture for filling
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, salt, and egg in a bowl.
Gradually add milk and melted butter, stirring until smooth.
Let batter rest for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour small amounts of batter to form thin circles.
Flip when edges lift and cook until golden.
Serve with cottage cheese and sour cream mixture.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the pork ribs in oil until golden, then remove.
Sauté onions in the same oil until soft.
Add garlic and tomato paste, cook for 1 minute.
Stir in beets and broth, bring to a boil.
Return pork to the pot and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.
Top each bowl with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Varenyky
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, salt, and water to form a stiff dough; knead until smooth.
Combine cottage cheese and sugar to make the filling.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold over and pinch edges to seal.
Boil in salted water for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Drain and toss with melted butter or fried in oil.

title: Kutia
instructions: Rinse wheat berries and buckwheat groats thoroughly.
Boil grains in water until very soft and mushy, about 45 minutes.
Drain excess water and mash the mixture with a fork.
Stir in honey, poppy seeds, walnuts, and raisins.
Cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Serve warm as a traditional Christmas dish.

title: Golubtsi
instructions: Mix ground meats, grated onion, rice, salt, and pepper.
Separate cabbage leaves by boiling briefly in water.
Place a spoonful of meat mixture on the center of each leaf.
Fold the leaf over and roll tightly to form a cylinder.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a pot.
Pour broth, tomato paste, and vinegar over the rolls.
Simmer covered for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender.

title: Draniki
instructions: Squeeze excess moisture from the grated potatoes using a clean towel.
Mix potatoes, onion, egg, flour, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Form the mixture into small, flat patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry patties for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Varenyky with Sour Cream
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
4 cups fresh or frozen sauerkraut, drained
instructions: Mix flour, water, and salt to form a smooth dough; knead for 5 minutes.
Wrap dough and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Mix sauerkraut, sour cream, sugar, and caraway seeds for filling.
Place filling in center of each circle, fold in half, and seal edges.
Boil varenyky in salted water for 10 minutes until they float.
Serve hot with additional sour cream.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in oil until soft.
Add garlic, tomato paste, and beets; cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in beef broth and add bay leaf; simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in cabbage and cook for another 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Remove bay leaf and serve hot with sour cream.

title: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: 6 large russet potatoes, peeled and grated
instructions: Squeeze excess water from grated potatoes and onions.
Mix potatoes, onions, flour, egg, and salt in a bowl.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Form mixture into small patties and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream.

title: Kutia
instructions: Soak wheat berries in water overnight.
Boil wheat berries until tender, about 1 hour.
Toast poppy seeds, walnuts, and sesame seeds separately.
Mash cooked wheat berries into a paste.
Mix wheat paste with honey, toasted seeds, nuts, cherries, and raisins.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and salt.
Serve warm as a traditional Christmas dish.

title: Golubtsi
instructions: Boil cabbage leaves until flexible, then cool.
Sauté onion in oil until soft.
Mix ground beef, rice, onion, tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Place filling in center of each cabbage leaf and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls in a pot and cover with beef broth.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until cabbage is tender.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onions and carrots in a pot until soft.
Add grated beets, tomato paste, and broth; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in diced potatoes and cook until tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot topped with sour cream.

title: Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and boiling water to form a dough; knead until smooth.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Mix mashed potatoes, cheese, and sautéed onion for filling.
Place filling on dough circles, fold, and seal edges.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, then sauté in butter.

title: Golabki
instructions: Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water until flexible.
Mix ground pork, rice, onion, carrots, salt, and pepper.
Wrap filling in cabbage leaves and roll tightly.
Place rolls in a pot with tomato, broth, and tomato paste.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until cabbage is tender.

title: Varenyky
instructions: Knead flour, water, and eggs into a soft dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Mix mashed potatoes, sour cream, onion, and butter for filling.
Roll dough thin, cut circles, and fill with potato mixture.
Seal edges tightly and boil in salted water for 5-7 minutes.
Drain and serve warm with extra sour cream and butter.

title: Kutia
instructions: Cook wheat berries in water until soft and creamy; drain excess water.
Toast poppy seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Mix cooked wheat berries, honey, walnuts, dried fruit, and spices.
Stir in toasted poppy seeds and sugar to taste.
Let cool and serve as a sweet dessert or snack.

title: Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper, then brown in a large skillet.
Add onion and garlic, cook until soft.
Stir in paprika and flour, cooking for one minute.
Pour in chicken broth and simmer until chicken is tender.
Stir in sour cream and heat through without boiling.

title: Kotlety (Polish Meatballs)
instructions: Mix meats, breadcrumbs, egg, onion, and parsley in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, then form into oval patties.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry patties until golden brown on both sides and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Borscht with Sauerkraut
instructions: Brown beef in a pot, then remove and set aside.
Sauté onion, carrots, and garlic until softened.
Add broth, tomato paste, and cabbage; simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in sauerkraut and return beef to the pot.
Add grated beetroot and cook until soup is deep red and flavors meld.

title: Ukha (Russian Fish Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb white fish fillets, such as cod
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse barley and place in a large pot with stock.
Add onion, carrot, bay leaf, and seasonings.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add fish fillets gently and cook until opaque.
Remove bay leaf, stir in fresh dill, and serve immediately.

title: Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water until pliable.
Mix meats, rice, onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Spoon mixture onto cabbage leaves and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a pot.
Add tomato paste, broth, and simmer covered for 1.5 hours.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot with salt and pepper.
Add onions, carrots, and bay leaves, cooking until soft.
Stir in the grated beets and cook for 10 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the shredded red cabbage and cook for another 30 minutes.
Remove bay leaves, ladle into bowls, and top with sour cream.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, egg, water, and salt to form a smooth dough; knead until elastic.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes, then roll into thin sheets.
Mix cooked potatoes with cheese and sauerkraut for the filling.
Cut dough into squares and place filling in the center.
Fold and seal edges, then boil in water for 4-5 minutes.
Drain and toss with melted butter before serving.

title: Romanian Sarbator (Braised Cabbage)
ingredients: 1 large head green cabbage, quartered and core removed
instructions: Fry onions and carrots in lard until soft.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Place cabbage leaves in a pot, add broth, bay leaf, and seasonings.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until tender.
Stir in sour cream and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Hungarian Goulash
instructions: Brown the pork cubes in oil until golden.
Add onions and garlic, cooking until translucent.
Stir in paprika, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the broth and simmer for 1 hour until meat is tender.
Add diced potatoes and cook for another 30 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Russian Pelmeni
instructions: Mix flour, egg, water, and salt to make a firm dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground meats, onion, tomato paste, and salt for the filling.
Roll dough thinly and cut into small squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in each square, fold, and seal edges.
Boil the pelmeni in water for 8-10 minutes until they float.
Drain and serve with melted butter.

title: Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in oil over medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and simmer until chicken is tender.
Stir in sour cream and heat through without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper.

title: Dumplings (Knedliky)
ingredients: Boiled potatoes or meat for filling
instructions: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in lard until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg and warm water; knead until smooth.
Divide dough into balls and flatten slightly.
Place filling in center and seal dough around it.
Brush dumplings with lard and steam for 20 minutes.

title: Borscht
instructions: Brown meat in a pot with onion and carrots.
Add water or broth and bring to a boil.
Stir in tomato paste and vinegar.
Add grated beets and simmer for 1 hour.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot garnished with fresh dill.

title: Salo with Garlic
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly fat, salted and cured
instructions: Slice cured pork belly fat into thin strips.
Peel garlic cloves and lightly crush them.
Combine juniper berries, peppercorns, and salt.
Arrange fat slices on a plate and top with garlic.
Sprinkle seasoning over the garlic.
Let sit at room temperature for 2 hours before serving.

title: Cabbage Rolls (Golabki)
instructions: Boil cabbage leaves until soft and remove stems.
Mix meats, rice, onion, salt, and pepper.
Spoon mixture onto cabbage leaves and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls in a pot with tomato paste and tomato sauce.
Cover with water and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Serve hot with sour cream on the side.

title: Chicken Paprikash
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika, then dredge in flour.
Brown chicken in butter over medium heat until golden.
Add chicken broth and simmer until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in sour cream and heat gently without boiling.
Serve over cooked egg noodles.

title: Varenyky with Sour Cream
instructions: Mix flour, salt, egg, sour cream, and butter to form a dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thin, cut into circles, and fill with potato mixture.
Boil varenyky in salted water until they float.
Drain well and serve immediately with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Borscht with Beef
ingredients: 1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
instructions: Sauté onion and carrots in oil until soft.
Add beef and brown on all sides.
Pour in beef broth and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add beets and cook for another 30 minutes until tender.
Serve hot topped with sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Dolma
instructions: Soak grape leaves in hot water for 10 minutes.
Mix lamb, rice, onion, tomato paste, mint, salt, and pepper.
Wrap filling in grape leaves, rolling tightly.
Place in a pot, cover with water, and simmer for 1 hour.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Zrazy (Meat Suet Patties)
instructions: Mix pork, breadcrumbs, egg, onion, flour, salt, and pepper.
Form into small patties.
Fry patties in butter until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with a side of fried potatoes or salad.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onions and carrots in a large pot until soft.
Add beets and sugar, cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot topped with sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, egg, water, and lard to form a smooth dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Combine mashed potatoes, cheese, sautéed onions, salt, and pepper for filling.
Roll dough thin and cut into squares.
Place filling in center of each square and fold to seal edges.
Boil pierogi in salted water for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Drain and toss with melted butter.

title: Russian Blini
ingredients: Cottage cheese and jam for serving
instructions: Whisk eggs, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Gradually add warm milk and flour, mixing until smooth.
Let batter rest for 1 hour at room temperature.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little butter.
Pour small ladles of batter to form circles.
Flip when bubbles appear and cook until golden.
Serve with cottage cheese and jam.

title: Hungarian Goulash
instructions: Brown beef cubes in a large pot until seared.
Add onions and garlic, cook until translucent.
Stir in paprika and tomato paste; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef stock and bring to a simmer.
Add carrots and potatoes; cover and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes until flexible.
Mix meats, rice, grated carrots, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of tomato paste on each leaf.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a large pot.
Cover with tomato paste and broth.
Simmer covered for 2 hours until meat is tender.

title: Ukranian Borscht
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in sunflower oil in a large pot.
Add onions and carrots, cook until softened.
Stir in beets, potatoes, cabbage, broth, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with fresh dill.

title: Polish Pierogi
ingredients: 1 lb farmer cheese or curd cheese
1/2 cup onions, finely diced and sautéed
instructions: Mix flour, egg, and water to form a smooth dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Combine mashed potatoes, cheese, sautéed onions, salt, and butter for filling.
Roll out dough thin and cut into squares.
Place filling in center of each square, fold, and crimp edges.
Boil pierogi until they float, then pan-fry in butter until golden.

title: Romanian Mămăligă with Sour Cream
instructions: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Slowly add cornmeal while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and cook for 20 minutes, stirring frequently.
Serve hot topped with butter, sour cream, and cottage cheese.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder or beef, cubed
instructions: Brown meat in oil until seared on all sides.
Add onions and garlic, cook until soft.
Stir in paprika and caraway seeds, toast briefly.
Add broth, potatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 1.5 hours.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
instructions: Combine diced tomatoes, cucumbers, and red onion in a bowl.
Add sunflower oil and vinegar; season with salt.
Top generously with crumbled feta and grated sirene.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

title: Dumplings with Sour Cream (Ravioli)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and salt to form a stiff dough, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft, then add ground beef and cook until browned.
Season the meat mixture with salt and pepper, then cool completely.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut into squares, and place a spoonful of meat in the center.
Fold the dough over the filling to seal, creating dumplings, and boil in salted water for 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot dumplings topped with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Slovenian Pot Roast (Štruklji)
instructions: Combine ground pork, beef, onion, carrots, breadcrumbs, eggs, tomato paste, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Mix the meat mixture thoroughly until well combined.
Place the shredded cabbage in a large pot with water, salt, and vinegar, then boil until tender.
Form the meat mixture into long, thin rolls and wrap them tightly around the cabbage leaves.
Place the rolls in a large pot, cover with water, and simmer for 2 hours until cooked through.
Remove, slice into thick pieces, and serve with a side of boiled potatoes.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then mash while still hot.
Mix mashed potatoes with fresh cheese, onion, melted butter, salt, and sugar, then let cool.
Make the dough by mixing flour, eggs, water, and salt until smooth, then knead until elastic.
Roll the dough thin, cut into squares, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and fold into half-moons.
Seal the edges firmly with a fork, then boil in salted water for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Drain and toss with a little melted butter, then serve with sour cream.

title: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
instructions: Dice the bell peppers, cucumber, tomato, and red onion into small, uniform pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the vegetables and toss gently.
Add the sliced hard-boiled eggs to the mixture.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Top generously with the crumbled aged white cheese.
Serve immediately without mixing the cheese into the salad.

title: Ukrainian Borscht
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add the beef cubes and cook until browned, then add garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the grated beetroot and cabbage, then add the beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour until the beef is tender.
Add the cubed potatoes and cook for another 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix sour cream with vinegar and a pinch of salt, then stir into the soup.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with a dollop of extra sour cream.

title: Ukranian Borscht
instructions: Brown the beef shank in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onion, carrots, and garlic; sauté until softened.
Stir in beets and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in beef broth and tomato juice; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add red cabbage and cook for another 45 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with sour cream and dill.

title: Polish Pierogi
instructions: Mix flour, water, eggs, and salt to form a smooth dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Mash potatoes with cheese, onions, and half the melted butter.
Roll dough thin and cut into squares.
Place filling in center of each square, fold, and seal edges.
Boil pierogi in salted water until they float, about 5 minutes.
Drain and toss in remaining melted butter.
Serve warm with sour cream if desired.

title: Romanian Sarmale
instructions: Mix pork, beef, rice, onion, tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Boil cabbage leaves until flexible, then chill.
Spoon filling onto cabbage leaves, roll tightly, and place in a pot.
Add water and bay leaves to cover the rolls.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2 hours.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Hungarian Goulash
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef cubes.
Add onion, carrots, and garlic; cook until soft.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add broth and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add potatoes and cook until tender, about 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine diced bell pepper, cucumber, tomatoes, and onion in a bowl.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a small cup.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss gently.
Top generously with grated white cheese.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

title: Slovak Beef Goulash (Huspenina)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in lard in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Remove beef, then sauté the onion until soft and translucent.
Stir in the crushed caraway seeds and tomato paste, cooking for one minute.
Return the beef to the pot and add the wine to deglaze.
Pour in the beef broth and bay leaf, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours until tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and serve hot with bread.

title: Slovak Potato Dumplings (Knedlíky)
instructions: Mix the flour, salt, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Stir in the grated raw potato and melted butter.
Gradually add the warm water while mixing until a soft dough forms.
Knead gently for 2 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Shape the dough into a log, cut into 1-inch pieces, and roll into balls.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 10-12 minutes until they float.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve immediately with stew or soup.

title: Traditional Slovak Sour Soup (Kysela Reďkovka)
ingredients: 1/4 cup sour whey (kislo mlieko) or buttermilk
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Bring the beef broth to a simmer in a pot.
Stir in the grated radishes and let them cook for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Remove from heat and let the soup cool slightly.
Whisk together the sour cream, sour whey, salt, and white pepper in a separate bowl.
Slowly pour the sour cream mixture into the radish soup while stirring gently.
Add the sliced hard-boiled egg and chopped dill.
Serve ladled into bowls, topped with a dollop of sour cream and toasted rye bread.

title: Slovak Cabbage Rolls (Kapustové Rolády)
instructions: Boil cabbage leaves in salted water for 2 minutes until pliable, then drain and cool.
Mix ground pork, beef, cooked rice, minced onion, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of the meat mixture on each cabbage leaf and roll it up tightly.
Place the rolls seam-side down in a large pot.
Whisk together sour cream, tomato paste, beef broth, and a splash of water to make a sauce.
Pour the sauce over the rolls, add butter, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the cabbage is tender.
Serve hot, optionally topped with additional sour cream.

title: Hungarian-Influenced Slovak Duck (Káčica na Slovensku)
instructions: Season the duck quarters generously with salt and pepper.
Render the lard in a large pot over medium heat until it foams.
Brown the duck pieces skin-side down for 5 minutes, then flip and brown the other side.
Remove duck and sauté the onions, carrots, and celery until softened.
Return the duck to the pot, add the bouquet garni, and pour in the wine.
Add the chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, turning the duck occasionally.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer for another 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve with lemon wedges.

title: Sarmale (Cabbage Rolls with Rice and Meat)
ingredients: 1 large head green cabbage, outer leaves removed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine minced pork, beef, rice, half the onion, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; mix well.
Boil the cabbage leaves in salted water until soft, then peel off the core and set aside.
Spoon the meat mixture onto each cabbage leaf, rolling it tightly into a cigar shape.
Arrange the rolls seam-side down in a large pot.
Stir together tomato paste, remaining onion, broth, and bay leaf to make the sauce.
Pour the sauce over the rolls, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.
Serve hot with mămăligă (polenta) and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză (Polenta with Cheese)
instructions: Bring water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Gradually add cornmeal while stirring vigorously to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low and stir constantly for about 20 minutes until thick and smooth.
Remove from heat and stir in the butter immediately.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then arrange on a serving plate.
Top generously with the crumbled cheese and a dollop of sour cream.
Garnish with fresh chopped dill and serve warm.

title: Piftie (Boiled Beef Feet and Tail)
instructions: Scrub the beef feet and tail thoroughly under cold water.
Place the meat in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Add the whole onion, carrots, garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam that rises to the top.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 4 to 5 hours.
Remove from heat and let cool in the broth until cold.
Peel off the skin and fat, then thinly slice the meat.
Arrange slices on a platter, drizzle with some of the reduced broth and vinegar.
Serve cold as an appetizer.

title: Ciorbă de Burtă (Sour Soup with Tripe)
ingredients: 500g beef tripe, cleaned and cut into strips
instructions: Simmer the cleaned tripe in plenty of water with salt until tender, about 2 hours.
Strain the tripe, reserving the cooking liquid, and set the meat aside.
In a separate pot, sauté the diced onion, carrot, and tomatoes until soft.
Dissolve the flour in a little cold water and stir it into the vegetable mixture.
Add the reserved tripe cooking liquid and bring to a boil, stirring constantly to thicken.
Add the boiled tripe strips and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the sour cream.
Season with black pepper and garnish with fresh parsley and dill before serving.

title: Mici (Grilled Lamb Sausages)
ingredients: 100g fresh bread, soaked in milk and squeezed dry
instructions: Combine the lamb, pork, grated onion, soaked bread, garlic, coriander, salt, pepper, and paprika in a large bowl.
Mix vigorously by hand for at least 10 minutes until the meat is sticky and elastic.
Chill the mixture for 1 hour to firm up.
Form the meat into small, finger-length logs and wrap around wooden skewers.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Brush the skewers lightly with oil and grill for 10-12 minutes, turning frequently, until well-charred and cooked through.
Serve immediately with fresh flatbread, pickles, and a spicy mustard sauce.

title: Zurek with Smoked Bacon and Buckwheat
instructions: Soak the buckwheat groats in cold water for 4 hours, then drain.
In a large pot, boil the soaked buckwheat in the sour rye kvass until soft, about 20 minutes.
In a separate pan, fry the diced smoked bacon until crisp.
Crush the garlic cloves into a paste and stir into the soup along with dried dill.
Serve in deep bowls, topped with fried bacon, fresh dill, a dollop of sour cream, and cracked black pepper.

title: Barszcz Czerwony (Red Borscht) with Uszka
instructions: Simmer the beef bones in water with onions and carrots until the broth is rich and dark.
In a separate pot, sauté grated beets, carrots, and onions in lard until the liquid evaporates and it darkens.
Strain the beef broth and add the beet mixture, simmering for 30 minutes until the soup turns deep red.
Mix flour with the beaten egg to form a dough, then stuff small pockets with the cheese mixture.
Fry the stuffed dumplings (uszka) in lard until golden, then serve them in bowls of hot borscht with a side of sour cream.

title: Gołąbki (Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Blanch cabbage leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes until pliable.
Sauté onions and garlic in butter, then add the ground meats, rice, paprika, salt, and pepper, cooking until browned.
Spread a layer of tomato paste mixed with flour in a large pot, then arrange the cabbage leaves in a single layer.
Place a spoonful of meat filling in the center of each leaf and roll them up tightly.
Stand the rolls upright in the pot, pour the beef broth over them, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours.

title: Pierogi Ruskie (Potato and Onion Pierogi)
instructions: Mix flour, egg, and warm water to form a smooth dough, then knead until elastic and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Sauté diced onions in butter until translucent, then mix with the mashed potatoes, salt, sugar, and pepper.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet, cut into squares, and fill each with a spoonful of potato mixture.
Fold the squares into half-moons and seal the edges by pressing with a fork.
Boil the pierogi in salted water for 3 minutes, then boil again for 2 minutes until they float.

title: Pierogi z Czosnkiem (Garlic Pierogi)
ingredients: 500g fresh cheese (ser wiejski) or farmer's cheese
instructions: Make the dough using flour, egg, and warm water, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the fresh cheese with crushed garlic, dill, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Roll the dough thin, cut into circles, and fill each with a generous amount of the cheese mixture.
Seal the edges tightly and place them on a floured surface.
Boil the pierogi in salted water for 3 minutes, drain, and serve immediately with melted butter on top.

title: Borscht with Beef and Dumplings
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot with lard until well-seared.
Add diced onions and cook until translucent, then add carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in 1 liter of water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add beets, grated carrots, and diced potatoes; simmer for another 20 minutes until beets are tender.
Stir in chopped cabbage and cook for 10 more minutes until wilted.
Season with salt, pepper, and minced garlic; remove from heat.
Serve hot, topped with a generous dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: 3 tbsp lard or butter for frying
Fresh dill or green onions for garnish
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes until smooth and let them cool slightly.
Mix in flour, egg, milk, sugar, and salt to form a thick batter.
Heat lard in a large skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot pan, flattening slightly with a spatula.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Varenyky with Sour Cream and Sugar
instructions: Knead flour, salt, and boiling water into a stiff dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or round cutter.
Mix cottage cheese, sugar, and vanilla until smooth for the filling.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each dough circle.
Fold in half and seal edges tightly with a fork to prevent leaking.
Boil in salted water for 4-5 minutes until they float to the surface.
Serve immediately with sour cream and a sprinkle of extra sugar.

title: Kutya with Buckwheat
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat groats and cook in water until tender and fluffy.
Drain excess water and let the buckwheat cool slightly.
In a large bowl, mix cooked buckwheat with honey, toasted poppy seeds, sunflower seeds, pine nuts, cinnamon, and chopped walnuts.
Stir gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Serve as a warm or room-temperature dish, garnished with fresh mint leaves.

title: Kholodets (Meat Jellied Aspic)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef shank or pork knuckle
Dill sprigs and pickled cucumbers for garnish
instructions: Place meat in a large pot with cold water, carrots, onions, parsley, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, skim off scum, then reduce heat and simmer gently for 3 hours until meat falls off the bone.
Remove meat and set aside to cool; strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve.
Return the broth to the pot and add vinegar, salt, and pepper; boil for 5 minutes to clarify.
Shred the cooled meat into bite-sized pieces and place in a serving mold.
Pour the hot broth over the meat, cover, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours until firm.
Unmold onto a platter, garnish with dill and pickled cucumbers, and slice to serve.

title: Borscht with Sour Cream
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the beef broth with the bay leaf until hot.
Add the grated beets, carrots, and potatoes to the broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the diced onion and tomato paste, cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the shredded cabbage and cook until tender, about 10 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf.
Ladle into bowls and top with a generous dollop of sour cream.

title: Pelmeni (Dumplings)
instructions: Mix the ground meats and chopped onion in a bowl.
Add eggs, salt, and pepper to the meat mixture and knead well.
Gradually add flour to the meat to form a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut into small squares.
Place a small amount of filling in the center of each square.
Fold the square over the filling and pinch the edges to seal.
Boil the pelmeni in salted water for 8-10 minutes until they float.
Serve with melted butter and dill.

title: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onions on a coarse grater.
Squeeze the mixture firmly in a clean kitchen towel to remove excess liquid.
Mix the potato mixture with eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Form the mixture into small flat patties.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Kholodets (Meat Aspic)
instructions: Place the beef brisket in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Add the onions, carrots, bay leaves, and peppercorns to the pot.
Simmer for another 30 minutes, then remove the vegetables.
Strain the broth and let it cool completely.
Add vinegar and salt to taste, then return the meat and vegetables to the broth.
Pour the liquid into a large mold and place the meat on top.
Refrigerate overnight until the aspic is fully set.
Unmold onto a serving platter and garnish with fresh dill.

title: Blini (Thin Pancakes)
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups milk, plus more as needed
Jam, honey, or caviar for serving
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder.
In another bowl, beat the eggs and add the sour cream.
Gradually mix the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients.
Slowly stir in the milk until the batter is thin and pourable.
Heat a small amount of butter in a hot pan.
Pour a ladle of batter into the pan to form a thin circle.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve immediately with your choice of sweet or savory toppings.

title: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate potatoes and onion into a bowl.
Squeeze out all excess liquid from the mixture with your hands.
Add eggs, flour, and salt, then mix until a stiff dough forms.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Scoop dough into the pan, flatten slightly, and fry until golden brown on both sides.

title: Kunysh (Bread Soup)
ingredients: 4 slices of dark rye bread, crusts removed and torn
instructions: Bring the beef broth to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add the torn bread slices and let them soak for 10 minutes.
Remove bread with a slotted spoon, chop finely, and stir back into the broth.
Add the chopped dill, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately, topped with sliced hard-boiled eggs and a pat of butter.

title: Kapusta (Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 1 large head of cabbage, sliced into shreds
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the grated carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage and potatoes, then add water to cover.
Season with salt and add the bay leaf, then simmer for 40 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the sour cream, and serve hot.

title: Draniki z Tvorogom (Cheese Pancakes)
instructions: Mash the cottage cheese in a bowl until smooth.
Mix in the egg, flour, baking powder, and salt until a thick batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat and brush with sour cream.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the pan and cook until bubbles appear.
Flip carefully and cook the other side until golden, then serve with sour cream.

title: Borscht
instructions: Sauté onion and carrots in a pot with oil until soft.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the beef broth.
Add the potatoes and cabbage, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the grated beets and cook for another 20 minutes until beets are tender.
Serve in bowls topped with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Jönköping-style Goulash (Húsleves)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a heavy pot with a little oil.
Add the onions and cook until soft, then stir in the paprika.
Pour in the beef stock, add bay leaf, caraway seeds, and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes and cook for another 30 minutes until soft.
Serve hot with sour cream and fresh bread.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash (Csirkepaprikás)
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Dust the chicken pieces lightly with flour and brown them in butter.
Remove chicken and sauté the onions in the same pot until golden.
Stir in the paprika and cook for one minute to release the aroma.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the broth.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Whisk the sour cream with a little broth and stir it into the sauce.
Season with salt and white pepper, then serve with egg noodles or rice.

title: Eggplant with Sour Cream (Tükörtojás stílusú uborka)
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the eggplant slices in oil until golden brown on both sides.
In the same pot, fry the onions until soft, then add the ground pork.
Cook the meat until browned, then add paprika and tomato paste.
Add the fried eggplant slices to the meat mixture and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the sour cream gently and heat through without boiling.
Garnish with fresh dill and serve with boiled potatoes.

title: Hungarian Beef Stroganoff (Szalonnaval)
ingredients: 500 g beef sirloin, sliced thinly against the grain
200 ml sour cream mixed with 2 tbsp water
Salt, pepper, and garlic powder to taste
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the onions and mushrooms until soft.
Add the flour to the pan and stir for one minute to make a roux.
Add the beef slices and cook quickly until browned on the outside.
Return the bacon to the pan and stir in the sour cream mixture.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder, then garnish with parsley.

title: Lángos with Sour Cream and Onion
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix in the flour and salt to form a soft, sticky dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into balls and flatten each into a thick pancake shape.
Heat plenty of oil in a deep pan to 180°C (350°F).
Fry the lángos on both sides until golden brown and crispy.
Top immediately with fried onions, salt, and a generous dollop of sour cream.

title: Trdelník (Mini Version)
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
instructions: Dissolve yeast, sugar, and salt in warm milk and water; let sit for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and melted butter into the yeast mixture to form a soft dough.
Knead on a floured surface until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise until doubled.
Divide dough into small balls, roll each into a long thin cylinder on a floured wooden spoon or ring mold.
Place on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for 30 minutes.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
Meanwhile, mix brown sugar and cinnamon together.
Roll the warm cakes in the cinnamon-sugar mixture, then drizzle with warm honey and sprinkle with walnuts.
Slice and serve warm.

title: Svíčková na smetaně
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef sirloin, trimmed and cut into large chunks
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and white pepper, then sear in a large pot with oil until browned on all sides.
Remove beef and sauté onions, carrots, and celery in the same pot until softened.
Stir in garlic, flour, and butter to coat the vegetables, then gradually add beef broth while whisking to avoid lumps.
Return beef to the pot, cover, and simmer gently for 1.5 hours until tender.
In a separate saucepan, combine heavy cream, salt, and white pepper; simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir the sour cream into the cream sauce and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Slice the beef thinly against the grain.
Dip slices into the melted butter, coat in breadcrumbs, and fry until golden.
Serve beef slices with the creamy sauce, garnished with a slice of fried bread or potato pancake.

title: Knedlíky (Dumplings)
ingredients: 500g fresh bread, crusts removed and torn into pieces
instructions: Boil the water with salt, then submerge the bread pieces and cook for 30 minutes until soft.
Drain the bread well and squeeze out excess liquid by hand.
Place the moist bread in a large bowl, add the beaten egg, flour, and softened butter.
Knead thoroughly until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Divide the dough into 4 equal portions.
Roll each portion into a long rope, then cut into 1-inch pieces.
Gently shape each piece into a small oval dumpling.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 15-20 minutes until they float to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve immediately with meat or stew.

title: Vepřové kotlety s žampiony
instructions: Season both sides of the pork cutlets with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat; fry cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Remove cutlets and keep warm.
In the same pan, sauté onions and mushrooms until softened and browned.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits.
Add chicken broth and butter, stirring until the butter melts.
Lower heat and stir in sour cream to create a creamy sauce.
Return cutlets to the pan, spoon sauce over them, and simmer for 2 minutes to warm through.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes or bread.

title: Hovězí guláš
instructions: Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat; brown beef cubes on all sides, then remove.
Sauté onions, carrots, and bell pepper until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in paprika, salt, and pepper; cook for 30 seconds to release the aroma.
Return beef to the pot; add broth, wine (if using), and caraway seeds.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
In a small bowl, mix flour with a little cold broth to make a slurry.
Stir the slurry into the pot and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in sour cream off the heat and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with bread or potatoes.

title: Slovak Sauerbraten (Marinated Beef)
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into cubes
instructions: Marinate beef in vinegar, wine, onions, and spices for 3 days in the fridge.
Remove beef from marinade, reserving the liquid.
Sear beef cubes in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Add reserved marinade, broth, bay leaves, and peppercorns to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Add carrots and cook for another 30 minutes.
Season with salt and sugar, then serve with dumplings.

title: Zalivanka (Pour-Over Soup)
instructions: Sauté onions and carrots in a pot until soft.
Add pork ribs and cook until browned.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and simmer until tender.
In a separate bowl, mix sour cream with a little hot broth and the beaten egg.
Stir the egg mixture into the soup slowly while stirring constantly.
Season with salt, pepper, and fresh dill.
Serve hot with sliced smoked sausage on top.

title: Knedliky (Potato Dumplings)
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes until smooth and cool slightly.
Mix in the egg, salt, and baking powder.
Gradually add flour to form a soft, sticky dough.
Knead gently for 2 minutes until elastic.
Roll the dough into a rope and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Drop dumplings into boiling salted water.
Cook for 15 minutes until they float to the surface.
Drain and serve immediately with gravy or meat sauce.

title: Bryndzové Halušky (Potato Dumplings with Cheese)
instructions: Grate potatoes and squeeze out excess liquid with a clean cloth.
Mix grated potatoes, flour, eggs, and water to make a firm dough.
Roll dough into a rope and cut into small pieces.
Boil dumplings in salted water for 10-12 minutes until tender.
Drain well and return to the pot.
Melt butter in a pan, add cheese and chives, and cook until melted.
Pour the cheese sauce over the hot dumplings and toss gently.
Serve immediately with sour cream if desired.

title: Kapustnica (Sauerkraut Soup)
instructions: Sauté onion and carrots in a pot until translucent.
Add rinsed sauerkraut and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in groats, broth, and caraway seeds.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes until groats are cooked.
In a separate bowl, mix beaten eggs with a splash of hot broth.
Stir the egg mixture into the soup slowly while stirring constantly.
Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.
Serve with a dollop of sour cream on top.

title: Sarmale in foi de varza
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the rice until it is half done.
Mix the minced pork, pork fat, rice, grated carrots, chopped onion, and garlic in a large bowl.
Season the mixture with salt, pepper, and tomato paste.
Separate the leaves from the cabbage and remove the thick core.
Place a small amount of the meat mixture on each leaf, roll it tightly, and tie with kitchen string.
Place the rolls in a large pot in a single layer.
Cover the rolls with the remaining broth and add a bay leaf.
Simmer covered for 2 to 3 hours until the meat is tender.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză de Vacar
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Slowly add the semolina while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat and stir continuously for about 20 minutes until the dough is smooth and pulls away from the sides.
Spread the hot polenta onto a serving dish.
Top generously with crumbled goat cheese.
Dot with butter and sprinkle with fresh dill before serving.

title: Ciorbă de Burtă
instructions: Clean the pork stomach thoroughly and boil it until tender.
Remove the stomach, shred the meat, and set aside.
In a separate pot, combine the broth, diced potatoes, sliced carrots, and sliced onion.
Add the shredded stomach meat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Mix the flour with cold water to create a slurry.
Stir in the flour slurry, grated tomatoes, vinegar, salt, and pepper into the soup.
Simmer for another 10 minutes until the broth thickens slightly.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill and coriander.

title: Sarmale la Grătar
instructions: Mix the ground pork, beef, rice, grated onion, garlic, beaten egg, and tomato paste.
Season the mixture well with salt and pepper.
Blanch the cabbage leaves in boiling water for a few minutes until flexible.
Place a spoonful of the meat mixture in the center of each leaf and roll it tightly.
Brush the rolls with olive oil.
Grill the sarmale over medium heat for about 15 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Serve immediately, optionally with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Cozonac cu Nuci
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in warm milk and let it foam for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix flour, sugar, softened butter, salt, and the yeast mixture.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, then let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Punch down the dough, divide it in half, and roll each half into a rectangle.
Spread the walnuts mixed with cinnamon over the dough and roll it up into a log.
Place the logs on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 40-50 minutes until golden brown.

title: Zielona Zupa (Green Soup)
instructions: Blanch the sorrel and dandelion greens in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Mash the cooled greens thoroughly with a potato masher until smooth.
In a pot, melt butter and add the mashed greens, stirring continuously.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the lemon juice, salt, and sugar.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Pierogi Ruskie (Meat Dumplings)
instructions: Mix the ground pork and beef with onions, salt, pepper, and half the beaten eggs to make the filling.
Chill the filling in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Combine flour, remaining eggs, milk, salt, and melted lard to make a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut into squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square, fold into a half-moon, and seal edges.
Boil the pierogi in salted water until they float, then drain.
Fry them in butter until golden brown and serve with sour cream.

title: Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
ingredients: 300 grams mixed sauerkraut or cabbage, shredded
instructions: Render the bacon and beef in a large heavy pot until browned.
Add the onions and carrots, cooking until softened.
Stir in the sauerkraut, mixed cabbage, apple, bay leaf, and thyme.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer uncovered for 30 more minutes until the liquid reduces.

title: Babka Jarowa (Carrot Loaf Cake)
ingredients: 50 grams sugar, for poppy seed filling
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a loaf pan.
Mix butter and sugar until creamy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder, vanilla, and grated carrots.
