In a separate bowl, mix poppy seeds with sugar and cinnamon for the filling.
Spread a layer of filling in the pan, add a layer of batter, and repeat.
Bake for 50-60 minutes until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack.

title: Kotlet Schabowy (Pork Cutlets)
instructions: Pound the pork cutlets between plastic wrap until very thin.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set up three stations with flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot with fried onions and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Borscht with Sour Cream
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion in oil until soft, then add carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Add grated beets, tomato paste, and a splash of water; cook for 10 minutes until beets soften.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil.
Add diced potatoes and simmer until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt, pepper, and fresh dill.
Serve hot in bowls topped with a generous dollop of sour cream.

title: Kutia
instructions: Rinse wheat berries and cook in water until very soft and mushy, about 45 minutes.
Drain excess water and mash the wheat into a thick paste.
In a separate pan, toast poppy seeds until fragrant.
Combine the wheat paste, toasted poppy seeds, honey, cinnamon, and salt in a pot.
Stir in chopped walnuts, apricots, and raisins.
Heat gently until everything is well blended and warm, then serve immediately.

title: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate potatoes and onion into a large bowl, squeezing out excess liquid from the potatoes.
Add eggs, sour cream, flour, salt, and baking powder to the mixture.
Mix until a thick batter forms that holds together when pressed.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and flatten slightly.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream or apple sauce.

title: Varenyky with Sour Cream and Chives
instructions: Mix flour, egg, and warm water to form a smooth dough; knead and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough thinly and cut into circles using a glass or cutter.
In a bowl, mix cottage cheese, egg yolk, sugar, sour cream, chives, and salt to make filling.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each dough circle and fold over to seal edges.
Boil in salted water for 4-5 minutes until they float to the surface.
Drain well, brush with melted butter, and serve warm with extra sour cream.

title: Makove (Poppy Seed Pancakes)
instructions: Soak poppy seeds in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain and mash into a paste.
In a bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and melted butter.
Add egg and milk to the dry ingredients, stirring until combined.
Gradually stir in the poppy seed paste until the batter is smooth.
Heat oil in a skillet and pour small amounts of batter to form small pancakes.
Fry on both sides until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm, optionally dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Borscht with Beef
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot until sealed.
Add onion and carrots, cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and grated beets, cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper, serve hot topped with sour cream.

title: Pelmeni (Dumplings)
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and salt to form a stiff dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground meats and minced onion; season with salt and pepper.
Roll dough thinly and cut into small squares.
Place a small spoonful of meat mixture in the center of each square.
Fold the dough over the meat and crimp edges to seal.
Boil the pelmeni in salted water for 8-10 minutes until they float.

title: Zelny Pirozhki (Cabbage Buns)
instructions: Sauté chopped cabbage and onion in sunflower oil until soft.
Season the cabbage mixture with salt and pepper.
Divide dough into small balls and flatten into discs.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each disc.
Fold the dough over and pinch edges to seal tightly.
Brush with beaten egg, let rise for 20 minutes, then bake at 375°F for 25 minutes.

title: Kholodets (Meat Aspic)
ingredients: Cold water, enough to cover meat
instructions: Place meat, vegetables, bay leaf, salt, and pepper in a large pot.
Cover with cold water and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook slowly for 3 hours until meat is very tender.
Remove meat, strain the broth, and let it cool completely.
Shred the meat and place it in a mold.
Pour the cold broth over the meat, cover, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours.

title: Zhurny (Vegetarian Pancakes)
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk milk, egg, and grated zucchini.
Combine wet and dry ingredients to form a thick batter.
Heat a pan with a little oil over medium heat.
Pour batter to form small pancakes and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve warm with sour cream or jam.

title: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, plus more for sprinkling
instructions: Grate the potatoes and onion into a bowl and let them sit for 10 minutes to release moisture.
Squeeze the liquid out of the mixture thoroughly using a clean kitchen towel.
Mix in the eggs, flour, and salt until a thick dough forms.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Form the mixture into small patties and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with sour cream.

title: Kolduny (Dumplings with Meat Filling)
ingredients: 500g ground beef, mixed with ground pork
instructions: Mix the ground meats, chopped onion, salt, and buckwheat groats together for the filling.
Wrap small portions of filling in squares of dough, sealing the edges tightly.
Roll the dumplings into small balls and place them in a pot.
Cover with cold water, add a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the dough is cooked through.
Drain, toss with melted butter, and serve with sour cream.

title: Drani (Raw Potato Salad)
instructions: Steam the cubed potatoes in vegetable oil until tender but not falling apart.
Allow the potatoes to cool slightly, then gently mash them with a fork.
In a large bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, grated carrot, and chopped eggs.
Stir in the mayonnaise, green onions, dill, salt, and pepper.
Mix gently until well combined and serve immediately.

title: Kupenniki (Potato Dumplings in Broth)
instructions: Boil the potatoes with their skins on, then peel and pass them through a ricer.
Mix the riced potatoes with flour, egg, salt, and water to form a soft dough.
Roll the dough into long ropes and cut into small pieces.
Drop the pieces into a pot of simmering chicken broth.
Cook for about 10 minutes until the dumplings float to the surface.
Stir in the butter, garnish with fresh dill, and serve.

title: Borscht (Beet Soup)
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the onions and carrots until soft.
Add the grated beets and cook for another 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the potatoes, and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the salt and vinegar, then let it rest for 10 minutes to allow the color to develop.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Huhn mit Paprika und Süßkartoffel (Csirke paprikás és sütőtökkel)
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, cut into pieces
3 large bell peppers (red, yellow, green), chopped
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
instructions: Fry the chopped onions in pork fat until soft and golden.
Add the chicken pieces and brown them well on all sides.
Stir in the sweet paprika powder and cook for one minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped bell peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth, add salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Add the cubed sweet potatoes, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until everything is tender.
Serve hot with a slice of dark rye bread.

title: Goulash with Smoked Paprika (Sajtós gulyás)
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and fry the diced onions until translucent.
Add the beef cubes and fry until the meat is browned on all sides.
Stir in the smoked paprika and caraway seeds, cooking for one minute.
Pour in the red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the carrots and beef broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until the beef is very tender.
Stir in the sour cream off the heat and season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately with soft dill noodles (tészta).

title: Rice with Cabbage and Mushrooms (Rizses káposzta)
ingredients: 200 g mixed mushrooms (oyster or button), sliced
instructions: Sauté the onion and grated carrot in vegetable oil until soft.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture.
Stir in the shredded red cabbage and cook for 10 minutes until wilted.
Add the rinsed rice, salt, paprika, and vegetable broth.
Cover the pot tightly and cook over low heat for 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, stir in the butter to melt, and fluff gently.
Let it rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Hungarian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls (Töltött káposzta)
instructions: Blanch the cabbage leaves in boiling water for 3-4 minutes until pliable, then drain.
In a large pot, fry the onions in oil until soft and golden.
Add the ground pork and beef, browning the meat well.
Stir in the rice, tomato paste, salt, pepper, and bay leaf, cooking for 5 minutes.
Lay a cabbage leaf flat, spoon a portion of the meat mixture in the center, and roll it up tightly.
Place the rolls seam-side down in a large pot in a single layer.
Pour the beef broth over the rolls until they are mostly submerged, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Remove the bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Roasted Chicken with Potatoes and Carrots (Pörkölt csirke zöldségekkel)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.5 kg), cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Heat lard in a large roasting pan and brown the chicken pieces on all sides.
Remove chicken and set aside; fry the onions in the same fat until soft.
Return chicken to the pan, sprinkle with sweet paprika, salt, thyme, and rosemary.
Arrange the potatoes and carrots around the chicken in the pan.
Pour the chicken stock over everything until it reaches halfway up the vegetables.
Cover the pan tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour.
Remove foil, increase oven temperature slightly, and bake uncovered for another 30-40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thickened.

title: Svíčková na smetaně
instructions: Season the beef strips with salt and pepper.
Dredge the meat in flour and sear in hot oil until browned on all sides.
Remove meat and add broth to the pan, scraping up browned bits.
Simmer the broth until reduced by half, then stir in sour cream.
Return meat to the pan and simmer gently for 2 hours until tender.
Serve with lemon slices and potato dumplings.

title: Vepřo-knedlo-zelo
instructions: Fry the bacon in a large pot until crispy, then remove.
Sauté the onion and carrot in the bacon fat until soft.
Add the pork slices and fry until browned.
Stir in the sauerkraut and add a splash of water if too dry.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until pork is tender.
Serve hot with bread dumplings and crispy bacon.

title: Kolonáček s marmeládou
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl.
Add milk, melted butter, and egg to form a soft dough.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut into long strips.
Brush strips with beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar.
Place apricot jam in the center of each strip and roll up.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Hovězí guláš
instructions: Fry the onions in lard until translucent.
Add the beef cubes and fry until browned.
Stir in paprika, carrots, and tomatoes, then cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and broth to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2 hours until meat is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving with dumplings.

title: Knedlíky s mákem
instructions: Mix poppy seeds with sugar, melted butter, and vanilla to make filling.
Combine flour, sugar, and baking powder.
Add milk and eggs to make a soft, sticky dough.
Roll dough into long ropes and cut into 2cm pieces.
Press filling into the center of each piece and seal the dough around it.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 5 minutes.
Serve warm with melted butter or jam.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 1/2 cup warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and rabbit, seasoning with salt and pepper, and cook until browned.
Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth and saffron mixture.
Add green beans and peas.
Simmer without stirring for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Combine all chopped vegetables, garlic, and basil in a blender.
Add olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, and sugar if using.
Blend until smooth, scraping down sides as needed.
Pour into a bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to chill.
Serve cold, optionally garnished with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Tortilla de Patatas
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add potato and onion slices; fry until soft and golden (about 15 minutes).
Drain excess oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Pour beaten eggs over the potatoes and onions.
Cover and cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom sets.
Invert a large plate over the skillet, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide back into the pan.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until set.
Let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Bring water, salt, and butter to a boil in a saucepan.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously until the dough forms a ball.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Pipe dough into hot oil in 4-inch lengths, turning occasionally until golden.
Drain on paper towels and roll in cinnamon sugar.
For chocolate sauce, heat cream with sugar until simmering.
Remove from heat, add chocolate chips, and stir until melted and smooth.
Serve churros immediately with warm chocolate sauce.

title: Crema Catalana
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar, plus more for topping
instructions: Combine cream, milk, sugar, vanilla bean, and salt in a saucepan.
Heat gently until just simmering, then remove from heat.
Whisk egg yolks in a separate bowl until pale.
Slowly pour warm milk mixture into eggs while whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it coats the back of a spoon (about 8 minutes).
Strain into individual ramekins.
Chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Before serving, sprinkle sugar over the top and caramelize with a torch or under a broiler.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh, cut into pieces
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 1/2 cup warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit pieces, then remove them.
Sauté onion, garlic, and bell pepper until soft.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the saffron-infused water and bay leaf.
Return the meat to the pan and pour in the hot chicken stock.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes without stirring.
Add green beans and peas, then cook for another 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup bread, crusts removed and soaked in water
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a food processor.
Add the soaked bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Add ice cubes and pulse briefly to chill without over-blending.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve chilled, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced potatoes and onions, then sprinkle with salt.
Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and golden (about 20 minutes).
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the remaining oil and 2 tablespoons of water.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes in the skillet.
Cook over medium-low heat until the bottom is set but the top is still slightly runny (about 5 minutes).
Run a spatula around the edges, then flip the tortilla using a plate.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until set.
Slide onto a plate, slice, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Chorizo y Garbanzos
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked chickpeas.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chorizo slices and cook until browned, then remove.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft, then add paprika and cumin.
Add chickpeas and chorizo back to the pot.
Cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until chickpeas are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then garnish with parsley.
Serve hot as a main dish or side.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: Heat milk, cream, and the scraped vanilla bean in a saucepan over medium heat until just simmering.
Whisk egg yolks and 1/2 cup sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot milk mixture into the egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return the custard to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it coats the back of a spoon (do not boil).
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a dish.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.
Just before serving, sprinkle sugar and cinnamon over the top.
Broil until the sugar caramelizes to a golden brown.
Serve immediately.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 1/2 cup warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken and rabbit with salt and pepper; sear until browned on all sides.
Remove meat and set aside; add onion and garlic to the pan and sauté until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Return the meat to the pan, stir in saffron and 1 cup of stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Arrange green beans and peas around the pan.
Slowly add remaining stock to reach the rice level; do not stir after this point.
Cook for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving with lemon.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 cup stale bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Soak the torn bread in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
In a blender, combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, soaked bread, olive oil, and vinegar.
Blend on high speed until completely smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and add cold water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Season generously with salt and taste for balance.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to meld.
Serve chilled in bowls, garnished with fresh basil leaves.

title: Jamón Ibérico Croquetas
ingredients: 4 oz high-quality jamón ibérico, finely chopped
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a small saucepan, heat milk until simmering.
Melt butter in another pan, add flour and whisk for 1 minute to make a roux.
Gradually add the hot milk to the roux, stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat, stir in jamón, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Let the mixture cool slightly, then beat in the egg until smooth.
Refrigerate the mixture for at least 2 hours to firm up.
Shape the mixture into small cylinders using your hands or a cookie cutter.
Roll each croqueta in breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Fry croquetas for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy; drain on paper towels.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Slice the potatoes thinly and soak in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain the potatoes thoroughly and pat dry with a clean towel.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and the optional water.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes to the skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes until they begin to soften.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes, ensuring even coverage.
Cook undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until the bottom sets.
Carefully flip the tortilla using a large plate or spatula to cook the other side for 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Chorizo con Patatas
ingredients: 1/2 lb Spanish chorizo, sliced into rounds
2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add the chorizo slices and cook until they release their oils and brown slightly.
Add the onion and garlic to the pan; cook until softened.
Stir in the potatoes and paprika, coating them in the oil and spices.
Pour in the white wine and bring to a simmer.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 30-35 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with salt, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and rabbit pieces; cook until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion, garlic, and bell pepper until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return meat to the pan and sprinkle with salt.
Dissolve saffron in a small cup of warm broth and pour over the rice.
Add the remaining warm broth and stir gently once.
Arrange green beans and peas in concentric circles around the pan.
Cook without stirring for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving with lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 6 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and seeded
instructions: Place all vegetables, garlic, vinegar, oil, salt, pepper, and sugar into a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Pour the soup into a large bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to chill thoroughly.
Serve cold over ice cubes, garnished with olive oil swirls or croutons if desired.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 1 lb russet potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss potato wedges with salt and paprika; spread on the baking sheet.
Bake for 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until edges are slightly crisp.
While baking, whisk flour, baking powder, salt, and paprika in a bowl.
Gradually add the beaten egg and water to make a smooth batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each potato wedge in the batter and carefully place in the hot oil.
Fry for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy; drain on paper towels.
Mix tomato sauce, tomato paste, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and water in a small saucepan.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until thickened, then serve immediately with the fried potatoes.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 1 cup thinly sliced onion, white part only
1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, divided
instructions: In a large bowl, beat the eggs until well combined.
Add the sliced potatoes, onions, salt, and pepper to the eggs; mix gently.
Heat 1/4 cup of olive oil in a 10-inch non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour the egg and vegetable mixture into the skillet, spreading it evenly.
Cook undisturbed for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is set and golden.
Place a large heat-proof plate over the skillet.
Holding the plate and skillet together, quickly flip them over to invert the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the skillet, uncooked side down.
Add the remaining 1/4 cup of olive oil to the skillet and cook for another 3-4 minutes until the top is set.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly before slicing and serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Churros con Chocolate
ingredients: Cinnamon sugar (cinnamon and sugar mixed), for coating
instructions: In a saucepan, bring water, butter, sugar, and salt to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low and gradually whisk in the flour until a dough forms and pulls away from the sides.
Remove from heat and let the dough cool for 5 minutes.
Gradually beat in the eggs one at a time until fully incorporated and smooth.
Transfer the batter to a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Pipe 4-inch strips of dough into the hot oil, twisting the bag slightly to create ridges.
Fry the churros in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden brown and puffy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and immediately roll in the cinnamon sugar while still warm.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with a cup of hot chocolate, grated dark chocolate, and whipped cream.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 500g rabbit, chicken, and duck breast, cubed
1 tsp saffron threads, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté until soft.
Add the meat cubes and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the hot stock and saffron mixture.
Arrange green beans and peas in a single layer on top.
Simmer uncovered for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving with lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup stale white bread, soaked in water then squeezed dry
instructions: Blend tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Add the soaked bread, olive oil, vinegar, and salt to the blender.
Blend again until the mixture is completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or vinegar if necessary.
Serve chilled over ice cubes with a drizzle of extra olive oil.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 1.5 kg Russet potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss potato wedges with olive oil, paprika, and salt.
Roast for 40-45 minutes until golden and crispy.
For the sauce, sauté garlic in oil until fragrant.
Stir in paprika, cumin, tomato sauce, water, and vinegar; simmer for 5 minutes.
For the aioli, whisk egg yolks, lemon juice, and salt until pale.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking vigorously until thick.
Serve hot potato wedges with bowls of spicy sauce and aioli.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Layer the sliced potatoes and tomatoes in a pot with 1/2 cup water.
Simmer over medium heat for 20-25 minutes until very tender.
Drain the vegetables thoroughly and press out excess liquid.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs, salt, and chives until frothy.
Add the cooked vegetables to the eggs and mix gently.
Heat remaining oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the egg mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is set but the top is still slightly wet.
Run a knife around the edge, invert the tortilla onto a plate, then flip it back into the pan to finish cooking the other side.

title: Churros con Chocolate
ingredients: Sugar and cinnamon mix for coating
instructions: Bring water, butter, salt, and sugar to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in flour until a smooth dough forms.
Let cool slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time until thick.
Add vanilla and transfer to a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
Heat oil to 375°F (190°C) in a deep fryer or pot.
Pipe churros into the hot oil and fry until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Drain on paper towels and roll in the sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Make chocolate sauce by melting chocolate chips and cream together.
Serve warm churros with a cup of dipping chocolate sauce.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 500g rabbit or chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the meat with salt and pepper, then brown it in olive oil in a large pan.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock mixed with saffron and bring to a boil.
Arrange the green beans, butter beans, and peas around the pan.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes without stirring.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
instructions: Toast the bread in a dry pan until golden, then set aside.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Add the toasted bread, olive oil, and vinegar to the blender.
Pulse briefly to incorporate the bread without making the soup too thick.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve ice cold, optionally garnished with diced vegetables.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Fry the onion slices in half the olive oil until soft and golden.
Add the potato slices and fry gently until they begin to soften but are not fully cooked.
In a bowl, beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Drain the oil from the pan, leaving the potatoes and onions.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes and onions.
Cook over medium-low heat until the bottom is set.
Run a knife around the edge, invert the tortilla onto a plate, then slide it back into the pan to cook the other side.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Bring the water, butter, sugar, and salt to a boil in a pot.
Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously until a dough forms.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one by one.
Transfer the dough to a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
Heat oil to 180°C (350°F) and pipe the dough into the hot oil.
Fry the churros until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Drain on paper towels and dust with powdered sugar.
Heat the chocolate and cream together until melted and smooth.
Serve the churros with the warm chocolate dipping sauce.

title: Crema Catalana
ingredients: 1/4 cup granulated sugar for the crust
instructions: Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick and lemon zest until steaming.
Whisk the egg yolks with the 100g sugar until pale and thick.
Stir in the cornstarch and slowly whisk in the hot milk in batches.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook, stirring constantly, until it thickens.
Strain the cream into a bowl and cool slightly.
Pour the mixture into individual ramekins.
Sprinkle the top of each ramekin generously with granulated sugar.
Broil under a hot grill until the sugar forms a golden caramel crust.
Let cool before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit pieces, then remove them.
Sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce, paprika, and saffron.
Return the meat to the pan and add stock and water to cover the rice.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes without stirring.
Arrange the green beans and peas in a circle on top.
Cook for another 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 cup stale white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Soak the bread in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
Place tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, and garlic in a blender.
Add the soaked bread, olive oil, vinegar, and water.
Blend until completely smooth.
Season with salt to taste.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold garnished with fresh basil.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Slice potatoes thinly and soak in water to remove starch.
Drain potatoes and pat dry.
Beat eggs in a bowl with salt.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Add potatoes and cook until golden on both sides, about 10 minutes.
Add the beaten eggs to the skillet and mix gently.
Cook until the bottom is set but the top is still slightly runny.
Place a large plate over the skillet and quickly flip the tortilla.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Cocido Madrileño
ingredients: 1 head romanesco broccoli, cut into florets
instructions: Cook soaked chickpeas in a large pot with water until tender.
In a separate pot, brown the pork and beef with onions and garlic.
Add carrots, celery, and wine to the meat mixture.
Simmer the meat for 2 hours until tender.
Add the chorizo and morcilla to the meat broth.
Combine the meat broth with the cooked chickpeas.
Add romanesco and green beans to the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with the broth, chickpeas, meat, and vegetables.

title: Croquetas de Jamón
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute to make a roux.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in chopped ham, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Cool the mixture slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Shape the mixture into small cylinders or balls.
Roll each piece in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry croquetas until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and rabbit, cook until browned on all sides, then remove.
In the same pan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in paprika and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return the meat to the pan and add warm stock, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Add green beans and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes.
Add peas and cook for another 10 minutes until rice is tender but firm.
Remove from heat, cover with a clean cloth, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Boil sliced potatoes and onions in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain well and let cool slightly.
Beat eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Mix the cooked potatoes, onions, and eggs together in a large bowl.
Heat 40g of olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Pour in half of the egg mixture and spread evenly.
Cook until the bottom is set but the top is still slightly runny, about 3-4 minutes.
Place a heat-proof plate over the pan and quickly flip the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the pan, pour the remaining egg mixture over the top.
Cook until the second side is set, then slide onto a plate.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Place tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and liquid.
Pour the mixture into a large bowl.
Whisk in olive oil, sherry vinegar, cold water, and salt to taste.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to meld.
Serve chilled in bowls, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and a slice of crusty bread.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: In a saucepan, combine milk, heavy cream, half the sugar, vanilla bean, lemon zest, and salt.
Heat gently until the mixture just begins to simmer, then remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks and the remaining sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the warm milk mixture into the egg yolks while whisking constantly to temper.
Pour the custard back into the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it coats the back of a spoon (about 170°C/340°F).
Strain the custard into individual ramekins.
Sprinkle a thin layer of sugar over the top of each custard.
Broil or caramelize the sugar until golden brown.
Serve warm or chilled, dusted with cinnamon.

title: Pulpo a la Gallega
ingredients: 1kg fresh octopus, cleaned and cut into chunks
instructions: Place the octopus in a large pot with cold water, bring to a boil, then drain immediately.
Return the octopus to the pot with fresh cold water and boil for 45-60 minutes until tender.
Transfer the octopus to a baking sheet and let it cool slightly.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Drizzle the octopus with olive oil and rub with fresh rosemary.
Roast in the oven for 10-15 minutes until the skin is crispy and slightly charred.
Season generously with sea salt and a dusting of paprika.
Slice the octopus into thick rounds and arrange on a serving platter.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/4 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp hot water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit pieces until golden on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast slightly.
Pour in the chicken stock, saffron mixture, and bring to a boil.
Return the meat to the pan and reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, then add green beans and peas.
Cook for another 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with lemon wedges and parsley before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1 cup cold water, or as needed
instructions: Place all vegetables and garlic into a blender or food processor.
Add sherry vinegar, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Blend until completely smooth, scraping down sides as needed.
Transfer mixture to a bowl and gradually add cold water until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold in bowls, garnished with croutons and sliced cucumber.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus more for cooking
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk eggs with salt until well combined.
Add sliced potatoes and onion (if using) to the eggs, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Cover and let sit for 15 minutes to soften the vegetables.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in the egg and potato mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cook undisturbed for about 4 minutes until the bottom is set and golden.
Run a spatula around the edge to loosen, then flip the tortilla using a large plate.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until set but still slightly soft in the center.
Slide onto a cutting board, slice into wedges, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Crepes (Galette Bretonne)
ingredients: Maple syrup or fruit compote for serving
instructions: In a blender, combine flour, eggs, milk, water, melted butter, vanilla, salt, and sugar.
Blend until completely smooth, then let the batter rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a non-stick crepe pan over medium heat and grease lightly with butter.
Pour a small ladle of batter into the center and tilt the pan to coat the bottom evenly.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the bottom is golden brown.
Flip carefully and cook for another 30 seconds.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter, greasing the pan as needed.
Stack the cooked crepes and serve warm with maple syrup or fruit compote.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 1 lb russet potatoes, cut into bite-sized cubes
instructions: Boil potato cubes in salted water until just tender, then drain and dry thoroughly.
In a bowl, mix flour, paprika, and salt. Dip potatoes in beaten egg, then coat in flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry potato cubes in batches until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and keep warm.
To make the sauce, combine tomato sauce, mayonnaise, smoked paprika, garlic, and cayenne in a small bowl.
Stir until smooth and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve the fried potatoes immediately, topped with the spicy mayonnaise sauce and sprinkled with parsley.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock, warm
1/2 lb chicken thigh, cut into pieces
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add rabbit and chicken; brown on all sides.
Add rice and stir to coat with oil and spices.
Pour in warm stock and saffron mixture; season with salt and pepper.
Add green beans, lima beans, and peas; do not stir again.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
Extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
instructions: Place tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, and water in a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour mixture into a large bowl.
Whisk in olive oil, sherry vinegar, salt, and cumin.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to chill.
Stir in fresh basil before serving.
Serve chilled with crusty bread, drizzled with extra virgin olive oil.

title: Jamón Ibérico con Queso Manchego
ingredients: 4 slices high-quality Jamón Ibérico de Bellota
4 slices aged Queso Manchego, room temperature
instructions: Toast the baguette slices until golden and crisp.
Drizzle toasted bread with olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt flakes.
Arrange arugula on a serving platter.
Layer slices of Jamón Ibérico and Queso Manchego on top of the bread.
Drizzle lightly with sherry vinegar and dust with smoked paprika.
Serve immediately as an appetizer or light meal.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Bring water, butter, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously until a dough forms.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Beat in eggs one at a time until smooth and glossy.
Add vanilla extract.
Pipe dough into hot oil in 4-inch lengths.
Fry until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Remove with a slotted spoon and roll in cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Meanwhile, melt chocolate and heavy cream together to make hot chocolate.
Serve churros with a cup of hot chocolate.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, divided
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add potato and onion slices; fry until soft and lightly browned.
Drain excess oil, leaving a thin layer in the pan.
Beat eggs with salt and optional water in a bowl.
Pour egg mixture over the potatoes in the pan.
Cook undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is set.
Run a spatula around the edge and flip the tortilla carefully.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until fully cooked.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Season and sear the chicken and rabbit until browned, then remove.
Add onion and bell pepper to the pan; cook until soft.
Stir in grated tomato and cook until the raw taste disappears.
Return meat to the pan and add the rinsed rice.
Toast the rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Dissolve saffron in a splash of warm broth and pour over the rice.
Add remaining broth, chicken stock, shrimp, green beans, and peas.
Simmer without stirring for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Soak the stale bread in water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture.
Place tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a blender.
Add the soaked bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, and cumin.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours to let flavors meld.
Serve cold, optionally garnished with olive oil swirls and diced vegetables.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Drain excess oil, leaving a thin layer in the pan.
Pour the beaten eggs over the potato and onion mixture.
Cook on medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is set.
Run a spatula around the edge to loosen, then flip the tortilla using a plate.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until fully set.
Slide onto a plate, let cool slightly, and slice into wedges.

title: Pulpo a la Gallega
ingredients: 1 whole octopus, cleaned and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Boil the octopus in salted water with vinegar for 45-60 minutes until tender.
Drain the octopus and let it cool completely.
Arrange the octopus pieces on a large baking sheet or wooden board.
Drizzle generously with olive oil over the octopus.
Sprinkle with paprika, sea salt flakes, and black pepper.
Garnish with thinly sliced red onions on top.
Serve immediately at room temperature as a tapa.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: Combine milk, heavy cream, cinnamon stick, lemon zest, and salt in a saucepan.
Heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer, then remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks, granulated sugar, vanilla, and ground cinnamon until pale.
Slowly pour the hot milk mixture into the egg mixture while whisking constantly to prevent curdling.
Strain the mixture back into the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring frequently, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (about 8 minutes).
Divide the custard into six shallow baking dishes.
Sprinkle a thin layer of extra sugar over the top of each dish.
Place under a broiler for 2-3 minutes until the sugar melts and turns golden brown.
Cool to room temperature and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and rabbit, cooking until browned on all sides.
Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic, sautéing until softened.
Stir in rice and paprika, coating grains evenly.
Pour in hot stock and add bay leaf, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes.
Add green beans and peas, continuing to cook until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 6 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and seeded
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a blender.
Blend until smooth, then strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture.
In a separate bowl, whisk together olive oil, vinegar, water, salt, and pepper.
Slowly drizzle the oil mixture into the blended vegetables while blending on low.
Stir in chopped parsley and season to taste.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 4 cups thinly sliced potatoes, boiled until tender
2 cups finely chopped onions, sautéed until soft
instructions: Boil sliced potatoes with a pinch of salt until very tender.
Sauté chopped onions in olive oil until translucent.
Beat eggs with salt and mix in the cooked potatoes and onions.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat with 1/4 cup olive oil.
Pour in the egg mixture and let it cook undisturbed for 3 minutes.
Flip the tortilla carefully using two plates or a large spatula.
Cook the other side for another 2-3 minutes until golden.
Slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Combine water, butter, sugar, salt, and vanilla in a saucepan; bring to a boil.
Whisk in flour all at once and stir vigorously until dough forms a ball.
Let dough cool slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Fill a pastry bag with the dough and cut off the tip with a star tip.
Heat oil to 375°F (190°C) in a deep fryer or heavy pot.
Pipe small lengths of dough into the hot oil, turning occasionally.
Fry until golden brown and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Roll churros in melted chocolate and serve immediately.

title: Rabo de Toro
ingredients: 2 lbs beef oxtail, cut into 4-inch pieces
instructions: Season oxtail pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown oxtail in olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove meat and add vegetables to the pot; sauté until softened.
Stir in wine and let it simmer until reduced by half.
Return meat to the pot and add stock, paprika, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 3-4 hours until meat is extremely tender.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in water
instructions: Season the chicken and rabbit with salt and pepper, then sear in olive oil until browned.
Remove meat and sauté the red bell pepper and garlic in the same oil until soft.
Add the grated tomatoes and cook until the liquid evaporates and it forms a paste.
Return the meat to the pan and stir in the rice, coating each grain.
Pour in the hot chicken stock mixed with saffron water and bring to a boil.
Arrange the green beans and peas around the meat, then reduce heat to low.
Cook uncovered for about 20 minutes without stirring until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
instructions: Place tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a food processor.
Pulse until roughly chopped but not pureed, leaving some texture.
Transfer mixture to a bowl and add olive oil, sherry vinegar, and cold water.
Stir well and season generously with salt.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve cold, garnished with croutons and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook until soft and translucent, about 10 minutes.
Add the potato slices and cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften, about 15 minutes.
Season the potato and onion mixture with salt.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs and remaining olive oil until well combined.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes in the skillet and spread evenly.
Cook over low-medium heat for about 5 minutes until the bottom is set.
Carefully run a spatula around the edges, then invert a plate over the pan.
Flip the tortilla onto the plate, slide it back into the pan, and cook the other side for 3-4 minutes.
Slide onto a serving plate, garnish with parsley, and let cool slightly before cutting.

title: Jamón Ibérico con Queso Manchego
instructions: Arrange the toasted bread slices on a serving platter.
Layer the cured Jamón Ibérico slices over the bread.
Top each slice of ham with a slice of Queso Manchego.
Place the tomato slices alongside the ham and cheese.
Drizzle the entire arrangement with extra virgin olive oil.
Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig.
Serve immediately at room temperature.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 2 tablespoons tomato sauce, mixed with 1 teaspoon vinegar and 1/2 teaspoon sugar for the brava sauce
instructions: Parboil the potato cubes in salted water until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Drain and toss with a little olive oil to prevent sticking.
Heat olive oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 4-5 minutes.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
In a small bowl, whisk together flour, garlic, paprika, cumin, salt, and water to make a smooth batter.
Heat a separate pan with a little oil and fry the batter in small spoonfuls until golden.
Serve the crispy potatoes immediately with the spicy tomato sauce and paprika sprinkled on top.

title: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and rabbit, browning on all sides.
Add garlic and bell pepper, cooking for 2 minutes.
Stir in rice and toast for 1 minute.
Pour in stock, saffron, and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes without stirring.
Add green beans and peas for the last 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
instructions: Place all vegetables, garlic, and bread crumbs in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Transfer mixture to a large bowl.
Whisk in olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Stir well before serving chilled.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add onion and potatoes, frying until soft but not browned.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour beaten eggs over the vegetables.
Cook slowly until eggs are set but still moist.
Run a spatula around the edge, then flip the tortilla.
Cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Bring water, butter, salt, and sugar to a boil in a saucepan.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously until a dough forms.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Fold in beaten eggs one at a time until smooth.
Pipe dough into hot oil in 4-inch lengths.
Fry until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Melt chocolate chips with heavy cream until smooth.
Roll churros in sugar and cinnamon.
Serve immediately with chocolate dipping sauce.

title: Albóndigas a la Madrileña
instructions: Soak breadcrumbs in milk for 5 minutes.
Mix ground meats, soaked breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, egg, salt, and pepper.
Form into 1-inch meatballs.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown meatballs on all sides.
Remove meatballs and set aside.
In the same pot, add ground beef for sauce with onion and garlic.
Cook until beef is browned.
Stir in tomato sauce, water, and paprika.
Return meatballs to the pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 cup green peas, fresh or frozen
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and rabbit, searing until browned on all sides.
Stir in onion and garlic, cooking until softened.
Add paprika and saffron, stirring for 1 minute to release aroma.
Pour in warm chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add rice, spreading it evenly to form a thin layer.
Arrange green beans and peas on top of the rice.
Cook undisturbed for 10 minutes without stirring.
Reduce heat to low and cook for another 10-15 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes to form the socarrat crust.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 6 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup stale white bread, crusts removed
instructions: Place bread in a bowl and cover with warm water to soften.
Drain the bread and squeeze out excess water.
Combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, and cumin in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Chill the soup in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold over ice cubes, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil if desired.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Bring water, butter, and salt to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Remove from heat and gradually whisk in flour until a dough forms.
Cover and let rest for 5 minutes to cool slightly.
Beat in eggs one at a time until the dough is smooth and thick.
Attach a star tip to a piping bag and fill with the churro dough.
Heat oil in a deep fryer to 375°F (190°C).
Pipe churros into the hot oil in long strips, cutting them into 3-inch pieces.
Fry until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Drain on paper towels.
Roll warm churros in cocoa powder and sugar mixture.
Serve immediately.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 2 lbs Russet potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss potato wedges with olive oil, salt, paprika, cayenne, and garlic powder.
Spread on a baking sheet and bake for 25 minutes, flipping halfway.
Meanwhile, mix tomato sauce, paprika, cayenne, and water in a small bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, vinegar, paprika, and cayenne in another bowl for the brava sauce.
Remove potatoes from oven and let cool slightly.
Serve hot potato wedges with tomato sauce and brava sauce on the side.
Garnish with lemon wedges.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Soak potato and onion slices in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add potatoes and onions, cooking until tender but not browned, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Beat eggs in a bowl and mix with the cooked potato-onion mixture.
Pour half the mixture into the skillet and cook on low heat for 3 minutes.
Carefully flip the tortilla using a plate, then cook the other side for 2-3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let cool slightly before slicing.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 1/4 cup water
instructions: Brown the chicken and rabbit in olive oil in a large paella pan over medium-high heat.
Remove meat and set aside; sauté the garlic in the remaining oil until fragrant.
Return meat to the pan and add the rinsed rice, stirring to coat.
Pour in the warm chicken stock and saffron water, bring to a boil.
Arrange the green beans around the edges and add peas, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer undisturbed for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, cover with a clean kitchen towel, and let rest for 5 minutes before serving with lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
1/2 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Soak the stale bread in a little water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Place all vegetables, bread, garlic, salt, vinegar, and oil in a food processor.
Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or vinegar if necessary.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve cold, optionally garnished with diced cucumber or a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 2 lbs russet potatoes, cut into large cubes
instructions: Boil potato cubes in salted water until just tender but not falling apart, about 8 minutes.
Drain and pat dry thoroughly.
Mix flour, paprika, salt, pepper, cold water, and olive oil to form a smooth batter.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Dip potatoes in batter and fry in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 4-5 minutes.
In a small saucepan, combine tomato sauce, hot sauce, and saffron; simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve hot potatoes immediately with the spicy tomato sauce on the side.

title: Tortilla Española
ingredients: 3 large potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Slice potatoes and onions very thinly using a mandoline.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat until shimmering.
Add potatoes and onions, cover, and cook until very soft, about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and let the mixture cool slightly in the pan.
Beat eggs with salt in a bowl, then pour over the potato mixture.
Cook over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is set but the top is still slightly wet.
Place a large plate over the pan, invert the pan onto the plate, and slide the tortilla onto the plate.
Flip the tortilla back into the pan if desired for a crispier second side, or serve soft.

title: Churros con Chocolate
instructions: Combine water, butter, salt, and flour in a saucepan; bring to a boil while whisking.
Remove from heat and quickly stir in flour to form a smooth dough.
Let dough cool slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Transfer dough to a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Pipe churros into the hot oil and fry in batches until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Drain on paper towels and roll immediately in the cinnamon-sugar mixture.
For chocolate sauce, mix cocoa powder, 1/4 cup hot water, and cream in a saucepan; simmer until thick.
Serve warm churros with the chocolate sauce for dipping.

title: Cocido Madrileño
ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed beans (chickpeas, white beans, and kidney beans), soaked overnight
2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Rinse the soaked beans and chickpeas, then place them in a large pot with cold water.
Add the chicken, pork shoulder, and ribs to the pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery, then continue simmering for another 2 hours.
Add the chickpeas and cook until tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the cabbage and cook for 15 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper, then ladle the broth over the torn baguette to serve.

title: Tortilla Española
instructions: Slice the potatoes and onions thinly and boil in salted water until tender but not mushy.
Drain the potatoes and onions and let them cool slightly.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt.
In a large frying pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and onions, then pour the egg mixture over them.
Cook on medium-low heat, covering the pan, until the bottom is set.
Run a spatula around the edges, then flip the tortilla carefully using a plate.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until golden and set, then let it rest before slicing.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 cup stale bread, soaked in water
instructions: Soak the stale bread in water until soft, then squeeze out excess water.
Place the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, and bread in a blender.
Add the olive oil, vinegar, and cold water.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust salt or vinegar as needed.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve cold, optionally garnished with croutons or a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Patatas Bravas
instructions: Boil the potato wedges in salted water until almost tender, then drain and let them dry.
Mix the flour, paprika, and salt in a bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a deep fryer or deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each potato wedge in the flour mixture and fry until golden and crispy, about 4-5 minutes.
For the sauce, mix tomato paste, water, sugar, cayenne pepper, and salt in a small pot.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until thickened.
Serve the hot fries with the spicy tomato sauce on the side.

title: Churros con Chocolate
ingredients: 1/4 cup lard or vegetable oil for frying
instructions: In a saucepan, bring water, butter, sugar, and salt to a boil.
Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously until the dough forms a ball.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly, then mix in the baking powder and beaten egg.
Fill a piping bag with the dough and cut the tip with a star-shaped cutter.
Heat the oil to 375°F (190°C) in a deep pan.
Pipe the dough into the hot oil and fry until golden brown, turning occasionally.
For the chocolate sauce, heat the milk with sugar until simmering, then stir in the chopped chocolate.
Once melted, add cinnamon and pour into a bowl to serve with the churros.

title: Cocido Madrileño
ingredients: 1 kg mixed beans (carraca, canari, garbanzos, and red kidney), soaked overnight
1 kg pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and place them in a large pot with plenty of cold water.
Add the pork shoulder, pork ribs, onion, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Add the chorizo and morcilla, continue cooking for 20 minutes.
Add carrots, potatoes, and tomatoes, cook for another 30 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Season with salt and pepper, let it rest for 15 minutes before serving with the broth.

title: Patatas Bravas
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, cut into bite-sized cubes
1 tsp smoked paprika (pimentón de la Vera)
For the sauce: 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 cups beef stock, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp smoked paprika
instructions: Boil the potato cubes in salted water until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Dry the potatoes thoroughly and toss with flour, eggs, water, garlic, paprika, cumin, and salt to coat evenly.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C (350°F).
Fry the potatoes in batches until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
To make the sauce, combine tomato paste, stock, vinegar, sugar, and paprika in a small saucepan.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes until thickened, then pour over the hot potatoes.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 6 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1 green bell pepper, seeded and chopped
instructions: Place all vegetables, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, and water into a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and more vinegar if needed.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let flavors meld and the soup chill.
Serve very cold in bowls, garnished with a drizzle of oil and served with crusty bread on the side.

title: Pollo al Ajillo
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and shallots, frying gently until fragrant and soft but not browned.
Add red pepper flakes and stir for 10 seconds.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down into the pan and cook for 5 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and cook for another 5 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken from pan, spoon some oil over it, and sprinkle with lemon juice and parsley before serving.

title: Huevos Rotos
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato sauce, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper; simmer for 5 minutes.
Crack the eggs directly into the simmering sauce, one at a time.
Cover the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes until the whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately on top of toasted bread.

title: Fabada Asturiana
ingredients: 1 kg white beans (fava beans), soaked overnight
300 g pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and place them in a large pot with cold water.
Add the pork chunks, chorizo, and morcilla to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 3 hours until beans are tender.
Add the chopped onions, bay leaves, and broth.
Continue cooking for another 30 minutes, seasoning with salt to taste.
Remove bay leaves before serving.

title: Cocido Asturiano
instructions: Combine soaked beans, beef, and pork ribs in a large pot.
Cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 2 hours.
Add chickpeas, vegetables, garlic, and broth.
Cook covered for another 2 hours until all ingredients are tender.
Remove meat from the pot, slice it thinly, and return to the soup.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Caldet de Pato
instructions: Season the duck quarters with salt and pepper.
Brown the duck in a heavy pot with half the onions.
Add the remaining vegetables, garlic, thyme, wine, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2.5 hours.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot, and skim any fat.
Serve the duck and vegetables in the broth.

title: Papas a la Asturiana
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until just tender, about 10 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chorizo and morcilla, frying for 3 minutes until slightly crispy.
Add the garlic and paprika, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the boiled potatoes to the skillet and toss to coat.
Season with salt and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Caldo de Gallina con Pan
instructions: Place the chicken pieces in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the onion, carrots, celery, bay leaf, and garlic.
Continue cooking for another 45 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Strain the broth, remove the meat from the bones, and slice it.
Serve the broth hot with the sliced chicken and crusty bread.

title: Caldo de Patatas y Garbanzos
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeaks, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: In a large pot, bring water to a boil with onion, garlic, and chickpeaks.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour until chickpeaks are tender.
Add potatoes and paprika; cook for another 20 minutes until potatoes are soft.
Season with salt to taste and remove from heat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Pulpo a la Gallega
ingredients: 2 lb fresh octopus, cleaned and patted dry
instructions: Place octopus in a pot with cold water and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour until tender.
Boil potatoes in separate salted water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Peel potatoes while warm and slice into quarters.
Arrange potatoes and octopus on a baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, paprika, and parsley.
Roast at 400°F (200°C) for 10 minutes until potatoes are crispy.
Slice octopus tentacles and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup stale bread, crusts removed and cubed
instructions: Toast bread cubes in a dry pan until golden, then set aside.
Combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic in a blender.
Add toasted bread, olive oil, vinegar, salt, and paprika.
Blend until smooth, then strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold over ice cubes, garnished with extra olive oil and paprika.

title: Tortilla de Patatas
instructions: Fry potato slices in olive oil over medium heat until golden and tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain excess oil, leaving a thin layer in the pan.
Beat eggs with salt, pepper, and water if using.
Pour egg mixture over potatoes in the pan, spreading evenly.
Cook on medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is set.
Run a knife around the edges, flip the tortilla using a plate, and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Fideuà de Peixe
ingredients: 1 lb fish fillets, such as monkfish or cod, cut into chunks
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: In a large pot, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add pasta, turmeric, and salt; stir for 1 minute to toast slightly.
Pour in hot fish stock and soaked saffron; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 8-10 minutes until pasta is al dente.
Add fish chunks gently and cook for 3-5 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Stir in the saffron water if not already added, and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls, garnished with lemon wedges.

title: Pa amb Tomàquet
ingredients: 4 slices rustic country bread, preferably from a local mill
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden and crisp in the oven or under a broiler.
Rub each slice of warm bread generously with the cut garlic clove.
Slice the tomatoes thinly and let them sit for a few minutes to release their juices.
Spread the tomato slices over the bread, allowing the juices to soak into the crust.
Drizzle a small amount of olive oil over the top and sprinkle with salt and rosemary.
Serve immediately as an appetizer or light meal.

title: Coca de Patates
instructions: Mix flour, salt, sugar, warm water, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil to form a soft dough; let it rest for 30 minutes.
In a separate bowl, combine the grated potatoes, Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper; squeeze out excess moisture from the potatoes.
Roll the dough out into a thin circle on a floured surface.
Spread the potato and cheese mixture evenly over the dough.
Roll the dough up tightly like a jelly roll, then place it on a baking sheet.
Brush the top with olive oil and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Slice and serve warm.

title: Coca de Pinya
instructions: Combine flour, salt, sugar, warm water, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil to make a pliable dough; let it rest for 30 minutes.
In a saucepan, mix pineapple rings, 1/2 cup sugar, and cornstarch; cook over medium heat until the sauce thickens.
Roll the dough out into a rectangle on a floured surface.
Spread the pineapple sauce over the dough, leaving a border around the edges.
Fold the dough over the filling to create a pocket, sealing the edges well.
Place the coca on a baking sheet, brush with melted butter and olive oil.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15-18 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbling.

title: Fideuà
ingredients: 1 lb mixed seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari), cleaned
1 cup short-grain rice (optional, for extra texture)
instructions: Bring fish stock to a boil with saffron and garlic; simmer for 10 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté the onion until soft.
Add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the noodles and rice, stirring to coat.
Pour in the hot stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10-12 minutes until noodles are tender.
Stir in the seafood and cook for another 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Remove from heat, let it rest for 5 minutes, then serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Pan con Tomàquet
instructions: Cut the tomatoes in half and rub the cut sides generously on the bread slices.
Rub each piece of bread with the cut side of the garlic clove.
Drizzle each slice with olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt.
Top with the remaining tomato halves and scatter fresh basil leaves over the top.
Let it sit for a minute to allow the flavors to meld, then serve immediately.

title: Pintxos de Idiazabal
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden and crisp.
Drizzle olive oil over each slice and sprinkle with salt.
Layer the Idiazabal cheese on top of the toast.
Garnish each pintxo with a green olive.
Serve immediately as an appetizer.

title: Txakolina eta Txerri
ingredients: 1 kg young pork loin, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Season pork with salt and cayenne pepper, then brown on all sides.
Pour in the Txakoli wine to deglaze the pan.
Simmer until the wine reduces and the pork is tender.

title: Callos a la Asturiana
ingredients: 500g beef tripe, cleaned and cut into chunks
instructions: Blanch the tripe in boiling water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Sauté onions, garlic, and carrot in a pot until soft.
Add the tripe, beef broth, and bay leaf to the pot.
Simmer gently for 2 hours until the tripe is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Bacalao al Pil Pil
instructions: Fry the garlic slices in olive oil until golden and crispy.
Add the flaked cod to the oil and fry for 2 minutes.
Crack the eggs directly into the pan.
Lower the heat and cover with a tight lid for 10 minutes.
Stir gently to create the creamy emulsion and serve with lemon.

title: Cochinillo Asado
instructions: Rub the pig quarters generously with salt, pepper, and olive oil.
Stuff the cavity with garlic and rosemary sprigs.
Roast in a very hot oven (200°C) for the first hour.
Reduce heat to 180°C and continue roasting until the skin is crisp and meat is tender.
Baste frequently with rendered fat during the final 30 minutes.

title: Polbo á Gallega
ingredients: 1 whole squid, cleaned and tentacles separated
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat until smoking slightly.
Add sliced garlic and peppercorns, frying for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the squid tentacles first, stir for 30 seconds, then add the body.
Pour in the white wine and add thyme sprigs.
Cook uncovered for 5-7 minutes until the squid is tender but not rubbery.
Drain any excess liquid, sprinkle with salt, and serve immediately.

title: Pulpo á Gallega
instructions: Place the octopus in a pot with water and lemon wedges; bring to a boil and cook for 2 hours until tender.
Drain the octopus, reserving the cooking liquid.
Heat olive oil in a clean pan over medium heat until very hot.
Add sliced garlic, peppercorns, and rosemary, frying until the garlic is golden.
Add the cooked octopus to the pan and toss quickly to coat.
Season generously with salt and serve hot.

title: Cociña de Abonigo
ingredients: 500g pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
300g white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Brown the pork chunks in lard or oil over medium-high heat until golden.
Remove meat, then sauté onions, carrots, and garlic in the same fat until soft.
Return the meat to the pot and add the beans, potatoes, wine, water, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat and beans are very tender.
Adjust salt and pepper, remove bay leaf, and serve.

title: Empanada de Pulpo
ingredients: 500g octopus, cooked and chopped into small pieces
instructions: In a bowl, mix the chopped octopus, mashed potatoes, onion, garlic, wine, paprika, and half the olive oil.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, ice water, and a pinch of salt to make a stiff dough.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut into circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg, drizzle with remaining olive oil, and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden.

title: Caldeirada de Peixe
ingredients: 500g mixed fresh fish (mackerel, monkfish, hake), cleaned and cut into chunks
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, garlic, and green pepper until softened.
Add the potato cubes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the clams and mussels, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until they open.
Add the fish chunks and bay leaf; pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flaky.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve in the pot.

title: Paella Valenciana
