ingredients: 400g rabbit meat, cut into small pieces
1 tsp saffron threads, dissolved in 1/2 cup warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat. Season rabbit and chicken with salt and brown them well on all sides. Remove meat and set aside.
In the same pan, add onion and sauté until translucent. Add garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the rice to the pan and stir for 3-4 minutes to toast the grains lightly.
Stir in the sweet paprika and saffron mixture, coating the rice evenly.
Return the meat to the pan. Pour in the warm chicken stock gradually, ensuring the rice is submerged but not boiling vigorously.
Add the green beans and lentils. Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for about 18-20 minutes without stirring, allowing the rice to absorb the liquid.
When the liquid is almost absorbed and the rice is tender but still firm to the bite (al dente), remove the pan from heat.
Let the paella rest for 5 minutes with a lid to let the flavors meld.
Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Fideuà de Marisco
ingredients: 100g squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
1 large potato, peeled and diced small
instructions: In a deep paella pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced potato and sauté until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the onion until soft. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the fideo noodles and toast them for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden, stirring constantly.
Stir in the sweet paprika and quickly mix to coat the noodles.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble until nearly evaporated.
Add the seafood stock and return the browned potato to the pan. Bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, prawns, and squid. Reduce heat to low and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Cook until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Remove from heat, squeeze lemon zest over the top, and serve immediately.

title: Arroz a la Cubana
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent.
Add the garlic, chorizo, and ground pork. Cook until the meat is browned and the chorizo is crispy.
Stir in the paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook down until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain with the tomato sauce. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the warm stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
In the last 5 minutes of cooking, make four small wells in the rice and pour the beaten eggs into them.
Cover and cook until the eggs are set and the rice is tender.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

title: Escalivada
ingredients: 3 large zucchini, cut into thick rounds
instructions: Preheat your oven broiler or grill to high. Alternatively, use a gas stove flame or a pan with high heat.
Roast the bell peppers, onions, zucchini, and eggplant until the skins are charred and blistered on all sides. This may take 15-20 minutes.
Place the roasted vegetables in a large bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap or transfer to an airtight container to steam for 20 minutes.
Peel off the charred skin from the vegetables while they are still warm. Slice the peppers and zucchini; chop the onions and eggplant.
In a large bowl, combine the roasted vegetables, garlic cloves (peeled but not crushed), and a generous amount of salt.
Pour the extra virgin olive oil over the mixture and toss well to coat everything evenly.
Let the Escalivada rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Sprinkle with sweet paprika before serving. Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.

title: Sofrito de Verduras
ingredients: 1 large red bell pepper, finely diced
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot or paella pan, heat the olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook slowly for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are very soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and bell pepper, continuing to cook for another 5-7 minutes until the pepper is tender.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until it darkens slightly.
Add the sweet paprika and mix well to release the aroma.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in the chopped parsley.
Let the sofrito cool and rest for 30 minutes to develop its full flavor base, which can be used for stews, soups, or rice dishes.

title: Salmorejo Cordobés
ingredients: 500g ripe red tomatoes, peeled and chopped
200g stale bread, crusts removed and soaked
instructions: Blend the soaked bread, tomatoes, garlic, and a pinch of salt until completely smooth.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while blending to create a creamy emulsion.
Stir in the chopped ham and egg yolks.
Taste and adjust salt if necessary.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least two hours before serving.
Serve cold garnished with a thin slice of ham and a whole egg yolk.

title: Cocido Madrileño
ingredients: 1 head of cauliflower, cut into florets
instructions: Boil the soaked chickpeas with the beef and pork until tender, about 2 hours.
Add the chorizo and morcilla, then the onion and carrots, cooking for another 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and continue cooking until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove the solids and save the broth separately.
Add the cauliflower florets to the remaining broth and cook until soft.
Serve the broth first, followed by the chickpeas and meat, and finally the vegetables.

title: Patatas Bravas
instructions: Boil the potato wedges in salted water until just tender, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Toss the potatoes in flour, dip in beaten egg, and coat again in flour.
Heat olive oil in a deep pan and fry the potatoes until golden and crispy.
Mix the paprika with a little oil to make a thick paste for the sauce.
Combine the paprika paste with mayonnaise and minced garlic.
Drain the fried potatoes on paper towels.
Serve the potatoes with a side of the spicy mayonnaise and lemon wedges.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, garlic, and bread until very smooth.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve for a silky texture.
Slowly add the olive oil while whisking to emulsify.
Stir in the sherry vinegar and season generously with salt.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for at least four hours.
Serve very cold over ice cubes, garnished with diced cucumber and tomato.

title: Tortilla de Patatas
instructions: Heat 40g of olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook until soft, then add the potatoes and fry until golden.
Season the potatoes and onions with salt and paprika.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the remaining 40g of olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Pour the egg mixture over the fried potatoes and onions in the pan.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, then run a knife around the edges to loosen.
Flip the tortilla onto a plate, then slide it back into the pan to cook the other side.
Slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Espetos de Sardiña
ingredients: 1 large red bell pepper, sliced into rings
instructions: Soak sardines in salted water for 1 hour to remove excess blood and slime.
Drain sardines and pat them dry with paper towels.
Insert a lemon half into the cavity of each sardine and tie the fish with thyme sprigs.
Place garlic cloves, bell pepper rings, and rosemary sprigs directly into the water.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pot or deep pan.
Skim off the foam that rises to the top.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer.
Carefully slide the sardines onto two skewers to create a spit.
Place the skewered sardines over the simmering water so they are half-submerged, cooking for about 10 minutes.
Remove from water, let drain briefly, and serve immediately with the cooking juices and lemon wedges.

title: Huevos Estrellados
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide, non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the smoked paprika over the onions and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Crack the eggs directly into the skillet, spacing them out evenly.
Season the whites and yolks with salt and pepper.
Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks remain runny.
Gently swirl the pan to create small 'stars' around the yolks if desired, or just let them set slightly.
Remove from heat and immediately sprinkle with fresh parsley.
Serve hot as a tapa or side dish.

title: Guiso de Garbanzos
instructions: Drain the soaked chickpeas and rinse them thoroughly.
In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add the tomato paste and cumin seeds, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in the chickpeas and oregano.
Add the broth, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until chickpeas are very tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Let the stew thicken slightly before serving.
Garnish with a drizzle of olive oil if desired.

title: Torrijas
ingredients: 6 slices of stale bread, crusts removed
Extra sugar and cinnamon for coating
instructions: Whisk the eggs, milk, water, and vanilla together in a bowl to create a batter.
Dip each slice of bread into the batter, ensuring both sides are fully soaked.
Heat a generous amount of butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the bread slices until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove from the pan and place on paper towels to drain excess fat.
In a separate bowl, mix the sugar, flour, and cinnamon.
While the torrijas are still warm, roll them in the sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Serve immediately as a dessert or breakfast treat.

title: Chuletón de Vacuno
ingredients: 1 large T-bone or ribeye steak (Chuletón), about 1.5kg
instructions: Remove the steak from the refrigerator 1 hour before cooking to bring it to room temperature.
Pat the steak dry with paper towels and rub all over with olive oil.
Generously season both sides with coarse sea salt and cracked black pepper.
Place the steak on a wire rack over a baking sheet and let it rest in a cool place for 20 minutes.
Preheat your grill or charcoal fire to high heat.
Place the steak on the grill and sear for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, pressing down gently to ensure contact.
During the last 2 minutes, add the crushed garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the grill to infuse the meat.
Baste the steak with the melted butter and lemon juice during the final minutes of cooking.
Remove from heat and let the steak rest under foil for 10 minutes before slicing.
Slice against the grain and serve with roasted potatoes and green beans.

title: Fabes con Chorizo y Morcilla
ingredients: 1 kg dried white beans, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Sauté the chopped dried peppers and onion in olive oil until soft.
Add the garlic, chorizo, and morcilla, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Stir in the soaked beans and chicken stock.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour until beans are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.

title: Caldetón de Mariscos
ingredients: 500g mixed fresh shellfish (mussels, clams, small shrimp)
instructions: Sauté the onion, carrots, celery, and garlic in a pot with a little oil.
Add the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Pour in the fish stock, bay leaf, and parsley.
Add the shellfish and cook for 5-7 minutes until they open.
Remove the bay leaf, discard any unopened shells, and serve immediately.

title: Cocido Asturiano
instructions: Cook the chickpeas and white beans separately until tender, saving their cooking water.
In a large pot, combine the pork, chorizo, onion, and garlic with fresh water.
Add the chickpeas, beans, potatoes, and baby potatoes to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Season with salt and serve with the broth.

title: Cocido de Garbanzos con Patatas
instructions: Cook the chickpeas until tender, then drain and set aside.
In a large pot, sauté the onion and garlic with the pork and chorizo.
Add the chickpeas, potatoes, and water to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Guiso de Puerros con Chistorra
ingredients: 1 kg leeks, cleaned and sliced into rounds
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add the leeks and chistorra, stirring for 5 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate.
Add the chicken stock, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 1/4 cup warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat.
Brown the chicken and rabbit pieces, then remove them.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and bell pepper until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast slightly.
Stir in the tomatoes, saffron water, broth, salt, and pepper.
Return the meat to the pan and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes.
Add the green beans and peas, then cook until rice is tender.
Create a small hole in the center of the rice and crack the eggs into it.
Cover and let the eggs poach for 3-4 minutes until whites are set.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Gazpacho Andaluz
ingredients: 1/2 cup stale white bread, soaked in water
instructions: Soak the bread in water until soft, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, bread, and cumin in a blender.
Add olive oil and sherry vinegar while blending until smooth.
Season with salt and taste for seasoning.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold over ice cubes.

title: Frittas de Calamares
ingredients: 1 lb fresh squid, cleaned and cut into rings
instructions: Pat the squid rings dry and toss with salt and paprika.
Set up three stations: flour for dredging, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each squid ring in flour, then dip in egg, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the squid in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Tortilla de Patatas
instructions: Slice the potatoes and onions thinly.
Fry the potatoes and onions in olive oil until soft but not browned.
Drain excess oil and let the mixture cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with water and salt in a bowl.
Add the potato and onion mixture to the eggs and mix well.
Pour the mixture into a hot, oiled non-stick pan and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Flip the tortilla using a plate to cook the other side for another 5 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and slice into wedges to serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Crema Catalana
instructions: Heat the heavy cream, milk, and half of the sugar in a saucepan until simmering.
Whisk the egg yolks, remaining sugar, salt, vanilla, lemon zest, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Slowly pour the hot milk mixture into the egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return the custard to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Pour the custard into shallow baking dishes.
Sprinkle a generous layer of sugar over the top of each dish.
Place under a broiler until the sugar melts and turns golden brown.
Garnish with a cinnamon stick and serve chilled.

title: Pa amb tomàquet
ingredients: 4 slices rustic Catalan bread, day-old preferred
instructions: Rub each slice of bread generously with a cut clove of garlic until aromatic.
Toast the bread slices in a pan or oven until golden and crisp.
Slice the tomato thinly and rub the cut side over the toasted bread, or spread the slices on top.
Drizzle generously with high-quality extra virgin olive oil.
Season lightly with salt and sprinkle with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Suquet de Peix
ingredients: 500g mixed white fish fillets (sea bream, monkfish)
1 teaspoon saffron threads, dissolved in warm water
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté the leek, onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add the tomato sauce and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the white wine and let it reduce slightly.
Pour in the fish stock and the dissolved saffron; bring to a simmer.
Add the fish fillets gently to the broth, ensuring they are mostly submerged.
Simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes until the fish is just cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot in deep bowls.

title: Coca de Patates
ingredients: Olive oil for frying or baking
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and melted lard in a large bowl; gradually add water to form a soft dough.
Gently fold in the grated potatoes and breadcrumbs until the mixture is uniform.
Shape the mixture into a log or place it in a greased baking dish.
Brush the top with the beaten egg.
Fry the log in olive oil until golden and crispy on the outside, then slice to serve, OR bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Escalivada
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place the peppers, onion, and zucchini directly on the oven rack or on a baking sheet with a little oil.
Roast until the skins are charred, blistered, and the vegetables are very tender (about 25-30 minutes).
Remove vegetables and place them in a sealed bag or bowl to steam and cool.
Peel off the charred skins from the peppers and onion.
Slice the vegetables and arrange them on a plate, drizzle generously with olive oil, and sprinkle with salt.

title: Brasat de Cordera
instructions: Season the lamb cubes with salt and pepper, then sear them in a heavy pot until browned on all sides.
Remove the meat and set aside; in the same pot, sauté the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with the white wine.
Return the meat to the pot, add the stock and bay leaf, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours until the lamb is falling apart.
Remove the bay leaf, adjust seasoning, and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Pintxos de Idiazabal
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet.
Top each slice with a tomato slice, then a piece of Idiazabal cheese.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and sprinkle with garlic, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 10 minutes until cheese melts and bread is golden.
Serve immediately as a tapas snack.

title: Bacalao al Pil-Pil
ingredients: 500g dried cod (bacalao), soaked and desalted for 3 days
4 anchovy fillets, dissolved in a little water
instructions: Fry the minced garlic in olive oil over low heat until very pale gold.
Stir in the dissolved anchovies and cook until the sauce emulsifies and thickens.
Add the cod pieces gently to the sauce, being careful not to break them.
Cook on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally to coat the fish.
Remove from heat, stir in fresh parsley, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Txistorria with Chimichurri
instructions: Grill the txistorria over charcoal or high heat until well charred and cooked through.
While grilling, combine parsley, onion, garlic, oregano, vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Whisk the mixture until it forms a loose sauce.
Slice the cooked sausage into rounds.
Serve the sausage warm with a generous spoonful of chimichurri on the side.

title: Marmitako
ingredients: 1 kg fresh tuna, cut into chunks
1 can (400g) of tuna in olive oil
Salt and black pepper to taste
Extra virgin olive oil for finishing
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the green pepper and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaf, and water; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Gently fold in the fresh tuna chunks and the canned tuna from the oil.
Simmer for another 5 minutes without boiling vigorously.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and drizzle with extra olive oil before serving.

title: Gazpacho with Egg Yolk
ingredients: 1 kg ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
instructions: Place all vegetables, garlic, bread, oil, vinegar, and salt in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or vinegar if needed.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Before serving, drop the hard-boiled egg yolks into individual bowls of gazpacho.
Serve cold with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil on top.

title: Polbo á Gallega
ingredients: 1 kg fresh squid, cleaned and cut into rings
instructions: Boil the baby potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot.
Add the squid rings and a generous amount of coarse sea salt.
Stir gently to coat everything in salt.
Cover the pot and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally.
Drain any excess water and sprinkle with fresh black pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil just before serving.

title: Fideuà
instructions: Soak the fideos in water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the squid and cook for 2 minutes, then add mackerel and cook another minute.
Pour in the fish stock with saffron and bring to a boil.
Add the drained noodles, peas, shrimp, and butter.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until liquid is absorbed and noodles are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Paella Valenciana
ingredients: 300g short-grain rice like Bomba or Calasparra
instructions: Sear the chicken and rabbit in lard until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Return meat to pan, add rice, and stir to coat with fat.
Pour in broth with saffron, rosemary, and peas.
Arrange chicken, rabbit, and broad beans on top of the rice.
Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, then reduce heat to low.
Cook for another 10-12 minutes until rice is tender and socarrat forms.
Stir in chicken liver in the last 3 minutes if using, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Arroz al Horno
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Sauté chicken, onion, and garlic in oil until chicken is cooked.
Add rice, paprika, and broth, then bring to a simmer.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, butter, and seasonings.
Transfer mixture to a baking dish and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake uncovered for 15 more minutes until crust forms.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Farrigat
ingredients: 250g short pasta like fideos or small shells
instructions: Boil broth with saffron until fragrant.
Sauté rabbit and chicken in butter until browned, then remove.
In the same pan, cook onion and garlic until soft.
Add tomatoes, green beans, peas, and rice to the pan, stirring well.
Return meat to pan and pour in the saffron broth.
Add the pasta and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook until liquid is absorbed and pasta is tender, then serve immediately.

title: Fideuà de Marisco
instructions: Soak the fideos in water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the squid and cook for 2 minutes, then add mackerel and cook another minute.
Pour in the fish stock with saffron and bring to a boil.
Add the drained noodles, peas, shrimp, and butter.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until liquid is absorbed and noodles are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown chicken in lard in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Remove chicken and set aside; deglaze pot with wine.
Add vegetables, garlic, and bouquet garni to the pot.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir to combine.
Return chicken to the pot and add stock and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add pearl onions and mushrooms; simmer another 20 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 head garlic, peeled and halved horizontally
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper.
Brown beef in butter in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove beef and set aside; sprinkle flour over pot and stir.
Add onion, carrots, and garlic to the flour and cook for 5 minutes.
Return beef to the pot and add wine and stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours.
Add bay leaf, thyme, and parsley; simmer another 30 minutes.
Add pearl onions, mushrooms, and bacon lardons; simmer 15 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Add eggplant and cook for 5 minutes.
Add zucchini and bell peppers; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, salt, pepper, basil, and oregano.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in fresh parsley and butter.
Serve hot or at room temperature.

title: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Line pie crust with parchment paper and fill with pie weights.
Bake crust for 10 minutes, then remove weights and parchment.
Sprinkle bacon into the crust.
Whisk together cream, eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Pour mixture over bacon in the crust.
Sprinkle Gruyere cheese on top.
Bake for 35 minutes until set.
Let cool for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Cassoulet
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Sauté pancetta in a large pot until golden.
Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir.
Add wine and stir to combine.
Add chicken stock, bay leaf, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add pork belly, duck confit, sausage, and beans.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours.
Transfer to a baking dish and bake for 30 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Sear the chicken pieces in a large Dutch oven until browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
Cook the bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp; remove with a slotted spoon.
Sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms until tender and browned.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to coat the vegetables, then gradually whisk in the red wine and chicken stock.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot; add thyme and parsley.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the chicken is tender.
Remove herbs, stir in tomato paste, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Whisk in butter off the heat and season with salt and pepper.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt and pepper; sear them in a heavy pot until browned; remove and set aside.
Cook the bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp; remove with a slotted spoon.
Sauté the onions, carrots, and pearl onions until softened.
Add garlic and mushrooms, cooking until the mushrooms release their moisture.
Stir in flour to coat the vegetables, then gradually whisk in the red wine and beef stock.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot; add thyme, bay leaves, and tomato paste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer low and slow for 2.5 to 3 hours until the beef is falling apart.
Remove herbs, stir in tomato paste, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Whisk in butter off the heat and season with salt and pepper.

title: Ratatouille Provençale
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and arrange the eggplant and zucchini slices in a single layer.
Drizzle the vegetables with half the olive oil, salt, and pepper; bake for 20 minutes.
While vegetables bake, heat remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes and bell peppers; cook until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens.
Stir in the roasted vegetables, vegetable stock, basil, and thyme.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and flavors are melded.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste before serving.

title: Cassoulet
instructions: Soak white beans in water overnight; drain and rinse.
Season pork and duck legs with salt and pepper; brown them in a heavy Dutch oven; remove and set aside.
Cook the bacon in the pot until crisp; remove with a slotted spoon.
Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in the bacon fat until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to coat the vegetables, then gradually whisk in the chicken stock and tomato paste.
Return the pork, duck, and bacon to the pot; add thyme and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the soaked beans and remaining stock; cover and simmer for another 1.5 hours until everything is tender.
Whisk in butter off the heat and season with salt and pepper.

title: Escargots de Bourgogne
ingredients: 12 large fresh snails or 12 frozen escargot shells
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Clean the snail shells thoroughly; if using frozen, thaw and clean them.
In a small bowl, mix softened butter, minced garlic, parsley, chives, thyme, nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.
Stuff the butter mixture into each clean snail shell.
Place the stuffed shells in a baking dish and top with a slice of lemon.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the butter is melted and bubbling.
Garnish with fresh parsley and thyme sprigs before serving hot.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the bacon in a large heavy pot and remove.
Sauté the onions, carrots, and garlic in the bacon fat until softened.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Add the chicken pieces, pearl onions, and mushrooms; cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in butter before serving.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, then brown in batches in a Dutch oven; set aside.
Render the bacon in the same pot until crisp; remove and set aside with the beef.
Sauté pearl onions and carrots in the bacon fat until lightly browned.
Stir in flour and tomato paste, then add the wine and stock; scrape up browned bits.
Return beef, bacon, thyme, bay leaves, and garlic to the pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Add mushrooms and simmer 20 more minutes until liquid reduces slightly.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, and onion with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet and roast for 25 minutes.
In a large pot, sauté garlic in remaining oil until fragrant.
Add roasted vegetables and chopped tomatoes; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in basil and thyme; adjust seasoning and serve warm topped with pine nuts.

title: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, plus extra for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, salt, and optional cornstarch until pale.
Heat cream and vanilla bean in a saucepan until just simmering; remove and discard bean.
Slowly pour hot cream into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Strain custard into a heatproof bowl and divide into ramekins.
Place ramekins in a baking dish, fill with hot water to halfway up sides.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until centers are just set.
Chill completely, then sprinkle sugar on top and burn with a torch before serving.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat; sauté onions until golden brown.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually add wine and stock.
Bring to a simmer, then stir in heavy cream and season with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Pour soup into a baking dish and top with toasted bread slices.
Sprinkle with Gruyère and Parmesan cheeses.
Broil in oven until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
4 tablespoons butter, cold, cut into cubes
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a Dutch oven with a little oil, then set aside.
Cook the bacon in the same pot until crisp, then remove.
Sauté the mushrooms and garlic in the bacon fat until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste, wine, stock, bay leaves, and bouquet garni; bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
Remove the bouquet garni, season with salt and pepper, and stir in the cold butter cubes one by one until melted and glossy.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, then brown it in batches in olive oil in a large pot.
Remove the beef and sauté the bacon lardons until crispy.
Add the carrots, pearl onions, mushrooms, and garlic to the pot and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, wine, stock, bay leaves, and thyme; return the beef to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 3 hours until the meat is falling apart.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes and let them sit for 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil and sauté the onions and garlic until soft.
Add the bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes, then add the zucchini and eggplant.
Pour in the tomatoes, add the herbes de Provence, salt, and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the remaining olive oil and the fresh basil just before serving.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onions slowly for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the sugar, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the beef stock and bay leaf, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and serve in bowls.
Top each bowl with a slice of French bread and sprinkle generously with Gruyère cheese before broiling until bubbly.

title: Crêpes
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, and eggs until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the milk, water, melted butter, and vanilla extract until the batter is thin and lump-free.
Let the batter rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Pour a ladle of batter into the center, tilting the pan to spread it evenly.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the edges lift, then flip and cook for another minute before stacking.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in bacon fat over medium-high heat; remove and set aside.
Sauté bacon in the same pot until crispy, then add onions and mushrooms until browned.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for another minute.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaves; return chicken to the pot.
Simmer covered for 1 hour until chicken is tender.
Whisk flour with cold butter to create a paste, then stir into the sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce before serving.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into cubes
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, then sear in batches in a large pot until browned.
Remove beef and sauté onions, carrots, and mushrooms until golden.
Add garlic and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot and add red wine, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in beef stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer gently for 2 to 2.5 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Whisk flour with cold butter to make a paste, stir into the stew.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken before serving.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cooking until soft.
Add eggplant and cook for 5 minutes until edges brown.
Add zucchini and bell peppers, cooking until tender-crisp.
Stir in tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil.
Serve hot as a main dish or side.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook slowly for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in stock and wine until smooth.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Season with salt, white pepper, and parsley.
Divide soup into bowls and sprinkle generously with Gruyère cheese.
Broil in the oven until cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a saucepan, heat cream, vanilla, and salt until it just begins to simmer.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks and 1/2 cup sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Divide the mixture into ramekins.
Place ramekins in a roasting pan and fill the pan with hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until the custards are set but still slightly jiggly.
Cool completely, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle each custard with granulated sugar and caramelize with a kitchen torch before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the bacon lardons in a large Dutch oven and remove with a slotted spoon.
Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper and brown them in the same pot.
Remove the chicken and set aside; add shallots and garlic to the pot and sauté until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the wine and chicken stock until smooth.
Add the tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaves, then return the chicken and bacon to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour or until chicken is tender.
Add mushrooms in the last 20 minutes of cooking.
Remove bay leaves, stir in the butter, and adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 lb carrots, cut into large chunks
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt and pepper and brown them in oil in a large pot.
Remove beef and brown the bacon lardons in the same pot, then remove bacon as well.
Sauté the pearl onions and garlic in the pot until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the wine and beef stock.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot, add carrots, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, cover, and transfer to a preheated 325°F oven.
Braise for 3 to 4 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaves, stir in the butter, and serve hot.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss eggplant, zucchini, tomatoes, and peppers with olive oil, oregano, basil, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Spread the vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast for 30 minutes, stirring halfway through.
Meanwhile, sauté the onion and garlic in a large skillet until soft.
Add the roasted vegetables to the skillet and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, garnish with fresh basil, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 3 large apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a heavy-bottomed skillet, melt butter over medium heat and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Arrange apple slices in concentric circles in the skillet, sugar-side up.
Bake for 25 minutes until apples are tender and caramel is bubbly.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface and place it over the apples.
Brush the edges of the pastry with beaten egg.
Carefully invert the skillet onto a serving plate.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a saucepan, heat the cream with the vanilla bean and seeds until just simmering.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, granulated sugar, and salt until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the egg mixture, whisking constantly to temper the eggs.
Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve into a heatproof bowl.
Pour the custard into six ramekins.
Place ramekins in a roasting pan and fill the pan with hot water until halfway up the sides.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes until centers are slightly wobbly.
Chill thoroughly, then sprinkle superfine sugar over the top and caramelize with a torch or under a broiler.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a large pot with the bacon lardons until golden.
Remove chicken and bacon, then sauté mushrooms and pearl onions until softened.
Add garlic and tomato paste, stir for 1 minute.
Return chicken and bacon to the pot, pour in the red wine.
Add bay leaves and thyme, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour until chicken is tender.
In a separate bowl, mix flour and butter to make a roux.
Stir the roux into the stew to thicken, cook for 5 more minutes.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot with the bacon lardons until deeply browned.
Remove meat and bacon, then sauté carrots and pearl onions until softened.
Add garlic and tomato paste, stir for 1 minute.
Return meat and bacon to the pot, pour in the red wine.
Add bay leaves and thyme, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2.5 hours until beef is very tender.
In a separate bowl, mix flour and butter to make a roux.
Stir the roux and beef broth into the stew to thicken, cook for 10 more minutes.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes.
In a large pot, heat remaining olive oil and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add roasted vegetables, diced tomatoes, and cherry tomatoes to the pot.
Stir in tomato paste (if using) or just the fresh tomatoes, then add basil and oregano.
Simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then garnish with fresh basil.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
ingredients: 4 slices French bread, cut into triangles
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, melt 4 tbsp butter over medium heat and sauté onions until very soft and golden (about 20 minutes).
Add beef broth, white wine, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat and cook uncovered for 30 minutes until thickened.
Remove bay leaf, season with salt and white pepper, and divide into bowls.
Place bowls in a baking dish, top each with bread triangles.
Drizzle melted butter over the bread and sprinkle generously with Gruyère cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browned.

title: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, plus extra for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a saucepan, heat heavy cream with the cinnamon stick until it just begins to simmer.
Remove from heat, discard cinnamon stick, and stir in vanilla extract.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 1/2 cup sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the egg mixture while whisking constantly to temper the eggs.
Strain the mixture into a heatproof bowl.
Pour the custard into ramekins and place them in a roasting pan.
Pour hot water into the roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until the center is just set.
Chill completely, then sprinkle sugar on top and caramelize with a torch before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.5 kg), cut into pieces
instructions: Sear chicken pieces in a heavy pot with butter until golden brown.
Remove chicken and brown bacon lardons in the same pot.
Add pearl onions and mushrooms, cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, thyme, and parsley.
Return chicken to the pot, add wine and stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until chicken is tender.
Remove herbs and serve hot.

title: Ratatouille
ingredients: 2 yellow summer squash, sliced into rounds
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season eggplant with salt, let sit for 15 minutes, then rinse and dry.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add eggplant, cooking until browned, then remove.
Add bell peppers and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add zucchini, summer squash, garlic, and herbes de Provence.
Stir in tomatoes and chopped eggplant.
Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with basil before serving.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, sear in butter until browned.
Remove beef and brown bacon lardons in the same pot.
Add carrots, pearl onions, and mushrooms, cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return beef to the pot, add wine and stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours.
Remove herbs, adjust seasoning, and serve with crusty bread.

title: Crème Brûlée
instructions: Heat cream with vanilla bean in a saucepan until just simmering.
Whisk egg yolks with granulated sugar and salt until pale.
Temper eggs by slowly pouring warm cream into egg mixture while whisking.
Strain custard into a heatproof bowl.
Pour custard into ramekins and bake in a water bath at 325°F (160°C) for 30-35 minutes.
Chill thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle superfine sugar on top and caramelize with a torch before serving.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook sliced onions slowly for 20 minutes until very soft and golden.
Add garlic and thyme, cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine and let it reduce by half.
Add beef stock and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and mustard.
Ladle into bowls, top generously with Gruyère cheese.
Broil until cheese is bubbly and browned, serve with baguette.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (approx. 1.5 kg), cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon lardons in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions and carrots until lightly browned.
Return chicken to the pot and sprinkle flour over everything.
Stir in the red wine, chicken stock, garlic, thyme, and rosemary.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for another 10 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in butter and adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until soft.
Add eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, and basil.
Season with salt and pepper, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Uncover, increase heat, and cook until liquid reduces and vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 bottles dry red wine (1.5 liters total)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper.
Brown the bacon lardons in a Dutch oven; remove and set aside.
Brown beef cubes in batches in the same pot; remove and set aside.
Sauté pearl onions and carrots in the pot until browned.
Return beef and bacon to the pot.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and vegetables; stir well.
Stir in tomato paste, garlic, thyme, and rosemary.
Pour in the red wine and beef stock.
Cover, bring to a simmer, and cook in a low oven (160°C/325°F) for 3 hours.
Add mushrooms during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Stir in butter before serving.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 800g Granny Smith apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
In a heavy skillet, melt 50g butter and mix with sugar until melted.
Arrange apple slices in a single layer in the skillet, overlapping slightly.
Drizzle remaining softened butter over the apples.
Roll out puff pastry and place it over the apples in the skillet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until pastry is golden and apples are tender.
Let cool for 5 minutes, then carefully invert onto a serving plate.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: 150g granulated sugar, plus more for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
In a saucepan, heat cream with the vanilla bean and seeds until just simmering.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 150g sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof dish.
Place the dish in a larger roasting pan and pour in hot water until halfway up the sides.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until the center is slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thin layer of sugar over the top and torch until caramelized.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a large pot with the bacon.
Add the garlic, pearl onions, and mushrooms; cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the red wine and bring to a simmer.
Add the bouquet garni and cover; simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until chicken is tender.
Whisk together butter and flour to make a paste, then stir into the stew to thicken.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, then sear in oil until browned.
Remove beef and sauté onions and carrots in the same pot.
Return beef to the pot, add stock, wine, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours.
In the last 30 minutes, add pearl onions and mushrooms.
Remove herbs before serving.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season eggplant with salt and let sit for 20 minutes to draw out moisture.
Sauté garlic in olive oil, then add eggplant and zucchini; cook until soft.
Add bell peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and fold in fresh basil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Cassoulet
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brown duck legs and pork belly in a large heavy pot.
Add sausages, onions, garlic, carrots, and tomato paste; cook for 10 minutes.
Add drained beans and thyme; cover with water.
Cover the pot tightly and bake for 2 hours.
Check liquid level and add more water if needed; continue baking until meat is falling apart and sauce is thick.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and add onions with sugar; cook slowly until caramelized and golden.
Stir in wine and beef stock; bring to a simmer.
Add cream and Worcestershire sauce; cook for 15 minutes.
Pour soup into a baking dish.
Top with French bread slices and generously sprinkle with Gruyère cheese.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes until bubbly and golden brown.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
In a large pot, cook bacon until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Sear chicken pieces in the bacon fat until browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add garlic and mushrooms to the pot, cooking until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return chicken and bacon to the pot along with thyme and bay leaves.
Add chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 1 hour until chicken is tender.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into 2-inch cubes
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season beef cubes with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
In a large Dutch oven, cook bacon until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Sear beef cubes in batches in the bacon fat until browned; remove and set aside.
Add garlic, pearl onions, carrots, and mushrooms to the pot, cooking until slightly softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine and bring to a simmer to reduce slightly.
Return beef and bacon to the pot along with the bouquet garni.
Add beef stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is very tender.
Remove bouquet garni and serve.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add eggplant and zucchini; cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add bell peppers and cook until softened.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes, salt, and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in fresh basil and thyme.
Cook uncovered for another 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Cassoulet
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into cubes
1 lb white beans (Cannellini or Haricot), soaked overnight
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Drain soaked beans and place in a large pot; cover with water and boil for 30 minutes.
In a separate pot, brown pork shoulder in duck fat until golden; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook bacon until crisp, then add onions, carrots, and celery; cook until softened.
Add garlic, thyme, and bay leaves; stir in white wine and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return pork to the pot, add drained beans and enough water to cover by 1 inch.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add duck legs and duck confit, stirring gently.
Cover and continue simmering for another 1 hour until beans are very tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Croque Monsieur
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Butter one side of each bread slice.
Layer ham and Swiss cheese on 4 slices of bread.
Top each with a slice of Gruyere.
Place the remaining 4 slices butter-side down on top to create sandwiches.
In a small bowl, whisk eggs and milk together.
Brush the tops of the sandwiches with the egg mixture.
Sprinkle grated Gruyere on top of the sandwiches.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until golden brown and cheese is melted.
Serve hot with mustard on the side.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until golden.
Remove chicken and sauté the bacon until crisp, then remove bacon.
Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in the bacon fat until browned.
Add garlic and thyme, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw taste.
Pour in the red wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits.
Return chicken and bacon to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until chicken is tender.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Season beef with salt and pepper, then brown in a large heavy pot.
Remove beef and cook bacon lardons until crisp.
Sauté carrots and mushrooms in the bacon fat until softened.
Stir in garlic, tomato paste, and flour, cooking for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot and add wine, stock, bay leaves, and herbs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer gently for 3 to 4 hours until meat is falling apart.

title: Crêpes
instructions: Whisk together flour, eggs, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add milk while whisking continuously to avoid lumps.
Stir in melted butter and vanilla extract.
Let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and grease with a little butter.
Pour a ladleful of batter into the center of the skillet.
Tilt and rotate the pan to spread batter thinly and evenly.
Cook until edges lift and surface looks set, then flip and cook for another minute.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add eggplant and zucchini, salt, and pepper; cook until softened.
Add bell peppers and onions; cook until vegetables are tender.
Stir in garlic, thyme, and chopped tomatoes.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and simmer for another 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Season with additional salt and pepper before serving.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add sliced onions, salt, and pepper; cook slowly until caramelized and golden.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw taste.
Pour in wine and beef stock, stirring constantly.
Add thyme and bring to a simmer until thickened.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls.
Top each bowl with a slice of bread and sprinkle generously with Gruyère.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until cheese is bubbly and browned.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a large pot with the diced bacon.
Remove chicken and bacon, then sauté onions, carrots, and garlic in the same pot.
Add mushrooms and tomatoes, cook for 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot, sprinkle flour over vegetables, and stir to coat.
Pour in the red wine, add thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until chicken is tender.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a Dutch oven with the bacon lardons.
Remove beef and bacon, then sauté carrots, onion, and garlic in the pot.
Return beef and bacon to the pot, add tomato paste, and stir.
Pour in the Burgundy wine, add thyme, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2 hours until beef is falling apart.
Add pearl onions and mushrooms, cook for another 30 minutes.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add eggplant and cook for 5 minutes, then add zucchini and squash.
Stir in tomatoes and bell pepper, season with thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

title: Croque Monsieur
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly.
Layer ham and cheese on three slices of bread.
Top with the fourth slice of bread to form a sandwich.
Brush the top with melted butter and sprinkle with grated Gruyère.
Grill the sandwich in a pan until the bottom is golden brown.
Flip and cook the other side until cheese melts and top is golden.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Brush a 9-inch ovenproof skillet with butter and sprinkle with sugar.
Arrange apple quarters cut-side down in the skillet, drizzle with melted butter.
Bake for 20 minutes until apples are soft.
Unfold puff pastry sheets and place them over the apples.
Press edges of pastry into the skillet, brush with egg wash, and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until pastry is golden brown.
Invert the tart onto a serving plate immediately after removing from oven.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the bacon in a large pot and remove it.
Sear the chicken pieces in the bacon fat until golden, then remove.
Sauté the mushrooms, onions, and garlic in the pot.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot.
Deglaze with red wine and add stock and bouquet garni.
Simmer covered for 1 hour until tender.
Make a roux with butter and flour, mix into the sauce, and simmer until thickened.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Brown the bacon in a heavy pot and remove.
Sear the beef cubes until browned on all sides, then remove.
Sauté carrots, onions, and mushrooms in the pot.
Return meat and bacon, add tomato paste and wine.
Add stock and bouquet garni, bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Simmer covered for 2.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Whisk butter and flour, stir into sauce to thicken, and simmer briefly.

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Season eggplant, zucchini, and peppers with salt and let drain for 30 minutes.
Pat vegetables dry and sauté in olive oil with garlic until soft.
Add tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes more.
Stir in basil, salt, and pepper.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with breadcrumbs.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes until bubbly.

title: Cassoulet
instructions: Brown the pork belly, duck, lamb, and sausages in lard, then remove.
Sauté onions, carrots, and garlic in the fat.
Add soaked beans, stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return meat and sausages to the pot.
Simmer covered for 2 hours until beans are tender.
Remove from heat, let rest, then serve hot.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon
instructions: Sauté onions in butter until soft and golden.
Add beef stock and wine, bring to a simmer.
Add thyme and cook for 15 minutes until onions are tender.
Strain the soup and return to pot.
Place bread slices in a baking dish, pour hot soup over them.
Top with Gruyère and cold butter cubes.
Broil until cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a large pot with the bacon until golden.
Sauté the garlic, mushrooms, and onions until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, flour, thyme, and bay leaves.
Pour in the red wine and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 1.5 hours until chicken is tender.
Remove herbs, stir in butter, and season with salt and pepper.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
instructions: Render the bacon in a heavy pot, then brown the beef cubes.
Add garlic, carrots, and onions; cook for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the meat and stir to coat.
Add red wine and bouquet garni, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours until meat is falling apart.
Add mushrooms and cook for another 20 minutes.
Stir in butter and season with salt and pepper.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add eggplant and zucchini slices; cook until tender.
Stir in bell peppers and tomatoes.
Season with salt, pepper, thyme, and basil.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
instructions: Slowly cook onions in butter until deeply caramelized and golden.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw taste.
Gradually add broth and wine, stirring constantly.
Simmer until thickened, then stir in cream and thyme.
Pour into a baking dish and top with cheese and bread chunks.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 1 lb apples (Bramley or Granny Smith), peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Melt butter in a heavy ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Arrange apple slices in the skillet, cut side up, and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Place puff pastry over the apples, trimming excess edges.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until apples are soft and pastry is golden.
Invert the tart onto a serving plate immediately.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and remove.
Cook the bacon lardons in the same pot until crispy, then remove.
Sauté the onion and garlic until softened, then add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mushrooms and cook until browned.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, add wine, thyme, parsley, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until chicken is tender.
Stir in chicken stock and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Remove herbs and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Bouillabaisse
ingredients: 3 tbsp rouille or aioli for serving
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Add crushed tomatoes, white wine, and bouquet garni; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the white fish and red snapper, cover, and cook for 8 minutes.
Add mussels and clams, cover, and cook until shells open, about 5 minutes.
Discard any shells that do not open.
Ladle the fish and broth into bowls, topped with mussels and clams.
Serve immediately with crusty bread and rouille on the side.

title: Ratatouille Provençale
ingredients: 2 yellow summer squash, sliced into half-moons
4 large red bell peppers, cut into strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Toss eggplant cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper; bake at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes.
In a large skillet, sauté onion and garlic until translucent.
Add bell peppers, zucchini, and yellow squash; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the baked eggplant, diced tomatoes, and tomato purée.
Add dried thyme, remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender.
Serve hot or cold as a side dish or main course.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season beef cubes with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
Cook bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp; remove and set aside.
Brown the beef cubes in batches in the bacon fat; remove and set aside.
Add carrots, pearl onions, and garlic to the pot; sauté for 5 minutes.
Pour in the red wine and beef stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot, add the bouquet garni.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3 hours.
Add mushrooms and simmer for another 30 minutes until beef is fall-apart tender.
Remove bouquet garni and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: 1 cup granulated sugar, plus extra for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Combine heavy cream, vanilla bean seeds, pod, and salt in a saucepan; heat until just simmering.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 1 cup sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the egg mixture while whisking constantly to temper.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl.
Pour the custard into six ramekins.
Place ramekins in a roasting pan and fill the pan with hot water until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until the custard is set but still jiggles slightly in the center.
Chill completely in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle a thick layer of sugar over each custard and caramelize with a kitchen torch or under a broiler.

title: Galette des Rois (Breton Style)
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add softened butter, milk, and egg; knead until a smooth dough forms.
Divide dough into two equal balls; let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll out first half to 1/8 inch thickness; spread almond paste in center.
Roll out second half and place over filling, sealing edges.
Cut slits in top with a knife to allow steam to escape.
Brush with egg yolk and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes until golden.
Let cool before slicing.

title: Omelette à la Bretonne
instructions: Whisk eggs, cream, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Melt butter in a small non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in egg mixture and let sit for 10 seconds.
Push edges toward center with a spatula to cook the bottom.
Sprinkle cheese and chives over the half-cooked omelette.
Fold the omelette in half gently when set.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

title: Couscous de Morlaix
instructions: Bring broth to a boil with saffron and salt.
Add semolina slowly while stirring constantly to prevent clumping.
Reduce heat to low; cover and steam for 15 minutes without stirring.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and let cool slightly.
Toss with olive oil, parsley, and toasted almonds.
Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Frites de la Mère
ingredients: 3 lbs potatoes, cut into thick strips
instructions: Soak potato strips in cold water for 30 minutes to remove starch.
Dry potatoes thoroughly with a clean towel.
Heat oil to 325°F (160°C) in a deep pot.
Fry potatoes in batches for 3-4 minutes until pale and soft.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Increase oil temperature to 375°F (190°C).
Return potatoes to oil for 2 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain, season with salt, parsley, and vinegar, and serve with lemon.

title: Kerouzelle (Seafood Stew)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add wine and stock; bring to a simmer.
Stir in saffron and let cook for 5 minutes.
Add mussels and clams; cover and cook until shells open.
Add cod and shrimp; cook for 3-4 minutes until fish is opaque.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in parsley and remove from heat.
Serve immediately in bowls.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Brown lardons in a heavy pot until crisp, then remove.
Sear chicken pieces in the fat until golden on all sides.
Add pearl onions, mushrooms, garlic, thyme, and bay leaves; cook for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the ingredients and stir to coat.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits from the bottom.
Return lardons to the pot and add enough stock to barely cover the chicken.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 1 hour until chicken is tender.

title: Moules Marinières
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh mussels, debearded and scrubbed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Discard any mussels that are cracked or open before cooking.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add shallots and garlic; sauté until soft and fragrant.
Pour in white wine and add thyme sprigs.
Add mussels to the pot, cover, and steam for 5-7 minutes until shells open.
Remove from heat and stir in chopped parsley.
Discard any mussels that did not open, and serve immediately.

title: Omelette Normande
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk eggs, cream, salt, and white pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Melt butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and let it set slightly around the edges.
Sprinkle Gruyère cheese and chives over the surface.
Fold the omelette in half gently using a spatula.
Slide the folded omelette onto a warm plate.
Top with a dollop of crème fraîche before serving.

title: Tarte aux Pommes
ingredients: 4 apples (Belle de Boskoop), peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface and transfer to a baking sheet.
Toss apple slices with sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Arrange apple slices in concentric circles over the pastry.
Brush the edges of the pastry with beaten egg.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden and apples are tender.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt immediately after removing from the oven.

title: Confit de Canard
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season duck legs generously with salt and pepper.
Pat the duck legs dry with paper towels.
Submerge duck legs completely in the duck fat in a deep pot.
Add thyme, garlic, and bay leaves to the fat.
Cover and cook in a low oven at 225°F (110°C) for 3 hours.
Remove duck legs from the fat and let cool, then store in the fat in the fridge.
To serve, crisp the skin in a hot skillet for 2 minutes and slice with roasted onions.

title: Choucroute Garnie
ingredients: 1 kg fresh or fermented sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
1.5 kg mixed Alsatian sausages (Mett, Saucisse de Strasbourg, and Andouillette)
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Place the rinsed sauerkraut in a large ovenproof pot.
Arrange the sausages, pork ribs, and hocks on top of the sauerkraut.
Scatter the sliced onion, crushed garlic, bay leaves, and juniper berries over the meat.
Pour the white wine over everything.
Season generously with salt and white pepper.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and bake for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Serve hot, traditionally with dark rye bread.

title: Tarte Flambée (Flammekueche)
ingredients: 250 g strong white bread dough, divided into 4 portions
150 g cooked smoked bacon lardons, diced
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F).
Roll out the dough into 4 thin rectangles, roughly 20x30 cm each.
In a bowl, whisk together the crème fraîche, beaten eggs, sautéed mushrooms, bacon, onion, and thyme.
Season the mixture with salt and white pepper.
Spread the mixture thinly over each dough rectangle, leaving a small border.
Bake on a baking stone or preheated tray for 5-7 minutes until the edges are golden and crispy.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Baeckeoffe
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F).
Season the meat cubes with salt, pepper, and mustard powder.
In a large heavy pot, combine the meat, onions, carrots, celery, and garlic.
Pour the white wine and stock over the ingredients until the meat is covered.
Add the bouquet garni and dried thyme.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or heavy-duty foil.
Bake for 3 to 3.5 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Toast the baguette slices in the oven for the last 10 minutes to serve alongside.

title: Kartoffelsauerkraut (Potato and Sauerkraut)
ingredients: 500 g fresh sauerkraut, well rinsed and drained
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, combine the drained sauerkraut, potatoes, carrots, and onion.
Add the broth, white wine, bay leaf, and thyme.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme sprigs before serving.

title: Wurstsalat
ingredients: 400 g sliced Alsatian sausages (Saucisse de Strasbourg)
instructions: Slice the sausages into thin rounds.
In a large bowl, combine the sausages, chopped eggs, onion, carrot, cucumber, and celery.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, sugar, and vinegar.
Season the dressing with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything is coated.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Sear the chicken pieces in a heavy pot with half the lardons until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook the remaining lardons until crisp, then add shallots and garlic until soft.
Stir in flour and cook for one minute, then gradually whisk in the red wine and stock until smooth.
Return the chicken and mushrooms to the pot; add thyme and bay leaves.
Simmer covered for 1 hour 15 minutes until the meat is tender, then finish with butter.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 lbs small carrots, cut into chunks
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large Dutch oven with half the lardons; remove and set aside.
Fry the remaining lardons until crisp, then add pearl onions and cook until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and stir for one minute before adding the wine and stock.
Return the beef to the pot along with carrots, mushrooms, garlic, thyme, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently for 3 hours until the meat falls apart and the sauce is rich.

title: Pot-au-Feu
ingredients: 1 whole beef shin, on the bone
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Place the beef and veal shanks in a large stockpot and cover with cold water; bring to a boil.
Skim off any scum that rises to the surface, then reduce heat and simmer gently for 2 hours.
Add the leeks, carrots, and turnips; continue simmering for 1 hour.
Add the cabbage and potatoes, then cook for another 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and white pepper, remove the bones and garnish, and serve with crusty bread.

title: Choucroute Garnie
ingredients: 1 kg pork ribs, cut into pieces
1 head green cabbage, cut into wedges
instructions: Layer the rinsed sauerkraut and lardons in a large pot; sprinkle with mustard powder.
Add the pork ribs, sausages, onion, garlic, and bouquet garni over the sauerkraut.
Pour the white wine and beef stock over the ingredients until nearly covered.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the cabbage wedges during the last 20 minutes of cooking and serve hot.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Toss the eggplant cubes with salt and let them sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, then add the tomato paste.
Add the peppers, zucchini, and eggplant; cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and herbes de Provence; simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, remove from heat, and garnish with fresh basil before serving.

title: Quenelles de Brochet à la Lyonnaise
ingredients: 1 lb fresh pike fillet, skin removed
1 cup pearl onions, poached in butter
instructions: Peel the pike fillet and cut into very small cubes, then mash them into a smooth paste using a pestle.
Whisk the egg yolks with the butter, flour, salt, and white pepper until a smooth paste forms.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the yolk mixture.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture into the simmering fish stock and cook gently until they float.
Poach the pearl onions in butter until tender, then arrange them on a warm plate.
Serve the quenelles alongside the onions, garnished with fresh chives.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Season the rooster pieces with salt and pepper, then dredge them lightly in flour.
Brown the bacon in a heavy pot, then remove and set aside.
Sear the chicken pieces in the bacon fat until golden on all sides, then remove.
In the same pot, sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms until they begin to brown.
Add the bouquet garni, deglaze the pot with red wine, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, cover with stock, and braise for 1.5 hours until tender.
Remove the bouquet garni, adjust seasoning, and serve.

title: Salade Lyonnaise
ingredients: 4 large green leaf lettuce leaves, torn
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the lardons in a skillet over medium heat until crispy and golden brown.
Whisk the raw eggs with white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and white pepper.
Arrange the torn lettuce and sliced red onion on a large plate.
Pour the egg mixture over the salad and immediately cook on a hot griddle or in the skillet until the eggs are set but still creamy.
Top with the crispy lardons and drizzle with olive oil before serving.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
instructions: Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add the eggplant cubes and cook until they begin to soften, then add the zucchini rounds.
Stir in the bell peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, and bouquet garni, then simmer for 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
