Season with salt and pepper, remove the bouquet garni, and serve hot or cold.

title: Omelette au Fromage
instructions: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and a tiny bit of nutmeg until well combined.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and add a small knob of butter.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan and let it set slightly on the edges.
Sprinkle the grated Gruyère cheese over the eggs, then fold the omelette in half.
Cook for another minute until the cheese is melted and the omelette is cooked through.
Slide onto a plate, garnish with fresh chives, and serve immediately.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 2 cups dry red wine, such as Burgundy
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then brown them in the bacon fat.
Add onions and mushrooms to the pot and cook until softened.
Stir in garlic, tomato paste, thyme, and bay leaves; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer uncovered for 1 hour until the chicken is tender.
Remove thyme and bay leaves, then whisk flour into the remaining stock.
Add stock to the pot and stir until the sauce thickens.
Return bacon to the pot and stir in the butter until melted.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Omelette à la Normande
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk eggs and cream together in a bowl, then season with salt and white pepper.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion and ham until the onion is translucent.
Add spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and let it set slightly around the edges.
Spread the Dijon mustard evenly over the surface of the omelette.
Fold the omelette in half and cook for another minute until the top is set.
Slide the omelette onto a plate, garnish with chives, and serve immediately.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: 4 red bell peppers, cut into strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add eggplant cubes and cook until they begin to soften.
Add zucchini slices and bell pepper strips, stirring to coat with oil.
Stir in grated tomatoes, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Cover the pot and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and continue cooking for another 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Taste the stew and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onions until golden brown.
Add garlic, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper, then cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add the beef stock and bring the soup to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the soup thickens slightly.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Arrange baguette slices in a baking dish and pour the hot soup over them.
Sprinkle the Gruyère cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 4 large Apples (Granny Smith or Boskoop), peeled and sliced
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus extra for the pan
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Melt butter in a heavy ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced apples and sugar to the skillet, cooking until the apples are golden.
Place the puff pastry on a floured surface and roll it out to fit the skillet.
Carefully lay the pastry over the apples, tucking the edges under slightly.
Bake for 20 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
Invert a serving plate over the skillet and quickly flip the tart onto the plate.
Dust the top with powdered sugar and serve warm.

title: Cassoulet Toulousain
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into chunks
instructions: Brown the pork belly cubes in duck fat until golden.
Add the onion, carrots, and garlic, cooking for 10 minutes.
Stir in the salted pork and cook for another 5 minutes.
Drain the soaked beans and add them to the pot.
Cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 2 hours.
Add the Toulouse sausage, duck confit, and bouquet garni.
Cook on low heat for another 1 hour until the sauce is thick and beans are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Let rest for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Magret de Canard à l'Orange
instructions: Score the duck skin in a crosshatch pattern without cutting into the meat.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Place skin-side down in a cold pan with duck fat and thyme.
Turn heat to medium-high and cook until fat renders and skin is crisp (10-12 minutes).
Flip the duck and cook for another 2-3 minutes on the flesh side.
Remove duck and let rest under foil.
Pour off excess fat, leaving a tablespoon in the pan.
Add butter, orange zest, and honey to the pan and deglaze with orange juice.
Slice the duck and serve with the orange glaze.

title: Piquepique de Canard
instructions: Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil until soft.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, wine, and thyme, coating the grains.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the shredded duck confit and cook for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Let the rice absorb the liquid and steam for 2 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

title: Moutarde de Canard au Pain
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden and crisp.
In a small bowl, mix the duck liver, Dijon mustard, honey, and cayenne.
Spread the mixture generously over the toast.
Drizzle the top with a little duck fat.
Sprinkle with chopped chives and crumbled bacon.
Serve immediately as an appetizer.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
instructions: Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 30 minutes to remove bitterness.
Rinse and pat dry the eggplant slices.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers, cooking until soft.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, thyme, and bay leaf.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.
Serve warm with crusty bread.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, then add eggplant and zucchini.
Sauté vegetables until they begin to soften and brown slightly.
Stir in bell peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in fresh basil and serve hot.

title: Galette de Sarrasin
instructions: Mix buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add water and lard, stirring until a smooth batter forms.
Let the batter rest for at least 2 hours at room temperature.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium heat and brush with butter.
Pour a ladle of batter into the center, tilting the pan to spread it thinly and evenly.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm with butter, ham, and cheese.

title: Omelette Bretonne aux Champignons
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Sauté the onions until soft, then add the mushrooms and cook until browned.
Season the mushrooms with salt, white pepper, and a pinch of cream.
Whisk the eggs with a splash of cream, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan with the mushrooms.
Shake the pan gently to create soft curds, then fold the omelette in half.
Slide onto a plate, garnish with chives, and serve immediately.

title: Quenelles de Brochet au Beurre Blanc
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash with butter and flour to make a smooth paste.
Fold in the beaten egg, then gently mix in the fish fillet until combined.
Moisten hands with cold water and wet flour, then shape the mixture into quenelles.
Boil the stock with the vinegar until reduced by half.
Drop the quenelles into the simmering liquid and cook gently for 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, make beurre blanc by whisking vinegar with cold butter cubes over low heat until emulsified.
Serve the quenelles topped with the warm beurre blanc sauce.

title: Crevettes à la Bretonne
ingredients: 500g large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and shallots, sautéing for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the shrimp to the pan in a single layer and cook for 2 minutes.
Flip the shrimp and cook for another 2 minutes until pink and opaque.
Remove from heat and immediately stir in lemon juice, zest, and parsley.
Serve hot with boiled new potatoes and a green salad.

title: Tartiflette Rurale
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a deep oven-safe skillet, fry the bacon lardons until crisp, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions and garlic in butter until translucent.
Layer the potatoes evenly in the pan, then sprinkle with bacon, cheese, and a little salt and pepper.
Pour the cream over the top to cover the ingredients.
Cover with a lid or foil and bake for 45 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Uncover and bake for another 10 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Omelette au Fromage
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the butter in a small non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and let them set slightly without stirring.
Sprinkle the grated Gruyère and chives over one half of the omelette.
Fold the omelette over the filling using a spatula.
Cook for another minute until the top is just set, then slide onto a plate.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Brown the lardons in a heavy pot, then remove and set aside.
Sauté the chicken pieces in the fat until golden, then remove.
Add the shallots to the pot and cook until soft.
Return the chicken and lardons to the pot; add wine, stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Simmer covered for 1 hour until the meat is tender, then thicken with a beurre manié if desired.

title: Soupe à l'Oignon
ingredients: 20g dark bread, crusts removed and cubed
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot and sweat the onions over low heat for 20 minutes until very soft and caramelized.
Stir in the thyme and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then pour in the stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the bread cubes and cook until the soup thickens.
Serve in bowls topped generously with the grated Gruyère.

title: Moules Marinières
instructions: Melt the butter and oil in a large pot; sauté the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the mussels, wine, and parsley to the pot.
Cover and cook over high heat, shaking the pot occasionally, until the mussels open (about 8-10 minutes).
Discard any mussels that remain closed.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Tarte Tatin
ingredients: 600g Granny Smith apples, peeled and thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Melt 200g butter and sugar in an oven-safe skillet.
Arrange apple slices in overlapping layers over the melted butter and sugar.
Bake for 25 minutes until apples are tender and caramel is bubbling.
Meanwhile, mix flour, cold butter, egg, and water to form a stiff dough.
Invert the tart onto a serving plate immediately after baking to reveal the caramelized apples.

title: Choucroute Garnie
instructions: Simmer the sauerkraut with sliced onion, lardons, and carrots in a large pot for 20 minutes.
Add the pork ribs, hocks, sausages, bay leaves, and wine to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Remove the hocks and ribs, chop them into bite-sized pieces.
Stir in the chopped spinach and serve hot with the meat.

title: Tarte Flambée (Flammekueche)
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, and water to form a smooth, elastic dough; let rise for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to its highest setting (250°C/480°F).
Roll dough very thin on a floured surface and transfer to a hot baking sheet.
Whisk together yogurt, crème fraîche, and melted butter, then spread over the dough.
Sprinkle evenly with bacon lardons, mushrooms, and beaten eggs.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until edges are crisp and golden.
Garnish with fresh chives before serving.

title: Kochwurst
instructions: Combine ground pork, pork belly, grated onion, white pepper, salt, sugar, and parsley in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly by hand until the mixture is uniform and slightly sticky.
Stuff the meat mixture into the soaked natural casings using a stuffer, tying off ends to form links.
Bring a deep pot of oil to 170°C (340°F).
Fry the sausages in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with mustard.

title: Baeckeoffe
instructions: Season the meat cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot and sear the meat in batches until browned.
Add the onions and carrots to the pot and cook until soft.
Pour in the white wine and tomato paste, stirring to deglaze the pan.
Add the potatoes, bouquet garni, and enough water to cover the meat halfway.
Cover the pot tightly and bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 3 hours.
Remove the bouquet garni before serving.

title: Kouglof
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, sugar, eggs, vanilla, and salt in a stand mixer with a dough hook.
Add the yeast mixture and butter, kneading until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Grease a traditional kouglof pan with butter.
Shape the dough into a ring, place it in the pan, and let rise again for 45 minutes.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 40-45 minutes until golden and springy to the touch.
Dust with confectioner's sugar while still warm.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 2 kg beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches until deeply colored.
Remove beef and set aside; render the lardons in the same pot until crisp.
Stir in the flour to coat the lardons and cook for one minute.
Deglaze the pot with the red wine, scraping up all browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef to the pot along with the carrots, pearl onions, garlic, bay leaves, and bouquet garni.
Pour in the beef stock until the liquid just covers the meat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 3 to 4 hours until the beef is tender.
Remove the bouquet garni and bay leaves before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.5 kg), cut into 8 pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Pat the chicken pieces dry and season with salt and pepper.
In a large Dutch oven, cook the lardons over medium heat until crispy, then remove and drain on paper towels.
Add the flour to the pot and stir for one minute to create a roux.
Deglaze with the red wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the chicken pieces, garlic, bay leaves, and bouquet garni to the pot.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the sliced carrots, celery, and onions to the pot.
Return the cooked lardons to the pot and continue simmering, covered, for another 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Remove the bouquet garni and bay leaves, then stir in the butter for gloss before serving.

title: Mirepoix Onion Soup (Soupe à l'Oignon)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter and olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions, sugar, and thyme; cook slowly for 45 minutes until the onions are deeply caramelized and golden brown.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with the red wine and let it simmer until the alcohol evaporates.
Pour in the beef stock and bring to a gentle simmer; cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and season with salt and white pepper.
Divide the soup into bowls and top generously with the Gruyère and Comté cheese.
Broil the bowls under a hot grill until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Serve immediately while piping hot.

title: Duck Confit
instructions: Remove the skin from the duck legs and rub the meat underneath with salt, pepper, and the cut side of the onion halves.
Place the duck legs skin-side up in a deep baking dish or Dutch oven.
Pack the duck fat, garlic, bouquet garni, rosemary, and peppercorns around the duck legs until they are completely submerged.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and seal with parchment paper.
Bake in a low oven at 100°C (212°F) for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is extremely tender.
Remove the duck legs and let them cool completely in the fat.
Once cool, store the duck legs submerged in the fat in the refrigerator for up to a month.
To serve, remove the legs from the fat, pat them dry, and pan-fry skin-side down over high heat for 2 minutes to crisp the skin, then flip to finish cooking the meat.

title: Escargots de Bourgogne
ingredients: 12 large Burgundy snails, cleaned and meat removed
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat and remove from heat.
Stir in the minced garlic, parsley, chives, thyme, brandy, and white wine until fragrant.
Mix in the breadcrumbs, salt, and pepper to create a thick paste.
Stuff each snail shell with about 1 tablespoon of the butter mixture.
Place the stuffed shells into a baking dish.
Brush the tops of the shells with a little extra melted butter.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 12 to 15 minutes until the butter is bubbling and golden.
Serve immediately in the shells with crusty bread for dipping.

title: Quenelles de Brochet à la Lyonnaise
instructions: Mix the pike paste with flour to form a stiff dough.
Add hot stock gradually while kneading to create a smooth, elastic paste.
Shape the paste into quenelles using two spoons.
Poach the quenelles gently in simmering fish stock for 15 minutes.
Make a roux with butter and flour, then add stock to create a thick sauce.
Season the sauce with lemon juice and pour over the quenelles.

title: Saucisson à la Lyonnaise
instructions: Render the Andouille slices in a pan until crisp, then remove.
Sauté the chicken livers and onions in butter until golden.
Stir in flour to make a roux, then gradually add beef stock.
Simmer the sauce until it thickens, then stir in cold butter cubes.
Add the cream and season with salt and pepper.
Return the crisp sausage to the pan and simmer briefly to coat.

title: Omelette aux Herbes de Provence
instructions: Whisk the eggs with salt, white pepper, and chopped herbs until frothy.
Heat a non-stick pan with a knob of butter over medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and let it set for 30 seconds.
Fold the omelette gently with a spatula to create a soft center.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately with a pat of butter.

title: Bouillabaisse Traditionnelle
ingredients: 500g mixed fish (sea bream, monkfish, hake), cubed
instructions: Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil until soft.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and fish stock, then bring to a boil.
Simmer the stock with the bouquet garni for 20 minutes.
Add the hard fish first and cook for 10 minutes.
Add mussels, squid, and remaining fish, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Serve in shallow bowls with rouille, crusty bread, and lemon wedges.

title: Poulet en Cocotte Lyonnaise
instructions: Dredge the chicken pieces in flour, shaking off excess.
Brown the lardons and remove from the pan.
Sauté the chicken pieces in butter until golden on all sides.
Add onions, carrots, and celery to the pan and cook until softened.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the stock, bouquet garni, and lardons back to the pan.
Simmer covered for 1 hour until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Coq au Vin
instructions: Sear the chicken pieces in butter until golden and set aside.
Cook the lardons in the same pan until crispy.
Add garlic and cook for one minute, then add the wine.
Simmer the wine with the bouquet garni until reduced by half.
Return chicken to the pan and add stock and pearl onions.
Braise in the oven at 350°F for 1.5 hours until tender.
Sauté mushrooms and flour in butter to make a roux.
Stir the roux into the braising liquid and simmer until thickened.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
instructions: Roast the eggplant cubes in the oven until soft and golden.
Sauté the garlic in olive oil until fragrant.
Add the peppers and zucchini to the pan and cook until tender.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato puree, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix in the roasted eggplant and fresh basil.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

title: Bœuf Bourguignon
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck, cut into cubes
instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt and pepper and coat with flour.
Sear the beef in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Add the lardons and cook until crispy.
Pour in the wine and tomato paste, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the carrots, pearl onions, garlic, and bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and bake at 325°F for 2.5 hours.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter until browned.
Stir the mushrooms into the pot and cook for another 30 minutes.

title: Tarte Tatin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F and grease a 9-inch skillet.
Arrange the apple slices in the skillet in concentric circles.
Sprinkle sugar and cinnamon over the apples, then pour melted butter around the edges.
Cover with the puff pastry, sealing the edges to the skillet.
Bake for 40 minutes until the pastry is golden and apples are tender.
Invert the tart onto a serving plate immediately after removing from the oven.
Warm the apricot jam and drizzle it over the top.

title: Soupe à l'oignon Gratinée
instructions: Sauté the onions in butter until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for one minute to remove the raw taste.
Add the beef stock, white wine, and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the soup for 15 minutes until the onions are very tender.
Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Place the bread slices in a baking dish and top with the soup.
Sprinkle the grated Gruyère cheese over the soup and bread.
Broil in the oven for 5 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and brown.

title: Poulet au Cassoulet
instructions: Brown the pork belly and sausage in olive oil until crispy.
Remove meat and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides.
Return the meat to the pot and add the soaked beans and stock.
Simmer covered for 2 hours until beans and chicken are tender.
Season with bay leaf and thyme before serving.

title: Foie Gras au Poivre Vert
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat butter in a pan and sauté the minced shallot until translucent.
Add the white wine and reduce by half.
Add the soaked green peppercorns and tarragon sprig.
Gently poach the foie gras slices in the sauce for 3-4 minutes.
Remove the tarragon sprig and season with salt and white pepper.
Serve immediately with toasted brioche.

title: Confit de Canard
instructions: Season duck legs generously with salt and let them cure for 24 hours.
Submerge the duck legs completely in duck fat in a heavy pot.
Add onion, carrots, thyme, and garlic to the fat.
Cook at a low temperature (90°C/195°F) for 3 hours until meat is tender.
Remove duck legs, skim fat, and store in the remaining fat.
Crisp the skin in a hot skillet before serving.

title: Bouillabaisse Marseillaise
ingredients: 1 kg mixed Mediterranean fish and shellfish
instructions: Sauté onions, garlic, and fennel in oil until softened.
Add tomato paste, wine, stock, and saffron; bring to a boil.
Add the larger, tougher fish pieces and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add smaller fish, mussels, and clams; cook until shells open.
Ladle into bowls topped generously with rouille.

title: Tarte au Fromage de Brebis
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and cold butter until crumbly.
Add eggs and milk to form a stiff dough; chill for 1 hour.
Roll out dough and line a tart pan; prick the bottom.
Bake the crust at 200°C for 10 minutes until pale gold.
Mix the fresh and aged cheeses until smooth.
Spread cheese mixture over the hot crust and bake for 15 minutes.
Brush with egg yolk and return to oven for 2 minutes to glaze.

title: Socca (Genoese Chickpea Pancake)
instructions: Mix chickpea flour, water, salt, and saffron in a large bowl until smooth and slightly thick.
Let the batter rest for at least 3 hours or overnight at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and place a cast-iron skillet inside to heat.
Drizzle olive oil around the edges and into the center of the hot skillet.
Pour the batter into the skillet, spreading it evenly to the edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden brown and the center is cooked through.
Slide onto a plate and cut into squares while still warm.

title: Ratatouille Niçoise
instructions: Season the eggplant with salt and let it sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture, then pat dry.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 1/4 cup of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until translucent, then add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers, stirring to coat with oil.
Cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomatoes, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Uncover and cook for another 10 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly before serving.

title: Socca (Marseilles Chickpea Pancake)
instructions: Mix chickpea flour, water, salt, and saffron in a large bowl until smooth and slightly thick.
Let the batter rest for at least 3 hours or overnight at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and place a cast-iron skillet inside to heat.
Drizzle olive oil around the edges and into the center of the hot skillet.
Pour the batter into the skillet, spreading it evenly to the edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden brown and the center is cooked through.
Slide onto a plate and cut into squares while still warm.

title: Tarte aux Oignons
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll out the puff pastry and place it in a tart pan or baking dish.
Brush the pastry with melted butter and prick the bottom with a fork.
Arrange the sliced onions in a single layer over the pastry.
In a saucepan, combine onions, wine, stock, cream, sugar, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Simmer the onion mixture over medium heat for 15 minutes until the liquid reduces and the onions are caramelized.
Pour the onion mixture over the pastry in the tart pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden and puffed.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving warm.

title: Socca (Marseilles Chickpea Pancake)
instructions: Mix chickpea flour, water, salt, and saffron in a large bowl until smooth and slightly thick.
Let the batter rest for at least 3 hours or overnight at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and place a cast-iron skillet inside to heat.
Drizzle olive oil around the edges and into the center of the hot skillet.
Pour the batter into the skillet, spreading it evenly to the edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden brown and the center is cooked through.
Slide onto a plate and cut into squares while still warm.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 4 cups fresh spinach, chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, mix spinach, feta, scallions, olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Brush a baking sheet with oil.
Place one phyllo sheet on the sheet and brush with oil.
Spread half of the spinach mixture over the sheet.
Cover with a second phyllo sheet, brush with oil, and add the remaining spinach mixture.
Cover with a third phyllo sheet, brush with oil, and cover with the last phyllo sheet.
Brush the top with oil and cut into squares.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Salt eggplant slices and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry. Fry in olive oil until golden.
In a large pan, sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add ground lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, and wine. Simmer for 20 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk milk, flour, and eggs to make the béchamel sauce.
Layer eggplant slices in a baking dish, pour half the meat sauce over them.
Repeat layers, finishing with a layer of meat sauce.
Pour the béchamel sauce over the top, mixing in the cheeses.
Bake for 45 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly.

title: Dolmadakia
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch grape leaves for 2 minutes.
In a bowl, mix ground lamb, rice, onion, pine nuts, olive oil, lemon juice, mint, salt, and pepper.
Place a grape leaf smooth side down on a work surface.
Put a small amount of filling in the center of the leaf.
Fold the sides of the leaf over the filling and roll tightly.
Place dolmadakia upright in a pot, packing them tightly.
Add water to cover the dolmadakia by 1 inch.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour over low heat.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 1 large ripe tomato, cut into wedges
1 green bell pepper, cut into chunks
8 oz feta cheese, a large block
instructions: Arrange tomato, cucumber, onion, and bell pepper in a large bowl.
Add Kalamata olives on top of the vegetables.
Place the block of feta cheese on top of the salad.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, vinegar, oregano, and pepper.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad just before serving.
Do not mix the vegetables; serve as presented.

title: Tzatziki
ingredients: 1 large cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
instructions: Grate the cucumber using a box grater.
Place grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out all excess water.
In a bowl, combine the yogurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic, olive oil, dill, mint, salt, and pepper.
Mix well until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving to let flavors meld.
Serve chilled with pita bread or as a dip.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb fresh spinach, chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix spinach, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil.
Layer half the phyllo dough in the dish, brushing each sheet with oil.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the dough.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before slicing.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in lamb or beef and cook until browned.
Add rice, wine, oregano, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Let filling cool slightly.
Wipe grape leaves dry and place a spoonful of filling on each leaf.
Roll tightly and place in a pot seam-side down.
Cover with water and simmer for 1 hour.
Let cool before serving.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Salt eggplant slices and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry eggplant slices until golden; set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic, then add lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in tomato sauce and oregano; simmer for 20 minutes.
Arrange potato slices in a baking dish, then layer eggplant.
Pour lamb mixture over the vegetables.
Top with béchamel sauce and parmesan cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Tzatziki
ingredients: 1 large cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
instructions: Grate cucumber and squeeze out excess water using a clean towel.
Mix yogurt, cucumber, garlic, olive oil, dill, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Stir until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Serve chilled with pita bread or as a dip.

title: Loukoumades
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water with a pinch of sugar; let foam for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Add yeast mixture and knead until smooth; let rise for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of dough into hot oil and fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and walnuts.
Serve warm.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic, then add ground lamb and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes, salt, pepper, and cinnamon to the meat mixture.
Layer potatoes and eggplant in a baking dish.
Pour the meat sauce over the layers.
Top with grated parmesan cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Mix spinach, feta, cream cheese, eggs, dill, salt, nutmeg, and half the olive oil.
Brush bottom of a 9x13 pan with butter and layer 4 sheets of phyllo.
Spread half the spinach mixture over the phyllo.
Layer 4 more sheets of phyllo, brush with butter, add remaining filling.
Top with remaining phyllo sheets and butter.
Bake at 350°F for 40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds until pliable.
Mix ground lamb, rice, onion, pine nuts, oregano, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Place a grape leaf shiny side down on a work surface.
Add a spoonful of meat mixture to the center.
Fold sides over the filling and roll up tightly.
Pack dolmades into a pot seam side down.
Cover with water and simmer for 45 minutes.

title: Pastitsio
instructions: Boil pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Sauté onion and ground beef, then add tomato sauce, salt, and pepper.
Whisk together milk, sour cream, eggs, flour, and half the olive oil.
Combine the sauce and the milk mixture, then stir in cinnamon.
In a baking dish, layer half the pasta, then half the sauce.
Repeat layers with remaining pasta and sauce.
Top with parmesan cheese and bake at 375°F for 30 minutes.

title: Tiropita
instructions: Whisk together feta, eggs, olive oil, water, cinnamon, salt, and sugar.
Brush bottom of a baking dish with butter.
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with butter.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Cut into squares or rectangles.
Bake at 375°F for 35 minutes until golden.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden, then salt and let drain.
Brown the ground lamb with onions and garlic in a separate pan.
Add crushed tomatoes to the meat mixture and simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk flour and milk to make a white sauce, then stir in half the Parmesan and all the feta.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, top with remaining white sauce and cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach in olive oil until wilted, then drain excess liquid.
Mix spinach with feta, ricotta, green onions, garlic, dill, and oregano.
Brush the bottom of a baking dish with melted butter.
Layer 5 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with butter.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the dough.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Cut into squares and bake at 350°F for 35 minutes until golden.

title: Greek Salad
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, onion, bell pepper, olives, and feta in a large bowl.
Whisk together olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately at room temperature.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Mix ground pork, rice, onion, garlic, olive oil, broth, lemon juice, dill, salt, and pepper.
Place a grape leaf shiny side down in your palm and add a small spoonful of meat mixture to the stem end.
Fold the sides of the leaf over the filling and roll tightly.
Pack the rolls into a pot and cover with warm water.
Simmer on low heat for 1 hour until tender.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Souvlaki
instructions: Combine olive oil, vinegar, oregano, garlic, salt, pepper, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Marinate the pork cubes in the mixture for at least 2 hours.
Thread the marinated meat onto skewers.
Grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Slice the cooked meat and serve on warm pita bread with fresh tomatoes and onions.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and set aside.
Brown ground lamb with onions and garlic in a large pot.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, wine, salt, and pepper; simmer for 30 minutes.
Make the béchamel sauce by melting butter and whisking in flour.
Gradually add milk while stirring until thickened, then remove from heat.
Stir in Parmesan cheese and beaten eggs into the béchamel.
Layer eggplant in a baking dish, top with meat sauce, then cover with béchamel.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.
Let rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Dolmades
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Mix ground lamb, rice, parsley, dill, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Place a grape leaf shiny side down on a work surface.
Spoon a tablespoon of filling onto the leaf near the stem.
Fold the sides over the filling and roll tightly into a cone shape.
Place dolmades in a pot in a single layer.
Cover with cold water and add vinegar and olive oil.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove from heat and let cool before serving.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté spinach with a little water until wilted, then squeeze out all excess liquid.
Beat eggs, then whisk in olive oil, flour, water, oregano, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Stir in spinach, feta, and dill into the egg mixture.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Place a sheet of phyllo on a baking sheet and brush with butter.
Layer 2-3 more sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Spread half the spinach filling over the phyllo.
Fold the edges over and roll up like a cigar.
Place seam-side down on a baking sheet.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Repeat with remaining filling to make two spanakopitas.

title: Gyros
ingredients: 2 lbs lean beef or pork, thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine sliced meat, olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Marinate the meat for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Thread the marinated meat onto a vertical spit or skewer.
Cook over high heat, rotating constantly until browned and cooked through.
Slice the cooked meat thinly.
Warm pita breads in a dry pan or oven.
Spread tzatziki sauce on each pita.
Layer lettuce, sliced cucumber, red onion, tomato, and hot meat onto the pita.
Roll tightly and serve immediately.

title: Tzatziki
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Grate cucumbers and squeeze out all excess water using a clean towel.
Place yogurt in a bowl and stir in the drained cucumbers.
Add minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, dill, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Stir until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let flavors meld.
Stir in fresh parsley just before serving.
Serve chilled with pita bread or as a dip for vegetables.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic, then add lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Layer eggplant, meat sauce, and béchamel in a baking dish.
Sprinkle Parmesan on top and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix spinach, feta, eggs, and ricotta in a bowl.
Place one phyllo sheet on a surface and brush with melted butter.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the buttered sheet.
Cover with second phyllo sheet, brush with butter, and fold into a triangle.
Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 8 oz feta cheese, a large block
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Arrange tomatoes, cucumbers, and onion in a large bowl.
Top with olives and place the block of feta on top.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and vinegar.
Season with salt and pepper, then toss gently before serving.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Boil grape leaves for 2 minutes to soften and drain.
Mix pork, rice, onion, tomato paste, and oil in a bowl.
Wrap a spoonful of mixture around each grape leaf tip.
Place dolmades in a pot with water and simmer for 1 hour.
Let cool slightly before serving with lemon wedges.

title: Tzatziki
ingredients: 1 cup English cucumber, grated and well-drained
instructions: Grate cucumber and squeeze out all excess water using a towel.
In a bowl, combine yogurt, drained cucumber, garlic, and dill.
Stir in olive oil and lemon juice until well mixed.
Season with salt and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden, then drain excess liquid.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add crushed tomatoes to meat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Whisk eggs with half the cheese to create an egg wash.
Layer fried eggplant, meat sauce, and remaining cheese in a baking dish.
Pour egg wash over the top and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach until wilted, then squeeze out all excess water.
Mix spinach, feta, dill, nutmeg, and half the beaten eggs.
Brush one phyllo sheet with oil and layer two sheets.
Spread spinach mixture over the base layers.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Cut into squares and bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Rinse grape leaves and blanch briefly in boiling water.
Mix ground pork, rice, pine nuts, oregano, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Place a small amount of filling on the base of each grape leaf.
Roll leaves tightly around the filling.
Arrange dolmades in a pot with olive oil and cover with water.
Simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes until tender.

title: Gyros
instructions: Marinate pork slices with oil, lemon juice, oregano, and salt for 2 hours.
Stack marinated meat on a vertical rotisserie and cook slowly.
Slice cooked meat thinly as it rotates.
Warm pita bread and fill with sliced meat.
Top with fresh tomato, cucumber, tzatziki sauce, and onion.
Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges.

title: Avgolemono Soup
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Poach chicken in chicken broth until cooked through, then remove and shred.
Return shredded chicken to broth and simmer gently.
Whisk egg yolks with lemon juice and a splash of hot broth.
Slowly drizzle warm broth into the egg mixture while whisking constantly to temper.
Pour the egg-lemon mixture back into the soup pot off the heat.
Stir in rice, olive oil, salt, and white pepper; serve hot.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and set aside.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in a pan.
Mix tomato sauce with half the milk and simmer.
Blend remaining milk, eggs, and flour into a smooth béchamel sauce.
Layer eggplant, meat sauce, and béchamel in a baking dish.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until golden.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: Sauté spinach with dill and nutmeg until wilted.
Mix spinach with feta and eggs.
Brush phyllo sheets with melted butter, stacking 3 layers.
Spread spinach mixture on the sheets and fold into a square.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes until crispy.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Sauté onion and meat with oil until browned.
Add rice, water, lemon juice, and spices; simmer until rice is tender.
Wrap a spoonful of filling in each grape leaf.
Arrange in a pot, cover with water, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and olives in a bowl.
Top with cubed feta cheese.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle dressing over salad and toss gently.
Serve immediately.

title: Souvlaki
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes in oil, garlic, lemon, oregano, salt, and pepper for 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with warm pita bread.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden, then bake until tender.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic.
Simmer tomatoes, oregano, and eggplant puree to make sauce.
Layer eggplant, meat sauce, and béchamel in a baking dish.
Whisk eggs with sour cream and cheese for topping.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Cook spinach until wilted, drain well, and mix with cheeses and spices.
Brush phyllo sheets with olive oil, stacking 8-10 layers.
Spread spinach mixture in center and fold edges inward.
Bake at 375°F for 30-35 minutes until crisp and golden.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Mince onion and mix with ground beef, rice, and oregano.
Season filling with salt and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf.
Roll tightly to form cones and place in a pot.
Cover with tomato paste, water, and lemon juice.
Simmer for 1 hour until rice is tender.

title: Tzatziki
instructions: Grate cucumber and press out excess water.
Mix yogurt, cucumber, garlic, olive oil, and dill in a bowl.
Stir in lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Serve chilled with pita bread or as a dip.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Arrange tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and pepper in a large bowl.
Place the block of feta cheese on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle oregano over the salad.
Season lightly with salt.
Serve immediately without tossing the ingredients.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden, then set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add ground lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 30 minutes.
Layer fried eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Pour béchamel sauce over the top, sprinkling Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Souvlaki
ingredients: Lettuce, tomatoes, and onions for serving
instructions: Mix olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss chicken cubes with the marinade and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with lettuce, tomatoes, and onions.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach and garlic in olive oil until wilted; drain excess liquid.
Mix spinach, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Brush a baking sheet with olive oil and layer 3 sheets of phyllo dough.
Spread spinach mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Cover with another 3 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with oil.
Cut into squares and bake at 375°F for 30-35 minutes until golden.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 1 minute, then remove and cool.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add meat, rice, tomato sauce, oregano, salt, and pepper; mix well.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf and roll tightly.
Arrange dolmades in a pot seam-side down, cover with water, and boil for 45 minutes.

title: Tzatziki
ingredients: 1 large cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
instructions: Grate cucumber and squeeze out all excess liquid using a clean towel.
In a bowl, mix strained yogurt, grated cucumber, minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, dill, and salt.
Stir until well combined and smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow flavors to meld.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves before serving.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden, then drain.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in a pan.
Stir in tomato sauce and simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk milk and flour to make a smooth white sauce.
Combine half the fried eggplant with half the white sauce.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Pour remaining white sauce over the top and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Mix ground pork, rice, tomato paste, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on the center of each grape leaf.
Fold the leaf around the filling to form a small cone.
Arrange dolmades tightly in a pot with bay leaf and broth.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour.
Drain and serve warm with olive oil and lemon juice.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb fresh spinach, chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Sauté onion in olive oil until soft, then add spinach and cook until wilted.
Mix spinach with feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, salt, and pepper.
Brush a baking sheet with oil and layer 4 sheets of phyllo.
Spread half the spinach mixture over the phyllo.
Layer another 4 sheets of phyllo, then repeat the filling and phyllo layers.
Brush the top with olive oil and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Souvlaki
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken breast, cut into cubes
Tomatoes and onions, sliced for serving
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot chicken with warm pita bread, sliced tomatoes, and onions.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, cut into wedges
1 green bell pepper, cut into strips
8 oz feta cheese, in a large block
instructions: Arrange tomato wedges, cucumber slices, onion rings, and pepper strips in a large bowl.
Place the block of feta cheese on top of the vegetables.
Sprinkle Kalamata olives and oregano over the salad.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden and set aside.
Brown lamb with onion and garlic in a large pot.
Add crushed tomatoes and oregano; simmer for 30 minutes.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Whisk eggs with yogurt and half the cheese; pour over layers.
Top with remaining cheese and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach in olive oil until wilted and drain excess moisture.
Mix spinach, feta, oregano, and eggs in a bowl.
Brush a baking sheet with olive oil and water.
Layer phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread spinach filling over phyllo.
Fold dough over filling and bake at 350°F for 35 minutes.

title: Souvlaki
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into cubes
instructions: Marinate chicken with garlic, oil, oregano, and lemon juice for 2 hours.
Thread chicken, bell pepper, onion, and zucchini onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes.
Turn skewers every 3 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges and tzatziki sauce.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Soak rice in vinegar for 10 minutes, then drain.
Mix lamb, rice, pine nuts, oregano, and garlic.
Place a spoonful of filling on each vine leaf.
Roll leaves tightly and place in a pot.
Cover with water and simmer for 1 hour.
Drain and serve warm or cold.

title: Kleftiko
instructions: Place lamb in a large roasting pan with garlic, oil, oregano, and lemon juice.
Add bay leaves and lemon slices.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 250°F for 8 hours.
Remove foil, increase oven temperature to 400°F.
Bake for 30 minutes until skin is crispy.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in a large pot.
Stir in tomato sauce and red wine, simmer for 10 minutes.
Whisk flour into milk to make a smooth white sauce, then stir in parmesan.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, top with white sauce.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach until wilted, squeeze out excess water, and let cool.
Mix spinach, feta, dill, eggs, water, oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Brush bottom of a 9x13 pan with melted butter.
Layer 4 phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Spread filling evenly over the sheets.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Cut into squares and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 1 minute to soften.
Mix ground beef, rice, onion, garlic, olive oil, tomato juice, dill, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf and roll tightly.
Arrange dolmades in a pot with enough water to cover them by 1 inch.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Let them cool in the liquid before serving.

title: Souvlaki
instructions: Whisk together olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Marinate chicken cubes in the mixture for at least 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto soaked wooden skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with pita bread and tzatziki sauce.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 1/2 cup feta cheese, a large block
instructions: Place tomato wedges, cucumber slices, red onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Top with a large block of feta cheese.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano.
Season lightly with salt.
Toss gently to combine and serve immediately.

title: Moussaka
ingredients: 2 cups béchamel sauce (flour, butter, milk, egg, nutmeg)
instructions: Fry eggplant slices until golden and drain on paper towels.
Sauté onion and garlic, then add ground lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and broth, simmer for 20 minutes.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish.
Pour béchamel sauce over the top, sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach until wilted, squeeze out excess water, and chop finely.
Mix spinach, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter and layer 3 sheets of phyllo.
Spread the spinach filling over the phyllo layers.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Cut into squares and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30-35 minutes.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Rinse grape leaves and blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Sauté onion and ground pork until cooked, add tomatoes and simmer.
Mix rice, cooked pork mixture, pine nuts, dill, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on a grape leaf, roll tightly, and place in pot.
Cover rolls with more leaves and pour olive oil and water over them.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until rice is tender.

title: Pastitsio
instructions: Boil pasta tubes according to package directions until al dente.
Brown ground beef with onion and garlic, then add tomatoes and ketchup.
Simmer meat sauce for 20 minutes and let cool slightly.
Layer half the pasta in a baking dish, then half the meat sauce.
Pour béchamel sauce over the meat layer, sprinkle with butter and cheese.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30 minutes until golden and hot.

title: Tiropita
instructions: Whisk feta cheese, eggs, milk, and oregano together until smooth.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and brush a baking sheet with butter.
Place phyllo sheet on surface, brush with butter, and spread cheese filling.
Fold phyllo over filling to create a half-moon shape.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly, then brush with softened butter and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and drain.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in a pan.
Mix lamb with tomato sauce, wine, and salt.
Layer eggplant, meat sauce, and cheese in a baking dish.
Whisk eggs and pour over the top.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until set.

title: Souvlaki
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes in oil, vinegar, oregano, garlic, salt, pepper, and lemon juice for 2 hours.
Thread chicken onto soaked wooden skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with Greek yogurt and tzatziki sauce.

title: Spanakopita
instructions: Sauté spinach in olive oil until wilted and squeeze out excess water.
Mix spinach with feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, and salt.
Brush phyllo dough with oil and layer in a baking pan.
Spread spinach mixture over the dough layers.
Bake at 350°F for 40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Baklava
instructions: Mix nuts with half the butter and spread in a pan.
Layer phyllo dough with butter between each sheet.
Cut the pastry into diamond shapes before baking.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Simmer honey, water, sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice.
Pour hot syrup over the hot pastry immediately.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Rinse grape leaves and boil briefly until soft.
Mix ground beef, rice, onion, garlic, oil, salt, and pepper.
Wrap rice mixture around each grape leaf.
Place rolls tightly in a pot and cover with tomato sauce.
Simmer covered on low heat for 45 minutes.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, then add lamb and cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Whisk milk, eggs, flour, and half the cheese to make the béchamel sauce.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a baking dish, top with béchamel.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Gyro
ingredients: 2 lbs ground beef and pork mix
instructions: Mix meat, yogurt, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Shape meat into a tall cylinder and cook on a grill or pan.
Slice the cooked meat thinly.
Fill warm pita breads with sliced meat, onion, tomato, and lettuce.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve immediately.

title: Dolmades
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Mix cooked rice, ground lamb, raw rice, onion, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each grape leaf and roll tightly.
Arrange rolls in a pot in a single layer.
Pour vegetable broth over the rolls and simmer for 1 hour.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and mix spinach, feta, eggs, ricotta, dill, and garlic powder.
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter and layer phyllo dough.
Spread the spinach mixture over the phyllo.
Cover with more buttered phyllo sheets.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden brown and crisp.

title: Greek Salad
instructions: Wash and chop all vegetables.
Place vegetables, olives, and feta cheese in a large bowl.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper together.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately.

title: Patisia (Epirotan Stuffed Tomatoes)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Roast the tomato halves cut-side up in the oven for 10 minutes to soften.
Sauté the minced garlic in olive oil until fragrant.
Mix the spinach, rice, garlic, feta, mint, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Stuff each tomato half with the spinach mixture.
Place tomatoes in a baking dish, drizzle with a little olive oil, and bake for 25 minutes until tender.

title: Makaronia me Ladera (Tomato-Olive Oil Pasta)
ingredients: 1/2 cup kalamata olives, pitted and chopped
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente, saving a cup of pasta water.
In a large pan, heat olive oil and sauté garlic until golden but not brown.
Add grated tomatoes, oregano, olives, and capers; simmer until the oil separates.
Toss the cooked pasta with the sauce, adding pasta water if needed.
Stir in toasted pine nuts and fresh parsley before serving.

title: Tigania (Epirotan Roasted Potatoes)
ingredients: 1.5 kg Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss potato wedges and onions with olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread mixture on a large baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 40 minutes, flipping halfway through, until edges are crispy and golden.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves before serving warm.

title: Sifaki (Saffron Rice with Lamb)
ingredients: 1 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: Brown the ground lamb with onions and garlic in olive oil; drain excess fat.
Add wine to the meat and let it reduce by half.
Rinse rice and add to the pot with stock, saffron water, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs and fluff the rice before serving.

title: Tzaziki with Wild Greens (Spithama)
ingredients: 1/2 cup wild greens (dika or rika), blanched and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the thick yogurt and grated cucumber.
Add the blanched wild greens, garlic, dill, mint, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, mixing gently to combine.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let flavors meld.
Serve chilled as a side dish with bread or vegetables.

title: Traditional Thessalian Moussaka
instructions: Boil the potato slices in salted water until tender, then drain and set aside.
Fry the eggplant slices in olive oil until golden brown on both sides.
In a large pot, sauté the onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add the ground lamb and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the wine, crushed tomatoes, parsley, mint, and cinnamon; simmer for 20 minutes.
Arrange half the fried eggplant in a baking dish, cover with the meat sauce, then top with the potatoes.
Pour the remaining béchamel sauce over the potatoes and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly.

title: Thessalian Village Kleftiko
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F).
Rub the lamb legs generously with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Stuff the cavity of each leg with the smashed garlic, lemon wedges, onion quarters, carrot, potato, and herbs.
Wrap each stuffed leg tightly in aluminum foil.
Place the wrapped legs in a large roasting pan and pour 2 cups of water into the pan.
Bake for 4 hours, basting occasionally with the pan juices, until the meat falls off the bone.
Carefully remove the foil and let the legs rest for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Thessalian Spinach and Ricotta Pie (Spanakopita)
instructions: Sauté the chopped spinach in olive oil until wilted, then squeeze out all excess moisture.
In a large bowl, mix the spinach, ricotta, eggs, feta, onion, garlic, dill, parsley, nutmeg, and 1/2 cup olive oil.
Butter a large baking dish and line it with 4 sheets of phyllo dough.
Spread the spinach mixture evenly over the phyllo layers.
Cover the filling with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter.
Cut the pie into diamond shapes with a sharp knife before baking.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and crispy.

title: Thessalian Lentil Soup (Kremmyda)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté the onions until translucent.
Add the carrots, celery, and garlic; cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed lentils, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for about 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are very soft and the soup is thick.
Remove from heat and stir in the fresh lemon juice.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

title: Thessalian Grilled Lamb Chops with Tzatziki
instructions: In a small bowl, mix minced garlic, olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper to create a marinade.
Rub the marinade all over the lamb chops and let them rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the chops for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached.
While the meat grills, make the tzatziki by mixing yogurt, grated cucumber, lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, and dill.
Let the chops rest for 5 minutes after grilling.
Slice the chops and serve immediately with a generous dollop of tzatziki on the side.

title: Traditional Greek Moussaka
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and drain on paper towels.
Brown ground lamb with onion and garlic in a separate pan.
Add crushed tomatoes, wine, and cinnamon to the meat; simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix yogurt with half of the grated cheeses.
Layer eggplant in a baking dish, cover with meat sauce, then top with remaining cheese and yogurt mixture.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Fried Calamari with Lemon
instructions: Rinse squid rings and pat dry thoroughly.
Whisk together flour, salt, pepper, cornstarch, and oregano in a shallow dish.
Dredge each squid ring in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a deep pan to 350°F.
Fry squid in batches for 2-3 minutes until crispy and golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle lightly with more salt if desired, and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Cycladic Spanakopita
instructions: Wilt spinach in a pan with a little water, then squeeze out all excess moisture.
Mix spinach, feta, dill, salt, nutmeg, and eggs in a bowl.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Place one sheet of phyllo on a baking sheet; brush with melted butter.
Add a second sheet and brush again, then spread half the spinach mixture over the bottom half.
Fold dough over filling, add another buttered sheet, then top with remaining filling and cover with two more buttered sheets.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Grilled Octopus (Kalamaraki)
ingredients: 1 whole octopus, cleaned and tentacles separated
instructions: Boil octopus tentacles in water with vinegar for 45 minutes until tender.
Brush tentacles with olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until charred but still juicy.
While grilling, make a marinade by mixing lemon juice, remaining oil, and a splash of water.
Serve hot tentacles with extra lemon juice and oregano on top.

title: Homemade Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ingredients: 1 large ripe tomato, cut into chunks
4 oz feta cheese, a large block
instructions: Arrange tomato, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Place the block of feta cheese on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Sprinkle dried oregano over the entire salad.
Gently toss just before serving to keep ingredients crisp.

title: Dolmades
ingredients: 250g ground lamb, mixed with 150g ground pork
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Mix the ground meat, rice, onion, oregano, salt, pepper, and half the olive oil in a bowl.
Fill each blanched grape leaf with a small amount of the meat mixture, rolling it tightly from the stem end.
Place the rolled dolmades in a large pot, standing them upright in a single layer.
Pour the broth and lemon juice over the dolmades until they are mostly submerged.
Add the remaining olive oil and cover the pot with a plate to keep the rolls submerged.
Simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes until the rice is tender.
Let them cool slightly before serving.

title: Kleftiko
ingredients: 1 whole lamb or goat, cut into large pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the meat generously with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Place the meat in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven and add the wine, broth, olive oil, and garlic.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and onion on top of the meat.
Cover and simmer on very low heat for 3 to 4 hours, or until the meat is falling apart.
Check occasionally to ensure liquid does not evaporate completely; add hot water if needed.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Avgolemono Soup
ingredients: 4 cups chicken stock, homemade or high quality
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a pot, bring the chicken stock and rice to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken and cook for another 5 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk the beaten eggs with the lemon juice until smooth.
Remove the soup from heat and let it cool slightly.
Slowly drizzle the egg-lemon mixture into the hot soup while stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
Stir in the olive oil and season with salt and white pepper.
Garnish with fresh dill and serve immediately.

title: Pitta with Tzatziki
instructions: Whisk together the Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, olive oil, dill, salt, and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Warm the pita breads in a toaster or oven until soft and pliable.
Spread a generous layer of tzatziki onto each pita.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry
1 small onion, finely chopped and sautéed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish with olive oil.
Mix the crumbled feta, ricotta, eggs, sautéed onion, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Fold in the dried spinach and mix well.
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo dough in the dish, brushing each with olive oil.
Spread the spinach and cheese mixture evenly over the bottom layer of phyllo.
Top with the remaining 6 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with olive oil.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Let cool for 15 minutes before slicing into squares.

title: Sofli (Traditional Thessaloniki Pancakes)
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, then gradually add the yeast mixture.
Knead the dough until smooth, cover, and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down the dough, add olive oil, and knead briefly.
Rest the dough for another 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into a large thin sheet, cut into squares, and fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Makaronades (Thessaloniki Pasta with Pine Nuts)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil salted water and cook the pasta until al dente, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté the onion until soft.
Add garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate.
Stir in the toasted pine nuts, walnuts, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Add the cooked pasta and the reserved pasta water to the pan.
Toss everything together over low heat until the pasta is coated and slightly moist.

title: Kontos (Thessaloniki Style Stuffed Tomatoes)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cut the tops off the tomatoes and scoop out the insides to create a hollow shell.
Mix the bulgur, pine nuts, cheese, garlic, salt, and chopped parsley in a bowl.
Stuff each tomato cavity with the mixture and press gently.
Place the stuffed tomatoes in a baking dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 40 minutes until the tomatoes are tender and the filling is hot.
Serve warm.

title: Fava (Thessaloniki Smooth Yellow Split Pea Purée)
instructions: Soak the split peas in cold water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain the peas and rinse them thoroughly.
In a large pot, sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the soaked peas, salt, and pepper, then cover with water.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer covered for about 1 hour until peas are very soft.
Remove from heat and blend the mixture until completely smooth.
Stir in the orange juice and fresh dill, then serve warm or cold.

title: Saganaki with Feta (Thessaloniki Style)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place the feta cheese in a shallow baking dish or on a baking sheet.
Drizzle the olive oil over the cheese.
Sprinkle the oregano, cinnamon, and nutmeg evenly over the top.
Bake for 10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and slightly browned on the edges.
Remove from the oven and drizzle with lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh mint and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Traditional Greek Moussaka
ingredients: 3 large eggplants, sliced lengthwise and salted
1 lb ground lamb, mixed with ground beef
2 cups béchamel sauce ingredients (flour, butter, milk, eggs, nutmeg)
instructions: Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Brown the meat with onions and garlic in a large pot.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer for 30 minutes.
Prepare béchamel sauce by making a roux, adding milk gradually, and finishing with beaten eggs and nutmeg.
Layer eggplant, meat sauce, and béchamel in a baking dish and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes.

title: Avgolemono Soup
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast or thighs, cooked and shredded
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and lemon juice until pale and thick.
Slowly temper the yolk mixture by adding a few ladles of warm chicken broth while whisking constantly.
Pour the tempered mixture back into the pot of warm broth off the heat.
Stir in the cooked rice and shredded chicken.
Season with salt, white pepper, and butter, then serve hot.

title: Spanakopita
ingredients: 1 lb fresh spinach, chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix spinach, feta, eggs, dill, scallions, salt, and olive oil in a large bowl.
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter.
Layer 8 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with butter.
Spread the spinach filling over the phyllo layers.
Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Cut into squares and bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden.

title: Gemista
ingredients: 1 lb small tomatoes or bell peppers, halved and deseeded
instructions: Sauté onions and garlic in olive oil, then add meats and cook until browned.
Stir in rice and season with salt and pepper.
Fill tomato and pepper halves with the meat mixture.
Arrange vegetables in a baking dish and pour broth and bay leaf around them.
Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 1 hour, then remove foil and bake 15 more minutes.

title: Tzatziki with Grilled Pita
ingredients: 1 large cucumber, grated and well-squeezed dry
1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil for brushing
instructions: Grate cucumber and squeeze out all excess moisture using a clean towel.
In a bowl, mix yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, olive oil, dill, and salt.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let flavors meld.
Brush pita bread with olive oil and grill until lightly charred.
Serve tzatziki alongside the warm grilled pita.

title: Dakos
ingredients: 1 cup coarse bulgur wheat, soaked in water for 10 minutes
instructions: Drain the soaked bulgur wheat well and place it on a serving plate.
Mix the chopped tomatoes, olive oil, oregano, and salt in a bowl.
Pour the tomato mixture over the bulgur.
Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese on top.
Serve immediately as a light meal or appetizer.

title: Fava
ingredients: 1 lb dried yellow split peas, picked over and rinsed
instructions: Rinse the split peas thoroughly and soak them in cold water for at least 2 hours.
Boil the soaked peas with the onion and garlic until very soft and mushy, about 45 minutes.
Drain the cooking liquid, keeping only 1/2 cup of the liquid.
Blend the cooked peas, onion, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and reserved liquid until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
Garnish with fresh dill before serving cold.

title: Moussaka
instructions: Brush eggplant slices with oil and roast until golden and tender, about 20 minutes.
In a large pan, fry the ground lamb with onion and garlic until browned.
Add broth and wine to the meat, then stir in crushed tomatoes; simmer for 30 minutes.
Make the béchamel sauce by melting butter, whisking in flour, and slowly adding milk until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in Parmesan cheese and eggs.
Layer the eggplant slices in a baking dish, then pour the meat sauce over them.
Cover the top with the béchamel sauce and the phyllo dough.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly.

title: Saganaki with Potatoes
ingredients: 4 large potatoes, peeled and sliced into rounds
instructions: Sauté the potato slices in olive oil until they are golden and cooked through.
In the same pan, cook the sliced onions until translucent.
Add the white wine and let it reduce slightly.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the mixture for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Arrange the cooked potatoes in a serving dish and pour the sauce over them.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Kleftiko Lamb
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
4 large carrots, cut into large pieces
instructions: Rub the lamb chunks generously with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place the lamb in a large baking dish and add the potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, lemon, thyme, and rosemary.
Pour 1/2 cup of water into the dish to create steam during cooking.
Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake at 325°F (165°C) for 3 to 4 hours until the lamb is extremely tender and falling apart.
Remove the foil, increase heat to 400°F (200°C), and bake for another 15 minutes to brown the top.
Serve with the pan juices and vegetables.

title: Gigantes Plaki
ingredients: 1 kg large white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and place them in a pot with fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until beans are tender but not falling apart.
Heat olive oil in a large baking dish and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in tomato puree, oregano, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Add the cooked beans and enough water to almost cover them.
Cover and bake in a preheated oven at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

title: Pastitsio
instructions: Brown the beef mince with chopped onion and grated carrots in a pan.
Add tomato sauce, cinnamon, and simmer for 15 minutes; set aside.
Cook pasta tubes in salted boiling water until al dente.
Whisk eggs, milk, and olive oil together for the béchamel base.
Heat olive oil in a saucepan, whisk in flour to make a roux, then gradually add the egg mixture while stirring constantly until thick.
