Stir in fresh coriander leaves and cook uncovered for another 5 minutes to dry the gravy.

title: Kadhi Pakora
instructions: Mix yogurt, 1/2 cup chickpea flour, cumin, turmeric, and salt in a bowl to make a smooth batter.
For pakoras, mix gram flour, chopped coriander, mint, salt, and water to form a thick dough.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry pakoras until golden brown.
In a separate pan, heat oil and fry cumin seeds until they pop.
Add the yogurt batter to the pan and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until thickened.
Serve hot kadhi with the crispy pakoras.

title: Dal Tadka
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal, soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked dal with water and turmeric until soft, about 3-4 whistles.
Drain excess water and adjust consistency with little water if needed.
Heat ghee in a pan and add cumin seeds, dried red chilies, and green chilies.
Sauté until the cumin splutters and turns golden brown.
Add ginger and asafoetida, cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the cooked dal and simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Vegetable Kofta Curry
instructions: Mix mashed potatoes, spinach, semolina, spices, and salt to form a dough.
Shape into small round koftas and roll in gram flour.
Deep fry koftas until golden brown and set aside.
Prepare onion-tomato gravy by sautéing onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste, and spices.
Simmer the gravy until it thickens.
Add the fried koftas to the gravy and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with roti or rice.

title: Baingan Bharta
ingredients: 2 large brinjals (eggplants), halved and stuffed with salt
1/2 tsp amchur (dry mango powder) or lemon juice
instructions: Roast the stuffed brinjals over an open flame or grill until charred and soft, then peel and mash them.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Sauté chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add red chili powder, turmeric, and garam masala, followed by the mashed brinjal.
Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture becomes a thick paste.
Stir in coriander, mint, and amchur or lemon juice.
Serve warm with roti or paratha.

title: Rajasthani Gatte ki Sabzi
instructions: Mix gram flour, yogurt, spices, salt, and baking soda to form a thick batter.
Heat oil in a kadhai and deep fry small dumplings of the batter until golden brown.
Prepare onion-tomato gravy by sautéing onions, tomatoes, and spices.
Add the fried gatte to the gravy and simmer for 10 minutes.
Finish with a dollop of ghee and a pinch of fenugreek seeds if using.
Serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Undhiyu (Mixed Vegetable Stir-fry)
ingredients: 1 cup young raw banana (plantain) slices, soaked in salted water
1/4 cup fresh fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
instructions: Steam all the prepared vegetables until they are 70% cooked.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Sauté the steamed vegetables with turmeric and salt.
Stir-fry on low heat for 10-15 minutes, adding a little water if needed.
Add amchur and crushed kasuri methi towards the end.
Garnish with coriander and mint leaves.
Serve as a standalone dish or with dal and rice.

title: Appam and Stew
ingredients: 2 cups rice flour, for appam batter
1 cup coconut milk, for appam batter
2 cups ripe banana, mashed, for stew
1/2 cup green chilies, slit, for stew
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, yeast, and jaggery to make a thin, non-sticky batter; let it ferment overnight.
Heat oil in a pan, pour batter in the center to form the cup shape, and place a lit matchstick in the middle to cook the appam.
In a separate pot, boil mashed banana with coconut milk, tomato puree, and diced potato.
Temper mustard seeds in a little oil, add green chilies and turmeric, then pour over the boiling stew.
Serve the fluffy appam hot with the sweet and tangy banana stew.

title: Karimeen Pollichathu
ingredients: 500g pearl spot fish (karimeen), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Grind coconut, green chilies, black pepper, salt, and ginger into a coarse paste.
Make small packets of banana leaf, place a piece of ginger in the center.
Stuff each pearl spot fish with the spice paste and wrap tightly in the banana leaf packets.
Heat mustard oil in a clay pot or pan over medium heat.
Place the wrapped fish gently into the oil and cook until the leaves are crisp and fish is done.

title: Avial
instructions: Steam the raw banana, pumpkin, drumstick leaves, and spinach until tender.
Grind the steamed vegetables with half of the grated coconut and turmeric into a coarse paste.
In a pan, temper mustard seeds and urad dal with oil until they crackle.
Add the vegetable paste to the pan, mix well, and cook on low heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining grated coconut and salt just before serving.

title: Meen Pollichathu (Fish Stuffed in Banana Leaf)
ingredients: 500g fresh sea fish, cleaned and boned
instructions: Grind coconut, coriander, green chilies, black pepper, salt, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Stuff the fish fillets with the spice paste and roll them tightly.
Wrap each stuffed fish in a banana leaf packet.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai over medium flame.
Place the banana leaf packets in the oil and fry until golden brown and crisp.

title: Pulissery
instructions: Boil the diced jackfruit in water with a pinch of salt until tender.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt ghee and fry the jackfruit pieces until golden.
Add grated jaggery and water to the pan and simmer until the syrup thickens.
Stir in cardamom, black pepper, cinnamon, and cloves powder.
Serve warm with steamed rice.

title: Sambar
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal, soaked and pressure cooked
1 cup mixed vegetables (drumsticks, carrot, beans, pumpkin), chopped
1/2 cup tamarind pulp, soaked in warm water
3 tbsp grated coconut, roasted and ground
instructions: Pressure cook the toor dal until soft and mash it slightly.
In a large pot, temper mustard seeds and green chilies in oil.
Add curry leaves and sauté for a minute.
Mix in the sambar powder and roasted coconut paste, stirring well to remove raw smell.
Add the tamarind water, salt, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped vegetables and cook until tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with rice.

title: Rasam
ingredients: 1 cup tamarind pulp, soaked in warm water
2 tbsp toor dal, pressure cooked and mashed
instructions: Mix the tamarind water, mashed dal, sambar powder, pepper powder, and salt in a pot.
Add 1 cup of water and bring to a boil, simmering for 5 minutes.
Temper oil in a separate small pan, add slit green chilies and curry leaves.
Pour the hot tempering into the boiling rasam and stir.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve warm with steamed rice.

title: Pulihora (Tamarind Rice)
ingredients: 1/2 cup tamarind pulp, soaked and extracted
instructions: Cook the basmati rice in water with a pinch of salt until fluffy and drain well.
In a bowl, mix the rice with the extracted tamarind water and salt to taste.
In a pan, heat oil and temper mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, and cumin seeds.
Add green chilies and curry leaves, then remove from heat.
Sprinkle the tempering over the rice and mix thoroughly.
Garnish with fried coconut and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Thosai (Lentil Crepes)
ingredients: 1 cup urad dal, soaked for 2 hours
1/2 cup moong dal, soaked for 2 hours
instructions: Grind the soaked urad dal, moong dal, and rice into a smooth, thin batter.
In a separate bowl, grind the grated coconut, coriander, green chilies, and salt into a coarse paste.
Heat a non-stick pan and pour a ladleful of batter, spreading it into a thin circle.
Sprinkle the coconut mixture in the center and sprinkle cumin seeds around the edges.
Drizzle oil along the edges and cook until golden brown on both sides.
Serve immediately with coconut chutney and sambar.

title: Pongal
instructions: Combine rice, moong dal, water, and salt in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the mixture becomes soft and creamy.
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, green chilies, and asafoetida when the dal starts to crackle.
Stir in the grated coconut and coriander leaves.
Drizzle ghee over the top and mix gently.
Simmer for another 2 minutes to allow flavors to meld, then serve hot.

title: Shukto
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds, wait for them to splutter.
Add green chilies and stir for 30 seconds.
Add snake gourd and drumstick leaves, cook covered for 10 minutes.
Add spinach, turmeric, black salt, and rock salt.
Cover and cook until all vegetables are tender.
Garnish with fresh grated coconut before serving.

title: Macher Jhol
ingredients: 1/2 kg Hilsa or Rohu fish, cleaned and cut into pieces
2 cups fresh fish stock or water
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a deep pan.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, let them splutter.
Add green chilies, turmeric, rock salt, and dried ginger powder.
Gently add fish pieces and coat them with the spice mixture.
Pour in the fish stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add whisked yogurt slowly while stirring to prevent curdling.
Simmer on low heat for 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked.
Garnish with fresh grated coconut and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Cholar Dal
ingredients: 1 cup split Bengal gram (chana dal), soaked for 2 hours
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked Bengal gram with turmeric and rock salt until soft.
Heat mustard oil in a separate pan.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, wait for them to pop.
Add the slit green chili and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the cooked dal and mash it slightly with a spoon.
Add dried ginger powder and black salt, mix well.
Stir in the grated fresh coconut and cook for another 2 minutes.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Bhapa Mach
ingredients: 1/2 kg Rohu or Katla fish, cleaned and scored
1 cup rice, cooked in a 1:1 ratio with water
instructions: Mix cooked rice with grated coconut, rock salt, black salt, turmeric, and half the coriander.
Make a hollow in the center of the fish pieces and stuff with the spiced rice mixture.
Heat mustard oil in a steamer basket.
Place the stuffed fish on a banana leaf or foil-lined steamer tray.
Cover and steam on high heat for 20-25 minutes until fish is flaky.
Drizzle remaining mustard oil over the steamed fish.
Garnish with remaining coriander and serve immediately.

title: Shorshe Ilish
ingredients: 1 whole Hilsa fish (Ilish), cleaned and scaled
instructions: Make deep diagonal slits on both sides of the Hilsa fish.
Rub the fish inside and outside with rock salt, black salt, dried ginger powder, and half the mustard paste.
Let it marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a non-stick pan over medium flame.
Place the fish in the pan, skin side down, and pour the remaining mustard paste over it.
Cover and cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Flip the fish gently, sprinkle grated coconut and slit green chilies on top.
Cover and cook for another 2 minutes until the coconut is slightly browned.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 500g chicken pieces, cut into large chunks
1/2 cup yogurt, whisked with 1 teaspoon vinegar
instructions: Heat oil in a large karahi or wok over medium-high heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 10 seconds.
Add sliced onions and cook until they turn golden brown and crisp.
Add chicken pieces, red chili powder, turmeric, and ginger.
Stir well and cook uncovered for 5-7 minutes until chicken is sealed and slightly browned.
Pour in the whisked yogurt mixture and stir gently to avoid curdling.
Add chicken stock, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add slit green chilies and cook for another 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with naan or roti.

title: Aloo Gobi
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan or wok over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft and translucent.
Add minced ginger and green chilies, cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle turmeric, coriander, cumin, and salt; stir for 30 seconds.
Add cauliflower florets and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Add potato cubes and stir to coat with spices.
Pour in about 1/2 cup of water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Check water level and add more if needed, cooking until potatoes are tender.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Finish with garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.

title: Chai (Masala Tea)
ingredients: 1 inch piece of fresh ginger, crushed
instructions: Crush the cardamom pods and add all whole spices (ginger, cloves, cinnamon, peppercorns) to a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add the water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
Once boiling, add the loose tea leaves and stir.
Reduce heat to medium and let it simmer for 3-4 minutes to extract the flavor.
Pour in the milk and continue to simmer until the milk reduces by about half.
Add the sugar (or jaggery) and stir until completely dissolved.
If desired, add a pinch of baking soda and stir vigorously to create a frothy foam.
Turn off the heat and let the chai steep for 2 minutes.
Strain the tea into cups, ensuring all the spices and leaves are removed.
Serve immediately while piping hot.

title: Raita with Cucumber and Mint
ingredients: 1 cup plain yogurt (dahi), whisked until smooth
1 small cucumber, peeled and grated finely
1 tablespoon roasted cumin seeds, crushed (optional garnish)
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the whisked yogurt, chopped mint, and chopped coriander.
Add the grated cucumber and toss gently to coat evenly.
Sprinkle the cumin powder, black salt, regular salt, and chaat masala over the mixture.
Mix everything thoroughly until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Before serving, stir again and optionally garnish with crushed roasted cumin seeds.
Serve chilled alongside spicy curries to cool the palate.

title: Litti Chokha
instructions: Boil the potatoes, eggplant, and tomatoes until very soft. Peel the skin off the eggplant and tomato while hot.
Mash the potatoes, eggplant, and tomatoes together in a bowl. Add cilantro, mint, green chilies, lemon juice, salt, and a little ghee. Mix well to make the chokha.
In a large bowl, combine semolina, whole wheat flour, yogurt, salt, and 2 tablespoons of ghee.
Gradually add water to form a stiff, non-sticky dough; knead well until smooth.
Roll the dough into small balls (litti), then flatten slightly and make an indentation in the center.
Fill each indentation with a generous portion of the chokha mixture.
Pinch the edges of the dough closed securely to seal the filling inside.
Heat a tandoor or a very hot charcoal grill. Place the litti on the grill.
Roast the litti, turning frequently, until the outside is charred and crisp and the inside is fully cooked (about 15-20 minutes).
Serve hot, brushing with extra ghee, alongside the remaining chokha.

title: Bhorta (Mashed Eggplant)
instructions: Roast the eggplants over an open flame until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Peel the eggplants and mash the flesh into a coarse paste.
In a pan, heat oil and fry the peanuts until golden brown, then remove them.
Fry the shallots and green chilies in the same oil until fragrant.
Add the fried peanuts, shallots, chilies, salt, and coriander powder to the mashed eggplant.
Mix everything together until well combined and serve with rice.

title: Shorshe Ilish (Mustard Hilsa)
ingredients: 4 whole Hilsa fish, cleaned and scaled
instructions: Season the Hilsa fish with salt and let it marinate for 15 minutes.
In a clay pot or heavy pan, heat mustard oil over medium heat.
Add the cardamoms and bay leaf, then add the chopped ginger, garlic, and green chilies.
Sauté the aromatics until the oil separates from the spices.
Stir in the mustard paste and cook for 2-3 minutes until it bubbles slightly.
Gently place the marinated Hilsa fish into the pot, skin side down.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes until the fish flakes easily.

title: Bhuna Shukto
ingredients: 1/2 cup green beans, cut into pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat mustard oil and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
When the seeds splutter, add the dried red chilies and curry leaves.
Add the grated ginger and green chilies, then fry for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, cauliflower, raw banana, green beans, and eggplant.
Add turmeric, salt, and 1 cup of water; cover and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the mustard seeds again if you like a stronger flavor, then let it cook for another 10 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.

title: Chingri Malai Curry
instructions: In a pan, melt butter and sauté the chopped onions until translucent.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies; cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chili powder, and salt; cook until the oil separates.
Stir in the coconut milk and fresh cream, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the prawns and cook for 5-7 minutes until they turn pink and are fully cooked.
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander leaves on top.
Serve immediately with steamed basmati rice.

title: Pitha (Sweet Rice Cake)
instructions: In a bowl, mix rice flour, baking powder, salt, and cardamom powder.
Gradually add milk and water to form a soft, non-sticky dough.
Heat ghee in a small pan and fry the grated coconut with jaggery until golden brown.
In a separate pan, melt the remaining ghee and add the fried coconut-jaggery mixture.
Add a little sugar if desired and stir until well combined.
Roll small portions of the dough into circles and flatten them slightly.
Place a small amount of the sweet coconut filling in the center of each flatbread.
Cook on a griddle with a little ghee until both sides are golden brown.

title: Rice and Curry (Thiyal)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked and drained
1 kg mixed vegetables (pumpkin, eggplant, beans, carrots), cut into chunks
1 cup grated coconut, soaked and grated
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry the sliced onions until golden brown.
Add the green chilies, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves, sautéing for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground coriander and cumin seeds, then add the mixed vegetables.
Pour in 1 cup of fresh coconut milk (made from grated coconut and water) and cook until vegetables are tender.
Rinse the soaked rice and add it to the vegetable curry with salt.
Cover and steam on low heat for 15 minutes until the rice is fluffy and absorbs the flavors.

title: String Hoppers (Thappal)
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated coconut, soaked and grated
1 cup coconut milk, made from grated coconut and water
instructions: Mix rice flour and salt in a bowl, then gradually add boiling water to form a soft, pliable dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and cover it to rest for 15 minutes.
Oil a bamboo string hopper maker and dust it with rice flour.
Take a small ball of dough, flatten it, and spread grated coconut on top.
Place the ball in the hopper maker and steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot with a side of coconut milk.

title: Kottu Roti
ingredients: 4 cups flattened roti, chopped into small pieces
200g chicken breast or beef, sliced thin
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large wok over high heat and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the meat and cook until browned, then stir in the curry powder and green chilies.
Add the cabbage, beans, carrots, and a splash of water; cook until vegetables are slightly softened.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble quickly, breaking them into small curds.
Add the chopped roti pieces and toss continuously, breaking them apart as they cook.
Season with salt and serve immediately while hot and crispy.

title: Hoppers (Appa)
ingredients: 1 tbsp grated coconut, soaked and grated
1 cup coconut milk, made from grated coconut and water
instructions: Mix rice flour and mung bean flour in a bowl, then add salt and gradually incorporate boiling water to make a smooth, thin batter.
Let the batter rest for 20 minutes to thicken slightly.
Heat a special hopper pan or a small non-stick pan with coconut oil.
Pour the batter into the center of the hot pan, tilting it to cover the bottom evenly.
Sprinkle a little grated coconut on top and cover with a lid.
Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and the edges are cooked, then flip and cook the other side.

title: Fish Cutlet (Muda Pol Hura)
ingredients: 500g firm white fish fillets (like kingfish or tuna), boneless
1 cup coconut milk, made from grated coconut and water
instructions: Mix the chopped fish, onion, green chilies, ginger, curry powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add rice flour, breadcrumbs, and beaten egg to the mixture and knead until it forms a firm dough.
Shape the mixture into oval patties and flatten them slightly.
Heat coconut oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve warm with a side of coconut milk or lemon.

title: Sarson ka Saag
instructions: Boil the mustard greens, spinach, and methi leaves until very soft, then drain.
Grind the cooked greens into a coarse paste.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry the potato cubes until golden.
Add the green paste to the pot and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a separate pan, melt butter and fry besan until it turns light brown to make the chilla, then mix the chilla pieces into the saag.

title: Dal Makhani
ingredients: 200g whole black lentils (urad dal), soaked overnight
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked lentils and beans with water and salt until soft.
In a pan, heat ghee and fry the sliced onions until golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes, chili powder, and cumin seeds; cook until tomatoes are mushy.
Mix the cooked lentils and beans into the onion-tomato masala and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in butter, fresh cream, and garam masala, then simmer on low heat for another 10 minutes.

title: Amritsari Kachori
instructions: Mix all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, chickpea flour, yogurt, baking soda, and salt to make a stiff dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and flatten them into discs.
Place a spoonful of the spiced chickpea filling in the center of each disc.
Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges tightly, then flatten again.
Deep fry the kachoris in hot oil until they are puffed up and golden brown, then dust with cumin powder.

title: Malai Kofta
instructions: Mix paneer cubes, mashed potato, breadcrumbs, spices, and flour to form a stiff dough.
Roll small portions of the mixture into smooth balls (koftas).
Deep fry the koftas in ghee until golden brown and set aside.
In a separate pan, melt butter and fry onions until translucent and slightly brown.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates, then add cream and kasuri methi.
Gently add the fried koftas to the gravy and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Lamb Rogan Josh
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: Marinate the lamb cubes with whisked yogurt, chili powder, turmeric, fennel, cardamom, and cloves for at least 2 hours.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot and fry the marinated meat until well browned.
Add sliced onions and cook until they turn golden brown and soft.
Add 2 cups of water, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick; cover and cook on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Adjust the gravy consistency with a little water, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve hot.

title: Dal Bhindi
ingredients: 1 cup green gram dal, soaked overnight
instructions: Cook the soaked dal with turmeric and salt until soft.
Heat oil in a pan and temper mustard seeds until they splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for one minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until the oil separates.
Mix in sliced okra, chili powder, and salt; cook on low heat until okra is tender.
Combine the cooked dal with the okra mixture.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Thepla
instructions: Mix all dry spices, chopped leaves, grated ginger, and half the ghee with the flour.
Add water gradually to form a stiff dough and knead well.
Rest the dough for at least 30 minutes covered with a damp cloth.
Roll out small portions of the dough into thin, round discs.
Heat a dry griddle or tawa on medium-high heat.
Place the rolled dough on the hot griddle and cook until bubbles appear.
Flip and brush the top with a little ghee.
Cook the other side until golden brown spots appear.
Serve warm with pickle or yogurt.

title: Khandvi
ingredients: 1 cup moth beans (matki), soaked and ground into a paste
instructions: Mix the bean paste, chickpea flour, yogurt, grated coconut, and spices to form a smooth batter.
Heat ghee in a pan and add the batter, stirring continuously to cook until thick.
Spread the cooked mixture thinly onto greased banana leaves or a plate.
Roll the cooled sheet tightly into a cylinder.
Cut the roll into 1-inch wide strips using a sharp knife.
Brush the strips with melted ghee before serving.
Serve immediately with chutney or pickle.

title: Undhiyu
ingredients: Mustard seeds and asafoetida for tempering
instructions: Steam all the vegetables separately until just tender-crisp.
In a large pan, heat ghee and temper with mustard seeds and asafoetida.
Add grated ginger, coconut, turmeric, and chili powder; sauté for one minute.
Add the steamed vegetables and mix gently to coat them with the spice paste.
Cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add salt to taste and adjust consistency with a little water if needed.
Serve hot with rice or as a standalone dish.

title: Khaman Dhokla
instructions: Mix rice flour, chickpea flour, yogurt, water, turmeric, and salt in a bowl.
Let the batter rest for 20 minutes.
Stir in baking soda and eno fruit salt just before steaming.
Pour the batter into a greased steamer tray.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until the cake is spongy and cooked through.
While steaming, heat ghee in a small pan and temper with cumin seeds, green chilies, and a pinch of sugar.
Once the dhokla is ready, remove from steamer and immediately pour the hot tempering over it.
Cut into diamond shapes and serve with green chutney.

title: Kerala Style Chicken Curry
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pot and fry the onions until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cumin seeds, sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces, turmeric, and red chili powder; stir well to coat.
Pour in the fresh coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in the crushed peanuts and slit green chilies just before serving.

title: Appam with Stew
ingredients: 1 cup fermented rice batter, thin consistency
2 tbsp jaggery, dissolved in warm water
1/2 cup chicken or mutton stew, ready-made or homemade
instructions: Heat coconut oil in an iron pan or appam maker and pour a small amount in the center.
Pour the fermented rice batter around the edges in a circular motion.
Drizzle the coconut milk over the batter.
Add the dissolved jaggery to the center of the appam.
Cook on medium heat until the edges are crisp and the center is soft.
Serve hot with a side of onion, green chili, peanuts, and a generous scoop of stew.

title: Parotta with Vegetable Stew
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (beans, carrots, potatoes), chopped
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Gradually add melted butter and knead into a soft dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes, then roll out thin layers, stacking them with butter between each.
Roll the stacked dough into a very thin, large circle and cook on a hot tawa until golden spots appear.
In a separate pot, heat coconut oil and fry onions until translucent.
Add mustard seeds, let them splutter, then add the chopped vegetables.
Pour in coconut milk, add slit green chilies, and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Serve the crispy parottas folded with the warm vegetable stew.

title: Erissery (Mixed Vegetable Curry)
instructions: Boil the green beans, raw banana, pumpkin, and yam separately until 70% cooked, then set aside.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and fry the chopped onions until golden.
Add grated ginger and mustard seeds, sauté for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground peanuts and the partially cooked vegetables.
Add the fresh grated coconut and slit green chilies.
Cook on low heat for 10 minutes, allowing the spices to infuse, then serve.

title: Pulissery (Coconut Rice with Curd)
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pan and temper with mustard seeds and asafoetida.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell disappears.
Pour in the thick coconut milk and whisk to combine well.
Add the whisked yogurt slowly, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Add the cooked rice, ground peanuts, and grated fresh coconut.
Season with salt and cook on low heat for 5 minutes until the rice is fully coated and creamy.

title: Sambar
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal, soaked and pressure cooked
2 cups mixed vegetables (drumstick, pumpkin, carrot, beans)
1 cup tamarind pulp, soaked in warm water
instructions: Cook toor dal with salt until soft.
Boil mixed vegetables until tender.
Temper mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, dried red chilies, ginger, and green chilies in ghee.
Add curry leaves and asafoetida to the tempering.
Add tamarind pulp and sambar powder to the dal and stir well.
Add boiled vegetables and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Appam
instructions: Grind rice and grated coconut together with yeast, salt, and boiling water to make a smooth batter.
Cover and let the batter ferment for 8-10 hours until it rises and becomes spongy.
Heat a cast-iron pan and add a little oil.
Pour a ladle of batter into the center of the pan.
Pour another ladle of batter around the edges.
Cover and cook on low heat until the edges are crisp and the center is soft.
Repeat with remaining batter.

title: Kootu
ingredients: 1 cup raw banana or yam, grated and pressure cooked
instructions: Pressure cook grated raw banana or yam with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
Cook toor dal until soft.
In a pan, heat oil or ghee and temper mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and green chili.
Add cooked vegetables, dal, grated coconut, coconut chutney, and turmeric.
Mix well and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Pulihora (Tamarind Rice)
ingredients: 1/2 cup tamarind paste, soaked in warm water
instructions: Cook rice with a little extra water until fluffy, then spread on a tray to cool.
Soak tamarind paste in warm water and squeeze to extract juice.
In a pan, heat ghee and temper mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, green chili, and asafoetida.
Add cooked rice, tamarind juice, jaggery, ground peanuts, turmeric, and salt.
Toss gently on low heat until the rice is coated and slightly crisp.
Serve warm.

title: Machan (Buttermilk Rice)
instructions: Cook parboiled rice with water until soft and fluffy.
In a pan, heat oil and temper mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and green chili.
Add cooked rice and turmeric powder, mix well.
Stir in buttermilk and grated coconut.
Cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with a side of chutney.

title: Macher Jhol
ingredients: 1 kg fresh silver carp or hilsa fish, cleaned and cut into large pieces
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat until it smokes slightly.
Add the ginger strips and cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf, then fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the water and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the fish pieces gently and the chopped tomatoes.
Season with salt and add the green chilies.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the fish is tender.
Serve hot with steamed white rice.

title: Shukto
ingredients: 1/2 cup French beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a wide pot and add cumin and mustard seeds.
Once they splutter, add the chopped onion and fry until golden.
Add ginger, turmeric, and green chilies, then stir well.
Add the harder vegetables (drumsticks, pumpkin, potato) and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining vegetables (beans, spinach) and stir to coat.
Add 1.5 cups of water and salt, then cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes.
Check if the vegetables are tender and the oil has separated; serve hot.

title: Kosha Mangsho
instructions: Marinate the mutton cubes with yogurt, turmeric, half the ginger garlic paste, salt, and spices for 2 hours.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot and add the whole spices.
Add the marinated mutton and cook on high heat until the oil separates from the meat.
Add the chopped onions and fry until they turn golden brown.
Stir in the remaining ginger garlic paste and green chilies.
Add 2 cups of water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
Uncover and cook on high heat to evaporate excess water until the gravy thickens.

title: Chingri Malai Curry
ingredients: 500 g large prawns (shrimp), cleaned and deveined
instructions: Melt butter in a pan over medium heat and add onions, garlic, ginger, and green chili.
Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt; stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the water and bring to a simmer.
Gently add the prawns to the simmering gravy.
Cook for 5 minutes until the prawns turn pink and the shells separate.
Stir in the fresh cream and cook for another 2 minutes without boiling vigorously.

title: Dal Puli
ingredients: 1 cup yellow lentils (chana dal), soaked for 2 hours
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked lentils with 2 cups of water and turmeric until soft (about 8-10 minutes).
Heat mustard oil in a separate pan and add cumin seeds and the bay leaf.
Add the sliced onions and fry until they turn deep golden brown.
Add the garlic and green chilies, then cook for another minute.
Pour the fried onion mixture over the cooked lentils and mix well.
Add salt to taste and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a pan until crispy and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks, grated cheeses, and plenty of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add hot pasta to the pan with guanciale (off heat) and toss to combine.
Pour the egg mixture over the pasta, stirring vigorously and adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Homemade Pizza Margherita
ingredients: 300g San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Mix flour, salt, and yeast in a bowl; gradually add water and knead until smooth.
Let the dough rise in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled in size.
Punch down dough and divide into portions; let rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to its highest setting (250°C/480°F) with a pizza stone inside.
Spread crushed tomatoes on the dough, leaving a border for the crust.
Top with slices of mozzarella and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves and sea salt before serving.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable stock, kept warm
150g saffron threads, soaked in 50ml warm water
instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer in a separate pot.
Melt half the butter in a heavy-bottomed pot; sauté onion until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add saffron-infused water and a ladle of hot stock; stir until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently until rice is creamy but al dente.
Remove from heat; stir in remaining butter, Parmigiano, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Serve immediately.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper; dust lightly with flour.
In a large Dutch oven, brown the veal shanks in batches; set aside.
Render pancetta in the same pot, then add onions, carrots, and celery; cook until soft.
Return veal to pot; pour in white wine and scrape up browned bits.
Add beef stock, cover, and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until meat is tender.
Serve hot osso buco topped generously with fresh gremolata.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: In a heatproof bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar over a simmering water bath until pale and thick.
Remove from heat; let cool to room temperature.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
Fold mascarpone into the cooled egg mixture, then gently fold in whipped cream.
Dip ladyfingers quickly into cooled espresso and arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half the cream mixture over the biscuits; repeat with another layer of biscuits and cream.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While the water heats, fry the guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy and the fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, grated Pecorino, grated Parmigiano, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Remove the skillet from the heat and toss the hot pasta with the crispy guanciale and fat.
Quickly pour the egg and cheese mixture over the hot pasta, stirring vigorously and adding splashes of pasta water to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and black pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable broth, kept hot
instructions: Melt 30g of butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the Arborio rice and toast it for 2 minutes until the edges become translucent.
Stir in the white wine and cook until it is completely evaporated.
Dissolve the saffron threads in a little warm broth, then add the broth to the rice one ladle at a time.
Stir constantly, adding more hot broth as the previous ladle is absorbed, until the rice is tender but still firm to the bite (about 18-20 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in the remaining 20g of butter and the grated Parmigiano cheese.
Mound the risotto onto warm plates and serve immediately.

title: Osso Buco
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and coat them lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy pot and sear the shanks on all sides until browned. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom, letting it reduce by half.
Add the canned tomatoes, stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Return the shanks to the pot, ensuring they are submerged.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender.
Remove the shanks, strain the sauce, and return the sauce to the pot to reduce slightly if desired.
Serve the shanks with the sauce, a squeeze of fresh lemon, and a garnish of gremolata.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Separate the egg whites from the yolks, ensuring no whites touch the yolks.
Whisk the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until thick and pale. Remove from heat and cool completely.
In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
Fold the cooled egg yolk mixture into the mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture to lighten it.
Mix the cooled espresso with the coffee liqueur in a shallow dish.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture and arrange them in a single layer at the bottom of the dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the cookies, then add another layer of dipped cookies, and top with the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight before serving, dusted generously with cocoa powder.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
In a skillet, cook diced guanciale over medium heat until crispy and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano, and black pepper.
Drain pasta, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
Remove skillet from heat and toss in hot pasta.
Quickly pour egg mixture over pasta while stirring vigorously to create a creamy sauce.
Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable broth, kept warm
1/2 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: In a pan, sauté chopped onion in butter until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in white wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Stir in saffron mixture and cook for 1 minute.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed before adding more.
Continue process for about 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy but still firm.
Remove from heat, stir in remaining butter and Parmesan cheese, and serve immediately.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Cook lasagna noodles according to package instructions.
Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in a pot with a little oil until soft.
Add ground beef and pork, cooking until browned.
Stir in red wine and simmer until reduced.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Layer sauce, cooked noodles, and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating layers.
Top with remaining sauce and sprinkle with Parmesan and butter.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in mascarpone cheese until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold egg whites into mascarpone mixture.
Mix espresso with coffee liqueur.
Dip ladyfingers quickly into coffee mixture and arrange in a dish.
Spread half of mascarpone mixture over ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining mascarpone.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Before serving, dust top generously with cocoa powder.

title: Osso Buco
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then coat lightly in flour.
Sear shanks in a Dutch oven with olive oil and butter until browned on all sides.
Remove shanks and sauté onion, carrots, and celery in the same pot.
Stir in flour to create a roux, then deglaze with white wine.
Return shanks to pot and add stock, tomatoes, and bay leaves.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot shanks topped with fresh gremolata.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Fry guanciale in a pan until crisp and fat renders.
Whisk egg yolks, Pecorino, Parmigiano, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss hot pasta directly into the pan with guanciale fat.
Remove pan from heat and quickly stir in egg mixture to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable stock, kept warm
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in warm water
instructions: Sauté onion in half the butter until translucent.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently until absorbed.
Stir in saffron mixture and remaining butter.
Remove from heat, stir in Parmigiano, and rest for 2 minutes.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Flour shanks and sear in oil until golden brown; set aside.
Sauté vegetables in the same pan until softened.
Return shanks to pan, add wine and simmer until reduced.
Add tomatoes and stock, then thyme.
Simmer covered for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Garnish with fresh gremolata before serving.

title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken and brown in olive oil; remove from pan.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in wine and scrape up browned bits; simmer until reduced.
Return chicken to pan with tomatoes, olives, and oregano.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until sauce thickens.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Mix espresso with liqueur, then dip ladyfingers quickly.
Arrange dipped biscuits in dish and cover with half the mascarpone.
Repeat layers and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a skillet until crispy and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, grated Pecorino, and plenty of black pepper.
Drain pasta, reserving 1 cup of starchy pasta water.
Add hot pasta to the skillet with guanciale, remove from heat.
Quickly pour egg mixture over pasta, tossing constantly to create a creamy sauce.
Add pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
Sear shanks in a Dutch oven with butter until golden brown on all sides.
Remove shanks and sauté onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in the same pot.
Add wine and scrape up browned bits from the bottom.
Return shanks to the pot, add canned tomatoes and broth.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
Serve hot shanks with gremolata (parsley, garlic, lemon zest) and lemon slices.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté beef, pork, onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in a large pot until browned.
Add wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, milk, and salt; simmer for 2 hours.
Meanwhile, cook lasagna noodles according to package directions.
Mix ricotta cheese with eggs and half of the Parmesan.
Assemble lasagna by layering noodles, meat sauce, and ricotta mixture.
Top with remaining Parmesan and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45 minutes.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving with fresh basil.

title: Risotto ai Funghi Porcini
ingredients: 250g dried porcini mushrooms, rehydrated and chopped
6 cups vegetable or chicken stock, kept warm
instructions: Soak dried porcini mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes; strain and reserve liquid.
Sauté onion in 2 tbsp butter until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add warm stock and mushroom soaking liquid gradually, 1/2 cup at a time.
Stir constantly until rice is creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Stir in remaining butter, Parmesan, thyme, and chopped porcini.
Season with salt and pepper; serve immediately.

title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
ingredients: 8 small veal scaloppine or chicken breasts
instructions: Place a sage leaf on each veal slice and top with a slice of prosciutto.
Secure each stack with a toothpick.
Season both sides of the stacks with salt and pepper.
Sear in a hot pan with a little oil for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Pour white wine over the pan and let it reduce by half.
Add butter and lemon slices, basting the meat continuously.
Remove toothpicks and serve immediately with fresh parsley.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh black pepper, freshly cracked
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy and the fat is rendered.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, grated cheeses, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Remove the skillet from heat and add the hot pasta and reserved water to the guanciale.
Pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing quickly and continuously until a creamy sauce forms.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter hot chicken or vegetable stock
1/2 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: Melt half the butter in a heavy-bottomed pan and sauté the onion until soft.
Add the Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until the edges are translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until completely evaporated.
Add the saffron mixture and the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
Continue adding stock and stirring until the rice is creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Stir in the remaining butter and half the cheese off the heat.
Mound onto plates, top with the remaining cheese, and serve warm.

title: Baked Ziti
ingredients: 2 cups cooked ground beef or Italian sausage
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Boil the ziti in salted water until just under al dente.
In a skillet, cook the meat with garlic until browned, then add crushed tomatoes and simmer.
In a bowl, mix ricotta, eggs, half the Parmigiano, and half the Mozzarella.
Combine the cooked pasta, meat sauce, and cheese mixture in a large baking dish.
Top with the remaining Mozzarella and Parmigiano cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 more minutes until bubbly.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar over a double boiler until pale and thick, then cool completely.
In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream to stiff peaks.
Fold the mascarpone into the cooled egg mixture.
Gently fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip ladyfingers briefly into the espresso-liqueur mixture and arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half the cream mixture over the cookies, then add another layer of dipped ladyfingers.
Top with the remaining cream, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Dust with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
instructions: Preheat the oven or broiler.
Rub each slice of bread with a halved garlic clove.
Arrange the bread on a baking sheet and toast under the broiler until golden and crisp.
In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, chopped basil, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Toss gently to mix well.
Serve the tomato mixture immediately on top of the toasted bread.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crispy and golden.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with grated Pecorino, Parmesan, and plenty of black pepper.
Drain pasta, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
Add hot pasta to the skillet with guanciale, removing from heat.
Quickly pour egg mixture over pasta and toss vigorously, adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in a pot until soft, then add beef and pork, browning well.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer the meat sauce for at least 2 hours.
Boil lasagna noodles according to package instructions.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Layer noodles, meat sauce, ricotta mixture, and Parmesan in a baking dish, repeating layers.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 more minutes before letting it rest.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable broth, kept warm
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in a little warm water
instructions: Sauté onion in half the butter until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until liquid is absorbed before adding more.
Stir in saffron mixture and remaining butter when rice is tender but still firm to the bite.
Remove from heat, stir in Parmesan, and let rest covered for 5 minutes.

title: Osso Buco
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
Brown the shanks in olive oil in a heavy pot, then remove and set aside.
Sauté carrots, celery, and onion in the same pot until softened.
Add wine and scrape up any browned bits, then return shanks to the pot.
Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock, bring to a simmer, and cover.
Bake in the oven at 325°F (165°C) for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
Finish by squeezing lemon halves over the dish and garnish with parsley.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar over a double boiler until thick and pale, then cool completely.
Fold in mascarpone and vanilla extract until smooth.
Mix espresso with coffee liqueur if using.
Quickly dip ladyfingers into the coffee mixture and arrange in a dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers and repeat layers.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before dusting generously with cocoa powder.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a large pan over medium heat until crisp and golden.
Remove pan from heat and stir in the grated cheeses and a generous amount of black pepper.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks with a little pasta water until smooth.
Drain the pasta, reserving a cup of cooking water, and toss immediately into the pan with the guanciale.
Remove pan from heat and quickly stir in the egg mixture, adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
ingredients: 4 veal shanks (osso buco), bone-in and cross-cut
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and dredge them lightly in flour.
In a heavy Dutch oven, heat olive oil and butter, then sear the shanks on all sides until browned.
Remove shanks and sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in the same pan until soft.
Return shanks to the pot, pour in the white wine to deglaze, and bring to a simmer.
Add the beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf, then cover and braise in the oven at 160°C for 2.5 to 3 hours.
Check occasionally and add a splash of water if the liquid reduces too much.
Remove the shanks and skim fat from the sauce, then serve the meat topped with fresh gremolata.

title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper and pat them dry.
In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium-high heat and brown the chicken pieces on all sides.
Remove chicken and sauté the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery until softened.
Return the chicken to the pot, pour in the red wine and let it simmer until reduced by half.
Add the canned tomatoes with their juices, rosemary, and thyme, then cover.
Simmer gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter warm chicken or vegetable stock
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: In a pot, heat half the butter and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the Arborio rice and toast it for 2 minutes until the edges become translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add the saffron and its soaking liquid to the rice.
Begin adding warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed.
Continue this process for about 18–20 minutes until the rice is creamy but still al dente.
Remove from heat, stir in the remaining butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano, then serve immediately garnished with parsley.

title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
ingredients: 1 lb veal cutlets or chicken breasts
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place a slice of prosciutto over a sage leaf and a piece of veal, then secure with a toothpick.
Season both sides of the bundles lightly with salt and pepper.
In a skillet, heat butter and olive oil over medium-high heat and sear the bundles for 3–4 minutes per side.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the chicken stock and rosemary, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes until the meat is cooked through.
Remove the toothpicks, discard the rosemary sprig, and serve immediately garnished with fresh thyme.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Fry pancetta in a pan until crispy, remove from heat.
Whisk eggs and grated cheese in a bowl with plenty of black pepper.
Toss hot pasta with the pancetta, ensuring the pan is off the heat.
Pour the egg mixture over the pasta and stir vigorously to create a creamy sauce.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté onions, carrots, and celery in oil until soft.
Add ground meats, cook until browned, then stir in wine, tomato paste, and tomatoes.
Simmer the meat sauce for at least 2 hours with stock.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Layer sauce, cooked lasagna sheets, and cheese in a baking dish, repeating until ingredients are used.
Bake for 45 minutes until golden and bubbly.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable stock, warm
instructions: Toast rice in butter with chopped onion until translucent.
Deglaze pan with white wine and stir until evaporated.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed.
Stir in saffron threads near the end of cooking.
Remove from heat, stir in remaining butter and Parmesan cheese until creamy.

title: Osso Buco
instructions: Dredge veal shanks in flour and sear in oil until browned.
Sauté onions, carrots, and celery in the same pan.
Add garlic, wine, and tomatoes; simmer until reduced.
Pour mixture into a pot, add stock, and return shanks to the liquid.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Finish by stirring in cold butter for richness.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Whip heavy cream and fold into the yolk mixture along with mascarpone.
Dip ladyfingers quickly into cooled espresso and arrange in a dish.
Spread half the cream mixture over the cookies.
Repeat layers and chill for at least 4 hours.
Dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry diced guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy and fat is rendered.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated cheeses, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Remove skillet from heat and toss the hot pasta with the crispy guanciale and some of the rendered fat.
Quickly pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing vigorously and adding splashes of hot water to create a creamy sauce without scrambling the eggs.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
ingredients: 4 veal shanks (osso buco), bone-in and cross-cut
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
In a large Dutch oven, heat olive oil and brown the veal shanks on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, melt butter and sauté onion, carrot, and celery until soft (soffritto).
Deglaze the pot with white wine, scraping up browned bits from the bottom.
Return veal to the pot, add crushed tomatoes, stock, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and bake at 325°F (160°C) for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Discard bay leaf and thyme, ladle into bowls, and top with fresh gremolata.

title: Ragù alla Bolognese
instructions: In a large heavy pot, sauté onion, carrot, and celery in a little oil until soft.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more, then stir in ground beef and pork.
Break up the meat with a spoon and cook until browned, about 10 minutes.
Pour in white wine and simmer until the alcohol evaporates.
Stir in tomato puree, milk, and beef stock.
Cover and simmer gently on low heat for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Stir in butter near the end to enrich the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, serve over fresh tagliatelle with grated Parmigiano.

title: Tiramisu
ingredients: 1/4 cup cocoa powder, plus more for dusting
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until thick and pale; remove from heat and cool.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream with vanilla and coffee liqueur until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the cooled egg mixture into the whipped cream.
Dip each ladyfinger quickly into the cooled espresso (do not soak), then arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half the cream mixture over the biscuits, then add a second layer of dipped biscuits.
Top with the remaining cream mixture.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Before serving, dust generously with cocoa powder.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 1 large eggplant (about 1.5 lbs), cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry eggplant cubes in olive oil until golden and tender; remove and drain on paper towels.
In the same oil, sauté garlic slices until fragrant but not browned.
Add chopped tomatoes, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1 cup of pasta water.
Toss the cooked pasta with the tomato sauce, adding pasta water as needed to loosen.
Stir in fried eggplant and torn basil leaves.
Serve hot topped with generous shavings of Pecorino Romano.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a large pan until crispy and the fat has rendered.
In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, grated cheeses, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Remove the pan from heat and toss the hot pasta with the crispy guanciale and some fat.
Pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing vigorously while adding splashes of hot pasta water to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable broth, kept warm
1/2 teaspoon saffron threads, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm water
instructions: In a large pan, melt half the butter and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until the edges are translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until fully evaporated.
Add the saffron mixture to the broth and stir to infuse.
Add the warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed before adding more.
Continue this process for about 18-20 minutes until the rice is creamy but still has a slight bite.
Remove from heat, stir in the remaining butter and Parmesan cheese until melted and glossy.

title: Osso Buco
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven and brown the shanks on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, carrots, and celery until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the shanks to the pot, add the crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, and thyme.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is fork-tender.
Serve with gremolata or polenta.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar over a double boiler until the mixture thickens and reaches 160°F (71°C).
Remove from heat and whisk in the mascarpone cheese until smooth and creamy.
In a separate bowl, mix the cooled espresso with the coffee liqueur and vanilla.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture for just 1 second.
Arrange a layer of dipped ladyfingers in the bottom of a 9x13 inch dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, then dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
instructions: Preheat the oven or toaster to broil.
Rub each slice of bread directly with a cut clove of garlic.
Drizzle the bread with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Broil the bread until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
While bread toasts, mix the diced tomatoes, remaining chopped basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add a splash of lemon juice to the tomato mixture if desired.
Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto the toasted bread slices and serve immediately.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
ingredients: Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with both cheeses and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Remove skillet from heat and toss hot pasta with the crispy guanciale and fat.
Pour the egg mixture over the hot pasta, stirring vigorously and adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter warm chicken or vegetable stock
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: In a saucepan, bring stock to a simmer and add saffron threads.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt half the butter and sauté onion until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in white wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until liquid is absorbed before adding more.
When rice is creamy but still al dente, remove from heat.
Stir in remaining butter, cheese, and season with salt and white pepper.
Let rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
Brown shanks in olive oil in a Dutch oven, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion, carrot, celery, and garlic until softened.
Add crushed tomatoes, white wine, and stock, then return shanks to the pot.
Add bay leaves, cover, and simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
In a small pan, melt butter and whisk in flour to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in 100ml white wine and cook until thickened to make a liaison.
Stir the liaison into the osso buco sauce, adjust seasoning, and serve with risotto or polenta.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar over a double boiler until pale and thick, then cool completely.
Fold in mascarpone cheese and vanilla extract until smooth.
Dip each ladyfinger briefly into cooled espresso and coffee liqueur mixture.
Arrange a layer of dipped ladyfingers in the bottom of a serving dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone.
Dust the top generously with cocoa powder and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Pizza Margherita
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, and salt in a bowl, add water and olive oil, then knead until smooth.
Let dough rest in an oiled bowl for 24 hours at room temperature.
Preheat oven to highest setting (250°C/480°F) with a pizza stone inside.
Stretch dough into a 12-inch circle on floured surface.
Spread crushed tomatoes evenly over the dough base.
Arrange sliced mozzarella over the tomato layer.
Bake on the stone for 8-10 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.
Remove from oven, top with fresh basil leaves and drizzle with olive oil and salt.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs, grated Pecorino, Parmesan, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add hot pasta to the skillet with guanciale, remove from heat, and quickly toss with the egg mixture.
Add reserved pasta water gradually while tossing vigorously until a creamy sauce forms.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in olive oil until soft, then add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add ground beef and pork, cooking until browned, then stir in wine and simmer until reduced.
Add crushed tomatoes, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Spread a thin layer of ragu in the bottom of a baking dish.
Layer lasagna sheets, ragu, and mozzarella slices.
Repeat layers until ingredients are used, finishing with a layer of cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes until golden.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter chicken or vegetable stock, kept warm
1 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion in half the butter until translucent.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Stir in the saffron mixture and cook for 1 minute.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until liquid is absorbed before adding more.
Continue adding stock and stirring for about 20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat, stir in remaining butter and Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and white pepper, then serve immediately.

title: Osso Buco
ingredients: 100g gremolata (lemon zest, parsley, garlic), for garnish
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
Brown shanks in oil on all sides in a heavy pot, then remove.
Sauté onions, carrots, and celery in the same pot until soft.
Add garlic, then pour in wine and scrape up browned bits from the bottom.
Return shanks to the pot, add stock, and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
In the last 10 minutes, whisk cold butter into the sauce to thicken it.
Serve hot shanks with gremolata and polenta or mashed potatoes.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until thick and pale.
Remove from heat and beat in mascarpone cheese until smooth and creamy.
Stir cooled espresso and liqueur into the egg mixture.
Dip ladyfingers briefly into the remaining espresso mixture so they are moist but not soggy.
Layer dipped ladyfingers in the bottom of a serving dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the first layer.
Repeat with another layer of ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight before dusting with cocoa powder.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a large pan until crispy and the fat has rendered.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, grated cheese, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the hot pasta directly to the pan with the guanciale, removing from heat.
Pour the egg and cheese mixture over the pasta, tossing quickly and adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 200g saffron threads, soaked in 50ml warm water
instructions: In a separate pot, bring the warm stock to a simmer.
Melt half the butter in a heavy-bottomed pan and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the Arborio rice, stirring to coat each grain and toast lightly for 2 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and stir until fully absorbed.
Add the saffron and its soaking water to the pan, stirring to release the color.
Add the warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding more.
When the rice is creamy and tender, stir in the remaining butter and half the Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Season with salt if needed and serve immediately with the remaining cheese.

title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
instructions: Remove the steaks from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking.
Generously season both sides of the steaks with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat a cast-iron grill pan or heavy skillet over high heat until smoking.
Sear the steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for a medium-rare finish, ensuring a deep crust forms.
Reduce heat and cook for another 2-3 minutes on each side if a higher doneness is desired.
Remove steaks from the heat and let them rest on a warm plate covered loosely with foil for 10 minutes.
Rub the garlic cloves directly onto the hot meat, then drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish with torn basil leaves and a generous dusting of grated Pecorino Toscano.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season the veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour.
In a large Dutch oven, fry the pancetta until crisp, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, brown the veal shanks on all sides and remove them.
Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in the rendered fat until soft.
Deglaze the pot with white wine, scraping up any browned bits, and let it reduce by half.
Return the veal and pancetta to the pot, add the stock and crushed tomatoes.
Cover and simmer gently for 2-2.5 hours until the meat is fork-tender.
In a small pan, melt the butter and whisk in the flour to make a roux, then slowly whisk in a ladle of the cooking liquid to create a thick, glossy sauce.
Stir the sauce into the osso buco, adjust seasoning, and serve topped with gremolata.

title: Tiramisu Classico
instructions: Brew the strong espresso and let it cool completely, mixing in the liqueur if using.
Separate the eggs, whisking the yolks with sugar until pale and thick.
In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the cooled egg yolk mixture into the mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture until fully combined.
Dip each ladyfinger quickly into the coffee mixture and arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the biscuits, then repeat with another layer of soaked biscuits.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Before serving, dust the top generously with cocoa powder.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with grated cheeses and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add hot pasta to the skillet with guanciale, remove from heat, and quickly stir in the egg mixture.
Add reserved pasta water gradually while stirring vigorously to create a creamy sauce without scrambling the eggs.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
ingredients: 1 liter warm chicken or vegetable stock
2 teaspoons saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat stock in a saucepan and keep it simmering.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt half the butter and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the wine and saffron mixture, stirring until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently and waiting for absorption before adding the next ladle.
Continue this process for about 18-20 minutes until rice is tender but still firm to the bite.
Remove from heat, stir in the remaining butter and grated cheese to create a creamy consistency.
Season with salt and white pepper, then serve immediately.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
In a large pot, heat oil and brown the veal shanks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, melt butter and sauté onions, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up browned bits, then add tomatoes and stock.
Return veal shanks to the pot, add thyme and bay leaf, then cover and simmer gently for 2.5 hours.
Check occasionally, adding stock if necessary, until meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove from heat and stir in the cold knob of butter to enrich the sauce.
Serve hot with gremolata (lemon zest, garlic, parsley) and polenta or mashed potatoes.

title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
ingredients: Sea salt and coarse black pepper
instructions: Remove steaks from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to bring to room temperature.
Rub steaks generously with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Preheat grill or charcoal fire to high heat.
Place steaks on the grill and cook for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, depending on thickness.
During the last 2 minutes, place halved garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs on the grill near the meat to infuse flavor.
Remove steaks and let them rest for 10 minutes under a loose tent of foil.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the rested meat and sprinkle with grated Parmigiano Reggiano before serving.

title: Tiramisu Classico
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until the mixture thickens and reaches 70°C (158°F).
Remove from heat, stir in vanilla extract, then fold in the Mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Divide the cooled espresso into two equal parts.
Dip each ladyfinger briefly into the first half of the espresso (do not soak) and arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with the second layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining mascarpone mixture.
Sift cocoa powder evenly over the top and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight before serving.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry guanciale in a skillet until crispy and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk eggs, grated cheese, and generous black pepper.
Drain pasta, reserving a cup of cooking water.
Toss hot pasta with guanciale fat, then remove from heat and quickly mix in egg mixture, adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Risotto ai Funghi Porcini
ingredients: 1 liter vegetable or chicken broth, kept warm
instructions: Soak dried porcini in warm water for 20 minutes, then chop them and reserve the soaking liquid.
Sauté onion in olive oil until translucent, then add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
