Pour in wine and stir until absorbed.
Add broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until liquid is absorbed before adding more.
Add chopped porcini and reserved soaking liquid in the last few minutes of cooking.
Finish with butter and Parmesan cheese, stir vigorously, and serve hot.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
ingredients: Gremolata: lemon zest, parsley, and garlic finely chopped
instructions: Season veal shanks with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
Brown shanks in a heavy pot with olive oil, then remove and set aside.
Sauté carrots, celery, and onion in the same pot until softened.
Return shanks to the pot, add wine, broth, and bay leaves.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender.
Remove shanks, skim fat from the sauce, and stir in gremolata before serving.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in oil, then add meat and cook until browned.
Deglaze pan with wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 2 hours to make ragù.
Prepare Béchamel by melting butter, whisking in flour, and gradually adding milk until thickened.
Layer noodles, ragù, and Béchamel in a baking dish, repeating layers.
Top with Parmesan cheese and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes until golden.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Tiramisu Classico
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar over a double boiler until thick and pale, then cool completely.
Fold in mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Whip heavy cream until stiff peaks form, then gently fold into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip ladyfingers briefly in cooled espresso and arrange in a dish.
Spread half the cream mixture over biscuits, then repeat with another layer of biscuits and the rest of the cream.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Tagliatelle al Ragù di Cinghiale
ingredients: 1 kg wild boar meat, cut into small cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat and fry the pancetta until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and sauté until soft.
Add the wild boar and pork, seasoning with salt, pepper, and rosemary, and cook until the meat browns.
Pour in the white wine and let it simmer until the alcohol evaporates.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the stock and the fried pancetta back into the pot.
Add the bay leaf, cover, and simmer on low heat for at least 3 hours until the meat is very tender.
Cook the fresh tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain the pasta, toss it gently with the ragù, and serve immediately.

title: Tortellini in Brodo di Cappone
ingredients: 500g fresh tortellini, filled with pork and ricotta
2 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
Freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano for serving
instructions: Place the whole capon, vegetables, leek, onion, bay leaf, and thyme into a large pot with 1 liter of water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any impurities, then reduce heat and simmer gently for 3 to 4 hours until the broth is rich and clear.
Remove the capon meat from the bones and shred it finely.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve to remove all vegetables and bones.
Heat the butter in a small saucepan and add the shredded capon meat, cooking briefly to warm through.
Bring the clear broth to a gentle simmer in a large serving bowl.
Drop the tortellini into the simmering broth and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they float.
Ladle the broth and tortellini into bowls, top with the capon meat, and serve with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese (Senza Latte)
ingredients: 500g fresh lasagna sheets, cut into strips
Salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste
instructions: In a large pan, heat olive oil and sauté the onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add the ground beef and pork, breaking them up with a spoon, and cook until browned.
Pour in the red wine and cook until it has reduced by half.
Add the tomato passata, stock, and seasonings; simmer for 2 hours until the ragù is thick.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a baking dish, layer a thin amount of ragù on the bottom, followed by a layer of pasta sheets.
Repeat the layers of ragù and pasta, finishing with a layer of pasta.
Sprinkle the grated Parmigiano Reggiano and Pecorino Romano evenly over the top.
Bake for 40 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly, then let rest for 10 minutes before serving with basil.

title: Cappelletti al Ragù
ingredients: 500g fresh cappelletti, filled with pork, beef, and pecorino
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot and fry the pancetta until it renders its fat and becomes crispy.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery, sautéing until soft and translucent.
Add the ground beef and pork, cooking until the meat is browned and crumbly.
Stir in the white wine and let it simmer until the liquid is mostly evaporated.
Mix in the tomato paste and stock, then add the bay leaf.
Simmer the ragù on low heat for at least 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Drop the cappelletti into the boiling water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they float.
Drain the cappelletti and toss them immediately with the hot ragù, serving right away.

title: Zuppa di Orzo con Salsiccia
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil and fry the sliced sausage until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the white wine.
Return the sausage to the pot, add the diced tomatoes, bay leaf, and parsley sprig.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the orzo pasta to the soup and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, remove the bay leaf and parsley sprig.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley leaves.

title: Tajarin al Tartufo
ingredients: 50g fresh black winter truffle, thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the tajarin until al dente.
While pasta cooks, melt the butter in a warm pan over low heat.
Drain the pasta, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the hot pasta with the melted butter and a splash of pasta water.
Remove from heat, sprinkle with Parmigiano, black pepper, and the sliced truffle.
Serve immediately on warm plates.

title: Crepes di Besciamella e Spinaci
ingredients: 1 cup fresh spinach, chopped and sautéed
Butter and flour for making crepes
instructions: Prepare the béchamel sauce and stir in half of the grated Parmigiano until smooth.
Sauté the spinach with a pinch of salt until wilted.
Spread a layer of béchamel on the bottom of a baking dish.
Arrange the crepes in a single layer over the sauce.
Spread the spinach mixture over the crepes, then cover with more béchamel and the remaining cheese.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes until golden and bubbly.

title: Tajarin al Tartufo
ingredients: 50g fresh black winter truffle, thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the tajarin until al dente.
While pasta cooks, melt the butter in a warm pan over low heat.
Drain the pasta, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the hot pasta with the melted butter and a splash of pasta water.
Remove from heat, sprinkle with Parmigiano, black pepper, and the sliced truffle.
Serve immediately on warm plates.

title: Bocconotti di Castagna
instructions: Separate the egg whites from the yolks and set aside.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form.
In a separate bowl, beat the yolks with the sugar and lemon zest until pale.
Fold the chestnut flour into the yolk mixture gently.
Carefully fold in the egg whites to maintain airiness.
Pipe small mounds onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 20-25 minutes until set.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Polenta con Salsiccia e Peperoni
instructions: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Slowly whisk in the cornmeal to prevent lumps.
Stir constantly and cook over medium heat for 20-30 minutes until thick and creamy.
While polenta cooks, sauté the sliced sausage and peppers in butter until tender.
Stir the cooked sausage and peppers into the finished polenta.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
ingredients: Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a large pan over medium heat until crisp and fat renders.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks, Pecorino, Parmigiano, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Remove the pan with guanciale from heat and toss in the hot pasta.
Slowly pour the egg mixture over the pasta, stirring constantly and adding pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra grated cheese and black pepper.

title: Cacio e Pepe
ingredients: 400g tonnarelli or spaghetti, broken if necessary
100g very cold water, plus more if needed
Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Toast the black pepper coarsely in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the pasta to a large pot of boiling salted water and cook until al dente.
While pasta cooks, slowly whisk the grated Pecorino into the cold water in a separate bowl until smooth.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Add the hot drained pasta to the pan with the toasted pepper and toss vigorously.
Add the cheese-water mixture and a splash of pasta water, tossing quickly to emulsify into a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with more black pepper.

title: Rigatoni alla Gricia
ingredients: Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the rigatoni in a large pot of salted water until al dente.
Fry the guanciale in a large pan over medium heat until golden and crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Return the pan to medium-low heat and add the rendered fat.
Add a generous amount of black pepper to the fat and toast until fragrant.
Toss the drained pasta directly into the pan with the fat and pepper, then add the cooked guanciale back in.
Remove from heat and stir in the Pecorino Romano, adding a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too dry.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

title: Orecchiette alle Cime di Rapa
ingredients: 500g broccoli rabe (cime di rapa), trimmed and chopped
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook the orecchiette until al dente.
While pasta cooks, boil the broccoli rabe in salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender, then drain well.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil and sauté the garlic slices until just golden.
Add the wine to the skillet and let it reduce by half.
Add the broccoli rabe to the skillet and cook over medium heat, tossing to coat in the oil and wine reduction.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Toss the pasta with the broccoli rabe mixture, adding pasta water and pecorino to create a light sauce.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve immediately.

title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
ingredients: 100g tomato paste, or 300g peeled San Marzano tomatoes
Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook the bucatini in a large pot of salted water until al dente.
Fry the guanciale in a large pan over medium heat until crisp and fat renders.
Add the chopped garlic to the pan and fry until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in the tomato paste (or whole peeled tomatoes) and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Toss the drained pasta directly into the pan with the sauce, adding pasta water as needed to loosen the consistency.
Remove from heat, stir in the Pecorino Romano, and serve immediately with extra cheese and black pepper.

title: Polenta e Osei (Polenta with Fried Squid)
instructions: Bring water to a boil, add salt, and gradually whisk in polenta to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and stir constantly until polenta is thick and creamy, about 45 minutes.
Remove from heat, stir in butter, and cover to keep warm.
Season squid with salt and pepper, then fry in olive oil until golden and tender.
Sauté garlic and tomatoes in a pan until soft, then toss in squid and parsley.
Serve the warm polenta topped with the squid and tomato mixture.

title: Frittura di Orata (Bream Fillets)
ingredients: 2 cups breadcrumbs, mixed with grated parmesan
instructions: Place flour in a bowl, eggs in a second, and the breadcrumb mixture in a third.
Dredge fish fillets in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry fillets gently for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon slices and the bouquet garni.

title: Ravioli di Zucca con Ragù di Salsiccia
instructions: Boil pumpkin until soft, then puree and mix with salt and nutmeg.
Knead flour, eggs, and half the pumpkin puree to form a smooth dough.
Roll dough thin, cut into squares, place small amounts of remaining pumpkin in center.
Seal squares into ravioli, boil in salted water until they float.
In a pan, sauté pancetta and onion until translucent, add sausage and cook until browned.
Deglaze with wine, add butter and parmesan to create a rich ragù.
Toss cooked ravioli in the sauce and serve.

title: Carpaccio di Manzo al Limone
instructions: Freeze beef for 1-2 hours, then slice extremely thinly using a mandoline or very sharp knife.
Toss beef slices immediately with lemon juice, zest, garlic, salt, and pepper to prevent browning.
Mound arugula on individual plates.
Top with beef slices, then shave fresh parmesan over the meat.
Dot with softened butter and capers, and serve chilled.

title: Cassuneta (Venetian Stuffed Squid)
instructions: Clean squid thoroughly, remove tubes, and chop bodies into small pieces.
Sauté pancetta, onion, and garlic in butter until soft, then add squid and cook briefly.
Season squid mixture with salt, wine, parmesan, and parsley; stuff into cleaned squid tubes.
Dredge stuffed squid in flour, dip in egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot olive oil until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Orecchiette alle Cime di Rapa
ingredients: 1 large bunch turnip greens (cime di rapa), stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook orecchiette until al dente.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and cook until lightly golden, being careful not to burn it.
Add the chopped turnip greens to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are wilted and tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain the pasta, reserving a cup of pasta water.
Toss the drained pasta with the greens and garlic in the skillet, adding a splash of pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Season generously with black pepper and stir in the grated pecorino cheese until combined.
Serve immediately.

title: Polpette di Patate e Cinghiale
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Extra virgin olive oil for frying
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, ground wild boar, chopped onion, minced garlic, breadcrumbs, pecorino cheese, and parsley.
Season the mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Mix everything thoroughly with your hands until the meat is evenly distributed and the mixture is uniform.
Moisten your hands with a little water and roll the mixture into small, bite-sized balls.
Heat olive oil in a deep skillet or frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the meatballs in batches until they are golden brown and cooked through on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the cooked polpette to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, optionally with a side of roasted vegetables.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water and cook the pasta until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, slice the eggplants into rounds and salt them generously, letting them sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture.
Rinse the eggplant slices and pat them dry with paper towels.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat and add the smashed garlic; cook until fragrant.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent.
Add the eggplant slices to the skillet and fry until golden and tender on both sides, about 5-6 minutes.
Remove the eggplant and set aside. Add the crushed tomatoes to the skillet and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Drain the cooked pasta, reserving a little water.
Toss the pasta with the tomato sauce, adding the fried eggplant slices back in.
Stir in the torn basil leaves, season with salt and pepper, and serve topped with grated pecorino siciliano.

title: Focaccia al Rosmarino e Olive
ingredients: 1/2 cup green olives, pitted and halved
1/4 cup black olives, pitted and halved
Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and honey in the warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt.
Pour the yeast mixture into the flour and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Add a tablespoon of olive oil and knead the dough on a floured surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and place a baking sheet inside to heat up.
Punch down the risen dough and transfer it to a lightly oiled baking sheet.
Press the dough out with your fingertips to create dimples all over the surface.
Generously drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with chopped rosemary, green olives, and black olives, pressing them slightly into the dough.
Let the focaccia rise again for 30 minutes.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the top is crisp.
Let it cool slightly before slicing and serving.

title: Baccalà alla Pugliese
ingredients: 500g dried salt cod (baccalà), soaked and desalted
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak the dried salt cod in plenty of cold water for 24-48 hours, changing the water 3-4 times until the salt is removed. Remove any bones and flake the fish.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until soft and translucent.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the flaked cod and the white wine, cooking until the liquid evaporates and the fish is heated through.
In a separate bowl, mix the breadcrumbs, pecorino cheese, parsley, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper to create a binding mixture.
Take small portions of the cod mixture and roll them into balls, then roll each ball in the breadcrumb mixture to coat completely.
Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Fry the cod balls in batches until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil salted water and cook rigatoni until al dente, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pan and fry sliced garlic until golden, then remove.
Add sliced eggplants to the oil and fry until tender and golden on both sides.
Return garlic to the pan, add canned tomatoes and cook down into a sauce.
Season sauce with salt, pepper, and fresh basil.
Toss the cooked pasta with the eggplant sauce and serve hot.

title: Arancini al Risi
ingredients: 1.5 liters chicken or vegetable stock, kept warm
instructions: Sauté onion in butter until soft, add rice and toast lightly.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until rice is creamy and cooked.
Remove from heat, stir in peas, ham, and parmesan.
Let rice cool completely, then shape into balls and flatten slightly.
Roll each ball in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy, then drain on paper towels.

title: Caponata
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan and fry diced eggplant until tender, then set aside.
In the same oil, sauté onion and bell pepper until soft.
Add capers, olives, vinegar, and sugar; simmer for 10 minutes.
Return eggplant to the pan and cook together for another 5 minutes.
Stir in toasted pine nuts just before serving.

title: Sfincione Siciliano
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, let foam for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, salt, and oil; add yeast mixture and knead until smooth.
Let dough rise in an oiled bowl for 1 hour until doubled.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F) and grease a baking sheet.
Press dough into a rectangular pan, spread tomato sauce evenly.
Top with anchovies, mozzarella, and sprinkle with fennel pollen.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until crust is golden and crispy.

title: Caponata di Zucchine
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté sliced zucchini until lightly browned, then remove.
In the same oil, cook onions and bell peppers until soft.
Add capers, vinegar, and sugar; simmer for 10 minutes to reduce.
Return zucchini to the pan and toss to coat in the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, then garnish with toasted pine nuts.

title: Spaghetti alla Norma
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente.
In a large pan, fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden and soft.
In the same oil, sauté garlic until fragrant, then add chopped tomatoes and simmer until thick.
Toss cooked pasta with the tomato sauce.
Top with fried eggplant, fresh mozzarella cubes, and a generous layer of toasted breadcrumbs.
Finish with fresh basil and drizzle with extra virgin olive oil before serving.

title: Ragù Napoletano
ingredients: 1 can whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Brown the beef and pork in olive oil until no longer pink.
Add onions, carrots, celery, and garlic; cook until softened.
Pour in red wine and let it reduce by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and the bay leaf; simmer on low heat for at least 3 hours.
Taste and adjust salt, then serve over pappardelle or polpette.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

title: Pizza Marinara
instructions: Stretch the pizza dough onto a floured surface or baking sheet.
Spread the tomato sauce evenly over the dough.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and sprinkle minced garlic.
Dust with dried oregano and a pinch of salt.
Bake in a preheated oven at 250°C until the crust is golden and bubbly.
Remove from the oven and immediately top with fresh basil leaves.

title: Arancini al Ragù
instructions: Make a tomato sauce by sautéing onion and garlic, then adding crushed tomatoes and simmering.
Mix the sauce with the Ragù and Arborio rice; let it cool slightly.
Shape the mixture into balls, flatten them, and fill with a small ball of mozzarella (optional).
Roll each ball in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot vegetable oil until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Frittata di Verdure
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until translucent.
Add zucchini and bell pepper; cook until tender.
Stir in spinach and cook until wilted.
In a bowl, beat eggs with salt and pepper, then mix in the vegetable mixture.
Pour into a hot, oiled skillet and cook until the bottom is set.
Flip the frittata carefully or fold it over, then cook the other side until golden.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before slicing.

title: Ribollita
ingredients: 1 lb cavolo nero or kale, chopped
1 lb cannellini beans, soaked overnight and drained
Sea salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add the beans and broth, bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in the chopped greens and cook for another 15 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot topped with the cubed stale bread and drizzle with more olive oil.

title: Pappa al Pomodoro
ingredients: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, peeled and diced
1 lb stale rustic bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until broken down.
Stir in the torn bread and let it soak in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Add the broth and oregano, simmer gently for 10 minutes until thickened.
Garnish with fresh basil and serve warm.

title: Cacio e Pepe
ingredients: 300ml warm water or pasta cooking water
Freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
In a separate pan, melt butter and toast the black pepper lightly.
Add the drained pasta to the butter and pepper, tossing vigorously.
Gradually add warm water and cheese off the heat, stirring constantly to create a creamy emulsion.
Serve immediately.

title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
ingredients: Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Pat the steaks dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Rub the steaks with olive oil, garlic, and rosemary.
Grill over high heat for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Let the steaks rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Fagioli all'Uccelletto
ingredients: 1 lb dried borlotti beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic in olive oil until softened.
Add olives, sun-dried tomatoes, bay leaf, and red pepper flakes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil, then add the soaked beans.
Simmer covered for 1.5 to 2 hours until beans are very tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in butter until soft.
Add meats and cook until browned, then stir in wine and let it reduce.
Add tomatoes and simmer for two hours until a thick ragù forms.
Mix ricotta with half the Parmigiano Reggiano.
Layer pasta sheets, ragù, and cheese mixture in a baking dish.
Cover with remaining sauce and cheese, then bake at 180°C for 45 minutes.

title: Tortellini in Brodo
instructions: Combine broth, water, vegetables, and bay leaves in a large pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add tortellini and cook for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Season with salt and drizzle with olive oil.
Serve immediately in bowls topped with shaved Parmigiano.

title: Cotoletta alla Milanese
instructions: Season cutlets with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
Dip each cutlet into beaten eggs, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets for 4-5 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Tagliatelle al Ragù
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in butter until translucent.
Add meats and brown well, then deglaze with wine.
Add tomatoes and simmer slowly for at least three hours.
Boil salted water and cook fresh tagliatelle for 2-3 minutes.
Toss pasta directly in the ragù with butter and cheese.
Serve immediately with extra Parmigiano.

title: Tiramisu
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in the mascarpone cheese until smooth.
Soak ladyfingers quickly in espresso and liqueur.
Layer soaked biscuits in a dish, then spread half the cream mixture.
Repeat layers and top with remaining cream.
Chill for at least 4 hours before serving.
Dust generously with cocoa powder before serving.

title: Polenta e Osei
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Bring water to a boil, gradually whisk in cornmeal and stir continuously for 20 minutes until thick.
Fold in lard and season with salt and pepper.
While polenta cooks, boil chestnuts until tender, then mash them with garlic.
Brown the wild boar sausage in a pan, then mix with the mashed chestnuts.
Combine the cooked beans and roasted chicken with the sausage mixture.
Serve the meat and bean mixture on top of the hot polenta.

title: Tajarin al Burro
instructions: Mix flour and salt, create a well, add eggs and knead into a smooth dough.
Wrap dough in plastic and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll dough through a pasta machine to a thickness of 1mm.
Cut into thin ribbons of tajarin.
Boil tajarin in salted water for 3 minutes.
Toss cooked pasta with melted butter, grated Parmigiano, and a knob of butter.
Serve immediately.

title: Ravioli di Zucca e Ricotta
instructions: Boil pumpkin cubes until tender, then mash and mix with ricotta, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Form ravioli filling balls and place on a floured surface.
Roll out pasta dough to about 2mm thickness.
Cut dough into squares and place filling in center of each.
Seal edges by pressing with a fork and cut into individual ravioli.
Boil ravioli in salted water for 3-4 minutes until they float.
Toss with melted butter and fresh sage leaves.
Serve hot.

title: Tortelli di Patate
instructions: Mix mashed potatoes with butter and seasonings.
Combine flour and eggs to form a dough, then fold in cheese mixture.
Roll dough thin and cut into circles.
Place small amount of potato filling in center of each circle.
Fold dough over filling and seal edges with fork.
Boil tortelli in salted water for 4 minutes.
Sauté fresh sage in butter and toss with tortelli.
Serve immediately.

title: Risotto al Tartufo
instructions: Sauté onion in butter until translucent.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring frequently until absorbed.
Continue adding broth until rice is tender but still al dente.
Remove from heat, stir in butter and cheeses.
Fold in sliced truffles and season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

title: Cacio e Pepe
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Toast the coarsely ground black peppercorns in a large skillet over medium heat until fragrant, then add a splash of pasta water to create a paste.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the pepper paste and toss over low heat.
Gradually add the boiling water and half of the grated Pecorino, stirring vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Remove from heat, add the remaining cheese, and toss until a smooth, glossy sauce coats the pasta.

title: Pasta alla Gricia
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook rigatoni until al dente, reserving 1 cup of cooking water.
In a large skillet, cook the guanciale cubes over medium heat until the fat renders and the meat is crispy, about 8 minutes.
Remove the skillet from heat and add the coarsely ground black pepper to the rendered fat.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the guanciale and pepper, tossing to coat.
Gradually add the reserved pasta water and half the grated Pecorino, stirring vigorously until a creamy sauce forms.
Remove from heat, add the remaining cheese, and serve immediately.

title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
ingredients: 12 slices of prosciutto crudo, cut into strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf on each veal escalope, season with salt and pepper, and roll into a cylinder.
Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the rolls for 2-3 minutes per side until the prosciutto is golden and crispy.
Pour the dry white wine into the pan and let it simmer until reduced by half.
Drizzle with a little more butter, toss to coat the meat in the sauce, and serve immediately with polenta or mashed potatoes.

title: Carciofi alla Giudia
ingredients: 8 large Jerusalem artichokes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch coins
2 cups vegetable oil for deep frying
instructions: Season the Jerusalem artichoke coins with salt and let them sit in cold water for 10 minutes to remove starch, then pat dry.
Set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each coin in flour, dip in the egg wash, and coat generously in panko breadcrumbs.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Fry the breaded artichoke coins in batches until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm as an appetizer.

title: Arancini alla Messinese
ingredients: 2 cups mozzarella cheese, torn into small pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Let the risotto with ragù cool completely, then shape it into small balls.
Flatten each ball slightly, place a piece of mozzarella in the center, and close the dough around it to form a sealed ball.
Dip each ball in flour, then in the beaten egg, and finally coat thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the arancini in batches until golden brown and the cheese inside is melted, about 4-5 minutes.
Drain on paper towels, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

title: Frittura di Polpo al Sale Marino
ingredients: 1 whole small octopus, cleaned and tentacles separated
1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, for frying
instructions: Boil the octopus in water with a splash of vinegar and some sea salt until tender (about 45-60 minutes), then let it cool.
Prepare the batter by mixing the flour, eggs, and milk until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a deep pot to 175°C (350°F).
Dip the octopus tentacles into the batter, ensuring they are fully coated.
Fry the tentacles in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Immediately sprinkle with sea salt flakes while still hot.
Serve with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Orecchiette alle Cime di Rapa
ingredients: 500g broccoli rabe (cime di rapa), stems peeled and chopped
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook pasta according to package directions.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add garlic slices and cook until fragrant and lightly golden, being careful not to burn.
Add the chopped broccoli rabe stems first and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the leafy tops and cook for another 4 minutes.
Pour in the white wine to deglaze the pan and let it reduce by half.
Drain the pasta, reserving 1/2 cup of cooking water.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with the vegetables, tossing to combine.
Add reserved pasta water if the sauce is too dry and toss for 1 minute.
Remove from heat, stir in parsley and pecorino cheese, and serve immediately.

title: Focaccia al Rosmarino
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more for brushing
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix flour and salt, then pour in the yeast mixture.
Knead the dough by hand for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in an oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down the dough and shape it into a rectangle in a well-oiled baking sheet.
Cover and let rise again for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Press dimples into the dough with your fingertips.
Brush generously with olive oil and sprinkle with chopped rosemary and sea salt.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden brown and puffy.
Cool slightly before slicing.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ingredients: 3 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and diced
1 cup fresh mozzarella cheese, diced (bocconcini or whole milk)
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to boil and cook pasta until al dente.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and onion, sautéing until soft and translucent.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Drain the pasta and toss it directly into the tomato sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in the torn basil leaves.
Arrange the diced mozzarella on top of the pasta.
Sprinkle generously with grated pecorino cheese.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Polpette al Sugo
ingredients: 2 cups cooked Italian sausage meat (sweet or hot), drained
1 can (28oz) San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large bowl, mix sausage meat, breadcrumbs, pecorino, egg, parsley, and half the garlic.
Moisten hands with water and roll the mixture into 1-inch meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a deep oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Brown the meatballs on all sides; do not cook them through yet.
Remove meatballs and set aside. In the same pan, add remaining garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, broth, and bay leaf, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return meatballs to the pan, cover, and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until cooked through and sauce is bubbling.
Remove bay leaf and serve hot.

title: Panzanella Rustica
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Toss the cubed bread with a little olive oil and salt, then spread on a baking sheet.
Toast the bread in the oven for 8-10 minutes until crispy.
In a large bowl, combine the diced tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and basil.
Add the toasted bread cubes to the vegetable mixture.
Whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Add diced mozzarella if using.
Let the salad sit for 10 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Caponata
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Salt the diced eggplant and let it sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add celery and bell pepper, cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in capers, raisins, vinegar, and sugar.
Season with salt and pepper, simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Let cool before serving as a side or appetizer.

title: Pasta alla Norma
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti according to package directions.
While pasta cooks, slice eggplants and toss lightly with salt and oil, then drain.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan and fry eggplant slices until golden on both sides.
Add minced garlic to the pan and sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Toss cooked pasta with the sauce, adding basil and parsley.
Serve immediately topped with Pecorino Romano and olives.

title: Couscous di Mandorle
instructions: In a bowl, mix semolina flour, ground almonds, and sesame seeds.
In a saucepan, combine milk, sugar, butter, and vanilla; heat until sugar dissolves.
Gradually add the milk mixture to the flour while stirring constantly.
Cook over medium heat, stirring vigorously, until mixture pulls away from the pan and thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in pine nuts and sliced almonds.
Let cool slightly, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Shape into balls or a loaf, brush with melted butter and honey, and serve.

title: Caponata
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Salt the diced eggplant and let it sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add celery and bell pepper, cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in capers, raisins, vinegar, and sugar.
Season with salt and pepper, simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Let cool before serving as a side or appetizer.

title: Arancini
ingredients: 500g leftover risotto with peas and ham
1 cup breadcrumbs, seasoned with parsley and garlic
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Gently fold mozzarella cubes and parmesan into the warm risotto.
Let the mixture cool completely so the cheese holds its shape.
Divide into small balls, roll in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry arancini in batches until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Ragù Napoletano
ingredients: 1 bottle San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the meat with salt and pepper.
Render the lard in a large pot over medium heat until clear.
Brown the beef and pork in batches, removing them when done.
Sauté the onions, carrots, and celery in the fat until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for one minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the meat to the pot, add the crushed tomatoes and bay leaves.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally.

title: Lasagne alla Napoletana
instructions: Brown the beef and pork with the diced vegetables in olive oil.
Add the crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, eggs, and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Boil the fresh lasagna sheets for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Layer the noodles, meat sauce, and ricotta mixture in a baking dish.
Repeat layers, finishing with a layer of sauce and cheese on top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30 minutes until bubbly and golden.

title: Cuoppo
instructions: Pat the seafood dry and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Dredge the seafood first in flour, then in beaten eggs, and finally in the breadcrumb mixture.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Fry the seafood in batches until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and season immediately with sea salt.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and a glass of white wine.

title: Baccalà alla Napoletana
ingredients: 1 lb salted codfish (baccalà), soaked for 2 days
3 large potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Soak the codfish in cold water with two changes daily for 48 hours until desalted.
Cut the fish into strips and boil in salted water for 15 minutes.
In a large pot, sauté the garlic in olive oil until fragrant.
Add the potatoes and tomatoes; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the drained codfish, capers, and raisins to the pot.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

title: Sfogliatella Riccia
instructions: Mix flour, butter, milk, egg, and salt to form a smooth dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thinly and cut into squares.
Layer each square with sugar, ricotta, citrus peel, pine nuts, and cinnamon.
Roll the filled dough tightly into a spiral shape, pinching the seam.
Place the rolls on a baking sheet and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes.
Dust with sugar while still warm.

title: Ribollita
ingredients: 1 lb stale bread, torn into chunks
4 cups San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion, carrots, and celery until soft.
Add garlic and cook for one minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and beans, then pour in the broth and bring to a simmer.
Add the kale and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Add the bread chunks directly into the pot and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
instructions: Score the fat cap of the steaks in a crosshatch pattern.
Rub the steaks generously with sea salt, smashed garlic, and rosemary.
Heat a heavy cast-iron grill pan over high heat until very hot.
Sear the steaks for 3 minutes on each side for medium-rare.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with olive oil and squeeze fresh lemon juice over the meat before serving.

title: Pappa al Pomodoro
ingredients: 8 cups ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1 lb day-old crusty bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 30 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the bread pieces and let them soak in the sauce for 10 minutes.
Gradually add the vegetable broth while stirring to create a soup consistency.
Remove from heat and stir in the fresh basil.
Serve immediately topped with grated Pecorino cheese and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Cacio e Pepe
ingredients: 1 cup Pecorino Romano cheese, finely grated
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, toast the black peppercorns in a large pan over medium heat until fragrant.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining the spaghetti.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with the toasted pepper and toss to coat.
Add small amounts of hot pasta water and grated cheese, stirring vigorously to create an emulsion.
Continue adding water and cheese until a creamy sauce forms that clings to the pasta.

title: Pici all'Aglione
instructions: Mix flour and warm water to form a stiff dough, then knead until smooth.
Roll the dough into long ropes and cut into 1-inch thick pici shapes.
Boil the pici in salted water for 3 minutes until they float to the surface.
While pasta cooks, sauté the sliced garlic in olive oil over medium-low heat until golden.
Add the fresh oregano to the oil and let it wilt.
Toss the cooked pici directly in the garlic and oregano oil until well coated.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and reduce heat to medium.
Simmer, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken, about 10 minutes.
Garnish with sliced green onion before serving.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Heat dashi stock in a pot over medium heat until just simmering.
Remove from heat and stir in miso paste until completely dissolved.
Add tofu cubes and wakame seaweed to the soup.
Stir in chopped spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with sliced green onion.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk eggs, water, soy sauce, sugar, sake, sesame oil, and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Divide the mixture into 3-4 equal portions.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat and brush with a little oil.
Pour in the first portion of egg mixture and swirl to cover the bottom.
When the bottom is set, roll the egg strip to one side and add the next portion.
Repeat until all egg is used, rolling the omelet layers together.
Cut the finished roll into 8 even pieces and serve warm.

title: Edamame
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add the thawed edamame and boil for 3-5 minutes until bright green and tender.
Drain the edamame well and let cool slightly.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, and sesame oil.
Toss the edamame with the sauce until evenly coated.
Sprinkle with chili flakes if desired and serve immediately.

title: Omu Rice
ingredients: 2 cups cooked short-grain rice, day-old preferred
instructions: Beat eggs, soy sauce, sugar, and salt in a bowl until well combined.
Heat sesame oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté grated onion until soft.
Stir in the cooked rice and toss to coat with the onion oil.
Pour the egg mixture over the rice and scramble gently until just set.
Press the mixture into a round oval shape using a spatula.
Serve topped with chopped green onions and a drizzle of soy sauce.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl.
Place chicken in a baking dish and pour the sauce over it.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25-30 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from oven and brush with remaining sauce.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Remove from heat and stir in miso paste until dissolved.
Add tofu and wakame seaweed.
Let stand for 2 minutes without boiling.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

title: Salmon Sushi Rolls
ingredients: 1 sheet rice paper or plastic wrap
instructions: Cook sushi rice and mix with sushi vinegar while warm.
Place a nori sheet on a bamboo mat.
Spread rice evenly over the nori, leaving a 1-inch border.
Arrange salmon, avocado, and cucumber in a line near the border.
Tightly roll the sushi using the mat.
Cut into 8 pieces and serve with wasabi.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix flour, cornstarch, and salt in a bowl.
Add ice water gradually to make a thin batter.
Dip shrimp into the batter, letting excess drip off.
Heat oil to 375°F (190°C) in a deep pot.
Fry shrimp in batches until golden and crispy, about 2 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Edamame
instructions: Bring water and salt to a boil in a pot.
Add edamame pods and cook for 5-7 minutes until tender.
Drain and rinse with cold water to stop cooking.
Shuck the beans from the pods if desired.
Toss with soy sauce, sesame oil, and chili flakes.
Serve warm as an appetizer.

title: Chicken Teriyaki (Teriyaki Chicken)
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Miso Soup (Miso Shiru)
instructions: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a small pot.
Add dried wakame and tofu; simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Whisk miso paste in a small bowl with a ladleful of hot stock until dissolved.
Stir the miso mixture back into the pot.
Garnish with green onions and nori before serving.

title: Sushi Rice (Shari)
instructions: Rinse rice in a fine-mesh strainer until water runs clear.
Combine rice and water in a heavy-bottomed pot; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Turn off heat and let stand covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a paddle.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl.
Transfer rice to a large non-metallic bowl, drizzle vinegar mixture over it, and fold gently until evenly coated.

title: Tempura Shrimp (Ebi Tempura)
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Place shrimp on a plate and cover with plastic wrap; freeze for 15 minutes to firm up.
Whisk flour, potato starch, and salt in a bowl; gradually stir in ice water to form a thin batter.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dredge shrimp in batter, letting excess drip off.
Fry shrimp in batches until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Gyoza (Japanese Potstickers)
ingredients: 1/2 cup cabbage, finely grated and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix pork, chicken, cabbage, carrots, green onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Place a wrapper in your palm and add about 1 tsp of filling in the center.
Wet the edge of the wrapper with water, fold in half, and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange gyoza in a large skillet with a little oil.
Cook over medium heat until bottoms are golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup water, cover, and steam until meat is cooked through and water evaporates, about 5 minutes.
Uncover and cook any remaining moisture until crispy.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve hot.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/2 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Combine dashi stock and wakame in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add tofu cubes and let simmer for 2 minutes without boiling.
Remove pot from heat and dissolve miso paste into the soup by stirring gently.
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with sliced green onions.
Serve immediately in bowls.

title: Tempura Vegetables
ingredients: 1 lb sweet potato, cut into thick sticks
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
Shredded nori and Japanese mayo for serving
instructions: Whisk flour, salt, and ice-cold water together, then stir in the beaten egg just until combined; do not overmix.
Heat oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Dip vegetables in the batter one by one, allowing excess to drip off.
Fry vegetables in batches for 2-3 minutes until crispy and golden.
Drain on paper towels, serve with shredded nori and Japanese mayo.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls)
ingredients: 1/4 cup nori sheets, cut into strips
1/2 cup cooked salmon or pickled plum (umeboshi), chopped
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear, then cook with water and salt until tender.
Transfer cooked rice to a large bowl, drizzle with vinegar if desired, and mix gently.
While rice is still warm, season with a pinch of salt and let cool slightly.
Take a handful of rice, shape into a triangle or oval, and pack firmly.
Press a strip of nori and a piece of filling in the center of the rice ball, then seal.

title: Gyoza (Pan-Fried Dumplings)
instructions: In a bowl, mix pork, cabbage, carrot, onion, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, vinegar, and cornstarch until well combined.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper, fold in half, and pleat the edges to seal.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Place gyoza in the pan seam-side down and fry until golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Add 1/4 cup water to the pan, cover immediately, and steam for 4-5 minutes until water evaporates.
Uncover, fry briefly until crispy, then brush with remaining sauce and serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy sauce, mirin, sugar, garlic, and ginger for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken strips until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir the marinade into the skillet and simmer until thickened and sauce coats the chicken.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a small pot.
Remove from heat and whisk in miso paste until fully dissolved.
Stir in tofu cubes and dried wakame seaweed.
Heat gently for 2 minutes without boiling, then remove from heat.
Serve hot, garnished with sliced green onions.

title: Salmon Sashimi
ingredients: 1 lb fresh salmon fillet, sashimi grade
instructions: Prepare sushi rice according to package directions and season with rice vinegar and sugar.
Rinse salmon thoroughly, pat dry, and slice into thin, even pieces against the grain.
Mix rice wine vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl for a light dip.
Arrange salmon slices on a plate with a bed of sushi rice.
Serve with wasabi, pickled ginger, and dipping sauce.

title: Tempura
ingredients: 1 lb sweet potato, cut into batons
instructions: Combine flour, potato starch, baking powder, and ice-cold water to make a light, runny batter.
Dip shrimp and sweet potato into the batter one by one.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Carefully drop battered pieces into the oil in small batches.
Fry until golden brown and crisp, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and sprinkle with shichimi togarashi.

title: Edamame
instructions: Bring water, soy sauce, mirin, and salt to a boil in a pot.
Add fresh edamame pods and reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook for 6-8 minutes until pods are tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain the pods and let them cool slightly.
Transfer to a serving bowl and sprinkle with sesame seeds and red pepper flakes.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until golden brown on all sides.
Push chicken to the side and add garlic and ginger, cooking for 30 seconds.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 3-4 minutes until thickened.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Heat dashi stock in a pot over medium heat until simmering.
Add dried wakame and let it rehydrate for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in miso paste until fully dissolved.
Add cubed firm tofu and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Stir in silken tofu and sliced green onions.
Serve immediately in bowls.

title: Salmon Sashimi
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh salmon fillet, skin removed
2 sheets nori, cut into thin strips
instructions: Freeze the salmon fillet for 24 hours to ensure safety, then slice thinly against the grain.
Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar to make a dipping sauce.
Arrange salmon slices on a serving platter.
Place wasabi paste on the side.
Serve with nori strips and pickled ginger.
Consume immediately.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss shrimp with a pinch of salt.
Mix flour and cornstarch in a bowl, then slowly add ice water while whisking to avoid lumps.
Dip each shrimp into the egg, then coat thoroughly in the cold batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry shrimp in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve with tentsuyu sauce.

title: Oyakodon
ingredients: 2 chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, halved
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces.
In a bowl, beat eggs with chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Place chicken pieces in a shallow bowl or pot and pour the egg mixture over them.
Cover and microwave or simmer on stovetop until the egg is just set.
Serve the mixture hot over steamed white rice.
Garnish with nori strips.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, and garlic in a bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken strips until golden brown and cooked through.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 3-5 minutes until thickened.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Miso Soup
ingredients: 1/4 cup silken tofu, blended into dashi (optional)
instructions: Bring dashi broth to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add blended tofu (if using) and simmer for 2 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and stir in miso paste until dissolved.
Add tofu cubes and wakame seaweed.
Simmer for 2 minutes, then remove from heat and stir in green onions.

title: Tempura
ingredients: 1/2 lb sweet potato, sliced into thick rounds
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and ice water to create a lumpy batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip shrimp and sweet potato slices into the batter one by one.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and season lightly with salt.

title: Sushi Rice
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear, then cook with water.
While rice cooks, mix vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl.
Transfer cooked rice to a large wooden bowl and fan it while mixing.
Gently fold in the vinegar mixture until fully absorbed.
Cover with a damp cloth and let cool to room temperature.

title: Gyoza
ingredients: 1/2 cabbage, finely chopped and squeezed dry
instructions: Mix pork, cabbage, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Fold wrapper in half and pleat the edges to seal.
Arrange gyoza in a pan, add oil to the bottom.
Pour water around the edges, cover, and steam for 5 minutes.
Uncover, fry until bottoms are golden, then serve.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, garlic, and ginger to make the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces and cook until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add tofu and wakame seaweed to the simmering stock.
Remove the pot from heat.
Whisk miso paste with a little warm stock in a bowl, then stir it into the pot until dissolved.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix flour, ice-cold water, and egg in a bowl to make a light batter; do not overmix.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip shrimp into the batter, letting excess drip off.
Carefully lower shrimp into the hot oil and fry until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels, season with salt, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Edamame
ingredients: 1 lb frozen shelled edamame beans, thawed
instructions: Combine soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Add thawed edamame beans to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes.
Drain the beans and immediately transfer them to the sauce mixture.
Toss to coat evenly, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Salmon Sashimi
instructions: Place the salmon fillet on a clean cutting board and slice thinly against the grain.
Whisk together rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil to create a glaze.
Arrange the salmon slices on a plate.
Drizzle the glaze lightly over the salmon.
Garnish with sliced green onion, shredded daikon radish, and a dab of wasabi.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, sesame oil, and ginger in a small bowl.
Sear chicken in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer until thickened and chicken is cooked through.
Garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Heat dashi stock in a pot over medium heat.
Add tofu and wakame, simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and dissolve miso paste into the soup using a spoon.
Stir in chopped green onions and serve immediately.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add ice water and stir quickly to form a lumpy batter.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 375°F (190°C).
Dip shrimp into batter and fry until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Salmon Miso Glaze
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix miso, mirin, sake, soy sauce, and honey in a small bowl.
Place salmon on a baking sheet and brush with the glaze.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until salmon is cooked and glaze is caramelized.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk eggs, water, soy sauce, sugar, and salt together in a bowl.
Heat a non-stick rectangular pan over medium heat and add sesame oil.
Pour a thin layer of egg mixture, swirl to coat, and cook until set.
Roll the egg omelet, remove from pan, and repeat with remaining mixture.
Layer rolls together, slice, and garnish with green onion.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic to make the sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Pour dashi broth into a pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add tofu and wakame seaweed to the broth.
In a small bowl, dissolve miso paste with a ladleful of hot broth.
Stir the miso mixture back into the pot; do not boil after adding miso.
Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Salmon Sashimi
instructions: Ensure the salmon is sashimi-grade and slice it thinly against the grain.
Arrange the salmon slices on a chilled platter.
Serve with soy sauce, wasabi, sliced green onions, and lemon wedges on the side.
Garnish the top of the fish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Serve immediately while cold.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and ice water to create a loose, lumpy batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each shrimp into the batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Carefully place shrimp into the hot oil and fry until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and sprinkle with salt.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls)
ingredients: 2 tbsp nori sheets, cut into strips
instructions: Cook rice in water according to package instructions until fluffy.
While rice is warm, mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Transfer cooked rice to the bowl and fold in the vinegar mixture until cooled slightly.
Take a handful of seasoned rice, place a pickled plum in the center, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap a strip of nori around the bottom third of the rice ball before serving.

title: Chicken Katsu
instructions: Dredge chicken in flour, then egg, then panko.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan.
Fry chicken until golden and cooked through.
Slice chicken and serve with shredded lettuce, carrot, and mayonnaise.

title: Miso Ramen
ingredients: 4 packs ramen noodles, instant or fresh
instructions: Simmer broth with miso paste until warm.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
Assemble bowls with noodles, broth, pork, egg, green onions, and bamboo shoots.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Mix flour, water, and baking powder into a light batter.
Dip shrimp into batter and shake off excess.
Fry shrimp in hot oil until crisp and pink.
Serve immediately with tempura sauce and lemon wedge.

title: Sushi Rolls
ingredients: 2 cups sushi rice, cooked and seasoned with rice vinegar
1/2 cup fresh crab meat or imitation crab
instructions: Season cooked rice with rice vinegar, sugar, and salt.
Place nori on a bamboo mat and spread rice evenly.
Add cucumber, avocado, and crab near the edge.
Roll tightly using the mat and slice into pieces.

title: Tonkatsu Sauce
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small saucepan.
Stir over low heat until sugar is dissolved.
Remove from heat and let cool.
Store in an airtight container for later use.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Heat dashi stock in a pot over medium heat.
Add tofu and wakame, simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and whisk in miso paste.
Stir in sliced green onions.
Serve immediately.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl.
Sear chicken in a hot skillet with oil until golden.
Pour sauce over chicken and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir frequently until sauce thickens.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss shrimp lightly with salt.
Mix flour, ice water, and oil to make a thin batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Dip shrimp into batter one by one.
Fry shrimp for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve.

title: Sushi Rolls (Maki)
instructions: Cook sushi rice according to package directions.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce; pour over hot rice and fold gently.
Place nori on a bamboo mat.
Spread rice evenly over nori, leaving a 1-inch border at the top.
Arrange cucumber and avocado in a line across the center.
Roll tightly using the mat, seal with water, and slice.

title: Katsu Curry
ingredients: 1 lb pork loin, cut into thick strips
instructions: Set up a breading station with flour, eggs, and panko.
Dredge pork strips in flour, dip in egg, then coat in panko.
Fry pork in oil until golden brown and cooked through.
In a pot, melt butter and dissolve curry blocks in water.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes until thickened.
Serve pork on rice with curry sauce on top.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch in a small bowl until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken slices and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden brown on both sides.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Pour dashi stock into a small pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to low and dissolve miso paste into the stock, stirring constantly until smooth.
Add cubed tofu and rehydrated wakame seaweed to the pot.
Stir in chopped spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Remove from heat, garnish with sliced green onions, and serve immediately.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss shrimp with a light dusting of salt.
Whisk flour, ice water, egg, and baking powder in a bowl to create a lumpy, cold batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each shrimp into the batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Carefully lower shrimp into the hot oil and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving.

title: Sushi Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer until the water runs clear.
Combine rinsed rice and water in a heavy-bottomed pot and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for another 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl until dissolved.
Transfer rice to a large wooden or non-metallic bowl, fan it while pouring the vinegar mixture over it, and mix until rice is cool and glossy.

title: Okonomiyaki
ingredients: 1 sheet dried nori, cut into strips
instructions: In a large bowl, mix cabbage, flour, grated carrot, eggs, dashi stock, and bonito flakes.
Fold in the sliced pork belly until evenly distributed.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat and spread the batter into a round cake shape.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is golden and crispy.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for another 3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate, drizzle generously with okonomiyaki sauce and mayonnaise, and top with nori strips.

title: Chicken Teriyaki (Teriyaki Chicken)
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 green onion, thinly sliced, for garnish
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and garlic in a small bowl to make the teriyaki sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces and cook until golden brown and nearly cooked through, about 5-6 minutes.
Pour the teriyaki sauce over the chicken and simmer until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken, about 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Miso Soup (Miso Shiru)
instructions: Pour dashi stock into a small pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add sugar and tofu to the simmering stock.
Stir in the white miso paste and sugar (if using) to dissolve the paste without boiling.
Add the rehydrated wakame seaweed and let it simmer for 1-2 minutes.
Turn off the heat, stir in the sliced green onions, and serve immediately in bowls.

title: Vegetable Tempura (Yasai Tempura)
instructions: Whisk flour, cornstarch, and salt in a bowl; slowly whisk in ice-cold water and egg until smooth and very cold.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip vegetable pieces into the batter, ensuring they are lightly coated.
Fry vegetables in batches until they are crispy and golden brown, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving.

title: Grilled Salmon with Dashi Broth (Salmon no Yaki)
ingredients: 1 green onion, thinly sliced, for garnish
instructions: In a small bowl, mix dashi, mirin, soy sauce, sugar, and grated ginger to create a glaze.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down on a grill pan or in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the skin is crispy and the flesh is cooked through.
Brush the salmon generously with the dashi glaze during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Katsu Curry (Tonkatsu Curry)
ingredients: 1 lb pork loin, cut into 2 equal pieces
instructions: Set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and panko breadcrumbs in separate dishes.
Dredge pork pieces in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly with panko breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C) and fry pork until golden and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat and whisk in all-purpose flour.
Gradually whisk in tomato soup, ketchup, and soy sauce until smooth and thickened.
Serve the fried pork slices with the hot curry sauce and steamed rice.

title: Chicken Katsu
ingredients: 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded thin
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes with flour, beaten eggs, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge chicken in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly with panko.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with mayo and cabbage.

title: Miso Ramen
instructions: Cook ramen noodles according to package instructions, then drain.
In a pot, combine broth, miso paste, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger.
Heat the broth until simmering but not boiling.
Divide noodles into bowls and ladle hot broth over them.
Top each bowl with a halved soft-boiled egg, green onions, and sesame seeds.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic in a bowl.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and add butter.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the pan and cook for 4 minutes.
Flip salmon and pour the teriyaki sauce over them.
Cook for another 3-4 minutes until sauce thickens and salmon is opaque.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Vegetable Tempura
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, cut into sticks
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
Shredded paper strips or lettuce leaves, for serving
instructions: Prepare vegetables: cut sweet potatoes, broccoli, peppers, and spinach into bite-sized pieces.
Mix flour, beaten egg, and ice-cold water to form a thin, lumpy batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each vegetable piece into the batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Carefully place battered vegetables into the hot oil.
Fry until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes, removing with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with shredded paper strips.

title: Edamame
instructions: Rinse the edamame pods under cold water to remove loose dirt.
Combine edamame, salt, and water in a large pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 5 more minutes.
Drain well and toss with a little extra salt if desired before serving.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until browned on both sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens and chicken is cooked through.
Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Miso Soup
instructions: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add tofu and wakame seaweed to the simmering stock.
Whisk miso paste with a few ladles of hot stock in a separate bowl, then stir it into the pot (do not boil after adding miso).
Add chopped spinach and cook until wilted, about 1 minute.
Turn off heat and stir in sliced green onions before serving.

title: Tempura Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
Soy sauce and shredded daikon for serving
instructions: Mix flour, egg, ice water, and salt in a bowl to make a thin, lumpy batter; keep batter cold.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Dip shrimp into the cold batter, allowing excess to drip off.
Carefully lower shrimp into the hot oil and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove shrimp, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately with soy sauce and daikon.

title: Matcha Green Tea Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Sift together flour, baking powder, and matcha powder.
Alternately add dry ingredients and milk to the butter mixture, starting and ending with dry ingredients.
Stir in vanilla extract until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30-35 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

title: Katsu Curry
ingredients: 2 large pork cutlets, about 1 inch thick
1 can (14 oz) curry paste or sauce
instructions: Set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge pork cutlets in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly in panko.
Fry cutlets in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 4 minutes per side.
In the same pot, heat oil and sauté onion, carrots, and potatoes until softened.
Stir in the curry paste or sauce and simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Serve the sliced pork over rice with the curry sauce poured on top.

title: Tonjiru (Pork Bone Soup)
ingredients: 1 large daikon radish, peeled and cut into chunks
1 bunch leeks, white parts only, cut into 3-inch lengths
instructions: Place pork bones in a pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, then discard the scum that rises.
Add fresh water, pork belly, and a bay leaf. Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until the broth is milky white.
Add daikon, carrots, and leeks. Cook for another 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in soy sauce, mirin, and salt to taste.
Garnish with green onions before serving.

title: Tonkotsu Ramen
instructions: Boil water in a bowl and blanch the ramen noodles for 1 minute, then drain.
Pour hot tonkotsu broth over the noodles in the bowl.
Arrange chashu pork, marinated eggs, and nori triangles on top of the noodles.
Sprinkle sliced green onions and dried bonito flakes over the soup.
Drizzle chili oil and add a dash of tare to taste.

title: Mentaiko Donburi
ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water
