instructions: In a pan, stir-fry the julienned carrots with a little oil until softened.
Add the ground pork and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in the soy sauce and tonkotsu broth, then add the cornstarch slurry to thicken into a sauce.
Remove from heat and fold in the mentaiko and mayonnaise gently.
Serve the mixture over steamed rice and garnish with green onions.

title: Chirashi Don (Assorted Sashimi Bowl)
ingredients: 200 g sushi rice, seasoned with vinegar
1 sheet nori, torn into small pieces
instructions: Fluff the seasoned sushi rice in a large bowl.
Arrange slices of salmon and yellowtail over the rice.
Top with cooked shrimp, julienned cucumber, avocado slices, and edamame.
Sprinkle torn nori pieces and sesame oil over the fish and vegetables.
Drizzle with a little soy sauce and serve immediately.

title: Oden
ingredients: 2 daikon radishes, cut into thick coins
3 blocks of firm tofu, cut into cubes
150 g lotus root, cut into batons
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and both types of sugar in a large pot and bring to a simmer.
Add konjac, daikon, tofu, narutomaki, and lotus root. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add chicken skewers and green onions. Simmer for another 5 minutes until flavors meld.
Skim off any scum that rises to the surface.
Keep warm on low heat and serve in a large bowl with chopsticks and spoons.

title: Goya Champuru
ingredients: 2 lbs bitter melon, sliced into thin half-moons
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large wok over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add minced pork and cook until no longer pink.
Add grated carrots, daikon, and tofu; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the sliced bitter melon and season with soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently until the melon is tender-crisp.
Pour in the beaten eggs and quickly scramble until just set.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

title: Soba-zushi
ingredients: 1/4 cup grilled tuna or beef strips
instructions: Cook soba noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse with cold water.
In a small bowl, mix sushi vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the hot soba noodles and toss gently to coat.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil; mix well.
Place shredded nori on a cutting board.
Layer the noodles, carrots, cabbage, daikon, and meat evenly over the nori.
Roll tightly into a cylindrical shape using your hands or bamboo mat.
Slice into 1/2-inch thick pieces and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Serve immediately.

title: Yakimiso (Grilled Miso Glazed Pork)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs pork belly or loin, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together miso, soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic to make the glaze.
Place pork cubes in a large ziplock bag and pour the glaze over them; massage to coat.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Remove pork from the marinade and place on the grill.
Grill for 4-5 minutes per side, basting occasionally with remaining glaze.
Cook until pork is charred and cooked through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Gochujang Ramen
instructions: Cook ramen noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes; drain and set aside.
In a pot, combine broth, gochujang, sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar, and white pepper.
Bring the broth to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the sliced pork belly to the simmering broth and cook for 3 minutes until slightly crisp.
Divide noodles among four bowls.
Ladle the spicy broth and pork over the noodles.
Top each bowl with a soft-boiled egg, green onions, kimchi, and cabbage.
Serve hot.

title: Onigiri (Rice Balls with Mackerel)
ingredients: 1/2 cup sushi vinegar (rice vinegar, sugar, salt mixed)
4 cans yellowtail or mackerel, drained and flaked
1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Wash the rice until water runs clear, then cook according to package instructions.
While rice is hot, mix in sushi vinegar, salt, sugar, rice vinegar, soy sauce, and pepper.
Fluff the rice with a fan or paddle to cool it slightly while keeping it warm.
Flake the fish and mix gently with a pinch of salt.
Moisten hands with a little water to prevent sticking.
Take a scoop of rice (about 1/3 cup) and shape it into a triangle.
Press the flaked fish firmly into the center of the rice triangle.
Wrap the triangle with a thin strip of nori.
Repeat with remaining rice and serve.

title: Miso Soup with Wakame and Tofu
ingredients: 3 tablespoons white miso paste, dissolved in a little hot water
1/2 block firm tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Pour hot dashi stock into a bowl.
Add rehydrated wakame and cubed tofu to the soup.
Stir in the dissolved miso paste until fully incorporated.
Drizzle with sesame oil.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.

title: Hiroshima-style Okonomiyaki
ingredients: 1/4 cup thinly sliced pork belly or bacon
1 sheet dried omelet, cut into strips
instructions: Mix flour, water, egg, and baking powder in a bowl until smooth.
Fold in the shredded cabbage, carrots, and pork.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and pour the batter.
Spread the batter thin and place the omelet strips and pork on top.
Cook for 3 minutes, then flip carefully and cook the other side for 2 minutes.
Drizzle generously with mayonnaise and okonomiyaki sauce.
Sprinkle with aonori and bonito flakes before serving.

title: Miso Glazed Baby Eggplant
instructions: Brush the cut sides of the eggplants with a little oil and roast until tender.
Whisk together miso, mirin, sake, sugar, and soy sauce in a small bowl.
Place roasted eggplants in a baking dish and pour the glaze over them.
Cover and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes until the glaze is bubbly.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Okazu: Simmered Radish and Daikon
ingredients: 1 large daikon radish, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks
instructions: Combine daikon, dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes until daikon is tender.
Add bonito flakes during the last 5 minutes of cooking to infuse flavor.
Remove from heat and let the bonito settle.
Skim off the bonito flakes before serving the simmered radish.

title: Grilled Oysters with Miso Butter
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated fresh cheese (optional, like koya-dofu or mild cheddar)
instructions: Mix softened butter, miso paste, ginger, and green onion in a bowl until well combined.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Place oysters in the shell on the grill.
Spread a generous amount of miso butter on top of each oyster.
Grill for 3-4 minutes until the oysters are closed and the butter is golden.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with panko and cheese if using.

title: Zosui (Sendai-Style Rice Porridge)
instructions: Bring water and rice to a boil, then simmer until soft.
Add seasoned soy sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add bonito flakes and dried sardines, cooking until broth darkens.
Remove solids, strain broth, and return to pot if needed.
Stir in green onions and serve hot.

title: Kurodare (Dark Sauce Meatballs)
instructions: Mix ground pork, soy sauce, sake, sugar, ginger, and pepper in a bowl.
Form mixture into small balls and place in a pot.
Add dashi stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Stir in green onions and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

title: Tsukimi Somen (Moon Viewing Somen)
instructions: Prepare broth by mixing chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, salt, and sesame oil.
Cook somen noodles according to package directions, then rinse in cold water.
Place noodles in a bowl and pour hot broth over them.
Arrange shirataki noodles, egg halves, nori strips, and green onions on top.
Serve immediately.

title: Hare Maki (Moon Shell Rolls)
instructions: Season rice with salt and furikake, then spread onto nori sheets.
Spread a thin layer of sweet red bean paste over the rice.
Add strips of carrot, cucumber, and umeboshi paste.
Roll tightly from the bottom edge of the nori.
Dip ends in kinako to seal the rolls.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and serve.

title: Tadai (Grilled Rice Cake)
instructions: Mix rice flour, sugar, water, baking powder, milk, and butter in a bowl.
Divide batter into two portions; mix matcha into one.
Steam both portions until set and golden brown.
Spread red bean paste on one half and top with matcha half.
Sprinkle with kinako and drizzle with condensed milk.
Cut into squares and serve warm.

title: Oyakodon
ingredients: 2 cups chicken thigh meat, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup egg, lightly beaten with a pinch of salt
instructions: In a small pot, combine chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and onion; bring to a simmer.
Add chicken pieces to the simmering broth and cook until no longer pink.
Pour the beaten egg mixture over the chicken and broth.
Reduce heat to low and gently stir the egg until it sets into a custard-like consistency.
Serve immediately over steamed white rice, garnished with chopped green onions.

title: Tamagoyaki
ingredients: Green onion, thinly sliced for garnish
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together eggs, water, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and salt until fully combined.
Heat a small non-stick frying pan over medium heat and add a thin layer of oil.
Pour in a small amount of egg mixture, spreading it evenly to form a thin rectangle.
Once the egg is set on the bottom but still slightly runny on top, fold the egg roll inward.
Add another small amount of oil, pour in more egg mixture, and repeat the folding process until all egg is used.
Remove from heat and let rest for 2 minutes before slicing into thick rolls and garnishing with green onion.

title: Miso Soup with Wakame and Tofu
instructions: Soak dried wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain and squeeze out excess water.
In a pot, bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer.
Add tofu cubes and mushrooms (if using) to the simmering stock.
Remove the pot from heat to prevent the miso from breaking.
Whisk miso paste with a little hot stock until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Stir in the rehydrated wakame and sliced green onions.
Serve immediately in individual bowls.

title: Tamago Kake Gohan
ingredients: 2 large eggs, hard-boiled and sliced into thin strips
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, sugar, and white pepper.
Place a generous portion of warm white rice in a bowl.
Arrange the sliced hard-boiled egg strips over the rice.
Pour the seasoned soy sauce mixture over the egg and rice.
Sprinkle grated ginger and crushed nori flakes on top if desired.
Serve immediately while the rice is still warm.

title: Chazuke
instructions: Brew the green tea and let it cool slightly to warm temperature.
Place cooked white rice in a bowl.
Arrange sliced salmon, tamagoyaki, pickled radish, and shredded nori on top of the rice.
Drizzle soy sauce, salt, and sugar over the toppings.
Pour the warm green tea over the rice and toppings.
Sprinkle sesame seeds on top and serve immediately.

title: Katsu Sando
instructions: Dredge pork in flour, then egg, then panko.
Fry pork until golden and cooked through.
Simmer cabbage in dashi and butter until soft.
Toast bread slices lightly.
Assemble by placing cabbage and pork on bread.

title: Takoyaki
instructions: Mix dashi, flour, sugar, and salt to make batter.
Fold in peas, cabbage, and octopus.
Heat takoyaki pan with butter until hot.
Pour batter into mold cavities.
Use skewers to flip balls until golden.

title: Osaka-style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Mix flour and dashi to form a thick batter.
Fold in cabbage, carrots, onions, pork, and eggs.
Pour onto a hot griddle.
Cook until edges are set, then flip.
Top with sauce, green onion, and katsuobushi.

title: Fugu Sashimi
ingredients: 200g fresh fugu fillet, cleaned by expert
instructions: Slice fugu fillet thinly against the grain.
Arrange slices on a serving plate.
Serve with soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, and wasabi.
Provide pickled ginger on the side.

title: Kitsune Udon
instructions: Boil udon noodles until tender, then drain.
Simmer tofu in dashi, sugar, salt, and soy sauce.
Place noodles in bowls.
Top with tofu and drizzle with extra sauce.
Garnish with green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Kyoto-Style Miso Soup (Miso Shiru)
ingredients: 4 cups dashi stock, homemade or store-bought
instructions: Heat the dashi stock in a pot until just simmering.
Add the tofu and wakame seaweed, then turn off the heat.
Dissolve the miso paste in a small bowl with a ladle of hot stock, then stir it into the pot.
Gently stir in the natto and drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve immediately in warm bowls.

title: Tofu and Vegetable Hot Pot (Nabe)
instructions: Dissolve the miso paste in 1/4 cup of the dashi stock to make a broth base.
Combine the remaining dashi with the miso broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the dried shiitake mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tofu, enoki, cabbage, konjac, and lotus root.
Cook until vegetables are tender, then serve hot with sesame seeds.

title: Homemade Tempura Batter (Tempura) with Shrimp and Sweet Potato
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, cut into batons
instructions: Place the egg whites in a separate bowl and the egg yolks in another.
Mix the flour with the egg yolks and ice water until smooth.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold them into the flour mixture.
Dip the shrimp and sweet potato into the batter, ensuring it is fully coated.
Heat oil to 340°F (170°C) and fry the tempura in batches until golden and crispy.
Season lightly with salt and serve immediately.

title: Seasoned Tofu (Agedashi Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1-inch cubes
Soy sauce and wasabi for dipping
instructions: Dredge the tofu cubes in the flour, then roll them in the potato starch.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) and deep fry the tofu until golden brown and crispy.
In a small saucepan, combine dashi, mirin, sugar, and salt; bring to a simmer.
Pour the hot sauce over the fried tofu right before serving.
Serve with soy sauce and wasabi on the side.

title: Grilled Eel (Unagi) with Sweet Soy Glaze (Tare)
ingredients: 1 whole freshwater eel, cleaned and grilled
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sugar, sake, butter, and grated ginger to make the tare sauce.
Grill the eel over charcoal or a grill pan until skin is charred and flesh is cooked through.
Brush the warm eel generously with the tare sauce.
Return the eel to the grill or broiler for 2 minutes to caramelize the glaze.
Slice the eel diagonally and serve over a bed of steamed rice.

title: Hokkaido Crab Sushi (Kani Maki)
ingredients: 1 large Hokkaido king crab leg, meat removed and flaked
instructions: Season cooked rice with vinegar, sugar, and salt until shiny and cool.
Place nori sheet on a bamboo mat, shiny side down.
Spread a thin layer of crab rice over the nori, leaving a 1-inch border at the top.
Distribute flaked crab meat and cucumber strips evenly over the rice.
Roll tightly using the mat, then slice into 6 pieces and serve.

title: Soup Curry (Soboro Curry)
instructions: Fry ground pork with diced onion in a pot until browned and oil renders.
Add diced carrots and potatoes, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Pour in beef broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Add soy sauce and curry roux, stirring until dissolved.
Simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in milk and frozen peas, cook for 2 more minutes before serving.

title: Soy Sauce Braised Sea Urchin (Unagi-style)
ingredients: 1 large sea urchin, cleaned and dried
1 sheet nori, cut into small pieces
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl.
Place the sea urchin in a heatproof bowl and pour the sauce over it.
Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap.
Microwave on high for 3 minutes, then let stand for 2 minutes.
Remove, discard the nori pieces if desired, and serve immediately.

title: Charcoal Grilled Corn (Yaki Imo)
ingredients: 4 large sweet corn cobs, husks removed
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce and melted butter in a small bowl.
Brush the corn cobs generously with the soy sauce mixture.
Grill corn over medium charcoal heat, turning every 2 minutes until charred.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the grilled corn while still hot.
Serve immediately with extra soy sauce if desired.

title: Sautéed Hokkaido Green Beans (Mame)
ingredients: 3 cups fresh green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Add garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add green beans, salt, and soy sauce, tossing quickly.
Pour in water, cover, and steam for 2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Toss to coat with pan juices and serve.

title: Tonkotsu Ramen
ingredients: 500g pork bones, cut into large chunks
instructions: Roast pork bones in an oven at 200°C for 20 minutes to remove impurities.
Place bones in a large pot with cold water and bring to a rolling boil for 10 minutes.
Skim off all the foam and scum from the surface, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer gently for 12 hours without lifting the lid, until the broth is creamy white.
Season the broth with soy sauce and sesame oil to taste.
Bring broth to a boil and cook ramen noodles for 2 minutes.
Assemble bowls with broth, noodles, pork belly, green onions, nori, and soft-boiled egg.
Garnish with fresh garlic chives and serve immediately.

title: Menchi Katsu
instructions: Mix ground pork, grated ginger, minced garlic, soy sauce, sake, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add the beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then mix thoroughly until the meat sticks together.
Shape the mixture into four round patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Set up a breading station with flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dip each patty first in flour, then egg, and finally coat generously with panko.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170°C and fry patties for 4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and let cool slightly before cutting into wedges.
Serve hot with a side of miso soup and pickled vegetables.

title: Hakata-style Tonkotsu Somen
instructions: Roast pork bones and render the pork fat together in a large pot until the fat is clear.
Add water and roasted bones to the pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 8 hours to create a rich, milky white broth.
Strain the broth and season with soy sauce, salt, and grated ginger.
Bring broth to a rolling boil and cook somen noodles for 30 seconds.
Drain noodles and transfer to a serving bowl.
Pour the hot broth over the noodles.
Top with chashu pork, shredded nori, green onion, and garlic chives.
Serve immediately while steaming hot.

title: Okinawan Goya Champuru
instructions: Salt the julienned bitter melon and let sit for 10 minutes, then rinse and squeeze out excess water.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and sauté garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it into small pieces.
Add black beans, tomato, and bitter melon to the wok.
Stir in soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and white pepper.
Cook for 5 minutes until the bitter melon is tender but still has some crunch.
Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble quickly until just set.
Serve hot over a bed of steamed white rice.

title: Miyako-age (Fukuoka Style)
instructions: Mix ground pork, breadcrumbs, egg, grated carrot, cabbage, ginger, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Form the mixture into six oval-shaped cutlets about 1 cm thick.
Prepare a breading station with flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs.
Dip each cutlet in flour, then egg, and coat evenly with panko.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 175°C and fry cutlets for 3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and let rest for 2 minutes to firm up.
Cut into wedges and serve hot with miso soup and pickled radish.

title: Goya Champuru
ingredients: 1 tsp goya no shio (bitter melon salt)
instructions: Fry minced pork in sesame oil until browned.
Add ginger and garlic, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add diced bitter melon and cook until slightly tender.
Season with goya no shio and soy sauce.
Pour beaten eggs over the mixture and scramble gently.
Stir in scallions and remove from heat.

title: Soki
instructions: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sugar, sake, ginger, and garlic in a pot.
Bring the sauce to a boil and simmer until reduced by half.
Add sliced pork belly and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in sesame oil and gochugaru.
Garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Udon Soba Noodle Soup
ingredients: 4 bundles udon noodles, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 bundles soba noodles, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a large pot.
Bring the broth to a rolling boil.
Add udon and soba noodles, cook until al dente.
Stir in julienned ginger and sesame oil.
Divide noodles into bowls, top with green onions and egg halves.

title: Gomoku Rice
instructions: Cook rice in water until fully done.
In a separate pan, stir-fry pork with ginger and garlic until browned.
Add soy sauce, sugar, mirin, sake, sesame oil, and gochugaru to the pork.
Simmer until the sauce thickens.
Mix the sauce into the cooked rice.
Garnish with chopped green onions and egg halves.

title: Rafute
instructions: Boil pork belly in water until tender, about 45 minutes.
In a pot, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, gochugaru, and water.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and add the boiled pork.
Cook on low heat until the sauce reduces and coats the pork.
Drizzle with sesame oil, garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Hiroshima-style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Mix flour, egg, and dashi to make a thick batter.
Sauté cabbage, pork, wakame, and green onion in oil until soft.
Pour batter into a hot oiled pan and spread evenly.
Place the sautéed filling in the center, then fold the batter over it.
Fry until the bottom is golden brown, flip, and fry the other side.
Slide onto a plate and top with sauce, mayo, cheese, and bonito flakes.

title: Hiroshima-style Tonkatsu
instructions: Pound the pork loin to an even thickness.
Dredge pork in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in panko.
Fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through.
Serve on a plate with tonkatsu sauce, pickled radish, and a strip of nori.

title: Katsuo Tare (Bonito Dashi Broth)
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat.
Remove from heat and stir in bonito flakes until they dissolve.
Strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve to remove solids.
Serve hot as a soup base with udon noodles and vegetables.

title: Kishimen (Flat Udon with Tonkotsu Broth)
instructions: Cook kishimen in boiling water until tender, then drain.
Simmer chikuwa, naruto, and wakame in tonkotsu broth.
Add dashi and green onions to the broth.
Serve the noodles in a bowl topped with the simmered seafood and broth.
Garnish with bonito flakes before serving.

title: Hiroshima-style Miso Soup
instructions: Add cabbage, tofu, and wakame to the dashi stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and dissolve miso paste by whisking it in off the heat.
Stir in grated daikon and green onions.
Serve immediately in a warm bowl.

title: Nigiri-zushi (Sendai-style)
ingredients: 2 cups short-grain rice, washed until water runs clear
1 sheet nori, cut into small pieces
instructions: Cook rice with water until fluffy and let it cool to room temperature.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl until dissolved.
Transfer cooked rice to a large bowl and drizzle with sesame oil.
Pour vinegar mixture over rice and cut through gently to season evenly.
Moisten hands with vinegar water and shape rice into small oblong mounds.
Place a slice of tuna on top of each rice mound.
Garnish with small pieces of nori if desired.

title: Miso Soup with Wakame and Tofu
instructions: Heat dashi stock in a pot over medium heat.
Add wakame seaweed and let it rehydrate for a few minutes.
Stir in rice wine and tofu, simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in miso paste until dissolved.
Garnish with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Ochazuke with Grilled Mackerel
instructions: Pour hot green tea over the cooked rice and stir gently to absorb.
Top with grated daikon radish and shredded dried seaweed.
Place a piece of grilled mackerel on top of each serving.
Drizzle soy sauce over the fish and rice.
Sprinkle with dried seaweed powder just before serving.

title: Mochi Rice Cakes with Red Bean Paste
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour, water, and salt in a pot.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thick and smooth.
Spread the mixture on a clean cloth and let it cool slightly.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Cut small pieces of dough and flatten them into circles.
Place a small amount of red bean paste in the center of each piece.
Wrap the dough around the filling and seal the edges.
Fry the mochi in vegetable oil until golden brown.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Kamaboko (Fish Cake Rolls)
ingredients: 1/4 cup nori sheets, cut into strips
instructions: Mix fish paste, water, sugar, salt, and ginger paste in a bowl.
Steam the mixture in a mold or on a tray for 15 minutes.
Let it cool and remove from the mold.
Cut the cooled fish cake into thin slices.
Arrange slices on a plate and top with nori strips.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

title: Omu Rice
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté the diced onion until soft.
Add the ground pork and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in ketchup, soy sauce, and sugar, then simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten eggs over the meat mixture and stir gently until scrambled.
Add the cooked rice and milk, mixing until fully combined.
Heat through for another minute before serving.

title: Tamagoyaki
instructions: Whisk eggs, water, soy sauce, sugar, and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Heat oil in a non-stick tamagoyaki pan over medium heat.
Pour a thin layer of batter into the pan and cook until the edges set.
Roll the omelet tightly and push it to one side.
Add a little more oil and pour another layer of batter next to the roll.
Repeat until all batter is used, rolling each new layer into the existing roll.
Serve warm.

title: Katsudon
instructions: Pound the pork chop thin, dip in flour, then egg, then potato starch.
Fry the breaded chop in oil until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Remove the chop and keep warm; drain excess oil from the pan.
Sauté the cabbage slices in the pan until slightly wilted.
Pour in dashi stock, ketchup, soy sauce, and sugar, bringing to a simmer.
Add the fried pork chop back into the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and place the chop on a bowl, pouring the sauce over it.

title: Gyudon
ingredients: 200g beef chuck, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and water.
Heat a pot over medium heat and add the beef slices in a single layer.
Let the beef sear for about 30 seconds without moving it.
Stir the meat gently to brown the other side, then remove from the pot.
Add the onion slices to the same pot and sauté for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot and pour in the sauce mixture.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the beef.

title: Chawanmushi
ingredients: 2 shiitake mushrooms, stems removed and sliced
1/4 cup cooked shrimp or chicken, chopped
instructions: In a bowl, whisk eggs, dashi, water, soy sauce, salt, and ginger until smooth.
Place the mushroom and shrimp pieces into a small bowl.
Pour the egg mixture over the toppings, ensuring they are submerged.
Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and poke small holes for steam.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 minutes until the eggs are fully set.
Remove from the steamer and let cool slightly before serving.

title: Osaka-style Chicken Karaage
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, boneless and skinless
instructions: Pound chicken thighs to even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Mix flour, garlic powder, and potato starch in a shallow bowl.
Marinate chicken in sake for 30 minutes.
Dredge chicken in the flour mixture, pressing to coat.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Chikuzenni (Braised Pumpkin and Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
1 bunch spinach, stems and leaves separated
1/2 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
instructions: Blanch spinach stems in boiling water for 1 minute, then add leaves for 30 seconds.
In a pot, combine pumpkin, tofu, mushrooms, water, dashi, mirin, and soy sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 15 minutes until pumpkin is tender.
Stir in sugar and sesame oil.
Add blanched spinach and cook for another 2 minutes.
Adjust seasoning if needed and serve hot.

title: Okonomiyaki (Osaka Style)
ingredients: 1 tbsp dried seaweed (nori), cut into strips
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, eggs, dashi, water, and sweetener until smooth.
Fold in the shredded cabbage thoroughly.
Pour batter into a hot griddle with oil and spread into a round shape.
Top with bonito flakes and nori strips.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface and underside is golden, about 5 minutes.
Flip and cook the other side until golden.
Slide onto a plate and drizzle with okonomiyaki sauce and mayonnaise.
Sprinkle with more bonito flakes and serve.

title: Kishimen (Thin Flat Noodles)
ingredients: 2 tbsp dashi stock for soup base
instructions: Bring chicken stock, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and sesame oil to a simmer.
Boil kishimen noodles in the seasoned broth for 2-3 minutes.
Drain noodles and place in a bowl.
Add a ladle of the hot broth to the bowl.
Top with sliced chashu pork, nori strips, and bonito flakes.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Fukujinzuke (Pickled Mixed Vegetables)
instructions: Boil carrots, daikon, burdock, and shiitake in water for 3 minutes, then rinse with cold water.
Place vegetables in a sterilized jar.
Combine rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce in a small pan.
Heat the mixture until sugar dissolves, then remove from heat.
Add kombu to the liquid, let it sit for 5 minutes, then remove kombu.
Pour the hot pickling liquid over the vegetables in the jar.
Seal the jar and let it ferment at room temperature for 2 days.
Move to the refrigerator and enjoy after 1 week.

title: Kyoto-Style Steamed Egg (Tamago Kake Gohan)
instructions: Whisk eggs with dashi, soy sauce, and sugar until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a shallow bowl and steam over boiling water for 8 minutes until set.
Cut into strips and serve warm over steamed rice.
Garnish with scallions and drizzle with sesame oil.

title: Vegetable Tempura (Yasai Tempura)
ingredients: Salt and grated daikon for serving
instructions: Mix potato starch, flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add ice-cold water and whisk gently to form a thin batter, leaving some lumps.
Dip vegetables into the batter one by one.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry vegetables for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with salt and grated daikon.

title: Kyoto Natto (Fermented Soybeans)
instructions: Open natto packages and mix well with chopsticks to stretch the beans.
Add soy sauce, grated ginger, and sesame oil, then mix thoroughly.
Place a spoonful of natto on each bowl of steamed rice.
Top with sliced green onion and nori strips.
Crack a beaten egg over the natto and simmer gently if desired.

title: Kinchaku Sushi (Sushi in a Silk Bag)
ingredients: Wasabi and pickled ginger for serving
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions and let it cool slightly.
Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pan and heat until dissolved.
Transfer rice to a large bowl, pour vinegar mixture over it, and mix gently with a rice paddle.
Spread rice onto a bamboo mat and arrange shrimp, egg, and cucumber in a line.
Roll tightly using the mat to form a cylinder, then wrap in nori strips.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and drizzle with sesame oil.

title: Kinpira Gobo (Braised Lotus Root and Carrots)
instructions: Soak julienned lotus root in water with vinegar to prevent browning.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok and sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add lotus root and stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar, then simmer for 10 minutes until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Hokkaido Tonjiru
ingredients: 1.5 kg pork belly, sliced into 1-inch cubes
1 daikon radish, cut into thick rounds
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Place pork belly in a large pot and add cold water; bring to a boil, then skim off any foam.
Add sake and garlic, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
Add potatoes, carrots, and daikon radish to the pot.
Simmer gently for another 30-40 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Stir in soy sauce, sugar, salt, and white pepper to adjust the flavor.
Serve hot in bowls, garnished with sliced green onions.

title: Kare Raisu
ingredients: Sliced fried chicken or beef for topping
instructions: Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion until translucent, then add carrot and potato, cooking for 2 minutes.
Stir in broth, ketchup, brown sugar, soy sauce, curry powder, and turmeric; bring to a simmer.
Add the cooked rice and stir gently until the grains are coated and liquid is absorbed.
Cook on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy.
Season with salt to taste, then serve topped with fried chicken or beef.

title: Somen Noodles with Ponzu
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook somen noodles according to package directions until firm but chewy.
Drain noodles and rinse immediately under cold water to stop cooking.
In a small bowl, whisk together dashi, soy sauce, rice vinegar, ponzu, sugar, green onion, and ginger until sugar dissolves.
Place noodles in individual serving bowls.
Pour the ponzu dressing over the noodles.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and pickled radish slices.

title: Menchi Katsu
ingredients: Japanese mayo and shredded cabbage for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix ground pork, chopped onion, breadcrumbs, soy sauce, sake, sugar, egg, and pepper until well combined.
Shape the mixture into 4-5 oval patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Set up three shallow dishes with flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each patty in flour, dip in egg, and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C) and fry patties until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve with shredded cabbage, mayo, and lemon wedges.

title: Genghis Khan
ingredients: 1 lb lamb shoulder or leg, cut into 1-inch cubes
Green onions and sesame seeds for garnish
Steamed buns or rice for serving
instructions: In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine lamb, garlic, onion, broth, sake, soy sauce, sugar, white pepper, garlic powder, and sesame oil.
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce to a simmer.
Skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Adjust seasoning if needed, then garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve hot directly from the pot with steamed buns or rice.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup spinach, blanched and seasoned with sesame oil
1 cup bean sprouts, seasoned with salt and sesame oil
instructions: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Season and blanch the spinach, then drain.
Stir-fry the zucchini, carrots, and bean sprouts separately with minimal oil.
Slice the beef bulgogi and arrange it on top of the rice.
Place the fried egg on top.
Serve in a bowl with gochujang and sesame seeds on the side for dipping.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and pork belly, stir-frying until the pork is browned.
Add the kimchi, kimchi juice, and water, then bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the kimchi is very soft and the flavors meld.
Add the tofu cubes and cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in green onions and serve hot in a stone pot or bowl.

title: Japchae
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and chop.
Stir-fry the garlic in sesame oil until fragrant.
Add carrots, onions, and bell peppers; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and cook for another minute.
Toss in the sweet potato noodles and spinach.
Season with soy sauce and sugar, then toss until evenly coated.

title: Dakgalbi
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces in soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and gochugaru for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet or grill pan over high heat.
Cook the chicken until browned and nearly cooked through.
Add the onions, potatoes, and carrots; stir-fry until slightly softened.
Add the cabbage and kimchi, then pour the remaining marinade over the mixture.
Simmer until the sauce thickens and the vegetables are tender.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 12 oz rice cakes (tteok), cut into sticks
instructions: In a large pot, combine gochujang, water, sugar, and garlic; stir until smooth.
Bring the sauce to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the rice cake sticks and fish cakes; cook for 10 minutes until the rice cakes are soft and the sauce thickens.
Add the dried anchovies if using, and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice and set aside to cool.
Blanch spinach, carrots, zucchini, and bean sprouts separately.
Season each vegetable with a little salt and sesame oil.
In a small bowl, mix gochujang, garlic, soy sauce, and sugar.
Assemble the dish by spreading rice in a bowl, arranging vegetables in a circle, placing the egg in the center, and drizzling with the sauce.
Serve immediately, optionally with sesame seeds on top.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until browned.
Stir in the chopped kimchi and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water or broth and bring to a boil.
Add gochugaru and sugar, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add tofu and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the noodles and cook until softened.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 1 cup beef, thinly sliced and marinated
instructions: Cook the sweet potato starch noodles according to package instructions, then rinse with cold water and drain well.
Blanch spinach, zucchini, bean sprouts, carrots, and mushrooms separately.
In a large bowl, toss the noodles with spinach, vegetables, and mushrooms.
Season with soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Add the marinated beef and stir to combine.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.
Toss gently to mix everything evenly.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 1 lb short ribs (galbi), trimmed and cut into pieces
instructions: Combine soy sauce, sugar, water, garlic, and sesame oil in a pot.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Add the short ribs and sliced onion to the pot.
Cover and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and sauce has thickened.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove from heat and let the meat rest in the sauce for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and chopped green onion before serving.

title: Sundubu Jjigae
ingredients: 1 lb soft tofu (sundubu), cut into cubes
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until slightly browned.
Stir in the chopped kimchi and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water or broth, gochugaru, and sugar.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the soft tofu cubes gently and cook for 3 minutes without stirring vigorously.
Stir in the noodles and cook until softened.
Season with soy sauce if needed, garnish with green onions, and serve immediately while hot.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 3 strips beef flank steak, thinly sliced and marinated
1 large zucchini, sliced into thin rounds
instructions: Prepare all vegetables and marinate the beef.
Cook the rice and let it cool slightly.
Assemble the rice in a bowl, arranging the vegetables in a circle around the center.
Place the fried egg in the center of the bowl.
Top with the marinated beef.
Serve immediately with a spoonful of gochujang on the side.

title: Kimchi
ingredients: 2 large Napa cabbage heads, halved lengthwise
instructions: Salt the cabbage halves and let them sit for 2-3 hours to draw out moisture.
Rinse the cabbage thoroughly and squeeze out excess water.
Mix the vegetables, garlic, ginger, spices, and seasonings in a large bowl.
Layer the seasoned vegetables between the cabbage leaves.
Pack tightly into a container, pressing down firmly.
Cover with a heavy weight and let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days.
Transfer to the refrigerator after the desired fermentation time.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 12 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked in warm water
1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in warm water until tender, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Stir-fry the vegetables with a little oil until slightly softened.
Stir-fry the beef with soy sauce and sugar until cooked through.
Combine the noodles, beef, and vegetables in a large bowl.
Toss everything together with the remaining seasonings.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Samgyeopsal (Pork Belly BBQ)
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Marinate the pork belly strips with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger for 30 minutes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Cook the pork belly strips on the grill, turning occasionally until crispy and cooked through.
Serve the grilled pork with rice, kimchi, and dipping sauces.
Add cucumber slices, green onions, and perilla leaves to the plate.
Serve immediately while the pork is hot and crispy.

title: Tteokguk
ingredients: 1 lb rice cakes (tteok), sliced into thin rounds
instructions: Simmer the chicken broth with the pork belly until the meat is tender.
Add the rice cakes to the broth and cook until they float to the surface.
Stir in the vegetables and mushrooms, cooking until they are tender-crisp.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, and garlic to the broth.
Drop the beaten eggs into the simmering broth to create egg ribbons.
Garnish with chopped green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve hot as a soup.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup mixed seasonal vegetables (spinach, zucchini, carrots, mushrooms), stir-fried
instructions: Cook the rice and let it cool slightly.
Stir-fry each vegetable separately until tender-crisp.
Season vegetables lightly with sesame oil and salt.
Divide the rice into individual bowls.
Arrange the fried vegetables in a circle on top of the rice.
Place a fried egg in the center of the rice.
Dollop gochujang in the middle.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Mix everything together before eating.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef ribeye, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and grated pear until sugar dissolves.
Add sliced beef and sesame oil to the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat until smoking.
Add the marinated beef in a single layer without overcrowding.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until browned and slightly charred.
Stir frequently to ensure even cooking.
Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Kimchi
ingredients: 2 lbs Napa cabbage, halved lengthwise and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Submerge cabbage pieces in a brine of water and coarse sea salt for 2 hours, flipping halfway through.
Rinse the cabbage thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess salt.
Squeeze out as much water as possible from the cabbage.
In a large bowl, mix gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger, sugar, daikon radish, and green onions.
Toss the cabbage with the spice mixture until evenly coated.
Pack the kimchi tightly into clean glass jars.
Seal the jars and place them in a cool place (around 70°F/21°C) for fermentation.
After 3-5 days, the kimchi will be ready to eat.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add diced pork and cook until browned.
Add chopped kimchi and sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in doenjang and gochugaru.
Pour in water and kimchi juice, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add cubed tofu and spinach, simmer for another 5 minutes.
Slowly drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring gently to create ribbons.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve hot.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 1 lb Korean short ribs (galbi), cut into pieces
instructions: In a bowl, combine soy sauce, sugar, grated pear, garlic, and ginger until sugar dissolves.
Add the short ribs to the marinade and let sit for 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place ribs and marinade into a deep baking dish.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1.5 to 2 hours, turning once halfway through.
Remove foil and add the remaining water and green onions.
Bake uncovered for another 30 minutes until the sauce thickens and the meat is tender.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Drizzle with sesame oil before eating.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions and let it cool slightly.
Blanch spinach, carrots, bean sprouts, and zucchini in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Season vegetables lightly with sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry the beef bulgogi until cooked through.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Assemble bowls by placing rice at the bottom.
Arrange each vegetable and the beef in separate sections on top of the rice.
Place the fried egg on top of the other ingredients.
Drizzle gochujang over the dish and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add garlic and onion, sauté until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on both sides.
Stir in doenjang and gochugaru, cooking for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Add the chopped kimchi and stir to combine.
Pour in the water or dashi stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until flavors meld.
Add napa cabbage and simmer for another 5 minutes until tender.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Japchae
instructions: Cook glass noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse with cold water.
Blanch spinach, zucchini, and carrots in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Sauté mushrooms and garlic in sesame oil until soft.
Add beef bulgogi to the pan and cook until heated through.
In a separate bowl, mix soy sauce, brown sugar, and sesame oil.
Combine cooked noodles, blanched vegetables, and beef in a large mixing bowl.
Pour the sauce mixture over the ingredients and toss thoroughly.
Fold in the spinach last to prevent it from getting too wet.
Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with green onions.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef ribeye, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and pepper.
Add the sliced beef to the marinade and stir to coat evenly.
Let the beef marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add the marinated beef in batches to avoid steaming; cook until browned and caramelized.
Remove cooked beef and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the sliced onions and bell peppers until tender-crisp.
Return the beef to the pan and toss everything together.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.

title: Bibim Guksu
instructions: Cook glass noodles in boiling water until al dente, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Blanch spinach, carrots, and bean sprouts in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
In a small bowl, mix gochujang, sesame oil, soy sauce, and sugar to make the sauce.
Combine the cooked noodles with the sauce in a large bowl.
Fold in the blanched vegetables and kimchi.
Arrange the sliced cucumber on top of the noodle mixture.
Place a fried egg on each serving portion.
Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (spinach, bean sprouts, carrots, zucchini), stir-fried separately
instructions: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Wash and sauté the mixed vegetables until tender-crisp.
Slice the beef bulgogi and sauté with sesame oil.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Assemble by placing rice in a bowl, arranging vegetables and meat in a circle, topping with egg.
Serve immediately with a dollop of gochujang on the side.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: In a large pot, combine kimchi, pork belly, and radish with water or broth.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the kimchi softens.
Add Napa cabbage and bean sprouts, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Stir in doenjang and gochugaru, adjusting seasoning to taste.
Drop beaten eggs into the simmering stew and swirl gently.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 8 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked and drained
instructions: Soak glass noodles in warm water until soft, then drain and toss with sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Stir-fry beef, onions, carrots, mushrooms, and spinach separately in a wok.
Combine the stir-fried vegetables with the noodles in the wok.
Add soy sauce and sugar, tossing to coat evenly.
Heat through for 2-3 minutes until well mixed.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve.

title: Bibim Guksu
ingredients: 4 oz instant ramen noodles or fresh wheat noodles, cooked
instructions: Cook noodles according to package directions and drain, reserving some broth.
Toss warm noodles with sesame oil to prevent clumping.
In a small bowl, mix gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, and a splash of reserved broth to make a sauce.
Arrange noodles in a bowl and top with beef, bean sprouts, carrots, and green onions.
Drizzle the spicy sauce over the top.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately.

title: Haemul Pajeon
ingredients: 1/4 cup green onions, sliced for garnish
instructions: Mix flour, cold water, and salt until a smooth batter forms.
Stir in half of the chopped green onions.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Pour batter into the skillet, spreading it into a thin circle.
Top with shrimp, clams, squid, and the remaining green onions.
Drizzle sesame oil over the top.
Cook until the edges are golden brown, then flip and cook the other side until crisp.
Slice and serve hot with gochujang.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the white rice according to package instructions and spread on a plate to cool.
Season the beaten eggs with salt and fry sunny-side up or scramble, then slice.
Sauté spinach with a little salt and sesame oil until wilted.
Stir-fry bean sprouts, zucchini, carrots, and mushrooms separately with sesame oil and soy sauce.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, and sugar to make a sauce.
Arrange the cooked rice in a bowl and top with the vegetables, fried egg, and sauce.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on both sides.
Stir in chopped kimchi, kimchi juice, gochugaru, and soy sauce.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Add tofu, mushrooms, and green onions, simmering for 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed before serving hot.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: In a bowl, mix soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger.
Place short ribs in a pot and pour the marinade over them.
Add quartered onions and green onions to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour.
Stir in the water and cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes until the sauce is glossy and ribs are tender.
Serve over steamed white rice.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 8 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked and drained
instructions: Soak glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Season glass noodles with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Stir-fry beef slices in a pan with a little oil until browned, then remove.
In the same pan, stir-fry carrots, zucchini, and onions with sesame oil.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar in a small bowl.
Mix the cooked vegetables, beef, and glass noodles together.
Pour the sauce over the mixture, toss well, and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef ribeye or flank steak, thinly sliced
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, rice vinegar, garlic, and ginger.
Add the sliced beef to the marinade and let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the marinated beef in batches until browned and cooked through, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove beef and stir in the sliced onions until slightly softened.
Return the beef to the pan and toss to combine with the onions.
Sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup beef thinly sliced, marinated in soy sauce and sesame oil
instructions: Cook rice and spread on a large plate to cool slightly.
Arrange seasoned spinach, stir-fried zucchini, mushrooms, and carrots in separate piles on top of the rice.
Place sliced beef and egg on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle gochujang around the rim of the bowl.
Sprinkle sesame seeds and drizzle sesame oil over the top.
Serve immediately and mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add diced pork belly and cook until browned.
Stir in doenjang and gochugaru, cooking for another minute.
Add chopped napa cabbage, kimchi, and kimchi water to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and green onions in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot in a deep bowl.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 1 lb beef short ribs, cut into small pieces
instructions: Combine soy sauce, sugar, mirin, and water in a pot to make the braising liquid.
Add beef short ribs to the liquid and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until tender.
Add sliced onions, carrots, and zucchini to the pot.
Continue simmering, uncovered, for another 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Drizzle sesame oil and sprinkle sesame seeds over the finished dish.
Serve with steamed white rice.

title: Japchae
instructions: Boil sweet potato noodles according to package instructions and drain.
In a separate pan, sauté garlic, beef, and onions until beef is cooked.
Add carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, and spinach to the pan and stir-fry.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Toss the noodles with the vegetable mixture and the sauce, stirring gently.
Transfer to a serving platter and sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Sundubu Jjigae
ingredients: 1 cup kimchi water or dashi stock
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and sauté garlic and onion.
Add diced pork and cook until browned.
Stir in doenjang and gochugaru, cooking for one minute.
Pour in the stock and bring to a rolling boil.
Add chopped kimchi and bean sprouts, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Gently add cubed silken tofu to the bubbling soup.
Simmer for 2 minutes without stirring vigorously to keep the tofu soft.
Top with fresh green onions and serve immediately with rice.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice according to package instructions.
Blanch and chop the spinach.
Blanch the bean sprouts.
Stir-fry the zucchini, carrots, and mushrooms with sesame oil.
Arrange the rice in a bowl.
Top with the vegetables, egg, and sesame seeds.
Serve with a dollop of gochujang on the side.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 1 bag napa cabbage kimchi, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add pork belly and onion; cook until the pork is browned.
Add kimchi and sugar; stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in kimchi juice or water and gochugaru.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Add bean sprouts and tofu; simmer for 10 minutes.
Garnish with sliced green onion before serving.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 200g glass noodles (sweet potato starch), cooked and drained
instructions: Cook the glass noodles according to package directions and drain.
Stir-fry the beef until browned; remove from pan.
In the same pan, stir-fry carrots, zucchini, and onions until tender-crisp.
Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute.
Return beef and noodles to the pan.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar; toss to combine.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef ribeye, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
Add beef slices and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Cook the marinated beef in batches until browned and caramelized.
Add mushrooms and green onions to the skillet.
Stir-fry for another 2 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 200g fish cake slices, cut into strips
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Combine gochujang, sugar, and water in a pot; bring to a simmer.
Add the rice cakes and fish cake strips.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until rice cakes are soft.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce.
Simmer for 2 more minutes until the sauce coats the ingredients.
Remove from heat and garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (spinach, zucchini, carrots, bean sprouts), sautéed
instructions: Cook the rice according to package instructions and spread it in a bowl.
Arrange the sautéed mixed vegetables in a circle around the rice.
Place the fried egg in the center of the bowl.
Drizzle soy sauce and sesame oil over the vegetables.
Top with gochujang, sesame seeds, and chopped scallions.
Mix everything together before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: In a large pot, fry the pork belly until slightly browned.
Add chopped onion and garlic; sauté until fragrant.
Stir in kimchi, kimchi juice, and doenjang; cook for 5 minutes.
Add gochugaru, tofu, and napa cabbage; stir well.
Pour in enough water to cover ingredients and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes until flavors meld and vegetables are tender.
Garnish with green onions before serving.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 8 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked and drained
1 lb beef flank steak, sliced thin
instructions: Soak glass noodles in warm water until soft, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Stir-fry beef in a pan until cooked; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté zucchini, carrots, and bean sprouts until tender-crisp.
Return beef to the pan and add scallions.
In a bowl, mix soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar.
Add the glass noodles to the pan and toss with the sauce until coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 1 lb short ribs, trimmed and cut into pieces
instructions: In a pot, combine short ribs, onion, carrots, broth, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger.
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the soaked black beans and continue simmering for another 30 minutes.
Skim any excess fat from the surface if desired.
Serve hot in a small clay pot with a side of rice.

title: Sundubu Jjigae
ingredients: 1 lb pork or beef, sliced thin
instructions: In a pot, sauté pork or beef with onion and garlic until browned.
Add doenjang, water or broth, and kimchi; bring to a boil.
Stir in gochugaru and sesame oil.
Gently add cubed soft tofu and simmer for 5 minutes without breaking.
Sprinkle green onions and sesame seeds on top.
Serve immediately in a hot bowl, optionally with a side of rice.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup spinach, blanched and seasoned with sesame oil
instructions: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Season and blanch spinach, bean sprouts, zucchini, carrots, and mushrooms separately.
Arrange the seasoned vegetables in a circle on top of the rice in a bowl.
Place a sunny-side-up egg in the center.
Serve with a dollop of gochujang and drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle sesame seeds.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 10 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked and drained
1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced
instructions: Blanch the glass noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, then rinse with cold water and drain.
Stir-fry the beef with garlic until browned, then remove from pan.
In the same pan, stir-fry carrots, zucchini, and bean sprouts until tender-crisp.
Add spinach and red bell pepper, cooking until wilted.
Combine all vegetables, beef, and noodles in a large bowl.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil, then pour over the mixture and toss to coat.
Top with toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: In a large pot, sauté the pork belly until lightly browned.
Add the kimchi, kimchi juice, mushrooms, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar.
Pour in the water or broth and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the kimchi is very soft and the flavors meld.
Stir in the beaten eggs gently to create ribbons.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve hot.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef ribeye, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and pear puree.
Add the sliced beef to the marinade and let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the marinated beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the sliced onions and bell peppers to the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes until tender.
Remove from heat and toss with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Samgyeopsal
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly (samgyeopsal), cut into thick steaks
instructions: Preheat a Korean BBQ grill or cast-iron skillet.
Arrange the pork belly steaks on the hot grill and cook for 4-5 minutes per side until crispy and cooked through.
While the meat cooks, prepare the side dishes by mixing garlic, scallions, and sesame seeds with ssamjang.
Chop the kimchi, radish, and cucumber into bite-sized pieces.
Once the meat is done, thinly slice it.
Wrap a piece of lettuce with a slice of pork, some vegetables, and a dab of sauce to eat.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice and let it cool slightly.
Sauté the spinach, zucchini, bean sprouts, and carrots separately with a little oil and salt.
Scramble or fry the eggs to your preference.
Assemble by placing rice in a bowl and arranging the vegetables around it.
Place the fried egg on top and drizzle with sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Serve hot with a dollop of gochujang on the side or mixed in.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot and sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add sliced pork and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in kimchi and cook for 5 minutes.
Add kimchi juice, water, gochugaru, and soy sauce; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add tofu, and simmer for 10-15 minutes until flavors meld.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 tbsp pear juice or grated pear
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, pear juice, and pepper.
Toss the beef slices and carrots in the marinade and let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a skillet or grill pan over high heat.
Cook the marinated beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with sliced green onions before serving.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 8 oz glass noodles (sweet potato starch), soaked and drained
instructions: Boil glass noodles according to package instructions, drain, and rinse with cold water.
Stir-fry carrots, zucchini, and bean sprouts separately with a little oil and salt.
In a pan, stir-fry beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and vinegar until cooked.
Combine noodles, vegetables, and beef in a large bowl.
Toss everything together thoroughly with the sauce mixture.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 1 lb Korean rice cakes (tteok), cut into sticks
1/2 cup flour (mixed with water to make slurry)
instructions: Bring water, gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, and sesame oil to a simmer in a pot.
Add rice cakes and fish cakes; cook until the sauce thickens and rice cakes are soft.
Stir in the flour slurry gradually to thicken the sauce.
Add sliced green onions and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot, optionally with a raw egg cracked on top or on the side for dipping.

title: Bibim Bap
instructions: Cook the white rice and let it cool to room temperature.
In a bowl, mix gochujang, sesame oil, sugar, and soy sauce until smooth.
Add the cooked rice to the sauce and toss thoroughly to coat every grain.
Season with black sesame seeds.
Serve the spicy rice topped with fried egg, shredded carrots, cucumber, and kimchi.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 1 cup glass noodles, cooked and drained
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a heavy pot and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add the doenjang and kimchi; stir for 1 minute to release aromas.
Pour in the water or stock and bring to a boil.
Add the cabbage, radish, and pork belly; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tofu and glass noodles; cook for another 5 minutes.
Top with green onions and serve hot.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 1 lb glass noodles (sweet potato starch), cooked and drained
instructions: Cook the glass noodles according to package directions, drain well, and rinse with cold water.
Stir-fry the beef in a wok until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add sesame oil and stir-fry onions, carrots, zucchini, and mushrooms until tender-crisp.
Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute, then remove vegetables from the wok.
In a large bowl, toss the cooked noodles with soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and pepper.
Add the beef and stir-fried vegetables to the noodles; toss to combine.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and serve.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 1 lb rice cakes (tteok), cut into strips
instructions: In a pot, combine gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, water, and garlic; stir over medium heat until the sauce thickens.
Add the rice cake strips and simmer for 5 minutes until they are tender.
Stir in the fish cakes and cook for another 2 minutes until heated through.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss gently.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Gochu Gangjeong
ingredients: 1 lb beef brisket, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: In a bowl, mix gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, water, and garlic to create a marinade.
Add the beef slices to the marinade and let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Heat sesame oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove beef from marinade (reserve liquid) and sear the beef in batches until browned on both sides.
Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet; bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and simmer until the sauce thickens and coats the beef.
Stir in scallions and toasted sesame seeds, then serve immediately.

title: Bibim Bap
instructions: Mix gochujang, sesame oil, sugar, and soy sauce in a small bowl.
Add sliced scallions and sesame seeds to the sauce mixture.
Toss the cooked rice with the sauce until evenly coated.
Serve topped with the fried egg.

title: Japchae
instructions: Boil glass noodles according to package directions, then rinse in cold water.
Sauté beef and ginger in a pan until cooked.
Add carrots, onions, and bean sprouts; cook until tender-crisp.
Combine noodles with vegetables, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar.
Toss everything together and garnish with sesame seeds.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot over medium-high heat.
Add pork belly and cook until browned.
Add kimchi, gochugaru, and soy sauce; stir to combine.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add tofu, bean sprouts, and green onions; simmer for 10 minutes.

title: Dakgalbi
instructions: Marinate chicken in the gochujang mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a heavy skillet and sear the marinated chicken until cooked.
Add potatoes and carrots; cook until slightly softened.
Add onions, cabbage, and bean sprouts; stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with green onions.

title: Naengmyeon
instructions: Boil buckwheat noodles until al dente, then rinse thoroughly in ice water.
Mix beef broth, cold water, soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil in a large bowl.
Place noodles in the broth and add cucumber, kimchi, and egg halves.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve chilled.

title: Kimchi-jjigae
ingredients: 1 tbsp frozen spinach, thawed and chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until slightly browned.
Stir in kimchi, gochugaru, gochujang, and doenjang; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water or broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add spinach and glass noodles; simmer for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped green onion before serving.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup beef bulgogi or bulgogi-style beef
1 tbsp gochujang, mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Cook rice and set aside.
Stir-fry spinach, bean sprouts, zucchini, carrots, and mushrooms separately in sesame oil until tender-crisp.
Season each vegetable with a pinch of salt and sesame oil.
Arrange hot rice in a bowl and top with each vegetable in distinct sections.
Place beef bulgogi in the center of the rice.
Drizzle the gochujang mixture over the vegetables and meat.
Top with a fried egg and sprinkle sesame seeds and green onions.
Mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 200g glass noodles (sweet potato starch), cooked and drained
1/2 cup beef or pork, thinly sliced
instructions: Cook glass noodles according to package instructions; drain and rinse with cold water.
Stir-fry spinach, carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, and onions in a wok until tender.
Add sliced meat and cook until browned.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl; stir into the vegetables.
Toss in the cooked glass noodles and coat evenly.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Sundubu-jjigae
ingredients: 2 cups tofu (silken or soft), cut into cubes
1 tbsp scallion oil or sesame oil
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and sauté garlic.
Add pork belly and cook until slightly browned.
Stir in doenjang, gochugaru, and kimchi; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water or broth and bring to a boil.
Add wood ear mushrooms, napa cabbage, and tofu cubes.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the soup is hot and tofu is set but still soft.
Top with chopped green onions and serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Haemul Pajeon
instructions: Mix flour, water, sugar, and salt in a bowl until smooth; let rest for 30 minutes.
Stir in green onions, shrimp, clams, pork, and perilla leaves.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Pour batter into the skillet, spreading it thinly with a spatula.
Fry until the edges are golden and the bottom is crisp (about 3-4 minutes).
Flip carefully and cook the other side for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with ssamjang or gochujang on the side.

title: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook rice and let it cool to room temperature.
Sauté zucchini, spinach, bean sprouts, carrots, and mushrooms separately in sesame oil with salt.
Season each vegetable with a pinch of sesame oil and salt.
Cook eggs sunny-side up until whites are set but yolks are runny.
Place a bowl of rice in the center of a bowl.
Arrange the seasoned vegetables in a circle around the rice.
Place the sunny-side-up egg in the center of the vegetables.
Drizzle gochujang and sesame seeds over the top.
Mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until browned on both sides.
Stir in kimchi and cook for 2 minutes.
Add water or broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add doenjang and gochugaru, stirring to combine.
Add bean sprouts and cook for another 5 minutes until tender.
Garnish with chopped green onion before serving.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced
instructions: Soak glass noodles in warm water until soft, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat sesame oil in a wok or large skillet.
Cook beef until browned, then remove and set aside.
Add onions, carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, and spinach to the pan.
Stir-fry vegetables for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return beef to the pan.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and glass noodles.
Toss everything together over high heat for 2 minutes.
Garnish with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Galbi
instructions: In a bowl, mix soy sauce, brown sugar, pear juice, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger.
Add short ribs to the marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove ribs from marinade and let excess drip off.
Grill ribs for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Serve on a platter garnished with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
Optional: Serve with grilled vegetables and rice.

title: Tteokbokki
ingredients: 1 lb rice cakes (tteok), cylindrical or square
1 cup anchovies, soaked and blended into sauce
instructions: Soak rice cakes in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
In a large pot, mix gochujang, sugar, water, fish sauce, and blended anchovies.
Bring the sauce to a boil over medium heat.
Add the rice cakes to the sauce and stir gently.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add minced garlic and green onions in the last 2 minutes.
Cook until the sauce thickens and rice cakes are chewy.
Garnish with sesame seeds before serving hot.

title: Bibimbap (Daegu Style)
ingredients: 1 cup bean sprouts, stir-fried with garlic
3 tbsp gochujang, mixed with sesame oil and a little sugar
instructions: Cook the rice and fluff it with a fork.
Season and stir-fry each vegetable until tender-crisp.
Whisk together gochujang, sesame oil, and sugar to make the sauce.
Assemble the bowl by spreading rice at the bottom.
Arrange the vegetables in a circle around the rice.
Place the fried egg in the center.
Drizzle the gochujang sauce over the vegetables.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.
Serve immediately and mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Jorim (Braised Pork Belly)
ingredients: 500g pork belly, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Place pork strips in a pot and add water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until pork is tender.
Remove pork and set aside; keep the cooking liquid.
In a separate pot, combine the cooking liquid, soy sauce, and sugar.
Add the pork strips and simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Stir in sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Simmer for another 2 minutes until flavors meld.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Jorim (Braised Beef)
ingredients: 500g beef brisket, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Place beef strips in a pot and add water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until beef is tender.
Remove beef and set aside; keep the cooking liquid.
In a separate pot, combine the cooking liquid, soy sauce, and sugar.
Add the beef strips and simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Stir in sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Simmer for another 2 minutes until flavors meld.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood Scallion Pancake)
instructions: Mix flour, water, egg, sesame oil, and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in green onions, minced garlic, and mixed seafood.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour the batter into the skillet, spreading it evenly.
Fry until the edges are golden and the bottom is crisp.
Flip the pancake carefully and cook the other side until golden.
Slide onto a plate and cut into wedges.
Serve warm with gochujang or ssamjang on the side.

title: Sundubu Jjigae (Soft Tofu Stew)
ingredients: 1 piece dried jeotgal (salted fish), soaked and chopped
1 tbsp green onion stalks, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: In a pot, combine water, gochugaru, minced garlic, jeotgal, and soy sauce.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Add the pork belly and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Gently stir in the soft tofu cubes and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the green onion stalks and sesame oil.
Simmer until the flavors blend and the stew is bubbling gently.
Serve hot in a bowl, topped with fresh chopped green onions.
Enjoy with a side of steamed rice.

title: Gangwon-Do Samgyetang (Ginseng Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 1 whole young chicken, cleaned and stuffed with ginseng, jujube, glutinous rice, and salted egg yolk
instructions: Place the stuffed chicken into a large pot with the water.
Add the soaked ginseng, jujube slices, and goji berries.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a low simmer.
Skim off any foam that rises to the top for the first 10 minutes.
Simmer uncovered for 3 to 4 hours until the chicken is tender and the broth is clear.
Season with salt to taste and garnish with green onion before serving.

title: Jeonju-style Kimchi Jjigae
ingredients: 4 cups water or watered-down kimchi juice
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced pork and cook until browned on both sides.
Stir in the chopped kimchi and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the doenjang and gochugaru, stirring well to combine.
Pour in the water or kimchi juice and bring to a boil.
Add the soaked glass noodles and green onions.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the noodles are cooked and the soup is rich.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Bindaetteok (Mung Bean Pancake)
ingredients: 1 cup dried mung beans, soaked for 4 hours
instructions: Blend the soaked mung beans with enough water to make a smooth, thick puree.
Squeeze out excess water from the puree using a cheesecloth or sieve.
Mix the bean puree with sweet potato starch, green onion, garlic, and salt.
Heat a thin layer of cooking oil in a hot skillet over medium heat.
Spoon portions of the batter onto the skillet and spread into small circles.
