Fry until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip the pancakes and cook the other side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and drizzle with sesame oil before serving.

title: Dongduki (Sliced Beef with Scallion Oil)
ingredients: 1 pound beef brisket, thinly sliced against the grain
1 bunch green onions, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Marinate the sliced beef with soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and black pepper for 30 minutes.
In a separate pan, fry green onions in cooking oil until they turn a deep golden brown.
Remove the fried onions and set aside, keeping the oil.
Heat the reserved oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Toss in the marinated beef and stir-fry quickly for 2-3 minutes.
Add the fried green onions back into the wok.
Toss everything together for 30 seconds until the beef is cooked but still tender.
Serve immediately as a side dish with rice.

title: Gangwon-Do Bibimbap with Okdureu
ingredients: 2 tablespoons gochujang (mixed with a little sesame oil and water)
instructions: Prepare the seasoned vegetables (spinach, zucchini, carrots, bean sprouts) ahead of time.
Cook the rice and spread it on a platter to cool slightly.
Arrange the beef bulgogi in the center of the rice.
Place a line of each seasoned vegetable around the beef in the center.
Place the fried egg on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle the gochujang mixture over the entire bowl.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top.
Serve immediately, allowing the diner to mix everything together.

title: Galbitang (Sliced Pork Rib Soup)
ingredients: 2 lbs pork belly ribs, cleaned and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 napa cabbage, cut into large chunks
instructions: Place ribs, carrots, cabbage, onion, kelp, and dried shrimp in a large pot.
Add 8 cups of cold water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours until the ribs are tender.
Season with salt and serve hot with chopped green onions on top.

title: Miyun-namul (Sautéed Water Spinach)
ingredients: 4 cups water spinach (mireukcho), washed and trimmed
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the water spinach for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat sesame oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the blanched spinach to the pan and toss quickly for 30 seconds.
Stir in soy sauce, salt, sugar, and pepper.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Gukbap (Rice Soup with Meat and Vegetables)
ingredients: Garnish: sesame seeds and chili powder
instructions: Combine rinsed rice and broth in a pot and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce heat and simmer until rice is cooked and soup is slightly thickened.
Add sliced beef, bean sprouts, and spinach to the soup.
Simmer for another 3 minutes until spinach wilts and beef is heated through.
Stir in sesame oil and salt, then serve topped with green onions, sesame seeds, and chili powder.

title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)
ingredients: 4 oz beef brisket, thinly sliced and stir-fried with garlic
1/2 cup bean sprouts, seasoned and sautéed
instructions: Spread cooked rice evenly into a shallow bowl.
Arrange sautéed beef, spinach, bean sprouts, and zucchini in separate sections around the rice.
Top with a fried egg and drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve with a side dish of gochujang for dipping.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly before eating.

title: Jorim Dak (Braised Chicken with Soy Sauce)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Place chicken pieces in a pot and add soy sauce, sugar, mirin, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and let the chicken cool slightly in the sauce.
Toss with sesame oil before serving.

title: Kimchi Jjigae (Daejeon Style)
ingredients: 1 head Napa cabbage, chopped into chunks
instructions: Sauté sliced onion and garlic in sesame oil until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook until the edges are slightly browned.
Stir in the chopped kimchi and gochugaru, cooking for 3 minutes.
Pour in the pork bone broth and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the cabbage chunks and pork liver, reducing heat to simmer.
Cook until the cabbage is tender and the flavors have melded, about 15 minutes.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Daejeon-style Fried Chicken (Gokdang Style)
ingredients: 1 cup flour for coating the outside
1/2 cup cornstarch for coating the outside
Soy sauce and vinegar for dipping
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces in cold water with salt and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Mix flour, cornstarch, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the drained chicken pieces in the flour mixture to coat evenly.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and let cool slightly.
Coat cooled chicken with a second layer of flour, cornstarch, salt, and pepper.
Fry again until crispy and golden, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve immediately with soy sauce and vinegar dipping sauce.

title: Bibimbap (Home Style)
instructions: Cook rice and set aside to cool.
Sauté garlic in sesame oil, then add spinach and cook until wilted; season with salt.
Blanch carrots, mushrooms, bean sprouts, and zucchini separately in boiling water, then cool.
Fry the egg sunny-side up and slice in half.
Arrange rice in a bowl, topped with vegetables in sections.
Place the fried egg on top.
Add a dollop of gochujang in the center.
Drizzle with a little soy sauce and sprinkle sesame seeds.
Serve immediately and mix thoroughly before eating.

title: Bindaetteok (Mung Bean Pancakes)
instructions: Mix mung bean flour, salt, and water to form a smooth, thick batter.
Sauté grated radish with minced garlic in sesame oil until soft, then cool.
Fold the radish mixture and chopped scallions into the batter.
Heat a small amount of oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Spoon batter onto the skillet, spreading it into small round pancakes.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook the other side until golden.
Remove from pan and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with gochujang and ssam leaves.

title: Jjapaguk (Stuffed Rice Soup)
ingredients: 1/2 cup squid, chopped into small pieces
instructions: Combine rice, water, salted shrimp, squid, pork, mushrooms, sesame oil, pepper, salt, and sugar in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover tightly.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the rice absorbs the liquid and becomes soft and sticky.
Stir gently to combine all ingredients into a porridge-like consistency.
If desired, top with a raw beaten egg yolk before serving.
Garnish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve hot in individual bowls.

title: Bibimbap
ingredients: 4 cups mixed vegetables (spinach, zucchini, carrots, bean sprouts, mushrooms), seasoned with gochugaru and sesame oil
instructions: Cook the rice and fluff it with a fork.
Season and sauté the mixed vegetables separately.
Arrange the rice in a bowl, top with vegetables in a circular pattern.
Place the fried egg on top.
Serve with gochujang, sesame oil, and sesame seeds on the side.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the onion and pork belly until browned.
Add the kimchi, kimchi juice, and broth; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the beaten egg to create ribbons.
Top with chopped green onion and serve hot.

title: Galbi Jjim
ingredients: 500g beef short ribs, marinated in soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and sesame oil
instructions: Place the marinated ribs in a pot and add the carrot, onion, and bean sprouts.
Add sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and gochugaru.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer for another 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Serve with the sauce poured over the meat and vegetables.

title: Japchae
instructions: Boil the glass noodles until al dente, then rinse with cold water and drain.
Stir-fry the beef with half the sesame oil and soy sauce until browned; set aside.
Stir-fry the vegetables with the remaining oil until tender-crisp.
Combine the noodles, beef, and vegetables in a large bowl.
Toss with sugar and sesame seeds, then mix well before serving.

title: Bulgogi
instructions: Mix soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Add the sliced beef and toss to coat evenly; let marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or skillet over high heat.
Cook the beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until caramelized.
Garnish with chopped green onion and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Jjigae-baegi Bibimbap
ingredients: 3 cups mixed vegetables (spinach, zucchini, carrots, onions)
instructions: Cook rice and set aside to cool slightly.
Sauté each vegetable separately with a little oil and salt until tender.
Mix gochujang, minced garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil to make the sauce.
Place a mound of rice in a bowl and arrange the cooked vegetables in a circle around it.
Add the chopped kimchi on top of the vegetables.
Crack the sunny-side-up egg over the center of the rice.
Drizzle the gochujang sauce over everything and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Eat immediately, mixing all ingredients together.

title: Bulgogi
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
1/4 cup pear juice or grated Asian pear
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, pear juice, and pepper.
Add the sliced beef to the marinade and mix well, covering and refrigerating for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add the marinated beef in batches without overcrowding, stirring quickly for 2-3 minutes until caramelized.
Remove beef and set aside on a plate.
Return the beef to the pan, add the chopped green onion, and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve immediately over a bed of steamed white rice.

title: Dakgangjeong
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 cups sweet and sour sauce (made from sugar, vinegar, ketchup, water, and ginger)
instructions: Toss chicken pieces in cornstarch until lightly coated and let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pot or wok to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the chicken in batches until golden brown and crispy, then remove and drain on paper towels.
In a small saucepan, simmer the sweet and sour sauce until slightly thickened.
Return the fried chicken to the pan with the sauce, tossing quickly to coat evenly.
Add the green onions and dried shrimp if using, and toss for another minute.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Miyeok-guk
ingredients: 200g dried sea vegetables (miyeok), soaked and cleaned
instructions: Soak the dried sea vegetables in water for 30 minutes, rinse, and cut into small pieces.
Boil the baby squid until it curls, then add the sea vegetables and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the sliced daikon and bean sprouts, and cook until tender.
Season with soy sauce, sesame oil, and gochugaru to taste.
Ladle the soup into bowls containing a scoop of rice.
Top with chopped green onions.
Serve with a small bowl of beaten egg on the side for dipping.

title: Japchae
ingredients: 1 pack of glass noodles (sweet potato starch), cooked and drained
1/4 cup spinach, blanched and squeezed dry
instructions: Cook the glass noodles in boiling water until tender, drain, and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
In a large pan, stir-fry the beef with half the sesame oil and season with pepper until browned; remove from pan.
Add onions, carrots, and mushrooms to the same pan and stir-fry until softened.
Return the beef to the pan and add the cooked noodles, spinach, and green onions.
Mix in the soy sauce, sugar, and remaining sesame oil until well combined and glossy.
Toss everything together over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

title: Jeonju Bibimbap
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (spinach, bean sprouts, zucchini, carrots, mushrooms)
instructions: Steam the rice and spread it evenly onto a serving bowl.
Sauté each vegetable separately with garlic and salt, then arrange them in a circle on top of the rice.
Place the sunny-side-up egg in the center of the bowl.
Drizzle gochujang, a mix of soy sauce and sesame oil, and sesame seeds over the vegetables.
Top with pine nuts and serve immediately.

title: Gochujang Jeon (Chili Pancakes)
ingredients: 1/2 cup glass noodles, soaked and cut
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, salt, and gochujang in a bowl.
Add water and egg to the flour mixture, stirring until smooth.
Fold in glass noodles, green onions, and kimchi.
Heat oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour batter into the skillet, spreading it into a thin circle.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

title: Samgyetang (Ginseng Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 1 whole young chicken, cleaned and stuffed
instructions: Stuff the chicken cavity with glutinous rice, ginseng slices, garlic, and jujube.
Place the stuffed chicken in a large pot and cover with chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 to 3 hours.
Skim any foam that rises to the top during the first 30 minutes.
Add salt to taste near the end of cooking.
Garnish with chopped green onions and drizzle with sesame oil before serving.

title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
instructions: In a heavy pot, sauté pork and beef with sesame oil until browned.
Add kimchi, kimchi juice, gochugaru, sugar, and salt; stir well.
Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes to meld the flavors.
Add mushrooms and tofu, then simmer for another 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped green onions and serve piping hot.

title: Bindaetteok (Mung Bean Pancakes)
ingredients: 1/2 cup glass noodles, soaked and cut
instructions: Mix mung bean flour, water, and salt to form a smooth, thick batter.
Stir in glass noodles, green onions, onion, and pepper.
Heat sesame oil and vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Pour small dollops of batter into the skillet, flattening them with a spatula.
Fry until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, about 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and fry the other side until crispy.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and cut into wedges.

title: Jeju Kimchi (Jeju-style)
ingredients: 2 tbsp jeju sea salted shrimp, mashed
instructions: Soak halved Napa cabbage in salted water for 2 hours, then rinse thoroughly to remove excess salt.
Mix cooked glutinous rice, fish sauce, sugar, green onions, garlic, and mashed shrimp to make the seasoning paste.
Layer the drained cabbage with julienned radish, then generously spread the seasoning paste between the leaves.
Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down to release air, and seal tightly.
Ferment in a cool place for 3 to 5 days until the cabbage becomes soft and sour.

title: Gogi-jeon (Vegetable Pancakes)
ingredients: 1 kg mixed vegetables (cabbage, carrots, radish, green onions), finely chopped
2 tbsp jeju sea salted shrimp, minced
instructions: Mix chopped vegetables, minced sea salted shrimp, and half of the sliced green onions in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, water, eggs, and the remaining green onions to form a thick batter.
Pour the batter over the vegetable mixture and stir gently until just combined.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon batter into the skillet, spreading it into round pancakes, and fry until golden brown on both sides.

title: Jang-keun (Jeju Fermented Soybean Paste)
ingredients: 100 g jeju sea salted shrimp, mashed
instructions: Steam the soaked soybeans and barley separately until fully cooked, then let them cool completely.
Grind the cooked soybeans and barley into a fine paste using a traditional stone mill or grinder.
Mix the ground paste with water, sea salt, mashed sea salted shrimp, and red pepper powder.
Pack the mixture tightly into a large earthenware jar (onggi) to remove all air pockets.
Seal the jar and let it ferment in a warm, dark place for 2 to 3 weeks until the aroma develops.

title: Gukbap (Rice Soup with Pork and Vegetables)
instructions: Cook the rice in a pot with water until it is soft and slightly mushy.
Add sliced pork belly to the rice and cook until the fat renders and the meat is tender.
Stir in chopped kimchi, bean sprouts, and blanched spinach, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Drizzle sesame oil and add minced garlic and sugar to enhance the flavor.
Swirl the beaten egg into the hot soup to create ribbons and serve immediately.

title: Bap-saeng (Salty Rice Cake)
ingredients: 1/2 cup jeju sea salted shrimp, minced
instructions: Mix rice flour, sea salt, and water in a bowl to form a smooth, stiff dough.
Knead the dough until it is elastic and no longer sticky to your hands.
Steam the dough in a steamer lined with a clean cloth for 30 minutes until cooked through.
While steaming, mix chopped green onions, minced sea salted shrimp, spinach, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Cut the steamed dough into small squares and coat each piece with the seasoned vegetable mixture before serving.

title: Bibim Guksu (Mixed Cold Noodles)
instructions: Cook buckwheat noodles according to package instructions, then rinse in cold water and drain.
In a bowl, mix doenjang, gochugaru, sesame oil, garlic, and vinegar to make the base sauce.
Add green onions and grated pear to the sauce and stir well.
Place cooled noodles in a serving bowl and pour the sauce over them.
Top with sliced egg, shredded cucumber, and a drizzle of sesame oil before serving.

title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
ingredients: 200g rice cakes (tteok), cut in half lengthwise
instructions: In a pot, combine water, gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil; simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the rice cakes to the sauce and cook for 5 minutes, turning occasionally to coat evenly.
Add the sliced fish cakes and cook for another 3-4 minutes until they are heated through.
Garnish with chopped green onions just before serving.

title: Jokbal (Pork Stomach Stew)
ingredients: 500g pork stomach, cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Fry the pork stomach pieces in sesame oil until lightly browned on both sides.
Add sliced onions and minced garlic to the pot and sauté until soft.
Stir in doenjang, water, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Garnish with chopped green onions and sesame seeds before serving.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood Scallion Pancake)
instructions: Mix flour, water, salt, sugar, and one green onion in a bowl to form a smooth batter.
Stir in the mixed seafood and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour the batter into the pan, spreading it evenly to a thin layer.
Cook until the bottom is golden brown, flip carefully, add a little more oil, and cook the other side until crispy.
Cut into wedges and serve warm.

title: Gomtang (Bonesoup)
ingredients: 1 kg beef bones, chopped and blanched
instructions: Place the blanched beef bones in a large pot and add water to cover.
Add carrots, parsnips, and onion to the pot.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3-4 hours until the broth is milky white and rich.
Season with salt and gochugaru if desired, then garnish with green onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.

title: Japchae (Stir-fried Glass Noodles)
ingredients: 16 oz sweet potato starch noodles, soaked and drained
1 cup mixed vegetables (carrots, spinach, onions, zucchini, mushrooms)
instructions: Blanch the sweet potato noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, then rinse with cold water and set aside.
Stir-fry the sliced beef in a wok with a little oil until cooked through, then remove.
Toss the vegetables in the wok until slightly tender-crisp.
Combine the noodles, beef, and vegetables in the wok.
Add sesame oil, soy sauce, and sugar, tossing quickly over high heat until glossy and coated.
Serve hot, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds.

title: Godeunaguk (Dried Scallop Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb dried scallops, soaked overnight until soft
instructions: Sauté the onions in a pot until translucent.
Add the rehydrated scallops and pour in the soaking water along with fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu and glass noodles, cooking until noodles are tender.
Stir in gochugaru, chopped green onions, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately as a comforting soup.

title: Gamjatang (Pork Bone Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs pork trotters, cleaned and cut into large pieces
1 bunch green onions, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Blanch the pork trotters in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities, then drain.
In a heavy pot, sauté onions and carrots in sesame oil until fragrant.
Add the blanched trotters, potatoes, and water.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Stir in gochugaru and cook for another 20 minutes to develop flavor.
Remove from heat, add chopped green onions, and serve with ssam (lettuce wraps).

title: Sundubu Jjigae (Silken Tofu Stew)
ingredients: 1 block soft silken tofu, cut into cubes
1 lb seafood (clams, shrimp, and squid), cleaned
instructions: Bring water, doenjang, gochugaru, and garlic to a simmer in a stone pot or deep pan.
Add the kimchi and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the seafood and cook until they change color.
Gently pour the cubed silken tofu into the stew without breaking it.
Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes until the broth thickens and tofu is warm.
Top with sliced green onions and serve with rice.

title: Naengmyeon (Cold Buckwheat Noodles)
ingredients: 16 oz buckwheat noodles (kalguksu or instant naengmyeon)
1 cup beef or chicken broth, chilled
1 slice of raw beef, thinly cut
instructions: Cook the buckwheat noodles according to package instructions, then rinse thoroughly in ice water.
Combine chilled broth, vinegar, sesame oil, and gochugaru in a large bowl.
Add the cold noodles to the broth and toss to coat.
Top with julienned cucumber, radish, green onions, sliced egg, and raw beef.
Serve immediately with a side of sliced radish and green onions for extra crunch.

title: Gwangju-style Daejanggori (Spicy Stir-fried Pork and Tofu)
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, cut into cubes
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant for 30 seconds.
Add sliced pork belly and stir-fry until the edges are browned.
Add tofu cubes and stir gently to coat.
Mix gochujang and soy sauce in a small bowl, then pour over the meat and tofu.
Stir continuously for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats everything evenly.
Garnish with chopped green onion and serve hot.

title: Gwangju Gukbap (Rice Porridge with Pork and Egg)
ingredients: 1 bunch green onions, white parts chopped, green parts reserved
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain.
In a large pot, sauté minced garlic in sesame oil until fragrant.
Add chopped white parts of green onions and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice, water, and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until rice is soft and porridge forms.
Add sliced pork belly and simmer for another 10 minutes until pork is cooked through.
Pour beaten egg slowly around the edge to create ribbons.
Garnish with reserved green parts of green onions and serve.

title: Jorim Namul (Braised Bean Sprouts)
instructions: Wash bean sprouts thoroughly and drain well.
In a small pan, combine soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and water.
Bring the sauce to a boil over medium heat.
Add the bean sprouts and toss to coat evenly.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sprouts are tender-crisp.
Remove from heat and drizzle sesame oil over the top.
Garnish with sliced green onion and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Jokbal (Pork Trotters)
ingredients: 1 lb pork trotters, cleaned and trimmed
instructions: Place cleaned pork trotters in a pot with onion, garlic, and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until tender.
Drain the trotters and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the trotters in sesame oil until golden brown.
Add soy sauce, gochugaru, and 1 cup of water; mix well.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Garnish with chopped green onion and serve with rice.

title: Japchae (Stir-fried Glass Noodles)
instructions: Cook sweet potato noodles in boiling water for 8 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Toss noodles lightly with sesame oil to prevent sticking.
In a hot pan, stir-fry beef until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté spinach and bean sprouts for 2 minutes.
Add noodles, beef, and green onions back into the pan.
Mix soy sauce and sugar, pour over the noodles, and toss for 3 minutes until coated and heated through.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately.

title: Daejeon-style Braised Pork Belly (Dongchae-jorim)
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into 2-inch cubes
1 cup dried mustard greens (dongchae), soaked and cut into 2-inch strips
instructions: Blanch pork cubes in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
In a large pot, combine pork, water, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, gochugaru, and sugar.
Simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until pork is tender.
Add the prepared dongchae and cook for another 10 minutes.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle sesame seeds, and serve hot.

title: Spicy Stir-fried Squid (Jjimdak-style or Seafood variation)
ingredients: 500 g fresh squid, cleaned and cut into rings
instructions: Marinate squid rings in 1 tablespoon soy sauce for 10 minutes.
In a large pot, sauté onion and garlic in sesame oil until fragrant.
Add the marinated squid and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in stock, water, remaining soy sauce, gochugaru, and sugar.
Simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens, garnish with green onions.

title: Daejeon Braised Beef Short Ribs (Bulgogi-jorim style)
ingredients: 1 kg beef short ribs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Season beef with half the soy sauce and brown sugar, then sear in a pan.
Transfer beef to a pot and add broth, water, onion, garlic, and remaining soy sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Stir in gochugaru and sesame oil, cooking uncovered for 10 minutes to reduce sauce.
Garnish with green onions and serve with rice.

title: Homemade Daejeon-style Kimchi (Baechu Kimchi)
ingredients: 1 bunch mustard greens, soaked and shredded
instructions: Salt the cabbage and radish separately, then soak them in cold water for 2 hours to remove excess salt.
Rinse thoroughly and squeeze out all water from vegetables.
Mix gochugaru, garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar, and shrimp paste into a paste.
Spread the paste evenly on the cabbage and radish, packing tightly.
Layer the vegetables in a jar, cover, and ferment for 2-3 days at room temperature.

title: Steamed Rice Cakes with Sesame (Tteok)
instructions: Mix rice flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl, then gradually add water while stirring.
Cook the mixture over medium heat in a non-stick pan, stirring constantly until it pulls away from the sides.
Transfer the dough to a greased bowl, knead briefly, and let cool.
Cut the dough into small cubes and place in a steamer.
Steam for 15 minutes until firm, then toss with sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds.

title: Bibim Guksu (Spicy Mixed Noodles)
instructions: Cook buckwheat noodles according to package directions and drain well.
In a small bowl, mix gochujang, minced garlic, sugar, soy sauce, and vinegar to make the sauce.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked noodles, julienned carrots, and julienned cucumber.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and toss gently to coat evenly.
Top with sliced hard-boiled eggs, sesame seeds, and sliced scallions.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately.

title: Kimchi Jjigae (Spicy Kimchi Stew)
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add sliced pork, onion, and garlic; stir-fry until the pork is browned.
Add chopped kimchi and gochugaru; stir-fry for 2 minutes to release flavors.
Pour in water or kimchi juice and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add tofu cubes and simmer for another 5 minutes until the broth thickens.
Stir in soy sauce, garnish with chopped green onion, and serve hot with rice.

title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
ingredients: 200g cylindrical rice cakes (tteok), cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 cup granulated sugar (if using less in paste)
instructions: In a saucepan, combine water, gochujang, soy sauce, and sugar; stir until the sugar dissolves.
Bring the sauce to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the cut rice cakes and sliced fish cakes to the simmering sauce.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5-7 minutes until the rice cakes are soft and the sauce thickens.
Stir in minced garlic and sesame oil during the last minute of cooking.
Remove from heat, garnish with chopped green onions and sesame seeds, and serve immediately.

title: Jorim Bulgogi (Braised Beef)
ingredients: 300g thinly sliced beef brisket or flank steak
instructions: In a bowl, mix soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger to create the marinade.
Toss the sliced beef in the marinade and let it sit for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a wok or skillet over high heat and add a little oil.
Remove beef from marinade and sear quickly on both sides until browned; remove beef and set aside.
Add onions and carrots to the same pan; stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
Return the beef to the pan, add the remaining water, and cover to simmer for 5 minutes.
Uncover, increase heat to reduce the sauce until it glazes the meat.
Drizzle with extra sesame oil, sprinkle with black sesame seeds, and serve.

title: Japchae (Stir-Fried Glass Noodles)
instructions: Cook the sweet potato noodles in boiling water until tender, then rinse thoroughly in cold water and drain well.
In a large bowl, toss the cooked noodles with soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil until evenly coated.
Heat a large wok over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Add beef (if using) and cook until browned; remove and set aside.
Add mushrooms and carrots to the wok; stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add spinach and stir-fry for another minute until wilted.
Return the noodles and beef to the wok, add minced garlic, and toss everything together vigorously for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a serving platter, drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and julienned scallions, and serve.

title: Jjimdak (Bibim Dakgalbi)
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Combine chicken, gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Add green onions and red pepper, cooking until chicken is tender and sauce thickens.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.
Serve with steamed white rice.

title: Haemul Pajeon (Seafood Scallion Pancake)
ingredients: 1 tbsp dried clams (haemul), soaked and drained
instructions: Mix flour, egg, and ice water until smooth; let rest for 10 minutes.
Stir in green onions, clams, shrimp, and dried clams gently.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour batter into the pan, spreading it evenly with a spatula.
Cook until golden brown on one side, flip, and cook until crisp on the other.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

title: Sundubu Jjigae (Soft Tofu Stew)
ingredients: 2 blocks soft tofu (sundubu), cut into cubes
1/2 cup green onion, cut into 2-inch lengths
instructions: Heat doenjang, water, gochugaru, garlic, and ginger in a pot until boiling.
Add pork belly and cook until slightly browned.
Add squid and simmer for 3 minutes.
Gently fold in tofu cubes and cook for 2 minutes without breaking.
Top with green onions and serve hot in a stone bowl.

title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)
ingredients: 1/2 cup spinach, blanched and seasoned with garlic and sesame oil
instructions: Cook rice and keep warm.
Season and blanch spinach, bean sprouts, zucchini, carrots, and mushrooms separately.
Arrange rice in a bowl and layer vegetables around it.
Place a fried egg on top and drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve with a side of gochujang for dipping.
Mix everything together before eating.

title: Japchae (Glass Noodle Stir-fry)
ingredients: 1/2 cup green onion, cut into 2-inch lengths
instructions: Soak noodles in warm water until soft, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Toss noodles with half the soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Stir-fry beef until browned, then remove from pan.
Stir-fry vegetables separately until tender-crisp.
Combine noodles, beef, and vegetables in a large bowl.
Drizzle remaining sauce and sesame oil, toss well, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Bibim Guksu (Spicy Cold Noodles)
ingredients: 200g buckwheat noodles, cooked and rinsed in cold water
instructions: Cook buckwheat noodles according to package instructions and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Whisk together gochujang, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Place noodles in a large bowl and pour the sauce over them, tossing well to coat.
Arrange the sliced beef, cucumber, green onion, and egg around the noodles.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top and serve chilled.

title: Gochujang-jorim Galbi (Spicy Braised Short Ribs)
ingredients: 500g beef short ribs, cut into small pieces
instructions: Season the beef ribs with salt and pepper, then sear them in a pan until browned on all sides.
In a separate bowl, mix gochujang, soy sauce, pear juice, sesame oil, garlic, sugar, and water.
Pour the sauce over the seared ribs in the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the chopped green onion just before serving.

title: Jeonju Mandu (Jeonju-Style Dumplings)
ingredients: 200g napa cabbage, finely chopped and salted
instructions: Drain the salted napa cabbage well and mix with minced pork, garlic, green onion, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar.
Add sesame oil and sesame seeds to the filling and mix thoroughly.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of a dumpling wrapper.
Fold the wrapper in half and pinch the edges tightly to seal, creating a half-moon shape.
Boil the dumplings for 5-7 minutes until they float and the dough is cooked through.

title: Gamja-guksu (Potato Noodles)
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
instructions: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for about 20 minutes until soft, then drain.
While potatoes are hot, beat the eggs and gently stir them into the potatoes.
Add minced garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, and sugar to the mixture and mix well.
Heat cooking oil in a large wok and fry the potato mixture, stirring constantly until it forms small noodle-like strands.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped green onions.

title: Dakgangjeong (Sweet and Spicy Fried Chicken)
ingredients: 1 kg chicken wings and drumettes, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Mix flour, cornstarch, and baking powder in one bowl.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, gochugaru, and garlic in another bowl to make the marinade.
Toss the chicken pieces in the marinade and let sit for 30 minutes.
Dredge the marinated chicken in the flour mixture until coated.
Deep fry the chicken in hot oil until golden brown and crispy, then toss in the remaining sauce if any and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Jeju Black Pork Bulgogi
ingredients: 1.5 lbs Jeju black pork, thinly sliced
instructions: Marinate the pork slices with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger for at least 2 hours.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Add the marinated pork in a single layer and sear quickly without stirring constantly.
Toss in green onions and sesame seeds during the last 30 seconds.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Ssam (Korean Lettuce Wraps)
ingredients: 1 bunch Napa cabbage leaves, washed and dried
instructions: Boil the cabbage leaves in water with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes until tender.
Immediately transfer leaves to an ice bath to crisp them up.
Whisk together gochujang, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic for the dipping sauce.
Season the leaves lightly with salt if desired.
Serve the leaves alongside the sauce for wrapping meat.

title: Jeju Black Pork Galbi
ingredients: 1 lb Jeju black pork ribs, trimmed
instructions: Combine pear juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Add the pork ribs to the marinade and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the ribs for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Garnish with green onions before serving.

title: Chamchi-jjim (Braised Spinach)
ingredients: 1 bunch spinach, washed and stems removed
instructions: Steam the spinach leaves for 3 minutes until wilted, then drain well.
In a pot, combine beef broth, doenjang, soy sauce, sugar, gochugaru, and minced garlic.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then add the spinach leaves.
Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until the liquid reduces and coats the spinach.
Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and garnish with green onions.

title: Kimchi-jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb fermented napa cabbage kimchi, chopped
1/2 cup pork bone broth or water
instructions: Sauté the sliced pork and chopped onion in sesame oil until the pork is browned.
Add the doenjang and gochugaru to the pot and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the kimchi juice, pork broth, and the chopped kimchi.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and glass noodles if using, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot in a bowl topped with chopped green onions.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh
ingredients: 1 lb fine bulgur wheat, soaked in ice water for 30 minutes
instructions: Drain the soaked bulgur thoroughly and pat dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine the ground lamb, drained bulgur, minced onion, garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Mix all ingredients together by hand until the mixture is uniform and sticky.
Divide the mixture into small balls or shape into patties as desired.
Serve immediately chilled.

title: Knafeh
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer knafeh sheets in a greased baking dish, brushing each layer with melted butter.
Sprinkle a layer of semolina cheese over the pastry, then repeat layers until the dish is full.
Top with a final layer of cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
While baking, mix powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla to make a syrup.
Let the knafeh cool slightly, then pour the warm syrup over the top.
Garnish with chopped pistachios before serving.

title: Shawarma Platter
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh meat, sliced thinly
instructions: In a bowl, combine olive oil, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, pepper, and salt.
Coat the sliced chicken with the spice mixture and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat a skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken in batches until fully cooked and slightly charred, about 5-7 minutes.
Warm the pita breads in a dry pan or oven.
Assemble the shawarma by spreading tahini sauce on the pita.
Layer the cooked chicken, lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and pickles on the pita.
Fold the pita and serve.

title: Baba Ghanoush
ingredients: 1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
instructions: Pierce the eggplants with a fork and roast them directly over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft, about 30-40 minutes.
Peel the charred skin off the eggplants and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the eggplant flesh with a fork until smooth.
Mince the garlic and add it to the eggplant along with olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, mint, cumin, and salt.
Mix everything together until well combined.
Drizzle with a little more olive oil and top with toasted pine nuts.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Lamb Kofta with Tahini
instructions: In a bowl, combine ground lamb, bulgur, grated onion, garlic, parsley, allspice, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Mix well with your hands until the ingredients are fully incorporated.
Form the mixture into small oval-shaped koftas.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the koftas, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 10 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk together tahini, warm water, and lemon juice to make a smooth sauce.
Serve the koftas warm with the tahini sauce on the side.

title: Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, boneless and skinless
instructions: Whisk together yogurt, garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, pepper, and olive oil in a bowl.
Add chicken thighs to the marinade and let sit for at least 2 hours.
Thread chicken onto a vertical rotisserie spit or skewers.
Cook over high heat, rotating frequently until chicken is golden and cooked through.
Slice the cooked chicken thinly.
Warm pita bread and stuff with chicken, lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and onion.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin in a food processor.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the processor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil.
Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the hummus reaches a creamy, dip-consistency.
Taste and add salt if necessary.
Transfer to a bowl, shape the top, and drizzle with olive oil.
Serve immediately with pita bread.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur wheat in beef or lamb broth for 1 hour, then drain well.
Mix ground lamb, soaked bulgur, onion, pine nuts, herbs, spices, and salt in a large bowl.
Knead the mixture thoroughly by hand until it forms a firm, cohesive ball.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Shape the chilled mixture into small balls or patties.
Fry in olive oil over medium heat until golden brown on all sides.
Serve warm as an appetizer.

title: Baba Ghanoush
instructions: Poke holes in eggplants and roast whole over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred and flesh is soft.
Peel the charred skin off and scoop out the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the eggplant flesh until smooth.
Add tahini, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, cumin, and salt.
Mix well until a creamy consistency is achieved.
Stir in chopped parsley.
Serve with pita bread.

title: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place baguette chunks on a baking sheet and toast until golden and crisp.
In a large bowl, combine cucumber, tomato, onion, parsley, mint, and radishes.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, oregano, and salt to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Top with the toasted bread pieces just before serving.
Serve immediately.

title: Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss chicken strips with the marinade and let sit for 1 hour.
Heat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken strips until golden brown and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Warm pita breads on the grill or in a toaster.
Spread tahini sauce on each pita.
Layer chicken, sliced onions, and pickles onto the pitas.
Roll tightly and serve immediately.

title: Hummus
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin in a food processor.
Process until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil until creamy.
Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish with paprika if desired.

title: Lamb Kofta
instructions: Combine ground lamb, onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice, salt, pepper, parsley, mint, and breadcrumbs in a bowl.
Mix thoroughly with clean hands until well combined.
Shape the mixture into small oval patties or logs.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook kofta for 3-4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with pita bread and yogurt sauce.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 4 pieces pita bread, torn into chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss pita chunks with 1 tablespoon olive oil and spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 10 minutes until crispy and golden.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce, cucumber, tomato, radishes, parsley, and mint.
Whisk together remaining olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, sumac, and salt.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently.
Add roasted pita pieces and toss again.
Serve immediately.

title: Baba Ganoush
instructions: Pierce eggplants with a fork and roast directly over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred and flesh is soft, about 30-40 minutes.
Peel the charred skin off and scoop out the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the eggplant flesh with a fork or potato masher.
Add garlic, tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt to the bowl.
Mix well until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Transfer to a serving dish, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika and parsley.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Combine lentils, rice, salt, pepper, and 3 cups water in a pot; bring to a boil, then simmer until tender and water is absorbed.
Heat olive oil in a separate pan; cook onions over medium heat until caramelized and soft, about 20 minutes.
Add minced garlic to onions and cook for 1 more minute.
Mix the cooked rice-lentil mixture with the onion-garlic mixture and serve hot.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned and drained
instructions: Combine chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a food processor.
Process until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, slowly drizzle in the remaining olive oil until the mixture is creamy.
Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
Transfer to a bowl, shape the top, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain and mix with onions, pine nuts, garlic, flour, spices, and salt.
In a large bowl, combine the meat mixture with the bulgur mixture.
Divide the mixture into small portions and shape into small balls or cones.
Fry the kibbeh in olive oil over medium heat until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve hot with yogurt and pickles.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brush the bottom of a baking dish with half of the melted butter.
Layer 10 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with butter, then sprinkle with half the nuts.
Repeat with another 10 sheets of dough and the remaining nuts.
Top with the final 10 sheets of dough, brushing each with butter.
Score the top into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through.
Pour the remaining butter over the top and bake for 45 minutes until golden.
While baking, mix sugar, water, honey, and cinnamon in a saucepan; boil for 5 minutes to make a syrup.
Pour the hot syrup over the hot baklava immediately after baking and let cool completely before cutting.

title: Shawarma Wrap
instructions: In a bowl, mix olive oil, cumin, paprika, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Coat the chicken slices with the spice mixture and marinate for 30 minutes.
Preheat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat; cook chicken until fully cooked and slightly charred.
Warm the pita breads in a dry pan or oven.
Place a portion of the cooked chicken on each pita.
Top with salad greens, cucumber slices, tomato slices, and tahini sauce.
Roll the pita tightly to enclose the fillings and serve immediately.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked and drained
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season chicken and lamb with salt, pepper, and half the onion slices; brown in oil in a large pot.
Layer bulgur, rice, and vegetables in the pot over the meat.
In a bowl, beat eggs and mix with flour and remaining oil to create a batter.
Pour batter over the ingredients, ensuring everything is coated.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Turn pot upside down onto a large platter to invert the dish.
Sprinkle with pomegranate seeds, pine nuts, and parsley before serving.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and garlic; cook until soft.
Add bell peppers and spices; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Create 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes until egg whites are set.
Garnish with parsley and feta cheese before serving.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak fine bulgur wheat in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Mix ground lamb, soaked bulgur, onion, garlic, spices, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Form mixture into small balls or patties.
Fry pine nuts and raisins in butter until golden.
Mix fried nuts and raisins with breadcrumbs.
Stuff each meat ball with the nut mixture.
Deep fry kibbeh balls in oil at 350°F (175°C) until golden brown.
Serve hot with yogurt.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, salt, and cumin in a food processor.
Blend until smooth, adding water gradually to reach desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Serve with pita bread.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brush bottom of a 9x13 inch pan with melted butter.
Layer 12 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with butter.
Sprinkle half the nuts over the layers.
Repeat with another 12 sheets of phyllo and remaining nuts.
Top with remaining 12 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Cut into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
In a saucepan, mix sugar, honey, water, and spices; boil for 5 minutes.
Pour syrup over hot baklava and let cool completely.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Cook the soaked chickpeas in a pot with water until tender, about 1 hour.
Drain the chickpeas and transfer to a food processor.
Add tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, olive oil, cumin, and salt.
Process until smooth and creamy, adding a little water if needed.
Serve chilled or at room temperature with pita bread.

title: Kibbeh
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak the bulgur wheat in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain well.
In a large bowl, mix the drained bulgur, ground lamb, onion, flour, and spices.
Knead the mixture by hand until it forms a cohesive dough.
Shape the dough into balls or stuffed with a filling of your choice.
Fry the kibbeh in olive oil until golden brown on all sides.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 2 pieces stale pita bread, torn into chunks
instructions: Toss the romaine, cucumber, tomato, red onion, pine nuts, and parsley in a large bowl.
Whisk together sumac, olive oil, and lemon juice to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Top with the torn pieces of stale pita bread.
Serve immediately while the bread is still crisp.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer 10 sheets of phyllo dough in a greased baking pan, brushing each with melted butter.
Sprinkle half the pine nuts and almonds over the first layer.
Repeat layering with 10 more sheets of phyllo and the remaining nuts.
Brush the top with melted butter and cut into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
Meanwhile, mix sugar, water, honey, cinnamon, and cloves in a saucepan and boil until thick.
Pour the syrup over the hot baklava and let cool completely.

title: Knafeh
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Melt butter in a large baking dish and sprinkle half the kataifi dough over it.
Layer half the cheese over the dough, then repeat with the remaining dough and cheese.
Top with the remaining kataifi and sprinkle with pine nuts.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until the dough is golden and crispy.
While baking, mix sugar, heavy cream, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a saucepan and boil until thickened.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot knafeh immediately after baking.

title: Mansaf
ingredients: 1.5 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes
2 tsp cumin seeds, toasted and crushed
instructions: Place lamb in a large pot and cover with water.
Add baking soda, salt, and pepper to the water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Strain the meat and reserve the cooking liquid.
Whisk yogurt with 1 cup of the reserved cooking liquid until smooth.
Add the yogurt mixture to the remaining liquid and stir in cumin.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Serve the yogurt sauce over the lamb and top with parboiled rice.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves.

title: Hummus
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked chickpeas.
Cook chickpeas in a pot with salt until very tender, about 1 hour.
Transfer chickpeas to a food processor.
Add tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt.
Process until smooth, scraping down sides as needed.
With the motor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil.
Add ice water a tablespoon at a time until the hummus reaches desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve immediately or chill until ready to eat.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur wheat in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Mix ground lamb with drained bulgur, chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper, allspice, and cinnamon.
Knead the mixture vigorously by hand for 5 minutes until it becomes sticky and elastic.
Shape the mixture into small balls or crescent shapes.
Fry the kibbeh in olive oil until golden brown on all sides.
For the filling, sauté diced onion and tomato with parsley.
Stuff the fried kibbeh shells with the warm vegetable mixture.
Drizzle with a little olive oil and serve hot.

title: Fattoush
instructions: Wash and dry all vegetables thoroughly.
Toss greens, radishes, cucumbers, tomatoes, red onion, lettuce, parsley, and mint in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together sumac, olive oil, lemon juice, and pomegranate molasses.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Top with toasted pita chips and pine nuts.
Serve immediately.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer 12 sheets of phyllo dough in a greased baking dish, brushing each with melted butter.
Sprinkle half the chopped nuts over the first layer.
Add another 12 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Sprinkle remaining nuts on top.
Cover with the remaining 12 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Cut the baklava into diamond shapes before baking.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
While baking, combine sugar, honey, water, cinnamon, and cloves in a saucepan.
Simmer the syrup until it thickens slightly.
Pour the hot syrup immediately over the hot baklava.
Let cool completely before serving.

title: Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, cut into strips
instructions: Mix yogurt, lemon juice, spices, oil, onion, and garlic in a bowl.
Toss chicken strips in the marinade and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook chicken until golden and cooked through.
Serve with pita bread and tahini sauce.

title: Falafel
instructions: Drain soaked chickpeas and blend with herbs, onion, garlic, and spices until coarse.
Mix in flour, baking soda, salt, and pepper; let rest for 30 minutes.
Shape mixture into balls and fry in oil at 350°F until golden brown.
Serve with pita and hummus.

title: Hummus
instructions: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin until smooth.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil while blending.
Add ice water gradually to reach desired consistency.
Season with salt and serve with pita.

title: Baklava
instructions: Brush phyllo sheets with butter and stack 10 sheets.
Sprinkle with half the nut mixture, then repeat with more sheets.
Cut into diamond shapes and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes.
Mix sugar, water, lemon juice, and honey; pour over hot baklava.
Let cool completely before serving.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur in hot water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Mix bulgur, meat, onion, and spices in a bowl.
Form into large balls, flatten, and seal with egg.
Fry in oil until golden brown.
Roll in sesame seeds and serve warm.

title: Chicken Kebab
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Mix well until the chicken is evenly coated.
Thread the chicken onto skewers.
Grill the kebabs for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until fully cooked and slightly charred.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup chickpeas, cooked or canned and drained
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, slowly drizzle in the olive oil until fully incorporated.
Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the hummus reaches a creamy, dip-consistency.
Transfer to a serving bowl, drizzle with more olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika.

title: Baba Ganoush
instructions: Pierce the eggplants with a fork and roast them directly over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft, about 30-40 minutes.
Peel the skin off the eggplants and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash the eggplant flesh with a fork or potato masher.
Add tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt, and paprika to the eggplant.
Mix thoroughly until smooth and creamy.
Transfer to a bowl, garnish with pine nuts if desired, and serve.

title: Falafel
ingredients: 2 cups dried fava beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked fava beans and chickpeas thoroughly.
Place beans, chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, baking soda, and salt into a food processor.
Pulse until the mixture is finely chopped but not puréed; some texture should remain.
Form the mixture into small balls or patties.
Deep fry the falafel in oil heated to 350°F (175°C) for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and bell pepper, cooking until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne, salt, black pepper, and sugar.
Bring the sauce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Create six small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook for 8-10 minutes until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

title: Chicken Kabsa
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Season chicken with cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft.
Add chicken and cook until browned.
Stir in tomato paste and stock.
Cover and simmer until chicken is tender.
Rinse rice and cook in boiling water until fluffy.
Fluff rice and mix with cooked chicken and sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Falafel
instructions: Drain and rinse soaked chickpeas.
Blend chickpeas, herbs, garlic, spices, baking soda, and flour until coarse.
Chill mixture for 30 minutes.
Form mixture into small balls.
Heat oil to 350°F.
Fry balls until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Hummus
instructions: Combine chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika.
Serve with pita bread.

title: Baklava
instructions: Mix nuts and cinnamon together.
Brush bottom of pan with butter.
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Sprinkle nut mixture over phyllo.
Repeat layers until phyllo is used.
Top with remaining butter.
Cut into diamond shapes before baking.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden.
Mix sugar, water, honey, and vanilla.
Pour syrup over hot baklava and let cool.

title: Shawarma
instructions: Marinate chicken with oil, cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, allspice, and salt for 1 hour.
Grill or pan-fry chicken until cooked through.
Layer pita bread with lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and chicken.
Drizzle with tahini sauce.
Roll tightly and serve.

title: Kibbeh
instructions: Soak bulgur in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain well.
Mix drained bulgur with ground lamb, onion, garlic, spices, salt, and pine nuts.
Shape mixture into small patties or balls.
Fry in oil until golden brown on both sides.
Serve warm with yogurt or pickles.

title: Fattoush
instructions: Toss lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and pita pieces in a large bowl.
Stir in parsley and mint.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, and cumin together.
Pour dressing over salad and toss gently.
Serve immediately.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer phyllo sheets in a pan, brushing each with melted butter.
Sprinkle nut mixture and spices over half the layers.
Fold dough over nuts to create a square, then cut into diamond shapes.
Bake for 45 minutes until golden.
Simmer sugar, water, honey, and lemon juice to make syrup.
Pour hot syrup over warm baklava and let cool.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Add lentils, rice, cumin, salt, and pepper; stir to coat.
Add 2 cups water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Let stand covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

title: Shawarma
instructions: Marinate chicken with oil, lemon juice, garlic, spices, and salt for 2 hours.
Cook marinated chicken in a pan or oven until fully done.
Warm pita bread.
Fill pita with lettuce, tomato, pickles, and cooked chicken.
Drizzle generously with tahini sauce and serve.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add chicken pieces, seasoning with salt and pepper, and cook until browned.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add preserved lemons, raisins, and saffron.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 1 hour until chicken is tender.
Garnish with toasted almonds before serving.

title: Fattoush Salad with Sumac
ingredients: 4 slices stale pita bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss pita pieces with a little oil and bake until crispy.
In a large bowl, combine greens, bell pepper, cucumber, radishes, parsley, and mint.
Whisk together olive oil, sumac, lemon juice, garlic powder, and cumin.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss well.
Add the crispy pita pieces just before serving.

title: Hummus with Tahini and Garlic
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, rinsed and drained
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Blend on high speed until smooth, adding water gradually to reach desired consistency.
Scrape down the sides of the bowl if necessary.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Drizzle with extra olive oil and sprinkle with paprika before serving.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh (Raw Lamb Meatballs)
ingredients: 2 cups fine bulgur wheat, soaked in cold water
1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted and chopped
instructions: Drain the soaked bulgur wheat thoroughly and let it sit to absorb excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine ground lamb, drained bulgur, garlic, pine nuts, parsley, mint, onion, salt, and pepper.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly with your hands until well combined.
Shape the mixture into small balls or patties.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Baklava with Honey and Pistachios
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brush a baking sheet with melted butter.
Layer phyllo sheets on the sheet, brushing each with butter, until 12 layers high.
Sprinkle half the nuts, sugar, and spices over the dough.
Add another 6 layers of buttered phyllo.
Sprinkle remaining nuts and spices, then add the final 6 layers of phyllo.
Cut the baklava into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through the bottom.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
Mix honey, water, and lemon juice; pour over the hot baklava immediately.
Let cool completely before removing from the pan and cutting completely.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 2 cups pita bread, toasted and broken into pieces
instructions: Toast the pita bread pieces in a dry pan until crisp and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, parsley, and mint.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, and salt to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Top with the toasted pita pieces and serve immediately.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh
instructions: Combine the ground beef and lamb in a large bowl.
Add the grated onion, minced garlic, salt, pepper, allspice, and lemon juice to the meat.
Gradually add the fine bulgur wheat while mixing thoroughly with your hands until the mixture holds together.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to meld.
Form into small balls or slices and serve chilled garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Knafeh
ingredients: 2 cups fine semolina cheese (akawi or labneh mixed with salt)
4 cups hot sweetened milk or milk-based syrup
instructions: Mix the semolina cheese with half of the sugar and set aside.
Brush a layer of phyllo sheets with melted butter and sprinkle with cheese mixture, repeating layers until all cheese is used.
Fold the phyllo over the filling to enclose it, sealing the edges with more butter.
Fry the knafeh in hot oil until golden brown on both sides and drain on paper towels.
Dissolve the remaining sugar, rosewater, vanilla, and milk in a pot to create a syrup, then boil until slightly thickened.
Cut the fried knafeh into squares, drizzle generously with the warm syrup, and sprinkle with chopped pistachios before serving.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Layer 10 sheets of phyllo dough, brushing each with melted butter.
Sprinkle the nut mixture evenly over the layers, then cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing with butter.
Cut the baklava into diamond shapes before baking.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
While hot, pour the mixture of sugar, water, honey, lemon juice, and orange blossom water over the baklava.
Let it cool completely in the pan before transferring to a serving dish.

title: Shawarma Platter
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken breast or lamb, thinly sliced
instructions: Marinate the sliced meat with olive oil, allspice, coriander, garlic, salt, and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Cook the marinated meat on a vertical rotisserie or in a hot pan until browned and cooked through.
Warm the pita breads in a toaster or dry pan.
Slice the cooked meat thinly.
Assemble the shawarma by layering meat, lettuce, cucumber, tomato, pickles, and sauces onto each pita.
Serve immediately while the meat is still warm.

title: Chicken Shawarma
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into strips
instructions: Mix yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, coriander, allspice, cinnamon, cayenne, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make marinade.
Add chicken strips to marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Place marinated chicken on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 20-25 minutes until cooked through and slightly charred.
Warm pita bread in the oven.
Shred cabbage, dice tomato, and slice pickles.
Whisk tahini and lemon juice together for sauce.
Warm pita, fill with chicken, cabbage, tomato, pickles, and drizzle with tahini sauce.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, plus more for drizzling
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas, reserving 1/4 cup liquid if using canned.
Add chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, and salt to a food processor.
Blend until smooth, scraping down sides as needed.
With processor running, slowly drizzle in reserved chickpea liquid or ice water until creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more lemon or salt if needed.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Drizzle with extra olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and olives.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix walnuts, pine nuts, flour, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl.
Brush a 9x13 inch pan with melted butter.
Layer 12 sheets of phyllo dough in pan, brushing each with butter.
Sprinkle half of the nut mixture over phyllo.
Layer another 12 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Sprinkle remaining nut mixture over phyllo.
Top with final 12 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Cut into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
While baking, combine sugar, water, honey, vanilla, and lemon juice in a saucepan.
Simmer until syrup reaches 240°F (115°C).
Pour hot syrup over hot baklava immediately.
Let cool completely before serving.

title: Kofta Kebabs
instructions: Soak bulgur wheat in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Mix ground lamb, bulgur, yogurt, olive oil, cumin, allspice, cinnamon, salt, pepper, cayenne, onion, parsley, and mint in a bowl.
Form mixture into small oblong kebab shapes.
Skewer kebabs, leaving space between each.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill kebabs for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges and pita bread.

title: Falafel
instructions: Drain soaked chickpeas and pulse in a food processor until coarse crumbs form, do not puree.
Add onion, parsley, cilantro, garlic, cumin, coriander, baking soda, cayenne, salt, and pepper to processor.
Pulse until mixture is sticky and holds together.
Chill mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Form mixture into small balls.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry falafel balls in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with pita bread and tahini sauce.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Cook chickpeas until tender, then drain and reserve cooking liquid.
In a food processor, combine chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, and cumin.
Process until smooth, adding ice water gradually to reach desired consistency.
Season with salt and transfer to a serving bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with paprika if desired.

title: Tabbouleh
instructions: Rinse bulgur under cold water and let drain for 10 minutes.
Cook bulgur in boiling water according to package directions until tender.
Fluff bulgur with a fork and let cool completely.
In a large bowl, mix cooled bulgur, parsley, mint, tomatoes, and onion.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over salad and toss gently to combine.
Chill before serving.

title: Shawarma Wrap
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh meat, sliced thinly
instructions: In a bowl, mix olive oil, turmeric, cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Toss chicken slices in the spice mixture and cook in a hot pan until browned and cooked through.
Warm pita breads in a dry skillet or oven.
Spread tahini sauce on each pita.
Layer shredded lettuce, cucumber, tomato, and cooked chicken on each pita.
Roll tightly and cut in half before serving.

title: Kibbeh
ingredients: 1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted and chopped
instructions: Rinse bulgur and soak in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Mix ground lamb, onion, pine nuts, parsley, flour, baking powder, allspice, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Add drained bulgur to the meat mixture and knead well until combined.
Shape the mixture into small balls or crescent shapes.
Heat olive oil in a pan and fry kibbeh until golden brown on all sides.
Serve hot as a snack or appetizer.

title: Baklava
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt half of the butter and brush a layer of phyllo sheets onto a baking tray.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts and repeat layers until all phyllo is used, brushing each layer with melted butter.
Cut the pastry into diamond shapes without cutting all the way through.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden and crisp.
In a saucepan, combine sugar, honey, water, cinnamon, and cloves; boil for 5 minutes.
Pour the syrup over the hot baklava and let cool completely before cutting.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 cup chickpeas, cooked or canned and rinsed
instructions: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, reserving some liquid.
Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Process until smooth, adding reserved chickpea liquid or water a tablespoon at a time until creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve with pita bread and extra olive oil.

title: Tajine of Lamb and Apricots
ingredients: 1.5 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or tagine over medium heat.
Add lamb cubes and cook until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add onions and garlic, cooking until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours until lamb is tender.
Add apricots and cook for another 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Shawarma Platter
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thigh meat, sliced thin
instructions: In a bowl, mix olive oil, lemon juice, yogurt, and all spices with salt.
Toss chicken slices in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Preheat a grill, skillet, or vertical rotisserie to medium-high heat.
Cook chicken in batches until fully cooked and slightly charred.
Slice cooked chicken into thin strips.
Warm pita bread on a griddle or in the oven.
Assemble sandwiches by layering lettuce, pickles, chicken, and tahini sauce in pita.
Serve immediately.

title: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Toast pita bread pieces in a dry skillet until crisp and golden.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, parsley, mint, and radishes.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Top with toasted pita pieces just before serving.
Serve immediately to keep the bread crisp.

title: Kebabs with Mint Yogurt
ingredients: 1 lb lamb or chicken, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Mix meat cubes with olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic powder, pepper, paprika, and salt.
Thread marinated meat onto soaked skewers.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
In a separate bowl, whisk yogurt, chopped mint, lemon juice, and minced garlic for the dipping sauce.
Serve kebabs hot with the mint yogurt sauce and grilled vegetables.

title: Manakish with Za'atar
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, and warm water to form a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and let rise for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C) with a baking stone if available.
Roll out dough into thin circles on a floured surface.
Brush each circle with olive oil and sprinkle generously with za'atar and pine nuts.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Serve warm with labneh or plain yogurt.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 4 large pita breads, torn into pieces
instructions: Fry torn pita pieces in olive oil until crispy and set aside.
In a large bowl, toss vegetables (pepper, cucumber, onion, parsley, mint, tomatoes).
Whisk together sumac, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and cumin for the dressing.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss well.
Add the crispy fried pita just before serving to maintain crunch.
Serve immediately.

title: Musakhan
instructions: Marinate chicken with half the olive oil, salt, and pepper for 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange sliced sweet potatoes in a large baking dish.
Layer marinated chicken and sliced onions over the potatoes.
Drizzle with remaining olive oil and sprinkle with za'atar, allspice, and cumin.
Roast for 45 minutes until chicken is cooked and potatoes are tender.
While roasting, toast pine nuts in a dry pan until golden.
Remove from oven, scatter toasted pine nuts and sumac over the top.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Jareesh (Cracked Wheat Porridge)
ingredients: 1/2 cup labneh or yogurt for serving
instructions: Rinse the jareesh well under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat ghee over medium heat.
Add the rinsed jareesh and toast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually add water or broth while stirring to prevent lumps.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes.
Stir frequently; the mixture will thicken and become creamy.
Remove from heat and stir in toasted pine nuts, sesame seeds, salt, parsley, and mint.
Serve hot with a dollop of labneh or yogurt on the side.

title: Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Marinate lamb with half the spices, garlic, and some oil for 2 hours.
In a deep pot, sear the lamb until browned, then remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and remaining garlic in oil until soft.
Add potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, then add tomatoes and remaining spices.
Return lamb to the pot, nestling it around the vegetables.
Rinse rice and spread it evenly over the meat and vegetable layer.
Pour enough water to cover the rice by 2 inches and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 20-25 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 10 minutes.
Grease a large serving platter with oil, place the pot upside down over it, and quickly flip the entire dish.
Garnish with toasted pine nuts, parsley, and mint before serving.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked and drained
1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté garlic in olive oil until fragrant, then add chicken and cook until browned.
Add ground lamb to the chicken and cook until the meat is no longer pink.
Mix in the soaked bulgur, flour, salt, and pepper; stir well to combine.
Layer the rice in a large pot, spreading it evenly.
Arrange potatoes, green beans, and the meat mixture on top of the rice.
Pour the tomato sauce over everything and cover the pot tightly with foil.
Steam over medium heat for 30-35 minutes until the rice is tender.
Invert the pot onto a large serving platter to flip the dish upside down.
