Garnish with fresh parsley, mint, and pine nuts before serving.

title: Musakhan
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1 lb fresh flatbread, cut into quarters
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté onions and garlic in olive oil until soft and golden.
Mix the flour, sumac, salt, and pepper into the onion mixture.
Place the chicken pieces on a baking sheet and brush with the onion mixture.
Roast the chicken for 25-30 minutes until the skin is crispy and the meat is cooked through.
Arrange the flatbread quarters on a large baking sheet.
Brush the flatbread with the beaten egg and sprinkle with pine nuts.
Place the roasted chicken on top of the flatbread.
Bake for an additional 10 minutes until the flatbread is golden and crispy.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 4 slices French bread, toasted and torn into pieces
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make the dressing.
Toss the torn toasted bread pieces with half of the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce, cucumber, bell pepper, tomato, radish, herbs, and green onions.
Pour the remaining dressing over the vegetables and toss gently.
Top with the seasoned bread pieces and toasted pine nuts.
Serve immediately as a fresh salad.

title: Kunafa with Cheese
ingredients: 1 lb white cheese (Akkawi or Halloumi), grated
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Melt the ghee in a baking dish and spread the grated cheese evenly on top.
Layer the kunafa sheets over the cheese, overlapping slightly.
Brush the top of the pastry with more melted ghee.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and crispy.
In a small pot, combine sugar, water, and cinnamon; simmer until the sugar dissolves.
Remove the kunafa from the oven and let it cool for 2 minutes.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot kunafa and cheese.
Garnish with toasted pine nuts and crushed pistachios before serving.

title: Zaalouk
instructions: Grill or roast the eggplant cubes until soft and charred.
Peel the skin off the eggplant and place the flesh in a food processor.
Add garlic, cumin, salt, cayenne pepper, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the processor.
Blend until smooth but slightly chunky.
Transfer the mixture to a pot and add the chopped tomato.
Simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes until the tomato is soft.
Stir in fresh parsley, mint, lemon juice, sumac, and the remaining olive oil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or lemon juice if needed.
Serve warm or at room temperature with tahini on the side.

title: Mujadara
ingredients: 1 cup dried lentils, soaked for 1 hour
instructions: Boil lentils in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Cook rice in a separate pot with salt until just half-cooked, then drain.
Sauté sliced onions in olive oil until deeply caramelized and golden brown.
Combine the cooked lentils, half-cooked rice, and caramelized onions in a large bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, mix well, and let it sit for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onions and cook until soft, then add garlic, cumin, and paprika.
Add tomatoes, bell peppers, water, salt, and pepper; simmer until sauce thickens.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Musaka with Eggplant
instructions: Salt eggplant slices and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden on both sides.
In the same pan, brown ground beef with onion and garlic until cooked through.
Add tomato sauce, water, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix the soaked bulgur wheat with chopped parsley.
Layer fried eggplant at the bottom of a baking dish, top with meat sauce, then bulgur.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25 minutes until bubbly and hot.

title: Hummus with Tahini
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Place chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt, and cumin in a food processor.
Blend until mostly smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the mixture reaches a creamy, dip-consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or lemon juice if necessary.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle with extra olive oil, and serve with pita bread.

title: Sabich
instructions: Boil eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel, and slice into wedges.
Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until tender and slightly crispy.
Toast pita breads lightly until warm and pliable.
Spread tahini sauce inside each pita.
Layer fried eggplant, sliced tomatoes, cucumbers, pickles, and egg wedges inside the pita.
Drizzle with sumac and sprinkle with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Maqluba (Upturned Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes
1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
4 cups tomato sauce, homemade or store-bought
1 cup frozen mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, corn)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil the soaked rice in salted water until 70% cooked, then drain.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper, allspice, and half the oil; fry until golden brown and remove.
In a large pot, sauté onions in the remaining oil until soft.
Add chickpeas, mixed vegetables, tomato sauce, and spices; simmer for 15 minutes.
Layer the fried chicken in the bottom of a large deep dish, followed by the rice, and top with the vegetable sauce mixture.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 10 minutes until the top is golden.
Run a knife around the edge, flip the dish upside down onto a serving platter, and serve hot.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 4 cups mixed salad greens (lettuce, parsley, cilantro)
4 slices stale pita bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Toss the mixed greens, cucumber, tomatoes, green onions, and radishes in a large bowl.
Heat a dry skillet and toast the pita pieces until crisp and golden, watching closely so they don't burn.
Toast the pine nuts and sunflower seeds in the same pan until fragrant.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Immediately add the warm toasted pita, pine nuts, and sunflower seeds and toss lightly.
Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish.

title: Mujaddara (Lentils with Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: In a large pot, combine lentils, 2.5 cups of water, salt, cumin, and pepper; bring to a boil and simmer until lentils are soft but not mushy, about 20 minutes.
While lentils cook, heat olive oil in a separate large skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and fry slowly, stirring occasionally, until they are deeply caramelized and dark brown, about 20-25 minutes.
Add the soaked rice and 2 cups of fresh water to the caramelized onions; stir well to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the mixture with a fork and gently fold in the cooked lentils.
Serve warm, often with a dollop of yogurt on the side.

title: Shorbat Fooseq (Cold Lentil Soup)
instructions: Rinse the lentils thoroughly and set aside.
In a blender, combine the onion, garlic, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, parsley, mint, dill, olive oil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Blend until completely smooth.
Add the rinsed lentils to the blender mixture and pulse a few times to distribute them without pureeing the soup too much.
Pour the mixture into a large bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until chilled.
Stir gently before serving to ensure all ingredients are evenly distributed.
Serve cold, garnished with extra fresh herbs if desired.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh (Raw Meat Balls)
ingredients: 1/2 cup fine bulgur wheat, soaked in ice water for 30 minutes
1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted and crushed
instructions: Drain the soaked bulgur wheat well and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground lamb, drained bulgur, pine nuts, allspice, cinnamon, black pepper, salt, minced onion, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Add ice water gradually while mixing with your hands until the mixture is very sticky and forms a cohesive ball.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to firm up.
Take small portions of the mixture and shape them into small, smooth balls using wet hands.
Arrange the kibbeh balls on a platter and sprinkle generously with pomegranate seeds.
Serve immediately as an appetizer.

title: Abgoosht
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shank, cut into chunks
1 lb beef chuck, cut into chunks
4 cups dried split peas, soaked overnight
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place lamb and beef in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours.
Add soaked split peas and chickpeas to the pot.
Simmer for another 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Add grated onion, grated tomato, carrots, and potatoes.
Cook for 45 more minutes until vegetables are soft.
Stir in crushed dried limes and chopped parsley.
Season with salt and pepper, then let it rest overnight to develop flavor.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi
ingredients: 2 lbs mixed herbs (parsley, cilantro, flat-leaf lettuce, fenugreek, chervil), finely chopped
2 cups dried white beans, soaked overnight
1 lb lamb neck or stewing meat, cubed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Grind the mixed herbs and dried limes into a coarse paste.
Sauté grated onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add the herb-lime paste and walnuts, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb meat and cook until browned.
Add the soaked beans and enough water to cover by 2 inches.
Simmer on low heat for 2 to 3 hours until meat and beans are very tender.
Season with turmeric, salt, and pepper.

title: Fesenjan
instructions: Sauté grated onion in butter or oil until golden brown.
Add chicken pieces and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in turmeric and salt.
Add pomegranate molasses and mix well to coat the chicken.
Add chopped walnuts and stir to combine.
Pour in water or stock to cover the chicken.
Simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add more walnuts if the sauce is too thick before serving.

title: Dolmeh
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Blanch grape leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Mix ground meat, grated onion, cooked rice, pomegranate molasses, and tomato sauce.
Add spices (allspice, turmeric, cinnamon), salt, and pepper; mix thoroughly.
Place a grape leaf flat on a board and spoon a tablespoon of filling in the center.
Fold the sides over the filling and roll tightly.
Pack the dolmeh into a pot in a single layer.
Cover with more blanched grape leaves and pour tomato sauce over the top.
Add water to cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours.

title: Kehvan
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
2 cups dried white beans, soaked overnight
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté grated onion in oil until translucent.
Add lamb cubes and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in tomato paste, turmeric, and crushed dried limes.
Add the soaked beans and enough water to cover by 2 inches.
Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until meat and beans are tender.
Stir in chopped walnuts and parsley.
Cook for another 30 minutes to let flavors meld.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Dolma (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 lb fresh grape leaves, salted and rinsed
1 lb ground lamb and beef mixture
1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse grape leaves thoroughly and remove any tough stems.
Mix lamb, beef, rice, pine nuts, herbs, vinegar, oil, and spices in a bowl.
Place a grape leaf shiny side down, top with a spoonful of filling, and roll tightly.
Pack dolma into a large pot in a conical shape, pressing down gently.
Pour hot water over the dolma until it is mostly submerged, adding a bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until rice is tender.
Serve warm or at room temperature with yogurt and sumac.

title: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes and Peppers)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Freshly ground black pepper (more for serving)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add tomatoes, bell pepper, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper; cook slowly for 10 minutes until soft.
Pour the beaten eggs over the vegetable mixture.
Stir gently with a spatula, allowing the eggs to set but remain soft and creamy.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh parsley.
Serve immediately while hot with warm bread.

title: Piyaz (Turkish White Bean Salad)
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) white cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the canned beans under cold water and drain well.
In a large bowl, combine beans, sliced red onion, cucumber, parsley, and mint.
In a small jar, shake together olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat evenly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to let flavors meld.
Serve chilled as a side dish or light lunch.

title: Mercimek Çorbası (Red Lentil Soup)
ingredients: 1 cup red lentils, rinsed and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Sauté onion, carrot, garlic, and red pepper flakes in a pot with a little oil until soft.
Add red lentils and broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until completely smooth.
Stir in yogurt, dill, and parsley; do not boil after adding yogurt.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in deep bowls, optionally garnished with more dill.

title: Kebap (Lamb Skewers)
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Wooden skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Mix lamb, bulgur, grated onion, herbs, olive oil, paprika, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Divide the mixture into portions and shape into flat patties, pressing firmly.
Thread the patties onto the soaked wooden skewers, spacing them evenly.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the kebabs for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred.
Serve immediately with grilled vegetables and flatbread.

title: Kibbeh bil Sanieh
ingredients: 300g fine bulgur wheat, soaked in cold water
1/2 cup fine bulgur wheat, soaked separately
instructions: Sauté onions in olive oil and butter until golden.
Mix lamb, soaked fine bulgur, flour, salt, pepper, allspice, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Add the sautéed onions and mix well by hand.
Shape the mixture into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Toast the finest bulgur wheat until golden brown.
Layer the flattened kibbeh balls in a greased baking dish.
Sprinkle toasted pine nuts, pistachios, and toasted fine bulgur between layers.
Repeat until the mixture is used, ending with a layer of toasted fine bulgur on top.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 20-25 minutes until the top is crispy.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 4 pieces stale pita bread, torn into chunks
instructions: Toss the pita bread pieces in a pan with a little olive oil until crisp and golden.
In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, romaine, cucumbers, tomatoes, red onion, radishes, parsley, and mint.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, dried mint, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Just before serving, add the crispy fried pita pieces and toss lightly.

title: Knafeh Bishara
ingredients: 400g fresh labneh or thick strained yogurt
instructions: Mix the labneh, semolina, wheat semolina, melted butter, baking powder, and salt in a bowl until a stiff dough forms.
Roll the dough into thin, small circles and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 10-12 minutes until the edges are golden and the center is firm.
In a small pot, combine sugar, water, and rose water; simmer until the sugar dissolves.
Remove the baked dough from the oven and brush with the sugar syrup immediately.
Arrange the syrup-soaked dough pieces on a serving plate.
Sprinkle the top with pine nuts and sesame seeds before serving warm.

title: Mujadara
instructions: Sauté onions in olive oil until translucent, then add garlic, cumin, salt, pepper, and cinnamon; cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils and rice to the pot; stir to coat with the onion mixture.
Cover with 4 cups of water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until lentils and rice are tender and water is absorbed.
Fluff the mixture with a fork and serve hot.
Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts and chopped parsley before serving.

title: Bamieh (Eggplant with Chickpeas)
ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
instructions: Sauté onions in olive oil until soft, then add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper; stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the chickpeas and eggplant cubes; add water to cover.
Simmer covered on low heat for 40-50 minutes until the eggplant is very tender.
Stir in the chopped parsley and toasted pine nuts before serving.

title: Kibbeh
ingredients: 2 cups fine bulgur, soaked in cold water
instructions: Squeeze excess water from the soaked bulgur thoroughly.
In a large bowl, combine drained bulgur, ground lamb, garlic, pine nuts, flour, salt, and pepper.
Knead the mixture by hand until it becomes a smooth, sticky dough.
Shape into small patties or balls.
Fry in olive oil over medium heat until golden brown on both sides.

title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 2 cups pita bread, toasted and broken into pieces
instructions: Toss lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, parsley, and mint in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, and salt to make the dressing.
Drizzle dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Add the toasted pita pieces and toss lightly so they absorb the dressing.
Serve immediately.

title: Manakish with Za'atar
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a bowl, mix flour and olive oil, then add the yeast mixture.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Punch down dough and divide into small balls, flattening each into a thin round.
Brush each round with olive oil and sprinkle generously with za'atar (and crushed garlic if desired).
Bake in a preheated oven at 425°F (220°C) for 10-12 minutes until puffed and golden.

title: Shawarma (Home Style)
instructions: In a bowl, mix olive oil, lemon juice, tomato paste, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Add the sliced chicken to the marinade and let sit for at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange marinated chicken in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, basting occasionally with remaining marinade.
Serve sliced chicken in flatbread or pita with pickled turnips and cucumbers.

title: Ful Medames
instructions: Soak the dried fava beans in water overnight or for at least 6 hours.
Drain beans and place in a pot with fresh water, baking soda, and cumin seeds.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until very tender.
Drain excess water and mash the beans partially, leaving some texture.
In a separate bowl, whisk tahini with lemon juice and garlic until smooth.
Stir the tahini mixture into the mashed beans along with salt and cayenne pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with fresh parsley.
Serve hot with warm pita bread.

title: Mansaf
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Marinate lamb in baking soda, salt, white pepper, cumin, and allspice for 30 minutes.
Place lamb in a large pot and add water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
In a separate bowl, mix strained yogurt until smooth.
Pour yogurt over the cooked lamb and serve immediately with hot rice on the side.

title: Fasool bi Laban
ingredients: 2 cups dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked beans and place in a pot with water, onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, and salt.
Boil until beans are very soft, about 45 minutes.
Strain beans and keep the cooking liquid.
Mix beans with some of the cooking liquid and add enough to make a thick stew.
Serve the bean stew in bowls topped with fresh yogurt and dried mint.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh
ingredients: 500 g bulgur wheat, parboiled and drained
instructions: Finely chop the onion and mix with minced garlic.
Combine lamb, bulgur, onion mixture, lemon juice, salt, pepper, allspice, and olive oil in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined.
Divide into small portions and shape into balls or flat discs.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Kushari
instructions: Boil lentils, macaroni, and parboiled rice separately until tender, then drain.
Fry sliced onions in a large pot until golden brown.
Add garlic, tomato puree, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, salt, vinegar, and sugar to the pot.
Simmer the sauce for 15 minutes until thickened.
Mix the cooked lentils, pasta, and rice with the tomato sauce and serve topped with chili flakes.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked and drained
1 kg chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, half of the spices, and some oil, then sear in a large deep pot.
Add potatoes, chickpeas, onions, and remaining spices to the pot, arranging them around the chicken.
Pour in tomato puree and water, then simmer until vegetables are tender.
Add the rice and top with the remaining oil.
Cook covered for 20 minutes until rice is done, then flip the pot upside down onto a serving platter to unmold.

title: Fattoush Salad
instructions: Wash and chop all vegetables and herbs.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce, parsley, mint, radishes, cucumber, and pomegranate seeds.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, sumac, lemon juice, and salt.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Add the toasted pita pieces just before serving to keep them crunchy.

title: Musakhan
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, cut into quarters
1/2 kg local Jerusalem bread, cut into pieces
instructions: Season chicken with half the allspice, cinnamon, cumin, and salt.
Fry chicken pieces in olive oil until golden and cooked through.
In the same pan, fry onions and garlic until soft and caramelized.
Whisk eggs with the remaining spices and a splash of water.
Spread the fried onions over the chicken in a baking dish.
Pour the egg mixture over the onions and bake until set.
Layer the bread pieces on top, then sprinkle with sumac, pine nuts, and parsley.
Bake for another 15 minutes until the bread is crisp.

title: Shawarma Rice
instructions: Rinse basmati rice until water runs clear.
In a pot, heat olive oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice, and salt; stir for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 15 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, fluff with a fork, and squeeze lemon juice over the top.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Kunafa with Cheese
ingredients: 1 kg white cheese (Labneh or Qudadi), crumbled
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt butter in a large baking dish and spread evenly.
Layer kunafa sheets over the butter, overlapping slightly.
Sprinkle crumbled cheese over the pastry layers.
Add another layer of kunafa on top of the cheese.
Mix condensed milk, powdered sugar, and cinnamon; pour over the pastry.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
Let cool slightly before cutting into squares.

title: Maqluba
instructions: Season lamb with allspice, cinnamon, turmeric, salt, and half the olive oil.
Fry lamb in a large pot until browned; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, fry onion, then add eggplants and potatoes; fry until soft.
Add soaked peas, tomato paste, and remaining spices; cook until peas are tender.
Add soaked rice and water (1.5 cups water per cup of rice); bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until rice is cooked.
Arrange fried lamb and vegetables on top of the rice.
Invert the pot onto a large platter to flip the dish.
Garnish with pine nuts and parsley before serving.

title: Shakshuka
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion and bell peppers until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, and paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Make six wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley, and serve.

title: Musakka
instructions: Salt eggplant slices and let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden brown on both sides; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions until soft, then add garlic.
Add tomatoes, allspice, oregano, and cinnamon; simmer for 15 minutes.
Layer fried eggplant slices over the tomato sauce in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the eggplant.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 25 minutes until bubbly.
Garnish with fresh mint before serving.

title: Hummus
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
instructions: Add chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and cumin to a food processor.
Process until the mixture begins to pull away from the sides.
Add ice cubes and process for 2 minutes until very smooth.
With the motor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil until creamy.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a bowl, shape the top, and drizzle with more olive oil.
Sprinkle with paprika and serve with pita bread.

title: Molokhia
ingredients: 1 bunch fresh molokhia leaves, washed and chopped
Cooked rice or flatbread for serving
instructions: Sauté sliced onions in ghee until translucent.
Add garlic, ground coriander, allspice, and red pepper flakes; cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped molokhia leaves and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they wilt.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over a bowl of rice or with flatbread.

title: Kunafa with Labneh and Honey
ingredients: 1 package (12 oz) phyllo dough (or thin kunafa sheets)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cut phyllo sheets into squares and layer them in a baking dish, brushing each layer with melted butter.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until golden and crispy.
Spread a layer of labneh over the warm pastry.
Drizzle generously with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Top with crushed pistachios and a dusting of sugar.
Cut into squares and serve warm.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked for 30 minutes
1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 large eggplant, cut into large chunks
instructions: Boil chickpeas in salted water with half the cumin and coriander until tender.
Sauté onions in half the oil until soft, add garlic and spices, then chicken, cooking until browned.
Add potatoes and eggplant to the pot with tomato paste, cover with water, and simmer until nearly cooked.
In a large deep pot, layer half the potatoes, half the eggplant, half the chicken mixture, half the rice, and half the chickpeas.
Repeat the layers and pour the remaining sauce over the top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes, then flip the pot upside down onto a serving platter.
Garnish with the remaining chickpeas, green beans, and fresh herbs.

title: Mujaddara
instructions: Combine the onions with 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot and fry until very soft and caramelized.
Add the split peas, rinsed rice, water, salt, pepper, and allspice to the pot.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-50 minutes until the rice and peas are tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the mixture with a fork and serve warm with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Kubba
instructions: Mix the ground beef, lamb, soaked bulgur, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, allspice, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Gradually add breadcrumbs and olive oil while mixing until the meat forms a sticky paste that holds together.
Form small, tight balls with the meat mixture and place them in a greased baking dish.
Cover the meatballs with the cooked bulgur wheat, then scatter the pine nuts and crushed dried limes on top.
Bake at 375°F for 30-40 minutes until the meat is cooked through and the bulgur is heated.

title: Maamoul
ingredients: 1/4 cup dates, pitted and finely chopped
instructions: Mix the butter, sugar, eggs, rose water, and cardamom in a bowl until creamy.
Gradually add the flour and mix until a soft dough forms; wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Combine the chopped nuts, dates, raisins, and sesame seeds to create the filling.
Roll small pieces of dough into balls, flatten them, place a teaspoon of filling in the center, and pinch the edges to seal.
Press the filled dough into a fluted cookie mold to create the shape, then bake at 350°F for 15-20 minutes until golden.

title: Mahshi
instructions: Mix the ground lamb, bulgur, grated onion, garlic, tomato paste, salt, pepper, and allspice into a stiff filling.
Place a small amount of filling in the center of each vine leaf, roll it up tightly, and place them seam-side down in a large pot.
Pour water and olive oil over the rolls until they are mostly submerged.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serve hot with a sprinkling of toasted pine nuts.

title: Tahchin (Saffron Rice Cake)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice, soaked for 2 hours and drained
2 tablespoons saffron threads, soaked in 1/4 cup warm water
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse the rice until water runs clear, then soak it for 2 hours and drain well.
In a bowl, whisk together the yogurt, beaten eggs, melted butter, saffron water, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Parboil the rice in salted water until it is about 70% cooked.
Drain the rice and mix it gently with the yogurt egg mixture, ensuring every grain is coated.
Butter a heavy-bottomed pot or tagine, layer half the rice mixture, add a thin layer of plain yogurt, then the remaining rice.
Cover tightly with foil and cook over medium-low heat for 45 minutes.
Remove the foil, brush the top with remaining melted butter, and cook uncovered for 10-15 minutes until the top is golden and crispy.

title: Kuku Sabzi (Herb Frittata)
ingredients: 3 cups fresh herbs (parsley, dill, and chives mixed), finely chopped
1 cup fine bulgur wheat, soaked in hot water and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak the bulgur wheat in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, yogurt, melted butter, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Sauté the chopped onions in a little oil until soft, then add the herbs and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir the cooked herb mixture into the egg batter, followed by the soaked bulgur.
Heat a large skillet with melted butter over medium heat.
Pour the batter into the skillet and spread it evenly.
Cook for 5 minutes on one side, then flip carefully (or cover and steam if flipping is difficult) to cook the other side until fully set.

title: Fesenjan (Pomegranate Walnut Stew)
ingredients: Optional: 1/2 cup basmati rice to serve alongside
instructions: In a large pot, toast the ground walnuts with a little oil over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the pomegranate molasses and stir constantly until the mixture thickens and turns a deep reddish-brown.
Gradually add the water or broth while stirring to prevent lumps.
Add the sugar and saffron water, then simmer on low heat for about 45 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot over steamed basmati rice, garnished with a few walnut pieces.

title: Kookoo Sabzi (Persian Spinach Frittata)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Wash the spinach thoroughly and blanch it in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and squeeze out all excess water.
Sauté the minced onion in half the melted butter until translucent.
Add the spinach and herbs to the onions, cook for 2 minutes, then remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs, yogurt, remaining butter, salt, and white pepper.
Fold the spinach mixture into the egg batter.
Pour into a buttered oven-safe skillet or baking dish.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30-35 minutes until the center is set and the top is golden brown.

title: Ash Reshteh (Red Lentil Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 bunch fresh greens (fenugreek, dill, coriander), chopped
1/2 cup dried fava beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 cup dried noodles (like Reshteh or thick spaghetti)
instructions: Soak the fava beans overnight and drain.
In a large pot, sauté the chopped herbs and oil until fragrant.
Add the red lentils, soaked fava beans, and a few cups of water. Simmer for 45 minutes until lentils are soft.
Add the dried noodles and continue cooking for 10-15 minutes until noodles are tender.
Stir in the barberries and sumac, adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle the soup into deep bowls and serve immediately with a dollop of cold yogurt on top.

title: Dolma (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: 1 cup cooked white rice, partially cooked
instructions: Mix ground lamb, rice, pine nuts, parsley, onion, mint, allspice, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Place a spoonful of filling onto each grape leaf, fold in sides, and roll tightly into cones.
Pack rolled dolma into a large pot upright, placing heavier ones at the bottom.
Add pomegranate molasses, olive oil, and water to cover the dolma by 2 inches.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.

title: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes and Peppers)
ingredients: salt and red pepper flakes to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until soft and translucent.
Stir in diced peppers and tomatoes, cooking until the tomatoes break down and release their juices.
Add minced garlic, salt, and red pepper flakes, cooking for 1 minute more.
Whisk eggs with a pinch of black pepper and pour into the pan.
Stir gently with a wooden spoon to create large curds as the eggs set.
Remove from heat immediately and stir in fresh parsley and mint before serving.

title: Piyaz (White Bean Salad)
ingredients: 2 cans navy beans or white beans, drained
instructions: In a large bowl, combine drained beans, sliced red onion, and chopped herbs.
Whisk together olive oil, sumac, paprika, cumin, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the beans and toss gently to coat evenly.
Add ice water gradually until the salad reaches a loose, salad-like consistency.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving.

title: Patlıcan Sarma (Eggplant Rolls with Minced Meat)
ingredients: 2 large eggplants, peeled and halved lengthwise
instructions: Grill eggplant halves until soft, then spread with olive oil and season with salt.
Mix ground lamb, soaked bulgur, grated onion, egg, tomato paste, mint, allspice, and spices.
Fill each grilled eggplant half with the meat mixture and roll up tightly.
Place rolls in a greased baking dish, seam side down.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30-40 minutes until meat is cooked through.
Serve hot with a side of plain yogurt.

title: Ezogelin (Lentil and Barley Soup)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat, then add grated onion and cook until soft.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, barley, and water or broth, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until lentils and barley are very soft.
Stir in fresh parsley and mint during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Season with sumac and chili flakes, then serve hot with extra sumac powder on top.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh
ingredients: 1 kg lean beef, minced very fine
2 tbsp pine nuts, toasted and chopped
instructions: Soak the bulgur wheat in ice water for 2 hours, then drain thoroughly.
Mix the ground beef with the soaked bulgur, crushed garlic, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Knead the mixture by hand until it forms a smooth, homogeneous paste.
Shape the mixture into small balls or into a large rectangular tray.
Garnish each serving with pine nuts, pomegranate seeds, and parsley.
Serve immediately on ice.

title: Kibbeh bil Laban
ingredients: 1 kg lean beef, minced very fine
instructions: Soak the bulgur wheat in cold water for 2 hours, then drain well.
Combine the ground beef, soaked bulgur, garlic, salt, pepper, and allspice.
Knead the mixture vigorously until it becomes a smooth, sticky paste.
Shape the mixture into small, uniform balls.
In a serving dish, mix the yogurt with a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil.
Arrange the kibbeh balls in a single layer over the yogurt.
Sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and serve at room temperature.

title: Mansaf
ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Season the lamb cubes with pepper, allspice, and cinnamon.
Fry the onions in half the butter until golden, then remove them.
Brown the lamb in the remaining butter, then add the onions back and fry together.
Dissolve the baking soda in the warm water and add it to the yogurt to create the jameed sauce.
Pour the yogurt sauce over the lamb and onions, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until tender.
Parboil the rice for 10 minutes, then drain.
Spread the rice on a large platter, cover with the lamb mixture.
Sprinkle generously with pine nuts, dried mint, and olives.
Serve hot with warm flatbread on the side.

title: Mloukhiyah
ingredients: 500 g fresh or dried jute leaves, chopped
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic, and ginger in olive oil until soft.
Add the chopped jute leaves and fry for 2 minutes until they wilt.
Stir in the black pepper, allspice, cumin, and salt.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the stew thickens.
Serve in deep bowls.
Top each bowl with a generous amount of pine nuts and dried mint.
Accompany with hot, soft flatbread to scoop up the stew.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 2 cups pita bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Toast the pita bread pieces in a pan until golden and crispy.
In a large bowl, combine the tomatoes, cucumber, lettuce, radish, green onions, parsley, and mint.
Whisk together the olive oil, sumac, lemon juice, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently to coat.
Add the toasted pita pieces and pine nuts to the salad.
Toss once more to distribute the bread evenly.
Serve immediately as a side dish or light meal.

title: Mujadara
ingredients: 1 cup bulgur wheat, soaked for 30 minutes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Drain the soaked bulgur and cook with salted water until soft, about 20 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a pot, sauté onions and garlic until golden.
Add lentils, allspice, salt, and pepper to the onions.
Add the cooked bulgur and 1 cup of water.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes until lentils are tender and water is absorbed.
Serve warm garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Maqluba
ingredients: 4 cups basmati rice, soaked and drained
instructions: Season and brown the chicken pieces in olive oil, then set aside.
In the same pot, fry eggplant cubes and potatoes until golden.
Add onions, tomatoes, and peas; cook until onions are soft.
Add the rice and enough water to cover by 2 inches; bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, and steam for 15 minutes.
Arrange chicken on top of the rice, then layer the fried vegetables.
Pour remaining hot oil over the top and cover tightly for 15 more minutes.
Invert the pot onto a large platter immediately to flip the layers.
Garnish with parsley and cilantro before serving.

title: Kibbeh Nayyeh
ingredients: 1.5 kg lamb shoulder, minced very fine
instructions: Mix the fine bulgur with grated onion and let it sit for 15 minutes to absorb moisture.
In a large bowl, combine lamb, bulgur mixture, garlic, allspice, cinnamon, and salt.
Add lemon juice and olive oil slowly while mixing by hand until the mixture holds together.
Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Form the mixture into small, thin patties or cones.
Serve immediately garnished with shredded lettuce and pomegranate seeds.
Do not cook the meat; serve chilled.

title: Shorbat Fulus
ingredients: 2 cups dried fava beans, soaked overnight
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Drain and rinse the soaked fava beans; boil them in water until tender, about 45 minutes.
In a separate pot, heat olive oil and sauté onions and garlic until fragrant.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add allspice.
Add the cooked fava beans and their cooking liquid to the pot.
Stir in salt and pepper, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend half of the soup with a stick blender to make it creamy.
Stir in fresh parsley, mint, and lemon juice before serving.
Serve hot with warm pita bread on the side.

title: Fattoush
ingredients: 1 large loaf stale pita bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Toast the torn pita pieces in a dry pan until crisp and golden.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, and red onion.
Add fresh parsley and mint to the vegetables.
Whisk together olive oil, sumac, allspice, cumin, lemon juice, and salt in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat.
Add the toasted pita pieces last and toss lightly to distribute.
Serve immediately as a fresh side dish.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried chipotle chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend chilies with vinegar, tomato puree, pineapple juice, achiote, cumin, pepper, garlic powder, and salt until smooth.
Brush pork slices with the marinade and let sit for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook pork slices in batches until charred and cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Warm tortillas on the griddle until pliable.
Slice pineapple into small chunks.
Assemble tacos by placing meat on a tortilla, topping with pineapple, onion, and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 30 minutes until soft.
Toast sesame, pumpkin, and almonds in a dry skillet until golden.
Blend soaked chilies, toasted nuts, raisins, garlic, onion, tomato, chocolate, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, salt, sugar, and enough water to cover until smooth.
In a large pot, heat lard over medium heat.
Add half the sauce and cook, stirring constantly, until it darkens and thickens, about 15 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until golden brown.
Add the remaining sauce and broth, simmer gently for 1 hour until chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and sugar if needed.
Serve over rice with warm tortillas.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skins are charred and blistered.
Peel, seed, and stem the peppers.
Stuff each pepper with 2 tablespoons of shredded cheese.
Dip stuffed peppers in flour, then coat with beaten egg.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry peppers in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side.
In a separate saucepan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add tomato sauce, cumin, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve peppers topped with warm sauce, sour cream, and cilantro.
Garnish with lime wedges.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
ingredients: 1 cup serrano chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: In a blender, combine tomatillos, serrano chilies, onion, garlic, cilantro, broth, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Simmer the green sauce in a saucepan for 10 minutes.
Cook ground meat with half the onion in a skillet until browned.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with meat, roll up, and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour half the sauce over the enchiladas.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20 minutes.
Top with remaining sauce, queso fresco, sour cream, and avocado.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skins are charred and blistered.
Peel, seed, and stem the peppers.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of ground meat, onions, and spices.
Toast walnuts and almonds until golden.
Blend toasted nuts with bread, milk, butter, onion, apple, pear, quince, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, salt, sugar, pomegranate juice, and water until smooth.
Simmer the walnut sauce over medium heat until thickened.
Fill peppers with the walnut sauce.
Arrange stuffed peppers on a platter.
Top with pomegranate seeds.
Serve immediately with a side of rice and beans.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1/2 cup black beans, soaked and boiled
1/4 cup dried chiles de árbol, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried chiles mulato, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried chiles pasilla, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast sesame seeds, almonds, and peanuts in a dry pan until golden, then grind into a coarse paste.
Soak dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Boil black beans until very soft, then mash into a paste.
Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato in lard until soft.
Add the chiles, sesame paste, bean paste, raisins, pineapple, cinnamon, cloves, and salt to the pan.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer, cooking for 1 hour until thick and dark.
Place chicken in a baking dish, pour the mole sauce over it, and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 6 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
1/2 cup oil or lard for frying
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skin blisters, then peel and slice lengthwise, removing seeds.
Stuff each pepper with shredded cheese.
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt and dip stuffed peppers in the egg wash.
Heat oil or lard in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry peppers gently until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, sauté onion and garlic in the same oil until translucent.
Add chicken broth, cumin, salt, and pepper to the onion mixture and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve peppers topped with the onion sauce and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Tamales
ingredients: 2 dozen corn husks, soaked in warm water
1 lb ground pork, seasoned with cumin, oregano, and garlic
instructions: Mix masa harina, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Beat softened lard with chicken broth and water until light and fluffy.
Gradually add the lard mixture to the masa, stirring until smooth and spreadable.
Season the ground pork and rice mixture.
Remove one corn husk, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and spread a layer of masa over it.
Fold the husk over the filling to enclose it tightly.
Steam the tamales in a pot lined with husks for about 1 hour until the masa pulls away from the husk.

title: Enchiladas Suizas
instructions: Bring chicken broth and half of the heavy cream to a simmer.
Whisk flour into the remaining cream, then slowly add the mixture to the simmering broth, stirring constantly.
Add butter, cilantro, lime juice, salt, and pepper to the sauce and simmer until thick.
Warm tortillas briefly on a griddle or in a microwave.
Place a portion of shredded chicken in the center of each tortilla and roll up.
Arrange rolled tortillas in a baking dish and pour the creamy sauce over them.
Top with grated cheese and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes until bubbly.

title: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Warm tortillas in a dry skillet until slightly crisp.
In a separate pan, sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add diced tomato, cumin, chili powder, and salt to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Fry eggs in a separate pan or skillet until whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Place one warm tortilla on each plate and top with a fried egg.
Spoon the tomato sauce over each egg.
Garnish with sour cream, chopped cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1 lb chicken breast, cut into pieces
4 dried mulato chiles, stems and seeds removed
4 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
1 dried chipotle chile, stem and seeds removed
instructions: Toast sesame, pumpkin, and almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Soak dried chiles in warm water for 20 minutes.
Blend toasted nuts, soaked chiles, chocolate, raisins, onions, garlic, tomatoes, epazote, oregano, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper with 1 cup broth until smooth.
In a large pot, heat lard over medium heat.
Cook chicken pieces in lard until lightly browned, then remove and set aside.
Pour the mole sauce into the pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot, add remaining broth, and simmer covered for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot with rice.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblano chiles over an open flame until skin blisters, then peel and halve lengthwise, removing seeds.
Stuff each chile half with a generous amount of shredded cheese.
Dip stuffed chiles into beaten egg, then coat in flour.
Heat lard and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry chiles until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
While frying, sauté onions, garlic, and bell peppers in a separate pan until soft.
Add chicken broth, cumin, salt, and pepper to the vegetables and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve fried chiles immediately with the warm vegetable sauce.

title: Tamales
instructions: In a large pot, cook pork, onions, garlic, tomatoes, epazote, cumin, salt, and pepper in lard until meat is tender and sauce is reduced.
Mix masa harina, chicken broth, softened lard, baking powder, and salt until smooth and pliable.
Remove corn husks from soaking water and wipe clean.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons of masa onto the center of each husk.
Place a tablespoon of pork mixture in the center of the masa on each husk.
Fold the husks over the filling to create a triangle or square packet.
Steam tamales in a large pot lined with wet towels for 1 hour.
Remove tamales and let cool slightly before serving.

title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
ingredients: 4 ears of corn, husked and shucked
instructions: Grill or boil corn until tender, about 10 minutes.
Cut kernels off the cob into a large bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, sour cream, cotija cheese, lime juice, chili powder, cumin, and salt.
Pour the mixture over the corn kernels and toss to coat evenly.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately while warm.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblano chiles over an open flame until skin blisters, then peel and halve lengthwise, removing seeds.
Toast walnuts, almonds, and pine nuts in a dry pan.
Blend toasted nuts, breadcrumbs, milk, chicken broth, sugar, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat lard in a skillet and sauté onions, garlic, and bell peppers until soft.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, then blend the mixture until smooth.
Stuff each chile half with a mixture of ground meat and onion (recipe not included here, assume standard picadillo).
Arrange stuffed chiles on a platter and pour the walnut sauce over them.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and cilantro leaves.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 lb chicken pieces, bone-in and skin-on
1/2 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the chilies, seeds, nuts, and spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Grind all toasted ingredients into a smooth paste.
Mix the paste with chocolate, broth, and spices to create the sauce.
Fry the sauce in lard until it thickens and darkens.
Simmer chicken in the sauce until tender and flavors meld.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast peppers until skin blisters, peel, and stuff with cheese.
Flour the stuffed peppers, dip in beaten egg, and fry until golden.
Sauté onion and tomato in lard until soft.
Add broth, vinegar, spices, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve fried peppers topped with the warm sauce.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chilies and garlic, then grind into a paste with vinegar and spices.
Marinate pork slices with the paste and pineapple chunks for 2 hours.
Cook marinated pork in a pan until caramelized and tender.
Warm tortillas on a griddle until pliable.
Assemble tacos with pork, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

title: Enchiladas Suizas
instructions: Sauté onion and tomato in butter until soft.
Make a white sauce by melting butter, whisking in flour, and adding milk.
Simmer sauce with broth, vinegar, spices, and cheese until thick.
Fill tortillas with chicken, roll, and place in a baking dish.
Pour sauce over enchiladas and bake until bubbly and golden.

title: Churros
instructions: Boil water, butter, salt, and sugar in a pot until bubbling.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously until dough forms.
Transfer dough to a piping bag and pipe into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
Roll churros in cinnamon-sugar mixture before serving.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 4 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
8 oz queso fresco or Oaxaca cheese, shredded
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until charred, then peel and seed them.
Stuff each pepper with shredded cheese and secure with a toothpick if needed.
Dip stuffed peppers in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in flour.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet until hot.
Fry peppers until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with tomatillo salsa.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups dried mulato chiles, stems removed
2 cups dried ancho chiles, stems removed
instructions: Toast chiles, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Grind toasted chiles, seeds, garlic, cinnamon, raisins, tomato, and onion into a paste.
Fry the paste in lard or oil until it darkens and oil separates.
Stir in chopped chocolate and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add water or broth to reach desired consistency.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes, seasoning with salt before serving over chicken.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried guajillo chiles, soaked and blended
instructions: Marinate pork slices in blended chiles, achiote, pineapple juice, oregano, and cumin for at least 4 hours.
Cook marinated pork in a skillet or on a grill until browned and slightly charred.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry pan until soft.
Assemble tacos by placing cooked pork and pineapple chunks on tortillas.
Top with diced onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush each tortilla with oil and fry briefly until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken and a sprinkle of cumin.
Place filled tortillas in a baking dish in a single layer.
Pour tomatillo salsa over the tortillas and top with shredded cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until cheese is melted.
Garnish with sour cream, cilantro, and green onions before serving.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 4 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
instructions: Stuff roasted poblanos with a mixture of ground pork, onion, garlic, and tomato sauce.
Fry stuffed peppers in oil until golden and set aside.
Blend walnuts, almonds, breadcrumbs, milk, and eggs to make the walnut sauce (nogada).
Heat the nogada slightly and pour over the stuffed peppers.
Garnish generously with pomegranate seeds.
Serve chilled with the walnut sauce and pomegranate seeds.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1/2 lb dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 lb dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 lb dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Boil chicken in salted water until tender, then remove and set aside.
Toast chiles, nuts, seeds, and garlic in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend toasted ingredients with tomatoes, onion, raisins, broth, chocolate, oregano, and cinnamon into a smooth sauce.
Sear chicken pieces in lard until golden brown on all sides.
Pour the blended sauce over the chicken in a heavy pot.
Simmer covered on low heat for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and flavors meld.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into thin strips
1/4 cup dried guajillo chiles, soaked and blended
1/4 cup dried chipotle chiles, soaked and blended
instructions: Marinate pork strips with blended chiles, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, cinnamon, oregano, and salt for at least 4 hours.
Grill or broil marinated pork until charred and cooked through.
Toast corn tortillas on a comal until slightly blistered.
Slice cooked pork and fresh pineapple into thin pieces.
Warm tortillas, pile on pork and pineapple, top with diced onion and cilantro, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Enchiladas Suizas
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cooked and shredded
instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add heavy cream, white wine, and chicken broth; simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in cream cheese, cilantro, salt, and pepper until the sauce is smooth.
Spread sauce on each tortilla, place shredded chicken in the center, and roll up.
Place rolled tortillas seam-side down in a baking dish and pour remaining sauce over them.
Sprinkle with Monterey Jack cheese and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until bubbly.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblano chiles over an open flame until blackened, then peel off the skin and slit them open lengthwise.
Carefully remove the seeds and stems, leaving the chiles intact.
Stuff each chile generously with shredded cheese.
Dip each stuffed chile into the flour, then into the egg and milk mixture to coat lightly.
Fry chiles in hot oil until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels, serve hot with lime wedges on the side.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 12 large poblano chiles, roasted and peeled
instructions: Mix ground pork and beef with onions, garlic, prunes, raisins, salt, and pepper; stuff into roasted poblano chiles.
Bake stuffed chiles at 350°F (175°C) for 30 minutes.
Blend toasted nuts (pine, walnut, almond) with milk, eggs, cream, sugar, and cinnamon until smooth.
Pour walnut sauce over the baked chiles.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and serve immediately.

title: Mole Negro
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1/2 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and soaked
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and soaked
1/2 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and soaked
instructions: Roast chicken pieces in a dry pan until skin is dark and crispy, then remove and set aside.
Grind soaked chilies, toasted seeds, nuts, raisins, garlic, spices, and chicken broth into a smooth paste.
In a large pot, melt lard and fry the ground paste over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the roasted chicken pieces back into the pot and simmer for 45 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with warm tortillas.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast peppers over an open flame until charred, peel off skin, and stuff with a mixture of cheese.
Dip each stuffed pepper into flour, then into the beaten egg.
Fry peppers in hot oil until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with warm salsa verde.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried guajillo chilies, soaked and blended
instructions: Mix chilies, pineapple juice, achiote, vinegar, spices, and salt to create a marinade.
Marinate sliced pork for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Cook pork on a griddle or grill until caramelized and cooked through.
Warm tortillas on a dry pan.
Assemble tacos with pork, pineapple slices, cilantro, onion, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblano peppers until charred, peel, and stuff with a mixture of ground meat, onion, and cilantro.
Fry stuffed peppers in oil until golden brown and drain on paper towels.
Grind pine nuts, walnuts, and almonds into a paste.
Blend cream, milk, cinnamon, and cloves with the nut paste to make the sauce.
Serve peppers topped with the creamy sauce and pomegranate seeds.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Toast fideo noodles in oil until golden brown and crispy.
Add chopped onion and ground beef to the pan, cooking until beef is browned.
Stir in tomato sauce, beef broth, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until noodles are tender and liquid is absorbed.
Garnish with cilantro and queso fresco before serving.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 1 lb tomatillos, charred and blended with 2 garlic cloves and 1/2 cup water
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until skins are blackened, then peel and seed them.
Stuff each pepper with a generous amount of grated panela cheese.
Dip each stuffed pepper into the beaten egg mixture, ensuring it is fully coated.
Fry the peppers in hot lard or oil until golden brown on both sides.
Simmer the tomatillo sauce with salt until thickened.
Serve the fried peppers topped with the warm tomatillo sauce and garnished with cilantro.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 3 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried chipotle chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast the sesame seeds and almonds until golden, then grind both into a coarse paste.
In a blender, combine soaked chiles, sesame-almond paste, raisins, onion, tomato, chocolate, and broth.
Blend until completely smooth.
Heat lard in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Pour the mole sauce into the pan and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in the slivered almonds just before serving.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and soaked
1/4 cup dried chipotle chiles, stemmed and soaked
instructions: Blend soaked chiles, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, pepper, and salt to create a marinade.
Marinate the sliced pork in the mixture for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Cook the marinated pork in a skillet or on a grill until browned and cooked through.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame until soft.
Assemble tacos by placing pork on the tortilla, topped with pineapple slices, diced onion, and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblano peppers until charred, peel, seed, and stuff with a mixture of ground meat, onion, garlic, and spices (optional filling step).
Simmer the stuffed peppers in a tomato-based sauce with pomegranate molasses until tender.
In a blender, combine toasted walnuts, almonds, hazelnuts, chicken broth, cream, and butter until smooth.
In a separate saucepan, cook apples, pears, cranberries, raisins, and spices in white wine until softened.
Warm the walnut cream sauce and pour over the stuffed peppers.
Garnish with the fruit mixture and a generous sprinkling of pomegranate seeds.

title: Churros
instructions: Combine water, butter, salt, and sugar in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously over medium heat until the dough forms a ball and pulls away from the sides.
Transfer the dough to a bowl and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until fully incorporated.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a star tip with the dough.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer to 375°F (190°C).
Pipe long strips of dough directly into the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and immediately roll in the cinnamon-sugar mixture.

title: Mole Negro
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast and grind almonds, sesame seeds, and raisins until fine.
Toast and grind guajillo, mulato, and ancho chiles until smooth.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, tomatillos, cilantro, epazote, and hoja santa; cook until soft.
Combine ground chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, chocolate, spices, and broth in a pot.
Simmer mixture over low heat for 2 hours, stirring frequently.
Add chicken and simmer until cooked through and sauce thickens.
Garnish with additional sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast chiles until skins blister and blacken, then peel and stuff with chicken and cheese.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Mix shredded chicken with onion, garlic, and spices.
Stuff chiles with chicken mixture and secure with toothpicks.
Beat egg and milk together, dip chiles in batter.
Fry chiles in hot oil until golden brown.
Serve with rice and beans.

title: Tamales
instructions: Mix masa harina with lard, water, and chicken broth until smooth.
Sauté onion, garlic, pork, cheese, chiles, and herbs in oil.
Spread masa onto corn husks.
Place filling in center of each husk.
Fold husks over filling and steam for 1 hour.
Serve warm with salsa.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Sauté tomatillos, onion, garlic, cilantro, epazote, and hoja santa in oil until soft.
Blend mixture and strain into a sauce.
Fry tortillas briefly to soften.
Fill tortillas with chicken and roll up.
Place rolled tortillas in baking dish and pour sauce over.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes.
Serve with sour cream and cheese.

title: Pozole
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Boil pork and chicken until tender.
Add hominy and cook until soft.
Sauté onion, garlic, cilantro, epazote, and hoja santa in oil until soft.
Add mixture to pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve with lime, radishes, and cabbage.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 4 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried chipotle chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chiles, sesame seeds, almonds, raisins, bread, tomato, onion, and garlic in a dry skillet until fragrant.
Blend toasted ingredients with chiles, broth, and chocolate until smooth.
Simmer mixture in a pot with melted lard and chicken stock for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Serve over fried chicken or turkey.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblano peppers until skin blisters, peel, seed, and stuff with cheese.
Dip stuffed peppers in flour, then egg wash.
Fry peppers in lard until golden brown.
Simmer fried peppers in chicken broth with onion and garlic for 15 minutes.
Serve hot.

title: Tacos Al Pastor
instructions: Mix achiote paste, lime juice, cumin, coriander, garlic, onion, and pineapple to make marinade.
Marinate pork slices for 2 hours.
Grill or pan-fry pork until cooked through.
Warm corn tortillas in a dry skillet.
Assemble tacos with pork and pineapple on top.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Roast tomatillos, onion, and garlic until soft.
Blend roasted ingredients with broth until smooth.
Simmer sauce in lard for 10 minutes.
Fill tortillas with shredded chicken and roll them.
Bake rolled enchiladas in sauce at 350°F for 20 minutes.

title: Churros
instructions: Boil water, lard, sugar, and cinnamon in a pot.
Add flour all at once and stir until dough forms.
Let dough cool slightly, then beat in eggs one by one.
Pipe dough into hot oil to form long strips.
Roll in sugar and cinnamon mixture after frying.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 8 large dried Anaheim chiles, roasted and peeled
1 lb mild white cheese, such as queso blanco or Oaxaca cheese
instructions: Roast chiles over an open flame until skin blisters, then peel and stuff with shredded cheese.
Dip stuffed chiles into beaten egg, then coat lightly in flour mixed with salt.
Heat oil in a deep skillet over medium heat and fry chiles until golden brown on both sides.
In a separate pan, sauté onion and tomato in a little oil until softened.
Add chicken broth and simmer for 5 minutes to create a simple salsa.
Serve the fried chiles topped with the warm tomato and onion sauce.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 3 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried chipotle chile, stemmed and seeded
1 pound chicken thighs, cooked and shredded
instructions: Toast chiles, seeds, nuts, and raisins in a dry skillet until fragrant.
Soak chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Blend toasted ingredients, soaked chiles, onion, garlic, cinnamon, salt, and broth until smooth.
Heat lard in a heavy pot and fry the sauce mixture over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add shredded chicken and simmer for 10 more minutes to absorb the flavors.
Serve over steamed white rice with a side of tortillas.

title: Tamales
ingredients: 2 cups lard or vegetable shortening, softened
30 large corn husks, soaked in warm water
instructions: Grind soaked hominy into a paste with lard, baking powder, salt, cumin, oregano, and broth until smooth.
Mix in shredded chicken and cheese to create the filling.
Dip corn husks in warm water and pat dry.
Place a spoonful of masa on each husk, spread evenly, and top with chicken filling.
Fold the husks over the masa to form a packet and steam in a large pot for 1 hour.
Serve warm with salsa or mole sauce.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 8 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
instructions: Stuff poblano peppers with seasoned ground meat mixture and broil until lightly browned.
Blend walnuts, pomegranate seeds, vinegar, and a little water to create a pink relish.
In a separate bowl, blend milk, cream, egg yolk, and vanilla to make the nut sauce base.
Heat the nut sauce base in a saucepan, whisking constantly until thickened.
Place stuffed peppers on a platter, top with the thickened walnut sauce and relish.
Garnish with additional pomegranate seeds and serve immediately.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb chicken thighs, cut into chunks
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded
8 white corn tortillas, cut into triangles
instructions: Soak hominy in water for 2 hours, then drain.
Sear pork and chicken in a large pot until browned, then remove.
Sauté onions, garlic, and chiles in lard until fragrant, then add tomato sauce.
Return meat to pot, add hominy, cumin, cinnamon, salt, and 6 cups of water.
Simmer for 2 hours until meat and hominy are tender.
Shred meat and return to pot, stir in cilantro and radishes.
Serve in bowls topped with tortilla triangles, lime wedges, and extra cilantro.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend chiles, garlic, and 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Fry chocolate, raisins, almonds, and sesame seeds in oil until golden.
Combine fried mixture with chile sauce in a pot.
Add chicken, lard, and remaining water.
Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until chicken is tender.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 12 large poblano chiles, roasted and peeled
instructions: Roast chiles over an open flame until skin blisters, then peel and slice open.
Stuff each chile with shredded cheese and secure with toothpicks.
Dip stuffed chiles in flour, then egg wash.
Fry in oil until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Tacos al Pastor
instructions: Marinate pork with achiote paste, onion, garlic, and salt for 2 hours.
Cook pineapple, cilantro, and garlic in oil until soft.
Grill marinated pork until cooked through.
Warm tortillas on a griddle.
Assemble tacos with pork, pineapple mixture, and cilantro.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
instructions: Blend tomatillos, green chiles, cilantro, onion, and garlic into a sauce.
Fry sauce in oil until thickened.
Fill tortillas with shredded chicken.
Place filled tortillas in a baking dish.
Pour sauce over tortillas, top with sour cream, and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 12 large poblano chiles, roasted and peeled
instructions: Stuff chiles with seasoned ground meat mixture.
Blend walnuts, apple, pear, and pomegranate seeds into a sauce.
Fry meat mixture in oil until cooked.
Place stuffed chiles in a baking dish.
Pour walnut sauce over chiles and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend chilies, pineapple, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, pepper, and salt into a smooth marinade.
Marinate pork slices for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a skillet or comal over medium-high heat with lard or oil.
Cook marinated pork in batches until browned and cooked through, turning occasionally.
Warm tortillas on the comal until pliable.
Slice cooked pork into thin strips.
Serve pork on warm tortillas topped with onion, tomato, and a slice of fresh pineapple.
Garnish with lime wedges.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Toast almonds, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, and pepitas in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend soaked chilies, toasted nuts, seeds, raisins, bread, chocolate, sugar, onion, garlic, cinnamon, pepper, and 1 cup of broth into a smooth sauce.
Heat lard in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Pour the blended sauce over the chicken and stir well.
Add remaining broth and simmer covered for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add chicken pieces back to the pot if they were removed earlier.
Simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes until thickened and flavors meld.
Serve hot over rice or with bread.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 1/2 cup pork loin, cooked and chopped
instructions: Roast poblano chilies over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred.
Peel, stem, and seed the chilies.
Halve chilies lengthwise and stuff with cheese and pork mixture.
Dip each stuffed chili into flour, then into beaten egg.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry chiles until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.
In a separate pan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add tomato, chicken broth, and salt; simmer until sauce thickens.
Serve chiles topped with the warm tomato sauce.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblano chilies over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred.
Peel, stem, and seed the chilies.
Halve chilies lengthwise and stuff with a mixture of raisins, pine nuts, and pomegranate seeds.
Toast walnuts, bread, and milk in a bowl until bread is soft.
Blend toasted walnuts, soaked bread, eggs, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt into a smooth sauce.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry stuffed chiles until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.
In a separate pan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add chicken broth and simmer until sauce thickens.
Serve chiles topped with the warm walnut sauce and garnish with pomegranate seeds.

title: Cochinita Pibil
instructions: Marinate pork cubes in achiote paste, vinegar, orange juice, garlic, oregano, pepper, and salt for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Chop banana leaves and place them in a large pot or slow cooker.
Add marinated pork, pork fat, onion, tomato, and chicken broth to the pot.
Cover with banana leaves and cook on low heat for 3-4 hours until tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove banana leaves and serve hot with rice and fried plantains.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 4 dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 dried pasilla chili, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend chilies with garlic, onion, and 1/2 cup chicken broth until smooth.
Toast sesame, pumpkin, and pumpkin seeds separately in a dry pan.
Toast almonds and peanuts in a dry pan until fragrant.
Combine all toasted nuts and seeds with raisins and almonds in a blender.
Blend the nut mixture with the chili sauce and melted chocolate.
Fry the blended mixture in lard until it thickens and turns dark.
Stir in oaxaca cheese until melted and smooth.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, adding more broth if needed.
Serve over fried chicken or turkey.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblanos over an open flame until charred, then peel and seed.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of crumbled queso fresco and bread crumbs.
Dip each stuffed pepper in beaten egg to coat completely.
Fry peppers in vegetable oil until golden brown on all sides.
In a separate pan, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add ground beef and cook until browned.
Stir in tomato sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix in cilantro and serve over the fried peppers.
Garnish with oaxaca cheese before serving.

title: Tamales
instructions: Soak corn husks in warm water for 1 hour until pliable.
Melt lard and stir into masa harina with chicken broth and egg.
Fold in cooked rice, diced pork, tomato sauce, cilantro, and onion.
Place a spoonful of filling on each soaked corn husk.
Fold the husk over the filling to form a triangle.
Steam tamales in a pot lined with more husks for 1 hour.
Serve hot with oaxaca cheese sprinkled on top.

title: Enchiladas Suizas
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in lard until soft.
Add chicken broth, cream cheese, sour cream, and lime juice to make sauce.
Simmer sauce until slightly thickened.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken and oaxaca cheese.
Roll tortillas and place in a baking dish.
Pour sauce over rolled tortillas.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 20 minutes until bubbly.
Garnish with cilantro before serving.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast poblanos over an open flame until charred, then peel and seed.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of ground meat, onion, and garlic.
Blend toasted nuts, seeds, and raisins with sesame seeds and almonds.
Fry the blended mixture in lard until it thickens and turns dark.
Stir in oaxaca cheese until melted and smooth.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, adding more broth if needed.
Serve over fried chicken or turkey.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 4 oz dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 oz dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 oz dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Roast chicken pieces in a hot oven until browned.
Soak chiles in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Toast nuts and seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
