Blend soaked chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, raisins, onion, garlic, chocolate, cinnamon, and cumin into a smooth paste.
Sauté chicken in oil until golden, then remove from pan.
Add the sauce mixture to the pan with broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan, cover, and simmer for another 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve.

title: Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until charred, then peel and devein.
Stuff the peppers with a mixture of ground beef, onion, garlic, tomato sauce, cheese, and salt.
Dip the stuffed peppers into the beaten egg mixture, then coat with flour.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the peppers until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Blend chiles, pineapple, onion, tomato, cilantro, achiote paste, vinegar, oil, and salt into a marinade.
Marinate pork slices for at least 2 hours.
Grill or pan-fry marinated pork until cooked through.
Warm tortillas on a griddle.
Assemble tacos with pork, pineapple, and onion.
Serve immediately.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cooked and shredded
instructions: Blend tomatillos, onion, garlic, cilantro, and broth into a sauce.
Sauté the sauce in oil until thickened.
Dip tortillas in the sauce, then fill with shredded chicken.
Roll tortillas and place in a baking dish.
Pour remaining sauce over the enchiladas and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes.
Garnish with sour cream and green onions before serving.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chilies, seeds, nuts, and spices in a dry skillet until fragrant, then grind into a paste.
Fry diced lardons until golden, add onion and garlic, cook until soft.
Add the ground paste to the pan and fry for 5 minutes to cook the raw flavor.
Stir in the chocolate and continue frying until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add broths, salt, and sugar, then simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Place chicken pieces in a baking dish, pour the mole over them, and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 12 poblano chilies, roasted, peeled, and stemmed
instructions: Stuff the roasted chilies with a mixture of seasoned ground pork and cook until firm.
Toast walnuts, pine nuts, and almonds, then blend with pomegranate molasses, broth, and spices until smooth.
Simmer the walnut sauce over low heat until it thickens to a creamy consistency.
Fry the sliced onions in vinegar and sugar until translucent and slightly caramelized.
Arrange the stuffed chilies on a platter, top with the walnut sauce and pomegranate seeds.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/4 cup dried chipotle chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 white onion, sliced into thin rings
instructions: Soak chilies in warm water, then blend with vinegar, oil, water, and spices to make a marinade.
Marinate the sliced pork with pineapple for at least 2 hours, then skewer the meat and fruit.
Cook the skewers on a grill or comal until the meat is charred and cooked through.
Warm the corn tortillas on the comal until soft and pliable.
Assemble tacos with meat, onion, tomato, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

title: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Fry the onion, tomato, cilantro, chilies, cumin, and salt in lard until the sauce thickens.
Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Warm the corn tortillas in the lard until crisp.
Place two eggs on each tortilla, top with the sauce, cheese, avocado, and sour cream.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 12 poblano chilies, roasted, peeled, and stemmed
instructions: Stuff the roasted chilies with cheese, then dip them in an egg batter.
Fry the chiles in oil until golden brown and crisp.
In a separate pot, make a sauce with chicken broth, flour, and oil, then add cheese to thicken.
Arrange the fried chiles on a platter and pour the cheese sauce over them.
Serve warm with rice and beans.

title: Mole Negro
ingredients: 1 lb turkey thighs, cut into pieces
1/2 cup dried mulato chiles, stems removed
instructions: Toast the chiles in a dry pan until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast the sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, almonds, garlic, and onion until golden.
Blend the soaked chiles with the toasted ingredients, chocolate, raisins, oregano, and broth until smooth.
In a large pot, heat the oil and fry the turkey pieces until browned.
Pour the mole sauce over the turkey and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 lbs sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 head nopal cactus, cleaned and chopped
instructions: Mix the achiote paste, sour orange juice, vinegar, oregano, cilantro, and onion to make the marinade.
Marinate the pork, sweet potatoes, and nopal in the mixture for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Line a large clay pot or Dutch oven with banana leaves and place the marinated ingredients inside.
Cover with more banana leaves and seal tightly with foil or a lid.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 3 hours until the pork is tender and falling apart.
Serve with rice and fried plantains.

title: Sopa de Azuay
ingredients: 1/2 lb octopus, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add the rice, green beans, and corn, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the octopus and shrimp, cooking until the shrimp turn pink and the octopus is tender.
Stir in the lime juice, cilantro, salt, and pepper.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Tamales Veracruces
instructions: Mix the masa harina, melted lard, water, and hominy until smooth and sticky.
In a separate bowl, combine the green chilies, cilantro, cheese, pork fat, onion, tomato, and garlic.
Soak the corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons of masa onto each husk, place a small amount of filling in the center.
Fold the husks around the filling to form a triangle.
Steam the tamales in a steamer for 1 hour until the masa pulls away from the husk.
Serve warm with a side of salsa.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 6 large poblano chiles, roasted and peeled
instructions: Roast the poblano chiles over an open flame until charred, then peel and stuff with the ground pork mixture.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion, tomato, garlic, bread crumbs, milk, sour cream, cheese, and cilantro until thick.
Add the chicken broth and vegetable oil to the pan and bring to a simmer.
Drop the stuffed chiles into the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve hot with rice and beans.

title: Mole Poblano with Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces, bone-in and skin-on
6 dried mulato chiles, stems removed and toasted
6 dried ancho chiles, stems removed and toasted
1/2 cup dark chocolate, broken into pieces
instructions: Roast chicken pieces over an open flame until skin is charred, then boil in water until tender. Remove and reserve the broth.
Toast dried chiles separately in a dry pan until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast sesame, pumpkin seeds, and raisins in a dry pan until golden.
Roast garlic cloves and onion halves directly over the flame until blackened.
Blend tomatillos, soaked chiles, toasted seeds, raisins, garlic, onion, chocolate, and a splash of reserved chicken broth until smooth.
In a large pot, heat lard over medium heat. Add the blended sauce and cook for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and serve hot with warm corn tortillas.

title: Barbacoa de Oveja
ingredients: 1 whole lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
2 dried guajillo chiles, toasted and seeded
1 dried ancho chile, toasted and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chiles in a dry pan until fragrant, then remove stems and seeds.
Place lamb chunks in a large pot and add water to cover by 2 inches.
Add the quartered onion, halved garlic, toasted chiles, cumin, oregano, and bay leaves to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover tightly. Simmer for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the meat from the bone and shred it into coarse strips.
Strain the cooking liquid and reserve it for making consomé or gravy.
Serve the shredded meat with warm corn tortillas and fresh cilantro.

title: Tamales de Maíz con Relleno de Carnitas
ingredients: 2 lbs dried white corn husks, cleaned and soaked
2 cups masa harina (corn flour for tamales)
instructions: Cook the pork shoulder with onion, garlic, orange juice, water, and oregano until tender. Shred the meat and mix with some of the cooking liquid.
In a large bowl, whisk together masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add the melted lard to the dry mixture, stirring until a thick, smooth paste forms.
Divide the meat filling into small portions.
Lay a soaked corn husk flat, spread a layer of masa, place a portion of meat in the center, and fold the husk to enclose the filling.
Steam the tamales in a large pot lined with wet towels or banana leaves for 45 to 60 minutes.
Unwrap and serve immediately while warm.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast the poblano chiles over an open flame until the skins are charred, then peel, devein, and stuff with the meat mixture.
For the meat filling, brown the pork and beef with onion and garlic. Add the apple, pear, onion, pomegranate molasses, spices, and salt. Cook until thickened, then cool.
For the walnut sauce, grind toasted walnuts, pine nuts, cinnamon, cloves, and a little water in a blender until smooth.
Boil the sauce in a pot for 15 minutes to cook out the raw nut flavor, then adjust consistency with water if needed.
Stuff the chiles with the meat mixture and arrange them in a serving dish.
Pour the warm walnut sauce over the stuffed chiles.
Garnish generously with fresh pomegranate seeds and serve with rice.

title: Pozole Rojo Tradicional
ingredients: 2 lbs dried white hominy, soaked overnight
3 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
6 dried guajillo chiles, toasted and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, toasted and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chiles in a dry pan until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 30 minutes.
In a large pot, combine the pork chunks, garlic, onion, peppercorns, oregano, and bay leaves with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the drained hominy to the pot and continue simmering for another 1.5 to 2 hours until the hominy is tender and the meat is falling apart.
Blend the soaked chiles with a little of the cooking liquid until smooth.
Add the blended chile sauce to the pot and simmer for another 30 minutes until the broth turns a deep red color.
Season with salt to taste and remove the bay leaves.
Serve in large bowls topped with shredded cabbage, diced onion, radishes, and lime wedges.

title: Huevos Rancheros
ingredients: 1 cup corn tortillas, cut into quarters
instructions: Fry the tortilla quarters in lard until golden and crispy, then set aside on paper towels.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and cook in a separate skillet until just set but still soft.
Warm the tomato salsa in a small saucepan until bubbling.
Place two tortilla quarters on each of two plates.
Top each with two eggs, a generous ladle of hot salsa, a sprinkle of queso fresco, and chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Ceviche de Camarón
ingredients: 1 cup sweet potato, boiled and cubed
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the diced onion, minced jalapeño, and chopped cilantro.
Add the cubed sweet potato and toss gently to coat.
Pour the lime juice over the mixture and let it sit for 5 minutes to mellow the onion flavor.
Add the raw shrimp and the cherry tomatoes, tossing carefully to mix.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes until the shrimp turns opaque pink.
Serve cold, optionally with a pinch of salt and extra lime wedges.

title: Tacos de Asada
ingredients: Salsa verde or roja to taste
instructions: Rub the beef steak with vegetable oil, toasted cumin, and garlic powder, then let it marinate for 1 hour.
Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill over high heat until very hot.
Sear the steak for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked to your liking.
Slice the rested meat thinly against the grain.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan until pliable.
Pile the sliced meat onto the tortillas, topped with fresh onion, cilantro, and a dollop of salsa.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the chiles, sesame seeds, peanuts, almonds, garlic, and cinnamon in a dry pan until fragrant.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain and blend with the toasted ingredients, broth, and chicken fat until smooth.
In a heavy pot, fry the chocolate and ground cinnamon in a little fat until it melts and darkens.
Pour in the chile sauce and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the shredded chicken and simmer for another 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve over rice with tortillas.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Toast the vermicelli noodles in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown.
In a large pot, heat the lard and sauté the onion until soft.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the toasted noodles and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until noodles are tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove from heat, and stir in the cheese and cilantro.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Mole Negro
ingredients: 2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried pasilla chile, stemmed and seeded
1 dried chipotle chile, stemmed and seeded
1 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Toast sesame seeds, pepitas, cinnamon, cloves, and anise seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend toasted seeds, chiles, chocolate, stock, onion, tomato, and garlic until smooth.
Heat lard in a large pot over medium heat and fry the blended sauce until it turns dark and thickens.
Add chicken thighs to the pot, ensuring they are fully submerged in the mole.
Simmer covered on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce coats the meat.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and return to the pot to heat through.

title: Tlayuda
instructions: Brush the large thin tortilla generously with melted lard.
Spread a thick layer of refried black beans over the tortilla.
Top evenly with shredded cheese, ensuring full coverage.
Place the tlayuda in a hot cast-iron skillet and cook until the bottom is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Arrange shredded chicken, avocado slices, pico de gallo, radishes, and cilantro on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chili powder before serving with lime wedges.

title: Tlayuda
instructions: Brush the large thin tortilla generously with melted lard.
Spread a thick layer of refried black beans over the tortilla.
Top evenly with shredded cheese, ensuring full coverage.
Place the tlayuda in a hot cast-iron skillet and cook until the bottom is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Arrange shredded chicken, avocado slices, pico de gallo, radishes, and cilantro on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chili powder before serving with lime wedges.

instructions: Brush the large thin tortilla generously with melted lard.
Spread a thick layer of refried black beans over the tortilla.
Top evenly with shredded cheese, ensuring full coverage.
Place the tlayuda in a hot cast-iron skillet and cook until the bottom is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Arrange shredded chicken, avocado slices, pico de gallo, radishes, and cilantro on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chili powder before serving with lime wedges.

title: Tlayuda
instructions: Brush the large thin tortilla generously with melted lard.
Spread a thick layer of refried black beans over the tortilla.
Top evenly with shredded cheese, ensuring full coverage.
Place the tlayuda in a hot cast-iron skillet and cook until the bottom is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Arrange shredded chicken, avocado slices, pico de gallo, radishes, and cilantro on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chili powder before serving with lime wedges.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried chipotle chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup Spanish black olives, pitted and chopped
instructions: Simmer chicken thighs in a pot with broth, onion, garlic, and epazote until tender, about 45 minutes. Remove chicken and reserve the liquid.
Toast chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant, then rehydrate in hot water for 15 minutes.
Toast sesame seeds, peanuts, pumpkin seeds, and raisins separately until golden.
Grind toasted seeds, nuts, and raisins into a coarse paste in a blender or molcajete.
Blend chiles with the reserved chicken liquid and remaining ingredients until smooth.
Heat lard in a heavy pot and fry the mole paste for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the cooked chicken back into the sauce and simmer for another 20 minutes until thickened.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with white rice and fried plantains.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 1 lb poblano chiles, roasted and peeled
instructions: Roast poblano chiles over an open flame until charred, peel, and stuff with the seasoned meat mixture.
Fry the stuffed chiles in lard until golden brown.
Toast pine nuts, walnuts, and almonds in a dry skillet.
Blend toasted nuts with pomegranate juice, spices, and cinnamon stick until smooth.
Simmer the nut mixture with heavy cream, sugar, and salt for 10 minutes to create the nogada sauce.
Place the fried chiles on a plate and pour the warm walnut sauce over them.
Garnish generously with fresh pomegranate seeds and serve immediately.

title: Tamales de Elote
ingredients: 1 lb fresh corn dough (masa de maíz)
instructions: Mix corn dough with lard, water, baking powder, and salt until smooth.
Combine grated corn, onion, green chilies, cilantro, cumin, oregano, broth, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Spread a thin layer of masa onto each corn husk.
Place a spoonful of the corn filling in the center of the husk.
Fold the husk over the filling and tie with string.
Steam the tamales in a large pot with water for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Let them rest for 10 minutes before serving warm.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb dried red chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast red chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant, then rehydrate in hot water for 15 minutes.
Sear pork shoulder in a large pot with lard, onion, garlic, epazote, and cilantro.
Add the rehydrated chiles, water, spices, and salt to the pot.
Simmer the pork in the chile broth for 2 hours until tender.
Stir in the drained hominy and cook for another 30 minutes.
Add the cooked pork ribs to the pot and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Serve in bowls topped with shredded cabbage, radishes, diced onion, lime juice, oaxaca cheese, and avocado.

title: Chapulines
ingredients: 1 lb fresh grasshoppers, cleaned and deheaded
instructions: Dust the grasshoppers with flour and fry them in lard until golden brown and crispy.
Remove the grasshoppers from the oil and set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the same oil until translucent.
Add the chili powder, salt, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, and onion powder to the onion mixture.
Stir in the lime juice, cilantro, and epazote, cooking for 2 minutes.
Toss the fried grasshoppers in the spice mixture until well coated.
Serve immediately as a snack or appetizer with tortillas.

title: Pollo Pibil
ingredients: 1 lb achiote paste, made from annatto seeds
1 cup white corn flour, toadstool style
instructions: Mix achiote paste, sour orange juice, cilantro, and epazote leaves to make the marinade.
Rub the marinade thoroughly over the chicken pieces and let rest for at least 2 hours.
Wrap the chicken tightly in large banana leaves.
Place the wrapped chicken in a clay pot or Dutch oven and cover with a layer of corn flour.
Bake covered in a very low oven or underground for 3 to 4 hours until tender.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ingredients: 3 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Combine achiote paste, sour orange juice, cilantro, epazote, onion, and garlic in a bowl.
Toss the pork chunks in the marinade and let sit overnight in the refrigerator.
Wrap the marinated pork tightly in banana leaves.
Cook the wrapped pork in an underground pit or a covered pot at very low heat for 4 to 5 hours.
Slice the cooked pork and serve with warm corn tortillas and pickled onions.

title: Panuchos
ingredients: 2 cups fried black beans, seasoned with garlic and cumin
instructions: Fry the plantain slices until golden and set aside.
Season the black beans with garlic, cumin, and salt, then keep warm.
Layer a corn tortilla with plantain slices, seasoned beans, cabbage, lettuce, and tomato.
Top with a generous amount of queso fresco and a sprinkle of green onion.
Cover with another corn tortilla and serve warm, optionally with a side of fried eggs.

title: Sopa de Lima
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
1/2 cup white corn flour, for thickening (optional)
instructions: Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add the rinsed rice and cook until tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice, olive oil, cilantro, and epazote.
Season generously with salt and black pepper.
If the soup is too thin, mix a little corn flour with water and stir it in until the desired consistency is reached.

title: Salbutes
instructions: Heat the corn tortillas on a dry skillet until they puff up slightly.
In a small bowl, mix mayonnaise, diced tomato, and green onion to make the sauce.
Place a layer of shredded cabbage and lettuce on the warm tortilla.
Add a slice of fried plantain and top with crumbled queso fresco.
Drizzle the mayonnaise mixture over the top and serve immediately.

title: Carne en Salsa Verde con Nopalitos
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 lb nopalitos, cleaned and cut into 2-inch strips
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a blender, combine tomatillos, cilantro stems, jalapeños, onion, water, oregano, and cumin; blend until smooth.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat; season beef with salt and pepper, then brown all sides.
Pour the green sauce over the beef, stir to coat, and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1 hour until beef is tender.
Stir in the nopalitos and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve hot with warm corn tortillas.

title: Pozole Rojo con Rábanos
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb pork belly, cut into cubes
4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
Carrots, cabbage, and radishes for garnish
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak in warm water for 20 minutes.
In a large pot, combine pork shoulder, pork belly, bay leaves, and enough water to cover; simmer for 2 hours until meat is tender.
While meat simmers, blend soaked chiles with onion, garlic, cilantro, and water until smooth.
Strain the chile sauce into the pot with the pork; stir well and simmer for 30 minutes.
Drain the soaked hominy and add it to the pot along with the pork belly; cook for another 20 minutes.
Season with salt, ladle into bowls, and top with lime wedges, shredded cabbage, carrots, radishes, and crushed corn chips.

title: Mole Poblano Casero
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
instructions: Toast chiles in a dry pan until fragrant, then blend with onion, garlic, cinnamon, bay leaves, cumin, and water until smooth.
In a large pot, fry almonds, sesame seeds, and pepitas in oil until golden; remove and set aside.
Sauté remaining chiles in the same oil until soft, then blend with the first mixture.
Add the blended chile mixture to the pot; stir in raisins and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the ground nuts and seeds; cook for another 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the melted chocolate and stir until fully incorporated; season with salt.
Place chicken thighs in the sauce, cover, and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Serve hot over rice with additional sesame seeds and cream on top.

title: Tamales de Elote con Guisado de Cerdo
ingredients: 12 corn husks, soaked in warm water
instructions: In a blender, combine tomatillos, onion, garlic, cilantro stems, water, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; blend until smooth.
Heat lard in a pot; add pork cubes and cook until browned.
Pour the green sauce over the pork, stir well, and simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
In a separate bowl, mix corn kernels, cheese, green onion, raisins, and 1/4 cup of the green sauce.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place a corn husk on a work surface; spread a thin layer of lard on the inner side.
Spoon the meat mixture onto the husk, then top with the corn and cheese mixture.
Fold the husk around the filling, securing with a toothpick or string.
Place tamales in a steamer basket over boiling water; cover and steam for 45 minutes.
Serve hot with additional salsa verde on the side.

title: Chiles Rellenos de Queso y Tocineta
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skin is charred; peel, seed, and slice lengthwise, leaving the stem intact.
In a pot, sauté onion and garlic in butter until translucent; add tomato, cilantro, water, oregano, cumin, and salt; simmer for 15 minutes.
In a separate pan, cook pork belly with sliced onion until crispy; set aside.
Stuff each pepper with a mixture of cheese and pork belly.
Dip stuffed peppers into beaten eggs, ensuring they are fully coated.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat; fry peppers until golden brown on all sides.
While frying, make a béchamel sauce by melting butter, adding flour, and gradually stirring in milk until thickened; stir in cheese until melted.
Serve hot peppers topped with béchamel sauce and garnished with corn chips.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
10 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and toasted
6 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and toasted
instructions: Roast the tomatillos, chiles, and nuts in an oven until charred but not burnt.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Toast the sesame seeds and peanuts in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend the chiles, tomatillos, seeds, nuts, garlic, and half the broth into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the lard over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the chocolate and remaining broth until melted and smooth.
Simmer the sauce for 20 minutes to develop flavor.
Roast the chicken separately until cooked through and serve it over rice with the mole.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 6 large poblano peppers, roasted and peeled
1 lb ground pork, 1/2 lb ground beef, 1/2 lb ground turkey
instructions: Stuff the roasted poblano peppers with a mixture of ground meats, onions, and spices.
Simmer the stuffed peppers in a tomato-based sauce for 1 hour.
Blend the pine nuts, walnuts, cream, and milk into a smooth white sauce.
Heat the sauce gently until thickened but not boiling.
Assemble the dish by placing the stuffed peppers on a plate.
Pour the walnut sauce over the peppers and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds.
Garnish with a few leaves of parsley.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried guajillo chiles, toasted and blended
1/4 cup dried ancho chiles, toasted and blended
1/4 cup dried chipotle chiles, toasted and blended
instructions: Marinate the pork slices in the blended chile mixture, onion, and spices for at least 2 hours.
Sear the marinated pork in a hot pan or on a grill until browned and cooked through.
Add pineapple chunks to the pan to caramelize slightly.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet or over an open flame.
Assemble the tacos by placing the pork and pineapple on the tortillas.
Top with diced onion and fresh cilantro.
Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, toasted and stemmed
instructions: Fry the tortilla triangles until crisp and golden.
Blend the roasted tomatillos, chiles, onion, and half the broth into a smooth red sauce.
Simmer the sauce over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the fried tortillas and let it sit for 2 minutes to soften slightly.
Top with sour cream, queso fresco, and cilantro.
Garnish with sliced radishes and serve immediately with extra broth on the side.

title: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Fry the corn tortillas until crisp and set aside on paper towels.
Blend the roasted tomatillos, chiles, onion, and broth into a smooth red sauce.
Simmer the sauce over medium heat for 10 minutes until thickened.
Poach or scramble the eggs in a separate pan.
Place two fried tortillas on each of four plates.
Top each tortilla with a poached or scrambled egg.
Pour the red sauce over the eggs and garnish with cilantro, queso fresco, avocado, and sour cream.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 2 cups dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
1 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Soak chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until soft.
Toast peanuts, sesame seeds, and almonds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Grind soaked chilies, toasted nuts, garlic, onion, tomato, and spices into a smooth paste using a molcajete or blender.
Heat lard or oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Fry the chili paste slowly, stirring constantly, for about 30 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Stir in chicken broth, panela, and salt to balance the heat and sweetness.
Simmer for another 15 minutes, adding more broth if needed to reach a pouring consistency.

title: Rajas con Crema
ingredients: 1 bunch poblano peppers, roasted, peeled, and sliced into strips
1 cup fresh corn kernels, cut from the cob
instructions: Melt butter or lard in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until soft and translucent.
Add the corn kernels and cook for 3 minutes until they begin to pop slightly.
Add the roasted poblano strips and stir to coat in the fat.
Sprinkle in cumin and salt, then pour in the chicken broth.
Reduce heat and stir in the heavy cream.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Carnitas
ingredients: 2 whole pork shoulders, about 4 pounds each
instructions: Score the pork shoulders in a diamond pattern and season generously with salt, pepper, and oregano.
In a large pot, sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add pork, orange juice, broth, and bay leaves to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover. Simmer for 3 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Remove pork from the liquid and let it cool completely.
Cut the cooled pork into large chunks.
Heat a deep pot or Dutch oven with oil over medium-high heat.
Fry the pork chunks in batches, turning frequently, until golden brown and crispy on the outside (about 15-20 minutes).
Serve immediately, shredding some pieces for the interior while leaving others whole.

title: Gorditas de Elote
ingredients: 2 cups masa harina (corn flour for tortillas)
1 cup fresh corn kernels, cut from the cob
2 green chilies, roasted, peeled, and diced
instructions: Mix masa harina, salt, and lard in a bowl; gradually add warm water until a soft dough forms.
Wrap dough in a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal balls and flatten each into a thick disc.
Place each disc on a hot comal or griddle and cook until bubbles form on one side.
Flip and cook until both sides are lightly browned.
Cut each cooked corn cake horizontally without cutting all the way through.
Fill the pockets with a mixture of corn, onion, cilantro, and green chilies.
Top with sour cream and crumbled cotija cheese.
Serve warm with lime wedges on the side.

title: Sopa de Fideo
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft.
Add ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Sprinkle fideo evenly over the meat and stir to toast lightly for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in oregano, salt, and pepper.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until noodles are tender.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh cilantro.
Serve in bowls with lime slices on top.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 1/2 cup raisins, soaked in warm water
1/2 cup dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chilies, seeds, and spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend chilies, tomatoes, garlic, onion, and spices with enough broth to form a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in lard over medium heat until it darkens and oil rises to the surface.
Stir in the ground nuts, raisins, chocolate, and remaining broth.
Simmer the sauce gently for 30 minutes until thickened.
Cook the chicken in the sauce until tender and fully coated.

title: Tacos de Canasta
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced
2 cups dried corn husks, soaked in water
instructions: Season the sliced beef with salt and cumin.
Soak corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes until soft.
Remove the corn from the husks, leaving the kernels intact.
Place kernels in a basket lined with a soaked husk.
Fry the basket in hot oil for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with cilantro and onion.
Serve immediately with lime wedges and hot sauce.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1/2 lb pork ribs, cut into chunks
1/2 lb corn tortillas, torn into pieces
4 dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chilies in a dry pan until fragrant and soften.
Blend chilies, garlic, onion, and spices with 1 cup of broth to make a paste.
Sear pork in a large pot until browned on all sides.
Add the blended chili paste and remaining broth to the pot.
Simmer the pork for 2 hours until tender.
Add torn tortillas to the pot and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Serve in bowls topped with shredded cabbage, radishes, onion, and cilantro.

title: Chiles en Nogada
ingredients: 12 green poblano chilies, roasted and seeded
instructions: Roast chilies until charred, peel, and stuff with a mixture of beef, pork, onion, and tomato.
Fry stuffed chilies in oil until golden brown.
Blend almonds, walnuts, sesame seeds, and pomegranate molasses with broth.
Strain the mixture to remove solids and whisk until smooth.
Spoon the walnut sauce over the fried chilies.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and fresh parsley.

title: Quesadillas de Queso Fresco y Guacamole
instructions: Mash avocados with lime juice, salt, and a pinch of onion for guacamole.
Place a tortilla on a griddle and sprinkle with queso fresco and cotija.
Fold the tortilla in half and cook until golden and cheese melts.
Serve immediately with a generous side of guacamole, diced tomato, and cilantro.

title: Carne Asada a la Sonorense
ingredients: 1.5 lbs flank steak, cut into strips
instructions: Mix garlic, cilantro, lime juice, oil, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss the steak strips with the marinade and let sit for 30 minutes.
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill over high heat.
Cook the steak for 3-4 minutes per side until charred but still juicy.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving with warm tortillas.

title: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Heat lard in a skillet and sauté onion, garlic, and bell pepper until soft.
Add tomatoes, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes.
Fry eggs in the same pan until whites are set but yolks are runny.
Place a tortilla on a plate, top with two fried eggs, then spoon the salsa over.
Serve immediately with extra salsa on the side.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ingredients: 1 lb farmer cheese or queso fresco, crumbled
instructions: Roast peppers over an open flame until skins blister, then peel and seed.
Mix cheese with salt, pepper, and half the onion; stuff into peppers.
Dip stuffed peppers in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on all sides.
Serve hot with the remaining onion, garlic, and tomato sauce simmered together.

title: Mole Poblano (Simplified)
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast chiles, almonds, and sesame seeds separately until fragrant.
Blend toasted chiles, raisins, almonds, sesame seeds, onion, garlic, and chocolate with a bit of broth until smooth.
Fry the sauce in lard until it darkens and thickens, stirring constantly.
Simmer chicken in a separate pot with broth until tender.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and serve with rice.

title: Gazpacho de Tomate
ingredients: 4 large ripe tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup fresh bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Soak bread in water for 10 minutes, then squeeze dry.
Blend tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, bread, oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to let flavors meld.
Stir in chopped parsley before serving.
Serve chilled with a drizzle of extra olive oil.

title: Mole Negro de Oaxaca
ingredients: 2 cups chicken or turkey stock, warm
1/2 cup dried mulato chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried pasilla chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup dried chipotle chilies, stemmed and seeded
1/2 cup raisins, soaked in warm water
instructions: Toast sesame, pumpkin, and black sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden; set aside.
Toast almonds in a dry pan until fragrant; set aside.
Fry chopped onion and garlic in lard until soft; set aside.
Grind toasted seeds, toasted almonds, fried onion, garlic, chilies, raisins, cinnamon, cumin, oregano, and fried tortillas into a smooth paste using a stone grinder or blender.
In a large pot, heat the lard and fry the ground paste over medium heat, stirring constantly for 15 minutes until it darkens.
Add the chopped chocolate, stirring continuously until melted and incorporated.
Gradually add the warm stock and water, stirring to combine.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes to an hour, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.
Serve over roasted chicken or turkey.

title: Tlayudas de Oaxaca
ingredients: 2 cups nopales (prickly pear cactus), chopped and drained
instructions: Mix flour, lard, salt, and warm water to form a stiff dough; let rest for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 equal portions and roll each into a large thin circle on an oiled surface.
Preheat a large comal or griddle over medium-high heat.
Cook each dough circle on the comal for 3-4 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Spread cooked beans in a thin layer over the hot tlayuda.
Top with chopped nopales, shredded cheese, chorizo, and shredded chicken.
Fold the edges of the tlayuda over the filling.
Drizzle with warm mole salsa and garnish with shredded lettuce and cilantro.
Serve immediately while hot and crispy.

title: Tacos de Calabaza
ingredients: 1 lb butternut squash, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss squash chunks with cinnamon, cumin, cayenne, and a pinch of salt.
Roast squash on a baking sheet for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
While roasting, warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.
In a small saucepan, melt lard and add the chicken broth.
Pour the warm broth over the roasted squash in the baking dish and let it soak for 5 minutes.
Mash the squash gently with a fork, leaving some chunks for texture.
Assemble tacos by placing a spoonful of squash mixture on each warm tortilla.
Top with crumbled cheese, diced onion, and cilantro.
Serve immediately with warm salsa verde on the side.

title: Quesabirrias
ingredients: 1 lb beef brisket or skirt steak, thinly sliced
instructions: Brown the thinly sliced beef in a hot skillet with lard until crispy on the outside.
Add diced onion and garlic to the skillet and cook until soft.
Stir in oregano, cumin, and warm salsa roja; cook for another 2 minutes.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry skillet until pliable.
Place a spoonful of the beef mixture on half of each tortilla.
Sprinkle crumbled cheese over the beef.
Fold the tortilla over the filling to create a half-moon shape.
Place folded tacos on a very hot skillet or comal.
Cook for 1-2 minutes per side until the cheese melts and the tortilla is crispy.
Garnish with sliced onions and cilantro before serving.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb pork ribs, cut into chunks
12 dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
12 dried arbol chilies, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chilies in a dry pan until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
In a large pot, fry the onion and garlic in lard until golden.
Add the pork shoulder and ribs to the pot and brown on all sides.
Drain the soaked chilies and add them to the pot along with the onion-garlic mixture.
Add oregano, cumin, and salt; stir to combine.
Add 8 cups of water to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the bones and shred the meat; return the meat to the pot.
Add the cooked hominy to the pot and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Serve in large bowls topped with chopped cabbage, radishes, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.
Provide extra salsa roja on the side for dipping.

title: Pollo Pibil
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1 banana leaf or large aluminum foil sheet
instructions: Marinate chicken with achiote, orange juice, vinegar, epazote, and cilantro for at least 4 hours.
Line a baking dish with banana leaves or foil.
Place chicken and plantain slices in the dish, pouring some marinade over them.
Cover tightly with another layer of banana leaves or foil.
Bake at 325°F (160°C) for 2.5 to 3 hours until chicken is tender and falling off the bone.
Remove from oven, let rest for 10 minutes, then serve.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ingredients: 4 lbs pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 banana leaf or large aluminum foil sheet
instructions: Marinate pork with achiote, orange juice, vinegar, epazote, and cilantro for 6 to 12 hours.
Line a large baking dish with banana leaves or foil.
Arrange pork, cabbage, and plantain slices in the dish, adding some marinade.
Cover tightly with another layer of banana leaves or foil.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 3 to 4 hours until pork is very tender and easily shreds.
Remove from oven, let rest for 10 minutes, then pull apart the pork and serve.

title: Sopa de Lima
ingredients: 1 cup cooked shredded chicken or beef
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together chicken broth, vegetable broth, lime juice, cilantro, epazote, and salt.
Add the cooked white rice to the broth mixture and stir gently.
Top each bowl with shredded cabbage, cooked meat, sliced hard-boiled eggs, grated onion, and radish.
Sprinkle with crumbled cotija cheese just before serving.
Serve immediately while the broth is still cool and crisp.

title: Pepián
ingredients: 1 cup dried pepita squash seeds, toasted and ground
1 cup pumpkin seeds, toasted and ground
1/2 cup sesame seeds, toasted and ground
1/2 cup raisin wine or red wine
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in lard or oil until sealed on all sides.
Remove beef and sauté onion and garlic in the same fat until soft.
Add cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the ground squash seeds, pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, raisins, and wine.
Return the beef to the pot and add beef broth and bay leaf.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2 to 2.5 hours until beef is tender and sauce is thick.
Season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaf, and serve hot.

title: Salbutes with Menudo
ingredients: 1 lb beef tripe, cleaned and cut into strips
1 lb beef feet, cut into pieces
1 lb beef intestines, cleaned and cut into pieces
For the dough: 2 cups masa harina, 1 cup warm water, salt
instructions: Boil tripe, feet, and intestines with onion, garlic, cumin, peppercorns, cinnamon, vinegar, water, and broth until very tender (about 2 hours).
Season the meat with salt and shred or cut into bite-sized pieces.
In a separate pot, boil cilantro and epazote in water for 5 minutes, then strain and set aside.
Mix masa harina with warm water and salt to form a smooth dough.
Roll out small circles of dough, place a spoonful of meat in the center, and fold over to create a half-moon shape.
Drop salbutes into boiling broth with the cilantro-epazote water, cook for 1 minute until they float.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve immediately in a bowl of warm broth.

title: Pozole Rojo
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 large dried guajillo chile, stemmed and seeded
1 large dried ancho chile, stemmed and seeded
1 large dried mulato chile, stemmed and seeded
1 head of nopal cactus, cleaned and cut into pieces
4 corn tortillas, torn into small pieces
instructions: Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
In a large pot, sauté garlic, onion, and oregano in oil until soft.
Add the pork chunks and cook until browned on all sides.
Drain the chiles, chop them finely, and add to the pot along with the nopal and water.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the pork, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
In a separate pan, fry the torn tortilla pieces in lard until golden and crispy.
Stir the fried tortillas into the soup and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot in bowls topped with shredded cabbage, cilantro, radishes, lime wedges, and a drizzle of lard.

title: Mole Poblano
ingredients: 12 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
6 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
6 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast the dried chiles, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, nuts, garlic, and onion in a dry skillet until fragrant.
Place the toasted ingredients in a blender with the chicken broth and blend until smooth.
In a large saucepan, melt the lard over medium heat.
Slowly add the blended chile mixture to the lard, stirring constantly to prevent splattering.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in the chopped chocolate and raisins, cooking for another 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the cinnamon strips and simmer for 10 more minutes to meld the flavors.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve immediately over boiled chicken thighs or turkey, garnished with sesame seeds.

title: Enchiladas Verdes
ingredients: 3 lbs chicken thighs, cooked and shredded
instructions: Blanch the corn tortillas in boiling water for 10 seconds, then drain and stack them.
Roast the tomatillos, onion, garlic, and serrano chiles over an open flame until charred.
Transfer the roasted ingredients to a blender with the cilantro and chicken broth.
Blend until smooth to create the green sauce.
Heat the lard in a large skillet and pour half of the sauce into it.
Dip each tortilla into the sauce, fill with shredded chicken, and roll them up.
Place the rolled enchiladas seam-side down in the skillet.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and sprinkle generously with crumbled cotija cheese.
Serve warm with a dollop of sour cream on the side.

title: Tres Leches Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x9 inch baking pan.
Sift together flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Beat egg yolks with granulated sugar until pale and creamy.
Fold in the dry ingredients, melted butter, milk, and oil into the yolk mixture.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the batter.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, mix the sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, heavy cream, and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Pierce the baked cake all over with a fork to allow it to soak.
Pour the milk mixture evenly over the cake and let it soak for at least 2 hours.
Serve chilled, optionally dusted with cocoa powder.

title: Chiles en Nogada
instructions: Roast the poblano chiles over an open flame until the skin is charred, then peel and stuff with the turkey mixture.
To make the turkey filling, sauté onion and garlic, then add ground turkey, beans, tomatoes, cilantro, mint, and spices.
For the walnut sauce (nogada), toast walnuts, almonds, pine nuts, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds until golden.
Blend the toasted nuts with chicken broth, sugar, vinegar, and spices until smooth.
Simmer the nut mixture over low heat for 20 minutes to thicken.
In a small saucepan, whisk together heavy cream, milk, and a pinch of sugar until frothy.
Arrange the stuffed chiles on a platter.
Pour the warm walnut sauce over the chiles and garnish with pomegranate seeds.
Serve immediately while the sauce is still warm.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 lb fresh firm white fish, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 lb fresh red snapper, cut into 1-inch cubes
4 large fresh red onions, thinly sliced
instructions: Place fish cubes in a non-reactive bowl.
Pour fresh lime juice over the fish until completely submerged.
Let sit at room temperature for 15 minutes until fish turns opaque.
Add sliced onions, chopped cilantro, and avocado to the bowl.
Gently toss to combine without breaking the fish.
Serve immediately with toasted corn or crackers.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
ingredients: 1 lb ground beef, cooked and seasoned with cumin and oregano
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix cooked beef with onion, garlic, raisins, olives, and eggs.
Roll out dough circles about 4 inches in diameter.
Place filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough in half to create a semicircle, crimp edges to seal.
Place on baking sheet and brush with egg wash.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 lb pork sausage, cut into chunks
1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain soaked beans and rinse.
Brown sausage, brisket, and pork shoulder in a large pot.
Add bacon, onion, garlic, bay leaves, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Add beans and cover with water by 2 inches.
Simmer on low heat for 2-3 hours until beans are tender.
Stir in roasted garlic and collard greens during the last 30 minutes.
Serve with white rice, collard greens, and farofa.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: Cook ground beef with onion, cumin, oregano, and salt until browned.
Mix cream cheese, egg, and flour to make a dough.
Layer potato cubes and corn in the bottom of a pie dish.
Add seasoned beef mixture on top.
Cover with dough and seal edges.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes until golden.
Let cool slightly before serving.

title: Uruguayan Asado de Cabrito
instructions: Mix olive oil, salt, pepper, paprika, cumin, and oregano.
Rub the spice mixture all over the goat.
Stuff rosemary, thyme, parsley, and garlic inside the cavity.
Roast in a wood-fired pit or oven at 300°F (150°C) for 4-5 hours.
Baste occasionally with olive oil.
Check internal temperature; remove when reaching 145°F (63°C).
Let rest for 15 minutes before carving.

title: Argentinian Asado de Chorizo
ingredients: 1 kg beef flank steak, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the beef cubes with salt, pepper, and half the chimichurri sauce.
Grill the beef over high heat until browned on all sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove beef and set aside.
Sauté the onions and garlic in a pan until softened.
Add the chorizo meat to the pan with the onions and cook until browned.
Return the beef to the pan, mix gently, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot with chimichurri drizzled on top.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 kg dried black beans, soaked overnight
500 g pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them.
In a large pot, combine beans, pork shoulder, smoked ribs, onion, garlic, and bay leaves.
Cover with water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 hours until beans are tender.
Season with salt to taste.
In a separate pan, sauté collard greens until wilted.
Serve the stew over a bed of white rice.
Garnish with fried plantains and a squeeze of lime.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 2 cups French fries, homemade or store-bought
instructions: Season the beef slices with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Sear the beef quickly for 1-2 minutes until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry the onions and garlic until fragrant.
Add the bell peppers and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the beef to the pan, add soy sauce and vinegar, and toss to combine.
Add the fries and cilantro, mixing well.
Serve immediately over rice.

title: Colombian Ajiaco
ingredients: 3 potatoes (white and yellow), peeled and cubed
instructions: Boil the chicken in chicken broth with onion and garlic until tender, about 1 hour.
Remove the chicken, shred it, and set aside.
In the same broth, add the potatoes and simmer until cooked through.
Stir in the cream of corn, capers, and olives.
Season with salt and pepper.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Chilean Empanadas de Carne
instructions: Sauté the onion, carrot, and beef in a pan until the meat is browned.
Add the boiled potato, raisins, olives, and eggs to the mixture.
Season with cumin, paprika, and salt, then mix well.
Roll out the empanada dough and cut into circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over to create a half-moon shape and seal the edges.
Brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 lb flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
1/2 cup French fries, homemade or store-bought
instructions: Marinate sliced beef in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and vinegar for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Sear beef quickly until browned but still pink inside, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions and bell peppers until tender-crisp.
Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to the pan and toss everything together.
Serve immediately over a bed of French fries, garnished with cilantro.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 2 lbs dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
1 lb dried beef, cut into large chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse soaked beans and place in a large pot with water, onion, garlic, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add pork, dried beef, and ribs to the pot.
Continue simmering, adding beef broth as needed, for 3 to 4 hours until beans and meat are very tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the stew hot over a bed of white rice.
Garnish with sliced cabbage, strips of orange, and a generous portion of farofa.

title: Argentinian Empanadas de Carne
ingredients: 2 lbs empanada dough, thawed if frozen
instructions: In a large bowl, mix ground beef, pork, onion, and garlic.
Stir in raisins, olives, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Divide dough into 12 equal portions and roll each into a 5-inch circle.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold dough in half to create a half-moon shape and press edges with a fork to seal.
Brush the tops with beaten egg.
Deep fry empanadas in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

title: Colombian Ajiaco Santafesino
ingredients: 3 lbs whole potatoes (white, yellow, and San Martín varieties), cut into chunks
1 lb chicken breast, cut into chunks
1 lb corned beef brisket, cut into chunks
3 green plantains, sliced into thick rounds
instructions: In a large pot, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add chicken pieces, corned beef, cumin, and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through.
Add all potato varieties and plantain slices to the pot.
Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in whole milk and heavy cream gently.
Simmer for another 10 minutes without boiling vigorously.
Serve in deep bowls topped with fresh cilantro and capers.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
instructions: In a skillet, cook ground beef and pork with onion, bell pepper, and garlic until browned.
Stir in raisins, olives, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for 5 more minutes.
Remove meat mixture from heat and stir in fresh corn kernels and heavy cream.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Press one sheet of puff pastry onto a baking sheet and spread the corn and meat mixture evenly over it.
Cover with the second sheet of pastry, crimping edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Brush the top with beaten egg and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing into wedges.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, sliced thinly against the grain
2 cups red potatoes, cut into wedges
1 cup yellow onions, sliced into rings
instructions: Boil the potato wedges in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add the sliced beef and stir-fry until browned, about 3 minutes, then remove from the pan.
In the same pan, add onions and bell peppers, stir-frying for 2 minutes until softened.
Return the beef and potatoes to the pan.
Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar, tossing everything to combine and heat through.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Ceviche Clásico
ingredients: 1 lb fresh white fish fillet, cut into 1-inch cubes
1/4 cup red bell pepper, finely diced
instructions: Combine the diced fish and lime juice in a large bowl, ensuring the fish is fully submerged.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 30 to 45 minutes until the fish turns opaque.
Dice the red onion, bell pepper, garlic, cilantro, and mint.
Drain any excess lime juice from the fish, reserving the liquid if needed.
In a serving bowl, combine the marinated fish, onion, pepper, and garlic.
Stir in the herbs and olive oil gently.
Season with salt to taste and serve chilled.

title: Feijoada
ingredients: 2 cups dried black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place the soaked black beans in a pot and cover with water; boil for 2 minutes, remove from heat, and let sit.
In a large pot, combine the beans, pork shoulder, sausage, beef ribs, onion, garlic, bay leaves, cumin, and oregano.
Cover with fresh water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, adding water as needed to keep the beans submerged, until the meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with white rice, collard greens, and orange slices.

title: Empanadas de Carne
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground beef, onion, bell peppers, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, pepper, raisins, and olives; mix well.
In a separate bowl, mix flour and cold water to form a smooth dough, then knead for 5 minutes until elastic.
Divide the dough into 12 equal balls and roll each into a 6-inch circle.
Place 2 tablespoons of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half to create a semi-circle, and pinch edges to seal.
Brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before serving.

title: Ají de Gallina
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, shredded
1 cup white rice, cooked and kept warm
instructions: Puree the roasted red peppers until smooth.
In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat and whisk in flour to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in the chicken broth, milk, cream, and red pepper puree until smooth.
Stir in the grated parmesan cheese, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Add the shredded chicken to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Serve the ají over warm white rice.
Top each serving with a dollop of mayonnaise.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 lb fresh white fish fillets, cut into cubes
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine lime juice, onion, cilantro, jalapeño, and garlic in a large bowl.
Add the fish cubes to the bowl and gently toss to coat.
Let the mixture marinate at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes until the fish turns opaque.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, optionally with boiled corn or sweet potato.

title: Argentinian Asado de Carne
ingredients: 3 lbs beef flank steak or skirt steak
instructions: Season the beef generously with salt and coarse black pepper on all sides.
In a large pot, combine wine, broth, garlic, rosemary, olive oil, and oregano.
Bring the liquid to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Place the seasoned beef in the pot and simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours until tender.
Remove the meat from the liquid, slice against the grain, and serve.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 1 lb dried black beans, soaked overnight
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them thoroughly.
In a large pot, sauté the onion in bacon fat until soft.
Add the pork, beef, garlic, bay leaf, and beans to the pot.
Cover with water and bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cook uncovered for 2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat is falling apart and the beans are creamy.
Season with salt and serve with collard greens, white rice, and farofa.

title: Chilean Pastel de Choclo
ingredients: 2 large sweet corn cobs, kernels removed
1/2 cup green olives, pitted and sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a skillet, cook the ground beef, onion, oregano, salt, and pepper until the meat is browned.
Stir in the corn kernels, olives, egg slices, and capers; heat through.
Butter the phyllo dough and roll it into a large rectangle.
Spread the corn mixture evenly over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
Roll the dough tightly around the filling to form a cylinder.
Place the roll on a baking sheet, seam-side down, and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown.
Let cool slightly before slicing into wedges.

title: Uruguayan Chivito
instructions: Toast the bread slices until golden brown.
On the bottom slice of bread, spread a layer of mayonnaise.
Layer the provolone cheese over the mayonnaise.
Add the sliced steak, ground beef, chorizo, ham, salami, eggs, tomato, and avocado.
Top with the remaining mayonnaise and cheese.
Place the second slice of toasted bread on top to close the sandwich.
Cut diagonally and serve immediately.

title: Peruvian Ceviche
ingredients: 1 lb fresh sea bass or corvina, diced into 1-inch cubes
1 lb fresh red onion, very thinly sliced
1 lb fresh ginger, peeled and grated
instructions: Place the diced fish in a large bowl and cover completely with the lime and orange juice.
Let the fish marinate in the citrus juice for about 15-20 minutes until the fish turns opaque.
In a separate bowl, mix the red onion, cilantro, ginger, tomato, serrano pepper, and culantro.
Drain the fish from the citrus juices and add it to the vegetable mixture.
Season with sea salt and toss gently to combine.
Top with crushed toasted peanuts before serving.

title: Argentinian Asado de Chorizo
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chorizo meat, dry red wine, olive oil, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Mix thoroughly until the meat is evenly coated with the seasoning.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow flavors to meld.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Shape the seasoned meat into large sausages or patties.
Grill the chorizo for about 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
While grilling, simmer the white wine vinegar and chopped parsley in a small saucepan for 5 minutes to make a quick sauce.
Serve the grilled chorizo hot with the parsley vinegar sauce on the side.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
ingredients: 2 lbs black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
1/2 lb pork ribs, cut into chunks
1/2 lb pork ears, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and cook until soft, then add minced garlic and cook for another minute.
Add the beef brisket, pork ribs, and pork ears to the pot and brown on all sides.
Stir in the sliced sausage, cumin seeds, thyme, bay leaves, and a splash of water.
Add the soaked black beans and cover with water to submerge the ingredients.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours until beans and meat are very tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaves and stir in fresh cilantro before serving.
Serve hot with white rice, collard greens, and farofa.

title: Chilean Empanadas
ingredients: 2 lbs all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Mix flour, salt, cold butter, and lard in a large bowl until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add beaten egg and ice water gradually until a dough forms; knead briefly and wrap in plastic to chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a separate bowl, mix ground beef, ground pork, onion, cumin, paprika, and oregano.
Fold in raisins, almonds, currants, hard-boiled egg, and pecans.
Roll out the chilled dough into thin circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle and fold into a half-moon shape.
Crimp the edges firmly to seal and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Serve warm.

title: Uruguayan Queso Quesadilla
instructions: Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
In a bowl, mix mozzarella, parmesan, cheddar, provolone, gouda, gruyere, fontina, edam, and swiss cheeses until well combined.
Spoon the cheese mixture into the hot skillet, spreading it into a thin layer.
Cook for about 3-4 minutes until the cheese starts to melt and the edges begin to brown.
Flip the quesadilla and cook for another 3-4 minutes until the other side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Remove from heat and cut into wedges.
Serve immediately while hot and gooey.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
instructions: Season the beef slices with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Sear the beef in batches until browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry the onions and peppers until softened.
Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beef to the pan and stir in soy sauce and oyster sauce.
Toss in the crispy fries and cilantro, mixing everything together.
Serve immediately over rice.

title: Ceviche Clásico
ingredients: 1 lb fresh white fish fillet, such as sea bass or corvina, diced
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the diced fish, red onion, cilantro, chili, and salt.
Pour the fresh lime juice over the mixture and stir gently.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes until the fish turns opaque.
Before serving, taste and adjust lime juice or salt if needed.
Garnish with sliced avocado and serve chilled with toasted corn chips.

title: Empanadas de Carne
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook until browned.
Stir in peas and raisins, then remove from heat and let cool.
Roll out the dough into 12-inch circles and cut into quarters.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each quarter.
Fold the dough to form a half-moon and crimp edges tightly.
Brush tops with beaten egg and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Let cool slightly before serving.

title: Ají de Gallina
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken thighs and breasts, boneless and skinless
8 slices white bread, toasted and crumbled
1 large egg yolk, beaten (optional, for thickening)
instructions: Boil chicken in chicken broth until tender, then shred the meat.
In a blender, combine cooked chicken, broth, milk, cream, butter, garlic, cilantro, parsley, salt, cumin, and pepper.
Blend until completely smooth.
In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat and whisk in flour to make a roux.
Slowly pour in the blended chicken mixture, stirring constantly.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the beaten egg yolk if using, then remove from heat.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot over toasted bread crumbs.

title: Pachamanca
ingredients: 1.5 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
1 lb corn on the cob, husked
instructions: In a large bowl, toss lamb, potatoes, sweet potatoes, corn, onion, garlic, cilantro, oil, cumin, coriander, pepper, and salt until evenly coated.
Prepare a fire pit or oven-safe container lined with hot stones or coals.
Place the marinated vegetables and meat directly onto the hot stones or in a clay pot placed over the coals.
Cover tightly with a metal lid or foil to trap steam and heat.
Cook for 60-90 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Remove from heat and let rest for 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh herbs and serve immediately.

title: Argentinian Asado de Chorizo y Morcilla
ingredients: 1 lb Argentine chorizo, sliced into coins
1 lb morcilla (blood sausage), sliced into coins
1 head of garlic, cloves separated and roasted
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat a grill or charcoal fire to medium-high heat.
Pat the chorizo and morcilla slices dry with paper towels.
Season both meats lightly with salt and pepper.
Place the sausages on the grill and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until well-charred.
Remove from heat and arrange on a platter.
Roast the garlic cloves until soft and golden.
Drizzle the grilled sausages with olive oil and top with chopped parsley and roasted garlic.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

title: Peruvian Causa Limeña
ingredients: 4 large yellow potatoes, boiled and peeled
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, then mash them while still warm.
In a bowl, mix mashed potatoes with mayonnaise, olive oil, lime juice, and salt until smooth.
Line a rectangular mold with plastic wrap and spread the potato mixture evenly.
Layer the shredded lettuce, diced eggs, olives, capers, and optional chicken on top of the potato base.
Smooth the top layer and cover with the remaining potato mixture.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour to set.
Invert the mold onto a serving plate and carefully remove the plastic wrap.
Slice into thick pieces and serve cold.

title: Brazilian Feijoada Completa
ingredients: 2 lbs black beans, soaked overnight and drained
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
instructions: Rinse the soaked beans and combine them with water in a large pot; bring to a boil and skim foam.
Add the pork shoulder, sliced sausage, smoked ribs, onions, garlic, bay leaves, pepper, and salt.
Reduce heat to low, cover partially, and simmer for 2-3 hours until beans and meat are very tender.
Remove the meat and bones from the pot, reserving the broth.
In a separate pan, sauté the chopped collard greens until wilted, then add the cabbage wedges.
Shred the cooked pork, sausage, and ribs.
Return the shredded meat to the bean broth and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Serve the feijoada in a deep bowl topped with the sautéed greens and cabbage.
Accompany with white rice, farofa (toasted cassava flour), and orange slices.

title: Chilean Empanadas de Carne
instructions: Mix flour, water, egg, and oil to form a smooth dough; knead until elastic and let rest for 30 minutes.
In a pan, sauté the diced onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the ground beef, cumin, paprika, and salt; cook until browned and meat is crumbly.
Stir in the raisins, olives, and chopped hard-boiled egg; remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Roll out the dough into small circles about 4 inches in diameter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over to create a half-moon shape and press edges firmly to seal.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

title: Colombian Sancocho de Gallina
ingredients: 2 cups green plantain, sliced into rounds
instructions: Place the chicken pieces in a large pot and cover with water; bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Add the onion, garlic, tomatoes, bay leaf, and salt; simmer for 45 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the yucca, white corn, and potatoes; continue to simmer for another 30 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Stir in the sliced plantain and cook for 10 more minutes until tender.
Remove the chicken from the pot and shred the meat into bite-sized pieces.
Return the shredded meat to the pot and stir gently.
Add the chopped cilantro and let simmer for 5 minutes to infuse flavor.
Serve hot in deep bowls with white rice and avocado slices on the side.

title: Ceviche de Camarón
ingredients: 1 lb fresh shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Rinse the shrimp and pat dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine the shrimp, lime juice, red bell peppers, red onion, cilantro, jalapeño, olive oil, and capers.
Stir gently to mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Serve chilled with fresh crackers or toasted cornbread.

title: Feijoada Tradicional
ingredients: 2 lbs dried feijão preto beans, soaked overnight
1 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
1 lb smoked pork ribs, cut into pieces
1 lb beef brisket, cut into chunks
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and rinse them well.
In a large pot, combine the beans, pork shoulder, smoked ribs, beef brisket, bacon, bay leaves, garlic, onion, carrot, and celery.
Add enough water to cover the ingredients by 2 inches.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 to 3 hours until the beans are tender and the meat is falling apart.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot with white rice and orange slices.

title: Empanadas de Carne
instructions: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic, sauté until soft.
Add the ground beef, carrots, peas, oregano, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Cook, stirring frequently, until the beef is browned and the vegetables are tender.
Let the filling cool completely.
Roll out the empanada dough and cut into circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold in half, and seal edges with water.
Brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

title: Pabellón Criollo
ingredients: 2 lbs beef flank steak, thinly sliced
instructions: In a skillet, cook the ground beef with onion and garlic until browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Heat butter in a separate pan and melt until foaming.
Add flour to the butter and whisk until smooth.
Gradually add beef broth while whisking to create a smooth sauce.
Add the sliced flank steak to the sauce and simmer for 15 minutes until the meat is tender.
Serve the beef, beans, rice, and sauce together on a platter.

title: Churrasco de Frango
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: In a bowl, mix soy sauce, olive oil, garlic, oregano, pepper, and salt.
Submerge the chicken pieces in the marinade and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and grill for 6-8 minutes per side until cooked through.
In a separate pan, combine pineapple chunks, lime juice, and brown sugar.
Cook over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the pineapple is slightly caramelized.
Serve the grilled chicken with the pineapple glaze.

title: Ceviche de Pescado
instructions: Place fish in a large bowl and cover completely with lemon and orange juice.
Let sit for 20 minutes until fish turns opaque.
Drain juice and add red peppers, onion, tomatoes, and cilantro.
Stir in olive oil and mix gently.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Feijoada Completa
ingredients: 2 lbs dried black beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Rinse beans and cook in water until tender.
Brown pork, beef, and sausage in a large pot.
Add onions, garlic, bay leaves, pepper, and cumin.
Add cooked beans and vinegar, simmer for 1 hour.
Serve with cabbage and white onion on the side.

title: Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, sliced thin
instructions: Boil potatoes until half-cooked, then fry until crispy.
Stir-fry garlic and onions in oil until fragrant.
Add beef and cook until browned.
Toss in bell peppers and season with soy sauce, vinegar, and cumin.
Serve over rice topped with fried potatoes and cilantro.

title: Empanadas de Carne
instructions: Mix ground beef, onion, carrot, potato, garlic, and spices in a bowl.
Roll out dough and cut into circles.
Place meat mixture in center of each circle and fold over.
Seal edges with fork and brush with egg wash.
Fry in oil until golden brown on both sides.

title: Asado de Chorizo y Morcilla
instructions: Marinate meats with wine, garlic, and rosemary for 2 hours.
Preheat grill with wood chips for smoking.
Grill onions and garlic until caramelized.
Cook sausages and skewers over medium heat until charred.
Serve with grilled onions and garlic.

title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
ingredients: 2 cups yellow potatoes, cut into wedges
instructions: Stir-fry beef in oil until browned, then remove from pan.
Fry potato wedges until golden and crispy.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add tomatoes and season with soy sauce, cumin, and red pepper flakes.
Return beef to the pan and toss everything together.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately.

title: Argentinian Empanadas
instructions: Cook beef with onions, peppers, carrots, raisins, and spices in oil until done.
Roll out empanada dough and cut into circles.
Place filling in center of each circle and fold to seal edges.
Brush tops with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.

title: Brazilian Feijoada
instructions: Soak beans overnight, then drain and rinse.
Brown meats in a large pot with onion, garlic, and bay leaf.
Add beans, water, and salt; simmer for 2-3 hours until tender.
Cook rice separately according to package instructions.
Serve feijoada hot with rice and cabbage on the side.

title: Colombian Arepa
