Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce heat and simmer for 4 hours.
Add sliced beef and cook for 2 minutes, then remove.
Slice noodles and place in bowls.
Strain broth and pour over noodles and beef.
Season with fish sauce and sugar to taste.
Garnish with spring onions, lime leaves, and Thai basil.

title: Adobo (Filipino Chicken Stew)
instructions: Combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, pepper, and salt in a pot.
Add lard or oil and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add water if the liquid reduces too much.
Simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot.

title: Nasi Goreng (Indonesian Fried Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, day-old preferred
200g shrimp or chicken, cooked and chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant, then add vegetables and meat.
Push ingredients to the side and scramble eggs in the center.
Mix everything together and add cooked rice.
Stir in sweet soy sauce and turmeric, tossing continuously.
Cook for 5 minutes until rice is hot and slightly crispy.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Nasi Lemak (Malaysian Coconut Rice)
instructions: Combine rice, coconut milk, pandan leaves, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Let the rice rest, covered, for 10 minutes before fluffing.
Fry anchovies until golden.
Toast coconut flakes in a dry pan until aromatic.
Assemble plates with rice, anchovies, toasted coconut, sambal, egg, and cucumber.
Serve immediately.

title: Khao Niao Mamuang (Thai Coconut Rice with Mango)
instructions: Soak glutinous rice for 4 hours, then drain.
Steam rice until fully cooked and fluffy.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, water, sugar, and salt.
Heat gently until sugar dissolves, then remove from heat.
Pour coconut mixture over steamed rice and mix well.
Let the rice cool slightly, then refrigerate for 1 hour.
Serve scoops of rice topped with mango slices, condensed milk, and mint.

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
ingredients: 2 lbs beef brisket, cut into strips
instructions: Roast beef bones in an open flame until charred, then break them into large pieces.
Combine charred bones, brisket, tendon, lemongrass, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, fish sauce, and water in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 12 hours.
Strain the broth into a clean pot and skim off any remaining fat.
Add sliced garlic to the hot broth and let it steep for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, blanch noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Assemble bowls with noodles, topped with raw beef slices, brisket, tendon, bean sprouts, basil, and mint.
Serve hot broth over the bowls with lime wedges and chili sauce on the side.

title: Filipino Adobo
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Rinse chicken pieces and pat them dry.
In a large pot, combine chicken, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Remove from heat and let the chicken cool in the sauce.
Heat oil in a separate pan over medium heat.
Remove chicken from the pot and fry in the hot oil until the skin is crispy and golden brown.
Return the fried chicken to the pot with the remaining sauce.
Simmer for another 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve over steamed white rice.

title: Indonesian Rendang
ingredients: 2 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
instructions: In a large pot, sauté shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, chilies, lime leaves, lemongrass, and spices in oil until fragrant.
Add beef cubes and stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in coconut milk, tamarind paste, turmeric, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, pepper, sugar, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the liquid reduces significantly.
Uncover and continue to cook on low heat, stirring frequently to prevent burning.
Cook for another 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is very tender and the sauce is dry and dark.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Malaysian Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, soaked for 30 minutes
For Sambal: 10 red chilies, 4 shallots, 4 cloves garlic, 1 inch ginger, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp tamarind paste
For Side: 100g anchovies, fried; 50g peanuts, roasted; 50g cucumber, julienned; 2 hard-boiled eggs, halved; 100g fried chicken or rendang
instructions: Drain soaked rice and combine with coconut milk, water, pandan leaf, galangal, lemongrass, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let the rice steam in the covered pot for another 10 minutes until fluffy.
To make sambal, grind chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and salt into a paste.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the chili paste with tamarind paste until oil separates and turns red.
Fry anchovies until crispy, and roast peanuts until golden.
Assemble plates with a scoop of coconut rice topped with sambal.
Arrange fried anchovies, roasted peanuts, cucumber strips, egg halves, and fried chicken or rendang on the side.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

title: Singaporean Chicken Rice
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, deboned and kept skin-on
3 cups chicken stock, made from bones and aromatics
For Marinade: 1 tbsp baking soda, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp ginger paste
For Soup: 1 onion, sliced; 2 carrots, sliced; 1 stalk celery, sliced; 1 tsp soy sauce; 1 tsp pepper
For Sauce: 1/4 cup dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces in baking soda, salt, sugar, pepper, and ginger paste for 2 hours.
Boil chicken in the first 3 cups of stock until cooked through (about 20 minutes), then remove and let cool.
Skim fat from the stock and reserve it for the soup.
Poach chicken skin in the reserved stock to render fat, then remove and set aside.
Cook rice in oil and 1/2 cup chicken stock with baking soda and salt until fluffy and oily.
Chop chicken meat into bite-sized pieces and slice the skin thinly.
Make the soup by boiling onion, carrots, celery, soy sauce, and pepper in the reserved stock.
Make the sauce by mixing dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and sesame oil.
Serve with a bowl of soup, a plate of rice, and the prepared chicken.
Top with sliced chicken skin, pickled mustard greens, green onions, and chili oil.

title: Pho Bo
ingredients: 1 lb beef flank steak, sliced thin
instructions: Combine beef bones, ginger, star anise, and cinnamon sticks in a large pot.
Add 4 quarts of water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 4 hours.
Strain the broth and return it to the pot with fish sauce, rock sugar, and 2 cups of water.
Bring the broth to a simmer and cook until the sugar dissolves.
Place rice noodles in individual bowls.
Top noodles with sliced beef and ladle hot broth over them.
Garnish with green onions, cilantro, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Adobo
ingredients: 2 lbs pork shoulder, cut into cubes
instructions: Combine pork cubes, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaf, and cloves in a large pot.
Add water and salt to taste, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until meat is tender.
Remove bay leaf and whole spices.
Uncover the pot and simmer further until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot over cooked white rice.

title: Nasi Goreng
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white rice, day-old preferred
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok over medium-high heat.
Add shallots and garlic, sauté until fragrant.
Stir in diced chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add tomato paste and sweet soy sauce, stirring to combine.
Push ingredients to the side and scramble the beaten eggs in the center.
Mix the eggs with the chicken and sauce.
Add the cooked rice and toss well to coat every grain.
Stir in sambal oelek and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Khao Tom
instructions: Combine rice, water, ginger, lemongrass, garlic, and lime leaves in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until rice is tender and water is absorbed.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar to the rice.
Stir gently to mix flavors.
Serve in bowls topped with shredded chicken and sliced hard-boiled eggs.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, scallions, and a drizzle of chili oil.

title: Lap Thap Hen
ingredients: 1 cup palm sugar, dissolved in warm water
instructions: In a large pot, combine chicken, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, garlic, and chilies.
Add water and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Strain the broth, reserving the liquid and the solid ingredients.
In a bowl, mix the strained broth with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar solution.
Add the cooked chicken, holy basil, and reserved solid ingredients to the broth.
Serve hot in bowls garnished with sliced cucumbers and fresh mint.

title: Pho Bo (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 kg beef shank, cut into chunks
1 liter beef bones, roasted until charred
instructions: Roast beef bones until dark brown, then place in a large pot.
Add beef shank, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil.
Skim off all scum that rises to the surface, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer gently for 4-6 hours until meat is tender.
Strain broth and discard solids.
In a small pot, combine strained broth with lemongrass, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, and garlic; simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove spices and season broth with fish sauce and rock sugar to taste.
Cook rice noodles according to package instructions until al dente.
Assemble bowls with noodles, sliced brisket, and hot broth.
Garnish with cilantro, Thai basil, green onions, lime wedges, and chili slices.

title: Adobo (Filipino Braised Pork)
instructions: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, minced garlic, bay leaves, black pepper, and peppercorns in a bowl.
Add pork cubes and let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat lard or oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Remove pork from marinade and brown on all sides.
Pour the remaining marinade into the pot and bring to a boil.
Add water or broth and reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until pork is tender and sauce is thick.
Season with salt if needed.
Remove bay leaves and peppercorns before serving.
Garnish with chopped green onions and tomato.

title: Nasi Goreng (Indonesian Fried Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, day-old and cold
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add ground meat and cook until browned.
Add mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs, scramble slightly, then mix with rice.
Add sweet soy sauce, salt, and white pepper; toss to coat evenly.
Remove from heat and cover for 1 minute to steam.
Serve immediately with fried eggs, cucumber slices, and lime wedges.

title: Laksa Sarawak (Malaysian Spicy Fish Noodle Soup)
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a large pot.
Add laksa paste, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add coconut milk, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and sugar; stir well.
Add fish cubes and cook for 5 minutes until just cooked through.
Add soaked rice vermicelli and stir gently to separate strands.
Simmer for another 2 minutes to infuse flavors.
Divide bean sprouts, cucumber, chili, and cilantro into bowls.
Pour hot laksa soup over the toppings.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Khao Tom (Thai-Style Broken Rice Soup)
ingredients: 4 cups cooked jasmine rice, broken into grains
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken stock, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves; bring to a simmer.
Add broken rice, carrots, and cabbage; simmer until rice is tender (about 15 minutes).
Stir in oyster sauce and sugar; adjust seasoning to taste.
Add bean sprouts and green onions; cook for 2 minutes.
Remove lemongrass and lime leaves.
Divide soup into bowls and top with poached eggs.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
Serve with Sriracha sauce and lime wedges on the side.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 100g pandan leaves, tied in a knot
8 small red chillies, deseeded and sliced
instructions: Combine coconut milk, pandan leaves, and palm sugar in a pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the glutinous rice and stir gently to coat with the coconut milk.
Cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the rice with a fork and let it rest covered for 10 minutes.
Serve the rice with sambal belacan, sliced chillies, fried anchovies, and egg quarters.

title: Laksa Sarawak
ingredients: 200g rice vermicelli, soaked in warm water
2 tbsp tamarind paste, diluted in 1 cup water
instructions: In a pot, bring the tamarind water to a simmer and add the ground belacan.
Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar until dissolved, then add the sliced meat.
Cook the meat until it is just cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Add the soaked rice vermicelli and bean sprouts to the soup.
Simmer for 2 minutes to heat the noodles, then ladle into bowls.
Top with sliced hard-boiled egg and chopped spring onions.

title: Nasi Kerabu
ingredients: 2 cups blue butterfly pea flowers, soaked in water
1 cup mung beans, boiled until soft
instructions: Boil the butterfly pea flowers in water until the water turns deep blue, then strain and cool.
Cook the jasmine rice with the coconut milk and blue water until fluffy and colored blue.
Layer the blue rice in a serving bowl.
Arrange the julienned cucumber, boiled mung beans, fried tofu, and keropok lekor on top.
Drizzle with a little extra coconut milk if desired.

title: Opor Ayam
ingredients: 1 tbsp tamarind paste, dissolved in 1 cup water
instructions: Fry the candlenut paste with turmeric, ginger, and pepper until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until the chicken changes color.
Pour in the tamarind water and simmer until the chicken is half cooked.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the sliced young coconut and palm sugar, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Rendang Daging
instructions: Fry the shallots, garlic, ginger, and turmeric in a large pot until golden.
Add the beef cubes and stir-fry for 5 minutes to brown the meat.
Pour in the coconut milk, ground spices, palm sugar, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered.
Stir occasionally for 2-3 hours until the coconut milk evaporates and the meat is dark brown and tender.
Serve with fresh steamed rice.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 1 cup pandan leaves, tied in a knot
2 whole kaffir lime leaves, cut in half
3 cups jasmine rice, soaked for 30 minutes
100g dried shrimp, soaked and fried until golden
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the pandan knot, lemongrass, and lime leaves.
Add the soaked rice and salt, then reduce heat to low and cook until the water is absorbed and rice is tender.
While rice cooks, mix the coconut milk, coconut cream, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan.
Heat the coconut mixture until it just begins to simmer and oil separates from the milk.
Drain the cooked rice and toss it immediately with the hot coconut mixture to coat evenly.
For the sambal, stir the tamarind paste with the sambal belacan and a splash of water until smooth.
To serve, place a portion of rice in a bowl, top with cucumber, egg, dried shrimp, anchovies, and a generous scoop of sambal.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 400g dried flat rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 20 minutes
4 spring onions, white parts chopped, green parts sliced
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
In a wok over high heat, stir-fry the Chinese sausage until slightly browned, then remove.
Add oil to the wok, then stir-fry the prawns, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Return the Chinese sausage to the wok, then add the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, pepper, and cooking wine.
Toss in the drained noodles and stir-fry vigorously for 2 minutes until they absorb the sauce.
Push the noodles to the side, pour the beaten eggs into the empty space, and scramble until just set.
Mix the noodles and eggs together, then add the bean sprouts and spring onion whites.
Stir-fry for another minute until bean sprouts are crisp-tender, then garnish with spring onion greens.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 2 cups chicken stock, reserved from poaching
1 cup jasmine rice, rinsed until water runs clear
2 tbsp chicken fat or lard, melted
instructions: Combine the chicken pieces with 1 liter of water, ginger, star anise, and lemongrass in a large pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Remove the chicken and let it cool in its broth, then shred the meat into bite-sized pieces.
Strain the poaching liquid to make a clear stock.
In a separate pot, combine the rinsed rice with the reserved stock, melted fat, salt, pepper, sugar, and soy sauces.
Bring the rice mixture to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is fluffy.
To serve, place shredded chicken on a plate, drizzle with chili oil and garlic chives.
Serve the rice with a side of chicken soup and a dipping sauce made of ginger paste, garlic paste, and stock.

title: Laksa Sarpo
ingredients: 2 cups rice vermicelli, soaked in warm water
1 tbsp shrimp paste (belacan), toasted and crushed
2 dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
instructions: Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan until fragrant, then set aside.
In a wok, heat coconut oil and sauté shallots, garlic, and galangal until soft.
Add the toasted shrimp paste and dried chilies, stir-fry for 1 minute until aromatic.
Pour in the tamarind paste, sugar, salt, pepper, and chicken stock.
Add the chicken slices, tofu puffs, fish balls, and squid, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the bean sprouts and spinach until just wilted.
Drain the soaked vermicelli and place in a deep bowl.
Pour the hot laksa soup over the noodles and garnish with coriander and a wedge of lime.

title: Satay with Peanut Sauce
ingredients: 500g chicken thigh meat, cut into 2-inch strips
400g roasted peanuts, blended into a paste
instructions: Marinate the chicken strips with soy sauce, ginger paste, garlic paste, pepper, and cornstarch for 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated chicken onto soaked bamboo skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces.
Oil the skewers and grill over charcoal or under a broiler, turning frequently until golden brown and cooked through.
In a small saucepan, combine peanuts, coconut milk, tamarind paste, palm sugar, salt, chili paste, ketchup, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Bring the peanut sauce to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens and oil separates.
Serve the grilled satay skewers immediately with a side of the warm peanut sauce, fresh coriander, cucumber slices, and pita bread.

title: Samlor Kanh (Fish Curry)
instructions: Blend lemongrass, galangal, chilies, lime leaves, palm sugar, and salt into a paste.
Fry the paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and tamarind water mixture, simmer for 20 minutes.
Gently add fish slices and cook until just done.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Num Banh Chok (Noodle Soup)
instructions: Soak noodles in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Mix fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind water to taste.
Stir-fry shrimp and pork with herbs until cooked.
Bring stock to a boil and add noodles.
Top noodles with sauce, fried shallots, herbs, and stir-fried meat.
Serve immediately.

title: Amok Trey (Fish in Coconut Milk)
instructions: Blend lemongrass, galangal, chilies, lime leaves, turmeric, tamarind, salt, sugar, and half the coconut milk.
Place fish in a clay pot or deep dish.
Pour the spiced coconut mixture over the fish.
Add egg white and cover tightly with banana leaf or foil.
Steam for 45 minutes until fish is tender.
Serve with cucumber and lime wedges.

title: Num Sangkaya (Coconut Rice)
instructions: Soak beans overnight and cook until soft but not mushy.
Rinse rice and cook with coconut milk, water, sugar, and salt.
When rice is almost done, stir in cooked beans.
Garnish with butter and mix well.
Serve warm as a side dish.

title: Kuy Teav (Noodle Soup with Chicken)
ingredients: Bean sprouts, basil, and mint for garnish
instructions: Boil chicken with onion, lemongrass, galangal, chilies, salt, and water until tender.
Strain broth and skim fat.
Cook noodles according to package instructions.
Add fish sauce and tamarind water to broth to taste.
Place noodles in bowls, top with chicken and broth.
Garnish with bean sprouts, herbs, and lime wedges.

title: Laotian Sticky Rice with Herbs (Khao Niao)
ingredients: 2 cups sticky rice, soaked for 4 hours
instructions: Steam the soaked sticky rice until fluffy and sticky.
In a bowl, mix the chopped holy basil, mint, cilantro stems, and minced garlic.
Toss the warm sticky rice with the herb mixture.
Drizzle fish sauce and lime juice over the rice.
Gently fold everything together and serve immediately.

title: Grilled Pork with Sticky Rice (Larb Moo)
instructions: Marinate the sliced pork in fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice for 30 minutes.
Grill the marinated pork over high heat until charred and cooked through.
In a large bowl, toss the cooked pork with toasted rice powder, green onions, and fresh chili peppers.
Add a splash of lime juice and fish sauce to taste.
Serve with sticky rice and sprinkle crushed peanuts on top.

title: Laotian Green Papaya Salad (Som Tum)
instructions: Mortar and pestle: Pound the garlic, chilies, lemongrass, palm sugar, and fish sauce until a paste forms.
Add the shredded green papaya and tomatoes to the mortar and pound gently until mixed.
Stir in the lime juice and toss to combine.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Garnish with crushed roasted peanuts and serve.

title: Steamed Fish with Coconut Milk (Nam Prik Noom)
ingredients: 1 whole freshwater fish, cleaned and scaled
instructions: Score the fish and stuff it with lemongrass and torn kaffir lime leaves.
Place the fish in a steamer basket over boiling water.
Steam the fish for 10-12 minutes until the flesh is opaque.
In a separate pot, combine coconut milk, water, fish sauce, and palm sugar; simmer until slightly thickened.
Pour the sauce over the steamed fish and garnish with fresh basil.

title: Laotian Eggplant Curry (Kuay Teua)
instructions: Fry the eggplant halves in oil until soft and slightly golden.
In a pot, sauté the chopped shallots until translucent.
Add the red curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and water, then add the fried eggplant.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves.

title: Bahan (Shan Style Fried Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and sliced shallots; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add cooled rice and break up clumps with a spatula.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and turmeric.
Toss in crushed peanuts and chopped green onions.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until well mixed and heated through.

title: Thoke Yoke (Shan Style Chicken Salad)
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thigh meat, diced and stir-fried with turmeric
2 tablespoons palm sugar, dissolved in warm water
instructions: Stir-fry minced garlic in oil until golden.
Add diced chicken and turmeric; cook until chicken is done.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, soaked dried shrimp, and peanuts.
Mix in dissolved palm sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and green onions.
Toss gently until all ingredients are evenly coated.

title: Mohn (Shan Style Pork Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add garlic, ginger, and onion; sauté until soft.
Add pork cubes and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Pour in water, fish sauce, palm sugar, and turmeric.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots and cook for 10 more minutes.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Mohinga (Fish Soup with Rice Noodles)
ingredients: 2 cups dried fish, cleaned and ground into paste
instructions: Fry the ground fish paste in oil until golden brown.
Add grated ginger, minced garlic, and lemongrass to the fried paste.
Pour in water and bring to a simmer.
Stir in fish sauce and cook for 10 minutes.
Soak rice noodles in warm water until soft.
Divide noodles into bowls and ladle hot soup over them.
Top with fresh coriander and fried garlic chips.

title: Tee La Hpa (Shan Style Vegetable Stir-fry)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (cabbage, carrots, bean sprouts)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add minced garlic and julienned ginger; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Toss in crushed peanuts and chopped green onions.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Cơm Tấm (Broken Rice with Grilled Pork)
ingredients: 2 cups broken rice, soaked and cooked until tender
1/2 cup fish sauce, mixed with 2 tbsp water and 1 tsp sugar
1 cup grilled pork leg meat, sliced
1/4 cup pickled carrots and daikon, sliced
instructions: Grill the pork belly slices over charcoal until charred on the edges but cooked through.
Grill the pork leg meat until slightly crispy.
Season the rice with a little salt and arrange it on a serving plate.
Top the rice with the grilled pork belly, grilled pork leg, and quartered eggs.
Arrange the pickled vegetables, cilantro, mint, and perilla leaves around the plate.
Serve immediately with the dipping sauce on the side.

title: Bánh Mì (Vietnamese Baguette)
ingredients: 1/4 cup pickled carrots and daikon, julienned
instructions: Toast the baguette slices lightly until crisp on the outside.
Pan-fry the pork sausage slices until browned.
Cook the pork belly slices until they release fat and become slightly crisp.
Grill the pork neck slices until lightly charred.
Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise and pate on the bottom half of the baguette.
Layer the pickled vegetables, cilantro, and cucumber on the bread.
Top with the fried sausage, cooked pork belly, and grilled pork neck.
Drizzle with a little chili sauce if desired and close the sandwich.

title: Cá Kho Tộ (Braised Fish in Clay Pot)
ingredients: 500g red snapper or sea bass, cleaned and cut into large chunks
instructions: Pat the fish chunks dry and season lightly with salt.
In a clay pot, melt the palm sugar over low heat until it turns dark amber.
Add the fish chunks to the caramelized sugar, coating them evenly.
Add the garlic, ginger, dried chilies, lemongrass, fish sauce, and water.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the fish is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the crushed peanuts before serving.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Phở Bò (Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 500g beef shank, cut into thick strips
500g beef brisket, cut into thin slices
200g fresh rice noodles, soaked until soft
1 liter beef bones, boiled and skimmed
instructions: Simmer the beef bones in water for 4 hours, skimming impurities regularly.
Add the beef shank strips to the broth and cook until tender.
Slice the cooked beef brisket thinly and set aside.
Strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve.
Boil the rice noodles briefly in separate batches.
Assemble bowls with noodles at the bottom, topped with beef shank and sliced brisket.
Pour the hot broth over the ingredients.
Garnish with cilantro, basil, bean sprouts, and green onions.
Serve with hoisin sauce, sriracha, and lime juice on the side.

title: Bánh Xèo (Crispy Rice Paper Pancake)
ingredients: 200g pork belly, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Mix rice flour, mung bean flour, water, salt, and turmeric to form a smooth batter.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and add a little oil.
Pour a ladle of batter into the pan, swirling it quickly to cover the bottom.
Push the batter to the edges with a spatula to create a crispy texture.
Place the pork belly strips on one half of the pancake.
Add bean sprouts to the pork and fold the pancake over.
Cook until the pancake is golden and crispy, then transfer to a plate.
Tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces.
Serve with fresh herbs, lettuce, and fried shallots, wrapped in rice paper.

title: Adobo
ingredients: 2 lbs pork, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Heat lard in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, peppercorns, and water.
Return the pork to the pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender.
Uncover and simmer for another 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Sinigang na Bangus
ingredients: 2 whole milkfish, cleaned and cut into 4 pieces each
1 cup tamarind paste or sour soup base
instructions: Heat lard in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the milkfish pieces, tamarind paste, water, and papaya.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Add the water spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Serve immediately in bowls.

title: Lechon Kawali
ingredients: 3 lbs pork belly, scored in a crosshatch pattern
instructions: Combine salt, minced garlic, and vinegar in a bowl.
Rub the mixture all over the scored pork belly and let it marinate for 2 hours.
Heat lard in a deep pot or wok over medium heat.
Carefully place the pork belly into the hot fat, skin-side up.
Fry for about 30-40 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Increase heat to high for the last 5 minutes to crisp the skin.
Drain on paper towels and serve with vinegar and garlic dipping sauce.

title: Pancit Bihon
instructions: Blanch the rice vermicelli noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a large wok over high heat.
Stir-fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and ground pork; cook until the pork is browned and shrimp are pink.
Add the carrots and bean sprouts, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, oyster sauce, sugar, and water.
Toss everything together for 3-4 minutes until the noodles are coated and heated through.
Serve immediately, garnished with shredded cabbage.

title: Kare-Kare
ingredients: 1/2 lb beef tripe, cleaned and sliced
2 tbsp peanut sauce (tahong or ground peanuts)
instructions: Boil the oxtail in water for 10 minutes to remove scum, then drain.
Brown the oxtail in lard over medium-high heat.
Remove meat, then sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in the same fat.
Return the oxtail to the pot, add water, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the eggplant and tripe; simmer for another 30 minutes.
Serve the stew over rice with a side of rich peanut sauce.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
ingredients: 3 cups cooked white rice, day-old and cooled
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Sauté garlic, shallots, and chilies until fragrant.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry for 5 minutes until grains separate.
Pour in the sweet soy sauce and toss to coat evenly.
Add salted fish if using and mix well.
Serve hot with fried eggs, cucumber slices, and lime wedges on the side.

title: Sayur Asem
instructions: Dissolve tamarind pulp in water and strain to get the juice.
Bring the tamarind juice to a boil in a pot.
Add jackfruit, green beans, long beans, and bamboo shoots.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Season with salt and palm sugar to taste.
Stir in the fried shrimp paste just before serving.

title: Soto Betawi
ingredients: 500g beef shank, cubed and boiled until tender
1 tbsp coriander seeds, toasted and ground
instructions: Simmer beef shank in water with lemongrass and lime leaves until tender.
Strain the broth and return it to the pot.
Add the ground coriander, palm sugar, and salt to the broth.
Stir in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the cooked beef cubes and warm through.
Serve in deep bowls topped with hard-boiled eggs, cucumber, and fresh coriander.

title: Gado-Gado Jakarta
ingredients: Shallots and chilies for the sauce
instructions: Boil bean sprouts, long beans, spinach, and potatoes until tender-crisp.
Fry tofu and tempeh until golden brown.
Boil eggs until hard and peel them.
Blend shallots, chilies, peanuts, and a little water to make a smooth sauce.
Mix the sauce with salt to taste.
Arrange all vegetables and proteins in a bowl.
Pour the peanut sauce over the top and serve immediately.

title: Sate Ayam Madura
ingredients: 50 skewers of bamboo, soaked in water
instructions: Mix minced chicken, flour, salt, pepper, garlic, and shrimp paste until sticky.
Stuff the mixture onto soaked bamboo skewers, packing it tight.
Arrange skewers on a grill over charcoal.
Brush the skewers generously with a mix of sweet soy sauce and coconut water.
Grill for 10-15 minutes, turning frequently until chicken is cooked and charred.
Serve hot with extra sweet soy sauce on the side.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, soaked for 30 minutes
5 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
instructions: Combine half the coconut milk, lemongrass, lime leaves, pandan, and salt in a pot.
Add the soaked rice, stir gently, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until rice is tender.
Remove from heat and let it steam for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Serve hot with sambal belacan, fried anchovies, cucumber, and hard-boiled egg.

title: Laksa Ceylon
ingredients: 1 tsp tamarind paste, dissolved in warm water
instructions: Blend turmeric, cumin, coriander, chili, and a bit of stock into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pot, fry the dried shrimp paste until fragrant.
Add the spice paste and stir for 1 minute until oil separates.
Pour in the remaining stock and tamarind water, simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and cook for another 2 minutes.
Blanch vegetables in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Boil noodles separately until soft, drain, and toss with a little oil.
Assemble bowls with noodles, vegetables, chicken, and ladle hot laksa sauce over.

title: Satay Ayam
ingredients: 500g chicken thigh, boneless, cut into 2-inch strips
instructions: Marinate chicken strips with soy sauce, peanut butter, honey, ginger, and garlic for 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto soaked skewers, leaving space between pieces.
Grill skewers over medium-high heat, turning frequently until chicken is cooked and slightly charred.
Whisk together chicken stock, remaining peanut butter, and a splash of water to make the dipping sauce.
Serve satay with crushed peanuts, cucumber strips, and sweet chili sauce on the side.

title: Kari Ayam
ingredients: 500g chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot, sauté onions until translucent, then add garlic and ginger.
Stir in curry powder, turmeric, cinnamon, and cumin, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they change color.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Add potatoes and carrots, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in coconut milk and green beans, simmer for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Ayam Penyet
ingredients: 500g chicken breast, marinated in soy sauce, garlic, and turmeric
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces in soy sauce, garlic, and turmeric for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, sear chicken on both sides until golden and cooked through.
Increase heat and press chicken flat with a heavy spatula to create crispy texture.
Season chicken with salt, garlic, and chili flakes while pressing.
Mound steamed rice on a plate and press down firmly with a mallet or heavy spoon.
Top the pressed rice with the crispy chicken, cucumber, onions, and stir-fried beans.
Garnish with fried shallots and serve immediately with sweet chili sauce.

title: Char Kway Teow
ingredients: 300g dried flat rice noodles, soaked in warm water until soft
1 stalk spring onion, chopped for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant, then add pork and sausage, cooking until browned.
Add prawns and cook until they turn pink.
Drain noodles and add them to the wok; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, sugar, and cooking wine; toss to coat evenly.
Push ingredients to the side and scramble the egg into the center, then mix everything together.
Add bean sprouts and spring onions, tossing quickly for 30 seconds until sprouts are just tender.
Serve immediately in deep bowls.

title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, soaked for 30 minutes
3 pandan leaves, tied in a knot
4 pieces sambal belacan, homemade or store-bought
instructions: Drain the soaked rice and place it in a pot.
Add coconut milk, water, pandan leaves, sugar, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it steam with the lid on for another 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork and remove the pandan leaves.
Serve each portion with a scoop of rice, a drizzle of coconut cream, cucumber, egg, fried anchovies, and sambal belacan.
Garnish with additional fried anchovies if desired.

title: Laksa Sarawak
ingredients: 300g medium egg noodles, boiled until al dente
2 cups clear chicken broth (optional for extra flavor)
instructions: In a pot, combine water and coconut milk, then bring to a simmer.
Add laksa paste, sugar, and fish sauce; stir until the paste dissolves completely.
Bring the soup to a boil and add the chicken slices; cook for 3-4 minutes until cooked through.
Add the pre-boiled noodles to the pot and stir gently.
Add bean sprouts and shredded cabbage, cooking for just 1 minute until wilted.
Remove from heat and ladle into deep bowls.
Garnish with chopped spring onions and serve hot.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
instructions: Boil the chicken in chicken stock with ginger and spring onion knots for 45 minutes until cooked through.
Remove the chicken and let it rest under cold water to tighten the skin, then carve into serving pieces.
In a separate pot, combine water, rice, oil, salt, and white pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Drizzle soy sauce and sesame oil over the rice before serving.
Arrange chicken pieces on a plate with a side of rice.
Serve with ginger-spring onion sauce and chili sauce on the side.

title: Satay with Peanut Sauce
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes with oil, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Soak skewers in water for 30 minutes if using bamboo to prevent burning.
Thread marinated chicken onto skewers.
Grill skewers over medium heat, turning frequently, until chicken is charred and cooked through.
In a saucepan, combine ground peanuts, coconut milk, tamarind paste, garlic, sugar, and soy sauce.
Simmer the sauce for 5-7 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Stir in chopped spring onions and let cool.
Serve skewers with the peanut sauce, cucumber slices, and lontong (rice cakes) on the side.

title: Num Banh Chok (Green Tea Noodles)
ingredients: 1 bundle rice noodles soaked in water for 30 minutes
1 cup green tea leaves steeped in 2 cups water
1/2 cup tamarind paste diluted in water
1 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
instructions: Boil garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and lime leaves in the green tea water until fragrant.
Add tamarind paste and stock, simmer for 10 minutes, then strain to remove solids.
Stir in ground dried shrimp and bring to a gentle simmer.
Boil pork slices in the broth until cooked, about 3 minutes.
Drain noodles and arrange in bowls.
Top with green beans, bean sprouts, basil, and mint.
Pour the hot tea broth over the noodles and top with cooked pork.

title: Larb (Minced Pork Salad)
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder, minced very fine
1 cup shredded green papaya or cabbage
instructions: Toast the rice powder in a dry pan until fragrant, then let it cool.
In a wok, stir-fry minced pork with garlic over high heat until browned and crispy.
Season the pork with fish sauce, tamarind paste, lime juice, sugar, and toasted rice powder.
Add the ground peanuts and chopped lime leaves, mixing well.
Transfer the larb to a serving bowl and toss with fresh cilantro and mint.
Serve immediately with shredded papaya or cabbage on the side.

title: Amok Tey (Fish in Coconut Curry)
ingredients: 1 whole snapper or sea bass, cleaned and boned
1/2 cup green tea leaves, steeped in 1 cup water
1/4 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
1/4 cup mung bean sprouts, for garnish
instructions: Steam the fish whole with kaffir lime leaves and green onions for 15 minutes, then remove and keep warm.
In a pot, mix coconut milk with steeped green tea water, galangal, lemongrass, and garlic.
Add ground dried shrimp, tamarind paste, and fish sauce, then simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Carefully pour the curry mixture over the steamed fish.
Cover and steam again for 10-15 minutes until the curry is thick and the fish is opaque.
Garnish with mung bean sprouts before serving.

title: Samlor Machu Krua (Stir-fried Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: 2 cups diced pork belly, fat trimmed
1 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
1 cup green beans, trimmed and cut
1 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Fry the diced pork belly in a wok until the fat renders and the meat is golden.
Add garlic and ground dried shrimp, stir-frying for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for another minute.
Pour in chicken stock, tamarind paste, and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Add green beans, papaya, long beans, and chayote, simmering for 5 minutes.
Add bean sprouts last and cook for 1 minute to keep them crisp.
Garnish with chopped green onion and serve hot.

title: Kuy Teav (Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1 lb beef shank, cut into small cubes
1 lb rice noodles, soaked in warm water
3 cups beef bones, simmered for 4 hours for stock
1/2 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
instructions: Simmer beef bones with garlic for 4 hours to create a rich stock, then strain.
In the strained stock, add beef cubes, fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind paste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in ground dried shrimp just before serving.
Drain soaked rice noodles and arrange in bowls.
Pour the hot beef soup over the noodles.
Top with bean sprouts, cilantro, mint, green onions, and halved hard-boiled eggs.

title: Larb Moo (Minced Pork Salad)
ingredients: 3 stalks lemongrass, white part only, minced
instructions: Stir-fry minced pork in a hot pan until cooked through and slightly crispy.
Add minced lemongrass and torn kaffir lime leaves to the pan and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and let the meat cool slightly.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, toasted rice powder, and chilies in a small bowl.
Combine the cooled pork mixture with the dressing and mix well.
Serve the Larb topped with shredded green papaya, mint, and cilantro.
Garnish with a dollop of raw egg white on the side or over the top.

title: Khao Soi (Curry Noodles)
ingredients: 2 cups rice noodles, broken in half
1 lb chicken thigh, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 tbsp curry paste (Lao style with lemongrass and galangal)
instructions: Boil the rice noodles according to package directions until tender, then drain.
In a large pot, heat oil and fry curry paste until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk, water, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Stir in lime juice and adjust seasoning to taste.
Ladle the curry and chicken over the noodles in a bowl.
Top with hard-boiled egg quarters, bean sprouts, and green onions.
Serve immediately with lime wedges, red chili flakes, and sesame oil on the side.

title: Tam Mak Hoong (Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 3 stalks lemongrass, white part only, minced
instructions: In a large bowl, combine shredded papaya, red bell pepper, and carrot.
Add minced chilies, lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves.
In a small bowl, whisk together fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and tamarind paste.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently to coat evenly.
Add crushed peanuts and dried shrimp.
Toss again until all ingredients are well mixed.
Serve immediately while the papaya is still crisp.

title: Khao Jee (Steamed Rice with Chili)
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: Rinse the soaked rice until the water runs clear.
In a pot, heat oil and toast cumin and coriander seeds until fragrant.
Add the lemongrass stalk and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir to coat with the spiced oil.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and steam for 15-20 minutes until the rice is tender and water is absorbed.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in chili flakes, cilantro, and green onion.
Serve hot in small portions with lime wedges and pickled mustard greens on the side.

title: Khanom Chin (Fried Rice Cakes)
ingredients: 1/4 cup toasted sesame seeds, for topping
instructions: Mix rice flour, tapioca starch, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add warm water, coconut milk, and pandan extract while stirring.
Knead the mixture until a smooth, soft dough forms that doesn't stick to hands.
Roll the dough into small balls and flatten them into thin circles.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the rice cake circles until golden brown on both sides.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Dip the fried cakes in sugar syrup if desired.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Bahan Thoke (Yang Htoe Thoke)
instructions: Fry sliced onions in mutton fat until golden and fragrant.
Add minced garlic and chili, stir for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add fish sauce, sugar, and peanuts, stir well to combine.
Toss the cooked rice noodles in the sauce until evenly coated.
Serve on a plate topped with lettuce, sliced eggs, coriander, and spring onions.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Mont Yoke (Fish and Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs fresh river fish, cleaned and cut into chunks
12 oz dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Bring stock to a boil in a large pot.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, ginger, and salt to the boiling stock.
Gently add fish chunks and cook for 3-4 minutes until the fish is just cooked through.
Add sugar and taste for seasoning.
Drain the soaked noodles and add them to the soup.
Stir in the sliced shallots and serve hot in bowls topped with coriander.

title: Nga Thoke (Shredded Chicken Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup dried shrimp, fried and crushed
instructions: Combine cabbage, carrots, and shallots in a large mixing bowl.
Add shredded chicken, crushed peanuts, chopped eggs, and fried shrimp.
In a small cup, mix lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, and chili powder to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Top with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish or main course.

title: Mont Ko (Steamed Fish with Ginger)
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, white part only, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tbsp dried shrimp, fried and crushed
instructions: Make three diagonal cuts on the fish body.
Stuff the ginger and lemongrass pieces inside the fish cavity.
Place fish in a steamer basket over boiling water.
Steam for 10-12 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
While steaming, mix fish sauce, sugar, white pepper, soy sauce, and oil in a small bowl.
Pour the sauce over the steamed fish.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts, fried shrimp, coriander, and spring onions.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Poke (Roasted Chicken with Chili)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs chicken thighs, boneless and skinless
2-3 bird's eye chilies, sliced (adjust to taste)
instructions: In a bowl, mix garlic, ginger, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and pepper.
Add chicken pieces to the marinade and let sit for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the marinated chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked through (about 8-10 minutes), turning occasionally.
Add sliced chilies to the pan during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Transfer cooked chicken to a serving platter.
Drizzle with lime juice and sprinkle with coriander, spring onions, and crushed peanuts.
Serve hot with steamed rice or as a main dish.

title: Pho Bo (Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 2 lbs beef shank bones, cut into large chunks
1 lb beef brisket, cut into large chunks
1 stalk lemongrass, bruised and cut into 4-inch pieces
12 oz rice noodles, soaked until soft
instructions: Roast beef bones and brisket in the oven at 400°F for 30 minutes to brown.
Place bones, brisket, ginger, lemongrass, star anise, cinnamon, and cloves in a large pot with water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 4 hours.
Skim off any scum that rises to the surface during the first hour.
Add brisket to the soup and cook for another 2 hours until tender.
Strain the broth and reserve the liquid.
Cook rice noodles according to package directions.
Assemble bowls with noodles, beef slices, and broth.
Garnish with green onions, cilantro, mint, lime, and fish sauce.

title: Com Tam (Broken Rice with Grilled Pork)
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and broken into small grains
1/2 lb pork belly, sliced into strips
instructions: Marinate pork belly and shoulder with fish sauce, sugar, lemongrass, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Grill pork slices over high heat until charred and cooked through.
Toast the broken rice in a pan with a little oil until fragrant.
Serve rice in bowls topped with grilled pork slices.
Arrange pickled vegetables, cucumber, eggs, cilantro, mint, and green onions on the side.
Drizzle with a little extra fish sauce or soy sauce if desired.

title: Bun Cha (Grilled Pork with Noodles)
ingredients: 1 lb pork belly, scored in a crosshatch pattern
instructions: Mix fish sauce, sugar, pepper, soy sauce, and water to make the marinade.
Marinate pork belly and shoulder in the mixture for at least 3 hours.
Grill pork belly over charcoal until crispy and well-charred.
Grill pork shoulder slices until cooked through.
Cook rice vermicelli noodles until soft.
Assemble bowls with noodles, grilled pork, and fresh herbs.
Serve with lime wedges, cucumber, pickled onions, and a dipping sauce made from fish sauce and lime.

title: Banh Mi (Vietnamese Baguette)
instructions: Marinate pork shoulder with fish sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and lemongrass for 2 hours.
Grill pork slices until cooked through and slightly charred.
Toast the baguette slices lightly.
Spread pate and mayonnaise inside the baguette.
Layer grilled pork, Vietnamese ham, pickled vegetables, cucumber, and herbs.
Drizzle with chili sauce if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Cao Lau (Central Highlands Noodle Soup)
ingredients: 1/2 lb pork belly, sliced into small pieces
instructions: Simmer pork belly, pork shoulder, and beef brisket in water with lemongrass, ginger, star anise, and cinnamon for 3 hours.
Strain the broth and reserve the liquid.
Cook rice noodles until soft.
Fry pork belly slices in oil until crispy.
Assemble bowls with noodles, fried pork, and sliced meats.
Pour hot broth over the ingredients.
Top with bean sprouts, cilantro, mint, and green onions.
Serve with chili oil and lime juice on the side.

title: Adobo
ingredients: 1 kg chicken parts, cut into serving sizes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaf; let marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Heat lard or oil in a heavy pot over medium heat until hot.
Remove chicken from marinade, discarding the solids, and brown on all sides.
Pour the reserved marinade and water into the pot with the chicken.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour until meat is tender.
Uncover, increase heat slightly, and simmer until the sauce thickens to a gravy-like consistency.
Serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat until smoking.
Add garlic and kaffir lime leaves, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add cooled rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Pour in sweet soy sauce, fish sauce, and salt; toss to coat evenly.
Add peas and scrambled eggs, mixing gently until heated through.
Serve hot with a side of fried egg and cucumber slices.

title: Soto Ayam Betawi
ingredients: 2 liters chicken broth, simmered with bones
4 slices longan fruit (can be substituted with lychee)
instructions: Simmer chicken broth with bones, ginger, galangal, lemongrass, and spices until flavorful.
Strain the broth and return to a gentle simmer.
Add shredded chicken and cook until just heated through.
Stir in longan fruit and salt.
Ladle into bowls, top with green onions, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Gado-Gado Jakarta
instructions: Boil bean sprouts, beans, spinach, and kangkung until tender-crisp.
Fry bean curd cake and tempeh until golden.
Blend peanut butter, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and tamarind with warm water to make sauce.
Arrange all vegetables and fried items in a bowl.
Drizzle generously with peanut sauce and serve immediately.

title: Rendang Daging Padang
instructions: Fry ground spices, garlic, shallots, and candlenuts in oil until dark brown.
Add beef and stir-fry until the meat releases its water.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer on low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add coconut cream and palm sugar, continuing to cook on very low heat.
Cook until the oil separates and the meat is dark, dry, and tender.

title: Sate Ayam Madura
ingredients: 100g peanut sauce ingredients (peanuts, shrimp paste, shallots, garlic, spices)
instructions: Marinate chicken with shallots, garlic, kecap manis, pepper, salt, and sugar for 2 hours.
Thread chicken pieces onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Grill skewers over charcoal until charred and cooked through, turning frequently.
Blend peanuts with spices and water to make a thick peanut sauce.
Serve hot sate with peanut sauce and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 2 lbs large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Bring chicken stock to a boil in a large pot.
Add galangal, lime leaves, chilies, lemongrass, and mushrooms.
Simmer for 5 minutes to release flavors.
Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes until pink.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot garnished with fresh lime leaves.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
Mix fish sauce, tamarind paste, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Scramble eggs and remove from pan.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add tofu, carrots, and bean sprouts; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return eggs to the wok, add noodles, and toss.
Pour in the sauce mixture and cook until coated.
Serve immediately topped with peanuts, cilantro, and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
ingredients: 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Pour off about 1/4 cup of coconut cream from the can, set aside.
In a pot, heat the cream with curry paste over medium heat.
Add stock and bring to a simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, bell peppers, and mushrooms.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry if desired.
Serve hot garnished with fresh basil leaves.

title: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-fry)
ingredients: Fried egg, sunny side up, for serving
instructions: In a wok, heat oil and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add ground meat and cook until browned.
Stir in fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar.
Add chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and toss in holy basil leaves.
Serve over steamed rice topped with a fried egg.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 cup beef stew meat or chicken thighs, cubed
instructions: In a pot, combine coconut milk, curry paste, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Add meat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add potatoes, eggplant, and onion.
Simmer for another 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve warm garnished with fresh cilantro.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Combine tamarind paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side, pour in beaten eggs, and scramble until set.
Add noodles to the wok and toss to combine with the eggs.
Pour in the sauce mixture and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until noodles are coated.
Add shrimp or tofu and cook until heated through.
Stir in bean sprouts and chili paste, then cook for another minute.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts, lime wedges, and extra bean sprouts.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
4 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a large pot, heat oil over medium-high heat.
Add lemongrass, galangal, ginger, and torn lime leaves; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add shrimp and cook until they turn pink, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chili paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in water, fish sauce, and lime juice; bring to a simmer.
Season to taste with more lime juice or fish sauce if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with whole lime leaves.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: In a large pot, heat 1/4 cup of the coconut milk over medium heat.
Add curry paste and sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in bamboo shoots, eggplant, lemongrass, and lime leaves.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in basil and chilies just before serving.
Serve hot over jasmine rice.

title: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-Fry)
instructions: In a small bowl, mix fish sauce, oyster sauce, and brown sugar.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until golden.
Add ground pork and cook until browned and crumbled.
Pour in the sauce mixture and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add Thai chilies and cook for another minute.
Stir in holy basil leaves and cook until wilted.
Top with scrambled eggs and serve immediately over jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: In a mortar and pestle, pound garlic and chilies until fragrant.
Add shredded papaya and long beans; pound lightly to break them down.
Stir in tomatoes and pound gently.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and water gradually to taste.
Stir well until the mixture is well combined and seasoned.
Top with crushed peanuts and cilantro leaves.
Serve immediately as a refreshing appetizer or side dish.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water until soft, then drain.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Scramble the eggs in the wok, then remove.
Add garlic and noodles to the wok, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Return eggs to the wok and add the sauce mixture.
Stir in bean sprouts and peanuts, cooking until heated through.
Garnish with green onions and serve with lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: Combine chicken broth, kaffir lime leaves, chilies, galangal, ginger, and lemongrass in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until they turn pink, about 3 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Kiew Wan)
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add green curry paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the thick part of the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and bell pepper; cook for 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime leaves.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Garnish with Thai basil and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add Massaman curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add beef, cinnamon stick, and cardamom; brown the meat.
Pour in the thick part of the coconut milk and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add potatoes and eggplant; cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Simmer until potatoes are tender and sauce thickens.
Remove cinnamon stick and cardamom pods before serving.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Place papaya, tomatoes, long beans, and water chestnuts in a mortar.
Add garlic and chilies; pound lightly to release juices.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar; pound gently to mix.
Stir in dried shrimp and peanuts without over-pounding.
Serve immediately as a salad.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add shrimp or chicken and cook until just done.
Push ingredients to the side, pour in beaten eggs, and scramble.
Add noodles and the sauce mixture, tossing continuously to coat.
Add bean sprouts and cook for another minute until heated through.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts, lime wedges, and fresh cilantro.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 3 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Bring stock to a boil in a large pot.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, chilies, and galangal; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar to taste.
Add straw mushrooms and shrimp to the broth.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until shrimp turn pink and mushrooms are tender.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil leaves.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: In a pot, heat the thick part of the coconut milk over medium heat.
Add green curry paste and stir until fragrant.
Pour in broth and bring to a simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and bell pepper; cook for 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until fully done.
Stir in palm sugar and fish sauce to balance flavors.
Add torn kaffir lime leaf and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Turn off heat and stir in fresh Thai basil leaves before serving.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Place shredded papaya, mung beans, chilies, garlic, and tomatoes in a mortar.
Pound gently to bruise the ingredients without turning them into a paste.
Add fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice; pound lightly to combine.
Add water or coconut milk gradually if a softer texture is desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more lime, salt, or sugar as needed.
Serve immediately garnished with fresh coriander.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: In a pot, combine coconut milk, broth, and curry paste; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add cinnamon stick and star anise to infuse flavor.
Add beef cubes and simmer covered for 1 hour until tender.
Add potatoes, onion, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Continue cooking uncovered for another 20 minutes until potatoes are soft.
Remove cinnamon stick and star anise before serving.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Fry garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add beaten eggs and scramble until set.
Add soaked noodles, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar; toss to coat.
Stir in bean sprouts and green onions.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: Bring stock to a simmer with lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal, and chilies.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Serve hot.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Kiew Wan)
instructions: Simmer coconut milk and stock together.
Add curry paste and stir until dissolved.
Add bamboo shoots, bell peppers, and eggplant.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar; garnish with lime leaves.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: Simmer coconut milk, stock, and cinnamon stick.
Add curry paste and stir well.
Add potatoes, onions, and eggplant.
Simmer until vegetables are soft.
Stir in peanut butter, fish sauce, and palm sugar; serve.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar until slightly crushed.
Add shredded papaya and long beans; pound gently.
Add tomatoes and stir to mix.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Top with peanuts and serve immediately.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 oz rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Drain and rinse soaked noodles, then set aside.
Whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar in a bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side, pour in eggs, and scramble quickly.
Add noodles and sauce mixture, tossing continuously for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in bean sprouts and chicken until heated through.
Remove from heat and garnish with peanuts and chili flakes.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large pot, combine chicken broth, lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal, chilies, mushrooms, and sugar.
Bring the broth to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp to the simmering broth and cook for 2-3 minutes until they turn pink.
Stir in fish sauce and lime juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot in bowls, garnished with extra lime leaves if desired.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté green curry paste for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in the thick cream from the coconut milk can and stir to combine.
Add the remaining coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and baby corn to the pot.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender but still crisp.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil leaves.
Serve hot over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/4 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Combine shredded papaya, chilies, shallots, tomatoes, long beans, and garlic in a mortar.
Pound the ingredients gently to bruish them slightly, being careful not to mush the vegetables.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and chili flakes, then pound again to mix.
Taste and adjust seasoning until balanced.
Transfer to a bowl, top with crushed peanuts and roasted peanuts.
Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish or main course.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 cup potatoes, cut into large chunks
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and sauté cinnamon stick and star anise for 1 minute.
Add massaman curry paste and stir for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the thick cream from the coconut milk can and stir well.
Add the remaining coconut milk, beef broth, potatoes, and onions.
Bring to a simmer, then add beef cubes.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until beef is tender and potatoes are soft.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Remove cinnamon stick and star anise, then stir in crushed peanuts.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving over rice.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Combine tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar in a bowl to make sauce.
Fry shrimp in oil until pink, remove and set aside.
Scramble eggs in the same pan, remove and set aside.
Cook noodles in boiling water until tender, drain.
Stir-fry garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add noodles, sauce, shrimp, and eggs to the pan.
Toss until heated through.
Garnish with bean sprouts, carrots, peanuts, and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: Heat stock in a pot and add kaffir lime leaves, chilies, lemongrass, and galangal.
Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, about 2 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer gently.
Season to taste with more fish sauce or lime juice if needed.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and fry green curry paste until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and bell pepper.
Simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and chicken stock.
Cook for another 5 minutes to meld flavors.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil leaves.
Serve hot over jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Grate green papaya and shred carrots into fine strips.
Cut long beans into 1-inch pieces.
Place papaya, carrots, and long beans in a mortar.
Add chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste if using.
Pound gently until slightly crushed but not mushy.
Pour in fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and water.
Pound again to mix and dissolve the sugar.
Stir in crushed peanuts.
Serve immediately as a fresh salad.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry curry paste until fragrant.
Add beef and cook until browned on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add onion, potato, and beef stock.
Simmer covered for 45 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste.
Add bell pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in crushed peanuts and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Adjust seasoning with more sugar or fish sauce if needed.
Serve over jasmine rice.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 oz rice noodles, soaked in warm water until soft
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
Whisk fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side and scramble eggs in the wok.
Add noodles and sauce mixture, tossing to combine.
Stir in bean sprouts and peanuts.
Serve hot with lime wedges on the side.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: Combine chicken stock, lime leaves, chilies, lemongrass, and galangal in a pot.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add straw mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until they turn pink (about 2 minutes).
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Serve immediately with rice noodles on the side.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Kiew Wan)
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup coconut milk in a pot over medium heat.
Stir in curry paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, and chicken.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, long beans, and eggplant.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and chili flakes.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-fry)
ingredients: 4 eggs, fried sunny-side up and sliced
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic and chilies until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned.
Mix oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar; pour over pork.
Stir quickly for 1 minute until sauce coats the meat.
Toss in holy basil leaves until wilted.
Serve immediately over steamed rice topped with fried egg slices.

title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
instructions: Combine chicken stock, lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, ginger, and mushrooms in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add chicken slices and cook until just done.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Strain the soup if desired, or serve with ingredients intact.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 2 lbs large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: In a large pot, combine chicken stock, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and shallots; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add mushrooms and straw mushrooms; cook for 3-4 minutes until tender.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and chili paste; simmer for 2 minutes.
Add shrimp and tofu; cook for 2-3 minutes until shrimp turn pink.
Turn off heat and stir in holy basil leaves before serving.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 1 lb rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
1/2 lb firm tofu, cubed and pressed
instructions: Whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Push garlic to the side; scramble eggs in the wok until set.
Add tofu and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Add drained rice noodles and the sauce; toss continuously for 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in bean sprouts and green onions.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts, dried shrimp, and lime wedges.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
ingredients: 1 lb green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat; sauté green curry paste for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in the thick cream from the coconut can; cook for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining coconut milk, water, and fish sauce; bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in bamboo shoots, eggplant, and green beans; simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add palm sugar and stir until dissolved.
Turn off heat and stir in kaffir lime leaves and Thai basil leaves.
Garnish with sliced red chilies before serving.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a mortar, pound lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, chilies, and shallots until fragrant.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar; pound gently to combine.
Add shredded papaya and long beans; pound lightly to mix.
Add cherry tomatoes and peanuts; toss gently by hand to avoid crushing tomatoes.
Serve immediately while ingredients are crisp.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: In a large pot, combine coconut milk, curry paste, cinnamon stick, and star anise; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add beef and cook for 15 minutes until browned.
Add potatoes and eggplant; simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar; simmer for another 5 minutes.
Remove cinnamon stick and star anise.
Stir in crushed peanuts and kaffir lime leaves before serving.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side, add eggs, and scramble until set.
Add noodles and sauce mixture; toss to combine.
Add bean sprouts and cook for 1-2 minutes until tender.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts, green onions, and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Bring chicken stock to a boil in a pot.
Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes until pink.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: Heat 100ml coconut milk in a pot until it just begins to boil.
Stir in curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add remaining coconut milk, stock, bamboo shoots, eggplant, and baby corn.
Simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: In a pot, fry curry paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add cinnamon stick, cardamom, and star anise; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add beef, potato, and carrot; cover and cook for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Stir in palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Remove spices with a slotted spoon.
Garnish with cilantro leaves and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: Combine fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar in a mortar; crush to dissolve sugar.
Add garlic and chilies; pound lightly to release flavors.
Add long beans and pound until slightly broken.
Add papaya and tomatoes; pound gently to mix without turning papaya to mush.
Stir in crushed peanuts and dried shrimp.
Serve immediately while crisp.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 2 lbs large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/2 cup lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Bring fish stock to a boil in a large pot.
Add lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved.
Serve hot.

title: Pad Thai
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain.
Whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and water to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add beaten eggs and scramble until set.
Add tofu (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Toss in drained noodles and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the sauce until noodles are glossy and coated.
Top with bean sprouts, green onions, and crushed peanuts.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: In a pot, simmer the thick part of the coconut milk with curry paste over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and bell pepper; cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the thin part of the coconut milk.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Add kaffir lime leaves and red curry leaves, then simmer for 1 minute.
Serve hot over jasmine rice.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: Brown the beef in a pot over medium heat; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, simmer the thick coconut milk with curry paste for 5 minutes.
Return beef to the pot and add potatoes and onions.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1 hour until beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in roasted peanuts and water if a thinner consistency is desired.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a mortar, pound garlic, chilies, lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar until well blended.
Add the shredded papaya and pound gently until slightly crushed.
