Add tomatoes, long beans, and peanuts; pound lightly to mix.
Add a splash of water if a softer texture is preferred.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Drain the soaked rice noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side, pour in beaten eggs, and scramble until set.
Add shrimp and cook until pink and cooked through.
Add noodles and the sauce mixture, tossing continuously for 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in bean sprouts and green onions.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken stock, lime leaves, galangal, garlic, chilies, lemongrass, straw mushrooms, and shrimp.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: In a pot, heat 100ml of thick coconut milk over medium heat until it just begins to simmer.
Add green curry paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add remaining coconut milk, bamboo shoots, eggplant, bell pepper, and baby corn.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer for another 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, discard lemongrass and lime leaves, and stir in Thai basil.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Massaman Curry
instructions: In a pot, combine curry paste, cinnamon stick, and star anise.
Add 100ml of coconut milk and simmer for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef or chicken and cook until the meat changes color.
Add onions, potatoes, and remaining coconut milk.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes until meat is tender.
Stir in crushed peanuts, evaporated milk, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Remove cinnamon stick and star anise, stir in basil, and serve with rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: In a mortar, pound garlic, chilies, and kaffir lime leaves to a coarse paste.
Add tomatoes, long beans, and peanuts; pound lightly to crush them slightly.
Add shredded green papaya and pound until the mixture is well combined and slightly bruised.
Gradually add fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar, pounding until dissolved.
Add crushed dried shrimp and toss to combine.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve immediately.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
Fresh cilantro and sliced peanuts for garnish
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
Whisk together fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add beaten eggs and scramble until just set, then push to the side.
Add noodles and sauce mixture, tossing continuously for 3-4 minutes.
Add chicken or tofu and bean sprouts, cooking until sprouts are crisp-tender.
Serve immediately with lime wedges, crushed peanuts, cilantro, and extra chili if desired.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 4 slices lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Bring broth to a simmer in a large pot.
Add kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes.
Increase heat to high and add shrimp; cook for 2-3 minutes until pink.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar to taste.
Remove from heat and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: In a medium pot, heat the thick part of the coconut milk over medium heat until just simmering.
Stir in green curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken strips and cook until no longer pink.
Add bamboo shoots, eggplant, and bell peppers; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves.
If using, add Thai long beans and cook for 2 more minutes.
Serve hot in bowls, topped with fresh basil leaves.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 can (14 oz) evaporated milk or full-fat coconut milk
instructions: In a pot, combine beef, cinnamon stick, star anise, and bay leaf with a splash of water; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in curry paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add onion, potato, and the thick part of the coconut milk; simmer for 20 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in evaporated milk, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer gently for another 10 minutes until sauce thickens and potatoes are soft.
Remove whole spices and garnish with crushed roasted peanuts before serving.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1 cup fresh long beans, halved and blanched
instructions: In a mortar and pestle, pound garlic, chilies, and a pinch of salt until paste forms.
Add palm sugar and pound until it dissolves.
Add lime juice and fish sauce; pound gently to combine.
Add shredded papaya, carrots, and long beans; pound lightly to release juices but keep texture.
Stir in crushed peanuts and mix well.
Serve immediately, garnished with tomato wedges and fresh cilantro.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 oz rice noodles, soaked in warm water until soft
2 tbsp palm sugar, dissolved in warm water
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
Whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and dissolved sugar to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side and scramble the eggs in the hot oil.
Add the noodles and toss to coat with egg, then pour in the sauce.
Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until noodles are heated through and coated.
Remove from heat and immediately toss in bean sprouts, crushed peanuts, and green onions.
Serve hot with extra peanuts and lime wedges on the side.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
6 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 lb fish balls, sliced into quarters
2 tbsp Thai bird's eye chilies, sliced
instructions: In a large pot, bring chicken stock to a boil over high heat.
Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies; simmer for 5 minutes to infuse flavors.
Stir in tomato paste and fish balls, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add shrimp and straw mushrooms; cook for another 2 minutes until shrimp turn pink.
Remove from heat and stir in fish sauce and lime juice to taste.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately in bowls.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
ingredients: 1 lb green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 cup bamboo shoots (optional for extra texture)
instructions: Pour the thick part of the coconut milk into a large pot and heat over medium heat.
Stir in the green curry paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add bamboo shoots and eggplant; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add green beans and red bell pepper; cook for another 5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, tasting to adjust saltiness and sweetness.
Stir in the fresh Thai basil leaves and turn off the heat.
Let it simmer for 1 minute to wilt the basil, then serve hot with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Prik Khanom
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain and set aside.
In a wok, heat oil over medium-high heat and stir-fry garlic until golden.
Add chicken slices and cook until just cooked through.
Add green beans and bean sprouts; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the drained noodles and toss to combine with the vegetables and chicken.
Pour in fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and chili paste; toss vigorously for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in chopped Thai basil before serving.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: In a large pot, heat a little oil and brown the beef cubes; remove and set aside.
Add star anise and cinnamon stick to the pot; fry for 1 minute, then add curry paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return the beef to the pot and add potatoes, onions, peanuts, brown sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Simmer covered on low heat for 1.5 hours until beef is tender and potatoes are soft.
Adjust seasoning if needed, then stir in fresh cilantro.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice and a side of cucumber salad.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 1 lb rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
2 tbsp palm sugar, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
1 cup shredded chicken or tofu, cooked
Fresh lime wedges and Thai basil leaves for garnish
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, and dissolved sugar.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add garlic and stir for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side, pour in beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add noodles, sauce mixture, and cooked protein; toss continuously for 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in bean sprouts and crushed peanuts.
Serve immediately topped with fresh lime wedges and Thai basil.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 lemongrass stalk, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, chilies, galangal, and onion; sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until tender.
Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes until they turn pink and opaque.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add green curry paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in half the coconut milk and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add broth, bamboo shoots, and eggplant; cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in red bell pepper and remaining coconut milk.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar.
Remove from heat and fold in fresh basil leaves.
Serve hot garnished with chopped peanuts.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp coriander seeds, toasted and ground
instructions: In a heavy pot, brown beef over medium-high heat until sealed on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion, cardamom, and cinnamon sticks for 2 minutes.
Stir in curry paste and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar; mix well.
Return beef to the pot along with half the coconut milk and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add potatoes and remaining coconut milk; cook for another 20 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in crushed peanuts.
Adjust seasoning with salt or sugar if needed.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup long beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Place a stone mortar in the center of the table.
Add garlic and chilies; pound gently with the pestle until slightly crushed.
Add dried shrimp and pound lightly to release flavor.
Add shredded papaya and long beans; pound and crush slightly.
Add peanuts and pound gently to mix.
Pour in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar; mix thoroughly.
Stir in chili powder if using.
Transfer to a bowl and top with cucumber slices.
Serve immediately.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 oz dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
2 tbsp palm sugar, dissolved in 1/4 cup water
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
Whisk together fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind paste.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Scramble eggs in the wok, then remove.
Add noodles to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return eggs to the wok and toss with the sauce.
Add bean sprouts and peanuts, cook for 1 more minute.
Serve immediately with green onions, lime wedges, and extra peanuts.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 lemongrass stalk, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, chilies, and galangal; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, about 2 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot garnished with fresh cilantro.

title: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
instructions: Heat 1/2 cup of coconut milk in a pot over medium heat.
Stir in curry paste and cook until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and water.
Add bamboo shoots and bell peppers; simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime leaf.
Remove from heat and stir in Thai basil leaves.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Mince garlic and set aside.
Combine fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and garlic in a mortar.
Pound the mixture until smooth.
Add chilies, tomatoes, green beans, and papaya; pound gently.
Stir in dried shrimp, peanuts, and a splash of water.
Mix well until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Massaman Curry
ingredients: 1 lb beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Toast coriander seeds and cinnamon stick in a dry pan until fragrant.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add curry paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef and brown on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add potatoes, onions, fish sauce, and sugar.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour until meat is tender.
Stir in peanuts before serving.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 8 oz dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
1/2 cup tamarind paste, diluted with 1 cup water
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the tamarind paste, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic until fragrant.
Push garlic to the side and scramble the beaten eggs in the hot oil.
Add the noodles and toss to coat with the egg.
Pour in the tamarind mixture and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until noodles are heated through.
Remove from heat and immediately toss in bean sprouts, peanuts, dried shrimp, and cilantro.
Serve hot with lime wedges on the side.

title: Tom Kha Gai
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
4 stalks lemongrass, white parts only, bruised
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken broth, lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal. Bring to a simmer.
Add the sliced chicken and cook for 3 minutes until just cooked through.
Stir in the straw mushrooms and cook for another 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer; do not boil vigorously.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice to taste.
Remove the lemongrass stalks and galangal slices before serving.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Khao Soi
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
1/2 lb rice noodles, flat wide variety
1 tbsp curry paste, red or green
instructions: In a heavy pot, sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in oil until soft.
Add curry paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, palm sugar, and fish sauce; simmer for 10 more minutes.
Remove chicken and shred the meat, discarding bones and excess fat.
Return shredded chicken to the soup and simmer for 5 minutes.
In separate bowls, place a layer of egg noodles and a layer of rice noodles.
Pour hot curry soup over the noodles and top with cashews and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup green beans, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Combine lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and shrimp paste in a mortar and pound until the sugar dissolves.
Add the garlic and dried chilies and pound gently to release their oils.
Add the green papaya, green beans, and tomatoes, and pound lightly to bruise but not mushy.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Stir in the crushed peanuts and roasted rice powder if using.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more lime, fish sauce, or sugar as needed.
Serve immediately as a side dish.

title: Khao Pad (Fried Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
1/2 cup sweet corn, fresh or frozen
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the minced pork until browned.
Push pork to the side and scramble the beaten eggs in the same oil.
Add the cooled rice, corn, and peas to the wok and break up any clumps.
Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, ensuring the rice grains are separate and hot.
Season with fish sauce, oyster sauce, and white pepper, tossing continuously.
Remove from heat and fold in the bean sprouts and chopped green onions.
Serve hot with lime wedges on the side.

title: Khao Soi
ingredients: 2 cups chicken stock, simmered for 2 hours
1 lb chicken thigh, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup tamarind paste, diluted with water
1/2 cup crispy egg noodles, broken into pieces
Fresh coriander leaves and sliced chilies for garnish
instructions: Fry the curry paste in oil until fragrant and slightly dark.
Add the chicken pieces and stir-fry until they change color.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add coconut milk, and simmer until the chicken is tender and the broth is rich.
Stir in the tamarind paste to taste for sourness.
Season with salt and fish sauce.
Serve the soup in a bowl, placing a portion of noodles and chicken on top.
Add a hard-boiled egg, sprinkle with crispy noodles, coriander, and chilies.
Serve immediately with a wedge of lime to squeeze over the top.

title: Pad Prik Khing
ingredients: 1 lb mixed vegetables (green beans, snow peas, carrots, bell peppers)
1 cup dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
instructions: Blanch the mixed vegetables in boiling water for 2 minutes, then shock in ice water.
In a wok, heat oil and fry the dried chili flakes until red and fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken and dried shrimp, stir-frying until the chicken is cooked through.
Pour in the chicken stock, fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar.
Simmer the sauce until it thickens slightly.
Add the blanched vegetables and toss to coat evenly in the spicy-sweet sauce.
Cook for another minute until the vegetables are heated through but still crisp.
Remove from heat and garnish generously with fresh basil leaves.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Gaeng Tai Pla
ingredients: 1 lb freshwater fish (like snakehead or catfish), cut into chunks
1/4 cup dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
instructions: Fry the yellow curry paste in a bit of oil until it releases its aroma.
Add the fish chunks and dried shrimp, stirring gently to coat with the paste.
Pour in half of the coconut milk and the stock, bringing to a simmer.
Add the Thai eggplant and green beans, cooking until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste and palm sugar to balance the flavors.
Reduce heat and let the curry simmer gently until the oil separates from the coconut milk.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk and the fresh basil leaves.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more sugar or tamarind if needed.
Serve hot with steamed rice and a side of lime wedges.

title: Tom Kha Gai
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
1/2 cup lemongrass, white parts only, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
Fresh Thai basil leaves for garnish
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken stock, galangal, lemongrass, and lime leaves. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the galangal is fragrant.
Add the chicken strips and cook until just opaque.
Stir in the coconut milk, water chestnuts, and straw mushrooms.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Season with fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar.
Remove the galangal and lemongrass pieces before serving.
Garnish with fresh Thai basil leaves and chopped peanuts.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Sai Oua (Northern Thai Sausage)
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried shrimp, soaked and ground
instructions: Mix the ground pork, chicken, and ground dried shrimp in a large bowl.
Add the toasted rice powder, shallots, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and lime zest.
Stir in the ground coriander, cumin, white pepper, palm sugar, fish sauce, and salt.
Knead the mixture thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined and the texture is uniform.
Soak the natural casings in water for 30 minutes to soften them.
Using a sausage stuffer, stuff the mixture into the casings, leaving small gaps between links.
Tie off the links with kitchen twine or string.
Boil the sausages in water for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from water, let cool slightly, and slice diagonally to serve with sticky rice and a spicy dip.

title: Khao Pad Sai-Ouan (Isan Style Fried Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
1 cup green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp palm sugar, dissolved in water
instructions: Season the beaten eggs with a pinch of salt and fry them sunny-side up, then chop into bite-sized pieces.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until bright green and tender-crisp.
Push the vegetables to the side and scramble the eggs in the empty space, mixing them with the beans.
Add the cooled rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until hot.
Pour in the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and sugar mixture.
Toss in the chopped fried eggs and crushed peanuts.
Stir-fry for another minute until the rice is evenly coated and heated through.
Serve immediately.

title: Larb Moo (Minced Pork Salad)
ingredients: In a mortar, pound the garlic, chilies, and half of the roasted rice powder until a coarse paste forms.
Add the remaining rice powder and pound briefly to mix.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and cook the minced pork until browned and cooked through.
Transfer the pork to a large bowl and let it cool slightly.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar to the pork and toss well.
Stir in the chili-garlic paste and mix thoroughly.
Fold in the mint, cilantro, and green beans just before serving.
Serve with sticky rice and fresh cucumber slices.

title: Nam Prik Num (Green Chili Paste Dip)
instructions: Combine the green chilies, tomatoes, garlic, and roasted rice powder in a mortar.
Pound the ingredients until they form a smooth, thick paste.
Transfer the paste to a small pot over low heat.
Add the fish sauce and palm sugar, stirring to dissolve.
Gradually pour in the water while stirring constantly to prevent splattering.
Cook for about 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Remove from heat and stir in the crushed peanuts.
Serve warm as a dip with grilled pork or sticky rice.

title: Gaeng Som (Isan Sour Soup)
ingredients: 1 cup tamarind concentrate, mixed with 1 cup water
1 cup fresh green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 cup red or green chilies, sliced
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the beef slices for 30 seconds, then remove and set aside.
In a separate pot, combine the tamarind concentrate, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the long beans and green beans, cooking until tender-crisp.
Add the blanched beef, tomato, chilies, lime leaves, and kaffir lime leaves.
Stir well and simmer gently for 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, and sweet.
Serve hot in bowls with sticky rice.

title: Khao Niao Tod (Fried Sticky Rice with Eggs)
ingredients: 2 cups sticky rice, soaked for 4 hours and drained
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat and scramble the eggs.
Once the eggs are set, push them to one side of the wok.
Add the sticky rice to the empty side and stir-fry until the grains separate and are hot.
Mix the rice and eggs together, then add the fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until the rice is slightly crispy on the outside.
Gently fold in the green beans, crushed peanuts, and sesame seeds.
Serve hot as a side dish or snack.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Drain noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, palm sugar, and fish sauce until dissolved.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and scramble the eggs, then push to the side.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add noodles and sauce mixture, tossing constantly for 2-3 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and peanuts, cook until heated through.
Serve immediately with lime wedges, cilantro, and chili flakes on the side.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 4 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken broth, coconut milk, lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and chilies.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes to release aromatics.
Add mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until tender.
Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes until they turn pink and opaque.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh basil leaves just before serving.

title: Gaeng Kiew Wan (Green Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the red chili and curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add coconut cream and stir well to combine with the paste.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add bamboo shoots, chicken, and eggplant. Cook for 5 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in lime leaves, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Simmer for another 3 minutes until the curry thickens slightly.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving with jasmine rice.

title: Khao Soi
instructions: In a pot, combine broth, coconut milk, curry paste, palm sugar, fish sauce, turmeric, and chili flakes.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Add chicken slices and cook until just done.
Add sliced onions and cook until slightly softened but still crisp.
In a separate pot, cook the wide rice noodles according to package instructions.
Divide noodles into bowls, top with the chicken curry mixture, and arrange egg quarters on top.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 cup long beans, sliced into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a mortar and pestle, pound the chilies, garlic, and lemongrass until slightly crushed but not pureed.
Add the shredded papaya, carrots, and long beans. Pound gently to release juices.
Stir in the lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar, tasting to adjust seasoning.
Toss in the crushed peanuts, tomatoes, and mint leaves.
Serve immediately in a bowl, ensuring the ingredients are evenly mixed.

title: Gaeng Som Pla (Fish in Sour Soup)
ingredients: 500g Thai sea bass or mackerel, cut into chunks
instructions: Bring tamarind water and fish sauce to a simmer in a pot.
Add galangal, lemongrass, and lime leaves to the soup.
Gently poach the fish chunks until they are just opaque.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer for 2 minutes without boiling.
Add cherry tomatoes and serve hot.

title: Pad Krapow Moo Saap (Holy Basil Stir-fry)
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic and dried chilies until fragrant.
Add minced pork and cook until browned and crispy.
Stir in fish sauce and oyster sauce.
Toss in holy basil leaves until they wilt slightly.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice with sliced eggs on top.

title: Khao Pad Gai (Classic Thai Fried Rice)
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, day-old and cooled
instructions: Scramble the eggs in a hot wok with a bit of oil and set aside.
Add more oil and stir-fry the diced chicken until cooked through.
Add the rice to the wok and break up any clumps.
Season with soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar, tossing to coat.
Mix in the scrambled eggs and green onions.
Serve hot.

title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
ingredients: 3 lemongrass stalks, lower part only, bruised
instructions: Combine chicken stock, lemongrass, galangal paste, and lime leaves in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add chicken slices and straw mushrooms; cook until chicken is done.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Serve with fresh cilantro.

title: Khao Niao Mamuang (Mango Sticky Rice)
instructions: Soak sticky rice in water for 4 hours, then drain.
Steam the rice until fully cooked and fluffy.
In a separate small pot, heat palm sugar and thin coconut milk until melted.
Drizzle the sweet coconut milk over the hot steamed rice.
Serve with sliced mango, extra thick coconut milk, and toasted mung beans.

title: Khao Pad Hat Yai (Hoi Tad)
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
4 tbsp sweet soy sauce, Thai style
instructions: Scramble the eggs in a wok with a little oil and set aside.
Heat sesame oil in the wok, sauté minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the cooked rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sweet soy sauce and palm sugar, tossing to coat evenly.
Add the shredded meat, scrambled eggs, bean sprouts, and green onions.
Cook over high heat for 3-4 minutes until everything is hot and slightly crispy.

title: Gai Tod Nam Jim (Fried Chicken with Dipping Sauce)
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and baking powder to make a batter, then marinate chicken pieces.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked through, then drain.
Combine tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, water, and lime juice in a pot.
Simmer the sauce until it thickens slightly, about 10 minutes.
Serve the fried chicken hot with the warm dipping sauce and crushed peanuts.

title: Khao Soi Hat Yai
instructions: Simmer chicken broth, lemongrass, dried chilies, and chicken until meat is tender.
In a separate pot, heat coconut milk, curry powder, turmeric, palm sugar, and salt.
Add the cooked chicken and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavor.
Blanch the egg noodles and rice noodles separately in boiling water.
Place noodles in a deep bowl, top with chicken pieces and coconut curry sauce.
Dot with a piece of butter and drizzle with chili oil before serving.

title: Pad Thai Hat Yai
ingredients: 2 cups rice noodles, soaked in warm water
1 cup chicken or pork, thinly sliced
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and toss with a little oil to prevent sticking.
Heat oil in a wok, stir-fry garlic and sliced meat until cooked.
Push meat to the side, scramble the eggs in the empty space, then mix everything together.
Add the noodles, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar; toss to combine.
Add bean sprouts and dried shrimp, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts, green onions, and lime wedges.

title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
instructions: Bring chicken broth to a simmer in a pot.
Add lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, chicken, and mushrooms; cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and white pepper.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling vigorously.
Remove lemongrass stalks, stir in Thai basil, and serve hot with roasted peanuts.

title: Pad Kra Pao Moo
ingredients: 1 bunch Thai holy basil leaves, chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add garlic and chilies, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add ground pork, break it up and cook until browned.
Stir in dried shrimp, oyster sauce, and fish sauce.
Add basil leaves and toss quickly until wilted.
Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Khao Pad Udon Thani
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add corn and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add cooked rice, breaking up any clumps.
Stir in fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Push rice to the side and scramble the eggs into the pan.
Mix everything together until heated through.
Garnish with bean sprouts and spring onions.

title: Gai Pad Prik Ging
instructions: Season chicken slices with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry chilies, garlic, and galangal until fragrant.
Add chicken and corn, toss until chicken is cooked through.
Add fish sauce and palm sugar, stirring to coat.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro.

title: Gaeng Som Tai Pla
ingredients: 1 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Dissolve tamarind concentrate in water and bring to a boil.
Add galangal, garlic, and lime leaves; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add long beans and straw mushrooms; cook for 2 minutes.
Add papaya and eggplant; simmer until tender.
Add fish slices gently and cook just until opaque.
Stir in palm sugar and fish sauce to taste.
Serve hot in small bowls with sticky rice.

title: Sai Ua Udon Thani
ingredients: 1/2 cup fermented soybean paste, mixed with water
1 tsp shrimp paste, dissolved in water
instructions: Mix pork, beef, fish sauce, palm sugar, white pepper, and basil.
Pack the mixture tightly into a banana leaf tube.
Place the tube in a steamer lined with banana leaves.
Steam over boiling water for 45 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from steamer and let cool slightly.
Slice the sausage into rounds.
Serve with a dipping sauce made of fermented soybean paste and shrimp paste.

title: Khao Niew Mamuang
ingredients: 100g fresh mangosteen, peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Steam the soaked glutinous rice until fluffy and tender.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, palm sugar, and evaporated milk over medium heat.
Stir constantly until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens slightly.
Pour the warm coconut mixture over the steamed rice.
Gently fold the rice and add fresh mangosteen chunks to serve.

title: Khao Soi
instructions: Sauté yellow curry paste in a pot with a little oil until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, fish sauce, lime juice, palm sugar, and tamarind paste; simmer until oil separates.
Add chicken slices and cook until cooked through.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil, then add the noodles.
Divide noodles into bowls, top with chicken, a hard-boiled egg, cilantro, and fried shallots.
Serve immediately while hot.

title: Nam Prik Num
ingredients: 10 dried chilies, soaked in warm water
instructions: Blend soaked chilies, garlic, and galangal with a little water until smooth.
In a wok, sauté the shrimp paste over low heat until fragrant.
Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Stir in the palm sugar and fish sauce.
Finally, add the ground peanuts and mix well before serving.

title: Khao Kha Moo
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into large chunks
5 stalks pandan leaves, tied in a knot
instructions: Place pork belly in a clay pot or heavy pot with coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, lime leaves, and lemongrass.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 hours until pork is tender.
Stir in ground white pepper and pandan leaves during the last 10 minutes.
Skim any excess oil from the surface before serving.
Serve the pork chunks with the rich coconut gravy over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Gaeng Phet Nam Khing
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté green curry paste until the oil turns green.
Add the sliced beef and stir-fry until the edges are slightly browned.
Pour in the coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and black pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes until the sauce thickens and beef is cooked.
Turn off the heat and stir in the chopped morning glory leaves before serving.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes
instructions: Drain the soaked noodles and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add dried shrimp and cook for 30 seconds.
Push ingredients to the side and scramble the eggs in the hot oil.
Add the noodles to the wok and toss to combine with the eggs.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until coated.
Add bean sprouts and basil, cooking just until wilted.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts, shredded cucumber, and lime wedges.

title: Tom Yum Goong
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
2 Thai bird's eye chilies, slit lengthwise
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken stock, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, chilies, and galangal.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms and straw mushrooms, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Increase heat to high and add the shrimp, cooking for 2-3 minutes until they turn pink.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot in bowls, garnished with extra lime leaves if desired.

title: Khao Soi
instructions: In a large pot, sauté onions in coconut oil until translucent.
Add curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Stir in tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the chicken cubes and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Add coconut milk and green beans, simmering for 5 more minutes.
In a separate pot, blanch the egg noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Divide the noodles into bowls, ladle the chicken and broth over them.
Serve with lime wedges and crushed peanuts on the side.

title: Green Curry with Pork
ingredients: 1 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the green curry paste for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the sliced pork and cook until it changes color.
Pour in the coconut milk, separating the thick cream from the thin milk if desired.
Add the torn kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots, long beans, and bell pepper, cooking for another 5 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar to taste.
Turn off the heat and stir in the Thai basil leaves until wilted.
Serve hot over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Mango Sticky Rice
instructions: Soak the glutinous rice in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Steam the soaked rice until tender and fluffy, about 20-25 minutes.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, sugar, water, and salt.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens slightly.
Pour the warm coconut mixture over the steamed rice and gently fold to coat evenly.
Let the rice rest for 10 minutes to absorb the coconut milk.
Serve warm or at room temperature, topped with sliced mango.
Garnish with toasted mung beans and sesame seeds if desired.

title: Gaeng Som
ingredients: 2 tbsp palm sugar, dissolved in water
1/2 cup tamarind concentrate, mixed with 1 cup warm water
1/2 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and fry garlic, chilies, and galangal until fragrant.
Add dried shrimp and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tamarind mixture and bring to a boil.
Add fish sauce, palm sugar, and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in shredded papaya, tomatoes, long beans, and lime leaves.
Simmer for another 5 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Khao Soi
ingredients: 2 cups rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Fry sliced shallots in oil until golden brown, then set aside some for garnish.
In a pot, sauté yellow curry paste in oil for 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk, turmeric, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and fish sauce; stir well.
Pour in chicken stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add soaked noodles and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Ladle soup into bowls, top with cabbage, noodles, and fried shallots.
Place a hard-boiled egg on top of each serving.

title: Pad Thai
ingredients: 1/4 cup chicken or pork, thinly sliced (optional)
instructions: Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and garlic to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok and scramble the eggs; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry garlic and dried shrimp until fragrant.
Add sliced meat if using and cook until done.
Toss in soaked noodles and pour the sauce over; stir-fry until coated.
Return eggs to the wok and mix well.
Add bean sprouts and green onions; cook for 1 minute.
Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts.

title: Khao Pad
ingredients: 3 cups jasmine rice, cooked and slightly underdone
instructions: Mix fish sauce, soy sauce, white pepper, and sugar to make the seasoning.
Heat oil in a large pan and scramble the eggs; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté garlic and dried shrimp until fragrant.
Add chopped meat or shrimp and cook until done.
Stir in the cooked rice and pour the seasoning over; toss to combine.
Add scrambled eggs and mix thoroughly.
Sprinkle green onions on top before serving.

title: Sai Oua
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh herbs (mint, cilantro, Thai basil), finely chopped
instructions: Combine ground pork, herbs, lemongrass, lime zest, fish sauce, palm sugar, chilies, and spices in a bowl.
Add rice flour gradually and mix until a firm dough forms.
Stuff the mixture into natural casings or wrap in banana leaves.
Boil the sausages for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Alternatively, pan-fry over medium heat until golden brown.
Slice into rounds and serve with sticky rice and chili dipping sauce.

title: Khao Kha Moo (Braised Pork Belly with Rice)
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, cut into chunks
instructions: Fry pork belly chunks in oil until golden brown on all sides.
Remove pork and set aside, leaving the oil in the pot.
Add lemongrass and peppercorns to the oil, fry until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot, add fish sauce, palm sugar, lime leaves, and water.
Simmer on low heat for 2 hours until pork is tender and sauce reduces.
Serve the braised pork over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Gaeng Som (Sour Thai Curry)
ingredients: 100 g dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
instructions: Fry minced lemongrass, galangal, and tomato paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add sliced pork and dried shrimp, stir-fry until pork changes color.
Pour in coconut milk, tamarind concentrate, fish sauce, palm sugar, and water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until flavors meld.
Add torn lime leaves and cook for another 2 minutes.
Serve hot with garnish of fresh basil and long beans.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Spicy Shrimp Soup)
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken stock, lemongrass, galangal, and dried chilies.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and eggplant, cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and shrimp.
Simmer gently for 4 minutes until shrimp turn pink.
Remove lemongrass and galangal stalks before serving.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Rice Noodles)
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain.
In a wok, fry shrimp until pink, remove and set aside.
Add oil to the wok, scramble the eggs and push to the side.
Add tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and chili flakes, stir to dissolve.
Toss in noodles and cook, stirring constantly for 3 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and shrimp back into the wok.
Toss in crushed peanuts and green onions.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried shrimp, soaked and crushed
instructions: Place shredded papaya, carrots, chilies, garlic, and lemongrass in a mortar.
Pound lightly until the ingredients are bruised but not mushy.
Add tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, salt, and peanuts.
Pound gently until sugar dissolves and flavors mix.
Stir in dried shrimp and lime juice.
Mix quickly by hand to prevent the papaya from turning brown.
Serve immediately garnished with cilantro.

title: Pad Thai with Shrimp
ingredients: 200g rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Combine fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry shrimp until pink, then remove.
Add garlic to the wok and cook until fragrant.
Push ingredients to the side, pour in eggs, and scramble until set.
Add soaked noodles and sauce, tossing quickly to coat.
Return shrimp to the wok and stir-fry for another minute.
Remove from heat, toss in bean sprouts and green onions.
Serve immediately garnished with crushed peanuts.

title: Tom Yum Goong
instructions: Bring stock to a boil in a pot.
Add kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and chilies.
Simmer for 10 minutes to release aromas.
Add shrimp and cook until just opaque.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar to taste.
If using, stir in coconut milk gently.
Serve hot in bowls.

title: Khao Pad Pad Thai Style (Fried Rice)
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, cooked and cooled
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and fry pork until crispy, then set aside.
Add a little more oil and scramble the eggs, then remove.
Return pork to wok and add remaining oil.
Add rice, tossing constantly to separate grains.
Pour in fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and pepper.
Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Add bean sprouts and cabbage, tossing briefly.
Fold in eggs and pork, garnish with chili and serve.

title: Gaeng Keow Wan (Green Curry)
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and fry curry paste until fragrant.
Add half the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add bamboo shoots and eggplant.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Stir in kaffir lime leaves and basil leaves.
Simmer for 5 more minutes until vegetables are tender.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
instructions: Place shredded papaya and carrot in a mortar.
Add chilies, garlic, and lemongrass and pound gently.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar, pounding to dissolve sugar.
Stir in peanuts and crushed dried shrimp.
Mix thoroughly until ingredients are well combined.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

title: Khao Pad Pad Thai (Stir-fried Rice Noodles with Shrimp)
ingredients: 200g dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water until soft, then drain.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, then push to the side.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble, mixing with the shrimp.
Add noodles, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar; toss well.
Stir in bean sprouts and green onions until just wilted.
Serve hot topped with crushed peanuts and a lime wedge.

title: Gaeng Som (Sour Pork and Fish Curry)
ingredients: 3 tbsp tamarind pulp, diluted in 1/2 cup water
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Fry shallots, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves in oil until golden.
Add pork and anchovies; stir-fry until the pork changes color.
Pour in the tamarind water and bring to a simmer.
Add coconut milk and let it thicken slightly.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, chilies, and remaining lime leaves.
Simmer for 10 minutes until flavors meld.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

title: Khao Niew Ma Muu (Sticky Rice with Mung Bean Paste)
instructions: Steam the soaked sticky rice until fully cooked and fluffy.
Mix mung bean paste, coconut milk, palm sugar, and salt in a small pot.
Heat the mixture over low heat until thickened.
Place a portion of sticky rice on a banana leaf or plate.
Top with a spoonful of sweet mung bean paste.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts, sesame seeds, mint, and dried shrimp.

title: Tom Yum Goong (Spicy Shrimp Soup)
ingredients: 4 stalks lemongrass, white part only, bruised
1/2 cup tamarind paste diluted in 1 cup water
instructions: Boil water with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies.
Add mushrooms and cook until tender.
Add shrimp and cook just until they turn pink.
Stir in fish sauce, tamarind water, and coconut milk.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice, bean sprouts, and cilantro.
Serve immediately in hot bowls.

title: Pad Pak Ruak (Stir-fried Morning Glory)
ingredients: 1 bunch morning glory, tough stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and chilies; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add morning glory and stir-fry vigorously for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in water, fish sauce, and palm sugar; toss to coat.
Add bean sprouts and cook until they wilt slightly.
If using, quickly scramble the egg into the mix.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve immediately.

title: Pad Krapow Moo Saap
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking slightly.
Add minced garlic and chilies, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground pork and break it up, cook until browned and crispy.
Mix fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and palm sugar in a small bowl.
Pour the sauce into the wok, tossing quickly until the pork is glazed.
Remove from heat and stir in the chopped basil leaves.
Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice with bean sprouts on the side.

title: Gaeng Som
ingredients: 1/2 cup tamarind paste, diluted in 2 cups water
1/2 cup long beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/2 cup green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup tamarind paste, diluted in 1 cup water
instructions: Boil the tamarind water (2 cups) in a pot and strain to remove solids.
Add garlic and chilies to the tamarind water, simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar until dissolved.
Add the long beans and green beans, cook for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add the tofu and chicken slices, cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in the torn kaffir lime leaves and the second batch of tamarind water.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Khao Niao Ma Mu
ingredients: 1/2 cup mung beans, soaked and cooked until soft
instructions: Steam the sticky rice until fully cooked and fluffy.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, palm sugar, pandan leaves, and kaffir lime leaves.
Heat over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves and it thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and stir in the coconut cream.
Mix the warm coconut milk mixture with the steamed sticky rice.
Line a small bowl with banana leaves and pack the rice mixture inside.
Steam the wrapped rice for 10 minutes to meld the flavors.
Unwrap and serve warm with the cooked mung beans on the side.

title: Nam Prik Num
instructions: Boil the green beans until tender-crisp, then drain and set aside.
In a mortar, pound the shrimp paste with a small amount of salt until smooth.
Add the garlic, chilies, and remaining salt, pounding until well combined.
Add the palm sugar, roasted rice powder, and roasted coconut powder, pounding gently.
Gradually add the lime juice while pounding to create a thick paste.
Mix in the cooked green beans and fresh crab meat.
Serve immediately as a dipping sauce with grilled pork or crackers.

title: Tom Kha Gai
ingredients: 3 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: In a pot, combine chicken broth, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse flavors.
Stir in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer, do not boil vigorously.
Add the sliced chicken and straw mushrooms, cook for 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked.
Stir in the lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar to taste.
Remove the lemongrass stalks and galangal slices before serving.
Garnish with sliced chili if desired and serve hot with rice.

title: Khao Soi (Northern Thai Curry Noodles)
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant and translucent.
Add cumin seeds and stir for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Stir in turmeric and cook for another minute.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add Thai eggplant and green chilies, cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and let it simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Cook the egg noodles in boiling water according to package directions, then drain.
Divide noodles into bowls and ladle the hot curry soup over them.
Serve immediately with lime wedges, fresh coriander, and fried shallots.

title: Pad Prik Khing (Spicy Basil Stir-fry)
ingredients: 4-5 bird's eye chilies, sliced (adjust to taste)
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and cook until soft.
Add ground meat and stir-fry until fully cooked and browned.
Toss in bird's eye chilies and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add fish sauce, palm sugar, oyster sauce, and white pepper; mix well.
Add fresh holy basil leaves and stir rapidly until they wilt.
Toss in bean sprouts and cook for another 30 seconds.
Remove from heat and serve hot over steamed jasmine rice.

title: Gaeng Kua (Northern Thai Sweet & Sour Curry)
ingredients: 2 cups beef stewing cubes, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté sliced onion and crushed garlic until softened.
Add beef cubes and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until browned.
Add turmeric powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add green beans and long beans; cook for 5 minutes.
In a separate bowl, mix tamarind paste, brown sugar, and fish sauce until dissolved.
Stir the sauce mixture into the pot.
Add torn kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes until the sauce thickens and meat is tender.
Serve with steamed sticky rice.

title: Gaeng Daeng (Red Curry)
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
1 cup long beans, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium-high heat.
Add lemongrass and Thai red curry paste; fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 1/2 cup of coconut milk and stir until the paste dissolves.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the color changes.
Add bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, bell peppers, and long beans.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and white pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot with jasmine rice.

title: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-fry)
ingredients: 1 egg, fried sunny-side up for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground pork and break it up with a spatula; cook until browned.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, white pepper, and sliced chilies.
Stir-fry rapidly for 1-2 minutes until the sauce coats the meat and reduces slightly.
Add fresh holy basil leaves and toss until wilted.
Sprinkle toasted rice powder over the stir-fry.
Serve immediately over a mound of jasmine rice with a fried egg on top.
Garnish with extra basil if desired.

title: Khao Soi Chiang Rai
ingredients: 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
instructions: Boil chicken with 1 cup coconut milk, curry pastes, sugar, salt, and lime leaves until tender.
Strain the broth and reserve the solids for serving.
Simmer the strained broth with the remaining 1 cup coconut milk until slightly reduced.
Divide noodles and chicken into bowls, pour broth over, and top with greens.
Serve immediately with lime juice on the side.

title: Gai Yang (Grilled Chicken)
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken legs and thighs, skin on
instructions: Marinate chicken in fish sauce, sugar, lime zest, lemongrass, oil, and pepper for at least 2 hours.
Grill chicken over charcoal or high heat until skin is crispy and meat is cooked through.
Brush with sweet chili sauce during the last few minutes of grilling.
Slice and serve with lime wedges and jasmine rice.

title: Som Tum (Papaya Salad)
instructions: Place papaya, tomatoes, beans, green tomatoes, and chilies in a mortar.
Pound gently to release juices without turning them into a puree.
Add fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and dried shrimp; pound lightly to mix.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then toss in peanuts before serving.

title: Khao Pad Sai Oua
ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, cooked and slightly undercooked
1/4 cup fermented pork sausage (Sai Oua), sliced
instructions: Stir-fry pork belly and beef in a wok until browned.
Add Sai Oua sausage and cook for 1 minute.
Add rice, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and soy sauce; toss to coat evenly.
Stir in green onions and cilantro, then top with fried egg and lime wedges.

title: Tom Kha Gai
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
1/4 cup lemongrass, bruised and cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Simmer chicken with galangal, lemongrass, and lime leaves in chicken stock for 5 minutes.
Add coconut milk and mushrooms; simmer gently until mushrooms are tender.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice.
Remove from heat, stir in Thai basil, and serve hot.

title: Classic New York Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C) and prepare a 9-inch springform pan.
Mix graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter; press firmly into the pan bottom.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in vanilla extract, sour cream, and lemon juice until combined.
Pour batter over the crust and bake for 60-70 minutes.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Southern-Style Fried Chicken
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Whisk eggs and buttermilk together in a shallow dish.
Combine flour, paprika, garlic powder, thyme, salt, pepper, and cayenne in another dish.
Dip chicken pieces into the egg mixture, then coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken pieces for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Apple Pie with Lattice Top
ingredients: 6 large Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss sliced apples with sugar, brown sugar, flour, spices, and lemon juice.
Roll out one crust and place it in a 9-inch pie dish.
Spread apple mixture evenly over the bottom crust.
Roll out the second crust and cut strips for a lattice pattern.
Weave the strips over the apples and crimp edges to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg and bake for 45-50 minutes until golden.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round cake pans.
Separate eggs; beat yolks with sugar until pale, then mix in butter, flour, and milk.
Whip egg whites until stiff peaks form and fold into the yolk mixture.
Fold in dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, salt) gently.
Divide batter evenly between pans and bake for 25-30 minutes.
Cool cakes completely, then slice each horizontally to create 4 layers.
Beat cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Assemble cake by layering sponge, cream, and sponge.
Frost the entire cake with remaining cream.

title: Key West Chicken Salad
instructions: Season chicken breasts with oregano, salt, and pepper.
Sear chicken in olive oil over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through.
Slice chicken thinly against the grain.
Whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, and lemon zest for the dressing.
Toss salad greens with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and olives.
Top the salad with sliced chicken, feta cheese, and dressing.
Serve immediately.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large bowl, toss apples with sugar, flour, cinnamon, and salt.
Place bottom crust in a 9-inch pie dish and fill with apple mixture.
Dot the top with butter cubes.
Cover with top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits for steam.
Bake for 45 minutes or until crust is golden and filling bubbles.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 4 lbs chicken pieces, thawed and patted dry
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
In a bag, mix flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Dip chicken pieces in buttermilk, then coat thoroughly in flour mixture.
Fry chicken in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Place fried chicken on a wire rack in the preheated oven to crisp up.
Serve immediately with mashed potatoes and gravy.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat; sauté onion, celery, and garlic until soft.
Add potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in clams and milk; simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in heavy cream and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Kansas City BBQ Pulled Pork
instructions: Mix dry spices and rub onto pork shoulder; let sit for 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C) and place pork in a roasting pan.
Bake uncovered for 6-8 hours until meat shreds easily with a fork.
Remove pork from bones and shred with two forks.
Stir shredded pork into BBQ sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve on buns with coleslaw.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round cake pans.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, butter, flour, baking powder, and salt.
Slowly whisk in milk until smooth.
Whip egg whites until stiff peaks form; fold gently into batter.
Divide batter between pans and bake for 30-35 minutes until golden.
Let cool completely, then split each cake horizontally.
Spread pastry cream on bottom layers, add top layers, and frost with buttercream.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 6 large Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and sliced
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Roll out bottom pie crust and place in a 9-inch pie pan.
In a bowl, toss apples with sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and butter.
Fill the crust with the apple mixture.
Cover with top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits for steam.
Brush crust with egg wash mixed with milk.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown and filling bubbles.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 1 pound fresh clams, cleaned and chopped
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and celery until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir for 1 minute to cook the raw taste.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in heavy cream and clams.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt, pepper, and parsley before serving.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels.
In a shallow dish, mix flour, paprika, thyme, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne.
Dip chicken pieces into buttermilk, then coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken pieces in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels before serving.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt; add butter, eggs, and milk.
Divide batter evenly between pans and bake for 25-30 minutes.
Cool cakes completely on wire racks.
Beat egg yolks, sugar, and water until thick and pale.
Add vanilla pudding mix and remaining butter; cook over low heat until thickened.
Let custard cool, then spread between cake layers.
Frost top and sides with chocolate ganache or buttercream.

title: Chicago-style Deep Dish Pizza
ingredients: 1/2 cup Italian sausage, cooked and crumbled
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water with olive oil and let foam for 5 minutes.
Mix flour and salt; gradually add yeast mixture to form a dough.
Knead for 5 minutes and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with a pizza stone or heavy baking sheet inside.
Roll dough into a thick circle and press into a deep-dish pan.
Layer cheese, tomato sauce, onions, and sausage in the crust.
Top with more cheese.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

title: Classic American Apple Pie
ingredients: 6 large Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced
2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
In a large bowl, toss apples with sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and butter.
Place bottom crust in a 9-inch pie dish and fill with apple mixture.
Cover with top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits in the top.
Brush crust with egg wash and bake for 45-50 minutes until golden brown.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: Old Fashioned Meatloaf
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soak breadcrumbs in milk until soft.
In a large bowl, mix beef, soaked breadcrumbs, onion, eggs, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, and parsley.
Form mixture into a loaf shape on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 1 hour, then cover loosely with foil and bake for another 30 minutes.
Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks), skin on
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.
In a shallow dish, mix flour, salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and thyme.
Dredge chicken pieces in buttermilk, then coat thoroughly in flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease two 9-inch round pans.
Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; set aside.
Cream butter and sugar, then add eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla.
Alternately add dry ingredients and milk to the butter mixture, mixing just until combined.
Divide batter between pans and bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely, then sandwich with vanilla custard and top with chocolate ganache and whipped cream.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat and sauté onion and celery until soft.
Add potatoes and chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in white wine and salt pork; simmer for another 10 minutes.
Add clams and bay leaf, cook for 5 minutes until clams open.
Remove bay leaf, stir in heavy cream and pepper, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 1 double-crust pie dough, homemade or store-bought
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, cold and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place bottom pie crust in a 9-inch pie dish and trim edges.
In a large bowl, toss sliced apples with sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cold butter cubes until coated.
Spoon apple mixture into the crust, mounding it slightly in the center.
Cover with top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits in the top for steam.
Brush crust with egg wash and sprinkle with sugar if desired.
Bake for 50-60 minutes until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Cook bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp; remove and drain, leaving fat in pot.
Sauté onion and celery in bacon fat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in clam juice and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Melt butter in a small bowl, whisk in flour, and slowly stir into the chowder.
Add milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes to thicken.
Stir in reserved bacon and chopped clams.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Rinse chicken pieces and pat dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, thyme, and cayenne.
Dredge chicken pieces in the flour mixture to coat evenly.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large pot to 350°F (175°C).
Carefully place chicken pieces in the hot oil without overcrowding.
Fry for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with gravy or coleslaw.

title: Boston Cream Pie
ingredients: 1 lb (450g) vanilla custard or pastry cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round cake pans.
Mix cake mix, egg yolks, sugar, milk, and melted butter according to package directions.
Divide batter evenly between pans and bake for 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cakes completely in pans, then remove and cool on wire racks.
Whip egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form; fold into cooled custard.
Pipe or spread half of the custard mixture onto one cake layer.
Place the second cake layer on top.
Frost the entire pie with the remaining custard, then chill for 30 minutes.
Whip heavy cream with vanilla until soft peaks form and spread over the chilled pie.
Drizzle melted chocolate over the top and serve.

title: Chicago-Style Deep Dish Pizza
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with a pizza stone inside if available.
Roll out pizza dough into a 12-inch circle and place in a deep-dish pan.
Brush the edges of the crust with olive oil.
Spread ricotta cheese evenly over the bottom of the crust.
Sprinkle half of the mozzarella cheese over the ricotta.
Spread tomato sauce over the cheese, leaving a 1-inch border around the edge.
Top with remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with fresh basil, and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Classic American Apple Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix apples, sugar, flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a large bowl.
Pour apple mixture into the bottom of the pie crust.
Dot the top with butter cubes.
Cover with the top pie crust and crimp edges to seal.
Cut slits in the top crust to vent steam.
Brush the crust with beaten egg.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
Cool for at least 1 hour before slicing.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a shallow dish, mix flour, salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder.
Dip chicken pieces into the beaten eggs mixed with buttermilk.
Coat each piece thoroughly in the flour mixture, pressing firmly to adhere.
Heat oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Place fried chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Bake for 5-10 minutes to crisp the skin.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicago-Style Deep Dish Pizza
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with a pizza stone inside.
Stretch the dough into a 10-inch circle and place in a deep-dish pan.
Spread tomato sauce evenly over the bottom of the crust.
Layer the low-moisture and fresh mozzarella cheeses over the sauce.
Drizzle olive oil over the cheese.
Sprinkle with Italian seasoning and parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is melted.
Remove from oven and immediately top with torn fresh basil leaves.
Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing into wedges.

title: BBQ Ribs
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs.
Season ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Bake ribs in a covered roasting pan for 2 hours until tender.
While ribs bake, mix ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, paprika, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, and remaining salt and pepper.
Remove ribs from the oven and discard any liquid in the pan.
Brush the sauce generously over the ribs.
Bake uncovered for another 30 minutes.
Brush with more sauce and broil for 3-5 minutes until caramelized.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Steam the clams in a pot with a little water until they open; discard any that do not open.
In a large pot, cook bacon over medium heat until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Sauté onion and celery in the bacon fat until softened.
Add potatoes and flour, stirring for 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in the milk and heavy cream, adding bay leaves and thyme.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Add the clams and cooked bacon back into the pot.
Simmer for 5 more minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in fresh parsley before serving.

title: Classic American Apple Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place bottom crust in a 9-inch pie dish.
Mix apples, sugar, flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a large bowl.
Stir in butter cubes until mixture is crumbly.
Fill crust with apple mixture and dot with remaining butter.
Cover with top crust, crimp edges to seal, and cut slits in top for steam.
Brush crust with egg wash.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until crust is golden brown and filling bubbles.
Cool completely before slicing.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen chopped clams
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, celery, and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute to remove raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in broth and milk to avoid lumps.
Add thyme, potatoes, and clams.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: Cornflakes or panko breadcrumbs (optional, for extra crunch)
instructions: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt.
Whisk buttermilk with remaining salt in a large bowl; soak chicken for at least 2 hours.
Mix flour, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, thyme, and baking powder in a shallow dish.
Dredge chicken pieces in flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a deep skillet or fryer to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken in batches for 12-15 minutes until golden and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Separate eggs; beat yolks with melted butter, then mix with cake mix and milk.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form and fold into batter.
Pour batter into pans and bake for 30-35 minutes.
Cool cakes completely on wire racks.
Whip cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Pipe or spread half the filling onto one cake layer.
Place second cake layer on top and pipe remaining filling around edges.
Drizzle with melted chocolate and chill before serving.

title: Chicago-Style Deep Dish Pizza
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F (245°C) with pizza stone inside if available.
Roll dough into a deep-dish pan, pressing edges up the sides.
Brush bottom and sides with olive oil.
Spread tomato sauce over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
Layer spinach, sausage, and mozzarella evenly over the sauce.
Sprinkle parmesan cheese on top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven, top with fresh basil and red pepper flakes.
Slice and serve immediately.

title: Classic Apple Pie
ingredients: 6 cups Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place bottom crust in a 9-inch pie dish.
Toss apples with sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Spread apple mixture into the crust.
Dot with butter cubes.
Cover with top crust and crimp edges.
Brush top with beaten egg.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden brown.

title: New York-Style Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Mix crumbs and melted butter; press into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth.
Stir in sour cream, flour, and vanilla.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing just until combined.
Pour batter over crust.
Bake for 55-60 minutes until edges are set but center jiggles slightly.
Cool completely before refrigerating for 4 hours.

title: Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Prepare two 9-inch round cake layers according to box directions.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cakes completely.
Whip heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Pipe a layer of frosting onto the first cake.
Place second cake on top and frost the sides.
Chill for 2 hours before serving.

title: Chicago-Style Deep Dish Pizza
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water and let sit for 5 minutes.
Mix flour, salt, and oil; add yeast mixture and knead until smooth.
Let dough rise for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C) with a pizza stone inside.
Press dough into a deep-dish pan.
Spread sauce over dough, leaving a border.
Add ground beef, then layer cheeses.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until crust is golden.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ingredients: 12 pieces chicken, cut into drumsticks and thighs
instructions: Place chicken in a bowl and cover with buttermilk; refrigerate for 4 hours.
Mix flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne in a large bowl.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, letting excess drip off.
Dredge chicken pieces thoroughly in the flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry chicken for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Classic New York-Style Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Mix graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter; press into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in vanilla and sour cream until combined.
Pour batter into the crust and bake for 60-70 minutes until edges are set but center jiggles slightly.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

title: Traditional Boston Cream Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then mix in flour, baking powder, salt, and milk.
Divide batter between two greased and floured 8-inch round cake pans.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cakes completely, then fill with vanilla pastry cream.
Melt chocolate chips and spread over the top of the cake.
Whip heavy cream with sugar until stiff peaks form and pipe around the edge.

title: Authentic Chicken Pot Pie
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Sauté chicken in butter until cooked through, then remove from pan.
In the same pan, melt remaining butter and whisk in flour.
Gradually stir in chicken broth, milk, thyme, sage, salt, and pepper.
Cook until mixture thickens, then stir in vegetables and cooked chicken.
Pour filling into a 9-inch pie dish and cover with top crust.
Crimp edges to seal and cut slits in the top crust to vent steam.
